prs.title: fix(cli): make image paste work on WSL2 (WSLg clipboard detection + BMP fallback)
prs.body:
Fixes #22274

Two things break image paste under WSLg:

1. `getUserLinuxClipboardTool()` only checks `XDG_SESSION_TYPE`. WSLg doesn't set it (it does set `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0`), so no clipboard tool is ever picked and paste silently fails. This falls back to `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` / `DISPLAY` when the session type is missing, keeping `XDG_SESSION_TYPE` as the source of truth when it is set.

2. When the image comes from the Windows side, the clipboard offers `image/bmp` instead of `image/png`, and the save path only ever asks for PNG. It now checks the offered types and, if BMP is what's available, fetches that and converts it to PNG (the API doesn't take BMP). The converter (`bmpToPng.ts`) is deliberately small — uncompressed 24/32-bit BMPs only, which is what clipboard sources produce — so this adds no new dependencies. Anything else still fails the way it did before, with a debug log.

Tests: new cases for the env fallback (WSLg-style env, X-only env, no display vars), the wl-paste BMP path end to end, and the converter itself (row flipping, top-down BMPs, the all-zero-alpha quirk you get from Windows clipboard BMPs). Existing clipboard suites pass (53 tests across clipboardUtils, clipboardUtils.windows and bmpToPng), and lint/format are clean.

One caveat: I don't have a Windows machine to test the real WSLg clipboard end to end, so that path is covered by unit tests with mocked tools rather than a live run. Happy to adjust if someone can try it on an actual WSL2 install.

issues.title: Sandbox: report the extra temp-storage read-write rule in sandbox.decision, and allow opting out

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
When a host passes a sandbox config with exactly one read-write path, the resolved policy reports two read-write rules (`sandbox.decision` / `policy_resolved` shows `readwrite: 2`). The second one is the temporary-storage grant, which follows `$TMPDIR`. It is not named in the event, and the schema's `readwritePaths` does not mention it either; the schema only says temporary storage "follows its own rules and stays granted".

Repro (Linux, bubblewrap, Copilot CLI 1.0.105; also seen with the SDK 1.0.24 runtime):
1. Start a session with a sandbox config whose only read-write path is the project folder, `addCurrentWorkingDirectory: false`, `allowDevToolAccess: false`.
2. Approve `touch "$TMPDIR/x"`: it succeeds. A sibling folder outside the project is refused, as expected.
3. The `sandbox.decision` event lists `readwrite: 2` without saying what the second rule is.

Requests:
1. Include the resolved rule paths (or at least the temp-storage path) in `sandbox.decision`, so a host can show the user exactly what is writable.
2. Offer an opt-out for the temp-storage grant (for example `allowTempStorage: false`), for hosts that want a strict policy and can give the session its own scratch folder.

issues.title: `/remote on` says "Incoming account connections are disabled" when another CLI on the machine already hosts remote control

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Only one CLI process on a machine can host remote control at a time. While another CLI holds the host, `/remote on` in a second CLI fails with:

```
Incoming account connections are disabled. Enable them in /environments > Incoming connections before sharing this session.
```

Incoming connections were already enabled: `ahpEnvironment.acceptRemoteConnections` was `true` in `~/.copilot/settings.json`, so the message sends the user to turn on a setting that is already on. The real cause was an earlier CLI process, still open, that held the host. While it ran, `.attached-host.owner` under `~/.copilot/ahp/<compute id>/sessions/` contained that earlier process's ID, and the second CLI never started its host.

After the first CLI exited, `/remote on` in the second CLI kept failing with the same message. It only worked after the second CLI was restarted.

### Affected version

1.0.112

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

This is the sequence I observed, not a separate controlled repro:

1. Incoming connections enabled (`ahpEnvironment.acceptRemoteConnections: true`).
2. In CLI A, run `/remote on`. It succeeds and reports that it is sharing the session.
3. Keep A open. Start CLI B and run `/remote on`. It fails with the message above.
4. Exit A with `/exit`, then run `/remote on` in B again. Same message.
5. Restart B. Its host starts normally.

### Expected behavior

The error says another CLI process on this machine is hosting remote control (ideally which one) and how to take over or stop it. Or more than one CLI can host. A CLI that could not host at startup should also pick up the host once it is free, instead of needing a restart.

### Additional context

- OS: Windows, OS build 26300
- CPU architecture: x64
- Shell: PowerShell 7.6

issues.title: Two mode: "immediate" messages taken in at one step reach the model as one string ("no" + "drop phase 7" = "nodrop phase 7")

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

issues.body: ### Describe the bug When two `session.send` calls with `mode: "immediate"` arrive while a tool runs, the CLI takes both in at the next step and puts them into **one** user message, one text block each. It also trims each block. The model then reads the blocks as one string with no separator. The user sent "no" and then "drop phase 7". The model read "nodrop phase 7". The session events are correct: there are two `user.message` events (`"no"` and `"drop phase 7"`, both `delivery: "steering"`). Only the model request merges them. ### Affected version GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.113-0 (macOS arm64), `copilot --headless --stdio`, protocol 4. Model `claude-haiku-4.5` (also seen with `claude-opus-5.5`). ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start `copilot --headless --stdio --log-level all --log-dir ./logs` and create a session with `permissions: { request: true }`. Approve permission requests. 2. `session.send` the prompt: "Run exactly this bash command first: sleep 12. After it finishes, reply with ONLY a JSON array holding the exact raw text of each user message you received after this one, one item per message." 3. When `tool.execution_start` arrives, wait 3 s, then send two steers back to back: - `session.send { prompt: "no", mode: "immediate" }` - `session.send { prompt: "drop phase 7", mode: "immediate" }` 4. Wait for `session.idle`. ### Result | Sends | Model answer | |---|---| | `no`, `drop phase 7` | `["nodrop phase 7"]` | | `no\n`, `drop phase 7\n` | `["nodrop phase 7"]` (the trailing newline is trimmed) | | second send only after the first one's `user.message` event | `["no", "drop phase 7"]` | The model request in the debug log: ```json { "role": "user", "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "no" }, { "type": "text", "text": "drop phase 7" } ] } ``` The model's reasoning starts with: `The user has sent a message "nodrop phase 7".` ### Expected behavior Two steering messages reach the model as two messages, or at least with a separator between the blocks (for example a blank line, as the interactive UI uses when it joins queued drafts). Two short messages glued together can change their meaning. ### Additional context Workaround in our client: send the next steer only after the CLI reports the previous one as a `user.message` event. System notifications (such as a shell completion) that arrive at the same step are added to the same user message, so the same issue may apply to them. Sent by Agency Coder on behalf of Radostin

issues.title: Organization-managed GPT models do not defer MCP tools despite Responses API and toolSearch enabled

labels.name: area:enterprise
labels.description: GitHub Enterprise (GHE/GHES) support, org policies, and enterprise settings

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
## Summary

Organization-managed GPT models load all MCP tool definitions upfront, even when tool search is enabled and the model uses the Responses API.

The same underlying model defers tools when accessed through GitHub’s hosted offering or a directly configured external provider using Responses.

This becomes expensive with large tool definitions: a separate organization-managed Sol test consumed **236,905 actual input tokens** for a simple “Reply OK” prompt that required no tools.

## Environment

- Copilot CLI **1.0.110**, macOS arm64.
- Custom model configured centrally through **GitHub organization settings**, not local BYOK.
- Selected model: `<org>/<key-name>/gpt-6-luna`.
- Organization configuration:
  - **Responses API**
  - Tool calling, Streaming, Vision and Thinking enabled.
- CLI setting: `"toolSearch": true`.
- MCP server setting: `"deferTools": "auto"`.

## Reproduction

1. Configure an organization-managed GPT model using Responses.
2. Connect enough MCP tools to exceed the tool-search threshold. Our test used 48 synthetic MCP tools.
3. Start a fresh interactive CLI conversation and select the organization-managed model.
4. Ask it to call one known synthetic read-only tool.
5. Inspect the `turn tool surface resolved` diagnostic.
6. Repeat with hosted and directly configured models.

## Results

Same tool inventory and underlying GPT‑6 Luna model:

| Connection | API | Total tools | Deferred tools |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Organization-managed | Responses | 49 | **0** |
| GitHub-hosted | Responses | 49 | **49** |
| Direct external Gateway | Responses | 49 | **49** |

The total includes one native function. All three cases successfully called the requested tool and returned its result.

The organization-managed case reports:

```json
{
  "tool_search_enabled": true,
  "model_tool_calls_allowed": true,
  "opted_out": false,
  "client_path": false,
  "builtin_path": false,
  "generic_path": false,
  "deferred_tool_count": 0
}
```

## Expected behavior / question

Organization-managed models should support on-demand tool loading where the model and endpoint support it, or clearly explain why tool search is unavailable despite being enabled.

Could the organization-qualified model ID or catalog `family: "custom"` be preventing selection of the Responses tool-search path? Is there a supported way for an organization administrator to enable this capability?

## Related

- microsoft/vscode#323699 — Capability propagation problems on the organization-managed model route; concerns Vision, not this exact behavior.
- github/copilot-cli#4613 — Earlier eager-loading regression, marked fixed in 1.0.105. This organization-managed case reproduces on 1.0.110.

issues.title: Python script execution replaces venv interpreter with global Python; behavior is not explained to the agent

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In Copilot CLI 1.0.112, standalone Python script commands execute through the venv interpreter’s resolved symlink target rather than preserving the venv path. Python consequently runs outside the activated venv, despite PATH and VIRTUAL_ENV still identifying that environment.

This also occurs when the command explicitly specifies the absolute venv interpreter path.

I don’t know whether this rewriting is intentional execution-validation behavior or a defect. Either way, the resulting interpreter change is surprising and was not apparent to the agent from its tool instructions. It required explicit testing and inspection of the child process’s parent-shell command to understand.


### Affected version

1.0.112

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Prepare an isolated reproduction in a normal terminal

repro_dir="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/copilot-venv-repro.XXXXXX")"
cd "$repro_dir"

python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

cat > probe.py <<'PY'
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

print(json.dumps({
    "executable": sys.executable,
    "prefix": sys.prefix,
    "base_prefix": sys.base_prefix,
    "VIRTUAL_ENV": os.environ.get("VIRTUAL_ENV"),
    "PATH": os.environ.get("PATH"),
    "sys.path": sys.path,
}, indent=2), flush=True)

subprocess.run([
    "/bin/ps", "-p", str(os.getppid()), "-o", "command="
], check=True)
PY

python3 probe.py

printf 'Probe path: %s/probe.py\n' "$PWD"
printf 'Venv Python: %s/bin/python3\n' "$VIRTUAL_ENV"

Confirm that normal terminal execution reports the venv’s prefix and that sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix.

2. Launch Copilot from that activated environment

copilot

3. Ask the agent to execute these separately

Substitute the literal absolute paths printed above:

python3 /absolute/path/to/probe.py

/absolute/path/to/.venv/bin/python3 /absolute/path/to/probe.py

Run each as its own Bash tool call, verbatim. Do not prepend diagnostic commands or combine them into a compound shell command: command shape affects the observed behavior.

4. Compare with explicit shell-wrapped execution

/bin/bash --noprofile --norc -c \
  'exec "${VIRTUAL_ENV:?Activate the intended venv first}/bin/python3" "$@"' _ \
  /absolute/path/to/probe.py

For standalone script commands:

• sys.prefix == sys.base_prefix: Python is outside the venv.
• sys.path contains global rather than venv site-packages.
• VIRTUAL_ENV and PATH still identify the activated venv.
• Packages installed in the venv cannot be imported.

The probe captured its parent shell executing a rewritten command shaped like:

/bin/bash --norc --noprofile -c command '/usr/local/Cellar/python@3.13/3.13.9/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.13/bin/python3.13' '…/probe.py'

Explicit shell-wrapped execution preserves the venv and finds its installed packages. No permission or sandbox settings were disabled during this comparison.


### Expected behavior

Ideally, execution validation should preserve the interpreter invocation semantics needed by Python venvs.

If this rewriting is intentional:

• Explain the behavior and supported venv invocation method in agent-facing tool descriptions or instructions.
• Expose the effective command/interpreter when it differs from the submitted command.
• Avoid leaving the agent to interpret the resulting import failure as evidence that dependencies are missing from the intended environment.

In our investigation, checking command -v python3 or running a separate python3 -c diagnostic showed the correct venv, while standalone script execution used global Python. That discrepancy made ordinary troubleshooting misleading.

### Additional context

Copilot CLI: 1.0.112, build 24d885ba
macOS, Intel
Homebrew Python 3.13.9
Activated symlink-based Python venv

issues.title: With forceRemoteSettingsRefresh, new sessions warn "Managed settings could not be confirmed" because no live policy fetch is started at session init

labels.name: area:plugins

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

My organization's managed settings include `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh`. Since then, opening a new session or switching sessions inside a running CLI often shows:

```
Initializing chat using settings required by your organization admin…
Plugins required by your organization admin could not be checked. Continuing with the current setup. Error: Managed settings could not be confirmed
```

The logs show that the cache-only startup path correctly refuses the cached policy (`source=none`), but no live fetch is started at that point. Managed plugin preparation waits about 12.5 s and gives up, and permission seeding times out after 5 s. The live fetch only runs at the next policy-refresh trigger, here the next session switch, and then succeeds immediately (`source=server`, `serverFetchFailed=false`).

In one CLI process today: 27 session registrations, 10 of these warnings and 13 `Permission seeding did not complete within 5000ms` warnings. The CLI does not hang; it continues without the policy for that init. The network is not the cause: `api.github.com` answers in about 0.3 s, and the live fetch, when it runs, completes immediately.

Possibly related to #5341 (same `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` setup, but there the CLI hangs; here it only degrades with a warning).

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.111 (first seen on 1.0.109, when the org started returning `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh`)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Sign in with an account whose organization's managed settings include `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh`.
2. Start `copilot` and use a session normally.
3. Open a new session (or switch to another one and back) a few times.
4. Some of the time, see the "Managed settings could not be confirmed" message. In `~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log`, see the sequence below.

Sanitized log excerpt (one occurrence):

```
18:50:31.510Z [INFO] Registering foreground session: <new-session>
18:50:31.615Z [INFO] [managedSettings] device MDM: no policy present on this device
18:50:31.615Z [INFO] [managedSettings] forceRemoteSettingsRefresh requires a live fetch for https://github.com/<org>/; cache-only startup will continue without server policy
18:50:31.615Z [INFO] [managedSettings] effective policy resolved: source=none, bypassDisabled=false, serverFetchFailed=false, ...
18:50:31.816Z [INFO] Signed in to https://github.com/<org>/ as <user>.
18:50:41.586Z [WARNING] Permission seeding did not complete within 5000ms for session <new-session>; releasing the extension load gate without authorizing interrupted work.
18:50:44.076Z [WARNING] Managed plugin preparation did not complete: Plugins required by your organization admin could not be checked. Continuing with the current setup. Error: Managed settings could not be confirmed
18:50:44.275Z [INFO] Registering foreground session: <previous-session>
18:50:44.531Z [INFO] [managedSettings] forceRemoteSettingsRefresh set — forcing a live fetch for https://github.com/<org>/ (a cached policy exists but will not be served or used as a fallback)
18:50:44.531Z [INFO] [managedSettings] server policy received from https://github.com/<org>/: bypassDisabled=false, keys=[features,extraKnownMarketplaces,model,permissions,forceRemoteSettingsRefresh]
18:50:44.531Z [INFO] [managedSettings] effective policy resolved: source=server, bypassDisabled=false, serverFetchFailed=false, ...
```

Between 18:50:31.6 and 18:50:44.5 no live fetch is logged for the new session.

### Expected behavior

When `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` makes the cache-only startup unusable, session init should start (or await) a live policy fetch. Managed plugin preparation and permission seeding would then receive the server policy instead of timing out and continuing without it.

### Additional context

- OS: Windows 11 Enterprise 10.0.26200 (build 26200)
- CPU architecture: x86_64 (AMD64)
- Terminal: Windows Terminal
- Shell: PowerShell 7.7.0
- Account: Enterprise Managed User; org policy fetched from github.com; no device MDM policy
- Full logs available on request

issues.title: Windows: stale copilot-keychain-chunk credentials accumulate and can exhaust Credential Manager

labels.name: area:authentication
labels.description: Login, OAuth, device auth, token management, and keychain integration

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
## Summary
On Windows, `copilot-keychain-chunk.*` entries appear to accumulate in Windows Credential Manager without being cleaned up. Once the per-user vault is full, **every** application on the machine fails to store credentials, which broke an unrelated tool's login.

## Observed
- Windows Credential Manager contained ~180 `copilot-keychain-chunk.<hash>.<uuid>.<n>` generic credentials (about two thirds of all entries in the vault).
- `CredWrite` from an unrelated process failed with Win32 error 8 (`ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY`, "Not enough memory resources are available to process this command") even for a ~1 KB blob. Free RAM was not an issue.
- An unrelated CLI that stores its OAuth token in Credential Manager then failed with an error mentioning "OS keyring is not reachable ... Not enough memory resources".
- After deleting all `copilot-keychain-chunk.*` entries (vault went from 265 to 83 entries), writes succeeded again.

## Suspected cause (inference, not confirmed)
Secrets are split into chunks, and when a secret is rewritten or refreshed (for example MCP OAuth tokens), the previous chunk set is not deleted. Failed or interrupted writes may also strand chunks. The middle UUID segment looks like a per-write version id.

## Suggested fix
1. On write: write the new chunks, update the index or pointer, then delete the old chunk set only after success.
2. On startup: sweep and delete any `copilot-keychain-chunk.*` entry not referenced by a current index.
3. Surface a clear warning when a credential write fails with a resource or quota error (related: #5399).

## Environment
- Windows 11
- Multiple MCP servers configured (several using OAuth)
- Not sure whether the writer is the CLI or the desktop app; both may share this storage code. Please re-label or transfer if this is the wrong repo.

issues.title: Security-review follow-up instructions are injected in non-interactive runs despite an explicit no-follow-ups prompt

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

> This report was drafted by an AI assistant (GitHub Copilot) from session logs and a reproduction on my machine, at my request; the reproduction below was run as written.

When the built-in `security-review` agent (run through the `task` tool) completes, the runtime adds a persistent instruction to the main agent's context (`instruction.update`, `name: "security-review-reporting"`, `authority: "runtime"`, `lifetime: "persistent"`, `boundary: "afterToolResults"`). It says, abridged:

> After the security review task completes, you MUST present the findings as a summary table using this exact format … Then, if any issues were found, use the ask_user tool (if available) to offer follow-up actions with these choices: "Fix highest severity issues" … "Fix all issues" … "Commit a summary of findings" … If the ask_user tool is not available, present the follow-up options as a numbered list and ask the user to reply with their choice.

It is injected regardless of the run's mode and instructions. The instruction appeared after all five security-review completions I observed (three in an earlier VS Code session, one in each of two CLI runs), including:

- in non-interactive `-p` runs (also with `--no-ask-user`);
- when the prompt explicitly forbade questions and follow-up offers.

Impact, seen in a long-running unattended session in VS Code's agent host (same runtime, 1.0.108-0), whose instructions forbade `ask_user`:

- after its second security-review subagent, and after delivering its findings, the agent called `ask_user` with exactly these three choices, prefaced "As requested, choose an optional follow-up". It treated the injected text as the user's request.
- The `ask_user` call remained pending for about 25 hours before a response was recorded.
- The offered choices ("Fix all issues", "Commit a summary…") would also have authorized code changes and commits in a task that was explicitly review-only.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.112 (latest), and the runtime 1.0.108-0 embedded in VS Code 1.146.0.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. In an empty git repo, add `app.js`:

   ```js
   const http = require('http');
   const { exec } = require('child_process');

   http.createServer((req, res) => {
     const host = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost').searchParams.get('host');
     exec('ping -c 1 ' + host, (err, out) => res.end(out));
   }).listen(8080);
   ```

2. Run:

   ```sh
   copilot -p "Use the security-review agent to review app.js. This is an unattended batch job: no human will read or answer questions. Do not ask any questions and do not offer follow-up actions. Print the findings, then the word DONE, and stop." \
     --no-ask-user --no-custom-instructions --allow-all-tools --allow-all-paths
   ```

3. Open the session's `~/.copilot/session-state/<session-id>/events.jsonl`. Right after `subagent.completed` with `agentName: "security-review"` (the matching `subagent.started` has `agentType: "security-review"`):

   ```
   instruction.update {"authority":"runtime","lifetime":"persistent","boundary":"afterToolResults","name":"security-review-reporting", ...}
   ```

   with the text quoted above.

In both short runs the model kept the prompt's "no follow-ups" (with the default model and with `--model gpt-6.1-sol`), but it switched to the injected table format. The earlier, long VS Code session did ask, as described above. I have not isolated why the outcomes differed (model, context length, host, runtime version or chance); the injection itself happened every time I looked.

### Expected behavior

- `-p` is non-interactive, so nobody can answer a follow-up question there. `--no-ask-user` disables the question form but still allows questions in replies. In a non-interactive run, or when the user explicitly forbids questions and follow-ups, the runtime should not inject an instruction to ask for a follow-up choice.
- Runtime-injected reporting hints should not override the user's prompt or custom instructions. At least, they should not be phrased as a "MUST", and they should say they are a default that the user's instructions take precedence over.
- Ideally, a way to turn the follow-up offer off (a setting or flag), and no offer to "Fix all issues" in a session the user told to change nothing.

### Additional context

- macOS 27.2.1, arm64, zsh; the `-p` run was started from a script, not an interactive terminal.
- Related, though about other features: #4318 (autopilot task-completion enforcement overriding explicit user instructions), #1088 (instructions ignored).

issues.title: source.path is ignored for git-based extraKnownMarketplaces in enterprise team settings

labels.name: area:enterprise

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When configuring a git-based marketplace via enterprise team managed settings, the documented source.path property appears to be ignored: [Enterprise Documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/enterprise-administrators/enterprise-managed-settings#strictknownmarketplaces).

Example:
```json
"Our-Marketplace": {
  "source": {
    "source": "git",
    "url": "https://dev.azure.com/...",
    "ref": "feature/testBranch",
    "path": "marketplaces/common"
  },
  "autoUpdate": true
}
```
The resulting managed-settings cache removes path and reports:
```json
"ignoredPaths": [
  "extraKnownMarketplaces.Our-Marketplace.source.path"
]
```

According to the Enterprise managed settings documentation, git sources support both optional ref and path.
Is path currently unsupported for extraKnownMarketplaces provided through enterprise team overrides, or is this a bug in the managed-settings validation?


### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.111-0.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure extraKnownMarketplaces as overridable in the enterprise managed-settings.json.
2. Map an enterprise team to a team-specific settings file using team-mappings.json.
3. In the team settings file, add a git-based marketplace containing url, ref, and path
4. Start or refresh Copilot so that the server-managed settings are retrieved.
5. Inspect the generated managed-settings cache under: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\copilot\managed-settings\`
6. Observe that the marketplace is present and url and ref are retained, but path has been removed.
7. Observe that path is explicitly listed under ignoredPaths:
```json
"ignoredPaths": [
  "extraKnownMarketplaces.Our-Marketplace.source.path"
]
```

### Expected behavior

source.path should be preserved instead of being added to ignoredPaths, and the marketplace should be loaded from the specified repository subdirectory.

### Additional context

Upon running /plugin marketplace browse Our-Marketplace, the output indicates that Copilot searches for the marketplace manifest in the following locations:
`Failed to browse marketplace: File not found: marketplace.json, .plugin/marketplace.json, .github/plugin/marketplace.json, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json`

For testing purposes, the repository contains a dedicated marketplace.json under the directory specified by the path property (marketplaces/common).

Our assumption is that path allows multiple marketplaces to be hosted in the same repository by using different subdirectories as their respective marketplace roots.

However, since path is removed from the effective managed settings and listed under ignoredPaths, Copilot appears to search for the marketplace manifest relative to the repository root instead of the configured subdirectory.

issues.title: Add /remove-dir command to revoke directory access

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Copilot CLI provides /add-dir and /list-dirs, but no corresponding command to remove a previously allowed directory. Users cannot reduce directory access during a session without restarting or otherwise resetting session state.

### Proposed solution

Add `/remove-dir <path>` as the counterpart to `/add-dir`. It should:

- Revoke file access to the specified previously allowed directory for the current session.
- Remove the directory from `/list-dirs` immediately.
- Unload trusted skills, agents, and instructions loaded from that directory when safe.
- Clearly report active references or running work that prevent immediate removal.
- Return a clear error when the path is not currently allowed.

This improves least-privilege workflows by allowing users to grant temporary access and revoke it as soon as it is no longer needed, without restarting the session.

### Example prompts or workflows

1. `/add-dir C:\work\shared-library`, work with files there, then run `/remove-dir C:\work\shared-library` when finished.

2. Run `/list-dirs`, identify an accidentally added directory, and remove it with `/remove-dir <path>`.

3. Temporarily allow access to generated artifacts, inspect them, then revoke access while keeping the current conversation.

4. Attempt to remove a directory used by a running task and receive a clear message explaining what must finish or stop first.

### Additional context

A dedicated removal command would make `/add-dir` reversible and provide a clearer least-privilege permission model. `/reset-allowed-tools` does not address directory access, and restarting a session is unnecessarily disruptive.

issues.title: [Bug] Subagents executing long tool-call sequences in a single turn fail prompt caching and compound token consumption

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

issues.body:
### Environment
- GitHub Copilot CLI v1.0.83
- OS: Windows 11 / PowerShell
- Primary Model: Gemini 3.8 Flash

### Problem Description
When executing autonomous subagents (such as custom agents via the `task` tool), the agent harness allows a subagent to run hundreds of tool calls within a single monolithic turn (Turn 0) without yielding or compacting context. 

Because each tool execution (file edits, test outputs, build diagnostics) is appended sequentially to the conversation history of the active turn:
1. **Prompt Caching is defeated**: The dynamic append of intermediate tool results changes the prompt prefix and prevents effective provider-side KV prompt caching.
2. **Exponential Token Compounding**: Every subsequent tool call re-submits the entire growing history (75k-100k+ tokens) to the model. In our session, a single subagent ran ~750 tool calls in Turn 0, compounding to over 120 million tokens consumed in under 40 minutes on local test/edit loops.
3. **No Turn-Yielding / Throttling Mechanism**: The agent does not yield control or checkpoint its context, and background interrupt signals (`write_agent`) are queued rather than preempting execution.

### Expected Behavior
- Subagent harnesses should enforce turn boundaries or context compaction/eviction after a reasonable threshold of consecutive tool calls (e.g. 15-20 tool calls) to preserve prompt caching and avoid runaway token compounding.
- An explicit cancellation/stop API (`stop_agent`) should exist to immediately interrupt runaway background subagents.

### Actual Behavior
The subagent executed 750+ tool calls in Turn 0 without yielding, burning >120M tokens on repeated compilation and test iterations, and could not be preemptively stopped via standard agent messaging.

issues.title: HydraFusion: emit per-phase model, verdict and credit attributes to OpenTelemetry

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

A HydraFusion turn can run several models, but from the outside I only get one answer and one credit figure. The CLI already writes every routing decision down in `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl`. None of it reaches OpenTelemetry or the UI, so the only way to see which model did what is to read session state, which carries no compatibility promise.

### Proposed solution

#### What the CLI emits today

I measured this on 1.0.84-2 with `COPILOT_OTEL_FILE_EXPORTER_PATH`, no collector involved. Every turn arrives as one `invoke_agent` span, several `chat hydrafusion` spans, and `execute_tool` spans. Every one of those chat spans carries `gen_ai.request.model=hydrafusion`.

That is correct. The [GenAI semantic conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) define `gen_ai.request.model` as the model the client asked for, and the client did ask for `hydrafusion`. The conventions have no notion of a router that expands one request into several model calls, so there is nowhere for the per-phase detail to sit. This is a spec that has not caught up with the architecture, not a defect.

The metric side has the same shape. Six instruments, no token metric, no credit metric, and `gen_ai.request.model` is always `hydrafusion`. A turn that spent 51 credits across two models from two vendors is indistinguishable from a cheap single-model turn except by duration.

#### Where the data already lives

All of it is in the session log, fully structured. One event per phase:

```json
{"phaseKind":"judge","role":"judge","model":"gpt-5.6-sol","status":"succeeded",
 "verdict":"reject","durationMs":4522,
 "usage":{"requestCount":1,"inputTokens":12500,"outputTokens":7,
          "cachedTokens":7680,"cacheWriteTokens":0,"totalNanoAiu":2249200000}}
```

Plus `session.fusion_resolved` for the routing decision (pattern, policy, `routeSource`, `routingLatencyMs`, the phase plan), `session.fusion_handoff` for escalations, and `session.fusion_completed` for the turn rollup. Per-phase credits sum to the turn total exactly, to the nanounit, across every turn I checked.

So the instrumentation work is basically done. The values are computed, named and written to disk. They just never leave the process through a supported channel.

#### 1. One span per fusion phase

Emit a child span per phase under the turn root, carrying the model that actually served it:

```
invoke_agent                        github.copilot.fusion.pattern = cascade
└─ chat hydrafusion                 gen_ai.request.model  = hydrafusion
   ├─ phase 1                       gen_ai.response.model = mai-code-1.1-flash
   │                                github.copilot.fusion.phase.kind = primary
   │                                github.copilot.nano_aiu = 575436000
   ├─ phase 2                       gen_ai.response.model = gpt-5.6-sol
   │                                github.copilot.fusion.phase.kind = judge
   │                                github.copilot.fusion.phase.verdict = reject
   │                                github.copilot.nano_aiu = 2457200000
   └─ phase 3                       gen_ai.response.model = gpt-5.6-sol
                                    github.copilot.fusion.phase.kind = repair
                                    github.copilot.fusion.phase.committed = true
                                    github.copilot.nano_aiu = 11686960000
```

`gen_ai.response.model` needs no spec change. The conventions already define it as the model that generated the response, and per phase that is unambiguous. Everything router-specific goes under a `github.copilot.fusion.*` namespace, which keeps it out of the way if the WG later standardises orchestration attributes. If GitHub wanted to take that shape to the semconv group as a routing extension, there is now a working implementation and 24 turns of data behind it.

Suggested attributes:

| Attribute | Source field |
|---|---|
| `gen_ai.response.model` | `model` on the phase event |
| `github.copilot.fusion.pattern` | `pattern` |
| `github.copilot.fusion.phase.kind` | `phaseKind` |
| `github.copilot.fusion.phase.role` | `role` |
| `github.copilot.fusion.phase.verdict` | `verdict` |
| `github.copilot.fusion.phase.committed` | derived from `finalSourceModel` |
| `github.copilot.fusion.route_source` | `routeSource` |
| `github.copilot.fusion.routing_latency_ms` | `routingLatencyMs` |
| `github.copilot.nano_aiu` | `usage.totalNanoAiu` |

Metadata only. No prompt or response content needs to cross this boundary.

#### 2. Token and credit metrics dimensioned by serving model

`gen_ai.client.token.usage` is already a standard semconv histogram and the numbers are all in the phase events. A credit metric with the same dimensions would let people answer cost questions without running a trace backend at all.

#### 3. Something in the CLI itself

Not everyone will stand up a collector. A `/usage` view, or an expandable breakdown on the turn that just finished, showing the phases, who drafted, what the reviewer said and where the credits went. The [announcement](https://github.blog/ai-and-ml/github-copilot/project-hydrafusion-frontier-quality-via-multi-model-orchestration/) explains that intermediate drafts are held back so unfinished work does not read as final, which is the right call while the turn is running. After it finishes, I would like to be able to ask.

#### 4. An official reference dashboard

Once the attributes exist, ship a Grafana dashboard JSON and a collector config alongside the docs. Right now anyone who wants this reverse-engineers their own, and they will all diverge. One maintained dashboard in-repo settles the question of what the panels are supposed to mean.

#### Why I think this is worth doing

Three of these were surprises I could only get at by reading the log, and they are the kind of thing I would expect an org paying for credits to ask about:

- Across 24 turns, the phases that did not supply the answer came to 2.5% of spend. I would not have guessed that low, and I could not have found it from the CLI output.
- One model took 42% of total credits from three phases, all of them heavy refactors. Per-model attribution is invisible today because every span says `hydrafusion`.
- `routeSource` was `capi_plan` on all 24 turns, meaning routing policy is served remotely and can change without a CLI release. Without per-phase telemetry, a policy change lands as an unexplained shift in the credit line, with nothing to diff against.

I built a working version to prove the data supports it: [samueltauil/hydrafusion-traces](https://github.com/samueltauil/hydrafusion-traces). It tails the session log and rebuilds each turn as a trace. It is roughly 400 lines of stdlib Python, and it will break the first time the log format moves, which is exactly the argument for doing this properly upstream.

### Example prompts or workflows

1. "Why did this turn cost 51 credits?" Today the answer is one number. With per-phase spans it is a draft phase at 51.11 and a critic phase at 0.69, and you can see immediately that the review was cheap and the draft was not.
2. Finance asks which models an org's credits went to this month. Currently unanswerable from telemetry, because every span reports `hydrafusion`.
3. A routing policy changes server-side and credit spend jumps 30%. With `github.copilot.fusion.pattern` and `route_source` on spans, you can see the mix shift. Without them you can only see the bill.
4. "Is the quality gate paying for itself?" Judge rejection rate needs `phase.kind=judge` and a verdict. My sample had 2 rejections out of 3, which is far too small to mean anything, and that is the point: nobody can gather this at scale right now.
5. A turn returns a weak answer and you want to know which model committed it. `phase.committed` answers it in one click.

### Additional context

The dashboard I ended up with, for reference on what the data supports:

![HydraFusion routing dashboard in Grafana](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samueltauil/hydrafusion-traces/main/docs/screenshots/dashboard.png)

One cascade turn as three phases. `mai-code-1.1-flash` drafted for 22 seconds and 0.58 credits, `gpt-5.6-sol` reviewed it, returned `reject`, then redid the work itself in 42 seconds and 11.69 credits. The CLI showed one answer and the figure 14.72:

![Tempo waterfall for a cascade turn showing draft, judge and repair phases](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samueltauil/hydrafusion-traces/main/docs/screenshots/cascade-waterfall.png)

The whole ask sits on two attribute rows. `gen_ai.request.model` is `hydrafusion`, per the conventions. `gen_ai.response.model` is `gpt-5.6-sol`, which my tailer added from the session log. Both are true, and only the first one is available today:

![Span attributes showing request model hydrafusion and response model gpt-5.6-sol](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samueltauil/hydrafusion-traces/main/docs/screenshots/span-attributes.png)

Credits split by phase kind, which is the question I actually cared about and could not answer any other way:

![Credits by phase kind: primary, draft, repair, judge, critic](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samueltauil/hydrafusion-traces/main/docs/screenshots/where-credits-went.png)

Caveats on my end. This is one machine, one operator, 24 turns, one small Python project. It describes what the telemetry contains and shows the dashboard works. It is not a benchmark and says nothing about model quality. HydraFusion is a research preview and is expected to change. Model identifiers above are routing labels I observed, not product names.

Measurements and method: [docs/SPIKE.md](https://github.com/samueltauil/hydrafusion-traces/blob/main/docs/SPIKE.md) for what the CLI actually emits, [docs/FINDINGS.md](https://github.com/samueltauil/hydrafusion-traces/blob/main/docs/FINDINGS.md) for the 24-turn breakdown, and a [write-up](https://samueltauil.github.io/github-copilot/devops/2026/09/10/hydrafusion-model-routing-grafana-traces.html) of how I got there.

Possibly related:

- #4782, desktop app spans omitting GitHub context attributes. Different surface, same general theme of telemetry not carrying enough to attribute work.
- #4726, `invoke_agent` roots missing input on resumed turns.

Happy to split this into separate issues for the span work, the metrics, the in-product view and the dashboard if that suits triage better. I kept them together because the last three depend on the first.

issues.title: AGENTS.md discovery follows resolved symlinks and walks every ancestor, importing unrelated repos’ instructions

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

## Summary

Custom instruction discovery canonicalizes the path of any file a tool touches, then loads `AGENTS.md` from **every ancestor directory** of the resolved path. Git repository boundaries are not honored.

For anyone whose dotfiles are a git repo with `~/.copilot` (or `~/.claude`, `~/.config/...`) symlinked into it — a very common setup — this means the dotfiles repo's own `AGENTS.md` is silently injected into **every unrelated session**, on every machine, as soon as the agent reads any file under the symlinked config directory.

The docs describe the behavior as `AGENTS.md` "in the git root and cwd". The actual behavior is much broader.

## Reproduction

```
~/dotfiles/                 <- a git repo
  AGENTS.md                 <- rules meant only for working on the dotfiles repo
  config/copilot/
    settings.json

~/.copilot -> ~/dotfiles/config/copilot     (symlink)

~/work/my-app/              <- an unrelated project, different git repo
```

1. `cd ~/work/my-app`
2. Start the CLI and ask it anything that causes it to read a file under `~/.copilot` — for example, `read ~/.copilot/settings.json`.
3. `~/dotfiles/AGENTS.md` is now in context.

Observed with `--log-level debug`; the log shows the dotfiles repo's `AGENTS.md` being registered as a custom instruction source.

## Expected

`~/dotfiles/AGENTS.md` should not load. The session's git root is `~/work/my-app`, cwd is `~/work/my-app`, and the user never asked for the dotfiles repo's conventions. Reading a config file is not a statement of intent to adopt another repository's instructions.

## Actual

The path is canonicalized to `~/dotfiles/config/copilot/settings.json`, and discovery then walks up through `config/copilot` → `config` → `dotfiles` → `~`, collecting `AGENTS.md` at each level.

## Why this is more than cosmetic

- **It is silent.** There is no indication in normal (non-debug) output that a foreign repository's instructions were loaded. Users experience it as unexplained behavior drift.
- **It is contagious.** The dotfiles repo is exactly where people put rules like "always commit and push when done" or "never run destructive cleanup here". Those rules are correct for that repo and actively wrong everywhere else.
- **It is triggered by the agent's own housekeeping.** The user does not have to do anything unusual; any tool call that touches the config directory is enough.
- **It affects the fix, too.** Users who notice and try to scope things out cannot.

## Workarounds tested — all fail

| Attempt | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Put the config dir in a `git worktree` of the same repo | Still leaks. Git root correctly resolves to the worktree, but discovery walks to the main repo root anyway. |
| Make the config dir its own independent git repo (own `.git`) | Still leaks. The ancestor walk goes straight past the nested git boundary. |
| Shadow with a nearer `AGENTS.md` | Does not shadow. All ancestor-level `AGENTS.md` files load simultaneously. |
| Use a junction instead of a symlink (Windows) | No difference; both are reparse points and both are collapsed by path canonicalization. |
| Disable the source via `/instructions` | Not persistent. The toggle lives in per-session state and resets on the next session, unlike skill toggles which are written to settings. |
| Set a config key | None exists. On-demand instruction discovery appears to be enabled unconditionally. |

The only workaround that works is renaming the dotfiles repo's `AGENTS.md` to something outside the auto-load list, which means giving up per-repo agent instructions for that repo entirely.

## Suggested fixes (any one would resolve it)

1. **Do not canonicalize for discovery purposes.** Walk ancestors of the logical path the user/tool referenced, not the resolved real path. This alone fixes the whole class of dotfiles cases.
2. **Stop the ancestor walk at a git boundary**, and do not cross out of the session's own repository into a different one.
3. **Do not run ancestor discovery for incidental file reads at all** — restrict it to the session's git root and cwd, matching the documented behavior.
4. **At minimum**, make it persistent-configurable: a `settings.json` key (`disabledInstructionSources`, or an allowlist of instruction roots) so the `/instructions` toggle survives across sessions.

Fix 1 or 2 would be the principled fix. Fix 4 would at least give users an escape hatch.

## Related

`~/.copilot/instructions/` only matches `**/*.instructions.md`. A file named `AGENTS.md` placed there is ignored silently, with no warning — which is easy to trip over given that `AGENTS.md` is the recognized name nearly everywhere else. A startup warning for non-matching files in that directory would save people a lot of time.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.83, but seems like any version is affected

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Make a git repo at `~/dotfiles` containing an `AGENTS.md` at its root (rules meant only for that repo) and a `config/copilot/` directory inside it.
2. Symlink `~/.copilot` -> `~/dotfiles/config/copilot`.
3. `cd` into an unrelated project in a different git repo, e.g. `~/work/my-app`.
4. Start the CLI there and ask it to read any file under the config dir, e.g. `read ~/.copilot/settings.json`.
5. Re-run with `--log-level debug` and grep the log for custom instruction sources.

`~/dotfiles/AGENTS.md` is registered as a source and is in context, even though it belongs to a different repository.

### Expected behavior

`~/dotfiles/AGENTS.md` should not load. Both the git root and cwd are `~/work/my-app`, and the docs describe discovery as `AGENTS.md` in the git root and cwd. Reading a config file that happens to live inside another git repo should not import that repo's instructions. Discovery should walk the logical path rather than the symlink-resolved real path, and should not cross out of the session's own repository.

### Additional context

_No response_

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Add support for selecting OpenAI's Flex tier (`service_tier: flex`) in the Copilot CLI model selector and configuration, allowing users to cut token usage   costs by 50% for non-time-critical tasks.

### Proposed solution

## Motivation

OpenAI Flex tier costs 50% less than Standard tier and according to [monitoring data from OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/openai/gpt-5.6-sol#performance) has roughly 30% higher E2E latency (e.g. 9.02s vs 11.56s for `gpt-5.6-sol`):

| Model | Output Price (Standard) | Output Price (Flex) | E2E Latency (Standard) | E2E Latency (Flex) |
| --- | ---:| ---:| ---:| ---:|
| `gpt-6-astra` | $50 | $25 | 10.95s | 11.34s |
| `gpt-5.6-sol` | $20 | $10 | 9.02s | 11.56s |

For many agentic tasks small increases of latency do not significantly impact user experience. 

Additionally, E2E latency for many agentic tasks depends more on tool call durations than on LLM response times (e.g. large C++ or Gradle builds, running extensive test suits, etc). Using Flex tier for these kinds of tasks would reduce cost without significantly impacting task completion time.  

Therefore, offering Flex tier would allow some developers to perform roughly twice as many agentic tasks withing a given AI budget.

## Proposed Solution
1. **Interactive Model Picker:** When selecting an OpenAI model, present a tier selection prompt (Standard vs. Flex) alongside the reasoning effort selection.
2. **CLI Flags:** Add `--tier <standard|flex>` (or `--service-tier <standard|flex>`) for scripted runs and aliases.

issues.title: Remote/HTTP MCP servers (e.g. atlassian) are stranded 'failed' after every /clear or session relaunch

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
## Summary

Remote (HTTP) MCP server connections are reliably stranded in a `failed` state whenever the CLI performs a foreground-session handoff — which happens on every `/clear`, and apparently on session resume/relaunch too. The MCP connection graph is torn down and rebuilt during the handoff, and slower remote/OAuth-backed servers lose the reconnect race and never recover automatically.

## Environment

- CLI version: 1.0.83 (macOS, confirmed already latest via in-app update check)
- MCP server affected: `atlassian` (`https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp`, HTTP transport with Authorization header)
- Other MCP servers configured (`github-mcp-server`, `codegraph`, `local-rag` — local/stdio) are *not* visibly affected, likely because their reconnect is fast enough to win the race.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start a Copilot CLI session with the `atlassian` MCP server configured (`~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`, HTTP transport).
2. Confirm it connects fine (`/mcp show atlassian` → connected, tools listed).
3. Run `/clear` (or relaunch/resume a session).
4. Run `/mcp show atlassian` again.

## Expected

`atlassian` reconnects cleanly like the other MCP servers.

## Actual

`atlassian` is left in:

```json
{
  "name": "atlassian",
  "status": "failed",
  "error": "MCP server \"atlassian\" connection was cancelled"
}
```

It does not self-heal — it requires a manual reconnect action or a full CLI restart, and even a full restart reproduces the same failure deterministically (confirmed across two separate relaunches, ~20 minutes apart).

## Root cause (from `~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log`)

Every `/clear`/relaunch briefly registers a *throwaway* foreground session, then immediately unregisters it in favor of the real one, within milliseconds:

```
17:27:22.425Z [INFO] Registering foreground session: 6266dbfb-39da-4797-9265-c37d9655a3fd
17:27:28.717Z [INFO] Unregistering foreground session: 6266dbfb-39da-4797-9265-c37d9655a3fd
17:27:28.720Z [INFO] Registering foreground session: d89d1d9a-99c4-4247-86fe-a75b4da5daad
17:27:28.783Z [INFO] Closing session 6266dbfb-39da-4797-9265-c37d9655a3fd
```

This handoff triggers a full MCP graph reload while a reload lock is still held from the previous teardown:

```
17:05:05.167Z [WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::session::mcp::session_host] MCP reload lock still held at disposal; draining the graph without it
```

Every MCP server — including `atlassian` — gets re-initialized and then almost immediately cancelled mid-handshake:

```
17:27:26.104Z [INFO] [rust:rmcp::service] Service initialized as client {... "name": "atlassian-mcp-server" ...}
17:27:28.809Z [INFO] [rust:rmcp::service] task cancelled
17:27:28.809Z [INFO] [rust:rmcp::service] serve finished {"quit_reason":"Cancelled"}
```

Local/stdio servers appear to reconnect fast enough afterward to recover; `atlassian`'s remote HTTP+OAuth handshake is slower and consistently loses the race, leaving it permanently `failed` with no automatic retry.

Confirmed not a network/auth issue independently:
- DNS resolves fine for `mcp.atlassian.com`.
- `curl https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp` returns `401` (server reachable, no valid header supplied in the manual test — expected).
- `ATLASSIAN_MCP_AUTH_HEADER` env var is set.

## Impact

Every `/clear` (a very common action) breaks the Atlassian MCP integration and requires a manual reconnect or CLI restart to restore it — significant daily friction for anyone using an HTTP-based MCP server.

## Suggested fix

- Don't tear down/reinitialize already-connected MCP servers on a foreground-session handoff that isn't actually changing MCP config.
- If a reload is unavoidable, retry a server that was cancelled mid-handshake instead of leaving it permanently in `failed` state.
- Respect the "MCP reload lock still held at disposal" case by waiting for the lock instead of draining the graph without it.

issues.title: Multiple-choice ask_user silently renders as a free-text prompt when trailing tool-call parameters leak into the preceding string argument

labels.name: area:models

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

An `ask_user` call that supplies `choices` sometimes renders as a **plain free-text prompt** ("Type your answer…") instead of the usual clickable option buttons — and the options themselves show up as a literal JSON array printed at the end of the question text.

The cause is upstream of any UI: the assistant emits Anthropic-style `<parameter name="…">` markup **inside** a string argument, and the argument parser recovers only the *first* parameter. Every trailing parameter is silently absorbed into that first parameter's string value. Unlike #3765 (where the whole `<invoke>` block leaks as text and the tool never runs), here **the tool call does execute** — just with silently truncated arguments, so nothing surfaces as an error.

Verbatim from the session transcript (`tool.execution_start`), reformatted only for line breaks:

```json
{
  "toolName": "ask_user",
  "arguments": {
    "question": "…Tests 244 → 247 passing, typecheck clean. Commit it?</question>\n<parameter name=\"choices\">[\"Commit (Recommended)\", \"Edit message\", \"Skip repo\", \"Cancel\"]"
  }
}
```

`arguments` has exactly one key. `choices` never arrives, so the client correctly renders a free-text prompt — it has no options to draw.

It is **not** `ask_user`-specific. The same shape corrupts ordinary tools, where the damage is worse because the call runs with wrong arguments and nobody notices. A `grep` call that lost its `-n`:

```json
{ "-B": "30\">\n<parameter name=\"-n\">true", "output_mode": "content", "pattern": "latched" }
```

### Affected version

Engine **1.0.84-4** (running inside the GitHub Copilot desktop app). Standalone CLI on PATH is 1.0.81-12. Occurrences in my logs span 2026-08-18 → 2026-09-11, so this is not new to one release.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Not deterministic on demand — it depends on model output. What reliably produces it:

1. Run a long session on `claude-opus-5`.
2. Have the agent call `ask_user` with a `choices` array and a **long** question (every affected call was 643–944 characters; nothing shorter ever broke).
3. Once one malformed call lands, **every subsequent tool call of that kind in the session is malformed too** — the model copies its own bad output from the transcript.
4. Run `/compact`. The bad exemplar leaves the context window and calls go back to normal.

Step 3–4 is the strongest signal and is fully reproducible from logs — see the investigation block.

### Expected behavior

Either the model never emits parameter markup inside a string value, or — more robustly — **the argument parser refuses to accept a partial parse.** A string value containing `</param>` / `<parameter name="…">` is unambiguously a serialization failure, and the trailing parameters are trivially recoverable from it. Today it silently succeeds with dropped arguments, which is the worst of the three options.

### Additional context

Suggested labels (I can't set them): `area:tools`, `type: Bug`.

Related: #3765 — same root family (parameter markup leaking), different failure mode: there the call is never executed; here it executes with silently truncated arguments.

#### Environment

```text
Engine version   1.0.84-4  (GitHub Copilot desktop app)
CLI on PATH      1.0.81-12
OS               Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0
CPU arch         AMD64
Shell            PowerShell 7
Surface          desktop app, project session
Model            claude-opus-5 (long-context tier)
```

#### Frequency

Measured, not estimated — scanned every `tool.execution_start` event in my local session store:

| Metric | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Tool calls scanned | 145,260 |
| Calls with leaked parameter markup | 18 (0.012%) |
| On `claude-opus-5` | 17 |
| On all other models combined | 1 (`claude-opus-4.8`) |

Tools affected: `ask_user` ×12, `grep` ×2, an ADO MCP tool ×2, a Bluebird MCP tool ×1, `create` ×1.

The global rate is low but **misleading** — it is heavily clustered. Within an affected session the rate is effectively 100% until a compaction clears it.

#### Extensions

Not tried with extensions disabled. Canvas extensions were loaded, but they cannot plausibly be involved: the corruption is present in the raw `tool.execution_start` event, before any client renders it.

#### Diagnostics available on request

- Redacted `events.jsonl` excerpts for both affected sessions
- The scan script used to produce the frequency table

<details>
<summary>In-depth investigation</summary>

**The corruption is already present in the raw event, before anything renders it.** The `tool.execution_start` record in the local session store shows `arguments` carrying a single `question` key. No client can draw option buttons from that — there are no options in the payload. So this is not a UI bug, and it will reproduce on any surface.

**Why it's easy to miss.** The stray `</question>` and `<parameter name="choices">` don't show up on screen — only the bare `["Commit (Recommended)", …]` array does. That makes it read as a formatting quirk rather than a dropped argument, which is why it took a log scan to find.

**Contagion, bounded by compaction.** This is the part I'd most like a maintainer to look at, because it turns a rare glitch into a session-wide outage.

Session A — 30 `ask_user` calls, all `claude-opus-5`:

```text
calls  1–6    ok
               ← 5 compactions in 31 minutes (heavy context pressure)
calls  7–11   MALFORMED   (contiguous, ~26 h, no compaction in between)
               ← compaction
calls 12–30   ok          (19 consecutive clean calls)
```

The malformed run is bounded *exactly* by compaction events on both sides.

Session B — 7 `ask_user` calls, `claude-opus-5`, **zero compactions for the life of the session** (74% of a 1M context window): **7 of 7 malformed**, starting with the very first one.

Reading: once one malformed call is in the context window it acts as a few-shot exemplar and the model reproduces its own broken shape indefinitely. Compaction rewrites the context, the exemplar disappears, and output returns to normal. Two sessions is a small sample, so I'd call this a strong inference rather than proven — but it matches both cases exactly and gives users a workaround (`/compact`, or switch model).

**The existing guard isn't holding.** The harness system prompt already carries a mitigation for this class — *"when calling a tool whose parameter is an object, emit a real JSON object for that parameter. Never put XML or angle-bracket markup inside string values of a tool call."* That instruction was in context for every one of the 18 malformed calls. A prompt-level guard can't win against the model's own prior output sitting in the same window; this needs a parser-level check.

**Suggested fix, in priority order:**

1. **Reject partial parses.** If a decoded string argument contains `</…>` or `<parameter name=`, treat the tool call as malformed rather than passing along truncated arguments. Silent success is the real defect here.
2. **Recover them.** `</question>\n<parameter name="choices">["a","b"]` is unambiguously parseable back into the intended arguments. A tolerant post-parse pass would fix the user-visible symptom outright.
3. **Break the contagion.** If a malformed call is detected, avoid replaying its raw text into subsequent context — otherwise one bad call poisons the rest of the session.

</details>

issues.body:
## Summary

The native GitHub Copilot desktop app does not render the custom status line or context-window footer configured in `~/.copilot/settings.json`, even though the same configuration works in the terminal-hosted Copilot CLI.

## Environment

- OS: Windows
- GitHub Copilot desktop app: `1.1.19`
- Desktop executable: `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\GitHub Copilot\github.exe`
- GitHub Copilot CLI: `1.0.84-4`

## Configuration

```json
{
  "statusLine": {
    "type": "command",
    "command": "powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \"C:\\Users\\<user>\\.copilot\\statusline.ps1\""
  },
  "footer": {
    "showContextWindow": true,
    "showCustom": true
  }
}
```

The configured PowerShell command reads the status payload from stdin and prints context-token usage.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure `statusLine.command`, `footer.showCustom`, and `footer.showContextWindow` in `~/.copilot/settings.json`.
2. Start Copilot CLI from PowerShell by running `copilot`.
3. Send a prompt and observe that the custom context usage (for example, `49.5k/? tokens`) appears in the terminal footer.
4. Close the terminal session and launch the native desktop app using `github.exe`.
5. Open a session and send a prompt.

## Actual behavior

The desktop app does not display the custom status-line output or a context-window usage indicator. The command itself is valid and works in the terminal CLI.

## Expected behavior

The desktop app should either:

1. honor `statusLine.command` and the relevant `footer.*` settings, or
2. provide a native equivalent that continuously shows used/remaining context-window capacity for the active session.

## Why this matters

Context-window visibility helps users decide when to summarize, checkpoint, or start a new session before earlier context is compacted or lost. Users moving between the terminal CLI and native desktop app should have equivalent visibility into session context usage.

### Describe the bug

A scheduled repository automation fails when the associated local clone is currently checked out to a branch other than the workflow/default branch. The failure instructs the user to switch the local clone back to the expected branch before rerunning the workflow.

A scheduled automation should not depend on whichever branch happens to be checked out in a mutable local working copy. This makes schedules unexpectedly brittle and allows unrelated local development activity to break them.

### Affected version

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

2. In the associated local clone, check out a different branch for unrelated work.
3. Allow the scheduled automation to run.

Scheduled automations should run against the configured workflow branch or repository default branch regardless of the local clone's currently checked-out branch.
