issues.title: Custom agent `target` frontmatter property is documented for the CLI but has no effect

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

The custom agents configuration reference documents a `target` property: "Target environment or context for the custom agent (`vscode` or `github-copilot`). If unset, defaults to both environments." That property table is scoped to "GitHub.com, the Copilot CLI, and supported IDEs (unless otherwise noted)," with no CLI exception noted for `target`.

In practice it has no effect. An agent declaring `target: vscode` is still loaded, still offered in the picker, and still runs.

This matters most for plugin-supplied agents, where a VS Code-only agent installed via a plugin appears in the picker with no way for the author to scope it out.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.84-4 (also reproduced on 1.0.84-3 and 1.0.83)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

No agent I could find in the wild sets `target` yet, so this needs a hand-written file to exercise the property.

1. Create `~/.copilot/agents/vscode-only.agent.md`:

```markdown
---
name: vscode-only
description: Only intended for VS Code
target: vscode
---
You are a VS Code-only agent.
```

2. Run `copilot` and open `/agent`. "vscode-only" is listed, with origin `user`.

3. Select it, or run `copilot --agent vscode-only`. It loads and responds normally.

Removing the `target` line changes nothing about steps 2 and 3, so the property has no observable effect either way.

### Expected behavior

An agent declaring `target: vscode` should not be offered or runnable in the CLI, since `vscode` and `github-copilot` are documented as distinct environments and omitting the property is what defaults to both.

If `target` is not intended to apply to the CLI, the reference should say so, since as written it reads as supported.

### Additional context

- Operating system: macOS 26.6.2
- CPU architecture: arm64 (Apple silicon)
- Shell: zsh

The same agent also appears in the GitHub Copilot desktop app's agent picker, so this is not CLI-only. The app caches its agent list, so a newly added agent file only appeared there after restarting the app — worth knowing when reproducing.

The case that prompted this: the `awesome-copilot` plugin ships `meta-agentic-project-scaffold`, a VS Code-specific agent, selectable in both the CLI and the desktop app. Filed on the content side as github/awesome-copilot#3017, but that fix depends on `target` taking effect here.

Related, though not duplicates — #1377 and #2133 both cover frontmatter fields that VS Code accepts but the CLI rejects. This one is the inverse: the field is accepted without complaint and simply does nothing.

Reference: https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/copilot/reference/custom-agents-configuration

issues.title: Sessions become unrevivable: a stale `inuse.<pid>.lock` from a crashed host is never reclaimed on open

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Several saved sessions became impossible to reopen ("crashed out / unrevivable"). On investigation the **session data was not corrupt** — the append-only `events.jsonl` replayed cleanly and the engine logged a successful resume. The sessions were blocked by **runtime/lifecycle issues**, not data loss.

The primary cause is **stale lock handling**. Each live session writes `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/inuse.<pid>.lock`. When the owning `copilot --server` process exits uncleanly (crash, force-quit, OS kill), the lock file is left behind. On the next open, the session is treated as in-use / unrevivable instead of checking whether that PID is still alive.

Scanning one local store, **14 of 184 sessions (~8%)** carried a fault signature; **8 held an `inuse.<pid>.lock` whose PID was dead**. Deleting the stale lock made each session openable again, and the app then spawned a fresh host and resumed normally — confirming the data was fine and only the lock blocked recovery.

Three related lifecycle defects compound the impact (details under Additional context):
1. **Orphaned engine host after a failed UI attach** — the engine resumes but no session host registers, leaving a live server holding the lock (which then becomes defect #1 on the next attempt).
2. **MCP OAuth timeouts block session readiness** — resume stalls ~5 minutes on `OAuth callback timeout` before the session is interactive, so users abort.
3. **Unbounded `events.jsonl`** makes replay hang on large/old sessions (appears to overlap #4251).

### Affected version

`1.0.83` (`copilot --server --stdio --no-auto-update`)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Primary defect (stale lock not reclaimed):

1. Open a session, then hard-kill its `copilot --server` process to simulate a crash / force-quit (`kill -9 <pid>`).
2. Confirm `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/inuse.<pid>.lock` remains, now pointing at a dead PID.
3. Try to reopen the session → it does not revive.
4. `rm` the stale lock file → the session reopens and resumes cleanly (a fresh host is spawned and `events.jsonl` replays without error).

### Expected behavior

On open, if the lock's PID is dead or a zombie, the app should **reclaim the session automatically** rather than treating it as in-use. A liveness check combined with a PID start-time comparison avoids the classic PID-reuse race. Recoverable work should never be gated behind a leftover lock file that only manual filesystem surgery can clear.

### Additional context

- **OS:** macOS · **shell:** zsh

**Defect 2 — orphaned engine host after a failed UI attach.** Engine log from a single resume: the host never registers, yet the engine reports the session resumed, so the process lingers as an orphan holding the lock:
```
[WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::session::pending_request_flow] pending-request event was not delivered to the session host
          {"error":"GenericFailure, no session host is registered for session <id>"}
...
[INFO]  Resumed session: <id>        (logged repeatedly)
```
Suggested fix: tie the engine host's lifetime to successful UI host registration; if registration fails/times out, tear the host down and release the lock.

**Defect 3 — MCP OAuth timeouts block resume (~5 min).** With several MCP servers configured, resume stalls until interactive OAuth flows time out. MCP init begins at `20:27`, first hard failures at `20:32`:
```
[ERROR] [rust:mcp_engine::session_authorizer] OAuth login failed after returning its authorization URL
        {"server_name":"...","error":"OAuth callback timeout"}
```
During that window the session looks hung and users abort — observed as sessions whose only recent events were `resume → abort (user_initiated) → shutdown`, twice in a row. Suggested fix: make MCP init lazy / non-blocking; never gate session interactivity on MCP OAuth.

**Defect 4 — unbounded `events.jsonl`.** The append-only log grows without bound; worst local session reached **38.6 MB / ~13k events with 42 compaction cycles** (173 re-injected `system.message` events ≈ 10.7 MB). Reopening replays the whole log, so large sessions hang on open even though nothing is corrupt. This looks like the same root cause as #4251; noting here for linkage. Suggested fix: snapshot-and-truncate the event log at compaction so replay cost stays bounded.

**Possibly related:** #4020 (session falsely "already in use by another client"), #4098 (truncated/concatenated events on resume), #4138 (resume compaction hangs), #4251 (large-session resume OOM/hang).

All four are addressable without changing the on-disk event format. Defects 1–2 turn recoverable work into apparent data loss; 3–4 make large/older sessions feel dead on open.

issues.title: Windows: with --sandbox, shell commands can't list or stat directories when the working directory is on a non-system drive

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows, when Copilot CLI's command sandbox is enabled and the working directory is on a drive other than the system drive (for example `D:\`), sandboxed shell commands cannot list, stat or change into directories on that drive. `Get-ChildItem`, `Test-Path`, `cmd /c dir` and git repository discovery fail with **Access is denied**, and the shell does not start in the working directory: `Get-Location` reports `C:\WINDOWS\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0`.

Reading a file by its full path still works, and so does .NET `[IO.Directory]::GetFiles`. The same commands work when the working directory is on `C:\`, and everything works on `D:\` without `--sandbox`.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Enterprise 26H1, OS build 28000 (x64)
- GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.101-0 (installed with WinGet)
- Windows PowerShell 5.1 as the sandboxed shell
- Volumes that reproduce it:
  - `D:` NTFS, fixed disk;
  - `E:` ReFS Dev Drive (trusted);
  - a freshly created 2 GB NTFS VHDX mounted as `T:`.
- Works: `C:` (NTFS, system drive).
- No sandbox settings beyond `--sandbox`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a test folder on a non-system drive:

   ```powershell
   New-Item -ItemType Directory D:\sandbox-probe | Out-Null
   Set-Content D:\sandbox-probe\existing.txt 'hello'
   cd D:\sandbox-probe
   ```

2. Run the CLI with the sandbox enabled and ask it to run this probe:

   ```powershell
   copilot --sandbox --allow-all --no-ask-user -s -p @'
   Run exactly this PowerShell, once, then print its raw output verbatim:
   $w = 'D:\sandbox-probe'
   "location=$((Get-Location).ProviderPath)"
   try { (Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $w -ErrorAction Stop).Name } catch { "Get-ChildItem: $($_.Exception.Message)" }
   try { Test-Path -LiteralPath $w -ErrorAction Stop } catch { "Test-Path: $($_.Exception.Message)" }
   cmd /c "dir /b D:\sandbox-probe"
   try { [IO.File]::ReadAllText('D:\sandbox-probe\existing.txt') } catch { "ReadAllText: $($_.Exception.Message)" }
   try { [IO.Directory]::GetFiles($w) } catch { "GetFiles: $($_.Exception.Message)" }
   '@
   ```

3. Run the same command **without** `--sandbox` as a control.
4. Optionally, repeat steps 1–3 with a folder under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp` on `C:` (adjust `$w`).

(`Set-Location` is left out of the probe because in `-p` mode it triggers a CLI approval prompt, which is unrelated to the sandbox. In our runs through the Copilot SDK with the same sandbox, `Set-Location D:\sandbox-probe` also fails with Access is denied.)

## Expected

The sandboxed shell starts in the working directory and can list and stat it, as it does on `C:`. `copilot help sandbox` says sandboxed commands can access the allowed paths, and the working directory is allowed by default. The sandbox's PowerShell setup is meant to make the working directory's drive enumerable when it isn't the system drive.

## Actual

With `--sandbox`, working directory `D:\sandbox-probe`:

```text
location=C:\WINDOWS\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0
Get-ChildItem: Access is denied
False
Test-Path: Access is denied
Access is denied.
hello

D:\sandbox-probe\existing.txt
```

Without `--sandbox` (control), same folder:

```text
location=D:\sandbox-probe
existing.txt
True
existing.txt
hello

D:\sandbox-probe\existing.txt
```

With `--sandbox`, working directory on `C:`: every probe succeeds, and `location` is the working directory.

Summary across volumes (sandbox on):

| Working directory | Get-ChildItem | Test-Path | cmd dir | git status | Read by full path | .NET GetFiles |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C: NTFS (system) | OK | True | OK | OK | OK | OK |
| D: NTFS | Access denied | Access denied | Access denied | "not a git repository" | OK | OK |
| E: ReFS Dev Drive | Access denied | Access denied | Access denied | "not a git repository" | OK | OK |
| T: new NTFS VHDX | Access denied | Access denied | Access denied | "not a git repository" | OK | OK |

## Diagnostics

- **Engagement:** the sandbox reports itself as engaged (`process_container` backend), and host support reports filesystem enumeration as supported.
- **Policy:** the effective sandbox policy includes an enumeration grant for both the system drive and the working directory's drive (for D:, the roots `C:\` and `D:\`), and the working directory is in the read-write paths.
- **Not drive-specific:** a freshly created NTFS VHDX fails the same way, so this isn't about one drive's history or permissions. Dev Drive filter policy isn't the cause either, since plain NTFS volumes fail too.
- **ACLs:** the volume roots have ordinary default ACLs. One difference: the `C:\` root carries an extra capability ACE (`S-1-15-3-65536-…`) that the other roots lack. Copying that ACE to `D:\` did not fix it (since reverted).
- **Filters:** `fltmc instances` shows `bindflt` attached to `C:` only, and `bfs` attached to `C:` and `D:`. Attaching `bindflt` to `D:` did not fix it (since reverted).
- **Process Monitor:** a trace of a failing run showed no ACCESS DENIED result on the test folder. The denial may happen at a layer Process Monitor doesn't observe, such as the sandbox's own brokering. Raw traces are available on request.
- **Partial enumeration:** .NET `Directory.GetFiles` succeeds where `Get-ChildItem` and `cmd dir` fail. So enumeration is not blocked outright; some directory-open or metadata queries are denied while others succeed.

## Workarounds tried

- Working directory on `C:`: works.
- Adding the `C:\` root's capability ACE to `D:\` and `E:\`: no change (reverted).
- Attaching `bindflt` to `D:`: no change (reverted).

## Impact

On machines where repos live on a data drive or a Dev Drive (which Windows recommends for development), turning on the sandbox makes the working directory unusable for ordinary shell commands and git, even though the CLI reports the sandbox as engaged. The failure looks like the agent "can't see the repo", not like a sandbox restriction, so it's hard to diagnose.

## Suspected component

The Windows `process_container` sandbox (MXC): the drive-root enumeration grant for a non-system working-directory drive appears not to take effect, or to cover only some directory operations. We have not confirmed the exact denied operation.

issues.title: Local sandbox 'Authenticate gh' silently uses an unrelated cached fine-grained PAT instead of active gh OAuth session, with no visibility into which credential is chosen

labels.name: area:authentication
labels.description: Login, OAuth, device auth, token management, and keychain integration

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

With local sandboxing enabled (`/sandbox enable`) and the "Authenticate gh" auth setting on (default), the `GH_TOKEN` exported into the sandboxed environment did not correspond to my active `gh` session.

- `gh auth status` (run on the host, outside the sandbox) showed I was logged in via the OAuth device flow, with a `gho_...` token and scopes `admin:public_key`, `gist`, `read:org`, `repo` — i.e. full private repo access.
- Inside a Copilot CLI sandboxed session, `echo $GH_TOKEN` / `gh repo list <org> --visibility private` showed access to only **one** private repository in my org, via a token in the fine-grained PAT format (`github_pat_...`).
- After investigating, I found the actual token being used: an old fine-grained PAT I had created previously and scoped intentionally to a single, unrelated repository (not the repo I was actively working in).
- This PAT is neither the active `gh auth status` OAuth session (keyring-stored `gho_` token) nor the GitHub App `ghu_` token found in `~/.config/github-copilot/auth.db`.

I was unable to determine, from inside a Copilot CLI session or from documentation, **why this specific cached PAT was selected** over my active OAuth login, or where exactly it was being read from/cached. The lack of visibility made this very difficult to diagnose — I only found the answer by manually checking GitHub's "Active tokens" org admin page and recognizing a token I had created weeks earlier for unrelated purposes.

### Expected behavior

When "Authenticate gh" is enabled for the local sandbox, I would expect one of the following:
1. The sandbox's `GH_TOKEN` to be derived from the currently active `gh auth status` account/session (respecting `gh auth switch`), not from some other cached credential, OR
2. If Copilot CLI intentionally uses a different/cached credential for the sandbox (e.g. a previously-supplied `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` env var), this should be clearly surfaced to the user — e.g. via `/sandbox` or `/env`, showing *which* token/account is being exported into the sandbox and why, without requiring the user to manually diff PAT prefixes and check GitHub's org "Active tokens" page.

### Reproduction steps

1. Log in normally via `gh auth login` (OAuth device flow), confirm with `gh auth status` that the active session has broad `repo` scope.
2. Separately, at some earlier point, create (or have previously created) a fine-grained PAT scoped to only one specific repository, for an unrelated purpose.
3. Launch `copilot`, enable local sandboxing (`/experimental on` if needed, then `/sandbox enable`), leave "Authenticate gh" at its default (on).
4. Inside the Copilot CLI session, ask the agent to run `gh repo list <org> --visibility private` or inspect `$GH_TOKEN`.
5. Observe that the token exported into the sandbox matches the old, narrowly-scoped fine-grained PAT from step 2 — not the active OAuth session from step 1 — with no indication in the CLI of which credential was selected or why.

### Additional context

- `/env` and `/sandbox` do not currently surface which specific token/account was selected for `GH_TOKEN` in the sandbox, making this essentially undiagnosable without manual, external investigation (comparing token prefixes, checking org "Active tokens" pages, etc.).
- Docs reference (`Configuring local sandbox settings` → Auth tab): "Authenticate gh: Export GH_TOKEN so that GitHub CLI ... works inside the sandbox without reaching its stored credentials (configuration directory or OS keychain), which the sandbox blocks." This explains *that* a substitute token is exported, but not how that substitute is selected when multiple credentials (OAuth session, GitHub App ghu_ token, cached fine-grained PATs) exist on the host.
- Related open issues that touch on adjacent auth-scoping concerns: #1460 (no scoped-auth workflow vs `gh auth login`), #953 (default OAuth grants excessive scope).

### Suggested improvement

- Add a way to inspect, from within a session (e.g. `/sandbox` Auth tab or `/env`), exactly which token/account is currently selected for sandboxed `gh`/git operations, including its origin (active `gh auth status` session vs. a manually-set `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` env var vs. some other cached credential) and its repository scope.
- Consider making the sandboxed `GH_TOKEN` follow the currently active `gh auth status` account by default, rather than silently preferring a possibly-stale `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` env var or other cached credential.

issues.title: Copilot CLI unusable after macOS update/reboot because `.mcp-writer.binding` persists stale filesystem device ID

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Immediately after installing the latest macOS security update and rebooting, all Copilot CLI sessions—both newly started sessions and resumed existing sessions—became unable to process prompts.


### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.90-3.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

## Environment
- macOS Golden Gate 27.0.1 on Apple Silicon
- GitHub Copilot CLI reports version 1.0.90-3

## What Happened
On startup after installing 27.0.1, I restarted my copilot sessions, and each of them reported:

`Failed to start MCP Servers: Error: The shared writer lock or its directory changed.`

Attempts to send prompts then hung/failed.

Copilot logs repeatedly contained:

`Scheduled queue processing failed; retrying once {"error":"Message(\"The shared writer lock or its directory changed.\")"}`

and:

`Scheduled queue processing failed after retry; queue drain abandoned {"error":"Message(\"The shared writer lock or its directory changed.\")"}`

## Root cause

`~/.copilot/.mcp-writer.binding` contained persisted Unix filesystem identities:

```json
{"root":{"platform":"unix","device":16777230,"inode":1767102},
 "lock":{"platform":"unix","device":16777230,"inode":45460913}}
```

After the macOS update/reboot, `stat` showed:

~/.copilot:
device=16777232 inode=1767102
~/.copilot/.mcp-writer.lock:
device=16777232 inode=45460913

Thus, the inode numbers remained exactly the same, but macOS had changed the filesystem device ID from 16777230 to 16777232.

Copilot apparently interprets this change in device ID as indicating that the shared-writer lock or its directory has been replaced/changed, even though these are the same filesystem objects.

The stale device ID appeared only in `.mcp-writer.binding`.

## Attempted workaround

Moving `.mcp-writer.binding` aside did not cause Copilot to regenerate it. Instead, a newly launched Copilot reported:

`Failed to start MCP Servers: Error: Shared writer storage I/O failed.`

and attempts to send requests failed with:

`Request session.send failed with message: Shared writer storage I/O failed.`

Restoring the binding file returned behavior to the original "shared writer lock or its directory changed" failure.

## Successful workaround

After backing up `.mcp-writer.binding`, I changed only the two persisted device IDs from:

`16777230`

to the device ID currently reported by stat:

`16777232`

producing:

```json
{"root":{"platform":"unix","device":16777232,"inode":1767102},
 "lock":{"platform":"unix","device":16777232,"inode":45460913}}
```

I then launched a new copilot process. MCP startup succeeded immediately and Copilot processed prompts normally.

At this point, running `\restart` in the existing copilot sessions allowed them to recover as well (prior to fixing the device id, `/restart` had gone right back to the same broken condition).

### Expected behavior

A macOS update/reboot that changes the filesystem device ID should not permanently prevent Copilot from starting its shared-writer storage.

Copilot should either:
1. tolerate a device-ID change when it can otherwise safely establish the identity/integrity of the shared storage, or
2. safely regenerate/rebind .mcp-writer.binding when the stored filesystem identity becomes stale.

In particular, removing a stale binding currently appears to make recovery worse because Copilot fails with Shared writer storage I/O failed rather than rebuilding the binding.

### Additional context

This effectively disables all Copilot CLI sessions after the OS update, including existing/resumable sessions, until the undocumented .mcp-writer.binding file is manually repaired.

issues.title: web_fetch tool fails on all URLs (TypeError: fetch failed) in IPv4-only sandbox environments

labels.name: area:networking
labels.description: Proxy, SSL/TLS, certificates, corporate environments, and connectivity issues

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
### Description

The built-in `web_fetch` tool fails on **every** URL, including trivial always-up test sites (e.g. `https://example.com`), returning a generic error:

```
TypeError: fetch failed
```

This happens both with `raw: true` and default markdown mode, and regardless of the target site (tested `https://example.com` and `https://www.intel.com/...`).

### Environment

- CLI version: 1.0.68
- OS: Linux (Copilot CLI cloud/session sandbox)
- Host network: no global IPv6 address on the primary interface (`eth0` only has a link-local `fe80::/64` address; `ip -6 route show` shows no default IPv6 route)

### Steps to reproduce

1. In a Copilot CLI session, invoke the `web_fetch` tool against `https://example.com`.
2. Observe `TypeError: fetch failed` with no further detail.

### Diagnosis / evidence that this is not a general network outage

From the same session's bash shell:
- `curl https://example.com` → succeeds (`HTTP 200`)
- `curl -4 https://example.com` (IPv4 forced) → succeeds consistently
- `curl -6 https://example.com` (IPv6 forced) → fails consistently: `Failed to connect to example.com port 443 ... Couldn't connect to server`
- Plain Node `fetch()` (same Node runtime available in the sandbox, v24.13.0) → succeeds, because Node's `fetch`/undici implementation performs Happy-Eyeballs-style fallback from IPv6 to IPv4 automatically
- DNS resolves both `A` (IPv4) and `AAAA` (IPv6) records for the target domains

This strongly suggests the `web_fetch` tool's underlying HTTP client attempts the IPv6 (`AAAA`) address first (as returned by DNS) and does not fall back to IPv4 on failure, causing an immediate, opaque `TypeError: fetch failed` in environments where IPv6 egress is unavailable (no global IPv6 address/route on the host, only link-local).

I even tried disabling IPv6 system-wide on the sandbox host via `sudo sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=1` (and `default`) — `curl`/Node fetch continued to work fine afterward, but `web_fetch` still failed identically. This indicates `web_fetch` likely executes in a separate process/container from the interactive bash sandbox, so host-level network changes made from within the session don't reach it — the fix needs to happen wherever that tool's HTTP client actually runs.

### Expected behavior

`web_fetch` should successfully fetch pages in environments with IPv4-only egress, ideally by:
- Implementing Happy Eyeballs / IPv4 fallback when IPv6 connection attempts fail, and/or
- Surfacing a more actionable error message (e.g., distinguishing DNS failure vs. connection refused vs. TLS failure) instead of a generic `TypeError: fetch failed`.

### Workaround

Using `curl` via the `bash` tool as a substitute for `web_fetch` works reliably in the same session.

issues.title: 400 `reasoning_text` in thinking mode must be passed back — triggered by runtime-synthesized assistant turn after a background shell exits

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

A session using a **custom OpenAI-compatible provider with `wireApi: "responses"`** (DeepSeek, model `deepseek-flash`) is killed by an HTTP 400 on the model call that immediately follows a **runtime-synthesized, model-less assistant turn**.

The trigger is the background-shell-completion flow:

1. A command is backgrounded (short `initial_wait`).
2. When it exits, the runtime emits a `<system_notification>` (`kind.type = "shell_completed"`).
3. The runtime then injects a **synthetic `assistant.message`** to read the shell output. That message has `model: undefined`, empty `content`, and — critically — **no `reasoningBlocks`**.
4. The next request to the provider is rejected because thinking mode requires the previous assistant turn's reasoning to be passed back.

Result: `session.error`, the session ends (`was_interrupted: true`, `interruption_reason: "error"`).

The provider and credentials are fine — the same provider/model served 160+ successful model calls in the same session. It is specifically the model-less synthetic turn that breaks the reasoning passback invariant.

### Affected version

- `copilot --version`: **1.0.95-3** (dist: `pkg/win32-arm64/1.0.95-3`)
- Host: Copilot app (`copilot-desktop-gh-2.98.0`)
- OS: Windows, ARM64

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure a custom provider:
   - `type`: `custom`
   - `baseUrl`: `https://api.deepseek.com`
   - `wireApi`: `responses`
   - `authKind`: `api_key`
   - model `deepseek-flash` (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash; **thinking mode is enabled by default**)
2. In a session, start a long-running command so it moves to the background, e.g. a `powershell` call with a short `initial_wait`:
   `dotnet test --project <integration test project> --filter-class "*SelectiveOperationScaleTests"`
3. Continue working while the shell runs. When it exits, observe the injected turn and the failure:
   - `system.notification` → `<system_notification>Shell command "…" (shellId: 68) has exited with exit code 2.</system_notification>`
   - `assistant.message` with `model: undefined`, `content: ""`, one `read_powershell` tool call, **no `reasoningBlocks`**
   - `tool.execution_complete` for `read_powershell`
   - HTTP **400** on the next model call → `session.error`
4. See error: session terminates.

Exact sequence from `events.jsonl`:

```
22:24:02.368Z  assistant.message           "Let me start the heaviest scale test in the background while I update the documentation."
22:24:02.380Z  tool.execution_start        powershell  { initial_wait: 12 }   → backgrounded as shell 68
22:24:45.826Z  system.notification         kind.type="shell_completed", shellId=68, exitCode=2
22:24:45.827Z  assistant.message           messageId=2414e771-…, model=undefined, content="",
                                           toolRequests=[read_powershell {shellId:"68", delay:0}],
                                           reasoningBlocks=<absent>
22:24:45.833Z  tool.execution_complete
22:24:48.944Z  (model call fails)
22:24:48.976Z  session.error               400 The `reasoning_text` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.
```

Raw error envelope and error context:

```json
{"type":"hook.start","data":{"hookType":"errorOccurred","input":{
  "error":{"name":"Error","message":"{\"message\":\"The `reasoning_text` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API. (request_id: 3821e7d3-e76b-4688-8be6-4461e1d1e46b)\",\"type\":\"invalid_request_error\",\"param\":null,\"code\":\"invalid_request_error\"}"},
  "errorContext":"model_call",
  "recoverable":true}}}

{"type":"session.error","data":{
  "errorType":"query",
  "message":"400 The `reasoning_text` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API. (request_id: 3821e7d3-e76b-4688-8be6-4461e1d1e46b)",
  "statusCode":400}}
```

The synthetic assistant turn (note the UUID-style `toolCallId`, versus the model's `call_00_…` style):

```json
{"messageId":"2414e771-73dc-4bb2-be5b-8b1e537e8982","content":"",
 "toolRequests":[{"toolCallId":"0666f48c-0b07-413f-ae92-aaf94b4ca60f","name":"read_powershell",
                  "arguments":{"shellId":"68","delay":0},"toolTitle":"Read shell output"}]}
```

### Expected behavior

The session should continue. Thinking-mode providers require the reasoning payload on assistant turns; the runtime should satisfy that invariant for **every** assistant turn it sends, including turns it synthesizes itself (or must otherwise exclude those turns from the reasoning-required history).

### Additional context

**Provider configuration (valid, working):**

```
type: custom, authKind: api_key, baseUrl: https://api.deepseek.com, wireApi: responses, headers: {}
model: deepseek-flash  (max_prompt_tokens 840000, max_output_tokens 128000)
reasoning efforts: none | low | high | max
```

DeepSeek documents both a Responses API and thinking mode (on by default) for `deepseek-flash`.

**Why this points at the client, not the provider:**

- 142 of 162 `assistant.message` events in the session carried correct reasoning blocks: `reasoningBlocks.provider = "openai-responses"`, block `type: "reasoning"`, content `[{type:"reasoning_text", …}]`, plus `encrypted_content`.
- 20 assistant turns had no reasoning block. 18 were ordinary model turns; **1 was the model-less synthetic turn above** — and the failure landed on the very next model call.
- Same provider/model serviced 160+ other calls in this session and all other sessions without this error.
- Across 44 local sessions with this provider, there is exactly **one** `session.error` of this kind. It was also the session's only `system.notification`. Correlation is 1:1.

- The injected turn is not a model output, so it cannot carry model reasoning; sending it as a plain assistant turn breaks the API contract for thinking mode.

**Impact:** the entire session is terminated mid-task, losing in-flight work. In this case the session was implementing changes across many files.

**Workarounds used:** avoid backgrounding commands (run them in the foreground) in thinking-mode sessions; set the model's reasoning effort to `none` to sidestep the passback requirement.

**Suggested direction:** when the runtime injects a synthetic assistant turn (e.g. `read_powershell` after `shell_completed`), either attach whatever reasoning payload the provider requires, or mark it so it is not presented to thinking-mode providers as a reasoning-bearing assistant turn (e.g. keep it out of the reasoning-required history, or fold the shell output into the following user/tool message).

**Related observation (possibly a separate issue):** the same provider also produced two genuine context-length 400s in an earlier session — `you requested 1049487 tokens (921487 in the messages, 128000 in the completion)` against a 1,048,576-token context — while `max_prompt_tokens` was configured as 840000. That suggests the app-side prompt budget does not reserve enough headroom for its own token estimation error. Happy to file separately if useful.

issues.title: Option for 1-hour prompt cache TTL for Claude models (5-minute cache expires during normal interactive use)

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Claude prompt caching in Copilot CLI appears to use Anthropic's default **5-minute** cache TTL. In normal interactive use (read the answer, think, write the next prompt) gaps of more than 5 minutes are common, so the full conversation gets re-written to cache on almost every turn instead of being read from cache.

I measured this with `copilot -p` / `--resume` in fresh sessions (~35k-token context), sending a follow-up after different idle gaps, and reading `cache_read_tokens` / `cache_write_tokens` from the local session usage data. Two independent runs gave identical results:

| Idle gap | Claude Opus/Sonnet/Haiku 5.5 | GPT-6.1-sol / GPT-6-sol / GPT-5.6-sol |
|---|---|---|
| 2 min | ~95% cache read | ~95% cache read |
| 11 min | **0% cache read** (~100% cache write) | ~95% cache read |
| ~85 min | 0% | 0% |

My broader session history (Claude 5.x, CLI) shows the same pattern: 98% cache read for gaps < 4 min vs ~1% for gaps of 6–60 min.

Anthropic supports a 1-hour TTL (`cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "1h"}`). VS Code Copilot Chat already has experimental settings for this (`github.copilot.chat.anthropic.promptCaching.extendedTtl` / `extendedTtlMessages`), though they currently miss Claude 5.x models (microsoft/vscode#340830, fix in microsoft/vscode#340831). Copilot CLI has no equivalent option.

### Proposed solution

Add an option in Copilot CLI (config setting and/or env var) to use the 1-hour cache TTL for Claude models, covering the Claude 5.x family. Consider making it the default for interactive sessions, since the higher write cost (2x vs 1.25x) is usually recovered after one or two follow-up turns with a pause longer than 5 minutes.

### Example prompts or workflows

Any interactive session with a large context where the user pauses longer than 5 minutes between prompts (reviewing diffs, testing changes, meetings).

### Additional context

- Related: #3808 (prompt caching for Claude), #4724 (auto-compact on idle aligned to cache TTL)
- Triggered by this discussion: https://www.reddit.com/r/GithubCopilot/comments/1xauf3s/anthropic_caching_is_this_a_bad_joke/
- Tested with Copilot CLI 1.0.102-1 on Windows.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Warn users before free tier quota exhaustion instead of silent 429
issues.body:
### Verification Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand this is a feature request, not a bug report

### Problem

When using free models (`-free` suffix) on OpenCode Zen, users hit `FreeUsageLimitError` (429) with no prior warning. The only feedback is a sudden "Free usage exceeded, subscribe to Go" dialog. This is especially painful for users behind shared IPs (CGNAT, corporate networks), where the quota may be exhausted by other users on the same IP.

Related issues: #15585 #42029 #42128 #33495

### Proposal

Add rate-limit response headers to zen API responses so clients can display a warning when quota is running low.

**Only include headers when remaining quota is below a threshold** (e.g., <20% remaining). This way:

- Users get advance notice before hitting 429
- The exact total limit is never exposed
- The official team retains full control over the numbers

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 8
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1786800000
```

When above the threshold, no headers are returned (current behavior unchanged).

### Why not expose on every request?

This keeps the daily limit opaque while still solving the core UX problem: users know they're running low and can plan accordingly, without learning the exact cap.

### Implementation scope

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `packages/console/app/src/routes/zen/util/ipRateLimiter.ts` | Return counts from `check()` |
| `packages/console/app/src/routes/zen/util/handler.ts` | Write headers when remaining < threshold |
| `packages/opencode/src/session/retry.ts` | Parse headers for early warning (optional) |

### Verification

- `curl -v` zen endpoint, verify headers appear when quota is low
- Confirm no headers when quota is high (no info leak)

### Note on duplicates

This may overlap with #40588 and #41684. Happy to consolidate there instead if preferred.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: i18n support for TUI (terminal interface)
issues.body:
### Description

The TUI (terminal interface) currently has all strings hardcoded in English. While the app/desktop/console packages have i18n support with 17+ locales, the TUI package (`packages/tui`) lacks any localization system.

This makes the terminal experience inaccessible for non-English speakers who form a significant portion of the user base.

### Proposed solution

1. Extract all hardcoded strings from `packages/tui/src/` into an i18n key system similar to `packages/app/src/i18n/`.
2. Add a `locale` config option in `opencode.json` (e.g. `"locale": "es"`).
3. Include at minimum: es, fr, de, zh, ja, ko, pt, ar, ru, uk, it, tr, pl, th, nl, vi, hi.

### Current behavior

All TUI labels, prompts, error messages, and status text are in English with no way to change language.

### Additional context

Related open issues:
- #32095 - Spanish settings showing English labels
- #36292 - i18n parity test failures across locales
- #17652 - Spanish docs outdated
- #12609 - ASCII-only output breaking non-English languages

The i18n infrastructure already exists in `packages/app/src/i18n/` and could be adapted for TUI use.

issues.title: desktop: zh locale has unreviewed machine-translation errors (壳牌, 出口, 个贝壳)
issues.body:
### Description

The Simplified Chinese (`zh`) catalog in desktop 2.0.18 contains a few machine-translation errors, and 93 of the 1828 keys in the English base catalog have no `zh` entry, so those strings fall back to English.

#### Wrong translations

| key | English | current zh | suggested |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `settings.timeline.category.shell` | Shell | 壳牌 | `shell 命令` |
| `ui.promptInput.exitShell` | Exit | 出口 | `退出` |
| `session.background.shell.other` | {{count}} shells | {{count}}个贝壳 | `{{count}}个shell` |
| `settings.timeline.title` | Timeline | 时间表 | `时间线` |
| `settings.timeline.preset.detailed` | Detailed | 详情 | `详细` |
| `settings.timeline.description.quiet` | Group edits and subagents. Hide other activity. | 对**已使用**的编辑和子代理进行分组。隐藏其他活动。 | 对**编辑**和子代理进行分组。隐藏其他活动。 |
| `settings.timeline.description.detailed` | Expand shell output and edits. Show subagents separately and group other activity. | 展开shell输出和编辑。 单独显示子代理，并在**已使用**中对其他活动进行分组。 | …并在**编辑**中对其他活动进行分组。 |

壳牌 (the Shell oil company), 出口 (customs/export exit) and 个贝壳 (a seashell) are clearly unreviewed machine translation. For reference, the rest of the catalog keeps "shell" in English in every sentence it appears in (`输入 shell 命令…`, `Shell 命令`, `{{count}}个shell`), so `settings.timeline.category.shell` is also inconsistent with the catalog's own convention. `description.detailed` additionally has a stray space after `。`.

#### Missing keys: 93

English base catalog 1828 keys, `zh` 1735 keys (94.9%). Most are the new provider-connect flow:

- `provider.connect.*` — 39 (the entire "Sign in to OpenCode Console" flow)
- `settings` — 18, `pair` — 10, `file` — 10, `session` — 8, `command` — 4, `home` — 2, `common` / `server` — 1 each

Happy to paste the full key list if useful.

#### Application menu bar is always English

The main-process catalog (`/out/main/translations-*.js` inside `app.asar`) contains no CJK at all, so the Windows menu bar (File / Edit / View / Go / Window / Help) is never localized even when the renderer UI is Chinese. Looks like an oversight rather than an intended limitation.

#### Where the catalogs live

Inside `resources/app.asar`: the `zh` catalog is `/out/renderer/assets/zh-*.js` (2 chunks, 13 KB + 81 KB) and the English base is inlined in `/out/renderer/assets/main-*.js`. The counts above come from parsing the asar and diffing the `"key": \`value\`` maps.

#### Suggestions

1. A build-time check that diffs each locale catalog's key set against the English base and fails (or warns) on missing keys, so new features cannot ship untranslated.
2. A review pass on `zh` additions — the three failures above are characteristic of raw machine translation.


### Plugins

none

### OpenCode version

2.0.18 (desktop app @opencode/desktop 2.0.18)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Desktop 2.0.18, UI language zh (system display language Chinese Simplified).
2. Settings > Timeline: the Shell category reads 壳牌.
3. Prompt input > Esc: the exit hint reads 出口.
4. Settings > Providers > Add account: the whole connect flow is in English.

### Screenshot and/or share link

_No response_

### Operating System

Windows 11 Home (zh-CN) 10.0.26200.8457, x64

### Terminal

OpenCode desktop integrated terminal (TERM=xterm-256color)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

issues.body:
## Summary

The `experimental.browser/attach` RPC hangs indefinitely when called with valid input. The OpenCode Desktop app (2.2.7) calls this RPC while restoring sessions; the call never completes, the app eventually times out (`request failed, timeout`), tears down all of its connections and reconnects — repeating every few minutes. As a result, desktop sessions are only intermittently usable. CLI/TUI sessions on the same service are unaffected.

## Environment

- opencode version: v2.2.7 (CLI/background service, channel `latest`); Desktop app 2.2.7 (Electron 44.9.1)
- OS: macOS 15.0.1 (Darwin 24.0.0, arm64)
- Terminal: N/A (issue is in the desktop app; TUI works fine)
- Shell: /bin/zsh
- Install/channel: latest — desktop app auto-updated 2.2.6 → 2.2.7 on Nov 10; the shared background service was restarted onto the app's bundled CLI 2.2.7 on Nov 11
- Active plugins: none configured

## Reproduction

1. Have the background service running (2.2.7) with at least one existing session.
2. Call the RPC with valid input — a `connectionID` and a `sessionID` belonging to the same location:

```sh
opencode api post /api/rpc/experimental.browser/attach \
  --data '{"input":{"connectionID":"<valid connectionID>","sessionID":"<valid sessionID, same location>","version":4}}'
```

3. Observe: the request never returns. In my test the client was killed after 25 s with zero bytes received; the server logged the response (499) only at the moment the client disconnected. No browser process is ever spawned — the hang happens before any browser launch.

Validation-order notes from probing the endpoint: missing keys fail fast with 400 (`Missing key at ["connectionID"]`, then `["sessionID"]`), and a session from another location fails fast with 400 `"Session belongs to another location."` — only a fully valid call hangs.

Via the desktop app (no API calls needed): open the app with existing sessions. Sessions intermittently show `request failed, timeout`, and the service log shows a recurring pattern every 2–10 minutes: all SSE (`/api/event`) connections closing at once, plus a pending `browser/attach` request aborted by the client (499) — i.e. the app's reconnect cycle.

## Expected Behavior

The attach RPC should return promptly — either attach the browser to the session, or fail with an error. A hung RPC should not be able to wedge the desktop app's connection state.

## Actual Behavior

- Valid `attach` calls hang forever: no response, no error, no browser process launched.
- The desktop app times out waiting, shows `request failed, timeout` on sessions, drops and reconnects all of its connections, then tries again — every few minutes, indefinitely.
- The same happens against a remote self-hosted server (over SSH/VPN) running the same version, so all sessions — local and remote — are affected.
- CLI/TUI on the same service is completely stable (event stream stays connected for hours), so the service is otherwise healthy.

## Additional Context

Service log (`~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`, `role=server`) around my direct reproduction — the 499 appears exactly when the test client is killed, 25 s after the request:

```
timestamp=2026-11-11T17:33:42.605Z level=INFO run=93110eb3 message="cli starting" version=2.2.7 channel=latest local=false args=["api","post","/api/rpc/experimental.browser/attach","--data",...] role=cli
timestamp=2026-11-11T17:34:07.559Z level=INFO run=c9857b2b message="Sent HTTP response" http.span=24950 role=server http.method=POST http.url=/api/rpc/experimental.browser/attach http.status=499
```

Desktop app reconnect cycles today (each cycle = burst of `/api/event` responses + `browser/attach` 499s): 15:39, 15:55, 16:01, 16:03, 16:13, 16:16, 17:20 — every 2–10 minutes, while the user was actively using the app.

Historical note: client-aborted `browser/attach` requests (499) appear sporadically in my log since Oct 19 (a few per day), but became constant with the 2.2.7 app + 2.2.7 service combination (16 within ~2 h today). Status distribution of `browser/attach` responses in my log overall: 4241x 404, 175x 400, 89x 499.

Workarounds: using the TUI instead of the desktop app (fully functional on the same service). Restarting the service does not help — the hang reproduces deterministically after restart.

issues.body:
### Problem

In a long session with many turns and tool calls, the transcript becomes one continuous scroll. There is no fast way to find where a specific message begins.

- PageUp/PageDown moves by screen, so reaching a particular turn means paging and visually scanning a lot of output.
- The timeline (`<leader>g`) lists only user prompts. It helps with "which prompt?", but not with "where does this assistant message start?".
- Message-navigation commands (`session.message.previous` / `session.message.next`, and the user-message variants) exist, but are unbound by default, so they are hard to discover.
- Long assistant turns with many tool calls are visually dense; the boundary between two messages is easy to miss, especially when a jump lands inside a message.

### Proposal

Add a message-level outline and make every message start a jump target:

1. **Message outline** — extend the timeline (or add a "Messages" dialog) to list *all* messages, not only user prompts, with role, timestamp, and a one-line preview. Selecting an entry scrolls that message's first line to the top of the viewport.
2. **Default keybinds** — bind previous/next message and previous/next user message by default (e.g. `ctrl+up` / `ctrl+down`), while keeping them configurable. Add `ctrl+home` / `ctrl+end` for first/last.
3. **Obvious landing** — when jumping, place the message header at the top and briefly highlight it, so it is clear which message was selected.
4. **Current-message indicator** — optionally show a compact sticky header (role, time, first line) while scrolling inside a long message.

### Why it matters

Reviewing a long debugging session often means returning to "the answer where the fix was proposed" or "the turn where the error first appeared". Today that requires repeated paging and visual scanning, and it gets worse as the session grows. An outline plus reliable jump-to-start would make long sessions navigable and also help keyboard-only users.

### Workarounds tried

`PageUp`/`PageDown`, `Home`/`End`, `<leader>g` (user prompts only), session search/export, and compacting the session. None gives a direct "jump to the start of this message" for arbitrary messages.

### Environment

- Surface: TUI (the outline would also help Desktop/Web)
- opencode version: 2.3.0
- OS: Windows 11

issues.body:
# Bug: local plugin loader caches a failed module link, poisoning the plugin for the process lifetime

## Summary

When a local plugin's module graph contains an import whose name the target module does
not export, the loader's link step throws:

```
SyntaxError: Export named '<name>' not found in module '<path>'
```

The failed evaluation is then cached, so every later reload of that plugin in the same
server process keeps failing the same way. The process keeps running the previous
generation of the plugin silently; the only trace is a single WARN line in
`~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` of the form
`level=WARN msg="failed to load plugin" target=<plugin path> ...`. The plugin
never recovers until the server is restarted.

This was observed with `@opencode/plugin` 2.2.5 (and 2.2.7) on Bun.

## Minimal reproduction

A ~40-line script that drives the loader the way OpenCode does, with a two-file
plugin in a temp directory. Run it with `bun`:

```js
import { mkdtempSync, cpSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs"
import { tmpdir } from "node:os"
import { join } from "node:path"
import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url"
import { createPluginSources } from "@opencode/plugin/source"

const fixture = "/path/to/two-file-plugin" // src/index.ts imports { greet } from "./dep.js"
const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "lp-"))
cpSync(fixture, dir, { recursive: true })

const entry = pathToFileURL(join(dir, "src", "index.ts")).href
const sources = createPluginSources(async () => {})

// First load succeeds.
await sources.read(entry)

// Rename the export in dep.ts without updating the importer.
writeFileSync(join(dir, "src", "dep.ts"), 'export function greet2() {\n  return "hi"\n}\n')

let err
try {
  await sources.read(entry)
} catch (e) {
  err = e
}
console.log(String(err?.message ?? err))
// => Export named 'greet' not found in module '/tmp/.../src/dep.ts'.

// Even after restoring a consistent graph, the cached rejection persists for
// this process; a restart is required.
sources.dispose()
rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })
```

Fixture contents:

`src/index.ts`
```ts
import { greet } from "./dep.js"

export default { id: "lp", effect: () => greet() }
```

`src/dep.ts`
```ts
export function greet() {
  return "hi"
}
```

## Expected behaviour

After the export is renamed (and, in a real workflow, after the importer is updated
to match), a subsequent `read()` of the same entrypoint should load the corrected
module graph. At minimum, a mismatch should be reported in a way the developer can
act on, and the loader should not permanently poison that plugin for the life of the
process.

## Actual behaviour

The link step throws `SyntaxError: Export named 'greet' not found in module
'.../src/dep.ts'.` and the failed promise stays cached. Every later `read()` of the
same entrypoint keeps rejecting the same way until a content edit changes the file
digest. The server keeps running the previous generation of the plugin.

## Impact

Local plugins silently stop updating for the lifetime of a long-running server. The
only trace is one WARN line in `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`
(`level=WARN msg="failed to load plugin" target=<plugin path> ...`), so the
regression is invisible during normal use. Renaming an export across versions is
enough to trigger it.

## Workaround

- Restart the server after changing a local plugin's source.
- Avoid renaming exports across versions; prefer additive changes.

## Evidence

This repository (`memory-persistent`) contains the reproduction as a regression
test in `test/loader.test.ts`, including the exact error message above. The test
deliberately does **not** assert that the brokenness is permanent, because that
behaviour is the defect being reported; it notes that a fix in the loader would
make a later successful reload (after a consistent edit) a meaningful expectation.
The companion self-check in `src/selfcheck.ts` exists specifically to catch this
mismatch before the loader ever sees it.

issues.title: Claude Agent: 5-hour plan limit drains ~1.8x faster because the SDK labels requests sdk-ts
issues.body:
### Description

With the Claude Agent provider, opencode uses the 5-hour Claude plan limit about 1.8x faster than the same work in Claude Code's own TUI.

opencode starts `claude` through the Agent SDK, and the SDK sets `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-ts` when it isn't already set. Requests labeled `sdk-ts`/`sdk-cli` use more of the 5-hour window for the same tokens. Weekly limits don't seem to be affected. This is tracked upstream in anthropics/claude-code#97074 (still open, with a controlled A/B test showing ~1.8x). T3 Code users measured the same thing with a custom label: 14-15 calls per 1% with `sdk-ts` vs 25-27 with any non-`sdk-*` name (pingdotgg/t3code#24649, pingdotgg/t3code#25597).

Users can't fix it from Claude Code's side either: opencode loads no `~/.claude` settings (`settingSources: []`), so the common `"env": { "CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT": ... }` workaround in `settings.json` has no effect. Only exporting it in the shell before starting opencode works today.

Suggested fix: set `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=opencode` next to the other variables in `ISOLATION_ENV`. The SDK keeps a value that is already set, and Claude Code keeps custom labels (it only rewrites `cli` to `sdk-cli` in `-p` mode).

_Written by Claude Opus 5.5 on behalf of @Salloxy._

### Plugins

none

2.2.5 / `dev` at c8a473b, Claude Code 2.1.316, Agent SDK 0.3.301

3. Compare the 5-hour usage per token with the same work in the `claude` TUI (`"entrypoint":"cli"`), or with opencode started with `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=opencode` exported.

issues.title: codemode: client-MCP reconnects repeat the same two notices across active sessions
issues.body:
### Description

A client advertised one tool in the directory it was attached to. As that client came and went, sessions taking a step in the affected directory recorded the same tool arriving and leaving. A session didn't have to call the tool to get the messages.

In one fixed 24-hour window, the server logged **284 attachments**, all advertising one tool. Two exact system-message texts accounted for **3,433 transcript entries across 382 sessions**: 1,726 additions (375 characters each) and 1,707 removals (123 each). That's 857,211 characters across those sessions. These are transcript counts, not billed tokens or a count of physical reconnects.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In the same directory, start two Code Mode sessions with a one-tool client-MCP provider attached. Let both take a step to establish their catalogs.
2. Detach the provider and let both sessions take a step that doesn't use it.
3. Reattach with the same tool list and let both take another step. Inspect the system messages in each session. Sessions that missed the outage need not see it.

Expected: a brief transport interruption should not add a removal and an identical re-addition to both transcripts. Calls should still fail immediately while disconnected, and real tool removals and permission changes must still take effect.

This concerns the **number** of notices, not the size of the catalog delta ([#62176](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62176)). The TUI reconnect in [#64230](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/64230) is related; no Claude Agent restart is required here.

### OpenCode version

2.3.0, desktop-managed service, macOS arm64. Observed with local plugins enabled; not isolated against a plugin-free setup.

prs.title: feat(core): send mid-conversation tool changes in place
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

None.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

When the tools offered to the model change mid-session (an MCP server connects or drops, a plugin tool appears, an agent loses a permission), core now sends the change in place on models that support it, instead of rebuilding the top-level tool list. The top of the prompt stays the same, so the prompt cache still hits. It builds on `Message.tools({ add, remove })` from https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64166.

**How it records and replays changes.** Before each step, the runner compares the tools it is about to offer (after context hooks and freeform filtering, the same definitions core already sends) with the tools the model has been told about. Tools are compared by name and canonical JSON, so reordering alone is not a change. A difference is recorded once, as one durable fact, before the request goes out:

```
session.tools.updated { add: [full definitions], remove: [names], model? }
  → projected as a hidden system message: { type: "system", text: "", tools: { add, remove, model? } }
```

With `model` set, the message is a baseline: `add` is the whole set. A change has no `model`. Requests are built from the history:

```
history:  user · [baseline A,B] · assistant · user · [+C −B] · assistant · user
request:  tools: [A, B]              ← latest baseline for this model, never changes
          messages: user, assistant, user, Message.tools({ add:[C], remove:[B] }), assistant, user
```

The step that records a change sends the marker at the same place, after the history and before any assistant prefill. The next step replays it from the stored message, so both requests carry the same bytes. The planner in `@opencode/ai` then sends it in place (Anthropic `tool_addition`/`tool_removal`, OpenAI Responses `additional_tools`) or folds it.

I kept this in the message history instead of adding a state table. History windowing already handles every case where the baseline has to change:

- **Session start**: no baseline yet, so the first step records one.
- **Compaction**: the window starts at the checkpoint and leaves the old baseline behind, so the next step declares the current tools again. Provider checkpoints don't keep tools added later, so this is required.
- **Model or provider change**: the latest baseline names another model, so a new one is recorded. Variants share the baseline.
- **Revert or fork**: only changes before the cut survive. The surviving prefix is what the provider already saw, so the next step just records the remaining difference. Reverting past the baseline starts over.

The current tools still execute as before: a tool added mid-conversation runs, and a removed one is refused, because `executeTool` uses the tools offered now, not the request's top-level list.

**Capability pass-through.** models.dev publishes `api.<protocol>.capabilities.tools.updates` per API (https://github.com/anomalyco/models.dev/pull/13856, live). I decode it for the API the model resolves to, drop unknown values, and treat the old boolean form in the bundled snapshot as none. It lands on `compatibility.supportsToolUpdates`, which the model resolver maps to the AI model's `capabilities.tools.updates`, the same path as `supportsEffortUpdates`. Config overrides it the same way (`compatibility: { supportsToolUpdates: [] }` turns it off).

**No change for models without `tools.updates`.** Core records only when the model's `tools.updates` overlaps what its route can encode. Other models record nothing, get no markers, and send the current tool list in today's order. A session that switches to such a model sends its plain current tools.

**Public surface (additive, optional):**
- `Model.Compatibility.supportsToolUpdates?: ("add" | "remove" | "replace")[]` (model-level only, not on provider compatibility)
- `Session.Message.System.tools?: { add: Tool.Definition[], remove: string[], model?: Model.Ref }`, plus the new `Tool.Definition` and `Tool.Changes` schemas
- `session.tools.updated` is an internal durable event, like `session.usage.recorded`: it is not in the public event manifest. It shows up only in the experimental session log type.

Client types are regenerated. The solid client store skips system messages with `tools`, so TUI, app and desktop transcripts never show them. Export and import keep them, and sanitized export redacts their descriptions and schemas.

Trade-off: each baseline stores the full tool definitions once (about 14 to 15 tools here, more with MCP servers), at session start and after each compaction or model switch. Clients receive these rows in message pages and drop them.

**Ships with:** https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode-console/pull/7776 makes the Zen gateway's free-tier and agent-tool checks see tools declared in `additional_tools`. It will ship well before a release with this change, so nothing here waits for it.

### How did you verify your code works?

Live, through a real `serve` process driven by the client (scripts in my notes). The run: two warm-up prompts, add an MCP server mid-session (`experimental.mcp.add`), ask for its tool, compact, ask again, remove the server, ask again. Values are cache read tokens for the first request after each event:

| | B (control) | after add | after compaction | after remove |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| claude-sonnet-5-5 | 11410 | **11425**, calls the tool | 0 (new prompt), calls the tool | **12007**, says no tool |
| claude-opus-5-5 | 11398 | **11413**, calls | 0, calls | **11940**, no tool |
| gpt-6-astra | 7271 | **7288**, calls | 0, calls | **7551**, no tool |
| claude-sonnet-5 (no `updates`) | 11470 | **0**, calls | 11482, calls | 11390, no tool |
| deepseek-flash (Chat, no `updates`) | 7680 | 6912, calls | 7680, calls | calls the removed tool, refused, then no tool |

On capable models the request after a change reads the whole previous prompt from cache. claude-sonnet-5 shows today's behavior (cache miss on the add), and nothing is recorded for the two models without the capability.

Tests:
- `packages/core/test/session-tool-changes.test.ts`: diffing (add, remove, redefine, re-add after remove, reorder only), epochs and replay.
- `packages/core/test/session-runner.test.ts` (`tool changes`): unchanged requests without the capability; the in-place marker and identical replay, also compiled to the Anthropic wire; running an added tool and refusing a removed one; baseline after compaction, model switch (not variant), revert; switching to a model without the capability and back; fork.
- `packages/core/test/models.test.ts`: models.dev decoding, unknown values, old booleans, config override.
- `packages/client/test/solid-data.test.ts`: the store leaves tool changes out of transcripts.
- The existing recorded and wire tests pass unchanged.
- `bun typecheck` in core, schema and client, and `bun run check` at the root. Core, schema, client, server and sdk suites pass, except tests that also fail on `dev` locally: core shell tool and parity tests, and server experimental artifacts, automations and media_blob tests.

### Visual

The Anthropic request after an MCP server swaps `lookup` for `fresh` (from the runner test, compiled to the wire):

```diff
 tools: [defect, echo, lookup, storefail]      ← dev sends [defect, echo, fresh, storefail] here, a cache miss
 messages:
   user  "First"
   user  "Second"
+  system [tool_addition fresh, tool_removal lookup]
```

### Screenshots / recordings

No UI change. Recorded tool changes are hidden from transcripts.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No issue. Desktop didn't render the ```` ```latex ```` fences in an assistant reply that the TUI already draws as formulas.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The TUI's built-in latex plugin draws ```` ```latex ```` and ```` ```math ```` fences as formulas. Desktop and web only render `$…$`, `$$…$$` and `\(…\)`, so those fences showed up as highlighted LaTeX source.

This adds fence rendering next to the existing math handling in `packages/ui/src/context/marked-parser.tsx`, so all of desktop's LaTeX logic stays in one module and KaTeX stays in the markdown worker:

- `markdownMath` now also has a `code` renderer. It renders a `latex` or `math` fence as KaTeX display math (the language check ignores case and the rest of the info string). An empty fence, or one KaTeX can't parse, returns `false` and falls through to the normal highlighted code. `markdownCode` is now registered before `markdownMath` so this renderer runs first.
- `markdown-stream.ts` (worker only): normally a top-level fence becomes a `code` block and skips the Markdown parser. A math fence still does that while it streams, so it shows as highlighted code. Once its closing fence arrives it becomes a `full` block, which the parser above turns into the formula.

Completed messages, and fences nested in lists or quotes, already go through the parser, so the renderer covers them directly.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `packages/ui`: new tests for `latex`, `math`, `LaTeX` and a fence with an info string after the language, a fence inside a list item, and empty, unterminated and unknown-command fences staying as code. `bun test src/context` passes (181 tests).

prs.title: feat(core): add the file operations Node fs needs to Environment files
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

None.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`Environment.Files`, the file layer every tool goes through, gains the operations Node's `fs` needs that it can't build from read/write/list today, and `stat` reports the rest of POSIX stat. This is groundwork for Code Mode's `fs` (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61186) to cover the whole API. Nothing calls the new operations yet, so behavior doesn't change.

```diff
 interface FilesImpl {
   read, write, stat, list, remove, move, mkdir
+  append(path, bytes)                       // add to the end, create when missing
+  writeAt(path, bytes, offset)              // positional write, no truncation (pwrite)
+  truncate(path, length)
+  chmod(path, mode)
+  chown(path, uid, gid, follow)             // follow: false is lchown
+  utimes(path, atimeMs, mtimeMs, follow)    // follow: false is lutimes
+  symlink(target, path)  readlink(path)  realpath(path)  link(existing, path)
+  statfs(path)
 }

 FileInfo { type, size, mtimeMs
+  dev?, ino?, mode?, nlink?, uid?, gid?, rdev?, blksize?, blocks?, atimeMs?, ctimeMs?, birthtimeMs?
 }
```

The new `FileInfo` fields are optional, so nothing that builds or reads one has to change.

Each implementation gets them:
- **local** (node:fs): the matching `fs` call. `writeAt` opens with `O_RDWR | O_CREAT` so bytes outside the range stay.
- **GNU exec** (remote environments): one script each, with the existing exit-code protocol for missing paths and wrong kinds: `cat >>`, `dd oflag=seek_bytes conv=notrunc`, `truncate -s`, `chmod`, `chown [-h]`, `touch -c [-h] -a/-m -d @t`, `ln [-s]`, `readlink`, `realpath -e`, `stat -f`. `stat` asks for every field in one call. Times from GNU `stat` are whole seconds, as `mtimeMs` already was.
- **memory** (tests): keeps mode, owner, times and inode per node. Its `symlink` helper, which tests already used, is now the interface method. A hard link is a copy there, since it keeps no link counts.
- **workspace** connections pass each operation through.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `test/lib/environment-conformance.ts` runs the same checks against all three implementations. New checks cover the stat fields, append, positional writes past the end (zero-filled), truncation both ways, chmod and utimes read back through stat, chown, symlink/readlink/realpath/link with their NotFound and WrongKind cases, and statfs. The existing "stat matches the info read returns" check now leaves out the access time, which reading can move.
- `test/environment.test.ts`: 32 pass on macOS (the GNU suite is Linux-only), and all 47 pass on Linux with GNU coreutils 9.4, including the GNU exec suite.
- Workspace, read, file access, session environment, location filesystem, execute and file-write tests pass (107). `bun typecheck` in core, app, cli, server, sdk and plugin, and `bun run check` from the root.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(codemode): let a host function write into byte arrays it is given
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

None.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

A host function marked `Extension.writesBytes` can fill a `Uint8Array` (or `Buffer`) a program passes it. Code Mode copies every argument into the host, so today a host can't write into the program's buffer. That's what `fs.readSync(fd, buffer, offset, length, position)` and `filehandle.read(buffer)` need, for the file descriptor part of https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61186.

```js
const buffer = Buffer.alloc(16)
const read = fs.readSync(fd, buffer, 0, 16, 0)   // before: buffer stayed all zeros
buffer.toString("utf8", 0, read)                 // now: the file's first bytes
```

```text
call a writesBytes function
  each Uint8Array argument crosses as a copy, as before, and the bytes it held are kept
  when the call settles (returned, threw, or its promise settled)
    → only the bytes the host changed are written into the program's array
unmarked functions: unchanged, they still can't change what they were passed
```

Writing back only changed bytes keeps what the program, or another call, wrote while an async call was running, so two `filehandle.read` calls into different parts of one buffer don't overwrite each other.

It's opt-in so the existing "values are converted, never shared" rule still holds for every other host. Only `fs` will mark functions. The write-back happens in `extensionWork`, the one place every extension call settles, so sync, sync-Effect and async calls all get it.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New test in `test/extensions.test.ts`: a marked function's writes come back for a plain sync call, a sync Effect, an async call, and a call that throws after writing. An unmarked function's writes don't.
- Concurrent async calls filling different parts of one buffer keep each other's bytes, and a byte the program writes while a call is pending survives. This test fails with a whole-copy write-back.
- The existing test that a host can't change an argument still passes unchanged.
- `packages/codemode`: `bun test` (1657 pass), `CODEMODE_ROUNDTRIP=1` for the extensions tests, `bun typecheck`.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(core): add Node-style fs and path to Code Mode behind full_codemode
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

None.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Builds on https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64363 (sync globals block on an Effect, which `*Sync` needs) and https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64365 (`Buffer`), both merged.

With `full_codemode` on, Code Mode programs get Node's `fs` (sync and `fs.promises`) and `path`, also importable as `node:fs`, `fs/promises` and `node:path`. Every call checks the same permission rules the file tools check. With the flag off nothing changes: no globals, same `execute` description.

```js
const fs = require("fs")
const files = fs.readdirSync("src")
const notes = fs.readFileSync("notes.txt", "utf8")
fs.writeFileSync("out.txt", notes.toUpperCase())
```

### How permissions apply

```text
readFile, readdir, stat, lstat, access, existsSync,
glob (on the pattern's fixed prefix)               → FileAccess.authorizeRead   read rule (+ external_directory)
writeFile, appendFile, copyFile (destination)      → FileWrite.write            edit rule, diff, format, BOM
mkdir, mkdtemp, unlink, truncate, binary writes    → FileWrite.authorize        edit rule
rm, rmdir, rename, cp                              → one edit request covering every path touched
denied → Error { code: "EACCES" }    missing → { code: "ENOENT" }    user feedback → the error message
outside the project → external_directory is approved before any disk check, so a denied program can't tell
                      whether an outside path exists (rm, rename, copyFile EXCL, appendFile)
```

Same actions and resource strings as the tools, so existing `permissions` rules and the plugin permission hook cover `fs` without changes. Each call gets a progress row (tool `fs`, method and path).

### Why permissions, not tool calls

Node's `fs` doesn't map onto the file tools: `read` returns line-numbered pages, `write` formats, and there's no stat/readdir/rename tool. Routing every call through a tool would change the semantics and pay a tool call per `stat` in a scan. So `fs` calls the services the tools use instead.

The trade-off: `tool.execute.before`/`after` hooks don't fire for `fs` calls, the same as `fetch` today. A plugin that blocks files through tool hooks rather than the permission system won't see them, which is one reason this stays behind the opt-in-only `full_codemode` flag.

### What it covers

- `readFile` (a `Buffer` without an encoding), `writeFile` (with `a`/`wx` flags), `appendFile`, `readdir` (`withFileTypes`, `recursive`, `encoding: "buffer"`), `stat`/`lstat` (with `throwIfNoEntry`), `access`, `mkdir` (recursive returns the first directory created), `mkdtemp`, `rm`, `rmdir`, `unlink`, `truncate`, `rename`, `copyFile`, `cp` (recursive) and `glob` (`cwd`, `exclude`, `withFileTypes`), each as `*Sync` and on `fs.promises`, plus `existsSync` (never throws) and `constants`. Dirents carry `name`, `parentPath`, `path` and every `is*()`.
- Writes keep exactly the bytes written: no formatter and no BOM handling, unlike the write tool. A missing parent directory is `ENOENT`, as in Node.
- `path` is the host's own module, with `path.posix` and `path.win32`. `resolve` and `relative` start from the session's directory, where `fs` resolves relative paths too.

### Known differences from Node

- `stat` has `size`, `mtimeMs`, `mtime` and the `is*()` checks only.
- Not here: callback forms, `chmod`/`chown`/`utimes`/`symlink`/`readlink`/`realpath`/`link`/`statfs` and the rest of `stat`, file descriptors and `FileHandle`, streams, and `watch`.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `packages/core`: `test/tool-execute.test.ts` (42 pass) covers reads and writes with the right permission requests, denied writes never touching disk (sync throws `EACCES`, promise rejects), `ENOENT` shape, listings, copy/rename/rm, and no `fs`/`path` without the flag, UTF-8 vs binary `readFile`, every outside-path call failing with `EACCES` whether or not the path exists, `mkdir`/`mkdtemp`/`rmdir`/`truncate`, `cp` and `glob` (dotfiles skipped like Node), `writeFile` flags, `throwIfNoEntry`, `existsSync` returning false when it may not check, writes keeping exact bytes even with a formatter that rewrites files (fails on the old write path), and `path.resolve` against the session directory. Codemode, tool registry, tool search and file access suites pass (134).
- Live, with the dev CLI and `OPENCODE_FLAGS=full_codemode` on Claude Haiku 5.5: a program listed `src`, read `notes.txt` and wrote `out.txt` through `fs`. With `permissions` denying `read notes.txt` and `edit src/*`, both calls failed with `Permission denied` and an allowed write succeeded. With the flag off, `typeof fs` was `"undefined"`.
- `bun typecheck` in core and codemode; `bun run check` from the root.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR
