prs.title: feat(desktop): signed-in browser pane with extensions, previews, prompts and agent safeguards
prs.body:
## What you can do now - **Click a link in the chat and you are already signed in.** Web links open beside the conversation, in one profile that keeps your sign-ins. - **Bring your sign-ins from your own browser in one click.** The pane offers Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari and 11 others, or a cookie file, and you choose which sites. - **Ask the agent about pages only you can see.** It reads and drives the same signed-in tabs you use, on servers on this machine. - **Decide what the agent may do.** Set `browser` to `ask` and every call prompts with the site, the script or the files it wants. - **See what the agent built, in the pane.** Workspace HTML and agent artifacts open as real pages, from local and remote servers. - **Keep working while it tests your app.** The agent screenshots and clicks tabs that are not on screen. - **Bring your extensions.** Store extensions install after a review of what they can access; ad blockers block. - **Use it like a browser.** Right-click menu, find in page, hard reload, clearing one site's cache, page dialogs, "Leave site?", permission prompts, HTTP sign-in and pop-up blocking. "Open in default browser" hands the page to your own browser. - **Your files stay yours.** A previewed page reads only its own folder, never dot or secret files, and the agent also obeys your read rules. - **Close the app and it is all still there.** Sign-ins, tabs, extensions and site permissions come back after a restart. | Area | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Profile | In-memory partition per attachment | One `persist:opencode-browser` profile | | Sign-ins | Lost on restart or tab close | Kept, encrypted; import from 15 browsers and files | | Remote servers | Signed out | Signed out unless you share sign-ins | | Links | System browser | Pane; modifier click keeps the system browser | | Workspace HTML | Native `file:` or a sandboxed iframe | `oc-preview:` page, folder-scoped, local and remote | | Agent artifacts | Not viewable on desktop | Open in the pane, one grant each | | Browser chrome | Select All only | Native menu, find, hard reload, site cache clear, notices, pop-up blocking | | Dialogs, permissions | Electron's native box; everything denied | In-app dialogs, permission bar, saved per site | | Extensions | None | Signed store installs, review, popups | | Agent tools | 20.7% of 14,974 calls failed; snapshot cut at depth 8 | Top error groups fixed or explained; snapshot and find at any depth | | Agent limits | Attach grant beat a configured deny | A denying agent sees no browser tools; deny, input, ask, then reads | | Chat links | App schemes did nothing; authored markup could cover the app | Reviewed app links; contained markup | | Packaged app | Plain-text cookies; runs as Node | Encrypted cookies; no run-as-Node, no remote debugging in prod | https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/feae78d7-0467-4f8b-a9dc-79b360980a70 22 seconds, real footage of this branch on made-up sites: signed in from a chat link, sign-ins imported in one click, the agent answering about a signed-in page, asking before it acts, a report it built opening in the pane, a checkout tested in a background tab, an ad blocker and Dark Reader at work, and everything still there after a restart. ## Screenshots | | | | --- | --- | | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7faa8da2-c5c9-44ed-808e-6636d0d50406)
Choose which sites to import | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b6dbbca5-1bc7-484c-87b5-7061138902c0)
The same chooser, dark | | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/acc42e87-d583-40c6-8703-297b76f97969)
Passkey refused, import the sign-in | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed2d5ae5-5e06-4d95-8879-24e8a92b6e65)
The passkey notice, dark | | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/97ceb89b-3211-4302-8e00-0870b83cd321)
Review an extension before adding | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c77c4f42-95d0-446f-a99f-2f99847fc2ef)
uBlock Origin popup over the pane | | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8e944604-6e32-4a82-8656-b05cd9db4a91)
Dark Reader popup | | | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f2542f4-5741-4935-89c4-90e81d2da1fa)
Agent activity dots on tabs | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/58b1564a-0a3a-411c-b271-5f485899839c)
Activity dots, dark | ## Why ### Measured tool-call errors Browser calls from the session databases of four devices (two Windows, one macOS, one Linux with a remote desktop): 14,974 calls, 3,099 errors. | Error group | adais | blade | air | vps | Total | After this PR | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `wait` without `condition` | 70 | 2,033 | 2 | 33 | 2,138 | Condition read from the keys present | | `screenshot` "needs a visible tab" | 88 | 207 | 1 | 9 | 305 | Captures hidden tabs | | `evaluate` without `script` | 81 | 55 | 3 | 1 | 140 | `expression`, `code` accepted | | `[browser.disconnected]` | 38 | 27 | 2 | 13 | 80 | Names the next step | | Page JavaScript threw | 16 | 52 | - | 12 | 80 | Top-level `return`, `await` run | | Message not stored | 8 | 64 | - | - | 72 | Code Mode keeps `toolCalls[].error` | | Invalid browser URL | 3 | 55 | - | - | 58 | Names the value; points to `preview` | | `click` `UnknownVizError` | 7 | 31 | - | 5 | 43 | Fixed | | `tab_unavailable` | 5 | 16 | - | 1 | 22 | Lists open tab IDs | | `wait` not met | 9 | 8 | - | - | 17 | Returns `met: false` | | 60 s timeouts | 11 | 9 | 2 | 4 | 26 | Not addressed | - Estimate, not measured after the change: about 2,290 errors become successful calls and about 160 become one precise message. ### Community issues - **Sign-ins:** Fixes #55920, Fixes #53580 (per-site import). Addresses #60313 (Linux restart not verified live), #60191 (passkeys fail fast; no real passkey support). - **User agent:** Fixes #55730. - **Permissions:** Fixes #61238, Fixes #61609, Fixes #54044 (a configured or agent deny hides the tools; #53294 and #56869 are closed duplicates). - **Agent tools:** Fixes #61625, Fixes #64217, Fixes #55795. Addresses #50781 (full-page capture works on background tabs; a minimized macOS window still fails fast), #52407. - **Pane:** Fixes #60152, Fixes #63278, Fixes #57708 (manual item for local HTML previews). Addresses #60892 (auto-open under a narrow rule), #31371 and #10309 (the links setting and Shift-click), #60233 (page right-click menu only). - **Chat links:** Fixes #56263. - **Plugin API:** Fixes #59787 (experimental tab handles). - **Extensions:** Addresses #52419 (password managers start; signed-in use unverified). - **Network:** Addresses #62234 and #59722 for servers on the same machine. - **Related, closed:** #50382, #63372, #62499, #62989, #52680, #59798. ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR link["chat, file tree or agent preview"] --> tab["pane tab"] tab --> kind{"what is it?"} kind -->|"web page"| profile["persist:opencode-browser"] kind -->|"workspace HTML or artifact"| handler["oc-preview: handler
profile/previews.ts, serve.ts"] handler -->|"local"| handle["open file, check kernel path
util/contained-file.ts"] handler -->|"remote"| read["server experimental.preview.read"] handler -->|"artifact"| art["artifact view, one grant"] profile --> guard["session-guard.ts
file: refused, downloads, client certs"] profile --> prompts["page-prompts.ts
dialogs, permissions, sign-in"] profile --> ext["extensions + extension-api"] remote["remote server partition"] <-.->|"cookies, only if shared"| profile agent["agent browser.* call"] --> order["deny, input, authorize,
attached, read rules"] order --> gate["desktop: extension refusal,
hit and focus check, picker guard"] gate --> tab ``` ## Profile and import One persistent profile for the whole app; remote servers stay signed out unless you share. - **Files:** `profile/index.ts`, `sources.ts`, `chromium.ts`, `firefox.ts`, `safari.ts`, `cookie.ts`, `probe.ts`, `link.ts`, `link-machine.ts`, `import-prompt.tsx`, `settings.tsx` (all under `packages/gui-plugins/src/browser/`). - **Sources:** 10 Chromium browsers, 4 Firefox family, Safari, and Netscape, Chrome-API JSON or Playwright files up to 32 MB. - **Honest results:** "Imported 1 cookie. Not imported: 1." Chrome and Edge `v20` app-bound cookies get their own line. - **Helpers by absolute path:** `powershell.exe` under `%SystemRoot%`, `/usr/bin/security`, `secret-tool` from `/usr/bin` or `/bin`. No shell, 60 s kill. - **macOS Keychain:** the prompt names "security". The app says to choose Allow, not Always Allow. - **Cannot save sign-ins:** a start-up probe cookie detects a denied key store, warns, and turns import off. - **Remote sharing:** "Share sign-ins with remote servers", off and global. While on, cookies mirror both ways by state comparison. Off removes the shared cookies. - **Sign out everywhere:** clears sites, cookies, caches, HTTP sign-ins and linked partitions. Extension service workers survive so their menus keep working. - **Choose sites** (`profile/sites.ts`): the chooser groups cookies by registrable domain and lists hosts and dates only; selection matches hosts exactly. Keyboard and screen readers work. - **Passkeys** (`webauthn-gate.ts`, `passkey-groups.ts`): requests fail fast on macOS and Linux, and in agent-driven tabs everywhere. - A notice explains it; its "Import sign-in" button opens the chooser on that site. - On Windows, a person's own tab keeps the system passkey dialog. ## Links Plain clicks on web links open in the pane; everything else keeps its old target. - **Chat:** `createWebLinks` in `packages/app/src/runtime/plugin/render.tsx` and `web-href.ts` take absolute `http(s)://` links only. - **Terminal:** `packages/gui-plugins/src/terminal/terminal-key-event.ts`. Ctrl/Cmd+click opens web links in the pane; Shift sends a link to the system. `file:` links never reach the OS. - **OSC 8 links:** a confirmation shows the real target before anything opens. - **Setting:** Settings › Browser › "Open links in the browser pane". - **App-scheme chat links** (`packages/app/src/runtime/plugin/app-links.ts`): a real click shows the pane's confirmation with the full target. - Printable ASCII up to 200 characters; the review expires after 60 s. - Editor and IDE schemes are Copy-only; `obsidian` opens `open` and `search` only; `mailto` only without attachments. - **Authored markup** (`packages/session-ui/src/components/markdown-cache.tsx`): model- and tool-written HTML passes tag and attribute allowlists. No positioning, pop-over, command or dialog. - The app's own renderer output is unchanged: 12 of 13 comparison screenshots are byte-identical. ## Local and remote previews and artifacts Every workspace HTML page and artifact loads through one handler on a random per-grant origin. - **Files:** `profile/previews.ts`, `profile/serve.ts`, `preview.ts`, `workspace-file.ts`, `remote-preview.ts`, `remote-address.ts`, `artifact-preview.ts`, `artifact-link.ts`, `packages/util/src/preview-scope.ts`, `packages/util/src/contained-file.ts`, `packages/server/src/handlers/preview.ts`. - **Desktop routing:** HTML from the file tree, Open file, chat links and `browser.preview` opens in the pane. The sandboxed iframe stays only in the web app. The pane menu has "View source". - **Why not `file:`:** a worker made by a `file:` page reads any local file past `webRequest`. That gap exists on `dev` too. | A previewed page can | A previewed page cannot | | --- | --- | | Load files in its own folder and below | Load a parent folder, dot path or secret-named file | | Run workers, modules, worklets, media with seeking | Register a service worker or load `file:///` URLs | | Follow relative links and `pushState` to real files | Run extension content scripts | - **Folder grant:** the opened document's folder, pinned at open. Refused names: dot components below the root, `id_rsa` and friends, `credentials`, `secrets.*`, `.pem`, `.key`, `.pfx`, `.p12`. - **Open-handle reads:** the handler opens the file, checks the kernel-reported path, then streams from that handle. A swap after the check cannot redirect the read. - **Remote:** `GET /api/experimental/preview/read`, session-scoped, same rules on the server. Older servers fail closed with "Update this session's server". - **Addresses:** local pages show `file:`, remote pages `workspace:///`, artifacts `artifact:///`. Only real workspace files become a shown address. - **Agent-driven previews:** every request is also checked against the session's `read` and `external_directory` rules. Ask and deny return no bytes. - **Takeover:** the first agent call on a user preview reloads it on a new origin with no old storage, and returns `document_changed`. - **Artifacts:** CSP sandbox, `Connection-Allowlist: (response-origin);webrtc=block`, no popups, forms or navigation away. A clicked link asks before it opens. - **Native `file:`:** refused in every web contents of the profile and remote partitions (`session-guard.ts`). - **Verification unavailable:** when the handle check cannot load, preview and artifact reads answer `503 file_verification_unavailable`, and the pane and agent show a distinct message. A missing file stays `404`. - **Native binding** (`packages/util/src/handle-path.ts`, `file-verification.ts`): - The compiled CLI embeds only the target's binding (`packages/cli/script/build.ts`). - workerd gets no native resolver, so contained reads are refused there. - The desktop `afterPack` hook requires the target's binding unpacked from the asar, of the right architecture, or the build fails (`packages/desktop/script/preview-binding.ts`). ```mermaid flowchart LR req["oc-preview://grant/path"] --> g{"live grant, GET or HEAD, own initiator?"} g -->|no| err["Response.error"] g -->|yes| s{"inside pinned folder, no dot or secret name?"} s -->|no| err s -->|yes| r{"agent tab: read rules allow?"} r -->|no| err r -->|yes| h{"opened handle's kernel path still inside?"} h -->|no| err h -->|yes| ok["stream from the handle, Range, nosniff, no-store"] ``` ## Browser chrome The pane now behaves like a browser around the page. - **Right-click:** `page-menu.ts`, `native-page-menu.ts`. Navigation, link, image, edit and spelling items, plus extension items for pages they may see. - **Find:** `page-find.ts`, `find-machine.ts`, `find-bar.tsx`. Ctrl/Cmd+F, Enter and Shift+Enter, Cmd+G or Ctrl+G and F3. The query stays with the tab. - **Refused navigations:** `refusal-notice.ts`, `notice-actions.ts`. One notice per tab with the real target. - Open for 24 app-link schemes (`mailto`, `slack`, `vscode`, `zoommtg` …); Copy link otherwise. - Agent-caused targets get Copy link only. - **Pop-ups:** a `window.open` without user activation is blocked with "Pop-up blocked" and an Open action. - **Host display:** `host-display.ts` elides long hosts from the left, keeping the registrable domain. IDN shows as punycode. - **Activation delay:** `activation-delay.ts`. Buttons on bars and dialogs ignore presses for 500 ms after they appear. - **Hard reload:** Ctrl+F5, or Cmd+Option+R on macOS (rebindable), Shift-click on Reload, the page menu and the View menu. - **Clear cache for this site:** origin-scoped; cookies and site data stay. - **Open in default browser** (`default-browser.ts`): a manual item for the current page or a local HTML preview, launched through the `https` handler. Only the person's click triggers it; previews and links still open in the pane. - **Agent pages:** the pane opens by itself only for an agent `preview` or `tabs.open` with `focus: true`, and never takes focus. - The person's selected tab is kept; the agent's tab gets an activity mark. - Settings › Browser › "Show pages opened by the agent" turns it off. - **Native view placement** (`packages/app/src/runtime/plugin/embeds.tsx`, `embed-geometry.ts`): the page view follows its placeholder and hides under floating app UI. Zero measure calls while the chat scrolls or streams. ## Dialogs, permissions and sign-in Pages ask in the app, not in native boxes, and a decision is kept per site and partition. - **Files:** `page-prompts.ts`, `prompt-machine.ts`, `prompts.tsx`, `site-permissions.ts`, `site-auth.ts`, `media-gate.ts`, `system-media.ts`. - **Dialogs:** `takeDialogs` replaces Electron's internal `-run-dialog` listener and answers over CDP. - alert, confirm and prompt draw in the tab; frames are named "An embedded page at …". - "Stop this page from showing more dialogs" from the second repeat. - User or agent: the first answer wins. - A focused prompt owns the keyboard: app and pane shortcuts do nothing inside. F6 and the address-bar shortcut leave without cancelling. AltGr characters, non-Latin layouts and IME composition work. - **Leave site?:** for the user's navigations and tab closes. Agent navigations skip it. | Request | Web page | Agent-driven tab | | --- | --- | --- | | Camera, microphone, location, notifications, clipboard read | Bar: Never, Allow this time, Always allow | Block or Allow this time only; denied after 20 s | | Clipboard write | Secure same-origin pages | Refused | | Anything else, cross-origin frames, insecure origins | Denied | Denied | - **Saved decisions:** Settings › Browser › Site permissions lists, changes and forgets them. Previews are never kept; remote partitions keep until you quit. - **macOS media:** `media-gate.ts` holds `getUserMedia` until you answer, so macOS asks after the bar. The bundle declares camera and microphone usage. - **HTTP sign-in:** top-level or same-origin only; three tries. The agent gets `sign_in_required` and never sees the credentials. - **Client certificates:** requests are cancelled; no certificate is ever sent. ## Extensions Store packages are verified, reviewed and pinned before they run. - **Files:** `profile/extensions.ts`, `install.ts`, `review.ts`, `integrity.ts`, `compatibility.ts`, `filter-startup.ts`, `profile/extension-api/`. - **Download:** HTTPS only to the store hosts, 128 MB cap, 90 s. Edge's HTTP names map to its TLS hosts. - **CRX3:** every RSA or ECDSA proof is verified; the signer must hash to the listing ID. - **Review:** shows capabilities, sites and source. A one-use token installs exactly the staged package that was reviewed. Updates show new access. - **Unpacked installs:** copied into app storage with an app-assigned ID. - **On disk:** file digests are checked at start. A changed package does not load: "Files changed on disk or were never verified." - **Pages:** an extension's API opens only its own package. Web pages and other extensions cannot load its private pages. - **Popups:** on a click only, own pages only; `action.openPopup` refused. - **Background events:** a FIFO per extension wakes a stopped worker or event page; install and update events fire on approval. - **APIs:** `tabs`, `windows`, `action`, `webNavigation`, `contextMenus`, `cookies`, `notifications`, `storage.sync` (quotas) are real. Others are stubs or Electron's own. - **Private tabs:** a tab whose URL is not revealed never matches a `url` or `title` filter. Unfiltered, `active` and window queries still return it redacted. A private tab without a `url` in a `url` query made uBlock Origin throw during startup and then pass every request. - **Other redaction:** `action.onClicked` shows tab details only with `activeTab` or existing access, and skips private tabs. Frames inside private tabs are not reported to `webNavigation`; no empty `tabs.onUpdated`. - **Blockers first:** local-profile `http(s)` navigations wait for request-filtering extensions to start. - All such extensions in parallel, up to one shared 5 s deadline; then pages load and nothing is unloaded. - Measured cold start of uBlock Origin plus Lite: 4.19 s median, 4.31 s worst of 10. - Previews, artifacts, remote tabs, pane registration and agent tools never wait. - Stop, a newer navigation, reload, back and forward cancel or join a pending load. Stop, Back and Forward keep the saved address and never show a typed address over another document. - An MV2 blocker whose internals are not the expected shape falls back to the generic signal at once and logs once. - **Stylesheets** (`extension-api/styles.ts`): `tabs.insertCSS` and `removeCSS` for MV2 extensions, so uBlock Origin's cosmetic filtering works and its TypeError on every page is gone. - **`activeTab`:** scoped to the tab of the pane that was clicked. - **Self-closing popups** (`extension-api/popup.ts`): a popup that closes itself (uBlock Origin's element picker) stays in the window until its page is gone. This fixes a macOS main-process crash: in the app the picker opens, Escape quits it, and the app stays alive. | First ad blocked after a restart, restored and new tabs | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | uBlock Origin | 0 of 3 | 3 of 3 | | uBlock Origin Lite | - | 3 of 3 | | Both | - | 3 of 3 | | Extension | Verdict | Latest live result | | --- | --- | --- | | uBlock Origin Lite | partial | Signature verified; blocks; popup (Windows, macOS) | | uBlock Origin (Edge) | supported | Signature verified; blocks after restarts (Windows, macOS); hides ad slots with no console errors (macOS); popup (Windows) | | JSON Formatter | supported | Formats web JSON (Windows, macOS) | | Dark Reader | partial | Install, review, popup (Windows, earlier run) | | Bitwarden, 1Password | partial | Start; sign-in or welcome page only (Windows, earlier run) | ## Agent browser tools The tools accept what models write, answer fast, and say what to do next. - **Files:** `packages/plugin-browser/src/{rpc,tools,files,machine,skill,preview-path}.ts`, `packages/core/src/codemode/tool.ts`, `gui-plugins/src/browser/{chromium,capture,child-targets,file-choosers,snapshot,field-value,agent-rendering}.ts`. | Call | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | `wait {tabID, text, timeout}` | `condition: Missing key` | Text wait, capped at 30 s | | `wait {tabID, timeout}` | same | Pause | | `wait` that times out | Throws | `met: false`, `observed` | | `evaluate {tabID, expression}` | `script: Missing key` | Runs; `await x` returns its value | | `snapshot {tabID}` | Depth 8, 500 lines | Any depth, 20,000-character budget | | `snapshot {tabID, interactive, maxLines}` | Unknown keys dropped | Controls only; line cap | | `find {tabID, query}` | `text: Missing key` | Runs (`query` is an alias of `text`) | | `network.get {id, includeResponseBody}` | Unknown key dropped | Response body only | | `reload {tabID, ignoreCache}` | Unknown key dropped | Reload ignoring the cache | | `tabs.list {}` without a desktop | Throws | `connected: false` with guidance | | `preview` of HTML | `{ path }` | `{ path, tabID, url }`, also off screen | | `preview` of a missing path | Success | Fails with the absolute path | | `preview` of a path outside the workspace | Success | Fails: "cannot show a file outside this session's workspace" | - **Snapshot and find** (`snapshot.ts`): refs at any depth within `maxChars` (default 20,000) and `maxLines`; `interactive: true` lists controls only. - A quarter of the budget keeps headings and the opening text. Long collections are summarised only when truncated. - A truncation footer says what to do next. Such a tab is throttled again after 30 s idle and woken before the next command. macOS fails fast when minimized or hidden. - **Full-page screenshots** work on background tabs, with a 15 s deadline; the capture resizes the page once. - **Fresh screenshots:** a capture holds a compositor-frame subscription and returns a redraw from `Page.captureScreenshot`. - No frame in time fails with the clear timeout; frames across a document status change are rejected. - Element crops are computed in captured pixels and clamped. - A restored tab that never opened its page says so. | Never-shown tab, page updated itself | Stale at `ce772bc1ac` | Stale after | | --- | --- | --- | | Windows, app window covered | 50 of 50 | 0 of 50 | | macOS, every window state | 30 of 30 | 0 of 30 | | Cross-origin iframe in it | - | 0 of 30, Windows and macOS | | Capture cost, median | `ce772bc1ac` | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Windows viewport PNG | 37 ms | 47 ms | | Windows element | 47 ms | 51 ms | | Windows hidden covered tab | 37 ms | 43 ms | | Windows JPEG | 37 ms | 49 ms | | macOS visible-tab PNG | 67 ms | 48 ms | - Both baselines are `ce772bc1ac`, a commit of this branch that already captured hidden tabs; on `dev` the same screenshot is refused with "needs a visible tab". - Windows figures are paired runs; about 13 ms is the wait for the redraw to be presented. The macOS run covered the first two capture commits. - **Failure codes:** `condition_unmet`, `document_changed`, `stale_ref`, `preview_unavailable`, `sign_in_required`. - **Replies:** every reply is validated before sending. An unencodable one fails as `[browser.invalid_result]` instead of a 60 s timeout. - **Restored sessions** answer at once after a restart or reconnect. - **Workers:** child targets are released after attach, so page workers run. ## Agent limits and permissions The agent acts only where your rules allow, and never as you at the OS level. ```ts // packages/plugin-browser/src/tools.ts, every call refuse(tool, input.type) // 1. configured deny, before anything is read parse(input) // 2. the call's own input authorize(tool, action, paths) // 3. ask / tool.use / saved: site, script, destination or paths // not attached: tabs.list answers connected: false; any other call throws [browser.not_attached] // 4. preview: read on the named and physical path; upload: read + external_directory // 5. tab lookup, request; exports: edit on the generated files ``` - **Prompt and save:** prompts name the site, up to 320 script characters, the destination or the paths. "Allow always" saves operation plus site; scripts and destinations add a SHA-256 digest. - **Rules:** a `permission.evaluate` hook applies per-operation deny and ask with core's matcher (`Wildcard.match`, `packages/schema/src/wildcard.ts`). Missing or disabled agents are denied. - **Listing:** an agent whose rules deny the browser sees no browser tools and no built-in browser skill. - Core builds one ruleset for listing and calling (`Permission.rules`, `packages/core/src/permission.ts`). - The browser plugin adds its deny through a deny-only `experimental.rules` hook. - The Code Mode catalog cache is keyed by the visible tool set. | Code Mode step, 3,000 tools, two agents alternating | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | `Tool.snapshot`, median of 20 steps | 92.7 ms | 1.3 ms | - **Hooks keep their ask:** core passes `experimental.approved` and `approvedSave` on the event (`packages/plugin/src/{effect,promise}/permission.ts`). - **Grants:** subagents lose the inherited grant before their first prompt; grants of killed servers are revoked at start. - **Input:** clipboard and context-menu chords are refused. `evaluate` gets no manufactured user gesture. - **Dispatch check:** each click hit-tests the point and node just before sending; keys check the focused frame and its ancestors. - **App shortcuts:** debugger-flagged agent keys never reach the shell, find, reload or zoom. - **Agent-driven tabs:** a tab stays agent-driven until the person clicks, types or runs a command in it. The mark is saved with the tab, restored before its first document, and inherited by pop-ups. Kept site permissions do not apply there, and passkey requests are refused in the browser process. - **Downloads:** captured for the agent only in an agent-driven tab, never from an extension page; yours use the save dialog. - **File pickers:** agent-caused choosers are cancelled with a pointer to `files.upload`. - **Extensions:** extension pages and every frame under one are refused; their console and network entries are left out. - **Exports:** written to a session-specific cache that is deleted with the session. ## Cookie encryption and fuses Packaged builds encrypt cookies and close the plain-Node and debugger paths to the key. | Setting (`packages/desktop/electron-builder.config.ts`) | dev | beta | prod | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `EnableCookieEncryption` | on | on | on | | `RunAsNode` | off | off | off | | `EnableNodeCliInspectArguments` | off | on | off | | `EnableNodeOptionsEnvironmentVariable` | on | on | on | | Remote-debugging switches, packaged (`src/main/diagnostics/options.ts`) | ignored | kept | ignored | - `NODE_OPTIONS` stays: packaged apps ignore all but two options, and off would strip `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` from the CLI. - Unsigned macOS builds are re-signed ad hoc after the flip. - **One-way:** a downgrade or turning encryption off signs you out of sites. - **What a local attacker can still do:** swap `app.asar`; decrypt cookies as the same Windows user (DPAPI); start Beta with `--inspect`. ## Verification | Area | Windows dev | macOS dev | Linux headless | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Preview boundary, folder rule, swap loops | pass | pass | pass (matrix, handler) | | Remote previews, artifacts, restore, reconnect | pass | pass | not run | | Dialogs, Leave site?, permissions, sign-in | pass | pass (media gate, no OS prompt) | real-Electron tests only | | Right-click, find, notices, pop-ups | pass | pass | not run | | Extensions: signed install, review, digests, events | pass | pass, without events | not run | | Agent limits: chords, keys, pickers, uploads, read rules | pass | pass (chords, keys) | not run | | Hidden tabs, restored sessions | pass | pass | not run | - Last live runs: - Windows: acceptance at `b8d2153b27`; the extension and screenshot fixes live on their own commits. - macOS: `5dea41d59b` for the main pass, `ce772bc1ac` for packaging (static), and a final pass at `9e20e99a4f`: - Screenshots of never-shown tabs: 0 stale of 60 (PNG and JPEG, window in front and covered). - uBlock Origin blocked 6 of 6 loads across three restarts, in restored and new tabs. Off and on in Settings with a preview open stays blocked. - A reload during the startup wait loads the saved address once; previews do not wait. - macOS at `573e5f155a`: Stop during the startup wait, page-prompt shortcuts, the hard-reload chord and menu, a full-page capture of a background tab (5.6 s), a dialog after idle and uBlock Origin without console errors all pass. Native-menu shortcuts with real key presses were not driven. - macOS at `5361344011`: a typed `file://` address of a workspace file opens as a preview, with and without uBlock Origin; outside the workspace the refusal notice shows and the page is kept. uBlock Origin's element picker opens on the page, Escape quits it, and the app stays alive. - Two final reviews (security and code) of the merged batch: no merge dropped a guarantee. Their findings are fixed in the commits after `53eebb7b55`. - Every real-Electron test starts through one runner (`packages/gui-plugins/src/browser/electron-run.ts`) that cannot show a native dialog and survives the Linux first-use install race. - Unit suites, including the three real-Electron tests, pass on all three systems. - Packaged builds: Windows x64 and macOS arm64 and x64 contain exactly one binding each. The binding loads under plain Node from the packaged layout on Windows x64 and macOS arm64. The compiled CLI is checked on macOS arm64 and x64 and Linux x64. Earlier a packed macOS beta launched. - CI: full tier green on `5361344011` (run 44006197713, 15 of 15 jobs on the first attempt), and all 7 PR checks pass. Earlier, full tier green on `53eebb7b55` (run 43998022742, 15 of 15, first attempt). - Across earlier runs, three tests this PR does not touch failed once on slow runners and passed on re-run: `packages/patchmark/test/slow-inputs.test.ts` (a 250 ms wall-clock bound), `packages/app/e2e/regression/command-palette.spec.ts:14` (a request-queue warning; the session page sends the same 47 requests on `dev` and here, 10 runs each) and `packages/app/e2e/regression/review.spec.ts:1159` (also flaky on `dev`'s run of the merged commit). - The video's ad-blocking beat uses uBlock Origin Lite, because the recording found the uBlock Origin startup defect fixed under Extensions. **Not verified:** - Chromium import "Allow" and encrypted cookie rows on macOS. - Password managers with a signed-in account. - Sign-ins surviving a restart on Linux (#60313): verified live on Windows and macOS only. - Remote sign-in sharing against a real remote server. - A launched packaged build on any OS since the media and debugging changes; a packed Linux desktop package; a load proof of the macOS x64 binding. - Linux: dialogs, prompts, extensions, chrome and OS hand-offs in a real desktop session. - Real camera, microphone and location grants; Digest and NTLM sign-in; a tampered CRX from a store. - Picking an element with uBlock Origin's picker, and the picker's own close button (it did not close it); native-menu shortcuts with real key presses. ## Known limits - **Extensions in agent tabs:** extension UI in the page DOM is page content. The agent can trigger an autofill and read the field. - **Moving extension overlays:** a frame that moves between the hit check and the click can still be hit. - **Clipboard:** for about 5 s after an agent click, page script can overwrite the clipboard. It cannot read it. - **Print:** an agent-run script can open the native print dialog. - **Restart:** a session not on screen after a restart has no browser tools until opened. After a configuration reload, for about 20 s. - **Network log:** the agent sees request and response bodies of signed-in pages; only cookie and authorization headers are redacted. - **Attachment:** any holder of the server credential who learns the connection ID can drive an attached browser. - **Remote tunnel:** no destination policy; remote pages reach the server's loopback. - **Hard links:** a hard link inside the workspace serves the file it points to. - **Updates:** installed extensions update only when you add them again. - **Embedded frames in previews:** an extension running in a web frame inside a private preview learns that preview's address and title through the native `sender.tab`. For a local preview this includes the file's path. - Electron builds `sender.tab` natively; Chrome does the same for a frame inside a `file:` page. - Only extensions with access to the embedded site. - **MV3 scripting:** MV3 extensions can reach a web frame embedded in a private preview through native scripting; the preload guard is advisory. - **MV2 stylesheets:** Electron 44 cannot remove an inserted user-origin style sheet from a live page. Hidden elements stay hidden until reload. - **Blocker start-up:** native pop-ups, `target="_blank"`, in-page links and redirects do not wait for request-filtering extensions in the first seconds after startup, install or enable. Replaying them could change opener, POST, referrer or history semantics. - **Unrecognised blockers:** when readiness cannot be recognised, the first page after a cold start can load before filtering starts, as before this PR. - **Hidden agent tabs:** a tab the agent has used stays un-throttled while hidden for 30 s after its last command. - **Policy listing:** a managed `tool.use` policy deny still lists the browser tools; calls are refused. - **Huge pages:** `find` and `snapshot` on a page of about 100,000 nodes stall the app's main process for about 2 s, the same as before this PR. - **`/var` spelling on macOS:** a `file:///var/…` address of a workspace file is refused as outside, because `/var` links to `/private/var`. The `/private/var/…` spelling works. - **Passkeys:** on Windows a tab the agent has driven refuses passkeys for the rest of its life. Real passkey support on macOS needs a newer Electron and a browser entitlement. - **Found, not fixed:** a chat link whose label holds display math with text around it can hang layout (the ingredients are on `dev`). Back after Stop on a held restore can lead to a blank page. - **Linux:** live coverage is partial. ## Notes for review - **Behaviour changes:** - Adding an extension stops once for a review. - Your downloads in the pane use the save dialog. - Remote servers' pages are signed out unless you share sign-ins. - Previews load only from the document's folder: no parent folders, dot or secret-named files. - Agent previews are slower: about +40% for 350 resources, from per-file rule checks. - `evaluate` has no user gesture; clipboard chords are refused. - `wait` returns `met: false`; unknown parameters are rejected; tool schemas change. - A configured `ask` prompts, with site and script. - Packaged prod ignores remote debugging; benchmark startup against Beta. - Sign out everywhere also clears extension pages' storage; only their service workers stay. - An agent whose rules deny the browser no longer sees the browser tools or skill. - A tab stays agent-driven until the person acts in it; there is no 30 s hand-back. - The pane may open by itself for an agent `preview` or `tabs.open` with `focus: true`; a setting turns it off. - Snapshots print filled form values, except sensitive fields; their output and size change. - Model- and tool-written HTML in the chat loses positioning, pop-overs, commands and dialogs. - **Security fix in the chat:** markup in a message or in tool output could enter the top layer or take clicks meant for the permission prompt and the composer. - `packages/app/component-tests/session-containment.spec.ts` fails 10 of 14 cases on the previous filter, which is byte-identical on `dev`, and passes 14 of 14 here. | Input (as text and as tool output) | Previous filter | This PR | | --- | --- | --- | | Block anchor card | pass | pass | | Fixed transparent anchor over the app | fail | pass | | Popover cover | fail | pass | | Invoker dialog | fail | pass | | Fixed tint | fail | pass | | Author-sized math | fail | pass | | Legitimate table, image, coloured span | pass | pass | - **Experimental API:** `GET /api/experimental/preview/read` (`client.experimental.preview.read`; `503 file_verification_unavailable` when handles cannot be verified), `experimental.approved` and `approvedSave` on `permission.evaluate`, and a deny-only `permission` `experimental.rules` hook. - **GUI plugin API:** - `Browser.experimental.open` returns a branded handle, and `experimental.close` closes only that plugin's tab. It rejects when the session is not on screen. Stable `Browser.open` is unchanged. - `ctx.system.openExternal` launches only `http(s)` and `mailto:` URLs; `file:` URLs and plain paths now do nothing. Use `ctx.desktop.launch(path)` to open a file. - **Electron internals:** the dialog takeover replaces Electron's `-run-dialog` listener. `electron-dialogs.test.ts` fails if Electron changes it. - **#59477** (client MCP draft) would move the tool-side code and drop the grant fixes. - **No feature flag:** GUI plugins cannot read server flags, and the fuses are one-way build settings. **How to review by area** (435 files, +34,908 / −1,728 against `dev`): | Area | Read first | Side branch | | --- | --- | --- | | Profile, import, sharing, passkeys | `profile/index.ts`, `link.ts`, `profile/sites.ts`, `webauthn-gate.ts` | `persisted-browser` itself, `browser-site-import` | | Previews, artifacts | `profile/serve.ts`, `util/src/preview-scope.ts` | `browser-html-preview`, `browser-sec-preview` | | Chrome, dialogs, permissions | `page-prompts.ts`, `page-menu.ts`, `default-browser.ts` | `browser-prompts`, `browser-prompt-keys`, `browser-pane-open`; menu and find on `persisted-browser` | | Chat links and markup | `app/src/runtime/plugin/app-links.ts`, `markdown-cache.tsx` | `browser-pane-links` | | Extensions | `profile/extensions.ts`, `extension-api/` | `browser-extensions`, `browser-sec-ext`, `browser-ext-fix` | | Agent tools | `plugin-browser/src/tools.ts`, `chromium.ts`, `snapshot.ts` | `browser-tool-fixes`, `hidden-screenshot`, `browser-fix-tools`, `browser-deep-snapshot` | | Agent limits | `plugin-browser/src/connection.ts`, `policy.ts`, `core/src/permission.ts` | `browser-deny`, `browser-sec-agent`, `browser-deny-listing` | | Fuses | `electron-builder.config.ts` | `cookie-encryption`, `browser-fix-fuses` | ## Follow-ups - An extension-free view for agent automation, to separate extensions from the agent. - Native Keychain read, so the prompt names OpenCode. - Asar integrity fuses and `GrantFileProtocolExtraPrivileges` off. - A timeline card for artifacts. - Downloads list, DevTools, real passkeys and other tab features. - Renderer-side candidate selection for `find` and `snapshot` on very large pages. - Per-server sign-in sharing and a signed attachment capability. - Browser tools for sessions not yet opened after a restart. - A per-channel updater cache name in `packages/desktop/script/pack.ts`. - A cancellable check before the native print dialog. - A background updater for extensions. --- _Added by the opencode bot (AI-generated)._ Fixes #53580 Related: #52419 Public API: adds experimental GET /api/experimental/preview/read (503 file_verification_unavailable when handles cannot be verified), experimental.approved/approvedSave on the permission.evaluate hook, a deny-only permission experimental.rules hook, and Browser.experimental.open/close tab handles for GUI plugins (stable Browser.open unchanged); prs.title: feat(app): redesign the inbox sidebar
prs.body:
## Summary

Redesigns the experimental Inbox sidebar (Settings → Interface → Inbox) so it is calmer, works at any sidebar width, and shows only what helps you act.

- **Live rows** (waiting on you, working, or finished and unread): avatar, `project / title`, and one text-only state slot (`Approve`, `Answer`, `Failed`, `Working 33s`, or the age). Under rows that need you, the pending request's own words: the command or resource for a permission (in the code font) or the question text for a form. That line aligns with the text, never sits under the avatar, and wraps before the state column, up to two lines.
- **Settled rows** (already read): one quiet line with the avatar, title and age, below a `Settled` divider. Archived sessions keep their own section.
- An open row stays live until you leave it, so marking it read does not move it under the pointer.
- Working sessions join the live list instead of the pinned Working shelf. Needs-you rows sort first, then by latest activity.
- A **project picker** (`All projects`) filters the inbox and is persisted. It only appears when the inbox spans more than one project, and rows only name their project when the list mixes projects.
- Rows drop the branch/worktree line and the server icon. A session on another server names the server in the avatar tooltip and in the picker. The now-unused branch loading is removed from the inbox model.
- Container queries: below 240px the project name drops and the avatar alone identifies it.

New English strings only: `sidebar.inbox.section.settled`, `sidebar.inbox.project.all`, `sidebar.inbox.action.approve`, `sidebar.inbox.action.answer`.

## Not in this PR

- A message line for done, failed and working sessions (last agent message or current step). The sidebar does not load messages for index sessions, so that needs data plumbing first.
- Hover/focus polish and a dedicated small avatar size.

## Verification

- `bun typecheck` and `bun run typecheck:tsc` in `packages/app`, `bun run lint:changed` from the root.
- Rendered the real app against the e2e mock server (approval, question, working, done, failed and read sessions across three projects) and checked the picker and filtering. Screenshots are in the Slack thread; GitHub attachment upload was not available to the bot.

prs.title: fix(desktop): only offer OpenCode 2 where it can run
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No linked issue. Follow-up to #64153, found while checking the OpenCode 2 offer before the v1 patch release.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Two guards on the OpenCode 2 offer in OpenCode 1 desktop. When and how often the card opens does not change.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| macOS 12 | OpenCode 2 is offered and installed, then cannot start | No offer |
| OpenCode 2 download keeps failing | About 300 MB retried every 10 minutes, without end | Stops after 3 failures until the next launch or Check for updates |

- **macOS 13.** OpenCode 2 ships Electron 44 (`LSMinimumSystemVersion` 13.0) and OpenCode 1 ships Electron 42, which still runs on macOS 12. The OpenCode 2 feed has no `minimumSystemVersion`, so the check is in the app.
- **Failed downloads.** Only a download that failed by itself counts. A feed that cannot be reached and a download cancelled by a newer 1.x release do not.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> unavailable
  unavailable --> downloading: 1.x is up to date, fewer than 3 failures
  downloading --> ready: OpenCode 2 downloaded, failures = 0
  downloading --> unavailable: download failed, failures + 1
  unavailable --> unavailable: Check for updates, failures = 0
```

```ts
export function supportsMajor(platform: string, system: string) {
  if (platform !== "darwin") return true
  return Number(system.split(".")[0]) >= MAJOR_MACOS
}
```

### How did you verify your code works?

- The macOS 12 guard has a unit test only. No macOS 12 machine was available.
- The download limit has unit tests for a failing download, an unreachable feed, and a retry after Check for updates.

### Screenshots / recordings

No visual change.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

### Issue for this PR

The `full_codemode` flag moves shell into Code Mode, but `read` stays on the native tool list. Its description also doesn't explain what happens to image/PDF reads inside a program.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Use the existing `full_codemode` flag for read's exposure and description:

| Flag | Read exposure | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Off | Native tool | Existing line-format instructions; old image sentence removed |
| On | `tools.read(...)` inside `execute` | Automatic media attachments; native line-format instructions omitted |

The Code Mode description says:

> Reading an image or PDF automatically attaches it to the execute result, even if the program doesn't return or print the media reference.

Remove the old "Images and PDFs are presented directly to the model" sentence in both modes. Only Code Mode gets the new attachment sentence. The native line-format instructions remain native-only, with no replacement guidance in Code Mode. Config changes re-register the tool through `ConfigEntryObserver`, as `shell` does. No plugin API or new flag is added.

The behavior is guarded by the existing opt-in-only `full_codemode` flag. Read's result schema, permissions and attachment behavior are unchanged.

- Core `bun typecheck` and `bun run typecheck:tsc` pass.
- Root `bun run check`: all 35 tasks pass.

The new tests check the exact description in both modes. They also cover read's catalog exposure and text execution, and PNG/PDF attachments when a program does not return the media reference.

### Screenshots / recordings

No UI changes.

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(core): opt-in sqlite full-text index of session history
prs.body:
Adds an opt-in SQLite FTS5 index of session history that SQLite keeps current itself, plus a one-time background build over existing history. Off by default in every build: `experimental.sqlite_fts: true` or `OPENCODE_FLAGS=sqlite_fts` (an opt-in-only flag, like `full_codemode`). This PR only builds and maintains the index. Nothing queries it yet: the search API (ranked results, excerpts, cursors), its endpoint, tools and a progress UI come in follow-ups.

Public API added: the `sqlite_fts` flag. Nothing else in HTTP, the SDK or plugins. The index lives in `opencode.db` as `session_search*` tables, a view and triggers, created at runtime when the flag is first on.

### Problem

Agents can't search past sessions. Scanning history without an index takes minutes per search on a large database (~2.5 min on a 37.5 GB one), so search needs an index that stays current without app code having to remember to update it on every write path.

### Change

```text
sqlite_fts on in a loaded location
  (the server forks SessionSearchBuild.run next to Schedule.run, where it waits; a small internal config
   plugin calls build.start once a loaded location's flags have it on, so global config turns it on everywhere.
   Config is per location, so this plugin is how a per-location flag starts one database-wide job; it goes away
   with the flag, when the server just starts the build)
  ─► ensure (once): pick a layout for this SQLite, create the FTS5 table, the source view and triggers
       SQLite 3.43+ ─► compact: contentless, contentless_delete      (~115 MB on a 37.5 GB DB)
       older        ─► text: FTS5 over session_search_document text   (~300 MB) e.g. macOS 13, 14.0–14.1
       no FTS5 / JSON functions ─► unsupported, nothing created
  ─► one-time build in the background (never blocks readiness), like the V1 import:
       newest first, ≤ 50 messages and ≤ 1 MiB stored bytes per transaction, cursor in kv,
       resumes after restart, skips rows that fail alone, records done/failed
  ─► afterwards SQLite maintains it: source triggers queue the changed ID, the queue's trigger
       reindexes it from the session_search_source view and deletes the queue row
flag turned off mid-build ─► the build keeps going until done or the process exits; the next process with the
  flag off doesn't start it, and it resumes from its cursor once the flag is on again. The index and triggers stay.
```

Around migrations (`Database.onMigrate`, registered by `search-index.ts`):

```text
pending migrations? ─► drop the view and every search trigger (tables and entries stay)
run migrations
every open, before any write ─► triggers this SQLite can't run? drop them, search off here
                              ─► view/triggers missing? recreate them and walk every source again
                                 (entries are replaced as it goes, so search keeps working)
```

Drizzle rebuilds a table by copy, drop, rename. Since SQLite 3.26 the rename rechecks every view and trigger, and ours refer to the dropped table, so without the drop the migration fails and OpenCode doesn't start. macOS's system SQLite turns `legacy_alter_table` on, which skips that check, which is why it only showed up on Linux.

Indexed: session titles, user text, finished assistant text (part rows, then inline), completed compaction summaries, each capped at 64 KiB. Never indexed: tool calls and output, reasoning, files, synthetic/system/skill messages, running or failed compactions. Every message type is listed as indexed or not, so a new type fails typecheck until decided. Tokenizer `porter unicode61 remove_diacritics 2`, plus ASCII folding for letters it leaves alone (`đ→d`, `ł→l`, `ø→o`, `ß→ss`, `æ→ae`, `œ→oe`, `þ→th`, …, as Lucene's `asciifolding` does), so "hoa don" finds "hóa đơn". The follow-up query has to fold its words the same way.

```text
packages/core/src/session/search-index.ts   # layouts, view, triggers, migration hooks, ensure, build chunks, state
packages/core/src/session/search-build.ts   # one-time background build and its status
packages/core/src/config/plugin/session-search.ts  # starts the build once a location has the flag on (temporary, goes with the flag)
packages/core/src/database/database.ts      # onMigrate: before (pending migrations only) / after (every open) hooks
packages/core/src/database/migration.ts     # beforePending option
packages/server/src/process.ts              # forks the build next to Schedule.run
packages/schema/src/config/flag.ts          # sqlite_fts, opt-in only
```

### Trade-offs and behavior to know about

Things that are true once someone has opted in:

- **Turning the flag off doesn't remove anything.** It only keeps a not-yet-started build from starting on the next run. The triggers keep indexing every write, and there's no command to drop the index yet; today that takes manual SQL.
- **Writes cost more.** Single writes: user message +29 µs, finishing a 221 KB assistant +1 ms. Bulk writes are much slower: 20k message inserts 529 ms vs 48 ms, a session delete cascading 20k messages 274 ms vs 30 ms. That hits imports, forks and project deletes.
- **A corrupt index breaks session writes.** If the FTS tables get corrupted, writes that touch indexed rows fail until the index is removed by hand. Same failure class as any corrupt table, but this adds tables. Planned follow-up: when a session write fails with SQLITE_CORRUPT and search triggers exist, drop them, mark the index failed and retry the write once; the next start rebuilds the index from scratch (under a new table name if the damaged one can't be dropped).
- **Every OpenCode upgrade that has a migration walks every source again** in the background (~2–2.5 min estimate on a 37.5 GB DB, newest first, search keeps working). It only runs while the flag is on.
- **A build without this PR that has its own table-rebuild migration fails to start on Linux/Windows** against a database that has the index (macOS passes but silently loses the rebuilt table's triggers, which the next build of this code repairs). A plain downgrade after merge is safe, since an older build has no pending migrations; the risk is branch builds and hotfixes on other channels sharing `opencode.db`.
- **The migration hook registers when `search-index.ts` loads.** The server, Node and Durable Object runtimes all import it today. An entry point that opens the database without importing it skips the hook.
- **It's one index for the whole database**, not per project; project filtering belongs to the follow-up query.
- **Index gaps:** forks re-index their parent's copied history (one entry per fork), assistants that never finish are never indexed, CJK text isn't split into words, and sources deleted while the triggers were off keep their entries, so the follow-up query has to join back to the source rows.
- **Progress is only in the logs** (`session search build started/finished`, skipped rows), until the follow-up adds a status API.
- **Failed builds:** three consecutive non-busy failures (disk full, I/O) mark the build failed; a later process retries it once.
- **Changing what's indexed needs a `Version` bump**, which nothing enforces beyond new message types.
- **Tables are created at runtime, not in a migration**, because the layout depends on the machine's SQLite.
- **Durable Objects:** nothing forks the build there, so it never runs.
- **A DB moved from SQLite 3.43+ to an older SQLite** loses search on that machine; writes keep working.

### Measured

| | |
|---|---|
| Index size on a 37.5 GB DB (21.4 GB of it current data) | ~115 MB compact / ~300 MB text |
| One-time build on that DB | ~2–2.5 min (estimate from a 1% sample and a full read-only scan) |
| Extra cost per write, compact (in-memory, Bun) | user message +29 µs, finishing a 221 KB assistant +1 ms, streaming rewrite +71 µs |
| Agent benchmark: 27 questions x 12 models (search + read tools over this index design) | 93.7% pass, 18k median tokens, vs 91.5% / 31k for a no-index search and 57% / 99k for a page-by-page scan |

### Verification

- `bun run check`: pass. Generated client and OpenAPI regenerated with no further diff.
- `packages/core`: `bun test test/session-search test/config test/database-migration.test.ts test/flag.test.ts`: 345 pass. Covers both layouts across edits, renames, reverts and cascade deletes, streaming assistants indexed once finished, every message type decided, dropping triggers an SQLite can't run, every migration since the index exists with `legacy_alter_table = OFF` including a Drizzle-style rebuild of `session_message` (fails with `error in view session_search_source: no such table` without the fix), the Database layer running the hooks around a real pending migration, the build starting only once started and only where the server runs it, resuming from its cursor, a failed build retried by the next process, ASCII folding, byte cap and skipped rows.
- Full `packages/core` suite: the same 18 local failures as a clean `dev` checkout (shell and HOME isolation), none from this PR.

### Issue for this PR

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

- [ ] Refactor / code improvement

### What does this PR do?

A client can attach its MCP tools to one session instead of every session in the directory. If a phone reconnects to session A while B is running alongside it, B's tool list stays unchanged and there is no phone notice to write into B's history.

prs.title: fix(plugin): leave serverUrl undefined without an HTTP listener
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Fixes #39561

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`PluginInput.serverUrl` no longer invents `http://localhost:4096` when the process has no HTTP listener. It mirrors `Server.url` and is `undefined` in that case. The `PluginInput` type marks the field optional and documents that `client` is the in-process route when it is absent.

A TUI started without `--port` has no listener, yet every plugin was told the server is at `localhost:4096`. Plugins that make raw HTTP calls to `serverUrl` (wake-ups, status probes, session prompts) then reach whatever else holds port 4096: another opencode instance, a leftover `opencode serve`, or an unrelated service. We hit this in practice: a plugin probed a stranger on 4096 (`/global/health` 200), posted a `prompt_async` there (204), and the wake meant for the local session was silently lost.

The SDK `client` handed to plugins was already correct: with no listener it fetches the in-process app directly. Only `serverUrl` misreported the situation.

Compatibility: `serverUrl: URL` becomes `serverUrl?: URL`. Plugins that read it unconditionally get a type error pointing at the case they were already mishandling; at runtime they see `undefined` instead of a URL that may belong to another process. Plugins that need to talk to this process should use `client`.

### How did you verify your code works?

`packages/opencode/test/plugin/server-url.test.ts` loads a real plugin through `Plugin.Service`:

- with no listener, `serverUrl` is `undefined` and `client.project.current()` still resolves the instance in-process;
- with `Server.listen({ port: 0 })`, `serverUrl` equals the listener URL and the client works over HTTP.

prs.title: fix(opencode): keep snapshot cleanup from failing and leaking packs
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #59766

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The hourly snapshot `git gc` can fail on every run for a store, and every failed or killed run leaves a `objects/pack/tmp_pack_*` behind that is about as large as the store. On one machine that was 600+ failures and several 650 MB leftovers a day.

Three causes, all reproduced on copies of real stores:

1. **Zero-byte loose object** (crash or full disk): gc fails with `object file ... is empty` / `unable to add cruft objects`. `git add` never rewrites it because the object looks present, so the store never recovers. Fix: when gc reports an empty object, delete zero-byte loose objects, reseed the index and retry once. On the real store this took it from 1.4 GB to 74 MiB.
2. **Alternate whose repo was deleted or moved**: gc fails with `bad tree object`, because the snapshot index still references trees that only existed in the alternate. Fix: drop alternates whose path no longer exists and reseed the index. The index is just a cache of the last staged state.
3. **Short-lived processes**: every process that opens a project runs cleanup a minute after start. A gc on a 650 MB store takes over 20 s, so processes that exit sooner kill git mid-repack. Fix: keep the schedule in the store (`opencode-cleanup.json`), so a store is collected at most once an hour across processes. Failures back off by doubling the interval, capped at a day.

After a failed or interrupted gc, cleanup also deletes the `tmp_*` files that appeared during that run. It never touches older ones, and it skips a store when another gc holds `gc.pid`.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New tests in `test/snapshot/snapshot.test.ts` cover each cause, the interrupt leak, backoff and the schedule. All 5 fail on current `v1` and pass with this change; the full snapshot suite passes (60/60) and `bun typecheck` is clean.
- Ran gc against copies of the failing stores: both failure modes reproduce on `git 2.55.0` and gc succeeds after the repair.

### Screenshots / recordings

prs.title: fix(ai): keep Anthropic cache hits after messages with many blocks
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #61689

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

On Anthropic's own route, auto now also marks the message before the newest assistant reply. The previous request ended there and wrote its tail entry there, so the new request reads that entry directly, however many blocks the reply and the new message add. Before, a prompt with 20+ blocks (10 attached images, say) left the only conversation breakpoint outside the 20-block lookback, and the whole conversation was written again.

The slot comes from the first system part, which only adds the base prompt to the tools prefix. It still gets a breakpoint whenever one is left over, as on a session's first request, so cross-session reuse doesn't change. Anthropic-compatible routes keep the current placement, since they may bill breakpoints differently.

Two smaller fixes in the same code, for every route:

- Message hints only go on blocks a protocol sends a marker on: non-blank text, media and client tool results. A reply with only thinking and `tool_use` blocks no longer takes a slot whose marker is dropped when lowering. A wrapped system update takes the last hint on any of its parts, so a trailing blank part doesn't drop the tail breakpoint either.
- Anthropic rejects a `ttl: "1h"` marker after a 5m one with a 400. Anthropic Messages, Bedrock Converse and OpenAI Chat now raise each marker to the longest lifetime after it once the body is built, in the order the provider reads them. Only the finished body has that order: on models that take native system messages, Anthropic Messages sends a system update after the user turn that follows it. Raising never moves the last 1h marker, and the prefix up to it is written at 1h anyway, so this costs nothing. It also repairs manual hints placed out of order.

Breakpoints are filled in the order tools, last system part, conversation tail, previous tail, first system part. A tail longer than the budget keeps its newest messages; before, the oldest message in the tail took the last slot and the newest content stayed uncached.

The first commit marked the second newest message instead. That is usually the reply the model just generated: in a tool loop its hint landed on a `tool_use` block and was never sent, and with parallel tool calls it marked another result of the same step. The second commit fixes that and raised auto lifetimes before a manual hint in request order. The third commit moves lifetime ordering to the finished body. Request order had missed a shorter manual hint before an auto marker, manual tool hints, and a system update moved after the next user turn, and each of these still sent a 1h marker after a 5m one.

Mixed lifetimes need manual hints. OpenCode itself doesn't set any (Core passes one request-level TTL), but plugins and direct `@opencode/ai` callers can.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun test` (2059 pass), `bun typecheck` and `bun run typecheck:tsc` in `packages/ai`; oxlint and prettier on the changed files.
- Tests cover the Anthropic placement, the first request keeping the first system breakpoint, a 25-block prompt after a reply, parallel tool results, a reply without markable blocks leaving its slot, auto hints before a manual 1h hint, a manual 5m hint before 1h markers, a manual tool hint, a system update moved after the next user turn, a held update that is lowered after the reply it goes out before, a wrapped update with a blank last part, OpenRouter and Bedrock markers before a manual 1h hint, and the newest-first fill order. 4 of the 6 tests added in the third commit fail on the second; the other 2 cover what moved out of the cache policy.
- A throwaway property test compiled 12,000 random requests: 4,000 shapes (tools with namespaces, system parts, system updates, tool calls, manual lifetimes, every cache policy) through Anthropic Messages on Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.8 or Opus 5.5, OpenRouter and Bedrock Converse. On the second commit, 2,860 bodies sent a longer lifetime after a shorter one; on the third, none did. With lifetimes ignored, the bodies match the second commit except where a hint on a multi-part system update is now sent.
- Compiling an 801-message request takes the same time within noise (about 5.9 ms against 5.6 ms).
- The long-tool-turn cassette pins the single-tail placement it was recorded with. I can re-record it with the new default if you prefer.
- Simulated a session through the real request builder: the step with 10 attached images writes ~14k tokens instead of ~56k. The later commits read the same entry, so the number holds. None of this was measured against the live API.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(core): keep one-off prompts out of the cached prefix
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #62554

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Some text goes out with one request only: the goal reminder after a compaction, the reconciled Plan mode reminder, the `session.generate` prompt with the instruction update previewed before it, and the compaction summary prompt with its template nudge. The conversation-tail cache breakpoint landed on that text, so the request wrote a cache entry that no later request could read. With an active goal after a compaction this happened on every step, so each step wrote the conversation again instead of reading it. #62554 has numbers from a 22-hour goal session on 2.2.7. adurgin's sessions ([comment](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63498#issuecomment-6883437204)) show the same pattern: cache reuse of 0-7.5% while the reminder was being added, 97.6-98.2% after the goal was paused, and 99.5% in a session whose history still had the goal text, where no reminder was added.

Changes:

- Text parts get an optional `transient` flag for request-local text. Automatic message breakpoints now stop before the first transient part, so the tail breakpoint sits on the last content the next request repeats. That can be the leading parts of a message whose last part is a reminder. The flag is never sent to a provider, and manual cache hints are not touched.
- The goal and Plan reminders are a transient part at the tail: appended to the last user message, or sent as their own message after a tool result or a reply. Before, they were a separate message, placed before the user's prompt when the history ended with one, so the next request also diverged from the cached prefix at that point.
- `session.generate` marks its prompt and the previewed instruction update as transient. Compaction marks the summary prompt and the nudge.
- When the history doesn't fit and compaction sends the text transcript instead, that request uses `cache: "none"`. No other request starts with the transcript, so breakpoints there only paid for writes.

One Anthropic detail: on models that take native system updates, an update followed by user content is sent after that content, and one followed by a reply stays in place. When request-local text follows a system update, the breakpoints therefore end before the update as well, so the next request still reads the entry.

This conflicts with #61690 in `markMessages` (`cache-policy.ts`). I'll merge `dev` into whichever of the two is still open when the other lands.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New tests in `cache-policy.test.ts` compile two consecutive Anthropic requests of a turn that carries a reminder and check that the first request's breakpoint is on content the second one still sends, and that a system update before request-local text stays out of the cached prefix. The goal, Plan, compaction and `session.generate` tests check where the reminder or prompt is placed and that it is marked.
- With `dev`'s sources those tests fail (2 in `packages/ai`, 11 in `packages/core`). With this branch they pass.
- Merged with `dev` at `1fa50dd28`: `bun test` in `packages/ai` (2190 pass, 0 fail) and a `tsc` check of `packages/ai`, plus the goal, plan, compaction, generate and session-runner tests in `packages/core` (390 pass). oxlint and prettier pass on the changed files at this head.
- The full `packages/core` suite on Windows, at an earlier head with `dev` at `101776024`: 6244 pass, 107 fail. The 107 are shell, ripgrep, MCP, config reload and symlink tests that don't run in my setup, and the same 107 fail with `dev`'s versions of the changed files.
- The `packages/core` typecheck reports errors only in `perf/*.bench.ts`, `src/mcp/client.ts` and `src/effect/client-tls/client-tls.node.ts`, because my install is older than `dev`'s lockfile. `dev` itself shows the same 34 lines, and none are in the files changed here.
- A throwaway check compiled a request with a transient part on eight routes (Anthropic Messages, Bedrock Converse, OpenAI Chat and Responses, OpenAI-compatible Chat, Gemini, Mistral, Cohere): the text is sent and the flag is not.
- The fix itself is not measured against the live API: the tests check where breakpoints land in compiled requests, not billed cache reads. The numbers above, from #62554 and adurgin, were taken without this branch.

Not a UI change.

### Issue for this PR

No issue. Follow-up to the `full_codemode` flag work.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement

### What does this PR do?

With `full_codemode` on, the `grep` and `glob` tools are no longer registered at all. They aren't direct tools, they aren't in the Code Mode catalog, and `tools.grep` / `tools.glob` don't exist. With the flag off nothing changes.

| `full_codemode` | `grep` / `glob` |
| --- | --- |
| off (default) | direct tools, same as today |
| on | not registered |

I left the `grep`/`glob` allow rules in the default agent permissions. They do nothing when the tools are missing. The Kimi system prompt still mentions `glob` and `grep`; I didn't change it since the flag is opt-in and still in progress.

prs.title: feat(codemode): add Node's Buffer
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

None.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Code Mode programs get Node's `Buffer`. Today they only have `Uint8Array`, so Node-style code like `fs.readFileSync(p).toString()` or `JSON.parse(buffer)` gets `"104,105"` instead of text. This is the binary type https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61186 needs for `fs` to behave like Node.

```js
const b = Buffer.from("héllo")
b.toString()          // "héllo"   (a Uint8Array gives "104,195,169,108,108,111")
b.toString("base64")  // "aMOpbGxv"
`${b}`, String(b)     // "héllo"
b instanceof Uint8Array, Buffer.isBuffer(b)   // true, true
```

How it works:

```text
Buffer.prototype → Uint8Array.prototype   (every Uint8Array method works on it)
BufferObj extends Bytes                    toString() is UTF-8, inspect() is <Buffer ..>
each method → the host's Node Buffer over the same memory (Buffer.from(bytes.buffer, offset, length))
host Buffer ⇄ program Buffer across extensions; snapshots keep it
```

- Encodings: utf8, hex, base64, base64url, latin1/binary, ascii, utf16le/ucs2. An unknown one is a `TypeError` with Node's `ERR_UNKNOWN_ENCODING`.
- Statics: `from`, `alloc`, `allocUnsafe`, `concat`, `byteLength`, `compare`, `isBuffer`, `isEncoding`. Methods: `toString`, `toJSON`, `slice`/`subarray` (views on the same bytes), `equals`, `compare`, `indexOf`, `includes`, `write`, `fill`, `copy`, and the integer and float `read*`/`write*` methods.
- It's only defined where the host has a `Buffer` (Node and Bun), so the package still runs in browsers, where `Buffer` stays undefined.

Not included: the `BigInt64` read/write methods (programs have no BigInt), and `Uint8Array` methods like `map` return a `Uint8Array` rather than a `Buffer`.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New `test/buffer.test.ts`: encodings and string coercion, `instanceof`/`isBuffer`, `concat` and shared-memory `subarray`, number reads and writes, `toJSON` and the unknown-encoding error, crossing an extension in both directions as a Buffer, and `import("node:buffer")`.
- A Buffer program added to the snapshot round-trip table in `test/snapshot.test.ts`.
- `packages/codemode`: `bun test` (1654 pass) and `CODEMODE_ROUNDTRIP=1` for the new tests, `bun typecheck`.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(codemode): let a synchronous global block on an Effect
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

None.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

A synchronous Code Mode global that returns an Effect now blocks the program until the Effect finishes and returns its value, or throws its error. This is what a host needs to offer Node-style sync APIs such as `fs.readFileSync` backed by Effect services. It's split out of https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61186, which builds `fs` on it.

```js
const text = fs.readFileSync("a")            // before: a pending promise, so `text` was not the file
try { fs.failSync() } catch (e) { e.message } // before: an unhandled rejection; now caught here
```

```diff
 startExtensionCall(host, args)
+  sync global returned an Effect   → settle in place: the program blocks until it completes
   Effect from an async global, or any Promise → program promise
   plain value or throw             → now
```

A global is async when it's an `async` function or marked with `Extension.async`, as before. For the published `@opencode/codemode` package this is a behavior change: an Effect from an unmarked global used to reach the program as a promise and now blocks, so several such calls in one `Promise.all` run one after another. Hosts that want concurrency mark the global async. The only host in core today, `fetch`, is marked async, so nothing in OpenCode changes behavior. `Extension.Services` now collects an Effect global's requirements at any depth (`fs.promises.readFile`), not just one level in.

### How did you verify your code works?

`packages/codemode` `bun test` (1647 pass), including a new test where a sync Effect global's value and error reach the next statement; `bun typecheck` in codemode.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

prs.title: refactor(core): simplify read tool structured output
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

`read` returns `file` for whole-file text and `text-page` for pages, tags every directory entry as `file`, `directory` or `symlink`, and includes image/PDF base64 in its structured output as well as its attachment.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Use these structured result shapes:

```ts
type Output =
  | { type: "text"; content: string; offset: number; lineCount: number; next?: number }
  | { type: "directory"; entries: string[]; next?: number }
  | { type: "media"; uri: string; mime: string; name?: string }
```

Whole text files and pages use the same shape. An absent `next` means EOF. Directory names keep their trailing separator and directory-first ordering; entries are plain names without a per-entry type.

Image/PDF bytes stay in the tool's separate content channel, so the model still receives the attachment. The structured result carries a file or skill URI instead of base64.

This changes the structured contract: callers matching on `file`, `text-page` or `list-page` must switch to `text`, `directory` or `media`, and check `next` instead of the output's `truncated` field. `metadata.truncated`, numbered text, continuation notices, permission checks, read limits and automatic media attachments remain unchanged. No audio support or explicit image-display API is added.

No flag: this refactors the existing read result without changing execution or attachment behavior. The PR does not change which tools are exposed inside Code Mode.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Read tests: 81 pass; 810/810 pass with `--rerun-each 10`.

prs.title: fix(service): retry Windows pipe spawn on packaged access denied
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #63892

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

On Windows, a shell command that uses Microsoft Store PowerShell 7 stops before it can run. Process creation fails with OS error -1073283067 (0xC0070005), so the caller gets no command output, in a project directory and in a temporary directory. The same commands still run under Windows PowerShell 5.1. Pipe-mode creation passes PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST to CreateProcessW and retries without a job when that attribute is refused. The retry matches only Win32 error 5. A packaged executable reports the same refusal as 0xC0070005, so the original spawn failure is returned unchanged.

create_process_refused_job treats both 5 and 0xC0070005 as a job-list refusal, and the Windows spawn path uses it to choose the jobless retry. When either code comes back from a job-backed attempt, the process is created again with no job attribute. A unit test covers both codes, the signed value -1073283067, that same code read from an io::Error, and non-matches for Some(2) and None.
