prs.title: feat(tui): add screen reader mode
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #39368

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [x] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Adds an opt-in screen reader mode. It runs on `opencode mini`, the append-only scrollback renderer, so output is plain text that screen readers can follow. The full-screen TUI redraws in place, which they cannot.

Turn it on with `--screen-reader`, `OPENCODE_SCREEN_READER`, or `screen_reader` in `cli.json` (flag > env > config; `--no-screen-reader` overrides config). Plain `opencode` hands off to mini when it is on.

In this mode:
- Speaker labels (`you:`) and a `Working...` line after the prompt.
- The terminal bell rings at turn end, when input is needed, and when a tool runs longer than 5 s.
- The terminal cursor sits on the selected row in menus, forms, permission prompts and the `/` and `@` autocomplete, so the reader announces the selection.
- Digits only select in forms, and Enter confirms.
- Prompt line starts with `$ `; the left rail is hidden. `NO_COLOR` is honored and animations stop.
- `--auto` works in mini (flag only, never the `autoaccept` config).
- Mini gets `/sessions`, `/rename`, `/fork`, `/undo`, `/redo` and `/mcp`, through one generic picker (`mini/session-actions.ts`). The mini handoff shares these files, so they are not split out.

Docs are in `services/site/src/docs/content/cli/tui.mdx`.

prs.title: feat(app): add /cd slash command to move a session
prs.body:
Adds `/cd <path>` to the desktop session composer, matching the TUI's `/cd`, including directory completion for the argument.

Before this, desktop could only move a healthy session between the current project's checkout and its worktrees (header workspace menu). `/cd` can move a session to any directory, including another project.

### Behavior
- `/cd <path>` calls `session.move` with the typed path; the server expands `~` and resolves relative paths against the session's directory (as in the TUI).
- Typing after `/cd ` lists directories the way the TUI does (`packages/tui/src/prompt/directory-completion.ts`, ported to browser-safe paths in `composer/directory-completion.ts`):
  - lists the directory the typed path is in, prefix-matched, with hidden directories only after a typed `.`
  - keeps the path as typed: relative to the session, `~/`, `/` or `../`
  - Tab fills the highlighted directory in and lists inside it; Enter fills it in and closes the list; the next Enter sends
  - with no matching directory, the list stays hidden and Enter sends the command
- Empty path: "Directory is required". Failed move: "Failed to change directory" with the server's error (same title as the TUI).
- Hidden from the command palette, which can't supply an argument (same as `/btw`).

### Implementation
- Commands declare `slashComplete: "directory"`; the composer passes those triggers to the suggestion machine, which opens a `directory` popover for their argument.
- Directory search reuses the `@` mention search machine (debounce, abort, timeout, stale results) through a second instance, with a new `literal` flag so blank and spaced paths are searched.

### Not yet at parity with the TUI
- No recent `/cd` directories.
- Not available in a new-session draft; desktop drafts select a project and worktree rather than a free directory.

### Testing
- Unit: suggestion machine (open, Tab complete, Enter select, Enter passthrough, Tab while loading), mention search `literal`, and the path parsing table.
- Manual, against a dev server: `/cd ` lists the session's directories, `pa` → Tab → `cor` → Enter → Enter moved the session to `packages/core`; `/cd ~/nope-xyz` → Enter showed "Failed to change directory".

### Flag
None. This is a client-only slash command over the existing, stable `session.move` endpoint, and it only runs when a user types it.

prs.title: feat(core): background slow Code Mode scripts behind full_codemode
prs.body:
**With `full_codemode` on, a Code Mode `execute` script that hasn't finished after 10 seconds becomes a background job and keeps running.** A fast script returns its result as today. A slow one returns `Script cm_… is still running; its result will arrive in this session.`, and the same VM continues from where it was. When it finishes, its result reaches the session the same way background shells and subagents report back: a synthetic inbox message that wakes the session.

- `packages/core/src/codemode/job.ts` (new): runs `execute` under `Job.Service`, waits up to 10s, then hands off and delivers the bounded result later.
- `packages/core/src/tool.ts`, `session/execution.ts`: route `execute` through it when a session provides it.
- `packages/core/src/session/synthetic.ts` (new, moved out of `session.ts`): shared synthetic-message admission used by the job.
- `job.ts`, `job/list.ts`, `job/recovery.ts`, `schema/src/job.ts`, protocol/client: new `codemode` job kind. On restart, a finished result is still delivered; a still-running script is reported as interrupted and never rerun.
- `job.ts` (`BlockingParent`): Ctrl+B releases the outer script; shells it awaits keep their own waits.
- A backgrounded script’s permission prompts stay pending and can be answered like a subagent’s. The script’s awaited tool call waits for the reply. The app shows the ordinary permission dock; the TUI gives it precedence over an open composer and shows it in the owning child session as well.
- `cli/src/run/noninteractive.ts`, `plugin/goal.ts`, plugin session types: know about the new kind.

Esc before the handoff cancels the script; after it, the script keeps running. Deleting the session cancels it.

🚩 **Flag:** `full_codemode` (opt-in only). With it off, `execute` is unchanged.

**Not in this PR (tracked for later):** pausing and resuming scripts across restarts, model-facing status/wait/cancel APIs, and dedicated client display for running scripts.

📊 **Proof**
- New tests in `subagent-idle-e2e.test.ts` (TestClock): a fast script returns normally; with the flag off a slow script stays in the foreground; a slow script hands off and its final value appears in the woken session's next model request.
- Permission follow-up: 271 core tests and 2 TUI permission tests passed. Core and TUI passed `typecheck:tsc`.
- 356 core tests pass across the job, shell, Code Mode and session suites; `typecheck:tsc` passes in core, schema, protocol, client, plugin and cli; `check:generated` passes in client and protocol.

prs.title: fix(codemode): accept a plain string query in search
prs.body:
### Summary

Code Mode's global `search(...)` now takes a plain string as the query.

- **Before:** `await search("notes")` failed with `InvalidToolInput: Invalid input for tool 'search': SchemaError(Expected object)`. Only `search({ query: "notes" })` worked, and models used the string form often enough to waste a step on it.
- **After:** `search("notes")` works exactly like `search({ query: "notes" })`, through the global `search`, the `tools.search(...)` alias, and when used sync, awaited or chained. Hooks see `{ query: "notes" }`.

The object form (`query`/`namespace`/`limit`/`offset`) is unchanged, and so is unknown-key handling. The string is mapped to `{ query }` in one place in `tool-runtime.ts`, before the existing schema decode. Other inputs (`42`, `null`, arrays, extra arguments) still fail with `InvalidToolInput`. A failed `search` input now comes with the suggestion `Pass search a query string or an object, such as search("issues") or search({ namespace: "github" }).`, where before it had no suggestion. The advertised signature only gains a prefix: `search(query: string | { query?, namespace?, limit?, offset? }): …`.

### Testing

- `packages/codemode`: `bun test` (1646 pass), with new cases in `test/tool-paths.test.ts`: a string query returns the same result as `{ query }` through bare, awaited, chained and `tools.search` calls; an empty string matches `{ query: "" }`; the object form is unchanged; non-string, non-object inputs and extra arguments still fail clearly.
- `packages/core`: `bun run script/test.ts test/codemode test/tool-search.test.ts test/tool-registry.test.ts test/session-store.test.ts test/mcp.test.ts test/config/policy.test.ts` (234 pass). The `catalog.test.ts` assertions now expect the new signature prefix.
- `bun typecheck` in codemode and core; `bun run check` from the root.

prs.title: chore: upgrade oxlint to 1.93.0
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No linked issue. Upstream: oxc-project/oxc#19395, fixed by oxc-project/oxc#22124 in oxlint 1.65.0.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Upgrades `oxlint` and `@oxlint/plugins` from 1.60.0 to 1.93.0, so `bun run lint` and `bun run lint:changed` stop reserving tens of gigabytes of memory on Windows.

- **Cause:** `.oxlintrc.json` loads the anti-slop rules as JS plugins. With JS plugins, oxlint 1.60.0 creates a pool of fixed-size allocators. Windows charges each whole block against the commit limit at once, where Linux and macOS charge only for pages that are touched. CI runs on Linux, so it never showed.
- **Fix:** since 1.65.0, the fixed-size allocators use `VirtualAlloc` to reserve address space and commit only what is used.
- **Version:** 1.94.0 is the newest release, but it is one day old and `minimumReleaseAge` in `bunfig.toml` blocks it. 1.93.0 is the newest release the policy allows.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph before["1.60.0 on Windows"]
    A[32 threads] --> B[fixed-size allocators, committed up front] --> C[takes all the commit it can get]
  end
  subgraph after["1.93.0 on Windows"]
    D[32 threads] --> E[address space reserved, pages committed on use] --> F[under 1 GiB]
  end
```

Full `oxlint` run of this tree on Windows 11, 32 threads, inside a job object with a hard memory limit so the baseline cannot take the machine's memory:

| | Job memory limit | Peak job commit | Wall time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.60.0 (`dev`) | 16 GiB | 18.2 GiB (at the limit) | 6.7 to 8.4 s |
| 1.60.0 (`dev`) | 48 GiB | 48.3 GiB (at the limit) | 3.4 s |
| 1.93.0 (this PR) | 16 GiB | 0.82 GiB | 3.6 s |

- 1.60.0 fills whatever limit it gets. The peak that the job object reports can read slightly above the limit.
- `bun script/lint-changed.ts` on 123 changed files peaks at 0.58 GiB on 1.93.0.

Rule behavior does not change:

- Both versions report the same 506 warnings and 0 errors, with identical file, line, column and rule for each one.
- The vendored anti-slop plugins load unchanged. Every name they import from `@oxlint/plugins` is still exported.
- `--format json` keeps the fields that `script/lint-changed.ts` reads.

### How did you verify your code works?

Measured both versions on the same tree under a Windows job object memory limit, and compared the two JSON reports diagnostic by diagnostic. See the table above.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

prs.title: fix(core): avoid WAL on Linux NFS databases
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Addresses the NFS/WAL startup failure in #56282, not the broader corruption/lock-storm report. Builds on #43141, narrowed to Linux NFS.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

Two files only: database initialization and its existing tests. Asynchronous `statfs` selects DELETE journaling on Linux NFS; the SQLite adapter receives `disableWAL` so it cannot enable WAL first. Other filesystems keep WAL. Detection errors warn and retain the previous default.

No new environment variable, configuration option, CLI changes, or service-registration changes. [SQLite WAL requires same-host shared memory](https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html); rollback still depends on reliable filesystem locking.

### How did you verify your code works?

**Sanity checks** are basic correctness/regression checks, not a stress test.

| Check | What it verifies |
|---|---|
| Journal selection | Local storage keeps WAL; Linux NFS selects DELETE. WAL/SHM sidecars match the selected mode while the database is open. |
| Reopen and conversion | Write a marker, close the database, reopen, and check the marker and SQLite integrity. Repeat after forcing the closed, initialized database to WAL. |
| File permissions | The database and any existing WAL/SHM files remain owner-only (`0600`). |

Fresh rerun of reduced commit `57e65c2`: 39 database tests pass separately on node-local storage and real NFSv3. The affected file also passes 10 repetitions on each filesystem (40 executions each). Core/CLI typechecks, lint and formatting pass. The NFS run exercises DELETE selection, WAL-to-DELETE conversion and absence of WAL/SHM sidecars.

**Fresh two-node reproduction of the same reduced patch**, on Delta NFSv3: stock's second foreground server exited with `SQLiteError: locking protocol`, so its load phase was skipped. Patched servers both started and completed all 576 session create/import/update requests with zero failures, preserving 384 acknowledged sessions and 768 messages. Integrity and foreign-key checks passed. Isolated state, disposable database, no model calls. This reproduces a startup failure, not corruption or a SQLITE_BUSY storm.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not applicable.

- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(core): pin npm cache generations while a plugin instance uses them
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Refs #62068

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`Npm.update` prunes the package cache after each install: `collect()` keeps the two newest generations plus anything younger than 7 days. But a plugin instance keeps importing from the generation it was loaded from for its whole lifetime, so a server that outlives that window loses its generation on a later update — the instance's next lazy import, or the old instance's teardown during a reload, then dies with `ENOENT`, and the location's provider catalog drops the configured providers until a manual `/reload`. This is the cache-cleanup cause flagged on #62068 (the teardown-isolation cause is covered by #57096).

The fix gives cleanup a notion of "in use". When the plugin registry activates an instance loaded from an npm generation, `PluginModule` records a lease marker under `<state>/npm-usage/` (generation path, pid, hostname) and removes it when the instance's activation scope closes. `collect()` consults those markers: a generation held by a live local process is skipped, a dead local process's marker is reclaimed as housekeeping, and a marker from another host — whose process cannot be probed from here — counts as live until it reaches the same 7-day retention the generations themselves get, which bounds a container killed without cleanup.

Why this shape:

- Locally, liveness is the holder process, not a heartbeat: a suspended server keeps its lease, a crashed one stops pinning as soon as its pid is gone, and pid reuse can only delay a prune, never delete a live consumer's generation.
- Foreign hosts have no pid to probe, so their markers expire by `createdAt` instead. A foreign holder that outlives the window stops pinning; that is the price of bounding a container killed without cleanup.
- No refcounting: several locations in one process, and separate processes, can hold the same generation, each with its own marker.
- Markers are written through a unique staging name; the sweep skips `.staging` entries so a concurrent cleanup cannot break the writer's rename, and both sides compare real paths so a symlinked cache (macOS `/var` → `/private/var`, a linked XDG cache) agrees.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New regression test in `packages/core/test/npm.test.ts`: a stale generation pinned through `Npm.pin` survives `Npm.update`'s cleanup while an unpinned stale generation next to it is pruned, and is reclaimed once the pin's scope closes.
- A second regression test: cleanup keeps a marker mid-write (`.staging`), keeps a fresh marker from another host, and reclaims an 8-day-old one.
- `bun test test/npm.test.ts` (19 pass) and `bun test test/plugin/` (537 pass) in `packages/core`, `bun test` in `packages/util` (140 pass), `bun run check` from the root (35/35). The remaining failures in the full `packages/core` run (spawn/process-environment tests) fail identically on a clean `upstream/dev` checkout, so they are pre-existing and unrelated.

### Visual


issues.title: AgentSession.abort() leaves steering/followUp queues intact; agent_end-queued messages leak into the next run

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Summary

`AgentSession.abort()` aborts the current agent run and waits for idle, but it does **not** clear the pending steering/followUp queues (`_steeringMessages`, `_followUpMessages`, `agent.steeringQueue`, `agent.followUpQueue`). Only `clearQueue()` drains them, and nothing calls it on the abort path.

Combined with a second behavior — messages queued by `agent_end` extension handlers "require a fresh run" before they are consumed (see the comment in `_runBeforeSettleBoundary`/`_handlePostAgentRun` area of `agent-session.js`) — this lets queued content survive an abort and silently leak into the *next* `session.prompt()` run.

## Reproduction

1. Start a run, then abort it while an `agent_end` extension handler queues a `followUp` (e.g. `pi.sendUserMessage(text, { deliverAs: "followUp" })` from an `agent_end` hook — a legitimate continuation/nudge pattern).
2. The aborted run's run-loop exits without draining that queued message.
3. Call `session.prompt("unrelated question")`. The fresh run drains the stale queue — the continuation/nudge message is delivered to the model, and the agent resumes the *aborted* task instead of (or alongside) answering the new prompt.
4. Same for a user message delivered mid-abort via `prompt(text, { streamingBehavior: "followUp" })`: the run dies before consuming it; it sits in the queue and is consumed by whichever run comes next, out of order.

## Expected

An aborted run should not leave deliverable payload behind. Options:

- `abort()` clears the steering/followUp queues by default, or accepts an option (e.g. `abort({ clearQueue: true })`), or
- `sendUserMessage`/`prompt` with `streamingBehavior` rejects (or no-ops) once an abort has been requested for the active run, so a dying run can't accept queue entries it will never consume, and
- the contract for agent_end-queued messages is documented (queued during unwind ⇒ delivered next run) so embedders can gate their own handlers.

## Context

Observed in `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.5.0` embedded in a chat product: user force-stops a reply; during unwind an `agent_end` extension handler queues a continuation; the next user send starts a fresh run that consumes the stale continuation first, so the agent "keeps working on the previous task" and the real user message appears unanswered.

Host-side workaround (in case it helps other embedders): on abort, explicitly drain the queues and gate extension `agent_end` handlers on a run-aborted flag before enqueueing.

4. `pi --list-models` still shows the previous llama.cpp models, or none if the router is down.

### Expected behavior

Either refresh the catalogs of providers that extensions provide, or report which providers were skipped. `pi update --models` currently reports success for a refresh that did not happen.

issues.title: Verify the ID token in Sign in with ChatGPT

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Verify the ID token in the Sign in with ChatGPT login (`packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/openai-chatgpt.ts`) and keep the verified account identity.

### Why?

OpenAI's Sign in with ChatGPT guide (https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/sign-in) asks clients to verify the ID token's signature against OpenAI's JWKS, its issuer, its audience (the issued client ID), its expiry and the nonce of the attempt, then use the verified `sub` as the account identity and check that a returning sign-in matches it. The flow sends a nonce but only checks that `id_token` is a non-empty string. Related: #10300.

### How? (optional)

- Verify with `jose` (zero dependencies, pinned exact). It loads only when this login runs; `lazy-module-load` still passes.
- Store the verified `sub` as `credential.subject`.
- Add `LoginOptions.expectedSubject` so an app can reject a returning sign-in as a different account.
- Verify any ID token returned on refresh against the stored account.
- Negative tests: wrong key, unknown kid, wrong issuer, wrong audience, expired, wrong or missing nonce, missing sub, `alg: none`, HS256, account mismatch on login and refresh.

I have this on a local branch (`npm run check` passes) and can open a PR if the direction is acceptable.

This issue and the patch were prepared with Claude Code; I reviewed both.

The host sends one prompt when the shutdown handler starts. The fake endpoint asks for a tool call on every request, so the old session keeps looping until the script kills pi after 3 seconds.

```text
[ext] session_shutdown begin
[host] prompt sent during session_shutdown
[ext] session replaced
[host] prompt response: {"disposition":"started"}
[server] request AFTER the session was replaced
[ext] tool executed
...
provider requests from the replaced session: 11
tool executions from the replaced session:   10
stale-ctx extension errors:                  11
prompt saved in a session file:              false
```

issues.title: pi -p (headless) still does not exit on 1.5.2 even with zero MCP servers — hangs whenever extensions are loaded at all

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
pi 1.5.2, macOS (arm64).

Follow-up to #12238 (closed on 1.4.0: `pi -p` hangs when a stdio MCP server stays connected). On 1.5.2 the hang is broader: `pi -p` prints its result but never exits whenever extensions are loaded at all — even with an empty `mcpServers` config and even when every extension file is removed from disk. Only `--no-extensions` exits cleanly.

Repro (all runs print the correct reply first, then hang):

```bash
# Baseline: exits in ~2s
pi -p --no-session 'Reply with exactly: ok'

# Empty MCP config: still hangs (exit 124)
echo '{"mcpServers":{}}' > ~/.pi/agent/mcp.json
pi -p --no-session 'Reply with exactly: ok'

# A single failing stdio server: still hangs (contradicts #12238's 'failure at startup does not block exit')
echo '{"mcpServers":{"dead":{"command":"/nonexistent/binary","args":[]}}}' > ~/.pi/agent/mcp.json
pi -p --no-session 'Reply with exactly: ok'

# Moving aside ~/.pi/agent/extensions, ~/.pi/agent/npm and ~/.agents/skills entirely: still hangs

# Only this exits cleanly:
pi -p --no-session --no-extensions 'Reply with exactly: ok'
```

Observed while hung: no TCP/unix sockets, just kqueue + a couple of pipes with closed peers; ~0% CPU. In `--mode json` the process emits `agent_end` and `agent_settled` events, then keeps running — so the agent loop finishes, but some handle registered by the extensions-loading path keeps the event loop alive.

Impact: any headless child that spawns `pi -p` or `--mode json` never exits. Concretely, extension-provided delegate tools (e.g. billion-context-pi's `acp_delegate`) spawn `pi -p` children — the child completes its task, then sits until the parent's watchdog kills it, so every synchronous delegate reports `timed out` even though the work finished and the output file has the full result.

Workarounds: `--no-extensions` for headless one-shots; wrap headless runs in `timeout`.

issues.title: RPC mode: session_start hooks block stdin attach — embedder readiness probes go unread, and start-hook dialogs can deadlock

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
Found while debugging FaqFirebase/pi-desktop#58, verified against pi 0.84.3 (line numbers are from the published npm dist, not the TS source).

In `--mode rpc`, startup ordering is:

1. `runRpcMode` awaits `rebindSession()` (`dist/modes/rpc/rpc-mode.js:289`), which awaits `bindExtensions` -> `extensionRunner.emit(sessionStartEvent)` (`dist/core/agent-session.js:1831`) — every extension `session_start` handler runs to completion.
2. Only then is the stdin JSONL reader attached (`rpc-mode.js:643`).

Two consequences for embedders:

- Any command written to stdin sits unread while session_start hooks run. Pi Desktop sends a cheap `get_state` probe to detect readiness; a hook that calls a slow provider (a local llama.cpp prefilling a 41k-token system prompt takes 20-30s cold) makes a healthy pi look unresponsive. Pi Desktop killed pi at 15s because of this; we have widened our deadline, but the probe still cannot get a truthful answer during bind.
- A `session_start` hook that opens a UI dialog (`confirm`/`select`/`input`) deadlocks: the `extension_ui_request` frame is emitted, but the `extension_ui_response` can only be consumed by the stdin reader, which attaches after bind completes. Only a dialog `timeout` set by the extension breaks the cycle.

Suggestion: attach the stdin reader before `rebindSession()`, then during bind either (a) resolve `extension_ui_response` frames and queue other commands until bind completes, or (b) also answer cheap read-only commands like `get_state` immediately. Either gives embedders a real liveness signal and un-deadlocks start-hook dialogs.

Happy to test a patch.

issues.title: [fullscreen] Large transcripts re-render every frame; every resize re-emits the whole transcript (1 core saturated)

labels.name: inprogress
labels.description: Issue is being worked on

issues.body:
> 🤖 Drafted by the reporter's local pi agent from measurements we collected together; the reporter verified the repro with `pi -ne` (no extensions). Disclosed per CONTRIBUTING.md.

## What happened?

On Windows 11 / Windows Terminal / **2 logical cores**, working in a session with a large transcript
(current session file ~1.6–2.4 MB) makes the TUI stutter badly on window resize and when scrolling.

Measured inside the pi process (wrapping `process.stdout.write` + sampling `process.cpuUsage()` deltas over 5 s windows):

| Scenario | pi process CPU | stdout written |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `regular`, each resize 120×30 ↔ 209×51 | **5.2–5.8 s CPU per 5 s window** | **3.9–5.2 MB per resize** |
| `regular`, scrolling | 3–5 % of one core | ~10–120 KB / 5 s |
| `fullscreen`, scrolling a large transcript | **66–101 % of one core** | ~30–360 KB / 5 s |

On a 2-core machine, 66–101 % of one core is 25–50 % of the whole machine spent on the render path, which is what
shows up as stutter. Switching `tuiMode` from `fullscreen` to `regular` removes most of it.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Windows Terminal, `tuiMode: "regular"` (default), resume a session with a large transcript
   (a few thousand entries / ~1.5–2.5 MB `.jsonl`).
2. Maximise → restore → maximise the window a few times (each resize with a large transcript).
3. Observe the stutter; confirm by measuring bytes passed to `process.stdout.write` and `process.cpuUsage()` deltas.
   With `tuiMode: "fullscreen"`, scrolling the same session saturates one core continuously.

## Expected behavior

Render and emit work should scale with the **visible viewport**, not with the total transcript size — both for
per-frame rendering and for resize.

## Version

pi 0.85.1, node 22.23.2, Windows 11 26100, Windows Terminal, 2 logical cores.
Only difference between the rows above is `tuiMode`.

## Additional context

- `createChatViewport()` places the transcript document inside `new ScrollView(document, { follow: "end", ... })`,
  and on resize the whole transcript appears to be re-emitted at the new width (3.9–5.2 MB per resize).
- The numbers were collected with one locally loaded panel extension that wraps `process.stdout.write` and samples
  `process.cpuUsage()`; that extension's own components render in **0.1–0.2 ms/frame** (instrumented), and the CPU burn
  also appears in windows where it renders nothing.
- Re-validated with **`pi -ne`** (no extensions): resizing with a large transcript still stutters → not extension-caused.

issues.title: RPC new_session/switch_session/fork/clone emit session_start twice
issues.body:
AI-assisted (per CONTRIBUTING.md): my coding agent reproduced this and drafted the text at my request. I reviewed the findings and stand behind them.

### What happened?

In RPC mode, `new_session`, `switch_session`, `fork` and `clone` emit `session_start` to extensions twice for the new session, with no `session_shutdown` in between. Interactive `/new` and the SDK emit it once.

Any extension that does setup in `session_start` runs it twice. For example, a handler that stores a `setInterval` handle and clears it on `session_shutdown` leaks the first timer, and `pi.appendEntry()` in `session_start` writes the entry twice into the new session file. `resources_discover` also runs twice.

Cause: since 1cc303d05 (#2860), rpc-mode registers `runtimeHost.setRebindSession(rebindSession)`, so the runtime already rebinds after a replacement. The four RPC handlers still call `rebindSession()` themselves afterwards:
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/b2b5c42f6138b73ec4b2f49ec0ca468800f88586/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/rpc/rpc-mode.ts#L435-L441 (same pattern at L606, L614, L626)

That commit removed the same manual calls from `commandContextActions` and from print mode, but not from these handlers.

### Steps to reproduce

`ext.ts`:

```ts
export default function (pi) {
  pi.on("session_start", (e) => console.error(`session_start reason=${e.reason}`));
  pi.on("session_shutdown", (e) => console.error(`session_shutdown reason=${e.reason}`));
}
```

Run `pi --mode rpc --no-session -e ./ext.ts` and send `{"type":"new_session"}` on stdin (keep stdin open until the response arrives). stderr:

```
session_start reason=startup
session_shutdown reason=new
session_start reason=new
session_start reason=new
```

`switch_session`, `fork` and `clone` behave the same.

### Expected behavior

One `session_start` per replacement, as in interactive mode.

### Version

1.0.2 (rpc-mode.ts and agent-session-runtime.ts are unchanged on main at b2b5c42f6)

### Fix

I'd like to fix this myself: remove the four redundant `rebindSession()` calls and add a regression test that counts `session_start` after RPC `new_session` / `switch_session` / `fork` / `clone`. No existing RPC test checks extension event counts, which is how this slipped through. I'll run `npm run check` and `./test.sh` before opening the PR.

issues.title: A codemode script fails before it runs when it declares a top-level variable named `tools`

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

Hello!
First thank you for creating Pi and numerous blog posts which truly resonate with me. I switched from Claude Code to Pi recently and it is like breath of fresh air.
I came across small issue and thought that you may be open for a PR to fix. My AI told me that I need to open issue first and got a lgtm before opening PR, that's why I am so detailed here. PR itself perhaps would be shorter 🙂 

So, here is what happened.
I configured a new mcp, called fluffyjaws, which is a knowledge base search assistant.
The problem is that when I ask him at the first time I see the following codemode block:
```
 codemode                                                                                                                                                             
 const tools = await searchTools('fluffyjaws');                                                                                                                       
 console.log(JSON.stringify(tools, null, 2));                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                      
 Script error:                                                                                                                                                        
 SyntaxError: invalid redefinition of parameter name                                                                                                                  
     at codemode.js:1:41                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                      
 No tool calls were made.                                                                                                                                             
 ```

On the next turn it recovers and everything works.

I talked with claude opus 5.5 model trying to understand if this is a bug or something which can be fixed upstream. And it turned out that the problem is in variable name `tools`. Here is what it told me:
> Models write `const tools = await searchTools(...)` on their own, so this happens without the user doing anything unusual. It costs a turn to recover. 
> The cause is that the script body is wrapped as `(async (tools, console) => { ... })` in `packages/codemode/src/runtime/vm.ts:327`, so those two names are function parameters.

I am happy to submit a small PR with the fix. Let me know if you're willing to accept such contribution.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `pi -ne` with codemode enabled
2. Ask pi to run **_exactly_** this codemode script:                                                                                                                       
    ```js
      const tools = await searchTools("read");
      return tools.length;
    ```

### Expected behavior
That script runs and returns a number.

### Actual behavior 
codemode ends up with an error:
```
Script error:
   SyntaxError: invalid redefinition of parameter name
       at codemode.js:1:41
```

### Version

1.3.0


### Potential approach for fix

`tools` and `console` are already globals: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/bd3c9b823762b7383954aa49e13ee350471015fe/packages/codemode/src/runtime/prelude-source.ts#L451-L453 so the wrapper could be `(async () => { ... })`, without `tools` and `console` arguments:
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/bd3c9b823762b7383954aa49e13ee350471015fe/packages/codemode/src/runtime/vm.ts#L327
A script's `const tools` would then hide the global for that script only. Line numbers and `"use strict"` would keep working.

issues.title: Built-in background bash with exit notification (and print mode that waits for it)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Make background commands a built-in feature of the bash tool instead of something extensions bolt on:

- `background: true` starts the command and returns at once.
- When it exits, its exit code and output tail arrive as a message that wakes the agent.
- Print mode (`pi -p`) waits for running background commands before it exits.

### Why?

Without it, models fall back to `cmd &` followed by `sleep` and `cat log` polling, which wastes turns and tokens.

Extensions can't do this reliably, because the parts that matter live in core:

1. **Session lifetime.** In `pi -p`, pi exits as soon as the agent is idle, and `session_shutdown` kills the extension's jobs. The result is lost (repro below).
2. **Message delivery.** Extension wake-ups race with compaction (#10982) and get dropped by Esc/dequeue (#9886).

`claude -p` and `opencode run` both handle this natively: they wait for the job ("waiting for 1 background job") and re-invoke the agent when it exits.

**Repro** (pi 1.5.2, pi-background 0.4.4):

```sh
pi install npm:pi-background
pi -p "Run 'sleep 15; echo done' with bg_run, then end your turn."
```

pi exits after ~3 s and the job log ends with `[bg] aborted`. The same prompt in `claude -p` or `opencode run` returns after ~20 s with the job's output.

### How? (optional)

Follow Claude Code / OpenCode: a `background` flag on bash, the exit notification delivered as a steer/follow-up message with `triggerTurn`, and print mode awaiting pending background jobs before shutdown.

Related: #4850, #11189, #11702, #11332.

---

*Drafted with an AI assistant (Claude) at my request; the repro was run on pi 1.5.2.*

issues.title: Retry pattern misses gateway wording "The provider is temporarily unavailable. Retry shortly."

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
**What happened.** With `retry.enabled: true`, `maxRetries: 3`, `baseDelayMs: 30000` a mid-stream gateway
error aborts the turn immediately — no `auto_retry`, no backoff. Sessions show the error 4–6 s after the
last tool result, i.e. Pi never retried.

**Why.** `isRetryableAssistantError` (`pi-ai/src/utils/retry.ts`) matches transient wording with

```
"service.?(?:is.?)?(?:temporarily.?)?unavailable"
```

which covers `The service is temporarily unavailable` (#10965) but not the wording that relays actually
send, e.g. OpenRouter-style gateways and Closerouter:

- `The provider is temporarily unavailable. Retry shortly.`
- `The provider ended the response before it was complete.`
- `The connection to the provider was reset. Retry shortly.`
- `The provider reported a failure while generating the response.`
- `The upstream provider is temporarily unavailable. Try again shortly.`
- `Upstream response did not include complete usage data`

Verified against pi 1.5.2 by calling the exported helper directly:

```js
import { isRetryableAssistantError } from "@earendil-works/pi-ai";
isRetryableAssistantError({ stopReason: "error", errorMessage: "The service is temporarily unavailable" })              // true
isRetryableAssistantError({ stopReason: "error", errorMessage: "The provider is temporarily unavailable. Retry shortly." }) // false
```

Note the two texts differ only in `service`/`provider`, and the second is the one a real gateway sends
mid-stream (`event: error` SSE frame, no HTTP status), so there is no status code to fall back on either.

**Impact.** Five aborts in ~30 minutes on one provider route (closerouter `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`,
2026-11-16 16:58–17:28 UTC+3); each one ends a working agent run and requires the user to re-prompt.
The same class of message has appeared in earlier sessions (2026-10-31, 2026-11-03, 2026-11-05).

**Suggested fix.** Treat the provider/service subject as equivalent and add the two partial-response
wordings:

```ts
"service|provider.?(?:is.?)?(?:temporarily.?)?unavailable",
"ended the response before it was complete",
"reported a failure while generating the response",
"connection to the provider was reset",
"ended unexpectedly before completion",
"without complete usage data",
```

All of them are transient by nature (the request can simply be repeated), and none is a quota/billing
stop reason, so the non-retryable list stays authoritative.

issues.title: ai: preserve structured provider failure metadata through AssistantMessage
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Provide a shared typed contract for HTTP status, provider error code and optional explicit retryability on terminal error events / `AssistantMessage`, using the existing diagnostics mechanism if appropriate.

### Why?

Cherry Studio Mobile needs these facts for retries, credential fallback and error presentation. Provider adapters already see structured SDK errors, but the [Responses catch path](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/8efd314fa3d3232ce197d8d7a6a5660530b9d83e/packages/ai/src/api/openai-responses.ts#L250) reduces them to display text, and generic retry classification uses `errorMessage` patterns.

For example, an opaque/localized message with status 503 should remain distinguishable from status 401. A provider error inside an HTTP 200 stream also needs its provider code preserved. Temporary rate limits and exhausted subscription quotas must remain distinguishable.

### How? (optional)

Our 1.3.0 patch carries these fields in `provider_response_failure` diagnostics across adapters and lets consumers prefer structured facts over text matching. Could this become a consistent public contract?

Related: #10697 (lost cause), #10600 (Retry-After transport), and declined #5617 (retry-classification hooks). This proposal focuses on preserving existing provider facts through the message boundary for all consumers.

Checked against main `8efd314` by source inspection. Downstream regression sources exist; no tests or builds were run for this proposal.

prs.title: feat(ai): record ttftMs and ttfaMs on streamed assistant messages
prs.body:
`AssistantMessageEventStream` already measures total response time (`durationMs`) with a monotonic clock. This extends it to also record first-token latency on the final `AssistantMessage`:

- `ttftMs`: time from stream creation to the first content delta (including thinking).
- `ttfaMs`: time from stream creation to the first non-thinking answer or tool-call delta.

Both fields share the existing timing guard with `durationMs`, so forwarding wrappers keep the inner stream's measurements and empty or deferred responses leave them unset.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): capture git and npm output while the interactive TUI runs
prs.body:
Related to #11264 (the last open follow-up from https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11264#issuecomment-6927957315).

## Problem

`DefaultPackageManager.runCommand()` spawns git and npm with `stdio: "inherit"`. Interactive mode installs and refreshes packages again while the TUI draws on the terminal:

- `/reload` after a package was added to settings
- `/resume` into a project with project packages that are not installed
- every session replacement with temporary `-e git:` / `-e npm:` packages, which refresh on each load

Their output (`Cloning into ...`, `Resolving deltas: 100% (3/3), done.`, npm summaries and warnings) lands on top of the TUI. Reproduced: adding `git:github.com/octocat/Spoon-Knife` and running `/reload` printed `Resolving deltas` over the editor. git can also prompt for a password on the terminal, which then competes with the TUI for input.

## Fix

The host chooses through the options it already passes down. There is no global state:

- `PackageManagerOptions.commandOutput?: "inherit" | "capture"`, default `inherit`. `DefaultResourceLoaderOptions` passes it through as `packageCommandOutput`, together with a new `onPackageProgress` callback.
- `main.ts` uses `capture` in interactive mode. `pi install`, `pi update` and the other modes keep `inherit`.
- In capture mode, `runCommand()`:
  - pipes output and waits with the existing `waitForChildProcess`, so a background process left by an npm script does not block it (the hang the review of #11966 found)
  - keeps the last 8000 characters of combined stdout and stderr and puts them into the error on failure
  - sets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, and `GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -o BatchMode=yes"` unless the user set `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`
  - when git failed because it could not prompt, adds: "git cannot ask for a password or passphrase while pi runs. Set up a git credential helper or an ssh agent, or install the package once from the shell with `pi install <source>`."
- `resolve()` now emits an `install` progress event for packages it installs. Until the TUI starts, `main.ts` prints it as `Installing <source>...` on stderr, so a first install at startup is not silent. Afterwards nothing is printed.

## Trade-offs

- At interactive startup, successful installs no longer show npm and git output, including npm lifecycle script output. A slow `postinstall` shows only `Installing <source>...` until it finishes. Failures show the end of the output.
- Private git packages that rely on typing a password or ssh passphrase now fail in interactive mode with the hint above. Credential helpers and ssh agents keep working.

## Verification

- `test/package-manager.test.ts`, "captured command output":
  - a failing command's stdout and stderr end up in the error
  - git gets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and ssh `BatchMode`, and the credentials hint is added
  - `resolve()` announces an install
  - a command whose background child still holds the pipes returns right away. This one also passes on main, where `exit` resolved; it guards the captured path
  - The first three fail on main.
- tmux, regular and fullscreen:
  - startup with `git:github.com/octocat/Spoon-Knife` prints only `Installing git:github.com/octocat/Spoon-Knife...` before the TUI
  - `/reload` after adding two packages and a nonexistent one installs both, keeps the screen clean, and shows the failure with git's output under `[Extension issues]`
  - a gitlab.com https repo that asks for a username fails with `terminal prompts disabled` plus the hint
- A failure is listed both under `[Extension issues]` and as a startup warning. That is the same on main and not changed here.
- `npm run check` passes. `test/package-manager.test.ts`, `test/resource-loader.test.ts` and `test/git-update.test.ts` pass (208 tests).

prs.title: fix(tui,coding-agent): make fullscreen scroll frames O(viewport)
prs.body:
Refs #9549 (fullscreen scroll part; regular-mode resize and the regular-mode spinner cost remain open)

## Problem

In fullscreen mode pi draws scrolling itself. Every wheel event (up to 60 frames/s) rebuilt the whole transcript:

1. `renderLayoutFrame` started each frame with an empty cache, so the whole transcript document was rendered.
2. `Container.render()` copied every line of every child into a new array, once per nesting level (~5 levels in the transcript). `Box` then compared all child lines one by one.
3. Only after that did the layout cut out the ~40 visible rows.

In regular mode the terminal scrolls its own scrollback, so pi does no work. That is why switching `tuiMode` removes the cost, and why it shows strongly on Windows Terminal with few cores. The cause itself is platform-independent.

Measured with the real transcript components on real sessions:

| Transcript | Scroll frame, full render | Scroll frame, view-only | Frame where content changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 26k lines | 4.2 ms | 1.0 ms | 3.0 ms |
| 104k lines | 15.3 ms | 1.1 ms | 12.8 ms |

Measured after rebasing on main. Before container caching, content frames at 60k lines took ~10.5 ms; with it, ~6 ms.

## Changes

- **View-only frames** (`tui.ts`, `layout.ts`, `tui-alt-screen.ts`): wheel, page/line keys, top/bottom, prompt jumps, scrollbar drag and selection auto-scroll call `requestViewRender()`, which reuses the previous frame's component output. `requestRender()`, input to the focused component, resize and focus changes still render everything.
- **Containers keep their output** (`tui.ts`, `box.ts`): `Container` and `Box` share `renderChildLines()`, which returns the previous array when children and their lines are unchanged, so ancestors skip their copy too.
- **Faster column slicing** (`utils.ts`): `sliceWithWidth` and `getGraphemeCellRange` skip `Intl.Segmenter` for runs of characters that always form their own grapheme (ASCII, Latin, punctuation, arrows, box drawing, CJK, kana, fullwidth forms). Only stretches around marks, joiners, variation selectors and astral characters are segmented. Single-character widths are cached. Verified against the previous implementation on 30k random strings (0 differences). This was 88% of a scroll frame after the other fixes, because the scrollbar slices every visible row.
- **`Component.render()` returns `readonly string[]`**: `Container`, `Box`, `Text`, `Markdown`, `Image`, `MouseRegion`, `ScrollView`, `SettingsList` declare it; components that build a new array (`Editor`, `Input`, `SelectList`, ...) keep `string[]`. `AssistantMessageComponent`, `UserMessageComponent` and the radius login selector modified `Container` output in place (OSC 133 markers would accumulate every frame); they now copy.
- Docs (`packages/tui/README.md`, `packages/coding-agent/docs/tui.md`) now state that render output is read-only. Neither said anything about it before.

## Breaking change

Code that modifies render output in place, including `super.render()` in a `Container` subclass or another component's output, must copy first. A scan of the 300 most-downloaded `pi-package` npm packages found one real break: `@xynogen/pix-runtime` splices tab rows into an embedded panel's output every frame, which now grows if the panel is a `Container`. `gentle-pi` pads `Container` output in place, which stays harmless. `Text`, `Markdown`, `Box` and `Image` already returned cached arrays, so the rule existed by implication; `Container` was the exception.

## Known limits

- A component that changes state without calling `requestRender()` now stays stale while scrolling, instead of being refreshed by the scroll. It was already stale without scrolling.
- Selection drag without scrolling still renders everything; it could use view-only frames too.
- Regular-mode resize (scrollback rewrite) and the regular-mode spinner (`applyLineResets` over the whole transcript) are not addressed.
- Not tested interactively in a real terminal yet.

## Tests

- `packages/tui/test/container.test.ts`: output reuse, invalidation on change, mouse dispatch by child heights.
- `packages/tui/test/tui-alt-screen.test.ts`: wheel and keyboard scrolling do not re-render components until content changes.
- `packages/tui/test/slice-graphemes.test.ts`: slicing across standalone characters and clusters.
- `assistant-message.test.ts`, `user-message.test.ts`: OSC 133 markers are added once across repeated renders.
- Build passes; root and examples `tsc`, browser smoke and biome pass. `npm run check` stops early on this machine at the install-lock step (unrelated; this PR changes no dependencies), so those steps were run directly.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): report pi.events handler errors like other extension errors
prs.body:
Related to #11264 (follow-up listed in https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11264#issuecomment-6927957315).

## Problem

Extensions get events two ways:

- `pi.on("session_start" | "tool_call" | ...)`: pi's lifecycle events. The extension runner calls the handlers and catches errors into `emitError()`, so they show as extension errors in every mode.
- `pi.events.on/emit(channel)`: the shared event bus for communication between extensions. The bus calls the handlers, and its only error handling is `console.error("Event handler error (...)")` in `core/event-bus.ts`.

In interactive mode, that `console.error` lands on the terminal behind the TUI's back and corrupts the screen, the same class of bug as #11264.

## Fix

- `pi.events.on()` wraps the extension's handler. A throw goes to the new `runtime.reportError()` with the extension's path, `event: "events:<channel>"`, message and stack, the same `ExtensionError` shape as other extension errors.
- The runner fills in `runtime.reportError` in its constructor, as it does for the other runtime actions, and calls `emitError()` until it is invalidated. Before the runner exists, errors are dropped.
- A handler that fails after its session was replaced (runner invalidated) is dropped instead of reaching the old session's listener, which would show it in the new session's UI.

The bus keeps its own `console.error` for subscribers that do not go through `pi.events`, which only SDK hosts calling `eventBus.on()` directly can create. An `onError` option on `createEventBus` was considered and not used: the bus does not know which extension registered a handler, and the error destination changes with every runner.

Not changed: an error from a `pi.events` handler that throws while extensions are still loading, or before the mode attaches its error listener, is lost, as for other extension errors today.

## Verification

- `test/suite/regressions/11264-pi-events-handler-errors.test.ts`: a throwing handler reaches `onError` with the extension path and does not call `console.error`; a handler that throws after `session.dispose()` reports nothing. Both fail on main. The stale case also fails with only the stale check removed.
- tmux, fullscreen: an extension command emitting a channel whose handler throws shows `Extension "<path>" error: demo handler failed` with its stack in the chat, like other extension errors. The screen stays clean.
- `test/suite/regressions/7193-event-bus-lifecycle.test.ts` passes. `npm run check` passes.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): report model fallback after /resume and in every mode
prs.body:
Related to #11264. Same class of gap as #12115.

## Problem

When a resumed or forked session's model no longer exists or has no login, `createAgentSession()` falls back to another model and sets `modelFallbackMessage`, e.g. `Could not restore model gone/missing-model. Using fake/fake-model`. Only interactive startup showed it (`InteractiveMode` `modelFallbackMessage` option):

- `/resume` or `/fork` into such a session: the runtime recomputes the message, nothing reads it, and pi switches models without notice.
- Print, JSON and RPC modes: `main.ts` never passed it on, so it was not shown even at startup.

## Fix

- `main.ts`'s runtime factory adds the message to the runtime diagnostics as a warning when a fallback model was chosen. #12115's reporting then shows it in every mode, at startup and after each replacement: in the chat in interactive mode, on stderr in print, JSON and RPC modes.
- Without any model, `modelFallbackMessage` is the "No models available. Use /login..." guidance, not a fallback. That case is unchanged: interactive mode still shows it at startup through the `modelFallbackMessage` option, and the other modes still exit with it. `main.ts` passes the option only in that case, so a fallback is not shown twice.

Also deletes `utils/deprecation.ts`. `warnDeprecation()` printed with `console.warn` and had no callers; the file is not exported from the package.

## Verification

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RPC `switch_session` into a session with a missing model (`test/model-fallback-diagnostic.test.ts`) | nothing | `Warning: Could not restore model gone/missing-model. Using fake/fake-model` on stderr, not on stdout. The test fails on main. |
| Interactive `/resume` into it, regular and fullscreen (tmux) | nothing | warning in the chat above "Resumed session" |
| Interactive `--continue` into it | warning once | warning once |
| Print `-c` into it | nothing | warning on stderr |
| No models at all, interactive / print | "No models available" warning / error exit | unchanged |

`npm run check` passes. `test/virtual-models.test.ts` and the #12115 and #11973 tests pass.

prs.title: fix(p2): device- and platform-aware gesture and key hints
prs.body:
## Problem

p2's web UI hints assumed one device: "tap" and "long press" everywhere (a desktop with a mouse right-clicks and clicks), and "Cmd" everywhere (Windows and Linux use Ctrl). Example: the Send button's tooltip said "long press for more", but on a desktop the tooltip is only seen with a mouse, where right-click opens the menu.

## Change

New `src/web/input-hints.ts` (exported through `@p2/app/v1/web`):

- `pointerKind()` / `usePointerKind()`: `touch`, `mouse` or `both`, from the `any-pointer: coarse` / `any-pointer: fine` media queries. The hook updates when they change, for example when a tablet keyboard with a trackpad is attached.
- `pressVerb(kind)`: "tap" / "click" / "click or tap"; `moreVerb(kind)`: "long-press" / "right-click" / "right-click or long-press".
- `APPLE`, `primaryChord(key)` ("⌘." vs "Ctrl+."), `ALT_KEY` ("⌥" vs "Alt"). `command-menu/keys.ts` now uses the same `APPLE`, so labels and key matching agree.

Updated hints:

| Where | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Send button tooltip | long press for more | right-click / long-press / both |
| Send menu shortcuts | Alt+Enter, always | ⌥ on Apple; hidden on touch-only devices, where Enter does not send |
| Scope prompt button | Cmd+. | ⌘. or Ctrl+. |
| Scope prompt banner | coarse vs fine only | adds a touch-laptop variant; "Esc to stop" whenever a mouse is present |
| Terminal paste fallback | Long-press the terminal | ⌘V / Ctrl+Shift+V with a mouse (keys `#keyDown` leaves to the browser); both on touch laptops |
| Workspace comment hints, voice picker, voice "audio blocked", sandbox folder toggle | Tap | Tap / Click / Click or tap |
| Devices sheet | tap Sign in (on the other device) | choose Sign in (the other device's input is unknown) |

TUI hints are unchanged; they already use pi's keybinding tables.

## Testing

- `npm run check` in `apps/p2` and at the root.
- `test/p2/input-hints.test.ts` covers the pointer kind for each media-query combination, and the verbs.
- Browser tests were not run: Chromium is not available here.

prs.title: fix(ai): recover from the Codex websocket 60-minute connection limit
prs.body:
Closes #12124

## Problem

The Codex backend closes a Responses WebSocket after 60 minutes with:

```
Codex error: Responses websocket connection limit reached (60 minutes). Create a new websocket connection to continue.
```

The provider handles this only before the first event, by reconnecting once. Once anything has streamed (`response.created`, rate-limit metadata, reasoning summaries), `websocketStarted` is true and the reconnect is skipped on purpose, because the partial output has already been pushed to the stream and cannot be replayed into it.

Trace for the issue (long thinking, no tool calls):

1. Request starts on a cached socket that is less than 55 minutes old, so `SESSION_WEBSOCKET_MAX_AGE_MS` lets it be reused. In the worst case only 5 minutes remain before the limit.
2. Reasoning summaries stream for minutes; the socket passes 60 minutes.
3. Server sends `error` with code `websocket_connection_limit_reached`. The provider drops the socket and clears the `previous_response_id` continuation, then ends the message with `stopReason: "error"`.
4. `isRetryableAssistantError` does not match the message, so the agent-level auto-retry never runs and the turn fails.

## Fix

1. **Retry the error.** Classify the connection limit as retryable in the shared retry classifier (`packages/ai/src/utils/retry.ts`), with one pattern, `websocket.?connection.?limit.?reached`, that matches both the error code and the message text. Step 3 already leaves a clean state (old socket closed, continuation cleared), so the outer retry opens a fresh WebSocket and sends the full context. Durable and compaction use the same classifier and get the same recovery.
2. **Make the limit less likely.** New requests stop reusing a cached socket after 45 minutes instead of 55 (`SESSION_WEBSOCKET_MAX_AGE_MS`). A response started on a reused socket then has at least 15 minutes before the limit instead of 5. Cost: one full-context request (no `previous_response_id` delta) per rotation, at most once per 45 minutes; the prompt cache key is unchanged.

## What a retry costs

The retry redoes the interrupted response from the start:

- The partial output of that response (thinking summaries, partial text) is discarded from model context. It stays in the session file and UI (`_omitRecoveryAttempt`).
- The tokens and time spent on the failed attempt are spent again.
- No actions run twice: tool calls run only after a complete assistant message, and results of earlier completed turns stay in context.

The interrupted response cannot be resumed. Codex runs with `store: false`, so the server keeps no response to continue, and partial reasoning cannot be sent back because `encrypted_content` only arrives in `response.output_item.done`. The official Codex CLI handles this error the same way: it maps it to a retryable error and retries the whole stream on a new connection (`responses_websocket_connection_limit_error_reconnects_and_completes` in openai/codex). Without this change the turn fails and a manual "continue" also starts the response over.

A single response that itself runs longer than 60 minutes would hit the limit on every retry until the retry budget runs out.

## Tests

- `packages/ai/test/retry.test.ts`: the message and the code are retryable; a generic "connection limit reached" is not.
- `packages/ai/test/openai-codex-stream.test.ts`: with a mock WebSocket, the limit error after metadata, rate-limit metadata, or partial thinking leads `retryAssistantCall` to a second, fresh socket (first one closed, no `previous_response_id`, no SSE fallback). The existing age test now checks rotation at 46 minutes; it fails with the old 55-minute limit.
- `packages/coding-agent/test/suite/regressions/12124-websocket-connection-limit-retry.test.ts`: tool call, then partial thinking with the error, then recovery; the tool runs once and the failed message is not sent on retry.

The new tests fail without the source changes. `npm run check` passes.

The first commit is the retry fix by @shenmuegit (https://github.com/shenmuegit/pi/commit/ce7dbba948467a3b8c011d02f1f92c322d5bfc82). The second merges its two patterns into one, trims tests already covered by the generic retry suite, and adds the changelog entry. The third lowers the socket age limit.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): emit session_start on reload after bindExtensions({})
prs.body:
## Problem

`AgentSession.reload()` emits `session_shutdown` to the old extensions, then emits `session_start` to the new ones only if the host set a UI context, command actions, a shutdown handler or an error listener. That check was meant as "the host called `bindExtensions()`", but a host that calls `bindExtensions({})` started its extensions without setting any of these.

Example: the SDK example `examples/sdk/13-session-runtime.ts` and `docs/sdk.md` (MCP: "call `session.bindExtensions()`") use `bindExtensions({})`. With an extension logging both events:

```
startup -> session_start(startup)
reload  -> session_shutdown(reload)          # no session_start(reload)
dispose -> session_shutdown(quit)
```

The reloaded extensions are never started; for example the MCP extension does not reconnect its servers after a reload.

## Fix

`bindExtensions()` sets `_extensionsBound`; `reload()` emits `session_start` (plus MCP reporting and resource discovery) when it is set. Hosts that never call `bindExtensions()` behave as before.

## Tests

`test/agent-session-runtime-events.test.ts`: reload after `bindExtensions({})` emits `session_shutdown` then `session_start` with reason `reload`. Fails on main, passes with the fix. All 24 test files that call `reload()` pass; `npm run check` passes.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): stream session_start events in JSON print mode
prs.body:
## Problem

`runPrintMode` subscribed to session events only after `bindExtensions()`. `bindExtensions()` runs the `session_start` handlers, so any event they emit, for example `entry_appended` from `pi.appendEntry()`, was emitted before the JSON writer was subscribed and never appeared in `--mode json` output.

Example: an extension that calls `pi.appendEntry("marker", ...)` in `session_start`, run with `pi --mode json "/renew"` where `/renew` calls `ctx.newSession()`. The output has the session header and the prompt events, but no `entry_appended` for the startup entry or for the new session's entry, although both are in the session.

This is the same ordering gap fixed for RPC mode in #12230. Interactive mode subscribes before binding on replacement.

## Fix

`print-mode.ts`: subscribe (event writer and backpressure) before `bindExtensions()`. The JSON session header is still written first, because it is written before the first bind.

## Tests

`test/suite/print-mode-session-start-events.test.ts` runs JSON print mode on a real `AgentSessionRuntime` and asserts the header comes first and the `entry_appended` events for the startup and the `ctx.newSession()` entries are both in the output. Fails on main (`[]`), passes with the fix. Like the other session replacement tests it builds the runtime by hand, because `suite/harness.ts` has no runtime. `test/print-mode.test.ts` passes; `npm run check` passes.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): emit session_start once on RPC session replacement
prs.body:
Closes #10470.

## Problem

In RPC mode, `new_session`, `switch_session`, `fork` and `clone` run extension `session_start` (and `resources_discover`) handlers twice for the new session, with no `session_shutdown` in between.

Trace for `new_session`: `runtimeHost.newSession()` -> `finishSessionReplacement()` -> the callback registered with `setRebindSession` -> `rebindSession()` -> `bindExtensions()` emits `session_start`. The RPC handler then calls `rebindSession()` again, which emits it a second time. Interactive and print mode only rebind through the callback.

Effect: an extension that starts a timer in `session_start` and clears it in `session_shutdown` leaks one timer per replacement; `pi.appendEntry()` in `session_start` writes the entry twice.

A second gap: RPC mode subscribed to session events only after `bindExtensions()`, so events emitted by `session_start` handlers (for example `entry_appended`) never reached the client, at startup or on replacement. Removing the duplicate calls alone would drop those events entirely on replacement.

## Fix

`packages/coding-agent/src/modes/rpc/rpc-mode.ts`:
- Remove the four handler-side `rebindSession()` calls; the runtime callback is the only rebind.
- Subscribe to session events before `bindExtensions()`, as interactive mode does on replacement (`renderBeforeBind`).

Behavior change: RPC clients now also receive events emitted by the startup `session_start`.

## Tests

`test/suite/regressions/10470-rpc-session-replacement-start-once.test.ts` runs RPC mode on a real `AgentSessionRuntime`, one test each for startup event delivery, `new_session`, `switch_session`, `fork` and `clone`. Each replacement test asserts exactly one `session_start` and one streamed `entry_appended` for the entry its handler appends. All five fail on main and pass with the fix. The test builds the runtime by hand like `agent-session-runtime.test.ts` and `2860-replaced-session-context.test.ts`, because `suite/harness.ts` has no runtime and cannot replace sessions.

`npm run check` passes; existing RPC tests pass.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): report diagnostics that appear on session replacement
prs.body:
Related to #11264. Complements #11973.

## Problem

`main.ts`'s runtime factory runs at startup and again on every session replacement: `/new`, `/resume`, `/fork`, import, RPC `new_session`/`switch_session`/`fork`, and extension `ctx.newSession()`/`switchSession()`/`fork()`. It returns diagnostics: settings errors, project-trust warnings, extension load errors and warnings, session option warnings, and (since #11973) model scope warnings. `AgentSessionRuntime` stores them in `runtime.diagnostics`, but only `main.ts` reads that list, once at startup. After a replacement, the new diagnostics are discarded.

Trace (RPC, before this change):

1. Start `pi --mode rpc` with `enabledModels: ["fake/fake-model"]`. No warning.
2. Change settings to `["fake/fake-model", "github-copilot/missing-model"]`.
3. Send `new_session`. It succeeds, with nothing on stderr and no event.

The same happens with `/new` in the TUI, and when `/resume` moves to another project whose extensions fail to load or whose settings are invalid.

## Fix

- `AgentSessionRuntime.takeUnreportedDiagnostics()` returns the current runtime's diagnostics that were not reported yet and marks them reported. `main.ts` takes the startup diagnostics with it too, so whoever reports a diagnostic takes it, and an SDK host calling it at startup gets the startup diagnostics.
- Each mode calls it in its rebind callback, which runs after every replacement:
  - interactive: in the chat, like startup diagnostics (shared `showRuntimeDiagnostics()`)
  - print/JSON and RPC: stderr, in the CLI's existing format. `main.ts`'s `reportDiagnostics()` moved to `modes/diagnostics-stderr.ts` so the modes can share it. RPC never writes these to stdout.

De-duplication: a diagnostic with the same type and message as one already reported (at startup or after an earlier replacement) is not repeated. An unchanged settings warning is not shown again on every `/new`. A problem that is fixed and then reappears with the same text is not shown again either; that seemed preferable to repeating every warning.

The new method is an addition to the exported `AgentSessionRuntime` class. Nothing existing changes shape.

## Verification

| Mode | Check | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RPC | `test/rpc-replacement-diagnostics.test.ts`: valid settings, `new_session`, add a bad pattern, `new_session` twice | Warning on stderr exactly once, never on stdout. Fails on main (zero warnings). |
| Runtime | `test/agent-session-runtime-diagnostics.test.ts`: startup diagnostics not returned, a new one returned once after `newSession()`, unchanged ones not repeated | Passes. Fails on main. |
| Interactive, regular | tmux: start with valid settings, add a bad pattern, `/new`, `/new` | First `/new` shows `Warning: No models match pattern "github-copilot/nope"` in the chat above "New session started". The second does not repeat it. Screen clean. |
| Interactive, fullscreen | Same | Same |
| Print/JSON | Same callback and code path as RPC | Covered by code review only. No print-mode replacement test exists, since it needs an extension that replaces the session. |

Existing tests for print mode, RPC semantics, runtime events, #2860 and #11973 pass. `npm run check` passes.

Not covered: `/reload` does not create a new runtime, so it is unaffected. Interactive mode also shows `modelFallbackMessage` only at startup; that is left as is.

prs.title: fix(ai,coding-agent): make system the default instruction role in openai-completions
prs.body:
TLDR:
On chat-completions api, change the default instruction role from developer to system.

Inspired by: #12101 by @qoli

---
The trigger was #10741: Groq's qwen/qwen3.8-27b failed on the first message:
`400: minijinja: rendering failed: raise_exception: Unexpected message role.`

Problem: openai-completions sent the system messages of every reasoning model with the `developer` role unless the catalog turned it off. `developer` is OpenAI's role; many other hosts' chat templates reject it, as Groq's Qwen template does.

Every new OpenAI-compatible provider or reasoning model hit the same bug until someone added `supportsDeveloperRole: false` to the catalog; about 20 provider files carried that line. Nothing in models.dev says which role a model accepts, so the catalog could not get this right on its own.

Solution: detectCompat() now defaults supportsDeveloperRole to true only for api.openai.com. Every other host gets `system`. This applies to the initial system prompt and to mid-conversation system messages.

Built-in models whose role changes from developer to system:
- groq: 5 (gpt-oss and Qwen)
- xiaomi, xiaomi-token-plan-*: 9 MiMo models
- openrouter: 89 openai/* and anthropic/* models; 12 of them (newer GPT models) also support mid-conversation system messages (supportsMidConvoSystemMessages), which change role too All other built-in Chat Completions models already sent `system`.

Why the default is only api.openai.com:
- api.openai.com keeps `developer` because OpenAI documents it as the role for its reasoning models. In practice this rarely matters: the built-in OpenAI models all use the Responses API, so it only affects custom models that call OpenAI through openai-completions.
- Azure is excluded. Its built-in OpenAI models also use the Responses API; its only built-in Chat Completions model is DeepSeek, which needs `system`.
- OpenRouter is excluded: its Chat Completions reference accepts `system` ("System message for setting behavior") and `developer` with the same fields, and gives no reason to prefer `developer` for any model (https://openrouter.ai/docs/api/api-reference/chat/create-a-chat-completion). The openai/* and anthropic/* exception came in with #5309 without a reported need.
- compat.supportsDeveloperRole still overrides the default.
- The Responses API has its own setting and is unchanged.

The now-redundant `supportsDeveloperRole: false` lines are removed from the catalog and the llama extension.

How we checked it is safe: live requests to the affected hosts, each model given the same instruction once as `developer` and once as `system`:
- Groq qwen/qwen3.8-27b: developer 400, system OK. Groq gpt-oss-20b: both OK.
- Xiaomi mimo-v2.6-pro and mimo-v2.6-flash: both roles OK.
- OpenRouter openai/gpt-5-mini, openai/gpt-oss-20b, anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5, moonshotai/kimi-k2.6, qwen/qwen3.6-plus, deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro: both roles OK.
- OpenRouter openai/gpt-5.4-mini and openai/gpt-5.5 with an instruction added mid-conversation: both roles OK.

Released clients: they fetch new catalogs from pi.dev and still default supportsDeveloperRole to true, so the removed `false` lines would make them send `developer` to hosts that reject it. MINIMUM_PI_VERSION is raised to 1.5.3 so they keep the last catalog published for them.

closes #10741 #12101
