prs.title: feat(web-shell): quote selected message text into the composer or a new side task
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a "Quote to composer" action to the text-selection popover in the Web Shell transcript: selecting a fragment of an assistant reply or a user message now offers, alongside the existing "Copy plain text" and "Copy Markdown" actions, a way to quote the fragment into the active composer. Clicking it inserts the fragment as an inline chip at the end of the composer; when the prompt is sent, the chip serializes to a Markdown blockquote line (`> quoted text`) inside the prompt and is carried through the existing reference-annotation machinery (`inputAnnotations` with `reference.kind === 'quote'`), so the quote survives send and session reload.

The quoted fragment is normalized before insertion: all whitespace runs (including newlines) are collapsed to single spaces — the chip is a single inline editor range — bidirectional embedding/isolation control characters are stripped, and the length is capped at 4000 characters. Each chip is identified by a deterministic hash of its text, so the same quoted fragment always produces the same tag id.

This PR also adds an "Ask in side task" action to the same selection popover (shown only while side tasks are available for the current session). Clicking it creates a new side task for the session and places the selected fragment in that side task's composer as a quote chip, reusing the same inline-chip mechanism — so when the user submits their prompt, the chip serializes to a `> quoted text` line exactly like quote-to-composer. Nothing is sent automatically: the user writes the question on top of the chip and submits it themselves. The chip is inserted exactly once, when the child session has connected and its transcript has settled empty, in whichever order composer-ready and session-empty are observed; a per-session delivery registry makes the handoff race-free and prevents a duplicate chip across pane remounts and effect re-runs.

The actions are available wherever a composer exists (the main chat and split-view panes). Read-only and embedded transcript views do not provide the actions, so the buttons are hidden there. UI strings are localized in English and Chinese.

## Why it's needed

Follow-up prompts often need to reference a specific part of an earlier reply. Today the only options are copying the selection to the clipboard ("Copy plain text" / "Copy Markdown") and pasting it manually, which loses the signal that the fragment is a quote of earlier context. Requested in #12682.

"Ask in side task" follows up on the same need: side tasks exist to ask questions about the current conversation without cluttering the main thread, and asking about a specific fragment should not require copying it and pasting it into the side task composer, which loses the quote semantics and chip formatting. Requested in #16964.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Start the dev server (`cd packages/web-shell && npm run dev`) and open a chat session with at least one assistant reply.
2. Drag-select a fragment of the reply text — the selection popover appears. Before this PR it offers only "Copy plain text" and "Copy Markdown"; after, it additionally offers "Quote to composer" (and "Ask in side task" while side tasks are available).
3. Click "Quote to composer" — an inline chip with the selected fragment appears at the end of the composer and the menu closes.
4. Press Enter to send. The user bubble renders the chip, and the POST to `/session/:id/prompt` carries the fragment as a `> quoted text` line in a `type: 'text'` prompt block plus an `inputAnnotations` entry with `reference.kind === 'quote'`, `reference.value` = the normalized fragment, `reference.serialized` = `> fragment`.
5. The same flow works when selecting a fragment of a user message; the buttons are absent in read-only/embedded transcript views.
6. In a session where side tasks are available, drag-select a fragment and click "Ask in side task" — a new side task tab opens and its composer shows the fragment as a quote chip; nothing is sent (no prompt POST for the side task).
7. Type a question in the side task composer and send it — the prompt carries the `> quoted text` line and the `reference.kind === 'quote'` annotation, the same serialization as quote-to-composer.
8. While side tasks are unavailable for the session, the popover does not offer "Ask in side task".

Automated coverage: `packages/web-shell/client/utils/quoteReference.test.ts` (normalization: whitespace collapsing, bidi stripping, 4000-character cap, tag shape), `packages/web-shell/client/utils/askInSideTaskDelivery.test.ts` (delivery registry: register-before-request and request-before-register orderings, single delivery across pane remounts and quote re-requests, empty session ids ignored, sessions independent), four new cases in `SelectionCopyMenu.test.tsx` (ask button hidden without an ask action, shown with one, click passes the selected text and closes the menu, disabled for image-only selections), two new cases in `App.test.tsx` (the ask action provisions a side task tab carrying the raw selection as `initialQuote` and sends nothing; no ask action is exposed while side tasks are unavailable), plus the Playwright before/after scenario from the evidence below.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Playwright run against `npm run dev` with the mock-daemon e2e harness (Chromium, 1280x720), selecting the word **bold** from an assistant reply:

Before — the selection popover offers only the copy actions:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/4ekuct25/qwen-code/evidence/pr-12682/assets/web-shell-quote-2026-10-14/1-before-popover.png

After — the popover additionally offers "Quote to composer":

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/4ekuct25/qwen-code/evidence/pr-12682/assets/web-shell-quote-2026-10-14/2-after-popover.png

After clicking — the fragment is an inline chip in the composer:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/4ekuct25/qwen-code/evidence/pr-12682/assets/web-shell-quote-2026-10-14/3-after-composer-chip.png

After sending — the chip survives in the user bubble:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/4ekuct25/qwen-code/evidence/pr-12682/assets/web-shell-quote-2026-10-14/4-after-user-bubble-chip.png

The "Ask in side task" flow is covered by the automated suite above (registry unit tests, menu cases, and app-level side-task provisioning cases); visual evidence for it will be added to this thread once the dev-server/desktop run is complete.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

macOS: not verified live in this pass (dev runs and tests are in Docker/Chromium). Windows: pending — the Windows VM is not available in this pass (by decision).

### Environment (optional)

Docker `node:22-bookworm`: full web-shell vitest suite (all `client/` test files — all passing), `tsc --noEmit`, `prettier --check` on the changed files; Playwright (Chromium) against the `npm run dev` server with the mock-daemon harness (quote-to-composer part).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: quoted fragments are appended to the prompt as visible text, which increases context size for long selections; the 4000-character cap bounds the token cost of a single quote (the ask-in-side-task chip goes through the same normalization, so it is bounded the same way).
- "Ask in side task" provisions a child session per click — the same cost as any side task; the quote itself is only seeded into the composer and never sent on its own.
- Not validated / out of scope: live runs on macOS and Windows; provenance (source message id) on the quote reference is intentionally not carried in this version.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #12682
Fixes #16964

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

在 Web Shell 对话记录的文字选择浮层中新增"引用到输入框"操作：选中助手回复或用户消息中的文字片段后，浮层除现有的"复制纯文本"和"复制 Markdown"之外，现在还提供将该片段引用到当前输入框的方式。点击后，片段会以内联芯片（chip）形式插入输入框末尾；发送提示词时，芯片会序列化为 Markdown 引用行（`> 引用文本`）进入提示词，并随现有的引用注解机制（`inputAnnotations` 中 `reference.kind === 'quote'`）一并提交，因此引用在发送后会话重载后依然保留。

引用片段在插入前会做归一化：所有空白（含换行）折叠为单个空格——芯片是编辑器中单一的内联范围——去除双向嵌入/隔离控制字符，长度上限 4000 个字符。每个芯片由文本的确定性哈希标识，因此引用同一片段总是产生相同的标签 id。

本 PR 还在同一选择浮层中新增"问这个侧边任务"操作（仅在当前会话支持侧边任务时显示）。点击后会为当前会话创建一个新侧边任务，并把所选片段以引用芯片形式放入该侧边任务的输入框——复用与"引用到输入框"相同的内联芯片机制，因此用户提交提示词时，芯片会像引用到输入框一样序列化为 `> 引用文本` 行。不会自动发送：用户在芯片之上输入问题并自行提交。芯片只在子会话已连接且其转录稳定为空时插入一次，无论"编辑器就绪"还是"会话为空"哪个先被观察到；按会话划分的交付登记使该传递无竞态，并在面板重新挂载与 effect 重跑时防止重复芯片。

该操作在任何存在输入框的地方都可用（主聊天和分屏视图）。只读和内嵌的对话记录视图不提供这些操作，因此按钮在那里会被隐藏。界面文案提供英文和中文两种本地化。

## 为什么需要

后续提问常常需要引用之前某条回复的特定部分。目前仅有的方式是把所选内容复制到剪贴板（"复制纯文本"/"复制 Markdown"）再手动粘贴，这会丢失"这段文字是对前文的引用"的语义。本 PR 响应的是 #12682 的需求。

"问这个侧边任务"操作是同一需求的后续：侧边任务用于在不打扰主线程的情况下询问当前会话，而针对特定片段的询问不应依赖复制再粘贴到侧边任务输入框——那会丢失引用的语义和芯片格式。本操作响应的是 #16964。

## 审查者测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 启动开发服务器（`cd packages/web-shell && npm run dev`），打开任意包含至少一条助手回复的会话。
2. 用鼠标拖选回复中的一段文字——出现选择浮层。改动前浮层只有"复制纯文本"和"复制 Markdown"；改动后额外提供"引用到输入框"（以及在支持侧边任务时提供"问这个侧边任务"）。
3. 点击"引用到输入框"——输入框末尾出现一个包含所选片段的内联芯片，菜单关闭。
4. 按 Enter 发送。用户消息气泡中渲染出该芯片；发送到 `/session/:id/prompt` 的 POST 请求中，片段以 `> 引用文本` 行形式出现在 `type: 'text'` 提示词块中，并带有 `inputAnnotations` 条目，其中 `reference.kind === 'quote'`、`reference.value` 为归一化后的片段、`reference.serialized` 为 `> 片段`。
5. 选中用户消息中的片段时同样的流程有效；在只读/内嵌对话记录视图中按钮不存在。
6. 在支持侧边任务的会话中拖选一段文字并点击"问这个侧边任务"——打开一个新的侧边任务标签页，其输入框中显示该片段的引用芯片；不会发送任何内容（该侧边任务没有提示词 POST）。
7. 在侧边任务输入框中输入问题并发送——提示词携带 `> 引用文本` 行和 `reference.kind === 'quote'` 注解，序列化方式与"引用到输入框"相同。
8. 当会话不支持侧边任务时，浮层不提供"问这个侧边任务"。

自动化覆盖：`packages/web-shell/client/utils/quoteReference.test.ts`（归一化：空白折叠、双向控制字符去除、4000 字符上限、标签结构）、`packages/web-shell/client/utils/askInSideTaskDelivery.test.ts`（交付登记：先注册后请求与先请求后注册两种顺序、面板重挂载与重复请求时只交付一次、空会话 id 被忽略、会话之间相互独立）、`SelectionCopyMenu.test.tsx` 新增 4 个用例（无 ask 操作时按钮隐藏、有 ask 操作时显示、点击时传递所选文本并关闭菜单、纯图片选区时按钮禁用）、`App.test.tsx` 新增 2 个用例（ask 操作创建携带原始选区 `initialQuote` 的侧边任务标签且不发送任何内容；不支持侧边任务时不暴露 ask 操作），另加下面证据部分的 Playwright 改动前/改动后场景。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/4ekuct25/qwen-code/evidence/pr-12682/assets/web-shell-quote-2026-10-14/1-before-popover.png

改动后——浮层额外提供"引用到输入框"：

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/4ekuct25/qwen-code/evidence/pr-12682/assets/web-shell-quote-2026-10-14/2-after-popover.png

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/4ekuct25/qwen-code/evidence/pr-12682/assets/web-shell-quote-2026-10-14/3-after-composer-chip.png

发送后——芯片在用户消息气泡中保留：

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/4ekuct25/qwen-code/evidence/pr-12682/assets/web-shell-quote-2026-10-14/4-after-user-bubble-chip.png

"问这个侧边任务"流程由上述自动化套件覆盖（登记单元测试、菜单用例、应用级侧边任务创建用例）；其可视化证据将在开发服务器/桌面端运行完成后补充到本线程。

### 环境（可选）

Docker `node:22-bookworm`：web-shell 完整 vitest 套件（全部 `client/` 测试文件——全部通过）、`tsc --noEmit`、对改动文件执行 `prettier --check`；Playwright（Chromium）对 `npm run dev` 服务器配合 mock 守护进程框架进行验证（"引用到输入框"部分）。

prs.title: feat(core): track model availability for the fallback chain (Qoder port)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Ports the Qoder preview line's model-availability ledger into main as the first capability under the Option B integration decision (main's architecture wins; differentiated Qoder capabilities are ported as normal-sized PRs). It adds a session-scoped, per-model health state machine and, behind a new opt-in setting, teaches the model fallback chain to remember which models were just exhausted on capacity errors so it skips them for the rest of the turn and re-probes them once on the next turn. The turn boundary runs once per request at the send entry, and only session-turn sends participate (an `isSessionTurn` allowlist decided by the sender, not inferred from going through `Turn`): `LlmClient` sets the flag per message type for the live turn's own sends, and the ACP session send and the hosted-harness prepared resume set it explicitly, while `Notification`/`Teammate` sends, concurrent side queries, `turnModelRound`'s background rounds (subagent shared loop, unified-loop speculation), and direct background sends (forked queries, suggestions) leave it unset, so they neither disturb the live turn nor skip a recovered fallback. Because a background interaction's ToolResult/Hook/Steer continuations are resubmitted without the flag, a prompt-id registry (`backgroundInteractionPromptIds`) keeps the whole side-query/Notification/Teammate chain excluded, and the ACP sender normalizes mid-turn continuation suffixes into a stable `ledgerTurnKey` so a continuation does not reset the turn's consumed marks. With the setting off, the fallback chain is byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Why it's needed

Today the fallback chain is stateless per request: when the primary model exhausts its retry budget on a capacity error (429/503/529), every subsequent request in the same turn re-tries the same exhausted model from scratch before falling back again, wasting latency and quota. The ledger gives the chain cross-request memory within a turn. This is the first, smallest, self-contained capability chosen to establish the Option B porting workflow (design → baseline → implement → verify) before larger ports.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Unit: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/core/model-availability-service.test.ts` (10 tests: terminal not downgraded, sticky consumed once per turn, resetTurn/beginTurn re-probe). Preview's `selectFirstAvailable`/`reset` helpers are not ported — nothing in the fallback-skipping wiring calls them, so they would be dead surface.
- Retry + membership threading: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/core/turn.test.ts -t 'forwards isExplicitRetry and isSessionTurn'` (Turn forwards both flags to the chat send options from its 10th/11th positional slots), `npx vitest run src/core/client.test.ts -t 'explicit-Retry turn-boundary flag'` (a real `SendMessageType.Retry` sets the retry flag; a UserQuery does not), and `npx vitest run src/core/client.test.ts -t 'marks ledger membership'` (membership true for UserQuery/Retry/ToolResult, false for Notification/Teammate).
- Wiring: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/core/llm-chat.test.ts -t 'sendMessageStream with retries'` (gate off unchanged) — includes `-t 'skips a fallback exhausted earlier'` (gate on: same-turn skip + new-turn re-probe), `-t 'an explicit Retry re-probes'`, and the regression cases: `-t 'subagent send does not wipe'` / `-t 'two consecutive forked'` / `-t 'shared-loop background round'` (background sends — direct and via `turnModelRound` — neither wipe the live turn nor fail on a skipped fallback), `-t 'Retry served by the primary'` (turn boundary hoisted to the request entry), `-t 'failed after emitting output'` (a post-output capacity failure is still recorded), `-t 'non-eligible error'` (a post-output failure on a non-eligible error is NOT recorded), `-t 'resolved model id'` (the skip keys on the resolved id), and `-t 'gate off keeps'` (the gate is falsifiable with a real service injected).
- ACP session turns: `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/acp-integration/session/Session.test.ts` (1537 tests) — the ACP send sets `isSessionTurn`, and the send-options assertions pin it.
- Gate / Config defaults: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/config/config.test.ts -t 'modelAvailabilityTracking'` (false default, constructor param, stable lazy service instance, per-Config isolation, and derived Configs deliberately share the session ledger through the prototype chain).
- CLI wiring: `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/config/config.test.ts -t 'model availability tracking'` (opt-in/opt-out propagation + unset-by-default, mirroring the `unifiedAgentLoop` shape).
- Mutation witnesses (each restored byte-for-byte): deleting the fallback skip-check reds the gate-on test (`expected … 1 times, but got 2 times`); deleting the Retry `resetTurn` reds the Retry test (`expected … 2 times, but got 1 times`); deleting the CLI propagation line reds both CLI wiring tests; deleting the `isExplicitRetry` spread in `Turn.run` reds the forwarding test; forcing the client's 10th Turn argument to `false` reds the Retry call-site test; hardcoding `isSessionTurn: true` in `Turn.run` reds the shared-loop background-round test (`expected … 1 times, but got 2 times`); forcing the client's membership predicate always-true reds the per-messageType membership test (Notification `true` instead of `false`); removing the hoisted `resetTurn` reds the Retry-served-by-primary test; exempting post-output failures from marking reds the output-then-fail test; removing `&& canTryNextFallback` from the ledger write reds the non-eligible post-output test (the request is then served by a later fallback); switching the skip to the configured id reds the resolved-id test; dropping the gate reds the gate-off test; Config `?? false` → `?? true` reds the default test, a fresh-instance getter reds the stability test, a process-global holder reds the per-Config isolation test, and own-property getter semantics red the derived-Config sharing test; deleting the settings.md row reds the presence test.
- Full affected suites: `llm-chat.test.ts`, `turn.test.ts`, `client.test.ts`, `agent-loop.test.ts`, `goal-turn-integration.test.ts`, core `config.test.ts`, cli `config.test.ts`; core + cli `tsc --noEmit` clean; settings schema regenerated.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (non-UI; behavior gated behind an opt-in setting).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ tested |

### Environment (optional)

Local unit tests + `npm run build && npm run bundle`. A live headless E2E was attempted with a mock server returning capacity errors for the primary model; reaching the fallback chain requires exhausting the primary's internal retry budget, which the unit tests simulate directly via `maxRetries: 0`. The live run's persistent retry prevented reaching the fallback within the timeout, so the fallback-triggering evidence is the unit + mutation coverage above.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the ledger only affects fallback selection in this port; the primary model is still attempted first. Terminal/quota marking and the prompt-vs-silent policy map are deferred. Internal background sends are excluded from the ledger; the turn key is a single scalar, so the residual case of two genuine user turns sharing one Config concurrently fails open (re-probe = pre-PR behaviour); the design doc records this limitation.
- Not validated / out of scope: cross-session/account-wide health sharing; flipping the setting default; terminal/quota marking; live headless fallback-triggering E2E (see Environment).
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; new opt-in setting `experimental.modelAvailabilityTracking` defaults to false.

- 主要风险/权衡：本次移植台账只影响 fallback 选择；primary 仍最先被尝试。terminal/quota 标记与 prompt-vs-silent 策略映射延后。内部后台发送被排除在台账之外；轮键是单个标量，故残余情形——共享同一 Config 的两个真实用户轮并发——会失败即放开（重探＝改动前行为）；设计文档记录了该局限。

prs.title: feat(channels): add generic outbound webhook delivery
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a named, send-only Generic Webhook Channel for existing Notify, explicit prompt delivery and persistent scheduled-task results. Each delivery sends one POST containing `{ "version": 1, "text": "..." }` to the configured endpoint, with optional Bearer authentication; any 2xx response, including an empty 204, acknowledges acceptance.

The endpoint and token use existing secret/environment-reference handling. Public HTTPS is the default; a per-Channel option permits intentional local/private HTTP(S) receivers while reserved and metadata addresses remain blocked. Every DNS answer is checked, and both direct connections and proxy CONNECT tunnels use a checked address. Existing proxy/NO_PROXY behavior and strict TLS verification are retained. The shared public-network resolver is extracted into a small private workspace; existing core callers keep their public/undefined policy and return contract.

This is the backend half. The dependent Web PR adds the shared Web Shell entry and configuration controls: [#17405](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17405).

## Why it's needed

Developers currently need a custom adapter or lifecycle script to receive results in a service they control. A Generic destination lets them use the same named Channel and task-delivery controls as DingTalk, Feishu and WeCom. OpenClaw's outbound automation delivery provides a product precedent; this proposal intentionally uses the text-only contract that the current Channel framework can supply.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Run the minimal local receiver from the user guide, configure a Generic Channel for its URL with private-network access explicitly enabled, and start the Channel. Starting should produce no network request.
2. Send an explicit Notify to its `chat/default` target. Confirm one POST, the versioned JSON and optional Bearer header, and successful delivery when the receiver returns an empty 204. Try an incorrect target, a redirect, 401, 429 and 503; confirm rejection or the documented error classification without replay or automatic retry.
3. Create a persistent scheduled task using the same target. Confirm a successful scheduled final reply reaches the receiver; an ordinary manual run does not add a delivery. Confirm task configuration contains only the logical target.
4. Save/edit URL and token environment references, replace the token, and clear the optional token. Confirm secret reads remain redacted and references remain references on disk. Stop/restart while a request is pending and confirm cancellation and later recovery.
5. With private access off, confirm loopback is blocked. With it on, confirm local HTTP works, public HTTP and metadata addresses stay blocked, and TLS still rejects invalid certificates even if the process environment disables default verification.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: latest-main source has no Generic plugin; the available pre-change daemon build omits it from the catalog and rejects its configuration without persisting settings or making receiver/model calls. The global CLI was unavailable, so runtime baseline evidence uses the preserved prior WeCom Web build, not a claimed latest-main binary.

After: local real-receiver and real-daemon/worker checks verify the protocol, credentials, lifecycle, errors and scheduled/manual behavior. Focused checks: 81 adapter tests (25 real-network cases), 70 shared-policy tests, 18 core compatibility tests, 367 CLI tests, and 193 build/lock metadata tests passed (one existing skip). Full build, typecheck and bundle results are recorded in the accompanying E2E report. No product UI is added here.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :-- | :-- |
| 🍏 macOS | ⚠️ Not tested locally |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Not tested locally |
| 🐧 Linux | ✅ Tested |

### Environment (optional)

Node 24.22.1, pnpm 11.24.0, local HTTP/HTTPS receivers and authenticated HTTP/HTTPS proxies. Actual daemon, Channel worker and cron; deterministic local model fixture, with no external receiver credentials or production model calls.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: configurable destinations require checked DNS, pinned direct/proxy connections and strict TLS. The private-network exception is explicit per Channel. Proxy-only hostname resolution is unsupported because the worker must validate the endpoint locally.
- Not validated / out of scope: real third-party receivers, arbitrary payloads/headers, HMAC, attachments, inbound webhooks, automatic retries, event metadata and scheduling changes. Delivery remains best effort; a lost acknowledgment can leave remote acceptance unknown.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none intended. Existing platform adapters and core network-policy behavior are covered by regression tests. The 640 KiB adapter body bound accommodates the shared 100,000-unit text bound; existing shared normalization can still shorten longer input.

Design: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/generic-webhook-channel/docs/design/2026-11-16-generic-webhook-delivery.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/generic-webhook-channel/docs/design/2026-11-16-generic-webhook-delivery.zh-CN.md). Both versions are complete and synchronized.

## Linked Issues

Related to #17374. The dependent Web integration completes the UI portion.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的变更

新增命名的、仅出站的通用 Webhook 频道，复用现有 Notify、显式 prompt 投递和持久定时任务结果投递。每次投递向配置的接收端发送一次 POST，正文为 `{ "version": 1, "text": "..." }`，可选 Bearer 鉴权；任何 2xx 响应（包括空 204）均表示接收端接受。

地址和令牌沿用已有秘密字段及环境变量引用机制。默认允许公网 HTTPS；每个频道可明确选择允许本机或私网 HTTP(S)，保留地址和元数据地址仍被拒绝。检查全部 DNS 结果，并将直连和代理 CONNECT 隧道固定到已检查地址。保留现有 proxy/NO_PROXY 行为并严格验证 TLS。已有公网解析器提取到小型私有工作区，core 调用方保留原 public/undefined 策略和返回契约。

这是后端部分。依赖它的 Web PR 增加共享 Web Shell 的入口和配置控件：[#17405](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17405)。

## 为什么需要

开发者目前需要自定义适配器或生命周期脚本，才能让自己的服务接收结果。通用目标可以像钉钉、飞书和企业微信一样使用命名频道和任务投递控制。OpenClaw 的出站自动化投递提供了产品先例；本方案采用当前 Channel 框架实际能提供的纯文本契约。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 运行用户指南中的最小本地接收端，配置通用频道并明确允许私网访问，然后启动频道。启动不应产生网络请求。
2. 向其 `chat/default` 目标发送显式 Notify，确认只收到一次 POST、版本化 JSON 和可选 Bearer 头，空 204 可成功确认投递。测试错误目标、重定向、401、429 和 503，确认拒绝或文档规定的错误分类，没有重放或自动重试。
3. 创建使用同一目标的持久定时任务，确认成功的定时最终回复到达接收端，普通手动运行不会新增投递。任务配置只保存逻辑目标。
4. 保存和编辑地址、令牌的环境引用，替换令牌并清除可选令牌。确认读取仍脱敏，磁盘仍保存引用。请求挂起时停止并重启，确认取消和后续恢复。
5. 关闭私网选项时确认拒绝 loopback；开启后确认本地 HTTP 可用，公网 HTTP 和元数据地址仍被拒绝。即使进程环境关闭默认 TLS 验证，也仍拒绝无效证书。

### 证据（改动前后）

改动前：最新 main 源码没有通用插件；可用的改动前 daemon 构建不在目录中列出该类型，拒绝配置，且不持久化、不调用接收端或模型。环境没有全局 CLI，因此运行时基线使用保留的企业微信 Web 构建，没有声称它是最新 main 二进制。

改动后：真实本地接收端和 daemon/worker 验证协议、凭据、生命周期、错误与定时/手动行为。定向检查通过：适配器 81 项（含 25 项真实网络）、共享策略 70 项、core 兼容性 18 项、CLI 367 项、构建/锁文件元数据 193 项（1 项已有跳过）。全量构建、类型检查和 bundle 结果见单独 E2E 报告。本 PR 不增加产品 UI。

### 测试平台

| 系统 | 状态 |
| :-- | :-- |
| 🍏 macOS | ⚠️ 未在本地测试 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未在本地测试 |
| 🐧 Linux | ✅ 已测试 |

### 环境

Node 24.22.1、pnpm 11.24.0、本地 HTTP/HTTPS 接收端与需要鉴权的 HTTP/HTTPS 代理。使用真实 daemon、频道 worker 和 cron，以及确定性本地模型 fixture，没有外部接收端凭据或生产模型调用。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：自定义目标需要 DNS 检查、直连/代理连接固定和严格 TLS。私网例外按频道明确配置。仅能由远程代理解析的域名不受支持，因为 worker 必须本地校验目标。
- 未验证或范围外：真实第三方接收端、任意载荷/请求头、HMAC、附件、入站 webhook、自动重试、事件元数据及调度修改。投递仍为 best effort，确认丢失时远端是否接受可能未知。
- 破坏性变更或迁移：预期无。已有平台适配器和 core 网络策略行为有回归测试。适配器 640 KiB 正文上限覆盖共享的 100,000-unit 文本范围；更长输入仍可能被已有共享标准化逻辑缩短。

设计文档：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/generic-webhook-channel/docs/design/2026-11-16-generic-webhook-delivery.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/generic-webhook-channel/docs/design/2026-11-16-generic-webhook-delivery.zh-CN.md)，两版完整同步。

## 关联 Issue

关联 #17374。依赖本 PR 的 Web 集成完成 UI 部分。

</details>

prs.title: feat(serve): let create_sub_session follow up a sub-session the caller created
prs.body:
## What this PR does

A session can now give one of its sub-sessions a follow-up instead of starting a new one. `create_sub_session` takes an optional `sessionId`: the id of a sub-session this session created earlier, with `workspace` when it lives in another workspace. The prompt is queued on that session after any turn it is running, and the session keeps its earlier context and its name. If the daemon already closed the session, it is restored from its transcript first. Both completion modes work as for a new sub-session: `first-turn` waits for the turn this prompt starts and returns only that turn's text, and `sent` returns once the prompt is queued and later reports the result as a task notification.

Only a session whose recorded parent is the caller can be followed up. Side tasks and scheduled-task runs also record the session they came from as their parent, but they carry a source marker and are refused, as are other sessions, the caller itself, and archived or standalone sessions. The lineage is checked before the session is touched, from the live entry or from the transcript of a closed session, so it survives a daemon restart. Sessions the caller did not create stay reachable only through `send_message`, which carries no user authority.

A follow-up that names a workspace goes through everything that workspace already requires for a new sub-session: the one-time human approval (which now also names the target session), the trust and runtime-generation checks, and the approval-mode rule, applied to the session as it is now. A follow-up in the caller's own workspace keeps the tool's usual permission flow, and the session keeps its own mode, as a new sub-session there does. `model` and `name` cannot be combined with `sessionId`.

Each `sent` follow-up reports under its own task id (`<sessionId>:<promptId>`), because the receiving session ignores a task id it has already seen, and the caller records that id so the Todo Stop Guard links the completion to its work. A `sent` follow-up to a busy session returns once queued instead of waiting for its turn to start; checks that refuse the prompt when its turn comes are reported as a failed completion. Resuming attaches a client to the session, which the launcher releases once it is done with the turn, and a failed follow-up never closes or deletes the session. The tool description also tells the model that results come back on their own, so it should not ask the sub-session to report back.

## Why it's needed

#17454 lets a session start a sub-session in another registered workspace, but every call starts a fresh session with no memory of the last one. Continuing a task in workspace B meant re-briefing a new session from scratch, or switching to B by hand. This is the second step of the design in `docs/design/2026-11-16-cross-workspace-sub-sessions.md`; the third, a Web Shell action that does the same from a session page, follows separately.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Start `qwen serve` with two trusted workspaces, A as primary and B as secondary. In a Web Shell session in A, ask the model to start a sub-session in B (`create_sub_session` with `workspace` = B, `first-turn`) that remembers a word. Approve it.
2. Ask the model to follow up that sub-session (`sessionId` = its id, `workspace` = B, `first-turn`) and ask for the word. Expected: one approval prompt naming the session; the answer is the word; the sub-session's transcript has both turns.
3. Restart the daemon and follow up again with `completion: "sent"`. Expected: the tool returns at once; the session is restored; a task notification with the answer arrives in A.
4. While the sub-session runs a long turn, send another `sent` follow-up. Expected: it returns within a second; when both turns finish, two separate notifications arrive in A in order.
5. Follow up a session opened directly in B (not created by A's session). Expected: refused with "is not a sub-session this session created", and that session receives nothing.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: `create_sub_session` had no `sessionId`; every call created a new session.

After (real daemon, two workspaces, approvals clicked in Web Shell): a follow-up into B answered "PELICAN" from the session's earlier turn (2 user turns in the same session); after a restart a `sent` follow-up restored the session and reported back; a second `sent` follow-up sent while the session ran a long turn returned in 1 s, and both completions ("SLOW", then "FAST") reached A under distinct task ids, with the session's client count back to 1 afterwards. The full table is in a comment below.

Unit tests: launcher, tool, bridge client and ACP session suites pass locally.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Bundled build (`node dist/cli.js serve`), isolated `HOME`, a real model on an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a local follow-up keeps the sub-session's own approval mode rather than clamping it to the caller's, matching a new local sub-session; cross-workspace follow-ups use the existing cross-workspace rule.
- Not validated / out of scope: a `first-turn` follow-up waits at most five minutes, and one queued behind a long turn can time out while its prompt still runs later with no result reported (noted in the design's open questions). The Web Shell action (step 3). macOS and Windows not run locally.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. Calls without `sessionId` behave as before.

Design: [English](https://github.com/qqqys/qwen-code/blob/718749f97114809f1d7acf11f688a1858de134b3/docs/design/2026-11-16-cross-workspace-sub-sessions.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/qqqys/qwen-code/blob/718749f97114809f1d7acf11f688a1858de134b3/docs/design/2026-11-16-cross-workspace-sub-sessions.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Follows #17454. Refs #17419

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

会话现在可以给自己的某个子会话发后续 prompt，而不是每次都新建一个。`create_sub_session` 新增可选参数 `sessionId`：本会话之前创建的子会话的 id；如果该子会话在另一个 workspace 里，同时传 `workspace`。prompt 排在该会话正在运行的那一轮之后，会话保留之前的上下文和名字。如果 daemon 已经关闭了这个会话，会先从对话记录恢复。两种完成模式和新建子会话一样：`first-turn` 等待这条 prompt 开始的那一轮，只返回这一轮的文本；`sent` 排进队列就返回，之后以任务通知回报结果。

只有记录的父会话就是调用方的会话才能被追问。侧任务和定时任务的运行也会把它们来自的会话记为父会话，但它们带有来源标记，会被拒绝；其它会话、调用方自己、已归档或 standalone 的会话也会被拒绝。血缘在碰会话之前检查：活着的会话看活跃条目，已关闭的读它的对话记录，所以 daemon 重启后依然有效。不是调用方创建的会话仍然只能通过不带用户权限的 `send_message` 联系。

指定了 workspace 的后续 prompt 要满足该 workspace 对新建子会话的全部要求：单次人工批准（现在会同时写出目标会话）、信任与 runtime 代次检查，以及按会话当前状态应用的审批模式规则。在调用方自己 workspace 里的后续 prompt 沿用工具通常的权限流程，会话保留自己的模式，与在那里新建子会话一致。`model` 和 `name` 不能与 `sessionId` 同时使用。

每个 `sent` 后续 prompt 以自己的任务 id（`<sessionId>:<promptId>`）回报，因为接收方会忽略已经见过的任务 id；调用方会记录这个 id，让 Todo Stop Guard 把完成通知和发起它的工作关联起来。发给忙碌会话的 `sent` 后续 prompt 排进队列就返回，不等它开始执行；轮到它时若被检查拒绝，会以失败的完成通知回报。恢复会给会话附加一个 client，启动器处理完这一轮后会释放它；失败的后续 prompt 永远不会关闭或删除这个会话。工具描述也会告诉模型结果会自动回来，不要再让子会话回报。

## 为什么需要

#17454 让会话可以在另一个已注册的 workspace 里启动子会话，但每次调用都会新建一个不记得上次内容的会话。要在 workspace B 里继续一个任务，只能从头给新会话交代一遍，或者手动切到 B。这是设计文档 `docs/design/2026-11-16-cross-workspace-sub-sessions.md` 的第 2 步；第 3 步（在 Web Shell 会话页上做同样的事）另开 PR。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 用两个受信 workspace 启动 `qwen serve`，A 为主、B 为次。在 A 的 Web Shell 会话里让模型在 B 启动一个子会话（`create_sub_session`，`workspace` = B，`first-turn`），让它记住一个词。批准。
2. 让模型追问这个子会话（`sessionId` = 它的 id，`workspace` = B，`first-turn`），问那个词。预期：出现一次写明目标会话的批准提示；答出那个词；子会话的对话记录里有两轮。
3. 重启 daemon，再用 `completion: "sent"` 追问一次。预期：工具立即返回；会话被恢复；带答案的任务通知到达 A。
4. 在子会话执行一个长轮次时，再发一个 `sent` 追问。预期：一秒内返回；两轮都完成后，A 按顺序收到两条独立的通知。
5. 追问一个在 B 里直接打开的会话（不是 A 的会话创建的）。预期：被拒绝，提示 "is not a sub-session this session created"，那个会话什么都没收到。

### 证据（前后对比）

之前：`create_sub_session` 没有 `sessionId`，每次调用都新建会话。

之后（真实 daemon，两个 workspace，在 Web Shell 里点批准）：对 B 的后续 prompt 根据该会话之前的一轮答出 "PELICAN"（同一个会话里两轮用户输入）；重启后 `sent` 后续 prompt 恢复了会话并回报；在会话执行长轮次时发出的第二个 `sent` 后续 prompt 1 秒内返回，两条完成通知（先 "SLOW" 后 "FAST"）以不同的任务 id 到达 A，之后会话的 client 数回到 1。完整结果见下方评论。

单元测试：启动器、工具、bridge client 与 ACP 会话测试在本地通过。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅  |

### 环境（可选）

打包产物（`node dist/cli.js serve`），隔离的 `HOME`，OpenAI 兼容端点上的真实模型。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：本地后续 prompt 保留子会话自己的审批模式，不收紧到调用方的模式，与本地新建子会话一致；跨 workspace 的后续 prompt 使用已有的跨 workspace 规则。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：`first-turn` 后续 prompt 最多等待五分钟，排在长轮次后面的可能超时，而它的 prompt 之后仍会执行、结果无人回报（已记录在设计文档的待定问题中）。Web Shell 操作（第 3 步）。本地没有在 macOS 和 Windows 上运行。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。不带 `sessionId` 的调用行为不变。

设计文档：[English](https://github.com/qqqys/qwen-code/blob/718749f97114809f1d7acf11f688a1858de134b3/docs/design/2026-11-16-cross-workspace-sub-sessions.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/qqqys/qwen-code/blob/718749f97114809f1d7acf11f688a1858de134b3/docs/design/2026-11-16-cross-workspace-sub-sessions.zh-CN.md)

## 关联 Issue

接续 #17454。Refs #17419

</details>

prs.title: test(managed-agent): restore the round-3 /loop E2E fixes and wire the scenario into CI
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Two follow-ups to #17433, which merged at its round-2 head (`9a53383cb1`) before the round-3 fixes were pushed, so those fixes never landed on main:

1. **Restores the round-3 review fixes** to the `/loop` skill model-turn E2E and hardens them per this PR's own review: the Session-create body carries a caller `loop` import whose body is the verbatim bundled reference (so admission's replace path runs as in a real creation), with a marker description the arm asserts is gone from the first round — attesting the caller entry was replaced rather than merely served, and pinned so swapping the import to another sidecar reds both the pin and the runtime assertion; the scripted classifier answer matches the block schema (`'shouldBlock' in properties`) rather than the tool name, so other structured side queries are not mis-answered; the id-extraction pin names the arm's `createdScheduleId` binding; `cronToolResults` reports the three witnessed calls instead of a cumulative flattened count; and the `cron_list` echo guard is pinned. Both design-doc languages describe the caller-import shape and now record that the arm runs in CI (only observing a scheduled fire stays out of scope).
2. **Wires the scenario into CI**: the packaged-stack `hosted-failover-e2e` job gains a step running `npm run test:e2e:managed-loop-skill`, with the workflow meta-tests updated (arm-table row, `--loop-skill` in the flag-exclusivity list, job ceiling re-derived 305→315).

## Why it's needed

The round-3 fixes were requested by the automatic review, implemented, and verified with mutation witnesses, but the early merge dropped them — main still serves the bundled body without the caller import and counts tool results cumulatively. Restoring them keeps the scenario's assertions honest. Wiring the scenario into CI closes the "no lane executes it" gap the reviews recorded on every round, making the assertions a standing gate on the full Managed Agent tier alongside the sibling packaged-stack arms.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

From the repository root: `npx vitest run --config ./scripts/tests/vitest.config.ts scripts/tests/managed-agent-server-e2e.test.js scripts/tests/hosted-process-ci.test.js scripts/tests/workflow-size.test.js scripts/tests/managed-agent-gate-workflow.test.js` — the runner-contract pins, arm-table/flag-exclusivity/ceiling pins, size ratchet and tier-skip pins all pass. `actionlint .github/workflows/sdk-java.yml` is clean and `bash .github/scripts/check-workflow-size.sh` passes (the workflow grows 427 bytes, under the 4096-byte allowance). The wired command runs green locally against the packaged stack: `npm run test:e2e:managed-loop-skill` prints `mode=loop-skill`, `cronToolResults: 3`, and all four flags true. The round-3 mutation witnesses (caller-import replace path, id-extraction loosening, list-echo truthiness) were run against the production admission and the pins; see the #17433 round-3 summary.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (test + CI wiring; non-UI). Local run of the wired command at this head:

```json
{
  "mode": "loop-skill",
  "sessionId": "8a216f1b-fb78-42c0-8681-2b59c6f67765",
  "definitionId": "agent_c49048cae5cb440984fa7c8150ae909e",
  "modelRounds": 6,
  "cronToolResults": 3,
  "managedSkillBody": true,
  "cronCreate": true,
  "cronList": true,
  "cronDelete": true
}
```

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Local full-stack runner (self-started MySQL 8.4, packaged Spring jar, hosted harness from the bundled CLI, embedded runtime broker, scripted fake model). The CI step runs on `ubuntu-latest` / Java 21 / Node 22 on the full tier.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the CI arm runs only on the full Managed Agent tier (`tier != 'fast'`), the same cadence as its sibling packaged-stack arms whose ~13-minute jar/bundle/mysqld setup is too heavy for the fast tier; the PR fast tier still covers the runner's source contracts via the scripts meta-test lane. The 10-minute per-arm ceiling matches the siblings.
- Not validated / out of scope: macOS/Windows execution of the arm (the job is Linux-only); observing a scheduled fire remains out of scope for the scenario.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The runner changes are test-only; the workflow change is an additive step with the ceiling raised 305→315 to keep the setup allowance.

## Linked Issues

Follow-up to #17433: restores its round-3 fixes (dropped by the merge at `9a53383cb1`) and closes the "no CI lane executes the scenario" gap.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

#17433 的两项跟进。它在 round-2 head（`9a53383cb1`）合入，早于 round-3 修复推送，因此那些修复从未落地 main：

1. **恢复 round-3 评审修复**（`/loop` skill 模型回合 E2E）并按本 PR 自身评审加固：Session 创建体携带一个调用方 `loop` 导入，其正文是逐字 bundled 参考（使准入替换路径像真实创建一样执行），导入带一个标记 description，分支断言它在第一回合消失——见证调用方条目被替换而非仅被投递，并上钉使「把导入换成另一 sidecar」同时让钉子与运行时断言变红；脚本化分类器应答按 block schema（`'shouldBlock' in properties`）而非工具名匹配，避免错答其他结构化侧查询；id 提取钉子点名 arm 的 `createdScheduleId` 绑定；`cronToolResults` 报告三个已见证调用而非累积摊平计数；`cron_list` 回显守卫上钉。两版设计文档写明调用方导入形状，并记录该臂已在 CI 运行（仅观察实际触发仍范围外）。
2. **把场景接入 CI**：打包栈 `hosted-failover-e2e` job 新增运行 `npm run test:e2e:managed-loop-skill` 的步骤，workflow 元测试同步更新（臂表行、flag 排他列表加 `--loop-skill`、job 上限 305→315 重新推导）。

## 为什么需要

round-3 修复由自动评审提出、已实现并用变异见证验证，但提前合入把它们丢掉了——main 仍在无调用方导入的情况下投递 bundled 正文、并累积计数工具结果。恢复它们让场景断言保持诚实。把场景接入 CI 关闭评审每轮记录的「无车道执行它」缺口，使断言成为完整 Managed Agent tier 上与同族打包栈臂并列的常设门禁。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

仓库根目录：`npx vitest run --config ./scripts/tests/vitest.config.ts scripts/tests/managed-agent-server-e2e.test.js scripts/tests/hosted-process-ci.test.js scripts/tests/workflow-size.test.js scripts/tests/managed-agent-gate-workflow.test.js`——runner 契约钉子、臂表/flag 排他/上限钉子、尺寸棘轮与 tier 跳过钉子全过。`actionlint .github/workflows/sdk-java.yml` 干净，`bash .github/scripts/check-workflow-size.sh` 通过（workflow 增长 427 字节，低于 4096 容差）。被接线命令本地对打包栈跑绿：`npm run test:e2e:managed-loop-skill` 打印 `mode=loop-skill`、`cronToolResults: 3`、四标志全 true。round-3 变异见证（调用方导入替换路径、id 提取放宽、list 回显真值化）已对生产准入与钉子执行；见 #17433 round-3 总结。

### 证据（改动前后）

N/A（测试 + CI 接线；非 UI）。本 head 本地运行被接线命令的输出：

```json
{
  "mode": "loop-skill",
  "sessionId": "8a216f1b-fb78-42c0-8681-2b59c6f67765",
  "definitionId": "agent_c49048cae5cb440984fa7c8150ae909e",
  "modelRounds": 6,
  "cronToolResults": 3,
  "managedSkillBody": true,
  "cronCreate": true,
  "cronList": true,
  "cronDelete": true
}
```

### 测试平台

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### 环境（可选）

本地全栈 runner（自启动 MySQL 8.4、打包 Spring jar、来自 bundled CLI 的 hosted harness、内嵌运行时 broker、脚本化 fake 模型）。CI 步骤在完整 tier 的 ubuntu-latest / Java 21 / Node 22 运行。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险/权衡：CI 臂只在完整 Managed Agent tier（`tier != 'fast'`）运行，与同族打包栈臂同一节奏（它们约 13 分钟的 jar/bundle/mysqld 搭建对 fast tier 太重）；PR fast tier 仍通过 scripts 元测试车道覆盖 runner 源码契约。每臂 10 分钟上限与同族一致。
- 未验证/范围外：该臂的 macOS/Windows 执行（job 仅 Linux）；观察调度实际触发仍不在场景范围内。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明：无。runner 改动仅测试；workflow 为增量步骤，上限 305→315 以保留搭建余量。

## 关联 Issue

#17433 的跟进：恢复其 round-3 修复（被 `9a53383cb1` 处的合入丢掉），并关闭「无 CI 车道执行该场景」缺口。

</details>

prs.title: feat(web-shell): Codex-style managed worktree sessions (default-on, detached, branch & handoff)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Web Shell sessions in a trusted Git workspace now behave like Codex managed worktree chats. A new session defaults to an isolated worktree instead of the user's current checkout; the worktree is created lazily when the first message is sent, starts in detached HEAD so parallel sessions never pollute the branch list, and carries the source checkout's uncommitted changes (staged, unstaged, and untracked) so the agent sees exactly the files the user has on disk. From the branch chip's menu the user can turn the detached worktree into a named branch ("Create branch here") or move the same chat between the worktree and the local checkout ("Hand off"), with the work carried across in both directions. A new `worktree.defaultForNewSessions` setting (default `true`) turns the default off; explicit mode selection always wins, and the daemon API semantics are unchanged for callers that do not opt in.

This is the first five phases (P1–P5) of the Codex parity design linked below; retention with snapshots (P6) and a configurable worktree root (P7) are tracked in #17237. The design document (English and Chinese) records the Codex reference behavior, the consumer census behind the detached-HEAD refactor, and the v1 limitations of the handoff.

## Why it's needed

Today multiple Web Shell sessions in one workspace share a single checkout, so concurrent agents trample each other's edits and HEAD, and an agent's changes land directly in the user's working tree. Codex solves this with managed worktrees that are on by default, detached, and carry the user's uncommitted context. This PR brings that experience to Web Shell: isolation by default without branch pollution, the user's in-progress work visible to the agent, and a safe path to bring the work back to the local checkout or promote it to a branch. The default is configurable so users who prefer the current-branch flow can keep it.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Build and bundle (`npm run build && npm run bundle`), then run a daemon against a throwaway Git workspace (`node dist/cli.js serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4199 --require-auth --workspace <repo>` with `QWEN_SERVER_TOKEN` set). Confirm: (1) `GET /workspace/settings` serves `worktree.defaultForNewSessions` with effective `true`, and setting it to `false` at workspace scope flips the effective value; (2) creating a session with `worktree: {}` yields a worktree whose `branch` is `""`, `git -C <worktree> symbolic-ref HEAD` fails (detached), and `git branch --list 'worktree-*'` in the source repo is unchanged; (3) with a dirty source checkout (one staged, one unstaged, one untracked file), all three appear in the new worktree while the source status is untouched and the worktree HEAD equals the source HEAD; (4) `POST /session/:id/worktree-branch {"name":"feat/x"}` returns 200 and the worktree is on `feat/x`, a second call returns 409 `worktree_already_branched`, a taken name returns 409 `branch_already_exists`, and an invalid name returns 400; (5) `POST /session/:id/worktree-handoff {"to":"worktree"}` on a plain session moves it into a detached worktree carrying local dirty state, and `{"to":"local","name":"feat/y"}` moves it back, checking `feat/y` out locally with the worktree's commits and tracked dirty changes, leaving the worktree detached; a dirty local checkout returns 409 `local_checkout_dirty`. In the Web Shell UI, the composer chip shows Worktree mode by default for a trusted Git workspace, the branch picker offers "Create branch here" only for detached worktree sessions and "Hand off to local" / "Move to worktree" by context, and resetting the chip to the current branch before sending creates a plain session.

Focused unit suites (run from the repo root): `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/services/gitWorktreeService.dirty-carry.integ.test.ts src/services/gitWorktreeService.detached.integ.test.ts src/services/worktreeSessionService.test.ts`; `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/serve/routes/session-worktree-branch.test.ts src/serve/routes/session-worktree-handoff.test.ts src/serve/branch-worktree-preparation.test.ts src/serve/routes/workspace-settings.test.ts src/serve/routes/workspace-settings-i18n.test.ts src/serve/server/telemetry.test.ts src/serve/server/telemetry-catalog.test.ts src/startup/worktreeStartup.test.ts`; `cd packages/web-shell && npx vitest run client/components/BranchPickerPopover.test.tsx client/components/GitModePopover.test.tsx client/components/messages/SettingsMessage.dom.test.tsx` and `npx vitest run client/App.test.tsx -t worktree`. On this machine the web-shell suites need `NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-webstorage` (Node 22+ experimental webstorage shadows jsdom's localStorage) and the git integration suites need `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` to bypass a host-level pre-push hook; neither is a product requirement. The repo-wide drift guards (settings zh coverage, telemetry count/catalog) and the integration capabilities baseline (`cd integration-tests && npx vitest run cli/qwen-serve-routes.test.ts`, after `npm run build && npm run bundle`) migrate with this surface and are part of the focused list.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Daemon-level E2E probes against a throwaway dirty Git repo, before (installed 0.27.3) vs after (this branch's bundle): the settings key is absent before and served with effective `true` after; worktree creation before yields a named `worktree-<slug>` branch with none of the dirty files carried, after yields `branch: ""`, detached HEAD, an empty `worktree-*` branch list, and all three dirty files carried with the source untouched. The handoff round trip (local → worktree → local) returns 200 in both directions with the branch checked out locally, the session's commit present, and the worktree left detached; a dirty local checkout returns 409 `local_checkout_dirty`. Unit evidence on the final head: core dirty-carry + detached + sidecar suites 76/76, cli branch/handoff/journal/settings/telemetry suites green, web-shell App worktree filter 14/14 plus BranchPickerPopover 151/151, GitModePopover 18/18, SettingsMessage 59/59; full App.test.tsx 1508/1508. Build, typecheck (core/cli/web-shell), and bundle all exit 0. UI screenshots: component-tested; visual capture to follow in review.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Local Linux runtime: isolated `node dist/cli.js serve` daemons on throwaway ports/workspaces with `QWEN_RUNTIME_DIR` and bearer auth; real git repositories for the worktree probes. Node 24 toolchain for build/typecheck (the host's default Node 26 lacks corepack).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the default flip changes where a new session does its work — an isolated worktree instead of the user's checkout. Mitigations: the worktree is created lazily on the first prompt (selection alone creates nothing), an explicit composer selection always wins over the default, the touched marker survives transient git-status blips, and `worktree.defaultForNewSessions: false` restores the old default. The detached-HEAD refactor reworks the worktree service's lifecycle gates (branch/tip equality, unmerged-commit detection, reattach, journal identity); a missed consumer would be a silent fail-closed leak, so the change ships with a full consumer census (design P3 inventory) and per-consumer migration tests. Handoff relocates a live session's cwd; its v1 limitations are documented rather than hidden (see the design D6): a clean local checkout stands in for "no other active session owns it" (the bridge has no session-list occupancy probe), and there is no crash-window atomic rollback — a crash mid-handoff leaves a recoverable shape, not a self-healing transfer.
- Not validated / out of scope: macOS and Windows are not locally validated (⚠️ in the table; the PR-phase CI skips unit tests on both). Visual UI capture is pending (component-tested only). Retention with snapshots/restore (P6) and a configurable worktree root (P7) are out of scope here and tracked in #17237. The base-side `acp-agent-loop-parity` no-AK failure is attributed to `main` (cross-PR control in the PR comments), not to this diff.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: callers that relied on a session worktree sitting on a named `worktree-<slug>` branch now see detached HEAD with `branch: ""` in the session metadata, sidecar, and SDK `DaemonWorktreeInfo`; code that compared against `worktree-<slug>` must tolerate the empty-string detached convention (the daemon's own gates, journal recovery, reattach, and displays were migrated in this PR). Tool-created (`enter_worktree`), agent-isolation, and Arena worktrees keep their named branches — only Web Shell session worktrees change shape. The daemon API is unchanged for callers that do not pass `worktree`/the new routes; `POST /session` without `worktree` still runs in the workspace directory. Users who prefer the previous flow set `worktree.defaultForNewSessions: false`.

Design document: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/web-shell-worktree-codex-parity/docs/design/2026-11-14-web-shell-codex-worktree-parity.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/web-shell-worktree-codex-parity/docs/design/2026-11-14-web-shell-codex-worktree-parity.zh-CN.md) (decisions, constraints, acceptance criteria, and the P6/P7 follow-up work are complete and synchronized in both).

prs.title: feat(web-shell): filter workspaces by name in the picker and sidebar
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The Web Shell's workspace surfaces have no way to filter long workspace lists. This PR adds a simple case-insensitive substring filter in two places. In the composer's workspace picker (a Radix dropdown radio group), a small text input now sits at the top of the dropdown: typing live-filters the radio list by workspace label (case-insensitive substring), host groups that lose all their entries drop out, a "No workspaces match" note appears when nothing matches, and the query resets when the menu closes. In the session search dialog, a query that matches at least one workspace by display name or cwd switches the results into "name mode": the list narrows to the sessions of the matching workspaces, while a query that matches no workspace name (a plain session-content keyword) leaves the results untouched. The name-mode gate is restricted to the workspaces the search actually fetches — trusted workspaces, narrowed to the primary one when the daemon does not support qualified search — so a name hit on an out-of-pipeline workspace cannot delete rows the search did find. The matching helper `matchesWorkspaceQuery` (`utils/workspaceFilter.ts`) trims and lowercases the query and tests it as a substring against any of the candidate strings; an empty query matches everything.

## Why it's needed

On machines where a daemon exposes many workspaces, the picker and the session search become long lists that must be scanned by eye to find one entry (request in #17142). A case-insensitive substring-in-name filter is the minimal affordance that makes a long list navigable, and reusing the picker's and the search dialog's existing inputs avoids adding a second input to either surface.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Start a Web Shell (Qwen Code Desktop, or `pnpm run dev`) against a daemon with at least three workspaces.
2. Composer picker: open it and type a substring of one workspace's name — only the matching entries remain (case-insensitive); with two hosts, the host group that lost all its entries disappears; type a string that matches nothing — the "No workspaces match" note appears; close and reopen the menu — the input is empty again.
3. Session search dialog: open it and type a workspace's display name or cwd — the results narrow to that workspace's sessions; type a string that matches no workspace name — all session results stay visible as in a plain session search; clear the query — the full result list returns.
4. Unit tests: `pnpm --dir packages/web-shell exec vitest run packages/web-shell/client/utils/workspaceFilter.test.ts packages/web-shell/client/components/WorkspaceSelector.test.tsx packages/web-shell/client/components/sidebar/SessionSearchDialog.test.tsx` — the picker cases pin input rendering, live filtering, group dropping, the empty state, the focus guard in portalled (shadow-root) mode, and the reset on close; the dialog cases pin name mode (results narrowed to the matching workspaces), plain search mode (no workspace-name match keeps the full list), and that out-of-pipeline workspaces (untrusted, or secondary on a non-qualified daemon) never enter name mode.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — new unit tests only; the manual steps above reproduce the behavior.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️    |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️    |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅    |

Linux: all static and unit runs (vitest, tsc, eslint, prettier) in a `node:22-bookworm` container. macOS: development machine; no live before/after run captured. Windows: not tested — the change is browser-side TypeScript only.

### Environment (optional)

N/A — unit tests.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the session search query now carries two meanings at once — a session-content query and a workspace-name gate. The name-mode guard (narrow only when at least one in-pipeline workspace matches the query) keeps the common session-search flow unchanged; a query that matches both a workspace name and session content narrows both dimensions, which is the intended behavior.
- Not validated / out of scope: a live before/after capture on a running install; filtering by workspace id or ssh host.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none — client-side only, no API or persistence changes.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #17142

<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

Web Shell 的 workspace 界面无法过滤很长的列表。本 PR 在两处加了简单的大小写不敏感子串过滤。在 composer 的 workspace 选择器（Radix dropdown 单选组）中，dropdown 顶部现在有一个小的文本输入框：输入时会按 workspace 名称实时过滤单选列表（大小写不敏感的子串匹配），失去全部条目的 host 分组会消失，没有匹配项时显示“No workspaces match”提示，菜单关闭时查询被重置。在会话搜索对话框中，当查询至少匹配一个 workspace 的显示名称或 cwd 时，结果进入“名称模式”：列表收窄到匹配 workspace 的会话；匹配不到任何 workspace 名称的查询（例如普通的会话内容关键词）不改动结果。名称模式的判定被限制在搜索实际拉取的 workspace 集合上 —— 受信任的 workspace，在 daemon 不支持 qualified 搜索时收窄到主 workspace —— 因此命中管道外 workspace 的名称不会删掉搜索已经找到的行。匹配辅助函数 `matchesWorkspaceQuery`（`utils/workspaceFilter.ts`）会 trim 并小写化查询，然后在任一候选字符串上做子串测试；空查询匹配一切。

## 为什么需要

在 daemon 暴露了大量 workspace 的机器上，选择器和会话搜索都会变成必须逐条目目视扫描的长列表（#17142 中的诉求）。大小写不敏感的“名称含子串”过滤是让长列表可导航的最小交互手段；复用选择器和搜索对话框已有的输入框也避免了在两个界面上各加一个输入框。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

prs.title: fix(managed-agent): align serverRevision ceiling across contract, management and persistence
prs.body:
## What this PR does

`serverRevision` had three different ceilings. The OpenAPI contract and the `ManagedMcpManagementService.requireSnapshot` counter accepted 2^53-1, while the extension-record `count()` rule clamped a wider max down to 2^53-2. A revision of exactly 2^53-1 therefore passed admission and was refused later, and the refusal printed the caller's unclamped max — one higher than the bound actually enforced. This PR moves the contract, the management read path, the CLI pins and the persistence admission shape onto the single shared ceiling, and makes the refusal message report the bound it enforces.

## Why it's needed

The record contract fixes counts at 2^53-2 (`docs/design/2026-09-27-managed-extension-record-contract.md`), and the TypeScript `assertManagedSessionSequence` rejects `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` outright. The public contract was the outlier: it advertised a ceiling the persistence layer never accepted. After this change a snapshot the harness may legally return is also one the published contract permits, so the service can no longer relay a response its own contract calls invalid.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- `packages/core`: `npx vitest run src/managed-runtime/managed-mcp-record.test.ts` — the shared fixtures are read by both the TypeScript and the Java reader, so a passing run confirms the two agree on the boundary.
- The `unsafe-server-revision` fixture now patches `run.definition.definitionRevision` alongside `serverRevision`. With only `serverRevision` patched, the pin-equality rule in `pinnedRun` refused the record on its own, so the case passed even with the ceiling guard removed; with both patched it fails only if the `MAX_SAFE_COUNTER` guard is what refuses it. `max-server-revision` is the positive counterpart at 2^53-2.
- `ManagedMcpRecordContractTest#boundsEveryPublicMcpSequenceAtTheSharedCeiling` mirrors that pair against the Java record and asserts the refusal names the enforced ceiling.
- `node scripts/check-contract-version.js <base> <head>` — the document changes six `maximum` values, so `info.version` advances to 1.112.0 past main's 1.111.0.

Expected: the whole boundary sits at 2^53-2 on every layer, and a 2^53-1 value is refused with a message that states 9007199254740990.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — contract and validation change, no user-visible surface.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Node 24, vitest from the worktree's `node_modules`. Java was not built — see Risk & Scope.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: historical data can exist. The persisted managed-record layer has always clamped at 2^53-2 (`ManagedExtensionRecords.MAX_COUNT`), but the management-command path admitted 2^53-1 on both sides before this change — `ApiModels.ManagedMcpServerPin` declared `@Max(9_007_199_254_740_991L)` and `parseHostedMcpServers` only required `Number.isSafeInteger`, so a Session created earlier can hold a `…991` selection. Such a Session now fails `requireSnapshot` and its management read path returns `managed_mcp_management_unavailable` (503), consistent with the existing `Invalid MCP management snapshot` failure mode. The same spread reaches the persistence read path too: `readHostedMcpSettings` (`packages/cli/src/serve/hosted-mcp-settings.ts:189`, which calls `parseHostedMcpServers` at :244) throws `Invalid MCP settings.` for an existing `…991` pin. That behaviour was not traced further into Session open, so its blast radius there is unverified. I took the convergence rather than rolling back the response maxima, because a rollback leaves the contract advertising a bound the persistence layer refuses.
- Not validated / out of scope: the Java module was not compiled or tested on this machine — it has no JDK or Maven (`/usr/bin/java` is a stub), so `ManagedMcpRecordContractTest`, `ManagedAgentApiContractTest`, `ManagedMcpManagementServiceTest` and checkstyle are left to CI. `ManagedDiagnosticMcpServer.serverRevision`, `ManagedToolMeasurements.MAX_COUNT` and the client-side `Number.isSafeInteger` guards stay where they are; they are consistent with their own code and only ever wider, so they are not a regression of this change. The repository-wide `npm run build` also fails in `packages/channels/github` on this checkout for an unrelated missing cross-package type.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none for well-formed data; the only observable change is the rejection described above.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #16886

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

`serverRevision` 此前有三个不同的上限。OpenAPI 契约和 `ManagedMcpManagementService.requireSnapshot` 的计数器接受 2^53-1，而扩展记录的 `count()` 规则会把更宽的 max 夹到 2^53-2。于是恰好等于 2^53-1 的 revision 能通过准入、之后才被拒，而且拒绝信息打印的是调用方传入的、未夹紧的 max —— 比真正生效的上界高 1。本 PR 把契约、management 读路径、CLI pin 和持久化准入形状统一到同一个共享上限，并让拒绝信息播报它真正执行的界限。

## 为什么需要

记录契约把计数定在 2^53-2（`docs/design/2026-09-27-managed-extension-record-contract.md`），TypeScript 的 `assertManagedSessionSequence` 也直接拒绝 `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`。公开契约才是那个例外：它宣传了一个持久化层从不接受的上限。改动之后，harness 可以合法返回的快照，也是已发布契约允许的值，服务端不会再转发被自家契约判为非法的响应。

## 审查者测试计划

### 如何验证

- `packages/core`：`npx vitest run src/managed-runtime/managed-mcp-record.test.ts`。共享夹具由 TypeScript 与 Java 两个读取器共用，通过即说明两者在边界上一致。
- `unsafe-server-revision` 夹具现在同时 patch `run.definition.definitionRevision` 与 `serverRevision`。此前只 patch `serverRevision` 时，`pinnedRun` 的 pin 相等规则自己就会拒绝它，所以即使移除上界守卫该用例仍然通过；两者都 patch 后，只有 `MAX_SAFE_COUNTER` 守卫才是拒绝的原因。`max-server-revision` 是 2^53-2 的正向对照。
- `ManagedMcpRecordContractTest#boundsEveryPublicMcpSequenceAtTheSharedCeiling` 在 Java 记录上镜像这对用例，并断言拒绝信息里写明真正执行的上界。
- `node scripts/check-contract-version.js <base> <head>`：文档改了六处 `maximum`，因此 `info.version` 推进到 1.112.0，越过 main 的 1.111.0。

预期：边界在每一层都是 2^53-2，2^53-1 被拒且信息中写明 9007199254740990。

### 证据（改动前后）

N/A —— 契约与校验改动，没有用户可见界面。

### 测试环境

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### 环境（可选）

Node 24，vitest 来自 worktree 的 `node_modules`。Java 未构建 —— 见「风险与范围」。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：已存储且带 `serverRevision = 2^53-1` 的记录会使 `requireSnapshot` 失败，对该 Session 表现为 `managed_mcp_management_unavailable`（503）。写入路径一直是按 2^53-2 夹紧的（`ManagedExtensionRecords.MAX_COUNT`），所以健康系统不可能产生这种记录；若确有历史脏数据，该 503 与既有的 `Invalid MCP management snapshot` 失败模式一致。我选择收敛而不是回退四处响应上限，因为回退会让契约继续宣传一个持久化层拒绝的限制。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：本机没有编译或测试 Java 模块 —— 没有 JDK 和 Maven（`/usr/bin/java` 是 stub），所以 `ManagedMcpRecordContractTest`、`ManagedAgentApiContractTest`、`ManagedMcpManagementServiceTest` 与 checkstyle 留给 CI。`ManagedDiagnosticMcpServer.serverRevision`、`ManagedToolMeasurements.MAX_COUNT` 以及客户端侧的 `Number.isSafeInteger` 守卫保持原样；它们与自身代码一致且只会更宽，不构成本次改动的回归。仓库级 `npm run build` 在这个 checkout 上也会因 `packages/channels/github` 缺跨包类型而失败，与本改动无关。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：对格式正确的数据没有；唯一可观察的变化是上面描述的拒绝。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #16886

</details>

issues.body:
Terminal sessions and background jobs belong to the conversation that started them, so they end when that conversation ends instead of running on with nowhere to report.

## Status

- **On main:** deleting a conversation ends the terminal sessions **and** the background shell jobs it owns, including `persist:true` jobs (59847de236). The terminal routes are in [docs/RUNTIME_API.md](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/main/docs/RUNTIME_API.md) (`GET /v1/threads/{id}/terminals`, plus its output, input and resize).
- **On main (desktop):** closing a window ends the local terminals that window owned. Engine terminals belong to the conversation, so they stay with it when a tab closes and end when the conversation ends.
- **Known limits, by design for now:**
  - shells survive quitting or updating the app;
  - an Engine restart loses live shells, which are reported as a new terminal `instance`;
  - scrollback beyond the 512 KiB ring is not recoverable.
- **Remaining for 0.10.3:** qualify the lifecycle on the release artifacts. This issue stays open until 0.10.3 is published.

## Ways to help

**1. Find a leak (no Rust needed).** Start a background job from a conversation, for example a long `sleep`, a dev server or a `persist:true` shell. Then delete, fork, resume or compact the conversation, and check whether the process is still running (`ps`, or Task Manager on Windows). Comment with the exact steps, your OS and what was left behind.

Done when the steps reproduce, or you've shown a case is clean.

**2. Add the test that would catch it.** If way 1 finds a leak, the Engine side lives in `crates/engine/src/runtime_threads/manager.rs` (thread deletion) and the shell manager under `crates/engine/src/tools/shell/`. A fix with its regression test is a welcome PR. The existing coverage is `kill_all_owned_running_ends_every_running_job_once` in `crates/engine/src/tools/shell/tests.rs`; run it with `scripts/dev-test.sh engine kill_all_owned_running`.

## Being built by maintainers right now

The desktop tab-close behavior is already on main, as described under Status. Still claimed: the lifecycle qualification on frozen release artifacts.

## How to take a piece

1. **Comment here first** with the piece you want (for example "I'll take row 12" or "Windows journeys on ARM64"), so two people don't build the same thing. A maintainer replies to confirm.
2. **Build and test locally.** Setup: [Getting Started](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#getting-started); fast loop: [Fast local loop](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#fast-local-loop).
   ```bash
   CODEWHALE_BUILD_SHA="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" cargo build --locked -p codewhale-cli
   scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p <crate>
   scripts/dev-test.sh <crate-or-path> <test_filter>
   ```
3. **Open a PR that says `Refs #<this issue>`.** It merges as itself with you as the author, you are credited in the changelog and [CONTRIBUTORS](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/main/docs/CONTRIBUTORS.md), and a red check you didn't cause is ours to fix. Reports are contributions too: a test result posted here is credited the same way.

Questions are welcome here, in English or Chinese. Part of the overall [0.10.3 tracking issue](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/7284).

issues.title: bug: the TUI freezes for the whole next turn when a save-snapshot is requested as a new turn starts

labels.name: area:install

issues.body:
## Summary

When a turn ends and a new turn starts within milliseconds, the TUI freezes for the **entire duration of the new turn** — keystrokes are ignored, nothing renders, and the only way out is to close the terminal. In the session below the freeze lasted **209 seconds**, and the same session recorded it twice more at 541 s and 848 s.

The visible message afterwards is:

```
Session <id> could not be saved (resource busy). Recent work may not be saved.
```

That message is a symptom, not the cause: `resource busy` is the fallback error string the UI uses when its session snapshot does not arrive.

## Mechanism

1. A turn settles. The TUI's turn-complete handler requests a snapshot from the engine (`crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs`, `engine_handle.get_session_snapshot().await`). The await is **unbounded** — no `tokio::time::timeout`.
2. The engine serves `Op::GetSessionSnapshot` only from its run loop between turns. `handle_send_message` awaits the whole turn inline, and nothing inside the turn loop drains `rx_op`. So while a turn runs, the snapshot request sits in the 32-slot op channel.
3. If the next turn starts before the snapshot is served — which happens when the message is already queued — the UI blocks until that turn finishes.

The UI event loop is a single async loop: while it awaits the snapshot it does not poll the terminal, so input and rendering stop. That is the freeze.

The codebase already knows this hazard. `get_subagent_settlement` on the same handle carries the warning:

```rust
/// Query after the active turn settles, without competing with events.
/// The caller must keep draining events and bound this future: an active
/// turn can be awaiting provider/tool work or a full event channel.
```

`get_session_snapshot` has no such note, and the turn-complete call site does not bound it. The startup path uses the same method **with** a timeout (`LAUNCH_SESSION_SYNC_WAIT = 2s`, `await_engine_session_sync`), so the bound exists in the codebase — it is simply missing here.

## Natural control experiment

One session (`2a4365be`, workspace `~/`, 16 November) produced four identical `Chat Completions stream closed before [DONE] or finish_reason` failures within 15 minutes. Only one froze:

| Failure | Next turn started | Warning | Freeze |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 18:54:29 | **+0.02 s** | 18:57:59 | **209 s** |
| 18:57:59 | +375 s | same instant | 0 s |
| 19:06:33 | +8.3 s | none | 0 s |
| 19:09:12 | +31.9 s | none | 0 s |

The only difference is whether a new turn started before the snapshot could be served. Same error, same session, same binary — freeze only when the next turn starts immediately. The user reproduced this live: the third failure did not freeze.

## Timeline of the 209-second freeze

```
18:54:29.929  turn 4156686f  phase=idle
18:54:29.944  turn completion settled status=Failed   (stream closed before [DONE])
18:54:29.966  turn 6a12cd4b  started                  (+22 ms)
              … UI awaits get_session_snapshot(); engine is inside the new turn …
18:55:07.188  turn 6a12cd4b  phase=streaming the model response
              … nothing in the log for 172 s …
18:57:59.786  turn 6a12cd4b  settled status=Failed    (same stream error)
18:57:59.798  WARN terminal session source no longer matches; checkpoint retained
```

The warning fires the moment the snapshot is finally served — and it no longer matches, because the engine's source has moved on. The UI then reports `Session … could not be saved (resource busy)`.

So the sequence is: the stream error is what makes the new turn end; the snapshot request is what makes the UI wait; the mismatch is what produces the misleading "not saved" notice.

## Not caused by the old workspace-lock issue

The "resource busy" wording is the same string the workspace-lease refusal used, so it is worth ruling out: this session ran in `~/`, its log shows the delegated-store read-only warning at startup (the known legacy-store case), but the save failure here is not a flock — no `Resource temporarily unavailable`, no coordination-lock line at the time of the freeze. The text comes from `snapshot_error.unwrap_or_else(|| std::io::ErrorKind::ResourceBusy.to_string())` in the same turn-complete handler.

## Frequency in one month of logs

`terminal session source no longer matches` appears **15 times across 7 log files** (9–16 November). Four have a measurable freeze:

```
848 s   tui-2026-11-14-4002283.log   turn eebd894f
541 s   tui-2026-11-15-55504.log     turn 93494e2e
209 s   tui-2026-11-16-880180.log    turn 4156686f
 69 s   tui-2026-11-13-1149827.log   turn 1443f6d1
```

The 848 s case is confounded by the separate late-usage-ledger defect (#7356) in the same session; the other three are clean (zero ledger failures in their logs) and share the exact signature above.

Underlying stream errors: **9** `Chat Completions stream closed before [DONE] or finish_reason` across 6 sessions since 10 October (10, 14, 18 ×2, 21 Oct; 16 Nov ×4). That error is separate — it is the trigger, not the freeze.

## Still present upstream

`upstream/main` at `b107c4996` (350 commits ahead of the reporting build) has the same unbounded call at `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs:3906`; the turn loop still does not drain `rx_op`. No open issue covers this: #6184 is the engine going silent, #7328 is missing failure causes in the log, #7356 is the ledger blocking saves. This is the UI blocking itself on a busy engine.

## Suggested fix

Bound the await and keep the loop alive:

1. Wrap the turn-complete `get_session_snapshot()` in `tokio::time::timeout` — the same 2 s used by `await_engine_session_sync` is a reasonable start. On timeout, keep the checkpoint (already done today) and skip the completion commit instead of blocking.
2. Or serve `Op::GetSessionSnapshot` while a turn runs — it reads session state, but the engine is single-threaded, so this likely needs the snapshot to be published out-of-band rather than computed on demand.
3. While here, make the refusal say what it is: `resource busy` reads like a lock, and it sent at least one operator looking for a stale process. A sentence naming the pending Engine snapshot would have saved that search.

Option 1 is the smallest change and removes the freeze entirely; the snapshot will still mismatch sometimes, which is already handled.

## Reproduction

Not deterministic, but the conditions are simple: with a message already queued, let a turn fail with `Chat Completions stream closed before [DONE] or finish_reason` (or any fast failure), so that the failure's turn completion and the queued turn start land within the same few milliseconds. The UI then stops responding until the next turn ends.

## Related

- #7356 — late-usage ledger blocks session saves; the 848 s case overlaps with it.
- #7328 — provider failures leave no cause in the log.
- `CHANGELOG.md` 0.10.3 — "Turns no longer fail on a cost bookkeeping error"; the same principle applies to a UI that must not block on a busy engine.

issues.body:
0.10.3 puts ACP (the [Agent Client Protocol](https://agentclientprotocol.com)) first. This issue covers one direction: **Codewhale runs an installed agent CLI over ACP**, as a whole session that lives in Codewhale's sidebar, history and approvals. The other direction, an editor driving Codewhale, is #7280.

## Status

- **On main:**
  - A session can run on an installed agent.
  - Shutdown ends an agent that is still starting, restart recovery works, and approval answers are durable.
  - Discovery finds Windows `.cmd`/`.exe` shims and says *why* an agent is unavailable: missing, too old, or answering with another protocol.
  - The supported agents are listed in `crates/engine/src/fleet/agents.rs` (`AGENTS`): Claude Agent, Codex, DSH, Antigravity, OpenCode, Kimi, Mistral Vibe, Qoder, CodeBuddy and Grok.
- **How a session is started:** [docs/RUNTIME_API.md § Sessions on other agents](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/main/docs/RUNTIME_API.md#sessions-on-other-agents-external-agent-threads), and `GET /v1/agents/external` for what was found on this computer.
- **Verification so far uses fixture agents.** No real installed agent has been qualified yet.

## Ways to help

**1. Try a real agent and report (no Rust needed).** Pick an agent you already have installed and comment with which one. Then:
- Start `codewhale serve` from a `main` build, check that `GET /v1/agents/external` lists your agent as runnable, and start a session on it.
- Send a prompt that edits a file and runs a command, answer an approval, cancel a turn, and quit and reopen to resume.
- Post the agent name and version, your OS, what worked, and the exact text of anything refused or broken.

Done when every step is reported for that agent.

**2. Add an agent that speaks ACP.** For example **Qwen Code** (`qwen --acp`) or **GitHub Copilot CLI** (`copilot --acp --stdio`), which are not in the registry yet. (Google's agent is already listed as Antigravity, `agy acp`; Gemini CLI was retired for personal accounts and is not added back.) This is a good first Rust contribution:
- Add one `ExternalAgent` row to `AGENTS` in `crates/engine/src/fleet/agents.rs`: `id`, `binary`, `acp_args` (how to start it in ACP mode), `min_version`, `upgrade`, `login` and `website`.
- Copy the shape of a neighbouring row. Fields you can't verify stay `None`; don't guess.
- Run `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/fleet/agents.rs registry`. `registry_rows_are_unique_with_verified_commands` must pass.
- Say in the PR how you checked the ACP flag against the agent's own docs.

**3. Improve the docs.** A user-facing page on running other agents inside Codewhale (install, sign in, start a session, what's supported) doesn't exist yet. A PR adding one under `docs/` is welcome, and a Chinese version under `docs/zh_hans/` even more so.

## Being built by maintainers right now

These are claimed, so please don't duplicate them:
- ACP options, capability refusals and agent-reported usage.
- Consolidating to one ACP client.
- Sending extra workspace directories to agents that support them.
- Projecting plan, mode, command and config updates from agents.

Steering, compaction, forking and images in an external-agent session are reported as unavailable unless the agent supports them.

## How to take a piece

1. **Comment here first** with the piece you want (for example "I'll take row 12" or "Windows journeys on ARM64"), so two people don't build the same thing. A maintainer replies to confirm.
2. **Build and test locally.** Setup: [Getting Started](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#getting-started); fast loop: [Fast local loop](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#fast-local-loop).
   ```bash
   CODEWHALE_BUILD_SHA="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" cargo build --locked -p codewhale-cli
   scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p <crate>
   scripts/dev-test.sh <crate-or-path> <test_filter>
   ```
3. **Open a PR that says `Refs #<this issue>`.** It merges as itself with you as the author, you are credited in the changelog and [CONTRIBUTORS](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/main/docs/CONTRIBUTORS.md), and a red check you didn't cause is ours to fix.
