issues.title: bug: a session whose late-usage ledger hits 1 MiB can no longer be saved at all — compaction fails and the transcript stops persisting

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:install
labels.description: Install, npm wrapper, release artifacts, Homebrew, winget, Docker, Nix

labels.name: area:core
labels.description: Engine core: turn loop, agent loop, runtime

labels.name: area:state
labels.description: Sessions, persistence and the state store

issues.body:
## Summary

Once a session's late-usage ledger reaches its 1 MiB bound, **every save of that session fails** — checkpoint, snapshot and completed-commit alike. Compaction dies with `Making room failed: late usage ledger exceeds its size bound`, and the conversation stops being persisted while it keeps running in memory.

A bookkeeping sidecar should not be able to stop the transcript from being saved.

## Provenance — not a stale binary, not two processes

Checked before filing, because the first hypothesis was "an old binary kept running after an update":

- Installed binary: `codewhale 0.10.3 (dev)`, commit `5af8a9a24`, built **2026-11-11 00:08 UTC**.
- The affected process started **2026-11-13T23:49:19Z** — two days *after* the build. It is the new binary.
- One `codewhale` file on disk: `/home/f2/.cargo/bin/codewhale` is the only hit; `/usr/local/bin`, `/usr/bin` and `~/.local/bin` have none.
- The ledger file itself was last written `2026-11-14T23:44:57Z`, i.e. by this process, not carried over from an older build.

So the failure is produced by the current binary and the current code, not by a leftover process.

## Observed

Session `c6d6e81d`, workspace `~/Documents/Shared/Research`, 1488 messages. The ledger `.late-usage/c6d6e81d….json`:

```
records      941
size         1,048,490 bytes
bound        1,048,576 bytes (1 MiB)
headroom     86 bytes
avg record   ~1,114 bytes
overflowed   true
unresolved   0
```

86 bytes of headroom, and one new record is ~1,114 bytes — so **every** further append fails, permanently. There is no pruning of settled records anywhere in the code to make room.

The log, 16 November:

```
14:51:25  WARN compaction: context compaction failed             auto=false
14:51:25  WARN persistence: persistence write failed             what=completed-commit:c6d6e81d…
14:51:34  WARN compaction: context compaction failed             auto=false
14:51:34  WARN persistence: persistence write failed             what=completed-commit:c6d6e81d…
14:56:02  WARN persistence: persistence write failed             what=checkpoint:c6d6e81d…
… 184 checkpoint failures carrying the same error, through 15:11 …
15:11:06  WARN persistence: persistence write failed             what=checkpoint:c6d6e81d…
```

Counts from that one log file, so a reader can reproduce:

```
184  persistence write failed what=checkpoint:c6d6e81d…   error=late usage ledger exceeds its size bound
  2  context compaction failed                            error=late usage ledger exceeds its size bound
```

The session document was last written at **14:50:16Z**; at the time of filing the clock was **15:11Z** — 21 minutes of turns running in memory only. A crash or a close loses that work.

One caveat, stated so the numbers are not over-read: three earlier checkpoint failures on **14 November** carry `error_kind=StorageFull` — a full disk, a different cause. Those are excluded from the counts above; every 16 November failure carries the ledger message.

The two compaction failures are manual (`auto=false`). The save failures are not: they are on the ordinary checkpoint path, so **the session is not being persisted at all** — not just compaction.

The only thing that clears the ledger is deleting the session (the `codewhale-session-deleted-v1` tombstone). While the session lives, the file can only grow.

## Root cause — three independent mistakes line up

**1. A hard 1 MiB cap with no eviction.** `MAX_LATE_USAGE_LEDGER_BYTES = 1024 * 1024` (`crates/engine/src/session_manager.rs`), and `write_late_usage_ledger` rejects anything larger with `InvalidData: late usage ledger exceeds its size bound`. Nothing prunes settled records; the file only grows.

**2. The cap is fatal to the session save.** `flush_pending_usage_admitted(&id)?` is called with `?` on all three write paths — checkpoint, snapshot and completed-commit. So a ledger write failure aborts the save of the conversation itself.

**3. The degradation path is already dead in this state.** `write_late_usage_candidate` has a fallback that writes a smaller "overflowed" ledger — but only `if !original.overflowed`. This ledger already has `overflowed: true`, so the fallback never runs and the error propagates unconditionally.

The three together produce a hard lock: the ledger cannot grow, cannot shrink, cannot be marked overflowed again, and the save cannot proceed.

## Why this is not #6842 or #7348

- **#6842** owns the *growth* — bounding the replay index while preserving spend deduplication (and it explicitly warns that truncating the fingerprint set can double-count money). It does not mention the 1 MiB bound, the size-bound message, or that hitting it blocks persistence; checked the body, no occurrences. This issue is about the *coupling*, not the growth.
- **#7348** owns the sibling defect one layer up: the in-memory journal cap (256 records) failing the *turn* before dispatch. This one is the on-disk ledger failing the *save*. Different cap, different file, different consequence.

The shared principle is the one the 0.10.3 changelog already states for settlement — "Turns no longer fail on a cost bookkeeping error" — and that `bc3ad117e` implemented for the settlement path. Persistence never got the same treatment.

## Confirmed in current upstream

Checked against `upstream/main` at `b107c4996` (2026-11-15), **350 commits ahead** of the build that produced this:

- `MAX_LATE_USAGE_LEDGER_BYTES = 1024 * 1024` — unchanged.
- `flush_pending_usage_admitted(&id)?` — still fatal, at all three save paths.
- `write_late_usage_candidate` — same `if !original.overflowed` guard.
- No `records.retain` / `records.clear` / `records.pop` anywhere in the ledger code — no eviction added.

Updating the binary does not fix this.

## Suggested fix

Make the ledger write non-fatal for persistence, and give the ledger a way out of the corner:

1. **Do not fail the save on a ledger error.** Log it with its code, write the conversation, and let the receipt say cost is unknown. Same shape as the settlement path already uses (`tracing::warn!(%error, "provider usage settlement failed; the turn continues")`). A local accounting sidecar must not block transcript persistence.
2. **Make the degradation path reachable.** The `overflowed` fallback only fires once; after that the ledger is stuck. Either allow rewriting a marked-empty ledger when the bound is hit, or drop settled records that are provably no longer replayable — the same trade-off #6842 is deciding, which is why this can be a small, safe slice rather than a redesign.
3. **Surface it once, not every save.** 184 identical checkpoint warnings in twenty minutes is noise; one operator-visible notice naming the ledger and the remedy is enough.

## Workaround for an affected session

The ledger is a per-session sidecar, `~/.codewhale/sessions/.late-usage/<session_id>.json`. Moving it aside (`mv … .bak`) makes the next save succeed again. That file is the spend-dedupe record, so the cost of the workaround is that a replayed usage receipt for this session can be counted twice — which is exactly the risk #6842 is deciding about. It is a stopgap for a stuck session, not a fix.

## Related

- #6842 — owns bounding the usage replay index without losing spend deduplication. This issue is the failure-mode half.
- #7348 — the same "bookkeeping must not block the product" principle, at the turn-dispatch layer.
- `bc3ad117e` — made usage-settlement failure non-fatal for the turn; persistence still lacks the equivalent.
- `CHANGELOG.md` 0.10.3 — "Turns no longer fail on a cost bookkeeping error".

issues.title: Named-turn undo reads the whole turn store twice before forking

labels.name: area:tui
labels.description: Terminal UI behavior, rendering, or interaction

labels.name: area:state
labels.description: Sessions, persistence and the state store

issues.body:
## Summary

`/undo` with a `turn_id` resolves the named anchor by loading every turn and every item of the thread, then calls the generic fork preparation, which loads the same turns and items a second time. A fork of a 200-turn thread opens 400 turn files where the depth-based fork opens 200.

## Environment

Codewhale 0.10.2 at commit 6391f4f307040851fca29d679d3c05a985828a54, local runtime store, 200-turn conversation (400 stored items).

## Expected behavior

The named-turn path already has the turns and items in memory when it resolves the anchor; the fork preparation should reuse them instead of re-reading the store. One whole-store pass per fork.

## Actual behavior

Both operations ran against the same 200-turn thread at the same commit. File opens were counted per phase.

| operation | turn-file opens | item-file opens | wall time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| depth-based fork (drops 100 tail turns) | 200 | 598 | 379 ms |
| named-turn undo (drops turn 100 and later) | 400 | 1,000 | 601 ms |

The named path reads twice as many turn records and about 1.7x as many item records for the same thread.

## Root cause

`fork_dropping_user_turn_in_sessions_dir` first calls `list_turns_for_thread` and `prepared_items_for_turns` to resolve the turn id through `fork_cut_for_user_turn`, then calls `prepare_fork_at_user_message_in_sessions_dir`, which calls `list_turns_for_thread` and `prepared_items_for_turns` again (crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs:13037-13051 and :13120-13160).

## Suggested fix

Pass the already loaded `turns` and `items_by_turn` (or the resolved cut index) into a preparation variant, for example `prepare_fork_at_cutoff_in_sessions_dir`, so the preparation does not re-read the store. The public depth and named-turn paths can then share one preparation that takes the loaded prefix.

## Impact

Every named-turn undo pays two full store passes instead of one. On stores with tens of thousands of items — the case the one-pass item helpers were introduced for — that is seconds of avoidable reads per undo, and it also extends how long the global admission guard is held.

issues.body:
## Summary

Forking a conversation by turn id (`/undo` with `turn_id`, and the retry endpoint) takes the manager-wide session admission guard and keeps it while the fork is prepared: the turn and item records are read, the source session document is captured and the fork is published. Because the guard is global, a fork of one conversation blocks restore, config and session operations on every other conversation for the fork's whole duration.

## Environment

Codewhale 0.10.2 at commit 6391f4f307040851fca29d679d3c05a985828a54, local runtime store, conversation with 1,200 user turns (2,400 stored items).

## Expected behavior

The admission guard should cover only the mutation that must be exclusive — resolving the cut and publishing the fork — not the read-only preparation and session copy. Acquiring the restore guard for an unrelated thread should not wait for a fork of another thread.

## Actual behavior

A named-turn fork of a 1,200-turn thread and, 20 ms later, a `thread_restore_guard` for a different thread:

| operation | duration |
| --- | --- |
| named-turn fork (1,200 turns) | 5,489 ms (4,237 ms in an earlier run) |
| restore guard for an unrelated thread | 5,468 ms (4,212 ms in the earlier run) |

The unrelated thread waited 99.6% of the fork's duration. The guard is manager-wide, so no restore or config reload could proceed while one conversation's fork was being prepared.

## Root cause

`fork_dropping_user_turn_in_sessions_dir` (crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs:13037) and `retry_thread_turn` (crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs:8687) call `thread_restore_guard`, which takes `session_checkpoint_guard` — a single `RwLock` owned by the manager, not by the thread — and move the owned guard into the worker that calls `prepare_fork_at_user_message_in_sessions_dir` and `publish_prepared_fork`. The preparation reads `list_turns_for_thread`, `prepared_items_for_turns` and captures the session document inside the guarded scope.

## Suggested fix

Narrow the guarded scope: resolve the cut and publish under admission, but read the turns/items and capture the session copy outside it. Alternatively key admission by thread id (or by session document) so a fork of thread A cannot block a restore of thread B. If the session document is the resource that needs exclusion, take the guard only around the document write.

## Impact

Every named-turn undo or retry on a large conversation stalls unrelated restores and configuration reloads for seconds. A desktop client and a CLI attached to the same runtime serialize behind one conversation's fork; the larger the conversation, the longer the stall.

issues.body:
### Summary

The prompt conformance family (`crates/tui/tests/fixtures/conformance/prompt/`) cannot pass on a host that has the optional host-probed tools installed. The pin file the check compares against — `host_probed_tools.golden.json` — has never existed in this repository, and nothing records it.

The `events` family does not have this problem, because it pins the recorded host's tool set before running. The `prompt` family does not pin, so its result depends on what the runner happens to have installed.

### The two families are not symmetric

`crates/tui/src/conformance/events.rs:300` pins the recorded host before the turn runs:

```rust
let _host_tools = codewhale_dependencies::pin_recorded_host_tools(recorded_host_tools(case));
```

`recorded_host_tools` reads `recorded_platform.host_tools` from the case file, and `pin_recorded_host_tools` (`crates/dependencies/src/lib.rs:396-412`) makes `host_tool_available` (`:375-388`) answer from that set for the thread. So every events case reproduces the recording host regardless of what the runner has — the events goldens do contain `image_ocr` and `pandoc_convert` even though the machines running them need not have tesseract or pandoc.

The prompt family has no equivalent:

```
$ git grep -n 'pin_recorded_host_tools\|recorded_platform' -- crates/tui/src/conformance/prompt.rs
(no output)
```

`capture_prefix` therefore records whatever the current host produced, because the catalog consults the live probe at `crates/tui/src/core/engine/tool_catalog.rs:308`, `:350` and `crates/tui/src/tools/registry.rs:1126`, `:1141`.

### What that produces

`crates/tui/src/conformance/prompt.rs:223-245` compares every host-probed definition this host produced against the pin:

```rust
let probed_path = dir.join("host_probed_tools.golden.json");
let mut pinned: BTreeMap<String, Value> = std::fs::read_to_string(&probed_path)
    .ok()
    .and_then(|text| serde_json::from_str(&text).ok())
    .unwrap_or_default();
let mut drift = Vec::new();
for (tool, definition) in &probed_seen {
    if pinned.get(tool) != Some(definition) {
        drift.push(tool.clone());
        pinned.insert(tool.clone(), definition.clone());
    }
}
if !drift.is_empty() {
    let merged = Value::Object(pinned.into_iter().collect());
    failures.record(
        "host_probed_tools",
        golden::check_golden(&probed_path, &golden::pretty(&merged))...
    );
}
```

The file has never existed at any commit on any ref:

```
$ git log --all --diff-filter=ADR --name-status -- '*host_probed_tools*'
(no output)
```

And none of the three prompt goldens contain any of the four tool names, so the fixtures were recorded on a host that offered none of them:

```
agent_suggest.tools.golden.json                 code_execution=no image_ocr=no js_execution=no pandoc_convert=no
plan_mode.tools.golden.json                     code_execution=no image_ocr=no js_execution=no pandoc_convert=no
trusted_project_instructions.tools.golden.json  code_execution=no image_ocr=no js_execution=no pandoc_convert=no
```

On a host with none of the four, the loop is empty, `drift` stays empty, the check is skipped (it prints `host cannot offer [...]; their pinned definitions were not checked`), and the family passes. On a host with any of them, `drift` is non-empty on the first run and `check_golden` (`crates/tui/src/conformance/golden.rs:66-91`) returns `missing golden ...` outside update mode. The family fails.

Re-recording does not resolve it durably. `CODEWHALE_CONFORMANCE_UPDATE=1` would write the *local* tool definitions into the pin, and those are version-dependent — a pandoc 2.x description and a pandoc 3.x description are different bytes — so the next contributor's machine drifts again, and the goldens become a function of whoever recorded last.

### The case files describe a host that did not do the recording

All nine case files carrying a `recorded_platform` block (six under `events/`, three under `prompt/`) declare the identical block:

```json
"recorded_platform": {
  "recorded_on": "macOS",
  "os": "macos",
  "shell": "/bin/bash",
  "sandbox_enforcement": "local_os",
  "no_new_privs_active": null,
  "host_tools": ["code_execution", "image_ocr", "js_execution", "pandoc_convert"]
}
```

For the events family this is live data and it does its job. For the prompt family it is inert — `prompt.rs` never reads it — and it contradicts the recordings, which plainly happened without those tools. So the field is misleading precisely where it is unused.

### Why this has not surfaced

No workflow runs this suite. The only `conformance` hit under `.github/workflows` is `pet.yml`, which is `workflow_dispatch`-only and exercises the Kotlin/Swift port under `pet/`. `CODEWHALE_CONFORMANCE_UPDATE` appears nowhere under `.github`, and `.gitignore` does not exclude the missing fixture. So the failure is only reachable by a contributor who runs the suite locally on a machine with those tools installed.

### Reproducing

On a machine with `pandoc`, `tesseract`, `node` and `python` on `PATH`:

```
$ cargo test -p codewhale-tui model_visible_prefix_bytes_match_goldens
```

The prompt cases fail on `host_probed_tools` with `missing golden .../host_probed_tools.golden.json`. On a machine with none of the four, the same command passes.

```
$ git log --all --diff-filter=ADR --name-status -- '*host_probed_tools*'
$ git grep -n 'pin_recorded_host_tools\|recorded_platform' -- crates/tui/src/conformance/prompt.rs
```

### Notes

* I am not proposing a fix. The two obvious directions — pin the prompt family the way events does, or drop the host-probed comparison from the prompt family — change different things about what the prompt goldens are supposed to guarantee, and that is a maintainer decision rather than a patch.
* Unrelated to #7153, which is about streaming during compaction.

issues.body:
A read-through of the engine, tools, util and repl crates found the following crashes, hangs and wrong outputs. Each one gets its own small PR, and this issue tracks them.

### Crashes and hangs

- [ ] **Retry config panic.** Setting `[retry] jitter = false, max_delay = -1` panics on the first transport retry, in `Duration::from_secs_f64(-1.0)` inside `RetryConfig::delay_for_attempt`. A negative value should be rejected when the config loads.
- [ ] **Exponential glob matching.** `matches_simple_glob` in `tools/search.rs` backtracks exponentially. An include pattern such as `*a*a*a*a*a*a*a*a*a*a*b`, matched against a file name of 40 `a`s, takes on the order of 10^8 recursive calls per file.
- [ ] **Patch hunks lose lines.** `parse_hunk_header` in `crates/tools/src/patch_preflight.rs` stops reading after `2*(old+new)` lines.
  - An under-counted hunk silently loses its later lines.
  - `@@ -1,18446744073709551615 +1,1 @@` overflows.

### Wrong output

- [ ] **`env -S` shebangs.** A plugin script starting `#!/usr/bin/env -S python3 -u` spawns a program named `-S`. Expected: run `python3 -u`.
- [ ] **Summaries that fit get an ellipsis.** `summarize_text` in `runtime_threads/manager.rs` appends `...` to text that already fits. For example, `"abcdefgh"` with a limit of 10 becomes `"abcdefg..."`. `task_manager.rs` has a byte-identical copy.
- [ ] **Non-ASCII file names collide.** `rlm::session::derive_session_name` keeps only ASCII letters and digits. `报告.txt` and `总结.txt` both become `txt`, so the second `rlm_open` fails with "already exists".
- [ ] **HTML entities decoded twice.** Web fetch and `web.run` text decode entities twice, so `&lt;b&gt;` comes out as `<b>` instead of `<b>`.
- [ ] **Context window labels.** `format_context_window` prints `1.50M` instead of `1.5M`, and `2.10M` instead of `2.1M`.
- [ ] **REPL output limit.** REPL `truncate_stdout` caps output by chars rather than bytes, so CJK output can be up to 3 times the intended limit.

Use release-blocker for the unresolved repair/qualification gates. issues.body:
Refs #4785

A dead-code sweep found these items. Each one is either never produced or only reached from tests. They were not removed because each looks like the start of a feature, and someone needs to decide whether to finish it or delete it. Every claim below was checked with `grep -rn` across `crates/` on current `main`.

**1. `SidebarRowAction::PrefillCommand` is never created (crates/tui/src/tui/app.rs:1289)**
- What happens: the variant is matched in `mouse_ui.rs:898` and `mouse_ui.rs:1643`. The only constructor (`mouse_ui.rs:1650`) re-wraps a value that is already a `PrefillCommand`. No sidebar row ever starts out as one, so the destructive-command "prefill, then press Enter" path cannot be reached. The allow comment cites TUI-DOG-008, but that ID is about working/phase chrome (`docs/MOTION_CONTRACT.md:25`), not this path.
- Expected: either a destructive sidebar row produces `PrefillCommand`, or the variant and its two match arms are removed.

**2. `FleetListOutcome::OpenDetail` / `FleetListOutcome::None` are never created (crates/tui/src/tui/views/fleet_list.rs:46-55)**
- What happens: `select_highlighted` and `confirm_delete` only return `FleetListOutcome::Done`. `outcome_to_action` (line 602) maps `OpenDetail` to `ViewEvent::FleetListOpenDetailRequested`, and `ui/handlers.rs:2582` handles that event by opening `FleetDetailView`. That whole chain cannot run. The allow says it is "reserved for the qualified-name flow".
- Expected: wire the qualified-name flow so selecting a fleet can open its detail view, or remove `OpenDetail`, `None`, `ViewEvent::FleetListOpenDetailRequested` and its handler.

**3. `RunReceipt` / `VerificationReceipt` / `VerificationOutcome` are only used by tests (crates/engine/src/core/runtime_contract/termination.rs:111-165)**
- What happens: no non-test code outside `termination.rs` names these types. `RunReceipt::validate` and `RunReceipt::pass_at_one` run only in that file's tests. The removed module allow said that "stream JSON is the first consumer", but no stream JSON code builds a `RunReceipt`.
- Expected: emit a run receipt from the stream-JSON / exec surface, or delete the types and their tests.

**4. `SkillMutationReceipt.before_digest` / `after_digest` are written but never read (crates/skills/src/mutation.rs:113-116)**
- What happens: every mutation path fills both fields (mutation.rs:615-994), and a TUI test builds them as `None` (`tui/src/commands/contract.rs:7038`). No code reads either field. The allow says "reserved for digest-diff UI". `action` on the same struct has a similar "future receipt toast" allow.
- Expected: show the digest diff in the skills manager / receipt toast, or stop computing and storing the digests.

**5. Fleet ledger/scheduler/executor functions only reached from tests (crates/engine/src/fleet/)**
- `ledger.rs:1770 FleetLedger::claim_next`: only callers are tests (ledger.rs:3306, 3401)
- `ledger.rs:1533 FleetLedger::record_alert`: only caller is a test (ledger.rs:4453)
- `ledger.rs:788 FleetLedger::mark_task_terminal_status_if_unchanged`: only caller is a test (ledger.rs:3707)
- `scheduler.rs:107 FleetScheduler::cancel_run`: only caller is a test (scheduler.rs:1048)
- `executor.rs:1150 all_terminal`: only callers are tests (executor.rs:2016, 2303)
- `task_spec.rs:617 record_verification_receipt`: only caller is a test (task_spec.rs:1393)
- `roster.rs:729 shadowed_for`: only caller is a test (fleet/tests/roster_shadow_and_trust.rs:38)

What happens: `ledger.rs`, `scheduler.rs` and `executor.rs` have `#![allow(dead_code)]` for the whole module. `task_spec.rs` and `roster.rs` items are `pub`. In both cases the compiler does not flag these functions. Production code claims tasks, cancels runs and records verification some other way, or does not do it yet.
Expected: for each function, either route the production path through it (for example operator cancel → `cancel_run`, alert delivery → `record_alert`), or move it under `#[cfg(test)]` / delete it. Then drop the module-level allows so new dead code shows up again.

issues.title: Deny rules miss hash -p / zsh =cmd rebinding, aliases run through eval, and the parallel, chpst, screen and at launchers

labels.name: area:sandbox
labels.description: Sandbox, container, or OS-level isolation behavior

labels.name: os:macos
labels.description: macOS-specific behaviour

labels.name: area:core
labels.description: Engine core: turn loop, agent loop, runtime

issues.body:
### What happened?

Deny rules (`denied_prefixes`, typed `Deny` rules and `execpolicy.toml` `deny`) are matched against the command lines `shell_expand` finds, and `tests/shell_parse_policy.rs` keeps a list of spellings that must stay denied. These spellings run a denied command and are allowed today, including under `AskForApproval::Never`, with a deny rule for `rm`:

| command | why it runs `rm` |
| --- | --- |
| `alias qq='rm -rf'; eval qq /` | zsh (the default `$SHELL` on macOS, which Codewhale runs commands with) expands aliases in code it parses later, such as an `eval`; the alias value is code |
| `hash -p /bin/rm r; r x` | bash: `hash -p PATH NAME` makes `NAME` run `PATH` |
| `hash qq=/bin/rm; qq x` | the zsh spelling of the same |
| `=rm x` | zsh `=cmd` expansion replaces the word with the path of `rm` |
| `parallel rm ::: x`, `parallel 'rm {}' ::: x` | GNU parallel runs its command (through a shell) |
| `chpst -u nobody rm x` | runit's launcher, like `setpriv` / `runuser` |
| `screen -dmS s rm x` | runs its operands as a command |
| `at now <<< 'rm x'`, `echo 'rm x' \| batch` | `at` / `batch` run a script read from stdin, like `sh <<< …` (already treated as dynamic) |

Repro (`crates/execpolicy`):

```rust
let engine = ExecPolicyEngine::new(vec![], vec!["rm".into()]);
let decision = engine.check(ExecPolicyContext {
    command: "hash -p /bin/rm r; r x",
    cwd: "/workspace", tool: Some("exec_shell"), path: None,
    ask_for_approval: AskForApproval::Never, sandbox_mode: None,
}).unwrap();
assert!(!decision.allow); // allowed on main
```

The module's known limits already cover script files, interpreters (`python -c`) and aliases defined in an *earlier* call. (Verified with `echo` in place of `rm`: `zsh -f -c` and `/bin/bash -c` on macOS.) These rows are same-call rebinding and launchers of the kind the wrapper table already lists (`pkexec`, `xvfb-run`, `eatmydata`, …).

### Expected

Each row is denied. A small fix in `shell_expand`: treat `alias NAME=VALUE` / zsh `hash NAME=PATH` values and the `PATH` of `hash -p` as code, mark a command word starting with `=` as only known at run time, add `chpst`, `parallel` and `screen` to the wrapper table (with `parallel` joining its operands like `watch`), and read `at` / `batch` stdin the way a shell's stdin is read. Ordinary uses (`alias ll='ls -la'`, `hash -r`, `parallel echo ::: a b`) stay allowed.

Still out of scope (unchanged): `tmux new 'cmd'` / `tmux send-keys`, `screen -X stuff`, and other programs that take keystrokes or code strings in their own syntax.

### Version

`main` at 4b8a30009 (0.10.3 source).

issues.title: Secret redaction misses provider keys written next to Chinese text or full-width punctuation
issues.body:
### What happened?

The bare-token pass of `redact_secrets` / `redact_model_bound_secrets` (`crates/sanitize/src/redact.rs`, also the last step of `sanitize_text`) only looks at words split on ASCII spaces, and only trims ASCII punctuation from them. Chinese and Japanese text does not put spaces around a key, so a provider key written in CJK prose is never masked, and a key followed by CJK text takes that text with it:

| input | `redact_secrets` on `main` |
| --- | --- |
| `密钥：sk-Z7qX4mNb2Vc9Lk3PwR8t` | unchanged (key leaks) |
| `我的密钥是sk-Z7qX4mNb2Vc9Lk3PwR8t` | unchanged |
| `（ghp_Z7qX4mNb2Vc9Lk3PwR8tZ7qX4mNb2Vc9）` | unchanged |
| `「sk-…」`, `key　sk-…` (U+3000 ideographic space) | unchanged |
| `令牌eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxIn0.c2lnbmF0dXJl` | unchanged |
| `sk-Z7qX4mNb2Vc9Lk3PwR8t，然后重试` | `[redacted]` (the following Chinese text is lost) |

The same words separated by an ASCII space (`key sk-…`, `(ghp_…)`) are masked today, so this is a gap in the word split rather than in the token shapes. These functions are the backstop for tool output sent to the model, logs, exports and diagnostics.

### Steps to reproduce

```rust
use codewhale_sanitize::redact::redact_secrets;
let key = ["sk-", "Z7qX4mNb2Vc9Lk3PwR8t"].concat();
assert_eq!(redact_secrets(&format!("密钥：{key}")), "密钥：[redacted]"); // fails: unchanged
```

### Expected

Every credential-shaped ASCII run inside a word is masked on its own, and the surrounding CJK text and full-width punctuation are kept: `密钥：[redacted]`, `[redacted]，然后重试`, `甲[redacted]乙[redacted]`. Credential tokens are ASCII, so splitting a word at non-ASCII characters before the existing checks finds them without changing what counts as a token.

Not covered here: keyed assignments that use a full-width colon with a non-prefixed value (`password：hunter2`) and Chinese key names (`密码=…`); those need vocabulary decisions, not a split fix.

### Version

`main` at 4b8a30009 (0.10.3 source).

issues.title: Network deny entries with internationalized domain names never match

labels.name: area:sandbox
labels.description: Sandbox, container, or OS-level isolation behavior

labels.name: area:state
labels.description: Sessions, persistence and the state store

issues.body:
### What happened?

A `[network]` deny entry written with a non-ASCII domain never denies anything (`crates/net/src/network_policy.rs`).

Hosts reach the policy from `host_from_url` / `Url::host_str`, which returns the ASCII (punycode) form, but `normalize_host` only lowercases ASCII. An entry written the way people type it never matches:

| entry | URL | host seen by `decide` | result on `main` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `deny = ["例子.com"]` | `https://例子.com/` | `xn--fsqu00a.com` | not denied |
| `deny = ["*.中国"]` | `https://www.例子.中国/` | `www.xn--fsqu00a.xn--fiqs8s` | not denied |
| `deny = ["BÜCHER.de"]` | `https://bücher.de/` | `xn--bcher-kva.de` | not denied |

With `default = "allow"` these requests go through; with `prompt` the user is asked about a host they denied. `/network deny 例子.com` writes exactly such an entry. Allow entries have the mirror problem (they never match).

### Expected

Entries and hosts are compared in the same form: `normalize_host` converts a non-ASCII entry to its IDNA ASCII form (the URL parser already does this for hosts), keeping the `*.` / `.` wildcard prefix.

### Version

`main` at 4b8a30009 (0.10.3 source).

issues.title: Git status hides the source of a rename that leaves the workspace from the worktree side
issues.body:
### What happened?

`split_by_workspace` in `crates/app-server/src/runtime_api/git.rs` projects repository-root rows into the workspace frame. When a rename leaves the workspace, it synthesizes a `deleted` row so the source is still visible inside the workspace, but the guard for that is `row.index == "R"`.

Since #7310 the parser also returns a **worktree-side** rename, whose index column is a space. For that shape the guard is false, so the source path — which really has disappeared from the workspace — appears in no row of `GET /v1/git` or `GET /v1/changes` at all. The index-side equivalent shows a `deleted` row.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
git init -q -b main r && cd r
mkdir sub && echo one > sub/a.txt
git add . && git commit -qm init
git mv sub/a.txt outside.txt
git reset -q
git add -N outside.txt
git status --porcelain=v1 -z | od -c    # " R outside.txt\0sub/a.txt\0"
ls sub/a.txt                            # gone from the worktree
git ls-files sub                        # still sub/a.txt in the index
```

Open the workspace at `sub/` and request `GET /v1/git` or `GET /v1/changes`. `detail.files` is empty: `a.txt` is not listed, although it no longer exists in the workspace. With `git mv sub/a.txt outside.txt` and no reset, the same request returns one row for `a.txt` with `index = "D"`, `status = "deleted"`.

### Expected

The source is listed as a deletion in both cases. The column the change actually lives in differs, so the synthesized row should say so: a worktree-side rename deletes in the worktree (`worktree = "D"`, `staged = false`), and the index-side row keeps `index = "D"`, `staged = true`.

Staging safety is not weakened by the gap — the outside row still carries its root-relative `old_path` and `compute_tokens` covers it — so this is a listing gap, not a guard gap.

`C` should not synthesize a row at all: copying in either column leaves the source in place. Git reports a worktree copy as `A` in the first place (`-c status.renames=copies` still emits `A b.txt`), so that half is defensive only.

### Version

`main` at `f5a3dda97` (0.10.3 source).

## Attribution

🤖 Generated by SpikeBot 000(CodeWhale-LOCAL)

prs.title: fix(tui): bound completed-turn session snapshot waits
prs.body:
## What and why

When a queued turn starts before the preceding completion handler receives its Engine snapshot, the TUI can wait for the entire new turn without polling terminal input or rendering.

Bound the completed-turn snapshot request, including mailbox capacity and reply waits, to the existing two-second session confirmation budget. A timeout reports a localized pending-snapshot reason and leaves the recovery checkpoint in place. The existing source, owner, session, workspace and message guards still gate the completed-session commit. Snapshot read failures no longer also log an unverified source mismatch.

This bounds the snapshot wait to two seconds; snapshots are still served between Engine turns. The provider stream failures described in the report remain separate.

## Where this came from

Fixes #7357.

Thanks @7jrxt42BxFZo4iAnN4CX for the session timelines, control comparison and diagnosis of the unbounded snapshot wait.

## How I tested it

- Five focused TUI regressions passed on the final commit (**5 passed, 0 failed**): the new busy-Engine regression plus four existing startup and persistence regressions.
- The new test covers both a held snapshot reply and a full request mailbox, including rejection of a late reply. Existing tests cover Engine session installation, retaining the checkpoint after a failed save, clearing it only after a successful save, and a complete fresh-session persistence lifecycle.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `bash scripts/preflight.sh --check`, `python3 scripts/check-tui-locale-parity.py` and `git diff --check`: passed. All 15 complete locale packs include the new reason.

The new regression uses the existing mock Engine handle to hold the reply or fill the mailbox. It exercises the completion snapshot helper rather than a live provider turn or a full PTY session.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main`.
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior.
- [x] Bug fix; no new feature registry entry is needed.

prs.title: fix(subagent): inherit the session's reviewed memory in child prompts
prs.body:
## What and why

A sub-agent's system prompt now carries the session's reviewed native-memory packet and its `## Memory Hygiene` guidance, the same bytes the root session's prompt carries.

Today a child gets neither: `Engine::new_child_admitted` clears `memory_enabled`, and `host_owned_system_prompt()` returns the child's role prompt before the memory block is ever composed. So a rule the user pinned in Context Lens — "cloud deploys need your approval", "edit code in the dev directory, not the runtime directory" — binds the orchestrator and silently not the agent that actually edits files. The memory tools still work in a child, but `memory_search` is lexical and explicit pins only enter through the packet path, so pins never surface there either.

The fix is one seam: `build_subagent_system_prompt_with_skills` composes the packet from the inherited `ToolContext.memory_path` and appends it after the role contract, before the skill catalog. A shared helper `memory_prompt_section` (extracted from the root prompt's inline formatting, byte-identical output) guarantees parent and child never ship the packet without its guidance.

Design notes:
- The packet is re-composed, not copied out of the parent prompt: a memory edited mid-session reaches a later spawn, and an isolated worktree still resolves to the same workspace scope through its shared git remote.
- No `memory_enabled` flip: enabling it on the child would run session-start reconciliation under the root session id, duplicating a receipt and possibly reporting false interruptions.
- Memory keeps its existing standing — untrusted evidence, not an authority channel.
- Nothing is injected when memory is disabled, the store is empty, or every entry is reviewed off; a child records no context receipt of its own.

## Where this came from

Not tied to an issue. A behavior gap found while investigating why pinned rules did not reach sub-agents.

## How I tested it

- `scripts/dev-test.sh engine child_system_prompt` — 3 passed. Asserts one packet, pin ordering, guidance after the packet, role framing ahead of it, nested children inheriting through `runtime_for_nested_agent_tools`, and no envelope when memory is disabled / empty / reviewed off.
- `scripts/dev-test.sh engine memory_guidance` — 5 passed (root prompt behavior unchanged).
- `scripts/dev-test.sh engine 'tools::subagent::tests::'` — 620 passed with one failure, `late_launch_permit_still_gets_the_full_work_budget`, a wall-clock/HTTP-fixture test whose context carries no `memory_path`; it passes 3/3 alone and the whole module passes 621/621 with `--test-threads=1`.
- `scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-engine --lib`, `clippy -p codewhale-engine --lib --tests -- -D warnings` (exit 0), `cargo fmt --all -- --check`.
- `scripts/preflight.sh --check` — OK.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [x] `docs/MEMORY.md` and `docs/SUBAGENTS.md` describe the inheritance; the `memory` row in `docs/features.toml` already points at `docs/MEMORY.md`

prs.title: feat: source navigation echoes and guarded fork-prefix inheritance
prs.body:
Native `read` windows retain their revision guard through the final model-request projection. `grep_files` adds bounded Rust navigation hints, and forked agents retain eligible parent prefixes.

<details>
<summary>GPT 6.1 Sol 900k High</summary>

## Source and scope

Current head: [`db1390a64`](https://github.com/AdityaVG13/CodeWhale/commit/db1390a64445533dcc0285bd3f8499ca05695e76), incorporating the approved upstream snapshot [`1f9ad30c1`](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/1f9ad30c1f8ab5c94652d77e6bed512eb97a4cc2). Earlier integration commits, including `f46d406da`, remain ancestors. Original contributor commits and credit are preserved; this is a non-rewriting update of the existing PR branch.

There is no replacement turn loop, persistent source index or indexing daemon.

- Revision-qualified Rust references carry a path, source window and revision. Changed source is refused; guarded continuations require forward progress and retain snapshot identity.
- Focused Rust searches can supply bounded declaration windows and small complete bodies. Syntax-derived identifier and one-hop call-candidate hints are bounded evidence, not macro expansion, name resolution, type resolution or a complete impact graph. Broad/truncated searches retain their ordinary output.
- Native `grep_files` is eager beside file-name search. Child/scout/workflow fixtures retain current catalog, cache-budget and root-goal authority boundaries.
- Echoes are append-only tool/history evidence, not volatile additions to the pinned system/tool prefix. Host observations, current authority and evidence actually delivered to a model remain separate.
- Fork-prefix inheritance requires matching route/model/opaque receipt and a supported dialect. Unsupported or changed identities take the cold path; no live-provider cache saving is claimed.
- The skill index keeps eligible names enumerable without exposing mutable native skill paths. Workflow events retain task/workspace ownership.
- Execution-matched canonical reads retain their native envelope through final Chat Completions projection. Legacy, missing/mismatched execution identities and over-budget results retain the ordinary backstop. A source-looking footer is not authority.
- Finite headless turns receive a logged working-deadline notice while tools remain usable. Exhausted ordinary turns can deliver a final text report without falsely becoming successful; cancellation and the distinct goal-pause contract remain intact.
- Configuration help and its generated website copy now match the native reader: 50 KiB by default, at most 2,000 lines, 2,000-character line truncation and an operator-only byte override up to 2 MiB. The model has no `max_bytes` parameter. Raising the read budget does not disable ordinary spillover.

## Verification of the integrated engine

The selected engine library suite compiled through a remote RCH job on Linux/aarch64. Its initial run had **318 passing tests and one failing Rust-format normalization assertion**. With no source changes, rerunning the same compiled selection produced **319 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored**. Both outcomes are retained; the first failure is not relabeled as a pass and its cause is not established.

The selection covers echolocation, native reads and dispatch, guarded search, wire projection, deadline/admission/report-only fences, catalog deferral, fork-prefix and warmed-tool behavior, schema-cache admission limits, goal pause and the shared base-prompt previews. The committed tree is `0d0c9bb7c3296ef443f74fe3c0623a8f95722cc7`, identical to the staged tree used for the declared input manifest.

The RCH job executed this one-package Cargo command:

```sh
cargo test --locked -p codewhale-engine --lib -- \
  tools::echolocation:: \
  tools::file::tests:: \
  tools::file_tool::tests:: \
  tools::search::tests:: \
  client::chat::stream_decoder_tests:: \
  admission_gates:: \
  small_surface_ \
  model_tool_catalog_applies_native_and_mcp_deferral \
  capability_compact_surface_defers_nonessential_core_tools \
  capability_full_surface_preserves_small_default_head \
  goal_turn_uses_goal_step_allowance_and_pauses_budget_limit_after_final_report \
  eager_agent_and_workflow_stay_offered_without_search_rejection \
  forked_subagent_messages_preserve_parent_prefix_then_append_task \
  session_projection_exposes_forked_prefix_cache_contract \
  warmed_surfaces_rebuild_byte_identical_wire_tools \
  best_match_survives_byte_overflow_eviction \
  oversized_schema_is_never_admitted \
  prompts::base_preview::tests:: \
  --test-threads=1
```

DSR reported that `codewhale` is not configured when queried with `dsr quality --tool codewhale --dry-run`; RCH was the fallback. This is bounded declared-input verification, **not an exhaustive compiler-input or source-content receipt**. There was no local heavy compilation or full workspace test run.

Additional checks passed:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and integration-relative whitespace validation.
- Four selected existing website test files: **37 passed**.
- Website TypeScript and generated-facts validation. The published v0.10.2 tag is absent locally, so its committed baseline was retained rather than claiming it was recomputed.
- UBS on the edited prompt file: **0 critical, 0 warnings**, five informational findings. This is not a security-audit claim.

The integration retains upstream's version-aware tool rows, fetch deadlines, scheduled-handler checks and regenerated public facts alongside the PR's guarded-read and cache contracts. Upstream-only changes outside these selected areas were not exhaustively retested. No packaged release or native macOS/Windows acceptance is claimed.

## Native CLI admission of this head

A fresh Linux/aarch64 development CLI for the integrated candidate passed the unchanged standalone v3 scripted native probe on both cold and pre-seeded startup paths. It reports `codewhale 0.10.3 (dev)`; binary SHA-256: `d91f36e98227210c71cde32c4a91da2ac804cc90a948eb1a27c917b0fd2536f1`.

The RCH job built only `codewhale-cli` and exited 0. The declared **2,358 source and embedded inputs** matched before and after the build. The build began from the merge worktree before its commit was created: the original identity retains the pre-commit `f46d406da` metadata, while the manifest records the verified merge tree `0d0c9bb7c3296ef443f74fe3c0623a8f95722cc7` subsequently committed as `db1390a64`. This is a bounded input manifest, not an exhaustive compiler-input receipt.

- A **101,904-byte** native read reached the final provider request byte-for-byte in both cases.
- All **five negative guards** rejected source/test mutations, a nonempty writer lease, an extra runtime file and an unlocked foreign descriptor.
- Both cases preserved the complete post-startup workspace snapshot and retained `failed / budget_exhausted` for intentionally exhausted turns.
- Four scripted loopback requests were used, with **zero live-provider requests**. The loopback listener is closed and both native processes have exited.

The probe sets an explicit 128,000-byte operator read budget and requests a 1,940-line window of an existing frozen file. It retains the greater-than-100,000-byte assertion and stays below the unchanged classic 100 KiB spillover threshold. Earlier failed default-budget and spillover attempts remain failures, not passing receipts. This developer-build proof does not establish live task quality, packaged-release acceptance or native macOS/Windows acceptance.

## Still draft: task-quality gates

This merge integrates the fixed, approved `1f9ad30c1` snapshot, including its website removals. It does not automatically track subsequent upstream changes or claim mergeability against a moving base. The shared base prompt now explicitly restricts tool recommendations to tools offered in the current request. That is a new source condition, not evidence that earlier prompt wording caused a particular model choice.

This remains draft in accordance with [the contributor's scope decision](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6393#issuecomment-6207193232). Earlier failed and incomplete comparisons remain in [the maintained progress record](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6393#issuecomment-6185897898) and [the previous findings](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6393#issuecomment-6524708140).

Earlier live controls remain unqualified. An unchanged earlier answer later passed the behavior oracle offline using retained grading dependencies; that diagnosis does not retroactively qualify its stopped paid block. Grading dependencies are now hash-pinned outside mutable worker build pools.

A fresh fixed-order screen on this exact executable qualified both controls, then stopped on its first treatment. All three submitted repairs passed the unchanged behavior oracle, preserved existing tests and source-write boundaries, used only allowed tools, and reconciled usage without new uncertain requests.

| Slot | Native outcome | Behavioral oracle | Elapsed seconds | Cost upper bound, USD |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| `none_execute_8` | Completed; qualified | Pass | 103.628877 | 0.047872212 |
| `none_fileops_8` | Completed; qualified | Pass | 37.960547 | 0.017406456 |
| `full_execute_8` | Failed: 16 working model steps exhausted; unqualified | Pass | 139.475011 | 0.081516144 |

The treatment delivered a final report but correctly retained `failed / budget_exhausted`; a correct repair is not equivalent to completing within the frozen runtime allowance. The remaining three slots did not run. There were no paid retries or substitutions. Two earlier launcher failures forwarded zero provider requests and remain recorded separately.

The three executed slots made 41 provider requests with an aggregate cost upper bound of **$0.146794812**. The cumulative campaign upper bound is **$3.079885524 of $5**, including the retained historical unresolved reservation. These are ledger upper bounds, not invoices. The prior ledger prefix is unchanged; the gateway and all three native processes exited, and its forwarding port was independently checked closed.

This is not a positive efficiency result: on the execute task, the full treatment took longer, cost more, and failed the completion gate while its control qualified. It is one observation per executed slot, not a general causal result. None of the three attempts used a revision-qualified read. Provider/model, prompt bytes for the matched task, tool-schema hash and executable identity matched; request-prefix checks were stable. These observations neither establish guarded-reference adoption nor measure live fork-cache economics.

No general task-quality improvement, speedup, cost reduction, guarded-reference adoption, live-provider cache saving, independent quality review or merge readiness is claimed. Fresh controls must qualify before any fixed-order treatment; earlier answers are not retried or substituted for successful trials. There are no live fork-cache trials in this six-slot block; selected local prefix tests do not establish provider cache economics.

Refs #6393, CW-6439

</details>

[0.8.39] - 2026-05-17

Fixed

  • Feishu/Lark bridge startup order is guarded. The bridge now keeps ThreadStore initialized before startup opens persisted thread state, with a regression test to prevent moving it below its first use.
  • /model picker opens instantly with the curated list again. Reverted the v0.8.38 live-catalog rework: the picker no longer makes a blocking network call on open and once again shows the curated auto / deepseek-v4-pro / deepseek-v4-flash rows. The /models command still lists the live provider catalog.
  • "Approve for session" groups by command family again. Session approvals are keyed by a lossy, arity-aware fingerprint once more, so approving cargo build also covers cargo build --release. Denials keep the exact per-call fingerprint from #1617, so denying one call no longer over-blocks later, different calls to the same tool.
  • Docker first-run state directories are writable. The image now pre-creates /home/deepseek/.deepseek with deepseek ownership so the documented named-volume launch can create runtime thread state on first use (#1684).
  • Runtime API system prompt overrides survive the first turn. Threads created with a system_prompt override now keep that prompt through mode/context refreshes before the model request is built (#1688).
  • Compaction keeps a user text query in tool-heavy histories. Automatic compaction now pins the latest user text message when the retained tail only contains tool calls/results, avoiding OpenAI-compatible Jinja template failures on the next request (#1704).
  • Pager jumps land at the visible bottom. Pressing G or End in the pager no longer overshoots the render clamp, so k/Up scrolls upward immediately afterward, and mouse wheels now scroll pager overlays directly (#1706, #1716).
  • Mouse-wheel-as-arrow scrolling preserves composer drafts. When composer_arrows_scroll is enabled, Up/Down now scroll the transcript even with text in the composer instead of replacing the draft with input history (#1677).
  • Multiline composer arrows move between input lines. Plain Up/Down now move the cursor within multiline drafts before falling back to input history, while single-line mouse-wheel-as-arrow scrolling remains unchanged (#1721).
  • Third-party reasoning_content streams no longer corrupt text output. Generic OpenAI-compatible providers that stream answer text in reasoning_content now render it as normal text unless the selected provider is one whose reasoning-content semantics are supported (#1673).
  • macOS system theme detection recognizes Light mode. When COLORFGBG is missing or unusable, theme = "system" now falls back to macOS appearance detection and treats a missing AppleInterfaceStyle key as Light mode

prs.title: fix(client): decide the reasoning dialect by endpoint, not by model id
prs.body:
## What and why

A provider row with `kind = "openai-compatible"` (the `custom` identity) that
carries a DeepSeek model id was sent DeepSeek's native `thinking` object on
`/v1/chat/completions`. `apply_route_reasoning_controls` promoted any `custom`
route whose model name matched `requires_reasoning_content` to the `deepseek`
provider kind, and that promotion was unconditional — it never looked at the
endpoint.

Aggregating gateways reject the field. Against a new-api style distributor:

```
400 invalid_request_error  param: "thinking"  code: "unsupported_parameter"
"thinking" is not supported on /v1/chat/completions and was not applied.
Use "reasoning_effort" (or "***.effort") to control thinking.
```

An OpenAI-compatible endpoint's request dialect is not knowable from the model
id alone. That is why every other gateway identity in `reasoning_effort.rs`
(`telecomjs`, `zenmux`, `edenai`, `csdn`, `custom`) already writes neither
`thinking` nor `reasoning_effort`; the `custom` row escaped that policy through
this one promotion.

The promotion stays, because forwarding the configured effort is what `008d21d69`
added it for — custom DeepSeek routes were silently dropping it. What changes is
that the dialect is now decided by the **endpoint**:

- a route labeled `deepseek` speaks DeepSeek's dialect (unchanged);
- a `custom` row pointed at one of DeepSeek's own hosts speaks it too, and keeps
  the native toggle;
- a `custom` row pointed anywhere else keeps the documented `reasoning_effort`
  spelling and loses the native `thinking` object.

`off` on that last kind of route is sent as `reasoning_effort: "none"`, the
compatibility spelling this repository already maps `off` to for other
compatible routes. On the gateway this was verified against, `none` stopped
thinking (`reasoning_tokens: 0`, no reasoning field) rather than merely omitting
the control. This also keeps the reasoning-replay gate self-consistent: it skips
`reasoning_content` for `off`, so sending no control at all would have left a
gateway that forwards to DeepSeek seeing thinking-on with no replayed reasoning
on assistant tool turns.

`a610a8602` fixes a regression the first commit introduced, found by review
before this PR was opened: `translate_prepared_with_usage` passed
`self.api_provider` instead of `chat_shape_provider`, so the named DS4 route (an
`openai-compatible` row that implements the first-party DeepSeek dialect) lost
`thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` on its translation requests. Both Chat
Completions call sites now agree on `chat_shape_provider`.

A note on the history: `c0b848807`'s message says the gateway cleanup "used to
sit before nine other shapers". That count is wrong. The correct figure is 11
shaper calls after the original position (local_reasoning, modelstudio, minimax,
inkling, openai, xai, direct_moonshot_k3, kimi_code_k3, zai, mistral, google),
of which 7 write or remove `thinking` (counting the generic effort layer makes 8).
The message is not amended because this fork does not force-push shared refs;
this paragraph is the correction. The code is unaffected either way: the cleanup
is now the function's last statement.

Known limitations, all stated in the code or below rather than discovered later:

- `none` handling depends on the gateway. One that validates the field fails
  loudly; one that silently ignores unknown values falls back to its own default
  while the replay gate skips `reasoning_content`. This mapping is only
  self-consistent on gateways that implement `none`.
- A row declared `kind = "deepseek"` and pointed at a gateway still sends
  `thinking`. That label is the operator stating "this is DeepSeek"; adding
  endpoint awareness to it would change every existing `[providers.deepseek]`
  mirror config, so it is out of scope here.
- `api.deepseeki.com` is in the host set on purpose. `docs/REBRAND.md` records it
  as a historical typo kept for existing configs, and the strict-tools and
  Responses paths accept it too — being inconsistent would make one host DeepSeek
  for those and not for reasoning.
- A `custom` row on an official host written as `http://` (or with a trailing
  dot in the FQDN) now falls into the gateway branch. Narrow, and consistent with
  how `deepseek_base_url_supports_strict_tools` already matches.
- `reasoning_content` replay on assistant tool turns is still keyed on the model
  name for these routes. That predates this change and is deliberate: a gateway
  that forwards to DeepSeek needs it. A gateway that validates message bodies
  strictly could still reject it.

## Where this came from

A bug fix with no issue — reported directly, reproduced against the gateway
before the change.

## How I tested it

Each test below fails against the code before its commit.

```
cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib client::tests::openai_compatible_gateway_gets_no_deepseek_thinking_dialect_from_a_model_name
cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib client::tests::a_custom_row_on_the_official_deepseek_host_keeps_the_thinking_toggle
cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib client::tests::a_lookalike_host_does_not_inherit_the_deepseek_dialect
cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib client::tests::the_deepseek_identity_keeps_its_thinking_toggle
cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib client::tests::deepseek_chat_wire_body_tracks_the_documented_effort_ladder
cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib client::ds4_tests::named_ds4_translation_keeps_the_disabled_thinking_toggle
cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib client::ds4_tests::a_gateway_translation_asks_for_none_instead_of_the_thinking_toggle

test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed    (each of the seven)
```

Beyond running them, each assertion was checked by breaking the code it covers
and confirming the test goes red:

- forcing `is_deepseek_chat_host` to `false` → both host-decision tests fail
  (`left: None`, expected `Some("disabled")`);
- deleting `rsplit('@')` → the userinfo case fails;
- deleting `split(':')` → the port case fails;
- making the `none` injection unconditional → the `auto` case fails
  (`left: Some("none")`, expected `None`).

Whole-module run, with the local HTTP proxy unset so mock-server loopback
requests are not intercepted:

```
cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib "client::" -- --test-threads=2
test result: FAILED. 676 passed; 1 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 6501 filtered out
```

The one failure is pre-existing and environmental, not from this change:

```
client::stream_entry::tests::refused_connection_names_the_host_and_skips_the_http1_hint
panicked at crates/engine/src/client/stream_entry.rs:628:
nothing listens on the port: Response { status: 503, headers: {"proxy-connection": "close", ...} }
```

It asserts `(connection refused)` while this host reports `(connection failed)`.
Reproduced on unmodified `upstream/main` (`71cab400f`) by stashing this branch
and re-running the same command — it fails identically there. The file it lives
in is not touched by this PR.

`cargo fmt --all -- --check` exits 0.

Live check with a CLI built from this branch against the gateway, on the config
that previously returned 400:

- plain turn → `OK` (200)
- `--auto` tool turn (tool call, tool result, `reasoning_content` replay) → 200
- `reasoning_effort = "off"` → `OK` (200)

The gateway was also verified by hand to accept `reasoning_effort: "none"`
(`reasoning_tokens: 0`), `minimal`, streaming, `tool_calls`, and replayed
`reasoning_content`.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it)

Not a new user-facing feature: this fixes the request dialect for an existing
provider identity. No `docs/features.toml` row applies, and no `CHANGELOG.md`
change is included.

## Attribution

🤖 Generated by SpikeBot 000(CodeWhale-LOCAL)

Release notes

Sourced from jsonschema's releases.

[Python] Release 0.61.2

Fixed

  • References inside a registered resource resolving against the URI it was registered under instead of its $id. #1862

Performance

  • Validation of deeply nested instances against recursive schemas takes time linear in their nesting depth.
  • unevaluatedProperties next to if, dependentSchemas, anyOf or oneOf checked in one pass over the object by is_valid, without validating those subschemas again.
  • Validation of Python instances checks the common value types inline.
  • propertyNames validating each str key itself instead of a new string built from its text.
  • allOf branches that only check properties, required or type: object checked in one pass over the object by is_valid.
  • required beside properties and additionalProperties: false checked in the same pass over the object by is_valid.
  • $refs to a subschema another $ref already compiled dispatched once instead of twice.
  • unevaluatedProperties matching property names by their first and last bytes instead of hashing them.
  • additionalProperties that only checks type decided without entering the subschema for each value by is_valid.
  • Literal-prefix patterns rejecting a property name on its first byte before comparing the rest.

prs.title: fix(engine): log safe provider failure diagnostics
prs.body:
Provider timeouts and transport failures can end a turn without leaving their cause in the default diagnostic log. Emit a structured warning from the existing `envelope_for_llm_error` boundary, shared by stream opening, stream reading, and context-recovery failures.

The warning records the existing error code/category and typed transmission state, plus an HTTP status or timeout duration only when the error retains that evidence. Untyped failures stay `OutcomeUnknown`; a zero timeout means the duration was not recorded. Raw errors, display messages, response bodies, URLs, and authentication context are not logged. Envelope conversion and retry/recovery decisions are unchanged.

Refs #7328 (partial). This slice adds diagnostic cause fields; provider/model/stage context, error-card presentation, and structured receipt fields remain outside its scope. Thanks to @7jrxt42BxFZo4iAnN4CX for the log/session analysis and measured timeout examples.

Validation:

- One regression captures warnings through an `info` filter across six failure cases, including an anyhow-wrapped timeout, unknown duration, pre-dispatch connection failure, 503 unknown outcome, 413 rejection, and an untyped network failure. It checks that raw error/context/secret fixtures are absent and the returned display message/recovery contract is preserved.
- `CODEWHALE_DEV_NEXTEST=0 bash scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/llm_error_envelope.rs` (repository-pinned Rust 1.100.0, Linux): `test result: ok. 7 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 7643 filtered out; finished in 0.01s`.
- `bash scripts/preflight.sh --check`: `preflight: OK`, including the formatting check.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- [GitHub Actions CI](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/43823653391) passed for `df2b0aa51725b451c7b82de361e1ef9785e7f621`: 10 jobs succeeded, including Clippy and compilation of every workspace target on Windows; 12 jobs were skipped. The full Linux Rust `Test` job was skipped in this fork run; the seven focused engine tests above ran locally.

The local tests ran on base `6278bbc2947f026185ad76c112ed5ec1ad1fb664` plus this patch. During the cold build, main advanced to `336cd8a49`; `llm_error_envelope.rs` is unchanged there and its three production consumers still use the same conversion boundary.

prs.title: feat(workflow): verify sealed candidates with an isolated host oracle
prs.body:
Refs #7250
Extracted from #7262

This is the maintainer-requested, opt-in verified evaluator slice. The evolutionary Draft PR remains separate and unchanged.

## Evaluator

- Freeze a versioned host spec, clean Git baseline, authorized write/protected scope, trusted public and held-out cases, executable identities, and a Linux bubblewrap capability probe.
- Accept completed Workflow worktrees; seal added/modified/deleted/binary/mode changes and replay from the sealed artifact after the writer worktree is gone.
- Run candidate commands in isolated processes and compare actual JSON output with the host oracle. Receipts bind spec, baseline, oracle, artifact/tree, sandbox and native binary identities. Public PASS requires public-plus-held-out replay.
- Wire the evaluator into the existing `operate_best_of_n` search Workflow only when `args.evaluator` is supplied. Results are `proposal_only`; there is no candidate apply, push, merge, policy genome, or mutation operator.

## Maintainer review fixes

- **Normal-user namespace creation:** the evaluator-specific `RLIMIT_NPROC` is 4096, and the probe reports that effective value. The old 32 limit counted all tasks owned by the Linux user. PID namespace isolation, `--die-with-parent`, cancellation, CPU/time bounds, filesystem/network restrictions and process cleanup remain in place.
- **Published-crate source identity:** the evaluator hashes the actual loaded Workflow source and compares it with a checked-in SHA-256 constant. The repository script path is referenced only by excluded test source. Exact checked-in content is accepted; a modified script fails closed. The update procedure is documented.
- **Evaluation deadline:** the aggregate budget counts active candidate evaluation and replay time, starting after generation. Receipts record effective start, elapsed time, deadline and stop reason; the delayed-generation regression passes.
- **Artifact capture:** a frozen policy records and excludes untracked root `target/` and `__pycache__/` outputs. Tracked and protected files remain checked, legitimate new source remains captured, and out-of-scope writes still fail. Exclusions appear in artifact and receipt provenance.
- **Descendant test and macOS:** the lifecycle test uses a writable in-sandbox marker, a surviving negative control, and timeout/cancellation cleanup checks. The non-Linux `UNSUPPORTED_ISOLATION` branch no longer has the unnecessary-return warning.

## Final validation at `61b889cf6ec10df5c048ef15715dbb272ccacf77`

- [Upstream PR CI](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/43344788042): 10 successful jobs, 12 path-skipped, 0 failed. Workspace format, strict Clippy and Windows all-targets check passed. The PR view also counts the successful triage check.
- [Hosted final-head build](https://github.com/axobase001/DeepSeek-TUI/actions/runs/43345093377): Rocky Linux 8 full CLI build, 9 focused Rust tests, evaluator crate checks and package file listing passed; Windows focused check and 5 tests passed; macOS focused check and strict Clippy passed. The hosted Linux runner lacked bubblewrap, so real isolation was validated separately.
- **Real non-root Linux isolation:** on the 47 VPS, `nobody` (uid 65534) owned 40 preflight tasks. A 32-limit bubblewrap control reproduced the namespace error; 4096 succeeded. All 9 evaluator tests then executed under bubblewrap and passed (113.64 s), including cancellation and descendant cleanup.
- **Native Workflow E2E:** the exact final-head CLI ran a local scripted provider. A false PASS claim failed 2 public cases; the isolated candidate passed 2 public and 3 public-plus-held-out replay cases, ending `proposal_only`. No-evaluator and modified-source rejection controls passed. An independent verifier recomputed 7 case outcomes and 2 sealed tree hashes.
- **Package file set:** [independent run](https://github.com/axobase001/DeepSeek-TUI/actions/runs/43345093627) compiled the exact listed engine files with the repository Workflow script removed, using local sibling 0.10.3 crates. The artifact records this final SHA.

## Evidence and release gate

The [final-head validation report](https://github.com/axobase001/DeepSeek-TUI/blob/experiment/7250-native-evidence/evidence/7250/PR7294_final_61b889c_validation_2026-11-13.md) and [100 KB evidence bundle](https://github.com/axobase001/DeepSeek-TUI/blob/experiment/7250-native-evidence/evidence/7250/CodeWhale_PR7294_Final_61b889c_Evidence_2026-11-13.zip) contain raw non-root/native receipts, the independent verifier, package file-set proof, and the standard package failure log. Historical failures remain in the [earlier evidence bundle](https://github.com/axobase001/DeepSeek-TUI/blob/experiment/7250-native-evidence/evidence/7250/CodeWhale_PR7294_Review_Fixes_Evidence_Lite_2026-11-13.zip). The [final Linux binary artifact](https://github.com/axobase001/DeepSeek-TUI/actions/runs/43345093377/artifacts/14001504445) binds the CLI and Rust test executable used on the VPS.

`cargo package --locked -p codewhale-engine` still exits 101 during dependency resolution: crates.io offers `codewhale-agent` up to 0.10.2, while this workspace requires 0.10.3. The [raw failure artifact](https://github.com/axobase001/DeepSeek-TUI/actions/runs/43345093377/artifacts/14002692655) is preserved. Standard package verification awaits the sibling crate release; the independently compiled package file set validates the removed out-of-crate source reference.

## What and why

Adds GitHub Copilot CLI to the external agent registry (`AGENTS` in `crates/engine/src/fleet/agents.rs`), the way 2 slice from #7279 that a maintainer suggested alongside Qwen Code (Qwen is covered by #7293). One row: `copilot --acp --stdio` launches its native ACP server; `docs/RUNTIME_API.md`'s agent list gains the name.

How I checked the ACP flag against the agent's own docs: GitHub's [ACP server page](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/acp-server) documents `copilot --acp --stdio` as the stdio-mode start command, and the [Copilot CLI command reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-command-reference) documents `copilot login` (OAuth) and `copilot update` ("download and install the latest version"), which is where the `login` and `upgrade` strings come from. `min_version` stays `None`: ACP support is in public preview and I found no verified floor; anything I could not verify stayed `None` per the issue.

One caveat to carry from the issue thread: [github/copilot-cli#845](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/845) reported edits applied without a `session/request_permission`. I did not qualify the real binary (not installed on my machine), so whether that still happens is unverified; if it does, Codewhale must not show the session as approval-gated — flagging for whoever runs the way-1 qualification.

## Related issue (optional)

Refs #7279

prs.title: fix(engine): honor native usage journal capacity fallback
prs.body:
## Superseded on main

Thanks for addressing the underlying accounting failure across execution paths. This narrow capacity fallback is now superseded by [b4625cec6](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/b4625cec68200f4aea1299b1c1d23810b2077a3a) and [0e511f413](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/0e511f413c5ebcda17c176ce04e3bfa18e29daf9).

The current main branch removes the native usage journal, reserved slots, and the pre-dispatch bind/admission calls that this patch repaired. The remaining 256-record limit bounds diagnostic records rather than provider admission. Closing this PR because its fix is covered by that replacement; rebasing it would restore code main intentionally removed. The original local validation is preserved below. This describes main, not a verified public release.

---

## What and why

Once an owner's native usage journal holds 256 sources, reservation already elects to continue without retention. The following retain call nevertheless rejects the inactive slot, aborting the turn before provider dispatch.

Track that explicit capacity refusal on the producer's slot and let the shared retain helper honor it after native-proof and owner validation. This also covers the second retain attempt when the captured runtime sink refuses a receipt. Subsequent observations retry reservation, allowing retention to resume after capacity is freed. The runtime warning no longer claims that every unpersisted receipt was retained.

Retention stays bounded. Overflow receipts can remain unretained while capacity is exhausted; this change does not promise complete accounting for them. Duplicate admission and source-ownership checks remain enforced. Session persistence errors and origin/bind failures retain their existing behavior.

## Where this came from

Refs #7348 (capacity fallback only).

Thanks for the precise log correlation and call-path diagnosis in the report.

## How I tested it

Using the repository-pinned Rust 1.100.0 toolchain on Linux, on head `18d0d9415` (base `e02d51da65ea`):

- `CODEWHALE_DEV_NEXTEST=0 scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/cost_status.rs`: **45 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored (7,604 filtered out)**.
- The new regression fills all 256 slots with live, unacknowledged native sources and a refusing runtime sink, then verifies that the next dispatch admission succeeds, retention stays bounded, duplicate/foreign/forged records remain rejected, and retention recovers after an acknowledged source closes. This exercises admission and publication without calling a model.
- `scripts/preflight.sh --check`: **preflight: OK**.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check`: passed.
- [GitHub Actions PR CI](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/43814871022): **passed**, including Rust lint and the Windows workspace-target compilation check.

Main advanced to `6278bbc2947f` during the build (execpolicy/workflow hardening); `cost_status.rs` is unchanged there. The local suite ran against its original source tree.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (`e02d51da65ea`)
- [x] Formatting passes
- [x] Focused regression suite: 45 passed, 0 failed
- [x] Feature registry/docs: not applicable to this existing accounting fallback bug

prs.title: fix(core): keep assignments inside CLI argument values literal
prs.body:
## What and why

The fallback parser's second `key=value` pass scans text already consumed as a `--argument` value. A shell command such as `--command "MODE=dev node app.js"` therefore invents an extra `MODE` tool parameter. File content containing assignments has the same problem.

Remove consumed flag arguments from the fallback key/value scan. Standalone key/value arguments still work alongside explicit flags. One regression checks both a quoted shell assignment and mixed flag/key-value input through the public parser.

## Where this came from

A focused bug found while checking upstream main (`5526e0590` on November 14), independently of the XML multiline repair in #7341. Prepared and tested with AI assistance (Codex).

## How I tested it

- The regression fails with the original scan because extra parameters appear.
- `scripts/dev-test.sh core tool_parser`: **test result: ok. 13 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 46 filtered out**.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check`, and `scripts/preflight.sh --check --base origin/main` pass. Existing missing-tag notices and warn-only lexicon findings remain.
- No live provider request or terminal interaction is used; the engine's fallback call site uses this parser directly.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change from upstream main.
- [x] Rust formatting and affected tests pass.
- [x] Feature registry/docs: N/A, preserves literal values in the existing parser.

## Current validation (November 16)

Merged upstream main `641a304248e1` into this contributor branch without rewriting the original fix. This picks up the main-branch repair for the TUI `println!` lint failures seen on the original PR head. The diff against that main remains confined to `crates/core/src/tool_parser.rs`.

- `scripts/dev-test.sh core tool_parser`: **test result: ok. 13 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 46 filtered out**.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check`, and `scripts/preflight.sh --check --base origin/main`: pass.
- `scripts/release/check-versions.sh --range-audit-advisory`: pass in the upstream per-PR mode. Historical release-note receipt warnings concern already-merged feature commits; the strict release-range audit still reports that existing debt.
- [Hosted CI for current head `e52f8751a88b`](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/43803214079) completed successfully: lint, Windows tests, version drift, integrations, VS Code extension, plugin conversion, and the extension-host runtime matrix pass. Broader jobs skipped under the upstream fork policy are not counted as executed tests. Maintainer review remains requested.
