prs.title: fix(execpolicy): hold deny rules against rebound command words and more launchers
prs.body:
**This touches command deny rules, which CONTRIBUTING lists as trust-boundary surface (sandbox policy) that needs maintainer sign-off first.** I opened #7305 with the reproduction before this PR. Please confirm the direction before reviewing the code; I am happy to change the approach or close this if you prefer to handle it yourselves.

## What and why

With a deny rule for `rm`, these spellings ran `rm` and were allowed, including under `AskForApproval::Never` (`crates/execpolicy/src/shell_expand.rs`). Two commits.

- **Rebound command words and launchers** (first commit)
  - `hash -p /bin/rm r; r x` (bash) and `hash r=/bin/rm; r x` (zsh) bind a new name to an executable. Now the `hash -p` path and the zsh `hash` value are expanded as code.
  - `alias qq='rm -rf'; eval qq /`: zsh expands the alias in code it parses later, and the alias value is code. Now alias values are expanded as code.
  - `=rm x`: zsh replaces a leading `=cmd` word with the path of `cmd`. Now a command word starting with `=` is known only at run time.
  - `parallel rm ::: x`, `parallel 'rm {}' ::: x`, `chpst -u nobody rm x` and `screen -dmS s rm x` run their operands as a command. `chpst`, `parallel` and `screen` are added to the wrapper table, and `parallel` joins its operands like `watch`. Only option values are listed for the new wrappers, so every other option is read both ways.
  - `at now <<< 'rm x'` and `echo 'rm x' | batch` run a script read from stdin, like `sh <<< ...`. `at` / `batch` stdin is now treated like a shell's: a heredoc body is expanded as the script, and other stdin is dynamic.
- **`parallel` with no command, and `at` job queries** (second commit)
  - **`parallel ::: `**: with no command of its own, `parallel` runs each input line, or each argument after `:::`, as a command line. `echo 'rm x' | parallel` and `parallel ::: 'rm x'` therefore still ran `rm`: the `:::` separator was taken as the inner command head, and nothing after it was checked. Now, when there is no real command after `parallel` (the separators `:::`, `:::+`, `::::` and `::::+` do not count as one), the line is dynamic, and each argument after `:::` / `:::+` is expanded as code. Arguments after `::::` / `::::+` are file names whose contents are not read, so they stay covered only by the dynamic marking.
  - **`at` / `batch` queries**: with the first commit, `at -l`, `at -r 3`, `at -d 3`, `at -c 3` and `batch -l` were treated as reading a job script from stdin, so these queries were refused next to any deny rule under `Never`. They only list, remove or print jobs, so they are exempt now.
  - **Why `at -q` is not exempt**: `-q QUEUE` only chooses the queue. `echo 'rm x' | at -q b now` still reads a job from stdin and schedules it, so it stays dynamic. `-q`, `-f` and `-t` take a value, which is skipped when looking for `-l`/`-r`/`-d`/`-c`, so `at -q a -l` is still a query and `at -qb now` is not. `at -f script.sh now` also stays dynamic. An option word that the shell rewrites at run time is not trusted, so it never makes a line exempt.

Still out of scope, as the issue says: `tmux new 'cmd'` / `tmux send-keys`, `screen -X stuff`, and other programs that take keystrokes or code in their own syntax.

## Where this came from

Closes #7305

## How I tested it

- New rows in `HIDDEN_RM` (`crates/execpolicy/tests/shell_parse_policy.rs`), checked by `deny_rules_hold_against_runtime_resolved_and_reserved_word_spellings` and `file_rules_fail_closed_on_runtime_resolved_words`. All 19 new rows are allowed on `main` (both tests fail) and denied with the fix:
  - `alias qq='rm -rf'; eval qq /`, `hash -p /bin/rm r; r x`, `hash r=/bin/rm; r x`, `=rm x`
  - `parallel rm ::: x`, `parallel 'rm {}' ::: x`, `parallel -j 2 -- rm ::: x`, `echo 'rm x' | parallel`, `parallel ::: 'rm x'`, `parallel -j 2 ::: ls 'rm x'`, `parallel :::: cmds.txt ::: 'rm x'`
  - `chpst -u nobody rm x`, `screen -dmS s rm x`
  - `at now <<< 'rm x'`, `echo 'rm x' | batch`, `at now <<EOF ... EOF`, `echo 'rm x' | at -q b now`, `echo 'rm x' | at -qb now`, `at -f script.sh now`
- New rows in `ordinary_commands_stay_allowed_next_to_a_deny_rule`, which stay allowed: `alias ll='ls -la'`, `hash -r`, `parallel echo ::: a b`, `at -l`, `at -q a -l`, `at -r 3`, `at -d 3`, `at -c 3`, `batch -l`
- `cargo test -p codewhale-execpolicy`: 236 + 1 + 11 + 8 + 1 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy -p codewhale-execpolicy --all-targets`: clean
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (not applicable: bug fix only)

prs.title: fix(sanitize): mask provider keys written next to CJK text
prs.body:
## What and why

The bare-token pass of `redact_secrets` and `redact_model_bound_secrets` (`crates/sanitize/src/redact.rs`, also the last step of `sanitize_text`) missed provider keys written in CJK prose:

- `密钥：sk-…`, `我的密钥是sk-…`, `（ghp_…）` and a key after U+3000 passed through unmasked.
- `sk-…，然后重试` was masked together with the Chinese text after it.

- **Root cause**: the pass split a line on ASCII spaces and trimmed only ASCII punctuation from each word. CJK text puts no space around a key, so the key and the text around it formed one word that matched no token shape.
- **Fix**: credential tokens are ASCII, so each word is now checked one ASCII run at a time, with the existing trims and token shapes. Each run that is a token is masked, and the non-ASCII text around it is kept. An ASCII-only word is a single run and is handled exactly as before.

Not covered here, as the issue says: keyed assignments with a full-width colon and a non-prefixed value (`password：hunter2`) and Chinese key names (`密码=…`). Those need vocabulary decisions, not a split fix.

## Where this came from

Closes #7301

## How I tested it

- New regression test `a_bare_token_next_to_cjk_text_or_full_width_punctuation_is_masked`. It fails on `main` (`密钥：sk-…` unchanged) and passes with the fix.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-sanitize --lib`: 12 passed, 0 failed

prs.title: fix(net): match network entries written as internationalized domains
prs.body:
**This touches network policy, which CONTRIBUTING lists as trust-boundary surface that needs maintainer sign-off first.** I opened #7302 with the reproduction before this PR. Please confirm the direction (compare entries and hosts in the IDNA ASCII form) before reviewing the code; I am happy to change the approach or close this if you prefer to handle it yourselves.

## What and why

A `[network]` entry written with a non-ASCII domain never matched (`crates/net/src/network_policy.rs`). With `deny = ["例子.com"]`, `https://例子.com/` was allowed under `default = "allow"` and prompted under `prompt`. `/network deny 例子.com` writes exactly such an entry. Allow entries never matched either.

- **Root cause**: hosts reach `NetworkPolicy::decide` from `Url::host_str`, which returns the IDNA ASCII form (`xn--fsqu00a.com`). `normalize_host` only lowercased ASCII, so an entry typed as `例子.com`, `*.中国` or `BÜCHER.de` was compared in a different form from the host.
- **Fix**: `normalize_host` converts a non-ASCII name to the URL parser's ASCII form, so entries and hosts use the same form. The `*.` / `.` wildcard prefix is kept. ASCII entries take the same path as before and are unchanged. A name the URL parser rejects is kept as written, as before.

## Where this came from

Closes #7302

## How I tested it

- New regression test `deny_entries_match_internationalized_domain_names` (`例子.com`, `*.中国`, `BÜCHER.de`). It fails on `main` (`https://例子.com/` -> `Allow`) and passes with the fix.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-net --lib`: 73 passed, 1 ignored, 0 failed

prs.title: fix(app-server): show the source of an outgoing worktree-side rename
prs.body:
## What and why

`split_by_workspace` projects repository-root rows into the workspace frame. When a rename leaves the workspace it synthesizes a `deleted` row so the source stays visible inside the workspace, but the guard was `row.index == "R"`.

Since #7310 the parser also returns a worktree-side rename (`" R outside.txt\0sub/a.txt\0"`), whose index column is a space. The guard is false for that shape, so the source — which really has disappeared from the workspace — appeared in **no** row of `GET /v1/git` or `GET /v1/changes`, while the index-side equivalent correctly produced a `deleted` row.

The guard now accepts a rename in either column, and the synthesized row carries the side the change actually lives in:

- worktree-side (`worktree == "R"`) → `worktree = "D"`, `staged = false`
- index-side → `index = "D"`, `staged = true` (unchanged)

The side is read from the worktree column instead of inferring it from `index == " "`. That is what keeps a copy out of this path by construction: only `R` synthesizes, because copying leaves the source in place and a `deleted` row for it would be false.

Staging safety is unchanged: the row still lands in `outside` with its root-relative `old_path`, and `compute_tokens` covers it. This is a listing gap, not a guard gap.

`docs/RUNTIME_API.md` and its `zh_hans` pair now say which side the synthesized row reports and that a copy is never shown this way.

## Where this came from

Closes #7324
Refs #7309

## How I tested it

Two new tests in the existing `runtime_api::git::tests` module.

`review_outgoing_worktree_rename_exposes_source_deletion` uses a real temporary repository, moves a tracked file out of the workspace from the worktree side (`git mv`, `git reset`, `git add -N`), and reads the workspace at its `sub/` subdirectory.

`outgoing_copy_keeps_its_source_inside_the_workspace` is a unit test on `split_by_workspace` with an index-side copy row, so the copy shape is pinned without needing a repository whose git config enables copy detection.

`cargo test -p codewhale-app-server --lib -- runtime_api::git` — **25 passed, 0 failed** (with `RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216`).

Both new tests fail on the shape they pin, which is the point of them:

- Before the fix, `review_outgoing_worktree_rename_exposes_source_deletion` fails because the source is in **no** row at all, not merely mislabelled:

```
thread 'review_outgoing_worktree_rename_exposes_source_deletion' panicked at
crates\app-server\src\runtime_api\git.rs:3256:9:
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: 0
 right: 1
```

- An earlier commit on this branch accepted `R` **or** `C` in the guard. On that version `outgoing_copy_keeps_its_source_inside_the_workspace` fails:

```
a copy leaves its source in place, so it must not read as a deletion: ["a.txt"]
```

That variant reported a staged deletion for a file present in both the index and the worktree, and it contradicted this branch's own description. An independent reviewer caught it; the condition now admits `R` only.

`cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean. `cargo clippy -p codewhale-app-server --lib --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` is clean.

One unrelated note so it does not read as a gap: plain `cargo clippy -p codewhale-app-server ...` (with dependencies) stops on `codewhale-runtime` with `clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks`. That error is present on `main` without this change, so I checked my crate with `--no-deps`.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [x] Not a user-facing feature: no new flag or command, so `docs/features.toml` is unchanged

## Attribution

🤖 Generated by SpikeBot 000(CodeWhale-LOCAL)

issues.body:
## Environment

OpenClaw 2026.11.3, macOS, Node 26. Counts from one host.

## What happens

`MAX_BATCH_BYTES` (64 MiB) is a constant. Transcripts whose compressed archive is larger stay in SQLite and are retried on every once-a-minute pass: 91 warnings in 16 days on one agent. They also keep the database large, and the selection transaction is slow (`cold transcript selection` holds: p50 1.2 s, max 27 s).

## Request

Make the limit configurable, or write large archives in chunks; log once per session until its state changes; report which sessions are blocked.

issues.body:
## Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

Feishu inbound `mentionTargets` are automatically attached to ordinary and error replies again after #93522, reintroducing the multi-bot mention cascade previously fixed by #71396.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use a Feishu group with the OpenClaw bot and at least one other mentioned user or bot.
2. Send a message that mentions both OpenClaw and the other participant.
3. Let OpenClaw send an ordinary final reply or an error/fallback reply whose generated text contains no mention of that participant.
4. Observe that the outbound Feishu message still contains a native `at` element for the other participant.

A deterministic unit-level reproduction is to create the Feishu reply dispatcher with inbound `mentionTargets`, deliver a plain `final` error payload, and inspect the first `sendMessageFeishu` call: it receives `mentions` even though the outbound body did not request them.

## Expected behavior

Inbound mentions should remain contextual metadata only. Ordinary, final, error, fallback, block, card, and streaming replies should not automatically mention other inbound targets.

Explicit outbound mentions, including caller-provided `mentions` and `<at user_id="...">...</at>` rendering, should continue to produce native Feishu `at` elements.

This was the behavior restored by #71396 / commit `43ea5c3e6fe8fe7a25a4ea8fc2ae256fd97f5289` for #70065.

## Actual behavior

PR #93522 / commit `e46bcb834faa94aac4f038c5f69cf0ab26533874` passed inbound `ctx.mentionTargets` back into `createFeishuReplyDispatcher`. The dispatcher then adds those targets to the first final reply or first independently sent block.

As a result, normal replies and terminal error messages can unexpectedly notify every user or bot mentioned in the inbound message. In multi-agent groups this can trigger an unintended reply cascade.

## OpenClaw version

2026.7.1 and current `main` as checked on August 11, 2026

## Operating system

Linux 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2

## Install method

Source checkout, built with pnpm, Gateway launched through a systemd user service

## Model

Model-independent; observed with `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`

## Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw direct model route; the bug is in the Feishu outbound dispatcher and does not depend on the model provider

## Additional provider/model setup details

No provider-specific setup is required to reproduce the dispatcher behavior.

## Logs

```shell
# Regression-introducing data flow
bot.ts:                         mentionTargets: ctx.mentionTargets
reply-dispatcher.ts (final):    mentions: mentionTargets
reply-dispatcher.ts (block):    mentions: mentionTargets
```

## Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- Original report: #70065
- Original fix: #71396 / `43ea5c3e6fe8fe7a25a4ea8fc2ae256fd97f5289`
- Regression: #93522 / `e46bcb834faa94aac4f038c5f69cf0ab26533874`
- The regression commit also replaced the earlier "does not attach automatic mentions" test expectation with an expectation that forwards inbound mentions.

## Impact and severity

- Affected: Feishu group chats, especially multi-bot or multi-agent groups where one inbound message mentions several participants.
- Severity: High in multi-agent groups; terminal error or fallback replies can wake multiple agents and create a cascade.
- Frequency: Deterministic whenever the dispatcher receives non-empty inbound `mentionTargets` and sends the affected first final/block reply path.
- Consequence: Unrequested notifications, unnecessary agent runs, extra model usage, and noisy multi-agent reply chains.

## Additional information

Last known good behavior: #71396, merged May 9, 2026.

Regression introduced: #93522, merged June 16, 2026.

The rendering improvement from #93522 should be preserved. The fix only needs to stop feeding inbound `ctx.mentionTargets` into the reply dispatcher; explicit outbound/native mention rendering remains available through the existing send path.

# [Bug]: Codex app-server notification path starves Gateway main thread for ~22s (quadratic reasoning-snapshot rebuild per delta)

## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.7.1-2 (`0790d9f`), Node 25.9.0, macOS 26.3 (arm64)
- Codex app-server runtime with GPT-5.6 (`openai/gpt-5.6-sol`)

## Symptom
The Gateway main thread stalls for ~22 seconds at ~100% of one core during ordinary Codex-backed turns. During the stall nothing runs: typing indicators die, channel messages queue behind the frozen event loop, and the diagnostic subsystem emits liveness warnings, e.g.:

```
warn diagnostic liveness warning: reasons=event_loop_delay interval=30s eventLoopDelayMaxMs=21810.4 eventLoopUtilization=1.000 ...
```

Two captured occurrences on 2026-07-22:

| Time (ET) | Event-loop max | ELU | Gateway CPU/core | Last recorded work |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 09:59:52 | 21,692.9 ms | 0.884 | 0.907 | Codex `item/completed` / `hook/started` |
| 10:14:41 | 21,810.4 ms | 1.000 | 1.019 | Codex `item/completed` / `hook/completed` |

The stalls are not the tool commands themselves: trajectory correlation shows one affected bash call with a Codex-reported process duration of 4,313 ms (wall gap ~22 s) and another with **0 ms** process duration (entire ~21.85 s outside the command). Result payloads were modest (0.4–21 KB).

## Root cause (traced in installed 2026.7.1-2 bundles)
An unbounded synchronous/microtask burst across three layers:

1. `CodexAppServerClient.handleLine()` (`dist/shared-client-*.js`) synchronously `JSON.parse`s every newline-delimited notification in the readline `line` callback and immediately fans out via `Promise.resolve(handler(...))`.
2. `CodexThreadRouter.enqueueNotification()` (`dist/run-attempt-*.js`) serializes per-thread notifications with `route.notificationTail = route.notificationTail.then(...)` — a ready burst drains as one continuous microtask chain with no macrotask yield.
3. `CodexAppServerEventProjector.handleReasoningDelta()` (`dist/provider-capabilities-*.js`) rebuilds the **full accumulated reasoning snapshot** (`collectReasoningTextValues(...).join(...)`) and awaits `onReasoningStream` for **every delta**. Total work grows quadratically with reasoning length. GPT-5.6's larger reasoning streams expose the pre-existing pattern.

Live stack attribution (out-of-process macOS `sample` at 100 Hz during production operation) shows busy main-thread samples under `uv__stream_io → JS callback → RunMicrotasks → PromiseFulfillReactionJob → AsyncFunctionAwaitResolveClosure`, with `ArrayPrototypeFlatMap`/`FlattenIntoArrayWithMapFn`, string hashing, and allocation dominating — matching the projector path. Quiet-window control sample was 94% idle in `kevent`, excluding background native threads.

## Proposed fix
1. **Macrotask yield in the per-thread notification drain**: preserve ordering but yield via `setImmediate` after ~50 notifications or ~5 ms of synchronous work. Smallest direct fix; scheduling-only, no protocol semantics change.
2. **Coalesce reasoning snapshots**: append deltas immediately but emit at most one full `onReasoningStream` snapshot per event-loop turn (or per 25–50 ms), always flushing before terminal completion. Removes the quadratic copying.
3. **Parse/dispatch budget** (~8 ms) on app-server stdout line handling, queuing the remainder to `setImmediate`, plus queue-depth/drain-duration diagnostics.
4. **Timing spans** around parse, fan-out, router, projector, and reasoning callback, logged only above ~50 ms (no content).

If scope must stay minimal, item 1 alone eliminates the multi-second starvation; item 2 is the big performance win.

## Related issues (different mechanisms, same symptom family)
- #87744 (codex Telegram turns time out waiting for `turn/completed`, 2026.5.27)
- #83366 (gateway event-loop starvation under cron/tool load)
- #83983 (Discord reasoning stream overwrites prior chunks)

Happy to provide the compressed native stack samples and the correlation trajectory excerpts on request.

### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Delegated `openclaw` calls can reach `openclaw.chat` without an active admitted-run authority and fail before the system agent can process the request.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start OpenClaw 2026.9.3 in a Discord channel with a Full Access turn.
2. Invoke the built-in `openclaw` tool for a permitted system-control request, such as a configuration change.
3. Observe the tool fail before the system agent acts.

### Expected behavior

`openclaw` should carry the authority of the current admitted run into the system-agent delegation, so permitted requests can reach the system agent.

### Actual behavior

The Gateway rejects the request with: `delegated OpenClaw approval requires an active run authority`.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.3 (1391f7c)

### Operating system

Linux 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2

### Install method

npm global

### Model

openai/gpt-5.6-terra

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw Gateway -> OpenAI OAuth -> Codex

### Additional provider/model setup details

Observed with the built-in `openclaw` delegate tool from Discord. The failing call carried session context and Full Access, but the delegated authority was absent at the system-agent approval boundary.

### Logs

```shell
Error: delegated OpenClaw approval requires an active run authority
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

**Affected:** system-control requests delegated through the built-in `openclaw` tool from Discord.
**Severity:** blocks workflow.
**Frequency:** reproduced from this channel until the locally installed runtime guard restored the current run authority.
**Consequence:** configuration and other permitted system-agent actions cannot run through the delegate path.

### Additional information

Regression status and version comparison: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

Root-cause investigation found `createOpenClawDelegateToolsForRun` receives `runId` in `OpenClawToolsOptions`, but its picked options omit it and the caller identity does not include `operationalRunInstance` or `approvalAuthority`. A local source patch that reacquires `getAgentRunContext(options.runId)?.delegatedAuthority` and passes that exact authority through the trusted caller context restored the path. A focused regression test passed (12/12 tests in `openclaw-delegate-tool.test.ts`). No upstream code change is included with this issue.

## Summary

Gmail watcher retries can start duplicate hook agent runs when the forwarding HTTP request disconnects before OpenClaw finishes agent admission.

## Reproduction

1. Send an authenticated `/hooks/gmail` or `/hooks/agent` request for a session whose hook dispatch is queued.
2. Disconnect the client before the hook agent enters the runner.
3. Allow the queued admission to proceed, then retry the same notification.
4. Without request-lifecycle cancellation, the abandoned request remains eligible to start until OpenClaw's 15-second admission deadline, so both attempts can execute.

This is visible with `gog gmail watch serve`: gog's hook client defaults to a 10-second timeout, treats delivery failure as retryable, and restores Gmail progress after a failed hook. Its current hook sender sets content type and authorization but does not send `Idempotency-Key`.

Dependency evidence:

- `openclaw/gogcli/internal/cmd/gmail_watch_types.go`: `defaultHookRequestTimeoutSec = 10`
- `openclaw/gogcli/internal/gmailwatch/processor.go`: failed hook delivery restores progress for retry
- `openclaw/gogcli/internal/gmailwatch/hook.go`: outbound hook headers omit an idempotency key

## Expected behavior

An HTTP request that disconnects before agent admission must lose eligibility to start work. Once the runner accepts the work, request lifetime must no longer cancel that independent run.

## Best fix

Bind pending hook admission to request abort/response close at the Gateway HTTP owner boundary, then detach that cancellation when `onExecutionStarted` records acceptance. Extending gog's timeout alone only moves the race and does not cover network loss.

## Residual risk

OpenClaw's existing idempotency replay cache is process-local. A retry after Gateway restart can still execute again; durable cross-restart replay protection is separate storage work and should follow the repository's SQLite ownership/schema rules.

<!-- agent-transcript:start -->
## Agent Transcript

<details>
<summary>Redacted Codex session transcript</summary>

```text
[user]
Gmail watcher 为什么报了这么多条重复的？

[assistant]
The same notification was accepted but not acknowledged before the forwarding client timed out. The retry was treated as a new hook request, creating duplicate agent runs. The immediate invariant is that a disconnected request must not remain eligible for pending admission.

[user]
是不是改个参数，让 gog 等久一些？

[assistant]
A longer timeout can reduce frequency, but it only moves the race. Network loss and slower admission can still trigger retries. The owner-boundary fix is to cancel only admission that is still pending when the request disconnects, while preserving work already accepted by the runner.

[user]
可以，继续修复吧。

[assistant]
Implemented request abort/response-close propagation into hook dispatch. Added regression coverage for blocked admission cancellation, accepted-work preservation, and a same-idempotency-key retry that executes exactly once. Focused tests and core type checks passed; structured autoreview reported no actionable findings.
```

</details>
<!-- agent-transcript:end -->

issues.body:
## Summary

CLI progress reporting can print a literal `NaN%` on screen and emit a malformed terminal OSC progress sequence when a progress producer reports a non-finite percentage.

## Environment

- Windows 11 (win32-x64), Node v24.16.0
- OpenClaw at upstream/main head `0dbfc6e1c45f`
- Any terminal when progress output is active (`openclaw models scan --probe`, `openclaw memory sync`, or any CLI/plugin using the progress reporter)

## Repro

`ProgressReporter.setPercent` clamps with `Math.max(0, Math.min(100, Math.round(nextPercent)))`. `Math.round(NaN)` is `NaN`, and both `Math.min(100, NaN)` and `Math.max(0, NaN)` are `NaN`, so a NaN input stores `percent = NaN`.

```ts
const rep = createCliProgress({ label: "L", total: 2, stream, fallback: "line" });
rep.setPercent(NaN);
// writes "\r\x1b[2K L NaN%"   -> literal NaN% on screen
```

The same path is reachable through `withProgressTotals`, which validates `total` (finite and > 0) but never validates `completed`. A producer reporting `completed: NaN` (for example a 0/0 ratio or empty-list math) flows straight into `setPercent(NaN)`:

```ts
await withProgressTotals({ label: "M", total: 2, stream, fallback: "log" }, async (u) => u({ completed: NaN, total: 5 }));
// writes "M NaN%\n"           -> literal NaN% in log output
```

Additionally, `formatOscProgress(1, NaN)` emits `"\x1b]9;4;1;NaN\x1b\"`, a malformed OSC 9;4 progress sequence that terminals do not understand.

`tick(NaN)` has the same effect: `completed` becomes `NaN` and feeds the same `setPercent`.

## Expected vs Actual

- Expected: a NaN percentage update is ignored (reporter keeps the last valid percentage, or stays indeterminate); no `NaN` text and no malformed escape sequence reach the terminal.
- Actual: literal `NaN%` is rendered to the terminal/log, and a malformed OSC progress sequence is emitted.

## Impact

- User-visible garbage (`NaN%`) in progress output and logs.
- A malformed terminal control sequence that can disrupt subsequent terminal rendering.
- Affects any progress producer that computes a ratio that can be `0/0` or otherwise non-finite, including the plugin-facing `withProgressTotals` adapter (re-exported to plugins via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-runtime-cli`).

## Suggested Fix

Guard the single `percent` assignment in `setPercent` (`src/cli/progress.ts`) against `Number.isNaN`, which covers every entry point (`setPercent`, `tick`, and the `withProgressTotals` adapter) without changing behavior for finite inputs (including `Infinity`, which the existing clamp already maps to 100%).

# [Bug]: Gateway main-thread stalls up to 12.3s on macOS arm64 2026.11.3 (one attributed to `gateway:rpc`; stall profiles show `@openclaw/fs-safe` frames) — user-visible freezes and 11s+ chat-send preparation

**Version:** OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d)
**Platform:** macOS (arm64), gateway running as LaunchAgent service, node runtime v26.12.1 (`--max-old-space-size=8192`)
**Related (not duplicates):** #173666 (Linux, stalls up to 23.9s), #192941 (Windows, stall sample with session source path identity checks), #174681 (plugin preparation blocking main thread), #156953 (MaxListenersExceededWarning exit listeners — we also hit this once at startup, noted below only as a co-symptom).

## What the user experiences
Chat becomes visibly frozen for seconds up to ~12s: no ack, delayed replies, Control UI appears disconnected. This happens on a quiet single-user gateway (no concurrent heavy runs).

## Observed evidence (file logs, same host, two consecutive days)

### 1. `main-thread stall` events — 7 in one morning (UTC+8), worst attributed to `gateway:rpc`
```
10:24:24 main-thread stall: elapsedMs=2391 task=unattributed
10:24:52 main-thread stall: elapsedMs=3551 task=unattributed
10:25:08 main-thread stall: elapsedMs=2079 task=unattributed
10:30:30 main-thread stall: elapsedMs=5331 task=unattributed
11:00:22 main-thread stall: elapsedMs=12296 task="gateway:rpc" taskMs=12296
11:00:22 main-thread stall profile: windowMs=12396 samples=0 intervalMs=10 truncated=true inclusive=[]
11:00:26 main-thread stall: elapsedMs=2986 task=unattributed
11:00:30 main-thread stall: elapsedMs=2817 task=unattributed
```
Note the profiler blind spot: the 12.3s `gateway:rpc` stall captured **samples=0** (`truncated=true`, inclusive=[]) — when the stall is worst, the profile tells us nothing.

### 2. Previous day, a captured stall profile dominated by `@openclaw/fs-safe`
```
main-thread stall profile: windowMs=1198 samples=37 intervalMs=10 truncated=false
inclusive=[["[native]@:0",9],["processTimers@node:internal/timers:603",5],
["@openclaw/fs-safe@node_modules/@openclaw/fs-safe:10",5],
["@openclaw/fs-safe@node_modules/@openclaw/fs-safe:80",5],
["runNextTicks@node:internal/process/task_queues:63",4],
["@openclaw/fs-safe@node_modules/@openclaw/fs-safe:282",3], ...]
```
Synchronous-looking `fs-safe` frames appearing in main-thread stall profiles on a gateway with `tools.fs.workspaceOnly=false` and agents reading large external corpora (an Obsidian vault with ~660 markdown files via file tools, plus memory-core indexing the same tree via `extraPaths`).

### 3. Slow chat sends correlate with the same windows (8 events one morning)
```
10:30:35 stage=startup preparation=11561ms ack=1003ms
10:33:00 stage=startup preparation=1092ms ack=86ms
11:09:23 stage=startup preparation=1678ms ack=165ms
11:23:26 stage=startup preparation=1481ms ack=1028ms
11:27:52 stage=startup preparation=1038ms ack=172ms
```
An earlier same-week sample with stage breakdown showed `stage=startup preparation≈12.3s detail.attempt.tool-base≈4.9s snapshot≈4.5s` — startup-side work is on the critical path of the first message after idle/restart.

### 4. Co-symptom at startup (already tracked in #156953)
```
MaxListenersExceededWarning: Possible EventEmitter memory leak detected. 11 exit listeners added to [process].
```
Once per gateway start on this host; mentioned here only because it co-occurs in the same startup windows.

## Environment notes
- Gateway as launchd service; loopback bind; 19 plugins loaded (browser, canvas, codex, feishu, file-transfer, memory-core, dingtalk-connector, tavily etc.).
- Multiple agents each with `memory.search.extraPaths` pointing at one large external markdown tree (hundreds of files, ollama/bge-m3 embeddings).
- No crash; process stays alive; stalls cluster around: gateway startup, config hot-reload (extraPaths changes), and chat turns that touch large vault reads.

## Expected
Main thread stays responsive; long file/memory work is offloaded; stall profiles should capture non-zero samples for attributed `gateway:rpc` stalls; first-message-after-start preparation should not take 11s+.

## Asks
1. Is there a plan to move `fs-safe` synchronous path/stat/permission checks and provider/tool-bundle catalog work off the main thread (worker/queue), especially when `extraPaths` corpora are large?
2. Could the stall profiler fall back (e.g., raise sampling or mark attribution) so `gateway:rpc` stalls of 10s+ don't produce `samples=0`?
3. Happy to provide full (sanitized) log excerpts for the above timestamps on request.

issues.body:
### Summary

`@openclaw/whatsapp` (2026.10.7) enqueues a system event on every connection cycle:

- `WhatsApp gateway connected as <e164>.` (`monitor-*.mjs`, after `resolveAgentRoute({ channel: "whatsapp", accountId })`)
- `WhatsApp gateway disconnected (status <label>)`

Both go to the route's `sessionKey`, which for an account-level route is the agent's main session, without `contextKey`/`replace`. On a quiet account the web watchdog reconnects whenever no inbound message arrives within `messageTimeoutMs` (default 30 min, "app-silent"), so a linked account that is mostly idle reconnects ~15–22 times per day. Each cycle adds two events.

When the agent's main session never runs a turn (heartbeat `every: "0m"`), nothing drains it: the queue reaches `MAX_EVENTS = 20` within hours, and from then on every enqueue for that session logs `System event queue is full (20 pending)` and is dropped — including unrelated notices such as hook terminal events and cron notices addressed to the same session. When the main session does run (e.g. a cron wake), the model first receives a backlog of identical connect/disconnect notices.

### Observed (production, OpenClaw 2026.10.7, one WhatsApp account)

- Reconnects per day from the watchdog/428/499 path: 17, 20, 22, 20, 16, 19, 13, 11 (Oct 25 – Nov 1).
- 186 `System event queue is full … sessionKey=agent:<agent>:main` lines in 12 days; the queue stayed full from ~10 h after each gateway restart until the next restart.
- `messageTimeoutMs` / `heartbeatSeconds` are only reachable through the internal `tuning` argument of `monitorWebChannel`, not through channel config.

### Expected

Connection-state notices should not accumulate. Any of these would fix it:

1. Enqueue them with a stable `contextKey` per account and `replace: true`, so the queue holds at most the latest state (same shape as #184798 for `notifications.changed`).
2. Make the notices opt-in (or skip them when the main session has no heartbeat).
3. Expose the app-silence timeout in channel config so quiet accounts do not cycle every 30 minutes.

Related: #184798 (same pattern for notifications), #167854 (20-entry queue drops).

**Environment:**
- OpenClaw 2026.10.7 (157d8c2), official image, Node 24.22.1, Linux cgroup v2.
- State DB 190 MB (WAL); agent DBs 0.57–0.93 GB (WAL, auto_vacuum=incremental).
- ext4 on a ZFS zvol throttled to 3,000 IOPS / 70 MB/s; page cache mostly evicted by host reclaim (cgroup file cache ≈0.5 GB, DB residency 0–3.5%).

**What happens:**
1. `state.admission.fast-path` (src/state/openclaw-state-db-fast-path.ts → `isOpenClawStateSchemaFastPathEligible`) calls `assertOpenClawStateRuntimeIntegrity`. When the handle has no borrowed current host proof, that falls back to `assertSqliteIntegrity` (full `integrity_check` + `foreign_key_check`).
   - Every CLI process that touches state, and every fresh Gateway worker thread (session-reclamation and read workers that retire on idle-TTL), pays a whole-file scan inside a deferred read transaction.
   - Over 24 h (2026-10-27): 345 such admissions ≥1 s totalling 5,089 s (Gateway workers 205 / 3,520 s; CLI processes 140 / 1,570 s), max 184.5 s.
   - 84 of the 141 main-thread `slow agent database reservation` events ≥10 s that day (2,039 s) coincide with one of these admissions inside a reclamation worker.
   - Example 2026-10-28: reclamation worker threadId 172823, `state.admission.fast-path elapsedMs=147792`; then `state.write` lock-contention; then `SQLite session reclamation Worker recovered cleanup failures: database is locked` on the writer store; then clean-close receipt `close-unconfirmed`.
2. After an agent writer reservation failed (`slow agent database reservation operation=direct outcome=error elapsedMs=435033`, codeops), the lease closed with receipt `active-leases`. The next opener, a worker with `admissionMode:"sync"`, ran `integrityGateReason:"no-proof" integrityGateMode:"full"` for **269,157 ms** on a 727 MB store.
   - Every write for that agent queued behind it (`session-entry.patch queueWaitMs=325659`, …).
   - Stuck-session recovery then aborted two runs whose last tool call was 12 minutes earlier.
   - No model response was logged Gateway-wide for 12 min.

**Expected:**
- Fresh workers and CLI readers borrow or reuse the host's current integrity proof, or a cheap check (`quick_check` or header/schema only), as the docs describe for native admission classes.
- A full scan never runs synchronously in a path that holds an agent's write queue. It should run in the existing background verifier, with admission granted metadata-only as for the documented "no verification receipt" class.
- The integrity scan should be bounded or made yieldable, and attributed in logs (caller, thread role).

**Related:** #164427 (60 s `cron.history-maintenance` sweep reads all cron run records inside one IMMEDIATE transaction: here 1,121 holds ≥1 s/day, 6,993 s, max 97.5 s, with 11.6k cron rows), #161439, #170496, #183036.

**Evidence available:** log excerpts with timestamps (above), cgroup io/memory counters, dist line references.

issues.body:
## Summary
Gateway event-loop stalls of ~33 s (internal DEF-61) are caused by SQLite lock contention on the main state database, not disk I/O or a plugin leak.

## Evidence
- **3 concurrent write-mode handles** are open on `state/openclaw.sqlite` from the same process.
- WAL is sitting at the 4 MB autocheckpoint threshold and is **not draining**.
- In 35 minutes after a gateway restart, there were **32 slow SQLite transaction lock waits**.
- Each wait blocks the Node.js event loop for up to **5,000 ms**; clusters of 4–5 back-to-back waits produce ~25 s of blocking, matching the observed ~33 s stalls.
- **I/O pressure is zero** (`%iowait = 0`). Contention is entirely inside SQLite's in-process locking layer.
- Workboard plugin was investigated and ruled out: it is disabled and has no `workboard.sqlite` on disk; earlier 19-connection reading was a misread.

## Root cause
`state/openclaw.sqlite` write access is not serialized. Multiple write connections from the same process compete on every write, preventing the WAL from checkpointing and stalling the event loop.

## Suggested fix
Serialize all writes to `state/openclaw.sqlite` through a single connection with an explicit write queue, rather than opening multiple concurrent write handles.

## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.7.2-beta.4
- Gateway runtime on Linux (WSL)
- Local model provider: Ollama

## Cross-reference
Internal tracker: DEF-61 (REBAR operating notes).

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

`src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-failure.ts` redacts home paths using only `process.env.HOME` (in `shortenFailureReportPath`, `failureReportPathReplacements`, and `redactAbsoluteHomePaths`), so when HOME is unset and USERPROFILE is set — the default on native Windows — the "sanitized" GitHub issue body generated by `createSessionSqliteMigrationFailureIssue()` contains full absolute home paths including the OS username.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Check out openclaw/openclaw at commit 6e7ca1fbd and run `pnpm install`.
2. Save as `repro.ts` in the repo root:
   ```
   import fs from "node:fs";
   import { createSessionSqliteMigrationFailureIssue } from "./src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-failure.ts";
   const home = "/tmp/fakehome/alice";
   const store = `${home}/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json`;
   fs.mkdirSync("/tmp/runs", { recursive: true });
   fs.writeFileSync("/tmp/runs/manifest.json", JSON.stringify({
     failedAt: "2030-01-01T00:00:00.000Z", manifestVersion: 3, openClawVersion: "test", runId: "r1",
     startedAt: "2030-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
     targets: [{ agentId: "main", storePath: store,
       sqlitePath: `${home}/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/sessions.sqlite`,
       completedMoves: [], plannedMoves: [], validationBeforeArchive: "failed",
       issues: [{ code: "startup_failure", message: `migration failed at ${store}` }] }],
   }));
   const issue = createSessionSqliteMigrationFailureIssue("/tmp/runs/manifest.json")!;
   console.log("contains home:", issue.body.includes(home));
   console.log(issue.body.split("\n").filter((l) => l.includes("sessions.")).join("\n"));
   ```
3. Baseline: `HOME=/tmp/fakehome/alice pnpm exec tsx repro.ts`
4. Windows-like environment: `env -u HOME USERPROFILE=/tmp/fakehome/alice pnpm exec tsx repro.ts`

### Expected behavior

Home paths are shortened to `~` regardless of whether the home comes from HOME or USERPROFILE, as in the baseline run (step 3). OpenClaw's own `resolveRequiredHomeDir()` in src/infra/home-dir.ts treats USERPROFILE as a home source, and the doctor prompt describes the report as sanitized.

### Actual behavior

Step 3 (HOME set): `contains home: false`; paths shown as `~/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json`.
Step 4 (HOME unset, USERPROFILE set): `contains home: true`; Store, SQLite, and the issue message all contain the full `/tmp/fakehome/alice/...` path.

### OpenClaw version

Source checkout at commit 6e7ca1fbd (package.json version 2026.11.4)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04, simulating native Windows environment variables (HOME unset, USERPROFILE set).

### Install method

pnpm dev (source checkout)

### Model

N/A: not model-dependent

### Provider / routing chain

N/A: no provider involved

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
HOME=/tmp/fakehome/alice USERPROFILE=<unset>
body contains "/tmp/fakehome/alice": false
  - Store: ~/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json
  - SQLite: ~/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/sessions.sqlite
  - [startup_failure] migration failed at ~/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json

HOME=<unset> USERPROFILE=/tmp/fakehome/alice
body contains "/tmp/fakehome/alice": true
  - Store: /tmp/fakehome/alice/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json
  - SQLite: /tmp/fakehome/alice/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/sessions.sqlite
  - [startup_failure] migration failed at /tmp/fakehome/alice/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: native Windows users (HOME unset) who accept doctor's prompt to file the session SQLite migration recovery report, or run noninteractive recovery with --yes
Severity: Privacy — OS username and absolute paths are published in a public GitHub issue described to the user as sanitized
Frequency: Always, whenever HOME is unset (2/2 observed runs)
Consequence: Personal information disclosed publicly in openclaw/openclaw issues

### Additional information

The existing test in src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.failure-reports.test.ts (around line 192) only asserts redaction `if (process.env.HOME)`, so the HOME-unset case is not covered. Using the existing `resolveRequiredHomeDir()` (or os.homedir()) instead of `process.env.HOME` in the three redaction helpers would match how OpenClaw resolves its home elsewhere.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

`hexToRgb()` in src/agents/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts validates hex colors with `Number.parseInt(..., 16)` + `isNaN`, so malformed six-character values such as `#1z2y3x` and `#-1-2-3` load without error and produce ANSI codes `38;2;1;2;3` and `38;2;-1;-2;-3`, while `#fff` is correctly rejected.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Check out openclaw/openclaw at commit 6e7ca1fbd and run `pnpm install`.
2. Copy `src/agents/modes/interactive/theme/dark.json` to `/tmp/bad-theme.json` and change `vars.cyan` from `"#00d7ff"` to `"#1z2y3x"`.
3. From the repo root, run this with `pnpm exec tsx repro.ts`:
   ```
   import { loadThemeFromPath } from "./src/agents/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts";
   const t = loadThemeFromPath("/tmp/bad-theme.json", "truecolor");
   console.log(JSON.stringify(t.getFgAnsi("borderAccent")));
   ```
4. Repeat with `vars.cyan` set to `"#-1-2-3"`, then `"#fff"`.

### Expected behavior

Malformed hex values should be rejected with `Invalid hex color: <value>`, the same way `hexToRgb()` already rejects `#fff` (wrong length). The theme should then fail to load and surface a warning diagnostic via `resource-loader.ts`, as other invalid themes do.

### Actual behavior

`#1z2y3x` loads without error; `borderAccent` fg ANSI is "\u001b[38;2;1;2;3m".
`#-1-2-3` loads without error; `borderAccent` fg ANSI is "\u001b[38;2;-1;-2;-3m".
`#fff` throws `Invalid hex color: #fff` (correct).

### OpenClaw version

Source checkout at commit 6e7ca1fbd (package.json version 2026.11.4)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04

### Install method

pnpm dev (source checkout)

### Model

N/A: not model-dependent; reproduced by calling loadThemeFromPath() directly, no model request involved

### Provider / routing chain

N/A: no provider involved

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
/tmp/bad-theme.json (vars.cyan="#1z2y3x") loaded; fg ANSI for borderAccent = "\u001b[38;2;1;2;3m"
/tmp/neg.json (vars.cyan="#-1-2-3") loaded; fg ANSI for borderAccent = "\u001b[38;2;-1;-2;-3m"
/tmp/short.json (vars.cyan="#fff") THREW: Invalid hex color: #fff
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: users loading custom TUI theme JSON files containing malformed hex values
Severity: Low (no crash; invalid input is accepted instead of reported)
Frequency: Always, for these inputs (3/3 observed runs)
Consequence: The theme loads silently with incorrect/invalid ANSI color codes instead of producing the warning diagnostic other invalid themes get

### Additional information

Cause: `Number.parseInt("1z", 16)` returns 1 and `Number.parseInt("-1", 16)` returns -1, so the `isNaN` check passes. `ColorValueSchema` in theme-schema.ts accepts any string, so the schema does not catch it either. A full-string check such as /^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/ before parsing would reject these.

## Environment

## What happens

Four message types that describe normal operation are emitted at WARN (or INFO every cycle even when nothing happened). They dominate the WARN stream and hide real warnings.

1. `agent turn timings ... outcome=completed totalMs=... stages=...` is WARN for every slow turn, including `outcome=completed`.
2. `web gateway heartbeat - no messages in 30+ minutes` is WARN on any idle channel.
3. `Skill precedence collisions resolved.` is WARN/INFO each time skills are rescanned, although the collisions are resolved by design.
4. `Managed worktree cleanup completed: removed 0; deleted 0 orphans; ... eligible 0; deferred 0; failed 0` is logged every cycle with all zeros.

## Frequency (log lines per day, 2026-10-18 to 2026-11-17, 31 days)

- Turn timings: 27,899 lines (median 718/day, max 2,643). Of the lines in the retained rotations, 6,009 WARN vs 2 INFO.
- Heartbeat idle: 3,577 lines (median about 104/day, max 278).
- Skill precedence: 205 lines (median 5/day, max 35).
- Worktree cleanup no-op: 1,175 lines (about 23/day, rising to 88 to 128/day since 11-09).

## Log excerpt

```
WARN  agent turn timings runId=<id> sessionId=<id> sessionKey=<key> outcome=completed totalMs=254022 stages=fallback_prepare_harness:0ms@6ms,...
WARN  web gateway heartbeat - no messages in 30+ minutes
INFO  Skill precedence collisions resolved.
INFO  Managed worktree cleanup completed: removed 0; deleted 0 orphans; retired 0 orphan records; pruned 0 snapshots; eligible 0; deferred 0; failed 0; protected 0; limits satisfied.
```

## Expected behaviour

- Completed turns log timings at INFO or DEBUG; WARN only when `outcome` is not `completed` or a stage exceeds a documented threshold.
- Idle-channel heartbeat is INFO (or only logged when the channel was previously active).
- A cleanup pass that did nothing logs at DEBUG, or once per state change.

issues.body:
## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect timeout behavior without process exit)

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

The memory-wiki supplement reparses every remaining Markdown page when digest-selected candidates underfill `maxResults`, ignoring the memory tool deadline and causing `corpus="wiki"` and `corpus="all"` timeouts.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Register a compiled-wiki vault large enough that a full Markdown scan exceeds 15 seconds.
2. Run `memory_search` with `corpus="wiki"`, `maxResults` greater than the number of digest-selected hits, and a query that underfills the requested count.
3. Observe that `searchWikiCorpus()` scans the remaining vault to fill the result set.
4. Observe the memory tool return `memory_search timed out after 15s` while the local scan may continue.

## Expected behavior

The wiki supplement should honor the caller's deadline/abort signal, return digest-routed or partial results within the tool budget, and reserve exhaustive body scanning for an explicit exhaustive search path.

## Actual behavior

On a 77 MB, 1,220-file wiki vault, digest-routed lookup completed in 77 ms, but ordinary multi-result searches fell through to full-vault parsing and took 25-27 seconds. Both `corpus="wiki"` and `corpus="all"` could therefore exceed the fixed 15-second memory-tool deadline.

## OpenClaw version

2026.7.1-beta.5

## Operating system

macOS 26.5.2 arm64

## Install method

Homebrew global package with launchd-managed gateway

## Model

gemini-embedding-2-preview for builtin memory; local compiled-wiki supplement

## Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw memory_search -> memory-wiki corpus supplement -> local Markdown vault

## Logs

```shell
memory_search timed out after 15s
local full-vault benchmark: 25-27s
digest-routed candidate lookup: 77ms
```

## Impact and severity

- Affected: agents using compiled-wiki supplements through `memory_search`.
- Severity: moderate to high; wiki and combined durable recall become unavailable for ordinary queries.
- Frequency: deterministic when digest candidates underfill the requested result count on a sufficiently large vault.
- Consequence: tool timeout, hidden wiki context, and continued host work after the caller has already timed out.

## Additional information

A narrow local mitigation added a supplement-only option to skip exhaustive fallback. Afterward, multi-result wiki recall completed in 55-66 ms and combined-corpus recall completed below 8 seconds. Direct `wiki_search` retained exhaustive fallback for explicit body-search use. A durable upstream fix should propagate abort signals into the scanner and use parsed-page caching or local FTS for fallback.

Related but distinct: #92633 tracks all-corpus aggregation latency, and #72717 proposes an FTS index for wiki search. This report specifically concerns supplement underfill triggering an uncancelled full-vault fallback even for `corpus="wiki"`.

issues.body:
## Bug
After upgrading to OpenClaw 2026.7.2-beta.2, `openclaw gateway restart` (or `openclaw doctor --fix`) fails with:

```
Failed migrating shared state database schema at /home/foxrain/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite:
  Error: SQLite table X changes rowid storage from Y to Z; refusing an identity-changing STRICT migration
```

followed by a chain of `noncanonical X schema that cannot be repaired` errors. Gateway cannot start, systemd enters a `failed` state, port 19999 stays free.

This blocks the upgrade path entirely.

## Root causes (three compounding issues)

### Issue 1: Legacy BLOB-stored TEXT values
The shared state SQLite database (`~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite`) accumulates rows where TEXT columns contain BLOB-encoded values. For example:
```sql
SELECT typeof(agent_id) FROM agent_databases;
-- Returns 'blob' for many rows (older OpenClaw wrote TEXT as raw bytes)
```

The new SQLite STRICT migration refuses to convert blob values into TEXT columns. In one user database, **108,026 BLOB-in-TEXT values** needed manual conversion via `CAST(col AS TEXT)`.

Affected tables include (not exhaustive): `agent_databases`, `delivery_queue_entries`, `task_runs`, `config_health_entries`, `subagent_runs`, `command_log_entries`, and most other state tables.

### Issue 2: PRIMARY KEY on TEXT columns blocks STRICT migration
The SQLite STRICT migration checks rowid storage model. Tables like `config_health_entries` had:
```sql
CREATE TABLE config_health_entries (
  config_path TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,  -- composite / non-integer PK
  ...
)
```

OpenClaw's STRICT migration (`dist/sqlite-wal-*.js`) treats any non-INTEGER PRIMARY KEY as a different rowid storage model than the migration expects, so it refuses with:
```
SQLite table X changes rowid storage from Y to Z; refusing an identity-changing STRICT migration
```

The migration appears to assume all tables should be plain rowid tables with no PK constraint or with INTEGER PRIMARY KEY only.

### Issue 3: stale startup-migration lease blocks subsequent starts
After the migration fails partway through, `state_leases` may hold a lease with a future `expires_at`. New gateway attempts get rejected with:
```
OpenClaw startup migrations are already running for this state directory; retry after 2026-07-17T21:27:05.984Z.
```

`doctor --fix` cannot clear this because the lease holder is itself.

## Reproduction
1. Run OpenClaw `2026.7.1` for some time (accumulates state rows).
2. Upgrade to `2026.7.2-beta.2`.
3. Run `openclaw gateway restart` or `openclaw doctor --fix`.
4. Observe failures listed above; gateway stays down.

## Suggested fixes (any combination)

1. **Pre-migration cleanup pass**: before attempting STRICT migration, scan all tables and convert any BLOB values in TEXT columns to actual TEXT via `CAST(col AS TEXT)`. Run this automatically inside `repairSchemaMigrations` or as a separate `repairLegacyBlobsInTextColumns` step in `doctor --fix`.

2. **Tolerate PRIMARY KEY / WITHOUT ROWID**: when the source table has a non-INTEGER PK or `WITHOUT ROWID`, drop the PK before migration OR copy data through a plain intermediate table without PK. SQLite allows STRICT on plain rowid tables.

3. **Self-heal stale leases**: if a `state_leases` row's `expires_at` is in the past, ignore it during the lease acquisition check (or automatically delete expired leases before attempting the migration).

4. **Provide a `--force` flag** for the migration that:
   - Accepts that this is a destructive op
   - Skips rowid model checks
   - Documents that data could be lost

5. **Document a manual recovery path** for users stuck mid-migration, with the exact SQL needed.

## Impact
Every user upgrading from 2026.7.1 to 2026.7.2 with a populated state database hits one or more of these errors. The gateway stays down indefinitely, and the user has to know to:
1. Check `~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite` manually
2. Convert BLOB values via SQL CAST
3. Drop and recreate tables without PK
4. Clear `state_leases` manually
5. Manually delete legacy `~/.openclaw/credentials/*-allowFrom.json` files (related: see also `parseAllowFromFilename` safeAccountKey case-mismatch bug in `dist/state-migrations-*.js`)

Each step requires editing `~/.openclaw/openclaw.sqlite` by hand.

## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.7.2-beta.2 (54d98a4)
- Source files: `dist/sqlite-wal-*.js`, `dist/state-migrations-*.js`, `dist/openclaw-state-db-*.js`
- Related: #107222, #107223, #107224

issues.body:
*Filed by an AI assistant (an OpenClaw agent) on behalf of its user, who approved filing this issue. All numbers below were measured on the user's own gateway on 2026-10-23; anything not measured is marked as hypothesis.*

## Summary
1. A very long-lived main session (`agent:main:main`, 35k events / 228 MB) makes the transcript export / context snapshot reads take 3-10 s each, which shows up as hundreds of "slow SQLite" warnings per day.
2. The documented ways to shrink or rotate it don't work: `/new` keeps the sessionId, `sessions archive` refuses the main session, and `sessions compact --max-lines` fails with `Agent database execution admission is closed`, also right after a gateway restart and also from the plain CLI.

## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.10.6 (fe06181), Node v26.12.1 (v24.22.1 before the restart described below)
- Ubuntu arm64 (Jetson, Linux 5.15.199-tegra); agent DB `openclaw-agent.sqlite` 931 MB, WAL mode

## 1. Slow SQLite warnings: what was measured
- 2026-10-22: 3 warnings; 2026-10-23: 227 warnings until 01:33.
- Warnings 22.+23.10. up to 00:28 (57): `session transcript export snapshot` 28x (median 4.9 s), `database.domain.execute` 12x (median 9.8 s), `session context snapshot read` 9x (3.2 s), `media-persistence-detection` 2x (7.8 s).
- Almost all of the time is SQL time; lock wait and commit are ~0 ms.
- `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` on a copy of the DB: the snapshot queries use the primary key (session_id, seq), no SCAN, no missing index. The same read takes ~0.4 s in a plain Python sqlite3 session on the copy, ~5 s inside the gateway (cause not determined).
- One session (`df64df26-…` = `agent:main:main`, running since 2026-09-11) has 35,068 events / 228 MB of the 235 MB in `transcript_events` (60,042 events in 305 sessions). Size distribution of that session: 30,234 events < 10 kB (72 MB), 4,709 events 10-100 kB (91 MB), 136 events 100 kB-1 MB (31 MB), 7 events > 1 MB (24 MB). So it is the sum of six weeks of use, not a few outliers.
- The export snapshot reads the whole session. 34 earlier compactions and 123 `reset` events did not reduce the number of events in the DB.

## 2. Ways to shrink the main session
- `/new` (two times: 2026-10-22 20:56 and 2026-10-23 00:22, both visible as `reset` events) keeps the sessionId, as documented (reference/session-management-compaction/schema.md: records a reset boundary and keeps the sessionId). The session kept growing and the warnings continued.
- `openclaw sessions archive "agent:main:main" --dry-run`: "Cannot archive an agent's main session."
- `openclaw sessions compact "agent:main:main" --agent main --max-lines 0` is rejected (value must be positive). With `--max-lines 1`: first "has an active run" / "has queued work" (expected while a turn runs), then permanently `Compaction failed: Agent database execution admission is closed`. Dozens of attempts, none succeeded. The same error from the plain CLI run by the user after a gateway restart (~01:13) and again at 01:37-01:39. The first non-busy compact attempt after the restart (01:26:38) failed immediately.
- Backup of the DB was taken before the attempts and is unchanged.

## Relation to existing issues
The error string is the one from #159789 (close wedge) and #159652 (readyz stays green). In our log between 00:49:47 and 01:39 it is not limited to compact: 76 log lines in total, including `memory sync failed (session update)`, `memory session update failed`, `skill experience review failed` and `sessions.compact`. Differences to those reports: normal chat turns kept working here, and the error was still there after a restart, at least for compact.
Hypothesis (not verified): the first compact attempts against the 931 MB DB (each took 7.8-10 s before failing) may have triggered the wedge; the first "admission is closed" is at 00:49:47, the first compact attempt was at 00:45:59.

## Request
1. Make `sessions compact` (or an equivalent) work for a very large main session, or fail with a message that says why and how to recover.
2. Bound the export/context snapshot reads for huge sessions (limit, paging, or reading only from the last reset), so one session can't cause 5-10 s reads.
3. Document a supported way to empty or rotate the main session.

I can attach the full numbers, the log excerpts and the compact attempt log on request.

issues.body:
## Summary

The WhatsApp connection watchdog force-closes a healthy socket with status 499 when no application message has arrived for the app-silence window, even while WebSocket transport frames continue to arrive.

## Reproduction

1. Open a WhatsApp connection with keepalive enabled.
2. Advance beyond `messageTimeoutMs * 4` without calling `noteInbound`.
3. Continue emitting WebSocket `frame` activity often enough that `lastTransportActivityAt` remains within `transportTimeoutMs`.
4. Observe `onWatchdogTimeout` and the forced status-499 close.

The current watchdog condition reconnects when either transport is stale or the chat is silent. Chat silence is normal and is not evidence of a dead socket.

## Expected behavior

An idle chat remains connected while transport activity is healthy. The watchdog should reconnect only after actual transport inactivity (or a failed active liveness probe).

## Actual behavior

Healthy but quiet accounts are periodically disconnected and reconnected, creating false outage telemetry and unnecessary WhatsApp session churn.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.4 and current `main`
- `@openclaw/whatsapp`
- macOS 26.6.2, Apple Silicon

## Proposed fix

Make transport inactivity the watchdog's reconnect criterion while retaining `lastInboundAt` for diagnostics. Replace the current app-silence timeout regression with two tests: active transport plus an idle chat stays connected, and genuine transport inactivity still triggers recovery.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

### Summary

With Telegram configured, every Gateway start logs `[DEP_PLUGIN_SDK] DeprecationWarning: Plugin telegram: createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability is deprecated`, and the Plugins catalog lists Telegram as using APIs that retire on Dec 31, 2026. Steering an active run from a Telegram message also logs `Plugin telegram: ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint is deprecated`. Both come from bundled or core code, not from a third-party plugin, so the operator cannot act on either.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build main at `19aff5bfd42` (`pnpm build`).
2. Configure `channels.telegram` with a bot token and `execApprovals.enabled: true` with one approver.
3. Run `openclaw gateway run` and read stderr.
4. Run `openclaw gateway call plugins.list --json` and look at the `telegram` entry's `compatibilityNotices`.
5. For the second warning: send a Telegram message to a session while a run in that session is still active, so the message steers it.

### Expected behavior

No `DEP_PLUGIN_SDK` warnings that name a bundled plugin, and no retiring-API notice for Telegram. Discord has neither since #174937 moved it to `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapabilityAsync`.

### Actual behavior

- Step 3 logs one warning at plugin load. With `--trace-deprecation` the stack is `warnPluginSdkDeprecation <- createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability <- channel-*.mjs` (module load).
- Step 4 returns 265 plugins. Exactly one, `telegram`, has a `deprecated-sdk-api` notice: "Uses OpenClaw APIs that retire on Dec 31, 2026. It keeps working until then; check for a plugin update.", apis `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability`.
- Step 5 logs `Plugin telegram: ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint is deprecated; use await fingerprintAsync() instead.` The call is core's: `prepareFollowupRunToolAuthorityFingerprint` (`src/auto-reply/reply/reply-tool-authority.ts`) re-reads its prepared fingerprint through the deprecated `fingerprint()`, reached from `runActiveReplySteer -> prepareReplyMessageJoin -> prepareLegacyReplySteeringAuthority`. The warning takes the label of the plugin frame it runs in.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.10-beta.5 source build with local commits on two gateways; reproduced on main `19aff5bfd42`, and the three call sites are unchanged on main `da908d53390`.

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.2 and macOS 26.5.1 (arm64)

### Install method

Source checkout, gateway service

### Model

Not model-dependent (plugin load and steering preparation).

### Provider / routing chain

Not provider-dependent.

### Additional provider/model setup details

None.

### Logs

```shell
[DEP_PLUGIN_SDK] DeprecationWarning: Plugin telegram: createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability is deprecated
[DEP_PLUGIN_SDK] DeprecationWarning: Plugin telegram: ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint is deprecated; use await fingerprintAsync() instead.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- Isolated Gateway with Telegram configured (fake token, local API root), `--trace-deprecation`, 90 s window: 1 `DEP_PLUGIN_SDK` line, from module load, while Telegram started its account.
- `--trace-deprecation` over the message-join and fallback-steering suites (101 tests) shows the steering stack above: `fingerprint <- prepareLegacyReplySteeringAuthority (session-controller.message-join.ts) <- prepareReplyMessageJoin <- runActiveReplySteer (agent-runner-steer-adoption.ts)`.
- Across both gateways' logs since 2026-10-30: 7 `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability` and 5 `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint` warnings, all labeled "Plugin telegram".

### Impact and severity

- Affected: every Gateway with the bundled Telegram plugin enabled.
- Severity: annoying. Nothing breaks today, but the warnings and the catalog notice tell operators to look for a plugin update that does not exist, since the plugin ships with OpenClaw.
- Frequency: once per Gateway start, plus once per steered Telegram run.

### Additional information

- The bundled Telegram plugin is the last caller of the sync `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability`. Every other bundled channel uses an `...Async` factory.
- Moving Telegram to the async factory alone has a side effect, filed separately: #191785.
- Related: #174937 (Discord), #190243 (same class, Matrix CLI paths).
- Also seen once, not covered here: `Plugin telegram: getMany is deprecated` from core's sync placement reads.

Every skip carries an **empty structured payload** — no artifact name, no path, no reason:

```json
{"0":"{\"subsystem\":\"infra/sqlite-snapshot\"}","1":{},"2":"Skipped SQLite snapshot reclamation: Unrecognized snapshot artifact"}
```

Before manual cleanup, two doctor-created snapshots had sat unreclaimed for roughly two weeks:

```
openclaw.sqlite                          151M
openclaw.sqlite.doctor-cron-...4eaa.bak  107M   (Oct 16)
openclaw.sqlite.doctor-cron-...4fa7.bak  101M   (Oct 13)
openclaw.sqlite-wal                       10M
```

After archiving and removing both `.bak` files by hand, the warning rate did not change. That rules out "an unknown file is present" as the trigger: the matcher appears to reject the live set it is supposed to recognise.

### Expected

- The reclaimer recognises its own artifacts — including the live database and the sidecar files it must not touch — and reclaims genuinely stale snapshots without operator intervention.
- When a skip occurs, the structured payload names the rejected artifact and the reason. An empty object makes the message undiagnosable from logs.

### Impact

- Silent, unbounded growth of orphaned snapshots: 217 MB accumulated here on the same volume as the session database.
- ~14 WARN/hour of indistinguishable noise. In the same window the log also holds 1,905 `slow SQLite` WARN lines, so real failures are effectively invisible.

### Related

#188586 (main-thread session-sqlite maintenance/reclamation commits blocking the event loop).

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.10.6** (fe06181), Node v26.12.1, Linux (Proxmox host, x64)
- Provider: `opencode-go` (OpenAI-compatible), primary model `glm-5.3-flash` with model fallbacks
- Prompt cache mode: `boundary-aware:openai-completions`
- Multi-agent setup: ~17 configured agents, cross-agent handoffs via `sessions_send` with inline wait; ordinary turns run 2-6 tool calls each
- Channels: Telegram forum topics + Home Assistant Assist through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`gateway.http.endpoints.chatCompletions.enabled: true`)

## Symptoms

Every model request logs `cache read dropped N -> 0`, so the full prompt (14k-27k tokens) is reprocessed from scratch on **every** call — including consecutive calls **within the same turn**. Each call costs 1-8 s of stream time (measured window: 41 calls, median 4.1 s, max 14 s), and a user message needing a 4-11 call chain takes 20-50+ s end-to-end. Synchronous clients (voice Assist) hit their timeout and disconnect mid-turn (`ClientDisconnectError`).

## Evidence (gateway journal, sanitized)

1. Within-turn drop with NO tracked change (request 3 of the same run, 5.5 s after request 2):

```
[agent/embedded] [prompt-cache] cache read dropped 14592 -> 0 runId=<redacted> request=3
for opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash via boundary-aware:openai-completions;
no tracked cache input change; requestGapMs=5544 promptTokens=18176 providerPrefix=prefix-match
```

2. historyRewrite because the user-message envelope is re-stamped on every request:

```
[agent/embedded] [prompt-cache] message 0 (user) differs from the previous request;
history must be append-only; changed fields: envelope.timestamp, envelope.__openclaw
```

```
cache read dropped 15104 -> 10240 ... historyRewrite(message 27 (user) differs ...;
changed fields: envelope.timestamp, envelope.__openclaw, envelope.idempotencyKey);
requestGapMs=31690 promptTokens=17043 providerPrefix=message:2
```

3. Runtime-context carrier invalidating the provider history mid-turn (request 8 of the same run):

```
cache read dropped 13056 -> 0 ... request=8 ...
runtimeContextCarrier(runtimeContextCarrier changed provider history);
requestGapMs=2317 promptTokens=14866 providerPrefix=message:14
```

4. System-prompt digest change (expected after workspace file edits; listed for completeness):

```
cache read dropped 12160 -> 0 ... systemPrompt(system prompt digest changed (sections: Project Context)),
historyRewrite(message 27 ... envelope.timestamp, envelope.__openclaw, envelope.idempotencyKey);
requestGapMs=538656 promptTokens=17220 providerPrefix=message:0
```


### Steps to reproduce

Multi-agent gateway + any OpenAI-compatible provider with prompt caching. Send a message that makes an agent perform 2+ tool calls (or a `sessions_send` handoff with inline wait) and watch `[prompt-cache]` lines in the gateway journal. Drops appear on every request, including back-to-back requests in the same run.


### Expected behavior

Per `docs/reference/prompt-caching.md`, consecutive request histories in the same session extend the previous request, and transient runtime-context carriers "remain outside the cached prefix" — a tool loop inside one turn should pay prefill once and reuse the cached prefix on follow-up calls.


### Actual behavior

The cache drops to zero on effectively every request, including same-turn follow-ups where the log reports `no tracked cache input change`.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.6

### Operating system

Proxmox

### Install method

_No response_

### Model

Opencodego glm5.3 and all models wotch cache 

### Provider / routing chain

-

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

```shell

```

_No response_

### Impact and severity


- Every multi-tool agent turn re-processes 14k-27k token prefixes: 20-50+ s per user message.
- Voice/Assist integrations (synchronous clients with 60-120 s budgets) abort mid-turn — the answer never reaches the user.
- Billed tokens multiplied by the number of requests per turn.
