prs.title: fix: avoid false identity errors when unlinked channel users create sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes independent session creation failing for an admitted, unlinked channel sender when the agent supplies a Team profile ID discovered outside the current request.

## User Impact

Admitted unlinked senders can use the same restricted creation path as calls that omit `user`. Valid linked-participant selection remains available; invalid or revoked linked selections remain errors. No new permissions, configuration, or account-linking requirement.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the optional selector and existing creation owner. Determine fallback eligibility from the ingress owner's original authenticated sender/account linkage result, not a model-supplied ID, another session's owner, or the absence of a current profile. Carry that fact privately to the admitted request and use it only for this independent-creation fallback.

The original refusal correctly prevented an unsupported identity selection; it was not a privilege escalation. This avoids an unnecessary failure without removing collaborative participant selection.

## Evidence

- **Red/green:** at the base, omitted-user creation passed while the same admitted unlinked source with a supplied unrelated profile failed before creation. The fix makes both use the existing contained creation path.
- **Final candidate:** 15 owning-boundary and reply-producer tests passed, exercising ingress, private handoff, run admission, the real tool/router, and SQLite creation. Restrictions remain inherited; mismatched, linked-without-grant, unverified, internal, serialized, known-bot, and retired sources do not gain fallback eligibility. Other tools retain explicit-user validation.
- **Sibling coverage:** 200 affected-consumer tests and 78 selected collaboration/native tests passed, including stable tool definitions, original-requester defaults, valid Bob selection, revocation, overlapping Alice/Bob calls, and queued custody. These broader results preceded the final private-handoff simplification; unchanged-input proof was reused, and every changed handoff contract was rerun in the final 15-test batch.
- Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, diff checks, and commit hooks passed.
- **Independent review:** shared autoreview using Codex CLI, complete P0–P2 assessment of the full candidate against base `b9a72b5bef8d648024f89b66af9579691ae40ce1`, returned `scoped-clean` with no findings. The committed diff matches the reviewed snapshot. Local ClawSweeper was not used because its available checkout was dirty/ambiguous; it was left unchanged. The reviewer did not run project tests.

**Limitations:** these are isolated production-owner/composition tests with fixed or mocked model/transport I/O, not live Discord/real-model end-to-end proof. No restart, upgrade, or native-engine E2E claim is made. The private finding deliberately does not survive serialization, restart reconstruction, or another operational run; those paths keep normal selection validation.

### Original failure

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Sender as Admitted unlinked sender
  participant Agent as Agent
  participant Tool as sessions_create
  participant Runtime as Trusted runtime
  Sender->>Agent: Create an independent session
  Agent->>Agent: Copy profile ID from another session's owner
  Agent->>Tool: Create with user set to copied ID
  Tool->>Runtime: Resolve admitted participant
  Runtime-->>Tool: No person authority for supplied ID
  Tool-->>Agent: Refuse before creation
  Note over Tool,Runtime: Correct identity guard; no security bypass
```

### After: preserve valid selection and the unlinked path

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Admitted messaging-service request] --> B[Ingress owner resolves sender and account linkage]
  B -->|Originally unlinked source| C[Retain private direct-source unlinked finding]
  C --> D[sessions_create ignores supplied user]
  B -->|Linked requester| E[Keep existing participant selection]
  E -->|Unknown or revoked selection| F[Refuse without creation]
  E -->|Valid selection or original-requester default| G[Existing creation owner]
  D --> G
  G --> H[Inherit sandbox, tool limits and permission ceiling]
  H --> I[Create independent session]
  J[Missing or unsupported source evidence] --> K[No fallback; existing validation applies]
```

### Identity, assignment, and permissions remain separate

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Human as Linked requester or authorized administrator
  participant Runtime as Admitted runtime
  participant Create as Creation owner
  participant Assign as Ownership assignment
  Human->>Runtime: Request creation
  Runtime->>Create: Validated requester or allowed unlinked context
  Create->>Create: Enforce inherited permission ceiling
  Create-->>Human: New session with normal ownership rules
  Human->>Assign: Assign to another person, if authorized
  Assign->>Assign: Change responsibility metadata
  Note over Runtime,Assign: Assignment does not replace requester identity or transfer authority
```

Worked on by:
- @Patrick-Erichsen

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Design and implementation discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bfd3fabc-af92-4506-8c7f-0e2043c807a0)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/00a0b766-1992-4358-a87a-45da91109d4b)

prs.title: fix: resource broker startup fails when parent and child disagree on the socket directory
prs.body:
Related: #200216, #200411

## What Problem This Solves

The native resource broker can fail to start with `Spawn broker failed before readiness: EEXIST: file already exists, mkdir '.'`. It happens when the parent process selects an endpoint with no private socket directory while the broker child runs on POSIX. Developers met it as 17 of 27 failures in `src/cli/update-cli.windows-lifecycle.test.ts` on macOS and Linux, each stopping before the test reached its subject.

The file passed 27 of 27 at the commit before #200216, which moved creation of the broker's private socket directory out of the parent and into the broker child.

While this PR was in progress, #200411 merged and turned those tests green by having the update lifecycle fixture create its authority under the host platform. The broker itself still fails the same way for any other caller that selects a directory-less endpoint; the new tests here reproduce that on current `main`.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Shipped installs are not affected: the parent starts the broker with its own runtime binary, so both processes see the same platform and already agree. The failure needs a parent and child that disagree, which today only happens in tests that simulate Windows in the parent while the real child runs on POSIX.

No data was at risk. I traced every path to a directory removal on `main`: each one runs only after the same broker's exclusive `mkdir` of that path succeeded, and `mkdir('.')` cannot succeed, so nothing reaches a removal of `.` or of any path the broker did not create itself.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two processes each decided whether the endpoint has a private directory. The parent's resource authority decides from its platform: a named pipe and no directory on Windows, otherwise `<private dir>/resource.sock`. After #200216 the broker child decided again from its own platform and the endpoint's parent path. When they disagreed, the child took the parent path of a pipe name, got `.`, and tried to create it.

The authority owns that decision, so the fix forwards it. The parent sends the authority whole in the broker's bootstrap message, and the broker creates, permissions, and removes exactly the directory it was given, or none. It no longer reads its platform or the endpoint's shape. Resource attachments handed to workers still carry only the endpoint and secret.

What #200216 set out to do is kept: the parent does no synchronous filesystem work for this directory, creation is exclusive, the mode is 0700, and cleanup is joined on close and on startup failure.

The wire change is one field on the internal parent-to-broker bootstrap message, which both ends read from the same build. There is no schema, config, public protocol, or dependency change.

#200411's fixture line is left in place. It keeps the update lifecycle tests on a private socket directory; without it, and with this fix, a POSIX child would listen on a socket file named like the pipe in the working directory, as it did before #200216.

## Evidence

Local runs are on macOS arm64. The local Vitest wrapper defaults to the Bun runtime; `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` selects Node. Head is 38d4f9f76fc on `origin/main` b9a72b5bef8. `main` moved several times during the work; none of the movement touched `src/process/spawn-broker/`.

**The reported failure, same command throughout**

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli.windows-lifecycle.test.ts`

| Tree | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 7cb238ad89a, the parent of #200216 | 27 passed |
| `origin/main` bbf7f75a32b, before #200411 | 17 failed, 10 passed, all 17 with `EEXIST ... mkdir '.'` |
| this change on cc6c3a733df, before #200411 | 27 passed on Bun, 27 passed on Node |
| this change on 81d8ceeaad9, which includes #200411 | 27 passed on Bun |

Only the third row separates this change from #200411: it is this change alone turning the file green.

**Root cause, and the alternative ruled out**

- With the parent's platform reported as `win32`, the real authority returns no directory and the endpoint `\\.\pipe\oc-br-<secret>`. POSIX `dirname` of that string is `.`.
- A stale directory or the working directory's contents do not explain it. `createBrokerNativeResourceServer` from `main`, run in a new empty working directory, fails with the same `mkdir '.'` for the pipe endpoint and starts normally for a POSIX endpoint in that same directory. The first case in the test file also failed, with no earlier case to leave state behind.

**Regression and guard tests through the real host and a real broker child** (`src/process/spawn-broker/resource-transport.test.ts`)

| Test | `main` source | This head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| serves an endpoint the authority gave no directory without creating or removing one | fails: `EEXIST` on `mkdir` of the endpoint's parent | passes |
| removes only the authority's directory when its endpoint cannot listen | fails: the child creates a different directory than the authority named | passes |
| refuses an existing resource directory without removing its contents | passes | passes |
| creates and retires a cold native resource without main-thread synchronous metadata | passes | passes |

Running the head's tests against `main`'s five source files gives 3 failed, 7 passed of 10 across `resource-transport.test.ts` and `resource-server.test.ts`, on both runtimes. The third failure is the in-process server test, which shows the reported `mkdir '.'` directly. On this head both files pass 10 of 10 on both runtimes.

What each test proves:

- **No directory given.** The first test pre-creates a directory with another owner's file in it and mode 0755, tells the host the endpoint has no directory, and attaches a real resource. While the broker is live the directory holds only that file and the socket. After close it holds only the file, with unchanged content and mode.
- **Startup failure, and nothing else removed.** The second test names a directory and points the endpoint at that same path, so listening can only fail because the broker created it. Afterward the parent directory holds only the other owner's file. Two temporary mutations confirm the test bites: skipping the startup-failure removal leaves the directory behind and fails it, and not forwarding the directory lets startup succeed and fails it.
- **Exclusive creation.** The third test is the existing one, now asserting `EEXIST` and the full directory listing.
- **Mode 0700 and removal on close.** The fourth test is the existing one, unchanged: it checks the mode under a hostile umask and that the directory is gone after the host closes.

**Suites and checks**

<details>
<summary>Commands, counts, and two unrelated intermittent failures seen locally</summary>

Runs marked "same tree" used commit 04c6c8e49ca on `origin/main` 81d8ceeaad9. Its seven changed files are byte-identical to this head; the later base movement touched none of them.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs 'src/process/spawn-broker/'`, Bun (same tree) | 116 passed, 94 skipped of 210; 22 files passed, 12 skipped |
| the same, Node (same tree) | 187 passed, 23 skipped of 210; 33 files passed, 1 skipped |
| `resource-transport.test.ts` and `resource-server.test.ts`, this head | 10 of 10 on Bun, 10 of 10 on Node |
| `src/cli/update-cli.windows-lifecycle.test.ts`, Bun (same tree) | 27 passed |
| `pnpm tsgo:all`, this head | exit 0 |
| `oxfmt --check` and `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the seven changed files (same tree) | clean |
| `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs` (same tree) | exit 0 |
| `check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base origin/main --no-merge-base`, this head | OK, +74 of 400 |
| `check-session-identity-ratchet.mts --base origin/main --no-merge-base`, this head | OK |
| `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts -t "PR wrapper inventory"` (same tree) | 1 passed, 22 filtered out |

The skips are existing `skipIf` conditions in files this PR does not touch; the command-transport tests skip under Bun. The dead-export scan was skipped and not run.

Two timing-sensitive tests in that directory failed intermittently on this machine while other jobs loaded it. Neither uses native resources, and both fail the same way with `main`'s five source files swapped in:

- `context.test.ts`, "keeps Gateway child spawning in-process after timeout admission": the 30-second `spawnSync` budget expires because the child's `fs.watch` never reports the marker its broker child wrote. With `main`'s source it failed 2 of 4 isolated runs.
- `proxy-retention.test.ts`, "releases completed command proxies after the host closes": `retained: 1` instead of 0 after forced collection. With `main`'s source it failed 4 of 6 runs, and 5 of 6 on this change.

Both passed in the two full-directory runs in the table.

</details>

The broker test directory passes on both runtimes. Typecheck, format, lint, the changed-file gate, and both ratchets are clean. The dead-export scan was not run. Two timing-sensitive broker tests that do not use native resources failed intermittently on a loaded machine, as often with `main`'s source as with this change; details are in the block above.

CI on 38d4f9f76fc finished with 62 checks passed, 57 skipped, and none failed. `checks-node-changed-8` ran `resource-transport.test.ts` (9 of 9) and `resource-server.test.ts` (1 of 1) on Linux under Bun. CI did not select `update-cli.windows-lifecycle.test.ts` for this diff, so that file's results above are local only.

**Test files audited in full**

- `resource-transport.test.ts`: added the two tests above and one shared fixture for a pre-existing owner directory. The existing "refuses an existing resource directory" case moved onto that fixture and gained the `EEXIST` and full-listing assertions; nothing it checked was dropped. In "keeps owner cleanup replies usable" an `expect` inside a socket callback moved after close, so a wrong value fails the test instead of stalling the callback.
- `resource-server.test.ts`: removed the temp-directory fixture and its two imports, restoring the synthetic endpoint the test had before #200216. That fixture existed only so the server's derived `mkdir` had somewhere to succeed; the test mocks `node:net` and asserts nothing about directories, so no coverage is lost. The `process.connected` override is now restored through `onTestFinished`, so a rejected startup cannot leak it.
- All cases in `resource-transport.test.ts` keep their existing `skipIf(win32)`; I did not change that.

**Review**

One independent read-only review by a fresh agent given the diff and the contract, with no access to my reasoning. It found no blocking issue and raised test and typing points.

- Applied: the startup-failure test could not tell "created then removed" from "never created", so it was reshaped as above. The directory is now an explicit `string | undefined` from one named authority type. The fixture and callback fixes are the ones listed under the audit.
- Not taken: listing the bootstrap fields one by one in `host.ts`. The bootstrap type is now defined as the authority plus a generation, so the spread sends exactly that type.
- Partly taken: the named authority type is used by the protocol and the tests, while the `host.ts` field keeps the equivalent `ReturnType<...>` to stay clear of that file's 700-line cap.

The repository's autoreview helper does not work on this machine, so it was not run.

**Not proven**

- Real Windows, where parent and child are both `win32`. By reading, the authority is unchanged there and the broker receives no directory, as before. No Windows run.
- The `/tmp` fallback for long temp roots has no dedicated test. The broker now receives that directory from the authority instead of deriving the same value.
- The parent's own removal after readiness when the broker died without cleaning up is not separately tested. The cold-resource test cannot tell the broker's removal from the parent's.
- Linux was not run locally; CI covered the two touched test files there, under Bun only.

prs.title: fix(ui): start session menu scrollbars closer to the rounded corners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In long session menu lists such as **Assign to…**, the scrollbar now stays inside the menu's rounded corners (#200393), but it stops well short of them. With the list scrolled all the way up, the thumb starts beside the search field, so it looks as if the list is not at the top.

## User Impact

User impact: the scrollbar in long session menu lists (**Assign to…**, **Move to group** and collections) starts and ends close to the rounded corners, while still staying inside the outline.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scrollbar track was inset by the full corner radius at each end. Half the radius is enough to keep the thumb inside the curve, so the inset is now half as large.

## Evidence

Both frames show the list scrolled all the way up. Before, the thumb starts beside the search field. Now it starts just inside the rounded corner.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: at the top of the list the scrollbar thumb starts beside the search field](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f61deaee-1f39-4d93-bec0-2741e29c40ae) | ![After: at the top of the list the scrollbar thumb starts just inside the rounded corner](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/72f91644-17cd-4026-9d2b-98e6ab717b62) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before, annotated: track inset 20 px at each end](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/838b2f2b-45e4-4191-840b-4d6b0a9c234f) | ![After, annotated: track inset 10 px at each end](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7af1a28b-7296-44cd-bb73-292213f4db35) |

Sidebar session menu → **Assign to…** with a 34-person directory, dark theme, pointer resting on the scrollbar. This is the real Control UI in headless Chromium against the mocked Gateway E2E fixtures, at 1280×900 and 3× scale, cropped to the top of the submenu from one frame per revision. Before is `main` at `a117ca5073`; after is this change (`fd7f958b51`, the same patch as the PR head). The bottom corner was captured in the same runs and mirrors the top.

- The session menu browser test now expects the smaller inset. It fails on `main` (`expected [ 20, 20 ] to deeply equal [ 10, 10 ]`) and passes with the change.
- The session owner assignment E2E suite passes (14 tests), including the 1,000-person directory.
- The Control UI size comparison against the base passes locally.
- Format, stylelint, oxlint and the UI test typecheck pass for the changed files.
- Local autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode against `origin/main`, P0 threshold) on `fd7f958b51`: scoped-clean, no accepted findings.

## Worked on by

- @Patrick-Erichsen

## Work sessions

prs.title: fix: keep plugin cleanup from stalling the Gateway
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Final asynchronous plugin-capture cleanup can block the Gateway event loop while committing its SQLite custody marker, stalling shutdown or same-process restart on a slow filesystem.

## User Impact

This candidate retires the custody marker off the Gateway thread. Synchronous callers and the existing off-main broker retain native ownership. No configuration, schema or migration changes.

**The frozen cold performance gate failed. This revision is held as a draft and is not eligible for merge under the published rule. Warm observations were not attempted.** Functional proof does not establish acceptable whole-workflow costs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The owner validates original physical identities and releases its handle. The existing cleanup transport reacquires exclusive custody, commits retirement before deleting payload, and preserves native bytes. Confirmed failures remain retryable; unknown cleanup retains the original rejected operation and claim. Broker paths stay native without another cleanup descendant. No new manager, cache, held worker or durability policy.

## Evidence

**[Complete frozen cold result: all raw values, 24 performance metrics, 15 counters and every adverse cell](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200432#issuecomment-6940912723).** All five original cold pairs completed with 3,000/3,000 valid requests. Population p95 of worst-request latency rose 68.939→86.004 ms (+24.753%); population median of maintenance-window request p95 rose 29.974→52.004 ms (+73.495%). The controller stopped before all ten warm observations. No outlier, replacement, replay or qualifier promotion is used.

- Exact head d72db8e2 passes [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44029888067) and [security enforcement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44031382490). The initial failed CI remains failed; its missing-wrapper-module and diagnostic-wording findings were repaired, not rerun for green.
- Exact d72db8e2/merge-base5275f439 builds and separately tagged cold/warm native qualification pass. Unchanged baseline qualifiers were re-audited without replay. These remain qualification, not performance acceptance.
- Real-child red/green proof covers off-host marker retirement, physical custody, marker-before-deletion, native retention, replacement refusal, retry and unknown-cleanup quarantine. Local CI repairs pass2 extraction,3 provisioning and6 retirement cases plus owning static gates. A filesystem-specific provisioning case remains locally skipped on a clone-capable volume; execution of that particular CI cell is not claimed here.
- The intact16-file P0-P2 review is retained for unchanged logic; subsequent repairs only add the canonical wrapper inventory entry and clarify a physical-custody diagnostic/assertion. Other14 reviewed paths are byte-identical. Filename-filtered unchanged token context remains a stated review limit, supplemented by its changed diff, source inspection and owning tests. No scanner, allowlist, physical guard or permission was weakened.

The [earlier PR200114 cold failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200114#issuecomment-6924663022) also remains terminal and unchanged. Broker context: #200320 and #200374. No performance acceptance or merge follows from either result.

<details>
<summary>Prospective acceptance protocol — unchanged after capture</summary>

# Prospective capture-retirement performance rule

This is a new, changed-source follow-up. The completed five-pair cold failure for PR200114 remains terminal and unchanged; none of its samples are replaced, pooled, promoted or relabeled.

1. Freeze the exact published candidate head, verified merge-base baseline, complete sourcePerformance build receipts, common committed workload e984e5333dacac9227712c9e802dc5cd813fd53c, private fixture bytes, image, protocol and this rule before the first formal capture. Read the actual PR body back before recording its publication/head binding. No baseline or candidate code changes within a cohort.
2. Exercise the actual isolated Gateway/agent, new-config default safeguard post-reply maintenance, controlled local model HTTP responses, and the same retained private long01 replay corpus. No live-provider semantic-quality, natural-pressure or global-idleness claim. The corpus stays private; publish metadata, not transcript or model-request contents.
3. Preserve Node24.22.1,8CPUs,16GiB RAM,zero swap,default heap,network=none,read-only source/dependencies,cleared environment and the same common committed scripts overlay. Record actual limits and host load. No CPU profiles in formal captures.
4. Qualification uses separately declared unique tags and never contributes acceptance observations. Formal order is exactly five serial baseline/candidate cold pairs, then five serial process-warm pairs only if the cold gate permits. Every capture keeps all300 unrelated-session request slots, including failures, timeouts and suppressions. Warmup is sacrificial, never an extra observation; measured warm work must use the same Gateway PID after native warm settlement and a distinct physical target.
5. Verify source/build/workload/fixture invariance, original native prefix, exact target/owner identity, durable compaction boundary, four post-pressure maintenance requests with the declared degraded outcome class, native settlement and cleanup. Missing, ambiguous, started, interrupted or failed originals stop collection. Never overwrite, replace or retry a failed tag, discard an outlier, change windows, or restart this cohort for better results.
6. Report all24 performance metrics and all15 observed worker/path counters, each arm's five raw values, median, nearest-rank p95 and spread, with every adverse cell. Full-capture costs include startup and warmup. Separate them from the immediately bracketed measured stream and broad maintenance-request scope. Worker-only counts do not establish total workflow work or zero host parsing.
7. Include whole-rig descendant CPU and whole-container kernel cgroup-v2 peak charged memory through rig settlement, before final fingerprinting. The latter includes descendants,page cache,startup/preflight and observer overhead; it is not total RSS or memory attribution. Keep Gateway RSS,main/worker heaps and thread counts distinct. Missing whole-container memory is an unobserved collection failure, never zero.
8. Any missing comparable performance metric or any median/p95 increase of20% or more is a hard stop before the next population and before merge. Smaller worse user-facing cells remain adverse and require explicit owner acceptance in the PR; no inferred tradeoff, noise waiver or automatic performance acceptance. Counter increases are disclosed separately, never hidden.
9. The required owning-boundary improvement is removing retirement PRAGMA/COMMIT from the Gateway thread while preserving original physical custody, marker-before-deletion ordering, committed/loaded native bytes, confirmed-failure retries and unknown-cleanup quarantine. Offloading relocates work: added cleanup-process cost must be measured, not described as deleted work. The controller never grants acceptance. Landing requires reviewed exact published bytes, the complete declared evidence, acceptable costs under this rule, required CI/security/review and verified merge; session closure follows, not precedes, that result.

The committed workload is retained in the team proof checkout, outside this product diff: 40 pure contracts pass, with base-red/fix-green metric mapping. Reproduction requires the authorized private corpus; no transcript contents are published.

</details>

prs.title: fix: redact Windows home paths in doctor SQLite failure reports
prs.body:
Fixes #200451

## What Problem This Solves

When native Windows supplies the home directory through USERPROFILE with HOME unset, doctor's session SQLite migration failure report includes the full home path and OS username in a GitHub issue described as sanitized. Error text using the other path separator can also retain the home path.

## User Impact

New failure reports redact the OS home in target paths and error text with either separator, including when HOME is unset. No configuration or migration action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the OS home once per report through the existing home-dir owner and pass it through all three redaction helpers. Using the OS home preserves redaction even when OPENCLAW_HOME points elsewhere. Keep the existing per-target rewrite optimization for large reports (#194621).

The pr-simplify pass retained the existing helpers and removed their independent HOME reads: +18 net production lines pass the shared result, and +48 test lines cover the issue/report boundary. The neighboring recovery and restore report modules have no separate HOME-only redactor, so no same-family follow-up was identified.

## Evidence

- On base b9a72b5bef8d648024f89b66af9579691ae40ce1, the regression produced **2 failed / 13 passed**: USERPROFILE home paths leaked, and HOME error text leaked its backslash form.
- With the fix, **15 passed / 0 failed** in `src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.failure-reports.test.ts`, run with `timeout 150s pnpm test <named file> --maxWorkers=1`. Vitest wall time: **39.77 s** (41.96 s including the test wrapper); the two new cases took 23 ms and 7 ms. CI seconds are pending.
- The regression exercises real generated and saved GitHub issue bodies and the JSON report with HOME and USERPROFILE, both separators, and a distinct OPENCLAW_HOME.
- Targeted type-aware lint, formatting checks, and `git diff --check` passed. Broad checks and standalone typecheck are deferred to PR CI under the host limits.
- Local ClawSweeper is unavailable. Independent Codex autoreview of the final local diff against the base above was **scoped-clean at P0–P2**, with no remaining findings; the reviewed source was committed unchanged.

## Limits

Native Windows execution was not available; the environment-variable and separator regression ran on Linux. The configured Crabbox provider could not allocate a box because its required credential was unavailable. Previously saved reports retain their existing publication/receipt contract; this change does not retroactively scrub them.

prs.title: fix: speed up backup capture in large state directories
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor's pre-repair capture can hit its 600-second deadline on large state directories. Profiling a macOS installation with roughly 1.1 million retained files and 85 exclusion roots attributed 81% of discovery samples to repeatedly resolving unrelated exclusion paths.

## User Impact

Backup discovery performs less CPU work on POSIX systems without changing which resources are included. Windows retains the existing containment checks. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the candidate once and reject unrelated normalized POSIX prefixes before calling the existing containment helper. Matching prefixes still use that helper, preserving path-segment boundaries and protected descendants. This adds no cache or new policy owner.

## Evidence

- Five focused tests pass through the repository runner: resource policy/privacy, database resources, and local companion coverage. Targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- The regression failed on the original implementation with 92 unnecessary relative-path calls for one included path; the candidate makes zero. It also checks excluded children, protected descendants, sibling prefixes, and unnormalized inputs.
- Preliminary synthetic benchmark: 10,000 mixed paths, five interleaved samples per variant; identical selection results. Median policy time fell from 1,110.5 ms to 33.2 ms. This measures the policy, not total backup latency.
- Preliminary live read-only discovery completed in 252.8 seconds with four database paths, using a source-built candidate policy loaded into the installed discovery process. No installed files were edited for that measurement.
- Independent Codex review of the initial two-file patch found no production defect; its test-normalization finding was fixed. The production patch is unchanged on this branch. Windows runtime validation remains outstanding.

An exact 2026.11.4 source backport also passes its regression test. A full capture attempt with that backport reached database snapshot verification in approximately 306 seconds, but remained unsealed because the active Gateway changed the shared database generation. A maintenance capture is still required. The local package build is pending in TypeScript declaration generation. This draft does not claim a verified complete capture or installed fix. Full current-main typecheck/build and broad platform tests remain for CI.

prs.title: fix: skip repeated removal of preserved worktrees
prs.body:
Related: #200350

## What Problem This Solves

A periodic cleanup script can repeatedly try to remove a worktree whose contents OpenClaw has already preserved because they cannot be snapshotted safely. Each call repeats snapshot work, while `worktrees list --json` omits the typed cleanup status the script needs to skip it.

## User Impact

User impact: cleanup scripts can filter `cleanup.state == "preserved"`; unfiltered removal exits 1 immediately with `removed: false` and typed `preserved` metadata. After repairing the cause, an operator can explicitly run `worktrees remove <id> --retry-preserved`. This flag reopens the existing safe removal path; it does not permit snapshot loss. `--force` alone does not reopen a terminal receipt. Existing `gc --retry-deferred` remains an explicit retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

The registry decoder projects the existing revision-bound receipt as `cleanup: { state, reason, attempts, nextAttemptAt }`. The removal owner checks it before acquiring the mutation lease or settling the workspace, so local CLI and Gateway callers share one decision. Session deletion continues reporting a retained worktree when removal returns that outcome. Clean-only cleanup releases its removal claim on refusal. The Worktrees UI offers an explicit safe Retry; the session organizer preserves its existing destructive confirmation and reports refused outcomes. No configuration, SQLite schema, cache, or preservation policy changes.

Production code grows by 77 lines to expose the typed contract, explicit retry, and visible outcome; tests grow by 190, generated validators by 3, docs by 16, and the existing benchmark by 11. The allocation-held implementation moves unchanged from the oversized service into its existing removal module; no duplicate owner is added.

## Evidence

The nested-repository regression fails on the original service at the repeated removal and passes with the fix: no new snapshot or Git command, unchanged attempt count, and unsaved nested bytes retained. Explicit retry performs another safe attempt. Real Commander parser tests cover the flag, conflict, JSON/text refusal, and exit 1. Focused preservation, removal safety, exact-state, CLI, registry, protocol, and Gateway tests pass; the final affected UI browser suites (91 tests) and Chromium E2E suite (5 tests) also pass. Hosted review caught a leaked clean-only removal claim and unhandled UI results; both have red/green regressions and are fixed. All 35 preservation tests pass again, including a repaired checkout that can be explicitly retried after clean-only refusal.

A production-shaped synthetic fixture on btrfs contains 5,000 sessions, a 35 GiB size-shaped database, and 62,000 files totaling 1.1 GB. Five interleaved baseline/candidate pairs (25 repeat calls per arm) show median owner wall time **1283.724 → 1.176 ms**, process CPU **1050.661 → 1.434 ms**, and main-isolate allocation **22,132,280 → 351,320 bytes**. Baseline calls range 848–2049 ms; candidate calls 0.60–6.25 ms. A/A controls have medians 3310/1310 ms, so host drift is substantial: these are synthetic work-count and cost measurements, not a production latency forecast. CPU excludes Git subprocesses; initial preservation is excluded. No production data was copied.

The isolated Linux `pnpm openclaw` flow also passes end to end: create → failed safe snapshot → list preserved state → fast refusal with exit 1 → explicit retry increments attempts to 2; unsaved bytes remain intact. All 12 session-lifecycle tests pass. Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2. `pnpm check:changed` exposes three inherited dead-export regressions, reproduced on exact main parent `346d231275b3930848b8e31239c74f689d361436`: `approval-shared.ts:isApprovalRecordVisibleToClient` (#200360, ff2cb7e8), `spawn-broker/host.ts:BrokerNativeResourceLease` (#200370, df787227), and `operation-types.ts:SystemAgentPluginCapabilityReview` (#200392, b0d95fd4). These are reported main regressions, not silently ignored checks. The follow-up check also caught a missing required reason in the new regression fixture; that is corrected, the targeted regression passes again, and every core test typecheck shard passes. All other changed-file gates passed. Exact-head PR CI will determine landing eligibility.

[Numbered review responses and inspected before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200434#issuecomment-6940301482).

CI follow-through: run 44029059502 exposed a lease test that still used force as an implicit preserved retry. The test now opts in with retryPreserved and releases its lease in finally, preventing assertion failures from hanging teardown. No production change. All 43 remaining #200350 GC, eviction, and lease tests pass (199.26s), completing that regression footprint; targeted typecheck/lint and a fourth Codex autoreview pass.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway with many sessions keeps the prepared restart-recovery session rows after recovery finishes. Long-lived admission callbacks retain the startup scope, which still points to the completed recovery closure and its parsed rows.

## User Impact

User impact: completed restart recovery releases its temporary session data instead of retaining it for the Gateway lifetime. Recovery order, readiness, failure handling, and session behavior stay the same.

## Why This Change Was Made

Clear the recovery reference in its existing settlement `finally`, before publishing completion. This removes a redundant retained graph without adding an interning table or cache. Reuse the existing synchronous assertion helper for an equivalent nearby try/catch so the startup owner remains below its line cap. Production delta: **−2 runtime lines**; the required PR-wrapper inventory entry is +1 (net −1 including tooling); tests: +39.

## Evidence

The collection regression fails on the unchanged parent for both successful and failed recovery, and passes with the fix while the real startup owner and its published callback remain alive. **84 focused tests across five files pass. Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2.**

Synthetic Gateway evidence uses 10,800 sessions, 4,300 settled restart candidates, 65 clients, 20 concurrent mock-provider runners, 40 plugins, 512 skills, and 62,000 workspace files. Each timing arm performs ten measured minutes of list/history/events/appends/tools traffic, then captures through `diagnostics.heapSnapshot`; source-reviewed labels identify retainers. Allocation sampling runs separately.

| Ten-minute measurement | A1 unchanged | A2 unchanged | B fixed |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Retained snapshot, MB | 610.76 | 613.01 | 597.74 |
| Main heap after snapshot, MB | 539.00 | 541.35 | 526.19 |
| Duplicate-string potential, MB | 36.99 | 37.48 | 29.12 |
| Excess string copies | 728,164 | 739,080 | 578,276 |
| Completed recovery graph, MB | 14.17 | 14.15 | absent |
| Main-thread CPU | 17.35% | 20.86% | 15.95% |
| Completed turns / timestamp writes | 220 / 110 | 220 / 110 | 220 / 110 |

MB is decimal. Duplicate accounting includes complete strings up to 1,024 characters; truncated longer groups are excluded. The fix removes 13.0–15.3 MB of retained heap and 7.9–8.4 MB of duplicate-string potential, beyond the A/A spread. Main CPU uses the ten full minutes before snapshot capture. Host load varied, so no CPU improvement is claimed.

Separate allocation A/A/B and the 35 GiB synthetic database validation are in progress; this evidence will be updated before landing.

The completed timing fixture has a 451 MiB agent database and approximately 1.1 GB of workspace files on APFS. It establishes session-cardinality and retained-owner behavior; it does not establish 35 GiB database I/O or btrfs performance.

`pnpm check:changed` ran. Its initial line-cap finding is fixed and the focused ratchet passes. Format, lint, typechecks, schema guards, and the other checks pass. The dead-export check reproduces three unrelated failures on exact parent `b4254cb2f6fa66805de3bfe0867a077ba7326efc`:

prs.title: feat(cron): add up to eight runs past the default when memory is free
prs.body:
Related: #196859

## What Problem This Solves

Due automations wait behind a fixed cap of eight runs, even on a host with plenty of memory to run more.

## User Impact

- Up to eight automation jobs run at once, as before.
- While all eight are busy and more jobs are due, each drain of the run queue starts one more job if at least 1 GiB of memory is free, up to 16 at once. The queue drains when a run ends and when jobs come due, so on a host with room the count grows by one job per drain.
- The reading is Node's `process.availableMemory()`, which counts the process's cgroup memory limit: in a 512 MiB container it reads about 500 MiB, while `os.freemem()` reads the VM's 5.4 GB.
- Running jobs are never stopped, condition checks do not use run slots, and there is no new setting.

## Why This Change Was Made

The run queue owns admission. The host adds one fact to each drain, whether one memory reading shows 1 GiB free, and the queue uses it to start at most one run past its eight default slots per drain. Each later drain reads memory again with that run counted, so the extra runs stop once memory gets short. No timer, threshold ladder or per-run memory estimate is involved.

Automation agent turns run in the cron lane, which shares one capacity budget with hook dispatch. That budget is 16 wide, since with it at eight an extra run would only wait in the lane for a slot. Hook dispatch keeps its own width of eight, so hooks alone never use more than they could before. Together, hooks and automation can hold up to 16 slots where they shared eight. Keeping them at eight combined would mean republishing the lane budget from the run queue on every drain, which this change leaves out. With hooks enabled, one of the 16 stays reserved for hooks, as one of the eight was.

Accepted edge cases:

- The eight default runs do not read memory. A small container with a heavy neighbour can still be OOM-killed with eight runs, as on main.
- One reading admits one run, and that run's memory may not show yet at the next drain. A run that later needs more than the memory left can still run short; each drain adds at most one run.

## Evidence

Targeted tests pass: `service.cross-tick-admission` (10), `service.run-queue` (16), `service.one-shot-schedule-ownership` (17), `service/ops.native-attempt` (7), `service/ops.gateway-mutations` (11), `service/ops.run-admission` (8), `service/manual-ack-durability` (3), `service/timer.regression` (16), `store/scheduler-actor.worker` (24), `server-lanes.hook-group` (3), `server/hooks.early-failure` (27).

- Twelve due jobs with 1 GiB free: the first drain starts nine, the next starts a tenth, and with one byte under 1 GiB a further drain starts none. With extra runs disabled it fails: eight start, not nine.
- The cron lane widens to 16 while hook dispatch stays at eight. With the lane at eight it fails.

Tests that fill exactly the eight default slots mock the memory reading to report no spare memory, so they do not depend on the machine running them. With the memory reading set to 16 GiB, as on CI, `timer.regression`'s slot fixture without the mock fails its two queueing cases (a queued run starts instead, and a wait times out); with the mock all 16 cases pass.

Cron suite, run once on this change with the memory mock applied to every cron test: 292 of 299 files passed. The mock then moved into the tests that fill the eight slots, and those tests were rerun (above). The seven failing files were rerun on this branch and on its merge base `4b0d586f272`. `maintenance-lifecycle` (18), `maintenance-snapshot` (5), `maintenance` (1) and `trigger-script.mcp` (3) fail the same on both. `service.pr-automation-feedback` and `service/command-timeout` pass on rerun. `service/manual-ack-durability` filled the eight slots with memory to spare and so started its queued request; it passes with the memory mock. Core, cron-test and gateway-server typechecks, lint and format pass; net test lines +63.

Gateway run of this change and its merge base in a private macOS VM, with 12 cron agent jobs due together and a synthetic model that holds every request open ([full table and script](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197394#issuecomment-6940499855)):

- Memory free: 9 runs start where the merge base starts 8; a drain without a run ending adds a tenth; a drain after a run ends refills that slot.
- Gateway memory reading at 512 MiB: no extra run starts, and the count falls back to 8 as runs end and holds there.
- Hooks: beside 8 automation runs, 10 hook requests get 8 hook turns running (the merge base runs 1 and answers the other 9 with 503).
- Restart on the same state keeps all 14 jobs and the config unchanged; all 14 runs end `ok`.

## Validation Limits

The model was synthetic. In the VM a macOS guest swaps instead of staying under 1 GiB, so for the low-memory steps the Gateway's `process.availableMemory()` was pinned at 512 MiB through a preload; the rest of the run was the shipped build. An upgrade from the latest stable was not shown, because main fails it on its own: starting main `b9a72b5bef8` on state written by 2026.11.4, in the same VM and without any scenario preload, fails after the state migration with `Startup failed: required secrets are unavailable. Error: disk I/O error | ERR_SQLITE_ERROR`. This head fails the same way there; that startup failure is separate from this change. Windows, Bun, x86 Linux, real channels and the full suite were not exercised.

prs.title: fix(memory): start default index managers at Gateway boot
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#194164 asks for memory indexing to be fresh right after a Gateway restart:
with the current demand-driven cold start, an agent's index opens on its
first search, flush, or turn, and until then `memory_index_sources`
receives nothing — the reporter observed roughly ten hours of stopped
indexing after an app relaunch.

The original draft of this PR restored eager boot-time indexing for every
configured agent. Review and history showed why that is the wrong default:
#167756 started Memory Core's index service eagerly on every Gateway start,
and #174718 (`6c050f8043`) deliberately reverted it after startup peak RSS
rose from ~1.1 GB to ~1.8 GB (startup catch-up touches every
session-transcript read lane, each spawning its own worker isolate). This
revision keeps that policy intact and adds an explicit operator opt-in
instead:

```jsonc
// memory.search.coldStart
"demand" // default — exactly today's behavior, unchanged
"eager"  // open every configured agent's index at boot and on later service starts
```

Each agent can override the global default with
`agents.entries.<id>.memory.search.coldStart`; the per-agent value wins over
the global setting in both directions, matching how the memory config
resolver treats other `memory.search` fields. Operators who need fresh
indexes immediately (the reporter's local-GGUF fleet) pay a known,
self-inflicted cost; everyone else sees zero change. The demand default, the
`liveIndexing` retention semantics, and the worker/RSS characteristics of
#174718 are untouched.

## The Change

- `memory.search.coldStart` (`"demand"` default | `"eager"`), registered in
  the config schema, field labels/help, and `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`.
- `memory-core-index` service start resolves the opt-in per agent:
  `resolveAgentConfig(cfg, agentId)?.memory?.search?.coldStart ?? global`.
  `"demand"` (effective) keeps `retainMemoryIndexingAgents` exactly as
  before; `"eager"` opens the agent's index through the existing host-aware
  runtime (`memoryRuntime.getMemorySearchManager`, which supplies the host's
  local-service acquisition — resolving the Revision 1 P2 finding). Manager
  construction marks each agent live, so later reloads retain them like any
  watched index.
- Boundary tests on untouched agents (so acquisition cannot be explained by
  prior demand): a per-agent eager override under a global demand default
  opens only that agent; a per-agent demand override under a global eager
  default keeps that agent lazy. Both fail against the previous
  global-only selector.

## Evidence

- **Unit/boundary tests** (worktree, committed source): `extensions/memory-core/index.test.ts` — 35 passed (2 new per-agent cold-start boundary cases; the previous single eager case was rewritten on untouched agents per review), and `src/config` schema regressions (config.schema-regressions, dead-config-keys, schema.hints) — 263 passed after registering the new field.
- **Regression check:** the two new boundary cases fail on the previous
  global-only selector (2 failed | 33 skipped) and pass with the per-agent
  resolution (35 passed).
- **Live redacted output, built from the committed source** (isolated
  state/workspace, local Ollama `nomic-embed-text`, synthetic data; the same
  state is upgraded in place between scenarios):

  ```text
  ===== SCENARIO 1: coldStart demand (default) =====
  gateway ready (demand)
  # memory file written + chat.send delivered, 45s watcher window, no consumer opens an index
  demand: memory_index_sources rows = 0

  ===== SCENARIO 2: upgrade in place -> coldStart eager =====
  gateway ready (eager)
  # same state, settings and sessions intact, 45s after boot, no consumer call
  eager: memory_index_sources rows = 2
      memory|memory/proof-demand-note.md
      sessions|sessions/main/34d590f2-28ad-4c95-91df-bda672a78c92.jsonl
  eager: memory_search -> {"ok":true,"results":[{"path":"memory/proof-demand-note.md",...
  ```

  Scenario 1 confirms the demand default is byte-for-byte unchanged
  (untouched agents stay lazy). Scenario 2 is the reporter's requested
  behavior, available under the explicit opt-in.

- **Latest-stable → candidate upgrade trace (redacted live output):** a
  dedicated run upgrades a state directory created by released
  **v2026.11.3** (npm, `847611d`) to the candidate built from this PR's
  head, covering both the upgrade-compatibility and data-model items:

  ```text
  ## PHASE S — stable v2026.11.3 (847611d), config without any coldStart key
  [stable] consumer memory_search -> {"ok":true,...}   # demand: index opens on first consumer
  [stable-final] memory_index_sources rows: 2          # memory/upgrade-note-a.md
  [stable-final] memory_index_chunks rows: 2           # + sessions/main/ff028686-….jsonl

  ## PHASE C-MIG — candidate refuses unmigrated DB (documented admission guard), then migrates
  "…uses schema version 27; … run openclaw doctor --fix to upgrade it to
   schema version 42 …" | gateway.maintenance_required
  $ openclaw doctor --fix --yes    ->  schema_meta primary = 42
  [post-migration] memory_index_sources: 2  memory_index_chunks: 2   # data survived

  ## PHASE C-A — candidate on migrated stable state, config UNCHANGED (demand default)
  booted healthy; memory_search retrieves the stable-era note
  [candA-final] memory_index_sources: 2                 # demand unchanged: no boot-time growth

  ## PHASE C-B — only delta: memory.search.coldStart = "eager"
  # new file written, then boot with NO consumer call
  [candB] rows BEFORE boot: sources=2 chunks=2
  [candB] rows AFTER eager boot: sources=3 chunks=3     # note B indexed at startup
      memory|memory/upgrade-note-a.md                    # stable-era data intact
      memory|memory/upgrade-note-b.md                    # newly indexed at boot
      sessions|sessions/main/ff028686-….jsonl            # stable-era session intact
  consumer memory_search("Post-upgrade synthetic") -> upgrade-note-b.md
  ```

  Existing settings are preserved (the stable-era config carries no
  `coldStart` key; the candidate boots it unchanged under the demand
  default), the stable-written database migrates via the documented
  `doctor --fix` path and loads/works (schema 27 → 42, index rows,
  session transcript, and provenance intact), demand semantics are
  unchanged after upgrade (no growth without a consumer), and the opt-in
  eager mode works on the upgraded state.

  Data-model note: this change adds an optional config field only — no
  stored index, session, or state format changes; the trace above
  demonstrates the stable-release upgrade end to end.

prs.title: feat(update): run Git checkout installs from releases behind the release link
prs.body:
## Problem

A Git checkout install runs its Gateway from `<checkout>/dist/index.js`, and `openclaw update` rewrites that same tree. Everything around the rewrite exists to survive it: the updater copies its own runtime first (133–892 s on a 183k-file checkout), builds the candidate in a private repository and imports it through a pack (256 MB cap), stops and parks the serving Gateway, and rewrites the service definition every update.

## Change

Extends #198835's linked package root (merged as `b868ed4c`) to Git checkouts, per the #197949 design. Based on `main`. It reuses #198835's release resolver, `switchPackageReleaseLink`, leases and 24 h collection unchanged. Its fallback follows `installStagedPackage`: when the layout can't be used, the update runs in place with a `recoverable-maintenance` warning, and the next update tries the layout again. The Gateway process never writes the release link. The only other writer is the boot launcher, and it only points the link back to the release recorded in a failed trial.

- **Layout.** `<stateDir>/git-install/lib/node_modules/openclaw -> releases/<id>/lib/node_modules/openclaw`. Each release is `git worktree add --detach` off the developer's checkout (shared object store, no clone or copy).
- **Stage.** The existing candidate preflight (candidate walk, local-commit replay, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, build, candidate checks) runs in the new release's worktree, then `--version` with the service's Node. A same-source no-op requires the serving release to be at the checkout's commit and its artifacts to verify (#158931).
  - Deviation from the design: the worktree is built at `releases/<id>/build`, then moved into place with `git worktree move`. Node refuses to strip types under `node_modules` (`ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING`), and the build runs `.mts` scripts. The built tree has no absolute symlinks, so the move is safe.
- **Switch.** `switchPackageReleaseLink` from #198835. The serving Gateway keeps its release (Node resolves the entry's real path), so nothing is stopped, parked or verified before the flip.
- **Restart.** The serving Gateway's maintenance tick sees the link move (installation replacement) and restarts itself into the new release. The updater waits for that successor (up to 90 s), then verifies. It falls back to a native restart only if no successor appears. A native restart from inside the service job (`update.run`) would end the updater itself.
- **Service.** Written once, at conversion, to a frozen launcher `<stateDir>/git-install/openclaw-launcher.mjs`. A unit that names the launcher is never regenerated. The launcher is needed because a release that fails while loading never reaches Gateway code.
- **Trial.** The switch writes `releases/.trial`. The launcher counts starts.
  - After two failed starts it switches the link back and restores `*.pre-<version>` state files (#198389's generation names). Each SQLite family is restored together, and trial-created WAL/journal/SHM/seal files without a preserved predecessor are removed. The launcher mirrors #198389's `companionRemovals` list because it must not load release code.
  - The trial ends when the Gateway's first maintenance tick runs, or when the updater verifies the restarted Gateway. The second path also covers targets that predate this PR.
  - Writes made during a failed trial are lost (approved).
- **The layout never fails an update** (#197949 decision 8). If `releases/` cannot be created, or something other than a release link sits at the package path, the update records a warning and takes the in-place runner. The next update tries the layout again.
- **Post-core work** (requested-channel persistence, plugin convergence) runs in the updater, but only after the restarted release verified and its trial ended. A failed trial therefore never leaves plugins that require the release it switched away from. It runs without Doctor maintenance, which the Gateway holds, and without a plugin cohort, because no core rollback exists to pair it with. If plugins changed, the Gateway is asked to restart again (SIGUSR2). Under `--no-restart` the release is unverified, so only the requested channel is persisted and plugins converge on a later update.
- **The developer's checkout** is never written. The first update builds the commit that serves now as the first release, rewrites the unit once, then stages the target.
- **Retention.** #198835's collection, followed by `git worktree prune`. `git-install` is excluded from backups and from the startup state-upgrade copy. The latter is the same change as #199770, included here so the stack stands alone.
- **One owner.** `usesGitReleases` selects releases. Windows checkouts and package-to-Git switches keep the in-place runner, and the in-place CLI tests are pinned to that runner.

For Git releases this skips:
- runtime retention
- the pack transfer/import
- the managed-service stop/park
- the database rollback capture
- the checkout's source-artifact lock
- the native restart from inside the service job
- per-update service regeneration

## In-place fallback (decided)

Windows Git checkouts, package-to-Git switches, and checkouts with no installed Gateway service still use the in-place runner, so this PR bypasses that runner on POSIX instead of deleting it. A checkout with no service is run by hand, so nothing would start through the release link and its next start would run the old commit. `gatewayServiceOwnsGitInstall` reads the installed service once and accepts it only when the service owns the checkout or its release link. The command decides once and hands that decision to the runner. Prod LOC is net **+980**. Decided 2026-11-16: Windows Git updates are not refused. A follow-up, slice 4b (stacked on this PR), moves Windows to releases using junctions and then deletes the in-place Git runner.

## E2E (mbp-m5, launchd, isolated profiles, shared-clone checkout; ≤15 min per run, ≤3 in parallel)

**Final head `2e692d67` (rebased on `main` at `8a82b5e0`): local ClawSweeper review clean** (gpt-6.1-sol, normal speed; report `~/.cache/clawsweeper-local-review/2e692d67a707.md`). After the rebase: `sweepPackageReleaseTemporaryLinks` is exported again, because the first Git publish uses it. The CI ratchets are satisfied: a lazy generation name, Node-only release tests, and an allocation record for the regression tests. A conversion's first release is now the commit the checkout's `dist` serves, not a pulled HEAD that was never rebuilt.

Rollback across same-version upgrades (decision d): the state upgrade now keeps a replaced file as `<file>.pre-<buildId>`, named after the build that replaced it, so two builds of one version each keep their own predecessor. Builds without a build ID, and earlier releases, still write `.pre-<version>`. Retention handles both forms. A failed trial restores the `.pre-<buildId>` of its own build, falling back to `.pre-<version>`. Fixes to the trial and launcher from the review rounds:
- the inventory is recorded before anything is restored, so an interrupted rollback can resume without losing a restored WAL;
- the trial's applied or interrupted upgrade plan is retired and the files it added are removed; a removal that fails is retried at the next start;
- the config path is the one the update resolved (`~` and external paths included);
- state is restored before the link moves back.

The release layout is used only when the release switch actually reaches the next start: either the service already starts the launcher, or it owns the checkout and this update rewrites its definition and restarts it. `--no-restart` on a converted install leaves the serving release selected. The next start, which the operator triggers, selects the new release, without the two-start fallback. A first conversion requested with `--no-restart` stays in place.

| Run (mbp-m5, isolated launchd profiles) | Head | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Release that crashes on boot | `073a1306` (launcher unchanged since) | update reports `build-id-mismatch` after 180 s; two "e2e boot crash" starts, then "failed to start twice; switched back"; link back on the previous release, trial cleared, `ready` |
| Conversion before the crash run | `073a1306` | ok, 267 s, longest outage 6.7 s |

**Current head `6d9acd6e` (on `main`), mbp-m5, isolated launchd profiles:**

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| Conversion (first update from a checkout service) | ok, root on the release link; 610 s with three runs in parallel; longest outage 9.7 s |
| Release → release | ok, 239 s, longest outage 9.9 s |
| `update.run` through the Gateway | `finished\|succeeded`, 135 s; link moved, Gateway restarted, plist unchanged; outage 7.8 s |
| Checkout with no Gateway service | updated in place: checkout HEAD moved to the target, no `git-install/releases`, result `ok`, mode `git` |
| Release that crashes on boot (at `0e3fefae`) | update reports `build-id-mismatch` after 188 s; after two "e2e boot crash" starts the launcher logs "failed to start twice; switched back", and the previous release serves `ready` |
| v2026.11.4 state → this head | see Data-model compatibility |

Older rows below ran at earlier heads.
Rows marked ‡ ran at head `8a720e49`, rows marked † at `6032dedf`; the rest ran at `1140b601`, before plugin convergence moved after verification. At the final head `99b7f080` (rebased onto `823fa6d2`), three runs ran in parallel on mbp-m5. (1) Conversion and release→release passed again, with the root on the release link and a longest outage of 7.6 s. (2) `update.run` finished `succeeded` (link moved, Gateway restarted, plist unchanged, outage 8.0 s). (3) A checkout with **no Gateway service** updated in place: checkout HEAD moved to the bumped commit, no `git-install/releases` was created, and the result was `ok`, mode `git`, root the checkout. An intermediate head `2d2387b6` keyed this choice on a preflight fact that Git installs never fill in, so conversion fell back to in-place (about 120 s outage). That head was never pushed.

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| † First update of a checkout install (conversion, head→head+1) | ok, 402 s wall (two builds, three runs in parallel), longest outage 7.6 s, total 13.1 s (unit rewrite, then a restart after plugin convergence); unit rewritten once to the launcher; checkout tree clean; no retention, pack or handoff steps |
| ‡ Release→release (head+1→head+2) | ok, 180 s wall, one outage of 7.2 s; unit untouched (mtime unchanged since conversion); service runs from `releases/` |
| ‡ `--no-restart` on a switched release | the updater leaves the Gateway running and converges no plugins; within the next maintenance tick the Gateway restarts itself into the release, and the trial is cleared; outage 7.5 s |
| † `update.run` via the Gateway (`openclaw gateway call update.run`) | run `finished|succeeded`, 140 s; link moved; the Gateway restarted itself; unit untouched; outage 7.4 s |
| Already-current rerun from the preserved checkout after conversion (head `60503ab3`) | `skipped: already-current`, link unchanged, 113 s |
| † Release that crashes on boot | two crashes, the launcher switched back to the previous release, Gateway ready again; the update reports `build-id-mismatch`; longest outage 28.9 s |
| kill -9 mid-stage | link and serving Gateway unchanged; the rerun succeeds; a partial release directory left by the killed run is collected after 24 h |
| kill -9 right after the link moves, before restart | the old Gateway keeps serving; the rerun reports `skipped: already-current`; the Gateway restarts itself into the new release and the trial is cleared |
| `env -i` + `umask 077` (conversion, then release→release) | ok, 376 s and 198 s, outages 5.5 s and 7.5 s; launcher `0700` under umask 077 |
| Install whose unit and state were written by 2026.11.3, moved to head, then converted | ok, 229 s, outage 5.9 s; state DB `integrity_check` ok. 2026.11.3's own updater could not reach head on mbp-m5: it walked back to `already-current` (Node 24.21 below head's `engines`), so that hop was done with `git reset` + `ocx build` |
| Production-shaped install (207,229-file checkout, +3 GB SQLite in state), release→release | ok, 145 s, outage 6.9 s, no retention step. Main was not timed on this host. Peanutto's production main run `90c601fc` took 4,150 s, with 892 s retention and a 300 s outage |

Not exercised: a plugin-only restart (SIGUSR2) after npm plugins actually change; the fixtures have no npm plugins.

## Data-model compatibility

- **No new state schema.** This diff adds or changes no SQLite schema, migration, or config schema file. The update ledger (`update_runs`), Gateway owner lease and config are read and written exactly as on the base.
- **`origin` stays compatible.** `UpdateRunRecordSchema.origin` (including #198835's `packageStage` and `packageRelease`) is unchanged, and Git-release updates write no new `origin` key. A Git release records its switch in the result step and the release directories, not the ledger. So rows written by older builds parse as before, and rows written by this build parse in an older build. A Git checkout that can't use the layout falls back to the in-place runner with a `recoverable-maintenance` advisory (`git-release-layout` step), the same contract as `installStagedPackage`'s swap fallback.
- **New on-disk state is additive and lives under `<stateDir>/git-install/`:** `releases/<id>/` (detached worktrees), the `lib/node_modules/openclaw` link, `releases/.trial`, and the launcher. An install without them is treated as unconverted and gets the conversion path. If the layout is unusable, the update falls back to in-place (decision 8).
- **Existing data proof: v2026.11.4 state upgraded and converted (E2E, `6d9acd6e`).**
  - The v2026.11.4 Gateway, started with `--profile`, created `state/openclaw.sqlite` (schema 22) and an agent DB.
  - This head's `gateway install` then stopped with "Client credentials require backed-up migration custody; … run openclaw doctor --fix". Plain `main` (`964ab522`) stops with the same message on a copy of that state, so it comes from `main`, not this diff.
  - Following the message, `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` migrated the state to schema 40. After that, install succeeded and the update converted the checkout onto the release link. The `update_runs` row in the stable-created database reads `finished|succeeded`, and the stable config (Gateway port) still reads back.
- **Rollback keeps data readable:** the crash-release trial switches the link back to the previous release, and the launcher restores the SQLite family (`openclaw.sqlite`, `-wal`, `-shm`) captured before the trial. The previous build reopens its own database (crash row, 28.9 s).

## Tests

- `src/infra/git-release.test.ts`:
  - trial fallback restores the SQLite family and drops trial-only companions
  - trial settlement
  - launcher mapping
  - a launcher unit is owned without regeneration
  - a non-link package path falls back to the in-place runner with a reason
- `src/infra/update-runner-git-release.test.ts`:
  - a same-commit release with unverified artifacts is rebuilt
  - a current release is reported prepared, so finalization never regenerates it
  - the first release comes from the serving worktree's commit, and the checkout's different target is still built
- `update-command-post-update.test.ts`: a switched release converges plugins only after its restart.
- `git-release.test.ts`: a checkout with no owning Gateway service keeps the in-place runner. The test fails without the gate.
- `update-command-execution-validation.test.ts`: when a developer build holds the checkout's artifact lock, a Git release update still runs. It never takes that lock, because releases build in their own worktrees. The test fails without the fix.
- `update-command-convergence-authority.test.ts`: under `--no-restart`, a switched release persists the channel and leaves plugins alone; an already-current rerun from the checkout of a converted install completes.
- `update-runner-git-release.test.ts`: a successful rebuild of an incomplete runtime reports the new release's verdict.
- `update-command-convergence-authority.test.ts`: release convergence runs in the updater, with no fresh process and no Doctor.
- `update-command-verification.test.ts`:
  - a verified release ends its trial
  - a switched release's Gateway restarts itself without a native restart
- `src/state/state-upgrade.test.ts`: `git-install` stays out of the startup upgrade copy.
- Gates: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm check:test-types`, oxlint/oxfmt on changed files. On mbp-m5 at `99b7f080`, the broad update suite plus the package-release and package-update tests pass 1,944 / 1,948, with 1 skipped. The 3 failures are environmental:
  - `update-runner-git-node-preflight` ×3: mbp-m5's Node 24.21 is below `engines`.

## LOC

prod +1018 / −38 (net +980); test +951 / −3.

Draft: lands after #198835. #198389 has merged; #199770 carries the same startup-copy exclusion for main.

prs.title: fix(queue): end queued input only on a recorded cause
prs.body:
## Problem

A message queued while a turn runs could be dropped because a check failed, not because anything ended it.

The custody contract (`docs/concepts/session-controller.md`) lets an accepted input end only as consumed, deliberately dropped, cancelled or interrupted, and requires every accepted input to stay accounted for. The access-policy contract (`docs/plugins/sdk-runtime/gateway-and-nodes.md`) says an owner aborts its signal when a source is revoked, and that an internal assertion error "refuses the operation without revoking the person or their admitted runs".

The code did the opposite in two places:

- The authority owners latched a revocation they found inside `assertCurrent()` without aborting their signal (`operator-run-authority.ts`, `admitted-run-context.ts`). Revocations found by event rechecks were recorded; ones found by a direct check were not.
- Seven queue and mailbox readers ended custody when `assertCurrent()` threw: `isFollowupOperatorAuthorityCurrent` and its four callers (followup runner, drain retry filter, stalled-turn handoff, goal return), mailbox claim release, early injection and steer admission, `reserveSteerCandidate`, and the channel steer caller. Each re-derived the owner's decision from the thrown error with its own rule.

On a real Gateway with an access-policy plugin, a 30 s policy outage while a message was queued dropped it as `withheld`; it never ran after the policy returned.

## Fix

- Owners record revocation: `assertCurrent` in `operator-run-authority.ts` uses its existing `revoke()`, and `createAdmittedRunOperatorAuthority` aborts a local revocation signal, composed with the upstream one, instead of keeping a private latch. A policy outage stays non-terminal.
- Queue and mailbox custody end only on recorded facts: the input's abort signal (which already includes the source authority's signal), retirement, cancellation, or consumption. A failed check now only refuses that attempt; the input stays queued and the drain retries it.
- Deleted `isFollowupOperatorAuthorityCurrent` and every inferred custody end listed above. The deletions in `drain.ts`, `agent-runner-execute.ts` and `goal-continuation-return.ts` match #200231.
- Notices survive the owner's new revocation signal. The stalled-turn handoff refuses a continuation while the source authority is aborted or refusing, without ending custody, so the original dispatch keeps its fallback notice. `runReplyAgent` still returns a prepared preflight failure notice when the operation was aborted by the source authority's own revocation; an explicit Stop, supersession or restart stays silent.

No new helper, flag, retry, backoff, schema or config. Production code: net −43 lines.

Replaces #200413, which taught two of these readers a wider "temporary" rule; that rule disagreed with the owner on remote-ingress "owner changed" errors and would have retried such an input forever.

## User impact

- A message queued during a temporary access-policy outage runs after the policy recovers.
- An internal policy error no longer silently drops a queued message.
- Revocation, Stop, delete and graceful restart behave as before: revoked, stopped and deleted messages are cancelled with zero model calls.

Affected installs: those using an access-policy plugin whose evaluation can fail. No built-in policy reaches the outage path.

## Evidence

- Regression tests, red on the merge base `b4254cb2`, green on this head:
  - mailbox: the exact controller input survives a refusing run or adapter authority (base: consumed);
  - followup runner: policy outage and an unsignaled internal assertion error keep the input (base: dropped);
  - authority owners: a revocation found by `assertCurrent` aborts the owner's signal, including remote-ingress owner replacement (base: signal not aborted);
  - steering: early and guarded steer assertions, `reserveSteerCandidate`, and the channel steer caller keep the source after an unsignaled failure and still end it on recorded cancellation (base: retired).
- Real Gateway from source (`ocx src`, isolated state, real model, a test access-policy plugin loaded through `plugins.load.paths` that reads its grant from a file; non-owner sender), base vs head, with the message confirmed queued before each event:

  | Event | Base `b4254cb2` | Head |
  |---|---|---|
  | 30 s policy outage (grant file moved away and back) | withheld; never answered | same queued run answered after restore; 0 model calls during the outage; no failure notice for the queued message |
  | Grant revoked | cancelled, 0 model calls, socket 4001 `grant-revoked` | same |
  | Outage, then grant revoked | already withheld during the outage | kept through the outage, then cancelled; 0 model calls |
  | Stop | cancelled, 0 model calls | same |
  | Delete | removed, 0 model calls | same |
  | Graceful restart | resumed and answered | same |

  During the outage the head logs 14 refused attempts in 30 s (peak 2/s), each refused before any model call.
- Accepted edge: a long outage keeps the message queued on the drain's existing retry cadence.
