prs.title: fix(signal): align autoStart daemon bind with local connection URL port
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A path-prefixed managed-native URL is a proxy, not the daemon bind. For a saved `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal`, autoStart reserves port 8080 for that proxy and binds the daemon on 8081. Readiness stays on the unchanged proxy URL. A URL on another port, such as `http://127.0.0.1:8082` with no `httpPort`, also stays the client endpoint. Set `httpPort` when the daemon should listen on a non-default port. Remote, HTTPS, and cross-family URLs stay independent.

Ref #116165

## Evidence

Head `4eaf1e5f323`. `extensions/signal/src/transport-prefixed-proxy.test.ts` prepares a saved `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal` URL with no httpPort, writes that transport, and prepares it again. The proxy URL stays on 8080 and the daemon port is 8081. The same setup binds the daemon on 8080 when the path check is absent. macOS, signal-cli 0.14.9.

The production resolver reserved 8080, allocated daemon port 8081, and kept `baseUrl` at `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal`. `spawnSignalDaemon` started signal-cli. A loopback forwarder stood in for the independent `/signal` proxy on 8080. `signalCheck` used the unchanged base URL.

```console
{
  "reserved": [8080],
  "allocated": 8081,
  "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal",
  "daemonPort": 8081,
  "signalCheck": { "ok": true, "status": 200, "error": null },
  "listeners": [
    "node ... TCP 127.0.0.1:8080 (LISTEN)",
    "signal-cl ... TCP 127.0.0.1:8081 (LISTEN)"
  ]
}
```

signal-cli listened on 8081. The readiness check against `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal` returned HTTP 200. No phone account was registered.

Upgrade on Windows 11 10.0.26300, Node v24.19.0. Published OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (`b556fdf`) wrote `channels.signal` with `config set`: enabled, a saved account, `transport.kind` `managed-native`, and `transport.url` `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal`. `httpPort` was left unset. `resolveSignalAccount` from the published `v2026.11.2` sources and from this head then read that same file.

```console
{
  "stable": {
    "savedUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal",
    "savedHttpPort": "omit",
    "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal",
    "httpPort": 8080,
    "urlKept": true
  },
  "head": {
    "savedUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal",
    "savedHttpPort": "omit",
    "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal",
    "httpPort": 8081,
    "urlKept": true
  }
}
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A config written by published OpenClaw 2026.11.2 with a path-prefixed loopback proxy URL stays the client endpoint on this head, and the daemon port moves to 8081. The published resolver keeps that same saved URL on port 8080.
- **Real environment tested:** Windows 11 10.0.26300, Node v24.19.0, published OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (`b556fdf`) for the saved config, head `1d08a5e9d41ee8a57dafde368361ada21a050ee8` for `resolveSignalAccount`. Earlier macOS proof used signal-cli 0.14.9 at the same head.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Published `config set` wrote `channels.signal.transport.kind` and `channels.signal.transport.url`. `resolveSignalAccount` from the v2026.11.2 Signal account owner and from this head read that file.
- **Evidence after fix:** The upgrade console block in Evidence. Published resolution reports `httpPort` 8080. This head reports `httpPort` 8081 and the same `baseUrl`.
- **Observed result after fix:** The saved proxy URL was not rewritten. This head reserves 8080 for the proxy and binds the daemon on 8081. Published 2026.11.2 still selects 8080 for that saved URL.
- **What was not tested:** A registered phone account, or two signal-cli daemons at once. This upgrade run did not start signal-cli again. The earlier macOS run already showed signal-cli listening on 8081 and a readiness check through the proxy URL.

## Summary

- Treat a non-root connection URL path as an independent proxy
- When that proxy uses port 8080, allocate the daemon on 8081 and leave the proxy URL unchanged
- Leave a saved URL on another port as the client endpoint
- A config written by OpenClaw 2026.11.2 still resolves that way on this head

## Test plan

- [x] Same-port path `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal` starts signal-cli on 8081
- [x] `signalCheck` against that unchanged proxy URL returns HTTP 200
- [x] Saved transport URL is not rewritten
- [x] Published 2026.11.2 config resolves to daemon port 8080, and this head resolves the same file to 8081

prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.



## Round 3 (ClawSweeper re-review findings + live-Gateway proof)

Head `1e502cd5e72` (synced with upstream/main, 0 behind). All review findings addressed:

- **[P1] Historical catalog hashes preserved** — the companion table leaked into predecessor schema generation, replacing historical hashes. New generation-owned transform `withLegacySkillSelectionCompanionAbsent` strips the unreleased table + indexes from every predecessor layout (`getOpenClawStatePredecessorSchema`, `state-before-provision-source`, `state-before-bootstrap-deferred` inputs). Historical inputs are byte-identical to upstream; the historical hash assertions are restored untouched; generated SQLite catalogs regenerated (228/235 inputs byte-identical, only current-layout inputs changed, as intended).
- **[P2] Input truncation marked before digest suffix** — names cut at the 64-char input budget are now marked truncated up front, so `aaa…(64)+alpha` vs `aaa…(64)+beta` keep distinct audit identities (regression test added).
- **[P2] Canonical decoder reused** — the writer owned a copied run/tool/message decoder; it now imports `parseAgentRunRow`/`rowToAuditEvent` from `audit-event-row.ts`, with companion decoding confined to `rowToStoredAuditEvent` + the distinct companion row shape.
- **[P2] Bootstrap privacy extraction removed** — the unrelated `workspace-bootstrap-privacy.ts` extraction is reverted; `src/agents/workspace.ts` is byte-identical to upstream again.
- **[P3] Stale sequence cache invalidated** — companion allocation consumes shared sequences outside the retention fast path (including duplicate-source attempts); the writer now drops the cached high-water mark on the skill path (regression test: ledger row after a skill write reports its true stored sequence).
- **Stale generated gateway validators** — the PR updated the protocol schemas but not the compiled predicates, so `kind=skill_selection` / `status=observed` failed gateway validation (2 gateway tests red). Regenerated via `scripts/generate-gateway-validators.mts`; 21/21 gateway tests green.
- **Test hygiene** — the `PRIVATE_PROMPT_CONTENT` absence assertion now supplies the sentinel as input (prompt/toolInput/skillFileContents); the unrelated expired-identity rendering case is removed from this PR.
- **Data-model compatibility proof** — new regression test builds a v39 pre-companion database with a stored legacy row, opens it with the current build (migrates 39→40, row intact), records a skill_selection (shared sequence continues at 2), and reads both rows back.

### Live-Gateway behavior proof (new, real Gateway + shipped CLI)

Production chain on a temp state dir — real tool-boundary read of a real `SKILL.md` through `wrapToolWithBeforeToolCallHook` → observer → recorder → store → **running Gateway** (fresh build, `--auth none`, loopback) → shipped CLI:

```
$ openclaw audit --kind skill_selection
TIME                          KIND             STATUS    AGENT  RUN           ACTION                     SELECTED
2026-11-14T23:42:01.167Z      skill_selection  -         -       observed  main   proof-run-1   skill.selection.observed  skill:proof--demo

$ openclaw audit --kind skill_selection --json
{"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":2,"eventId":"2c71cbfc-…","sourceSequence":1,
"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main",
"sessionKey":"agent:main:proof","sessionId":"proof-session-1","runId":"proof-run-1",
"action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection",
"actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"proof--demo"}]}
```

Stored rows: ledger `agent.run.started` (seq 1) → companion `skill.selection.observed` (shared seq 2, `main`/`agent:main:proof`/`proof-session-1`/`proof-run-1`/`proof--demo`) → ledger `agent.run.finished` (seq 3). Metadata-only, no prompt/tool content persisted. (An LLM-driven variant was attempted with local ollama `qwen2.5:7b`/`gemma4:12b`; the agent loop stalled at the reply watchdog, so the trigger is the repo-blessed scripted tool call — every stage after it is production code on a live Gateway.)

### Verification on this head

- `test/scripts/sqlite-schema-catalog-equivalence.test.ts` 203/203
- `runtime-skill-selection` + `audit-events.skill-selection*` incl. new upgrade/sequence tests green
- `audit-events` (37), `commands/audit` (36), `gateway/server-methods/audit` (21/21) green
- `tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files, line-cap ratchet clean vs upstream merge-base


## Round 4 (re-review findings, head `883b4d8d003`)

Both P2 findings fixed, plus the requested proof/test adjustments:

- **[P2] Buffered run starts retained until acceptance** (`src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts`) — the skill path now keeps the buffered start for the existing paired-settlement contract when `writer.record(start)` returns false, while skill observations still record independently. Regression test: with a rejecting writer, the terminal settles as one paired `recordRun(start, finish)` instead of a lone finish.
- **[P2] Companion counts bound to transaction outcomes** (`audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts`) — tentative counts stage `rollback`/`invalidate` hooks through `stageSqliteTransactionState`, as the canonical ledger does. Negative control verified: without the fix a rolled-back overflow batch leaves the cap violated at 100,001 rows; with it the next insert trims honestly to 98,976. Covered by `drops tentative companion counts when their batch rolls back`.
- **Upgrade proof targets v2026.11.3** — confirmed the 2026.11.3 release is schema v39 (no companion table), so the regression test builds exactly that layout, opens it with the current build (migrates 39→40, `schema_meta` intact), and shows the stored audit row plus continued shared sequencing.
- **Flagged low-value tests removed** — unrelated date/empty-limit CLI variants and the full marker-construction equality case are out; encoding, truncation, and production-boundary coverage retained.
- Real-agent/model invocation remains best-effort: local ollama models (`qwen2.5:7b`, `gemma4:12b`) stall at the agent reply watchdog in this environment, so the trigger stays the repo-blessed scripted tool-boundary call; every stage after it (observer → recorder → store → running Gateway → shipped CLI) is production code, demonstrated in Round 3.

Verification on this head: skill-selection storage 7/7 (incl. rollback + v2026.11.3 upgrade), audit-events + commands/audit 45/45, gateway 21/21, runtime-skill-selection green, `tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean.


## Round 5 (re-review: settlement intent + true v2026.11.3 fixture, head `4fd73e177bc`)

- **Buffered run-start settlement intent documented** (`src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts`) — the skill path flushes the buffered start as a best effort so the ledger holds the run before its independent skill rows arrive (readers join by run; legacy run/tool views stay coherent), while rejection retains the start for the existing paired settlement boundary. This keeps the PR #178220 paired-start/finish contract: the terminal still settles as one paired run.
- **Upgrade fixture is the true v2026.11.3 layout** — verified the 2026.11.3 release is schema v39 without the companion table (release commit `50330aa9cf5`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 39`, no `audit_skill_selection_events`). The regression test now builds the fixture from the current schema minus only the unreleased companion table at version 40 (matching the release lineage), opens it with the current build, and asserts: `user_version`/`schema_meta` intact, a stored workspace setting row byte-identical, the stored audit row readable, lazy companion creation on first skill write, and continued shared sequencing with correct readback.
- Real-agent/model invocation remains environment-blocked (local ollama models stall at the agent reply watchdog; xAI cloud models need the `xai` extension whose dist build is broken by a pre-existing missing-`@solidjs/compiler` resolution from root, unrelated to this PR). The live-Gateway proof in Round 3 (production tool boundary → recorder → store → running Gateway → shipped CLI) stands as the in-environment maximum.

Verification on this head: skill-selection storage 7/7, audit-events + commands/audit 45/45, gateway 21/21, runtime-skill-selection green, `tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean.


## Round 6 (head `a71b0be6d94`)

- **True v2026.11.3 upgrade fixture** — the reviewer correctly noted the published v2026.11.3 is schema v22 (verified: release tag → commit `847611dcaa3`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 22`, no companion table), not v39. The compat regression test now builds the fixture from `getOpenClawStatePredecessorSchema(22)` (verified to reproduce the release's `audit_events`/`schema_meta`/`workspace_setup_state`/`config_machine_state` tables byte-identically; only later-dropped device/gateway tables differ, which audit admission does not touch). The fixture migrates 22→40 (backup custody via the standard test-support helper, as a real install would back up first) with `schema_meta`, a stored workspace setting, and the legacy audit row byte-identical, then records a skill_selection via lazy companion DDL with continued shared sequencing and correct readback.
- **Removed the remaining flagged whitespace-only decision-limit variant** in `src/commands/audit.test.ts` (restored the upstream single-case form).

prs.title: fix(tui): load long replies whole when reopening a session
prs.body:
Fixes #200408

## What Problem This Solves

After `openclaw tui` is closed and reopened on a session, an assistant reply longer than 8,000 characters ends in `...(truncated)...`. The stored reply is complete, and the TUI showed it in full before it was closed.

The TUI requested `chat.history` with `sessionKey`, `agentId` and `limit` only, so the Gateway applied its default 8,000-character display cap. The TUI renders history rows as-is and has no per-message expansion, so the capped text looked like the whole reply. `openclaw tui --local` applied the same default cap.

## User Impact

Reopened TUI sessions show each reply in full, up to 500,000 characters. Tool results keep the Gateway's default 8,000-character preview, so history payloads grow only by the long replies themselves.

## Why This Change Was Made

The issue names two documented routes: a per-request `maxChars` on `chat.history`, or `chat.message.get` per truncated entry (what the Control UI does). This PR takes the first.

- The TUI now sends `maxChars: 500000` (the schema maximum) and `toolResultMaxChars: 8000` on `chat.history`.
- `--local` passes the same two limits to `readChatHistoryPage`.
- Both limits live in `src/tui/tui-backend.ts` so the two backends cannot drift.

`maxChars` was chosen over `chat.message.get` because the TUI has no lazy-expansion surface: it would have to fetch every truncated row before rendering anyway, which adds a hydration step, concurrency bounds and a failure fallback for the same result. The Control UI's complete-history read already uses `maxChars: 500_000`. I am happy to switch routes if maintainers prefer `chat.message.get`; another contributor proposed that route on the issue.

Accepted limits:

- A reply over 500,000 characters is still capped.
- A newer TUI connected to a Gateway that predates `toolResultMaxChars` would have its history request rejected as an unknown parameter. I could not determine which release added the parameter; please say if a fallback is wanted.

## Evidence

Real Gateway over WebSocket (temporary test in `src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts`, not committed): a stored 11,532-character assistant reply ending in `THE END`, read with the TUI's old and new `chat.history` parameters.

| Request | Text returned | Ends with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before: `limit` only | 8,018 characters, `truncated: true`, `reason: "display-cap"` | `...(truncated)...` |
| After: `maxChars: 500000`, `toolResultMaxChars: 8000` | 11,532 characters, identical to the stored reply | `THE END` |

The 8,018 matches the issue report (8,000 cap plus the 18-character marker).

Checks run on this head:

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/tui/gateway-chat.test.ts src/tui/embedded-backend.test.ts`: 164 passed. The updated assertions cover the request parameters in Gateway mode and the page-reader parameters in `--local` mode.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed.
- `pnpm format:check` on the touched files: passed.

Not done: the reopened reply has not been viewed in a live `openclaw tui` with a real model. The development container had no systemd user session for the launcher's Gateway check and no configured model provider.

prs.title: fix(agents): settle cleanup claims after run retirement
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Stop can retire a subagent run while its browser-cleanup claim waits for registry persistence. The queued claim then raises `Subagent cleanup execution changed`, making an otherwise completed Stop fail.

## Solution

Distinguish queued lifecycle owner loss from other registry rejections. Browser cleanup treats that specific pre-commit rejection as settled after retirement. Initial admission, database authority, address changes, and committed or unknown write failures still propagate.

A regression uses real cleanup bookkeeping to retire a killed run ahead of its queued browser claim. It verifies settlement without browser dispatch, announcement, row resurrection, or leaked root work.

## Evidence

- Main failure: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44024086924/job/133840779195.
- New regression fails on the base with the same lifecycle-persistence error, then passes with this fix.
- All 11 terminal-effects tests and all 8 yielded-Stop Gateway tests pass under pinned Bun.
- Scoped subagent typecheck, targeted lint, formatting and diff checks pass.
- Independent source review and autoreview found no actionable P0–P3 issues.

prs.title: fix(ci): balance hosted storage stripes within file limits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Full hosted main planning exceeds its existing job allowance after the storage test inventory grows. The planner balances by cost, then slices those groups at the file limit, leaving avoidable small groups that cannot share another storage row.

## User Impact

Restore a complete hosted plan within existing capacity limits. Test coverage, worker limits, runtime/build ownership, and job deadlines remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the existing 64-file storage limit into the weighted splitter and reserve enough groups before balancing. Preserve the runtime partition and all downstream admission checks. No new packing algorithm or increased cap.

Failing CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44017298685/job/133818733311.

prs.title: feat(gateway): opt-in Cloudflare Access JWT verification for trusted-proxy auth
prs.body:
Closes #200361

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in the documented Cloudflare Access setup, any process that can reach the Gateway from a trusted proxy address can claim any email (with a garbage or unsigned `cf-access-jwt-assertion`) and be admitted as that user, including `operator.admin`.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can set `gateway.auth.trustedProxy.cloudflareAccessJwt` so the Gateway admits a Cloudflare Access request only when its assertion is signed by their Access team for their application. Forged identity headers are refused. The setting is off by default and existing configs behave exactly as before.

```json5
trustedProxy: {
  userHeader: "cf-access-authenticated-user-email",
  requiredHeaders: ["cf-access-jwt-assertion"],
  allowLoopback: true,
  cloudflareAccessJwt: {
    issuer: "https://example.cloudflareaccess.com",
    audience: "your-application-aud-tag",
  },
}
```

## Why This Change Was Made

With the setting on, trusted-proxy admission verifies `cf-access-jwt-assertion` before trusting the user header:

- RS256 only, against the team's keys from `<issuer>/cdn-cgi/access/certs`. Keys are read with a 64 KB limit and fetched on demand: again on the first request after ten minutes, or for an unknown key id, at most once every 30 seconds per issuer. A failed fetch keeps the last good keys.
- `iss` must equal `issuer`, `aud` must contain `audience`, `exp` is required, and `exp`/`nbf` allow 60 seconds of clock skew.
- The user comes from the signed `email` claim. The user header must match it (case-insensitive), because other code still reads that header.
- Failures have distinct reasons: `trusted_proxy_access_invalid`, `trusted_proxy_access_user_mismatch`, `trusted_proxy_access_keys_unavailable`. They are documented in the trusted-proxy troubleshooting list.

Things reviewers should weigh:

- **Hand-written RS256 on `node:crypto`.** Verification is about 60 lines over `createPublicKey` and `crypto.verify` with `alg` pinned to RS256. The only JWT library in the repo (`jose`) belongs to the OpenAI plugin, and adding it to core would be a new core dependency. Happy to switch if maintainers prefer `jose` in core.
- **New config key** `gateway.auth.trustedProxy.cloudflareAccessJwt` (`issuer`, `audience`), with labels, help text and the regenerated config baseline. The issuer pattern is shared with `cloudflareAccessOidc.issuer`.
- **Fails closed with enterprise browser delegation.** Delegated identities are not Access emails, so delegated requests are refused while verification is on. The docs say so, and a test covers it.
- **Service-token JWTs have no email.** Nodes that pass Access with a service token send no user header, so they keep the existing `trusted_proxy_user_missing` outcome before any JWT work, then authenticate with their own credentials. A service-token assertion paired with a forged email header is refused as a mismatch.
- **Translations not regenerated.** The new config labels and help text are English only. The UI translation memory (`ui/src/i18n/.i18n/*.tm.jsonl`) is left to the normal i18n job.

## Evidence

- **Regression tests** (`src/gateway/auth.test.ts`, `src/gateway/trusted-proxy-delegation.test.ts`): forged unsigned assertion, another key's signature, another application's `aud`, expired assertion, forged user header, verified user admitted, service-token request, certs endpoint down, last good keys kept with one fetch per backoff window, and delegation refused. On `main` the forgery and delegation cases fail because the requests are admitted (`ok: true`). With this change, all pass.
- **Forgery harness over the Control UI HTTP surface** (the same requests as the issue): with the setting on, a garbage assertion, an unsigned JWT, a JWT signed by another key under the team's key id, and a valid assertion with a forged email header all get HTTP 401 with no operator config in the response. A correctly signed assertion gets HTTP 200. With the setting off, the forged requests are admitted, as on `main`.
- **Upgrade from latest stable, shipped Gateway, clean macOS VM** (macOS 26.6 guest, Node 24.21): `openclaw@2026.11.4` installed from npm ran the documented Cloudflare config (`docs/gateway/cloudflare-access.md` step 3) and admitted all three forgeries sent with curl from the same host. The same state was then upgraded to this branch (built from its `git archive`) with `openclaw doctor --fix` (exit 0). `gateway.auth`, `trustedProxies` and the MCP config were kept byte for byte, and with the setting off the branch behaves like stable. `openclaw config set gateway.auth.trustedProxy.cloudflareAccessJwt ...` was accepted and hot-applied; after it, all three forgeries got HTTP 401 with no operator config in the response. The third forgery names a key id from a real Access team's live `/cdn-cgi/access/certs`, so the Gateway fetched those keys and rejected the signature. Team name redacted.

  <details><summary>Guest transcript (redacted)</summary>

  ```text
  ##### 1. stable 2026.11.4 Gateway, forged requests (04:02:57Z)
  gateway stable pid=2165 ready after 8s
  [garbage assertion] HTTP 200, operator-only MCP config in response: yes
  [forged unsigned JWT] HTTP 200, operator-only MCP config in response: yes
  [real team key id, attacker signature] HTTP 200, operator-only MCP config in response: yes

  ##### 2. upgrade the same state to this branch: doctor --fix, then Gateway with the setting off (04:03:08Z)
  doctor exit=0
  gateway.auth kept unchanged across upgrade: yes
  mcp server kept: true trustedProxies: ["127.0.0.1","::1"]
  gateway branch-off pid=2593 ready after 7s
  [garbage assertion] HTTP 200, operator-only MCP config in response: yes
  [forged unsigned JWT] HTTP 200, operator-only MCP config in response: yes
  [real team key id, attacker signature] HTTP 200, operator-only MCP config in response: yes

  ##### 3. turn on cloudflareAccessJwt through the branch CLI (04:03:40Z)
  config set exit=0
  Updated gateway.auth.trustedProxy.cloudflareAccessJwt. Change will apply without restarting the gateway.
  {"mode":"trusted-proxy","trustedProxy":{"userHeader":"cf-access-authenticated-user-email","requiredHeaders":["cf-access-jwt-assertion"],"allowLoopback":true,"cloudflareAccessJwt":{"issuer":"https://<team>.cloudflareaccess.com","audience":"made-up-aud"}}}
  gateway branch-on pid=2931 ready after 5s
  [garbage assertion] HTTP 401, operator-only MCP config in response: no
  [forged unsigned JWT] HTTP 401, operator-only MCP config in response: no
  [real team key id, attacker signature] HTTP 401, operator-only MCP config in response: no
  ```

  </details>

- **Live Cloudflare Access** (this head, temporary Access application, tunnel and hostname, all deleted after the run; identity, audience, team and hostname redacted): the branch Gateway ran on loopback with `cloudflareAccessJwt` set to that application's issuer and audience. Its Access policy allowed one existing Cloudflare account identity.
  - A real browser sign-in through Access was admitted: `/startupz` returned its authenticated details (version and build ID), which the Gateway serves only after trusted-proxy admission succeeds. That still held after the forgery below was rejected.
  - A forged RS256 assertion with the real issuer, audience and published key ID, a matching email and a current expiry, signed by an unrelated RSA key and sent straight to the Gateway origin, got HTTP 401 `Unauthorized` on `POST /tools/invoke`. A request with no assertion also got 401.
  - Control: with verification turned off, the identical forged request passed authentication and reached request validation (HTTP 400, `tools.invoke requires name`). With verification back on, it got 401 again.
  - Not covered by this run: a full Control UI WebSocket session, a model turn, or a channel flow.
- **Focused checks:** 10 test files, 149 tests, all pass: the two files above, the trusted-proxy device auto-approve, device pairing, git co-author admission and auth-mode policy suites, and the config schema, hints, tiers and doc-baseline suites. Core and gateway-test typecheck, lint, format, the assertion-safety and CI baseline ratchets, `config:docs:check`, the test-line ratchet (+133 of 400) and `git diff --check` are clean. Not run locally: the full test suite.

The detached cron preparation tests froze native retry timers during real plugin registry startup. After restoring those timers, cold Linux startup also exposed a five-second fixture script timeout that expired before artifact preparation completed.

prs.title: fix: keep GitHub publication bookkeeping out of conversation lists
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After `github_publish`, internal publication records appear as child conversations with generated identifiers and inflate the conversation's child count. This is the presentation regression following #196168 and #199525; the publication checkout still needs its own recovery record.

## User Impact

Publication bookkeeping stays out of normal conversation lists and child counts, including records from existing installations. **Show system sessions** reveals it with a friendly name. Ordinary child conversations and explicit human names remain visible under the existing filters.

No configuration or data migration is required. Publication permissions, checkout custody, PR identity, and recovery behavior remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The publication producer stamps the existing immutable creation-surface field. The Gateway recognizes that stamp and both deployed reserved-key forms, then owns their background classification and display names. Sidebar trees, references, adopted rows, and catalog counts consume the existing system-session filter consistently.

Existing-record recognition requires a reserved publication key, spawn provenance, and parent linkage; a matching label alone never hides an ordinary conversation. Stored labels remain intact for recovery. The incognito publication regression verifies the new stamp without making private rows durable.

The operator explicitly approved replacing unavailable local independent review with hosted ClawSweeper, and accepted the measured **+90 B gzip** Chat/New route cost. The Chat cap rises by exactly **88 B** to its measured total; no extra headroom is added. Startup JavaScript, requests, and CSS are unchanged. The base already exceeds the largest-CSS and Chat-request caps; those inherited overages remain visible.

## Evidence

Candidate: `a487714744982a28150263366bfcee50fc9f3e78`, based on `054fd9788bc0f86303e161ca3b2ab36a1ed8cd65`. The tested product source matches this commit; subsequent changes are the approved asset-budget constant and the fixture-only corrections below.

- The regression fails on base `054fd9788bc0f86303e161ca3b2ab36a1ed8cd65`: deployed publication records classify as ordinary dashboard sessions, and the browser reports three children instead of one.
- The registered Gateway list handler passes cold-read, filtering, explicit-name, ordinary-lookalike, and stored-label preservation checks. Publication/private-session, actual tool-handoff, and affected sidebar coverage passed; targeted core/UI typechecks, lint, format, protocol generation, and docs checks passed. Final production and full-tree unused-file scans both passed with zero entries.
- Browser E2E passes: default count **1**, system toggle count **3**, friendly publication names when shown, and filter persistence after reload. Screenshots below use synthetic records and a mocked Gateway transport in the real Control UI renderer.
- A built Gateway in a task-owned Linux UTM VM, with a real OpenAI GPT-4.1 model, delivered and persisted the reply; session classification/filtering and the reply survived Gateway restart, and a fresh model turn also delivered afterward. This presentation smoke seeded publication records: it did not publish to GitHub or simulate accepted publication receipts. Test and process cleanup passed.
- The candidate `qaRuntime` build passed. The initial source-script smoke hit an unchanged native-owner/source-loader mismatch on both candidate and exact base; the supported compiled E2E harness passed without weakening process ownership.
- Initial exact-head CI found the new regression fixture omitted the required human-creator `source: "profile"`. The one-line fixture correction passes the Gateway test typecheck, regression test (1.1 s body; 10.5 s wrapper total), lint, and format checks. That job subsequently passed in CI on `38d03f9f551e`.
- CI also exposed an affected Details-panel fixture that marks its parent system-created while expecting its children in a default-filtered sidebar. The test passes on the pinned base and fails on the candidate; diagnostic replay confirmed the parent is filtered and its expansion cleared. It now explicitly enables **Show system sessions**, preserving its system-creator facts and all child/reload assertions. The corrected Details scenario and default-hidden publication scenario pass together (2 tests, 46.4 s including compiler preparation); its test typecheck, lint, and format pass. Neither CI correction changes production source or weakens assertions. Exact-head CI: [run 44024168553](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44024168553); its terminal status is authoritative.
- Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; local autoreview failed authentication and produced no review. This is an approved review-order exception, not a clean local-review claim. Current hosted-review status is recorded in the ClawSweeper comment; current CI status is recorded in the linked run above.

### Asset cost

Same-toolchain comparison against `054fd9788bc0`; generated asset hashes normalized:

| Metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Chat boot JavaScript gzip | 1,324,689 B | 1,324,779 B (+90 B) |
| New Session boot JavaScript gzip | 815,755 B | 815,845 B (+90 B) |
| Startup JavaScript gzip | 91,018 B | 91,018 B |
| Chat / New JavaScript requests | 21 / 17 | 21 / 17 |

The adjusted cap check confirms Chat gzip now meets its cap; its only remaining violations are the two unchanged base overages described above. No startup baseline, request cap, or CSS cap was changed.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and proof commands</summary>

- Gateway regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/session-list-publication-tasks.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (test body 1.1 s; 33.9 s including native fixture preparation).
- Browser regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts ui/src/e2e/sidebar-publication-tasks.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (test body 6.9 s; 27.9 s total).
- Real-model/restart smoke: temporary diagnostic fixture through `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/publication-presentation.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, using built runtime and isolated state (1 passed; body 134.4 s, total 558.5 s including first native compilation). The diagnostic fixture is not part of the product patch.
- UI comparator: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-control-ui-performance-base.mts 054fd9788bc0f86303e161ca3b2ab36a1ed8cd65`.

The linked CI run records hosted durations. Against the base: production +71/-12 lines; tests and registration +388/-105; generated validator +112/-110; docs +6. The test growth includes extracting the existing private-session case to keep its owner below the file-size cap. Simplification retained the existing creation metadata, Gateway projection, and filter owners; no new state store, manager, migration, or UI-only naming workaround was introduced.

</details>

### Clean comparison

Before:

![Before: publication bookkeeping appears as two extra child conversations](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0888a952-ca70-402f-b0f9-b91b7df307b5)

After:

![After: only the ordinary child conversation is counted and shown](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/20e003a8-54db-436c-860b-fe28db57ad66)

### Annotated comparison

Before:

![Before: child count includes both publication records](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/13c4f9d7-b696-4c0c-b013-c1fe20c29318)

After:

![After: child count includes the ordinary conversation only](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f6d04f65-cff9-419c-b593-3682c23c678b)

prs.title: feat(ui): add Santa Claws to the Lobsterdex
prs.body:
Closes #199466

Merge before the Clawnadian (#199443): Santa Claws takes entry #50 and the Clawnadian follows as #51.

## What Problem This Solves

The Lobsterdex has pop stars, emperors and inventors, but nobody brings presents.

## User Impact

A new rare visitor, **Santa Claws**, can arrive in the Control UI and be collected in the Lobsterdex as entry #50, right after Alexander Graham Shell. The collection grows from 49 to 50 entries. Saved discoveries, names, first-visit dates and shiny sightings are kept. A finished 49/49 collection loses its golden trim until Santa Claws visits, the same current-catalog rule #159815 used.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Santa Claws:** red shell, a Santa hat with a white fur brim and pom-pom (it covers the antennae), a curly white beard and moustache, a black belt with a gold buckle, a white fur strip down the front, and a candy cane raised in its right claw. "Makes a list. Pinches it twice."

It reuses the palette, artwork, held-prop, lore and discovery code from #159815, with the same rarity as those seven characters. The candy cane goes in the right-claw prop slot next to the microphone, brush and telephone receiver, so it waves and snips with the claw and replaces the moving-day bag.

Accepted edge case: like the other characters with their own hair or hat, a visitor that also rolls headwear (crown, sprout, or the December Santa hat) wears it on top of the built-in hat.

prs.title: fix(gateway): accept verified Serve UI identity with trusted-proxy auth
prs.body:
## Problem

With `gateway.auth.mode: "trusted-proxy"`, managed Tailscale Serve requests for the Control UI fail on the Cloudflare Access required-header gate, even when `gateway.auth.allowTailscale=true` and the Serve ingress and Tailscale identity are verified. Native macOS has a related distinction: its `openclaw-macos` `ui` client is **not** classified as a browser Control UI client; its separate `node` connection must not inherit user-level Tailscale authorization.

Related to #190474. Also relevant: #17761 and #73034.

## Root cause

- The `trusted-proxy` branch in `src/gateway/auth.ts` returns its Cloudflare-header failure before reaching the managed-Serve identity branch.
- `captureGatewayAuthPolicy` treats `tailscale` as disabled whenever the configured mode is `trusted-proxy`.
- The WebSocket auth context previously selected a Control UI auth surface for every WS connection, conflating native operator UI and node-role admission.

## Change

- Evaluate verified, internally attributed **managed Serve** user identity on eligible operator-UI auth surfaces before the trusted-proxy branch, while preserving Cloudflare's ordinary-listener header and allowlist checks.
- Include native-app `ui` clients in this operator-UI authentication surface using the existing `isNativeAppUiClient` classifier. **Do not** change their device-pairing policy or the server's `isControlUi` pairing classification.
- Select a separate non-Control-UI WebSocket auth surface for nodes and other clients. They cannot authenticate from Tailscale user identity alone; their existing device-token verification and role/scope/pairing checks remain authoritative.
- Keep Tailscale-based operator grants valid under trusted-proxy mode only while `allowTailscale` remains enabled.
- Rate-limit failed, credential-free Serve WhoIs authentication attempts in trusted-proxy mode; preserve other auth-mode rate-limit handling.
- Improve actionable missing-header, node-credential, and Serve-identity diagnostics in both the Gateway and the native macOS onboarding UI, including typed Swift auth error classification and explicit SSH/device-token recovery.
- Preserve pre-existing OpenClaw ID tunnel node admission on the non-Control-UI WS auth surface after separating Tailscale UI and node authorization (regression found by ClawSweeper; fixed in a26644a, tested in 6e61006).
- Document the independent trust boundaries: Cloudflare's `trustedProxy.allowUsers` applies to the proxy listener, whereas managed Serve admission relies on verified tailnet identity and tailnet access policy.

## Before / after

| Request | Before | With this patch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cloudflare Access with trusted proxy identity, required headers, allowed user | Accepted | Accepted (unchanged) |
| Cloudflare with missing/spoofed required identity, untrusted source, or disallowed user | Rejected | Rejected (unchanged) |
| Managed Serve, `allowTailscale=true`, verified WhoIs and operator browser/native UI | Trusted-proxy header failure | Accepted as verified Tailscale UI identity, with normal device rules |
| Managed Serve, invalid/missing WhoIs, `allowTailscale=false`, or forged/unmanaged ingress | Rejected | Rejected |
| Managed Serve, native node with no valid device credential | Rejected | Rejected (not made tokenless) |
| Managed Serve, native node with valid paired/role-scoped device token | Existing credential path after shared-auth failure | Existing credential path retained |

## Reproduction

1. On a non-production Gateway, configure `gateway.auth.mode="trusted-proxy"` with Cloudflare Access user and required JWT-assertion headers, the correct `gateway.trustedProxies`, and `gateway.auth.allowTailscale=true`.
2. Independently expose the loopback Gateway through OpenClaw-managed `gateway.tailscale.mode="serve"` and reach the dedicated Serve listener.
3. From a tailnet member with matching `tailscale whois`, connect an operator browser UI or native `openclaw-macos` `ui` session. The previous implementation reports `trusted_proxy_missing_header_cf-access-jwt-assertion`; this patch admits only the verified operator UI identity.
4. Repeat with the native `node` session: only a correctly provisioned, approved, role-scoped device token may authorize it. A matching tailnet login is insufficient.

## Security / boundaries

- The managed Serve provenance comes only from the listener-owned request marker; forwarded Tailscale headers on the ordinary proxy listener do not grant Serve privileges.
- The login must match the daemon's `tailscale whois` result. Failed identity verification does not become a trusted-proxy principal.
- The Cloudflare trusted proxy still requires its configured trusted source, identity and required headers, and `allowUsers` policy. **Cloudflare's allowlist is not a Serve allowlist**: verified tailnet users can authenticate over managed Serve even if their usernames are not in `trustedProxy.allowUsers`; apply narrow Tailscale grants/ACLs and only enable `allowTailscale` for a trusted tailnet.
- No general token/password fallback was added to trusted-proxy mode. The existing **local-direct only** password fallback remains unchanged.
- HTTP API routes never inherit Tailscale identity authentication; read-only Control UI HTTP keeps same-origin restrictions.
- Native node/device identity and pairing remain enforced; the patch does not auto-pair nodes or turn tailnet membership into device authorization.

## Tests and validation

Validated on the isolated development checkout on an Apple Silicon Mac mini against **commit `e0b9b75428f1`** (Node 24.22.3, pnpm 12.15.0, Xcode 27.2). No production Gateway or user configuration was touched.

- **Gateway Vitest**: 16 targeted files, **315 passing tests**, including trusted proxy, Serve/ingress attribution, node device tokens, auth policy revocation, Cloudflare hardening, browser origins, native UI admission siblings, OpenClaw ID tunnel/node and role/pairing behavior. Commands used repository `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` with the gateway shard config.
- **OpenClaw ID P1 regression proof**: the exact new node-WebSocket test **fails on the prior 03bb6d1 implementation** and **passes with the fix** on HEAD. Node principals remain disallowed on generic HTTP.
- **TypeScript core typecheck**: `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- **Gateway scope Oxlint**: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.core.json ...` passed (0 warnings, 0 errors).
- **Swift shared kit**: `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter GatewayErrorsTests --jobs 2` passed (**26 tests**), including new typed trusted-proxy identity-header mapping.
- **Native macOS app**: `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter OnboardingRemoteAuthPromptTests --jobs 2` passed (**13 tests**). This compiled the native app and exercised the newly added identity-header/Tailscale recovery and presentation cases.
- **Formatting/syntax**: `git diff --check`, oxfmt on docs, and Swift parser checks passed.

**Remaining validation gap:** tests use isolated Gateway/Swift fixtures; we have **not** run a real Cloudflare Access + Tailscale managed Serve + macOS primary UI/node end-to-end session on a live Gateway, nor the entire repository CI matrix. A maintainer must confirm policy and live behavior before this Draft can be marked ready.

## Limitations / maintainer decisions

- This fixes the independently valid mixed operator-UI ingress boundary. It does **not** provision a missing native macOS device credential. Previously approved pairing alone is not proof that the app has a usable token; first-time primary-node onboarding must use a supported explicit credential/bootstrap route (e.g., SSH tunnel with local-direct gateway password) until a full native flow is agreed and verified.
- The interactive configuration wizard currently disables trusted-proxy + Serve; manual setup and its constraints are documented here. Changing the wizard and simplifying first-time native onboarding are separate product decisions.
- Real Cloudflare Access + Tailscale Serve + macOS primary/node end-to-end integration should be confirmed by maintainers before marking this PR ready. In particular, the mixed ingress auth policy is an explicit product/security decision, independent from the implementation tests. No production Gateway, credentials, Tailscale, Cloudflare or LaunchAgents were modified.

**Draft intentionally:** full upstream CI, real ingress integration evidence and maintainer approval of the mixed-ingress security policy are outstanding. ClawSweeper's earlier review was against the pre-regression-fix head; please re-review this exact updated revision.

prs.title: fix: prevent startup refusals in chat and queued model discovery
prs.body:
Related: #197784

## What Problem This Solves

A first chat can be refused when background model discovery creates its database after the request has captured session facts. Queued discovery can also fail because it inherits a temporary SQLite inspection scope that closes before the queued work starts.

## User Impact

First chats can proceed while remote discovery finishes asynchronously. Read-first startup keeps its existing write restriction, and queued catalog work can read auth after the caller's inspection ends. The real Gateway regression preserves custom-store sessions, history and settings and completes a synthetic model-backed chat.

Cold native initialization moves earlier. Historical owner measurements observed about 771 ms more work before publication, warm repeat process CPU of 7.50→9.69 ms (+2.20 ms observed, not established causal overhead), and +4.8792 µs at warm background-callback entry. These are correctness tradeoffs, not throughput improvements. Already-admitted existing databases skip native preparation. There is no new schema, configuration option, cache, retry policy or operator action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Independent catalog persistence from #197784 (`76385fd77e3f77604489178112344be0b3ffed43`) could create a database after chat captured its absence. Registration checks then correctly rejected the stale facts. Configured model publication now awaits existing native preparation within its current build budget before capturing auth facts, only when writable admission permits it. Read-only startup publication does not borrow write authority.

The existing background catalog launch now exits only the caller's SQLite inspection scope. Spawn-broker and database-engine context remain intact, and the current plugin-generation and authority owners still govern the work when it starts.

The final change adds **37 production lines across four files**. A controlled subtraction removed the entire proposed startup-path expansion: the real custom-store Gateway case still preserved session authority, catalog persistence, stored data and chat. This PR therefore does not add canonical-path preparation to the writable startup owner. The remaining growth carries the awaited callback through its existing budget and provides the narrow background lifetime transfer. Affected fixtures use the maintained writer to establish the native storage prerequisite before simulating Gateway publication; their original assertions and deadlines remain.

## Evidence

Reviewed candidate: `44ae9fd79e9bae3f819dfea40cbf3d01454da8e5`, composed on exact main `282d5efe4b21f96339d915359dfef7978afd969e`. This baseline contains the landed Goal completion fix #200391 (`bbefb541`) and WebKit animation-check fix #200399 (`282d5efe`), both repairing actual failures in this PR's previous CI. The previous hosted candidate was `60ae9e5`. The final 20-file working tree is bound as `f6e05e0a450851648266dd8a9285be160e07f48c`; fresh local review and affected checks are complete as reported below; new-head hosted CI and Claw review remain pending.

- **The defect still exists on the selected main.** Its unchanged original xAI case passes under Node but fails under pinned Bun with `SESSION_MUTATION_AUTHORIZATION_CHANGED`. With only the deterministic test packet added, the same request/catalog interleaving fails under both runtimes. The real queued custom-store catalog case fails under Node with `SQLITE_READONLY_WORKER_SCOPE_CLOSED`; its Bun arm passes. These observations do not establish a runtime-only defect.
- **The integrated fix passes the real flows.** At signed `a1c31b49`, the controlled xAI case and real custom-store catalog case pass under both Node and pinned Bun. The tests use actual catalog persistence, retain independent authority witnesses and preserve the original request assertions.
- **The smaller source is supported by a removal control.** Replacing only the startup owner with its exact main version, while retaining the admission guard and background scope fix, passes the complete Node catalog case in 17.237 s. It preserves read-first admission, the captured witness through catalog persistence, session creation and stored ID, model-backed chat/history, and existing transcript/settings. This is why the 14-line startup companion was deleted. Additional affected proof for this final source: the smaller source passes the real catalog case under pinned Bun, eight selected ownership/auth/scope cases under each runtime, and all 15 Node prompt-prefix cases. The Node catalog subtraction control already uses the exact final inputs. Prior xAI Node/Bun results are reused through the documented default-layout call-path equivalence, not presented as reruns. The external prefix receipt initially expected 14 cases and was corrected after all 15 actual cases passed; no test was repeated.
- **Review and required checks:** Fresh independent LOCAL Codex review of all 20 changed files and 63 context files, three complete passes with zero actionable P0–P2 findings; reviewed staged tree equals the signed checkpoint tree. Cumulative `pnpm check:changed --base 282d5efe4b21f96339d915359dfef7978afd969e --staged --timed` passed 35/36 gates and exited 1 in 694.735 s; only the dead-export scan failed with 7 production/3 full-tree symbols. The exact 282 baseline scan reproduced the complete same sets in 100.792 s with identical 254 install inputs; all type/lint/format and remaining guards passed. This qualifies the local baseline failure only, not hosted CI or an inherited landing exception. Actual cumulative growth remains **701 test lines**, with **301** explicitly allocated beyond the unchanged 400-line allowance. Final-source context binding and ratchet receipts: all 20 source/63 review-context hashes and the whole final tree match the signed checkpoint; the current changed check passed its line-growth and mock ratchets. The allocation remains 701 / (400 + 301).
- **Remaining CI gap:** run `44001040624` on hosted `60ae9e5` failed Goal, UI and heartbeat jobs. Goal and UI have separately landed source repairs now incorporated through the selected baseline. The heartbeat timeout did not reproduce in the recorded Mac and Linux parent/merge replays, and has no identified introducing cause. It remains unexplained; those passes are not a fix or an inherited-failure waiver. A new exact-head CI verdict is still required.

<details>
<summary>Historical causal proof, previous failed gates, and compatibility limits</summary>

The original xAI investigation forced the real catalog-save interleaving: Bun failed on the original owner, an explicit pre-#197784 save control passed, and the fix passed under Node and pinned Bun with actual persistence. Independent session-entry and database-absence witnesses still reject actual changes. Historical `842fe0b` startup proof exposed an unconditional eager-write refusal on both runtimes; its exact invoking publication phase was not uniquely recorded. That evidence supports preserving read-only admission, not claiming the now-deleted startup expansion was independently necessary.

Both original background-owner variants failed with `SQLITE_READONLY_WORKER_SCOPE_CLOSED`; the scope repair passed the owner cases under Node and Bun with broker/engine restrictions intact. The final Gateway fixture uses real catalog-limiter occupancy. Canonical SQL assertions retain the supported identity and birthtime contract added by #200192; the earlier cross-base claim that the birthtime field was inert was withdrawn. Its failed typecheck and intermediate checks remain historical, not final-source qualification.

The overlapping agent add/delete fixtures reproduced on Linux under Node and Bun. The correlated failure retained the original dispatch while the configured owner was replaced. Removing only this PR's first-birth addition made the original nine-case prefix pass. With production unchanged, persisting the union of required stores before initial roster publication made the prefix pass under both runtimes. Later reload ordering, snapshot publications, generation checks and deadlines stayed intact. This qualifies fixture initialization, not a Bun-only defect or an inherited CI exception.

Earlier CI exposed additional fixture consumers. The complete retained census is 17 failed cases in eight files; a catalog-projection case was missed in the initial census and corrected later. The actual-merge originals failed under Node/Bun, exact-parent controls passed, and the maintained-writer corrections passed without changing their assertions. The 100 ms no-replay test retains its timer, exact work counts and zero-owner precondition; real persisted-reader setup occurs before the timed contract. Partial logger/legacy mocks retain real module exports, with only the two obsolete baseline rows removed.

Prior full/correction checks remain recorded with their actual nonzero exits. The integrated 13-file check passed 35/36 and exited 1 solely on 14 production/108 full-tree export findings. Later eight- and two-file correction checks passed 25/26 and exited 1 on exactly those same sets; type/lint/format passed. Those findings matched the exact 2435 main-parent run and all 113 symbols had source causes: #200114, #198133, #198835, #198933, #198936, #198943 and `94e34f956969a2070aa7ad614894b443a6b63049` (PR unidentified). This was local baseline qualification only. It does not qualify a different parent or waive new hosted CI. An earlier aggregate exited2 on the material birthtime API mismatch. Previous independent Codex reviews were scoped-clean on their respective supplied sources, did not execute project code, and reported unavailable surrounding/sensitive context. The current source has the separate fresh LOCAL review and exact tree binding reported above.

The original first-birth measurement used a real synthetic 35 GiB agent database and 5,000 sessions, with comparison samples and A/A controls. Warm native preparation remained 0→0. Cold publication plus later save measured 974.01→896.45 ms wall, 1332.13→1343.65 ms process CPU, and 38.62→39.04 MB sampled host-JS allocation. Warm repeat wall was 7.41→8.30 ms; CPU A/A range was 29.20%. This covers the original 842 insertion, not subsequent source revisions. Its workspace was empty; it does not demonstrate a 62,000-file traversal.

The background-launch measurement used the retained synthetic 35 GiB database, 5,000 sessions and actual 62,000-file workspace path through an APFS COW clone. The scheduler/auth read does not traverse that workspace. Three counterbalanced A/B pairs and two independent A/A pairs performed equal work: 220 actual canonical reads with matching results and context checks. Warm callback entry was 4.7166→9.5958 µs (+4.8792 µs), above the observed A/A difference. End-to-end wall changes were inconsistent, including one increase beyond A/A bounds; no speedup, neutrality or noise-only conclusion follows. Sampled host-JS allocation was inconclusive. Both measurements are single-agent APFS owner controls with uncontrolled GC/page cache, not btrfs, fleet, total native-allocation or Gateway-throughput proof. Changed main auth/catalog contexts prevent treating these as fresh final-base measurements.

Installed compatibility proof remains bound to historical `553b9430143c4013cd818635e122016ccaabeccd`, before the background-scope repair: stable 2026.11.4 (`d843d6af`) → that exact package through verified backup, external package installation and Doctor. The installed Gateway retained the same custom-store session ID, thinking/verbosity settings, transcript prefix and remaining configuration except the explicitly asserted supported Workshop migration/marker from #192766. One real inference request to a synthetic Responses server produced a retained assistant reply. This is not a packaged upgrade of the final head, self-update, live xAI, or attribution of which operation created the database during the combined transition. Failed setup attempts and the corrected same-specimen assertion remain recorded; proof resources were cleaned up.

All fixtures are synthetic. Final-head CI and zero-open Claw review remain separate landing requirements. Previous successful reviews and passing replays do not waive them.

</details>

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): carry provider-native chat id into session-event turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#199701: while a backgrounded task runs, a human correction sent from the
same conversation sits queued (observed 95-153 seconds) and the running
assistant never receives it — it keeps acting on superseded instructions.
Steering was rejected with `tool_authority_mismatch` even with
collaborative steering enabled, and an `@mention` retry did not help.

Root cause: session-event turns (background completion finalization,
restart recovery, scheduled automation prompts) are injected through
`buildSessionEventContext`, which never set `MsgContext.ChatId`. Run
assembly copies `conversationId` from that field, so the
same-conversation authority projection compared against an empty
conversation id and rejected the correction. The reporter confirmed
supplying the matching conversation id re-enables the unchanged
authority snapshot.

## The Change

- Session-event targets retain the host-captured `nativeChannelId`
  alongside permission settings (`SessionEventTarget["settings"]`,
  destination settings, and the narrowing function — identity is a fact
  that follows current, never an intersected authority).
- The captured id is read through the canonical origin reader
  (`sessionDeliveryOrigin(entry)?.nativeChannelId` via
  `resolveSessionEventDestinationSettings`), not a route address.
- `buildSessionEventContext` populates `ChatId` from that captured id
  **only**: route addresses (`channel:<id>` for guild channels,
  `user:<id>` for DMs) are not the native conversation identity and do
  not substitute for it; the field stays absent when no identity was
  captured.
- Revocation, route, and thread checks are untouched: they read the same
  snapshot and now receive the identity they were already checking for.

## Evidence

- **Regression-first**: the ChatId case asserts the captured id flows
  through while a prefixed route address (`channel:<id>`) stays out of
  `ChatId` (it remains on `OriginatingTo`) and the field stays absent
  without a captured identity. First revision failed exactly as the
  projection would (`expected undefined to be '123456789012345678'`).
  Full file: **7/7** (the real-shaped-entry case covers a real `delivery.origin.nativeChannelId` through destination settings into context construction; the duplicated first captured-ID case was removed per review) (`session-event-context.test.ts`).
- **Sibling suites stay green**: session-event handoff, automation
  result, permissions, policy, config re-admission, and webchat-route
  files — **40/40**; authority and steering suites
  (`agent-runner-execution-message-authority`, `queue.authority`,
  `agent-runner-fallback-steering`) — **23/23**.
- Focused command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run
  src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-context.test.ts` on head
  `a2dd7462a14` (Node 26, isolated worktree).

- **Shipped dist build is green**: the dist declaration build
  (`write-unified-entry-dts`) compiles on head `a2dd7462a14`. On the
  prior head it failed with TS2304 (`SessionEntry` used without an
  import in `resolveSessionEventDestinationSettings` — vitest strips
  types without checking, so only the dist build exposed it); fixed in
  2f2f04ff14c.

## Risk / compatibility

Additive field population on internal event turns only. The field's
consumers either want it present (authority projection, run assembly,
hook identity context) or treat it as optional template context. No
permission expansion: the id is the host-captured conversation identity
the session already stores, and the revocation and route/thread checks
are unchanged.

prs.title: fix: make a newly installed Gateway available in the terminal
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After installing a native Gateway, opening a terminal and running `openclaw` can fail to find the command or use a different profile. A fresh named-profile macOS installation also leaves its bundled command out of the shell's search path.

## Intended User Impact

A fresh installation should establish a discoverable, profile-bound terminal command. Later installations must preserve the established default and operator-managed launchers, including configured profiles whose Gateways are offline. Explicit profile arguments and environment overrides remain supported. No existing state is migrated and no running Gateway or app is restarted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Install the terminal launcher only after successful service installation, and let fresh bundled named-profile installations establish the default when no selection exists. Preserve first-install ownership rather than switching defaults based on live reachability or the app's current selection. Existing selections should receive a contextual command instead of being silently replaced.

## Evidence

- Review status remains **changes requested**. The original independent review demonstrated PATH-command shadowing/custom-wrapper recursion, unsafe concurrent launcher refresh, PATH initialization ordering, default-install offline-profile claiming, and ignored shell startup directories. Revision `1828a5c1443146adf4487cbaa86755abf89abe17` implements responses to those five findings, but has not received a clean independent re-review and is not approved for landing.
- Revised-source isolated execution passed 25/25 terminal cases, including real fish 4.9.3 with default/custom configuration roots, 18/18 service-install integration cases, and 35/35 completion cases. Five Windows-only completion cases were skipped on macOS. The operator PATH table was then expanded to both default/named profiles and both local/npm bins: its separate focused run passed 4/4, with 23 nonmatching cases skipped by that filter.
- Regression coverage exercises actual generated launchers and interactive/login shells, offline configurations, late launcher-symlink substitution with unchanged canary bytes/permissions, and concurrent shell edits through the real atomic-file helper. Initial new TypeScript regressions failed before the implementation changes. Touched test files were audited; redundant native assertions/calls were removed while distinct lifecycle, operator-file and failure coverage was retained.
- A standalone fixture compiled and executed the actual native CLI extension with declaration-only peers, not the Mac app. Five native shell/default-selection scenarios failed against the original candidate after a logging-only compilation repair in the temporary baseline, then passed against the revised extension. The original native OSLog concatenation compilation error is corrected. This is not a full native app build or native runtime-suite pass; fake CLI profile checks demonstrate argument/environment transport, not final packaged-app profile selection.
- Scoped TypeScript lint, Oxfmt, SwiftFormat, SwiftLint (zero violations across three changed native files), Swift syntax parsing, native i18n verification and diff checks passed. The supported i18n generator updated only the two changed shell-command inventory entries. Native seeding now carries the installation's shell context so fixtures do not inherit operator PATH/startup directories.
- Local TypeScript typechecking still did not execute: the repository declaration-input guard rejects compiler/dependency paths in the shared pnpm store outside the checkout. The guard was not bypassed and no duplicate dependency tree was installed. Exact-head CI typechecking/builds, full native tests and Windows execution remain pending. Draft CI skipped its main validation jobs; skipped jobs are not passing proof. No new broad CI dispatch, readiness change or merge was performed.
- Consumed disposable fish bottle/cache and native harness files were removed. No live Gateway, desktop app, operator shell configuration or credentials were changed.

Source checkpoint: `1828a5c1443146adf4487cbaa86755abf89abe17`, based on `cc6c3a733dfa9e226efcf4b2c221c45fe40f9acc`. Published head: `0f1cc83811512e7930f7eb1b840e7f44c93427c7`; the official GitHub commit API reports the identical source tree `820d548b2721e5d472368fd612dcc69da8affab1`.
