prs.title: fix(build): Git install updates fail with "Declaration input escapes checkout" since #198661
prs.body:
Closes #200357

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update` on a Git install fails at `preflight-build` with `Declaration input escapes checkout` for every main commit since #198661, and the install stays on its old commit.

## User Impact

User impact: Git installs can update to main again. Normal builds keep the fast command-line declaration pass. A dependency that exists only outside the checkout still fails the build and names the escaped file.

## Why This Change Was Made

On POSIX the updater builds each candidate in a worktree inside the install it replaces (`<install>/.artifacts/.openclaw-update-preflight-*/worktree`). The Anthropic and OpenAI SDK declarations type `RequestInit` with relative `node_modules/undici` imports up to 10 parent directories up, so the compiler also reads the install's own `node_modules/undici`. The command-line pass from #198661 cannot deny that read, so it fails the build.

This keeps #198661's intent: declarations still depend only on files inside the checkout, and normal checkouts keep the fast pass. #198661 accepted "parent-install shadowing now fails loudly" because the command line cannot hide those reads. The updater's own preflight worktree is such a parent install, and already shipped updaters choose that path, so moving the worktree cannot fix updates from them.

When the command-line pass lists a file that is outside the checkout by path and by real path, the build discards that pass and emits through the bounded API filesystem from before #198661, which treats outside candidates as absent (the contract from #158674). Links that leave the checkout still fail as before. If the bounded compile fails, the error shows the compiler's diagnostic first, then the escaped read.

Maintainer decision: this undoes #198661 behavior change 1 for parent installs (fall back to the bounded compile instead of failing).

## Evidence

### Runtime output

Fresh Git install at `v2026.11.4` (d843d6af39a4), built with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build && pnpm ui:build`, macOS arm64, home directory not a symlink, internal disk. Gateway stopped, isolated state and config. Command:

```
OPENCLAW_UPDATE_DEV_TARGET_REF=<target sha> node <install>/openclaw.mjs update --channel dev --yes --no-restart
```

Base, target f947bdc94981:

```
install at d843d6af39a4 (2026.11.4), target f947bdc94981
update exit 1
install now at d843d6af39a4
[... 8 lines cut ...]
  ✓ preflight-checkout (229ms)
  ✓ preflight-deps-install (15.85s)
  ✗ preflight-build (23.11s)
    Failing check preflight-build (command-failed): Error: Declaration input escapes checkout: [redacted-path]
  ✓ preflight-cleanup (13.21s)
Failed: validating
[... 1 line cut ...]
```

`preflight-build` fails on the escape and the install stays at d843d6af39a4. The updater redacts the path. Building f947bdc94981 by hand in the same nested layout shows it:

```
Error: Declaration input escapes checkout: <install>/node_modules/undici/types/utility.d.ts -> <install>/node_modules/.pnpm/undici@8.12.2/node_modules/undici/types/utility.d.ts.
```

Head, target 133cfd5d3f76 (this PR), same built install:

```
install at d843d6af39a4 (2026.11.4), target 133cfd5d3f76
update exit 0
install now at 133cfd5d3f76
[... 8 lines cut ...]
  ✓ preflight-checkout (366ms)
  ✓ preflight-deps-install (27.42s)
  ✓ preflight-build (330.54s)
  ✓ candidate-state-snapshot (2.04s)
  ✓ candidate-doctor (14.96s)
  [... 18 lines cut ...]
  ✓ git-checkout (18.96s)
  ✓ git-runtime-activation (111ms)
  ✓ database snapshot (3.65s)
  ✓ database migration writes (0ms)
  ✓ git-verify-head (14ms)
  ✓ preflight-cleanup (15.4s)
```

`preflight-build` passes, the candidate checks run, and the install moves to 133cfd5d3f76.

Bisect from the same install: target 1c1814a0bf78 (parent of #198661) exit 0, target 5a7d1718aa5 (#198661) exit 1 with the same escape.

### Tests

- `test/scripts/native-declaration-boundary.test.ts`, `bounds optional SDK relative imports to a checkout nested in a parent install`: on base f947bdc94981 it fails with `Declaration input escapes checkout`. On head it passes. With the fix reverted by `git apply -R` it fails again. It also checks that changing the parent install changes neither the declarations nor the inputs.
- Declaration consumers on head: `native-declaration-boundary`, `tsdown-declaration-resolution` (the escaped ancestor module, ambient types, package symlink, source symlink and source reference cases still refuse), `native-declaration-subprocess`, `write-plugin-sdk-entry-dts`, `run-tsgo-worktree`, `prepare-extension-package-boundary-artifacts.native`: 6 files, 77 passed, 7 skipped.
- `pnpm check:changed --base f947bdc94981` on head: passed. The dead export scan was skipped: on this base it reports unused exports only in files this change does not touch.

### Local review

Local ClawSweeper (`review --local-range`, Claude runner) on base f947bdc94981, head 133cfd5d3f76, complete review: patch is correct, security cleared, no maintainer decision required, patch rating B. Remaining: one P3 suggesting the escape note be added only when the bounded compile fails on module resolution. The compiler's diagnostic now comes first; matching diagnostic codes was left out to keep the error path simple.

prs.title: fix(cron): keep automations running when their chat's id changes
prs.body:
## Problem

Automations created from a chat stop, and recurring watchers are disabled, when that chat changes while the automation runs.

- A running automation restores its creator's authority through `restoreGatewayOperatorSource`. Its session-identity subscriber revoked that authority on any identity mutation that named the chat's key: a message edit (`sessions.rewind`), a reset, a compaction successor or a key move. Before #200314, creating any unrelated chat for the same agent also matched (`undefined === undefined`, #200307).
- A revoked condition or script ends as code `aborted`. `classifyCronScriptFailure` mapped `aborted` to `permanent`, and `applyJobResult` disables an `operatorSource` job on its first `permanent` error. One interrupted check therefore turned a recurring watcher off for good. #180891 intended the opposite: "Aborts (restarts, cancellation) are rethrown unchanged and stay retryable."
- Failure-repair turns compared the restored target's transcript id with the source's. Since #199512, key-linked sources no longer record that id, so the comparison was always unequal and every repair turn was silently downgraded to a non-owner.

Observed in production: a watcher was disabled twice in one day. Each time its condition aborted ~3.4 s in, ~0.1 s after another job started an isolated run (a new session).

## Fix

- `restoreGatewayOperatorSource` revokes only when the target chat is deleted (`kind === "delete"` for the target key). Edits, branch switches, resets and compaction keep the chat's authority; device, token, role, profile and grant revocation still end it through their existing subscriptions. The target type drops `sessionId`; the cron callers stop passing it.
- `classifyCronScriptFailure` maps `aborted` to `{ kind: "aborted" }`. The scheduler already treats that as an interrupted attempt: it does not count toward the failure streak and the next occurrence runs. Real script failures stay `permanent`. If the creator's authority was genuinely revoked, the next occurrence's source restore refuses it and that refusal still retires the job.
- `captureCronJobTurnTarget` drops the transcript-id comparison and links the repair turn to its chat by key.

Not changed here: sandboxed stream automations pin the exact transcript in `cron-stream-sandbox-authority.ts` (follow-up). Plugin session work (`service-session-work.ts`) shares the subscriber but keeps its own transcript/lifecycle check at each use.

Production code: +13 / −20.

## User impact

- Editing a message, switching branches, resetting a chat or compacting it no longer stops the automations it created.
- A watcher whose condition is interrupted runs again at its next occurrence instead of being disabled.
- Deleting the chat still stops its running automations.
- Already-disabled jobs are not re-enabled; run `openclaw automations enable <id>`.

## Evidence

- Regression tests, red on the merge base `b4fc0534`, green on this head:
  - `operator-run-recovery.test.ts`: key-linked authority stays current across an unrelated chat, a new transcript id and a reset, and is revoked when the chat is deleted (base: revoked at the edit).
  - `timer-outcomes.regression.test.ts`: a key-linked watcher whose condition ends `aborted` stays enabled and scheduled; `internal_error` still disables it (base: `aborted` disabled it).
- Touched and consumer suites pass on this head (`ocx test`): operator recovery, operator cancellation, cron operator source, repair notifications, isolated operator continuation/child/bind-parent, trigger evaluation, failure alerts, failure text, server-cron, outcome regressions. `operator-run-cancellation.test.ts` now cleans up the sender's run session with the real delete (`run-continuation-cleanup.ts` deletes it) instead of a transcript-id replacement.
- `config/session-identity-allowlist.txt` shrinks 6584 → 6580 pins: `cron-job-turn-target.ts` no longer compares an identity, and `operator-run-recovery.ts` drops two comparisons.
- Real Gateway from source (`ocx src`, isolated state, `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`), base vs head. The agent creates a 30 s condition watcher (`sleep 20` in the condition) from its own chat; the harness waits until a condition is `running`, then mutates the owner chat:

  | Event while a condition is running | Base `b4fc0534` | Head |
  |---|---|---|
  | Message edit (`sessions.rewind` + resend) | condition `aborted`; watcher disabled after 1 evaluation | condition completes (×3) |
  | Reset (`sessions.reset`) | not reached (already disabled) | condition completes |
  | Another chat created | not reached | condition completes |
  | Final job state | `enabled=0`, `cron trigger evaluation failed (aborted)` | `enabled=1`, 0 errors, 6 evaluations |

  A second, unsynchronized base run reproduced the same disable at the first edit that landed during a condition (abort in the same second as the edit).

prs.title: fix(ui): keep lazy panel menu actions ready for selection
prs.body:
Dashboard options can ignore Expand Dashboard or Restore split just after opening.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/6a1b6fef-8de4-46d1-8db7-8a8e43aa305c)

## What Problem This Solves

When lazy panel-menu content is already loaded, enabled rows can render before their selection handlers are registered. Clicking one then silently does nothing and leaves the root menu open. Five unrelated UI E2E jobs fail in the same layout-preservation test: three select Restore split and two select Expand Dashboard.

## User Impact

Dashboard and Layout menu actions become available together with their handlers, so the first actionable click can change the layout and dismiss the menu even during its opening phase.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rendering and activation now share the registered handler snapshot. Until it is ready, both use the existing disabled Loading row. This removes the independent body-rendering path that exposed actions before activation could find them. The shared test helper and its menu-hidden assertion are unchanged.

One shared panel-menu factory owns registration, loading items, lazy group rendering, error recovery, selection, and focus handoff for both consumers. The lazy components register their handlers; the factory renders only registered rows. This removes duplicate group renderers, the unused render callback bridge, and the separate boundary wrapper, preserving the readiness fix and unchanged regression. Production is net 38 lines smaller than the original base; the regression adds 105 lines. No budget or baseline file changes.

## Evidence

- A deterministic Node/jsdom regression exercises the real Dashboard menu, primes its lazy component in a separate mount, then clicks the first enabled connected leaf while frame callbacks are held in `opening`. It does not mock `onReady`, menu activation, or selection. Both labels fail on the base with no `menu-select` event and pass with the fix, including the expected layout update and menu closure.
- Final regression: 2/2 pass in 0.861 s Vitest wall time (179 ms in test callbacks); the exact regression fails 2/2 on original production source in 0.957 s. The CI Bun run also passed both cases in 256 ms total (193 ms / 63 ms).
- The current follow-up plus existing pane-header and dashboard-presentation consumer suites: 80/80 pass across three named files in 4.47 s. The readiness regression is unchanged.
- Touched-file type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Lint reports existing warnings in the unchanged layout-model function.
- Strict touched-file typecheck was attempted but stopped before checking source because the repository wrapper rejects a compiler outside the worktree; the existing dependencies are in a shared cache. No compiler guard was bypassed. CI production and test typechecks subsequently passed; the local placement limitation remains recorded.
- Fresh follow-up Auto Review (Codex, P0–P2) reviewed the complete local candidate, including the shared helper and unchanged regression, against `9f441adcf1e7307e1dfd0a496660106c4922dfe8` with the menu, machine, overlay lifecycle/control, and lazy-content owners supplied: scoped-clean, no findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable.
- No browser, Chromium, container, dependency installation, or broad local sweep was run on the Team Gateway host. The CI artifacts identify the matching root-menu state but do not retain activation history for the original five failures; exact-head PR CI must supply the browser result.


### Sizing acceptance for the follow-up

The normalized **chat boot JS gzip** measurement in PR CI's existing `pnpm ui:check-performance:base` head/base build comparison must have **head minus base <= 0 bytes**. Use that CI pair for the same workload and normalization; the preceding candidate was +30 bytes. This is an artifact-size comparison, not a latency sample. No local UI build or performance/packaging script is run on the Team Gateway host. No budget or baseline changes are permitted.

Current candidate: `7016bddcdba19b81ae033da6e96be93058e72a53`. [Its control-ui-performance check passes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44012963534/job/133804985780): normalized chat boot JS gzip **1,324,689 → 1,324,606 bytes (−83)**, **85 bytes below** the unchanged 1,324,691-byte ceiling. The CI pair uses base `a564030a2b6ea08a2198a16d6865f1d9928dd496` and merge checkout `64c6fd806b805ecb09818b5d99345a7ad2012bb1`, with Node v24.22.1 / Vite 8.3.5 / Pako 3.0.3. This meets the <=0-byte acceptance rule.

Fresh P0–P2 Auto Review of the complete candidate is scoped-clean; all 80 focused tests and touched-file type-aware lint/format pass. [Exact-head production types](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44012963534/job/133805937383) and [selected UI E2E smoke shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44012963534/job/133804985754) pass. Test types, CI lint and UI unit shards were still running at the result capture; no full-CI success claim is made. The original browser layout caller remains outside the observed smoke selection.

[The preceding fdda84cb performance check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44011903578/job/133801349082) measured **1,324,689 → 1,324,707 bytes (+18)**, against base `f52f728d34158e66c0d11ce48cc7fb1c7a0cd6a7`; the current shared renderer addresses that remaining growth. Production and test typechecks and the selected UI E2E shard passed on that prior head. Its performance failure was not rerun.

[The cf709361 performance check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44010220663/job/133795978659) measured **1,324,689 → 1,324,703 bytes (+14)**, 12 bytes above the 1,324,691-byte ceiling. This supersedes the earlier +30-byte candidate but still fails the acceptance criterion.

[The latest main run that actually ran performance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44010442679/job/133796400798), at `054fd9788bc0f86303e161ca3b2ab36a1ed8cd65`, measured **1,324,689 bytes**, 2 bytes below that ceiling. Newer main push runs skipped the performance job or had no such job. Thus cf709361 adds 14 bytes against the same measured main/base; its gzip failure is attributable to this diff. Exact byte figures come from only the scalar comparison lines in the job output; the check summary has no byte figures. No full logs or local builds were used.

### Prior-head PR CI results

[CI run 44007450967](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44007450967) covers head `80923235eae1b1762d024709fe000d738801f5e4` through merge checkout `3a2e5808f80a2a109c114995b63c545dffbaa704`.

- [UI shard 1/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44007450967/job/133786879688) passes, including both new readiness cases on Bun. UI shard 3/3, production/test typechecks, architecture guards and baseline ratchets also pass.
- [UI E2E shard 1/2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44007450967/job/133786879480) passes: 12 tests across five selected smoke files. This selection does **not** include `chat-panel-layout.e2e.test.ts`; the original browser caller remains unrerun. No Chromium/Playwright run was attempted on the Team Gateway host, and blocked remote credentials were not bypassed.
- [UI shard 2/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44007450967/job/133786879718) fails `chat-position-rail.test.tsx > conversation position rail > keeps the focused run marker through streaming and retargets its persisted answer` (`expected false to be true`). The fixture mounts only ChatThread/transcript and ChatPositionRail; it never renders or calls the panel-menu factories changed here. The new readiness test ran in shard 1/3, a separate process from this shard. This failure is unreachable from this diff and is left untouched; it is not the l74 wheel/layout assertion.
- [Control UI performance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44007450967/job/133786879735) fails. Its own head/base comparison reports chat boot JS gzip **1,324,689 → 1,324,719 bytes (+30)** against a 1,324,691-byte limit, so this change crosses that budget by 28 bytes. Both builds also violate the shared CSS ceiling (59,191 vs 58,315 bytes) and chat request count (21 vs 20). No budget, baseline, or exception was changed.

That prior-head CI run completed with failure. The PR remains ready and unmerged; the follow-up is measured by a new automatic PR run after its source commit.

prs.title: test(clawrouter): exercise stored speech auth through TTS
prs.body:
## Summary
- Exercise stored ClawRouter speech credentials through the existing TTS entry point, including its normal provider-readiness phase.
- Preserve the explicit 5,000 ms synthesis budget, selected-profile rejection assertions, credential-precedence checks, and the separate 250 ms HTTP deadline/socket-release regression.
- No production changes, timeout increases, policy bypasses, new helpers, or cache changes.

## Why
The stored-credential case called provider.synthesize directly with a changed configuration before TTS readiness. In an isolated reproduction, the optional synthetic-auth policy lookup loaded the provider runtime for that configuration and spent about 6.3 seconds before any network request, exhausting the 5-second synthesis deadline. Production TTS resolves isConfiguredAsync before synthesis. The test now protects the same stored-key contract through that owning boundary rather than implicitly testing cold module loading inside the request budget. This does not claim to fix or bound cold provider initialization latency.

prs.title: fix(reply): keep queued messages through a temporary access-policy outage
prs.body:
## Problem

A message queued while a turn is running is dropped when a Gateway access policy is briefly unavailable.

The authority contract says an unavailable policy evaluation is temporary: "An unavailable evaluation returns UNAVAILABLE with `details.code: OPERATOR_ACCESS_UNAVAILABLE`; before dispatch, it is retryable and does not authorize the failed operation" (`docs/plugins/sdk-runtime/gateway-and-nodes.md`). Two readers of queued-input custody did not follow it. Both treated any exception from `assertCurrent()` as a revocation:

- `isFollowupOperatorAuthorityCurrent` (`auto-reply/reply/queue/types.ts`), made the single rule by #200213: the queued input was consumed and the chat showed `withheld: Gateway access policy is unavailable; retry the operation.`
- `releaseSessionControllerClaim` (`sessions/session-controller.mailbox-claim.ts`): a second, older reader. On release it marked the claim's authority as not current, so the drain dropped the input even when the first reader kept it.

Affected installs: those with an access-policy plugin (`registerGatewayAccessPolicy`) whose evaluation can fail. No built-in policy reaches this path.

## Fix

- `infra/operator-authority-error.ts` gets `isOperatorAuthorityRetryableError`, next to the existing `isOperatorAuthorityUnavailable`: a policy outage (also nested) or a retryable `GatewayDispatchUnavailableError`.
- Both readers use it. A temporary outage keeps the input queued; admission still refuses the operation during the outage, so nothing runs without a current check. Any other failure is still a revocation.

Production code: +16 / −4.

Accepted edge: while an outage lasts, the input is retried on the drain's existing cadence (observed about 1.4 refused attempts per second, each refused before any model call, with one log line each). A policy that never recovers keeps the input owed until the policy is fixed or the chat is stopped. This replaces silently losing the message.

## User impact

- A message queued during a brief access-policy outage runs after the policy recovers instead of being dropped as `withheld`.
- A real revocation still never runs the queued turn.

Not changed: when a grant is revoked while the input is queued, it is cancelled without a visible `withheld` notice (same as before this PR).

## Evidence

- Regression tests, red on the merge base `941ae776`, green on this head:
  - `followup-runner.test.ts`: retains queued input after a temporary admission refusal (direct policy error, nested policy error, retryable dispatch error); ordinary revocation and non-retryable dispatch still withhold visibly. Base 3 failed; head 33 passed.
  - `session-controller.mailbox.test.ts`: the exact controller input survives a temporary run/adapter policy failure through real reservation, claim deferral, release and reclaim. Base 2 failed (consumed instead of waiting); head 29 passed.
- Real Gateway from source (`ocx src`, isolated state, real model), base vs head. A test access-policy plugin, loaded through `plugins.load.paths` and using only the documented plugin SDK, reads its grant from a file. A non-owner sends a second message while the agent runs a 20 s command; once the queue receipt shows the input queued, the grant file is renamed away for 30 s and back:

  | | Base `941ae776` | Head |
  |---|---|---|
  | Queued input during the outage | consumed as `withheld`; never answered | kept; the same queued run answers after the file returns |
  | Grant revoked while retrying | — | cancelled, zero model calls |

- Reader audit: the predicate's callers (`followup-runner.ts`, `queue/drain.ts`, `agent-runner-execute.ts`, `goal-continuation-return.ts`) and every other authority assertion on the queued-input path (`queue/delivery-context.ts`, `queue/lifecycle.ts`, `queue/enqueue.ts`, `queue/drain.ts`) were checked; only the two readers above treated a temporary failure as revocation.

prs.title: fix: keep handed-off services running after logging
prs.body:
Related: #199079

## What Problem This Solves

A service started by an agent can survive the completed command, then lose its connection as soon as it writes another log message. Release qualification reproduced this as ECONNRESET in the real service-handoff test.

## User Impact

Handed-off services keep working and logging after the originating command finishes. Timeout, cancellation, and ordinary output-failure handling remain intact. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The output pipeline retained ownership of the child stream even after it was unpiped. Closing the host output during handoff therefore destroyed the service writer. A bounded relay now separates pipeline teardown from the child stream: it flushes already accepted output to the host, then drains later service output until the writer closes. Ordinary destination failures still close the owned source.

The existing output owner serves both normal delivery and handoff; the old release-only helper is removed. Two redundant stream aliases were simplified without changing stdin behavior. No timeout, authority, or retention policy changes.

## Evidence

- Before: unchanged main owner fails the real 20-requests-after-handoff test with ECONNRESET (proxy disabled).
- After: all 48 focused Node tests pass, including 13 real process tests and output, preparation, and retirement siblings.
- Final shape: 2 new stream lifecycle regressions and all 13 real process tests pass on Node.
- Pinned Bun: 25 tests pass (2 stream regressions, 13 real process tests, 10 preparation tests), including the original handoff reproduction and cancellation cases.
- Canonical three-file type-aware lint, core typecheck, formatting, and diff checks pass.

The added cases protect handoff flushing/writer survival and normal destination-error teardown. Independent review was explicitly waived for this release repair; normal PR CI and required security checks remain required.

prs.title: docs: propose a linked package root and staged candidate handoff for updates
prs.body:
Related: #145252

## What Problem This Solves

Update reliability work has no written plan for its two structural causes: a package update moves the running release off its path, and the installed updater drives the whole run, so a fix in a new release cannot help the release that is failing.

## User Impact

User impact: none. This is a design proposal for maintainers to accept, change, or reject. It adds one page under `docs/reference/` and changes no behavior.

The page records seven decisions, which a maintainer accepted on November 13, 2026. Decision 2 was revised the same day, from extending the activation journal to not extending it. Three are ones this repository reserves for explicit approval: recording a pointer intent in the activation journal, the retention rule for release directories, and the package marker that #197922 adds. Accepting them sets the direction; each slice still needs its own review.

## Why This Change Was Made

#197922, now merged, implements the first slice of this plan, and its reviewers had no place to see where it leads. The page records:

- The recommendation: on OpenClaw-owned prefixes, the installed package directory keeps its path and becomes a link to a release directory. Activation and rollback are one rename each. A staged transfer of update work to the candidate sits beside it.
- Four approaches that were considered and rejected, with the source facts behind each: a launcher in the npm package, extending the immutable installation owner to user installations, rebinding the service to a new package root, and describing the candidate handoff as moving an existing one.
- Step timings from a published-updater Docker run, with the swap step broken down. The link can remove at most about 32 s of the 139 s that run took.
- A first-hop table, including what a published updater does when it meets a linked package root. That case has now run for `2026.10.9` and `2026.11.3`: the update passes and the link stays, but the updater rewrites the release directory behind the link in place. The page predicted the link would be replaced by a directory, and it now adds a release identity rule to the recommended route because of the result.
- A correction to the second slice, from two source traces at `649ca5f879f1e`. No handoff rule is needed for a linked package root, because the updater already rebinds its post-core child to the activated root. A later design pass recommends against extending the activation journal for the link switch, and decision 2 is revised to match: the link is the record, and the update run record gains one optional field naming the two releases. The page records that design, the order of an activation, what each crash point leaves, and what it does not cover.
- What was not traced or measured.

This is the fourth version of the page. The third recommended rebinding the service to a release path. That rested on a wrong premise, which the page states under rejected approaches.

It follows the form of the existing `team-immutable-update-design.md`. Like that page, it is not listed in `docs/docs.json`.

## Evidence

Docs-only change. Run against this page at `526f6d63cab40`:

- `scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs` on the page: passed.
- `oxfmt --check` on the page: clean.
- `markdownlint-cli2` with the repository config: 0 issues.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- Links: the page links to six pages and two anchors on other pages, unchanged from the previous version, and five anchors within itself. All resolve.

Not run: `pnpm docs:check-links`. The worktree is a sparse checkout without installed dependencies, so the audit could not start there.

The design comes from reading source, from two tests with toy packages on macOS (Node resolving a linked entry, and npm's handling of a linked global package), from the Docker runs recorded on #197922, and from one new Docker test.

**Published updaters on a linked package root.** In the published-driver update cell on linux/arm64, I moved the installed release into `releases/<version>/` and left a relative link at the package path, then ran a normal update to a build of `089d8b8`.

| Published updater | Result | Package path after | Directory behind the link after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026.11.3 | PASS, Gateway ready, version and sessions verified | Same link | Holds the new build |
| 2026.10.9 | PASS, Gateway ready, version and sessions verified | Same link | Holds the new build, under the old version's name |

The cell's installed-tree budget check refuses a linked root, so I pointed it at the link's target for these runs; the harness copy with that change and the layout recording was not committed. Not covered: rollback after a failed update on a linked root, a second update, a Gateway-initiated update, older updaters, and Windows.

The link switch itself has not run on an OpenClaw installation. The page's "Evidence limits" section lists the rest.

## What Problem This Solves

After an update that keeps the agent schema version unchanged, `openclaw database port --family agent --to sqlite` can refuse with “observed changed canonical rows or allocations.” This blocks returning to SQLite, including before a downgrade, and leaves an active recovery manifest until rollback.

Closes #200356.

## User Impact

Users can return agent databases to SQLite after an update while preserving the release metadata recorded in PostgreSQL. No schema or protocol bump is needed.

An existing failed manifest that already recorded a restamped working copy still requires `--rollback`, then a fresh port attempt.

## Why This Change Was Made

Choose option (a): skip the private SQLite migration for PostgreSQL exports. PostgreSQL source admission already requires the descriptor's schema version, so this migration is unnecessary and can change canonical `schema_meta.app_version` and `updated_at` before exact staging verification.

SQLite sources still migrate. Checkpointing, durable working-copy recovery, target admission, and exact row/allocation comparisons remain in place. This avoids changing global metadata semantics or excluding bookkeeping columns from verification.

The simplification pass retained one existing owner and one condition: production +4 net lines; tests +37 net lines, reusing existing fixtures.

## Evidence

- Base `b4fc05346afb4d6c88b4ab2e8ae3d1eba380917f`: preparation regression **1 passed, 1 failed**, with the reverse-port row changed from `original` to `canonical`; the PostgreSQL file's **7 cases skipped**.

The two working-copy cases took **193 ms**; cold worker preparation accounted for **30.84 s**. prs.title: fix: allow Git updates to build nested candidate checkouts
prs.body:
Closes #200357

## What Problem This Solves

Git-install updates launched by the shipped v2026.11.4 updater can abort at `preflight-build` with “Declaration input escapes checkout”. The updater builds inside the existing installation, where optional SDK type imports can reach the parent installation’s dependencies after #198661.

## User Impact

Candidates containing this fix can emit checkout-local declarations in the nested layout used by already-shipped updaters. Parent-install types remain excluded. No updater change or operator configuration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the fast compiler CLI path for contained inputs. If its input list escapes the checkout, discard its output and private staging files, then recompile through the existing bounded API filesystem. This also bounds fallback callers that omit an admission callback; historical declaration-only API callers retain their existing behavior.

The former “fails closed when optional SDK relative imports reach a parent install” test encoded the update regression. It now leaves the parent shadowing package installed and checks successful emission of only local inferred types, local inputs, and local source maps. Required parent-only dependencies still fail before publication; their diagnostics now identify missing modules/files because bounded resolution hides those paths. Escaping local symlinks still fail at the checkout boundary.

The fallback pays for a second, slower compilation only when the CLI encounters escaping inputs. Moving future preflight worktrees outside the installation is a separate follow-up and cannot repair already-shipped updaters.

## Evidence

- Verified current main’s emitter matches the assigned base (`b4fc05346afb4d6c88b4ab2e8ae3d1eba380917f`) and read #198661’s original safety contract.
- Red: the updated nested-layout real-compiler regression fails on the base with `Declaration input escapes checkout` at `native-declaration-emitter.mts:386` (1 failed, 17 filtered/skipped).
- Green: 32 passed, 5 platform/filesystem skips across the three named files below. The nested regression covers explicit and omitted admission callbacks. Required parent imports, escaping symlinks, inherited configs, publication preservation, and compiler shutdown remain covered.
- `native-declaration-boundary.test.ts`: 15 passed, 3 Windows skips; 4.410 s test time, 6.21 s command wall time.
- `tsdown-declaration-resolution.test.ts`: 14 passed, 2 platform/filesystem skips; 18.560 s file time. Together with the 3 passing subprocess tests, command wall time was 22.34 s. First CI snapshot: 13 pending, 6 skipped, no failures reported. CI seconds are not available yet.
- Touched-file type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Targeted typecheck of the three touched files and their imports also passes (temporary config with repository compiler settings, script `allowJs`, and explicit file roots).
- Independent review: shared Codex autoreview, complete local snapshot against `b4fc05346afb4d6c88b4ab2e8ae3d1eba380917f`, P0–P2 coverage, `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Full emitter, changed tests, and boundary/caller context supplied; reviewer did not independently execute tests. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because discovered checkouts were dirty; ClawSweeper posted its automatic PR receipt; hosted review is pending, with no duplicate manual request.
- `pr-simplify`: no new owner or helper; replaced the hard failure with reuse of the existing bounded emitter. Production delta +32/-13 lines; test delta +30/-13 lines. Remaining growth selects the fallback and preserves boundary/diagnostic proof.

prs.title: fix(update): a failed shell completion or service definition refresh is never retried after an update
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an update succeeds but cannot refresh shell completion or the Gateway service definition, OpenClaw prints a warning at most and then forgets about it. Nothing records that the step is still outstanding, nothing retries it, and with `--json` a failed shell completion refresh is not reported at all.

This is the first slice of "owed steps": an update should finish and repair afterwards, instead of failing or forgetting a follow-up step the new version can run without.

## User Impact

User impact: after an update that could not refresh shell completion or the service definition, `openclaw update` still exits 0, names the step as owed with its reason, and `openclaw update status` keeps showing it until a later `openclaw update` or `openclaw update repair` settles it.

- `openclaw update --json` now carries the warning as an advisory step. `openclaw update status --json` and `openclaw update repair --json` list `owedSteps`.
- An already-current `openclaw update` now refreshes shell completion when an earlier update owes it. It does not prompt. While that refresh keeps failing it can add up to the completion cache timeout (30 s) to the command.
- Required database migrations, refused or invalid configuration, Doctor refusals and Gateway readiness still block. A failed or rolled-back update owes nothing.

No SQL schema, config, Gateway protocol, wire-schema or step-status change.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Contract.** The update run ledger owns owed steps. An owed step is a `finalize:owed:<id>` row in the run's existing `steps` JSON: status `skipped` while owed, `completed` once it is settled, reason in `detail` (bounded to 500 characters and kept through compaction). The ids are a closed set, `shell-completion` and `service-definition`, defined with their label and retry hint in `src/infra/update-run-owed-step.ts`. The ledger exposes `recordUpdateRunOwedStep`, `settleUpdateRunOwedStep` and `readOwedUpdateSteps`, so no caller writes a step name. A row can be recorded and settled on a finished run that kept its result; the generic step writer still treats finished runs as immutable. The newest of the last 50 runs that mentions a step decides whether it is owed. Failed and rolled-back runs neither owe nor decide. A run that still owes a step an earlier run recorded writes its own row and leaves the earlier row unchanged, so the earlier run owes the step again if the later run fails. The next slice (plugin convergence, post-plugin Doctor) adds an id and registers its retry; the contract does not change.

**Consumers.** A failed shell completion refresh after a core update (cache write or profile install), and the two service definition paths where the update continues on the previous definition (installer failure, or the definition still outside the updated installation).

**Retry.**

| Step | Next `openclaw update` | `openclaw update repair` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shell completion | Refreshes again, also when the core is already current. Settles when the cache refresh did not fail and the shell profile is not on the slow pattern. | Settles on the same rule after its completion cache phase. |
| Service definition | Settles only when this update's own service refresh succeeded. Otherwise the step stays owed and the warning repeats. | Does not run the installer. After Doctor maintenance, settles on the updater's existing service verdict: the definition is owned and targets the active installation, or the service is proven absent. |

A retry that fails or cannot run keeps the step owed, warns again and never fails the command. Gateway start does not retry owed steps.

**Which process runs this.** The installed updater runs first and cannot be patched. This table is read from source; no published-updater run was made.

| Behaviour | First update to a release with this change | Following update |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Record an owed step and retry earlier ones during `openclaw update` | Installed updater, old code: nothing is recorded, as today. Exception: when the update migrated state so that only candidate code may finish it, the candidate process finishes the update and records. | Installed updater, this code. |
| Hidden post-core `update finalize` child | Candidate, this code: leaves completion and owed steps to its parent. | Same. |
| `openclaw update status` and `openclaw update repair` after the update | New CLI, this code. | Same. |

**Published readers.** Read from source at `v2026.11.4`, not proven by running a published build:

- Its report and `updateRunWarningMessages` ignore a `skipped` `finalize:owed:*` row, so an older reader shows nothing for it.
- Its codec keeps the row because of the `finalize:` prefix. If it rewrites a run that is over the byte budget it can drop the row's `detail`; this version then shows "no reason recorded".
- Its Control UI step list shows the row under its raw name with status `skipped` and its reason.
- The wire schema accepts the row: it uses only existing fields and statuses.

**Tradeoffs and limits.**

- For an installer failure where the definition already targeted the installation, repair's check cannot prove the definition's content was rewritten. It relies on Doctor maintenance having run first. I read that call in `src/commands/doctor-maintenance-restoration.ts` but did not prove it runs in every repair.
- After a manual `openclaw gateway install --force`, an already-current `openclaw update` keeps the service definition step owed until a core update refreshes the service or `openclaw update repair` rechecks it.
- A repair that finds a healthy Gateway and skips finalization leaves owed steps unchanged.
- `update-command-post-update.ts` was 710 lines on `main`, over the 700-line lint cap (advisory in CI, an error locally). Calling the retry on the already-current paths needed the service-skip block moved into the maintenance module, which also brings the file back under the cap.

## Evidence

**Before (base).** Through the real `openclaw update` entry point with a private state database: an update whose shell profile install fails exits without error, and `openclaw update status` then shows no trace of the failure. Writing a settled owed row to a finished run through the existing step writer is silently dropped.

**After (this branch).**

- The same update records the step; the update's own report and `openclaw update status` both print `Shell completion refresh is owed: EACCES: permission denied. Retried by the next openclaw update; run openclaw update repair to retry it now.`
- `openclaw update --json` with a failing completion cache exits 0 with an advisory step, and `openclaw update status --json` lists the step in `owedSteps`. With a working cache the same update settles a step an earlier run owed.
- A core update whose service installer fails records the service definition step; one whose installer succeeds settles an earlier one.
- An already-current update settles an owed shell completion refresh, keeps it when the refresh fails again, keeps the service definition step it did not refresh, and exits 0 in both cases, with and without a running managed Gateway.
- `openclaw update repair` settles both steps when the completion cache refreshes and the service targets the active installation. It keeps both, lists them as `owedSteps` in its JSON and warns on stderr, when the cache fails and the service targets another installation. Owed steps do not change the finalization `status`.
- A step taken over by a later update that then fails is still owed by the earlier update. Before the second commit the later update settled the earlier row on takeover, and the step was dropped without a record when that update failed.
- Negative control: an update whose Gateway stays unhealthy still fails with exit 1, settles nothing, and `openclaw update status` still shows the earlier owed step.
- Ledger: record, list and settle on running, succeeded and skipped runs; nothing owed on a failed run, including a row recorded before it failed; other finished history stays immutable; the newest run decides; a step id from a newer release is still listed; the row and its reason survive step-count and byte compaction.

<details>
<summary>Commands, counts and commits</summary>

Head `c2ead8e6692`: the first commit `6b917db72ac` (base `1139903ee16`), a second commit `2f6b5b1cfbd`, two commits that fix the CI failures described below, and `main` merged in (last at `24c8d1636de`). The paragraphs below describe the first commit unless they say otherwise. The test runs below were made on the same change at base `827a749e2c6`. `827a749e2c6..1139903ee16` touches release scripts, CI, unrelated docs and `src/commands/triage-update.ts`, none of which the update run ledger, the update finishing path or these tests read, so the runs were not repeated after the last two rebases. The ledger test file, format, lint and both ratchets were rerun at `fd8d012d70c`.

Red on base (production files restored to `9a6a00e3e2b`, tests from this branch): 15 of 15 new or changed cases fail. One fails on behaviour (`owes a shell completion refresh whose profile install fails`, on the status assertion); the other 14 fail because the contract does not exist on base. The dropped write to a finished run was shown with a throwaway test that is not committed. With only the codec change reverted, the compaction case fails because the reason is lost.

Green:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update-run-owed-step.test.ts src/cli/update-cli.test.ts src/cli/update-cli.already-current.test.ts src/cli/update-cli.finalizer.test.ts`: 4 files, 75 tests passed. `src/cli/update-cli.already-current.test.ts` rerun after its last assertion was added: 21 passed.
- Affected suites (ledger, compaction, report, record, `update status`, post-update, post-update repair, lifecycle, service, terminal outcome and authority, sentinel env, command runner, the already-current path, repair command): 20 files, 507 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:all`: exit 0.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the 16 changed source files: clean.
- `oxfmt --check` on the 18 changed files and `git diff --check`: clean.
- Test-lines ratchet: net +358 of 400. Mock-export ratchet: OK.
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: exit 0.
- `pnpm deadcode:exports` fails on `main`-owned entries: 126 unused exports, none in a file this change touches.
- Docs: `pnpm format:docs:check`, `pnpm docs:check-mdx`, `pnpm docs:check-links` (0 broken) and `pnpm lint:docs` on both pages pass. `pnpm docs:check-links:anchors` reports 3 broken fragments, none in the pages changed here.

Second commit (`2f6b5b1cfbd`):

- CI on the first commit failed `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`: the session identity ratchet, which reached `main` after this branch was cut, counts every `runId` comparison under `src`. The retry pass and `openclaw update status` compared update run ids in three places. They now group owed steps by the run that holds them and match the displayed run's steps by step id. `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-session-identity-ratchet.mts --base origin/main --no-merge-base`: OK.
- New `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-owed.test.ts`: red against the first commit's `update-command-owed.ts` (`expected [] to deeply equal [ { id: 'service-definition', … } ]`), green on the head.
- `src/cli/update-cli.already-current.test.ts`: the assertion that the earlier run's report stops saying owed after a takeover no longer matches the contract. It now checks that a settled step leaves the earlier report and a step still owed stays on it. 21 passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli/update-command-owed.test.ts src/infra/update-run-owed-step.test.ts src/cli/update-cli.test.ts src/cli/update-cli.finalizer.test.ts`: all pass on the second commit's sources; with the already-current file, 5 files and 110 tests.

These ran before the last merge of `main`, which touches no update, ledger or ratchet file; only the session identity ratchet was rerun after it.

CI fixes after run 43996671701 on `dc74b5e5bae` (five red test files; each reproduced locally first):

1. `src/cli/update-finalization-output.process.test.ts`, `completion-hang`: expected `status: "ok"`, got `"warning"`. Cause: this change made owed steps set the finalization `status` to `warning`. That status is the Doctor and plugin maintenance outcome: the test pins `ok` for a completion failure, and a parent updater reads the child's status as the plugin result. Fix: owed steps are reported in `owedSteps` and on stderr and no longer change `status`. The case now also asserts `owedSteps` lists `shell-completion`. Red before, green after (1 passed).

Locally the file fails the same 17 of 27 cases with this branch's production files restored to `main`. Cause on `main`: #200216 (`775be7a709f`) makes the broker child create `dirname(endpoint)`; when a test mocks `process.platform` to `win32`, the parent passes a `\\.\pipe\…` endpoint to a POSIX child, whose `dirname` is `.`. The file passed 27 of 27 in the CI of #200181 (job 133541759038), which ran just before #200216 merged. `main`'s own push CI skips the Node test shards, so it does not show this.

Cause: three earlier cases in the file fail completion on purpose and shared the worker's ledger with later cases. With the second commit a step stays owed until something settles it, so the later cases took it over. It did not show on the first commit, where a run that took a step over settled the earlier row; I did not trace which case ended that chain. Every update test file under `src/cli` and `src/infra` whose name starts with `update`, plus the two script tests: 441 files listed, 439 run on `03796b070e9` (the two not run are a `.live.` and an `.e2e.` file the runner excludes). 5,986 tests passed. 38 failed in 9 files, none caused by this change:

- `update-cli.windows-lifecycle.test.ts` (17): item 3 above.
- `update-command-database-rollback.test.ts` (3) and `update-doctor-migration-attribution.test.ts` (2): 120 s timeouts while the machine was at load 38; both files pass alone (64 tests).
- `update-startup.campaign-apply-error.test.ts` (8), `update-startup-cached.test.ts` (1), `update-candidate-state.result.test.ts` (2), `update-command-rollback.test.ts` (1), `update-command-handoff.test.ts` (3), `update-command-node-engine-preflight.test.ts` (1): each fails the same cases with this branch's production files restored to `main`. Test audit: every touched test file was read in full, including `update-finalization-output.process.test.ts`, `update-command-post-update.test.ts` and the `update-restart-module-outcome.mjs` harness in this round; nothing in them was dead or redundant, and nothing was removed. `keeps update completion refresh best-effort when profile install fails` was replaced by `owes a shell completion refresh whose profile install fails`, which keeps its two assertions and adds the report and status checks. `uses the installed Git CLI when service env refresh cannot complete` became a two-case test that also runs the success path, which had a fixture but no test. **Not proven.**

- No published-updater × candidate update was run; the process table is from source.
- `src/cli/update-cli.windows-lifecycle.test.ts` is red on `main` since #200216 and stays red here; see the CI notes above.

prs.title: fix(ci): dependency checks fail on private helper exports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: scheduled main CI fails its dependency gate when module-private Slack and Control UI helpers are exposed as unused exports.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior or rendering change. This restores the hard-zero dependency check while preserving test cases, assertions, timing, worker limits, and performance budgets.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three helpers become module-private. A fourth, single-use tool-call predicate is inlined unchanged at its existing consumer. The chat-activity projection moves byte-for-byte to the existing history-snapshot owner, with both production request paths and all fixture callers migrated together. The Slack test independently checks the same documented eight-minute boundary.

No exceptions, fake consumers, wrappers, configuration changes, new production modules, or budget increases are added. The final change is 12 files, +43/−56 lines.

## Evidence

- The exact [scheduled-main failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44003207635/job/133772863599), attempt 1 at `53278c30303fd9609599a123160469724370cf26`, reported five production and three full-tree unused exports. The original `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-deadcode-exports.mts --all` entry point reproduced those findings before edits and passed all three reports on the final source. Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, Knip 6.40.0; frozen private dependencies.
- Final affected proof: 32 UI files / 503 tests passed, plus UI typecheck, targeted lint, formatting and whitespace checks. The unchanged Slack and browser-approval inputs retain their prior 5-file / 55-test proof, covering 37 files / 558 cases overall. Every test case, assertion and elapsed timing is preserved; the activity move and inlined predicate expression were independently checked for exact preservation.
- The first published head failed the [hosted performance comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44012573076/job/133803528126). On its exact merge source `075a92e7c3bfdaab732d154413b479b3c91fa746`, parent reproduced 1,324,709 B chat-boot gzip against base `a564030a2b6ea08a2198a16d6865f1d9928dd496` at 1,324,689 B and the fixed 1,324,691 B ceiling. The final same-input official comparison passed at **1,324,615 B**, 94 B below the failing head and 76 B below the unchanged ceiling. Node 24.22.1, Vite 8.3.5, Pako 3.0.3; normalized built-asset accounting. Inherited CSS/request violations remain separate and unchanged; no baseline or ceiling was edited. This is artifact-size qualification, not a latency claim.
- Fresh independent final autoreview (Codex, P0–P2): one complete 292,051-byte pass, scoped-clean with no actionable findings. Reviewed original base `53278c30303fd9609599a123160469724370cf26`; final reviewed tree `ffccbd16c60b8aef471592e1920529a4a8c8654a` equals local commit `336a6d1ea39ff05297aa4307a1201975bce477a6` and published head `23c982a3ae8e83b017ba45ab35f786344095189e`. Author pr-simplify pass completed. Rejected projection experiments are not included.

Scope limits: this does not establish full-main health or live Slack/Gateway/browser behavior. Passing fixture tests emitted Solid warnings; they were not repaired or baseline-attributed. Hosted checks must cover the updated head before landing.

Thanks @vincentkoc for directing this repair.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/939b9e73-b5e6-469e-a7f3-062b54fda817)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/6cf927dc-929c-4537-beb0-8ba6af4a19e0)

The original discussion session also contains the follow-up CI reproduction, byte repair, and verification.

- @vincentkoc

prs.title: fix: chat plugin installs reject Git and third-party npm sources
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: asking an agent in Telegram or another chat to install a Git or third-party npm plugin is rejected before approval and sends the owner to a terminal.

## User Impact

Owners can review the source and declared capabilities, approve the installation, and receive its runtime result in the requesting chat without enabling /plugins. Non-ClawHub sources still require explicit acknowledgement; capability acceptance does not grant conversation access or bypass installation policy. No configuration migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing exact-proposal approval owner and managed plugin installer instead of the curated-only setup rejection. Required capability consent becomes a separately approved continuation bound to the source, plugin identity, and reviewed declarations. Keep the source card applying until that continuation settles and keep internal model instructions out of the capability card.

Source approval trusts the selected publisher/ref, not immutable package bytes; changed declarations require fresh review. Authenticated source URLs are redacted in review/history and useful audit metadata while the installer retains its operational spec.

## Evidence

- 225 focused cases across parser, executor, tool, direct/delegated approval, and prefix-stability coverage. The Git/npm entry-point regression fails on the base. The final audit-source-identity regression fails before its metadata adjustment and passes afterward.
- Targeted core/test typechecks, lint, formatting, and diff checks passed; QA runtime builds passed.
- Real Telegram Test Server DM with a deterministic provider: natural-language delegation, distinct source/capability approvals, canonical Git install, persisted capability acceptance, live runtime application, and an actual installed-tool result delivered to Telegram, with /plugins disabled. All 15 recorded behavior checks passed, including the corrected approval messages. This is channel/installer integration evidence, not real-model planning qualification.
- Production proof hashes are retained; the subsequent audit-metadata-only adjustment is separately covered by the owning regression. Local autoreview through P2 and independent review were completed; findings were investigated and addressed, including the audit metadata's source readability. No remaining actionable code-review findings.
- CI follow-up corrected three PR-caused issues: a missing test conditional brace, a property access on the audit reader's unknown result, and exactly one retired CLI-mock baseline entry. The matching services typecheck, CI core lint configuration, both focused files (53 cases), formatting, and the mock-export guard without pruning pass locally. No production behavior changed in this follow-up.
- The remaining [current-head Windows-emulation lifecycle job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44013637481/job/133807199548) has 17 SQLite snapshot worker startup failures with `ERR_SPAWN_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE` / `EEXIST: mkdir '.'`. An independent full-tree canonical-main checkout at `f27bc2417fea7448c9165e6329a457f05b66685b`, with its own frozen dependencies, reproduced all 17 failures. The fixture, spawn-broker and worker-runtime input objects are identical across that main commit, the actual CI baseline `df78722789e096c3dfc7154526d67037d6ed4803`, and the tested merge `77c0b41c5c233c70a1990a84858ce69505bda3b2`. This establishes baseline attribution beyond the automated report's earlier unknown classification. CI remains failed; this PR does not claim to repair the unrelated fixture. Landing uses only the repository's protected inherited-failure route with live writer, review and security gates intact.

Reported by @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/fd92f4e5-99e8-4883-892f-ade364288c2c)
- [Telegram integration verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/fecafc8a-e3e2-452b-9cae-55527666df2e)

## Worked on by

- @vincentkoc

prs.title: fix(process): Windows process helpers fail to load without the VC++ redistributable
prs.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
Use a parenthesized scope only when it adds clarity:
fix(auth): login redirect loops when session cookie is expired

Types: feat, fix, improve, refactor, docs, chore.
For fixes, describe the user-visible symptom and trigger:

Avoid implementation details such as:

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.
-->

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

Fixes: on Windows machines without the Visual C++ redistributable, OpenClaw's native process helpers fail to load. `openclaw doctor` reports `proc-safe: load-failed` (`ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED`), and process identity, process census, Job-object supervision and AppContainer token checks are unavailable.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

User impact: on a clean Windows x64 or ARM64 install, the process helpers load with no separate VC++ runtime install. Doctor reports `proc-safe: loaded`, and the creation-time PID-reuse guard, process census, Job-object kill-on-close supervision and token queries work. No config, API or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

`@openclaw/proc-safe` 0.4.2's Windows natives import `VCRUNTIME140.dll`, which a clean Windows install doesn't have. 0.6.0 includes openclaw/proc-safe#40: the Windows x64 and ARM64 natives link the VC runtime statically and keep the OS-serviced UCRT. This PR adopts 0.6.0.

0.4.2 → 0.6.0 is additive for OpenClaw: no breaking entries in the changelog, and the typed API only gains an opt-in Job-child stdin pipe and a Linux `filesystem-launch` subpath. No OpenClaw call site changes. `pnpm-workspace.yaml` gets a reviewed exact-version release-age exception that expires seven days after publish, matching earlier fs-safe bumps.

The same release also changes two other platforms:
- **Linux:** glibc 2.28–2.33 hosts now load the native instead of using the existing `/proc` fallback.
- **macOS:** identity reads for protected processes such as `login` now come from validated kernel records. The native ancestry walk can therefore continue past Terminal's `login`, so the `ps` fallback from #193164 isn't reached in that case. Ancestry results stay the same or become more complete. The fallback is kept because it still covers the case where both native interfaces deny access.

fs-safe has the same VC++ dependency. Its hybrid-CRT fix isn't released yet and will follow separately.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. For visual web/macOS/iOS/Android changes, follow

Reviewers will inspect the code, tests, and CI. Use this section to make the
validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

Head `65dabc2f958bcf38183d8310e6fb2c902e030d96` on base `d29fad4e3e687dedf683e38ec35b12cb85510637`.

**Clean Windows x64 guest, before and after.**
- **Guest:** Hyper-V Win11 build 29683 with no VC++ runtime. Before and after the runs there was no `VC\Runtimes\x64` key, and every `vcruntime140*`/`msvcp140*`/`concrt140`/`vccorlib140`/`vcomp140` DLL failed LoadLibrary with 126. Only Node 24.22.1 was added.
- **Build:** one OpenClaw tarball built from this head with `node scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs --allow-unreleased-changelog` (SHA-256 `B15256DA…2C239838`, matched on the guest).
- **Installs:** npm-installed twice. `before` adds an npm override back to `@openclaw/proc-safe` 0.4.2, which loads its nested `proc-safe-win32-x64-msvc@0.4.2`. `after` is this head's own dependency, 0.6.0. proc-safe is the only variable.

| Probe, from the installed `openclaw` dependency tree | before (0.4.2) | after (0.6.0) |
|---|---|---|
| `getProcSafeNativeStatus({ probe: true })` | `reason=load-failed`, `loadErrorCode=ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED` | `reason=loaded`, `win32-x64-msvc@0.6.0` |
| `openclaw doctor --lint --only core/doctor/native-status --severity-min info --json` | `warning: proc-safe: load-failed` | `info: proc-safe: loaded` |
| `readProcessIdentity(self)` / a child's identity and parent | `helper-unavailable` | ok / ok, parent = probe |
| `listProcesses({ pids: [self], includeCommand: true })` | `helper-unavailable` | ok: identity and `node.exe` |
| `readCurrentAppContainerSid()` | `helper-unavailable` | `null` (not contained) |
| `WindowsJob.create({ killOnJobClose: true })`, spawn, then close | `helper-unavailable` | child admitted (`processIds` = [child]) and gone after close |

Both Doctor runs also report `fs-safe: load-failed`, which is out of scope here and is why Doctor exits 1 in both. The probes ran over SSH as a local administrator at High integrity in session 0, and none of these operations depend on the session or integrity level.

**ARM64 (static only, no ARM64 guest).** PE imports of the exact registry natives:
- `proc-safe-win32-{x64,arm64}-msvc@0.4.2` import `vcruntime140.dll`.
- `@0.6.0` import no VC runtime DLL (no delay imports either) and still use the UCRT `api-ms-win-crt-*` set.

**Local checks on Windows (x64, Node 26.13.0).**
- The canonical package build passed, including `check-cli-bootstrap-imports`.
- `node scripts/check-openclaw-package-tarball.mjs --require-bundled-workspace-deps <tgz>`: "OpenClaw package tarball integrity passed." The packer's 300 s wrapper timed out on this host; the direct run took 635 s.
- `pnpm test` over all 47 non-e2e test files that import proc-safe. These pass: daemon (3 files), process and supervisor (9, 1 skipped), `shared/pid-alive`, cli and update-handoff, and infra. The infra files include doctor native-status, process census (including `.windows`), restart-stale-pids ancestry, managed-service handoff identity/native/process, Windows process start, AppContainer spawn, process-respawn and update continuation.

prs.title: fix(gateway): leave a replaced installation to the update run that holds it
prs.body:
## Problem

During `openclaw update --no-restart` with the Gateway running, the Gateway's installation check (`src/gateway/server-maintenance.ts`, every 30 s) sees the new `build-info.json` and restarts the Gateway into the new package while the update still owns the installation. The update's own Gateway start then waits on state ownership held by the self-restarted process, stalls for 120 s, and the update fails with `activated-gateway-startup-failed` and rolls back (exit 1). This happens on plain package installs and on the release-directory layout from #198835. The natural rate is about the race window divided by 30 s. #198835 measured that window at 1.75–1.88 s, which gives about 6% per run; I did not re-measure the window.

## Change

The update run is the one owner of the installation while it holds the install lease (the same `managed-update-handoffs` row the updater's executor takes). `checkGatewayInstallationReplacement` (`src/gateway/stale-install.ts`) now skips the self-restart while a live process holds that lease. A Gateway the run leaves stale restarts on a later check, after the lease is released.

- The lease key is captured with the installation root when the observer registers.
- Lease reads and process-identity probes are synchronous, so they run in the existing handoff worker (`prepareManagedHandoffParentStore`), never on the serving thread. They run only when a changed build is observed.
- An unreadable lease keeps today's behavior (self-restart).
- No new gate in the updater, no schema or config change.

## Impact

`--no-restart` updates with a running Gateway no longer race the update's Doctor and Gateway start. Behavior outside an update run is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Unit:** `src/gateway/stale-install.test.ts` › "leaves a replaced installation to the update run that holds it". It holds a real lease, checks that a changed build does not restart the Gateway, releases the lease, then checks that the next tick does restart it. Red on `2435c1faa791` (handoff called once while the lease is held), green on this head; the other 14 tests in the file pass.

**E2E (mbp-m5, real `openclaw update --no-restart` against a launchd Gateway, isolated `--profile`):** the reproduction makes the installation check fire every 250 ms in the *running* build. Only `server-maintenance` changes in a packed copy; the build ID differs, the code is otherwise identical. Each arm: install, start the Gateway service, then `update --no-restart --tag <next build>` with the Gateway running.

| Arm | Layout | Result | Update wall time |
|---|---|---|---|
| main `2435c1fa` | release dirs (`install-cli.sh` prefix, adopted) | **fail**: self-restart at T+0.25 s, `activated-gateway-startup-failed`, rolled back | 351 s |
| main `2435c1fa` | plain user npm prefix | **fail**: same | 455 s |
| this PR `d6f23896` | release dirs | **ok**, no self-restart signal, Gateway healthy on the new build | 133 s |
| this PR `d6f23896` | plain user npm prefix | **ok**, no self-restart signal, Gateway healthy on the new build | 188 s |

Gates: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm check:test-types`, oxlint and oxfmt on changed files all pass.

Local ClawSweeper review (gpt-6.1-sol, normal speed) at `d6f23896`: patch is correct, 0 findings. The previous head's single finding (synchronous lease reads on the Gateway thread) is fixed by the worker move.

Not covered: the missing-runtime-chunk path in `classifyGatewayStaleInstall` still restarts on a request failure during an in-place swap. That path triggers on a real load failure and was left as is.

prs.title: feat(auth): enable guests to access sessions through selected mentions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Team guests need their own sessions, explicitly invited sessions and sanitized public links without discovering unrelated conversations.

## User Impact

Enables opt-in `gateway.roles.definitions.<role>.sessions.others: "invited"` after the preceding read guards. A creator/admin selecting a person in a committed original message grants session membership. Plain text, replay and later Inbox delivery cannot grant access.

Visitor Access accepts the documented role for invitations and renewals. Ordinary invited readers need session access for attachments; real administrators retain standalone media access.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepare invitation authority at the authenticated human-input owner, retain approved offsets through recovery, and commit membership with the original transcript write. Retained readers observe the committed membership. Inbox notification failure has a visible outcome and does not undo a committed message or cancel agent dispatch.

Stack step **17/17**, based on [invitation UI wording](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184514). Review and merge in [stack order](#stack-order). This PR owns full-stack integration coverage; preceding PRs retain their narrow production boundaries.

Contributor credit: @vincentkoc (PR author), with @jalehman (stack owner).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/0c2aaa61-d7c9-4c74-b24e-d1c501b07a43)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/701a3a5e-b345-4ca7-b5e0-e6e31ad7ac72)

## Evidence

### Current CI repair — November 17

**Landed November 17:** exact reviewed head `488654e4ec99930cfefeffe73d014329a7049181` merged as [62a982bb24b5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/62a982bb24b505b1dce270b5069d56c546fd71f6). [Final CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44014894287) and required `openclaw/ci-gate` succeeded; the [exact-head hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184515#issuecomment-6414255818) is Ready with no findings or before-merge items. Native replacement recovery used existing completed hosted CI, with no new CI dispatch, compute lease, writer switch or gate bypass. The landed commit retains exactly one credit trailer each for @vincentkoc and @jalehman.

Replacement candidate `488654e4ec99930cfefeffe73d014329a7049181` repairs the PR-caused [session-identity ratchet failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44011554160/job/133800370619). The previous pinned auto request was explicitly retired through its native owner before this head was published; it was not overwritten or re-armed blindly.

The permission hook now revalidates the current sender and approved recipient authority, leaving transcript/view preconditions with the existing session-store writer. A redundant caller-side transcript comparison is removed. Invited media policy consumes the prepared sharing owner's authoritative entry and membership instead of comparing two caller-side incarnation IDs. The identity allowlist is unchanged; the exact session-identity check now passes.

A new regression **failed before and passed after** this repair: refreshing descriptive caller metadata must not become an authorization refusal, while changing recipient eligibility still refuses the invitation and the original writer precondition remains intact. The affected repair run passed 87 cases with one stale error-text expectation; that expectation was corrected, and the failed case, new regression and all four actor/non-actor authority cases then passed (6 targeted cases). The media/resource cases were already green and unchanged by that expectation correction. No unresolved product assertion failure is hidden by a passing replay. The actual native composer flow passed **3/3** again on the repaired source. Core/methods types, scoped typed lint, committed diff, test-line and session-identity checks passed; fresh independent review of the repair is scoped-clean.

Net test growth is **+3,505**, standard allowance **400**, exact credit **3,105**, including this required regression; the reason is also in the squash body. No identity-ratchet allowance, protocol/schema version, default or permission gate was raised. The prior native AWS proof stays pinned to its original head/base below; no new lease or workload replay was used. Fresh replacement-head CI and the requested hosted review are tracked separately from the prior failed run.

### Pre-repair integration qualification — 3e08c1f2

Candidate `3e08c1f23dd553c2a109824cfb334138b354353f` is based on `054fd9788bc0f86303e161ca3b2ab36a1ed8cd65`. The new conflict was resolved by retaining main's `administratorMemberPolicy` alongside membership-aware `canRead`/`canInvite`, and preserving main's origin-owned continuation recovery. Main intentionally retired the large hello update-scope suite in #198943; this PR does not resurrect it. Canonical `frames.auth.test.ts` retains and passes the transport-schema cases, including `invited`.

On this candidate, **117 affected cases across 13 files passed**, covering the seven guest consumers, selected-mention commit/replay/failure paths, current member-administrator policy, recovery authority, actor/non-actor transcript custody, native role config and canonical hello auth schemas. The actual native composer flow passed **3/3** again for `none`, `view` and explicit `invited`, with committed access, outsider exclusion, HTTP JSON/SSE, stop/start persistence and next-request revocation. Core/methods types, scoped lint/format, validators, canonical config-doc checks, committed diff checks and the exact test-line ratchet passed. Fresh independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean.

Net test growth is now **+3,484**, with standard allowance **400** and exact allocation **3,084**; the three-line reduction follows the upstream test consolidation. All remaining current-main tests are retained. The task-only browser driver is retained as evidence outside the checkout and is not shipped. The AWS execution below remains pinned to its actual tested head/base; it is not relabeled as a November 17 execution. Current mention/recovery/schema integration was requalified with the affected real-Gateway and native UI checks above. Final-head CI and one hosted re-review remain required before landing.

### November 16 integration qualification — 10d24137

Prior candidate `10d24137b2562eb108b01f230851da3d69005da4` is based on `a139d420834e6e04641303c79eb7c6e0e4444fa5`. While AWS qualification ran, main advanced and conflicted only in generated config hashes. The canonical generator resolved that conflict. Range-diff shows no invitation-production delta; every production file changed by this PR is byte-identical to AWS-qualified `e6193da7`. Dependency and agent DB schema-version inputs did not change. After integration, **41 focused cases across 10 files** passed, including all 30 guest/resource/mention cases and main's new transcript-memory/skills consumers.
