The retained task-only browser driver was removed from the checkout and is not shipped in the PR. The earlier 444-case qualification is recorded separately below. Exact final-head CI and hosted re-review remain required before merge.

### Pre-conflict qualification — e6193da7

Tested revision `e6193da716b1107e7b4375698fa76a13731d553a` was replayed onto `60c112a1bfa94ea4a5d43e4302e18375429d879f`, after merged #184514. Range-diff preserves the original activation slice. The enum now lives in main's extracted `src/config/zod-schema.gateway-roles.ts`; main's OpenClaw ID connection ceilings, mention ranking/display identity and recovery-unavailability handling remain intact. Generated config metadata was regenerated, not hand-edited.

- **444 scoped cases across 29 files passed**, including original-message commit/replay, queued recovery, invitation-aware RPC/HTTP/event/resource consumers and Visitor Access. **3/3 real native Control UI scenarios passed locally** for `none`, `view` and `invited`, through actual picker selection and Send, committed access, outsider exclusion, HTTP JSON/SSE, Gateway stop/start and next-request revocation. No enum/auth overlay is used.
- Core and Gateway methods/server/root test type graphs, scoped typed lint/formatting, all five validator checks and the exact test-line ratchet passed. Independent P0–P2 source review completed scoped-clean for this head.
- Idle and queued Inbox failures emit targeted `mentions.failed` without undoing committed input/membership or failing dispatch. Native queued replay forwards only the profile reauthenticated by the existing Gateway recovery owner; its two invitation regressions failed without that handoff and pass with it.
- **Config/schema delta:** add only the literal `invited` to `gateway.roles.definitions.<role>.sessions.others`; extend Visitor Access eligibility to explicitly configured invited roles; regenerate config documentation hashes. No new key, shipped default change, DB schema/version change, protocol-version bump, Doctor transform or config migration. The already registered `mentions.failed` event is now emitted to the original sender’s connections on post-commit notification failure, carrying `gatewayInstanceId`, `sessionKey`, `agentId`, `messageId` and a fixed `errorMessage`; no new RPC or event schema is introduced. Existing absent/none/view behavior remains unchanged.
- Net test growth **+3,487**, standard allowance **400**, exact justified allocation **3,087** in `config/test-lines-allocations/184515-guest-invitation-access.txt`. All current-main tests are retained. Two obsolete pre-activation expected-error comments were removed without removing assertions.
- Exact-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43884453965) and [required CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43886570075) succeeded. Hosted exact-head re-review is the remaining source-review follow-through; no merge is claimed here.

### AWS native acceptance — November 16

Head `e6193da716b1107e7b4375698fa76a13731d553a` and base `60c112a1bfa94ea4a5d43e4302e18375429d879f` both built successfully on one isolated AWS c7a.8xlarge (measured 32 CPUs / 62,909 MiB), with Node 24.22.1 and pnpm 12.15.0. The native config is used without an enum/auth overlay. The identical task-only browser driver and fixture bytes were injected on the base only after its clean production build.

| Native policy | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `none`, head and base | Uninvited guests cannot read the owner’s session or be selected for a notification/invitation. | Matched: picker eligibility false; guest/outsider lists and reads exclude the session; HTTP 404; no membership. |
| `view`, head and base | Preserve existing shared-session reads, including unrelated role-view readers; selected mentions do not add membership. | Matched: actual composer selection + Send, retained message, guest/outsider access, HTTP JSON/SSE 200; no membership. |
| Explicit `invited`, head | Creator A selects B; only the committed message grants access. C stays excluded. Revocation applies on the next request; Gateway stop/start retains the committed state. | Matched through the actual composer, native TLS/WebSocket RPC and HTTP: B lists/reads/events/JSON/SSE work after commit; C remains excluded; stop/start preserves B’s access/message; A removes B and its next list excludes the session and read/HTTP requests return not found. |
| Inbox failure, head | Targeted `mentions.failed` without failing idle or queued dispatch. | Matched in both fault-injected handler integration cases; committed input and membership remain intact. |

The AWS runs completed **3 head browser cases + 2 base comparison cases**, **30 real-Gateway/resource and dispatch-failure cases across 8 files**, and **two CLI Doctor upgrade cases**: frozen released-schema preservation and a replay through the actual stable **2026.11.4** CLI before candidate `none → invited → invited`. Memberships, exact retained transcript bytes and hidden-profile mention watermarks are preserved. This is isolated service stop/start and CLI upgrade proof, not a deployment or crash-reboot claim. No live Team Gateway configuration or deployment was changed.

The workload exited **0**. Its complete evidence archive was downloaded and all **19 artifact hashes** verified; head/base driver-input hashes match. Archive SHA-256: `a4abbe5737b07ef80deccaea6f897033b2a6ad67974075edcb075626692abbef`.

**Provider recovery and cleanup verified:** the workload originally exited 0 but the CLI wrapper exited 7 after coordinator finish/release/inspection requests returned HTTP 401. After access returned, the missing original receipt was inspected and recovered using its unchanged signed finish file, signer and finish hash—no workload replay or replacement lease. A fresh server read verifies the original terminal receipt with exit 0. prs.title: fix: use hosted catalog limits and input for live-listed models
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Some providers list their models live from the account: Together, Tencent TokenHub/TokenPlan, and other OpenAI-compatible live catalogs. When a listed model is missing from the plugin's built-in rows, OpenClaw ignores the hosted catalog's details for it and uses discovery defaults: 128k context, a 32k output cap and text-only input. For example, Together `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` has a 1M context window and accepts images according to the hosted catalog. Before this change, the picker showed it as 128k text-only and requests were capped at 32,768 output tokens.

## User Impact

Live-listed models now get the hosted catalog's context window, output limit, input modalities, reasoning/compat data and price. This reaches the picker, `models list`, run-time model resolution, compaction limits and request `max_tokens`. The account listing still decides which models exist. A catalog row the account does not list stays hidden, and a listed ID with no catalog row keeps its discovered values. Stored catalog rows are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The planner already merges bundled and hosted rows correctly (`planEffectiveModelCatalogRows`). The prepared catalog then drops planned rows for runtime/refreshable providers on purpose (#143837): a manifest row must not publish a model the account does not list. The live projection is left to fill in the details for a listed ID, but it only searches the plugin's own static rows.

This change does not add a second merge. `ModelRegistry`, when it reads a generated (live-listed) provider catalog, describes each listed ID with that planner's effective row. The catalog value wins field by field, and a discovered value fills only what the catalog omits. The row keeps its ID, its route and a declared non-chat kind.

<details><summary>Single-owner trace: every consumer reads the registry rows</summary>

- **Picker / `models list`:** `buildModelsListResult` reads the published snapshot from `prepareFullCatalogFacts` (`src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.full-catalog.ts`). It passes `templateModelRegistry.getAll()` (`ModelRegistry`) as `models` into `buildPreparedModelCatalogSnapshot`, whose `dynamicManifestKeys` filter (`src/agents/model-catalog.ts`) still drops the planned rows, so registry rows are the only source for these providers.
- **Run-time resolution:** `resolveModelAsync` → `resolveExplicitModelWithRegistry` (`model.registry-resolution.ts`) reads `preparedCatalogModel ?? modelRegistry.find(...)`. `preparedCatalogModel` comes from `completeConfiguredRuntimeModels`, which resolves through the same registry.
- **Context window / compaction:** `src/agents/context.ts` projects `owner.modelCatalog.entries`, the registry-derived snapshot above, and the resolved model's `contextWindow`.
- **Request max tokens:** taken from the resolved runtime model (above). The captured request moves from 32768 to about 1M for Kimi-K3.
- **Usage cost:** `withResolvedPricing` → `resolveModelCostConfig` and the Gateway usage paths (`captureModelCostPricing`) price through `prepareModelPricingContext`. That pricing owner already reads the same planner plus hosted prices, so turn cost was already correct for these rows on main (measured below). The registry row now carries the same price, so the two agree. No change was made to the pricing owner.
- **Persistence:** `models-config.plan.ts` keeps the plain admission filter (`filterGeneratedPluginModelCatalogProviders`), so stored generated rows stay as discovered and the description is applied at read time only.

</details>

## Evidence

Regression test `model-registry.catalog-description.test.ts`: it fails on base `f52f728d3415` (the listed row keeps `name`/`maxTokens`/`input` discovery defaults) and passes on the branch.

Real E2E, base main `f52f728d3415` vs this branch, both dist builds. Each side ran an isolated Gateway with dummy keys and a candidate hosted catalog republished from the branch with `scripts/publish-model-catalog.mts`, served on loopback. Provider traffic for the real Together and Tencent host names went to a self-signed TLS mock through a test-only preload; the configured base URLs stayed the real ones.

| row | base: list | base: request / cost | branch: list | branch: request / cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| together `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` (hosted-only) | **128000, text** | **max_tokens 32768** / $0.000105 | 1048576, text+image | max_tokens 1020067 / $0.000105 |
| together `zai-org/GLM-5.2` (control) | 262144, text | 131072 / $0.000036 | same | same |
| tencent-tokenhub `hy4` | 1024000/960000, text+image | 64000, effort high / $0.0000208 | same | same |
| tencent-tokenhub `hy4-flash` | 1048576/983040, text+image | 65536, effort high / $0.0000021 | same | same |
| tencent-tokenhub `hy4-preview` (control) | 1024000, text | 64000, effort high / $0.0000208 | same | same |

Tencent `hy4`/`hy4-flash` are already correct on main because the bundled Tencent manifest now carries their rows, so they serve as controls here. On 2026.11.4 the same hosted rows showed 128k text-only; that is the case this change fixes for any provider whose plugin lacks the row.

Gates: consumer tests (model registry, `model-catalog`, prepared runtime catalog projection/publication/configured catalog, `models list` prepared catalog, manifest planner, pricing), `src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint and format on the changed files all pass.

Production delta against the merge base: +68/−3 lines in `src/agents` (one read-time function plus a call-site swap). Test: +109.

**Merge danger:** low. The change is read-time only, with no schema, protocol or stored-row change. If a hosted row is wrong for a listed model, its values now apply to that model, where before they were silently ignored.
**Blast radius:** generated (live-listed) provider catalogs read through `ModelRegistry`. These are providers with `modelCatalog.discovery: runtime | refreshable` whose plugin manifest or the hosted catalog has a row for a listed ID. Static providers and authored `models.json` rows are untouched.

prs.title: fix(agents): preserve published catalog in setup probes
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #196817.

Read-only setup probes could lose the startup-published subscription model catalog because the lease compared execution-owner identity instead of the canonical catalog source. Compare the existing canonical source projection for passive inventory while retaining separate execution ownership, auth binding, credential scope, and plugin-generation lifecycle checks.

This is a fresh replacement for #198054, which its author closed on the stale base and explicitly invited replacing from a fresh branch. It uses the canonical source projection rather than a custom fingerprint policy. Attribution and prior discussion: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198054. That PR remains closed.

## Validation

- 101 focused tests passed across six targeted suites.
- Distinct unit isolation and negative controls: base regression fails; repaired regression and controls pass.
- Real isolated Gateway public `openclaw.setup.verify` regression: unchanged production base returns auth failure; repaired production selects `openai/subscription-model` and invokes the synthetic provider stream exactly once.
- Targeted production and test typechecks, type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent review on the configured OpenClaw route completed successfully with no scoped P0–P2 findings. Reviewed base: `f947bdc94981e299fe26b5a71af8bfdd4e7ac125`; complete patch SHA-256: `ba112504c0aea1f39c3d9056de91f46754af5a200a70e7dc323fbf0ff6d98abb`.
- Current published head `d825a840d9f3d6cea27349368c82a6590ebe0863` has the same source tree as the reviewed commit. Hosted review found no actionable correctness/security findings.
- On the exact CI integration tree, the catalog regression and negative controls passed **5/5**, and the real isolated Gateway public setup regression passed **1/1**.

## CI baseline attribution

CI run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44005561326 remains failed in `checks-node-changed` (job `133780799835`). Its actual checkout was merge `5c7c32c43447910c949c2994756259c3de47eaf8`, combining this PR with main `9f441adcf1e7307e1dfd0a496660106c4922dfe8`.

On November 17, the documented secretless, network-none pinned-Bun runner reproduced both exact CI failures on **both the CI merge and its main parent without this PR**:

- `src/gateway/chat-goal-created-authority.e2e.test.ts`: revoked-return history expected 9 messages, received 8.
- `test/e2e/gateway-transcripts-discord-capture.e2e.test.ts`: native-resource attachment rejected as `unexpected socket destination null:NaN`, followed by retained-resource cleanup failures.

Both comparisons failed 2/2 with matching signatures. This establishes inherited failures rather than a catalog-patch regression. The automated failure table initially reported unknown because no comparable main job existed; the exact-base comparison supplies the missing evidence. The earlier isolated 2/2 pass used the older source candidate, not the CI integration tree. Host proxy-confounded attempts remain excluded from accepted proof.

The same CI merge separately passed the changed catalog tests and public setup flow **6/6**. All three isolated runs confirmed container absence on cleanup; the owned source branch was restored clean. Image: `sha256:a0d7b2b49ffa0e99787a00b7ec2af46eca58020082713f002ca9f0f1cfd1a017`.

Retained log SHA-256 values:
- Exact CI merge failures: `ec53a60921721bcfda20d6e24f18ff6d35c12ab79734cba92e1baeeb38256ae8`.
- Exact main-parent failures: `1d86efe433b2943db47d0183a0f9cba25ff5c5ecce9c344f58124852a6ab639f`.
- CI-merge catalog/public setup passes: `ef9bc858c626b752bcc3d3aa3fca56f10366ff597e3e651dcb1e411709344bba`.

Native review artifacts validate with `READY FOR /prepare-pr`, zero findings, `tests.result: fail`, and exact-head `tests.preExistingCi` attribution to run `44005561326`, attempt 1. Prior native preparation remains at unchanged head with `gates_mode=github_pending`; no push was needed. The PR is review-ready with documented inherited CI failures, not green or merge-ready. Protected merge remains blocked; no CI rerun, merge, or bypass was requested.

## Limits

The public Gateway regression uses synthetic subscription credentials and provider transport; it does not claim a real account, real model response, or live OAuth service validation. Independent review did not execute tests or fully inspect refresh internals. The exact introducing commits for the inherited failures were not fully bisected. No migration, configuration change, merge, or deployment is included.

prs.title: fix: handle retired animation IDs in WebKit checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The WebKit loading-animation check can abort while inspecting an animation that has already been retired, leaving CI unable to report whether detached shimmers remain.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible behavior change. The animation census continues past a retired Inspector ID while retaining its checks for live detached animations.

## Why This Change Was Made

WebKit removes retired IDs before delivering its deferred destruction event. Handle only the exact missing-ID response from animation resolution; every other inspection failure still propagates. The all-animation consumer and existing zero-detached/running assertions remain unchanged.

## Evidence

A native Linux WebKit regression fails with the old helper and passes with the fix. It retires one real announced animation through one native collection, verifies the actual missing-ID response, and still counts a retained detached running shimmer and a connected non-shimmer. The unchanged session-churn case also passes with the fix.

Proof used Node24.22.1, Playwright1.64.1 and WebKit27.2 revision2370 on Ubuntu24.04.4. The unchanged original case passed on the parent, so that observation does not establish inheritance of the CI failure. The deterministic regression proves the lifetime assumption; the specific animation lost in CI remains unidentified.

Fresh isolated Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 issues. The required changed-file check passed 21/23 stages. Its test-only overload-order lint finding was corrected, and targeted format, lint and UI E2E type checks passed. The remaining dead-export findings exactly match a retained scan of parent f1d7daed (5 production / 3 full-tree); those main regressions are attributed to [#143882](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143882), [#200088](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200088) and [#199111](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199111), remain separately owned, and are not a future CI waiver. The final delta from review is only the mechanical overload ordering. Production LOC delta: 0; shared test helper +16, regression +139.

prs.title: improve(ios): avoid reformatting unchanged parts of streaming replies
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

While a native iOS reply streams, unchanged Markdown sections are repeatedly prepared for display. A long answer with 32 stable sections and a growing final paragraph performed 66 block preparations per processed update.

## What changed

Keep preparation in the mounted streaming view and reuse prepared blocks only when their semantic input, completion state, reveal role, and localized disclosure summary still match. Changed segments still use the complete Markdown parser, so later references and structural changes remain parser-owned.

The current-main integration narrows this PR to two renderer files, their focused preparation tests, and one generated translation-source entry for the existing “Details” key. The former parent, #192232, has landed. Its old reader, list, and fence changes are no longer part of this PR's delta; current main's scrolling and incomplete-fence behavior are preserved.

There is no global cache or new throttle. The retained data is the current streaming snapshot, not a history of updates. A single growing paragraph still requires its normal parsing and preparation.

## Current verification

Candidate: `a1606c583ec86db498114f565476cec3c4fd2a23`, integrated with main `4cbd215af463775faa6807aea90621292b28af15`. Its full tree matches the independently reviewed and tested four-file port.

Actual compiler-coverage counts, with separate cold and warm processes:

| Workload | Main | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 32 sections: initial block preparations | 66 | 66 |
| 32 sections: preparations over 128 subsequent updates | 8,448 | 128 |
| One growing paragraph: preparations over 128 updates | 128 | 128 |
| Full snapshot/parser initialization over 129 inputs | 129 | 129 |

This proves less repeated preparation, not faster full parsing. No first-content latency, frame-rate, CPU, or memory improvement is claimed.

- 129 permanent shared-package tests across five suites passed on macOS, plus the temporary measurement workload, which was removed afterward.
- SwiftLint, SwiftFormat, generated translation inventory verification, and independent whole-change review passed.
- Both normal iOS app builds passed. In Simulator, the same simulated loopback Gateway sent 32 sections with bold text/links and 128 tail updates. Sending, streaming reveal, scrolling, Jump, and final content were checked on both builds. Final text was identical.
- After a manual scroll had settled, two pre-update readings and the readings after further deltas and finalization had the same Y coordinate on each build: **0-point movement** in both.
- The first fixture launch omitted a connection-state flag and produced no reply; it was excluded and corrected. An initial scroll capture included gesture deceleration; the settled controls above resolve that ambiguity.
- The fixture is simulated, not a real model/provider or persistence qualification. Link destinations were not opened. GitHub CI remains separately visible on the published head.

## Before/After

The images below show the same streaming checkpoint and completed tail. They are cropped native-app captures with synthetic content. The matching checkpoint images are byte-identical.

Videos show streaming and manual navigation. The baseline video joins its first eight and last ten seconds to remove an idle inspection interval; these clips are **not a timing comparison**.

![Before: native iOS streaming checkpoint on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e6e6f57c-e731-4a04-b8e9-34dc2a03d793)

![After: same native iOS streaming checkpoint with block reuse](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a390d3f8-7380-4da2-863a-d63291a20d33)

![Before: completed response tail on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f134e71-a813-4fc3-8b37-885d7aeb40ff)

![After: identical completed response tail with block reuse](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bca3e5e4-2f5e-4f98-8603-6055ee410f74)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c36030b-c605-452d-ae3b-43cee4f50cd0

## CI qualification

The [iOS screenshot job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44011875795/job/133801210281) built the app successfully and passed three of four screenshot cases. The static chat case failed at `OpenClawSnapshotUITests.swift:269` because the “Mermaid diagram” button did not appear.

The renderer trace shows the WebKit document remained in its loading phase, with `documentReady=false`, until its watchdog expired after 27,048 ms. The HTML resource had been delivered, but the document never reported ready.

This screenshot uses completed fixture history, not a streaming reply. The new streaming preparation is not instantiated; the shared snapshot receives `preparesReveal=false` and no previous snapshot, so the new reuse branch does not execute. The screenshot, fixture, Mermaid loader/resources, and build inputs are byte-identical between the actual CI baseline `f52f728d34158e66c0d11ce48cc7fb1c7a0cd6a7` and tested merge `6543bb204ee8d18a8093f3c032f20db408e1785b`. That merge contains the exact published head and only this PR's four-file change relative to its baseline.

Independent source review agrees this failure is outside the optimization's changed behavior. The underlying WebKit loading cause has not been isolated, and no baseline rerun is claimed. This failure is retained explicitly for the native unrelated-CI qualification; it is not reported as a passing screenshot test.

**Current landing hold:** [Android Play tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44011875795/job/133801210239) also ended **cancelled**, after GitHub's 20-minute job deadline. The step reached `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest`; cancellation is not a passing test result. The complete `apps/android` tree is identical between the tested baseline and merge (`5ef9c3f110fd6a64af44b50993323a5c8b0ad622`). The Apple transport and Periphery workflows subsequently passed. The native landing verifier refused admission because this Android deadline cancellation is not covered by its supported cancellation-provenance cases. No merge was performed, and auto-merge was retired. The prepared head and evidence are retained; no timeout or CI limit was changed.

prs.title: improve(ci): reduce docs link audit overhead
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The docs link audit rebuilds per-character source-location tables even when a rewrite returns exactly the original text. Follow-up to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200052.

## User Impact

Link diagnostics and source locations stay the same. The full docs link-audit command is 10.77% faster in the controlled comparison below. No configuration or authoring changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Evaluate each replacement callback as before, then retain the existing source map for an unchanged result. A later real replacement still copies the intervening original locations. There is no new cache, parser API, dependency, or configuration.

## Evidence

Candidate: `aa2b4e8cbbe4c0a5874a51d9d0f9fa4a9c3247aa`, against frozen baseline `10f6b53ce51827256689604e821c34a7f5e84323`.

The unmodified full `CI=1 node scripts/docs-link-audit.mjs` command passed with 16,793 internal links and zero broken links. A separate temporary diagnostic probe counted 1,576 wholly unchanged rewrite passes rebuilding 39,881,153 source-map entries. Mixed passes are excluded from that savings count. All 65,557 tracked source blobs/modes and all 22 pinned ClawHub docs input blobs were verified. Input: `openclaw/clawhub@b03a08f546be828cc3ccfa319366092618ad53b7`.

The final candidate passed formatting, scripts lint, tooling test typecheck, and all 60 tests across the five selected parser/component/link/source-location files. Syntax, whitespace and commit hooks also passed. On the same verified source, baseline and candidate audit output was byte-for-byte identical; all callback/pass counts matched, while identity-only copies and entries dropped to zero.

Local ClawSweeper 0.3.3 completed the full committed range above with zero reported findings and no summary priority filter. An independent source review also found no issue. The predeclared performance rule passed on the same verified candidate. The native source capsule uses a temporary carrier commit: its same-run source identity, exact tree, index and every tracked blob/mode were checked against the pinned candidate before validation.

### Predeclared performance decision

Use the full command above on one repository-default Boat VM, requested large and observed 8 CPUs / 16,767,762,432 bytes RAM, Node 24.22.1. Use identical pinned repository and ClawHub inputs for both sides. Run one excluded warmup per side, then five serial AB pairs. Compare exact output and successful exits; separately require unchanged callback/pass counts and zero candidate identity-only source-map copies.

Accept only if median command wall time improves by **at least 5% and 0.2 seconds**, and observed p95 wall time, CPU time, and maximum-child RSS are **no more than 5% worse**. Stop if any measured pair is more than **20% worse** for any of those metrics. Five-sample nearest-rank p95 is the maximum. No extra samples, relaxed thresholds, or replacement VM to obtain a win. Reject and close if the completed comparison fails this rule.

This focused experiment cannot establish whole-job, invoice, or PR-throughput savings. The small sample limits tail estimates. The ClawHub fixture verifies authored docs/assets; it does not test external links over the network, and preserves the existing default-branch fallback for non-doc GitHub URLs.


### Measured result

One excluded warmup per version, followed by exactly five serial AB pairs on the same VM. Both versions returned identical output and exit0 for every run. All three metrics improved in every pair; no stop condition was reached.

| Pair | Wall baseline → candidate (s) | CPU baseline → candidate (s) | Peak RSS baseline → candidate (KiB) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 13.687 → 11.940 | 15.98 → 13.98 | 1,063,236 → 982,588 |
| 2 | 13.867 → 12.862 | 16.10 → 15.20 | 1,032,844 → 977,312 |
| 3 | 14.203 → 12.527 | 16.52 → 14.84 | 1,038,464 → 996,788 |
| 4 | 14.755 → 12.478 | 17.24 → 14.85 | 1,065,492 → 994,324 |
| 5 | 13.984 → 12.098 | 16.42 → 14.52 | 1,065,552 → 985,456 |

| Metric | Median baseline → candidate | Change | Observed p95 baseline → candidate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Full audit | 13.984 → 12.478 s | -10.77% | 14.755 → 12.862 s |
| CPU | 16.420 → 14.840 s | -9.62% | 17.240 → 15.200 s |
| Peak RSS | 1,063,236 → 985,456 KiB | -7.32% | 1,065,552 → 996,788 KiB |

The median saves 1.506 seconds per full audit. The five-sample p95 is the maximum, not a production tail estimate. Temporary diagnostic instrumentation was removed for every timed run.

prs.title: fix(plugins): prevent Gateway stalls while copying reload recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Keeps plugin reload recovery from blocking the Gateway event loop while creating and copying its private recovery source.

Follow-up to #198262, #200320 and #200136. #198262 already adapted and credited Wes (@akmad)'s rollback-capture work from #181491; this change addresses the remaining physical metadata inside that asynchronous copy, while preserving its synchronous fork contract. The motivating Team incident (25c97908, 2026-11-16 05:02 PST) held MAIN in `openat2(O_CREAT)` for 1.97 seconds while btrfs waited for a transaction. After physical preparation custody moved to the broker, the real serving-plugin reload recovery path still performed synchronous root creation and metadata work in the copy filter on MAIN. Awaiting `fs.promises.cp` did not move those filter callbacks off the event loop.

## User Impact

Reload recovery still waits for its source copy, but unrelated Gateway work can continue during a filesystem stall. No configuration, schema or operator action changes.

The measured tradeoff is explicit: normal cold owner time increases by about 30 ms, from 94.750 to 124.388 ms. Warm median owner time is 87.023 versus 86.476 ms, but its maximum increases from 227.783 to 266.447 ms. These costs are accepted for removing the foreground filesystem boundary; this is not an overall speedup claim.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing broker resource now owns the complete asynchronous recovery copy: root creation, copy/filter work, link relocation, native-reference validation and physical cleanup. The host retains native leases and path mappings. Failed-copy roots stay recorded under the same owner until cleanup succeeds; sequential release/close settlement preserves both failures.

The retained synchronous fork and broker-owned asynchronous copy share one physical copy algorithm. No second manager, cache, schema, configuration switch or public protocol is introduced. Production grows by 159 lines for the private command/adapter and complete lifetime handoff; duplicated copy/filter policy is removed. Existing synchronous recovery forks and runtime-selected synchronous imports remain separate contracts, so this PR does not claim every Gateway filesystem path is asynchronous.

## Evidence

The existing main-thread filesystem observer reproduces the defect through the real loaded serving-plugin recovery owner. In five compiled fault pairs, the baseline executes 28 selected MAIN sync calls and records heartbeat gaps of 2,007–2,014 ms; the candidate executes zero and records 7–14 ms while the actual broker create is delayed for about two seconds. Median heartbeat gap is 2,010 versus 10 ms. The recovery operation itself still waits: fault owner medians are 2,132.034 versus 2,164.273 ms.

The synthetic plugin actually imports 199 companion payloads and proves their evaluated lengths through its retained provider callback. Every run copies 202 regular files totaling 1,647,404 bytes, verifies copied entry bytes, joins removal and retains the serving callback. A minimal three-file qualification exposed an undersized workload and was replaced before accepted measurements; the unused 2 MiB native fixture input is not counted as copied work. Surrounding 35 GiB/5,000-session/62,000-file fixtures are synthetic and are not scanned by this owner. No Team data was copied.

Canonical built Node 26.12.1/APFS proof ran 20 normal processes (five A1/A2 controls and five A/B pairs, each cold/warm), then five two-second A/B fault pairs. All 30 processes and observed brokers exited; source/build/driver/fixture hashes were verified and every row retained. The baseline is the physical-custody revision `03b70d9`; the candidate also includes its later source-acquisition error projection and sender/type repair. The error projection is inactive on successful samples, and the subsequent pure type-leaf move changes no executable behavior. These dependency differences are explicit rather than described as identical bytes.

| Normal metric | Baseline median | Candidate median |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Cold owner ms | 94.750 | 124.388 |
| Warm owner ms | 87.023 | 86.476 |
| Cold MAIN CPU ms | 44.200 | 6.504 |
| Warm MAIN CPU ms | 35.311 | 5.224 |
| Cold MAIN allocation MB | 32.651 | 5.297 |
| Warm MAIN allocation MB | 30.196 | 5.642 |
| Whole process-tree CPU ms | 3,440 | 3,440 |

MAIN counters exclude broker work. Whole-tree CPU includes fixture generation, imports and initial plugin loading; it is not an exclusive recovery CPU measure or a global savings claim. A/A cold owner medians were 123.342/101.710 ms, warm 105.621/111.534 ms. Host one-minute load ranged from 27.257 to 41.711 despite pausing this task's other local work. Variability limits precision; no tail is dismissed as noise. Candidate warm capture maximum was 255.886 ms versus 171.691 ms, while cold capture maximum improved from 145.623 to 117.785 ms.

Rerun using the committed `scripts/perf/plugin-capture-custody-measure.mjs` and fixture setup from #200320. Build each pinned checkout with `pnpm build sourcePerformance`, then invoke the candidate driver against each `--repo` with the same fixture and a fresh label:

```sh
node --expose-gc scripts/perf/plugin-capture-custody-measure.mjs \
  --repo <built-checkout> --fixture <synthetic-fixture> --label <arm> --operation recovery
```

Add `--fault recovery --delay-ms 2000`, plus candidate `--expect-off-main`, for the fault arms. Run A1/A2/A/B five times serially, followed by five A/B fault pairs; wrap processes in `/usr/bin/time -l` for whole-tree counters. Fixture generation, initial loading and byte verification are outside the owner timing intervals.

Focused consumer proof passes 56 tests with one existing cross-filesystem skip. The final Gateway regression gates the actual broker copy, proves the event loop advances while it is pending, checks the real source/destination and exact copy count, and observes zero selected MAIN sync calls through capture and joined disposal. Core and affected test types, scoped lint/format/line limits and the static import-cycle guard pass. Independent final publication Codex review is scoped-clean; its complete source receipt includes the adapted Gateway gate, scaled workload and error-cause fields.

The earlier full `pnpm check:changed` retained 14 production/108 full-tree dead-export identities identical to its exact parent, with no added or removed identities. Its task-owned style issues were fixed and rechecked. This is a recorded local failure, not an all-green census or an inherited-CI exception. Exact-head CI and final-head zero-open ClawSweeper review remain landing gates.

The final 14 reviewed file hashes apply unchanged to main `53278c30303`, which contains #200320. The dependency lock and scoped instructions are unchanged. Both current-main Gateway cases pass. The final `pnpm check:changed` run passes every gate except the unused-export scan: five production findings and three full-tree findings in Slack/UI, outside this patch. Both scans reproduce identically on exact clean parent `53278c30303`. The Slack exports were introduced by `abdc09f1355` (#143882), browser approval by `1ce9df608b4` (#200088), and the two other UI exports lost their last production consumers in `c3baf0d8484` (#199111). These are named main regressions for follow-up, not ignored noise. No inherited-CI exemption is claimed; exact-head green CI remains required. This is a current-main follow-up, not a rewrite of the older contributor fork.

CI repair: the first exact-head run `44005730906` found four newly reachable modules missing from the extracted PR-wrapper inventory. Both closure tests failed locally before the correction and passed afterward. The two applicable provisioning cases pass on macOS; the third case requires Linux and remains covered by the new CI run. Four inventory entries complete the existing extraction contract, with no production change or exception. Fresh independent Codex review of this correction is scoped-clean.

The live entry-point proof now passes through an isolated built Gateway and the public `plugins.reload` RPC. With exactly one successful recovery-root create held for two seconds, the baseline blocked Gateway MAIN and overlapping HTTP/WebSocket health requests took up to 1,998/2,088 ms. The candidate held the separate broker for 2,007 ms while 48 HTTP and 23 WS responses completed during the hold; overlapping maxima were 223/249 ms. Both reloads published the synthetic plugin from v1 to v2 without restarting, removed the recovery root, and completed a real `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` assistant turn with the expected response and normal stop. Those turns were requested during the hold and completed afterward; inference completion within the hold is not claimed.

Both canonical live wrappers and cleanup exited successfully. This uses retained canonical builds whose recovery runtime matches the final patch, with only a later erased type-import difference; it is not presented as an exact-final-head full build. Exact-head CI is separate. This bounded APFS fault proof supplements the accepted CPU/allocation campaign without rerunning it. One earlier injector qualification mistakenly included a preparation-worker root; its failed evidence was preserved, the path predicate and receipt identity were corrected, and it is excluded from accepted results.

The second CI run (`44008299130`) exposed a cold test-worker preparation defect: the first timed heartbeat build-graph case waited for a 76,348 ms full worker compilation (20,233 inputs), exceeding its unchanged 60-second deadline. The existing runner preparation owner now admits that test before launch. The new direct/projects boundary cases fail before the correction because no prepared manifest exists at launch; all 55 runner cases pass afterward in 31.39 seconds, including exclusion and cleanup. The original Bun build case passes in 483 ms after preparation is visibly completed before test startup. No timeout, graph selection, assertion or cache contract changes. Independent Codex review is scoped-clean. This is a concrete runner repair, not an inherited-CI exemption or a rerun for green.

The repair-only `pnpm check:changed --staged --base cfcdaaadda05` passes all gates except the same five production/three full-tree Slack/UI exports already reproduced and attributed above. Script export findings remain zero. Gateway production remains +159 lines; this CI correction adds three tooling lines and 13 net test lines.

The third run (`44012000507`) identified one consumer fixture missed by that enrollment. Its unrestricted tooling case mocked compiler success without writing a manifest. A one-line fixture migration now uses the existing controlled compiler for that selection, retaining the real preparation owner and existing compiler-count/receipt assertions. The exact eight-case table reproduces one failure before the change and passes all eight afterward (7.58-second wrapper). No production change, added test, timeout change or weaker assertion; independent Codex review is scoped-clean. ClawSweeper accepted the live Gateway proof and identified this same fixture as its sole remaining item.

The fixture-only changed-check run again passes every gate except the identical five production/three full-tree Slack/UI unused exports, with zero script export findings. All 18 final file hashes are recorded; the eight Gateway production files remain unchanged.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep the scrollbar inside the rounded corners of long session menus
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a session menu list is long enough to scroll, such as **Assign to…** on a team with many people, its scrollbar pokes past the menu's rounded corner at the top and bottom of the list. It reads as the scrollbar escaping the menu.

## User Impact

User impact: the scrollbar in the long session menu lists (**Assign to…**, **Move to group** and collections) stays inside the rounded outline. Nothing else changes; the scrollbar's travel is shorter by the corner radius at each end.

## Why This Change Was Made

Browsers do not clip a scrolling element's own scrollbar to its rounded corners, so a thumb resting at either end of the track was drawn over the corner. The scrollbar track for these lists now starts and ends where the corners do, so the thumb only moves along the straight edge.

The rule sits beside the one that makes these lists scroll. A first version applied it to every menu and popover, but that shared style is also embedded in the chat boot script, where it added 17 B gzip against 2 B of remaining budget and failed the Control UI size check. Other menus only scroll when the window is too short to fit them, so they keep the old behavior; fixing them too needs a budget decision.

Firefox has no track inset control and is unchanged by this PR; it was not checked.

## Evidence

Before, the scrollbar thumb crossed the menu's rounded corner. Now it stops where the corner begins.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: the scrollbar thumb runs over the rounded top corner of the Assign to menu](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/991443f9-6ffb-4b77-8be7-c20ff6c447e9) | ![After: the scrollbar thumb starts below the rounded corner](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f73338f1-f2b8-413b-9f3a-7e88d2ca6bf2) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before, annotated: the thumb crosses the corner](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/95750b5f-5af8-4dfe-bc36-e15b318c87e6) | ![After, annotated: the thumb stops below the corner](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0694109b-0200-4ba8-b23b-58a9cafc5084) |

Sidebar session menu → **Assign to…** with a 34-person directory, dark theme, pointer resting on the scrollbar. prs.title: improve(ci): avoid recompressing candidate registry artifacts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The shared FRV candidate producer recompresses the prerelease plugin registry, which already consists almost entirely of gzip-compressed npm tarballs. Its neighboring package/image uploads and the other registry uploaders already disable this redundant compression.

## User Impact

No validation or published package changes. Set the existing upload action’s compression level to zero; retain every registry file, manifest/digest check, artifact identity, missing-file error and consumer. This is a small runner-efficiency improvement, not a claim of minutes saved from FRV.

## Evidence and Wall-Time Assessment

- Real input: [candidate run 43998194486, artifact 14291137296](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43998194486/artifacts/14291137296), 54 files / 130,006,985 bytes.
- Five interleaved Python ZIP proxy pairs over those exact files: median level-6 wall **1.800 s**, stored wall **0.098 s**. Archive sizes **129,960,111 → 130,015,299 bytes**: +55,188 bytes, approximately 0.042%. Every member’s bytes were verified after every archive round trip. This measures local ZIP work, **not** the hosted action or whole FRV.
- The transfer tradeoff is explicit: the extra ~54 KiB would erase the measured ~1.70 s saving only below roughly 32 KiB/s incremental throughput. No extra job, queue delay, setup, dependency barrier or concurrent memory load is added. Parent wall improvement can be zero while another qualification branch dominates.
- The pinned [upload action](https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/blob/cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9/action.yml) supports level zero for incompressible data. Registry upload began in a0deb8edae1a (#120107); this does not undo a documented compression requirement.
- Compact workflow regression fails on the base’s missing compression setting. The complete package-acceptance workflow suite passes: **587 tests, 147.56 s** on the pinned Bun runner. Scoped canonical typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, diff checks, and pinned actionlint/zizmor/workflow guards pass.
- These are configuration/coverage and archive-byte proofs; no end-to-end hosted upload speedup is claimed.

## Simplification

Production **+1/-0**, tests **+6/-0**, two files. No new helper, policy owner, benchmark framework or committed bulky fixture. The regression extends the existing registry-consumer contract and retains missing-file failure behavior.

## Review readiness

Verified November 17, 2026, 03:36 UTC at **a6f06b529aa2c37dffd2706183831440680095f6**: conflict-free; ClawSweeper completed with no findings or before-merge items. Exact-head CI completed with no related failing checks. CI is **not all green**: its sole substantive failure is the unchanged private-UI ownership inventory assertion (91 versus 90), reproduced locally and independently on #200380; the aggregate gate reflects it. [Failure attribution and source comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200386#issuecomment-6937350407). No baseline was relaxed or failure hidden. Ready for review with that unrelated CI failure and the hosted-performance limitation disclosed.

prs.title: fix(signal): reaction approvals do nothing on prompts forwarded to Signal approvers
prs.body:
Closes #195620

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: 👍 / 👎 reactions never resolve exec or plugin approvals that are forwarded to a Signal approver (`approvals.*.mode: "targets"`); the prompt arrives without the "React with:" hint and approvers have to type `/approve`.

## User Impact

Approvers who receive forwarded approval prompts in Signal can approve or deny with a reaction, as they already can for approvals that start in a Signal chat. Setups without reaction approvers keep the same manual prompt text as today.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signal's forwarded-prompt renderer returned the reaction runtime's manual fallback payload, which has its presentation stripped. Outbound delivery only calls Signal's `renderPresentation` for payloads with a presentation, so the existing checked hint renderer (approver, route and target-author checks) never ran and `afterDeliverPayload` had no hinted message to register.

Forwarded prompts now keep their command text plus the approval button presentation, so delivery goes through that existing checked renderer and registration. The forwarded render itself still carries no reaction hint, so controls are only advertised when the route is actually bound. When the hint cannot be added, `renderPresentation` now returns Signal's materialized approval text for approval payloads instead of `null`; otherwise the generic fallback would flatten the buttons and repeat the Allow/Deny commands already in the text. Non-approval payloads behave as before.

## Evidence

- New regression in `extensions/signal/src/core.test.ts` (exec and plugin): a Control UI–origin request forwarded to a Signal target renders with the hint, `afterDeliverPayload` registers it, and a 👍 on the delivered message resolves to `allow-once`; without reaction approvers the rendered text equals the manual prompt. On `main` both cases fail at the missing presentation; dropping the `renderPresentation` fallback makes the no-approver assertion fail.
- `core.test.ts`, `approval-native.test.ts` (including the existing "no unbound reaction choices" target-mode check), `approval-reactions.test.ts`, `monitor.approval-reply-delivery.test.ts`: 53 passed.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean on changed files.
- Authority boundary for the forwarded path (`approval-reactions.test.ts`): a target-mode prompt rendered through `addSignalApprovalReactionHintToStructuredPayload` and registered through delivery does not call `resolveApprovalOverGateway` for a reaction from an unlisted actor or from an approver removed from `allowFrom`, and resolves once for a current approver. Existing cases in the same file keep covering wrong conversation / wrong bot identity, missing explicit approvers, and a changed top-level approval route. The resolution and authorization code itself is unchanged by this PR; it only makes forwarded prompts reach it.
- Test-line growth is allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/196419-signal-forwarded-approval-reactions.txt` (79, exact net growth); `check:test-lines-ratchet` passes after merging current `main`.
- The full `extensions/signal` run on Windows has 8 failures in untouched files (Unix socket paths, temp-dir permissions, Windows env names, and a database-worker timeout in `event-handler.partial-delivery.test.ts`); that approval test fails the same way on unmodified `main`. No live Signal round trip was run.

prs.title: perf(gateway): answer exact configured database targets without per-target file probes
prs.body:
Fixes #200267.

## What Problem This Solves

`isConfiguredAgentDatabaseTarget` probes the filesystem on its per-target path. The gateway boot database preflight calls it
once per candidate row with the configured targets first, so a `statSync` of the row is paid **once per target per row** — the
quadratic cost #200267 measured at 7.1M of 8.8M main-thread file calls during boot with ~470 agents.

For a row that names a configured path, an `fs.statSync` per preceding target is work with a known answer: the row and the
target are the same string.

## Why This Change Was Made

The function now answers an exact configured path from the strings alone, before any filesystem probe, and keeps the row's own
`statSync` at one call for the whole row instead of one per target. This is the fix shape suggested in #200267, applied to the
current source.

The alias walk is unchanged: a row that does not name a configured path still compares against every target and still uses
`isSameOpenClawAgentDatabasePath` for targets that exist, so symlinked, hardlinked and case-folded aliases keep resolving the
same way. The remaining per-row cost is the string comparison plus at most one probe of the row.

`#200267` also reports a second quadratic in fresh state (the missing-suffix alias probe running for every pair of agents). That
is a different loop in a different function and is **not** touched here.

## User Impact

Gateway boot with many configured agents stops paying a file probe per (row, target) pair. The `ready` phase the report measured
went from 101.6 s and 36.4 s to 42.4 s and 14.0 s with this shape applied locally; the admission database-readiness phase went
from 23.1 s and 10.4 s to 1.1 s and 0.7 s. Behaviour is otherwise identical: the same row answers the same way, including for
missing files, aliases and case-folded paths.

## Evidence

New `src/config/sessions/targets-database-match.test.ts` counts `fs.statSync` calls on the real function:

- an exact configured path answers with **zero** file probes;
- 50 rows x 200 existing configured targets stay at **one** probe per target per row instead of two;
- an alias that does not exist still resolves to `false` through the walk.

Red on base: `1 failed | 2 passed` — the "probes each target at most once per row" case is the failure.
Green with this change: `3 passed`.

Unchanged behaviour, from the suites that own this function:
`targets.test.ts` **60 passed | 3 skipped**, `state/openclaw-agent-db.test.ts` **17 passed**.
`check-test-lines-ratchet`: net +68 test lines, inside the 400-line allowance. `oxlint` clean on both touched files.

## AI Assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance from the issue report; the author reviewed the change and its evidence.

prs.title: fix(gateway): prevent readiness probes from freezing the main thread
prs.body:
Related: #200038, #150564

## What Problem This Solves

Readiness requests can freeze every WebSocket client and RPC on a large Linux Gateway. In the reported November 16 production incident at `aeabca2e`, an approximately 8 GB RSS Gateway stalled for 3,682 ms during `gateway:http`; its main thread spent 3,576 ms in D-state while launching the child-runtime probe. An earlier observation stalled for 877 ms.

## User Impact

When a spawn broker is available, asynchronous runtime viability checks launch from that small process. Readiness and health keep detecting removed/replaced runtimes and loader failures on every observation, with the same unavailable results and recovery hook. CLI and other scopes without a broker retain native execution. No configuration, protocol, or persisted-state changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The probe added by #200038 called native `execFile(process.execPath, ["--version"])` directly. Linux `uv_spawn` forks using `clone(SIGCHLD|CLONE_CHILD_SETTID|CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID)`, so the calling Gateway thread copies its large address space. Under btrfs I/O pressure, the observed stack was `clone → copy_process → dup_mm → dup_mmap → __vma_start_write → __vma_start_exclude_readers`; the JavaScript profile reached `prepareChildRuntimeViability → probeChildRuntimeExecutable → execFile → spawn` through readiness preparation.

Use the existing host's `spawnExeca` launch primitive directly. It never enters the command runner's runtime-failure diagnosis, so a failed probe cannot recursively request another probe. Preserve the 1-second timeout, 8 KiB output bound, caller environment/cwd, and loader diagnostics; drain and join the broker child before publishing. There is no result cache or polling skip.

Separate the existing broker scope/state from Gateway startup so low-level runtime workers can read the current broker without importing its lazy host factory. Both existing context exports and the probe use the same state owner. The host contract is separate from its implementation so this lookup also avoids a static dependency cycle; the existing factory and operations are unchanged. Include the new runtime state module in the trusted PR wrapper inventory so isolated bootstrap/provisioning retains its complete import closure. A transport failure still checks executable existence asynchronously, so an unavailable broker cannot hide a removed runtime during its own restart.

Thanks to @obviyus (Ayaan Zaidi) for the original runtime/loader detection in #200038; this preserves that behavior while following #150564's spawn ownership.

## Evidence

- Owning-boundary regression with a real broker (Node on macOS): base **2 failed / 1 passed**, each new case recording **3 parent `execFile` launches** despite a ready broker. Final candidate: **3 passed**, zero parent `execFile`/`spawn`/`spawnSync` launches, three broker requests per case, and unavailable publication for removed and loader-broken runtimes. The removed-runtime case also closes the broker before the failure observation.
- Codex review found that a registered but unavailable broker could hide removal during restart. This reproduced as **1 failed / 2 passed**, with `available: true` instead of `false`; the async existence check fixes it without a native retry. The final affected runtime/recovery run passed **33 tests**. The prior **93-test** run also covered health/readiness, run-loop recovery, broker startup fallback, and native broker lifecycle paths. The final contract extraction rerun passed all **15 viability tests** and **16 host tests**, plus three of four startup fallback cases. The timeout fallback case reached its outer 30-second `spawnSync` deadline; a scoped replay passed (**1 passed / 3 filtered skips**, 58.12 s wall). After integrating `main`, the final rerun passed all **35 viability/broker tests**, including all four startup fallback cases, in **74.94 s** wall. The earlier timeout cause is not established, and passing replays are not claimed as a fix.
- Regression command: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test src/infra/child-runtime-viability.async.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Final affected run included that file plus `child-runtime-viability.test.ts` and `process-respawn.runtime-unavailable.test.ts`: **33 passed**, **108.03 s** wall including worker preparation (**84.17 s**); the three tests in the changed file totaled **2.78 s**. This proves launch routing and detection, rather than reproducing the Linux kernel stall duration.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, targeted infra/services test typechecks (**3.8 s / 3.3 s**), changed-file oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Full `pnpm build` with integrated `main` passed in **5m 26.4s**, including declarations and runtime/lazy-boundary checks. The build caught the initial startup-import expansion; the state split removes it. First-head CI caught a type-import cycle in `check-guards-architecture` ([run 44005142337](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44005142337)); the host contract extraction fixes it, and the local Madge guard now reports **0 cycles**. CI then compiled newer `main` lifecycle callers against the extracted contract and found two missing resource-state getters ([run 44007179770](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44007179770)). Integrating `main` and including those existing getters fixes that failure: the full SDK declaration preparation and selected **codex/slack/telegram package boundary compile passed** locally (**111.494 s**). Core types and the cycle guard passed again. A one-line host lint overage was resolved by combining the type exports; final targeted lint/format pass. Subsequent CI exposed the missing `context-state.ts` wrapper inventory entry through eager-import closure and native provisioning tests; adding that runtime source completes the cutover without pulling the host startup factory into low-level workers. After the repair, the three failed files rerun locally with **41 passed / 1 failed / 1 skipped** (**819.47 s** wall): both closure files pass all **24 tests**, and the CI-failing provisioning cases exercised on macOS pass (the unsupported-filesystem cell is platform-skipped). The remaining failure is the additional macOS-only warm/sparse sibling scenario, which hit its existing **120 s** timeout with **246.517 s** observed. No assertion failure identified a functional regression; the timeout cause remains unresolved, and no timeout relaxation or suppression was added. Current-head CI passed in [run 44011585588](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44011585588). The CI watcher reported GREEN with zero pending checks; 21 superseded checks explain the raw GitHub failure rollup. Native landing verified head `718b3368d3986726b1656143b9c35dccbefa5f0c` merged as `df78722789e096c3dfc7154526d67037d6ed4803`.
- `$autoreview`, Codex engine, complete local snapshot against the integrated `b4fc05346afb4d6c88b4ab2e8ae3d1eba380917f` baseline, on the complete final staged snapshot, integrated with `main` at `b4fc05346afb4` and committed as `718b3368d3986`: **scoped-clean through P2**, no remaining accepted findings. Author simplification pass retained only the routing, necessary build boundary, and regression repair. Production **+66 net lines**; tests **+65 net lines**, two new parameterized cases.
- Synchronous runtime probing remains at `src/infra/child-runtime-viability.ts:286`, called only by the synchronous SQLite reader at `src/infra/sqlite-readonly-worker.ts:614`. Readiness and health runtime observations use async preparation and do not reach it. No STOP condition or broker protocol gap.

prs.title: fix: reuse release evidence after waivers and tooling changes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Full Release Validation needlessly reruns completed workloads after a new waiver or a change to trusted release tooling.

## User Impact

With reuse enabled, an initial required run can be reused after its recorded failure is covered by current policy. Accepted retained evidence returns before another child workflow is dispatched. Changing publisher/release-tooling P alone does not invalidate unchanged candidate qualification.

Candidate, coverage, inputs, workload closure, artifact integrity, original producer provenance, and current attempts remain enforced. Missing, expired, incompatible, or unwaived evidence still requires fresh work. Frozen workflows without admitted-P routing are not retrofitted by changing P alone.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Use the existing waiver-aware `policyTargetVersion` path for ordinary discovery, execution-state collection, and strict summary verification—not just receipt recovery.
- Run discovery from admitted P while reading dispatch defaults from frozen Q.
- Permit completed failed receipts to reach existing exact waiver and aggregate-log checks; keep raw failures unchanged.
- Remove publisher identity equality from whole-parent reuse while independently authenticating both publishers and preserving candidate/Q, coverage, inputs, and source digests.
- Keep failed-parent recovery on sealed child receipts. A fresh parent must still complete admission, collection, and final verification successfully.

Integrated current main (`6ba51132e323`) to retain its existing receipt recovery, workload-closure checks, evidence-bound waivers, and independent-Q handling. No duplicate waiver API or policy implementation. Added 95 net test lines with an exact allocation.

## Evidence

- Original cross-P regressions failed on the old base and pass with the fix.
- Existing authenticated ZIP receipt regression now proves ordinary discovery and revalidation reuse a policy-waived failure through the default authenticated log transport, including exact-candidate waivers, and refuse it without current policy. Both review regressions failed before the fixes (missing log reader and missing candidate SHA). The affected four suites passed afterward: 351 tests.
- Real workflow shell regression proves successful reuse returns without a new workflow dispatch, uses admitted P, and preserves frozen-Q input source and candidate version.
- Integrated focused suites: 420 tests passed across seven files (child reuse, qualification/publication consumers, strict summary, execution state, receipt recovery, dispatch wiring, and nightly workflow).
- Staged test-line ratchet passed against current main: +95 net lines, +95 allocation credit; PR diff whitespace check passed.
- Tooling and scripts typechecks, scoped lint, formatting, workflow security checks, and documentation lint passed.
- Independent original review was clean. Integration review found two P2 issues (missing default log reader and candidate SHA); both were fixed with red/green regressions. Follow-up independent review confirmed both resolved with no remaining actionable findings.

Limitations: no authenticated hosted Actions/FRV run was dispatched. Real owners are tested using fixed external-I/O fixtures; shell routing and strict-consumer proofs are separate rather than one hosted end-to-end run. Local ClawSweeper and Codex CLI were unavailable, so independent native review was used without claiming helper-owned isolation.

prs.title: fix: agent session searches stall on large histories
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agent session searches stall on large histories because every query first pages through the complete session inventory.

## User Impact

Agents can search existing conversation text without listing every session first, with the same bounded result shape and visibility rules. No configuration, schema, index, or migration changes are required.

Short CJK substring searches retain their documented behavior. Because timestamps are not indexed, that fallback completes one streaming text pass even after finding matches, retaining only the best `limit + 1` hits and one bounded authorization batch. A miss can still scan the text corpus.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transcript worker now discovers candidates using the existing word FTS index; Gateway visibility owners authorize bounded candidate batches before result limits, applying both current Gateway rules and the tool’s captured restrictions. The tool's inventory paging and per-agent 200-key RPC loops are removed. The embedded Gateway and RPC handler share this owner, while explicit-session search keeps its existing path. Broad search reuses the projection’s admitted store topology instead of rediscovering filesystem stores on each request; configured logical agents still retain their shared-store mapping.

The simplification removes a single-use request adapter and duplicate ordering/visibility plumbing. Production delta is **+298 lines total: +253 authored and +45 generated predicates**; authored code is reduced from the earlier +261 proposal, and tests remove 145 net lines. The initial simplification removed 45 authored lines; preserving the pre-existing pinned caller-policy boundary adds 37 back. Admitted-topology reuse removes three more runtime lines, and keeping its store targets out of the row-selection input contract adds three type-only lines. The remaining growth implements the bounded worker cursor and Gateway authorization boundary that replace **85 inventory pages plus 90 search RPCs** per search on the synthetic fixture. No new cache or session-row projection optimization is included.

Integration note: #200076 adds a cold-archive exclusion predicate to the same query kernel. This change moves that kernel from `session-transcript-search.ts` to `session-transcript-search.worker.ts`; preserve that predicate there when integrating whichever PR lands second. #160237 shares the scope test file but changes the separate UI search path.

## Evidence

The 17,000-session synthetic fixture uses 8 agents, 13,700 archived metadata rows, 30 active runs, and one indexed message per session. It contains no production data. Two baseline controls and candidate runs use 2 warmups and 5 measured searches, with timing and sampled main-thread JS allocation measured separately.

| Query | Baseline A1 / A2 median | Final candidate | Main-thread CPU before → after | Allocation before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Word | 2,641 / 2,719 ms | 26.9 ms | 2,227–2,365 → 8.8 ms | 1.982–1.990 GB → 3.79 MB |
| Short CJK | 2,700 / 2,610 ms | 68.4 ms | 2,134–2,178 → 15.0 ms | 1.980–1.981 GB → 3.53 MB |

Both candidate paths use **0 inventory pages / 0 inventory rows / 1 search RPC**, versus **85 / 17,000 / 90**. Final p95 is 29.5 ms (word) and 73.2 ms (CJK). This was a busy shared host; no quiet-host claim. Measurements exercise the real tool, embedded Gateway and native worker, not a remote model round-trip. The fixture represents session cardinality, not a 35-GiB database or a filesystem-scale workload.

Complete top-N result digests match baseline and candidate, including snippets and flags:

- Word: `378af0fc548a5b970756d143775fbf73a7cd00757250ade78ed5e305f16eca9b`
- CJK: `be44535ac95c4887e43eaf52c811c8efdf61821a7d3868f8c330f816f4452375`
- Dense word: `2475ff7a16b61ce3a7675cb156dfa84cf306b4529ebcf5d48832c89f30ce1cbd`
- Miss: `753826edc7256a0e891a56ed820740d2682753e75128c7e72988ec7949b25ee9`

Focused tool/protocol/native-search/Gateway tests pass, including no inventory paging, cross-agent and operator privacy, sandbox/tree boundaries, shared stores, and a CJK match at the end of the text rows that must enter the timestamp-ordered top-N. The no-paging regression fails on the exact parent. The final topology rerun passes 36 Gateway/embedded tests; the selection fixture consumer passes 6 tests and the updated selection suite passes 8. The 15 prompt-stability tests, affected UI browser test, and real-Gateway UI-e2e test pass. Codex autoreview reports no actionable P0–P2 findings.

The final-head `pnpm check:changed` run passes every gate except the inherited dead-export check, including all typecheck, format, lint and database-worker guards. The dead-export gate has 116 unique findings, all reproduced among 121 findings on exact parent `aeabca2e109167fe9dbc0037fd698848a2378b63`; no new dead-export findings. Three replay-session-state re-exports are attributable to `472cd0a2f542599eea763f013eba2d34033ca25f`; the remaining entries have exact-parent reproduction without individual introduction attribution. These are inherited main regressions, not passing checks. CI exposed two stale inventory-shaped consumer suites. Converting the visibility fixture to real indexed search also exposed a lost pinned caller-policy restriction; that regression fails on the first PR head with a foreign hit and now passes. The repaired 62-test focused run, affected UI browser and real-Gateway UI-e2e tests, and fresh Codex review pass. CI also required the static identity-pin allowance to shrink 12→8; the canonical generator lowers that single entry. No runtime configuration changed. Final-head CI run 44006736986 has the heartbeat build-test timeout described below; ClawSweeper revision 2 reviewed final head `32a654caeaad813b75c5f8a1be703085eed7aedd` with zero open items ([review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200355#issuecomment-6936101577)); both prior items are addressed in the [numbered response](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200355#issuecomment-6936669842).

A previous-head CI build-graph timeout also reproduces on exact parent `aeabca2e109167fe9dbc0037fd698848a2378b63`: the state lease heartbeat optional-import test reaches its 60-second timeout. The 60-second heartbeat build test originated in #191272 (`c3b3d56c37c90`), and #198194 generalized it; the exact source of build-time variance remains unproven. The same parent also fails the transcript-worker graph guard (623 forbidden Gateway inputs); this branch has the same existing import path plus the new recall module. These are recorded main regressions, not passing proof. Final hosted CI evaluates the current merge context.

On the exact CI parent `f57dbb4ff67efb110bed6568f49ea008bc43c4a2`, the full build-graph file passes under the local default runtime, and the isolated heartbeat case passes under both default and Bun runtimes. The isolated case also passes on tested merge `7fe920ad2bf412ff9100e77aa135035678dc548c`. These passing replays are not a fix. Independent attribution now also compares the complete heartbeat dependency closure: all 559 source inputs, plus the test and build configuration, are identical between that CI parent and tested merge. Together with the exact original-parent timeout reproduction, this qualifies the authorized inherited-only landing exception. The automated CI table remains `unknown` because its scheduled-main comparison did not execute this heartbeat case. The timeout is an inherited main regression requiring follow-up, and failed hosted CI is not reported as green.

prs.title: fix(ios): approval alerts retain an earlier ID role
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes iOS approval notifications continuing to use an earlier OpenClaw ID role after the member's access changes.

## User Impact

New approval alerts follow current ID membership, permissions, and request visibility. Separately paired local devices keep their local permissions, and cleanup notifications can still dismiss earlier prompts. No new configuration is required. Earlier preview native pairings without ID attribution must be removed and paired again through OpenClaw ID before reuse; existing local approvals are not reassigned automatically.

## Why This Change Was Made

The iOS delivery owner now evaluates the complete approval record using current pairing, membership, and session facts, then checks again when the push provider starts. Native operator pairing saves ID attribution before installing its approval, including tokenless connections.

If saving attribution succeeds but a same-key ID regrant later fails, that device can remain bound to ID and require owner recovery. This conservative outcome does not grant additional access; unchanged local reconnects are unaffected.

## Evidence

- 79 focused tests passed: approval push policy, native authentication/pairing retry, and direct/relay APNs behavior. Reused passing evidence for 156 unchanged consumer checks.

The member received the pre-downgrade alert; afterward, exactly the same new approval reached an independent local device once and the member zero times through final shutdown. ## Summary

The Doctor admission fixture installed an IPC message listener in every child that inherited its preload. Scope request observation to the canonical SQLite readonly worker marker so unrelated IPC children retain their normal listener state. Keep the native SQLite proxy, wrong-path preflight, and PID-bound guard witness active for every child.

The regression completes a real readonly session and verifies its row, then checks an unrelated IPC child exits cleanly with no message listener and still writes the SQLite guard witness. Fixture disposal verifies the real session requests.

## Validation

- Baseline `43c2926ba69479fdc68f5fccb4fd3a089763c9fb`: [hosted Node regression](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43984176652) completed all 17 cases: 16 passed; the new case failed at `expect(listeners).toBe(0)`, receiving 1 after the session, exit, and witness checks passed.

prs.title: feat: add WhatsApp phone-code login
prs.body:
Closes #85867

## Problem and behavior

Users who cannot scan a QR code need a way to link WhatsApp from the CLI. `openclaw channels login --channel whatsapp` now offers **Scan QR code** (the default) or **Link with phone number**. Phone linking accepts an international number and displays the code to enter in WhatsApp’s Linked Devices screen.

The WhatsApp plugin owns this flow, including number validation, socket readiness, pairing restarts, and cleanup of incomplete managed credentials. Completed credentials are preserved across the native post-pairing restart.

## Review repairs

Phone-code sockets use Baileys’ maintained `Browsers.macOS("Chrome")` profile for both the initial socket and replacements. This follows [VishalJ99’s physical iPhone report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101294#issuecomment-5837741000): the custom profile failed, and the maintained profile linked successfully. QR, startup, and ordinary reconnect sockets retain their existing profile. Phone-code linking uses the Mac OS/Chrome companion identity.

Ordinary sockets log credential-save failures and remain connected. Guarded or persistence-observed sockets abort on failure, so interactive login cannot report success before its credentials and keys are saved. Setup authority checks remain active before guarded writes.

The login tests are split into general login, phone-code login, and recovery suites with shared fixtures. Existing cases are preserved; regressions cover the initial/replacement profile and ordinary, guarded, error-observed, and task-observed save failures.

## Validation

Rebased onto main `f17c94115978d10e0702dd48170464a1f4c84dc0`. All 19 original commits remain separate, with their author identities, author dates, and complete messages preserved. Head: `6d36f73327c9eabe62a6f46a2540161b9cf12906`.

- Full `pnpm build` passed remotely in 3m45.5s on Node 24.22.1. This ran on `cfd75523dc575453ce4b43a7d9d69192a5b87548`; the final head changes only one test fixture and its test-line allocation. Production files are identical.
- On the final head, all 205 tests in 31 WhatsApp files passed, including phone-code login, QR recovery, credential persistence, socket restarts, auth-path guards, and bounded last-route settlement. All 20 channel catalog contract tests passed. Runner wall time: 60.24s for WhatsApp and 59.68s for the catalog contract, including setup. PR CI seconds remain pending.
- The WhatsApp package typecheck passed after `pnpm build:plugin-sdk:dts`. Focused typed lint passed with no warnings or errors.
- Formatting, whitespace, and the test-line budget check passed. The allocation records 1,598 lines above the 400-line allowance for pairing, persistence, restart, cleanup, and preserved session/controller coverage.
- An independent read-only conflict review inspected the original and rebased ranges plus the integration changes. Its two P2 findings—unused imports and a missing synchronous socket-close test case—were repaired and covered by the final checks. The final comparison also preserved the PR's catalog label and regenerated lockfile.

Remote proof: [Blacksmith Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43771912090), lease `tbx_01m7gpqfh7e8ypbzsrm2ktz0ta`, with 4 CPUs and about 15 GiB RAM. The Crabbox wrapper verified the selected source and completed the final checks with exit code 0.

Exact-head live validation remains outstanding for phone pairing and its native restart, QR login, existing linked-session startup, and existing-account upgrade behavior. The reported physical iPhone success applies to an earlier candidate with the selected browser profile. PR CI results for this head are not yet verified.
