prs.title: fix(pr): avoid disk-heavy exports during review and merge preparation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PR review and merge preparation can read gigabytes and stall the host while exporting only a few wrapper files from a partial clone. `git archive` builds a whole-tree index before filtering paths, and its cache-tree update can fetch every promised blob.

## User Impact

Maintainers can prepare PRs without scanning unrelated source trees or hydrating unrelated files. No configuration or repository maintenance is required; there is no end-user behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

All three revision exports now share a literal-path tree listing and one `git cat-file --batch` process. A disposable index containing only the selected entries lets Git batch missing blobs through its existing promisor routing; the working index remains unchanged. The standalone exporter is obtained from the authenticated revision and independently verified before execution. Existing provenance, source-byte, mode, and lifetime checks remain. Frozen dependency installation still exports its required full source tree. The wrapper's revision comparison also scopes its existing single tree walk to the requested components.

The contract is raw Git bytes, executable modes, and symlinks; archive attributes and checkout filters cannot transform code past the existing independent verification. Runtime production code grows by 63 lines to replace three archive pipelines with one shared decoder and its bootstrap qualification. No new cache, configuration, dependency, or schema is added.

## Evidence

A synthetic 62,000-file / 1.1 GB repository reproduces both expensive cold reads and eager partial-clone hydration, without delta chains. It has 357 packs, 341 promisor markers, and no multi-pack-index or commit graph. Five interleaved A/B pairs per state follow two A/A controls. Exported bytes and modes match the old archive output.

| Median | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Cold physical input | 1,121,357,824 B | 2,940,928 B |
| Cold wall / CPU | 252.3 / 213.6 ms | 87.2 / 73.7 ms |
| Cold peak child RSS | 58.7 MB | 37.0 MB |
| Warm wall / CPU | 52.1 / 51.9 ms | 28.5 / 28.7 ms |
| Warm peak child RSS | 97.8 MB | 12.7 MB |
| Populated packed-object accesses | 629 | 6 |
| Fresh partial clone fetched packs | 1,117,142,032 B | 70 B |
| Fresh partial wall / CPU | 85.809 / 116.283 s | 0.047 / 0.042 s |
| Fresh partial peak child RSS | 1,166.3 MB | 37.0 MB |

Separate allocator instrumentation measured 24.4 MB → 9.9–10.2 MB of cumulative requested bytes. Calls rose from 7,032 to 8,092–8,101 with the added Git index processes; this instrumentation was excluded from timing runs. Linux Docker/Git 2.39.5 supplied physical I/O measurements; Git 2.56 on macOS independently reproduced hydration. These are synthetic results, not production latency claims or btrfs measurements. The host was loaded: partial-clone A/A controls took 69.9 and 50.1 seconds; cold controls took 0.629 and 0.204 seconds. Cold runs followed partial runs, so reported child RSS includes the harness's fork/startup memory floor. Fresh partial-clone physical input counters were cache-confounded, so transferred pack bytes are reported separately. All table values are from the final batched exporter.

The committed benchmark is `python3 scripts/perf/pr-export-tree.py NEW_DIRECTORY --samples 5 --states warm partial cold` (cold requires Linux). Trace2 identifies `fetch_count:62000` inside archive index preparation; the filtered archive tree walk itself took only 17 ms in the macOS reproduction. Git's relevant owners are [`archive.c`](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.56.0/archive.c), [`unpack-trees.c`](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.56.0/unpack-trees.c), and [`cache-tree.c`](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.56.0/cache-tree.c).

Regression proof covers exact exported sets, binary/empty/unusual filenames, executable modes and symlinks; selected revision comparison is bounded to four packed-object reads and selected export to nine. The revision bound fails on the original script (105 reads). A real-wrapper partial-clone test fails before the fix because the archive fetches unrelated content, then passes with the exporter. Focused wrapper tests also cover exporter qualification, corrupt producers, retained anchors and rejection of altered frozen install source before package hooks. The dependency-cache suite and wrapper inventory check passed. A cold-clone regression exposed per-object lazy-fetch fanout in the first PR head; the final exporter now performs exactly one fetch for both selected and full-source exports, leaves the 100 unrelated fixture blobs missing, and preserves the working index byte-for-byte. The new assertion fails on the first PR head (four fetches instead of one).

Codex autoreview is clean through P2. Changed-test lint and targeted typechecks pass. `pnpm check:changed` found five unrelated dead exports, reproduced by `pnpm deadcode:exports` on the exact parent c3baf0d8484bd6404dc2164912b12c9263b81c9e: the two Slack exports originate in abdc09f135501; the unused browser-approval export in 1ce9df608b43b (#200088); the last external consumers of the tool-card and chat-history exports were deleted by c3baf0d8484bd (#199111). These are existing main regressions, not ignored noise. The final changed-file run passes every other gate, including lint, formatting and targeted typechecks; the initial test lint violation was corrected. One workflow-binding sibling test suffered an unreproduced Bun process-launch crash; its exact isolated replay passed. That replay is not claimed as a repair.

prs.title: improve(ci): avoid duplicate release source guard scans
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Release qualification's combined source check runs the full database-first legacy-store scan twice: once during fail-fast preflight and again at the end of architecture checks.

## User Impact

No user-facing behavior changes. Developers and release qualification retain the same checks, but a combined architecture run performs one full legacy-store scan instead of two. Standalone architecture and policy-only invocations still enforce the guard. No migration or action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the early preflight guard and share the remaining architecture chain through a package script. The existing check orchestrator selects that chain only when its ordered preflight stage also runs successfully. A failed preflight still stops before typechecking; no cache, environment flag, parallel runner, or new planner is added.

Historical intent is preserved: commit 50c82b3020064d553ff0110c668b465325cff569 wired the guard into both preflight and standalone architecture. This removes only their duplicate composition, not either independent entry point.

## Evidence

- Production orchestrator regression: on the base, the combined invocation records **two** actual package-script guard leaves and fails the new assertion; with this change it records **one**. Full, non-lint, preflight-only and policy-only modes retain one guard, standalone architecture retains one, and an injected preflight exit 7 prevents typechecking.
- Focused suites: **84 tests passed** across check orchestration, architecture environment, and legacy-store checks. Targeted TypeScript, scoped script/test lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Measured existing workload: [npm qualification job 133761031368](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43995795589/job/133761031368) ran the guard at 02:03:53–02:08:28 UTC, then again at **02:31:00.701–02:31:51.175 UTC (50.474 s)** on November 17. The first overlaps other preflight work; only the trailing copy is removed.
- **No measured patched-host or whole-FRV speedup claim.** About 50 s is a log-based per-job opportunity, not a benchmark promise. Other qualification jobs/independent CI can dominate the parent barrier, yielding zero parent improvement. Setup, job count, runner allocation and dependency barriers are unchanged, so this does not trade a new queue/setup cost for less aggregate work.
- Simplification: production +9/-3; tests +39/-1 against the merge base. Necessary growth keeps standalone/fail-fast coverage and tests the duplicate at the production orchestration boundary. No redundant test-only production hooks.

Hosted exact-head CI and ClawSweeper review are pending; this PR is not yet claimed review-ready.

prs.title: fix(codex): preserve prompt projection through quota fallback
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Beta qualification exposed two failures in the real-Gateway quota path: inherited HTTP proxies intercepted the fixture's loopback provider, and native-to-embedded fallback attempted to freeze the current model prompt after native dispatch had already marked the user turn sent. The latter reproduced in all three quota storage-fault cases before fault injection.

## User Impact

Native provider fallback retains the canonical hook-enriched current user input without duplicating native conversation history or workspace policy. Transcript annotations continue to bind to the same admitted turn after its recorder freezes that projection. The quota fixture reaches its owned loopback provider without changing external proxy routing.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Capture through the existing transcript recorder immediately before native turn/start; preserve the existing late-capture guard.
- Let the annotation owner follow only the exact recorder-owned projection metadata addition on the same admission and message. Edits, retargeting, and authority invalidation remain rejected.
- Append loopback exclusions to both inherited no-proxy environment spellings in the fixture.
- Add one database-backed native regression and route it through the existing database-worker test project. No new state owner, schema, retry, timeout, dependency, or public SDK API.

## Evidence

- New pre-dispatch projection regression fails on the original source and passes with the repair. It checks hook enrichment, exclusion of older history, native mirror annotation, and idempotent capture after native acceptance.
- Final annotation suite: 22/22 pass. Native protocol/projection tests: 8/8 pass. Plugin-refresh siblings: 5/5 pass.
- All three previously failing real-Gateway quota storage-fault cases pass: claim-write I/O, result-write I/O, and claim-write constraint failures. Each exercises the formerly failing automatic native-to-embedded fallback; operational writes preserve healthy fallback and constraint failures refuse admission.
- Canonical core, extension production, and extension test typechecks pass; five-file type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. CI found an incomplete target type in the new regression fixture; the fixture now uses a concrete target, and its focused replay and lint pass. A direct package-boundary compiler invocation produced configuration/rootDir errors and is not used as qualification; the canonical checks above replace it.
- Original controlUi:true fresh saved-clear admission passes. Full local browser proof remains blocked by missing libatk and is not claimed. Exact-head PR CI and exact-candidate FRV remain required.
- Independent review waived by the release owner. Scoped self-review and simplification retain the existing recorder/annotation owners and preserve invalidation checks.

prs.title: fix(ci): keep Boat quota exhaustion from blocking tests
prs.body:
Closes #200228

## What Problem This Solves

Whole-run Boat routing can exhaust the rolling sandbox-start allowance and fail CI before any tests execute, even while compute credit remains.

## User Impact

CI keeps hybrid capacity for overflow and can request one hosted retry when Boat's start limit is the only workload failure. Paid overflow remains disabled. The repository currently remains on `hybrid`; activating the new mixed policy uses the existing `boat` backend setting after validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary admitted runs send at most 20 of their longest eligible Node rows to Boat. Preflight checks the scoped account's day/hour/minute limits, keeps 20% headroom, and paces starts against the daily allowance. Unknown or exhausted capacity selects no Boat jobs. Existing memory classes, CPU limits, prepared-workspace exceptions, and explicit qualification routing remain intact.

The quota check is a snapshot, not an atomic account-wide reservation. A metadata-only recovery workflow covers overlapping runs: it accepts only first-attempt, current-head, same-repository runs whose failed workloads all stopped in Boat setup with a sandbox-start plan-limit annotation. Real test failures and second attempts are not retried.

## Evidence

- Incident: [CI run 43847874702](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43847874702) had 21 Boat runner-setup failures with the daily-start-limit annotation, plus the aggregate gate failure.
- Native replay exercised the production preflight with available, exhausted, malformed, and mismatched-account responses. Admission and recovery checks passed, including hourly/minute recovery, unrelated plan-limit rejection, stale heads, and an existing retry.
- `node scripts/check-workflows.mts` passed: pinned actionlint, zizmor, generated Git-owner check, composite-action interpolation check, and conflict-marker check.
- Commit hook formatting, line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local ClawSweeper completed reviews of `ed770a5d5189..89b0056dbd3b`, `89b0056dbd3b..9c1f57b5f193`, and the workflow-size repair `9c1f57b5f193..a48316f10de1`. Independent source review also passed.
- [Prior-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43941078264) completed for `9c1f57b5f193089fad0b9db0009566d5953370ec`: 219 jobs passed, 36 failed, 4 were cancelled, and 11 skipped. Preflight and build-artifacts passed; logs confirm the requested checkout SHA. Broad failures have not all been attributed to a baseline.
- That run exposed a regression in this patch: `ci.yml` exceeded the 480,000-byte guard. `a48316f10de1` extracts the unchanged runner-profile shell body into the trusted harness, including both harness checkout routes. The workflow is now 475,552 bytes. All 80 native routing parity cases, Bash syntax, workflow validation, and commit hooks passed. This local proof does not make the prior CI run green or establish exact-head hosted coverage.
- [Exact-head preparation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43978136807) at `a48316f10de1d0ebb6eb17a57c3500e6ea6ca479`: preflight executed the extracted script; build-artifacts, production/test typechecks, and all three changed-file jobs passed. Focused suites passed: capacity, recovery, Boat runtime (28), planning (815), workflow guards including size (226), workflow completion (124), portable scripts (140; 3 skipped), and native launch (30).
- The same run reported the same three unused symbols and two unused fixtures as [the earlier dependency check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43941078264/job/133559865983); their source files are unchanged by this patch. This is matching prior-run evidence, not a green dependency check or independent main-baseline reproduction. Remaining manual work was cancelled once preparation passed and normal PR CI started, to avoid duplicate execution.
- [Prior PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43979905320) finished with 58 successful jobs. Its only workload failure was `oxc/no-map-spread` in the added shard fixture. `b30363e1a660` uses `Object.assign` on the newly created rows, preserving fixture values. The pinned lint rule rejects the prior source and accepts the correction; formatting and commit hooks pass. Local ClawSweeper reviewed `a48316f10de1..b30363e1a660` with no findings and security cleared.
- [Current PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44009564186) is running for `b30363e1a66006052e22e68ba57568d67114fd24`. The earlier [main-tier request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43977841442) was rejected in preflight because that tier requires a same-revision main target; it ran no build or tests.
- Focused Blacksmith proof was attempted through the maintained wrapper. Its allocation queued and was stopped before tests; [the workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43977679855) is confirmed cancelled and the Testbox completed. No test success is claimed from that attempt.
- Pending: normal PR CI and required landing gates; `ci-swift-cache-lifetime.test.ts` execution was not established by this scoped run. This local checkout has no qualified dependency install; the shared installation was preserved. The new recovery workflow becomes active only after default-branch publication, so its live retry effect is not yet qualified.

prs.title: fix(ci): isolate simple-completion diagnostics from provider hooks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes four simple-completion diagnostics tests failing in a shared worker after another fixture installs provider hooks.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. The diagnostics tests can exercise their request lifecycle without inheriting another fixture’s provider runtime.

## Why This Change Was Made

Skipping provider bootstrap does not remove an already installed process-wide transport host. The fixture now uses the existing scoped host API around each completion, retaining real preparation and lifecycle logic and deterministic completion outcomes. Existing assertions are unchanged.

## Evidence

- [Scheduled main CI failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43858232113/job/133268713317), at `97427b800378e88d1f58de00a7af6ddad1172440`: four failures from an inherited provider mock missing `resolveProviderStreamFn`.
- Local Node 26.13 regression: the same pinned 15-file order produces **80 passed / 4 failed** with the original fixture and **84 passed** with this patch. File order was compared directly; diagnostics runs last. The shorter two- and three-file subsets did not reproduce the leak.
- Prompt serialization, success, returned errors, thrown errors, duplicate usage, and activity cleanup assertions remain intact.
- Targeted oxlint, oxfmt, and `core.test.agents-root` typecheck passed.

prs.title: improve(ui): Cmd+K lists named settings first and improves session search
prs.body:
Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1a5cfb8d-a446-47ff-bd14-38afb5b63bf2)

## What Problem This Solves

Searching for a setting in Cmd+K buries it below any session that mentions the same word, and archived sessions never show up at all.

## User Impact

User impact: typing a setting or command name in Cmd+K shows it first, sessions follow newest first, and archived sessions whose title matches appear in their own muted "Archived" group (at most three) instead of being missing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Results now follow intent instead of a single match score:

1. Settings and commands whose name matches the query.
2. Sessions: an exact match first, then newest first. Where a word falls inside a sentence-like session title no longer changes the order.
3. Archived: up to three archived sessions whose title matches, newest first, muted. A separate best-effort `sessions.list` call with `archived: true` and `searchTitlesOnly: true` supplies them. Live results appear without waiting for that lookup; a failed archive lookup only omits archived rows until the next search.
4. More results: commands, settings, plugins, skills and models that match only by description or keywords, in their own group so they cannot crowd the top.
5. In messages: transcript hits, unchanged.

Archived message text is still not searched; the existing palette note about that remains. The Sessions filter tab counts active and archived sessions together.

## Evidence

Scenario: query `appearance` with three active and two archived matching sessions. Control UI E2E harness with a mocked Gateway and fixture sessions, 1280×900, light theme. Before: `main` at 48cd549. After: this branch at 9ea31d4. Dark theme was also checked.

### Clean comparison

![Before: three sessions listed above the Appearance setting; no archived sessions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f1fa358-4627-468f-90ab-3a0fb754fe68)

![After: Appearance setting first, then three sessions, then two muted archived sessions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b5a5f1e-34b1-4bea-be7e-6c63547c0217)

### Annotated comparison

![Before, annotated: sessions listed first, Appearance setting after sessions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d58bb8a9-97f9-4d4e-80ca-07311f83730e)

![After, annotated: named setting first; archived sessions in their own muted group](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d70d5675-01a1-4472-a732-399fb567690d)

Checks:

- Command palette unit suites: 146 tests passed, including new ordering and archived-group cases.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint on changed files and `pnpm lint:ui:styles` passed.
- Opening an archived result navigates to the session's existing archived view with its Unarchive action (verified in the same harness).
- Local autoreview (Codex, gpt-6.1-sol) on branch range 48cd549..9ea31d4 at P1: scoped-clean, no findings.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

<!-- openclaw-publication:23ab8be0-c4c2-4026-8eae-5a05aa62cd83 -->

## Maintainer repair and verification

The repair in `8f1d76d648b` preserves this design and fixes three result-handling defects:

- A setting-name match stays ahead of description matches before the catalog's ten-result cap. The name-match flag is computed once per item.
- Available live results appear while archived search is pending. Later archived results preserve the item already selected with the keyboard.
- Archived title matching happens in the existing Gateway filter before pagination, so ten newer model/provider matches cannot hide an older matching title. The optional `sessions.list.searchTitlesOnly` parameter defaults to the existing search behavior. Query identity and the generated runtime validator include it. No database migration or saved-preference change is involved.

The two client regressions and the Gateway filtering regression failed before the repair. Validation covered 131 palette tests, 10 query-ownership tests and 7 Gateway filter tests; the four affected catalog cases and lint passed again after the final catalog cleanup. Core, UI and selected test typechecks passed, as did the official validator-generation check and an independent P0–P2 review.

A real isolated Gateway, built from the repaired sources, returned:

| Query | Page size | Total matches |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Existing broad search | 10 | 13 |
| Title-only search | 1 | 1 |
| Explicit `searchTitlesOnly: false` | 10 | 13 |

The title-only result was the intended older conversation. The first RPC attempt exposed the missing compiled validator in the repair; regenerating it with the official owner and rebuilding fixed that rejection. No provider or model execution was needed. Private-row exclusion was checked at the existing filter owner, not with a separate live private-identity RPC.

The captures below compare the original PR with the repair while the archive lookup is held, then show the completed results. They use the real Control UI with a scripted Gateway; the real RPC check above is separate. All data is synthetic.

![Original PR: live results wait for the archived lookup](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1630fa75-a482-4e41-bc2e-f42742185f97)

![Repaired: live results are available while archived search waits](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/46cfe305-cd68-46c5-8cb3-294d93b029b2)

![Repaired: archived results join without replacing the live results](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a176ab0-a4fd-4b2a-9a14-fe3e103835ea)

prs.title: fix(ios): keep Talk replies below the spoken turn that prompted them
prs.body: Closes #197129 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: iOS Talk sometimes saves the assistant's reply above the user's spoken turn when speech transcription finishes after the reply transcript. ## User Impact User impact: client-owned realtime Talk sessions preserve spoken-turn order when transcript finals arrive out of order. No settings change is required. ## Why This Change Was Made - Reserve each turn's place when it starts, then persist completed transcripts in that order. - Interleaved frameless fragments retain their open reservation. An explicit audio-cleared interruption or empty completion releases an unfinished reply without saving empty text. - A five-second timeout abandons only the oldest blocker; newer unfinished turns retain their own grace period. Stop still flushes held transcripts immediately. Consult gives the current blocker its remaining grace period, then releases stalled entries without following successive timers. - Both standard OpenAI and frameless events are covered. Web Talk is unchanged. ## Evidence ### Maintainer verification — November 16 I repeated the ordering test through the native iOS client and a real, isolated Gateway, then opened the stored conversation in the normal app. - Main `48440fc199d`: the assistant row was saved first, followed by the user's question. - PR `c8a12ebd530`: the same out-of-order final events were saved as user, then assistant. - Both used Gateway `d29fad4e3e6`. Session/voice metadata was created through the owning API; no transcript rows were inserted directly. - My only source change is test formatting in `54bc3850c9b`. All four PR-touched files match the final simulator candidate. All **18 focused native tests passed again**, as did configured SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint. The 63 raw JSON test expressions are unchanged. - The source review found no remaining actionable issue in ordering, interruption, timeout release, or bounded consult flushing. This proves scripted native data-channel events → authenticated Gateway RPC → durable history → normal-app readback. It does **not** claim physical microphone, live-provider, or `talk.client.create` coverage. The videos show the stored result, not event injection; both use the same crop and retain normal playback speed. **Current CI qualification:** [CI run 44004407062](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44004407062) failed its general screenshot test because the Mermaid document did not become ready and its loading watchdog expired. The test then could not find the diagram button. The exact CI merge changes only the two realtime Voice files and their two tests; the screenshot test, chat/diagram rendering, fixture and build owners are identical to the tested main parent. This test does not exercise Talk. The failure remains recorded; I am treating it as unrelated to this PR, not claiming a green screenshot run or a repaired Mermaid issue. The native ordering tests and real-Gateway proof above pass. | Main | PR | | --- | --- | | ![Main: assistant response precedes the user question](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d91d95e-86fe-486b-9a24-203746ca01b2) | ![PR: user question precedes the assistant response](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1fb9d62a-8d89-459d-912f-15bf2e9f557e) | Before video: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/243238fc-0af6-4536-87c2-781c53bfd6d3 After video: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7773a676-c81e-4f46-b911-11a348d1dab8 ### Consult ordering follow-up (November 15) Native iPhone after-fix capture from the OpenAI/WebRTC retest on OC 102505: the spoken question appears above the consult preamble. The final answer is not shown. This capture precedes the bounded-wait refinement, whose 15-test simulator result is recorded below. - Previous-head regression: delayed question saved after the consult preamble; expected question first. - Physical OpenAI/WebRTC iPhone retest: question appeared before “Let me check that for you,” confirmed by the tester. This capture did not show the final consult answer. - Independent reviews identified successive-timer waiting in the initial repair. Consult now waits only for the hold present when flushing starts, then uses the existing stalled-turn fallback. Stop and the production five-second timeout are unchanged. - Controlled successive-timer red: 1 test, 1 failure (flush still waiting after the first expiry). Bounded fix: **15 XCTest tests, zero failures**, lint enabled, Xcode 27.2. Includes delayed question/preamble, stalled flush, stop, timeout rearming and interruption coverage. `git diff --check` passed. - [Sanitized evidence and AI-assisted session log](https://gist.github.com/Marvinthebored/815e768291fa4de9cf75915c2b722c7e). The device retest preceded the bounded-wait refinement; the final refinement has simulator coverage above. ### Controlled timeout regression (November 14 follow-up) Replaced the overlapping-timeout test's 600/700 ms sleeps with a controlled sleeper and explicit timer-registration/transcript-delivery synchronization. Production sleep and the five-second default remain unchanged. Lint-enabled iOS simulator validation, one selected integration test per variant: - Old timeout callback (`releaseHeld`): FAIL, saved `A1., A2., U2.` instead of `A1., U2., A2.` (5.652 s). - Fixed callback (`expireHoldingTurn`): PASS, 1 test, 0 failures (0.138 s). - Independent review: no actionable findings; `git diff --check` passes. This follow-up validates deterministic timeout handling. The existing scripted native-to-Gateway proof below remains distinct from a live provider WebRTC session. The original iPhone reproduction saved the assistant reply above the user's earlier speech: **Focused simulator validation, Xcode 27.2, lint enabled:** four follow-up regressions fail on the prior PR head (five assertions). With this change, 21 XCTest tests and five Swift Testing tests pass. Coverage includes late interleaved fragments, explicit interruption, empty completion, overlapping timeout windows, stop, consult, event decoding, and transcript writes. `git diff --check` passes. **Real Gateway persistence proof, November 14:** a native simulator XCTest fed scripted frameless events through `TalkRealtimeWebRTCSession` and a real `GatewayNodeSession`, then read `chat.history` from an isolated Gateway. The assistant final arrived before the user final, with a late user fragment interleaved. A fresh session and voice ID prevented reuse of earlier writes. The readback contained exactly two new rows: ```text seq role text recordTimestampMs 1 user Proof question R6. 1794664438173 2 assistant Proof answer R6. 1794664438173 Native XCTest: 1 passed, 0 failures; lint enabled. ``` This demonstrates native event-to-Gateway persistence with scripted events, not a live microphone or physical-phone test of the fixed build. Independent read-only Codex review of the final four-file follow-up found no actionable defects; it covered interruption, timeout rearming, empty completion, and interleaved fragments. The reviewer did not run tests. Prior-head CI failed in `OpenClawSnapshotUITests.testReleaseChatScreenshot`: the Mermaid diagram button did not reappear after preview dismissal. Settings passed. Attribution to main or a flake has not been established; this is not claimed as passing CI. AI-assisted: implemented and tested with OpenClaw and independently reviewed with Codex, directed by @Marvinthebored.

prs.title: fix: preserve gateway administrator permissions across native UI clients
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An authenticated native-app administrator could receive caller-scoped automation inventory and “not found” for another conversation’s job, despite holding Gateway admin authority. The invariant is **same authenticated administrator, same effective scopes and policy, same Gateway permissions**, regardless of Control UI or native UI client. Rendering features remain separate.

## User Impact

User impact: native UI administrators can inspect and repair existing automations across conversations with the same effective scopes and policy as browser administrators. Caller-only caps, requester isolation, and live revocation remain enforced. The [maintainer direction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194443#issuecomment-6935746079) endorses native UI administrator parity; separate current-head sensitive-security approval remains required.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuse shared authenticated UI-admin classification for fresh-turn automation admission and durable recovery, without labeling native clients as Control UI or granting direct-local execution.
- Retain recorded automation-admin delegation across scheduled recovery and repair/notice continuations. Legacy browser grants remain compatible; historical native snapshots without recorded delegation are not upgraded.
- Preserve scope intersections, principal-only snapshot contracts, exact-device reconnect custody, requester identity, and the existing authorization gates for provider-review acknowledgment, dashboard reads, task suggestions, and signed-in mentions.
- Retain deployment caller caps, tool policy, fresh/direct-turn and exact-run binding, and live authority/revocation checks through the final effect. Browser origin checks and transport-specific rendering remain separate.

## Evidence

### Current-main integration and verification — November 17, 2026

Current head: `f31e6ff01f633fa825ad97c0045567506b3ac7d1`. Integrated main: `4cbd215af463775faa6807aea90621292b28af15`.

- Updated the existing contributor branch through the supported signed, ancestry-preserving integration route. Original contributor commits are preserved; hosted ancestry was not replaced.
- Resolved six integration conflicts while preserving the canonical extracted grant-type owner, current-main recovery claim/policy separation, reconnect refusal checks, requester restrictions, and the private Control-UI-only Template Add route. The generic current-main regression that retires the requester claim and then tests an allowed child write plus a rejected revoked final write remains intact, alongside the separate native cron final-effect tests.
- **Exact-head secretless AWS validation passed:** full `pnpm build` (Gateway, public declarations, and Control UI); **235 tests in 10 files across three Vitest shards**; core typecheck plus the four affected gateway-root, gateway-methods, services-cron, and root-tooling test type graphs; targeted lint for all 32 changed code files; formatting for 33 changed supported files; whitespace checks; and a final unchanged tracked-tree check. The focused tests took 248.99 seconds. These are fixture-authenticated production-boundary tests, not a new native-app/real-model E2E claim. No contributor code ran on the maintainer host.
- The successful build emitted advisory Control UI bundle-budget overruns. These warnings are not represented as a passing bundle-budget check; no size budgets or baselines were changed.
- Fresh independent **canonical autoreview, Codex, P0–P2**, reviewed the complete committed range from the integrated main to this exact head: **scoped-clean, no actionable findings**. Static review is separate from the runtime checks above.
- The current per-change test-line budget passes: **600 net LF test lines**, the ordinary **400-line allowance**, and an allocation of exactly **200 excess lines**. The historical scalar-ratchet results below are not current-head results.
- [Exact-head broad CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44004707664) completed with **61 successful, 24 skipped, and 2 failed jobs**. The sole test failure is [the compact tooling shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44004707664/job/133780733428); the other failure is the dependent aggregate gate. The failing private-Control-UI-server inventory assertion discovers `extensions/openclaw-id-access/browser/recovery-uses.e2e.test.ts`, which is absent from `uiE2ePrivateServerTestFiles`. The file entered main through #200145. All scanned `ui/` and `extensions/` sources, the assertion/support module, UI test configurations, parser, and CI node-plan owner are byte-identical between integrated main `4cbd215a` and this head. This is an inherited main inventory defect, not an authorization-test failure. The exact-baseline CI run was cancelled, so no passing baseline replay is claimed. No unrelated fix, expected-failure exception, budget adjustment, or rerun-for-green was made; **broad CI is not green or waived**. Execution approval was not the separate sensitive-security approval. No merge or deployment was performed.

The November 6–7 evidence below is retained as historical proof, not substituted for the exact-head checks above.

Historical review repair head: `1d59863f8e6155adb544bb806acf134706c91c0e`.

### Review repairs and expanded proof — November 7, 2026

- **Architecture finding fixed:** replaced the scope module's import from the Gateway handler-type barrel with its minimal structural input contract. `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` now reports **0 cycles**, versus **1 cycle** on the reviewed head. Runtime authorization logic is unchanged.
- **All four current-head CI test-type failures repaired:** narrow the recovery snapshot discriminant, retain browser classification separately in the restored-source fixture, supply the native transport fixture's authenticated profile, and strip native-only delegation when building a principal snapshot. Core typecheck and the four affected canonical test-type graphs pass.
- **Recovered native owner continuation:** `operator-run-recovery.effects.test.ts` now takes a serialized native snapshot through a persisted CronService row, the production job target and failure-repair event owners, admitted child authority, and a host-bound file write. An allowed write persists; device revocation, email reassignment, and reassignment-then-restoration during the next held write reject it, with the file unchanged. This extends and relocates existing final-effect cases rather than duplicating them.
- **Native provider-review final effect:** `sessions-provider-review.integration.test.ts` exercises the real Gateway router, scope/session authorization, acknowledgment owner, and worker SQLite compare/commit. An authorized native writer clears the exact pause. Read-only, foreign-owner, and non-UI callers never reach runtime handoff; device revocation at commit leaves the entire session entry unchanged. External model acceptance is a fixed fixture: this is production-boundary proof, not a live native-app/provider E2E claim.
- **Latest-stable upgrade:** an actual released `openclaw@2026.11.1` store writer created a disabled synthetic automation. Supported backed-up Doctor migration and current-source `loadCronStore`/`CronService.list/update` preserve its authored prompt, disabled state, creator, owner, delivery, interval, and unrelated fields. Exact whole-store comparison permits only verified canonical metadata additions: every-schedule anchor, owner profile from stored creator, and versioned account tool policy from stored owner. Subsequent service update persists without changing unrelated fields. This proves the released-store → Doctor → current-service boundary, not a full native-package upgrade. No jobs or Gateway ran. Existing dependencies were reused without installing packages or overriding install policy.

Focused validation: **154 tests pass across separate runs**, not one all-green monolithic suite: recovery 43, recovered final effects 3, provider-review final effects 5, automation transports 15, scheduled-session custody 15, cron-context replay 13, and CI source-owner routing 60. Recovery effects took 43.69 s including compilation (3.97 s summed cases); the new provider-review cases initially took 45.81 s including compilation. Scheduled-session custody took 10.79 s (12.44 s wrapper). CI execution seconds for these new files are pending.

The first combined replay exposed the extracted recovery file running in an incompatible thread pool (host database broker unavailable). Registering it in the existing database-worker lane resolves that setup failure; the corrected effects shard and routing suite both pass. The repaired files pass focused lint, formatting, whitespace checks, and the affected type graphs. Regression check: substituting the pre-generalization job target (`a43f5e814047`) and original provider-review handler (`d482d7616512`) produces four intended failures: missing recovered native owner authority and native continuation denial. Restoring the reviewed repair makes **8/8 pass**, Vitest 41.34 s / wrapper 45.61 s. No setup failure is counted as negative authority proof.

Fresh independent **autoreview, Codex, P0–P2**, covers reviewed head `697096f44c77820f7fde61cc005bd425a8227513` → the complete local repair snapshot, including untracked test files and the database-lane registration: **scoped-clean, no actionable findings**. It inspected supplied source/context and did not execute project tests. The helper's first preflight refused a shared temporary directory; the completed run used the OS-reported private macOS temporary directory without disabling isolation.

Test growth is allocated explicitly: **463 net LF lines** across the complete PR for distinct admission, recovery/continuation, forbidden-caller, revocation, and final-effect contracts. The shared test-line scalar is unchanged. Existing authority and persistence owners are reused; the handler-type dependency is removed and no parallel policy registry is introduced.

**Upgrade-proof side effect:** Doctor also cleaned 3,387 recognized obsolete files in its shared temporary archive-read cache. Source inspection confirms it targets that cache, not original archives; no live Gateway or configuration changed. No further Doctor runs were performed.



**Inherited test-line ratchet failure (not waived or masked):** the clean merge base `d482d7616512` independently reports `6,552,043` LF lines against ceiling `6,551,994` (**49 over**, delta 0). This head reports `6,552,506` against `6,552,457` (**49 over**, delta +463). The PR adds exactly 463 lines and 463 allocation credits; it does not increase the inherited debt. The ratchet command still exits nonzero on this positive-delta branch. No unrelated tests, scalar baseline, or extra debt credit were changed. Broad exact-head CI remains to be assessed.

## Updated real-app proof — November 6, 2026

**Main proof uses the normal, web-backed Mac app interface, not the experimental native SwiftUI chat.** Experimental-native results from earlier preparation are supplemental only and are not substituted for the normal-interface results below.

### Provenance and signing

- Gateway and served Control UI built from proof head `697096f44c77820f7fde61cc005bd425a8227513`.
- Real macOS client: installed version `2026.10.4`, source metadata `3561a19c06ec0294c022b7b0ca3829a073f52ef5`, copied into a separate proof bundle and explicitly ad-hoc re-signed. Its client revision is older than the Gateway; this is not an exact-head native-package build claim.
- Proof bundle identifier: `local.openclaw.pr194443-installed-proof`. `codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2` reported **valid on disk** and **satisfies its Designated Requirement**.
- The normal embedded UI authenticated through the native bridge as `client=openclaw-macos`, `mode=ui`, `role=operator`; it was not replaced by a script claiming that client name. The real model invoked the production OpenClaw automation tool through a normal `chat.send` turn.
- Separate loopback Gateway, state, workspace, app profile, and disabled synthetic job. No LinkedIn or other external automation ran. The existing operator Gateway and installed `/Applications/OpenClaw.app` bundle were not modified or restarted.

**Signing constraint:** Ad-hoc signing is the signing path available to this contributor. This evidence does not claim Developer ID/distribution signing, notarization, or TCC permission persistence. Please assess the observed native authentication/authorization chain on that basis; if distribution signing itself is a material dependency, identify it and route that additional verification to a maintainer with distribution-build access.

### Normal-interface observations

| Scenario | Actual observed behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Native admin manages another conversation’s job | The real model listed disabled jobs, updated the foreign-conversation fixture through the automation tool, and read it back. Independent persisted-state read showed `STANDARD-MAC-ADMIN-PR194443-VERIFIED`; the job remained disabled. |
| Explicit `tools.gatewayPolicy.automations.scope: "caller"` | Through the same normal Mac app interface, the real model attempted the foreign-job update and received `cron job not found`. Persisted job state was unchanged and disabled. |
| Native device revoked during an in-flight delayed update | The model’s tool-orchestration call awaited a 60-second timer before attempting its write. The supported `devices revoke` CLI revoked the proof device’s operator authority while that run was active. The Gateway terminated the original run with `operator source authority is no longer active` and stopped model fallback because the caller signal was aborted. After the timer deadline, independent persisted-state comparison showed the entire job unchanged; the attempted new marker was absent. |

Sanitized Gateway receipt for the passing revocation run:

```text
21:21:47 [gateway] device token revoked device=<proof-device> role=operator
21:21:47 [agents/harness] error="operator source authority is no longer active"
21:21:47 [diagnostic] runId=9e343352-93e6-4fa3-8a2b-6230ba6378d9 durationMs=39586
21:21:47 [model-fallback/decision] stopped: reason=caller_signal_aborted
post-deadline persisted job comparison: unchanged=true; enabled=false
```

The shared-bootstrap-token app subsequently reconnected/re-paired. That did **not** restore the original run’s authority or persist its attempted update. This live case proves in-flight revocation before the delayed tool call; it is not represented as a write already held inside Cron’s commit guard.

Earlier revocation setup attempts used an insufficiently scoped generic RPC client or omitted the explicit credential required by a URL override. Those attempts are **not** counted as negative proof; an earlier timer completed without a successful revocation. The passing case above used the supported device-management CLI with explicit, disposable proof-Gateway credentials. No credential values or private endpoints are included here.

### Additional live scope-demotion proof — November 6, 2026

A second disposable loopback fixture used the same PR-head Gateway and the identified installed `2026.10.4` client, copied to bundle `local.openclaw.pr194443-demotion`, ad-hoc signed and strictly signature-verified. The **normal web-backed Mac app interface** was used; experimental native experience remained disabled.

1. Through a real model turn and the production automation tool, the native admin read a disabled foreign-conversation job, updated its message to `DEMOTION-ADMIN-CONFIRMED`, and read it back.
2. The same turn entered a tool-orchestration call awaiting a **90-second Promise timer** before attempting a second update to `DEMOTED-MUST-NOT-PERSIST`.
3. While that run was active, the supported `devices rotate` CLI narrowed the proof device’s operator token to **`operator.read,operator.write`**, removing `operator.admin`, approvals, questions, and pairing. This was scope demotion, not device removal or token revocation.
4. At **21:43:43 PST**, the Gateway recorded the narrowed scopes and immediately terminated the original run with `operator source authority is no longer active`; fallback stopped with `caller_signal_aborted`. The app subsequently reconnected, but that did not restore the original run.
5. After the original 90-second deadline, an independent Gateway read verified every persisted job field against the pre-demotion tool readback: unchanged, disabled, and no forbidden marker. The CLI list adds only derived `effectiveAgentId` and `status` fields; those are not treated as stored mutations.

This proves **live scope-demotion propagation to an in-flight native-app model run before its delayed tool write**. It does not claim a fresh non-admin model turn, a write already paused inside the Cron commit guard, persistent denial after a new bootstrap-authenticated reconnect, or distribution signing. No live operator Gateway, installed app bundle, or real automation was changed.

## Earlier-head automation final-write boundary proof

Re-executed on `697096f44c77820f7fde61cc005bd425a8227513`:

```sh
pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/cron-creator-transports.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

**15/15 passed**; Vitest wall time 66.86 s, wrapper 70.65 s. This in-process suite uses fixture-authenticated connection facts and production admission, automation tools, and Cron handlers. It independently covers admin success, explicit caller-cap denial, native `operator.write` without admin denial, and device revocation while the update is held in Cron validation: resumed final write rejects and stored state is unchanged. It complements, rather than substitutes for, the real-app evidence above.

Earlier same-head focused validation: all **68 recovery/reconnect/session-run checks passed** after correcting a fixture to publish production revocation rather than merely rotate a token. Seven other focused files passed in the preceding broader run. This is combined focused evidence, not one all-green monolithic suite. Core typecheck, focused lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Current proof also built the Gateway runtime and Control UI successfully.

Base reproduction and earlier narrow proof remain at `d482d7616512`, `c13ab576c5059102aa143ec3355540bdf2d12422`, and `a43f5e81404718b2e15dd1379bbf885513c967c0`; those are prior-head evidence, not substitutes for the current-head runs above. Independent local read-only review previously found no remaining P0–P2 defects; this is not an autoreview-helper-certified result.

## Remaining boundaries and gates

- A normal-app **non-admin real-model run** remains uncompleted. Non-admin final-write denial is covered by the production-boundary tests, not claimed as native-app E2E evidence. Historical live in-flight scope-demotion proof is recorded above.
- No distribution-signed/shipped-package or TCC-persistence proof. The historical cold Swift build was stopped during dependency download; the app proof used the explicitly identified existing client instead. No new exact-head native package build is claimed. The latest ClawSweeper review accepts ad-hoc signing for the demonstrated authentication path and does not require distribution signing from this contributor.
- [Maintainer direction endorses native administrator parity](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194443#issuecomment-6935746079). Broad current-head CI is not green because of the inherited inventory failure above, and fresh current-head `/allow-security-sensitive-change` approval remains required; the branch update, execution approval, static review, and focused validation do not grant or bypass these gates. No merge or live deployment was performed.

Simplification: existing classification, run-authority, and recovery owners are reused; browser identity is not widened and no competing authorization registry is introduced. The current test allocation and verification are recorded in the November 17 evidence above.

prs.title: fix: let the macOS app answer the first chat instead of reporting low memory
prs.body:
Fixes #200340

## What Problem This Solves

On the macOS app, the first message after onboarding fails with "This host is low on memory, so it could not start another session", even on a Mac with plenty of free memory. The app's local Gateway runs on Bun. On macOS, Bun's `process.availableMemory()` counts only truly free pages, about 0.5 GB on a 48 GB Mac in normal use. The 1 GiB Claude CLI live-session guard therefore refuses the session.

The same reading also made optional background work think the process was out of memory on every Mac. Bun reports `process.constrainedMemory()` as physical RAM, so "available ≤ 20% of the limit" was always true. Cron retention, update checks, GitHub publication scans, post-ready maintenance and startup prewarming were deferred indefinitely.

## User Impact

macOS app users get a reply to their first message. Background maintenance and prewarming run again on Macs. Gateway and node host stats report reclaimable memory instead of only free pages. Node runtimes, and Bun on Linux and Windows, are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readProcessAvailableMemoryBytes()` in `src/infra/host-memory.ts` is now the single owner of the "available memory" reading. Under Bun on macOS, it binds `host_statistics(HOST_VM_INFO)` from libSystem once through Bun's built-in FFI. It returns the same formula Node uses (libuv `uv_get_available_memory`: free + inactive + purgeable pages × page size). Speculative pages are already part of `free_count`. Each reading is one Mach call, about 0.1 ms after the first, with no cache.

Callers that read `process.availableMemory()` directly now use the owner:
- `readHostFreeMemoryBytes()`: the CLI live-session guard, doctor rebuild concurrency, `system.info`, node host stats.
- `isConstrainedProcessLowOnMemory()`.
- `resolveUpdateHashWorkerCount()`.
- `scheduleGatewayPrewarm()`, which repeated the same 20% check inline. With the shared check, Node/Linux hosts without a cgroup limit also prewarm. Node reports `constrainedMemory()` as 2^64 there, which the shared check already treats as no limit.

Tests that faked memory pressure by stubbing `process.availableMemory()` now stub `isConstrainedProcessLowOnMemory()`. On a Mac under the Bun test runner, the old stub would be bypassed. The threshold itself stays covered in `host-memory.test.ts`.

Not changed: the guard error is still classified as `rate_limit`/429. Changing that alters failover and user-copy behavior beyond this fix; it is noted as a follow-up in the issue.

## Evidence

**Real hardware** (Josh's 48 GB M-series MacBook Pro, macOS 26.5.1). The final `host-memory.ts` (sha256 `e31ed057…c965`) runs under the app's bundled Bun 1.4.4 (`~/.openclaw-onboarding/runtime/current/bin/bun`), alternating with Node 26.12.1 at the same moments:

| Reading | Bytes |
|---|---|
| Bun raw `process.availableMemory()` | 496,746,496 (0.50 GB) |
| Fixed helper under Bun | 20,420,755,456 (20.42 GB) |
| Node 26.12.1 `process.availableMemory()` | 20,415,102,976 (20.42 GB) |

Under Bun, the fixed helper passes the 1 GiB guard and `isConstrainedProcessLowOnMemory()` is `false` (`constrainedMemory()` = 51,539,607,552 = `totalmem()`). The first call, including the FFI bind, takes 1.6–5.4 ms; later calls take 0.01–0.13 ms. `memory_pressure` reported 71% free.

**Tests:**
- `src/infra/host-memory.test.ts` simulates Bun on macOS (`availableMemory() == freemem()` = 512 MiB, `constrainedMemory()` = 48 GiB) with fake Mach counters. Plentiful reclaimable memory admits a CLI live session through the real `ensureCliLiveSessionMemory`. Genuinely low Mach memory (256 MiB) still throws `cli_live_session_host_memory`. Further cases cover pressure, update-hash workers and Node's unchanged reading.
- Red on base: with `origin/main`'s helper, 3 of the 4 Bun cases fail. The guard fails with the same "Host memory is too low for another CLI live session" as the issue.
- Touched and consumer suites pass: host-memory, host-stats, system-info, execute-plugin, doctor rebuild concurrency, cron maintenance, update-startup schedule, GitHub publication runtime, runtime-services maintenance, startup prewarm and database page cache. `pnpm check:changed` passes; its dead-export scan was skipped because of existing failures on `main` in files this PR does not touch. Test-lines ratchet: +101 of 400.
- Independent review (OpenClaw subagent) found two P2 issues. Both are fixed: the inline prewarm check, and pressure tests that would read real memory on a Mac.

**Gap:** I did not package the app and send a first message after a fresh onboarding. The proof above runs the changed helper under the app's own Bun runtime on the affected Mac, plus the guard under simulated Bun semantics.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: fix: keep Kimi Code keys out of Moonshot doctor discovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #199773.

With only Kimi Coding configured, `KIMI_API_KEY` currently makes Doctor discover both Kimi and Moonshot. Those providers do not accept interchangeable credentials. Doctor consequently recommends an unrelated Moonshot installation. This is a configuration/authentication fix for the November 16–22 Simple Setup focus week.

## User Impact

Doctor no longer infers an extra Moonshot install from the shared key when Kimi Coding is explicitly configured. Explicit Moonshot plugin/model/auth/web-search selections and dedicated `MOONSHOT_API_KEY` credentials remain supported. Bare environment-only discovery remains unchanged when neither provider is explicitly configured.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep precedence in the shared Doctor install-discovery owner, filtering only environment-derived Moonshot candidates in both model-provider and web-search discovery. This also covers release backfill. Explicit candidate unions stay intact; runtime credential lookup, catalog aliases, configuration schema, and provider endpoints do not change.

## Evidence

- **Natural report:** #199773 describes Kimi-only setup on NixOS with a membership key and unwanted Moonshot installation/401 probes.
- **Real CLI baseline:** independently reproduced the wrong install intent on latest stable `2026.11.4 (d843d6a)` and installed `2026.11.5-beta.1 (bc061f9)`, Windows / Node 24.19.0. With isolated home/state/config, no installed plugins, only `plugins.entries.kimi.enabled: true`, and a synthetic `KIMI_API_KEY`, `doctor --lint --only core/doctor/configured-plugin-installs --json` reports missing **kimi and moonshot**, recommending both packages. No `doctor --fix` or live credentials were used.
- **Patched packaged CLI - PASS:** a fresh isolated installation of the supported private runtime-only package from exact head `7cbf4811d51e64a79121305969444c860e765113` was executed through its installed `openclaw.mjs`. With identical Kimi-only configuration and synthetic key, the stable package reports `[kimi, moonshot]`; the patched package reports `[kimi]`. A fresh explicit-Moonshot control still reports `[kimi, moonshot]`. Each invocation runs exactly `core/doctor/configured-plugin-installs`; exit 1 is expected because the selected provider packages are intentionally not installed. No production owner was mocked or replaced. Raw JSON and assertion receipts are retained locally.
- **Stable-to-patched upgrade - PASS (pnpm):** the same isolated installation prefix was upgraded from stable `2026.11.4 (d843d6a)` to the exact-head candidate `2026.11.4 (7cbf481)` without recreating either saved test configuration. Kimi-only discovery changed from `[kimi, moonshot]` to `[kimi]`; the explicit-Moonshot control stayed `[kimi, moonshot]`. Both configuration files remained byte-for-byte identical (SHA256 receipts below). The alternative uses a documented package-manager choice: npm lock import followed by pnpm 12.15.0 replacement, explicitly an **npm-to-pnpm switch**, not proof that the stalled npm-only upgrade works. Exact candidate lifecycle approval ran preinstall/postinstall successfully; a subsequent frozen-lockfile install exited 0. No agent skills were approved or installed. The npm stall is preserved separately as an environment limitation.
- **Regression proof:** on base `687dc6c99a32714473a646942382ebcd7f5e6552`, the original two plugin/model regressions fail specifically on the extra Moonshot candidate, while nine controls pass. With this patch, **32 tests pass** across Doctor intent and release-backfill suites. Coverage preserves dedicated Moonshot credentials, explicit plugin/model/search selection, Kimi auth alias, unrelated environment discovery, and legacy ambiguous discovery.
- **Local gates - PASS:** core `tsgo`, targeted source-backed core lint, formatting, staged documentation freshness, and the maintained source-runtime build all pass.
- **Independent review:** a separate read-only patch review found no substantive blocker. Hosted review also identified zero actionable correctness findings, but requested these runtime receipts and a human maintainer decision on explicit-Kimi precedence. That product decision remains outstanding; no maintainer approval, broad CI pass, or merge is claimed.

**Limits:** this verifies Windows read-only Doctor discovery through an installed core package. It does not exercise `doctor --fix` installing provider packages, successful live provider authentication, or the reporter’s NixOS environment. The private runtime-only tarball is a CLI test artifact, not a publishable release: the package-wide guard flags absent Control UI assets. No package-wide/release integrity pass is claimed. The pre-existing difference between the official install catalog alias `kimi-coding` and the installed manifest’s additional `kimi-code` alias is unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Redacted installed-CLI receipts (exact head)</summary>

Candidate source: `7cbf4811d51e64a79121305969444c860e765113`. Private runtime-only tarball SHA256: `dfb44397e0f25bd70adb9c9d5ba83aaa9b2deb439cb0380e07c5bd461f5a7f3e`.

All runs execute the real installed entry point with isolated home/state/config and synthetic credentials, using `doctor --lint --only core/doctor/configured-plugin-installs --json`. Provider packages are intentionally absent; exit 1 is expected for the missing-install findings. The following is a redacted summary of the asserted CLI JSON, not a replacement discovery implementation:

```json
{"setup":"fresh stable", "pluginIds":["kimi","moonshot"], "checksRun":1, "exitCode":1}
{"setup":"fresh patched", "pluginIds":["kimi"], "checksRun":1, "exitCode":1}
{"setup":"fresh patched, explicit Moonshot", "pluginIds":["kimi","moonshot"], "checksRun":1, "exitCode":1}
{"phase":"before", "case":"kimi-only", "version":"2026.11.4 (d843d6a)", "pluginIds":["kimi","moonshot"], "settingsSha256":"f5f78e850e54034bf0172909418487a56ea69ddc878f558e2f3e5b69a95f13d1"}
{"phase":"after", "case":"kimi-only", "version":"2026.11.4 (7cbf481)", "pluginIds":["kimi"], "settingsSha256":"f5f78e850e54034bf0172909418487a56ea69ddc878f558e2f3e5b69a95f13d1", "settingsUnchanged":true}
{"phase":"before", "case":"explicit-moonshot", "version":"2026.11.4 (d843d6a)", "pluginIds":["kimi","moonshot"], "settingsSha256":"132f679b50e9b58e124c60f6a7474a3a4995708213736c91b5b3a572e947f77b"}

```

The retained settings include the pre-existing gateway mode/port and configured plugin selections. They were compared with the original saved bytes before and after each Doctor invocation, not regenerated after the upgrade. No live credentials, running Gateway, service replacement, provider inference, or `doctor --fix` were used. The fixture proves the scoped read-only install-intent behavior, not live provider authentication or the npm-only installer path.

<!-- kimi-doctor-runtime-evidence:7cbf4811d51e64a79121305969444c860e765113 -->
</details>

<details>
<summary>Focused commands</summary>

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor/shared/missing-configured-plugin-install.ids.test.ts src/commands/doctor/shared/release-configured-plugin-installs.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

prs.title: feat(memory): shared memory database for multi-agent deployments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When multiple agents share a single OpenClaw instance, each agent creates its own memory database. This wastes disk space, causes inconsistent search results across agents, and triggers unnecessary full reindexing when extra memory paths change.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR introduces shared memory database support for multi-agent deployments by making four coordinated changes:

1. **Force shared memory index** (`memory-search.ts`): When the system agent is configured with an explicit default workspace (`agents.defaults.workspace`), force `memorySearch.enabled=true` and redirect `store.databasePath` to a shared sqlite keyed by workspace hash.

2. **Exclude extraPaths from scope hash** (`manager-reindex-state.ts`): Remove `extraPaths` from the scope hash calculation so adding/removing extra memory paths doesn't trigger a full reindex of the shared database.

3. **Skip shared memory ownership assertion** (`openclaw-agent-db.ts`, `openclaw-agent-db-schema-helpers.ts`): Allow multiple agents to open the same shared memory database without triggering ownership errors.

4. **Use canonical workspace for system agent** (`memory-runtime.ts`, `manager.ts`): When the system agent has an explicit default workspace, use that path directly for the shared memory database instead of a per-agent subdirectory.

## User Impact

- Multi-agent deployments share a single memory database, reducing disk usage and improving search consistency
- Adding/removing extra memory paths no longer triggers expensive full reindexing
- System agent and memory plugin lifecycle use the same canonical workspace and SQLite database

## Evidence

- Tested against OpenClaw v2026.9.2 source
- All four changes are minimal and focused on the shared memory path resolution
- No changes to memory search behavior, embedding, or ranking logic

prs.title: improve(workers): reuse verified prepared snapshots and worker code
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fresh cloud sessions repeat completed snapshot setup and worker-code extraction instead of reusing verified prepared content.

## User Impact

Fresh default-branch sessions can reuse compatible completed ancestor snapshots. Explicit refs and pinned sessions retain exact-source preparation. Seed-only requests prepare the requested revision without running an unauthorized setup recipe. The actual completed base reaches preparation, inspection and binding; current repository access remains required.

Verified worker packages reuse exact aliases, with verified archive installation as fallback. Legacy peers retain registration-time verification; negotiated peers defer verification to first binding with its full timeout. Exact binding replay preserves private edits.

**Current status — November 17:** main integration and reviewed CI repairs are published at `118b0cf6…`; current-head **CI is green**, with source conflicts clear. Complete readback: **127 successful checks, 48 skipped, one neutral, zero failed/pending**. The CI, dependency-review and security-sensitive-review commit statuses are successful. This completes the requested main-refresh/push/CI-green scope, **not** PR landing or completion of AUTH-2/full UPGRADE-3 acceptance.

**Dependency update:** [#193873](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193873) merged as `8e6768f91235b7b094f7f8dde96735d727a3f748`; #193749 as `21f7dc609de2c28082c056946c0bed5299183a7f`. Both are incorporated through official main `6a6007663b36db8badd6967e7f2bed5c6b3a724e`. Installed snapshot/publication acceptance is separate. Capture normalization and diagnostics in #193776 remain a separately owned scope.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing admission, prepared-workspace and installer owners serve the flow. Strict registration excludes receipt-only fields. Negotiated verification preserves old/new peer contracts without a protocol-version bump; actual-base propagation, preparation callbacks, memoization, capture verification and diagnostics remain intact.

The admitted repository/account owner checks snapshot ancestry. Missing or oversized comparisons decline optional reuse only after access revalidation; authentication, revocation, cancellation and transport failures still fail closed. The metadata size limit is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(agents): continuation-skip turns tell the model its workspace instructions were removed
prs.body:
Related: #196122

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with `contextInjection: "continuation-skip"`, every continuation turn on routes that pin the system prompt (direct Anthropic, official OpenAI Responses) tells the model that AGENTS.md, USER.md, MEMORY.md and every heading inside them were "(removed)".

## User Impact

On those routes, skipped turns keep the workspace instructions the model already has, without a system update revoking them. Skipped turns still send no workspace files, and an explicit `contextInjection: "never"` still announces the removal. Sessions that already received a false removal from an earlier skipped turn get their files redelivered once on the next skipped turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

A skipped continuation withholds files that the pinned prompt prefix still carries, but the prompt series diffed the file-less prompt against that prefix and reported each Project Context section as removed. The bootstrap stage now reports that it withheld already-delivered context, and the pinned series reuses its own Project Context block for that comparison, placed inside the framed stable region (before `<!-- /openclaw:attempt:STABLE -->`, or the cache boundary when unframed). If the saved comparison state already lost the block, the block comes from the admitted prefix, which still has it.

Scope: this does not change what unpinned routes (OpenRouter, most OpenAI-compatible providers) receive on skipped turns. Whether those routes should keep workspace files under `continuation-skip` is the separate product question in #196122; this PR leaves the #154923 behavior as is.

## Evidence

- Regression in `session-prompt-state.test.ts` built from real `buildAttemptSystemPrompt` output (with STABLE/DYNAMIC framing): on a pinned series, a withheld turn emits no update; redelivering unchanged files emits nothing; a removal without the withheld flag reports `(removed)` for the file and its inner headings; a comparison state that already lost the files redelivers them (`Be brief.`) once.
- Mutation checks: ignoring the STABLE terminator makes the "no update" assertion fail; dropping the admitted-prefix fallback makes the redelivery assertion fail.
- `session-prompt-state.test.ts`: 36 passed. `tsc` for `tsconfig.core.json`, `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-other.json`, `tsconfig.scripts.json`: no errors in changed files or for `workspaceContextWithheld`. `check:test-lines-ratchet` passes with the allocation. `oxfmt --check` / `oxlint` clean.
- Evidence gap: I have not captured a live provider request on a pinned route. Pinned routes require a direct Anthropic or official OpenAI endpoint with a real key, so the existing loopback Gateway fixture (`gateway.continuation-skip-bootstrap.integration.test.ts`) resolves as unpinned and cannot show this path. `attempt-bootstrap-prepare.test.ts` hits `EMFILE` on Windows for 14 cases, identically on unmodified `main`.

prs.title: fix(ui): Escape doesn't stop a running reply when focus is outside the composer
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: pressing Escape does not stop a running reply when keyboard focus is anywhere other than the message box, for example after reloading the page during a run or after clicking in the conversation.

## User Impact

User impact: Escape now stops the visible run from anywhere in the chat pane. Menus, dialogs, panels, text fields, and reply quotes still handle Escape first, so the first press closes an open menu and only an unclaimed press stops the run.

## Why This Change Was Made

Escape-to-stop lived only in the composer textarea's keydown handler. After a reload, focus lands on the page body, and clicking the transcript focuses the transcript, so Escape reached nothing. This was not a regression: the shortcut has always required composer focus.

The composer keeps ownership of the stop policy (no stop while its menus, dictation, or a reply target are active). It exposes that policy through its pane state, and the active pane listens on `window` in the bubble phase. Window listeners run after every element and document handler, so existing Escape owners, including document-level ones like the message context menu, act first. The pane then applies the same exemptions the chat already uses when it forwards typed letters to the composer: open dropdowns, overlays, modal surfaces, fields, and autotype-exempt docks.

## Evidence

Maintainer retest of `49e9872bb77eeb97c01ad276fde92cb77b3cdf6e` in Chromium, using the real Control UI and a mocked Gateway:

- On main `f1d7daedced8b1d34e6f368bd481e66884d1c297`, the body-focus regression failed specifically because no `chat.abort` arrived after Escape. The Gateway was connected, the run was active, and Stop remained available.
- On this PR, all 15 cases across composer shortcuts, retained-pane Escape and split-pane focus passed. UI typechecking also passed.
- A focused two-running-pane check confirmed that each Escape aborts only the selected pane's run.
- Menu, quote and IME checks preserve their existing Escape ownership. The document menu handler prevents propagation before the window listener.
- The new menu test initially failed twice because it sent Escape before the menu's next-frame keyboard-listener initialization. The maintainer change synchronizes that setup with one animation frame; assertions, timeouts and production code are unchanged.
- Independent review found no unresolved production issue; its test-readiness finding was resolved by the tested four-line change.

The original report came from a real session: the page reloaded mid-run, and no abort arrived until Stop was clicked. The browser checks above do not claim a separate native WKWebView test.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/82d01e39-3ea3-482e-a3c5-be450839415f)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix: stop retained sends after device revocation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes retained in-process sends continuing after their originating device is revoked when the continuation is reconstructed from tokenless saved facts. Found while qualifying the release after #200313.

## User Impact

Revoked work is refused and reports the refusal instead of delivering. Allowed work still finishes after its accepting request ends. No configuration or stored-credential changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the existing device revocation owner across authority wrappers and subscribe detached continuations to that owner. Do not inherit the accepting request/turn lifetime or add a device credential to tokenless recovery snapshots. The product fixture also keeps loopback mock traffic out of inherited HTTP proxies without changing external proxy routing.

## Evidence

- New regression fails on the unmodified release source at the post-revocation assertion, then passes with the fix.
- Full operator-run recovery suite: 39/39 passes, including accepting-request completion and tokenless recovery cases.
- Real Gateway retained-send product test passes both allowed and revoked cases: allowed has one delivery; revoked has zero deliveries and one refusal notice.
- Canonical type-aware lint passes on the three runtime/regression files; formatting and diff checks pass.
- Exact pushed main-context head a689b8fedd8ebc77961841e100a1ce15db8dbef7: all 40 recovery tests and the real Gateway allowed/revoked product test pass (two shards, exit 0); canonical type-aware lint passes on all four changed files.
- Head 13f53fd890abdb261a59b9a2eb54c6889d4f8d90 changes only the refusal text to “Gateway device authorization was revoked.” The current session-identity ratchet and formatting pass; the earlier full product proofs remain applicable to the unchanged behavior. The prior generic “no longer active” text triggered the ratchet in run 44001214982, job 133766215772; this PR-caused failure was repaired, not bypassed.
- Independent review waived by the release owner; focused self-review preserves the existing revocation owner and avoids persisted authority or parent-lifetime changes.
