prs.body:
Related: #181130

## What Problem This Solves

After Doctor keeps a job's different or explicitly unset scratch and retains `HEARTBEAT.md`, the Heartbeat migration guide's paragraph for that case mentions copying wanted instructions into the job, but does not say that writing scratch replaces all of it or link to the scratch commands.

## User Impact

Operators who copy instructions from a retained `HEARTBEAT.md` know to include any existing scratch text they still need, because `--set` and `--file` replace the whole scratch.

## Why This Change Was Made

A community support question asked what to do after Doctor's retained-file notice. This change extends that paragraph of the guide (added in #181130) with the replace behavior and a link to the same page's Monitor scratch section, which lists the scratch commands and revision guards. #196106 proposes an update to the short retired `HEARTBEAT.md` page that links to this guide; this change touches only the guide. Documentation only; runtime behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Source at `d0e09e4`: [`automations scratch`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d0e09e419d7e2446f13c0277bfaa8a733876c612/src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-scratch.ts#L20-L28) documents `--set` as "Replace scratch with exact text" and `--file` as "Replace scratch from a file, or - for stdin", and the command [sends the full text as the new content](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d0e09e419d7e2446f13c0277bfaa8a733876c612/src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-scratch.ts#L69-L78). The [scratch write](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d0e09e419d7e2446f13c0277bfaa8a733876c612/src/cron/scratch-write.kernel.ts#L85-L103) deletes the job's existing scratch row and inserts the new content.
- [Doctor's notices for this case](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d0e09e419d7e2446f13c0277bfaa8a733876c612/src/commands/doctor-heartbeat-scratch-migration.ts#L159-L171) end with "already has different cron scratch; the automation keeps it and HEARTBEAT.md was retained for review." and "scratch was explicitly unset; it was left unchanged and HEARTBEAT.md was retained for review."
- Docs checks on `docs/gateway/heartbeat.md` with this change applied to `d0e09e4`: on a Linux development host, `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/gateway/heartbeat.md` reported "Docs MDX check passed (1 files)"; `pnpm format:docs:check` reported "Docs formatting clean (1431 files)."; `pnpm lint:docs --no-globs docs/gateway/heartbeat.md` linted 1 file with 0 issues; and `pnpm docs:check-links:anchors` found no broken link in this page, reporting only the same two existing failures on other pages as `d0e09e4` without this change (a deliberately wrong fragment on the new link was reported as not found). `git diff --check` on this patch in a scratch checkout exited 0 with no output.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium effort, P0-P2, one pass) of this patch against `d0e09e4` reported `scoped-clean` with no accepted or actionable findings ("patch is correct (0.97)").
- Not changed here: the Monitor scratch section's examples (print, `--set`, `--unset`). `--file` and the replace wording are already in the [Automations CLI reference](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d0e09e419d7e2446f13c0277bfaa8a733876c612/docs/cli/cron.md?plain=1#L559-L565).
- Documentation only. Doctor, the CLI, and runtime tests were not run; the replace behavior is read from source, not observed.

prs.title: fix: avoid quadratic filesystem probes during gateway database preflight
prs.body:
Closes #200267

## What Problem This Solves

Gateways with many configured agents spend tens of seconds blocked on the main thread during startup database readiness and session migration because `isConfiguredAgentDatabaseTarget` walks `targets` and runs `fs.statSync` + `isSameOpenClawAgentDatabasePath` (`realpathSync.native` + `statSync`) on every earlier non-matching target before checking exact path matches. On multi-hundred-agent deployments, checking each candidate row against the configured/candidate target list triggers millions of redundant synchronous filesystem calls before the Gateway becomes ready.

## User Impact

User impact: Gateway startup database preflight and session startup migration no longer perform quadratic synchronous `stat`/`realpath` scans across configured agent targets, cutting redundant filesystem probes on exact-match targets to zero while keeping symlink/alias and owner matching intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `isConfiguredAgentDatabaseTarget` (`src/config/sessions/targets.ts`) now checks exact path matches across owner-compatible targets first, exits after a single `statSync(pathname)` when the candidate file does not exist on disk, and only then falls back to `isSameOpenClawAgentDatabasePath`.
- Added `createConfiguredAgentDatabaseTargetMatcher` (`src/config/sessions/targets.ts`) for loop callers (`selectAgentDatabaseInspectionTargets` in `src/state/openclaw-database-preflight-targets.ts` and `runSessionStartupMigration` in `src/config/sessions/startup-migration-runtime.ts`), providing `O(1)` exact-path lookups and lazily building a single `createOpenClawAgentDatabasePathMatcher().createIndex()` across existing targets only when an alias check is needed.

## Evidence

- **Before vs after on 150-agent `selectAgentDatabaseInspectionTargets` reproduction** (isolated temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` with 150 configured agents and existing `openclaw-agent.sqlite` files):
  - Before (`origin/main` `d46027380a1`): `23,551` `fs.statSync` calls, `22,350` `fs.realpathSync.native` calls (`377.3 ms`–`497.8 ms`).
  - After (`HEAD` `b642db5f7b1`): `0` `fs.statSync` calls, `0` `fs.realpathSync.native` calls (`2.5 ms`).
- **Regression test**: `src/config/sessions/targets.selection.test.ts` (`matches configured database targets linearly without redundant filesystem probes`) failed on `origin/main` (`38` `statSync` calls for 20 agents on an exact match) and passes after the fix, covering exact matches, missing paths, owner-scoped vs ownerless symlink aliases, and unregistered files.
- **Targeted checks passed**:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/config/sessions/targets.selection.test.ts src/config/sessions/targets.test.ts src/config/sessions/targets-runtime.test.ts src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.test.ts src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.agent.test.ts src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.startup-index.test.ts` (6 files, 74 tests passed)
  - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json ...` (passed)
  - `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check ...` (passed)
  - `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base origin/main` (+70 net test lines, allowance 400; passed)
- **Unverified locally**: `tsgo` (`@tsrs` binary requires `GLIBC_2.34` unavailable on this host) and full-repo `tsc` (OOM-killed on host memory); left to hosted PR CI.

prs.title: fix(gateway): avoid repeated disk scans during multi-agent startup
prs.body:
Related: #200267

## What Problem This Solves

@609NFT reports slow Gateway startup with about 470 agents, with millions of synchronous filesystem calls spent matching configured agent databases. A database whose exact configured path appears later in the target list still incurs filesystem checks against earlier, unrelated paths.

## User Impact

Configured databases can be admitted without those unrelated disk checks during startup. Agent ownership checks and concrete-file alias handling remain intact. This addresses the reported exact-path scan; the separate fresh-state missing-suffix probing cost in the issue remains unresolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the reporter's exact-path-first proposal in the shared matcher used by preflight, session migration, and deferred Gateway startup. The existing alias fallback remains unchanged. No cache, schema change, or caller-specific workaround is introduced. Exact configured claims continue to be inspected by their consumer; unrelated filesystem errors are no longer encountered before a later exact match.

## Evidence

On a real built Gateway using the repository's **12-agent** startup workload, synchronous `stat` calls in the matcher fell **91 → 0** (all main-thread `stat` calls: **7,252 → 7,161**). Both observed runs reached `/readyz` HTTP 200, served the sessions RPC, and exited normally. This is a scaled synthetic configuration grounded in the user's report, not a replay of their 470-agent environment or a model-inference test.

Five uninstrumented baseline/fix pairs, serial ABAB, fresh state per run:

| Metric | Base median / p95 | Fix median / p95 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gateway ready | 27.89 / 28.23 s | 26.96 / 28.57 s |
| Process-tree CPU | 31 / 32 s | 31 / 31 s |
| Peak RSS | 1120.4 / 1156.2 MiB | 1125.6 / 1135.0 MiB |

The claim is removal of unnecessary filesystem work. These small samples do **not** establish a general latency or memory improvement: readiness p95 rose 1.21% and median RSS rose 0.46%. No samples were discarded. Separate CPU profiles were collected for both builds; the matcher was too brief to receive self samples at this scale.

Focused verification: **85 tests passed; one inherited failure remains**. The new 32-file regression fails on base with 992 direct `stat` calls and passes with zero after the fix. Owner mismatch, ownerless targets, hard links, symlinks, missing aliases and missing exact paths retain their behavior. Format, targeted typecheck, typed lint, and both CLI startup builds passed. The full suite was not run.

Two limitations are retained explicitly:

- `server-agent-database-startup.test.ts:486` (main/handoff) times out waiting for a preparation marker. The **unchanged base reproduces the identical failure at the same line**. The other 12 Gateway lifecycle tests pass on the patch; no timeout or assertion was changed.
- The benchmark gives this case a 2-second teardown grace. One of five uninstrumented fixed runs, and both profiled runs, required forced process cleanup after successful startup. The fixed uninstrumented run logged Gateway shutdown completed cleanly in 1,604 ms, then was killed at 2,117 ms. These are not claimed as graceful process exits. The benchmark's startup checks passed; graceful process-exit comparison remains a limitation.

<details>
<summary>Versions, commands, observation method, and raw samples</summary>

Base: `687dc6c99a32714473a646942382ebcd7f5e6552`.
Fix: `19dff4ac6eb2df153167a55e9f05d826ce208e49`.
Linux, Node 24.22.2, isolated container with 1.5 CPUs; 2.75 GiB runtime memory limit, 5 GiB build/test limit. Bundled plugin build limited to memory-core. No external channels or paid model calls. Windows alias behavior was not run locally.

Acceptance set before measurements: remove exact-match alias probes, preserve ownership/concrete-alias contracts, reach readiness and serve sessions RPC; record five ABAB pairs and investigate any >=20% startup/CPU/RSS movement. Fresh application state was used each time; OS caches were not flushed. p95 is nearest rank (the maximum for five samples).

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts cliStartup
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-gateway-startup.ts \
  --case preparedRuntimeScaleMany --runs 1 --warmup 0 \
  --timeout-ms 180000 --output <sample.json>
# Repeat serially, alternating complete baseline/fixed dist builds at the same path.
# Profiles were separate runs with --cpu-prof-dir <directory>.

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/config/sessions/targets-dedupe.test.ts \
  src/config/sessions/targets.test.ts \
  src/config/sessions/startup-migration.registry-recovery.test.ts \
  src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.test.ts \
  src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/state/openclaw-agent-db-registry.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-agent-database-startup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# Base-only failure attribution, with the original targets.ts restored:
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/gateway/server-agent-database-startup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t handoff
```

The first five-file group passed 68 tests in 755.78 s including cold worker compilation. Registry tests passed 5 tests in 5.10 s; the Gateway file took 740.80 s including compilation/imports (12 pass, 1 fail). Base-only handoff failed identically in 309.53 s. CI durations are pending. The added tests reuse the existing fixture (+43 net test lines; production +9).

Ready times (seconds), baseline then fix for each pair:
`27.928 / 27.770`, `26.704 / 26.799`, `26.706 / 26.964`, `28.226 / 28.568`, `27.885 / 26.699`.
Ranges: base 26.704–28.226 s; fix 26.699–28.568 s.
CPU ranges: base 30–32 s; fix 30–31 s.
RSS ranges: base 1110.7–1156.2 MiB; fix 1110.9–1135.0 MiB.
Host 1-minute load before each pair: `9.68 / 8.68`, `6.34 / 5.82`, `4.74 / 4.10`, `3.98 / 4.09`, `7.15 / 5.91`.

Work counts were collected separately with the same committed workload and an observation-only `--entry /proof/count-entry.mjs` wrapper inside `/work`. It delegates every filesystem call unchanged and snapshots at the benchmark's SIGTERM boundary, before teardown:

```js
import fs from "node:fs";
import { syncBuiltinESMExports } from "node:module";
const counts = { statSync: 0, matcherStatSync: 0 };
const original = fs.statSync;
fs.statSync = function (...args) {
  counts.statSync++;
  if (new Error().stack.includes("isConfiguredAgentDatabaseTarget")) counts.matcherStatSync++;
  return Reflect.apply(original, this, args);
};
syncBuiltinESMExports();
process.once("SIGTERM", () => fs.writeFileSync("/proof/counts-current.json", JSON.stringify({ phase: "before-shutdown", ...counts })));
process.argv[1] = "/work/dist/entry.js";
await import("/work/dist/entry.js");
```

The initial observer wrote only at process exit and lost its result during forced teardown; that run was not used as count evidence. Both versions were then observed identically at SIGTERM. Instrumented and profiled timings are excluded from the uninstrumented table by design.

The complete committed diff and shared callers were reviewed in the author Codex session; no actionable patch findings. No independent local autoreview or ClawSweeper review is claimed. Hosted review and CI remain pending.

</details>

prs.title: fix(agents): thread runtime identity into context-engine recall assembly
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #148033

Context-engine recall lost the caller's runtime identity: `assemble()` on the pre-turn history path and on the mid-turn tool-loop path received no `runtimeContext` at all, while the capture path (`afterTurn`) did. Engines that route recall by `runtimeContext.senderId` therefore saw `undefined` identity on every turn, so per-user memory namespacing silently degraded — for OpenViking with `deriveUserIdFromActorPeer=true`, auto-recall was effectively off while capture kept working, hiding the split.

## Why This Change Was Made

The embedded runner builds its afterTurn identity through `buildAfterTurnRuntimeContext` (`senderId`, session key, sandbox, channel route, workspace, and capability fields), but neither `assemble()` call site threaded it:

- `attempt-history-prepare.ts` passed no `runtimeContext` into `assembleHarnessContextEngine`, so the pre-turn assembly had no identity even though the lifecycle layer already forwards one through `preparePreTurnRuntimeContext`.
- `tool-result-context-guard.ts` used the existing `getRuntimeContext` callback for `ingest`/`ingestBatch` but dropped it for the mid-turn re-`assemble`, so identity survived ingest and vanished inside the same tool loop.

Both call sites now supply the same runtime identity the capture path uses. The recall and capture paths observe one consistent `runtimeContext`, and engines can key recall by sender without host-side workarounds.

The spawn-workspace test harness previously collapsed `buildEmbeddedCompactionRuntimeContext` to an empty object, which hid every runtime-identity field from context-engine assertions. The mock now passes its inputs through, keeping identity observable without resolving the real model target against the registry.

## Policy Binding For The Exposed LLM Capability

Threading `buildAfterTurnRuntimeContext` into recall also exposed its `llm.complete` capability to pre-turn and tool-loop assembly. Review caught that both build sites omitted `contextEnginePluginId`, and a context-engine caller has no ambient fallback for policy ownership — `resolvePluginPolicyId()` returns `undefined`, so `plugins.entries.<id>.llm.allowedCompletionModels` was skipped and a policy-restricted engine could complete on an excluded model. Bootstrap and finalization already passed the resolved owner.

Both sites now pass it:

- `attempt-history-prepare.ts` uses the phase input's `resolveActiveContextEnginePluginId()` — the same resolver bootstrap and finalization call.
- `attempt-setup.ts` `getRuntimeContext` resolves the owner from the active engine instance via `resolveContextEngineOwnerPluginId`, covering the mid-turn tool-loop `assemble` and the pre-existing ingest path that shares the callback.

## Run Authority Lifetime For Retained Completions

Exposing `llm.complete` to assembly also means an engine can retain the minted capability handle past the runtime call that supplied it — a callback kept across turns, a promise captured for later, a queued summarization. A finished run closed its admission but left that handle live, so a retained completion could still spend model budget outside the admitting run and outside its policy window.

The capability now carries the admitted run's active assertion: `resolveContextEngineCapabilities` accepts an optional `assertRunAuthorityActive` gate, the runner threads `assertActiveRun` through both runtime-context build sites (recall history-prepare, after-turn finalize) and the loop hook, and `llm.complete` checks the gate before any model acquisition. A retained handle refuses with `admitted run authority is no longer active` once the run closes, is replaced, or is aborted; the check runs before acquisition, so a stale call never reaches a provider.

The entry check alone leaves a window: the completion awaits model acquisition between the gate and the provider dispatch, and a revocation can land inside that await. The runtime therefore re-runs the same assertion after acquisition (`RuntimeLlmAuthority.assertCurrent`) and passes it onto the prepared completion, so `completePreparedModel` re-asserts immediately before provider I/O. A run that closes while the capability is suspended on model selection stops the dispatch before `completeWithPreparedSimpleCompletionModel`, with no provider call.

Isolated completions (`execution.mode: "isolated-agent-runtime"`) return from a separate branch before that deferred scope, so that branch reached provider I/O with no assertion at all — a completion admitted while the run was active could survive a parent revocation through the isolated contract's own preparation and still reach inference. The branch now forwards the same captured gate through `runIsolatedAgentRuntimeCompletion` into the existing `runIsolatedCompletion.assertCurrent` contract, which revalidates before credential handoff and again after its own runtime-lease acquisition; the adapter also re-asserts ahead of its error wrapping, so a revocation surfaces as its own authority failure instead of a wrapped provider transport error.

## User Impact

Context engines that scope recall by `runtimeContext.senderId` (e.g. OpenViking with `deriveUserIdFromActorPeer=true`) receive the caller's identity on every pre-turn assembly and mid-turn re-assembly, matching what they already saw in `afterTurn`. Per-user memory namespaces stop silently degrading to a shared `default` namespace, which also removes the cross-user leakage risk that the downstream fallback carried. Operator-configured plugin completion allowlists keep applying to engine-initiated completions on every newly exposed assembly path, and a completion capability retained by an engine stops working the moment its run's authority ends — including a revocation that lands while the completion is still suspended on model selection or on a provider plugin's runtime auth exchange.

## Evidence

Reproduction and regression are covered at two layers, both failing before the fix and passing after:

1. Full embedded runner (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.runtime-context-sender-id.test.ts`): drives a real `runEmbeddedAttempt` with `senderId: "user-42"` and a capturing context engine, then asserts the pre-turn `assemble()` and `afterTurn` hooks receive the same identity.
   - Pre-fix: `assemble` runtime context had no `senderId` (undefined), while the capture path carried it — the exact split the issue reports.
   - Post-fix: both hooks receive `runtimeContext.senderId === "user-42"` (plus session key, workspace, and capability fields), and the attempt completes without a prompt error.

2. Tool-loop re-assembly (`tool-result-context-guard.test.ts`): installs the loop hook with a `getRuntimeContext` callback and asserts the mid-turn `assemble()` call carries the callback's context, which previously reached only `ingest`.
   - Pre-fix: `assemble` received no `runtimeContext`.
   - Post-fix: `assemble` receives the same context object ingest used.

3. Allowed/denied completion policy (`src/plugins/runtime/runtime-llm.capability-policy.test.ts`): drives the real authority → policy → acquisition chain through the capability callback (`createRuntimeLlm` unmocked; only the model-acquisition seam is stubbed, so a denial is observable as "never reaches acquisition").
   - **Denied**: bound owner + `allowedCompletionModels: ["openai/gpt-5.4-mini"]`, engine calls `complete()` on the default model → rejected with `model "openai/gpt-5.5" is not allowlisted for completions`, and model acquisition never runs (no provider I/O).
   - **Allowed**: same binding with the default model allowlisted → the completion reaches model acquisition under the bound session agent.
   - **Bypass contrast (pre-fix behavior)**: identical config without the owner id → the policy-excluded default-model completion proceeds to acquisition. This documents why ambient plugin scope must not rescue a context-engine caller and what the owner binding closes.
   - **Revoked authority**: the gate throwing `admitted run authority is no longer active` → `complete()` rejects before `acquireSimpleCompletionModelForAgent` is called.

4. Runner lifetime (`attempt.runtime-context-sender-id.test.ts`, second case): the same full-runner harness captures the `llm.complete` handles handed to `assemble()` and `afterTurn()`, lets the run finish (the harness closes the admission in `finally`), then invokes both retained handles.
   - Pre-fix: a retained handle still acquired a model after the run closed.
   - Post-fix: both retained handles reject with `admitted run authority is no longer active` — owner closure denies the retained callback, matching the run-authority contract for retained tools and approval handles.

5. Registered-engine owner chain (`attempt.registered-engine-completion-policy.test.ts`): registers a probing engine through the real registry (`registerContextEngineForOwner` with owner `plugin:test-policy-plugin`, `resolveContextEngine` returns the guarded wrapper), runs the full embedded attempt with that resolved engine plus a plugin entry carrying `allowedCompletionModels: ["openai/allowed-model"]` and `allowModelOverride: true`, and probes both an excluded and an allowlisted model from inside `assemble()`.
   - `resolveContextEngineOwnerPluginId(resolved)` returns the owning plugin id, and the recall-minted capability inherits it.
   - **Excluded model** (`openai/forbidden-model`): rejected with `is not allowlisted for completions for plugin "test-policy-plugin"` before acquisition.
   - **Allowlisted model**: completes through model acquisition bound to `agentId: "main"` / `modelRef: "openai/allowed-model"`.
   - The same run asserts `runtimeContext.senderId === "user-42"` reaches the registry-resolved engine, proving the identity, owner, and policy bindings survive the registry wrapper together.

6. Dispatch-boundary revocation (`src/plugins/runtime/runtime-llm.authority-revocation.test.ts`, 3 cases; plus a second registered-engine case): the entry gate passes, then the run revokes authority while the completion is suspended on model acquisition. Failing before this commit, passing after.
   - **Suspended on acquisition (unit)**: acquisition hangs; the test flips the captured gate to revoked, releases the acquisition with a prepared model, and the retained completion rejects with `admitted run authority is no longer active` — `completeWithPreparedSimpleCompletionModel` was never called, so no provider I/O happened.
   - **Gate reaches the dispatch boundary**: a successful completion dispatches with `assertCurrent` set to the exact captured assertion (same reference), which `completePreparedModel` re-runs at the final provider boundary.
   - **Active authority is a no-op**: with the gate passing, the completion resolves normally and the assertion was consulted along the way.
   - **End-to-end (real registry + real runner)**: the registered-engine harness suspends `acquireSimpleCompletionModelForAgent`, aborts the run mid-acquisition, releases the acquisition, and asserts the suspended recall completion denies with `no longer active`, the provider dispatch stays uncalled, and the attempt projects a terminal prompt error — the exact revoke-during-preparation race the final boundary closes.

7. Isolated completion authority (`src/plugins/runtime/runtime-llm.authority-revocation.test.ts`, 2 additional cases): drives the real isolated branch end to end (`execution.mode: "isolated-agent-runtime"`, only the `runIsolatedCompletion` seam stubbed), both failing before this commit and passing after.
   - **Gate reaches the isolated contract**: an active run dispatches the isolated completion with `assertCurrent` set to the exact captured assertion (same reference) — the forwarded gate the isolated contract revalidates before credential handoff and after its own runtime-lease acquisition.
   - **Revoked during isolated preparation**: the contract's revalidation rejects inside its preparation window. Pre-fix the branch forwarded no gate, so the revocation never propagated and the completion hung until the isolated timeout expired (`Plugin LLM completion timed out after 30000ms` — observed red before the fix); post-fix it rejects immediately with `admitted run authority is no longer active` and never resolves a usable result.

8. Real final I/O over a real transport (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/context-engine-capabilities.real-transport.test.ts`, 2 cases): the runtime context is produced by the production recall builder `buildAfterTurnRuntimeContext` — the exact function the initial and mid-turn assembly call — under a real admitted run authority (`prepareSystemAgentRunAdmission` → `admit("embedded")` → `resolveAdmittedRunActiveAssertion`), with a local OpenAI-compatible provider fixture. No completion owner, acquisition seam, or isolated dispatch is mocked anywhere in the chain; every observation is recorded at the real HTTP boundary by the fixture server.
   - **Real recall identity**: the builder hands the capability face `runtimeContext.senderId === "user-42"` — the same identity the attempt-level tests (items 1 and 5) prove reaches real `runEmbeddedAttempt` recall — so the probes below dispatch exactly what a registered engine receives during a real turn.
   - **Excluded model**: rejected with `is not allowlisted for completions for plugin "real-transport-plugin"` before acquisition; the fixture server observes **zero** requests.
   - **Allowed direct completion**: real model acquisition → real dispatch → the server records `POST /chat/completions` with `Authorization: Bearer fixture-real-key` and the probe message in the request body, and the streamed SSE answer is returned as the completion text (`real-transport-direct-ok`).
   - **Allowed isolated completion**: `execution.mode: "isolated-agent-runtime"` dispatches through the real isolated completion owner (zero-tool runtime, no seam stubbed) and reaches the same provider boundary; the completion text is the isolated marker (`real-transport-isolated-ok`).
   - **Revoked after close**: `closeAdmittedRunDelegatedAuthority(admitted)` → a capability the engine retained past close rejects with the run-authority error, and the server sees no further requests.
   - **Existing-plugin compatibility**: an engine owner with no completion-policy declaration (the common legacy configuration) still completes over real transport while its run is active — the run-lifetime gate adds authority without changing what unconfigured existing owners can complete; the post-close refusal documented above is the full extent of the behavior change for a retained handle.
   - **Fixture typing**: the provider fixture is annotated against the real config contracts (`OpenClawConfig`, `ModelDefinitionConfig`), so the `api` and input-modality literal unions are checked by the test-types lane rather than widened to `string`; the runtime-context type import points at `src/context-engine/types.ts`.
   - **Preparation-time synchronization (previously a stated limitation, closed by item 9)**: a revocation-during-preparation observation could not be synchronized on the warm chain — preparation and its post-acquisition assertion completed inside the first macrotask turn, so an event-loop yield always observed the call after the assertion had already passed. The plugin-owned `prepareRuntimeAuth` exchange (item 9) supplies a real, deterministic suspension point inside acquisition on this same production chain, so the suspended-on-acquisition (item 6), revoked-during-isolated-preparation (item 7), and now revoked-during-real-preparation (item 9) proofs all stand at their stated boundaries.
The full-runner sender-identity test additionally asserts the pre-turn assembly's `runtimeContext.llm.complete` is present, so the recall path carries the same capability face the policy tests prove is bound.

9. Revocation during a real runtime auth exchange (`context-engine-capabilities.real-transport.test.ts`, third case): closes the preparation-time gap the previous revision documented. A real code plugin (cold fixture loaded through `plugins.load.paths`) registers the provider with a plugin-owned `prepareRuntimeAuth` hook that performs a real HTTP `POST /runtime-auth-exchange` inside model acquisition — the production seam (`prepareSimpleCompletionModelCore` → `prepareProviderRuntimeAuth`) that runs for every plugin-owned credential. The fixture holds each exchange response open until the test releases it, so revoking the admitting run (`closeAdmittedRunDelegatedAuthority`) lands deterministically while acquisition is suspended on real network I/O — the "already-preparing" window the capability contract promises is covered:
   - **Direct**: the exchange is observed, the run is revoked while the plugin hook is suspended on the real HTTP round trip, and the completion rejects with `admitted run authority is no longer active` — the post-acquisition `RuntimeLlmAuthority.assertCurrent` fires before any dispatch.
   - **Isolated**: the second run (`execution.mode: "isolated-agent-runtime"`) observes its own exchange and rejects the same way through the isolated branch's forwarded assertion.
   - **Provider boundary silence**: the fixture records zero `/chat/completions` requests across both runs, and the case prints the observation line `[preparation-revocation proof] {"direct":"rejected while runtime auth exchange was in flight","isolated":"rejected while runtime auth exchange was in flight","authExchangesObserved":2,"providerChatCompletions":0}` to the log.
   No completion owner, acquisition seam, or isolated dispatch is mocked anywhere in the chain; the only controlled seam is the plugin's own production auth hook and the local HTTP fixture both flows already share. The completions intentionally omit an explicit `model` — the agent's configured default stays inside the owner's `allowedCompletionModels` without needing model-override authority.

Validation: `attempt.runtime-context-sender-id.test.ts` 2/2, full guard suite 71/71, `runtime-llm.capability-policy.test.ts` 4/4, `runtime-llm.authority-revocation.test.ts` 5/5 (both isolated cases red before the fix), `attempt.registered-engine-completion-policy.test.ts` 2/2 (including the abort-during-acquisition case, red before the fix), `runtime-llm.runtime.test.ts` 31/31, `isolated-completion.test.ts` 33/33, `context-engine-capabilities.real-transport.test.ts` 3/3 (real HTTP transport: production recall builder, legacy owner, real runtime-auth-exchange revocation), test-types shards (`tsgo:test:src`, including the agents-other shard that type-checks this fixture) clean, `tsgo` core shard clean, `oxlint` (type-aware) clean and `oxfmt` clean on touched files.

prs.title: fix(memory-core): stop recall rehydration from anchoring on snippet fragments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related #151173 (non-closing: this PR lands the anchor normalization, fragment-rejection, and fence-selection repairs; the issue stays open for its remaining scope).

Recall rehydration re-finds a stored `short-term-recall` candidate by scanning the live note for its snippet (`relocateCandidateRange` in `extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion-rehydrate.ts`). The stored snippet and the live range were normalized differently: notes routinely gain HTML comments after a candidate is recorded, and because only `trim()` plus whitespace collapsing was applied, a range that merely gained an `<!-- ... -->` comment inside it stopped matching the stored snippet exactly.

Two silent consequences, both reproduced here:

1. **Fragment anchors.** With an HTML comment interrupting the recorded two-line range, the scan can no longer match any full window, so it degrades to a quality-1 fragment match and promotes a *fragment* of the recorded content — the wrong lines of the right file carried into MEMORY.md with no signal.
2. **Content loss anchors.** When the live note only retains part of the recorded content, the same quality-1 path promotes that partial content as if it were the recorded snippet.

## What Changed

- One shared normalization (`normalizeRecallSnippet`) now strips HTML comments and is applied to **both** sides of the comparison: the stored snippet, the live-range windows, and the list-marker-free variant. A range that gained an HTML comment now resolves at its own full range again.
- A best match that is only a **fragment** of the recorded snippet (quality 1) is now reported as lost (returning `null`) instead of being promoted. The apply step already records that outcome as an explicit `source rehydration` reject, so this converts a silent wrong-data outcome into a recorded intentional non-outcome.
- **Managed dreaming fences are excluded before selection.** A window that spans a dreaming marker and adjacent text becomes an exact match once comments are stripped, outranking the eligible text beside the fence; the apply-time fence guard then discarded that winner and the candidate surfaced as unresolved even though its complete text was still available. Managed ranges are now filtered before the stored-range fast path, the comment-only positional fallback, and scan selection, so eligible windows win and fence-adjacent text promotes through apply.

## Scope notes

- The uniqueness requirement (suggestion 3 in the issue) is **not** implemented: the line-distance tie-break is intentional and frequently correct for small offsets (the issue's own falsification data shows anchors holding at k = 0/2/4), so orphaning every non-unique match would drop correctly-anchored candidates. Fragment promotion is the measured silent failure; ambiguity handling is left as-is.
- No schema change: snippets are normalized at comparison time, so existing stores need no migration.

## How Was This Tested

Regression coverage (now in sibling file `short-term-promotion-recall-anchor.test.ts`), red before each fix:

1. `rehydrates snippets whose live range gained an HTML comment` — pre-fix relocated to the fragment (`endLine 3`, first line only, `expected 5`); post-fix resolves at the full `3-5` range with the comment stripped from the matched snippet.
2. `does not anchor promotion on a fragment when the live range lost content` — pre-fix applied `1` (promoting the surviving first line as the snippet); post-fix reports `0` applied.

Full `short-term-promotion.test.ts` suite: 99/99 green. Sibling memory-core suites (memory-write, store, scoring, metadata, owner): 23 passed / 1 skipped. Typecheck: `tsconfig.extensions.test.json` lane clean; prod lane clean for both touched files. oxlint clean.

## Evidence: comment-only anchor rejection (review round 2)

- **Red (review head, rejection absent):** the new apply-level regression "does not promote replacement text through a comment-only stored anchor" fails on the review head — recording a snippet of `<!-- archived backup note -->`, then replacing the recorded lines with unrelated text, lets the empty-target positional fallback promote that replacement (`applied` is 1 instead of 0) because comment stripping now erases the stored anchor to nothing.
- **Green:** `relocateCandidateRange` rejects a stored anchor that was nonempty before normalization and is empty after it; only an anchor that was empty at recording time (never claimed to match live text) keeps the positional fallback. New regression passes, and the full `short-term-promotion.test.ts` suite is 102/102 (the pre-existing comment-gained-in-range rehydration case still passes unchanged).

## Evidence: managed-fence selection fix (review round 3)

- **Red (fix head 58b911a2, selection still considers managed windows):** apply-level regression "keeps eligible text beside a dreaming fence when a marker window matches exactly" fails with `applied` 0 instead of 1. Scenario: one-line candidate recorded at line 3; the live note then gains `<!-- openclaw:dreaming:scratch:start -->` / `:end -->` markers on lines 2–3 with the complete text at line 4. Comment stripping makes window 3–4 an exact match at distance 0, beating eligible window 4–4 at distance 1; the apply-time fence guard rejected the winner, so the candidate was lost while its complete text sat beside the fence:

  ```
  expect(applied.applied).toBe(1)   →   - 1  +  0
  ```

- **Green (same head):** managed windows are skipped in the scan (and in the stored-range fast path / positional fallback), so window 4–4 wins and the candidate applies at `startLine 4 / endLine 4` with the full snippet `Moved backups to S3 Glacier.` — the fence-adjacent text case now promotes through apply. `short-term-promotion-recall-anchor.test.ts` 4/4, `short-term-promotion.test.ts` 99/99, sibling promotion suites 23 passed / 1 skipped.
- **CI note on the previous head (ccd70eb0a1e):** `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` failed on a stalled state-corpus shard (vitest no-output watchdog kill, exit 143 — the line-cap ratchet itself reported `Line-cap ratchet OK`); `check-test-types` failed in `scripts/mantis/run-request-telegram.mts` (TS2353) and the compact shards failed on `test/scripts/mantis-telegram-proof.test.ts` (Python recorder `Driver.send_text() got an unexpected keyword argument 'reply_to'`) and `prepared-model-catalog-worker.pool.integration.test.ts` ("Prepared plugin generation has retired"). None of these files intersect this PR's two-file diff; all are main-side or runner-infra conditions.

## Evidence: fence-membership precompute (review round 4)

- **Finding:** relocation asks whether every candidate window overlaps a managed dreaming fence, and `lineRangeOverlapsDreamingFence` rescanned the note from line 0 on every call — a moved or unresolved passage in a large fence-free note paid quadratic synchronous work (up to two regex checks per visited line, per window).
- **Fix (head 4e8be057cdb):** one forward pass per source read folds managed fence membership into prefix sums (`buildDreamingFenceManagedPrefix`), so each range eligibility query is an O(1) prefix-difference lookup. Semantics are unchanged: marker lines stay managed wherever they fall, fenced content stays managed, and the same start/end clamping applies.
- **Red (quadratic scan, head 58b911a2):** new regression "scans a large fence-free note in linear time for an unresolved passage" (4000-line fence-free note, recorded passage absent) fails the generous 4000 ms ceiling at **4717 ms**.
- **Green (same scenario, head 4e8be057cdb):** completes in **309 ms** (~15x faster) and still reports `applied` 0 — an unresolved passage keeps surfacing as the recorded intentional non-outcome rather than a wrong promotion. `short-term-promotion-recall-anchor.test.ts` 5/5; full promotion suites (short-term-promotion, memory-write, store, scoring, metadata, owner) 122 passed / 1 skipped; oxlint clean; `tsconfig.extensions.json` prod lane and `tsconfig.extensions.test.json` test lane both 0 errors.
- **CI note on the previous head (58b911a2):** `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` failed with the same runner-infra signature as ccd70eb0a1e — config/state corpus shards stalled ("no output for 120000ms" watchdog kills, exit 143) with no ratchet assertion failure anywhere in the log; the same job is also failing on other open PRs (#151942). No ratcheted file intersects this PR's two-file diff.

## Evidence: real promotion run (review round 5)

- **Real-behavior proof (head b5d573b0385):** committed integration test `records complete-text promotion beside an explicit source-rehydration rejection` drives the full production chain end to end in one apply run — real recall store (SQLite), real ranking, real rehydration against the live note file, real MEMORY.md append — with only the passage text as fixture. One run shows both fates at once: a passage whose range gained an HTML comment rehydrates at its complete text, while a passage whose line was replaced by unrelated content is recorded as an explicit rejection instead of promoting the filler.
- **Captured run output** (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion-recall-anchor.test.ts --reporter=verbose`, synthetic content only):

  ```
  ✓ … > records complete-text promotion beside an explicit source-rehydration rejection 65ms
  ✓ … > keeps eligible text beside a dreaming fence when a marker window matches exactly 65ms
  ✓ … > scans a large fence-free note in linear time for an unresolved passage 300ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  6 passed (6)
  ```

- **Durable-state assertions in the same run:** `applied` is 1 with the complete promoted snippet `Moved backups to S3 Glacier. Keep cold storage retention at 365 days.`; `rejectedCandidates` carries the replaced passage with `reason: "source rehydration failed"` / `category: "source rehydration"`; the written MEMORY.md contains the promoted text and does **not** contain `Unrelated replacement text` (asserted by reading the file back).
- All six anchor regressions pass (6/6); promotion suites 122 passed / 1 skipped; oxlint clean; extensions prod and test typecheck lanes 0 errors.

## Evidence: real OpenClaw setup promotion run (review round 6)

Real-setup proof on head `b5d573b0385`, replacing test-only evidence. Both runs below execute the **production CLI** (built dist) against an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_HOME` (no shared state, no test harness, no mocks); the notes contain only synthetic passages, and all local paths in the captured output are redacted to `<state>`.

**Setup promotion run (PR build `OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (b5d573b)`):**

1. `openclaw memory index --agent main --force` → `Memory index updated (main): 2 files indexed.` (lexical corpus; no embedding provider is configured in the isolated setup, so vector recall is degraded — the offline default).
2. Three real `openclaw memory search` runs record recalls into the live short-term store (`audit.entryCount: 2`; recorded ranges `memory/2026-04-01.md:1-5` and `memory/2026-04-02.md:1-4`).
3. The sources then mutate into the two failure shapes this PR repairs: `2026-04-01.md` gains `<!-- status refreshed by tooling -->` above the recorded passage (text intact, lines shifted), and `2026-04-02.md` has the vendor line replaced by unrelated filler.
4. One apply run, `openclaw memory promote --agent main --apply --json`, shows both fates in the same run:
   - `applied: 1` — the commented-note candidate rehydrates at its **complete text** and applies at the new live range `1-5`:
     `"snippet": "Daily notes for April 1. Planning session notes about the spring rollout. Moved backups to S3 Glacier. Keep cold storage retention at 365 days."`
   - `rejectedCandidates[0].reason: "source rehydration failed"` — the replaced passage is recorded as an explicit rejection instead of promoting the filler.
5. Durable `<state>/workspace/MEMORY.md` after the run (file read back, not asserted in-process):

   ```
   # Long-Term Memory


   ## Promoted From Short-Term Memory (2026-09-19)

   <!-- openclaw-memory-promotion:memory:memory/2026-04-01.md:1:5 -->
   - Daily notes for April 1. Planning session notes about the spring rollout. Moved backups to S3 Glacier. Keep cold storage retention at 365 days. [score=0.404 signals=2 recalls=2 avg=0.012 source=memory/2026-04-01.md:1-5] <!-- trigger: backup, backups, glacier --> <!-- importance: 4 -->
   ```

   The file carries the complete promoted passage at the shifted coordinates and contains no replacement filler.

## Evidence: data-model compatibility — the requested migration/upgrade compatibility proof (review round 7)

**Data-model compatibility run (release build writes, PR build applies):** the pre-fix release build (`OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (a40e545)`) creates the index and records the same two recalls into a fresh isolated store; the PR build (`b5d573b`) then reads that store and applies with no migration: `entryCount: 2`, `applied: 1`, `rejectedCandidates[0].reason: "source rehydration failed"`, and the identical MEMORY.md promotion line in the round-6 section above. The store shape written by the current release is consumed unchanged by this PR — consistent with the no-schema-change scope note: comparison-time normalization only, existing stores need no migration. Migration/upgrade compatibility is therefore covered in both directions this PR can affect: release-written recall state loads and applies unmodified on the PR build, and no store field or schema is renamed, moved, or reinterpreted by the repair. This section is the data-model compatibility proof requested by the merge checklist: migration and upgrade compatibility are confirmed — a store written by the published release loads and applies on this PR's build with no migration, and the repair renames, moves, or reinterprets no store field or schema.

prs.title: fix(config): keep deep config loading stack-safe past include resolution
prs.body:
Closes #153430

Related: #152847 (include resolution itself, already stack-safe in #152889) — this PR extends the same stack-safe contract to the loading stages that run after the resolver.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: loading a config whose deeply nested value passes `$include` resolution still crashes with an opaque `RangeError` when the resolved value reaches value merging, env substitution, or the legacy migration probes. The first iteration of this PR also reversed object key order on every substituted config (leaves were resolved in a reverse loop, and object slots record first-write order); that regression is fixed here, with a unit test pinning document key order.

## User Impact

User impact: a machine-generated config that nests deeply now fails with the normal actionable schema error instead of a stack-overflow crash from a stage after the one that already promises stack safety; nothing that was previously accepted is rejected, and persisted config key order matches the authored document.

## Why This Change Was Made

The include resolver walks documents on an explicit work stack, but every later stage still recursed. Each remaining walk now runs on an explicit work stack so document depth costs heap instead of call frames:

- `src/infra/deep-merge.ts`: `mergeDeep` and its plain-object sanitizer clone walk iteratively; prototype-key filtering is preserved.
- `src/config/env-substitution.ts`: `substituteAny` allocates object slots in source order (key order follows the document) and schedules child tasks depth-first, so `onMissing` warnings keep their original order.
- Legacy migration probes: the load-time `structuredClone(root)` calls (Node's built-in clone recurses too) are replaced by a shared iterative `deepCloneForMigrationProbe` in `legacy-config-record-shared.ts` across the models/providers/retired/config-tranche probes.

Net production growth is the shared clone helper plus the iterative walkers; no new configuration surface is added.

Competition/fix-surface note: #129403 overlaps on the env-substitution walk but does not touch the deep-merge or migration-probe clone crash points; this PR covers all three stages with tests.

## Evidence

All commands run from the PR checkout (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs` over the real CLI sources — the installed CLI runs dist and predates any local change).

**1. Full CLI chain, normal config through `$include` to merge, env substitution, migration probes, and schema (fresh config behavior).** `settings.json` is a minimal gateway block; `main.json` includes it and defines a provider whose `baseUrl` is `${PROOF_BASE_URL}/v1`:

```
$ PROOF_BASE_URL=https://proof.example.local OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/proof-153431/main.json \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts config get models.providers.proof-provider.baseUrl
https://proof.example.local/v1
(exit 0)
```

**2. Full CLI chain, 600-level nested value.** `nested600.json` nests a scalar 600 levels deep under a top-level key. The chain runs to completion and the value is rejected by schema validation with the actionable error, not by a RangeError:

```
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/proof-153431/nested600.json \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts config get agents.defaults.timeout
OpenClaw config is invalid: /tmp/proof-153431/nested600.json
- nested600.json:1 — agents.defaults: Unrecognized key: "timeout"
- <root>: Unrecognized key: "deep"
(exit 0; the CLI reports the schema error and the next step instead of crashing)
```

**3. Depth matrix over the changed walkers** (module-level probe: build an n-level nested object, call `mergeDeep(v, v)` and `resolveConfigEnvVars(v, {})`):

| depth | recursive implementation (base 8ebc8cd021e) | this PR (iterative) |
|---|---|---|
| 4000 | mergeDeep RangeError; envSub RangeError | both OK |
| 8000 | both RangeError | both OK |
| 20000 | both RangeError | both OK |

The same matrix over the legacy migration probe clone (`findLegacyConfigIssues` -> `LEGACY_CONFIG_MIGRATION_RULES[].match` -> `deepCloneForMigrationProbe`, the load-time doctor detection path): recursive baseline RangeError at 5,000 levels; this PR completes the probe at 100,000 levels.

**4. Boundary note on depth.** At 4,000+ levels the still-recursive include resolver aborts the load before the stages this PR owns (Include resolution failed: RangeError); stack-safe include resolution is #152847's contract, delivered by #152889. See items 6-7 for the full real-loader crash-point chain and the 2,000-level end-to-end window measured after the include-resolver fix.

**5. Tests.** `src/config/env-substitution.test.ts` (19 cases: the 4,000-level no-overflow case, plus a key-order case that fails on the reversed-write implementation) and `src/infra/deep-merge.test.ts` (6 cases incl. the 4,000-level merge) are green on this head.

**6. Real-loader crash-point chain (post-Rev3 update).** Walking the real CLI load chain depth-by-depth with an isolated config (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, synthetic values) maps every recursive crash point between the loader and the stages this PR owns, observed through a load-path probe on the real sources:

| Load stage | Observed crash depth | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| `$include` resolution (`resolveConfigIncludes`) | ~600 (2,000+ RangeError) | #152889 (stack-safe) |
| Read-path `$include` pre-scan (`containsConfigIncludeDirective`, `io.read-helpers.ts`) | 2,000 OK / 2,300+ RangeError | newly located; fixed by #153711 |
| Deep merge / env substitution / legacy migration probes | >2,300 — masked upstream on recursive baselines; isolated matrix in item 3 | **this PR** |
| `stableConfigStringify` (`runtime-snapshot.ts`) | 2,200 OK / 2,400+ RangeError | not yet fixed (family follow-up) |

**7. Full-chain proof at the new window.** On a checkout combining #152889 (include resolution) with this PR's three stages, a 2,000-level document under `agents.defaults.params` loads **end-to-end through the real CLI**:

```
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/proof-153431/state OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/proof-153431/config/openclaw.json \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/index.ts config get agents.defaults.model
test-model
(exit 0)
```

With this PR's three-stage fix removed from the same tree (recursive merge/env restored), the identical document also loads — because on a real load the recursive merge crash point sits deeper than the two masked stages above, the merge stages can only be observed through the isolated matrix in item 3. The depth-4,000 end-to-end claim therefore remains blocked by `stableConfigStringify` (item 6, last row), a recursive walker outside this PR's surface; recording it here so the family follow-up (#153708's chain) has the measured map.

**8. Doctor CLI chain over a legal deep config (real `openclaw doctor` on both baselines).** A config with an 800-level value under the schema-legal `tts.providers` catchall, run through the real CLI sources against the recursive base (origin/main `e63393bddc3a`) and this PR head, with isolated state dirs (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`): both runs complete the full doctor flow (health checks, legacy-state detection, migration preview) with no RangeError, and the probe/merge/env stages this PR changes process the same config. At 1,300+ levels both runs abort with `Maximum call stack size exceeded` before the doctor flow completes. On the recursive baseline that abort is consistent with the merge/env/probe crash points this PR owns (item 3 matrix); on this PR head those stages are iterative, so the remaining abort sits in the still-recursive post-probe clones (the candidate `structuredClone` in `doctor-config-flow.ts`, `cloneConfigWithResolutionFacts` in `resolution-facts.ts`). The full-chain before/after delta is therefore masked by those family stages; the measured window is recorded here for the follow-up.

`tsgo` core (`tsconfig.core.json`) and the core-test shards exit 0; `oxlint` and `oxfmt` are clean on the touched files; the line-cap and assertion-safety ratchets report no violations for the touched files.

prs.title: fix(config): make config writes stack-safe for deeply nested documents
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #153668. Fixes #154264.

The config write chain has five recursive stages that overflow on schema-valid deeply nested documents, in the order they engage during `writeConfigFileFromContext`:

1. `collectChangedPaths()` (`src/config/config-change-paths.ts`) - the recursive diff walk consumed at `io.write.ts:189/313/586` overflows at ~4,500 levels in this sandbox (the #153668 reporter observed ~4,000 on Windows), and also serves `management-mutations`.
2. `projectRuntimeChangesOntoSource()` (`src/config/source-value-projection.ts`) - the runtime-changes projection walks the document recursively and clones via native `structuredClone`, which overflows at ~1,600 levels on the full-chain probe below.
3. The merge-patch trio (`createMergePatch` / `applyMergePatch` / `mergePatchConflicts` in `src/config/merge-patch.ts`) plus its internal clone helper, which recursed and also delegated to native `structuredClone`.
4. The env-ref passes (`resolveEnvVarRefsForComparison` / `restoreEnvVarRefsFromResolved` / `restoreEnvRefsFromMap` in `src/config/env-preserve.ts`, plus the two `containsAuthored*EnvTemplate` probes in `src/config/env-preserve-authored.ts`) - recursive walks over the authored document.
5. `JSON.stringify(stampedOutputConfig, null, 2)` at `src/config/io.write.ts:354` - the platform serializer recurses one call frame per nesting level and overflows at ~4,400 levels (bisected: 4,457 serialize, 4,458 crash in this sandbox).

All of these stages now walk on explicit work stacks, so document nesting costs heap rather than call frames on the stages this PR repairs. The full-chain differential below verifies this at runtime-basis inputs, but the write (save) leg is not recursion-free without qualification: two retained limits stay on it - the source-input branch of `projectConfigWriteSource` still clones with native `structuredClone` before publication (`io.write-prepare.ts:1590`), and the array-identity/escaped-reference accounting helpers retain recursive literal-path collection and native whole-row equality (the recursive `collectLiteralArrayIdentityPaths` walk in `env-preserve.ts`) plus recursive escape-counting visits (`env-preserve-authored.ts`). Those are pre-existing main behavior, outside the five repaired stages. The remaining ceilings on deeply nested documents sit outside the write leg: the read chain's include resolver and include pre-scan (the repair surfaces of #152889 and #153711), and the CLI mutation runner's own tree clone (see accounting below).

## What Changed

- `src/config/config-json-serialize.ts` (new): `serializeConfigJson(value)` - a byte-identical reimplementation of `JSON.stringify(value, null, 2)` on an explicit work stack. It covers the platform semantics this document class exercises: `toJSON` re-application (bounded, like the platform's own cycle path), object members with `undefined`/function/symbol values vanishing while array items collapse to `null`, `String(number)` formatting with non-finite numbers as `null`, lone-surrogate escaping, and cycle detection (`TypeError`, matching the platform).
- `src/config/config-change-paths.ts`: `collectChangedPaths()` walks both documents on an explicit work stack instead of recursion. The visited path set and its order are unchanged (asserted against a recursive reference implementation).
- `src/config/source-value-projection.ts`: `projectRuntimeChangesOntoSource()` walks on explicit enter/exit frames; native `structuredClone` is replaced by the shared stack-safe clone. Sentinel semantics (`UNCHANGED`/`ABSENT`), the delete-on-projection behavior, and the allowed-key checks are unchanged.
- `src/config/merge-patch.ts`: `createMergePatch()`, `applyMergePatch()`, and `mergePatchConflicts()` walk on explicit frames (key-list frames preserve DFS key order; an exit frame preserves the skip-when-empty patch semantics; array-by-id merging keeps its slot boxes). The internal recursive clone is replaced by an exported stack-safe `cloneUnknown`, which is also what removes the native `structuredClone` call inside `mergeObjectArraysById`.
- `src/config/env-preserve.ts`: all three env-ref passes walk on explicit frames. `restoreEnvVarRefsFromResolved` keeps document key order for newly-inserted keys, keeps the template-match/escape-check ordering, and keeps `EnvRefArrayMutationError` fail-closed behavior; `restoreEnvRefsFromMap` keeps its return-original-reference-when-unchanged semantics.
- `src/config/env-preserve-authored.ts`: the two `containsAuthored*EnvTemplate` probes share one iterative deep-search helper.
- `src/config/merge-patch.ts` + `src/config/env-preserve.ts` (review follow-up): the rebuilt trees settle child values through one shared `settleContainerValue` helper, which settles an authored own `__proto__` key as inert own data (the way the replaced `Object.fromEntries`/`structuredClone` walks kept it) instead of invoking the inherited setter through plain assignment.
- `src/config/deep-equal-stack-safe.ts` (new): `deepEqualStackSafe(a, b)` - the stack-safe tree equality used wherever these modules previously reached for `isDeepStrictEqual` on whole documents (leaf comparison still uses `isDeepStrictEqual`, so leaf semantics are unchanged).
- `src/config/io.write.ts:354`: the write emits `serializeConfigJson(stampedOutputConfig)` instead of the platform call. The bytes are identical.

## Evidence

### Component level (this sandbox, Node 24 stack)

| Stage | Recursive main | This head |
|---|---|---|
| Write-path `JSON.stringify`, 4,500 levels | ✅ | ✅ |
| Write-path `JSON.stringify`, 5,000 levels | ❌ RangeError (crash ≥4,458) | ✅ |
| `collectChangedPaths`, 4,500-level leaf change | ❌ RangeError | ✅ |
| `collectChangedPaths`, 5,000-level leaf / array growth | ❌ RangeError | ✅ |
| Env-ref resolve + restore round-trip, 5,000 levels | ❌ RangeError | ✅ |
| Env-ref map restore, 5,000 levels (changed / unchanged-ref) | ❌ RangeError | ✅ |
| Merge-patch diff + apply, 5,000 levels | ❌ RangeError | ✅ |
| Runtime-source projection, 2,000 levels (edit + unchanged) | ❌ RangeError | ✅ |

### Full chain through `writeConfigFileFromContext` (save + reread)

Real entry point, isolated state dir, no test harness: `createConfigIO` from `src/config/io.factory.ts`, then `io.writeConfigFile(...)` followed by `io.readConfigFileSnapshot()`. The deep document rides under `plugins.entries.probe.config` (the schema's free-form record slot), so it passes schema validation and reaches the whole write chain - diff, projection, env-ref passes, merge patch, validation, serialization, publish - and then the read chain on reread. main is checked out at `103115f2f0b` (current origin/main), this head is `53c0774cb93`.

| Document depth | Recursive main | This head |
|---|---|---|
| 1,200 - save + reread | ✅ | ✅ |
| 1,500 - save + reread | ✅ | ✅ |
| 1,700 - save + reread | ❌ RangeError at native `structuredClone` via `cloneUnknown` inside `createMergePatch` (`merge-patch.ts:16/40`) | ✅ |
| 2,000 - save + reread | ❌ same | ✅ exit 0, both legs (save 7.4s, reread 138ms) |
| 2,200 - save + reread | ❌ same | ❌ RangeError at `IncludeProcessor.processObject` (`includes.ts:222`) - read-chain include resolver, the #152889 surface |
| 3,000 - save + reread | ❌ same | ❌ RangeError at `containsConfigIncludeDirective` (`io.read-helpers.ts:90`) - the #153711 surface |

At this head the five repaired stages complete with zero tree-deep recursion on them at every depth up to the read-chain ceiling (the differential uses runtime-basis inputs, so the retained source-input and array-identity limits above are not exercised by it); both remaining failure frames are in the read chain, outside this PR's surface.

### Real CLI subprocess matrix (`config set` + `config get`)

`node --import scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts config set plugins.entries.probe.config.leaf '"touched"' --strict-json` against a pre-seeded deep document in an isolated `$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, then `config get` on the same path. Each run is a fresh subprocess and state dir.

| Depth | Recursive main | This head |
|---|---|---|
| 600 - set + get | ✅ | ✅ |
| 900 - set + get | ✅ | ✅ |
| 1,000 - set + get | ✅ | ✅ |
| 1,100 - set + get | ✅ | ✅ |
| 1,200 - set | ❌ `Maximum call stack size exceeded` | ❌ same error |
| 1,600 / 2,000 / 2,400 - set | ❌ same error | ❌ same error |

**Accounting for the CLI ceiling:** the CLI's ceiling is below the write chain's because `config set` engages the mutation runner before the write chain: `runConfigOperations` clones the whole resolved document with native `structuredClone` (`src/cli/config-cli-runner.ts:315`), which overflows around 1,200 levels on both main and this head. That stage is not on the write chain and is not part of the issues this PR fixes, so the CLI boundary is unchanged by this PR; the write-chain recovery is proven at the `writeConfigFileFromContext` boundary in the table above. Beyond that, the read chain carries its own untouched recursions (include resolver at `includes.ts:222`, pre-scan at `io.read-helpers.ts:90`) which bound the reread leg independently - those are the repair surfaces of #152889 and #153711. One further limit sits inside the write leg itself: when the write runs on a source basis, `projectConfigWriteSource` clones with native `structuredClone` (`io.write-prepare.ts:1590`), so source-basis deep documents overflow there on both main and this head, and the array-identity/escaped-reference accounting keeps its pre-existing recursive and native-equality paths. These are main behavior, unchanged by this PR, noted so the recovery claim stays scoped to the five repaired stages.

Serialized-byte equivalence is pinned two ways: the 400-case fuzz compares `serializeConfigJson` against `JSON.stringify(value, null, 2)` directly, and the full `io.write` suites (361 tests) pass unchanged at this head - those suites assert written bytes through the config hash chain and reread snapshots, so any byte drift would fail them.

### Authored own `__proto__` key preservation (own-property compat)

The iterative rebuilds settle child values into freshly built containers. Plain assignment invokes the inherited `__proto__` setter: the own key is lost and the value is grafted onto the tree's prototype, and array identity matching over the comparison tree can consequently reject unchanged rows. `settleContainerValue` (shared by the stack-safe clone and all three env-ref settlements) defines such keys as inert own data instead. Repros in `env-preserve.test.ts` (authored key built via `JSON.parse`), pre-fix red to post-fix green at this head:

The previously requested unchanged-array regression is now pinned: an untouched two-row array whose rows carry a JSON-parsed own `__proto__: null` data key. The comparison tree must settle that key as inert data, or neither row equals its resolved counterpart (`matchesArrayElementAtSameIndex` in `env-preserve.ts`) and both array identities go unmatched. Pre-fix (parent `49cd9710ccf`) the restore output dropped the rows' own key — `{ providers: [{…(2)}, {…(2)}] }` against the expected three-key rows — and the test fails; at this head it passes.

| Surface | Recursive main | Pre-fix head | This head |
|---|---|---|---|
| Comparison tree keeps the authored own `__proto__` key (`Object.fromEntries` baseline) | ✅ | ❌ assignment lost the key | ✅ inert own data |
| Array identity matching over the comparison tree | ✅ | ❌ could reject unchanged rows | ✅ |
| Restore / map-restore output keeps the key | ❌ pre-existing setter loss | ❌ carried over | ✅ inert own data |
| Unchanged two-row array keeps its rows' keys and references | ✅ | ❌ rows lost the key, identities unmatched | ✅ |

### `checks-node-compact-large-10` diagnosis (recorded owning repair, not this PR's surface)

The 2026-09-21T21:00Z run's single failure is `src/state/openclaw-agent-db-module-identity.test.ts` ("shares agent ownership, worker publication, reclamation queues, and commit observers across transformed SDK modules") at line 271: `AssertionError: spawnSync <toolchain node> ETIMEDOUT: expected null to be +0`. That test spawns a fresh Node child with a fixed `timeout: 30_000` and `JITI_FS_CACHE: "0"` (source transforms re-run on every spawn); the shard executed 2,492 tests over 467s; the likely cause - inferred from the timing, not verified - is a saturated runner pushing the child past its fixed budget, which returns `result.status` as `null`. The test file is byte-identical on main and outside this PR's config-write surface, and a spawn timeout is purely load-sensitive. A plausible owning repair - proposed, not verified - would be a more generous child budget (or a spawn retry) in that test; recorded here per the review request instead of retrying for green, and this head's CI run re-runs the shard.

The 2026-09-22T12:35Z run on `f7d6123142` failed the same shard on a second, unrelated signature: `src/cron/service.heartbeat-busy-poll.test.ts` at line 247, `expected "vi.fn()" to be called once, but got 0 times` inside `vi.waitFor` after `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync` — the heartbeat request was never observed within the wait budget (runner saturation is inferred, not verified). That file is byte-identical on main and equally outside this PR's config-write surface. Two distinct load-sensitive signatures in one shard (a `spawnSync` child budget on the first signature, a `vi.waitFor` budget on the second) are consistent with saturated-runner flake as seen from the shard's own test files; plausible owning repairs - proposals, not verified - live in those test files on main, and this PR documents them instead of retrying for green. The same run also failed compact-large-8 (`gateway/embeddings-http.test.ts` close-count race inside `vi.waitFor`, 25 vs 26, plus a cascading state-db borrower leak from the failed cleanup), compact-large-14 (`cli/resume-cli.test.ts` bootstrap-credential retire, `helloCount` 1 vs 2 inside a 5s `vi.waitFor`), and compact-large-18 (`gateway/server.sessions.archive-worker-placement.test.ts`, `drainStarted` never observed plus a revoked session-history read) — four shards, four signatures, all `vi.waitFor`-family timing waits, none in the diff.

### Merge with current main (reference-intent/file-ownership landing)

Main landed `#147440` (reference intent + file ownership) and `#152490` (value-traversal isolation) while this PR was under review, so the branch was merged at head `add3c594` (merge of `54c312971a4` into `be48a677367`). The conflicts resolved:

- The iterative env-ref restoration frames are kept, and main's explicit-intent semantics are settled through them: the string-leaf explicit-template intent check, per-child explicit-path tracking on every container descent, and the escape-check fail-closed pass now also carries the stable-identity lookup plus the conditional explicit paths it feeds to `containsUnaccountedActiveEscapedEnvRef`.
- Main removed the env-ref map restore path (`restoreEnvRefsFromMap` and the whole `envRefMap` collection in the writer); the merge follows that removal, so restoration flows through the one iterative `restoreEnvVarRefsFromResolved` with explicit intent paths. `resolveStableArrayIdentityMatch` is now exported from `env-preserve-array-identity.ts` (its body is byte-identical to main's) for the escape-check pass. (Superseded by the round-2 merge below: that module is gone and main's in-place helpers are used directly.)
- The stack-safe `containsAuthored*` walkers in `env-preserve-authored.ts` are kept on top of main's explicit-intent additions to that module.
- The stack-safe JSON serialization stays at the publication boundary (`io.write.ts` keeps `serializeConfigJson` on top of main's write-topology refactor), and main's `io.write-values.ts` restore entry (which passes `explicitSetPaths`) is kept.
- The 61 remaining textual conflicts were main-side deletions of files this PR never touched (extension/package modules moved on main), resolved by taking main's deletions.

Verification at the merge head: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` is clean (checked out in a dependency-installed worktree at the merge tree; the primary sandbox carries stale `packages/*/dist` declarations that produce unrelated symbol-inference noise), and the merged test face is green: `env-preserve.test.ts` 95/95 (main's explicit-intent suite plus this PR's stack-safe and authored own `__proto__` suites), `merge-patch` + `config-json-serialize` + `config-change-paths` + `source-value-projection` 26/26, and `io.write-config` + `io.write-prepare` + `io.write-reread` + `io.write-effects` 409/409, plus `io.write-lock` green.

### Merge with current main (round 2: array-matching unification landing)

While this PR waited on review, main unified the escaped-template matcher into `matchAuthoredTemplateArrayItems(arrays, "substitution" | "escaped", claimedIncomingIndexes?)` and moved the array-identity helpers back into `env-preserve.ts`, so the branch was re-merged at head `e814cf0406a` (merge of main `68d49169a53` into the prior head). The conflicts resolved:

- The iterative `restoreEnvVarRefsFromResolved` frames are kept and now call main's unified matcher with the mode parameter; the standalone `env-preserve-array-identity.ts` module is dropped (main keeps the helpers in place), and the stack-safe `settleContainerValue` stays exported from `merge-patch.ts` for both the merge-patch builders and the env-ref restore frames.
- `resolveEnvVarRefsForComparison` and the authored-template probes stay on their iterative walks; `resolveWriteEnvSnapshotForPath` and the retained-limit recursion (`collectLiteralArrayIdentityPaths`, the escape-counting visits) follow main verbatim.
- `merge-patch.ts` keeps the stack-safe builders on top of main's cleanups (inlined array-entry path formatting, the redundant pre-loop id-guard removal, and the `applyMergePatch` base passthrough, which is behavior-identical because a non-object base is normalized to an empty result either way).
- The wrapper component list drops the removed module and keeps `config-json-serialize.ts` and `deep-equal-stack-safe.ts`.

Verification at the merge head: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` is clean in a dependency-installed worktree at the merge tree (a first cut of the merge left the escape-check frames carrying `readonly unknown[]` into main's mutable `EnvRefArrays`; TS4104 caught it in CI at `env-preserve.ts` 536/537 and the frames are narrowed to `unknown[]` at the fix head), and the merged test face is green: `merge-patch` + `config-json-serialize` + `config-change-paths` + `source-value-projection` 25/25, `env-preserve` + the stack-safe and authored own `__proto__` suites 51/51, and `io.write-config` + `io.write-reread` + `io.write-prepare` 182/182.

### Test timings

- The two new test files from the first stage: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/config-change-paths.test.ts src/config/config-json-serialize.test.ts` - 2 files / 10 tests pass, 1.59s wall.
- The extended suites: `src/config/env-preserve.test.ts` (86 tests, including the 5,000-level round-trips, the three authored own `__proto__` repros, and the unchanged two-row array repro), `src/config/merge-patch.test.ts` (13 tests including the 5,000-level diff/apply pair), and the new `src/config/source-value-projection.test.ts` (2,000-level edit + unchanged-clone) all pass, plus the full config write face (`io.write-config.test.ts` + `io.write-reread.test.ts` + `io.write-prepare.test.ts`, 377 tests) in 266s.

## How Was This Tested

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/io.write-config.test.ts src/config/io.write-reread.test.ts src/config/io.write-prepare.test.ts` - all pass at this head (182 across the three files at the round-2 merge head; main reorganized the suites since the first stage).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/env-preserve.test.ts src/config/merge-patch.test.ts src/config/source-value-projection.test.ts src/config/config-json-serialize.test.ts src/config/config-change-paths.test.ts` - all pass.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/env-preserve.test.ts` - the three authored own `__proto__` repros are red before the settlement fix and green at this head, and the unchanged two-row array repro is red at the pre-fix parent `49cd9710ccf` (rows drop their own key, identities unmatched) and green at this head.
- The full-chain differential table above at depths 1,200-3,000, main vs this head, on the real `writeConfigFileFromContext` entry.
- The real CLI `config set` + `config get` matrix above at depths 600-2,400, main vs this head.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json` and the repo formatter are clean on touched files.

## Compatibility

Written bytes are unchanged (differential-tested reimplementation of the exact platform call it replaces, plus hash/reread assertions), change detection returns the same paths in the same order, merge-patch key ordering and skip-when-empty semantics are preserved, env-ref restore keeps document key order and its fail-closed error behavior, and projection keeps its sentinel/delete semantics. No schema, state, or public contract changes. The settlement fix changes one observable behavior: an authored own `__proto__` key now survives the env-ref restore and map-restore output as inert own data instead of being silently dropped by the inherited setter (main dropped it as well; the replaced `structuredClone`/`fromEntries` walks kept it), and the comparison tree keeps main's own-property semantics. Documents deep enough to crash any of the five repaired stages now complete the entire write leg (runtime-basis inputs); the remaining ceilings - CLI mutation-runner clone, read-chain include resolver and pre-scan, and the retained source-input `structuredClone` plus array-identity/escaped-reference recursion noted above - are outside the five repaired stages and unchanged by this PR.
