prs.title: fix(agents): emit before_model_resolve on the CLI-backed turn path
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`before_model_resolve` never fires for CLI-backed models (`agentRuntime.id = "claude-cli"` and siblings). `runAgentAttempt` dispatches those turns to `runCliAgent` and returns before the embedded runner's model setup, which is the only place the hook was emitted. Plugins therefore cannot do per-turn model routing on the CLI runtime — every turn stays on the configured primary model (#156038).

## What Changes

- New `src/agents/cli-runner/model-resolve-hook.ts`: emits `before_model_resolve` once per CLI-backed turn, before CLI preparation normalizes the model for the child process, via the shared `resolveHookModelSelection` seam. It reports the logical provider (e.g. `anthropic`) in the hook context, not the execution backend.
- Override acceptance on the CLI path is bounded: only overrides that resolve back to the already selected CLI execution backend are applied to the child's `--model`; cross-runtime overrides preserve the caller's selection and log a warning instead of silently changing the transport. `modelSelectionLocked` sessions skip the hook, matching the embedded path. Isolated completions and backend control operations never enter agent hooks.
- ~~`before_prompt_build` hook context reported the logical provider~~ — reverted in round 3 per review: the prompt-build context keeps reporting the execution backend (`params.provider`) as on main; only the new `before_model_resolve` context reports the logical provider.
- `resolveHookModelSelection`'s local `HookContext` type gains an optional `modelProviderId` passthrough.

## How It Was Verified

- New unit suite `src/agents/cli-runner/model-resolve-hook.test.ts` (5 tests, all passing):
  - no hook registered → caller selection untouched;
  - same-backend override (`anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` → `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`, both mapped to `claude-cli`) is applied and the hook fires exactly once;
  - cross-runtime override (`openai/gpt-5.6` mapped to `openclaw`) is rejected and reported via `rejectedOverride` with the caller selection preserved;
  - hook context reports `modelProviderId: "anthropic"` (logical provider, not `claude-cli`);
  - `modelSelectionLocked` session never invokes the hook.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts` (184 tests) passes unchanged — covers the `before_prompt_build` context change including the `modelProviderId` assertion.
- `tsgo`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` clean for all touched files.

## Notes

- The hook can only act before the child process is spawned, so a same-backend override replaces the model passed to the backend; a cross-runtime override cannot be honored without changing the execution transport, which is why it is explicitly rejected rather than applied.
- `runCliAgentInternal` stays under the file's line budget by owning the wiring in `model-resolve-hook.ts`.

## Evidence

Before fix: `resolveHookModelSelection(...)` was called only from embedded-runner model setup (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/model-setup.ts`), and `runAgentAttempt` returned into `runCliAgent` before that setup, so a plugin registering `before_model_resolve` never saw CLI-backed turns — the reported repro (hook log line absent, effective model stays `claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5`) follows directly from that dispatch structure.

After fix (new suite, all 5 passing):

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

- Same-backend override applied: `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 → anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` (both mapped to `claude-cli` via `agentRuntime.id`), hook fired exactly once, hook context reported `modelProviderId: "anthropic"`.
- Cross-runtime override rejected: `openai/gpt-5.6` (mapped to `openclaw`) → `applied: false`, `rejectedOverride` reported, caller selection preserved.
- `modelSelectionLocked` session never invoked the hook.
- Regression: `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts` — 184 tests passed, including the `before_prompt_build` `modelProviderId` assertion.
- `tsgo`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` clean for all touched files.


### Round 2: review findings and CI fixes (head 36c8074b707)

- CI: the turn helpers are no longer production exports — `resolveCliModelOverrideForTurn` and `runCliModelResolveHookForTurn` are module-private behind the exported `applyCliModelResolveHookForRun` seam (clears the knip `check-dependencies` red and the `check-test-types-core-2` TS2488, which the test rewrite fixes by typing the mock call non-optionally). Local knip production run is clean.
- Provider-only override rejection: a hook response that changes only the provider (model unchanged) previously hit the unchanged-selection early return and was silently dropped. It now falls through to backend resolution and is reported via `rejectedOverride` with the warning log, same as a cross-runtime override.
- Channel routing context: the CLI hook context now carries the same channel/account projection the prompt-build hook context reports (`buildAgentHookContextChannelFields` → `channelId`/`accountId`), so both CLI-side hooks see identical routing fields. `HookContext` gains an optional `accountId` passthrough.
- Test suite rewritten against the exported seam (`vi.mock` of the global hook runner) and extended: 7 tests passing, including the provider-only rejection and channel-routing assertions.

### Round 3: real-plugin proof and review findings (head c2dce2f3962)

- **[P1] prompt-build provider value preserved:** `before_prompt_build` hook context again reports `modelProviderId: params.provider` (the execution backend), the value current main reports; the logical-provider projection is now limited to the new `before_model_resolve` hook context. `prepare.test.ts` still passes unchanged (184 tests, `modelProviderId` assertion included).
- **[P2] auth-profile-aware override check:** the backend-resolution comparison in `model-resolve-hook.ts` now passes the caller-selected `authProfileId` to `resolveCliRuntimeExecutionProvider`, mirroring how `runAgentAttempt` resolves the configured runtime (`attempt-execution.ts` passes `selectedAuthProfile?.id`), so a same-backend override on a profile-selected CLI runtime is no longer rejected as cross-runtime.
- **Real-behavior proof:** new committed CI test `src/agents/cli-runner/model-resolve-hook.real-plugin.test.ts` — a plugin file on disk is loaded through the production `loadOpenClawPlugins`, activated through the production `initializeGlobalHookRunner`, and a CLI-backed turn is driven through the exported `applyCliModelResolveHookForRun` seam (the exact call site `runCliAgent` invokes before CLI preparation):
  - the plugin's `before_model_resolve` handler fires exactly once and appends a trace record showing the hook context it received: `{"prompt":"route this turn","modelProviderId":"anthropic","sessionId":"session-1","trigger":"agent-turn","channelId":"chan-1"}` (logical provider + channel routing);
  - the same-backend override (`claude-opus-5-5` → `claude-sonnet-5`, both on `claude-cli`) is folded into the run's model before the child is prepared;
  - pre-fix check: with `src/agents/cli-runner.ts` and the hook module restored to the pre-fix parent (735e46e75b8), the same test fails with `TypeError: applyCliModelResolveHookForRun is not a function` — the CLI path had no emission point.
- CI TS red fixed: the stub hook runner's `runBeforeModelResolve` mock now declares its `(event, ctx)` parameters so the call assertions typecheck (`TS2493`/`TS2532`).


### Round 4: attachment metadata and full-turn child proof (head dd10a7c9b8a)

- **[P2] attachment metadata forwarded:** the CLI hook call now passes `attachments: buildBeforeModelResolveAttachments(params.images)` — the same projection the embedded runner derives from prompt image refs (`model-setup.ts`) — so image-aware routing plugins see identical `before_model_resolve` input on embedded and CLI turns. New test covers an image-bearing turn: the hook event arrives as `{ prompt, attachments: [{ kind: "image", mimeType: "image/png" }] }`.
- **Real-behavior proof at full turn depth (no adapter invocation, no spawn mocks):** new committed CI test `src/agents/cli-runner/model-resolve-hook.full-turn.test.ts` drives one complete turn through the exported production entry `runCliAgent`:
  - a plugin file on disk is loaded via `loadOpenClawPlugins`; it registers a plugin-owned CLI backend (`registerCliBackend`, `modelProvider: "stub"`, command = a real local executable) and a `before_model_resolve` router;
  - the turn completes against a **real spawned child process** (the stub CLI executable logs the exact argv it was spawned with) and returns its reply: `finalAssistantVisibleText === "stub reply after routing"`;
  - the child's recorded argv contains `exec` and `--model stub-routed-model`, and does not contain the caller's `stub-base-model` — the loaded plugin's override reached the CLI-backed child;
  - the hook handler itself traced exactly one `before_model_resolve` firing with the turn prompt;
  - nothing on the spawn path is mocked — the test never imports `execute.test-support`, so the real process supervisor spawns the child.
  - `--model` here is the backend-configured model flag (`modelArg`), the same argv slot `claude-cli`'s `--model` occupies.
- Suite totals: `model-resolve-hook.test.ts` 6 tests (incl. image-bearing turn), `model-resolve-hook.real-plugin.test.ts` 1, `model-resolve-hook.full-turn.test.ts` 1 — all passing.
- CI note (head c2dce2f3962): the single `checks-node-changed-compact-large-22` failure is `src/gateway/session-utils.queued-collector-admission.test.ts` ("Queued collector session changed before cancellation publication"), a gateway/session admission test in a subsystem this PR does not touch (`src/agents/cli-runner/*` only); it belongs to the known gateway SQLite/session flaky pool. Re-run requires admin rights this fork account does not have.

### Round 5: measured test cost (head 596e27e02a6)

Measured one-worker wall time per new test file (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <file> --pool=forks --maxWorkers=1`, this machine, head 596e27e02a6):

| Test file | Tests | One-worker wall time |
|---|---:|---:|
| `src/agents/cli-runner/model-resolve-hook.test.ts` | 8 | 97.1s (worker includes spawn-prep overhead; vitest in-run test time 2.5s) |
| `src/agents/cli-runner/model-resolve-hook.real-plugin.test.ts` | 1 | 33.0s (in-run test time 0.4s) |
| `src/agents/cli-runner/model-resolve-hook.full-turn.test.ts` | 1 | 64.1s (in-run test time 2.0s) |

CI seconds (run 36113720283, `checks-node-changed-compact-large-31/-32`, branch CI on the predecessor head dd10a7c9b8a — same three files, per-test durations identical in kind to 596e27e02a6 whose shard rerun was cancelled by the unrelated compact-large-19 flake):

- `model-resolve-hook.test.ts`: 8 tests, 2.5s summed test time in shard `agentic-agents-support-hosted-1` (shard total 419.49s for 137 files).
- `model-resolve-hook.real-plugin.test.ts`: 1 test, 384ms in shard `agentic-agents-support-hosted-2`.
- `model-resolve-hook.full-turn.test.ts`: 1 test, 2049ms in shard `agentic-agents-support-hosted-1` (real spawned child dominates).
- Job totals: `checks-node-changed-compact-large-31` 14m25s (success), `-32` 7m08s (failed on the gateway flake above, before agents shard rerun).

Per-file budget is dominated by per-worker runtime preparation (identical for pre-existing files in the same shard); the marginal in-run test time added by these three files is ~4.9s CI seconds.



## Round 8 — CS Rev7 finding: logical provider on subscription-auth dispatch

- **[P2] Pass the logical provider from subscription-auth dispatch**: `runEmbeddedAgentViaCliBackend` now passes `modelProvider: params.provider` to `runCliAgent` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/cli-backend-dispatch.ts`), so the CLI-side `before_model_resolve` hook on the subscription-auth caller sees the caller's logical provider (e.g. `anthropic`) instead of the CLI backend name (`claude-cli`), and a same-backend override naming the logical provider is folded into the routed model instead of self-rejecting. Callers that never resolved a provider pass `undefined`, which keeps the runner's existing `modelProvider ?? provider` backend fallback — behavior identical to before for those.
- **Tests** (`cli-backend-dispatch.test.ts`, 41/41 green): the canonical-ref dispatch cases now pin `modelProvider: "anthropic"` on the dispatched `runCliAgent` params (pre-fix red: `undefined` under the same assertions, 4 failed), and a new case pins that a caller without a resolved provider still dispatches with `modelProvider: undefined` (fallback preserved). Together with the existing full-turn test (override reaches the spawned child's routed `--model` when the hook receives the logical provider), this covers the subscription-auth caller end to end: dispatch → hook context → child model.
- Repo `tsgo`, oxlint, and oxfmt clean on the changed files. Head `ed965f23360`.


## Round 9 — CS Rev8 P1: keep backend-keyed tool policy on subscription-auth dispatch (head 69cfcf25234)

- **[P1] The Rev7 fix routed the logical provider into preparation's policy input**: `modelProvider` is preparation's tool-policy input ("Selected model provider used for tool policy; distinct from a CLI runtime id", `src/agents/cli-runner/types.ts`). Supplying `anthropic` from dispatch also changed turns with no model hook: preparation feeds that value into the MCP capability profile (`prepare.ts` `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile`), whose `tools.byProvider` lookup matches provider keys, so a restriction keyed to `claude-cli` stopped matching and a previously denied MCP tool could reach the child.
- **Fix — carry the logical provider to the hook without replacing the policy input**: dispatch now passes the new hook-only field `hookModelProvider: params.provider` and leaves `modelProvider` untouched (`undefined`, exactly the pre-Rev7 shape — the entire preparation policy surface is byte-identical to main for subscription-auth turns). `applyCliModelResolveHookForRun` reads `logicalProvider: params.hookModelProvider ?? params.modelProvider ?? params.provider`, so the hook's routing context still reports `anthropic` and same-backend overrides keep working; every other `modelProvider` consumer (synthetic-turn meta, settlement, transcripts, diagnostics) falls back to the backend name, which is main's existing behavior for this dispatch.
- **Pre-fix red → post-fix green**: with the new assertions on `HEAD~1` (`hookModelProvider: "anthropic"` and `modelProvider` untouched on the dispatched params), 4 tests failed; with the fix, `cli-backend-dispatch.test.ts` is 41/41. The pin now enforces both halves of the invariant: the hook surface routes on the caller's logical provider, and dispatch never replaces the policy input.
- **Regression suites**: `cli-runner/model-resolve-hook.test.ts` + `model-resolve-hook.real-plugin.test.ts` 9/9, `model-resolve-hook.full-turn.test.ts` 1/1 (hook still receives the logical provider through the new field — the fallback chain keeps every existing caller green). `tsgo`, oxlint, `oxfmt --check` clean on the four touched files.
- **On the remaining proof request** (denied MCP tool rejected before execution on a subscription-auth child): the code-level invariant is now pinned by test — dispatch leaves the preparation policy input at its main-state value, so backend-keyed `tools.byProvider` denials resolve exactly as they do on main. The full-chain child-level observation (deny firing before final I/O) is environment-gated on a real spawned child with a configured backend-keyed denial; we will add it as a follow-up evidence round rather than claim it from the unit surface.



## Round 11 — CS Rev10 P2: report the selected model id in the CLI hook context (head de55d10a68d)

- **[P2] The CLI-side `before_model_resolve` context omitted `modelId`**: the embedded path passes both `modelProviderId` and `modelId` in the hook context (`run-orchestrator.ts` `hookCtx` → `resolveEmbeddedRunModelSetup` → `resolveHookModelSelection`), but the CLI-side emission reported only the provider (`src/agents/cli-runner/model-resolve-hook.ts`). A routing plugin reading `ctx.modelId` received `undefined` on CLI-backed turns and could not compare the caller-selected model before proposing an override.
- **Fix — same selection the embedded context reports**: the CLI hook context now carries `modelId: params.modelId` (the caller-selected model), and the shared hook-context projection in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/setup.ts` gains the optional `modelId` field (additive; the embedded path already supplied the value, so its behavior is unchanged).
- **Pre-fix red → post-fix green**: the new assertions (`ctx.modelId === "claude-opus-5-5"` on a CLI turn, in both the stubbed seam and the loaded-plugin trace) fail on the predecessor head (`modelId` observed `undefined`); with the fix, `model-resolve-hook.test.ts` + `model-resolve-hook.real-plugin.test.ts` + `model-resolve-hook.full-turn.test.ts` are all green on the rebased head. The loaded-plugin path now traces and pins `modelId` alongside `modelProviderId`, so the context contract is enforced end to end through the production loader.
- Repo `tsgo`, oxlint, and `oxfmt --check` clean on the touched files. Head `de55d10a68d` (rebased onto the round-5 merge of main).
- **On the remaining Rev10 proof request** (subscription-auth child denied at a backend-keyed forbidden MCP tool before execution): unchanged from Round 9's note — the policy-input invariant is pinned by test; the child-level final-I/O observation is environment-gated and will land as a follow-up evidence round.


## Round 12 — CS Rev19 P2: refresh vision capability after a same-backend hook override (head 5a2ca9e47b2)

- **[P2] Stale `modelHasVision` after routing**: a same-backend `before_model_resolve` override rewrote `params.model` (and `requesterModel`) but left `params.modelHasVision` carrying the caller's original selection (`src/agents/cli-runner/model-resolve-hook.ts`). CLI preparation copies that value into the MCP grant, and vision-dependent tool surfaces resolve against it — so routing between models with different image support exposed or suppressed the wrong tool surface.
- **Fix — re-derive from the same catalog preparation reads**: when an override is applied, the routed model's image support is re-derived from the manifest + configured catalog overlay (the identical `loadManifestModelCatalog` + `overlayConfiguredModelCatalog` pair preparation uses) with a literal provider/id match. A routed model without a catalog entry keeps the caller's value — an entry is the only evidence that can overturn the caller's derived capability. Rejected overrides never touch it.
- **Pre-fix red → post-fix green**: new regressions in `model-resolve-hook.test.ts` — routing vision→text-only must flip `modelHasVision` to `false` and text-only→vision must flip it to `true` — both fail on the predecessor head (stale caller value observed); the routed-model-without-entry and rejected-override cases pin the keep semantics. Full file 12/12 green; tsgo and oxlint clean on the touched files.
- `findModelInCatalog` was deliberately not used for the re-derivation: its miss path consults the provider policy surface (route canonicalization), which is an aliasing side quest for a hook-supplied literal id and would keep the caller's capability anyway on a miss.


## Round 13 — CS Rev21 P2: resolve CLI aliases before deriving routed vision capability (head 178531188b0)

- **[P2] Alias routes miss the catalog row**: the Round 12 re-derivation matched the hook's literal model id against catalog rows only, but a hook can route to a CLI alias (e.g. `sonnet` on claude-cli) whose catalog entry lives under the alias target — the literal lookup missed it, kept the caller's `modelHasVision`, and passed the stale value into the MCP grant.
- **Fix — mirror preparation's alias contract**: candidate identities are now the literal routed id, the claude-cli context alias (`CLAUDE_CLI_CONTEXT_MODEL_ALIASES`, the same table preparation consults), and the backend alias-table normalization (`resolveCliBackendConfig` + `normalizeCliModel`). All candidates still match catalog rows only — a total miss keeps the caller's capability, never consulting the provider policy surface.
- **Pre-fix red → post-fix green**: two new regressions — routing to `sonnet` (text-only catalog target) must clear `modelHasVision`, routing to `fable` (vision-capable target) must grant it — both fail on the predecessor head; an alias-target-without-entry case pins the keep semantics. Full file 15/15 green; sibling suites (full-turn, cli-backend-dispatch) green; tsgo and oxlint clean on the touched files.
- **CI true red also fixed**: the merge head's `check-test-types-core-2` failure (TS2322 ×3) came from main tightening `ModelDefinitionConfig`/`ModelProviderConfig` (`name`, `reasoning`, `cost`, `maxTokens`, `baseUrl` now required); the test fixtures were brought up to the new schema.
- **On the remaining Rev21 proof request** (final MCP tool surface after alias routing through the production path): the same environment-gated final-effect observation noted in earlier rounds; the helper-level contract is now pinned by the alias regressions above.


## Round 14 — rebase onto current main via preparation's alias resolver (head 885779c885b)

- **CI true red after the rebase**: `TS2459` in `model-resolve-hook.ts` — main made the claude-cli context alias table module-private behind the new `resolveClaudeCliContextModelId` export in `prepare-claude.ts`, so the Round 13 import of the raw `CLAUDE_CLI_CONTEXT_MODEL_ALIASES` table no longer type-checks.
- **Fix**: the hook now calls preparation's resolver and treats an unchanged result as "no alias" (pushing only when the resolver actually maps the routed id elsewhere) — the candidate set and its catalog-matches-only contract are unchanged. 15/15 `model-resolve-hook` and the full-turn case green; oxlint and oxfmt clean.


## Round 15 — CS Rev24 P1: guard the CLI model hook with the live session generation (head f216ae01da4)

- **[P1] Hook context lacked claiming-hook admission**: the CLI emission built its `before_model_resolve` context without the admission assertion, so `resolveHookModelSelection` ran routing hooks without the session-generation assertion and its guarded-request authority. A routing plugin awaiting work could still reach transport after the generation was revoked; revocation was only observed during later CLI preparation — too late.
- **Fix — mirror the reply hook and embedded selection path**: `runCliAgentInternal` already owns `generation.assertCurrent`; it is now threaded through `applyCliModelResolveHookForRun` into `withClaimingHookAdmission` on the hook context, so the shared selection seam asserts before the hooks and wraps their network I/O in `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority`.
- **Pre-fix red → post-fix green**: two regressions — the hook context must carry the caller's assertion through `readClaimingHookAdmission`, and a revoked generation must reject the turn before `runBeforeModelResolve` is invoked (both fail on the predecessor head). Full `model-resolve-hook` file 17/17 green; full-turn and real-plugin suites green; oxlint/oxfmt clean on touched files.
- **On the outstanding transport proofs** (revoked-generation rejection at the real boundary; allowed/forbidden MCP outcomes after alias/image routing): the unit regressions now pin the admission seam and revocation-before-hook behavior; the production-path observations remain environment-gated as noted in earlier rounds.


## Round 16 — CS Rev25 P1: fence ordinary-turn hook work behind all live turn authorities (head 138e62ee8a5)

- **[P1] Admission carried only the cron-generation assertion**: both CLI hook seams received `generation?.assertCurrent`, and `prepareCronRootSessionGeneration` returns undefined for non-cron sessions — so ordinary turns ran their `before_agent_reply` and `before_model_resolve` handlers with **no admission at all**, and even cron-rooted turns were unguarded against caller revocation, a fired abort signal, or a rotated gateway lifecycle while a routing hook awaited plugin work. The subsequent guarded fetch had no assertion for those authorities and could start network I/O after they changed; the checks at the top of `runCliAgentInternal` (and the later preparation checks) sit outside that await boundary.
- **Fix — one composed admission closure**: `runCliAgentInternal` now builds `assertHookAdmission` (lifecycle generation + abort signal + caller `assertCurrent` + session-generation assertion) and hands it to both seams, so every hook-owning turn is fenced behind the same authorities the post-hook preparation re-checks. No new surface: the fences already exist on the run path, the hooks now observe them too.
- **Pre-fix red → post-fix green** (`cli-runner.before-agent-reply-cron.test.ts`, 20/20): the new ordinary-turn regression asserts the admission exists for a non-cron turn and rejects on caller revocation and on a fired abort signal; the existing "ordinary session" scenario updated from "no claim held" to "no generation claim, but the caller/abort/lifecycle fence is live" (it fails on the predecessor head exactly as the new test does). `model-resolve-hook` 18/18 unaffected; oxlint clean on touched files.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep claude-cli catalog auth when partial refreshes omit it
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #158922

After a Gateway restart on main, `models.list` reports `available: false` for every `claude-cli/*` model even though claude-cli runs work fine, hiding the Control UI Effort picker. A `models.list` call with `{"provider":"claude-cli","refresh":true}` fixes it until the next restart. Regression after #157459.

Root cause: `replacePreparedModelCatalogAuth` treated a partial refresh as authoritative for **every** provider in its scope, even providers the refresh result carried no entry for. Startup runs partial refreshes for other providers; the passive worker result omits claude-cli's auth entries (claude-cli auth re-enters only through synthetic refs, which are scoped down to the asked providers), so the merge blanked `authModes`/`credentials`/`authStore` entries for claude-cli. `model-auth-availability` then resolves claude-cli models to unknown, which `models-list-result` projects to `available: false`. On a full `refresh: true` the worker re-discovers claude-cli auth, which is why that call repaired it until the next restart.

## Fix

In `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.catalog-auth.ts`, a partial refresh is now authoritative **only for the entries it actually produced**: per-key, entries from the scoped result replace the prior ones, but a scoped provider the result omits keeps its prior `authModes`/`credentials` entry, its prior `authStore` profile, and its prior `providerAuthLabels` label. Explicit re-discovery still replaces stale entries. No new probing is added — passive read semantics from #157459 are unchanged, so the catalog-renewal stall that PR fixed cannot return.

Production change: one function, +27/−16 net, no new seams; all three call sites (`catalog-access.ts` partial refresh, native-discovery merge, `loadAuth` merge) inherit the corrected invariant.

## Evidence

- **Pre-fix failing test** (new `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.catalog-auth.test.ts`, "retains a scoped provider's auth entries when the partial refresh omits them"): a previous auth with `authModes["claude-cli"]="oauth"` merged with a claude-cli-scoped result that carries no claude-cli entries previously produced `authModes["claude-cli"] === undefined` and dropped the `claude-cli` auth profile (verified red on the pre-fix function); post-fix the entry, credential, and profile are retained while out-of-scope providers stay untouched.
- **Replacement still works**: the sibling test "still replaces a scoped provider's entries when the refresh re-discovered them" confirms a provider the refresh *did* re-discover takes the new values, preserving the scoped-credential-provenance behavior #157459 introduced.
- **No passive-read regression**: `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.scope.integration.test.ts` 4/4 (including "retains refreshed CLI auth while acquiring an unrelated provider catalog"), `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.native-renewal.integration.test.ts`, `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.auth-recovery.test.ts`, and `src/gateway/server-methods/models-list-result.openai-routes.test.ts` all green on the fix branch.
- Repo `tsgo` typecheck, oxlint, and oxfmt clean on the changed files.

## Round 2 — CS Rev1 findings

- **[P1] Clear auth when a scoped refresh observes logout**: `replacePreparedModelCatalogAuth` now takes an `observeScopedRemovals` option. The `loadAuth` merge in `catalog-access.ts` — the explicit auth-refresh path, and the only merge whose worker request actually reads each scoped provider's credential source — passes it, so a scoped provider the refresh result omits is treated as an observed removal: its prior `authModes`/`credentials`/`authStore` profile entries are dropped. That restores the existing logout contract the worker integration test pins (a deleted credential file makes the next prepared-auth result omit the profile). The two catalog-discovery merges stay passive and keep the retention this PR introduced, so the #158922 startup blanking stays fixed.
- **[P2] Keep labels for providers outside the refresh scope**: the prior-label filter now applies the scope check itself (`!includesProvider(provider) || ...`), so an out-of-scope provider whose label the worker result happens to carry keeps its previous label instead of losing it to the filtered-out replacement.
- **Tests**: new "drops a scoped provider's prior entries when an observed refresh omits them" (pre-fix red: the prior entries survived the observed removal) and "keeps an out-of-scope provider's label the partial refresh result also carries"; all four `prepared-model-runtime.catalog-auth.test.ts` tests, `prepared-model-catalog-worker.scope.integration.test.ts` 4/4, `prepared-model-runtime.auth-recovery.test.ts`, and `models-list-result.openai-routes.test.ts` green on the fix branch; core test-types stripe clean.


## Round 3 — CI red root cause (catalog-publication rotation test)

`checks-node-changed-compact-large-37` failed on `prepared-model-runtime.catalog-publication.test.ts` "adopts current model facts after persisted oauth rotation" (`expected 3 to be greater than 3`). Verified red on this branch, green on current `main` — a real behavioral difference, not flake.

Root cause: on `main`, the partial-refresh merge drops the scoped provider's `providerAuthLabels`, so the discovery publication's content differs from the published catalog only by that lost label. `retainPreparedModelCatalogPublication` then publishes a fresh catalog identity, `modelFactsChanged: true` reaches the session projection, and it re-reads the catalog — the test's `readCatalog` count assertion was passing on the back of exactly the churn this PR fixes. With label retention in place, the auth-only rotation publication is content-identical to the published catalog (the rotated auth is already live on the shared snapshot), so the catalog identity stays stable and the projection has nothing to re-read.

Fix (test-only, +7/−2): the rotated-oauth case now pins that stability — `modelFactsChanged: false`, no projection re-read (`readCatalog` count unchanged), rows untouched, rotated auth visible on the discovered catalog. The rotated-token case (context window 32k→64k) keeps asserting the real facts-change path: `modelFactsChanged: true`, projection re-read, full row rebuild. Full file 13/13 green on the fix branch; oxlint/oxfmt clean.



## Round 4 — after-fix Gateway restart evidence (Claude CLI availability retained)

- **Setup**: isolated proof environment (state-dir sandbox + loopback gateway + PATH-shimmed `claude` stub, no machine credentials). The fix-branch gateway is the PR's own build artifact — the dist bundle contains this branch's `observeScopedRemovals`/`keepsPriorEntry` merge symbols, confirming the running code is this PR, not `main`. The gateway was restarted against a state dir that had gone through a scoped partial refresh, then queried through the real gateway RPC.
- **After-fix restart, `models list --all --provider claude-cli` through the live gateway**: all 11 `claude-cli/*` catalog rows report `Auth yes` — Claude CLI availability is fully retained after the restart that follows a partial refresh. Before this PR, a scoped partial refresh blanked the scoped providers' auth on merge, so the restarted gateway's catalog showed those rows without auth.
- **Honest negative on current main**: the same restart-then-query against current `main`'s static code does not reproduce the blanking — current `main` already retains out-of-scope providers on this path (the merge the issue reported was tightened separately), so the issue's exact trigger scenario no longer reproduces end-to-end there. We did not run a provable `main`-artifact gateway for a side-by-side table (entry provenance for the earlier `main`-dist process could not be confirmed after the environment aged), so we report this as a code-level negative rather than a runtime table: the PR's behavior is strictly the retention this PR adds, and `main` does not currently exhibit the loss the issue describes.
- **Still open**: the logout final-effect trace (credential-removal safety through final provider I/O) and maintainer security approval remain as previously scoped.


## Round 5 — CS Rev7 P1: scoped catalog refresh observes logout

The Rev7 finding is correct and is implemented on head `e4c979da302`. Round 2 recorded the provider-scoped catalog merge as passive; this round supersedes that stance for that merge.

- **Why the scoped catalog merge observes removals**: a provider-scoped `models.list` refresh (`acquireProviderCatalog` in `prepared-model-runtime.catalog-access.ts`) runs `worker.loadCatalog(providerIds)`, and the worker refreshes auth through the same `refreshAuthStore` the explicit auth-refresh path uses — the durable profile-store read is global and the external-CLI overlay is scoped to the request's `providerIds` — so the returned auth generation is an observation of each scoped provider's credential source. A scoped provider its result omits was observed removed; keeping its prior entry let the Gateway keep reporting a logged-out provider as available. That merge now passes `observeScopedRemovals: true`. The native-membership alignment merge in `acquireNativeCatalog` stays passive by design: it aligns a foreground harness fact, not a credential-source observation.
- **Label boundary follows the same observation rule**: when a refresh omits a scoped label, only a provider whose auth was observed removed loses its prior label; a rediscovered provider keeps it as a fallback, so an unobserved label omission cannot change the publication content — the Round 3 no-churn invariant holds and the persisted oauth rotation still publishes with `modelFactsChanged: false` (pinned by the existing rotation test, green).
- **Tests**: new `prepared-model-runtime.catalog-publication.test.ts` "stops publishing a scoped provider's auth after an observed logout refresh" — pre-fix red on this branch (the retained oauth profile survived the logout refresh: `expected { type: 'oauth', … } to be undefined`), post-fix the published catalog's profile, credentials, and auth mode for the removed provider are all cleared; measured cost ~4.9s. New unit test "keeps a rediscovered provider's prior label an observed refresh omits, drops a removed one's" (1ms) pins the label boundary. All 5 `catalog-auth` unit tests and all 8 `catalog-publication` tests green; `tsgo`, oxlint, and oxfmt clean on the changed files.
- **Still open**: the removed-credential final-I/O trace through the Gateway's final provider effect and exact-head maintainer security approval remain as previously scoped.



## Round 6 — CS Rev10 P1: native discovery also observes logout

The Rev10 finding is correct and is implemented on head `ffd59495f5e`. Round 5 recorded the native-membership merge as passive "by design"; that stance is superseded for the discovered-provider scope: the native acquisition is not a purely foreground fact — it observes credential sources.

- **Why the native merge observes removals**: when full inventory acquisition completes without a selection, `acquireNativeCatalog` calls `worker.loadAuth({ providerIds: discoveredProviders })` (`prepared-model-runtime.runtime.catalog-access.ts`, native branch) — the same worker auth read the explicit auth-refresh path uses — so a discovered provider whose result omits it was observed removed, not passed over. The merge kept the prior entry anyway (no `observeScopedRemovals`), so a native re-acquisition after a logout republished the logged-out provider's retained auth profile as still available. That merge now passes `observeScopedRemovals: true`; startup providers stay out of the scope (`discoveredProviders` excludes them), so their entries are untouched, and the Round 5 label boundary applies unchanged (only observed removals lose labels).
- **Tests**: new `prepared-model-runtime.catalog-publication.test.ts` "stops publishing a discovered provider's auth after an observed logout" — a native harness discovers a provider whose credential the first acquisition pairs; the next acquisition re-reads the source and finds it gone. Pre-fix red on this branch (retained oauth profile survived: `expected { type: 'oauth', …(6) } to be undefined`), post-fix the profile, credentials entry, and auth mode are all cleared. All 5 `catalog-auth` unit tests and all 9 `catalog-publication` tests green; `tsgo` (core + src test shards), oxlint, and oxfmt clean on the changed files.
- **Still open**: the removed-credential final-I/O trace through the Gateway's final provider effect and exact-head maintainer security approval remain as previously scoped.



## Round 7 — CS Rev12 P1: failed scoped discoveries no longer clear prior auth

The Rev12 finding is correct and is implemented on head `923361917f6`: all three production merges passed `observeScopedRemovals: true`, so the retention branch never ran in production and the reported restart fix was unreachable at the Gateway entry point. This round refines the Round 5 stance — the scoped catalog merge is an observation only for providers whose discovery actually completed.

- **What makes an omission "observed"**: a scoped `worker.loadCatalog(providerIds)` result carries `providerOutcomes`. A `ready` or `auth-rejected` outcome means the worker re-read that provider's credential source, so an auth omission there is a genuine observed removal (logout stays effective). An `unavailable` outcome means discovery never completed for that provider — its credential source was never read — so its omission is not an observation of removal, and clearing its prior auth blanked still-valid credentials (exactly the restart regression in #158922: a startup discovery failure silently logged the provider out of the published catalog). The scoped auth merge in `acquireProviderCatalog` now expresses that boundary as an `observedRemovals` predicate on `replacePreparedModelCatalogAuth` (providers whose outcome observed the source), while the merge scope itself stays the full requested set — an interim head that narrowed the scope instead dropped a cli backend's freshly re-read auth when its outcome was unavailable, caught red by the existing scope integration test, so fresh entries always enter the merge and only the removal boundary is outcome-aware. Unavailable omissions keep the prior entry until a later refresh observes that provider again. The native-membership merge and the explicit auth-refresh merge are unchanged — their scopes are already observation-complete.
- **Tests**: new `prepared-model-runtime.scoped-refresh.test.ts` "keeps a failed scoped provider's prior auth, still drops an observed logout omission" — a scoped refresh whose result carries an `unavailable` outcome and omits the provider's auth. Pre-fix red on this branch (prior credentials dropped: `expected undefined to be defined`), post-fix the prior entry survives; the same refresh with a `ready` outcome still clears the entry, pinning that the logout semantics from Rounds 5-6 are unchanged. All 18 `scoped-refresh` tests, all 5 `catalog-auth` tests, all 9 `catalog-publication` tests, and all 4 `scope.integration` tests (including "retains refreshed CLI auth while acquiring an unrelated provider catalog", red on the interim head) green; oxlint and oxfmt clean on the changed files.
- **Still open**: the removed-credential final-I/O trace through the Gateway's final provider effect and exact-head maintainer security approval remain as previously scoped.



## Round 8 — CS P1: the unavailable carve-out contradicted the worker's read order

The recurring removal-semantics finding is correct and Round 7's factual premise was wrong; it is implemented on head `68c585f9c50`. Round 7 reasoned that "an `unavailable` outcome never observed the credential source, so its omission must keep the prior auth." The worker's actual order is the opposite: `prepared-model-catalog.worker.ts` runs `refreshAuthStore` — the durable credential read for the entire requested `providerIds` scope — **before** `prepareAgentCatalogSource` starts any per-provider discovery, and the refreshed store is what the catalog result publishes as its auth. A provider's discovery outcome therefore says nothing about whether its credential was observed: `unavailable` only means model discovery failed after the store read had already happened. Excluding `unavailable` outcomes from `observedRemovals` gave that post-read discovery failure the power to resurrect a credential the store no longer contains, leaving a logged-out provider published as available — the exact authority-staleness CS flagged.

- **Fix**: `acquireProviderCatalog` in `prepared-model-runtime.catalog-access.ts` no longer filters `unavailable` outcomes out of the removal observation. The observation boundary is unchanged where it matters: the merge scope is still exactly the requested `providerIds`, out-of-scope providers are untouched, and a credential still present in the refreshed store re-enters the merge as a rediscovered entry (fresh value, not prior). Absence from the refreshed store is conservative — secret-backed entries are carried forward by `preserveResolvedSecretBackedCredentials` and external CLI profiles are re-overlaid — so an omission means every source was consulted and came up empty.
- **Tests**: `prepared-model-runtime.scoped-refresh.test.ts` "drops a removed scoped provider's auth regardless of discovery outcome" (pre-fix red on this branch: the `unavailable` leg retained the prior credential, `expected undefined to be defined`) and "keeps a scoped provider's fresh auth when discovery is unavailable but the credential remains" (pins that a still-present credential survives an unavailable discovery with its fresh value). The Round 7 test's `unavailable` leg asserted the opposite semantics and was rewritten. All 20 `scoped-refresh`, all `catalog-auth`, and all `catalog-publication` tests green; tsgo clean.
- **Still open**: the removed-credential final-I/O trace through the Gateway's final provider effect and exact-head maintainer security approval remain as previously scoped.


## Round 9 — CS Rev22 findings: removal observation follows the credential-read scope

**P1 — removed auth retained when discovery emits no provider outcome (fixed, `c59de4a4522`).**
Accepted. The scoped refresh derived `observedRemovals` from the worker's `providerOutcomes`, but the credential read covers the whole requested scope before discovery runs. A configured provider without a runtime catalog hook emits no outcome at all, so its removed credential survived in the published catalog. The call site now passes only `observeScopedRemovals: true` and lets `replacePreparedModelCatalogAuth` treat every in-scope omission as observed — observation tracks the credential-read scope itself, not outcome presence. This subsumes the earlier unavailable-outcome handling.

**P2 — legacy `agents.list` roster in the logout fixture (fixed, same commit).**
The added logout fixture is now `entries: { default: {} }`, matching the current `AgentsConfig` shape; `check-test-types-core-2` no longer reports TS2353.

**Regression coverage.** `prepared-model-runtime.catalog-publication.test.ts` now parameterizes the observed-logout refresh over `unavailable` and `omitted` outcomes; both fail on the prior head (the omitted case retains the logged-out credential) and pass after the fix. The equivalent scoped-refresh coverage moved into the same file so the scenarios share one owner-level fixture.

Still outstanding, unchanged: redacted final-effect removal proof (production path) and exact-head maintainer security approval.

prs.title: fix(agents): store hook prompt context in the append-only runtime carrier
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #166271. On models that use append-only runtime context (`bindsClaudeThinkingPrefix`: Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1), `prependContext`/`appendContext` returned by a `before_prompt_build` hook was folded into the active user prompt for one run only and never stored. The next run replayed the earlier user message without the injected block, so the request was no longer an append-only extension of the previous one:

- every cache entry written during the run sat after that rewritten message, so none of them could be read again — a plugin injecting on every message (memory recall is the common case) restarted the prompt cache on every turn;
- every replayed thinking block after that message was dropped (`replayed thinking dropped ... prefix_binding_mismatch`, `prefix_mismatch_behavior: "drop_block"`).

OpenClaw's own per-turn context does not have this problem: it rides the runtime-context carrier, is stored hidden with the turn, and replays byte-identically. Hook context went down the older one-run rewrite path instead.

## The Fix

`prepareEmbeddedAttemptPromptAssembly` gains `appendOnlyRuntimeContext`. When it is true and the prompt is non-empty, the joined hook `prependContext`/`appendContext` is no longer folded into `effectivePrompt`; `prepareEmbeddedAttemptPromptContext` instead adds it as a `conversation-data` runtime-context fragment, so it is stored hidden with the turn and replayed unchanged — the same treatment OpenClaw's own facts get, so plugin text is not raised to instruction level.

One routing decision, published once: review round 2 caught that the routing predicate was re-derived independently at each consumer and keyed on different fields — carrier construction keyed on the transcript prompt, submission on the assembled prompt. A runtime-only turn (non-empty prompt, empty `transcriptPrompt`) therefore failed both: assembly skipped the fold, carrier construction excluded the hook text, and submission suppressed `prependContext`/`appendContext`, so the model never received it. Assembly now publishes `routePromptBuildContextThroughRuntimeCarrier` in its result, and carrier construction, submission, and the compaction budget all consume that single decision; the runtime-only submission path delivers the stored carrier to the model.

Redaction (review round 7, P1): the carrier bypasses the canonical prompt-projection redaction on both consumption paths — the provider dispatch and the durable custom-message append — so hook text that `logging.redactPatterns` would have removed from the recorded prompt previously reached both the model and the retained transcript unsanitized. Carrier construction now applies `redactTranscriptText` (same policy, same config object the canonical capture uses) to the joined hook context before it becomes a fragment, so dispatch and replay see identical sanitized bytes. The legacy fold path is untouched: it still passes through `capturePersistedModelPromptProjection`, which already sanitizes.

Kept on the legacy path:

- runs without the append-only contract (all other models): the one-run prompt rewrite, unchanged;
- context-only turns (blank prompt) on append-only models: the fold, so hook context alone still reaches the model;
- the transient per-run rewrite is also withheld from `submitEmbeddedAttemptPrompt` (`prependContext`/`appendContext`) and from `pendingAdditivePrompt` in the compaction request budget, since the carrier now carries those bytes and is counted through `pendingContextMessages` — no double injection, no double counting.

Trade-off inherited from the issue discussion: stored hook blocks accumulate in history until compaction or reset; the reporter's local patch of this shape estimated 500-850 tokens per injected block, and an explicit one-run opt-out on the hook result remains possible upstream work.

## Evidence

Reproduction and regression tests (all offline, no network):

- `attempt-prompt-build.decision.test.ts` "prompt assembly hook prompt context": on `appendOnlyRuntimeContext: true` with a `before_prompt_build` hook returning `prependContext`, the assembly keeps `effectivePrompt` transcript-identical (`"Hello"`, no hook text) while still reporting `promptBuildPrependContext` for the carrier route; the legacy fold is pinned for append-only-off and for blank-prompt turns.
- `attempt-prompt-context.test.ts`: the carrier carries `{ kind: "conversation-data", text: <hook context> }` (prepend and append joined in order), while `promptForSession`, `promptForModel`, and `llmBoundaryPromptForPrecheck` stay bare user bytes; with the append-only contract off, the carrier contains no hook text and the folded model prompt is preserved.
- Empty-transcript regression (review round 2 finding): `attempt-prompt-context.test.ts` "routes hook prompt context through the carrier when the transcript prompt is empty" pins the runtime-only turn (`effectivePrompt: "Runtime ask"`, `effectiveTranscriptPrompt: ""`) delivering the hook text through the carrier — `promptSubmission.runtimeOnly` is true, `promptForModel` stays bare, and `runtimeContextMessageForCurrentTurn` carries the hook fragment; `attempt-prompt-build.decision.test.ts` "publishes one carrier-routing decision for empty-transcript runtime turns" pins the published decision itself.
- Redaction regression (review round 7 P1): `attempt-prompt-context.test.ts` "applies the transcript redaction policy to hook context stored in the carrier" — with `logging.redactPatterns: ["sk-TEST-HOOK-SECRET-[a-z0-9]+"]` and a hook returning a `prependContext` containing `sk-TEST-HOOK-SECRET-9f2`, the carrier fragment must not contain the raw secret and must equal `redactTranscriptText(hookPrepend, config)` byte-for-byte; `promptForModel` stays clean too.

Pre-fix red runs (tests only, fix reverted):

- Routing: empty-transcript regression fails — `promptSubmission.runtimeOnly` is `undefined` (no runtime context at all reaches the turn) and the hook fragment is absent from the carrier.
- Redaction: `expect(fragment?.text).not.toContain("sk-TEST-HOOK-SECRET-9f2")` fails — the raw secret is present in the carrier fragment, exactly the round-7 P1 path.

Post-fix:

- `attempt-prompt-context.test.ts`: 29/29 (28 pre-existing + 1 new redaction test)
- `attempt-prompt-build.decision.test.ts`, `attempt-prompt-submit.projections.test.ts`, `attempt-context-advancement.test.ts`, `interrupted-input-context.integration.test.ts`, `tool-result-truncation.test.ts`: all green on the same tree.

Branch state: rebased onto current `main` (`571040c310`), latest head `e3dc40b08b`: `0949de0b07` (carrier fix carrying the routing-decision and redaction rounds) → `0e62acd2f9` (aliased-import test helper) → merge refreshes onto successive `main` tips (the net diff vs `main` was verified byte-identical to the reviewed patch: 8 files, 248+/10-, every changed line matching).

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): preserve native chat identity in followups
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Queued native follow-up turns retain the authenticated raw chat ID in `originatingChatId`, but the shared follow-up execution adapter dropped it while rebuilding `TemplateContext`. V2 plugin tools therefore received no `nativeChannelId` even though the requester, channel, account, and delivery route remained present.

Fixes #184730.

## Solution

Restore the already-captured `originatingChatId` as `NativeChannelId` in `buildFollowupTemplateContext()`. This keeps the raw conversation identity separate from the requester and delivery target and preserves the existing invocation-authority checks.

The regression now follows a queued turn through embedded execution projection into an actual V2 plugin factory and tool invocation. It covers:

- allowed Telegram DM and group identities;
- a different requester and chat rejected before the synthetic effect;
- a retained invocation rejected after admitted-run authority is revoked during an await.

The earlier mock-call field-copy assertion was removed.

## Impact

Identity-dependent plugin tools can keep failing closed for absent or mismatched facts while valid queued follow-ups receive the same authenticated native chat identity as immediate turns. No new inference, lookup, state, or authorization path is introduced.

## Evidence

- Previous head `cdddd9494f1daaef9f45c2094361c1b7235e79bc`: full hosted CI, CodeQL, Workflow Sanity, OpenGrep, and dead-code report workflows passed.

prs.title: fix(auth): refresh Anthropic OAuth credentials inside the pre-expiry window
prs.body:
Closes #103846.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Anthropic OAuth refreshes silently returning the unchanged credential while it is inside the manager's pre-expiry refresh window.

## User Impact

Anthropic OAuth credentials now rotate when the auth manager has already admitted a refresh, instead of waiting until the stored raw expiry and repeatedly treating a no-op as success.

## Why This Change Was Made

The manager deliberately enters the refresh path within its five-minute margin, but the built-in fallback delegated to `getOAuthApiKey`, whose default contract refreshes only raw-expired credentials. The explicit refresh adapter now calls the same helper with `forceRefresh: true`. The default helper behavior, plugin precedence, provider lookup, error wrapping, and the manager's existing persistence path remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- `anthropic.test.ts` seeds an Anthropic credential with four minutes remaining, requests an explicit refresh through the real built-in helper, observes the token request, and verifies rotated credentials.
- The low-value mock call-shape assertion was removed.
- Current-head CI run `40685495353` completed successfully: all 30 jobs finished with 22 successes and 8 conditional skips. This includes `checks-node-changed-1`, `checks-node-changed-2`, and `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`.
- Current-head Workflow Sanity, OpenGrep, CodeQL Critical Quality, CodeQL, and macOS dead-code reporting also passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.fallback-to-main-agent.test.ts src/llm/utils/oauth/anthropic.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Local targeted Vitest could not load the existing configuration because this dependency snapshot lacks `@solidjs/vite-plugin` and `@openclaw/proc-safe/windows-job`; it failed before collecting tests.
- Required scoped oxlint could not load the existing configuration because the same snapshot lacks `eslint-plugin-solid`; `tsgo` is absent from the snapshot. No dependency files or `node_modules` contents were changed.

## Behavior Proof (manager admission → token exchange → durable rotation)

A real-flow proof was recorded in an isolated container with an isolated state dir and a network-isolated token endpoint (`https://platform.claude.com` routed to a local TLS stub via HTTPS_PROXY + NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS; no mocks in the code path). The shipped `openclaw doctor` auth health auto-fix (`--yes`) drove the real `createOAuthManager` admission → built-in Anthropic helper forced refresh → real `fetch` over real TLS → real persistence into the agent auth-profile store.

1. Seed — credential four minutes from expiry:
```
seeded profile=anthropic:proof-profile access=seed-a… refresh=seed-r… expires=2026-11-03T13:21:42Z
```
2. Shipped flow result (doctor auth health finding after the fix):
```
{"checkId":"core/doctor/auth-profiles","severity":"warning","category":"recommended",
 "message":"Auth profile anthropic:proof-profile is expiring (55m).",
 "target":"anthropic:proof-profile"}
```
3. Token exchange reached (isolated endpoint, redacted):
```
[proxy] CONNECT platform.claude.com:443 HTTP/1.1
[stub] POST /v1/oauth/token HTTP/1.1 grant_type=refresh_token refresh_token=seed-r…bbbb
```
4. Durable rotation (re-read from the agent auth-profile store):
```
access:  STUB-r…cdef  rotated: true
refresh: STUB-r…3210  rotated: true
expires: 2026-11-03T14:21:42Z   (≈55m remaining; stub issued expires_in=3600)
refresh-fence: false
```

Both tokens rotated and were persisted; no refresh-failure fence was written.

## Current Review State

A manager-level persistence proof was attempted on two owner-store arrangements, but both hosted runs showed that the test fixture exited before the built-in provider call. Those failing experiments were removed rather than leaving unreliable coverage in the branch. Current-head CI is green. The requested manager-admission-to-persisted-rotation proof is provided above. Maintainer security approval for the workflow run remains open.

prs.body:
Closes #133108.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw sessions --json` omitted the canonical stored session category even though adjacent metadata such as color was already projected. Offline scripts could not group the same sessions as Gateway and Control UI consumers without reading private state directly.

## User Impact

JSON session rows now include `category` when it is stored. Unset or cleared categories remain omitted, and the human-readable table is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change extends the existing `toSessionDisplayRow` ownership boundary by one optional field, with focused coverage for present and cleared values and a CLI documentation update.

## Real Behavior Proof

The proof used this PR head with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. A session was written through the production session accessor, then read through the shipped CLI entry point:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<isolated-state> node --import tsx src/index.ts sessions --json
{
  "sessions": [
    {
      "key": "agent:main:proof",
      "sessionId": "proof-session",
      "label": "category-proof",
      "category": "Research",
      "visibility": "shared"
    }
  ]
}
```

The same stored row was then cleared through `patchSessionEntryCore` and read through the same CLI command:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<isolated-state> node --import tsx src/index.ts sessions --json
{
  "sessions": [
    {
      "key": "agent:main:proof",
      "sessionId": "proof-session",
      "label": "category-proof",
      "visibility": "shared"
    }
  ]
}
```

Observed result: the stored category is emitted as `"category": "Research"`; after clearing it, the `category` property is absent rather than serialized as null or an empty value. The proof state contained only synthetic identifiers and was removed after capture.

## Evidence

- Base-red focused test failed only because the expected `category` field was absent.
- Focused regression: 1 passed.
- Full `src/commands/sessions.test.ts`: 17/17 passed (Vitest duration 83.04s).
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`: passed.
- Scoped oxfmt, oxlint, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Shipped CLI proof above covers both stored and cleared categories.

prs.title: Fix update: refuse cross-root updates that cannot rebind drop-in-owned services
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #196321 (root cause half). When a Linux systemd Gateway service has an operator `ExecStart` drop-in and points at a different (older NVM) install root, `openclaw update` from a newer NVM Node's global CLI silently redirected the update at the older managed service package root: the invoking CLI stayed on the old version while shared `~/.openclaw/npm/projects/*` plugin generations migrated to the new release — a split-version state with broken plugin discovery and contradictory `status` / `doctor --fix` guidance.

## Fix

In `resolveManagedServicePackageUpdatePlan`, the cross-root decision previously fell straight through to `plan.rootRedirect` whenever `hasGatewayServiceDefinitionOverrides(command)` was true (operator drop-in owns the definition, so rebind is impossible). That redirect now refuses with a `GatewayServiceUpdateOwnershipError` carrying actionable guidance (update/remove the drop-in, or reinstall the gateway service from the invoking install), instead of silently creating the split-version state. Bun, Windows, explicit `rebind: false`, and non-refreshable verdicts keep the existing redirect behavior.

## Evidence

- Regression: the `managedOverrides` and `managedDefinition` selection cases now reject with `GatewayServiceUpdateOwnershipError` (message: "operator drop-in"); pre-fix red verified against `2865438503` (old code silently redirecting, test fails), post-fix green — all 16 `update-command-service-selection` cases pass on the pre-4700-commit baseline. The rest of the matrix (bun, win32, `rebind: false`, plain, empty) is unchanged.
- Net +15 production lines in one guard branch; no behavior change for any non-drop-in path.
- `oxfmt` clean, line-cap ratchet OK, `tsgo` core clean.

Note: this covers the update-behavior root cause from the issue. The separate stale guidance in `status`/`doctor` for launcher-overridden services (#196321's expected behavior #2) is intentionally untouched here — #196379 is already reworking the doctor diagnostic side, and I did not want to entangle the two fixes.

## Verification note

Local vitest against the current `main` baseline could not complete in this environment (runner stalls); the full pre-4700-commit-baseline red/green loop plus typecheck/format were verified locally, and CI is the final arbiter on the fresh baseline.

Fixes #196321

prs.title: fix: slow worktree cleanup blocks new sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: new sessions wait behind unrelated managed-worktree snapshots, hydration, and cleanup when capacity maintenance or restore holds the global allocation lease.

## User Impact

User impact: a slow snapshot no longer prevents another session from reserving an available worktree slot. Failed capacity snapshots now preserve the checkout instead of purging it. No configuration or schema migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the allocation lease around authoritative capacity decisions and pending-slot reservation. Existing checkout mutation leases own snapshot, restore, rollback, and retirement work. Restore consumes its existing pending slot atomically when publishing the live row; removal claims and exact registry predicates arbitrate eviction versus reuse. Orphan cleanup briefly revalidates and detaches a directory, then deletes it outside allocation custody.

This adds 159 production lines: capacity reservation for restores and custody for cleanup replace protection previously supplied by the long global lease. It introduces no cache, schema, or configuration surface.

## Evidence

- The concurrent-allocation regression fails on parent `6a03a947c275d` with the allocation lease held, then passes with this change. It calls the real service while snapshot completion is gated.
- The original 235 focused tests passed. CI/review repair runs additionally passed 106 worktree tests, 29 GC tests, and 89 workspace-projection tests (overlapping suites; two existing projection cases skip). Coverage includes capacity accounting, historical and concurrent restore, exact-state retries, eviction/run exclusion, stale generations, failed-snapshot preservation, pending recovery, source lifetime, and closure-bound delegated authority. The final name-collision repair additionally passes 63 tests across pending-slot, canonical-path, and eviction suites. The new orphan-retry regression fails on the first PR head and passes after repair.
- Staged Codex autoreviews are scoped-clean through P2, including the subsequent inferred-name collision repair. ClawSweeper reviewed final head `2a79ccf02d8d` with zero findings/open items, resolving all four prior items. `pnpm build` passes on `1a476cb55b0f`. The final two-file name-collision delta passes 63 focused tests and Codex review; `check:changed --base 1a476cb55b0f --timed` passes every gate except those same 116 unused exports (zero added/removed). `pnpm check:changed --base 3d557fffac078 --timed` also passes every gate except the same 116 parent unused exports described below (zero added/removed).
- `pnpm check:changed --base 6a03a947c275d --timed`: all changed-scope type, lint, format, size, schema, and ownership guards passed. The command exits 1 only for 116 unused-export findings, exactly matching the unchanged parent (zero added/removed). Recent baseline introducers include `472cd0a2f542` (compaction exports), `94e34f956969` (Talk thinking), `b868ed4c21ba` / #198835 (package release exports), and `1ce9df608b43` / #200088 (browser approval export). These remain main regressions, not passing checks.
- The inferred-name regression holds the second owner after destination planning, fully publishes the first owner, then releases the second. It fails on `1a476cb55b0f` with the worker uniqueness error and passes by creating `release-planning-2` after repair. The short decision now considers both live owner and live name collisions before retrying; no additional worker query round trip.
- Previous-head CI run 43998245974 timed out in the state-lease-heartbeat static-import build test. Exact CI main parent `a958f1d25c1d` passed focused reproduction on macOS and 2-CPU Linux ARM64 with pinned Bun; CI was Linux x64. Its cause remains unproven. No timeout increase, CI rerun, or inherited-failure waiver was used.
- Synthetic Linux/btrfs proof: 4 CPUs / 8 GiB, 5,000 sessions in a physically allocated 35 GiB database, and 62,000 workspace files / 1.1 GB. A two-second snapshot delay starts before a slot becomes available and a concurrent real service.create runs. A/A controls precede five serial interleaved A/B pairs; production bytes match final head `2a79ccf02d8d` (all recorded source hashes verified). Acceptance: available-slot admission must escape the snapshot delay, with no unexplained >20% whole-operation CPU/allocation regression.

| Metric | Before, median [p95] | After, median [p95] |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Request allocation wait | 7,745 [8,110] ms | 26 [48] ms |
| Create wall time | 12,688 [29,810] ms | 10,609 [32,048] ms |
| Whole GC/create wall time | 33,987 [115,047] ms | 40,017 [78,227] ms |
| Whole GC/create process CPU | 17,979 [66,970] ms | 21,014 [46,996] ms |
| Whole GC/create main V8 allocation | 2,678.68 [2,685.53] MB | 2,625.09 [2,625.47] MB |

All five paired samples are retained and every paired snapshot completed. Candidate allocation wait is 6–48 ms; baseline is 5,784–8,110 ms. Whole-operation median CPU is +16.9%, wall time +17.7%, and main V8 allocation -2.0%. No >20% median CPU/allocation regression appeared. These CPU differences are not asserted causal on the shared host: A/A controls report 7,422 / 15,528 ms allocation wait, 18,893 / 29,223 ms whole CPU, and 2.670 / 2.673 GB main allocation. The second baseline control hit the old snapshot timeout/purge path; it remains recorded and flagged. Source preparation overlapped the other checks. With five samples, p95 is the maximum, not a production-tail estimate. The principal result is removal of snapshot-length allocation blocking. Earlier-candidate measurements remain in the local evidence, separately pinned.

These owner-boundary counters include the measured Node process and thread workers but exclude child-process CPU; V8 allocation is main-isolate only. The synthetic database matches file size, not production transcript distribution. The existing memory checkpoint occurs at create return, when cleanup is at different stages, so no peak-RSS or retained-memory improvement is claimed. Separate CPU profiles from the earlier candidate are diagnostic only, not final-head performance evidence. No production data is used.

Real product proof on `1a476cb55b0f` before the subsequent name-collision-only repair: an isolated built Gateway ran `sessions.create → chat.send → agent.wait → chat.history` while a victim's actual Git object census remained paused. Allocation wait was **4 ms**, session creation **482 ms**, and a real OpenAI `gpt-4.1` assistant reply **5,131 ms**, before releasing the snapshot. The assistant returned `ALLOCATION_REPLY_OK`. Raising capacity while paused intentionally changed cleanup's runtime configuration; after release, cleanup rejected the stale commit and preserved the exact victim bytes. The Gateway shut down cleanly.
