prs.title: test(qa-lab): replayed plugin media paths stay text in the next provider request
prs.body:
Closes #168610
Related: #101866

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: nothing fails when a media path from a plugin tool registered under a core tool name, replayed from Telegram history, reaches the next provider request as an image or file input or with its text rewritten.

## User Impact

User impact: no runtime change. QA Lab gains a Crabline Telegram regression on the final provider request for replayed media references, and a mock-provider directive that scripts exact tool calls. The Crabline dependency patch gains Telegram reply ingress, used only by QA, so that regression can send its second turn as a reply.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR used to expect replay to rewrite the plugin's path to `[unverified media reference removed]/generated/...`, the behavior #101866 proposed. That expectation was wrong. #101866 was closed unmerged on October 31, and the [closing comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101866#issuecomment-6541917131) found that on main replayed references stay literal text, produce no `input_image` or `input_file` payloads, and leave stored rows unchanged. It asks that a follow-up preserve stable conversation bytes and start from a final-provider-request regression. This PR is that regression.

`telegram-plugin-core-name-media-history` installs a run-owned, non-bundled plugin that registers `music_generate` and returns a PNG under the state media directory. No music provider is configured, so the plugin's tool is the one that runs. The state media directory is a local media root, so the prompt image loader would accept that file. Turn 1 calls the tool and replies with the path through the real Telegram plugin. The last provider request on turn 2 must have:

- no `input_image` or `input_file` part anywhere in `input`, and `imageInputCount` 0;
- the turn 1 reply, byte for byte, as the bot's own `(you):` line in the Telegram chat window of the current turn's runtime context, and separately in the earlier assistant message.

Turn 2 is a Telegram reply to the bot's turn 1 message. Since #183190, an existing plain Telegram DM carries its history in the session transcript and leaves the chat window out of the turn's runtime context; replies, topics, groups and fresh DMs keep it (`shouldSuppressPersistedDmChatWindowContext` in `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-context.session.ts`). Sent as a plain DM, turn 2's request has no window line for the reply. On the reply path the window is the plugin's own (`Conversation context (chronological, selected for current message)`), which names the bot's messages `<first_name> (you)` (`buildTelegramSelfSenderName` in `extensions/telegram/src/group-history-window.ts`), so the check matches `(you): ` followed by the exact reply. The reply quote, `[Replying to: "..."]`, carries the same text without that prefix.

`QA tool plan:` works as before: the mock calls each listed tool in order with the given arguments, then replies, and `{{media:N}}` becomes the first media path the Nth result carried. It now sits at the end of main's scripted automation chain, so `server.ts` is identical to main.

pr-simplify, against merge base `f5f27c3ef6e`:

- Removed: the placeholder expectation and its `path.sep` suffix; the unmanaged control path, which only made sense for selective redaction; the `server.ts` hunk, which after merging main grew it from 2251 to 2253 counted lines against the line-cap ratchet; and the `exec_command` ordering case with its cron argument checks, which test the cron planner rather than this change.
- Still protected: a plan never preempts a scripted cron turn, plan order and media substitution, undeclared tools, drive-rooted Windows paths, and Code Mode `wait`.
- Delta against main `5767fe7aae6`: no production code. qa-lab mock +119/-2; tests +155/-1 (`server.tool-plan.test.ts` +124, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/qa-tool-plan-directive-168610.txt`, and the Crabline reply case +31/-1); qa-lab reply mapping +43/-1 (`crabline-telegram-replies.ts` +33, `crabline-transport.ts` +10/-1); scenario +240; Crabline patch +125; `patches/README.md` +2; `pnpm-lock.yaml` 4 patch-hash lines.

Crabline patch: Crabline 0.2.0's Telegram server had no reply ingress. Admin inbound never set `reply_to_message`, the server kept no sent messages to quote, and its `sendMessage` events did not carry the assigned `message_id`, so the harness could not name the bot's message. For Telegram only, `patches/@openclaw__crabline@0.2.0.patch` now keeps accepted sends, `editMessageText` results and admin inbound messages by chat and `message_id`, records `messageId` on accepted send events, and turns an admin inbound `replyToMessageId` into a Bot API `reply_to_message` (without a nested reply), refusing an unknown target with `message to be replied not found`. The bridge forwards `OpenClawCrablineInboundInput.replyToId` as that field. The patch grows by 125 lines; its existing Feishu hunks are byte-identical, Crabline stays at 0.2.0, and `pnpm-lock.yaml` changes only its 4 patch-hash lines (`87093d75728e` -> `616107004291`). qa-lab maps a bot send's bus ID to the recorded `messageId` in `crabline-telegram-replies.ts`; inbound bus IDs already are Telegram message IDs. `patches/README.md` records the hunks and the test that retires them. Crabline main has the same gap; filed upstream as openclaw/crabline#377, offering the patch as a PR there so this one can go.

## Evidence

### Merged with main `5767fe7aae6`, turn 2 as a reply (head `e3e14dbee94`)

Main `5767fe7aae6` merged in (`314bb6233df`), then `27a15890e05` for the reply and the Crabline patch, and `e3e14dbee94` for the window check. On an M4 Pro, same command as below:

- This head passes twice: 1/1, 19.6 s and 20.2 s for the scenario (76 s and 23 s for the command; the first includes the build). The checked line: `#3 … [reply target] Crabline (you): QA-CORE-NAMED-<id> plugin <state>/media/generated/qa-core-named-<id>.png`, with 0 media parts and `imageInputCount` 0.
- Turn 2 sent as a plain DM, without `replyToId`, fails the window check. Its request has 0 `(you): <reply>` lines, 0 reply quotes and no copy of the reply at all: the runtime context is the conversation info and no window (#183190).
- With the reply kept and only the window line's reply text replaced before the check, it fails too. That request still has `[Replying to: "<reply>"]` once, so the quote alone does not satisfy the check.
- With main's `mock-openai-automation-turns.ts`, turn 1 fails: `timed out after 90000ms; final bus-event kinds=[inbound-message,outbound-message]`. Turn 1 waits up to 90 s for a reply carrying the marker. Main's mock has no `QA tool plan:` directive, so it never calls `music_generate`; its one reply, sent 1 s after the inbound, is `Protocol note: acknowledged. Continue with the QA scenario plan and report worked, failed, and blocked items.` That run was on `27a15890e05`; `e3e14dbee94` only changes turn 2's check.
- The merge alone, before the reply, failed the old history check because main's #183190 dropped the window from the plain-DM turn 2. Removing that one `deliveryOnly` line locally made it pass.

Unit and gates on this head:

- 37 qa-lab test files pass: 14 mock-openai files, the 6 catalog and report files, every `crabline-*.test.ts` (the Feishu wire round trip included) and `proper-lockfile-runtime.test.ts`. Main's #198943 deleted `server.tool-routing.test.ts`, so the plan cases now live in `server.tool-plan.test.ts` (124 lines, 5 cases).
- With main's `mock-openai-automation-turns.ts`, 4 of the 5 plan cases fail (`Expected music_generate tool call`, and `expected 'Protocol note: acknowledged. Continue…' to be 'BUG-QA-TOOL-PLAN-UNDECLARED…'`). That is the same shape as the scenario's turn-1 timeout: main's mock answers a plan with its generic protocol note. The earlier evidence below removed the plan at this unit level only; it had no scenario run with main's mock.
- The new `crabline-transport-message-id.test.ts` case replies to the first of two bot sends and reads `reply_to_message` with that send's text back from `getUpdates`. With main's Crabline patch installed it fails: `Telegram QA reply target <uuid> has no Crabline message_id.`
- On `27a15890e05`: `tsgo` (7 lanes, 0 errors), oxlint, oxfmt, the test-lines (+154, allowance 400, credit 124), line-cap, max-lines and assertion-safety ratchets, `deps:patches:check`, `deps:npm-lock:check:changed` and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` pass, and the installed Crabline files match all 8 target blobs in the patch. On `e3e14dbee94`, which only changes the scenario: oxfmt on it, the two scenario catalog test files and the four ratchets pass.
- Cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Bun, macOS arm64, two runs): `crabline-transport-message-id.test.ts` 37.6 s cold and 9.8 s warm wall, the new case about 300 ms. `server.tool-plan.test.ts` 32.8 s and 6.1 s.

### Earlier head `fa0ef91b76c`

Main `f5f27c3ef6e` merged in, on an M4 Pro, with `node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite --channel-driver crabline --channel telegram --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario telegram-plugin-core-name-media-history --concurrency 1 --fast`:

- That head passed: 1/1, 22.4 s for the scenario, 105 s for the whole command including the build. The second request has 0 media parts, `imageInputCount` 0, and 2 replayed copies of the reply, both with the path unchanged.
- With a local patch that makes prompt image preparation also scan the replayed inbound history, it fails: `the replayed plugin path became provider media: {"mediaParts":["\"type\":\"input_image\""],"imageInputCount":1}`.
- With a local patch that rewrites the replayed channel-history text the way #101866 did, it fails: `second request did not replay the first reply with the plugin path unchanged`. The assistant-message copy kept the path; the channel-history copy read `[unverified media reference removed]/generated/qa-core-named-<id>.png`.
- With channel-history replay disabled locally (history limit 0), it fails: `the current turn's channel history did not replay the first reply unchanged`. The previous head `e57316ac0fa` passed that same run on the assistant-message copy alone, which is the gap ClawSweeper found.
- None of these patches is on the branch.

Unit and gates on that head:

- The `server.tool-routing.test.ts` and qa-lab catalog tests (scenario catalog and channels, coverage report, CI smoke plan, profile selection, tool coverage report) pass: 7 files, 102 tests. All 13 mock-openai test files pass: 200 tests.
- Removing the plan from the chain fails the four plan cases. Putting it first fails the ordering case (`Expected message tool call`).
- oxfmt, type-aware oxlint (a planted error is reported), `tsgo:all`, and the line-cap, assertion-safety, test-timeout-race and max-lines ratchets pass.
- The test-lines ratchet reports `over by: 10` with this change's +92 allocated. Those 10 lines are already over on main.

Cost: the scenario is crabline-only and its primary coverage ID, `plugins.plugin-tools`, is not in `smoke-ci`, so nothing per-PR runs it unless selected.

- Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Bun, the local default, macOS arm64, two runs each): `server.tool-routing.test.ts` 32.8 s (cold worker cache, 24.3 s of it compiling) and 6.8 s wall, 525 ms and 403 ms of tests. CI run 42426840111, Bun: `server.tool-routing.test.ts` 999 ms of tests in a shared run (`checks-node-changed-extensions-config`).

Not covered:
- A trusted core tool's managed path; I did not look for a synchronous core tool in QA that returns one.
- Windows; the path comparison handles JSON-escaped separators, but I have not run it there.
- Crabline refuses to start from a checkout with a group-writable ancestor directory, so I ran from a checkout of the same commit on a separate volume.

prs.title: fix: keep automations running when you open another chat
prs.body:
Closes #200307

## What Problem This Solves

Opening another chat while an automation is checking for updates can interrupt that check and turn the automation off. The CI checker also rejected the missing-ID safety check needed to repair this bug.

## User Impact

Opening a separate chat no longer stops affected automations in this way. No settings changes are needed. Automations already switched off still need to be re-enabled.

The CI correction allows direct null/undefined presence checks while continuing to reject growth in real identity comparisons and explicit identity pins. No authorization rules, retry policy, or intended cancellation behavior are changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two missing IDs were treated as a match, so creating an unrelated chat could cancel the automation. The existing guard prevents that false match. This PR now also corrects the CI checker: asking whether an ID exists is not the same as comparing it with another identity.

The allowlist is regenerated downward only, removing 318 false-positive counts across 205 entries. No allowance is increased, and the earlier session-continuity improvements are not reverted.

## Evidence

- **41 automation/operator-source tests passed**, including real authority restoration and persisted SQLite session mutations: unrelated chat creation preserves authority; replacement of the relevant target still cancels it.
- **6 checker/CI-orchestration tests passed.** Both new checker regressions fail against the previous checker and pass with the correction. The boundary test also proves that adding a real identity comparison still fails.
- The previously failing `check:session-identity-ratchet` passes locally against the PR base: 1,674 files, 6,587 grandfathered counts. All 205 changed allowlist entries strictly shrink.
- Script and tooling-test typechecks, touched-file lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent AutoReview of the complete expanded candidate, P0–P2: **scoped-clean, no actionable findings**.

Exact-head GitHub CI is pending. No full scheduled, model-driven Gateway run or production deployment is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Scope, provenance, and validation details</summary>

- #199512 made the target ID optional while retaining the unguarded equality. #200099 added the initial CI checker; #200191 broadened it to the comparison pattern that rejected this repair.
- The checker remains its existing line-based lexical scanner; this change is not a parser rewrite. It retains adjacent real comparisons, explicit pin-name checks, and inference-refusal checks.
- Six changed files overall: runtime guard, runtime regression, checker, checker regressions, shrink-only generated allowlist, and CI documentation. Runtime delta remains +2/-1 lines; checker delta +9/-2; test additions total 87 lines. No new owner or runtime abstraction.
- Automation validation: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/operator-run-recovery.test.ts src/gateway/cron-operator-source.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 41 passed; runner wall time 107.38 seconds; new runtime regression 956 ms.
- Checker validation: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/check-session-identity-ratchet.test.ts test/scripts/ci-baseline-ratchets.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 6 passed; runner wall time 1.35 seconds; new checker file 77 ms. CI timings are not yet available.
- `pnpm check:session-identity-ratchet --base df315eb3bb99eeb23e5395893e61a9e9daba80e3 --no-merge-base` passes after generated pruning, without `--prune`.
- Typechecks: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.scripts.json --noEmit` and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json --incremental`.
- AutoReview used Codex, GPT-6.1 Sol, medium reasoning, P0–P2, on the local candidate against `df315eb3bb99eeb23e5395893e61a9e9daba80e3`, committed as `a706a5d9fbde3350c548c91e9e5c96ff9dc36b40`. The reviewer assessed the supplied code and context; repository test execution and count validation were performed separately as recorded above.

</details>

Contributor: @hannesrudolph reported the issue, authored the original repair, and requested the expanded scope.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: fix: keep Send disabled after switching agents on a global chat until that agent's history loads
prs.body:
Related: #197151

## What Problem This Solves

Follow-up to #197151. In a pane on the unqualified `global` conversation, switching the selected agent keeps the same session key and connection. If the first agent's history read came back empty and the second agent's read or subscription then fails, the composer still treats the conversation as proven absent and leaves Send enabled for the second agent. The Gateway refuses that send under the second agent's permissions, so the person sees an enabled composer that cannot deliver.

## User Impact

User impact: after switching agents on a global conversation, a session-scoped person only gets an enabled composer for an unused conversation when the read for the agent now selected proved it empty. No change for agent-qualified session keys.

## Why This Change Was Made

The empty-history proof added in #197151 checked the connection and session key but not the agent the read was made for. The neighbouring accepted-history checks already require that a global key's read belongs to the selected agent. This change moves that check into one small helper and applies it to the absence proof too, so all three checks share it.

## Evidence

- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-main-session-absent.test.ts` gets a case: an empty read for `main` on `global` enables Send, then the selected agent switches to `research` on the same connection and its read fails. Without the fix the composer stays enabled (`expected true to be false`); with it Send is disabled.
- Same run, fixed: `chat-main-session-absent`, `session-method-access` and `chat-history-subscription-errors` pass (38/38).

prs.title: feat(pdf): add explicit OpenAI native document opt-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Platform users cannot explicitly choose native PDF document input through the PDF tool while preserving existing upload and model-selection behavior.

## User Impact

`agents.defaults.pdfNativeOpenai: true` opts an already-selected OpenAI vision model into complete-document input. **Unset or false preserves extraction and the existing provider order**, including saved configurations upgraded from the latest stable release. Selecting an OpenAI model alone does not authorize complete-document upload.

Page selection, passwords, unknown completeness, page/text/image truncation, size-limit violations, custom endpoints, Codex/ChatGPT transports and text-only models retain bounded extraction. Completeness checks still require the configured extractor. Existing Anthropic and Google paths are unchanged.

## Implementation

This replaces the earlier automatic-upload/provider-preference proposal with one default-off core boolean at the existing PDF configuration owner. The bundled OpenAI provider implements a narrow optional media-understanding hook using the official [PDF input contract](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/file-inputs): inline `input_file`, official Platform HTTPS `/v1/responses`, `store: false`, each PDF under 50 MB and combined PDF input at most 50 MB. There is no persistent Files upload, automatic provider preference or new dependency. The official configuration generator records the single additional core leaf; channel/plugin surfaces are unchanged.

Prepared credentials, headers and symbol-attached request/auth overrides use the existing scoped egress helpers. The native branch also reuses the host-owned `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority` scope with `assertModelCurrent`, the **original model's** credential authority and the retained provider-resource assertion. The existing HTTP guard rechecks these synchronously immediately before dispatch after asynchronous preparation and on redirects. This closes the assert-only operator/credential retirement gap across lazy provider and DNS awaits without adding an authorization abstraction or changing shared HTTP behavior.

prs.title: fix(slack): stop untagged bot loops with opt-in explicit mentions
prs.body:
Related: #160750, #160752.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot reject untagged bot thread replies without also making humans repeat mentions or changing existing bot handoffs on upgrade.

## User Impact

Slack operators can opt into `requireExplicitBotMention: true` alongside `allowBots: "mentions"` at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Strict mode rejects untagged bots that otherwise qualify through reply-to-bot or thread participation. Human follow-ups, explicit bot mentions, DMs, authorized commands, configured mention patterns, and `allowBots: true`/`false` retain their behavior.

Omitted or false preserves shipped implicit bot handoffs. This is an alternative to #160752's default change, not a downstream adoption decision. **Slack-owner acceptance of the new optional public setting remains required.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing bot-admission gate owns this choice. The unchanged mention classifier moves to the existing thread-mention sibling, keeping the oversized prepare module smaller. Existing no-restart reload metadata covers all four projections. No new admission mechanism, retroactive revocation, persistence schema, migration, private runtime patch, or distribution is added.

Integrated fixed official main `228b5e9e7df8b978a85a0f3f3aa249b705f383aa` with an ordinary merge to repair actual preparation-owner and generated-output conflicts. Main retains a single `prepareSlackMessage` owner; retired helper frames are not restored. Existing mention decision and unchanged source classification live together in the existing mention sibling to satisfy the shrink-only line-cap. Current canonical generators own the metadata/baselines. The schema regression uses main's direct `safeParse` assertions after its former test helpers were removed; all validity/default/type assertions remain.

<!-- forone-adoption-decision-20261102:start -->
## Adoption decision and fresh distribution evidence — 2026-11-02

The Slack-owner decision remains whether to expose the compatibility-preserving `requireExplicitBotMention` opt-in. The current submission section below owns the latest head and CI status; maintainer edits remain enabled. Owner acceptance is still outstanding.

The historical [advisory review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177555#issuecomment-6274222081) reports no actionable findings and sufficient recorded isolated-Gateway output, and recommends accepting the opt-in. It does not record Slack-owner acceptance. Its two outstanding checklist entries both concern that same public-contract decision. The review is scoped to `39d01116dd2d5e01fa7f8ab50dbb1e44613a0e9a`; the earlier12-input comparison was bound to8fa0cc0d85711ab2ee19e488ec9e325309a476c2. That earlier integration retained11 byte-identical inputs; access-control documentation only adds accepted official Slack read-bound guidance. The strict opt-in authored delta and committed Gateway scenario are retained. The older proof retains its original head; that earlier head's CI supported its integration. No fresh live Slack run or current employee acceptance is claimed.

Recorded official distribution evidence confirms that the need remains after the implicit-thread silence repair: unmodified Core/Slack **2026.10.10-beta.5**, build `7e15622f37bd0ced194a3b0fccacb4ad6bc78d85`, still admits untagged bot messages through both `bot_thread_participant` and `reply_to_bot` in the isolated distributed-function/compiled-gate fixture. The same 20-case matrix passes 17, with these two strict-admission requirements and the separate optional-completion policy remaining. Package integrity and the scope are recorded in the [release follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164877#issuecomment-6266458621). This is not a new live Slack incident or a claim that existing documented defaults were silently changed.

**Decision requested from the Slack owner:** accept or reject this optional public setting at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Omitted/false keeps existing implicit bot handoffs. With `allowBots: "mentions"` and the opt-in enabled, untagged bot activation is rejected while explicit bot requests, implicit human follow-ups, DMs, authorized commands, and existing sender restrictions retain their controls. This is the compatibility-preserving alternative to #160752's default change; no new default change is requested here.

This PR decides **admission**, not whether an already admitted explicit bot notification may finish empty. That latter product-policy question remains separate in #186514. A scoped acceptance/rejection of this opt-in is the missing adoption decision; existing code/proof work is not being represented as owner approval. No new review command or redundant behavior replay was added for this mechanical integration.
<!-- forone-stable-adoption-evidence-20261103:start -->
### 2026-11-03: the same admission requirement remains in stable2026.10.10

Official npm/latest Core/Slack **2026.10.10**, distributed Core build`7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be`, was checked with the unchanged20-case synthetic matrix: **17PASS / 3FAIL**. The two untagged-bot admission cases (`bot_thread_participant` and `reply_to_bot`) still admit the bot under existing mentions-only behavior. The two implicit-thread optional/silent conditions from merged #164877 nowPASS in stable; the third remaining failure concerns #186514's separate explicit-bot completion policy.

The [stable distribution follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164877#issuecomment-6266458621) fixes the verified immutable Core/Slack hashes and execution scope. This is actual distributed Core-function / verbatim compiled Slack-gate evidence, with unchanged cases/assertions and shipped package bytes. prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves

Let an agent recall sibling threads in one verified channel without exposing every session owned by that agent.

## User Impact

Opt-in `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` enables same-channel retrieval while excluding other agents, channels, accounts and workspaces. Existing defaults and other visibility modes are unchanged. Sibling send, status/model changes and session mutations remain denied.

Cross-session list, history, search and transcript-backed recall require a Gateway-hosted owner and fail closed when that owner, route, incarnation, or policy is withdrawn. Ordinary memory/wiki results remain available.

## Implementation

- Require matching stored provider, explicit account, opaque channel destination, chat kind and workspace/space under the same agent.
- Recheck route, incarnation, aliases, physical owner, and policy at final disclosure.
- Carry query-local transcript-owner bindings through memory and direct Wiki consumers; filter final snippets, citations, and recall side effects synchronously.
- Preserve self-only reads, ordinary memory/wiki retrieval, and archived metadata-only inventory behavior.

prs.title: perf(ios): stop redrawing the model menu and buttons on every keystroke
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Editing a draft makes the clean chat composer observe draft changes outside the editor and primary controls, causing unnecessary parent work on each keystroke.

## User Impact

Draft edits stay within the draft-dependent composer sections. The existing Send, Talk, placeholder, and model-picker layout is unchanged. This does not claim a measured typing-latency improvement.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing `ChatComposerSection` observation boundary for the editor overlay and clean primary controls. No new state, renderer, or cache is introduced. The small wrappers are necessary observation boundaries.

## Evidence

Published author verification is recorded here; the maintainer update below identifies the current checks and remaining limitations.

- Baseline regression compiled and failed: outer draft observation invalidations were 1, expected 0.
- Patched focused suite: 15 tests in 2 suites passed. A strengthened assertion also verifies the deferred primary-controls body still observes draft changes; that run passed all 15 tests in 0.077 seconds.
- Simulator: compact composer/draft growth and Stop availability while drafting during an active response passed. Rotation/sidebar test skipped because the simulator lacked expanded window space (2 passed, 1 skipped).
- Inspected recording frames show the rendered follow-up draft and keyboard during an active response. No device or typing-latency proof is claimed.
- Same-family Codex and cross-family Grok reviews found no production correctness defect. Addressed coverage findings by adding positive child-body observation and narrowing the test name. The observation test does not claim to exercise rendered menu invalidation or the Talk branch.
- Scoped SwiftFormat: 0/3 files require formatting. Scoped SwiftLint: no errors; one pre-existing `empty_string` warning at line 219 of the parity test.
- Simplification: retained the existing observation owner and no duplicate rendering path; every production hunk serves draft isolation.

AI-assisted implementation and review.

### Inspectable simulator artifacts

- [Simulator recording (full duration, compressed)](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/9c1f9b79364d4d896b5b11b5f532f3a1c57e1331/sim-tests.mp4)
- [Evidence scope and provenance](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/9c1f9b79364d4d896b5b11b5f532f3a1c57e1331/README.md)
- [Baseline failing observation output](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/9c1f9b79364d4d896b5b11b5f532f3a1c57e1331/red-r2-kit-test.log)
- [Strengthened passing observation output](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/9c1f9b79364d4d896b5b11b5f532f3a1c57e1331/green-kit-r2-kit-test.log)
- [Simulator execution log](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/9c1f9b79364d4d896b5b11b5f532f3a1c57e1331/green-r1-sim-test.log)

![Simulator draft and primary-control samples](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/9c1f9b79364d4d896b5b11b5f532f3a1c57e1331/draft-contact.jpg)



### Mounted runtime proof

One additional simulator UI test passed (iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 27.2). Temporary instrumentation on the published source fix records the actual mounted composer, model-controls, editor, and primary-control evaluations. From the first nonempty editor event through deletion back to empty, the composer and model-controls each evaluated **zero** times; the editor and primary controls observed the draft changes. Startup/keyboard-focus evaluations precede that interval. SwiftUI coalesced some edits (editor lengths 1,4,5,4,3,2,0), so this is not a one-render-per-keystroke assertion.

XCTest and visually inspected screenshots verify empty Talk/no Send → “mount” with enabled Send/no Talk → cleared Talk/no Send. Synthetic fixture, not live gateway or device proof; no measured latency claim. Instrumentation is evidence-only and is not shipped.

- [Scope and provenance](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/12651e1eefcad3f19cec34236caa36fb1639cdab/mounted/README.md)

![Cleared Talk](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/12651e1eefcad3f19cec34236caa36fb1639cdab/mounted/cleared-talk.png)


## Maintainer verification

Reviewed candidate: `bbe4a082ad69f85edfeac1b54ed517500051bb4f`.

The production fix is unchanged. The maintainer follow-up replaces the test-only lock/count wrapper with `Mutex`, preserves both the parent-isolation and positive child-observation assertions, and sorts the imports. Scoped SwiftFormat and SwiftLint pass; an independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issue.

The earlier native-app regression run executed and passed `ChatInputResponsivenessTests` on this production source. That run temporarily included the shared test in the app test target; the temporary copy was removed. Fresh attempts to run the untouched package test target on iOS are disclosed separately: the package cannot compile unrelated `OpenClawClientCredentialStoreTests` uses of `Process`, and the product schemes have no test action. Those attempts did not execute this test. No source exclusions or new test transplant was used to hide that limitation; the new head still requires its normal CI.

These are retained recordings from the native iPhone simulator in this review, using the same isolated Gateway and synthetic conversation. Left: the two observation boundaries removed for the baseline. Right: the published production fix. Both show typing the same draft and clearing it, with the keyboard and Talk → Send → Talk transition preserved. Initial idle time was trimmed independently and the takes were paired at normal playback speed. The video demonstrates interaction parity, not a latency benchmark; the observation-count evidence above supports the reduced-work claim.

prs.title: fix(plugins): avoid Gateway stalls during source preparation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway event-loop stalls when plugin preparation creates source/native capture directories and their physical staging tokens on a filesystem waiting for a transaction commit.

Related: #200136, #200193, #200216. The motivating Team incident (25c97908, 2026-11-16 05:02 PST) blocked the Gateway MAIN thread for 1.97 seconds in `openat2(O_CREAT)` under `scheduler:update.remote-model-catalog`; the kernel waited in `btrfs_create → start_transaction → wait_current_trans`. The catalog's redundant lock was removed separately. This change handles the remaining physical capture-root owner.

## User Impact

Plugin preparation can wait on filesystem creation while the Gateway event loop remains responsive. There is no configuration or schema change and no operator action required.

The tradeoff is explicit: measured cold owner time increases from 183.267 to 453.257 ms, warm owner time from 141.459 to 182.479 ms, and whole process-tree CPU from 1,050 to 1,310 ms. A separate loaded-addon profile on the preceding revision observed 127.828 MiB RSS in the retained broker (summed process RSS increased 120.922 MiB; shared pages and profiling overhead included). The final revision proves ordinary same-process restarts reuse that broker; it does not remeasure that RSS observation. These costs are accepted for removing filesystem-transaction stalls from the Gateway thread, not described as an overall speedup.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing broker resource owner now creates and retains the physical source/native roots and staging tokens. Preparation workers borrow paths; host cache and recovery leases retain the physical custody after execution ends. Loaded native code keeps its token until host exit. Ordinary Gateway restarts reuse the existing broker, and a fresh source replaces permanently failed or sealed authority without reopening old claims or inventing cleanup receipts.

This is the smallest complete root-custody cutover: moving only mkdir would leave token creation and lifetime operations on MAIN. Production grows by 685 lines across 21 production modules plus a net-zero build import adjustment. Twenty of those lines complete the shared lease type and preserve source-acquisition error classification across the new broker boundary. The growth is the private resource adapter and lifetime handoff; the old parent allocation callback and duplicate independent-resource count are removed. Existing pool/dependency declarations are moved intact to keep their owning modules within the repository's limits. No new manager, cache, database table or public protocol is introduced.

This does not claim all Gateway filesystem work is asynchronous. Recovery-copy/binding, runtime-selected synchronous JS/CJS/native imports, and the existing native-load realpath observation remain separate work.

## Evidence

The real preparation boundary records 28 synchronous root operations on the exact parent, including seven mutations, and zero on the candidate. Actual two-second source/native `mkdtempSync` faults move from the Gateway process into the broker: fault-interval heartbeat gaps are 2,029/2,010 ms before and 7/7 ms after; whole-operation candidate maxima are 14/12 ms. Existing physical custody and cleanup assertions remain active.

The timing and injected-delay results below were measured on runtime source corresponding to `03b70d95e1d71ab021158898cbcc06eaea7568a1`. Subsequent CI repairs preserve the create algorithm while correcting error projection, the shared lease type, and a broker sender binding, and removing an unnecessary await of a synchronous commit. These are prior-revision performance measurements, supported by focused regression proof of the changed paths, rather than a claim that final-head bytes were remeasured.

Canonical built Node 26.12.1/APFS proof used a synthetic surrounding 35 GiB agent database, 5,000 sessions and 62,000 workspace files; this owner does not scan those unrelated files. No Team data was copied. Five A1/A2 controls and five A/B pairs each include cold and warm phases (20 processes); four additional processes exercise the actual source/native faults. All 24 processes, observed brokers and source/artifact verification joined successfully. No samples were discarded. Host one-minute load was 9.376–11.450; tails are retained rather than attributed to noise.

| Metric, median (p95) | Parent | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Cold owner ms | 183.267 (188.857) | 453.257 (520.810) |
| Warm owner ms | 141.459 (145.714) | 182.479 (199.514) |
| Warm preparation ms | 135.386 (139.533) | 136.144 (147.538) |
| Warm retirement ms | 6.073 (6.310) | 47.427 (57.649) |
| Cold MAIN CPU ms | 30.188 (31.737) | 26.220 (30.325) |
| Warm MAIN CPU ms | 14.153 (15.320) | 7.827 (9.243) |
| Cold MAIN allocation MB | 30.943 (31.248) | 14.589 (16.491) |
| Warm MAIN allocation MB | 22.608 (25.778) | 6.557 (8.737) |
| Whole process-tree CPU ms | 1,050 (1,340) | 1,310 (1,440) |

Main allocation excludes the broker, so it is not a global memory-saving claim. A/A cold owner medians were 186.086/184.935 ms, warm 147.092/145.145 ms, and tree CPU 1,060/1,050 ms.

Rerunnable workload: build each pinned checkout with `pnpm build sourcePerformance`, then run `node --expose-gc scripts/perf/plugin-capture-custody-measure.mjs --repo <built-checkout> --fixture <synthetic-fixture> --label <arm>`. Use `--fault source` or `--fault native` with `--delay-ms 2000` and candidate `--expect-off-main` for the injected faults. The driver and preload are included in this PR.

<details>
<summary>Synthetic fixture setup and repeatable workload</summary>

Create the surrounding fixture once with the existing generator, outside the measured window:

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/catalog-publication-measure.mjs \
  --state-dir /absolute/new-fixture --create --sessions 5000 --database-gib 35 \
  --workspace-files 62000 --workspace-file-bytes 17742 --samples 1
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs --input-type=module - /absolute/new-fixture/physical <<'NODE'
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
const root = path.resolve(process.argv[2]);
fs.mkdirSync(root, { recursive: true });
process.env.OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR = path.join(root, 'fixture-setup-state');
process.env.OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH = path.join(root, 'absent-config.json');
const { createFixture, nativeSize } = await import('./src/plugins/plugin-generation-artifact.admission.test-support.ts');
const { bytes, ...fixture } = createFixture(path.join(root, 'source'), false);
if (bytes.length !== nativeSize) throw new Error('Unexpected synthetic native payload size');
fs.writeFileSync(path.join(root, 'fixture.json'), JSON.stringify({ fixture, nativeSize }) + '\n');
NODE
```

Build baseline and candidate separately. Invoke the candidate's committed driver against each built `--repo`, with unique labels and the same `--fixture /absolute/new-fixture/physical`. Run A1/A2/A/B five times serially, then A/B for each source/native fault. Wrap each process in `/usr/bin/time -l` for the whole-tree CPU column. Preserve source/build hashes and every JSON row. The synthetic payload is 2 MiB; real addon loading and post-exit reclaim are separately proven by the focused lifecycle test.

</details>

Focused proof covers the original main-thread guard, preparation cancellation/deadline/settlement, physical cache retention, real addon loading and reclaim exclusion, old-lease/successor overlap, ordinary same-process restart reuse, and actual broker-loss recovery. The sealed-only intermediate candidate failed the real process-loss regression; the final owner predicate passes all 17 lifecycle and 18 transport-retirement cases. A test-only watcher barrier timed out during validation; it now uses a bounded async sentinel wait under the unchanged deadline, and all four affected/cascading cases passed. Final affected types, lint, formatting and independent Codex reviews pass.

Before the CI-repair commit, full `pnpm check:changed --staged --base 2435c1faa791de766688ba27ca7a14a92e30b7e4` passed every gate except dead exports: 113 identities match the exact parent, plus one task-owned benchmark export. The benchmark now uses an explicit shared installer; its targeted script-export scan, lint/format and all four baseline/candidate source/native fault qualifications pass. The 113 parent findings remain a failed local gate, not a green result or an automatic CI waiver. Exact-head CI and final-head zero-open ClawSweeper review are required before landing.

The first exact-head CI run, 43987530227, found incomplete consumer migrations: a missing wrapper inventory entry, stale capture-root observations and low-space injection, an overbroad physical commit return type, an unregistered fixed protocol export, a new lint suppression, and test-line growth. The repair restores the existing contracts. The real broker low-space test also exposed lost source-acquisition classification before session creation; forwarding that existing fact restores startup containment while leaving transport and cleanup failures fatal. No failures from that CI run are claimed inherited. Repair head `d82c6f178d6b4cb1c09de4974664cd5140fb3f88` passes focused regressions, production types and all affected test type graphs, type-aware lint, formatting, the export-owner guard, the 400-line test budget without allowance, and independent Codex review. Its CI run completed with only the static type-cycle failure described below; ClawSweeper cleared all six items on that head.

Local provisioning covers 16 of the 17 Linux CI failures; the remaining filesystem case is platform-specific and remains CI proof. The selector also included a Darwin-only full cold/warm sibling case already known to have an unexplained timeout: it exceeded its 120-second deadline, reporting 202.398 seconds while synchronous subprocess work finished. That local failure is retained and is not classified inherited; its passing sibling cases are not a claimed fix. No full provisioning replay or blind CI rerun was performed.

CI run 43995776480 on `d82c6f1` passed the previously failing checks but exposed one static type dependency cycle between admission state and the lease module. Head `274e2ab300d4866700dec1891bf67dbe2e60568f` moves the unchanged contract into an import-free type leaf and updates all four consumers. The exact Madge guard now reports zero cycles; core types, type-aware lint, format and independent Codex review pass. This five-file change contains no executable behavior change and does not require remeasuring the prior performance results. Final-head CI and ClawSweeper re-review remain required; no inherited-failure exception is claimed.

prs.title: fix: keep Knowledge memory to decisions and outcomes, not step-by-step progress
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With Knowledge as the memory provider, agents save step-by-step progress as permanent memory. Long tasks fill a subject's page with claims like "CI failed at commit abc", "rebased and pushed", "waiting on results" or "as of 3pm, prices unchanged". These claims stop being true almost at once. One busy project in a real vault had about 950 claims in 18 days. About 60% of the claims the agent made from its own tool output were this kind of progress. The memory prompt causes this: it tells agents to save "project-state changes" before every final reply, and in a long task almost every turn changes something.

## User Impact

User impact: Knowledge keeps what you decided, said and finished, not every step it took to get there, so recall and subject pages have far more signal and far less churn. The guidance is written for any kind of work, such as trips, health, home projects, writing and code, not only software development.

## Why This Change Was Made

The always-on memory prompt, the pre-compaction flush, the `knowledge_remember` tool description, the capture skill and the docs now share one rule:

- **Save outcomes, not progress.** Save decisions, preferences, corrections, commitments, remember requests, and outcomes: something done, chosen, finished, cancelled or abandoned. Steps taken, intermediate results, routine waiting and "as of" snapshots stay in the conversation, which already holds them. Constraints and blockers the user states still count.
- **The user's words come before the agent's observations.** Agents save their own observations only when the observation is such an outcome.
- **Page State changes at the same level as claims.** State is rewritten when where the subject stands changes: a milestone, a new or cleared blocker, or a changed plan or next step. Otherwise progress would just move from claims into page edits. This rule also applies when an agent can edit pages but can't save claims.
- **Shared profile guidance updated.** It no longer sends individual pull requests and CI runs to claims. Only their outcomes and decisions are saved.

The capture skill gets a short table of progress and outcome pairs from several areas (travel, health, home, writing, code). The always-on prompt stays general and grows by about 450 characters.

## Evidence

**Simulated save decisions, old prompt vs new prompt.** There were 13 short scenarios across travel, health, home, writing and code. Seven contain only progress, and six contain a user decision or a finished outcome. Each prompt was run twice on Claude Opus and twice on GPT Astra, without the model knowing which prompt was which. The policies were labelled p1 and p2 and nothing was saved.

| | Old prompt | New prompt |
|---|---|---|
| Progress turns that saved claims | 9 / 28 | 2 / 28 |
| Progress turns that rewrote page State | 14 / 28 | 0 / 28 |
| Decision or outcome turns that saved claims | 24 / 24 | 24 / 24 |
| Outcome turns that rewrote page State | 20 / 20 | 20 / 20 |

The new prompt didn't lose any legitimate saves. User preferences such as "never red-eyes with a layover" and "no money in floats" were saved in every run. With the old prompt, Astra dropped the "PR merged" outcome in both of its runs. The new prompt kept it.

The remaining two progress saves are one case, run twice on Astra. That turn was an in-task edit request ("still too long, move the stats lower"), and Astra saved it as a correction. The new skill table covers this case, but the always-on prompt doesn't.

**Checks.** These tests pass: `memory-provider-entry` (now covers the new rule, the State trigger, and the rule applying when the agent can edit pages but can't save claims), `conversation-grants` and `skill-packaging`. `tsgo` for extensions passes and `oxfmt` is clean. The shared references were regenerated with `scripts/sync-skill-references.mjs`. An independent review on GPT Astra raised three P2 findings, and all three are fixed:

- The shared guidance sent PRs and CI runs to claims.
- Agents could still record progress on pages as their own conclusions.
- Blockers the user states were excluded along with routine waiting.

**Gaps.** This is a simulation in which the model reports what it would save. It is not a live check of real tool calls, and the repository has no live Knowledge capture scenario yet. Claims already saved aren't changed; cleaning those up is separate consolidation work.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: refactor(sessions): stop chat work by a recorded cause, not by a changed id
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Work was stopped by inference. Two checks compared ids that change on their own and treated a change as a stop:

- **Typed Stop refused.** A `chat.send` "/stop" (queue mode other than steer) had to see the same session id and, with an empty view, an empty transcript. A client that had not loaded history yet sent "/stop" during a running turn: the Gateway answered "active branch changed; review and retry" and the turn kept running.
- **Retained send fenced by revision.** A `sessions_send` held during a plugin reload replayed with the target's lifecycle revision and transcript id pinned. A reset was caught only because it rotates the revision ("Target session lifecycle changed before retained send."). A compaction successor of the target changed the transcript id, so the replay was refused even though the chat was the same.

## Why This Change Was Made

A stop is a recorded act with a cause, on the existing stop paths. No new service.

- **Typed Stop** stops the chat's work as it is when the Gateway receives it. Deleted: the `stop` branch of `assertExpectedLeafActive`, `assertExpectedLeafActiveAsync`, and the `beforeAbort` hook in the chat abort runtime. Work that starts after the Stop is not captured, so it is not cancelled.
- **Retained sends** are addressed by chat key. Reset and delete stop them in their shared runtime cleanup (`clearSessionResetRuntimeState`) with the cause `reset` or `deleted`. The replay reports `{ status: "not_delivered", stopCause }`. Deleted: the lifecycle-revision compare and its option, the replay's transcript-id pin, and the "refused target incarnation" check. Retained sends are held through `WeakRef`, so a handoff that never replays does not keep them.
- `config/session-identity-allowlist.txt`: 6587 → 6584 pins on current `main`.

Accepted edge: a reset that lands after the replay has started does not stop that replay. A started request may finish, as before.

Production code (`src`, `extensions`, without tests): +73 / −127.

## User Impact

- A typed "/stop" stops the running turn even if the client's view is empty or behind.
- A Stop does not cancel a turn, a replacement chat or a child started after it.
- A reset or delete of the target stops a held send, with the cause in the result.
- A held send to a compacted target is no longer refused for the new transcript id.

## Evidence

Base = merge base `726a8dd49857`, head = this PR.

| Journey | Tier | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|---|
| Turn 1 runs a 45 s foreground exec; client sends `chat.send` "/stop" with `expectedLeafEntryId: null`, queue mode followup; then sends turn 2 at once | `ocx src` scratch Gateway, real Claude model | Stop refused (`active-leaf-changed`); turn 1 not stopped | Stop ok, turn 1 `aborted`; turn 2 (started after the Stop) `final` with the expected reply |
| Caller holds a reloading plugin, sends to its child (held), child is reset before replay | real Gateway, real plugin reload, scripted model (scratch variant of `server.plugin-reload-send-continuation.product.test.ts`) | `error`: "Target session lifecycle changed before retained send."; child got 0 sends | `not_delivered`, `stopCause: "reset"`; child got 0 sends |

Tests:
- `chat.stop-cascade.test.ts`: a Stop with a stale leaf and another session id stops the chat's work; after a parent replacement or branch, the original child is cancelled and the successor's runs and child are not.
- `sessions-send-self-hold.test.ts`: a reset of the target settles the held send once with `stopCause: "reset"` and never replays it.
- `server.plugin-reload-send-continuation.product.test.ts` (resume, followup, failed reload) passes on head.
- `server-worker-placement-cancel.test.ts` revoked worker Stop authority in a microtask after the first check and relied on an await that this change removes. It now revokes before the effect's own check.

`server.plugin-reload-send-revocation.product.test.ts` times out the same way on base and head locally.

Gates: oxfmt, oxlint, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm check:test-types`, import-cycle checks, `check:session-identity-ratchet`, and `ocx test` on the Stop, abort, chat-send, self-hold and reset-cleanup suites. Local review: complete, no findings.

prs.title: fix(worktrees): partial-clone removal times out scanning promisor packs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes managed-worktree cleanup aborting after 120 seconds when a large partial clone has unfetched HEAD blobs. Related: #188525, #189288.

Between 13:55 and 15:06 PST on November 16 (release `344cc75d`), cleanup failed 16 times across 16 checkouts, every 2–3 minutes after no earlier failures that day, under sustained btrfs I/O pressure, with approximately 360 promisor pack files, another 53 new packs, and a 10 GB temporary pack. Each failure spent approximately 120.4 seconds in snapshot preparation before preserving the checkout and deferring an otherwise repeatable failure for 1–2 hours. Concurrent preparations recorded 110–141 seconds waiting for allocation/reservation; five conversations waited 2–2.5 minutes for a first reply. Those overlapping timings do not establish the lease holder.

## User Impact

Removal hydrates missing HEAD contents directly and requires local custody before snapshotting, without scanning unrelated promisor packs. Failed hydration, remaining missing objects, corruption, and lost removal authority still preserve the checkout. Worktrees without missing objects retain their existing path. No configuration, timeout, schema, worker, or lazy-import boundary changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The snapshot owner ran `rev-list --missing=allow-promisor` before the existing batch hydrator. Git initializes promisor membership by scanning every promisor pack; `--max-count=1` does not bound that work. The fix deletes this classification and uses the existing selected-promisor batch fetch, transport isolation, and Git mutation admission from #188525. An offline `--missing=print --max-count=1 HEAD` census then requires no remaining missing objects before capture. Its work follows the selected commit's contents rather than unrelated promised pack contents.

Data safety depends on recoverability, not historical promise membership. A remote can serve an exact object ID even if that blob was originally authored locally. Fetch success alone is insufficient: the clean-snapshot fast path can otherwise publish HEAD without reading unchanged blobs. The new offline census closes that gap; capture retains its existing offline dirty/index validation and authority gates. Missing unpromised data that cannot be recovered still preserves the checkout. The retained unpromised-object maintenance fixture now expects one attempted fetch rather than zero; its byte preservation, backoff, and eventual repair assertions are unchanged.

Allocation investigation: ordinary removal acquires only `core:managed-worktrees:mutation/<id>` (`service.ts:717`, `allocation.ts:73`), while creation uses `core:managed-worktrees:create/capacity` (`allocation.ts:58`). The whole-pack proof did not enter the ref-mutation queue (`git.ts:215`). Its content slot is shared with snapshot/content reads, while preparation has a separate worker lane (`git-worker.ts:150`). However, global allocation owners can retain their lease while awaiting that checkout: `withWorktreeAllocationLease` nests the checkout lease (`allocation.ts:62`), including restore (`service.ts:866`) and removed-name reuse (`service.ts:489`). Rollback directly snapshots under global allocation ownership (`service.ts:367`, `service.ts:395`), and count-cap enforcement invokes snapshotting eviction under that lease (`capacity-owner.ts:313`, `capacity-owner.ts:185`, `eviction.ts:108`); eviction supplies its own five-second cancellation signal (`eviction.ts:99`). The restore/rollback ownership interval includes checkout acquisition and native settlement, not a fixed short critical section. **STOP for Goal 2:** separating those responsibilities requires a broader capacity/lease redesign, so lease scope is unchanged under the requested escape hatch. The incident's exact holder is not identifiable from the supplied timing lines alone.

Simplification: one hydration owner remains; the whole-pack classification is removed. Production delta: **−8 lines**. Net test delta: **+22 lines**, one added table case and one extended existing case, no new suite. Acceptance: promised removal/restoration succeeds with a synthetic stalled whole-pack command, exactly one real batch fetch, and zero global membership scans; unsuccessful or incomplete hydration preserves checkout bytes and registry custody. This is a work-count/behavior regression, not a production latency benchmark.

## Evidence

- Red on base `f947bdc94981e299fe26b5a71af8bfdd4e7ac125`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/worktrees/service.removal-safety.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'removal \((promisor|incomplete)\)'` → **2 failed / 20 skipped**. The first failure is caused by the synthetic whole-pack timeout; the second resolves `{ removed: true }` rather than preserving missing blobs. The second table label was subsequently shortened from `incomplete` to `noop`; fixture behavior is unchanged.
- Green: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/worktrees/service.removal-safety.test.ts src/agents/worktrees/service.removal-budget.test.ts src/agents/worktrees/service.capacity.test.ts src/agents/worktrees/service.remove-lease.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → **85 passed**: 52 infra cases (208.38 seconds) and 33 removal-budget cases (61.49 seconds), **296.24 seconds total wall time** including worker preparation/verification. This retains real Git partial clones, one-batch hydration, transport-denied byte-for-byte restore, unavailable/unpromised/corrupt-object preservation, removal authority, backoff, and allocation-capacity contracts. These existing files exceed 30 seconds because they exercise native Git, worker settlement, and persisted registry/removal custody; the regression adds no suite or product startup.
- Targeted typecheck: `node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json '["src/agents/worktrees/service.removal-safety.test.ts","src/agents/worktrees/service.removal-budget.test.ts"]'` → **agents-tools passed**. It initially caught missing synthetic result metadata; adding `timeoutMs: 0` corrected the fixture type without changing behavior.
- Targeted `run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` on all three TypeScript files, `pnpm format:check` on all four files, and `git diff --check` **passed**. Worker and lazy-import boundaries are unchanged, so no build-boundary change is claimed.
- Shared autoreview, **Codex engine**, complete local candidate against `f947bdc94981e`, **P0–P2**: **scoped-clean**, no accepted/actionable findings. Final review includes the fixture metadata correction; unchanged hydration, snapshot inventory, isolated transport, Git execution, and worker owners were supplied as context. Pr-simplify retained the existing hydration owner and removed the redundant classification path.
- Exact-head [CI 43978838698](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43978838698), head `9c7a93e2f44cc2e0937e39dd0289b19275f743fa`: **completed success, 74 jobs (45 successful / 29 skipped), no failures or cancellations**. No CI reruns or repair pushes. The baseline-ratchet job took 16 minutes 47 seconds; its final result was success. No inherited-failure exception was used. Native review/preparation and accepted auto-merge reconciled the exact attempted head as **merged**, commit `b220220905f2bd2d38ccfd95b0e6983a9cce5bd7`.

prs.title: refactor(doctor): consolidate browser readiness tests
prs.body:
Related: #171994

## What Problem This Solves

Browser readiness proof is split between a direct facade fixture and the existing Doctor flow suite.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. Production code, configuration, defaults, dependencies, permissions, and browser-profile privacy behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the meaningful configuration-forwarding, facade-address, finding-data, and actionable failure-diagnostic checks into the existing Doctor entry-point cases. Retire the lower two-case fixture and exactly its obsolete mock-export baseline row. Existing filtering, repair, dry-run, and plugin-owned privacy checks remain intact; an undocumented private array-container identity assertion is not promoted into a broader contract.

Thanks @vincentkoc for directing this behavior-preserving cleanup campaign.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/09f057fa-3479-4e1d-b851-0cad5cf713a7) — also restart recovery and final verification.
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/fcf0e733-89e1-4869-bf78-3fa13c02e0a1) — initial implementation and baseline/candidate runs.

## Evidence

- Baseline **47/47** in five files; candidate **45/45** in four. Only the two consolidated facade cases disappear; all 45 retained expanded names/order match. Existing eight-case Doctor keeper, seven repair siblings, two error siblings, and 28 plugin readiness cases pass.
- Five temporary producer controls fail at their intended assertions: dropped configuration, wrong facade artifact, missing finding fixHint, missing diagnostic prefix, and missing Doctor rerun guidance. Exact producer restoration verified; final keeper **8/8** passes. No real browser, CDP/login, personal-profile, native-host repair, or live-Gateway operation was performed.
- Targeted flows and Doctor typechecks, lint, format, non-pruning mock-export guard, and diff checks pass. Baseline/candidate runs were inspected and reused after restart; remaining checks completed in the retained checkout without replaying completed work.
- All seven removal-scan phases ran on clean base and candidate. Two unused-file phases and script exports pass; the remaining four dependency/export phases have **byte-identical complete outputs and exit codes** to clean base. None names the changed paths. Aggregate is not green; no unrelated fix, ignore, or exception.
- Final independent Codex autoreview: **P0–P2 scoped-clean**, one complete 123,913-byte frozen packet against base df315eb3bb99eeb23e5395893e61a9e9daba80e3, now committed as ec420ce5538755692910e1cde4f1b034ad697723. Reviewer did not independently rerun tests.
- Three files, +15/−65: production 0, test/support net −49, baseline −1. No performance or full-package-build claim.
- Exact-head [CI run 43997865713](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43997865713) succeeded on 801bd3a9ca172e67d7d6dc0fa7847fe1e65a0657; the single rollup watcher reported GREEN. All 61 jobs were accounted for (31 succeeded, 30 skipped): 778 reported wall seconds and 4,280 summed non-skipped job seconds, not billed cost or a benchmark. Native exact-head review and preparation are complete; landing is pending.

## Worked on by

- @vincentkoc

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: selected chat text stays highlighted when clicking the blank space beside the transcript.

## User Impact

User impact: clicking either blank side of the conversation clears the selection normally. Text dragging, Select All, message actions, and media behavior are preserved. No settings or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transcript was excluded from native selection, so clicks in its empty space could not dismiss an existing selection. Restore native behavior on the transcript and keep only avatars and message-footer chrome excluded. No JavaScript event handler or new state is needed.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `241a53fad0bbfcee1efd35faaf9003019c684172`.

- Maintainer verification reproduced the stuck selection on main `d29fad4e3e687dedf683e38ec35b12cb85510637` for both blank sides.
- All five existing selection E2Es pass again after consolidating the unchanged `user-select: text` declarations into one shared rule. The same-scope production CSS build is 29 raw bytes smaller than the original PR (gzip +2 bytes). No limits were changed; the new CI will evaluate its own integrated base.
- Independent reviews of the full original diff and the consolidation found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Formatting and scoped CSS lint pass.


- The regression fails before the fix for both blank-side clicks and passes afterward.
- All five focused chat-selection E2E cases pass: side clicks, double-click drag bounds, cross-message dragging, Select All, image/spacing preservation in light and dark themes, and reasoning selection in flat and bubble views.
- The affected form-controls browser test passes.
- UI typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, CSS lint, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Actual Control UI with synthetic data, Chromium, 1366 × 900, light theme: the same native drag and side click leave a stale selection before and clear it after. Before/after screenshots below show the same gesture.
- Safari/WebKit is unverified: the mock application did not render a visible transcript in two bounded attempts. No Safari result is claimed.

The side click leaves the selection stuck.

![Before: text remains selected after clicking the blank side](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b76d5f9a-3d1d-46c6-b111-8a93d53e114d)

The maintainer simplification keeps the original CSS-only behavior and existing tests. The before/after images above were reinspected; the consolidation does not change their visual result.

prs.title: fix(ui): long tool activity summaries run past the reply text in Safari and Firefox
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a long tool activity summary ("Ran commands, read files, called …") runs past the right edge of the reply text in Safari and Firefox, and continues under the Details panel, instead of stopping where the text column ends.

## User Impact

User impact: the collapsed tool summary now ends where the reply text ends, and shows an ellipsis when it is too long, in every browser.

In 1:1 threads at the default width, tool rows and the activity block are 8 px wider than before, so they end at the reply's edge instead of just short of it. Shared threads and saved chat widths keep their current widths.

## Why This Change Was Made

The summary limits its width to a percentage of the grid track it sits in, and that track had no size of its own. WebKit and Firefox size such a track to the unwrapped summary, so the limit followed the text instead of the column. Chromium kept the summary in the column but cut it mid-word. The group now has a track as wide as the reading column, and every summary label gets the ellipsis that only the live headline had.

Tool rows and the activity block also carried a 760 px cap from before the conversation column became 768 px wide. They now take the column's width, as they already did under a saved chat width.

## Evidence

Shared thread with the Details panel open, in WebKit (Playwright build 2370, Safari 27.2), 1317×560 at 2×, dark theme. Before is `main` at d29fad4e3e6; after is this change at 285aed1f2d0, which the PR head carries unchanged on current `main` (same patch ID; `main` did not touch `ui/` in between). The session is a mocked-Gateway fixture rendered by the real Control UI build, and the turn's folded activity was opened with a click.

### Clean comparison

**Before**

![Before: the tool summary continues past the right edge of the reply text and is cut mid-word](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7543bcad-9ade-4a57-83a6-bed2d68a4c81)

**After**

![After: the tool summary ends at the reply's right edge with an ellipsis](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05d80827-2386-412b-8b72-e01f0c890b22)

### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![Before, annotated: an arrow marks the summary text beyond the reply's right edge](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e3a8eb5-d7ae-4ee6-9c54-fc11f2572993)

**After**

![After, annotated: a guide through the right edges of the summary and the reply shows 0 px between them](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/13dcf35f-ad81-4acd-a26f-bb2ee8eb589d)

Measured in the same captures:

|        | Summary                         | Reply paragraph | Summary label                           |
| ------ | ------------------------------- | --------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Before | 1484 px wide in a 668 px column | 668 px          | `text-overflow: clip`, never truncated   |
| After  | 668 px                          | 668 px          | `text-overflow: ellipsis`, truncated     |

- **Regression test:** `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-activity-summary-width.browser.test.tsx` covers direct and shared threads with framed and standalone activity. On `main` it fails in Chromium (`expected 'clip' to be 'ellipsis'`) and in WebKit (`expected 1358 to be greater than 1358`: the label is never truncated). On this branch all 4 cases pass in both, in 1.1 s (Chromium) and 1.5 s (WebKit) of wall time. The file joins the WebKit lane's list so CI runs it there.
- **Changed expectation:** `chat-responsive.browser.test.ts` asserted the 760 px default for tool rows and the activity block. It now asserts that they match the thread at the default width, as it already did for a saved width.
- **Sibling suites:** the chat column, activity layout, responsive and disclosure browser suites pass with the new file (82 tests in five files), and so do the tool-outcome, canvas detail width, bubble activity and heartbeat rollup E2E suites (25 tests).
- **Checks:** `pnpm check:changed` passes with the dead-export scan skipped (no exports changed; CI runs it): guards, format, type checks for the UI and core test graphs, lint and stylelint.
- **CI:** run [43992829096](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43992829096) on this head has two failed jobs, both outside this change. `checks-ui (1/3)` fails `chat-transcript-projection-scale.test.ts` › "moves live activity to the current eligible group after replacement and run changes" with the same assertion as `main`'s scheduled run [43979180619](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43979180619); it passes locally on this change three times. `checks-ui-e2e (6/10)` times out selecting a layout menu item in `chat-panel-layout.e2e.test.ts` › "preserves live content and saved geometry across main, dock, focus, and narrow layouts"; locally the same timeout occurs with `main`'s chat CSS in 3 of 4 runs and with this change in 1 of 4. This PR touches neither test nor their helpers. The WebKit lane, which runs the new test, passed (76 files).

prs.title: fix: compact tool input hints hide required arguments when a schema is wide
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agents call tools with the wrong arguments when a tool's schema is too wide for its 300-character compact input hint, because the hint stops at the first field that doesn't fit and drops required arguments behind `...`, or collapses to `unknown`.

## User Impact

User impact: for every tool, the compact input hint now names every required argument once it would overflow. That hint appears in the Code Mode quick index, `describe().input` and the "Expected input:" suffix of argument-validation errors. Hints that already fit are unchanged. Validation and tool schemas do not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The compact hint used to render keys in order until the budget ran out. A required key with a long type, or the trailing `; ...` pushing a nearly full hint over 300 characters, could hide required arguments or turn the whole hint into `unknown`.

New rule:
- **Full hint fits:** rendered exactly as before.
- **Full hint overflows** (including a nested object, array item or union variant that overflows on its own): only required keys are rendered, at every level. Optional keys are dropped everywhere, and each object that dropped keys ends with `; ...`.
- **Required types that still don't fit** are re-rendered to the remaining budget, then reduced to a shallow type (`Array<...>`, `{ ... }`, a bare primitive name such as `number`, or `unknown`).
- **Required key names alone don't fit:** the hint is `{ ... }`, because a partial required list would look like the whole contract.

In required-only mode, union and nullable variants keep their required keys instead of collapsing to `unknown`. A root union that overflows also gets the required-only retry. Output hints are unaffected.

The Knowledge prompt changes that were in this PR have moved to their own PR.

## Evidence

Hint strings from the real fsn1 catalog:

| Tool | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `knowledge_remember` | `{ attribution: string; excerpt: string; ... }` | `{ attribution: string; excerpt: string; items: Array<{ kind: "fact" \| "preference" \| "decision" \| "commitment" \| "event" \| "belief"; text: string; ... }>; ... }` |
| `sessions_spawn` | `unknown` | `{ task: string; ... }` |
| `knowledge_create_relationship` | `unknown` | `{ attribution: string; body: string; evidence: Array<{ path: string; sha256: string; ... }>; expectedOntologyFingerprint: string; from: string; label: string; requestId: string; title: string; to: string; ... }` |
| `knowledge_extract_section` | `unknown` | names all 8 required keys (296 chars) |
| `knowledge_records` | `unknown` | `{ ... }` (no required keys) |

Why those four tools render `unknown` on `main`: each one's body fit at 296–299 characters, then the trailing `; ...` was appended, pushing it to 301–304, and anything over 300 becomes `unknown`. The fit check now includes that suffix.

The 8,000-char Code Mode index, simulated against fsn1's real catalog (111 non-MCP tools) and usage ranking, imports `src/agents/tool-schema-hints.ts` from this branch:
- Usage-ranked rows: **33 on `main` → 38 with this PR**. Added: `knowledge_relink`, `ask_user`, `knowledge_chronicle_since`, `knowledge_connections`, `knowledge_ontology`, `nodes`. Dropped: `github_read`.
- Unranked rows: 17 → 17.
- Total hint text across all rows: 28,654 → about 25,500 chars.

Checks:
- The new tests in `tool-schema-hints.test.ts` fail against `origin/main`'s implementation and pass here.
- Focused tests pass: `tool-schema-hints`, `tool-search`, `agent-tools.prefix-stability`.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes.
- A pre-PR Astra review found P2 gaps (nullable/type-array variants and root unions did not get the required-only retry). They are fixed here with regression tests.
- Gap: there is no live-model before/after run yet.

prs.title: fix(a2a): own the gateway prefix so unknown subpaths answer JSON
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`GET /a2a/v1/agent-card` did not answer as an API route. The A2A channel registered `/.well-known/agent-card.json`,
`/.well-known/agent.json` and `/a2a/v1` as exact paths, so anything else under the prefix missed the plugin route
entirely and fell through to the Control-UI single-page app: HTTP 200 with ~21 kB of `text/html`. A client probing a
sibling path under the same prefix got a web page instead of a JSON error.

The handler already answers unknown paths with a JSON 404; it simply never saw them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway route registration now carries the match mode per path:

```ts
const a2aGatewayRoutePaths = [
  { path: "/.well-known/agent-card.json", match: "exact" },
  { path: "/.well-known/agent.json", match: "exact" },
  // The handler answers unknown paths under this prefix itself. Registering the prefix keeps
  // `/a2a/v1/anything` out of the Control-UI SPA fallback, so API clients get a JSON 404.
  { path: "/a2a/v1", match: "prefix" },
] as const;
```

The well-known agent-card routes stay exact, so their behavior is unchanged. Prefix matching is boundary aware
(`prefixMatchPath` accepts `/a2a/v1` and `/a2a/v1/...`, not `/a2a/v10`), and the handler's existing
`pathname !== "/a2a/v1"` branch now covers unknown subpaths with `{"error":"Not found"}`.

## User Impact

A2A clients and probes under `/a2a/v1/...` get a JSON 404 instead of an HTML app shell, so a mistyped or unknown
endpoint is distinguishable from a working web UI. Existing agent-card and JSON-RPC behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- New regression in `extensions/a2a/src/http.test.ts` against the real account registration and handler:
  - the `/a2a/v1` route is registered with `match: "prefix"`;

prs.title: fix(subagents): record a settled missing reply as a permanent outcome
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A subagent completion whose requester finished successfully but produced no visible reply was recorded as
`disposition: "retryable"`. Retrying cannot create text that was never written, so re-admission repeats the same failure until the
dedupe window expires, and the completion keeps looking pending instead of settled.

## Why This Change Was Made

`missingVisibleReplyResult` in `src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-direct-response.ts` marks the case
`retryable` whenever the requester completed successfully. That is the one case where another attempt has nothing left to deliver:
the run is over and the reply is absent. `disposition: "permanent_failure"` is the existing vocabulary for this
(`subagent-announce-completion-delivery.ts:495`), so the settle path stops re-admitting a settled outcome.

Two cases keep the old value:

- **A state conflict** (`requester_state_conflict`) is transient — the saved state may reconcile — so it stays `retryable`.
- **A yielded or still-continuing response** is not settled: another attempt may still produce its visible reply, so it stays
  `retryable` too.

## User Impact

A completed subagent completion with no visible reply settles once instead of being retried until the dedupe window closes. Failed,
pending, and intentionally silent completions keep their current dispositions.

## Evidence

`subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts` asserts the settled-missing-reply case records `disposition: "permanent_failure"`.

- Rebased onto current `main` after the announce classifier was refactored (#156540); the disposition decision now lives in the
  classifier's closure.
- base (`main`): **1 failed** / 112 passed — the new assertion is the only failure.
- with this change: **113 passed**.
- `check-test-lines-ratchet`: net 0 test lines, inside the 400-line allowance.
- `oxlint` on both touched files: no findings.

The live-Telegram proof in the original review still applies to the settled-versus-retryable distinction; nothing in this revision
changes delivery paths other than which disposition the settled case records.
