prs.title: fix(cli): keep multi-line id rebind warnings readable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw id rebind` commits the key move, then checks publication. When that follow-up fails with a multi-line error, the
CLI prints the whole message on one line with the newlines escaped as literal `\n` sequences:

```
Moved to new keys (committed). Follow-up check failed: gateway transport failed: refused\n  remedy: …
```

Gateway transport errors are intentionally multi-line (message, remedy, connection details, sometimes a `Possible causes:`
list), so the escaped form is the least readable case that shows up right after a successful key move.

## Why This Change Was Made

`writeCommittedWarning` passed the whole message through `sanitizeTerminalText`, whose contract is *single-line* rendering of
untrusted values — it maps `\n` to the two characters `\` + `n` on purpose so a value cannot break a line.

The message here is not a bare untrusted value: the transport builds it as several text lines and the layout is ours. The fix
sanitizes each line and rejoins them, which is the idiom already used for the same reason in
`src/infra/control-ui-assets.ts:269` (`split` → `map(sanitizeTerminalText)` → join). Control characters inside a line are
still stripped, so nothing regains the ability to inject escapes or raw control bytes.

## User Impact

A failed publication check after `id rebind` now prints the transport error as the several lines it was written as: the
message, the remedy, and the connection details stay separately readable while the "committed, don't repeat" framing is
unchanged. Single-line errors render exactly as before.

## Evidence

New case in `src/cli/id-cli.commands.test.ts`: a three-line follow-up error with a trailing `\u0007` control byte, asserting
the output keeps the newlines, contains no escaped `\n`, and drops the control byte.

- base (`main` @ `6b22db7fa32`): **1 failed | 9 passed** — `expected 'Moved to new keys (committed).\nFollo…' to contain
  'refused\n  remedy: …'`.
- with this change: **10 passed**.
- `oxlint` on both touched files: no findings.

prs.title: fix(cli): surface attach session-target remedies as expected CLI errors
prs.body:
Closes #200142

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw attach` (and `tui`/`chat` aliases) silently swallow their already-composed remedies when a session target conflicts with `--url`, is ambiguous, or does not resolve — the operator sees only "[openclaw] The CLI command failed." plus a Doctor hint, not the actionable fix (e.g. "pass one target: use either the session URL or --url, not both").

## User Impact

User impact: `attach <url> --url <other>`, an ambiguous short reference, or a not-found session now print the exact remedy on stderr instead of generic guidance, so operators can immediately correct their flags or reference.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveSessionTarget` throws plain `Error` for these operator failures. The root failure renderer (`src/cli/failure-output.ts`) only prints the remedy verbatim for `ExpectedCliError`; plain errors from non-whitelisted commands fall through to generic "[openclaw] The CLI command failed." + Doctor hint, dropping the already-composed message. The merged shared-wrapper repair (#199970) explicitly does not cover paths that fail outside `runCommandWithRuntime`; `resolveSessionTarget` is called directly by `attach`/`tui` and is one of those uncovered paths (see issue #200142).

This reclassifies the three operator remedies at their producer as `ExpectedCliError`, matching the established pattern already used elsewhere in `attach-cli.ts` (`throwExpectedCliError` for `--session` conflicts) and across the CLI (`pair-cli.ts`, `pairing-cli.ts`, `models/shared.ts`).

The "Gateway returned a session without a consistent agent identity" error is intentionally **not** reclassified: it is an internal invariant failure, not an operator remedy (per ClawSweeper review on #200142).

## How It Works / What Changed

- `src/cli/session-target.ts`: 3 plain `throw new Error` reclassified to `throwExpectedCliError` / `return throwExpectedCliError`:
  - "pass one target: use either the session URL or --url, not both"
  - ambiguous short reference table
  - "No session found. …"
- `src/cli/session-ref.test.ts`: discriminant assertions that the conflicting-target and ambiguity cases now throw `ExpectedCliError` (folded into the existing tests for those branches), a new test for the resolved-but-not-found classification, and a hardening assertion that the inconsistent-agent error stays a plain `Error`.

## Evidence

### Discriminant tests (red on base, green with fix)

`pnpm test src/cli/session-ref.test.ts src/cli/session-target.test.ts src/cli/attach-cli.action.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 57 passed (including the new `ExpectedCliError` assertions). Before the fix, the new assertions failed: `resolveSessionTarget` rejected with a plain `Error`, not `ExpectedCliError`.

### Shipped CLI reproduction (real dist)

Environment: isolated `HOME`, `node v24.22.1`, built `dist` via `pnpm build` (worker-deploy bundle skipped with `OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1 OPENCLAW_BUILD_WORKER_DEPLOY_BUNDLE=0` due to the pre-existing highlight.js standalone-chunk build bug).

Command: `openclaw attach https://gw.example/dashboard/main/abc123 --url wss://other.example`

**Base** (2f90c70, pre-fix dist `session-target-CGM8qKc4.mjs`):
```
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
```
The remedy "pass one target: …" is dropped.

**Head** (this branch, dist `session-target-BE2kgjYz.mjs`):
```
pass one target: use either the session URL or --url, not both
```
The remedy is surfaced verbatim; no generic "The CLI command failed." frame.

## Test Plan / Verification

- `pnpm test src/cli/session-ref.test.ts src/cli/session-target.test.ts src/cli/attach-cli.action.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` ✅
- `pnpm format:check -- src/cli/session-ref.test.ts src/cli/session-target.ts` ✅
- `git diff --check` ✅
- oxlint on changed files ✅

## Related

- Closes #200142

prs.title: docs(mcp): state the offline ownership requirement for mcp login
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`docs/cli/mcp/transports.md` told readers that "the operator, **or an agent with shell access**, can then run
`openclaw mcp login <name>`". That is not true while a Gateway owns the state: login writes into the owner-only store, so it
refuses with `This operation requires exclusive offline state ownership`. The people most likely to hit it — agents with a
shell — are exactly the ones the sentence invites.

## Why This Change Was Made

`offlineMcpAction` runs every MCP login through `runWithLocalStateOwner` with `onForeignOwner: "refuse"`
(`src/cli/mcp-cli-state-owner.ts:10-22`), and `registerMcpLoginCommand` registers login through it
(`src/cli/mcp-cli.ts:1051`). So a shell plus a running Gateway is not enough; the state must be owned exclusively.

The replacement sentence says what the command actually needs and points at the two ways to get it (stop the Gateway, or run
where no Gateway owns the state), matching how `docs/cli/templates.md:354` and `docs/cli/plugins.md:16` already describe the
same precondition.

## User Impact

An operator reading the OAuth workflow now knows login is an offline-ownership operation instead of trying it against a
running Gateway and meeting a refusal. Nothing else in the page changes; the agent-facing behaviour is unchanged.

## Evidence

Docs-only change, verified against the current guard rather than from memory:

- `src/cli/mcp-cli-state-owner.ts:10-22` — `offlineMcpAction` → `runWithLocalStateOwner({ onForeignOwner: "refuse" })`.
- `src/cli/mcp-cli.ts:1051` — login is registered through that wrapper.
- `docs/cli/templates.md:354`, `docs/cli/plugins.md:16` — the same requirement, already documented for neighbouring paths.

Checks: `pnpm -s format:docs:check` → "Docs formatting clean (1431 files)"; `pnpm -s lint:docs` → "0 issues in 0 files";

prs.title: fix(setup): require the planner schema's command property for strict mode
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw setup --message "<free text>"` failed on every OpenAI default model:

```
LLM request rejected: Invalid schema for response_format 'openclaw_response':
'required' is required to be supplied and to be an array including every key in properties. Missing 'command'.
```

OpenAI structured outputs in strict mode require every declared property to appear in `required`, and the planner schema
declared `reply` and `command` but only required `reply`, so setup could not plan a turn at all.

## Why This Change Was Made

`SYSTEM_AGENT_PLANNER_RESPONSE_SCHEMA` now makes `command` nullable and required:

```ts
properties: { reply: { type: "string" }, command: { type: ["string", "null"] } },
required: ["reply", "command"],
```

A reply-only plan expresses "no command" as `null` instead of omitting the property, which satisfies strict mode and stays
valid for providers without it. No parser change is needed: `parseSystemAgentAssistantPlanText` already treats a
non-string `command` as absent (`typeof record.command === "string" ? … : ""`), so a `null` command parses to a
reply-only plan exactly as an omitted one did.

## User Impact

`openclaw setup` can plan again when the effective default model is OpenAI: the request is accepted and a chat-only plan
produces a reply without a command. Non-OpenAI providers are unaffected — `null` is a normal JSON value for them, and the
parser ignores it.

## Evidence

The existing configured-plan test already pins the exact `responseFormat` sent to the runner; it now asserts the
strict-mode invariant on that captured value rather than only the literal shape:

- `required` equals the property keys (this is the rule strict mode enforces);
- `command` allows `null`.

Red on base behaviour: reverting only `assistant.ts` fails with
`expected [ 'reply' ] to deeply equal [ 'reply', 'command' ]` (`1 failed | 11 passed`); with the change the file reports
`12 passed`.

- `oxlint` on both touched files: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Test lines carry an allocation in `config/test-lines-allocations/setup-planner-strict-schema.txt`.

## AI Assistance

prs.title: fix(images): keep a staged sandbox copy readable next to a transfer binding
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An admitted image attachment failed to hydrate when the same turn was **sandboxed** and the workspace exposed
`prepareTurnAttachments` (the file-transfer workspace service). That turn logged `Native image: failed to load`, loaded
zero images, and never read through the sandbox bridge. Either condition alone worked.

## Why This Change Was Made

`loadMediaRef` already documents the rule — "Admitted managed originals belong to Gateway; staged and discovered paths stay
sandboxed" — but the `gatewayAttachment` test did not honour the staged half:

- with a binding present it became true even for a **staged** ref, so `sandbox` was dropped;
- the local roots then narrowed to the media directory, and the staged copy lives under the sandbox root, so
  `loadWebMediaRaw` raised `path-not-allowed` and the failure was swallowed into a log line.

The staged flag now survives the fact-to-ref conversion (`mediaFactToImageRef` carries `staged: fact.staged === true`,
typed on `MediaFileRef`), and `gatewayAttachment` excludes staged refs, so a sandbox-staged copy keeps the sandbox reader
that produced it. Gateway-owned originals (`media://` facts without a staged twin) behave exactly as before.

## User Impact

Sandboxed turns that also use the file-transfer workspace now hydrate their staged images instead of silently dropping
them, so the model receives the picture the transcript says was attached. Non-sandboxed turns and Gateway-owned originals
are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(ui): sidebar loads older sessions when a session list is collapsed
prs.body:
Related: #192154

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: collapsing a sidebar session list makes it fetch older sessions and show "Loading…", its attention dot does not match the unread dot, and "Load more sessions" turns into "Loading…" whenever the sidebar refreshes in the background.

## User Impact

User impact: in the ungrouped view the session list simply continues when you reach its end, and nothing loads or appears under a list you have closed.

- **Ungrouped view:** reaching the end first shows more of the sessions already loaded, then fetches older ones. There is one control at the end of the list instead of **Show more** and **Load more sessions** stacked together.
- **Collapsed list:** no control and no request. Open it again and it continues from its end.
- **Grouped views and People sort:** unchanged layout. **Show more** stays in each group, and one **Load more sessions** sits below all groups, because an older page can belong to any group.
- **Loading feedback:** only a request for older sessions shows "Loading…". Background refreshes no longer dim or relabel the control, and a click made during one is carried out when it finishes instead of being ignored.
- **Collapsed-group dot:** same size, color and finish as the unread dot. Its meaning (a session inside needs attention) is unchanged.

No configuration change or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first version of this PR removed the automatic loading and left a manual **Load more sessions** button under the collapsed list. That treated the symptom. These are the causes:

1. **The control was in the wrong place.** In the ungrouped view every unpinned session is in one list, but the control that continues that list was rendered below all sections, outside the list. Closing the list did not hide it. It moved it into view, and that was read as "the user reached the end". The control now belongs to the list's own end, so a closed list has nothing to continue from.
2. **It fetched before showing what it had.** One page is 200 sessions and the list starts at 30. Reaching the end fetched another 200 and revealed 15. With 600 sessions on `main`, two visits to the end fetched 400 more sessions to show 30 more, and then the list stopped at 60 with only a manual **Show more**. Now loaded sessions are shown first, 15 per visit, and a page is fetched only when they run out.
3. **"Loading…" reported the wrong thing.** The control used the roster's shared loading state, which is also set by every background refresh. The sidebar now tracks its own request for older sessions.

Accepted edge case: a short ungrouped list whose end is already on screen loads one older page when the sidebar opens or the list is expanded. That is the existing behavior from #192154 and stays bounded to one step per time the end comes into view.

## Maintainer verification

Current candidate: `252c7c9b488b3766974f37e9aec1ff6b38eb239f`. The visual captures below remain from `738e0022`; production code is identical. Before: main `d29fad4e3e687dedf683e38ec35b12cb85510637`.

The original bug still reproduces on that main: collapsing Other leaves a Loading control and sends an older `sessions.list` request with `offset: 16`. The same browser flow on this PR leaves no continuation under the closed list and sends no older-page request.

- All six existing pagination/browser cases passed: loaded rows before older pages, grouped manual pagination, collapse without a request, hidden-only pages, failure/retry, and carrying a click through a same-list background refresh.
- The session-feedback unit lane and its required canaries passed: 531 tests in 56 files.
- Additional cold and previously-visited agent-switch checks did not reproduce an inappropriate append to the replacement agent. Existing owner guards intervene; no speculative production fix was added.
- Maintainer changes remove the computed width/color/radius/shadow equality and keep the inert IntersectionObserver stub limited to the simulated test environment. CI exposed the stub replacing the real browser observer; the same existing roster-visibility assertion failed locally before the repair and passes afterward. All 537 cases in the visibility/feedback selection and required canaries pass. No assertion was weakened and no production behavior changed. The appearance was inspected directly.
- Focused formatting/lint and the independent full-feature review passed. The current source merges cleanly with main `fd8d012d`; no unnecessary baseline merge was added.
- The browser proof uses the real built Control UI, a mocked Gateway and synthetic sessions. It is not a live-Gateway or physical-device claim. Current-head hosted CI remains required.

### Clean before / after

Sidebar crops from the same 1100 × 500 browser scenario. Closing Other starts the unexpected read before; after, the closed list is quiet. The attention indicator retains its meaning and uses the shared unread-dot appearance.

| Theme | Before — main | After — candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dark | ![Collapsed list unexpectedly loading](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2fec9b7a-8c7b-434e-9894-a7edfff40aa6) | ![Collapsed list without a loading control](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9de0d645-5bdc-4c2d-bc8d-7b50e930d93e) |
| Light | ![Unexpected loading in light theme](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd6d7a75-a934-463a-b16b-06c9fb398318) | ![Closed list stays quiet in light theme](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7ced9cc6-0c53-4c04-883e-aa4dac6df07d) |

### Annotated comparison

Outlines identify the closed section and, before the fix, its misplaced loading control.

| Theme | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dark | ![Closed section and misplaced loading control highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2db329c0-8204-4db0-9194-6fd82062807b) | ![Closed section highlighted after the fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e0c7144-f2e6-4661-9a38-004873c964b7) |
| Light | ![Misplaced loading control highlighted in light theme](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ff9c801-5d31-49bd-a83e-dd96e8c783ed) | ![Closed section without continuation in light theme](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1f930753-4895-4022-be8f-0f0bbf6b4d8f) |

Requested by and co-authored with @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: feat(release): choose tooling from a workflow input
prs.body:
Related: #181446

## What Problem This Solves

Release Prepare currently rejects `main`: operators must first cut and select a frozen tooling tag outside the workflow. Newly merged release changes therefore do not become available just by starting preparation from main.

## User Impact

Operators can start **OpenClaw Release Prepare** from `main` and choose `tooling_ref`, defaulting to `main`. A full main-history SHA or an existing protected tooling tag can select a specific version. No per-release SHA needs editing in code.

The workflow resolves the selection once and links the preparation run at its frozen cut. Existing preparation requests retain their recorded tooling during recovery, even after main advances. There is no installed-product behavior change.

The new main-only launcher needs Actions write and permission to create protected tooling tags. Existing tag rules remain enforced; `contents: write` is not a bypass. Workflow-token tag-creation permission is unverified, and an existing-tag input avoids minting a new tag. No live rules, environments, App grants, or publishing identities are changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing tag allocator rather than introduce another freeze mechanism. Move it into the dependency-free tooling-identity owner and migrate its preflight/checklist callers and declaration. The launcher uses the same bounded, non-retrying dispatch owner and records its exact tooling/run receipt before dispatch.

The frozen child still owns preparation/sealing, the release button, and publication. Publisher protected-tag guards, npm environment restrictions, artifact qualification, and approval checks stay unchanged. Newer tooling does not requalify old evidence. An uncertain launcher dispatch preserves its receipt and is not blindly replayed.

Simplification pass: no parallel tag owner, new publisher, checked-in tooling pin, or change to release identity contracts. Against the base: production/workflows +143 net lines, tests +141, documentation +27.

## Evidence

Validated signed head: `4f2c77cb99aac8cfbacd9afcdbd4880699fb6ec8` (base `687dc6c99a32714473a646942382ebcd7f5e6552`). The committed tree exactly matches the checked candidate; checkout is clean.

- **414 tests passed in five focused suites**, final wrapper wall time **75.97s**. Suites cover readiness (145), checklist (152), tag/evidence (39), tooling identity (71), and publish preflight (7).
- Six new workflow-boundary cases execute the real launcher step/CLI against synthetic external GitHub I/O: default main resolving only once while main advances, explicit SHA/tag selection, recorded-cut recovery, rerun refusal, and an ambiguous dispatch retaining its receipt. Focused launcher run: 2.75s Vitest duration / 4.61s wrapper wall time. Existing readiness suite is 60.54s; the new subset exercises real subprocess/dispatch wiring rather than duplicating helper-only assertions. CI seconds are not yet available.
- Baseline reproduction: the original production CLI rejects the new workflow selector before GitHub I/O; the fixed workflow-boundary cases pass.
- Tooling test typecheck, targeted script/test oxlint, oxfmt, JavaScript syntax, and whitespace checks passed. `pnpm check:workflows` passed pinned actionlint, zizmor, generated CI-owner, composite-input, and conflict-marker checks using a process-local Python 3.14 runtime; no global runtime setting changed.
- Fresh independent complete-diff review: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Local ClawSweeper exact committed-range review completed against the base/head above: no actionable correctness or security findings; review status complete, security cleared. Both reviews were read-only and did not claim live permissions or delivery proof.

No live release workflow dispatch, protected tooling-tag creation, package/Store publication, or environment/permission mutation was performed. The actual workflow token's protected-tag creation authority and end-to-end hosted launcher behavior remain unverified; local fixtures do not establish those live permissions. Broad exact-head CI and required owner review remain separate.

prs.title: fix(muse): carry MSP's cutOff mark as an incomplete reply
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When Muse's provider stream dies mid-reply, MSP commits the partial `agentMessage` with `cutOff: true` and fails the turn.
The Muse runtime ignored the mark: `consumeTurn` built the assistant message with the default `stopReason: "stop"`, so
OpenClaw delivered half an answer as an ordinary completed reply with nothing signalling it was incomplete.

## Why This Change Was Made

`extensions/muse/src/events.ts` now maps the mark onto the transport field the host already understands:
`assistantMessage(params, …, item.cutOff === true ? "length" : "stop")`.

No new contract and no core change: the host already treats `stopReason: "length"` as an incomplete reply
(`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/settled-turn-finalization.test.ts` exercises exactly that shape via
`cutOffAttempt`). MSP's own schema defines `Item.cutOff` as "the wire mark for the gate-off 'incomplete response'
rule", so carrying it is the documented intent rather than a new invention.

The text, the transcript bytes, and every other item kind are untouched; only the stop reason on a cut-off assistant
message changes.

## User Impact

A truncated Muse reply is now marked incomplete instead of being presented as the complete answer, so the existing
cut-off handling applies. Non-cut-off replies keep `stopReason: "stop"` exactly as before.

## Evidence

`extensions/muse/src/events.test.ts` gains a parameterised case (`cutOff=false` / `cutOff=true`) driving the real
`consumeTurn` with a folded `agentMessage` item and asserting the persisted message's `stopReason`.

Red on base behaviour: reverting only `events.ts` fails with
`expected 'stop' to be 'length'` (`1 failed | 3 passed`); with the change the file reports `4 passed`.

- `oxlint` on both touched files: 0 warnings, 0 errors.

prs.title: fix(gateway): preserve clean exit while releasing retained state leases
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an orderly Gateway stop exiting with failure when a retained state lease needs its final SQLite cleanup worker.

## User Impact

Completed orderly cleanup preserves exit status 0, so service managers and deployment tooling do not classify it as a crash. Real cleanup failures still propagate. No configuration or schema changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The broker marked itself draining before canonical state cleanup finished. Releasing a retained lease then tried to open its cleanup worker and failed with `SQLite worker host is closing | closed`. The broker now seals ordinary clients and cancels queued admissions immediately, finishes canonical state cleanup, and only then closes host admission and workers. Accepted work still settles.

The faulty callback ordering is present in #188496 (`83064b3ae1155`); the implicated owner files are unchanged between `4bce7604` and `344cc75d`. This identifies the current faulty implementation, not the first historical occurrence or the production trigger.

## Evidence

The retained-lease regression fails on base `2cc6988bc28bd` through `drainGlobalSingletonLifecycleState("shared-state")` with the reported error, while direct database close passes. It passes with the fix and verifies that accepted work settles and the lease row is removed.

Focused broker, lifecycle, capacity, state-lease and Gateway state-ownership tests passed (73 tests). A production-shaped synthetic owner harness uses real SQLite workers, an admitted lease, final singleton drain and the Gateway cleanup exit classifier: base exits 1 with the exact cleanup error; candidate exits 0. No live data was used. Fixture: 5,000 sessions, 35.1 GiB SQLite database, 62,000 workspace files / 1.1 GB on APFS. This does not claim Linux/systemd or full channel-drain proof.

The same synthetic harness also reproduces the failure on `4bce7604`, confirming that this defect predates the supplied release range.

Five alternating pairs: base/fixed median owner elapsed 9.814/51.674 ms, process CPU 13.768/54.821 ms, sampled main-isolate allocation 2.26/2.95 MB. All seven base runs (two controls plus five measured) exit 1; all seven fixed runs exit 0. A/A elapsed controls were base 40.836/8.753 ms and fixed 37.268/53.203 ms. One fixed outlier was 598.619 ms under shared-host load. These are failing-path versus completed-cleanup measurements, not a speedup claim.

Production delta: **+3 lines** (25 added, 22 removed). The shared sealing loop preserves queued-write cancellation; successful registry clearing remains with the lifecycle owner. No new policy/state/cache was introduced. The implementation and final bookkeeping change passed independent Codex autoreview at P0–P2; the final braces-only measurement-script lint follow-up also passed scoped review.

`pnpm check:changed` completed: types, lint, format, import cycles and all structural/schema/worker guards pass. Its sole remaining failure is the unused-export scan: **115 identical findings on exact parent `2cc6988bc28bd` and this PR; zero PR-only findings**. The initial baseline scan lacked workspace dependency links and was discarded; the qualified rerun has no resolution errors. No skip or allowlist was added.

These are recorded main regressions, not noise. The historical consumer-removal patches account for 100 findings across #198933 (`9bfad2b180b4d`), #198936 (`a0423637196f7`) and #198943 (`b90c5739fa5cb`). The remaining 15 exports trace to compaction `472cd0a2f542`, Talk thinking `94e34f956969a`, package release directories #198835 (`b868ed4c21ba0`), desktop protocol movement #193487 (`8af714898fa6e`), subagent presentation #198133 (`18136c960eaf7`), and browser approval #200088 (`1ce9df608b43b`). This PR leaves those unrelated owners unchanged. Exact-head PR CI remains the broad landing gate.

prs.title: refactor(subagents): restore completion authority from saved origin facts
prs.body:
## Scope

Authority from saved facts, slice B (slice A: #200176). Detached work (a subagent completion, a queued follow-up, a cron occurrence) now restores its authority from saved origin facts and current policy at turn admission. The existing operator-recovery restore path (`restoreGatewayQueuedOperatorRecovery`) is the only path; `authorizeTurn` is a thin entry on that owner, not a new module.

## What Problem This Solves

- **Completion custody.** A child result held a live closure over the request that spawned it (`completionAuthorities`). The closure was lost on every restart and released when its source signal fired, although nobody revoked access. The result then failed with "Subagent completion authority is no longer active" (986 and 480 production occurrences on two hosts before slice A).
- **Owner widening after restart.** After a restart, the custody was rebuilt from the requester **session owner**. In a shared session, a guest's child result then ran as the owner.
- **Cron edits killed runs.** A running occurrence re-checked its job definition and occurrence marker on every authority check, so editing a job (for example its name) ended a run that was already in progress.
- **Queued input on a live closure.** A queued follow-up ran on its request's live authority and needed separate liveness probes (`isFollowupOperatorAuthorityCurrent`) at three call sites.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Saved origin on the run row.** `subagent_runs.payload_json` gets `originFacts` (additive JSON, no table, column or migration):
  - a `gateway` or `channel` recovery snapshot (the existing codec);
  - `{ kind: "session", profileId }` when the spawning turn ran as the session principal (restart resume, system turns), restored through `prepareSessionPrincipalRunAuthority`;
  - `{ kind: "system", scopes }` for a launch without an operator principal;
  - `{ kind: "none" }` for a launch without a Gateway authority, which delivers in its caller's scope as before.
- **Refusals are visible; outages are not refusals.** A completion or queued input whose origin cannot be authorized is withheld: a row without `originFacts` (written by an older build), an `unavailable` origin, or a restore that current policy refuses. It never widens to the session owner. A withheld completion settles as a permanent failure, and the parent chat shows the same `withheld: <reason>` notice that #200213 ships for queued input, followed by the result text, so the result stays readable. There is no second renderer and no refusal classifier. The one exception in `toTurnWithheld`: a policy outage (`GatewayOperatorAccessUnavailableError`) or a retryable dispatch outage is not a revocation. The completion stays owed through the existing preparation retry, and queued input keeps its normal retry.
- **Accepted fallback: origins beyond the recovery codec bounds.** Slice A's fallback to live authority now covers only origins the recovery codec cannot serialize (for example a role with more than 256 deny wildcards, or a channel model policy that has no snapshot). Those children run on their live authority and their completions are withheld visibly; queued input from such an origin keeps its live authority check at admission. Session-principal turns no longer use the fallback: they save `{ kind: "session" }`. Removing the rest needs a codec change and is left for a follow-up.
- **Deleted:**
  - the completion custody: map, `requiredCompletionEntries`, bind, release, transfer authority, batch identity comparison, the settle pass, and `subagent-registry-memory.types.ts`;
  - the restart owner-authority rebuild (restart now readmits owed rows by key);
  - the cron per-check occurrence and definition closures in `restoreCronOperatorSource`, `captureCronJobTurnTarget` (including its `sessionId` comparison) and `prepareCronStreamSourceAuthority`;
  - `isFollowupOperatorAuthorityCurrent` and its uses in the drain, the stalled-turn handoff and goal continuation.
- **Not in this PR:** revoked input queued through `chat.send` still fails on the live source before follow-up admission (`operator-run-cancellation` and the steering path), so it shows no notice. That is the next A-auth slice.
- **Kept:** the physical store-switch boundary (`retireCompletionAuthority`, #152828 / #152288) and requester-turn accounting, which is not authority. The accounting now lives in a `WeakMap` that needs no settle pass.

## Upgrade behaviour

- A `subagent_runs` row written by an older build has no `originFacts`. After the upgrade its completion is **withheld**: the parent chat shows `withheld: the origin of this child run was not saved` followed by the result text, so the result stays readable.
- These rows are **not** recovered through the session owner. Restoring them as the session owner would widen authority: in a shared session a guest's child result would run as the owner.
- No schema, stored-row or protocol change: `originFacts` is additive JSON on the existing row payload. Rows written by this build carry it.
- A child still running at upgrade time is re-steered by the restart-resumed parent, which saves `{ kind: "session" }` facts (Upgrade journey in the E2E table).

## Security model

- **Authority** is saved origin facts intersected with current policy, checked at turn admission. Restart, queued input, cron and completions all use the same restore path.
- **Revoked by** a policy change: device revoked, shared token rotated, role or profile changed, channel link removed, or the session principal losing access to the chat. The restore refuses, and the chat shows `withheld: <reason>`. Cancel is explicit: Stop, cron disable or removal. The end of the parent turn, an edit, an abort plus a new message, or a cron job edit no longer revokes anything.
- **Ceiling:** facts come only from the host-issued authority at launch or enqueue (the capture asserts the live authority first, and snapshot scopes are intersected at capture). A session origin restores exactly the principal its spawning turn ran as. Nothing falls back to the session owner or to a live closure.

## User Impact

- A child result reaches its parent after a parent edit, a Gateway restart or an upgrade, under the authority of the person (or session principal) that spawned it.
- Editing a cron job no longer kills its running occurrence.
- A revoked origin shows a visible `withheld` notice that keeps the result readable, instead of a silent drop or a generic "couldn't be delivered" message.

## Evidence

Production diff: net −42 (+476/−518, tests excluded) against merge base `726a8dd4`. E2E table posted below (ocx src, scratch Gateway, real model on the cliproxy route).

prs.title: fix(doctor): clean up a failed heartbeat archive write so retry succeeds
prs.body:
Closes #200083

## What Problem This Solves

`archiveSource` in `src/commands/doctor-heartbeat-scratch-migration.ts` writes the HEARTBEAT.md snapshot to `state/backups/heartbeat-migration/<agent>-<sha256>.md` with an exclusive create (`flag: "wx"`). If the **content write fails after the file has been created** (ENOSPC, EDQUOT, EIO…), the partial file is left behind and the error propagates. Every later `openclaw doctor --fix` then hits `EEXIST`, reads the partial bytes back, fails the hash check, and reports:

```text
HEARTBEAT.md was not migrated: heartbeat migration archive collision at
  <state>/backups/heartbeat-migration/main-<sha>.md | EEXIST ….
  Rerun doctor to retry safely.
```

The remedy in that warning is false: rerunning never succeeds, because the stranded file is never removed. The legacy `HEARTBEAT.md` never migrates, `doctor --fix` keeps warning forever, and the only recovery is hand-deleting a file under `state/`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Same defect class and same fix shape as the two merged precedents for this exact failure mode:

- Precedent: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199447 (templates `create` — partial write blocks retry)
- Precedent: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199426 (plugins `pack` — partial artifact blocks retry)

Open the exclusive file first, record it as owned **before** writing content, and on any failure unlink what this attempt created before rethrowing. The `EEXIST` branch is untouched: an archive that already exists and hashes to the source is still the idempotent success path, and a genuine hash mismatch still raises the collision error.

Fix classification: **behavior-completing** — restores the behavior the warning already promises ("Rerun doctor to retry safely") for the write-failure case; no message, setting, schema, or public-API change.

## User Impact

- After one failed archive write (full disk, quota, I/O error) during `doctor --fix`, the next run migrates normally instead of warning forever.
- No behavior change when the archive already exists and is complete (idempotent rerun), or when it exists with different content (collision error preserved).
- Production +7/-1, tests +35/-1. No new files, no new exports, no config surface.

## Evidence

Shipped-run proofs — both dists built from this machine per the `proof-recipes-2026-10.md §2026-11-15` recipe (`OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1 OPENCLAW_BUILD_WORKER_DEPLOY_BUNDLE=0` + `copy-bundled-plugin-metadata`), base `618bf31` (= the merge-base used below; the two touched files are byte-identical to current `main` `84a378c`), candidate = base + this diff. prs.title: fix(slack): hand transport authority to route-discovery lookups
prs.body:
Fixes #190078

Related: #185972

## What Problem This Solves

Slack outbound route discovery keeps issuing authenticated Slack API requests after the transport authority that authorized the send has been invalidated. The Slack `resolveOutboundSessionRoute` implementation (`extensions/slack/src/channel.ts`) drops the `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` callback that `src/sessions/confirmed-visible-message.ts:235` forwards into it, so none of its three remote lookups revalidate current authority before touching the network:

- Enterprise owner-heartbeat DM workspace discovery — `users.info` + `auth.teams.list` (`extensions/slack/src/enterprise-user-route.ts`)
- D-prefix conversation classification — `conversations.info` (`extensions/slack/src/channel-type.ts`)
- G-prefix conversation classification — `conversations.info` (same owner)

When a Gateway restart or delivery supersession invalidates the worker admission between message acceptance and route discovery, Slack still receives authenticated destination-metadata requests. Remote consequence: a workspace-controlled D/G conversation id or a revoked token keeps being probed after local authority expired; the request cost lands on the operator's credentials.

**Precedent: #185972** — `fix(googlechat): stop metadata lookups after sender authority expires` (merged 2026-10-27). Its body states verbatim:

> "Separate follow-up: audit Slack's analogous route-discovery callback handoff."

This PR is that follow-up. Same shape, same mechanism: forward the **existing** `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` callback into the route-discovery network owner; zero new validators/options/config.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SDK contract already documents the parameter's purpose (`src/channels/plugins/types.core.ts:619-620`):

```ts
/** Revalidates transport authority before new route-discovery network requests. */
assertDirectAdapterHandoff?: () => void;
```

Slack already implements the guard everywhere except the route path:

| Path | State before this PR |
| --- | --- |
| Action path (`action-runtime.ts:276-282`, `312-319`, `actions.ts:229`) | already forwards the callback into `createSlackLookupClient` / write clients |
| Send path (`client-delivery.ts:390`) | already fences delivery via `beforeRequest` |
| Conversation metadata (`channel-type.ts:60-67` → `client-options.ts:176-190`) | `resolveSlackConversationInfo` already accepts the callback and `fenceSlackReadFetch` asserts it before every fetch |
| **Route path (`channel.ts` `resolveOutboundSessionRoute`)** | **dropped it — the only remaining gap** |

This change forwards the already-supplied callback at the three route call sites, widens `resolveSlackChannelType`'s parameter type to pass it through, and hands it to `createSlackLookupClient` in `resolveSlackEnterpriseUserTeamId` (that factory already accepts and fences it). The fence implementation itself is untouched; action and send paths are untouched; no other channel is touched.

Production LOC: +15/−13 (net +2 across three files: `channel.ts` +12/−12 — the two identical conversation-lookup argument objects consolidate into one shared lookup scope, which both forwards the callback and keeps this over-cap file from growing, as the line-cap ratchet requires; `channel-type.ts` +1; `enterprise-user-route.ts` +2/−1). Test LOC: +154/−5 (net +149).

Classification: `behavior-completing` — completes #185972's transport-authority handoff coverage for Slack's analogous route-discovery path.

## User Impact

An accepted message keeps its successful receipt and local history. With **current** authority, route discovery is byte-for-byte unchanged: the same requests go out and the same routes resolve (proven live below). With **invalid** authority, Slack no longer receives new route-discovery metadata requests; the route resolution fails with the authority error instead of silently completing a lookup the operator's admission no longer covers. Callers without handoff context (`src/gateway/conversation-list.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`, `src/infra/outbound/targets.ts`, cron delivery targets) pass no callback and behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

### Heads

- Base (RED): `d45ff6de6c486eb7d68931492e84af4842e02e44` (`docs: point logo work to the brand-kit README (#186198)`, current `main` at pickup)
- Candidate (GREEN): `c9dd1c0a42` (branch `fix/slack-route-discovery-handoff`, rebased onto main `dafda2f722`; production diff identical to the originally reviewed head. Red/green and dist proofs below were recorded at pre-rebase head `45b95e3f9650d22d847d1d81bcd74a1b8f31f35e`; the rebases left the production diff byte-identical. History: `45b95e3f` → rebased to `08e8c0e99c` (baseline bump dropped) → `fe08c2f4c3` (contributor-side rebase onto newer main) → `c9dd1c0a42` adds the `enterprise-user-route.test.ts` assertion alignment, see Maintainer edits.)

### Trigger reachability (producer-chain)

The stale-authority input is produced by production code, not by a test-only seam:

1. **Producer** — `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-transcript.ts:64`: `assertDirectAdapterHandoff: () => stateContext.workerContext.admission.assertCurrent()`. The worker admission assertion is the owner-held liveness check; it fails after Gateway restart or when the delivery is superseded by a newer admission.
2. **Forwarder** — `src/sessions/confirmed-visible-message.ts:228-236`: the **only** caller that forwards the handoff into `resolveOutboundSessionRoute` (`:235`).
3. **Drop point (base)** — `extensions/slack/src/channel.ts` route implementation discards `params.assertDirectAdapterHandoff` for all three remote lookups.
4. **Fence (already shipped)** — `extensions/slack/src/client-options.ts:176-190` `fenceSlackReadFetch` asserts the callback before every fetch once it is attached.

### Red → Green assertions

- **RED (base)**: with a handoff callback that throws, route resolution still completes and the remote lookups still fire — `users.info`/`auth.teams.list` (Enterprise), `conversations.info` (D/G) — and the callback is never invoked. Exactly the 3 new stale tests fail at their `.rejects.toThrow("transport authority expired")` assertion; all other 53 tests pass.
- **GREEN (candidate)**: the same stale callback is invoked before any request and the route rejects with the authority error with **zero** network requests (stub request-log delta `[]`).
- **Legal control (no false positives)**: with a current callback, both base and candidate resolve the same routes (`to: team:T11111111:user:U12345678`, `to: user:U09G2DJ0275`) and the lookups run normally — the fence only rejects genuinely invalid authority.

### Commands × exit

```sh
node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/slack/src/channel.test.ts extensions/slack/src/channel-type.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

| Head | Exit | Result | Wall time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base `d45ff6de6` | 1 | 3 failed / 53 passed (56) — fails exactly at the 3 stale-authority assertions | 1m19.6s |
| candidate (pre-rebase `45b95e3f`) | 0 | 56 passed (56) | 1m22.2s |
| candidate (rebased `08e8c0e99c`) | 0 | 55 passed (55) — one low-value passthrough test removed, see Maintainer edits | 3m16.4s |
| candidate (final `c9dd1c0a42`) | 0 | 66 passed (66) — adds `enterprise-user-route.test.ts` (11) to the run; its exact-args expectation was aligned with the forwarded callback | 3m50.2s |

```sh
pnpm exec oxlint extensions/slack/src/channel.ts extensions/slack/src/channel-type.ts extensions/slack/src/enterprise-user-route.ts extensions/slack/src/channel.test.ts extensions/slack/src/channel-type.test.ts
node scripts/run-format.mts --check <the same five files>
node scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mjs --base d45ff6de6 --no-merge-base
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-max-lines-ratchet.mts --base d45ff6de6 --no-merge-base
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-mock-exports.mts --base d45ff6de6 --no-merge-base
node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base d45ff6de6 --no-merge-base
```

| Check (candidate) | Exit | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| oxlint | 0 | 0 warnings / 0 errors (5 files, 259 rules) |
| format `--check` | 0 | all matched files use the correct format |
| line-cap ratchet | 0 | OK — no new violations or over-cap growth (`channel.ts` stays at/below its base counted lines) |
| max-lines ratchet | 0 | OK — 407 grandfathered suppressions unchanged |
| mock-export ratchet | 0 | OK — 6576 grandfathered factories unchanged |
| test-lines ratchet | 0 | OK with no ceiling change (`Test lines OK: 6293949; ceiling: 6294048; slack: 99` at final head vs pinned base `dafda2f722`) |
| `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.extensions.json --noEmit` | 2 | 17 errors, **all in untouched extensions** (codex/line/nostr/onepassword/policy/test-support/vault/visitor-access, TS2883/TS4023/TS4058 portability noise); zero errors in any slack file. The repo's tsgo gate cannot run on this host (tsrs binary needs glibc ≥2.34); classic tsc substituted. |
| `pnpm build` (dist) | 0 | dist built from candidate sources for the shipped-run proof |

### Shipped-run proof (dist artifacts + real HTTP, loopback Slack API stub)

Setup: `pnpm build` dist; loopback stub records every request (`users.info` / `auth.teams.list` / `conversations.info`) and answers Slack Web API shapes; driver invokes the **dist** plugin route contract (`dist/extensions/slack/api.js` → `slackPlugin.messaging.resolveOutboundSessionRoute`) with `SLACK_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/`, proxies unset, and a seeded installation-identity state (Enterprise for the heartbeat cases, workspace for the D-channel cases — mirroring what the monitor owner registers after `auth.test`).

In the dist build with `SLACK_API_URL` pointing at the loopback Slack stub, the candidate route-discovery path invokes the forwarded handoff before each request: with current authority the enterprise heartbeat route issues `users.info` + `auth.teams.list` against the stub and resolves `team:T11111111:user:U12345678` (handoff asserted 2×), the D-channel route issues `conversations.info` and resolves `user:U09G2DJ0275` (handoff asserted 1×); with stale authority the handoff throws first and the stub request-log delta is **empty** for both paths.

```text
candidate (dist) driver output, one line per case:
{"label":"candidate-d45ff6de6+fix","case":"enterprise-heartbeat-current-authority","outcome":{"resolved":true,"to":"team:T11111111:user:U12345678","baseSessionKey":"agent:main:main:account:default:team:t11111111"},"handoffCalls":2,"stubRequests":["users.info","auth.teams.list"]}
{"label":"candidate-d45ff6de6+fix","case":"enterprise-heartbeat-stale-authority","outcome":{"resolved":false,"error":"A request error occurred: transport authority expired (proof fixture)"},"handoffCalls":0,"stubRequests":[]}
{"label":"candidate-d45ff6de6+fix","case":"d-channel-current-authority","outcome":{"resolved":true,"to":"user:U09G2DJ0275","baseSessionKey":"agent:main:main"},"handoffCalls":1,"stubRequests":["conversations.info"]}
{"label":"candidate-d45ff6de6+fix","case":"d-channel-stale-authority","outcome":{"resolved":false,"error":"transport authority expired (proof fixture)"},"handoffCalls":0,"stubRequests":[]}
```

Base dist comparison (same driver, same stub, same command): with stale authority the lookups still go out and the routes resolve — the shipped defect shape.

```text
base dist driver output (same command, same stub, stale-authority cases resolve and the stub receives the requests):
{"label":"base-d45ff6de6","case":"enterprise-heartbeat-current-authority","outcome":{"resolved":true,"to":"team:T11111111:user:U12345678"},"handoffCalls":0,"stubRequests":["users.info","auth.teams.list"]}
{"label":"base-d45ff6de6","case":"enterprise-heartbeat-stale-authority","outcome":{"resolved":true,"to":"team:T11111111:user:U12345678"},"handoffCalls":0,"stubRequests":["users.info","auth.teams.list"]}
{"label":"base-d45ff6de6","case":"d-channel-current-authority","outcome":{"resolved":true,"to":"user:U09G2DJ0275"},"handoffCalls":0,"stubRequests":["conversations.info"]}
{"label":"base-d45ff6de6","case":"d-channel-stale-authority","outcome":{"resolved":true,"to":"user:U09G2DJ0275"},"handoffCalls":0,"stubRequests":["conversations.info"]}
```

**Evidence grading (honest):**

- **shipped-run** — everything in this section: dist-built Slack plugin artifacts, real fence, real HTTP to the loopback stub, base-vs-candidate comparison at the dist route boundary.
- **producer-chain** — the *live-Gateway orchestration* of a naturally invalidated admission (Gateway restart / delivery supersession mid-flight) was **not** orchestrated on this host; the stale-authority input's production origin and invalidation owner are the file:line chain above, and its fence behavior is proven at the dist boundary. The dist driver seeds the installation-identity state directly (the monitor owner's `auth.test` registration path is not exercised).

### Test-lines ratchet

No ceiling change. The pre-rebase head bumped `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` 6286403 → 6286591, which conflicted with `main`. The first rebase dropped the bump, but CI pins an immutable comparison commit (`ci-ratchet-base`, here main `874dc86b` at push time) whose ceiling 6293290 sat 475 below its own test total, so this PR's net +149 failed the gate there (`over by: 624`). Re-rebasing onto current main `dafda2f722` — whose ceiling was since raised to 6294048 — absorbs the +149 cleanly. Measured at the final head with the ratchet's own working-tree method against the pinned base: `Test lines OK: 6293949; ceiling: 6294048; slack: 99`. If a future rebase re-trips this gate, the fix is to raise the ceiling by exactly the PR's net add with this note as justification.

### Scope and risk

| File:line (candidate) | Change | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `extensions/slack/src/channel.ts:369-374` (Enterprise heartbeat lookup call) | forwards `params.assertDirectAdapterHandoff` into `resolveSlackEnterpriseUserTeamId` | With current authority, no behavior change (same requests, same routes). With invalid authority, route resolution now fails instead of issuing `users.info`/`auth.teams.list` discovery. |
| `extensions/slack/src/channel.ts:387-394` (shared conversation-lookup scope) → `:395` (D-branch) / `:407` (G-branch) | both classification call sites share one lookup scope carrying the callback | Same as above for `conversations.info`; consolidating the duplicated argument object is also what keeps this over-cap file at its base counted lines (line-cap ratchet). |
| `extensions/slack/src/channel-type.ts:148-155` | `resolveSlackChannelType` parameter type widened to carry the optional callback (runtime passthrough already existed) | Additive optional parameter; every existing caller unaffected. |
| `extensions/slack/src/enterprise-user-route.ts:8-13,25` | accepts the optional callback and passes it to `createSlackLookupClient` (already-fenced factory) | Additive optional parameter; non-route callers of this function pass nothing and behave as before. |

- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: **none** — no new option, validator, or configuration surface.
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the shipped `fenceSlackReadFetch` / `createSlackLookupClient` handoff plumbing from #185972's era; nothing new invented.

### Cleanup

Proof scaffolding lives in `/tmp/oc-slack1-proof` (loopback stub, driver, request logs); the stub process is killed after capture. No production Gateway, session, token, or config was touched; no real Slack API was contacted.

### Not tested

- Live Gateway-process heartbeat delivery with a naturally invalidated admission (not orchestrated on this host; producer-chain + dist-boundary proof instead).
- Real Slack API (all HTTP targets are the loopback stub).
- Socket Mode / monitor / action / send paths (untouched by this change; their existing fence tests remain green).
- The repo's `tsgo` typecheck gate (host glibc too old for the tsrs binary); classic `tsc -p tsconfig.extensions.json --noEmit` substituted — zero slack-file errors.

<details>
<summary>Maintainer edits</summary>

- Production change is forwarding one existing optional callback at three route call sites plus one parameter-type widening; `fenceSlackReadFetch`, the action path, and the send path are untouched.

prs.title: fix(slack): match canonically equivalent names in allowlist resolution
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An allowlist entry written in NFC form (e.g. `@Renée`, precomposed) fails to resolve a Slack profile whose display name is stored in NFD form (`Rene\u0301e`, decomposed), and vice versa. The two strings compare unequal under `===` even though they are canonically equivalent, so the user is reported `resolved: false` instead of being matched.

The same omission predicate affects the user's exact-name comparison against `user.name`, `profile.display_name`, and `profile.real_name`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveSlackUserAllowlist` in `extensions/slack/src/resolve-users.ts` compares the allowlist entry name against profile names with `===` on lowercased strings. Lowercasing does not canonicalize Unicode, so NFC/NFD-equivalent spellings of the same name never match. Both sides of the comparison are now normalized with `normalize("NFC")`.

This is the same shape already accepted for the feishu sticker-search path (`#190043`, `extensions/feishu/src/sticker-catalog.ts`) and the slack/feishu/msteams directory lookups that normalize query and candidate before matching.

**Security guard (P1):** canonical matching is a fallback, never a replacement. Exact (lowercased) spelling stays the primary comparison, preserving the pre-existing principal selection. If two active humans have display names that differ only by normalization form (one NFD, one NFC), the configured name resolves to the exact-spelling match even if the canonically-equivalent user appears earlier in the directory. This prevents NFC normalization from displacing the configured principal with a different Slack user id.

Production LOC is `+28/-3` across one file. No new validator, option, config item, or persistence strategy is added.

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## User Impact

Allowlist entries that differ from the stored profile name only by Unicode normalization form now resolve to the correct user id instead of being reported unresolved. Matching for already-canonical names is unchanged. NFC normalization is a canonical-equivalence relation used as a fallback only: it never merges two distinct names, and it can never displace an exact-name match, so it cannot admit a different principal than the one the configured name denotes.

## Evidence

### Shipped entry-point proof (production WebClient over local fixture)

The real exported `resolveSlackUserAllowlist` is exercised through its production `createSlackLookupClient` WebClient path against a local `users.list` fixture, using the existing `SLACK_API_URL` seam the plugin itself supports. No Slack client is mocked: the same code path that ships resolves entries over the fixture.

- Product head SHA: `0e25f23c568a73ea54c92cb926e7ea39bce2225b`
- Current-main RED baseline: `632dced4affb7a338d0def2b7059c246ed33b0af`
- Production entry: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/slack/src/resolve-users.live-proof.test.ts`
- Canonical owner exercised: `resolveSlackUserAllowlist` (`extensions/slack/src/resolve-users.ts:99`) over the production `createSlackLookupClient` (`extensions/slack/src/client.ts:47`) and its `users.list` fetch.
- Decision surface: allowlist entry name matched against `user.name`, `profile.display_name`, `profile.real_name`.
- Recorder/readback boundary: the `resolved` flag and resolved `id`/`name` in `resolveSlackUserAllowlist` output.

Base (`resolve-users.ts` without `normalize("NFC")`):

```text
 Tests  6 failed | 4 passed (10)
  - both NFC/NFD cross-form resolve cases fail (resolved: false)
  - both canonical-direction admission cases fail (no derived grant, sender denied)
  - competing-principal case fails (active grant never derives, intended sender denied)
  - removal case fails (first turn never admits)
  - exact-name / accent-stripped / same-form / ASCII controls pass
 FAILED (exit 1)
```

Head (this PR):

```text
 ✓ resolves NFC entry against an NFD profile through the production WebClient and local users.list fixture
 ✓ resolves NFD entry against an NFC profile through the production WebClient and local users.list fixture
 ✓ keeps exact-name matches ahead of canonically-equivalent directory entries
 ✓ does not admit a different principal (accent-stripped) through the production path
 ✓ keeps same-form and ASCII controls unchanged through the production path
 ✓ name-derived grant through production admission > admits the canonical sender for NFC/NFD entries through production ingress
 ✓ ... > rejects the competing principal while the canonical grant is active
 ✓ ... > denies a different sender (unresolved accent-stripped name) before any agent/provider I/O
 ✓ ... > denies subsequent messages once the name-derived grant is removed
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
 [test] passed 1 Vitest shard
```

### Shipped CLI trace (`openclaw channels resolve`)

The shipped CLI entry point is executed against the same local `users.list` fixture through the plugin's own `SLACK_API_URL` seam (loopback only; the fixture logs every request). No Slack client, transport, or resolver code is mocked or substituted: the command runs the real bundled slack channel plugin (`plugin.resolver.resolveTargets` → `resolveSlackUserAllowlist` over the production WebClient). One CLI invocation is one directory-query batch; the fixture serves a fixed directory per scenario and logs `POST /api/users.list` for each run.

Setup (synthetic token, loopback fixture, nothing public):

```text
$ export SLACK_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:47891/api/        # local users.list fixture on loopback
$ export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=$PWD/proof/openclaw.json    # channels.slack.botToken="xoxb-synthetic-proof" (synthetic)
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs channels resolve --channel slack --kind user <entries>
$ node --version   # v24.22.1
```

Base (`resolve-users.ts` at current main, same tree minus this PR's slack files):

```text
# directory: one user, display name stored NFD (decomposed)
$ channels resolve --channel slack --kind user '@Renée' '@Renée' '@Renee'
@Renée -> U_NFD_STORED (Renée)   # same-form exact match (pre-existing behavior)
@Renée -> unresolved             # cross-form NFC entry vs NFD-stored profile: the defect
@Renee -> unresolved             # accent-stripped distinct name: control
# fixture: [fixture][nfd-stored] POST /api/users.list

# directory: one user, display name stored NFC (precomposed)
$ channels resolve --channel slack --kind user '@Renée' '@Renée'
@Renée -> U_NFC_STORED (Renée)   # same-form exact match (pre-existing behavior)
@Renée -> unresolved            # cross-form NFD entry vs NFC-stored profile: the defect
# fixture: [fixture][nfc-stored] POST /api/users.list

# directory: NFD-stored user listed FIRST, NFC-stored exact spelling second
$ channels resolve --channel slack --kind user '@Renée'
@Renée -> U_INTENDED (Renée)     # exact-name precedence (pre-existing on base)
# fixture: [fixture][precedence] POST /api/users.list
```

Head (this PR, head SHA `0e25f23c568a73ea54c92cb926e7ea39bce2225b`; built from a tree whose slack files are byte-identical to the head SHA):

```text
# directory: one user, display name stored NFD (decomposed)
$ channels resolve --channel slack --kind user '@Renée' '@Renée' '@Renee'
@Renée -> U_NFD_STORED (Renée)   # cross-form NFC entry now resolves (fixed)
@Renée -> U_NFD_STORED (Renée)   # same-form exact match unchanged
@Renee -> unresolved             # accent-stripped distinct name still unresolved
# fixture: [fixture][nfd-stored] POST /api/users.list

# directory: one user, display name stored NFC (precomposed)
$ channels resolve --channel slack --kind user '@Renée' '@Renée'
@Renée -> U_NFC_STORED (Renée)   # cross-form NFD entry now resolves (fixed)
@Renée -> U_NFC_STORED (Renée)    # same-form exact match unchanged
# fixture: [fixture][nfc-stored] POST /api/users.list

# directory: NFD-stored user listed FIRST, NFC-stored exact spelling second
$ channels resolve --channel slack --kind user '@Renée'
@Renée -> U_INTENDED (Renée)     # exact-name precedence intact: the canonically-equivalent
                                 # earlier directory entry never displaces the exact-spelling match
# fixture: [fixture][precedence] POST /api/users.list
```

Both NFC→NFD and NFD→NFC directions resolve on head and were unresolved on base; same-form matching, the accent-stripped control, and exact-name precedence are unchanged. IPs are loopback, the token is synthetic, and no non-public endpoint is touched.

### Authority-chain proof: production DM ingress through final effect

The authority chain no longer stops at the resolver return value or a bare admission boolean. `createMonitorTestContext` returns a context whose `readRuntimeContext` is the real `createSlackRuntimeContextReader`, so awaiting it runs the production `resolveWorkspacePolicy` (`extensions/slack/src/monitor/runtime-policy.ts:239-250`), which resolves the allowlist names through the real `resolveSlackUserAllowlist` over the local `users.list` fixture and merges the derived ids into `ctx.allowFrom` via `mergeAllowlist`. The resolved policy context is then handed to the production DM ingress entry point `prepareSlackMessage` (`extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/prepare.ts`), the function the monitor calls for every inbound message; it runs the DM admission gate `authorizeSlackDirectMessage` and, on admission, returns the exact `PreparedSlackMessage` object the monitor dispatches to the agent/provider. No admission helper, Slack client, or dispatch seam is mocked.

- **Both canonical directions admit the intended Slack ID at final effect.** `@Renée` (NFC) against an NFD-stored profile, and the NFD spelling against an NFC-stored profile, each resolve to `U_ACCENT` through production policy reload, the id lands in the allow-from list, and `prepareSlackMessage` returns a non-null `PreparedSlackMessage` for sender `U_ACCENT` — the object that reaches agent/provider dispatch.
- **The competing principal is rejected while the canonical grant is active.** With `@Renée` derived to `U_ACCENT` and present in allow-from, a message from `U_OTHER` — a distinct sender with its own fixture display name and identity, resolved per user id exactly as production resolves sender names (`prepare.ts:381`) — returns null: the DM gate drops the event before any agent/provider I/O. The derived grant admits exactly the resolved principal and never a different Slack user id.
- **A distinct name is denied before any agent/provider I/O.** With the accent-stripped `@Renee` configured (unresolved), `U_ACCENT` never becomes a derived grant and both `U_ACCENT` and `U_OTHER` are dropped before dispatch.
- **Removing the name-derived grant denies subsequent messages on the same runtime policy reader.** First turn `@Renée` resolves and `U_ACCENT` is admitted at final effect. The published config is then replaced with one whose only entry is the stale `@Renee`; the same reader rebuilds policy on its next read (`runtime-policy.ts:116`, `current.cfg !== cfg`), the derived id leaves allow-from, and a subsequent message from `U_ACCENT` is dropped before dispatch — the same live-policy-change path the monitor uses, no reconnect or fresh monitor.
- **Exact-name principal is preserved (P1 regression).** With `U_OTHER` (NFD display name) before `U_INTENDED` (NFC display name) in the directory, `@Renée` resolves to `U_INTENDED`, not the canonically-equivalent earlier entry. This test fails on the pure-canonical head (selects `U_OTHER`) and passes on this head.

Base (`resolve-users.ts` without `normalize("NFC")`):

```text
 Tests  6 failed | 4 passed (10)
 FAILED (exit 1)
```

Pure-canonical head (without exact-first guard):

```text
 × keeps exact-name matches ahead of canonically-equivalent directory entries
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 9 passed (10)
 FAILED (exit 1)
```

Head (this PR):

```text
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
 [test] passed 1 Vitest shard
```

### Focused unit regression

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/slack/src/resolve-users.test.ts` — 9 passed on this head. The NFC/NFD cross-form cases are covered by the production-WebClient live-proof group instead of duplicated mocked-client cases; the focused unit suite retains its existing mocked-client coverage of resolution inputs and outputs.

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/slack/src/resolve-users.live-proof.test.ts` — 10 passed, 1 shard, ~50s wall.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/slack/src/resolve-users.test.ts` — 9 passed, 1 shard.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- Not tested: no live Slack API call and no full gateway process boot. `resolveSlackUserAllowlist` resolves names to IDs from a `users.list` response; the fixture drives the real WebClient through the plugin's own `SLACK_API_URL` seam. The authority chain runs the production policy reload and the production DM ingress over the fixture; the remaining runtime path (socket-mode event reception) is exercised by existing monitor tests, not re-driven here.

## Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+28/-3`
- Test LOC: `+390/-0` (live-proof integration, including the authority-chain group); the focused unit suite is unchanged (added NFC/NFD mocked-client cases were dropped per review as duplicates of the live proof).
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the existing `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty` helper already used in this file; adds only `normalize("NFC")` on both comparison sides, matching the accepted feishu sticker-search fix (#190043).
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none. NFC normalization is a canonical equivalence used as a fallback only — it collapses only spellings of the same name and never displaces an exact-name match, so it cannot widen admission to a different principal; the P1 two-id regression and the accent-stripped control prove distinct names are still denied, the competing-principal case proves the derived grant rejects every other sender identity at the production ingress boundary, and the same-reader removal case proves the grant is revoked by the same live-policy path that created it.

prs.title: fix(gateway): blank --url silently reports the default gateway status
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw gateway status --url ""` (or `--url "$VAR"` where the variable is empty) exits 0 and prints the **configured default Gateway's** service/connectivity report instead of rejecting the blank target. The same command with a non-empty `--url ws://…` probes exactly that URL, so an explicitly passed empty value is silently treated as "flag not provided" while any other value is honored.

`openclaw gateway probe --url ""` has the same silent drop: it prints the full `Gateway Status` report for the configured local/remote targets (byte-identical to running `gateway probe` with no `--url` at all).

Root cause: two independent drop points turn `""` into "absent" before any target is resolved.
- `src/commands/gateway-status.ts` (`gatewayStatusCommand`, the engine behind `gateway probe`): `ensureExplicitGatewayAuth({ urlOverride: opts.url?.trim() })` early-returns on an empty override, `resolveTargets()` maps `""` → `normalizeWsUrl` → `null` (no explicit target), and `hasExplicitUrl` reads `opts.url.trim().length > 0` → `false`.
- `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.ts` (`runDaemonStatus`, behind `gateway status`): `opts.rpc.url` is passed straight through and `status.gather.ts` treats a falsy override as "use the configured target" (`if (opts.deep && !trimToUndefined(opts.rpc.url))`).

## User Impact

User impact: scripts and operators that pass an empty `--url` (typically `--url "$GATEWAY_URL"` with an unset variable) now get a clear error and exit 1 instead of a successful report about a **different** Gateway than the one they asked about — before any probe, SSH tunnel, Bonjour discovery, or service inspection starts. Blank values fail at command entry, so no partial output is produced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a 3-line blank check at the top of `gatewayStatusCommand` and a 4-line blank check at the top of `runDaemonStatus`, reusing the repository's existing `must not be blank` contract (the same wording and shape as `agentCliCommand` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts`, `account-selector.ts`, `channel-selector.ts`, and the merged `--agent must not be blank` guard from #193336). Each check sits at the entry of the command that owns the `--url` option, before any of its consumers run.

Not introducing: no new error type, no config validation, no shared resolver change, no owner/state/schema/API change, no SDK-visible surface. `resolveGatewayRpcOptions` / `addGatewayClientOptions` (shared by `gateway call`, `health`, `stability`, `diagnostics export`, `exec-policy`, …) are deliberately untouched — that is a wider family with its own blast radius and is recorded as a follow-up rather than folded into this fix.

## Evidence

Base `37706a74a81129f8ec85289399a2703abf98c2b4` (branch base = `origin/main` at branch creation) → Candidate `166efe4ed6ad68a3dceeee079eececc8dbfd564f` (branch `fix/gateway-status-blank-url`).

Environment: Linux x64, Node v24.22.1, normally built `openclaw.mjs` (`OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1 pnpm build:docker`), isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` + `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (+ isolated `HOME`), no Gateway running, no network dependency, no seed data. Every case below was run **twice**; each pair was compared with `cmp` (exit code + stdout + stderr), not by eye.

### Shipped CLI (each leg run at least twice)

| case | base | candidate |
|---|---|---|
| `gateway status --url ""` ×2 | **exit 0**, stdout+stderr **byte-identical** to `gateway status` with no flag (md5 `358f247acd194509801e9873eed89e45` / `f8cb63b30f259108654742cce8c82c30`) — blank silently dropped | **exit 1**, stderr `Gateway status failed: --url must not be blank` |
| `gateway status` (no `--url`) ×2 | exit 0 | exit 0, **byte-identical to base** |
| `gateway status --url "ws://127.0.0.1:9"` ×2 | exit 0, `Check target: ws://127.0.0.1:9` (explicit target honored) | exit 0, **byte-identical to base** |
| `gateway probe --url ""` ×2 | **exit 1**, stdout+stderr **byte-identical** to `gateway probe` with no flag (stdout md5 `f930c0cfd768d2f066ce142512e2e10d`, stderr empty `d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e`) — blank silently dropped | **exit 1**, stderr `--url must not be blank` |
| `gateway probe` (no `--url`) ×2 | exit 1 (`Gateway Status / Reachable: no`) | exit 1, **byte-identical to base** |
| `gateway probe --url "ws://127.0.0.1:9"` ×2 | exit 1, explicit target probed | exit 1, **byte-identical to base** |

All eight "unchanged" comparisons were byte-identical (`cmp` clean on both streams) between the base build and the candidate build in the same isolated home/state directory.

### Regression RED → GREEN (remote, real vitest)

Remote proof host (Docker `lexiflow-all:latest`, Node `v24.22.1`, `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`), production files at `37706a74a81` bytes (verified md5-identical to `git show origin/main:<path>` for all four files before the run):

```text
sh node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts \
  src/commands/gateway-status.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
sh node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts \
  src/cli/daemon-cli/status.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

- **base production + new test → RED.** `commands` shard: `1 failed | 30 passed (31)` — `rejects a blank --url before reading config or probing` fails with `AssertionError: promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting` at `src/commands/gateway-status.test.ts:234` (the blank value silently proceeded past the guard). `cli` shard: `1 failed | 7 passed (8)` — `rejects a blank --url before gathering status` fails with the same `promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting` at `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.test.ts:140`.
- **candidate production + the same tests → GREEN.** `commands` shard: `31 passed (31)`; `cli` shard: `8 passed (8)` (the new `rejects a blank --url before gathering status` case is green).
- **Siblings/consumers on the candidate (all green):** `src/cli/gateway-cli.coverage.test.ts`, `src/cli/gateway-cli/register.option-collisions.test.ts`, `src/cli/daemon-cli/register-service-commands.test.ts`, `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.install-hints.test.ts`, `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.gather.test.ts`, `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.print.test.ts` → `6 passed (6)` files, `156 passed | 2 skipped (158)`; `src/commands/gateway-status/helpers.test.ts` (root matrix) → `1 passed (1)` file, `18 passed (18)`.

### Local gates

```text
oxlint (v1.88.0) src/commands/gateway-status.ts src/commands/gateway-status.test.ts src/cli/daemon-cli/status.ts src/cli/daemon-cli/status.test.ts → 0 findings, exit 0
node scripts/run-format.mts --check <those four files> → All matched files use the correct format
node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base 37706a74a81 → Test lines OK (allocation credit equals this PR's +18 delta)
git diff --check → clean
```

### Line counts

Whole-PR delta: production **+7/-0** (2 files), tests **+18/-0** (2 files), `config/test-lines-allocations/gateway-status-blank-url.txt` = **18** for exactly this PR's net test growth. Shared scalar `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` untouched. On a clean `37706a74a81` the ratchet reports `Test lines OK: 6496704; ceiling: 6496746; slack: 42`, so this branch stays inside the ceiling with the allocation applied.

### Negative claims

- Not claimed: `gateway status`/`gateway probe` against a **running** Gateway — both legs run with no listener, and the proof is exit code + byte-identical output identity, not live capability data.
- Not claimed: the shared `--url` consumers (`gateway call`, `health`, `stability`, `diagnostics export`, `exec-policy`, …). They share the shape but are a wider family; fixing them belongs to a separate, explicitly scoped change.
- Not claimed: whitespace-only `--url "   "` at the CLI (covered by the same `.trim()` expression; the shipped CLI leg exercises `""`, and the unit test exercises both `""` and `"   "` for `gateway probe`).

## Focused Checks and Simplification

- 7 production lines across 2 production files; each guard is a straight-line `if` at the existing command entry, no helper, no wrapper, no new export, no new error class.
- Tests were merged into the two files that already own these commands (`gateway-status.test.ts`, `status.test.ts`), reusing their existing mock-not-called assertions so no new harness was introduced.
- Test-lines: this PR adds an allocation of exactly its +18 growth and leaves the shared scalar alone.

## Compatibility and Merge Risk

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous silent fallback without migrations or persisted state changes. Blast radius is `--url` validation at exactly two command entries (`gateway status`, `gateway probe`); both fail **before** config reads, probes, SSH tunnels, Bonjour discovery, and service inspection. Unchanged adjacent behavior: omitted `--url`, non-empty valid URLs, non-empty invalid URLs (still probed and reported as before), `--token`/`--password`/`--port`/`--ssh` handling, `--json` output shape for every non-blank case, and every other command.

Collision check (run against `origin/main` minutes before opening): no open PR modifies `src/commands/gateway-status.ts`, `src/commands/gateway-status.test.ts`, `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.ts`, or `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.test.ts`; `gh pr list --search "gateway status"` / `"blank url"` and per-file `gh api pulls/<n>/files` checks returned only unrelated work (the one parallel-lane PR touching remote URLs, #193538, edits `src/commands/onboard-remote.ts` only).

## Status

Reopened: this pull request was closed by mistake during a session cleanup on 2026-11-12 while it was still `proof: sufficient` + `ready for maintainer look`. The branch was rebased onto `611bea727f21` (the only conflict was a neighbouring test in `status.test.ts`, resolved by keeping both cases) and the diff is byte-identical to the previously reviewed head. No new behavior was added.
