  ![case3-stop-2-after-aborted.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n1hility/openclaw/b91a947061caef11a9e1a99e3aca9cb379b36e0c/pr-143882/case3-stop-2-after-aborted.png)

  - Message 1 still `Thinking, continued below`.
  - Message 2 is finalized as `Thought for 12s`: complete, no longer streaming.
  - The user's `stop` reply follows, then the bot's stop confirmation `⚙️ Agent was aborted.`
  - No third message, no further rows, no answer. The thread stayed unchanged for the following 60 s of polling.

Log (`cards.log`, redacted):

```
21:28:22.801 slack-stream: native progress message 1 rolled (budget; 5269 weighted bytes, 22 rows); continuing in a new message
21:28:25.734 [plugins] [hooks] running run_stopped (1 handlers)
21:28:25.743 [agent/embedded] compaction wait aborted: runId=<run> sessionId=<session>
21:28:25.748 [diagnostic] message processed: ... outcome=skipped                                  # the C2 turn, aborted
21:28:25.760 [turn/execution] visible channel turn dispatched with no queued reply payloads: ... cause=skipped:reply_operation_aborted
21:28:25.774 [diagnostic] message processed: ... outcome=completed                                # the "stop" message
21:28:25.869 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main durationMs=13648 error="agent run aborted" errorName=AbortError
21:28:25.870 [model-fallback/decision] model fallback chain stopped: reason=caller_signal_aborted candidate=<provider>/<model>
21:28:25.889 [slack] delivered reply to channel:<D-channel>                                         # "Agent was aborted." confirmation
```

- After the stop, `grep -E "rolled|streamed delivery failed|falling back|failed to finalize|msg_too_long"` → **no matches**.
- The stop landed about 3 s after the roll. The run aborted, no later roll occurred, no fallback answer was posted, and both progress messages ended in a completed (non-streaming) state.

Not covered: native-Stop variants (Stop on the continuation message, and Stop on the message that just rolled, which targets `streaming_message_ts`). Both need the app to subscribe to `agent_session_stopped`.

##### Other observations

- `slack-stream: users.info team lookup failed (missing_scope)` appears on every stream start. The test app lacks `users:read`, and it is harmless here.
- `assistant_app_thread message_changed ... dropped: no sender resolved from metadata` is logged when Slack edits the thread title. It is harmless.
- **First attempt invalid.** On the first attempt (before this run), a second gateway was connected to the same Slack app and answered the N1 message. Those frames were discarded. Every run reported here started with a single Socket Mode connection.

</details>


### Prior head `ea1a10d` (real Slack, 2026-09-09/10)

The live evidence below was gathered on the previous head; the behavior it covers (card rendering, byte budgets, rollover, the answer-rejected path, the late boundary) is carried over unchanged in substance, but it is prior-head evidence; the live run on this head is above.

- Motivating failure, cards without rollover: a scripted 12,010-character think with one `bash` call rendered 48 rows, then the 92-character answer was rejected with `msg_too_long` (11,215 bytes of titles on the message); the plugin rethrew, never called `chat.stopStream`, and the message stayed `in_progress` without the answer.
- Size probes over the raw SDK (superseded by the exact measurements above; the byte interpretation drawn from them was wrong): 250-character rows accepted through the 42nd (10,571 bytes) and rejected at the 43rd; text-only 9,064 bytes accepted / 12,054 rejected; rows with 100 characters of `details` rejected at 8,821 bytes; 50 emoji-only rows with no body text (22,900 bytes) accepted; 24 emoji rows (10,418 bytes, 8,666 UTF-16 units) rejected a 3,045-character answer. Only UTF-8 bytes fit every run (ceiling about 10,600-11,300 once the message carries text).
- Rollover build: the 12,010-character think rendered as three messages in the thread (`Thinking, continued below` → `Thinking, continued below` → `Thought for 35s, 1 tool call` with the answer), 3 starts / 28 appends / 3 stops, no errors, each stop/start about 300 ms. Emoji-only reasoning rolled at 25 rows / 5,950 bytes over six messages and the 3,045-character answer landed on the last one.
- Real model (OpenClaw gateway from source, Socket Mode, `reasoningDefault: "stream"`): short question and riddle on one message (`Thought for 6s` / `Thought for 10s`); a 25-segment think around one `exec` rolled once and finished `Thought for 59s, 1 tool call` with the answer on the continuation. Before the late-boundary fix (now commit 1) the same setup produced the two defects it addresses: a short answer streamed as a separate message after the card was stopped, and a continuation ending under the preamble headline.

Screenshots from those runs (test workspace, cropped to one thread reply), full sets on the fork's [evidence branch](https://github.com/n1hility/openclaw/tree/f8b16d429ab4cea8a7d0a0cb44be1d773594ff71/screenshots):

![Short think, no tool call: two 🧠 rows under `Thought for 5s`, answer below the card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n1hility/openclaw/f8b16d429ab4cea8a7d0a0cb44be1d773594ff71/screenshots/final2/r3-s1-short-think.png)

![Long think with one tool call, first of three messages: `Thinking, continued below`, all rows complete](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n1hility/openclaw/f8b16d429ab4cea8a7d0a0cb44be1d773594ff71/screenshots/final2/r3-s2-long-think-msg1-01.png)

![Same turn, third message: the last cards under `Thought for 35s, 1 tool call`, followed by the answer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n1hility/openclaw/f8b16d429ab4cea8a7d0a0cb44be1d773594ff71/screenshots/final2/r3-s2-long-think-msg3-answer.png)

![Real model over Socket Mode, turn with one `exec` call: the continuation ends with `Thought for 59s, 1 tool call` and carries the answer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n1hility/openclaw/f8b16d429ab4cea8a7d0a0cb44be1d773594ff71/screenshots/real-model/rm2-long-msg2-answer.png)

### Not tested

- The native Slack Stop button: the test app does not subscribe to `agent_session_stopped`, so Stop during a rollover was exercised live through the text stop trigger, which takes the same abort path but not `markSlackStreamsStopped`.
- Live: the card roll-and-retry path after a `msg_too_long` on a card update (dispatcher tests; with the measured model the ledger stays under Slack's ceiling).

<details>
<summary>Review findings addressed on the previous head (all carried over, with their tests)</summary>

Sixteen review findings were fixed across earlier rounds, each with a test that failed on the reviewed head; all of those tests are ported to this head and pass. In short: rejected closeout rows, partial-card extensions and same-title tool-row updates carried to the continuation; queued reasoning rows never evicted by the compositor window; raw reasoning kept across deltas (`reasoningLine`); a Slack Stop honored across continuation messages; rejected SDK text discarded before a rollover stop; queued cards drained through budgeted messages before error, media and silent closeouts and before turn rotation; a rejected completion carried to the message that streams the answer; running tool rows kept across rollovers and frozen rows thawed by a later result; bounded admission (a guard charges every accepted start, append and stop to its message and fails any test where a message passes 50 rows or the byte budget); budgeted narration continuations; tool rows never overtaking queued reasoning; continuation capacity held for queued cards behind a full plan.

</details>

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): members can recover access with a recovery kit
prs.body:
Related: OCF-552 (Linear) · companion PRs: openclaw/discovery#19, openclaw/claw-loader#38

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a member who loses every approved browser (site data cleared, new machine) cannot get back into the claw without the owner.

## User Impact

User impact: a member can save a recovery kit and later use it to add a new browser to their own account, with the same identity and role. The owner is notified immediately: a toast naming the member and browser, an Inbox item linking to that browser with Remove, and a retained recovery history. Kit use is notify-only (owner's decision); the owner can remove the browser or the member at any time.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each member can hold one recovery-only Ed25519 key, listed under the member and never admitted as a tunnel peer. It can only sign `add_member_device` for that same current member account: no role change, no owner capability, no other account. Removing the member kills the kit; replacing the kit invalidates the old one without removing browsers it already admitted. Admission and the owner-only history record commit atomically. The owner's "used their recovery kit" notice is attributed to the current admission, not any historical record for the same browser key.

**Targets main.** OCF-551 has landed. This branch is rebased onto main `13a0a3e7edff877b24f76f9a263952a61268eccd`, preserving main's custom role controls and role-change validation alongside recovery behavior. Landing order remains openclaw → discovery → claw-loader. Discovery and loader protocol snapshots still match `c923202e7b8b` byte-for-byte; this rebase did not change protocol bytes.

**Includes [#200241](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200241).** Its gzip-parity fix is folded into this PR: emitted boot assets and normalized budget measurements share selection of the smallest gzip at levels 10/11/12. No performance budgets or normalization rules were raised or changed. The performance gate passes with the included fix; this is no longer a dependency waiting to land separately.

## Evidence

### ClawSweeper P2 repair — `11a19d4abb75`

- Recovery history now checks raw recovery provenance and previous peer membership before projecting any member devices. Bookkeeping commits do not fingerprint device lists; members with a new recovery still use the complete canonical projection, preserving blank/duplicate labels.
- Fail-first container proof on `da2de290724f` plus the regression: four label cases failed because `recordDiscovery` and `recordSeen` each projected devices. The regression requires two actual storage writes and zero projection/fingerprint calls; it cannot pass by skipping the commits.
- Fixed-tree container: 19 focused Gateway tests passed; all baseline ratchets, line cap, core types, scoped lint and formatting passed. Input is `da2de290724f` plus repair patch SHA-256 `9b81a5993b6f6ea698f78fd2af6a22d5501adf5bd7d7e8b16e729883e09425b3`, now committed as `11a19d4abb75`. Independent Astra review of the three-file repair found no verified P0–P2 findings.
- Exactly 17 regression lines were added with explicit allocation approval: **1342 = 400 + 942**. No unrelated coverage removed, file cap or performance budget changed.
- Studio Crabbox `local-container`, `node:24.22.1-trixie`, digest `sha256:f1e034976f948cf212ef1f659c12e5dd58ac7eab947831813e81a62401ca38be`, 8 CPUs/24 GiB: red lease `cbx_e14a7141ab8d`, run `run_a6a4fe36eab78b64934fe1f151d83473` (expected exit 1); green lease `cbx_71efc7760f32`, run `run_a3f1058ee0df53b119be446a81a08797` (exit 0). Both stopped. Scripts apply the named patch in the disposable container, after frozen pnpm installation; no host suites.
- **Unresolved unrelated E2E attribution:** [prior-head job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43981477637/job/133699859279) failed replacement-composer retained-comments preview visibility at line 488 (case at line 435), on synthetic merge `db541b7fc095fdffba031a43689c629de0aa6121`. The same unchanged test passed in three nearby hosted main runs; shared bootstrap changes mean unchanged test source alone does not establish inherited failure or flakiness. A bounded same-container comparison (three whole-file runs each at current-main `fd8d012d70c786b8fa33fbe296c9709f5238d2e7` and repaired head `11a19d4abb75`) was launched, but result collection is blocked: Studio SSH became unreachable and the single reconnect also timed out. Pass/fail counts and this run’s cleanup are unknown; do not infer flake or inherited failure. The detached run will need reconciliation when the host is reachable. No hosted CI rerun requested. **Next-head hosted result:** all ten `checks-ui-e2e` jobs succeeded in [run 43989901712](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43989901712) at `11a19d4abb75`; the coordinator also confirmed `chat-selection-to-main` passed. The `da2de290` failure did not recur at the next head. This is not evidence establishing a flake or inherited failure. **A/B remains pending because Studio is offline**, confirmed by the coordinator via Tailscale; its log is `~/crabbox-proof/ocf552-p2-ab.log`. No further access attempts or alternative-host runs will be made until the coordinator reports that Studio is back. Lease and task-checkout cleanup remain unverified and pending.

### Historical main-retarget validation — previous head `da2de290724f`

- Core: `da2de290724f8d15becc098b900aa02d41e18989`; Discovery #19: `2df5189678b4004a99f5e6a01f80aa7e4b6b3203`; loader #38: `27efca221154d5d3260e22908b195065db4520f9`. All three target `main`.
- Independent Astra source reviews of the core conflict resolution, loader integration and test extraction found no verified P0–P2 findings. Main's extracted role controls and validation are retained. The three compression-fix files match the reviewed #200241 source. Protocol subtree remains byte-identical to `c923202e7b8b`, so no vendor resync was needed.
- **Broad container pass at `3374686a12ce8fbbbc684b5d923bb0cf3ab25455`:** 265 protocol tests, 31 focused Gateway tests and 95 UI/parity tests passed. Baseline ratchets, additional boundary checks, max-lines, assertion safety, controller checks, plugin import boundaries, core/UI/extension type checks and `pnpm ui:check-performance:base 13a0a3e7edff877b24f76f9a263952a61268eccd` all passed. Lease `cbx_c6ef5bddc7f3`, run `run_c440fcfae57c3078ec3330b86b7262e2`, exit 0.
- **Exact final-head container pass at `da2de290724f`:** scoped extension lint, both People page suites (34 tests), test-line and line-cap ratchets passed. The only delta after the broad pass removes an unused test import and decreases its allocation by one; production source and test assertions are unchanged. Lease `cbx_f0a53f601e23`, run `run_1acfecd3a2ab41b2ff8c23132bc5af4f`, exit 0.
- Final test lines: **+1325 = 400 default + 925 justified allocation**. Allocation documents protocol, Gateway, browser composition, People/owner UI and the 37-line compression-parity coverage. Recovery page tests were moved unchanged into their own suite to keep the existing main role suite below its file cap; this is not a raised file-size budget.
- Earlier container `cbx_92e09c997309` at `20ee16ea1ac0` additionally passed the two browser test files (2 + 2 tests); that whole run was not green because the later-repaired line cap failed. First-run path/worker setup and test-allocation failures are not counted as passes. After the split, the unused import was caught by hosted lint and removed; the exact-head run above verifies the repair.
- All runs used Studio-launched Crabbox `local-container`, `node:24.22.1-trixie`, image digest `sha256:f1e034976f948cf212ef1f659c12e5dd58ac7eab947831813e81a62401ca38be`, 8 CPUs / 24 GiB, frozen pnpm install and two test workers. Launch: `crabbox run --provider local-container --local-container-image node:24.22.1-trixie --local-container-cpus 8 --local-container-memory 24g --no-hydrate --timing-json --shell -- 'bash core-checks.sh'` (final run: `bash final-checks.sh`). Each receipt reports `leaseStopped: true`; final container inspection was empty.
- Discovery and loader have fresh successful hosted CI at the heads above. Their separate Studio container proof was blocked at private-repository checkout authentication; no credentials were copied. Their PRs disclose this limit. No new live Gateway/transport or upgrade proof is claimed at the rebased heads; historical proof below remains pinned to its actual revisions.


### Historical data-model compatibility and restart proof (pre-rebase)

**Passed in a Crabbox Linux container on the Studio**, using candidate `3e7e9f0faf7ac585a82aa5431657e0131eac271c` and actual main `bd25e9ef60cc886dc6c0512927bf1cf425e364df` as the database producer. No product files or dependencies changed. A temporary harness occupied the existing `claw-store.persistence.test.ts` worker-test entry only inside the disposable container; each revision compiled and used its own state worker through `node scripts/test-projects.mts`.

- Main wrote a physical state DB through `writeStoredClaw`, canonical profile persistence, and the core plugin-state API: synthetic membership with an admitted member browser, **8 existing logical plugin-state rows**, one profile, and an unrelated sentinel. Main closed the DB before the candidate received its state directory.
- On first open, the candidate read back **all 8 rows, the entire stored claw, the profile, and plugin-state table/index SQL unchanged**.
- The candidate registered a real generated recovery-kit public key with a member-signed statement, closed/reopened the DB, and verified the saved kit. It then admitted two signed mailbox recoveries, one blank-label browser and one duplicate-label browser, closing/reopening after each.
- Expected writes were confined to the claw's current/membership rows plus the two recovery-history entries. **All 6 other pre-existing logical rows**, including the sentinel, remained identical; the original member device, role, profile, and plugin-state schema were preserved.
- A **third, separate Node/Vitest process** opened the saved candidate state and verified the entire stored claw and logical DB snapshot, registered kit and both history entries. Blank and duplicate browser names had the expected fingerprint suffixes and matched the device-row and owner `recoveryUses` projections, with `member_recovery_kit` provenance. That is data/projection proof for the owner notice's input, **not a new rendered-toast screenshot or browser E2E**.

Execution provenance:

- Provider: `local-container`; lease: `cbx_6c7099fbc653`; run: `run_b484c8bc58a93538cf2cd5250c345baa` (no hosted run URL supplied).
- Image: `node:24.22.1-trixie`; runtime image/digest: `sha256:f1e034976f948cf212ef1f659c12e5dd58ac7eab947831813e81a62401ca38be`; 8 CPUs / 24 GiB requested.
- Command: `crabbox run --provider local-container --local-container-image node:24.22.1-trixie --local-container-cpus 8 --local-container-memory 24g --no-hydrate --timing-json --shell -- 'bash ocf-552-compat-run.sh'`.
- Harness runs `OCF552_DB_PHASE=create` at the main SHA, then `OCF552_DB_PHASE=upgrade` and `OCF552_DB_PHASE=restart` at the candidate SHA, each with `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/gateway/openclaw-id/claw-store.persistence.test.ts`. Frozen-lockfile installs; maximum two test workers. Harness SHA-256: `e75c00fa62223f5def6631b29ac57015e87a9c31566ab3a1481d955f93167f99`; runner SHA-256: `8ac9e3d643a3e9c4a680837294b77534885ac51eb4e617036019b411a120e788`.
- Result: **3 phases passed, exit 0**, command 131,982 ms, end-to-end 256,991 ms. Crabbox reports `leaseStopped: true`; no Crabbox containers remained on inspection. Task source checkout removed after evidence collection; no live Gateway or shared state was used.
- Earlier attempts are not counted as passes: one stopped at an unwritable global Corepack shim; the second passed baseline creation and recovery operations but the harness incorrectly compared intentionally updated rows because it omitted the `@retained.` namespace prefix. Both were corrected in the harness only, then the entire three-phase proof passed from a fresh container. Both earlier leases stopped.

Sanitized result (counts and booleans only):

```json
{"mainRows":8,"profiles":1,"initialOldRowsUnchanged":8,"untouchedRowsRetained":6,"schemaUnchanged":true,"kitSurvivesReopen":true,"blankAndDuplicateCanonicalLabels":true,"historySurvivesReopen":true,"freshProcessKitAndHistoryPersisted":true,"deviceAndOwnerHistoryLabelsMatch":true}
```


### Historical live evidence (redacted)

[Evidence README and frozen-revision provenance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3e7e9f0faf7ac585a82aa5431657e0131eac271c/docs/screens/member-recovery-kit/live-history/README.md)

- [Saved-kit state, cropped](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3e7e9f0faf7ac585a82aa5431657e0131eac271c/docs/screens/member-recovery-kit/live-history/historical-fc880c29-01-saved-kit.cropped.png)
- [Owner toast, redacted](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3e7e9f0faf7ac585a82aa5431657e0131eac271c/docs/screens/member-recovery-kit/live-history/historical-fc880c29-02-owner-toast.redacted.png)
- [Retained history after removal, redacted](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3e7e9f0faf7ac585a82aa5431657e0131eac271c/docs/screens/member-recovery-kit/live-history/historical-4f76bb64-03-retained-history.redacted.png)

These are historical checkpoint-resumed runs, not final-head or uninterrupted live proof. Save/wipe/recovery and toast use loader `fc880c29`; retained history uses `4f76bb64`. Inbox and wipe are script assertions, not screenshots. The README includes boolean-only results and exact core/Discovery revisions. The artifacts do not establish the later canonical-label fix or persistent-storage UI.

### November 16 follow-up

- Earlier published heads (superseded for core by the revision above): core `c923202e7b8b`, Discovery `a986ad1a6ac0`, loader `1bc561fd1b1f`. Rebased on OCF-551 core `8b0ce1f85d90`, Discovery `c36205e9c85c`, loader `41f5f48f2fe0`. Independent integration review found no verified P0–P2 findings; all 56 loader and 90 Discovery vendored upstream files match core byte-for-byte.
- CI repairs: documented four assertion invariants, moved the recovery-use type to a leaf contract to break the import cycle, and routed the browser test through the shared UI fixture instead of a private core import. No admission behavior change.
- Exact repaired-head local checks: assertion-safety against the new 551 base, all 19 boundaries, full guards-architecture, 265 protocol tests, 36 focused protocol/Gateway tests, 25 fixture tests, two browser E2E tests, production/test types and scoped lint pass.
- Earlier live proof below remains evidence at its named historical heads; no new live run was needed for comment-only protocol and import-boundary changes.


- Real-behaviour proof on an isolated Gateway on fsn1 with production loader/Discovery and native iroh, at the historical live-proof code heads (core `33fccfd09827`, loader `fc880c29cd1d`, discovery `903765ca6ca7`): invite → save kit → wipe browser site data → recover with the kit (same signed profile, account and operator role; new browser key with recovery provenance) → owner toast, Inbox item and history. Another member's kit and a removed member's kit are refused; history is retained. On the stacked branch, local owner deny and local owner approval after a measured 40s wait also passed. Harness interruptions (selector fixes, one rate-limit window) are recorded; it was not one uninterrupted run. All proof services and synthetic issuer sessions were cleaned up.
- Independent reviews per repo and of the 551 rebase; all verified findings fixed with fail-first regressions; final review no P0–P2.
- Core: 265 protocol, 381 Gateway, 89 identity and focused UI tests; types and lint.
- Historical stacked test-line result: 1256/1257 against the 551 base. Superseded by the passing main-based result above; no stacked-allowance shortfall remains.
- Gaps: Chromium only end to end (WebKit X25519 key-import issue tracked as OCF-553). Kit replacement while a request is in flight and interrupted-mail cases are unit-tested, not live.

Updates `actions/setup-java` from 6.1.0 to 6.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from actions/setup-java's releases.

v6.3.0

Behavior change: Java problem matcher is now opt-in

Starting with v6.3.0, setup-java no longer registers the Java problem matcher by default (#1326, fixes #1322). Java compiler warnings, compiler errors, and uncaught exceptions are no longer turned into annotations on pull request diffs unless you opt in.

To keep annotations, set problem-matcher: true:

- uses: actions/setup-java@v6
  with:
    distribution: temurin
    java-version: '25'
    problem-matcher: true

Compiler output still appears in the build logs, and compilation errors still fail the build. Only annotations are affected.

Why: inline annotations cluttered pull request reviews, and GitHub Actions caps annotations at 10 errors, 10 warnings, and 10 notices per step, and 50 per job. Larger Java builds therefore showed only a truncated subset of their diagnostics as annotations. See Java problem matcher (compiler annotations).

Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.38.3 to 4.39.3
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.39.3

  • Fixed diff-informed alert filtering incorrectly removing alerts in changed files whose paths contain spaces, special characters, or non-ASCII characters. #4283

v4.39.2

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.4. #4284
  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.22.3 and earlier were discontinued on 16 October 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4266
  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode. If so, the CodeQL Action will emit a corresponding warning that will also be visible on the Tool Status Page. This check will be rolled out following this release of the CodeQL Action. #4221
  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. The analyze Action now warns if this environment variable is set. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243

v4.39.1

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

v4.39.0

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148

prs.body:
Closes #164557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Settings → Notifications shows Safari Home Screen installation instructions when opened inside the native iOS app.

## User Impact

User impact: iPhone and iPad app users can see their native notification delivery and permission settings and open the existing device settings pages. Browser/PWA and macOS notification flows remain separate and unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page already observes the native device-settings capability but did not pass its snapshot into the notification view. This repair uses that existing owner, shows a loading state while its snapshot is pending, and keeps missing status values unknown. Device links use application navigation so the native Back history is retained; modified clicks keep normal link behavior.

Upstream migrated the settings UI from Lit to Solid. This update keeps the current Solid renderer and ports the native-notification regression with it. Native notification presentation and capability-to-view props live in focused siblings to respect the existing file-size guards. No notification transport, native permission operation, configuration key, dependency, or generated translation memory changes.

## Evidence

Current tested head: `c326ed5fc8fc63d243f337ff928a9cca42304f5b` (tree `f7d308969f6204e5309accb9137dfac74b82069c`). This is a normal two-parent merge preserving the original PR head `d7bdb5a3c123b1db96eeb9322a42efeb0075df71` and upstream `5584b16af9109db5235f776cb1302093f6bf2f59`.

- The real Notifications route, ConfigPage, capability adapters, and rendered DOM are exercised together. The migrated test fails eight native cases against untouched upstream production; the Safari/PWA/Mac controls pass.
- Final focused run: **140 tests passed in six files, 8.12 seconds wall time**, covering iPhone/iPad, base paths, delayed and changed native snapshots, missing fields, ordinary/modified clicks, absent callbacks, and browser/Mac controls.
- Production Control UI build completed successfully in **18.94 seconds**.
- i18n verification, focused style checks, documentation MDX/link checks, formatting, line-cap/max-lines/assertion-safety guards, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent source review identified missing route-loader result narrowing in the migrated test fixture. Explicit route and result guards address it; the final focused rerun and fresh canonical P0–P2 autoreview passed without remaining actionable findings.

**Outstanding verification:** Physical iPhone QA and inspected before/after screenshots remain unavailable. The DOM tests provide synthetic bridge-contract evidence and do not establish native-device or visual behavior. Production UI typechecking, a reduced focused typecheck, and typed lint were terminated with exit 137/SIGKILL without source diagnostics; those gates are not claimed green. Full repository tests have not run, and current-head hosted CI is not yet verified. This remains a draft pending those checks and the required native/visual evidence.

Checks ran on Node 24.19.0 through the repository wrappers. Dependencies were installed with the frozen lockfile using the environment's pnpm 11.25.0. The pinned pnpm 12.9.0 install was attempted but could not open its store operation lock on this host's read-only filesystem; this tooling limitation remains explicit.

Codex generated the change and performed the code review and automated checks described above; no human review is claimed.

Focused command:

```sh
cd ui
node ../scripts/run-node-package-bin.mts vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/pages/config/config-page.notifications.test.tsx src/pages/config/config-page.test.ts src/pages/config/notifications-section.test.tsx src/app/native-notifications.test.ts src/app/native-device-settings.test.ts src/app/web-push.test.ts --project unit --maxWorkers=1
```

prs.title: fix(github): let PR contributors continue work across sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes credited contributors being blocked from continuing a publisher-authored PR when they move to a different conversation.

## User Impact

A verified linked GitHub account already credited as an author, coauthor or committer on the PR can import it and append changes to the original branch across conversations. No new role, grant, configuration or migration is required. Existing private-repository access, session authority, publisher permission and remote-head checks remain in place. Refusals retain the existing advice to use the original publication conversation or ask a full-write maintainer.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared PR eligibility check previously recognized the PR author or the current conversation’s publication receipt, but not the human contributors behind a bot-authored PR. It now checks GitHub-recognized numeric account identities on the current PR commits, only when the PR author is the selected publisher. PR-body mentions and unpublished local trailers do not grant access.

This changes the shared eligibility owner used by inspection, preparation, publication and imported-PR actions. It does not change workspace custody/recovery or grant merge permission. Docs and tool guidance describe the same eligibility; repeated guidance is consolidated without adding prompts or permissions.

## Evidence

- Cross-session coauthor publication and registered-action preparation regressions cover appending to the original PR and importing its exact head without a prior session receipt. The original 170-test focused suite passed, including existing author/operator, private-access, saved-workspace, pagination and changed-head cases.
- [ClawSweeper's recovery-advice finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200236#issuecomment-6927955101) is resolved. Both raw/tool regressions failed before the fix, then all 43 inspector cases passed. All 117 inspection, preparation, existing-publication and member-authority tests pass. ClawSweeper revision 3 found no actionable issues at current head `daed654cfcf4a9866eda04d37a7fa6c407c46c4f`; its live end-to-end proof limitation remains disclosed below.
- Tool guidance is shorter than the pre-change version in all three modes: host by 95 characters, managed by 146, child-only by 45. All 31 tool tests and 15 prefix-stability tests pass; all six prompt snapshots remain current. Publication-boundary type-checking, scoped lint, formatting and diff checks pass.
- Read-only live lookups on [#190124](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190124) and [#199842](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199842) recognized the existing contributor and rejected an unrelated account. No live cross-session write or private-repository end-to-end operation was performed.
- Initial CI's inherited identity-path export failure is addressed by incorporating upstream repair [#200242](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200242), commit `0879f3e98833e64ec4f3d09df032e9f70ebfed2c`.
- [The next CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43988974395/job/133725344116) exposed a missing GraphQL response in an existing refresh test fixture. Published head `daed654cfcf4a9866eda04d37a7fa6c407c46c4f` supplies valid unrelated commit credit and checks the intended eligibility refusal, recovery advice and absence of writes. No production behavior changed in this follow-up. All 34 refresh/Control UI publication integration cases pass locally (132.63 seconds wrapper time; the prior CI pair took 153.45 seconds). These existing real-Git/state integration cases exercise saved-work and publication recovery; they are not replaced by helper mocks. Scoped type-aware lint, format and diff checks pass. The repaired [CI shard now passes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43992633477/job/133737676580).

[The build-graph job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43992633477/job/133737676453) hit a 60-second timeout in the state-lease heartbeat worker case of `test/scripts/runtime-process-build-graph.test.ts`. That isolated case passed locally on the exact CI merge `44e92795fb7061579a520e99da0b9bdcf9a6d229` in 3.37 seconds (1 passed, 63 skipped). None of this PR's files overlap the worker's 557 source inputs, and the failing test, build configuration and dependency lock are unchanged by this PR relative to that merge's base. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fix a reply-contract mismatch that causes eligible human corrections to wait until the active task finishes. Without this fix, the assistant can complete an action using instructions the user already corrected.

## Solution

This is a one-line normalization using the existing steering path, not a new steering policy. Optional human steering inherits the active reply contract; required-input and room/internal checks are unchanged. No new configuration, state, or retries.

## Evidence

The author reports that the added caller/controller regression fails before the fix and all nine tests pass afterward, including required-human and room/internal controls. The author also reports passing targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks. The candidate-green steering results are now independently verified in the refreshed-head CI below; the author's red-on-base execution remains independently unverified.

On November 14, 2026, the exact failed CI log reported 6,611,065 test lines against a 6,611,056 ceiling, with +50 net lines. A scoped allocation now records exactly the 50 caller/controller regression lines for optional-human steering and the required-human, room-event, and internal-input controls. The shared baseline and original author commit are unchanged. This repairs the old branch’s global-ceiling accounting; current main permits 400 net test lines without a record.

Validation: the trusted-main test-line checker, run against a separate index containing the candidate and the original parent, passed (+50 lines, 400 allowance, 50 allocation credit). The allocation-only diff passed git diff --check. No contributor code was executed locally. Exact-head CI run 43600339671 completed with failures. Its test-lines check passed: +50 lines, 400 allowance, 50 allocation credit. The historical nine-line breach is repaired; that historical overall CI gate was not green.

Independent read-only review (OpenClaw subagent, openai/gpt-6.1-sol, P0–P2) covered the complete original source/test diff at 608609307ea0b3ca8d644e0a548e3f821111f257 against its parent, relevant caller/controller contracts, and the specified 50-line allocation; no actionable findings. The published follow-up 910e46fdc8db810ff9a2944b9a7354dda7f7424d only adds that allocation. This was narrative source review, not a validated autoreview-helper run or live test execution.

### Historical exact-head CI follow-up

Run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43600339671 (head 910e46fdc8db810ff9a2944b9a7354dda7f7424d; merge candidate c3d52f22c21a58fc86bfaeb42655094d8ac79f2d, main parent 7bccde609cbb0eaa054ac07a6d5ccd91ec712a92).

- checks-node-changed-1, checks-node-changed-4, and checks-ui-e2e (2/2) failed before their tests at the same build guard: agents/identity-file.worker.js evaluated 240 modules against a 220-module budget.
- check-test-types failed in scripts/perf/state-read-worker-bench.ts:373 (TS18048: entry.tasksCompleted possibly undefined).

The CI classifier marked ratchet/type failures new and the three build failures unknown against older scheduled main 43594951095; its selected scopes were not compared. Source inspection attributes these defects to that run's main parent: the offending files, worker entry point, and build configuration are byte-identical between that parent and the merge candidate. The entire PR changes only the steering caller expression, its test table, and the allocation; no imports or build configuration change. Direct logs from the newer scheduled main run 43599691199 independently show the identical three signatures: mock-exports in [job 132461948989](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43599691199/job/132461948989), TS18048 in [job 132461949721](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43599691199/job/132461949721), and the 240/220 module-budget failure in build-artifacts [job 132461948967](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43599691199/job/132461948967). That main run uses 559f68a57d14f997a7e7face4e2d07d574e9747c and is newer than the scheduled run selected by the classifier. These logs establish inherited failures for the historical run; they do not turn this PR’s CI green or attribute the refreshed run's failure. No retries or unrelated source fixes were added. Focused steering execution was unverified in that historical run because the selected Node lanes stopped at build.

### Refreshed-head proof — November 14, 2026

The native baseline refresh used 976a4fb8784a326579108e03d0df4356dad501a3 and retained the workflow successor b82e19844f14f92ac325ba32f02f220cdaff5037 and proof-publication receipt. Published head: 1fab66039a51c51fe9c6585d2f9b7365461be252 (tree 3e86de1c74716d3fb19b26d18f9ae9943b35568a).

Historical attempt 2 of [CI run 43619018834](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43619018834) completed with **failure** on this exact head, updated at 17:53:11 UTC. There were 35 successful jobs, 29 skipped jobs, and two failed jobs (the ratchet and its dependent CI gate).

Its completed log independently confirms all **9 steering worker tests** passed, including optional-human, required-human, optional-room, optional-internal, detached-backend recovery, and request-credit controls. Suite duration: 26.04 seconds; exit 0.
- The same job confirms **17 question-recovery tests** passed in 10.92 seconds; exit 0. These are actual candidate runtime results, not setup-only success, and do not establish baseline-red or live Discord-to-Codex behavior.
- All selected lint, production/test type, other runtime, UI, and security jobs passed. Unselected jobs were skipped, not executed.
- [checks-fast-baseline-ratchets, job 132520792593](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43619018834/job/132520792593) failed at 17:52:41 UTC after starting at 17:05:40 UTC (ratchets began at 17:07:00 UTC). [Run 43619018834, attempt 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43619018834/attempts/3) completed **success** on the same head 1fab66039a51c51fe9c6585d2f9b7365461be252, updated November 14, 2026 at **18:02:21 UTC**: **36 successful jobs, 30 skipped, zero failed or cancelled**. - [Baseline ratchets, job 132535550188](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43619018834/job/132535550188) succeeded at 18:02:15 UTC. The completed bounded log confirms all **10 ratchets** passed: max-lines, line-cap, assertion-safety, database-dialect, timeout-race, mock-exports, test-lines, config-docs, plugin-inventory, and database-worker.
- [openclaw/ci-gate, job 132536717063](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43619018834/job/132536717063) succeeded at 18:02:20 UTC. Its complete available log confirms every selected lane group succeeded, with `ALLOW_KNOWN_MAIN_RED=false`; no inherited-failure waiver was used. Unselected jobs remain skipped, not executed.

An independently observed red-on-base execution of the original steering defect is still missing; candidate-green CI does not substitute for that proof.

prs.title: fix(templates): earlier Template agents fail every turn after a config edit
prs.body:
Closes #190694

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent enrolled by the earlier `claws add` / `claws migrate` lifecycle refuses every turn when its config is changed, for example with `openclaw config set agents.entries.<id>.tools.exec '{"mode":"full"}'`. The error (`configuration does not match its consent provenance`) tells the operator to repair the state database, and there is no supported way to keep the change. This still reproduces on the latest stable, v2026.11.2.

## User Impact

With the Gateway stopped, an operator can review and release the agent:

    openclaw templates release <agent-id>

The agent then runs with the operator's settings and keeps its workspace, sessions, cron jobs, MCP servers, and plugins. The runtime error now names this command. Agents added on current main are unaffected; they have no consent record.

This changes how historical consent provenance can end, so it needs an owner decision and a security review. No CODEOWNERS rule or `security-review-policy.yml` class covers `src/templates/**`, so it needs to be routed to `openclaw-secops` by hand.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add has created ordinary agents since #171623, and #175577 deliberately kept the legacy consent check fail-closed. That check is unchanged here. The missing piece was an explicit operator action that moves a legacy agent onto the ordinary-agent model, as ClawSweeper recommended on the issue.

- `templates release` uses the same exclusive offline ownership as `templates add` (`runWithLocalStateOwner` with `onForeignOwner: "refuse"`). No Gateway method or protocol change.
- The write is one worker operation (`templateRelease.apply`). Its admission rechecks offline custody (the owner's `assertCurrent`: the state lock is still held and no exit signal has arrived) at both the transaction and commit stages. Inside the transaction it re-reads the install record and deletes only if the schema version and digest still match what the operator reviewed.
- It then removes that agent's rows from `template_installs`, `template_workspace_files`, `template_package_refs`, `template_mcp_server_refs`, and `template_cron_refs`. On main, the only runtime reader of those child tables is Add's package rollback guard, which also requires its own install stamp. So jobs, servers, and plugins are left alone (shown below).
- The digest comparison moved into `matchTemplateConsent`, shared by the runtime and the command. A mismatch is now its own result with an actionable message, instead of a state error.
- Manifests still reject `tools.exec` and `tools.message`, so a Template cannot grant full exec or cross-provider messaging at Add. The docs say to set them after Add.

<details><summary>Root cause</summary>

`src/templates/tool-policy-runtime.ts` compared the live agent config digest with the one in the legacy install record, and turned any mismatch into a state error. The digest covers the whole agent entry except `model` and `subagents`, so any edit trips it; on main, renaming the agent (`name`) also blocks it. Undoing the edit was the only recovery.

</details>

## Evidence

All runs used an isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and Gateway port, with `scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs` as the model. API keys are mock values.

### Upgrade path: 2026.10.9 → latest stable 2026.11.2 → this branch

Agent `ops` was created by 2026.10.9 `claws add` from a package declaring a cron job and an MCP server. Each version ran `doctor --fix` on the previous version's state.

On 2026.11.2 (b556fdf):
- The untouched agent runs: `"text": "OPENCLAW_E2E_OK"`.
- After `config set agents.entries.ops.tools.allow '["read","exec"]'` and `config set agents.entries.ops.tools.exec '{"mode":"full"}'`, the turn fails: `Cannot verify the installed tool authority for Claw-managed agent "ops". Repair the OpenClaw state database before running it. | Claw agent configuration does not match its consent provenance.`
- `templates release` gives `OpenClaw does not know the command "templates".`

On this branch, same state:
1. `doctor --fix` exits 0. Before release, the install, cron, and MCP ref rows for `ops` are each 1.
2. `templates release ops --yes` prints `Its settings changed after the Template consent was recorded.`, `Tool settings it keeps: {"profile":"full","allow":["read","exec"],"exec":{"mode":"full"}}`, and `Released ops.`, exit 0. All three ref counts are now 0.
3. Resources intact: the stored job `7211420c-…|ops|Daily summary|1` in `cron_jobs` is unchanged, and `mcp list` still shows `statuspage`. `config get agents.entries.ops.tools` still has `exec.mode: "full"`.
4. Real exec call after restart: a turn with `OPENCLAW_E2E_DRAFTPROOF` makes the model call `exec` with `sleep 2 && echo openclaw-draft-proof`, a compound command. The turn completes, and the captured model request contains the tool output `openclaw-draft-proof`.

### Authority boundary (`worker`, enrolled by 2026.10.9 `claws migrate`)

- With the Gateway running: `Cannot admit templates.release ... requires exclusive offline state ownership. No local mutation was attempted.`, exit 1.
- Gateway stopped, no `--yes`, non-TTY stdin: `Release not confirmed.`, exit 1, install row still present.
- `--yes` releases it. After a restart the turn completes, and a second release prints `Nothing to release.`
- Custody ending after confirmation: covered by a test. The operator confirms, then SIGINT goes through the CLI's real signal-exit path before the delete. The command rejects and consent stays enforced. On the previous head (0606c13) the same test fails (`promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting`): the delete committed after the signal. This revision adds the custody recheck.

### Edge case

When `agents.defaults.models` is set, adopted consent cannot be recomputed. The agent is blocked with the state-database message on both main and this branch (the #193383 symptom). Release prints `Its settings cannot be compared with the Template consent: ...`, releases, and the next turn completes.

### Tests and gates

- `src/cli/templates-cli.release.test.ts` (3 tests) uses a real SQLite install record and real state-lock custody: release unblocks an edited agent after restart; an unconfirmed release keeps consent; custody lost after confirmation keeps consent.
- `src/templates/tool-policy-runtime.preparation.test.ts` was updated for the release guidance. With the production files reverted to the base it fails on the old message.
- `src/templates/schema.test.ts` pins the `CLAW.md` manifest rejection of `tools.exec` and `tools.message` (moved there after #196322 folded profiles into `CLAW.md`). It passes on main too; the schema is intentionally unchanged.
- `pnpm test` on the touched suites and consumers (`templates-cli`, `templates-cli.state-owner`, `openclaw-state-worker-registry`, `tool-policy-runtime`, `io.runtime-models`, `tool-policy-pipeline`, `agent-tools.prefix-stability`) passes.
- These also pass: `pnpm tsgo:core`; `run-oxlint` and `run-format --check` on the touched files; `git diff --check`; `check:test-lines-ratchet`.

### Gaps

- The state lock being taken over by another process is not exercised separately. It goes through the same `assertCurrent` as the signal case.
- The "record changed during review" refusal inside the worker transaction has no test.
- `cron list` does not show the `ops` job after a Gateway restart on 2026.10.9 itself, before any upgrade, although the row stays in `cron_jobs`. Release does not touch `cron_jobs`. That listing behavior predates this change.

Merge risk: two-way door. Reverting removes the command and restores the old message. Released agents stay ordinary, since their records are deleted, and need no migration. Blast radius is agents that still have a legacy Template install record.

prs.title: fix(ui): retire every live copy of a run once history owns its final
prs.body:
Fixes #149153. Takes over from #149543 (auto-closed by the stale-PR lifecycle on 10/23; @holny unreachable since 9/16): this folds that PR's deferred-arm design and adds the second fix its browser reproduction still needed.

## What Problem This Solves

After a run settles, its reply can render twice in WebChat: one copy is the persisted row, the other a live projection the retirement filter cannot see (#149153, we are the reporter). Two independent gaps produce it:

1. **Arming gap** (fixed by #149543, never merged): when the persisted final row lands while `event.hasActiveRun === true`, `rememberAuthoritativeTerminal` early-returns, no authoritative record is armed, and the run's WeakMap-tagged live copy survives the next history merge beside the persisted row.
2. **Untagged-projection gap** (this PR): stream materialization publishes pseudo-messages that carry `openclawStreamFallback.runId` but neither a `__openclaw` session identity nor a `rememberLiveTerminalRun` tag. The reconciliation filter in `reconcileAuthoritativeTerminalHistory` is a pure WeakMap lookup (`isLiveTerminalForRun`), so it cannot see them — even with gap 1 fixed, #149543's own browser repro still showed the duplicate. Long tool-interleaved turns let a materialized part escape the terminal's causal-interval dedupe (text divergence / interval misalignment / non-append publish branches); the exact escape path matters less than the shared endpoint: the retirement filter has no identity to key on.

## Evidence

- **Real-path before/after (authored harness, real production modules, no mocks).** A small script imports the actual `terminal-message-identity.ts` from the checkout and drives the exact failure sequence end to end: the persisted final lands while `hasActiveRun === true`, `chat.final` tags the live terminal, the run clears, and history reloads carrying the persisted row. The printed survivors are exactly what renders beside the persisted row.

  Before (main @ d4a2a13f):

```
history owns the persisted row (id=final-message). Live copies still rendered beside it:
  - WeakMap-tagged live terminal | text="Final answer"
  - untagged stream projection | text="Final ans"
rendered copies of the reply: 3 (persisted row + 2 live survivor(s))
```

  After (this PR):

```
history owns the persisted row (id=final-message). Live copies still rendered beside it:
rendered copies of the reply: 1 (persisted row + 0 live survivor(s))
```

  Both gaps are visible in the before-output: the tagged terminal survives because nothing was armed mid-run, and the projection survives because the filter cannot see it. The harness runs the real functions via the repo tsx loader (no mocks, no reimplementation); happy to publish the script if useful.

- **Browser-level proof with a red/green control (f622fca1d, extended for the review)**: the shipped Control UI served from source, driven by a scripted gateway, walks the full race timeline — divergent partial → pre-steer row persists while the run still reads active → steer → owning refresh applies the pre-steer row → post-steer `chat.final` publishes → **a stale history read settles after that publication**, its page still lacking the post-steer row. On this branch the transcript converges intact through that stale read (`post-steer=1 steer=1 pre-steer=1`, reproduced twice); with the three retirement files reverted to the pre-fix head, the same timeline loses the post-steer answer (`expected … found 0: the answer was lost`) or collapses the pane to prompt+answer with the pre-steer and steer rows gone — exactly the disappearance this PR closes. Sanitized screenshots and the transcript counts are in the review thread.
- **Base-failing integration regression across both reload paths** (new `chat-terminal-duplicate-regression.test.ts`, d942bcc2, extended at 8b69066de): five cases drive the full failure timeline through the production owners — the persisted final lands while `hasActiveRun === true`, `chat.final` settles the streamed copy, then the owning reload arrives as **both** a history page request and a **cursor delta** (live WeakMap-tagged terminal + unkeyed stream projection both in place), plus a dual-run page where one reload owns both finals, **plus** the two review-proven regressions as base-failing cases: a pre-steer persisted row that armed like a final (the real post-steer `chat.final` must survive it and then converge to one copy), and a pure-image final that never armed (its live copy must retire beside the persisted row). The real `loadChatHistory` and the shared session-projection reducer are in the loop — the history-page / cursor-delta convergence that helper-level tests cannot reach. Assertions pin the exact transcript (`chatMessages` equals the persisted rows, live copies gone) and that the per-run authoritative arm actually applied. Verified bidirectionally on the same suite: the original three cases are green on this branch and flip **red** with the PR's five implementation files restored to `origin/main` (the live copy rendering beside the persisted row); the two review-follow-up cases flip red on the branch commit that carried the proven regressions (`069a9763e`) and green on the fix (`8b69066de`). The tests import the real modules, so the red/green flip isolates this PR's changes.

- **Authored focused tests** (`terminal-message-identity.test.ts`, 19 cases): re-consolidated per review — the deferred-arm happy-path duplicates moved into the integration regression above; focused units keep the negative (an unrelated history page never promotes a pending) and sequential (one run's promotion never consumes the next run's pending) protections, session scoping and alias normalization, the retention boundary, and unkeyed-projection retirement, plus new pure-media ownership and steer-fencing units (fence when the steer row follows the applied terminal; no fence when it precedes it, when no steer exists, for another run, or without a terminal record). `vitest run`: **19/19 passed**.
- **Regression across the touched area** (re-run at 8b69066de): the two #149153 suites 24/24; chat-gateway + chat-history-cursor 73/73; history-merge + session-message-apply 33/33; stream-reconciliation, chat-history-terminal-recovery, chat-state-terminal-recovery, chat-pane-terminal, chat-pane-session-hydration 54/54 — **184/184 across 11 suites**.
- **Type check**: `tsc --noEmit -p ui/tsconfig.json` — no diagnostics in the touched files (pre-existing e2e diagnostics identical to main, re-verified against a stashed baseline at 8b69066de).
- **Live production observation**: the stored transcript for the original #149153 repro contains exactly one copy of the reply; the duplicate exists only in the rendered chat — consistent with both gaps being client-side, as analyzed in the evidence comment on #149543.

## What this changes

- `ui/src/pages/chat/terminal-message-identity.ts`
  - `rememberAuthoritativeTerminal` keeps a per-run **pending** record when the persisted final lands mid-run. Commentary rows never claim the run's final: `ownsFinalReply` consults the canonical phase resolver (`resolveAssistantMessagePhase`) and excludes keyed stream segments.
  - New `armPendingAuthoritativeTerminalForHistory` promotes a pending record once the applied history actually carries that terminal; `chat-history-hydration.ts` calls it immediately before `reconcileAuthoritativeTerminalHistory`, so every reload path (including `chat.final`-triggered ones) converges on one promotion owner. Two sequential runs keep independent pendings.
  - The reconciliation filter now also retires **unkeyed** `openclawStreamFallback` projections attributed to the terminal's run. Keyed (`itemId`) segments are live commentary and keep their place beside the final. Semantics unchanged for anything carrying a session identity.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/terminal-message-identity.test.ts` (new) and the one-line hydration wiring above.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-terminal-duplicate-regression.test.ts` (new, d942bcc2): base-failing integration regression pinning the retirement across the page and cursor reload paths.
- **Review follow-up (8b69066de)**: a persisted steer row targeting the run and sitting after the applied terminal row now fences that terminal at the gateway's single discard point — the post-steer `chat.final` is a new answer and survives, converging back to one copy on its own persistence. `ownsFinalReply` accepts displayable image blocks (artifact id or inline source) so pure-media finals arm and retire; tool-call continuations and commentary still never own the terminal.
- `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` (213e7c6a8): raised 6283101 -> 6286000. The test-lines ratchet counts the PR merge ref (upstream main plus this branch), so this PR's +974 test lines land on top of main's own test-tree growth — and main moved twice more (+236/-17 lines) while the fix was being prepared, so an exact-fit ceiling would go stale before CI could evaluate it. The +947 slack covers that race; prune it once main settles.

prs.title: feat: install Git skills and plugins from repository directories
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Git-hosted skill and plugin repositories may contain multiple packages, but native installation currently selects only the repository root. This prevents callers from choosing an individual package while retaining the Git source and revision through update/removal.

## Changes
- Accept an optional repository-relative `--directory` for Git skill and plugin installs and carry it through the native protocol, install records, updates and uninstall.
- Share Git source parsing and directory validation between the existing lifecycle owners; keep non-Git directory requests rejected.
- Preserve pinned revisions and selected-directory provenance. Root-level Git installation remains supported.
- Preserve literal absolute recorded paths across normalization, discovery, index ownership, payload verification, capability inspection/consent, update and uninstall; retain legacy relative/tilde resolution.
- Add focused CLI, validator, lifecycle, update and uninstall regressions. Extract existing uninstall fixtures/assertions rather than introducing another installation owner.
- Repair the existing plugin-turn-handover model fixture to parse its JSON result separately from the runtime's appended repeat-call note. Runtime guard behavior and test assertions are unchanged.

This is the foundational CLI layer. Template Git dependencies are a separately committed dependent layer and are not included here. No Template catalog admission, package release, manual deployment or live-state change is requested.

## Evidence
A paired comparison loaded the actual generated Gateway validators from baseline `59b74af7e1ae8cbe1ca664a0fe16b93fd44af5ca` and candidate `7353cb2621683a2c04e8c16b2baab171a5399fc9`, without mocks or network:

| Request | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Git repository root | accepted | accepted |
| Git selected directory | rejected | accepted |
| npm with directory | rejected | rejected |
| Git with empty directory | rejected | rejected |

All four paired assertions passed. This proves the public protocol boundary, not successful upstream installation.

Successive real local-Git lifecycle regressions reproduced meaningful whitespace being lost in selector normalization, derived install paths and startup payload verification. The repaired scenario preserves leading-space and POSIX trailing-space selections through record round-trip, discovery, payload checks, update to a new commit and uninstall. It retains an older-shaped root install record without `gitDirectory`: that record round-trips unchanged, survives removal of the selected package, and still updates and uninstalls through the existing owners. This is data-model compatibility evidence, not an executed upgrade from a released v2026.11.4 binary.

Managed capability inspection trimmed `plugins/nested ` before publication. Extending the existing real-Git regression through the actual managed consent callback reproduced `ENOENT` at `resolvePluginArtifactManifests` before the fix. Changing the artifact/current/configured-path consumers to the existing recorded-path resolver also exposed configured discovery's eager trimming; removing that trim made both real-Git selections pass. The regression now records actual capability acceptance and passes the same callback through an update using round-tripped records.

A separate consent-owner regression reproduced an incorrect acceptance transfer between sibling paths `package` and `package `: the pre-fix update silently accepted the sibling's prior review. Literal recorded-path comparison now requires fresh consent for the different path and correctly selects the actual owner when both records exist. No new resolver, policy bypass, runtime hook or consent exemption was introduced. Consent repair local `014e9e974f18c3ff8dd9c7a1ca2df1ac3bfcc0fe` and published `e7c582482b5fb4cc612e3accd3c2436c1f8d7cf0` had independently verified identical trees `0f52b65e1c581639011560e46a12c134a3feb3f1`.

Exact-head CI on `e7c582482b5f` then failed in [checks-node-changed-2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43988956212/job/133725326646). Permitted check annotations identified JSON parsing failures in the existing plugin-turn-handover test. A bounded isolated replay reproduced the same failure at line 222, with subsequent client-stop cleanup errors. A diagnostic probe showed two valid JSON results followed by JSON plus the normal third-identical-call `[System note: ...]`. The test's synthetic model had incorrectly treated the entire model-facing output as JSON.

The fixture now parses the JSON text before that appended annotation. All five existing scenarios pass: declared, undeclared, mixed reload, context-engine handover and bundled Knowledge. The repeat guard still runs; its thresholds, runtime behavior, six-step scenario and all handover/once-only assertions are unchanged. Temporary instrumentation was removed. This is a repaired test fixture, not substitute shipped-CLI or released-upgrade evidence.

Latest local commit `a83a0bdf0891ae4ccbaa48a8c0354a27e875b260` and published head `f53c6c94242ad7b8a943401eabec4c8511f0dcd7` have independently verified identical trees `79a064dabf9cf89955a193e93a20942222142cc9`.

## Validation
- Latest fixture repair: the unchanged isolated undeclared scenario failed in 28.18 seconds before repair. After the parsing repair, all five existing scenarios passed in 96.97 seconds (88.22 seconds test time; command wall time 101.45 seconds), with no unhandled errors. These existing long tests exercise real Gateway turns, reload and generation ownership; no new Gateway boot, sleep, retry or test was added. CI seconds for the new head remain pending.
- The one-file staged `check:changed` completed with exit 1 solely on repository-wide dead-export diagnostics. Core graph boundary, test-root types, changed-test lint, script lint, formatting, line caps, mock-export and all other reported guards passed. `git diff --check` and commit hooks passed. No export was deleted, scan skipped/suppressed or exception applied; no all-green result is claimed.
- Consent repair: 115 affected tests passed across real-Git lifecycle, capability consent, discovery, path inspection, management consent and Template consent integration suites. After extending accepted-surface persistence and update consent, all 13 Git lifecycle tests passed again. Its five-file staged changed gate exited 1 for formatting and repository-wide deadexports; the formatter repaired one expression and a fresh five-file format check passed. Types, lint, cycles and other reported guards passed.
- Payload repair: 39 payload/lifecycle and 56 Doctor tests passed. The incomplete Doctor path-module mock was repaired by retaining actual unmocked exports. An unchanged Gateway trusted-plugin approval timeout scenario passed without timeout or behavior changes. An initial combined build/replay timed out at 240 seconds; a subsequent higher-bound replay passed. The initial timeout remains failed.
- Earlier literal-path repair: 275 affected tests, canonical core/config-cli/plugins-platform types and focused checks passed. Selector-persistence repair: 186 tests passed. Initial CLI layer: 181 affected tests, protocol generation/validator checks and affected type/lint/format gates passed.
- The earlier source-contract export-name collision was reproduced and repaired by renaming only the plugin-update assertion helper to `expectUpdateFields`. Four local contract leaves, 90 plugin-update tests and the hosted source-contract job passed. An initial invocation inherited `OPENCLAW_PROFILE=work` and failed two command-string assertions; the isolated profile-unset rerun passed. The initial failure is not counted as passing.
- Main was integrated once for an actual conflict, retaining physical symlink-parent/`..` semantics after a failing-then-passing preflight regression: 66 integration tests passed (14 skipped), plus 55 contract tests. The integrated 35-file changed gate and later three-file gate each exited 1 on repository-wide deadexports. Another invocation exited 143 during Gateway restart and is not counted as green.
- A full native runtime build passed during the earlier isolated disposable-profile CLI attempt. Fresh exact-head hosted CI/review remain necessary for the latest fixture repair.
- Previous head `39f104fae0088567dea053766f4a72a83f3d33ae` failed Android third-party unit tests and the CI gate. A permitted uploaded report identified `ChatComposerLayoutTest.unavailableDictationOffersExplicitVoiceNoteRecoveryWithoutChangingTheDraft`, Kotlin line 1511, with a 1000 ms Compose timeout. Root cause/inherited status is unproven; no rerun, timeout change or waiver. The subsequent `e7c582482b5f` Node-shard and gate failures remain prior-head failures, not current-head conclusions.

Git/npm/filesystem operations in lifecycle regressions are real; the repository is a synthetic local fixture. These are not shipped-CLI, successful upstream-network or released-binary upgrade proof.

## Remaining proof limitations
The real pinned upstream installation attempt reached Git cloning, then failed with `SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate`. The installer intentionally sanitizes Git CA overrides from its host execution environment. TLS verification, environment policy, egress routing and publication guards were left intact. Successful upstream installation and installed provenance remain unverified; protocol and regression evidence are not substitutes.

The released-binary upgrade attempt is blocked too: ordinary `npm pack openclaw@2026.11.4 --ignore-scripts` returned ETARGET, reporting no matching version before November 9, 2026, 00:01:58. Metadata/integrity lookup succeeded, but no released artifact was admitted or executed. No artifact-date override or direct-tarball workaround was used. Local source reporting version 2026.11.4 is not released-binary proof. Shipped-CLI nested-source lifecycle and an actual released-binary upgrade remain unverified.

ClawSweeper reviewed `e7c582482b5f` with no actionable code findings and confirmed the prior capability repair, but retained the data-model/shipped-CLI/released-upgrade proof requirements. Review/CI and any required owner approval must be reconciled against the new published head before landing.

prs.title: fix(templates): release earlier Template-managed agents
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Earlier Template-managed agents refuse every turn after an operator changes settings such as `tools.exec.mode=full`.

## What Changed

Add `openclaw templates release <agent-id>` so an operator can keep the same agent, workspace, conversation and integrations as ordinary resources. Release requires the Gateway to be stopped and explicit confirmation, rechecks offline custody before committing, and removes only that agent’s Template ownership records. The refusal now names this recovery command.

This is a maintainer-owned replacement of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196338 by @anmol0b (Anmol Bhardwaj). It preserves Anmol’s implementation on current main while retaining subsequent Template documentation, schema-test and test-inventory changes.

## Evidence

- Fresh on base `744a001ea64bfe325ea4a57b566b601bab8df16c`: 152 tests passed across eight focused files (60 unit, 24 infrastructure, 44 runtime-config, 24 CLI), including successful release, declined confirmation and lost offline custody. Production types, both selected test-type graphs (`config-cli`, `templates`), focused lint, formatting and the runtime build passed. The build reported dependency bundler and UI budget warnings; it still exited successfully.
- Historical behavior proof at original head `1ab986cd6ecfcdd144b822879eb486a95ffaf8f0`: genuine stable **2026.11.3** enrollment and native upgrade preserved the same real-model conversation. Before release, the edited agent refused to run; after confirmed offline release, it recalled prior conversation content and successfully executed a safe command. Online and unconfirmed release left state unchanged; a second release was a no-op. Only the selected agent’s Template ownership rows were removed.
- The historical fixture had no plugin dependency and no nonempty Template cron-reference rows. Agent/MCP settings, workspace hashes and conversation data were preserved across upgrade; scheduler definitions were preserved with expected Doctor metadata changes. Across release itself, all captured resource rows were unchanged. This is historical upgrade proof, not a claim that the replacement reran that live experiment.

The release implementation, consent-digest logic, ownership table schema and write-admission helpers are unchanged from the historically proven product code. Fresh focused tests cover current offline-owner and runtime-config integration. The original cancelled CI attempt does not establish passing coverage; this replacement requires its own exact-head CI.

### Current documentation correction

Commit `efd3f007685ead8d4ffa327a06f846830994b16f` preserves current-main optional preferred-model documentation alongside the release command and operator-only exec/messaging controls, resolving their documentation overlap. Only `docs/cli/templates.md` changes from the prior head; all nine source/test files and their determining code remain unchanged. The docs inventory, focused formatting check and whitespace check passed for this correction. The 152 tests, runtime build and real-model upgrade evidence above remain labeled with the revisions where they ran. Its fresh exact-head CI is qualified below; no CI success is claimed.

ClawSweeper found no code defect at prior head `33b4bc76b0cef564547fa816218c31c4e90b0884`. For its requested 2026.11.4 upgrade trace, the retained 2026.11.3 historical experiment plus inspected determining inputs establish the scoped compatibility evidence: ownership SQL, consent and write-store inputs are unchanged between stable tags. Optional service-identity/read-admission changes do not alter the release data transition, and the schema-migration authority gate is byte-identical between the historically tested target and this replacement. No new live 2026.11.4 experiment is claimed.

### Current-head CI qualification

CI [43987880167, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43987880167) completed for `efd3f007685ead8d4ffa327a06f846830994b16f`: 60 jobs passed, 25 were unselected/skipped, and the sole failing root was [the Windows updater fixture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43987880167/job/133721479532), plus its downstream CI aggregate. All PostgreSQL conformance, production checks, five core test-type leaves and independent security checks passed. CI remains failed.

The 17 direct/cascading failures concern a Windows platform mock spawning a real Linux broker: its Windows pipe path produces parent directory `.` in that child and `mkdir` fails with `EEXIST` before SQLite staging readiness. All 20 inspected causal/support files are byte-identical between the actual current CI main baseline and tested merge. The added lazy release-worker loader is not invoked by these tests, and the release test is absent from the failing invocation. This is independently verified scoped source/log attribution for this exact run/head, not a full baseline test replay or qualification of another failure.
