prs.title: fix(agents): stop provider fallback for unavailable transcript projections
prs.body:
Related: #153976.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes provider fallback attempts and failure attribution when a local session transcript projection is rebuilding.

## User Impact

The original storage error stops the turn without consuming another configured provider candidate. There is no configuration or stored-data change. This does not wait for rebuilding, retry the user's message, or improve rebuild speed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add the existing projection exception to the existing runtime-coordination classification. That owner already stops fallback for local failures, including errors preserved through provider-looking wrappers. The change leaves failure wording, visibility and recovery ownership in place.

The hydration recovery proposed in #164843 addresses a separate wait/retry boundary. This change only prevents a storage error that reaches fallback from being treated as a provider failure.

## Evidence

A direct Node 26.5.0 probe calls the real `runWithModelFallback` owner with two synthetic candidates and the actual storage exception, in isolated state with no provider transport. On both unpatched main `38c85c2fe23` and the real published OpenClaw 2026.10.5 package, the direct exception and a provider-looking `503` wrapper execute two candidates and report a provider failure. With this fix, each executes once, reports no provider failure or fallback step, and preserves the identical original error. The wrapper previously lost that error in aggregate fallback failure.

The two regression cases extend the existing fallback-owner table; they add no test-only production seam. The full touched suite passes 51/51 with the official agents-core Vitest config on Node 26.5.0 (296.16 seconds wall on the local Mac). A focused run of the two new cases also passes (2/2; 92.70 seconds wall). The owner boundary is needed to verify that neither another candidate nor provider-failure callbacks run; a classification-only test would miss that behavior.

Targeted formatting, typed lint, the owning `agents-other` test typecheck and `git diff --check` pass.

No new state, policy, configuration, retry owner or recovery path was added; the production delta is one error-classification entry. Gateway-entry evidence with a local fake provider is in the next section. No live provider request, channel or production transcript is used or claimed.

## Gateway-entry proof at the current head — 2026-11-16 (UTC)

Built the exact head `f45f5ff9995a47ad512f65dc5e7e7adbbb816711` (`pnpm build`, Node 26.5.0, macOS) and ran it as a loopback-only Gateway with isolated state, no messaging channels, and two model candidates (`mock-primary/primary-model`, fallback `mock-backup/backup-model`) served by a local fake OpenAI-compatible endpoint that records each requested model. The head still merges cleanly into `main` at `687dc6c99a32`.

**Trigger (induced on purpose, not a natural production occurrence):** after a few normal turns, the test session's projection was marked for rebuild (`UPDATE session_transcript_index_state SET needs_rebuild = 1`, the state that the repository fixtures use and that the session-table migration sets on upgrade), and one stored, non-leaf event of that session was made undecodable, so the rebuild fails and the projection stays unavailable. A slow rebuild alone does not reach the fallback decision on this head, because the turn waits for the rebuild within its time limit. The error reaches fallback only when the rebuild ends and the projection is still unavailable, which is the state induced here. Every run used:

```
openclaw agent --agent main --session-key agent:main:<test-session> --message "<text>" --json --timeout 60
```

| Build | Fallback decision | Candidate attempts | Error returned to the caller |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PR head (two runs) | `chain stopped: reason=local_runtime_coordination` | 1 | `Session transcript projection is rebuilding: <session-id>` |
| Same build with only this PR's entry removed from the two built bundles (restored afterwards, SHA-256 checked) | `candidate_failed reason=unknown next=mock-backup/backup-model` | 2 | same text |

The fake endpoint received no model requests in either variant, because the failure happens while the session is opened. After the stored event was restored, the next turn on the PR head completed normally with `mock-primary/primary-model` (one model request).

Limits: the failure is induced as described. The caller-visible error text is the same in both variants; the difference is the extra candidate attempt and the fallback decision. The provider-looking 503 wrapper is covered only by the owner-level probes, not at the Gateway entry. No live provider, channel or production data was used.

prs.title: improve(ui): offer "Report a bug" only on chat errors OpenClaw cannot explain
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Every chat error notice carries a "Report a bug" link, including errors with a known cause and a clear next step, such as a draft that could not be saved, a busy session, or an expired sign-in. The link is accent-colored and sits where the recovery action belongs, so it reads as the main action on notices where reporting does not help.

## User Impact

User impact: chat error notices offer "Report a bug" only when OpenClaw cannot explain the failure, and the link is a quiet secondary link after the recovery action.

- Notices with a written explanation no longer show the link: draft storage, session busy, sign-in, permission and connection messages, and the discard-and-reload start conflict.
- Notices that can only show a raw failure keep it: a reply that failed for an unknown reason, a session that could not start, and failed reactions, session suggestions, task suggestions, forks from a message, and session-menu actions.
- A notice with no recovery action and no link has no action slot. On phones the recovery button stays beside the title and the link moves to the last row.
- The reply-failed card in the transcript follows the same rule. A failure with a named cause, such as rejected credentials, billing, a rate limit, an overloaded provider, or a timeout, has no link. A failure without one keeps a quiet link after the recovery actions.
- "Report a bug" in the sidebar Help menu and on the connection error page is unchanged.

Sources are opted in one at a time, and the default is no link. An unexpected failure from a source that is not opted in loses the one-click link; the Help menu entry still opens the same form.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared chat error notice attached the link unconditionally and received page-level errors as plain text, so it could not tell a written explanation from a raw failure. Deciding from the message text would be guessing. Instead, a source that has no explanation of its own now passes the raw failure along with its message, through the detail channel the error owner already had, and the notice offers reporting only when that raw failure is present. The reply-failed and session-start notices already know their failure kind and pass the decision directly. No new state or props travel through the chat pane.

Two side effects of reusing that channel:

- A raw failure that carries extra Gateway details now also gets the existing "Show details" disclosure.
- A raw failure that spans several lines keeps its first line as the title and the rest under details, as before.

Accepted edge case: a missing-permission error that reaches one of the opted-in sources is shown with its written explanation and still gets the link. These actions are checked for access before the request is sent, so this needs a permission change while the request is in flight.

The transcript card already receives the failover reason of the failed run. It offers reporting when there is no reason, or when the reason leaves the cause open: `format`, `empty_response`, `no_error_details`, `unclassified`, and `unknown`. A reason added later counts as explained until it is added to that list.

Overlap: #197822 restructures the same card and will need a rebase over this change. Its author asked for this order.

prs.title: fix: continue updates when initial SQLite capture is stale
prs.body:
Related: #200260

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes updates aborting with `SQLite migration source changed after update capture: credentials.sqlite` when normal credential activity changes a database between the updater's snapshot and Doctor's initial admission.

## User Impact

Updates can migrate the current database instead of failing solely because the original capture is stale. Automatic database restoration remains unavailable for that update, so a later failure cannot overwrite newer data with the stale backup. Existing integrity, maintenance-ownership, and post-admission writer checks remain in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

Separate initial migration admission from rollback eligibility: adopt the observed generations at first admission while preserving the sticky `unchanged=false` receipt. This generalizes the existing WAL-index workaround and deletes its special-case helper. PostgreSQL migration wrappers and post-admission checks are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the stale-credential failure before the fix at the actual SQLite migration guard.
- After resolving conflicts with main, four focused suites passed: **123 tests passed**, **3 PostgreSQL cases skipped** (`client-credential-update`, `update-doctor-migration-attribution`, `update-doctor-result`, and `update-database-generations`).
- Preserved #200260's successful-boot write attribution and verified both new boot cases alongside stale-capture rollback refusal.
- Real SQLite capture → Doctor credential migration → attempted public rollback verifies the newer synthetic token survives, the credential source is retired correctly, and stale restoration is refused.
- Existing post-admission foreign-writer checks remain passing; legacy capture variants now migrate while retaining rollback refusal.
- Infra and services TypeScript checks, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Self-review and simplification completed. Local independent review was explicitly opted out; remote ClawSweeper review was requested after publication. No clean independent-review result is claimed.

Validation gaps: no full installed-version npm upgrade with a real Gateway/model was run; PostgreSQL tests requiring a service were skipped. This is a forward-admission change, not removal of all update integrity checks.

## Matrix — causal original-module qualification

### Real Matrix homeserver proof — November 17, 2026

[Hosted run 43990720491 / job 133730280334](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43990720491/job/133730280334) **passed all three required live contracts** against unchanged candidate bf8ee2c6152a18386a175ad329013bc20a4a8051, using execution tooling b25f1009d0b0dfafc2e1ffe624751f28fa94ee0f. The earlier causal/timing jobs were not rerun.

Disposable Ubuntu 24.04 / Node 24.22.1 ran real Synapse 1.165.0, pinned to ghcr.io/element-hq/synapse@sha256:b7f105b3c5f6d8bdb0a1aaff51ec4264dd109d8ed5532009d176bcb28a57ca0a. Temporary local Alice/Bob accounts exercised the production SDK, transport, SQLite-backed durable plan, and crypto.

- Authenticated send: Bob independently read exactly one event matching the returned event ID and sender (0.969 s).
- Accepted-then-429: the proxy received upstream HTTP 200 before returning 429; retry reused the identical transaction path and event ID, with one delivery callback and one recipient event (2.700 s).

[Artifact 14286724744](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43990720491/artifacts/14286724744), goal24-matrix-live-43990720491, is 3,677 bytes; archive SHA-256 0c2c15a77af0ac2cd7d06e32681af4ea4a496d686ad7acc9caaf367191193b48. Downloaded report/observations passed exact identity and three-case admission. Fixture SHA-256 d5337fc5ce60f4741ed87bab770c1dd40e35ae9ef3c3366b01aee277c30d23dc. Inspection found no token/password fields or bearer credentials; raw SDK/server-state/install logs were not uploaded. Container cleanup exited 0.

Initial run 43990033248 at c408675efbcce1a96ca983a4478aa7d8df66664e passed authenticated delivery but could not open SQLite for the remaining cases. The driver correction selected the canonical isolated database-worker configuration, narrowing only its include list; the unchanged fixture then passed. This is a harness correction, not a product-code fix. Six admission tests plus targeted lint, format, syntax, and whitespace checks passed. Prior independent findings were addressed; @RomneyDa explicitly waived further independent/formal review for this proof-only patch on November 17, 2026. No new formal review is claimed.

Reused the unchanged exact-head independent source review; no new review or signature is claimed. Native `review-init`, `review-checkout-pr`, and `review-validate-artifacts` completed with `READY FOR /prepare-pr`, zero findings. The native gate receipt is `github_pending` (not a fabricated successful-test stamp); separately observed exact-head CI run 43618778733 attempt 2 and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. PR remains open, non-draft and mergeable; no merge was requested.

### Historical failures and environmental limits

- Historical head `4aa0faa30907ba9ce07cfaccdaa7dd21c4bbf1b9`: CI run 43606138401 attempt 2 failed on M4 fixture collision and inherited scripts TS18048. It passed message-tool execution (74 tests), scheduled lifetime (18), accepted results (35), production types and lint. None of this is current-head runtime proof.
- Secretless AWS allocation failed before any lease because credentials were unavailable. No AWS tests or credentialed fallback ran; no contributor runtime executed on the trusted local host.
- The earlier absence of live Matrix credentials was resolved by the disposable, secretless Synapse fixture above; no production credentials were used.

The results below belong to the contributor's earlier head and are retained for attribution/history, not current-head proof.

<details>
<summary>Historical contributor description and earlier-head evidence (superseded where noted above)</summary>

## What Problem This Solves

A `message` tool send can pass the point where the channel may already have accepted it and still come back as a failure — #196802 has Matrix answering `/send/m.room.encrypted/<txn>` with `429 Server is unavailable` after it accepted the event. The tool then reported a plain failure (`message failed: MatrixError: [429] ...`), the model did what "failed" implies, and the room got the same text twice. The delivery queue already knew better: it recorded `unknown_after_send` and reconciled the entry as already sent minutes later, but that knowledge never reached the tool result.

The queue's terminal failure already carries it. `OutboundDeliveryError.sentBeforeError` is set when an earlier attempt of the same intent started or its outcome is unknown, which is exactly the "may have landed" state. This projects that one case as a `delivery_unconfirmed` tool result so the model waits instead of minting a second send.

Two facts decide what the model may be told, and both already exist on the error:

- **Who owns reconciliation.** `owner.project(...)` stamps `queueCustody = "held"` while the durable queue still owns the attempt and `"released"` once it is retired; a `skipQueue` send (`message-tool-execution.ts:575`, scheduled direct sends) has no owner at all. Only `"held"` keeps the Gateway-reconciliation wording. Undefined or `"released"` reports `No queued retry owns it, so the send may already have reached the recipient; check it before resending.` — because there is no row to reconcile and promising one would be false.
- **What the provider already proved.** A permanent pre-dispatch rejection can carry `sentBeforeError` evidence from another payload in the same batch. When the error graph holds a `PlatformMessageNotDispatchedError{retryable:false}`, the projection returns nothing and the rejection keeps its actionable error and cause.

Everything else keeps its current behavior: a failure that provably never left still throws, and a failure with confirmed platform sends keeps its existing partial-delivery path (`projectScheduledMessageActionPartialResult`), because the projection requires an empty `results` list.

Open question for the Matrix owner: `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk/transport.ts:269-283` wraps `PlatformMessageNotDispatchedError` only when the fetch never started, so a post-dispatch 403 is still reported as `sentBeforeError` and is indistinguishable here from an accepted-then-429 send. Classifying those as `retryable: false` in the adapter would route them through `isProvenDeliveryNotSentError` and out of this projection; that policy is not decided inside a tool-result projection.

Closes #196802

## Evidence

Red — both new behaviours fail against the previous projection, test kept (`node scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/tools/message-tool-execution.test.ts`):

```
×  message tool unconfirmed delivery > does not promise a queued retry when custody is undefined
×  message tool unconfirmed delivery > does not promise a queued retry when custody is released
×  message tool unconfirmed delivery > keeps a provider-proven rejection actionable
   Tests  3 failed | 70 passed (73)
```

Green — same command on `937f77cb2`:

```
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  73 passed (73)
```

Other checks, on `origin/main` at `584084d77`:

- `src/infra/outbound/message-action-execution.accepted-results.test.ts` — passed.
- `src/agents/tools/message-tool.scheduled-lifetime.test.ts` — 17 passed, 1 failed (`settles provider revocation during send via direct as accepted`). That failure reproduces identically with this change reverted, so it is a pre-existing Windows baseline, not a regression.
- `oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json` on the touched files — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-root.json` — no diagnostics for the touched files (the repo's pre-existing `@openclaw/fs-safe` drift in unrelated files is unchanged).
- `run-format.mts --check` — all files formatted.
- Test-line ratchet: `config/test-lines-allocations/196802-message-tool-unconfirmed-delivery.txt` = 67, matching the +67 test lines.

Diff against `584084d77` is +96/-3 across `message-tool-execution.ts` (rename), `message-action-execution.ts` (projection), the test file, and the ratchet allocation.

Why the proof is not here: this machine cannot build the dist (`@openclaw/fs-safe` in `node_modules` predates `preserve`, so `build-all.mts runtime` dies in `plugins:assets:build`), and the remaining item needs a live homeserver that accepts a message and then answers 429 without an event id. A maintainer proof run only has to assert `status: "delivery_unconfirmed"` with `delivered: false` on the tool result plus one recipient event.

</details>

prs.body:
## Summary

Recovered the missing focused Goal 24 execution evidence without running contributor code on a credentialed operator host, modifying the product branches, or touching main.

Temporary proof-only workflow on `proof/goal24-secretless-20261115`, explicitly authorized by @RomneyDa on November 15, 2026, including billed macOS execution. No merge, backport, release, or main-branch mutation is requested. This draft is an evidence carrier, not intended to merge.

## Verified product proof

### History — PASS

PR #198091, source `eb919fb0d0b19dfa86c3e7055145b5a83ae27ef9`; tooling `c95caafe0fc52d86bdae05ebba9515085a300b3d`.

[Hosted run 43768728614](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43768728614/job/132979610910): 6 transcript recent-text tests and 5 inbound-context tests passed. Includes all physical-row boundaries, oversized-user barriers, shared 64 MiB budget, and the replay-suppression-after-restart regression. JSON reports prove selected test execution.

### Prefix stability — PASS

The earlier 11 history tests do **not** cover `src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts`. The focused correction at tooling `9838c5239d071ab5845c061da812f2aa76f1db5c` runs that entire suite against the same immutable PR #198091 source `eb919fb0d0b19dfa86c3e7055145b5a83ae27ef9`, requiring all 14 cases and the completion-handoff authority regression. Zero or partial execution is rejected.

[Hosted run 43771398337, history job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43771398337/job/132987885912) passed: all **14 prefix-stability assertions**, 6 recent-text tests, and 5 inbound-context tests (25 total). The downloaded JSON reports and summary agree on the exact source/tooling SHAs above, with every assertion passed. Prefix cases cover browser/CLI/ACP wakes and recovery, GitHub catalog stability, completion/scheduled/message definitions, wake-screen gating, and completion-handoff authority. Ubuntu 24.04 x64, Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0. This is focused suite evidence, not a real-model end-to-end claim.

Correction validation: 10 synthetic driver/preflight cases pass, including prefix-zero and partial-suite rejection. Against the prior driver, the new selection/zero/partial checks fail as expected (7 pass, 3 fail); this is harness regression proof, not product base-red evidence. Targeted lint/format, workflow validation, and 1,416 workflow/native-launcher regression tests pass. Initial workflow validation hit an empty-token environment error; rerunning with those empty variables removed passed.

Fresh native independent review of the exact correction from `a493a0599f16ed151dc8c773f280d9f8c349e7c0` to `9838c5239d071ab5845c061da812f2aa76f1db5c` found no P0–P2 findings. Reviewed diff SHA-256: `28b466d8d024083d844ab23859180ab6441370b42f54ac4c34edf06d5d818cf3`. This is the explicit native fallback, not an autoreview/ClawSweeper result; the configured autoreview service credit failure remains unresolved, and no model or service route was switched.

### Audio — converter regression PASS; shipped delivery remains unproven

PR #198525, source `a9a084486e3df10193dfa9ac5ab9faa9f53a4619`; initial tooling `c95caafe0fc52d86bdae05ebba9515085a300b3d`.

[Hosted run 43768728614](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43768728614/job/132979610823): both focused budget cases passed. The exact timeout-removal mutation failed both cases, including the expected `[5000, 5000, 5000]` versus `[5000, 2000, 1000]` assertion. This is mutation evidence, not a base-red claim.

Real unmocked FFmpeg 9.0.2 → afconvert → afinfo control proof passed on macOS 27.0.1 arm64: a two-second synthetic MP3 converted to mono 24 kHz CAF, exactly 48,000 valid frames versus 48,000 independently decoded PCM frames; tiny exhausted-budget rejection and scratch cleanup verified. This control did not reproduce the original segmented-MP3 truncation. Tiny-budget proof does not claim subprocess termination. The production temp resolver selected its standard root outside isolated TMPDIR; both roots were checked for leftovers.

#### Original ten-segment regression — independently reproduced and repaired

[Hosted run 43772299539, audio job 132990706530](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43772299539/job/132990706530) passed on November 15, 2026, using tooling `d43289d7095dadf3c3adc9c41792281cb1e67a12`, the same pinned product head, macOS 27.0.1 arm64, Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, and FFmpeg 9.0.2. The job took 5m58s.

The exact committed synthetic fixture is 166,176 bytes, SHA-256 `7b2d8a3b1244383a4cfc3beaa57ba756c0d76c7d485fa80f927a458bdb60c0f0`. It contains ten independently encoded mathematical-tone segments; no private/user audio or provider call was used.

| Measurement | Independently decoded mono 24 kHz PCM | afinfo valid frames |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source MP3 | 1,153,775 frames / 48.073958 s | n/a |
| Original converter | 79,440 frames / 3.310000 s | 79,200 |
| Fixed converter | 1,154,088 frames / 48.087000 s | 1,153,775 |

The baseline is the unchanged production converter module from pre-fix commit `e80a6dd9fdb4c7ce724472dd5d1b216afb4e70a7`, SHA-256 `867e5fd7ad1b477b1f4ab1023e15d440873c6f9d3d98253bfa6ac4240f6b370d`, loaded alongside the fixed checkout's unchanged runtime dependencies. Only the converter, two tests, and fixture differ between that pre-fix commit and the product head. This is causal original-module red/fixed-module green proof, not a full baseline package build: original conversion succeeded, then the preservation assertion failed specifically on decoded frame loss; the fixed module passed. No helper or codec was mocked.

Fixed output differs by 313 decoded frames (13.042 ms), within the 480-frame Opus-padding allowance. Independent frequency checks at all ten segment centers matched 440, 477, 514, 551, 588, 625, 662, 699, 736, and 773 Hz, with non-silent energy. These samples establish segment presence/identity, not whole-waveform or speech-semantic equivalence. Fixed conversion took 731 ms inside the existing five-second budget. Both variants left no conversion workspaces in the product temp root or isolated TMPDIR.

Downloaded summary and separate native logs agree on the source/tooling/fixture identities and exit statuses (baseline 1, fixed 0). The receipt gate rejects missing/duplicate cases, setup failures mistaken for baseline red, incomplete segment proof, and missing cleanup. Earlier budget/mutation/control proof was retained, not rerun.

**Distinct unfulfilled gates:** no installed-package TTS delivery, Messages transport, receiving-device playback, or shipped missing-FFmpeg/original-attachment fallback was exercised. No paired external device is available to this session (`nodes.list()` returned none). The converter result does not satisfy these gates and makes no overall readiness/merge claim.

### macOS permissions — candidate PASS; causal callback failure reproduced

PR #198869, source `77ee3e8424d789b7bad5804a9dc5a1693f34c91e`; tooling `a493a0599f16ed151dc8c773f280d9f8c349e7c0`.

[Hosted run 43769449537](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43769449537/job/132981863979): app/tests compiled; all 10 PermissionManagerTests passed. Retained Swift Testing events prove discovery, start, and completion of `speech authorization completion can enter from a background queue`. Xcode 27.1 / Swift 6.4 / macOS 27.0.1. This is candidate-only regression coverage, not by itself causal base-red/fix-green evidence or interactive signed-app TCC behavior.

The initial permissions job stopped at an overly exact Swift 6.3 preflight on the supported newer Swift 6.4 image, before building or executing tests. The repair enforces the Package.swift minimum (6.3+) and accurately classifies setup failures. Only the missing permissions job was run again; the passing history/audio results were retained. The next history-only matrix collected the missing prefix-stability proof. At that stage, the matrix ran only the newly added segmented-audio comparison; completed history, permissions, and audio-budget proof were not repeated.

#### Off-main callback causal proof — collected November 16, 2026

Final proof head: `9325008d1f891d8539c6ec0155e6388cacf3c95f`. Product code was not changed by this proof: candidate `77ee3e8424d789b7bad5804a9dc5a1693f34c91e` and full baseline `2f4ae4d3284bf17ad4930cf6770dac14c025bfc1` differ only in PermissionManager.swift and its original tests.

The same added Swift test, `Goal24SpeechFrameworkBoundaryTests.offMainFrameworkCompletion`, is explicitly **transplanted into both immutable checkouts**. It calls the real `PermissionManager.ensure([.speechRecognition], interactive: true)`. An Objective-C fixture intercepts only Speech authorization status/request selectors, dispatches the framework's actual received completion on a global queue, and records exactly one off-main invocation. No Swift production method, package setting, or actor-checking flag is patched. The candidate must return an authorized result, resume on MainActor, and report one request.

| Native execution | Product / tooling | Observed result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Candidate, run 43783553823 / job 133026037240](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43783553823/job/133026037240) | candidate above / `924b7db5b02bcd42305bcbe3e7f34ed9dc2bdd4d` | Build passed; exactly one selected function started/completed; off-main marker once; test passed in 0.012 s; native launcher exit 0. |
| [Initial baseline, same run / job 133026037588](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43783553823/job/133026037588) | baseline above / same tooling | Build passed; same test started; marker once; Signal 5; no completion; launcher exit 1. The job remained red because Swift's crash helper could not produce the required stack. |
| [Baseline stack diagnostic, run 43786255830 / job 133034441205](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43786255830/job/133034441205) | baseline above / final tooling above | Build passed; one start, zero completions, marker once; actual SIGTRAP captured; launcher exit 1; strict expected-failure gate passed with executor and original production callback frames. |

The collected crashing-thread stack is: `_dispatch_assert_queue_fail` → `dispatch_assert_queue` → `_swift_task_checkIsolatedSwift` → `swift_task_isCurrentExecutorWithFlagsImpl` → the original `PermissionManager.ensureSpeechRecognition` authorization callback → Speech block bridge → fixture's background dispatch block. This is the required callback-entry actor-isolation failure, not a compilation, setup, or zero-selection failure. The fixture's diagnostic SIGTRAP handler records an actual signal and exits 133; it never raises one. SwiftPM/launcher reports exit 1. Candidate execution was retained, not repeated for this diagnostic.

**Environment qualification:** the paired candidate/initial-baseline jobs both used macOS 27.0.1 arm64. The later hosted baseline diagnostic image had advanced to macOS 27.2 arm64; Xcode 27.1 (27A9275), Swift 6.4 (swiftlang-6.4.0.34.1), Node 24.22.1 and pnpm 12.15.0 were unchanged. The final stack is therefore a cross-image corroboration of the earlier same-image differential, not a claim of same-image stack capture. Both variants' Swift test SHA-256 is `07670b386db7e63744294bfe64193bc2f8a496fc2c78f01c0e73bddcb0159352`. The Objective-C fixture changed only to add diagnostic signal capture; its hashes are `5e2d8fd2ca8a7f26ac5af7376a6bd050c8fdc5a70ba6b2dbdedb47156ef4eec7` before and `6dc25ce0a5952fa911d0f1303f76baf865b7365c9e5738a27fa28cf6fcc37746` after.

Earlier [Swift-seam control run 43780908432](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43780908432) did **not reproduce**: both variants executed one function and passed. Its initial event gate counted suite and function events together. Corrected local replay identified candidate success and control nonreproduction; no macOS rerun was spent on that parser correction. prs.title: feat(release): request stable and beta Gateway Store delivery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway betas need to reach the Microsoft Store Development flight automatically, not stop at signed GitHub prereleases. Regular stable releases need the same central, release-manager-approved Store handoff for Production.

## User Impact

After upstream GitHub activation, both release entry points request the exact signed Gateway source:

- **Beta on npm `beta`:** packaging signs and publishes x64, ARM64, and bundle GitHub prerelease assets, never Latest. Core waits for the successful build/publication, validates its source and current-attempt Store witness, then requests central **Development-flight** delivery.
- **Regular stable on npm `latest`:** packaging builds the Store bundle without sideload signing or a packaging GitHub release, then core requests central **Production** delivery.
- Alpha, extended-stable, failed activation, and mismatched channel/tag combinations remain excluded. Native publication stays detached from npm/GitHub completion.

**A queued request is not proof of delivery.** Both destinations require central release-manager approval. Automatic Development requests also require the central owner's operational activation flag and configured flight. Core adds no Store credential, flight GUID, or activation flag.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one detached `Windows Gateway Release Request` owner for both destinations. Beta retains `release_channel=beta`, exact published `gateway_version`, signed full-SHA `openclaw_ref`, `signing_mode=official`, and `publish_release=true`; it never follows the moving npm beta selector. Stable retains `signing_mode=store` and `publish_release=false`.

Both paths wait for the exact selected packaging-main run, verify the signed upstream source and separately selected release identity, and consume `openclaw-source-resolution/source-resolution.json` plus the current API `run_attempt` artifacts:

- `openclaw-gateway-msix-store-submission-<attempt>`
- `store-release-source-<attempt>/store-source.json`, binding run, attempt, packaging commit, source channel, exact packaging release/bundle identity, and SHA-256.

Core validates this routing evidence; central alone downloads/hashes the bundle and revalidates protected-main source history, signed payload/identity, published beta packaging release, approval, and destination. The central dispatch is `{product: gateway, run_id: <successful build>, channel: development | production, automatic: true}` to `openclaw/releases/windows-store-publish.yml` on `main`.

The existing release GitHub App (`2729701`, `GH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`) needs Actions write and Contents read on core, packaging, and releases for **both** channels. No PAT or new Store secret is needed; installation grants remain unverified. Post-wait authority validation, original-request replay ownership, and ambiguous-dispatch evidence remain intact. Recover retained downstream runs rather than republishing npm or blindly redispatching.

The 45-minute build wait and 55-minute request-job timeout are unchanged. A build that outlasts that budget remains a retained downstream recovery task; core does not create a replacement build.

## Evidence

Head: `bef89564d9107a0070be8a8b89bd758b95455391` (valid GPG signature; additive merge, no force push).
Integrated main: `f4d2e45592438dbaae12975e1c4223a991285b7a`.
Validated/committed tree: `feab6a3ba49ea55f859cb5ed0f7d56028227fcdc`.

The conflict-free integration preserves the original eight-file authored delta exactly: 1,155 insertions / 2 deletions. Stable/latest requests Production and beta/beta requests Development from both publish and promote entry points. No release or Store workflow was dispatched.

Fresh validation on the integrated tree:

- **54 tests pass:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/release-windows-gateway.test.ts test/scripts/release-publish-finalize.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot`.
- **Former CI failure now passes:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts --testNamePattern "keeps private Control UI servers and resource-sensitive files under one serial owner" --maxWorkers=1` (1 passed, 225 filtered). The inherited pinned-snooze inventory defect was fixed by merged [#194356](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194356), included in this main integration; no unrelated fix is added here.
- Tooling typecheck: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json --incremental` passed after a frozen dependency install.
- Targeted `run-oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, JavaScript syntax, and base-relative whitespace checks passed.
- `pnpm check:workflows` passed pinned actionlint, zizmor, generated CI-owner, composite-input, and conflict-marker checks.
- The prior independent review was P0–P2 scoped-clean at `af77d00673cffe7ac7a140defa199fae65d56286`; the authored patch is unchanged. No fresh independent review of this mechanical integration is claimed.

**Hosted CI:** new-head checks are pending; local proof does not claim green hosted CI.

**Unrun:** live App mint/dispatch/denial, Windows package builds and installed upgrades, protected Azure signing, GitHub asset publication, central activation/admin/federation changes, release-manager approval, and Store acceptance/certification/flight delivery. Both Store destinations retain central approval. No live settings or credentials were changed by this repair.

## Coordinated Rollout

Do not enable the core handoff until these dependencies and administrative setup are ready:

1. [Gateway beta build support: packaging #246](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-packaging/pull/246), then [current-attempt Store bundle/witness support: packaging #247](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-packaging/pull/247).
2. [Evidence-writer prerequisite: releases #47](https://github.com/openclaw/releases/pull/47), [central Store publisher: releases #48](https://github.com/openclaw/releases/pull/48), and its review/environment/App/federation/Development-flight setup.
3. [Gateway request-only cutover: packaging #212](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-packaging/pull/212), stacked on #247, retiring direct/automatic Store writers. Coordinate the [Companion request-only cutover: node #1891](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/1891) under the same central owner.
4. Land core and cut updated protected release tooling for **both** core release entry points. Existing frozen tooling cuts do not change when this PR merges.

Land evidence-writer compatibility before enforcing PR-only main. Both Store destinations use the central protected release-manager environment; automatic Development activation is central-only. Configure exclusive central Store federation and revoke the old repository's Store federation. Merging these PRs alone does not establish working production approvals or authorize a Store submission.

prs.title: fix(daemon): gateway install fails when unit drop-ins exist before the first install
prs.body:
Fixes #197377 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: `openclaw gateway install` fails with "Managed service artifacts changed during publication. The previous service definition could not be restored." on Linux when the unit's own systemd drop-ins (`~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway.service.d/*.conf`) already exist before the first install. ## User Impact User impact: hosts that provision operator drop-ins before OpenClaw's installer runs (configuration management, image builds, declarative dotfiles) can install the Gateway service in that order; the drop-ins stay in place and take effect. A drop-in that appears while the unit is being written still aborts the install, and unsafe waiting drop-ins (symlink, foreign owner, group-writable) are now refused before anything is written instead of after the unit was already published. ## Why This Change Was Made systemd reports a unit's drop-ins only once its fragment exists (`LoadState=not-found`, empty `DropInPaths` before the first install). The pre-write fingerprint therefore missed them, and the post-write check in `refresh(true, firstUnitPublication)` treated them as a concurrent edit, because its exception only admits type-wide `service.d` defaults. When systemd has not loaded the unit, `inspect()` now also fingerprints the visible `*.conf` files already waiting in `.d` next to the unit path, with the same checks as loaded drop-ins. After publication systemd reports exactly those files, so the fingerprints match. The `service.d` exception and every other check are unchanged. Drop-in directories elsewhere in systemd's search path (`/etc/systemd/user/.d`, `user.control`, prefix directories such as `openclaw-.service.d`) are out of scope; they behave as before. The regression test needs 12 new test lines; `main` had exactly 12 lines of slack at the base commit, so `config/test-lines-allocations/gateway-install-unit-dropins.txt` records the exact growth instead of consuming shared headroom. ## Evidence Same fresh Hetzner CCX13 server, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, systemd 255, Node 24.22.1, one new user with linger per run. prs.title: fix(sessions): shipped updaters refuse the next release because the transcript worker re-emits the Gateway graph
prs.body:
Related: #200114 introduced the regression and its feature is kept. #164494 is an open proposal to run the installed-tree budget on main pushes.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: already-published updaters would refuse the next release, because a clean build of `main` installs to 52,229 entries and those updaters reject installed trees over 50,000.

The 47,500-entry release budget exists to catch this before a release. `main` has been over it since #200114, and the scheduled published-driver update cell fails with `Installed candidate tree exceeds the release budget`.

## User Impact

User impact: a clean build of this branch installs to 46,826 entries, 674 under the 47,500 budget, so `openclaw update` from a published version can install the next release. Compaction still prepares large histories in the transcript reader, as #200114 added.

No config, schema, protocol or dependency changes. The budget, the cap and their counting rules are unchanged.

**The headroom is thin.** 674 entries is 1.4% of the budget. That is roughly where `main` stood before #200114, not new slack. Earlier measurements that I did not repeat put the parent of #200114 at 46,795 and published `openclaw@2026.11.4` at 47,481. More headroom needs separate reduction work and is not part of this fix.

**Update behavior.** This changes what the package contains, not how an update runs. The installed updater still walks the candidate tree against its frozen cap, and the candidate now fits. Nothing keys on updater markers and no operator state is read or changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transcript reader is built on its own, with code splitting and private chunk names, so it shares no chunks with the main bundle. Every module it can reach, statically or through `import()`, is emitted again as a private file.

#200114 made the reader lazily import `session-compaction-prepared.worker.ts`, which constructs `SessionManagerCore` to read the active branch. That class also carried host-side hydration. The traced edge:

```
src/config/sessions/session-transcript.worker.ts            import()
-> src/config/sessions/session-compaction-prepared.worker.ts
-> src/agents/sessions/session-manager-core.ts
-> src/agents/sessions/session-manager-incognito.ts          also reached through session-manager-reload.ts
-> src/config/sessions/session-transcript-hydration.ts
-> src/config/sessions/session-cold-storage-read.ts          import()
-> src/config/sessions/session-cold-storage.ts
-> src/sessions/session-controller.lifecycle.ts -> ... -> src/plugins/loader.ts
-> ... -> src/agents/tools/in-process-gateway.ts -> src/gateway/server-methods/*
```

Only the host restores cold storage. A read worker reports a cold transcript to its host and stops. On `main` the reader's graph is 11,596 source modules by esbuild metafile, against 1,831 without that import, and it builds to 5,792 private chunks.

The fix moves the five host hydration methods out of `SessionManagerCore` into a new `SessionManagerHydration` class between the core and `SessionManagerNativePersistence`. The method bodies are unchanged, and `SessionManager` inherits every one of them through the same chain. The reader still constructs the core, and nothing it reaches imports host hydration now. Its graph is 2,068 modules and it builds to 382 private chunks.

The smaller graph exposed one more edge. The session codec's static import of the root logger landed in the same chunk as the lazy `import("../logger.js")` in `src/process/exec.ts`, and the build rejects an ineffective dynamic import. The codec now calls `createSubsystemLogger("parseJsonlEntries")` directly. The root logger already routed that prefixed line to the same subsystem logger, so the log line is unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Options considered</summary>

- **Build the reader, or only the lazy module, without code splitting.** One file would carry the 11,596-module graph. The entry count drops, but the reader ships and parses Gateway code it never runs, and the build-graph guard stays red. Building the whole reader unsplit also removes the lazy boundaries between its handlers.
- **Let the reader share the main bundle's chunks.** Every reader thread would evaluate shared Gateway chunks. The private build exists to prevent that.
- **Narrow the imports. Chosen.** It removes the files and restores what the guard already states, that a standalone worker does not contain the Gateway graph.
- **Cut at the cold-storage `import()` instead.** `session-transcript-hydration.ts` imports that module statically and is itself reached from the core, so this cut needs a restore hook registered by the host. Moving hydration off the core needs no new hook.
- **Revert #200114.** Not needed.

</details>

### Why PR CI missed it, and what guards it now

The installed-tree budget runs in Package Acceptance, which is dispatched manually or called from release checks, and in the published-driver update cell on scheduled `main` validation. Neither runs on pull requests. `shouldRunPublishedDriverUpdate` returns false for `pull_request`, and the cell shows `skipping` on #200114. The scheduled cell did catch it afterwards. [CI run 43959978735](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43959978735) failed on Linux with `Installed candidate tree exceeds the release budget (52228 entries, 619284167 bytes)`.

A cheaper guard already existed and already fails on `main`. `test/scripts/runtime-process-build-graph.test.ts` asserts that no standalone worker contains the Gateway server graph. It bundles the workers at test time, so the PR planner's import graph never connects it to `src/**`, and the planner treats files under `test/scripts/` as release-only tooling unless a change selects them. With #200114's 100 changed files and the options PR CI passes, the planner on `main` selects 1,826 test files and not this one.

This PR registers that test with the existing source policy watch, next to `eager-import-closure.test.ts`, so source changes select it on PRs. It adds no workflow. With the watch entry, the same input selects it. The test also gains two checks:

- Each code-split worker builds to at most 1,000 chunks. This catches a worker re-emitting the application graph. It is not the release budget.
- The reader's graph contains none of `session-manager-hydration.ts`, `session-transcript-hydration.ts` and `session-cold-storage.ts`.

I did not add an installed-entry count to PRs. It needs a full build, a pack and an `npm install` per PR, which is a slow job. #164494 proposes it for main pushes.

## Evidence

macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1, npm 11.20.0. One clean build each, with no `dist`, `dist-runtime` or `.artifacts` beforehand.

```bash
node scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs --allow-unreleased-changelog --output-dir <fresh> --output-name openclaw-candidate.tgz
npm install -g --prefix <fresh> --cache <fresh> --no-fund --no-audit <fresh>/openclaw-candidate.tgz
node scripts/check-openclaw-installed-package-budget.mts <prefix>/lib/node_modules/openclaw
```

| Build | Tarball entries | Tarball bytes | `dist/config/sessions/transcript-*` | Installed entries | Installed size | Budget check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `main` 9a6a00e3e2b | 27,102 | 123,873,280 | 5,792 | 52,229 | 597.0 MiB | exit 1 |
| this diff on 910f6b9427d | 21,697 | 113,530,880 | 382 | 46,824 | 565.1 MiB | exit 0 |
| this PR, bbd2cac281c on 2cc6988bc28 | 21,699 | 113,530,880 | 382 | 46,826 | 565.1 MiB | exit 0 |

The base moved twice while I worked, from 9a6a00e3e2b to 910f6b9427d and then to 2cc6988bc28. Neither range touches a file in this diff, the build configuration, the lockfile or the budget script. I did not repeat the full red install on the later bases. With this PR's `src` change reversed on 910f6b9427d, the reader alone builds to 5,796 chunks, and with the change it builds to 383, counting its entry file.

**The lazy module still loads from built output.**

- `src/agents/sessions/session-manager-hydration-stream.test.ts` drives `readPreparedSessionCompactionInWorker` through a real reader thread for plan, render, cancellation and oversized-history cases. The test runner compiles that reader with the same private-chunk options as `dist`. All 12 cases in that file pass.
- Against the npm-installed tree of this PR, a worker thread imported the chunk the built entry names, `./transcript-session-compaction-prepared.worker-Wt6Onj7f.mjs`, found `readPreparedSessionCompaction` as its export and ran it to its first cancellation check. Loading that chunk evaluates its whole static closure from installed files, `SessionManagerCore` included. The smoke does not read a database.
- No existing built-runtime lane reaches prepared compaction. I did not run a built Gateway compacting a session against a model.

**Guard, red then green.** With this PR's `src` and planner changes reversed on 910f6b9427d, three cases in the two touched test files fail. The reader builds to 5,796 chunks against the 1,000 limit, the reader's graph contains 623 forbidden Gateway, flows and wizard modules, and the planner does not select the guard for a source change. With the change, all 64 cases pass. `ci-changed-node-test-plan.source-owners.test.ts` now expects the guard among the tests any source change selects, and that expectation fails without the watch entry.

**Checks.** The diff is identical across the rebases below, and each line names the base it ran on.

| Check | Result | Base |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `oxfmt --check` on the 11 changed files, `git diff --check` | clean | 2cc6988bc28 |
| `pnpm tsgo:all` | pass | 2cc6988bc28 |
| `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <changed files>` | pass | 910f6b9427d |
| `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs` | exit 0 | 910f6b9427d |
| Guard, routing and both hydration test files | 4 files, 175 tests pass | 2cc6988bc28 |
| Guard plus the CI planner test files | 21 files, 1,010 tests pass | 910f6b9427d |
| Session manager, #200114's tests, compaction and hydration worker tests | 50 files, 641 tests pass | 910f6b9427d |

PR CI on bbd2cac281c finished with 83 checks passing and none failing, `build-artifacts` included. The guard file ran there on Linux in `checks-node-compact-small-8`, 64 tests in 21.5s. This PR edits the guard file, so that run does not by itself show the new watch selecting it. The planner numbers above do.

The dead-export scan is skipped in `check-changed`. Run alone, `pnpm deadcode:exports` exits 1 with 126 entries, and none is in a file this PR changes.

**Test files audited in full**

- `test/scripts/runtime-process-build-graph.test.ts`. All three existing behaviors stay: the shared-entry filter, the lazy optional handlers and the Gateway-graph exclusion. The inlined tsdown build became one helper that the new chunk cases share, with the same build options, disposal and temp-dir owner. Nothing was removed.
- `test/scripts/ci-changed-node-test-plan.source-owners.test.ts`. One expectation gained an entry. I found no dead, vacuous or duplicate case to prune.

**Not proven**

- Linux and npm 12 installed counts for this branch. The Package Acceptance budget step installs with an npm 12 prefix, and my numbers are npm 11 on macOS. The only Linux number is the red one from scheduled CI.
- The published-driver Docker cells against this branch.
- An end-to-end compaction through a built Gateway, as noted above.
- `scripts/perf/session-reload-measure.ts` swaps `session-manager-core.ts` and `session-manager-codec.ts` for A/B runs. I left it alone. The async reload entry point it calls now lives in `session-manager-hydration.ts`.

**Review.** A fresh agent reviewed the diff read-only and found no blockers. This head addresses its findings on the chunk guard, the comments and a stale doc reference. The autoreview helper cannot run on this machine, so there is no autoreview result.

prs.title: fix(templates): blocked Template Add leaves an agent Retry cannot finish
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #198761.

A reviewed `templates.add.apply` can admit an ordinary agent before the Template source reveals a plan blocker. That refusal currently returns a retained partial agent, so Retry cannot finish setup. Return the blocker after removing the resources this request created.

## What Changed

Use the existing admission ownership flag to protect recovered agents. The continuation owner removes a newly admitted agent, pending conversation and empty workspace, then throws the original refusal. If agent removal fails, preserve the existing partial outcome. After agent removal succeeds, conversation cleanup failure is logged and the refusal still stands, so a removed agent is never reported as retained.

Keeping this complete cleanup/refusal outcome in the existing continuation owner also keeps the apply coordinator within its unchanged size limit. Chat Add continues through its current creation owner. The final change affects three backend files.

## Validation

### Evidence

- Matched regression proof: the same two blocked-review cases fail against unchanged `744a001ea64` production owners because Add resolves with `status: partial` and `agentRetained: true` instead of rejecting the plan blocker. Both pass on the final source, including the conversation-cleanup failure case. The baseline's original test bytes were restored and its production files stayed unchanged.
- Final-source apply/pending contracts: 32 passed. Final signed-head Gateway handler contracts: 33 passed; 65 focused contracts passed in total.
- Core types, scoped lint with the unchanged 700-line rule, format and diff checks passed.
- These checks use real isolated persisted configuration, canonical chat and workspace operations. ClawHub source resolution and runtime readiness are stubbed. They do not claim a fresh full Gateway, real-model or release-package run.

Fresh Gateway execution could not start: both the source-run `qaRuntime` profile and canonical `pnpm build:runtime` fail on the unchanged `744a001ea64` baseline in the standalone source-module URL guard: `highlight.js/lib/index.js` has no emitted output. The candidate runtime build was not attempted after reproducing that baseline failure. No guard was weakened and no OCM environment was started.

The contributor’s original isolated Gateway/UI evidence remains historical evidence for its original revision, rather than current-candidate runtime proof.

### Current-head CI

[CI run 43985583328, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43985583328/attempts/2) completed with 39 successful and 30 skipped jobs. One test job failed, with the CI gate failing downstream: [Windows updater fixture cases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43985583328/job/133715104835) hit an existing simulated-Windows/real-Linux broker mismatch (`EEXIST`, `mkdir '.'`) before SQLite snapshot readiness. The 17 observed failures include downstream assertions. All 20 determining/support files are byte-identical between the actual tested merge and its main baseline; the three changed Template Add files do not participate in that updater fixture. This failure is independently qualified as unrelated baseline evidence for the repository's native exception route. CI remains red; no full baseline replay is claimed.

The separate PR-description heading failure was fixed without a source change; [the latest context check passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43986307704).

prs.title: improve(ui): show project icons in the New Session project picker
prs.body:
Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/d0da0223-3f95-4864-b576-136e6b6b99f3)

## What Problem This Solves

The New Session project picker shows the same generic glyph for every project, while the chat header already shows a project's own icon.

## User Impact

User impact: registered projects show their own favicon in the picker rows and on the picker trigger. GitHub search results, recent repositories and a selected GitHub repository show the filled GitHub mark. The trigger's default icon is now `folder-git-2`. Projects without an icon keep a generic glyph.

## Why This Change Was Made

Picker rows have no session yet, so the existing session-keyed workspace icon route can't serve them. A sibling Gateway route, `/__openclaw__/project-icon/<projectId>`, resolves a project through the existing requester-specific visibility owner and reuses the existing workspace icon scanner and cache. The browser only names a project ID it can already list, never a host path. The route requires `projects.list` read access, applies the same per-project visibility policy as the project list, revalidates authority before responding, and keeps the remote-workspace exclusion from the session route. Hidden project IDs return 404 before scanning their checkout.

The UI reuses the existing `openclaw-workspace-icon` element, which now accepts a fallback glyph. The chat header and the picker share one route/auth helper, replacing the header-only version. The session menu's stroke reset was hollowing filled brand marks into outlines, so filled icons now keep their fill there and on the picker trigger. Project artwork loads lazily when a selected project or the opened picker needs it. Existing loading/error boundaries retain the fallback glyph. The boot manifest was regenerated after integration.

## Current maintainer verification

Compared main `d29fad4e3e687dedf683e38ec35b12cb85510637` with integrated candidate `90430eec1800ac74a755595c0264a67690037004`.

The current-main search field, autofocus, keyboard navigation, scroll area and footer were preserved when resolving the integration conflict. Optional artwork was removed from the unselected New Session startup path.

- Both revisions ran a matching production UI and isolated real Gateway. Two temporary Git projects were registered through `projects.register`: Northstar with an SVG favicon and Field Notes without artwork.
- Filtering, clearing the search, selecting a project and retaining its ID worked before and after. The candidate served and decoded the SVG in the row and selected trigger; the no-artwork response was 404 with a visible fallback.
- Pasting a GitHub repository URL and selecting it produced the GitHub-marked pending clone draft. No clone, model request or external GitHub search was needed or claimed.
- Desktop (1280 px), tablet-width (820 px), phone-width (400 px) and dark-theme browser checks passed. These are Chromium viewports, not physical-device qualification. The observed interaction runs recorded no layout-shift score outside recent user input.
- 29 Gateway HTTP/scanner/access cases and 529 UI cases, including mandatory canaries, passed. Coverage includes private registered projects after a writer warms the cache, access changes, unknown projects, local/remote workspaces and selected-trigger fallback.
- Full builds for the candidate and baseline passed. Scoped Gateway/UI type checks, lint, CSS lint, formatting and diff checks passed. The independent integrated-source review found no actionable P0–P2 defect.

The previous security repair remains: a read-only caller cannot retrieve artwork from a private registered project, including through a warmed cache. The original failure and fix are documented in the [earlier maintainer verification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197607#issuecomment-6828294550).

### Before / after

Same registered project and selection on the matched revisions. The outlined pair highlights the project row and selected trigger. Captures contain synthetic project data.

| Before — main | After — candidate |
| --- | --- |
| ![Generic project icon before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/08b12f16-2674-4f50-bd8c-3dacacb0223e) | ![Project favicon in the row and trigger after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/18070930-c959-4e58-ad36-a9ef5fa3dcd3) |

| Before — annotated | After — annotated |
| --- | --- |
| ![Generic row and trigger highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e89ee7d4-62dd-43e1-83c2-9aab86e2f725) | ![Matching project artwork highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b3a629a8-5261-4524-80ea-25e6109518c4) |

### Asset budget result

The paired, normalized production build still fails fixed asset caps. This is recorded as a remaining gate, not a runtime or test pass, and no limit was changed.

| Measurement | Change from matched main |
| --- | ---: |
| Initial-entry JavaScript, gzip | 0 B |
| New Session boot JavaScript, gzip | +661 B |
| Chat boot JavaScript, gzip | +531 B |
| Largest JavaScript chunk, gzip | +441 B |
| Total CSS, raw / gzip | +269 B / +50 B |
| Initial-entry CSS, gzip | +16 B |

Initial-entry and route-boot request counts are unchanged. Largest-CSS and chat-request-count absolute overages also occur on the baseline. The five byte-cap failures above include candidate growth and are not being classified as inherited-only failures. Hosted CI and any budget exception must be resolved before landing.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: improve(ui): give the Systems desktop more room with a collapsible health strip
prs.body:
On the Systems page the selected device is now the page title, with its status dot and device facts (for example "This computer · macOS 26.5") on the line under it. The Stats and Device details buttons stay at the right. The page no longer repeats the generic Systems title and subtitle, including its Learn more link, because the section sidebar already names the section.

Load, memory, disk and backups now sit in one row of equal cards directly under the device. One caption line follows: the volumes link on the left, the sample time on the right, and a small chevron that collapses the row.

Collapsed, the row becomes a single quiet line with the load, memory used of total and disk available of total. Clicking it expands the row again. This browser remembers the choice, and the buttons report their state with `aria-expanded`.

The desktop viewer sits in its own card with the theme's large corner radius and takes the rest of the page height. When the row is collapsed, the viewer grows into the space. Its toolbar keeps every control.

In the Systems sidebar, each device row shows the name on one line and its existing device fact under it. The group labels no longer show a count.

prs.title: fix(update): keep SQLite contention frames in bounded failure reports
prs.body:
Related #200289

## What Problem This Solves

Failed-update diagnostics can discard the SQLite call site when a Doctor failure's stack appears in the middle of long stderr.

## User Impact

Operators can inspect the contention error and up to 12 leading stack frames in the saved failure JSON linked from the update report and in repair prompts. This is a diagnostic improvement, not a root-cause fix for the SQLite lock or prolonged update reported in #200289.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing triage owner retains an optional `sqliteContentionCallSite` excerpt with the same secret/path redaction and a separate 1 KiB JSON-encoded UTF-8 cap. It survives artifact writing, reading, and prompt sanitization. Ordinary stderr retains its 384-byte head/tail limit, and the 8 KiB artifact and 4 KiB prompt-record limits still apply. Existing whole-record pruning can still omit older failed steps, and the byte cap can shorten long stacks.

The Markdown report already links this support JSON; its existing layout is unchanged. The failure-report documentation now describes the retained excerpt and bounds.

## Evidence

- Loss on the pinned base: `src/infra/update-run-step.ts:105-110` drops ordinary exit-1 Doctor stderr from the ledger projection; `src/infra/update-run-report.ts:433-440` bounds the summary to 300 characters and only emits stderr for signals or candidate snapshots. `src/infra/update-failure-report-artifact.ts:33-35` likewise restricts its stderr appendix to signal failures and links support JSON at line 246. That JSON loses the middle stack at `src/commands/triage-update.ts:371-374` (384-byte head/tail excerpt).
- Red on base `d29fad4e3e687dedf683e38ec35b12cb85510637`: the middle-block regression failed; 12 existing tests passed. Fixed: **33 passed across four named files**, including realistic multi-KB stderr, first-frame retention, the 12-frame limit, oversized UTF-8/JSON-escaped frames, redaction, repeated sanitization, rollback readers, prompt composition, and artifact writing.
- Focused command: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node timeout 120s pnpm test src/commands/triage-update.test.ts src/commands/triage-update-rollback.test.ts src/commands/triage-prompt.test.ts src/infra/update-failure-report-artifact.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Runner wall time: **6.66 seconds**; the changed-file command shard took 1.19 seconds. CI seconds are not yet available.
- Touched-file type-aware lint and `--type-check` passed through `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`; formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Broad validation is left to PR CI under the host's limits. The original production update incident was not reproduced.
- Test-audit and pr-simplify completed: extraction stays in the existing sanitizer with one optional schema field. Against the base: production +12 lines, tests +85 net lines, docs +2 lines.
- Independent local autoreview (Codex, P0-P2) reviewed the complete local candidate over the pinned base, including the full sanitizer and its artifact/prompt/redaction consumers: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. The reviewed candidate was committed unchanged as `7eceae3b44f3461db4e241af0f2de58e070b49fa`. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; hosted review follows the repository fallback.

Reported by @pestelence2k

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/78580230-7d1b-4329-a7dd-72554eb66323)

prs.title: fix(memory): memory forget preview fails with too many SQL variables on large sessions
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #200276

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where users who run `openclaw memory forget --session <id> --dry-run --json` on a session with enough indexed chunks (above SQLite's variable limit, 32,766 on stock SQLite) would get `Memory forget failed: too many SQL variables` instead of the promised read-only preview report.
- The same unbounded binding shape was also present in the purge path, so the actual forget (non-dry-run) would fail the same way once planning succeeded.
- **Related:** #164283 / #167838 fixed the same failure class for the session-memory origin-sync queries; this path (forget-index plan + purge) is a distinct query owner and was not covered. ClawSweeper review confirmed current main retains both unbounded count queries and asked for bounded bindings across preview and purge.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** Both SQLite count queries in the forget preview (FTS row count, vec0 row count) and both purge deletes (vector rows, chunk rows) now pass the selected chunk-ID set as a single bound JSON value consumed via `json_each(?)` (`sqliteStringSet`), instead of one SQL variable per ID. Counts and deletions stay exact; the read-only dry-run semantics and transaction ownership are unchanged.
- **Out of scope:** No schema, configuration, or policy changes; PostgreSQL paths unchanged (they already used `sqliteStringSet`).
- **Highest-risk area:** vec0 virtual table compatibility with `json_each`-based `IN` predicates. Verified empirically (count and delete both work on sqlite-vec v0.1.9) and covered by the regression test.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The regression test seeds `MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER + 1` chunks for one session with live FTS and vec0 tables and asserts exact preview counts, read-only preview, and the exact surviving rows after the real purge.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** `memory forget --dry-run --json` returns a bounded, non-mutating report for a single session regardless of how many chunks reference it, and the subsequent real forget purges exactly the selected chunks/FTS/vector rows while preserving survivors.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `extensions/memory-core/src/memory-forget-index-read.ts` (two preview count queries) and `extensions/memory-core/src/memory-forget-kernel.ts` (two purge deletes); regression test `bounds selected chunk bindings for selections above SQLite's variable limit` in `extensions/memory-core/src/memory-forget.sources.test.ts`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** isolated worktree at `aispace/worktrees/issue-200276` on Linux x64, Node v26.12.1, node:sqlite 3.54.0 (`MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER=32766`), sqlite-vec v0.1.9.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # RED on base (fresh worktree at origin/main):
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/memory-core/src/memory-forget.sources.test.ts -t "bounds selected chunk bindings"
  # -> WorkerTaskError: too many SQL variables (1 failed)

  # GREEN with this patch (same command):
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/memory-core/src/memory-forget.sources.test.ts -t "bounds selected chunk bindings"
  # -> 1 passed

  # Full affected test files:
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    extensions/memory-core/src/memory-forget.sources.test.ts \
    extensions/memory-core/src/memory-forget.test.ts \
    extensions/memory-core/src/memory-forget-recovery.test.ts
  # -> Test Files 3 passed (3), Tests 37 passed (37)

  # Type checks + kysely guardrails:
  pnpm tsgo:extensions && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test && pnpm lint:kysely
  # -> all exit 0
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  ✓ memory forget source removal > bounds selected chunk bindings for selections above SQLite's variable limit (25605ms)
  ```
  The test seeds `MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER + 1` (= 32,767) session chunks with live FTS + vec0 rows, then asserts: dry-run preview reports `indexChunks/ftsRows/vectorRows` all exactly 32,767 and leaves all tables untouched; the real forget leaves exactly the one survivor chunk in `memory_index_chunks`, `memory_index_chunks_fts`, and `memory_index_chunks_vec`; a tombstone is recorded for `target`.
- **Observed result after fix:** the planner returns a bounded, non-mutating report for a selection above SQLite's variable limit, and the purge deletes exactly the selected rows.
- **Before evidence (optional, visual changes encouraged):** on base `origin/main`, the same fixture fails during planning with `WorkerTaskError: too many SQL variables` before any report is produced (see RED log below); field report in the issue observed the same message from `openclaw memory forget --dry-run --json` on a 74,970-chunk install.
- **What was not tested:** a production-scale gateway database (the regression fixture uses a synthetic disposable database with 32,767 chunks); PostgreSQL deployments (behavior unchanged there — the same `sqliteStringSet` form was already used for PostgreSQL).
- **Proof tier:** L2
- **Proof limitations:** `pnpm exec oxlint` with the repository's `jsPlugins` (oxlint-boundary-guards) deterministically panics the native oxlint allocator on this Linux host (reproduced with an unmodified file in a clean worktree, oxlint 1.89.0). Lint was run instead with the repository config minus jsPlugins/solid (exit 0), and the diff was inspected for the jsPlugin-guarded calls (no `process.exit`, recursive readdir, `registerHttpHandler`, or `window.open` added). `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` passed. CI lanes pending.
- **Review state:** Awaiting CI + maintainer review.

prs.title: fix(release): freeze published stable version in maintenance notices
prs.body:
## Summary

Extended-stable release notices incorrectly named the publisher tooling package version as the current regular stable release. Resolve GitHub Latest for initial publication instead, then reuse the prepared or already-public notice for later rendering, canonical readback, and fresh-parent recovery. Standalone preflight uses the same distinction.

Main-derived maintenance-line retirement remains separate from the informational published version. Canonical source-body verification, retired-line approval, and docs-publication ownership remain enforced. This reuses existing release-body files; there is no new schema, state machine, retention policy, or release mutation. Existing renderer callers retain their prior defaults.

## Evidence

Validated patch: `f4d2e45592438dbaae12975e1c4223a991285b7a..e79892e96eb8e84da0316e8a049e00b18d5ce8bd`.

- Before the fix: four real shell/renderer and standalone-preflight regressions failed because tooling and published stable differed.
- Independent review identified fresh-parent recovery after Latest advances; both recovery regressions failed before the follow-up repair.
- Focused publication, preflight, and renderer suites: 57 passed across four files; wrapper wall time 10.06 seconds. Final draft-fixture change: 23 passed in 6.87 seconds.
- Scripts typecheck and tooling-test typecheck passed. Targeted lint, formatting, Bash syntax, and git diff whitespace checks passed.
- Fresh independent native source review of the complete five-file patch against `f4d2e45592438dbaae12975e1c4223a991285b7a`: previous recovery finding resolved, no remaining P0–P2 findings.
- Simplification: removed tooling version as notice authority and reused the existing prepared/public body rather than adding persistent context machinery.

## Hosted CI follow-through

Historical head `4ab8d0e731251109cc26de45611becd754169e69` failed CI run [43797970683](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43797970683), lint job [133072637830](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43797970683/job/133072637830): `src/agents/tool-search-prepared-catalog.ts:118:48`, `unicorn/prefer-structured-clone`. Source blob `5226ae58848652825503bb9c0558b70b73c7baf0` matched the original base, establishing inherited source attribution, not a green CI claim.

Current head `ac96ea4c816e79786a68cd7d05eee0faad0efa5a` applies the exact upstream #199944 correction (`54070dcab8c21f2b24cf0bf4e9c9439ff44cb753`), preserving intentional JSON semantics without a runtime behavior change. Focused lint, all 14 allowlist tests, formatting, and diff checks passed. Current-head CI and hosted review are tracked separately; prior-head reviews do not certify this update and no gate is waived.

## Limits and remaining gates

Proof uses production shell/renderer paths with synthetic GitHub responses. No live publication or authenticated Actions recovery was performed.

Native independent review is not local ClawSweeper/autoreview machine certification. Local ClawSweeper and autoreview were unavailable through the supported tools in this execution environment; no completed local machine review is claimed. This disclosure does not waive required review or CI gates.

prs.title: fix(release): generate notes from large commit histories
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes release-note generation aborting with `spawnSync git ENOBUFS` when canonical or release commit history exceeds the subprocess-output limit (originally 16 MiB; current main uses 64 MiB).

## User Impact

Release maintainers can generate audited notes from long histories without changing the selected refs or raising unrelated command limits. No runtime, public-ref, schema, permission, or retention changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both history readers now share a synchronous temporary-file-backed reader that decodes complete records, preserving ordering, commit bodies, UTF-8, and contribution matching. Temporary files are removed on completion or failure. Temporary disk usage scales with the log; existing commit collections still retain their normal history data. Concurrent-edit protection is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Original real-CLI reproduction on historical `v2026.9.35` and pinned main `f4d2e45592438dbaae12975e1c4223a991285b7a`: the 26,489,828-byte canonical log failed with ENOBUFS; the identical command passed with the fix. The isolated fixture uses an empty release range to exercise canonical discovery without GitHub requests; this is not full release acceptance.
- Original 18 MiB multibyte-history CLI regression was red before and green after. After integrating main `fd8d012d70c786b8fa33fbe296c9709f5238d2e7`, increased it to 66 MiB so upstream's 64 MiB buffer cannot make it pass without the streaming fix; verifies contribution membership.
- At `c81649b507cce4586d47ca3ef821bd7ee30e6e8f`: all 203 verifier tests passed (25.56s wrapper wall time), including the 66 MiB regression (992ms). Targeted lint, tooling typecheck, canonical formatting, and diff checks passed. Earlier related ledger suite: 17/17 passed.
- Conflict resolution preserves both sets of filesystem imports and upstream pinned-source/historical-issue behavior. Final change against pinned main remains two files, +52/−7; complete resulting diff independently inspected.
- Original fresh independent read-only review found no actionable findings. Supplementary checks covered record/chunk framing, UTF-8, and cleanup failures.
- Local ClawSweeper/Codex executables were unavailable. Local autoreview using its OpenClaw engine was attempted on the original complete patch at P0–P2: preflight passed, reviewer execution failed, and no verdict was produced. No alternate-route retry was made. This is not local review certification; prior-head review does not certify the updated head.

### Exact-head CI follow-up

Historical CI run `43797277538` at `7531034e3c6ab431cc0da5b33d5c3a361bd1bb3b` failed on unchanged base code: `src/agents/tool-search-prepared-catalog.ts:118:48`, `unicorn/prefer-structured-clone` (job `133070406129`; aggregate `133072296949`). The source blob matched original base; automated comparison was **unknown**, not a passing attribution check.

Applied the exact upstream #199944 correction (`54070dcab8c21f2b24cf0bf4e9c9439ff44cb753`), then retained it through the main integration. Focused lint and all 14 allowlist tests passed, with formatting/diff checks clean. The inherited lint defect is corrected; current-head CI and hosted review remain separate gates, not implied green by local proof. No gate was waived.

Related: #190042 addresses remote-first release-ref resolution; #167243 addresses separate consolidated-provenance recovery. Neither is the log-buffering repair provided here.

## Worked on by

- @vincentkoc
