prs.title: fix(auto-reply): a message sent after /stop fails replay admission when the Stop reply is delivered late
prs.body:
Closes #194303

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a message sent right after `/stop` can be recorded ahead of the Stop exchange in session history, and when its turn is replayed it fails admission ("Persisted user turn changed before replay admission") and is never answered, whenever the Stop reply reaches the channel late.

## User Impact

User impact: after `/stop`, the next message waits until the Stop reply is delivered and recorded, then runs and gets its answer, with the Stop exchange first in history. Input that was already waiting when the Stop arrived is still canceled, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

A `/stop` typed into the conversation it stops cancels its own controller source along with the pending input it selects, and that source is then consumed at once. The Stop reply records its `command-input` / `command-reply` exchange only after delivery, at dispatcher settlement (`dispatch-from-config.transcript.ts`, `sendReplyWithTranscriptMirror`). Nothing in the session owner holds the next turn across that delivery: the fast-abort path never claims a reply operation, so it gets none of the after-clear barrier ordinary replies register. A turn accepted after the Stop can therefore persist its user row before the Stop's rows land.

This change fixes the order the rows are written in. Once a stop request is recognized, and before the Stop selects anything, dispatch registers retention work on the Stop message's own source. The Stop still cancels that source, but the mailbox does not select past a source with unsettled work. When `finishFastCommand` hands the exchange to the direct dispatcher, it adds the dispatcher settlement as more retention work, bounded by `resolveFollowupAdmissionBarrierTimeoutPolicy`, the same bound an ordinary reply's barrier uses. The routed path already records inline. The source retires when the exchange is recorded, the delivery fails or the bound expires, and the next turn starts after the Stop's rows.

Unchanged: Stop's selection, command classification, the command history itself, and replay admission and its refresh.

#194336 and #194396 take the other route: both make command exchanges traversable for replay admission (`pre-persisted-user-turn.ts` and `session-manager-current-turn.ts`). ClawSweeper flagged that as changing the intent of `c2cb56c665e`, where ordinary commands stay context-bearing, with an owner decision required. This PR touches neither file and no replay or transcript predicate. A command row written before a turn still bars a stale replay exactly as on main. ClawSweeper's review of #194303 named this shape as the best fix: "Sequence Stop transcript recording through the existing session owner".

#195358 takes the replay route as well (`session-manager-current-turn.ts`, crossing context-free commands and `/stop` exchanges), and it reports the same unanswered follow-up after a delayed `/status`. This PR changes only the Stop path, so a delayed `/status` exchange behaves as on main here.

## Evidence

**Merged with main** (head `77660e883de`, main `5767fe7aae6`, macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1). The branch was 2,521 commits behind and conflicted in two files:

- `abort.ts`: main moved `FastAbortRequestParams` and `FastAbortResult` to `abort.types.ts`. `onAbortRequest` moved with them, and `dispatch-from-config.prepare-operation.ts` now imports `FastAbortResult` from there.
- `vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs`: main replaced `attempt-session-replay.test.ts` with `attempt-session-replay.steering.test.ts`. The Stop delivery test is listed after it.

Apart from those import paths, the diff against main is unchanged. Re-run on the merge:

- Regression tests, with main's `abort.ts`, `abort.types.ts` and `dispatch-from-config.prepare-operation.ts`: `attempt-session-replay.stop-delivery.test.ts` fails 2 of 2 with `SessionWorkStartChangedError`, and `dispatch-from-config.command-transcript.test.ts` fails 2 of 4 with `expected [ 'next-turn', 'command-input', …(1) ] to deeply equal [ 'command-input', …(2) ]`. On the merge: 2 of 2 and 4 of 4 pass.
- 15 test files, 201 tests, 0 failed: those two, the replay steering and cohort tests, the six `abort*` tests, the `dispatch-from-config` acp-abort, terminal-recovery and binding-activity tests, `reply-scaffolding.dispatch-from-config.test.ts` and `test/vitest-scoped-config.test.ts`.
- `tsgo`, all 7 lanes, 0 errors. oxlint and oxfmt clean. Test-lines (+239, allocation 239), line-cap, max-lines and assertion-safety ratchets pass.
- Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, local default runtime): `attempt-session-replay.stop-delivery.test.ts` 44.6 s cold and 12.8 s wall; `dispatch-from-config.command-transcript.test.ts` 18.9 s and 9.6 s.

Everything below is from the pre-merge head `272d4c60652`.

Base: main `51471b750b2`. Head: `272d4c60652`. macOS arm64. Everything below except the test-cost line ran with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` on Node 26.12.1 (the test-cost line uses `pnpm test` as written, on the local default Bun, which is what CI's shards run); the Gateway children log `native runtime: {"node":"26.12.1",...}`. Correction: my first run of this evidence used the default local runtime, OpenClaw's pinned Bun 1.4.4, and I labeled it Node. Every number below is from the re-run under Node. The conclusions hold, but the counts and timings changed: one mutation control behaves differently (noted below), the Gateway timings moved, and the changed-files run has 3 failures where Bun had 1, each explained below.

**Regression tests**, red on main (main's production files, these tests) and green here:
- `dispatch-from-config.command-transcript.test.ts` > "records a late-delivered /stop before the next turn's row", with and without an active run. It drives the real `dispatchReplyFromConfig` with a real reply dispatcher whose delivery is held, then starts the next turn. On main both cases fail with `expected [ 'next-turn', 'command-input', ...(1) ] to deeply equal [ 'command-input', ...(2) ]`. Here: 4/4, three runs.
- `attempt-session-replay.stop-delivery.test.ts` > "replays a turn admitted after a /stop whose reply is delivered late", for both replay-reader windows (initial selection and the selected reader). On main both throw `SessionWorkStartChangedError` (`SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED`). Here: 2/2, three runs.
- Mutation controls: releasing the retention as soon as the Stop returns, and retaining it only after the Stop's selection, each fail both files. Waiting for dispatcher idle instead of dispatcher settlement (the exchange is recorded by a settled task that runs after idle) fails the replay file. Under Node the dispatch file passes it; under Bun it failed both.

**ClawSweeper's commands from #194303:**
- `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-replay.test.ts`: 61/61.
- `... dispatch-from-config.command-transcript.test.ts abort.target-owner.test.ts src/config/sessions/transcript.test.ts`: 4, 54 and 46, all passed.
- `... src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts`: 14/14.

**Gateway run.** A real Gateway child from each tree's `dist`, a local fake Telegram Bot API and a scripted Responses provider, in one DM:
- The sequence: a long turn, a second message queued behind it, `/stop`, and a third message 300 ms later. The fake Bot API holds the Stop reply for 4 s.
- On main: the third message's turn sends its model request at 14.37 s, while the Stop reply is held until 17.33 s. `chat.history` afterwards reads `LONG-TURN`, `LATER-ACCEPTED`, `ANSWER-LATER`, `/stop`, `Agent was aborted.`
- Here: that turn starts only after the Stop reply is delivered (delivery at 17.08 s, typing at 17.22 s, model request at 17.31 s). History reads `LONG-TURN`, `/stop`, `Agent was aborted.`, `LATER-ACCEPTED`, `ANSWER-LATER`.
- Both: the queued second message never reaches the model, and the third is answered once.
- The local fake stands in for Telegram here. The Telegram E2E skill needs the OpenClaw Convex broker, and the Mantis proof workflow does not run on fork PRs.

On main, this harness reproduces the order but not the admission refusal itself. Its turns go from saving the user row to admission in under a second, and Stop replies held from 300 ms to 4 s never landed in that gap. The refusal is what the replay regression above pins, and what I saw live on 2026.10.10, twice, as reported in #194303.

**Checks at the head:**
- `pnpm tsgo:all`: pass.
- `ci-baseline-ratchets.mts --base 51471b750b2`: all ok. Test lines OK, slack 50. Merged onto current main `3855c896edd`, CI's baseline ratchets pass 9 of 9 (`Test lines OK: 6592607; ceiling: 6592607; slack: 0.`), and the line-cap ratchet passes.
- Test lines: `config/test-lines-allocations/194303-stop-exchange-order.txt` allocates 239, the net growth of the two regression files above (`dispatch-from-config.command-transcript.test.ts` +109, `attempt-session-replay.stop-delivery.test.ts` +117) and the replay test support they share (+20 -7). They pin the producer order this fix changes, which no cheaper layer can show: the late Stop delivery has to go through the real dispatcher and replay admission.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 51471b750b2`: every guard passes except "changelog attributions". That one fails identically on unmodified main, with the same 20 lines in files this PR does not touch: 18 `Thanks @steipete-oai` in `CHANGELOG/2026.6.8.md`, `CHANGELOG/2026.7.1.md` and `CHANGELOG/records/2026.6.8.md`, and 2 `Thanks @roboclaw-bot` in `CHANGELOG/records/2026.10.6.md`.
- `node scripts/test-projects.mts --changed 51471b750b2`: 942 files, 7751 passed, 3 failed.
  - `plugin-preparation-exec-argv.test.ts` > "publishes and loads the selected closure with the caller's real worker conditions" and `worker-task-pool.memory.test.ts` > "collects a completed large external payload while keeping the bounded worker warm" fail the same way on unmodified main under Node.
  - `provider-request-header-redaction.test.ts` failed once in the full run (`content-type` redacted too) and passes 9/9 alone, three runs out of three.

- Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Bun, the local default, macOS arm64, two runs each): `attempt-session-replay.stop-delivery.test.ts` 50.9 s (cold worker cache, 25.3 s of it compiling) and 15.2 s wall, 5.1 s and 4.7 s of tests; `dispatch-from-config.command-transcript.test.ts` 20.0 s and 9.8 s wall, 3.7 s and 2.2 s of tests. CI run 42556683622, Bun: `attempt-session-replay.stop-delivery.test.ts` 12.8 s Vitest duration, 6.6 s of tests (`checks-node-changed-1`); `dispatch-from-config.command-transcript.test.ts` 18.5 s Vitest duration, 5.4 s of tests (`checks-node-changed-4`).

Not covered: real Telegram, Linux, and the routed (non-dispatcher) reply path end to end. The routed path records inline and is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(subagents): private child results no longer show as delivered in the parent's context
prs.body:
Related: #173650

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the parent agent's runtime context and the `subagents` tool report `delivery=delivered` for a `completionTarget: "parent"` child when the result was only processed in a private turn and nothing was sent to the user.

## User Impact

User impact: after a private subagent completion, the parent's own facts no longer claim the result was delivered. It sees `delivery=consumed_privately`, so it has no runtime fact telling it the user already has the result. When the turn that processed the result did reach the user (a private turn that sent its final with `message`, or a yielded parent's resumed answer), the label stays `delivered`. Settlement outcomes, retries and channel delivery are unchanged, and nothing new is sent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main settles a private completion as `delivered` once the private requester turn processes it (`resolvePrivateCompletionDeliveryResult`: "no external receipt is owed"), and `docs/tools/subagents/announce.md` says later parent turns own any outstanding answer (#185388). This PR keeps that contract. The problem is the projection: `buildSubagentList` copied `delivery.status` into the list view and `buildActiveSubagentRuntimeContext` printed it as `delivery=delivered` under "Recently Completed Subagents" for 30 minutes, the same label an announced child gets. The `subagents` wait view copied it too. In #173650 (2026.10.3, `1ecf113bef64`, same rendering code) the registry recorded `delivered` with 0 messaging-tool outcomes and no channel send, and 13 minutes later, inside that block's 30-minute window, the parent told the user the result was already "in the thread above". That turn's request was not captured, so the label is the likely source of the claim, not a proven one.

- Settlement records the fact. Both settlement writers, `recordAnnounceDeliveryResult` (direct private turn) and the requester batch in `subagent-completion-mutation.kernel.ts` (settle wakes, including a yielded parent's resumed turn), call `recordPrivateConsumption`. It sets `delivery.consumedPrivately` for a `completionTarget: "parent"` result only when the host did not confirm a visible final (`requesterVisibleFinalDelivered`).
- `resolveSubagentDeliveryStatus` in `subagent-list.ts` reads that fact. The list view (runtime context and `subagents` list) and the `subagents` wait view both call it.
- My first revision inferred private-only consumption from a missing `requesterVisibleFinal`. That was wrong: it is a per-requester-turn dedupe receipt that the requester release deletes, that is bound only while `requesterTurnRunId` is set, and that the batch settlement never writes, so a yielded parent's answer that reached the user was labeled `consumed_privately`. The projection no longer reads it.
- Rows settled before this change have no `consumedPrivately` and keep reporting `delivered`. No migration: it is an optional field in `subagent_runs.payload_json`.
- Docs: the private parent completion section and the `subagents` tool reference.

Not changed:
- Settlement outcomes. The existing case "preserves private parent consumption and final evidence: private text" still pins `delivered: true` with no visible final and no send, and the QA scenario still waits for `delivery.status=delivered` on both private runs.
- No tracking of an update the model promised in prose. That is the open product question in #173650.
- "Child results awaiting delivery" keeps the raw status: rows there are outstanding, and the one way a `delivered` row lands there (a retained settle marker) is what #166270 removes.
- The private final text stays in the parent's model transcript as hidden assistant text. That can also feed an "already sent" claim; this PR does not touch it.

pr-simplify: one helper decides private consumption and both settlement writers call it; one helper projects it for both readers. No schema version and no change to settlement outcomes. Removed in the review round: the projection's reads of `requesterVisibleFinal` and `completionTarget`, and the seeded-receipt test. Deltas vs main: production +28/-2 in 6 files, tests +58 (allocation 58), QA scenario +50/-1, docs +9/-2.

## Evidence

**Merged with main** (head `dcd997f6f2f`, main `5767fe7aae6`, macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1). The branch was 2,873 commits behind. Main's #199695 reworked requester settlement: the requester batch now marks delivery through `markDelivered`, the registry records the requester's consumption as `requesterDelivery`, and a blocked completion whose input the requester already consumed (a private continuation cancelled by a restart, for one) is now also marked `delivered`. That last path is a third writer of the label this PR fixes. Conflicts:

- `subagent-completion-mutation.kernel.ts`: main's version, with `recordPrivateConsumption` after both `markDelivered` calls. The requester batch passes the outcome's `requesterVisibleFinalDelivered` as before. The blocked path passes `false`, because its outcome delivered nothing to the user.
- `subagent-registry-lifecycle-delivery.ts`: both imports.
- `subagents-tool.ts`: `deliveryStatus` keeps `resolveSubagentDeliveryStatus`, next to main's new `requesterDelivery` field.
- `subagent-completion-admission.requester-wake.test.ts`: both sides' new cases.

Main's cancelled-continuation test (`subagent-requester-delivery.test.ts`) now also checks the reported status: `consumed_privately` without a visible final and `failed` with one, through both the requester batch and the blocked path. Re-run on the merge:

- QA Lab `subagent-completion-direct-fallback` (mock-openai, qa-channel): passes 1/1, follow-up labels `consumed_privately`, `consumed_privately`, `delivered`. With main's 6 production files it fails at `[private-follow-up] later parent turn mislabeled private or announced child delivery`, labels `delivered`, `delivered`, `delivered`.
- With main's two writers (`subagent-completion-mutation.kernel.ts`, `subagent-registry-lifecycle-delivery.ts`), 4 cases fail with `expected 'delivered' to be 'consumed_privately'`: requester-wake `visible=false`, lifecycle `completionTarget=parent visibleFinal=undefined`, and the two `visibleFinal: false` rows of the cancelled-continuation test. With all 6 production files from main, `subagent-active-context.test.ts` fails `expected '## Recently Completed Subagents\nChil…' to contain 'delivery=consumed_privately;'` and the `subagents` tool case "reports private parent consumption without claiming user delivery" fails. All pass on the merge.
- Dropping only the blocked-path call fails only the `{"kind":"block","visibleFinal":false}` row.
- 18 test files, 405 tests, 0 failed: the 10 completion files, registry lifecycle (222 tests), lifecycle wake retry and settle-yielded, delivery state, list, active context, SQLite store, requester delivery and the `subagents` tool.
- `tsgo`, all 7 lanes, 0 errors. oxlint and oxfmt clean. Test-lines (+58, allocation 58), line-cap, max-lines and assertion-safety ratchets pass.
- Test cost of the changed `subagent-requester-delivery.test.ts` (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, local default runtime): 35.8 s cold and 7.5 s wall, 4 tests.

Everything below is from the pre-merge heads.

Base `f5f27c3ef6e`, head `519a4826f87`, macOS arm64. Correction: the QA lab run and the test suites in this section used the local default runtime, which since #172625 is OpenClaw's pinned Bun, not Node 26.12.1 as this line said. The real-model run, the upgrade runs and the Node re-run below are on Node 26.12.1.

**QA lab** `subagent-completion-direct-fallback` (mock-openai, qa-channel, real Gateway child). After both private children settle, the scenario sends one more DM in the private conversation, reads that turn's model request from the mock, and checks the `delivery=` label for the two private runs and the announced `visible` run.

| Source | Result | Labels (private-first, private-second, visible) |
|---|---|---|
| this branch | pass, 1/1 | `consumed_privately`, `consumed_privately`, `delivered` |
| main's 6 production files | fail at `[private-follow-up]` | `delivered`, `delivered`, `delivered` |

On this branch the same labels appear on the session's turns after `gateway.restart`, so the recorded fact survives the SQLite round trip. Both private runs still settle `delivery.status=delivered`. In the private conversation qa-channel saw only "Worker started." and the follow-up reply; 0 of 20 captured outbound events carried private child text or media.

**Real model, real Gateway** (head `cb4d3469f05`, macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1). An isolated Gateway from this build ran the bundled Telegram plugin against a loopback Bot API, with a real model behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`qwen3.8-27b-uncensored-r9700`; an earlier run with `qwen3.8-27b` gave the same labels for P, V and A). Every model request was recorded. One DM session. The model was told the exact `sessions_spawn` arguments and made the calls itself:

| Child | Spawn and parent's handling | Registry after settlement | Sent to the chat |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lp-private` | `completionTarget: "parent"`; the private turn ended `NO_REPLY` | `delivered`, `consumedPrivately: true` | only "Worker P started."; the child text 0 times |
| `lp-visible` | `completionTarget: "parent"`; the private turn sent the result with `message` (`final: true`) | `delivered` | "Worker V started.", then "Child V says LP191857-CHILD-V-..." |
| `lp-announced` | default target | `delivered` | "Worker A started." |
| `lp-yield-visible` | `completionTarget: "parent"`, then `sessions_yield`; the resumed parent's final was "Child Y says ..." | `delivered` | "Child Y says LP191857-CHILD-Y-..." |
| `lp-yield-private` | the same, but the resumed parent ended `NO_REPLY` | `delivered`, `consumedPrivately: true` | nothing |

The yielded parents were resumed by the requester-settle run (`announce:requester-settle:...:yield-1` in the Gateway log), the batch settlement path the Codex P2 was about.

On the next DM turn, the parent's own request listed all five under "Recently Completed Subagents": `consumed_privately` for `lp-private` and `lp-yield-private`, `delivered` for the other three. The model then called `subagents` `list` and `wait` (`timeoutSeconds: 0`); both returned the same five `deliveryStatus` values, and the model's reply listed them. After a Gateway restart on the same state, the same turn read the same five values in all three places. In the whole run the Bot API got 7 `sendMessage` calls: the five texts in the table and the two check replies.

Before the change, on released 2026.11.1 with the same private spawn (registry `completionTarget: "parent"`), the parent's context, `list` and `wait` all said `lp-private=delivered`. Without this PR, same five children with the same model: this PR's base `d44c9ad927d` and current main `3855c896edd` both label all five `delivered` in the parent's context, `list` and `wait`, before and after a restart, including the two silent ones.

**Upgrade from the latest releases**, 2026.11.1 (asked for) and 2026.11.2 (npm `latest`). Installed from npm into a scratch prefix, isolated state, the same real Gateway setup. The released CLI wrote `agents.defaults.subagents.maxConcurrent: 4`, `archiveAfterMinutes: 240` and `runTimeoutSeconds: 600`. The released Gateway ran a private child, an announced child and a check turn, then stopped.

This build on the same state:
- `config validate` is clean before and after main's own `doctor --fix --non-interactive` (exit 0: schema migrations 22 to 39 and 27 to 41, with pre-migration backups). Plain main `d44c9ad927d`, upgraded in a separate 2026.11.1 run (model `qwen3.8-27b-uncensored-r9700`; there the release's own private row had already ended `suspended`, the release failure below), gives the same `validate`, `doctor --fix` and settings results, and a new private child on it reads `delivered`.
- The three subagent settings read back unchanged. Doctor's only config edits are `meta.migrations.skillLibraryToolSplit`, `agents.entries.main {}`, `channels.telegram.groupAllowFrom`, three `skills.entries.*.enabled: false` and `wizard.lastRun*` (and, from 2026.11.2, `meta.lastTouchedVersion` to 2026.11.1, this build's package version).
- The session continued with the released build's turns in its history.
- The released build's rows load as they were stored: its private row has no `consumedPrivately` and still reads `delivered`, as described above for rows settled before this change. Its announced row reads `delivered`.
- A new private child on this build reads `consumed_privately` in context, `list` and `wait`, before and after a restart.

On 2026.11.2, the released build's own private completion failed in that run: `Session transcript keyed user is outside the current turn`, row `suspended`, `permanent_failure`. This build loaded that row as `suspended`. The failure is the release's, not this change's: in my runs it hit 4 of 6 private spawns on 2026.11.2 and 2 of 5 on 2026.11.1, against 0 of 11 on this head's build across five runs. Released 11.1 and 11.2 still treat a private completion turn as owing an answer, so a `NO_REPLY` there is retried as an empty response; main settles it quietly since #185388.

**Settlement**, through the real writers instead of a seeded receipt:
- Lifecycle receipt cases (`recordAnnounceDeliveryResult` via announce cleanup): parent without a visible final -> `consumed_privately`; parent with `requesterVisibleFinalDelivered` -> `delivered`; non-private -> `delivered`.
- Persisted requester batch (`mutateRequesterBatch` on SQLite): private batch with a confirmed visible final -> `delivered`; without -> `consumed_privately`.
- On the first revision `2a25638df1e` the visible-final case fails in both: `expected 'consumed_privately' to be 'delivered'`.
- Removing the visible-final check, the `completionTarget` check, the kernel call or the lifecycle call each fails exactly one of these cases.

**Projection**: `subagent-active-context.test.ts` and `subagents-tool.test.ts` render a settled `consumedPrivately` row as `delivery=consumed_privately` and `deliveryStatus: "consumed_privately"`.

**Focused suites**: 33 files, 668 tests passed (completion admission and kernel, registry lifecycle, delivery state, list, active context, requester yield, maintenance, SQLite store, catch-up integration, announce delivery and requester-settle cases, `subagents` tool, runtime facts, prefix stability, gateway prompt cache, recent-subagents prompt, silent-completion and announce-owner product tests).

**Focused suites on Node** (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`, Node 26.12.1, head `cb4d3469f05`): 6 files, 303 tests passed, 0 failed, including the requester-wake cases `keeps a private batch delivered only with a confirmed visible final`.

**Checks**: `pnpm tsgo:all` exit 0; oxlint and oxfmt clean; line-cap and assertion-safety ratchets OK. Test-lines: +54 with a matching allocation; at `f5f27c3ef6e` main itself is 10 lines over its ceiling (6421662 vs 6421652), so the ratchet reports "over by: 10" until main is back under. Merged onto current main `3855c896edd` at head `cb4d3469f05`, CI's baseline ratchets pass 9 of 9 (`Test lines OK: 6592422; ceiling: 6592422; slack: 0.`) and the line-cap ratchet passes.

- Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Bun, the local default, macOS arm64, two runs each): `subagent-completion-admission.requester-wake.test.ts` 67.2 s (cold worker cache, 22.7 s of it compiling) and 36.8 s wall, 30.3 s and 29.2 s of tests; `subagent-active-context.test.ts` 8.0 s and 7.2 s wall, 51 ms and 40 ms of tests; `subagents-tool.test.ts` 11.4 s and 6.4 s wall, 30 ms and 28 ms of tests. CI run 42424691592, Bun: `subagent-completion-admission.requester-wake.test.ts` 40.9 s of tests in a shared run (`checks-node-changed-compact-large32-1`); `subagent-active-context.test.ts` 108 ms of tests in a shared run (`checks-node-changed-compact-large32-1`); `subagents-tool.test.ts` 89 ms of tests in a shared run (`checks-node-changed-compact-large-22`).
- Over 30 s: `subagent-completion-admission.requester-wake.test.ts` runs 29.2 s of tests locally and 40.9 s in CI, but 39 of its 41 tests are existing ones this diff leaves unchanged (28.3 s locally, 39.7 s in CI). The 2 tests this PR adds take 0.86 s locally and 1.17 s in CI. They pin the stored delivery status after a real requester settlement: `resolveSubagentDeliveryStatus` reads `delivered` only when the settle outcome carries `requesterVisibleFinalDelivered: true`, and `consumed_privately` otherwise. They reuse the file's SQLite completion database because the fact under test is what `settleRequesterCompletionBatch` persists, which a hand-built record cannot show.

Not covered: real Telegram (the channel side is the Telegram plugin against a loopback Bot API, and the change does not touch channel code).

prs.title: fix(web): self-hosted web tool endpoints can redirect requests to other hosts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a self-hosted web tool endpoint (for example a private search instance) can redirect a request to a different host, and the request follows it with private-network access still enabled.

## User Impact

User impact: requests to a self-hosted web tool endpoint now stay on the hostname that was configured, on every redirect hop. Configured private endpoints and same-host redirects keep working.

Required action for some deployments: if a self-hosted endpoint relies on redirecting to a different hostname, configure that destination hostname directly. Such redirects are now rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Self-hosted endpoints need private-network access, but the shared self-hosted policy granted it without restricting the destination hostname. The policy is now derived from the configured endpoint URL using the existing URL hostname allowlist helper, together with the private-network grant. The allowlist is applied on each redirect hop, including environment-proxy dispatch. No new parser, guard or transport was added, and the helper's signature is unchanged for its consumers.

## Evidence

Run with Node 24.22.2 and pnpm 12.15.0. No live endpoint, provider or proxy was contacted; DNS and transport are mocked.

- The new regression (`src/agents/tools/web-guarded-fetch.redirects.test.ts`) calls `withSelfHostedWebToolsEndpoint` with the real redirect and network guards. On `main` it fails 2 of 5 cases: in both direct and proxy mode, a same-host hop followed by a hop to another host returns that host's response. On this branch all 5 pass, including private DNS, IPv4 and IPv6 endpoint controls.
- A second, separately written test set through the same helper: 41 failed / 13 passed on `main`, 54 passed on this branch. Off-host requests stop before the second transport call; private-service and same-host controls succeed.
- The affected consumer suites (guarded fetch, web search provider common, Brave, Firecrawl, web fetch tools): 100 tests passed.
- Full build, test typechecking, scoped lint, formatting and the test-line budget check passed. The regression adds 57 test lines with an equal dedicated allocation.

Gap: the broad `pnpm check` reports 22 line-cap errors outside this change, which reproduce with identical diagnostics on an untouched `main`. Live provider and proxy integration were not exercised.

### Real network dispatch (loopback)

The exported `withSelfHostedWebToolsEndpoint` helper was run from source with real DNS, real HTTP servers and the real transport. Nothing is mocked: no DNS or fetch replacement, no injected policy or dispatcher.

- Base: `b382a29a688a`. Head: `a2c15cc68999`, this change before it was rebased onto current `main`; the patch is identical. Node 24.22.2.
- Server A is the configured endpoint at `localhost`. Server B is a different hostname, `127.0.0.1`, on another port. Both listen only on loopback inside a network namespace with no external interface.
- A serves `/control` (200), `/same-host` → `/same-host-result` (302 then 200), and the chain `/search` → `/next` → B `/result` (two 302s). B logs every TCP connection and request.
- Proxy mode points `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` at a local forward proxy that supports CONNECT and logs what it forwards.

| Scenario | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| Direct, private control | 200 from A | 200 from A |
| Direct, same-host redirect | 200 from A | 200 from A |
| Direct, redirect to other host | **B receives `GET /result`; callback gets B's response** | rejected after A's second hop; B receives 0 requests and 0 TCP connections; callback not called |
| Proxy, private control | 200 from A | 200 from A |
| Proxy, same-host redirect | 200 from A | 200 from A |
| Proxy, redirect to other host | **proxy opens a CONNECT tunnel to B; B receives `GET /result`; callback gets B's response** | rejected after A's second hop; no CONNECT to B; B receives 0 requests and 0 TCP connections |

Head rejection message in both modes: `Domain policy: Blocked hostname (not in allowlist): 127.0.0.1. Permitted hostname patterns: localhost.`

Limits: loopback fixtures over plain HTTP, not a real search provider or TLS endpoint; this exercises the shared helper boundary, not a full agent turn. The latest-stable upgrade run is below.

### Upgrade trace: v2026.11.4 to this head

A real Gateway was started on each version against one persisted state directory, and `web_search` was invoked three times through `POST /tools/invoke` with the real SearXNG provider. The search servers are loopback HTTP stand-ins; no model takes part. On both versions requests started only after `/startupz` returned 200 with `status: started`.

- Release: `v2026.11.4` (`d843d6af39a4`). Head: `621237fdf4c6`. Frozen-lockfile install and full build passed on both. Node 24.22.2.
- Persisted setting: `plugins.entries.searxng.config.webSearch.baseUrl = "http://localhost:19390"`. The config file was byte-identical from release shutdown through head Doctor and head Gateway (SHA-256 `17f338d5eed03df4f52eb58948fd83550c4795e0ce6cad276e2b60c1e392206d`). No manual state edit and no downgrade override.
- Server A is the configured endpoint, `localhost:19390`. Server B is a different hostname, `ip6-localhost:19391`.

Provider requests in arrival order, all `GET`:

| Order | Server and request | v2026.11.4 | Head |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A `/search?q=ordinary&format=json` | 200 | 200 |
| 2 | A `/search?q=same&format=json` | 302 to A | 302 to A |
| 3 | A `/same-final` | 200 | 200 |
| 4 | A `/search?q=cross&format=json` | 302 to B | 302 to B |
| 5 | B `/cross-final` | **200; B's result returned to the tool** | **no request** |

Ordinary and same-host searches return results on both versions. The release follows the cross-host redirect and B receives 1 request. Head rejects `ip6-localhost` under the hostname policy, B receives 0 requests, and the tool returns a SearXNG `provider_error` payload.

Limits: this shows request behavior after a release-to-head state handoff, not a clean upgrade. `openclaw doctor` exited 0 on the release and 1 on head: head refused the `session-entry-state` migration before Gateway start and reported two shared-state inspection failures afterwards. Head's Gateway migrated state/agent schemas from 22/27 to 40/42 using its built-in generic-copy fallback (previous databases retained, conservation reported OK). This change touches only `src/agents/tools/web-guarded-fetch.ts` and its tests; `main` without it was not run as a control. The fixture is isolated, with no model configured and a restricted temporary directory, which produced the same warnings on both versions. Plain HTTP stand-in servers; no HTTPS. The agent-turn run is below. The same trace run from `v2026.11.3` gave the same request results.

### Agent turn through the Gateway: v2026.11.4 and this head

The same three searches, driven by full agent turns rather than direct tool calls. Each turn was sent with the documented `openclaw agent --agent main --message … --json` through the running Gateway, after `/startupz` returned 200. The agent loop made two model requests per turn: the model asked for `web_search`, the product ran the real SearXNG provider, and the model received the tool result and replied. The model is a deterministic loopback stand-in speaking the native Ollama protocol, not a hosted model; every model request body was captured. Same builds, setting and servers A and B as the upgrade trace, on a fresh state directory provisioned by the release.

| Turn | v2026.11.4: requests in order | v2026.11.4: tool result shown to the model | Head: requests in order | Head: tool result shown to the model |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ordinary | A `/search` 200 | results from A | A `/search` 200 | results from A |
| same-host | A `/search` 302, A `/same-final` 200 | results from A | A `/search` 302, A `/same-final` 200 | results from A |
| cross-host | A `/search` 302, **B `/cross-final` 200** | **results from B** | A `/search` 302, **no request to B** | **tool error, `provider_error`** |

All six turns completed with CLI exit 0 and a final reply. B received 1 request across the release turns and 0 across the head turns. On head the Gateway logged `Blocked hostname (not in allowlist): ip6-localhost`, and the model's reply reported the error instead of B's content.

Limits: model and search servers are loopback stand-ins; no hosted model, external search engine or HTTPS. The Doctor and state-migration observations from the upgrade trace apply unchanged to this run.

prs.title: fix(release): retry timed-out plugin source fetches
prs.body:
Related: #133368

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes plugin npm preflight and publication jobs failing immediately when their exact-source Git fetch times out transiently.

## User Impact

Release operators can recover from a transient fetch timeout within the existing job instead of restarting the publication workflow. Fetch attempts remain bounded; no publication is retried by this change. There is no installed-product behavior change or required migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both source-manifest read steps now use the existing Git owner’s retry-capable fetch operation. It preserves the selected immutable SHA, depth-one/blobless fetching, subprocess cleanup, and cancellation behavior, with up to three attempts and a five-second backoff. The manifest read remains outside the retry. The currently pinned action already supports this operation; no action pin or ownership policy changes are needed.

This is a maintainer-directed release-tooling repair. The release repair removes 20 production lines and adds 19 regression-test lines, without another retry implementation or test-only production seam. A subsequent patch-identical application of upstream #199944 corrects the inherited lint failure described below.

## Evidence

- **Red:** both workflow-entry regression cases failed against unchanged production with exit **124** and no manifest output after the first stalled fetch.
- **Green:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/plugin-release-git-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **47/47 passed**, 28.00 seconds in Vitest / 28.85 seconds wrapper wall time. Hosted CI time is not yet measured.
- The regression executes the actual YAML/Python policy entry points with a stalled first fetch followed by success, checks both attempts retain the same SHA, and requires one successful manifest read. Shared fixture assertions check descendant cleanup before subsequent operations and preservation of preexisting locks.
- Passed targeted root-scripts typecheck, changed-test lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and `scripts/check-workflows.mts` (including actionlint and zizmor).
- Fresh native independent source review found no P0–P2 findings on the complete original two-file diff based on `f4d2e45592438dbaae12975e1c4223a991285b7a`, including direct inspection of the pinned action’s fetch/export contract. Release-repair commit `44f7ad857814fb4d39fcc77050c02fe38d2cf717` is patch-identical to that reviewed snapshot. **Local review tools were unavailable; this was not machine-validated autoreview or a clean ClawSweeper certification.**
- Hosted ClawSweeper review subsequently reported no actionable findings at `cc8e2b13c83990e5c40e7735fa1f5b0fc7062451`. That prior-head review is not a certification of the subsequent lint correction or current head.
- The lint correction was verified patch-identical to upstream `54070dc` (#199944), with focused lint red/green proof, **14/14 suppression-guard tests**, and formatting checks. Existing valid release-repair proof was retained rather than unnecessarily rerun.

**Proof limits:** controlled Git subprocess I/O, virtual fetch deadlines/backoff, and accelerated TERM escalation; the harness uses the current local owner, with pinned-owner compatibility source-inspected. No live release fetch, remote release-workflow dispatch, OIDC, or npm publication was exercised. Publishing this PR is separate from release-publication proof.

## Hosted CI follow-through

**Historical failure:** at old head `cc8e2b13c83990e5c40e7735fa1f5b0fc7062451`, CI run [43798181775](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43798181775) failed lint job [133073262681](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43798181775/job/133073262681): `src/agents/tool-search-prepared-catalog.ts:118:48`, `unicorn/prefer-structured-clone`; its aggregate CI gate was also red. The failing source blob `5226ae58848652825503bb9c0558b70b73c7baf0` was identical at the original base and that old head. This established an inherited failure; it was not passing proof or a waiver.

**Current correction:** commit `4a5d6dfe0915282e9fc65b09092541de71bcfd90` applies the exact upstream #199944 correction: document why JSON encoding intentionally drops undefined metadata, and register that intentional suppression in the existing guard test. Patrick Erichsen's authorship and both human co-author trailers are preserved. Published head `81ad078c4c2093b94710679119e6ef944a329caf` has the same tree as the prepared correction. Fresh checks are attached to that head and pending; the old lint failure does not describe the corrected source, and local lint success does not claim current hosted CI is green. Hosted review remains separate from CI.

## Worked on by

- @vincentkoc

prs.title: docs(install): describe the Ansible user service and onboarding accurately
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Ansible install guide sends operators to a system service that openclaw-ansible never creates (`sudo systemctl status openclaw`, `journalctl -u openclaw`, `/opt/openclaw`, `/tmp/openclaw-setup.sh`) and lists systemd hardening (`NoNewPrivileges`, `PrivateTmp`) that the installer does not apply.

## User Impact

User impact: operators following `docs/install/ansible.md` now get commands that work on an openclaw-ansible install: onboarding with `openclaw onboard --install-daemon`, then `openclaw gateway status`, `systemctl --user status openclaw-gateway.service` and `openclaw logs` as the `openclaw` user. The page no longer claims Tailscale is always installed or that the Gateway unit is hardened. No behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page now follows what openclaw-ansible `main` (238f100) and its own docs state:

- The role prepares the `openclaw` user and directories; `openclaw onboard --install-daemon` creates `openclaw.json` and the systemd **user** unit `openclaw-gateway.service` ([`roles/openclaw/tasks/openclaw.yml`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-ansible/blob/main/roles/openclaw/tasks/openclaw.yml), [`docs/installation.md`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-ansible/blob/main/docs/installation.md)). There is no `/opt/openclaw`, no system unit `openclaw`, and no setup script in `/tmp`.
- "Do not assume `NoNewPrivileges`, `PrivateTmp` … are enabled by this installer" ([`docs/security.md`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-ansible/blob/main/docs/security.md#native-gateway-service)).
- Tailscale and its UFW rule only apply with `tailscale_enabled=true` (default `false`); Node comes from NodeSource with the major set by `nodejs_version`.
- The service user is deliberately not in the `docker` group, so Docker troubleshooting runs from an administrator account. The sandbox build step now points to [Images and setup](/gateway/sandboxing/images-and-setup) and an administrator-owned checkout instead of running a service-user-writable script as root.

The page still uses `./run-playbook.sh` like the openclaw-ansible README.

## Evidence

Docs checks on head `d761a50bb91` (UTC 2026-11-10 21:25–21:27): `pnpm format:docs:check` (1422 files clean), `pnpm docs:check-mdx` (1434 files passed), `pnpm docs:check-links` (16536 internal links, 0 broken), `pnpm lint:docs` (0 issues).

Live check of the documented commands on a fresh Hetzner Ubuntu 24.04.4 server after openclaw-ansible 238f100 (+ `-e nodejs_version=24.x`) and `openclaw onboard --install-daemon`, OpenClaw 2026.11.2, from an interactive `sudo -i -u openclaw` shell (UTC 2026-11-10 21:20–21:22):

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| System unit `openclaw` (old page) | not created by the role (its `docs/architecture.md`: "does not create … `/etc/systemd/system/openclaw.service`"); onboarding installed `~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway.service` |
| `systemctl --user status openclaw-gateway.service` | `active (running)` (the role's `.bashrc` sets `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`) |
| `openclaw gateway status` | `Service: systemd user (enabled)`, loopback `ws://127.0.0.1:18789` |
| `openclaw logs` / `openclaw logs --follow` | Gateway log lines from `/tmp/openclaw/openclaw-<date>.log` |
| `systemctl --user show openclaw-gateway.service -p NoNewPrivileges -p PrivateTmp -p ProtectSystem` | `NoNewPrivileges=no`, `PrivateTmp=no`, `ProtectSystem=no` |
| `journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway.service` | "No journal files were opened due to insufficient permissions" (system user, UID 999), so the page does not suggest it |

prs.title: docs: help readers understand PRs without reading the code
prs.body:
Related: #200314

## What Problem This Solves

A PR can describe an internal code change without telling someone who uses OpenClaw what was broken or what will work better. Readers then have to inspect the diff or ask for a rewrite just to understand its purpose.

## User Impact

PR authors get concrete examples of titles and problem statements that readers can understand without knowing the implementation. Validation summaries explain what was checked before presenting commands and logs.

There are no new required sections, checklists, or review gates. Internal-only changes still describe the actual developer or operator workflow rather than inventing a user benefit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Strengthen the existing template instead of adding another policy document:

- Contrast a clear title such as “keep automations running when you open another chat” with an implementation-only description.
- Ask for the task, what goes wrong, and why it matters in a short problem statement.
- Lead evidence with the behavior checked and its result, leaving technical detail in links or an optional disclosure.

Only `.github/pull_request_template.md` changes. Its existing headings, maintainer-edit guidance, and wording used by the triage bot remain intact.

## Evidence

- Reviewed the revised examples against the unclear wording that prompted the rewrite in #200314.
- Existing template-consumer checks passed, confirming that an untouched template is still recognized correctly. **No tests were added.**
- Documentation sanity, Markdown formatting, and whitespace checks passed.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed the final committed range and found no actionable correctness or security issues.

prs.title: feat(doctor): check OpenClaw ID member roles and honor an optional roles default
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor does not know that `gateway.roles.default` is optional or that OpenClaw ID member roles come from `gateway.roles.definitions`. With role definitions and no default, it wrongly reports that automations will lose owner access. It also has no check for a member whose role is not defined, for missing preset roles, or for role settings that have no effect.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw doctor` reports member-role problems in plain words and can write missing preset roles after asking.

- Fixed: with role definitions and no default, Doctor no longer reports that an automation "will lose access at the next run" or that owner status is unverified.
- New checks when OpenClaw ID is on:
  - a member whose role has no definition, with the member and role named;
  - a missing preset definition, with a repair that writes it. The repair asks first and says that the config file is rewritten as JSON and loses its comments;
  - a sandbox-required role held by a member, or set as the default, when no sandbox backend is available.
- New check for any Gateway: stored role assignments with no `gateway.roles.default`, which means named-role enforcement is off and the assignments have no effect.
- A Gateway with no `gateway.roles`, and one with a default set and OpenClaw ID off, get the same Doctor output as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The cron ownership checks and the replay script now ask whether named-role enforcement is on, as runtime admission does, and no longer test for the presence of `gateway.roles`.
- The member checks read the local claw record, so they work with the Gateway stopped. A claw that has never linked has no record and gets no warning. A record that exists and cannot be read, or whose member list is malformed, is reported with a fixed message that contains nothing from the record.
- The preset repair uses the same code as turning on OpenClaw ID: it adds only missing presets and never writes `default` or `assignments`.
- Docs for roles and OpenClaw ID describe the optional default, member presets, which role applies to a connection, and what a sandbox-required role does and does not contain.

## Evidence

- Doctor suites: 31 tests in 3 files pass at the review-fix commit. A reviewer separately ran 94 tests in 6 files, covering Doctor, activation presets, the config schema and Doctor's consent modes, all passing.
- Core and test typechecks, lint, format and ratchets pass.
- Independent review found no P0 or P1 and three P2 in the new member check: a corrupt record could put a fragment of an invite key into Doctor's output, a malformed member list passed silently, and a never-linked install got a false warning. The fourth commit fixes all three, with a test that plants a synthetic secret in a corrupt record and asserts none of it is printed. A second review found nothing.
- Two docs anchor checks fail the same way on `main`, in pages this PR does not touch.

Not run: a whole-Doctor output comparison against the parent, a repair while a live Gateway reloads, and real Docker or Podman probing.

Rebased onto main after #197782 merged; six commits, replayed without conflicts. This PR also changes one production path outside Doctor: when the local claw record stores members in chunks (as current main does), a chunk whose member collection is not an object is now an error instead of being read as if valid. That is what lets Doctor report a malformed member list; three existing Doctor assertions depended on it after main moved to chunked storage. After the rebase the Doctor checks were checked against what landed underneath: the guest preset and required sandbox, start-of-change role validation from the role picker, and administrator member roles. 135 focused tests, 197 Doctor, cron and access tests (2 PostgreSQL-gated skips) and 7 storage tests pass, with typechecks, static checks and ratchets.

Known, not changed here: the development replay script (`scripts/dev/cron-context-replay.mts`) fails with "User profile catalog is not ready" when replaying a job under a named `gateway.roles.default`; it reproduces the same way on main, and Doctor's own checks are unaffected.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Package Acceptance rejecting a just-published OpenClaw release with npm ETARGET because the source checkout applies a seven-day dependency cooldown to the candidate itself.

## User Impact

Release operators can verify the exact package immediately after publication without disabling dependency cooldowns or changing package integrity checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing candidate pack runner now excludes only the root openclaw package from the release-age filter for that download. It still validates the package spec, suppresses package scripts, preserves the selected tarball identity, and runs the existing digest and tarball checks. No repository-wide npm configuration or dependency installation policy changes.

## Evidence

- Reproduced with the actual source=npm CLI on main f4d2e45592438dbaae12975e1c4223a991285b7a: exact openclaw@2026.11.5-beta.4 failed ETARGET under npm 11.20.0 because it was younger than seven days.
- Same CLI with the fix downloaded that exact version and passed the complete tarball integrity checker. SHA-256: 0be5af77a78a5b7860b8e20e5f76267491ed07883ce40c653f9443bd78f47a7d. No publication or hosted acceptance workflow was dispatched.
- Added a real-npm regression using a private loopback registry and fresh package timestamp: red ETARGET on base, green after repair; another fresh package remains rejected under the same configuration. The regression ran using pinned npm 12.2.1 under the repository test runtime.
- Candidate resolver: 45/45 tests; npm runner sibling: 9/9 tests. Combined wrapper wall time 6.16 seconds; changed file test time 2.27 seconds. Hosted CI duration pending.

prs.title: Preserve complete MP3 audio when creating macOS Opus CAF voice attachments
prs.body:
# Preserve complete MP3 audio when creating macOS Opus CAF voice attachments

## What Problem This Solves
On macOS, direct MP3 → Opus CAF conversion with afconvert can exit successfully while retaining only the first segment of a concatenated MP3. The synthetic regression fixture decodes to 48.074 seconds, but direct conversion produces only 3.310 seconds.

## Change
For MP3 → CAF only, decode with FFmpeg to mono 24 kHz signed 16-bit PCM WAV, validate its RIFF structure, then encode with afconvert. Probe the resulting CAF and reject unexpected format or frame count. Other input formats continue using direct afconvert. All stages share the existing default 5-second timeout budget; temporary files are cleaned on success and failure.

Long clips now produce complete voice memos when conversion fits the budget, or retain the original MP3 attachment when conversion fails or exceeds it. A loaded host or sufficiently long clip may therefore receive an MP3 attachment rather than a voice memo; previously it could receive a silently truncated voice memo. No per-stage reset extends the total conversion budget. The once-only warning is neutral: a conversion failure does not necessarily mean FFmpeg is missing.

## Historical evidence (superseded by executed proof below)
- Native macOS regression compares decoded PCM frame counts, allowing one 20 ms Opus packet of padding; it skips on non-macOS hosts or when FFmpeg is unavailable. Both the availability probe and PCM decoder resolve FFmpeg through the same trusted-system `resolveFfmpegBin()` helper as production, not an independent PATH lookup.
- Unit coverage includes malformed WAVs, shared timeout exhaustion, missing FFmpeg, encoder/probe failures, cleanup and non-MP3 routing.
- Original author-reported proof (before the corrections below): focused red run against the original module fails; candidate focused tests pass (39/39); targeted oxlint and git diff whitespace checks pass.
- Original author-reported native red/green after aligning the FFmpeg lookup: original module produced 79,440 decoded frames; the fixed module produced 1,154,088 against 1,153,775 input frames (313-frame difference, within 480).
- No independently verified native macOS run or live Messages playback is claimed by the current readiness review.

Original reported patch SHA256: `8c7477de221cb321477eaa91b12e3676ab6de5ff631980d809c57350f4f36f6b`.

### November 14 readiness continuation
- Correction `5880b70884bc1a95164db2ccf1a7527e0eec2bfd` gives `probe-timeout` otherwise-valid two-frame output and reserves 99 frames for `probe-mismatch`.
- Current signed candidate: `a9a084486e3df10193dfa9ac5ab9faa9f53a4619`. The terminating WAV-header validator now uses a function declaration for strict control-flow narrowing; the corruption fixture uses Buffer byte methods. Independent two-file and full-candidate source reviews found no P0–P2 findings. `git diff --check` passed.
- After verifying the fork head and unchanged workflow files, CI run `43602980089` was approved through GitHub's supported fork-run approval endpoint. Attempt 2 completed with failure. Production types, all five core test-type stripes, SDK declaration/package boundaries, changed formatting/lint, and all five core lint stripes passed. The previous audio type diagnostics and missing SDK-artifact failures are resolved.
- In job `132481381272` (`checks-node-changed-4`), `src/media/audio-transcode.test.ts` passed **27/27 tests**, including the corrected probe-timeout case. The native macOS test was **skipped on Linux**, not passed as native proof.
- The only remaining failing work lanes are `check-test-types` (`132481749728`) and browser UI/build (`132481380912`). Their errors exactly match scheduled-main run `43599691199`: `state-read-worker-bench.ts:373` reports possibly undefined `entry.tasksCompleted`, and the identity worker has 240 evaluated modules against a 220 budget. These files are unchanged by this PR. Main commit `d43de8d733674c942c8eb7bfb7333a30de4f910f` separately addresses the eager idle-GC logging import behind the worker budget failure. No budget was relaxed here.
- The requester approved the FFmpeg-required PCM-first route with original-MP3 fallback. Timeout-check-removal mutation proof remains blocked: the required secretless AWS route failed during credential discovery before allocating a lease or running contributor code. No alternate credential-hydrated or trusted-local execution was used.
- The native review remains `NEEDS WORK` pending mutation proof and the separately tracked executed native/shipped-delivery proof. No merge, backport, or release was performed.

## Fixture rights and regeneration
`src/media/fixtures/tts-ten-segment.mp3` is entirely mathematical sine tones generated offline, not speech, recordings, model output or private audio. It is dedicated under CC0 1.0 Universal (including the fallback license): https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/legalcode.en . No FFmpeg binary is distributed.

Generation uses ten separate FFmpeg sine inputs at frequencies `440 + 37*n` Hz (n=0..9), mono 24 kHz, libmp3lame VBR quality 2. Segment durations in seconds: `3.3, 5.3, 5.475, 5.2, 4.9, 4.075, 6.55, 4.125, 4.025, 4.375`. Encode each independently, then concatenate the MP3 bytes without remuxing, retaining each segment’s Xing header and delay/padding fields. Set each Xing encoder-identification field to `LAME` followed by five spaces, blank encoder-version digits elsewhere, and remove ID3 and format/stream tags. This is a deliberately constructed triggering layout, not a claim about an original encoder. Other FFmpeg/libmp3lame versions may produce different bytes.

The accompanying `fixture-build.py`, `fixture-README.md` and `fixture-LICENSES.md` provide the generator, detailed construction and rights statement. Fixture size: 166,176 bytes. SHA256: `7b2d8a3b1244383a4cfc3beaa57ba756c0d76c7d485fa80f927a458bdb60c0f0`.


Addresses #197531.

## November 16: independently executed converter proof

The earlier statements about unexecuted native and timeout-mutation proof are superseded by the evidence below. These results executed source `a9a084486e3df10193dfa9ac5ab9faa9f53a4619`, not a new run on current head `d51696b32be02844d1801dd31819912401859b88`. The converter and both named audio test files are byte-identical between those heads; broader current-head CI is separate.

- [Run 43768728614 / job 132979610823](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43768728614/job/132979610823): both focused budget cases passed; the timeout-removal mutation failed both, specifically showing a reset `[5000, 5000, 5000]` instead of shared `[5000, 2000, 1000]`. Mutation evidence is not baseline-red proof. Real FFmpeg/afconvert/afinfo control, tiny-budget rejection, and scratch cleanup also passed.
- [Run 43772299539 / job 132990706530](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43772299539/job/132990706530), tooling `d43289d7095dadf3c3adc9c41792281cb1e67a12`, exercised the committed ten-segment synthetic fixture on macOS 27.0.1 arm64 with FFmpeg 9.0.2. The unchanged original converter from `e80a6dd9fdb4c7ce724472dd5d1b216afb4e70a7` yielded **3.310 seconds / 79,440 decoded frames**; the fixed converter yielded **48.087 seconds / 1,154,088 frames**, versus 1,153,775 independently decoded input frames. The 313-frame difference is within the 480-frame padding allowance.
- All ten independently sampled tone frequencies matched their source segment identities. Fixed conversion took 731 ms inside the existing five-second budget. Both variants left no conversion workspaces. The original-module run failed specifically at frame preservation (exit 1); fixed passed (exit 0). This is original-module differential proof in candidate dependencies, not a full historical-baseline build.

## November 17: installed-package fallback and attachment dispatch

[Run 43984943020 / job 133710563419](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43984943020/job/133710563419) passed on a disposable secretless macOS runner, using reviewed tooling `4b1f4fcff29fd77f0510dc04935a13d3003dc522` and exact current source `d51696b32be02844d1801dd31819912401859b88`. The source was packaged with the canonical packaging helper and installed in a clean directory. Installed package version was `2026.11.4`; tarball SHA256 was `d88dc20ab104bb6f4ce4c64e44879941f68b8c77593a0c614b499a6e35f3fc63`.

- The installed Gateway loaded a synthetic speech provider and recording channel through public plugin APIs. Real FFmpeg was absent from all six trusted macOS binary directories; no converter mock or PATH-only substitution was used.
- Public runtime TTS attempted MP3-to-CAF conversion and emitted the real neutral fallback warning. Its persisted attachment retained the original `.mp3`, all **166,176 bytes**, and SHA256 `7b2d8a3b1244383a4cfc3beaa57ba756c0d76c7d485fa80f927a458bdb60c0f0`.
- The installed Gateway's normal `send` RPC dispatched that persisted attachment to the synthetic recording adapter. The independently read adapter input had the same extension, byte count, and SHA256. This is installed TTS and outbound adapter-dispatch proof, not native Messages transport.
- Converter and both audio test blobs were rechecked identical to the retained native-proof source. No completed native, budget, or mutation proof was rerun; all four previously completed hosted jobs were skipped.

**Required device-delivery gap remains:** actual Messages transport and receiving-device playback were not exercised. Those explicit acceptance requirements are not downgraded to optional checks. No RFR or merge-ready claim is made.

prs.title: fix(templates): failed `templates add` leaves the new agent behind
prs.body:
Closes #196048

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw templates add` leaves the newly registered agent and its workspace behind when Add fails after registering it (for example a cron Template while the Gateway is unreachable), and each retry adds another agent (`-2`, `-3`).

## User Impact

User impact: a failed CLI Add now removes the agent it created, so retrying after fixing the cause creates the same agent ID instead of a duplicate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI rollback removes the agent with `pruneAgentConfig` but wrote config without `allowedAgentRosterRemovals`, so `assertCanonicalAgentRosterRetainsEntries` rejected the write. The rollback now passes the new agent's ID, as `openclaw agents delete` does. The Gateway Add path rolls back through `deleteAgentConfigEntry` and is unaffected.

Not changed here: the CLI still prints `Added agent: <id>` before the failure message even when the rollback removed the agent. That line predates this change.

## Evidence

Isolated install (temp state dir and home, unused Gateway port, Templates enabled in Labs), Template with one cron job, run through `pnpm openclaw`:

- main f615e96: exit 1 with `agent cleanup failed: Config write would drop agent roster entries without an explicit deletion: incident-triage.`; `agents list` still shows `incident-triage`, the workspace remains, and a retry adds `incident-triage-2`.
- This branch: exit 1 with the Gateway error only; `agents list` shows only `main`, no workspace is left, and a retry adds `incident-triage` again.
- Control (same Template without the cron job): adds with exit 0 on both.

<details>
<summary>Terminal output</summary>

main f615e96:

```
$ openclaw templates add ./cronOnly
Added agent: incident-triage
Workspace: <tmp>/hm-red/.openclaw/workspace-incident-triage
Gateway did not apply the Template agent configuration in time: gateway config.get requires credentials before opening a websocket
Fix: configure gateway.auth token/password, pair this device, or pass --token/--password.
Config: <tmp>/st-red/openclaw.json agent cleanup failed: Config write would drop agent roster entries without an explicit deletion: incident-triage..
exit=1
$ openclaw agents list
- main (default)
- incident-triage (Incident triage)
$ ls ~/.openclaw | grep workspace-
workspace-incident-triage
$ openclaw templates add ./cronOnly   # retry
Added agent: incident-triage-2
Gateway did not apply the Template agent configuration in time: gateway config.get requires credentials before opening a websocket
Config: <tmp>/st-red/openclaw.json agent cleanup failed: Config write would drop agent roster entries without an explicit deletion: incident-triage-2..
```

This branch:

```
$ openclaw templates add ./cronOnly
Added agent: incident-triage
Workspace: <tmp>/hm-green/.openclaw/workspace-incident-triage
Gateway did not apply the Template agent configuration in time: gateway config.get requires credentials before opening a websocket
Fix: configure gateway.auth token/password, pair this device, or pass --token/--password.
Config: <tmp>/st-green/openclaw.json
exit=1
$ openclaw agents list
- main (default)
$ ls ~/.openclaw | grep workspace-
$ openclaw templates add ./cronOnly   # retry
Added agent: incident-triage
```

Control on both:

```
$ openclaw templates add ./mcpOnly
Added agent: incident-triage
exit=0
$ openclaw templates add ./mcpOnly   # retry
Added agent: incident-triage-2
```

</details>

New test in `add-stateless.test.ts` uses the real config-file write (the existing tests inject `commitConfig`); it fails on main with the guard error and passes with the fix. `add-stateless.test.ts` 20/20; `templates-cli`, `gateway-add-apply`, `gateway-add-apply.plugin-batch` and `packages.runtime` 79/79. `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint and format check are clean on the touched files.

prs.title: improve(ci): shorten candidate registry preparation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Release candidate registry preparation repeatedly starts the same Node/tsx build tooling for every companion plugin. The measured candidate producer spent **92 seconds** preparing 55 plugins.

## User Impact

Internal release validation improvement; no product behavior changes. Five interleaved local pairs of the actual 55-plugin cohort reduced median registry creation from **64.51s to 40.62s (23.89s / 37.0%)**, with identical artifacts. **Whole-FRV wall-time improvement is not measured** and can be zero when independent CI/native work dominates.

## Why This Change Was Made

Build and pack up to four plugins **serially** in each Node/tsx child, reducing outer starts from 55 to 14 while retaining all 55 builds, all 55 npm packs, source restoration, runtime-floor admission, identity checks, hashing, and final registry verification. No extra jobs, parallel builds, runner slots, setup, retries, or downstream barriers.

The build/pack operation has one shared owner and two small CLI adapters. A distinct batch entry detects support in the selected source; frozen releases without it keep their existing combined or separate entrypoints. This extends—not reverses—the deliberate serial/shared-startup policy in [e827c232](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e827c232db3f6c582933659275172eca7b4cae0f).

Memory tradeoff: median maximum-process RSS rose **8.7%** (1,020,236 → 1,108,884 KiB), within overlapping sample ranges; maximum observed RSS was slightly lower (1,151,596 → 1,135,496 KiB). An unbounded prototype was rejected for a >20% RSS increase. These are not aggregate process-tree memory measurements. Explicit build/pack failures stop immediately; malformed successful pack output is rejected at the end of at most four serial packages, before publishing a registry manifest.

## Timing and regression evidence

Measured candidate `ee6e8e2c9a18dc1637e19908179504c14d586806`; base `3f33eb94d5b0f5a5371a16ccc72a53b8d476ea85`. Registry implementation and its three test/fixture files are byte-identical in the current integration head.

| Pair | Base wall | Batch wall | Base peak RSS KiB | Batch peak RSS KiB |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 71.68s | 37.32s | 1,020,236 | 1,108,884 |
| 2 | 57.99s | 41.10s | 1,151,596 | 718,624 |
| 3 | 64.51s | 40.62s | 773,524 | 1,135,496 |
| 4 | 66.30s | 44.35s | 768,452 | 1,103,844 |
| 5 | 62.16s | 40.33s | 1,110,664 | 1,111,460 |

- Same 55-plugin cohort, source, Node 26.12.1, npm, existing caches and serial workload; alternating AB/BA order, not cold-host measurements. Original registry/helper modules were copied beside their import roots; only the baseline helper path was relocated. All ten runs completed the production registry CLI and source guards, retaining 55 logged builds. Independently recalculated SHA-256s confirmed **all 55 tarballs and the complete manifest byte-identical across all ten runs**. Manifest SHA-256: `3088a494dcc44b70a365631021d8f9b0bf2429adb96de7bed27bcfa1618ca62d`. Four preprovided core/root bundles were omitted from both arms.
- Hosted reference: [candidate producer 43968859755](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43968859755/job/133656788195), registry step 22:25:25–22:26:57 UTC on November 16. Its [parent FRV](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43961391414) had failed npm qualification and independent CI/native work. Applying the local percentage proportionally suggests roughly 34s off the candidate path: **an unverified estimate, not whole-FRV savings**.
- Real registry regression fails on base for five child starts instead of two, while preserving correct builds/restored metadata. Candidate verifies distinct executable outputs. A second regression proves mid-batch failure stops later builds and publishes no manifest. Legacy and standalone build/pack failure coverage remains.
- Prior Node consumers: **87 passed, 2 environment failures**; pinned Bun registry: **19 passed, 1 environment failure**. A closed localhost server returns HTTP 502 through this environment's proxy instead of rejecting fetch. Original base and standalone HTTP-server control reproduce it. No proxy bypass or weakened assertion.
- Simplification: no new planner, cache, pool, configuration, or committed benchmark. Original production/config +99/-52, tests/fixtures +67/-6. Integration adds only one replacement lint expression beyond that original diff against the updated merge base; test growth is unchanged.

## CI repair and current readiness — November 16, 2026

Current head: `bdadf08266341f97747222ab9de1ef53de57608c`. **Fresh exact-head CI and hosted review are pending; not currently claimed review-ready.** Prior green main CI and completed ClawSweeper review apply to `ee6e8e2`, not this head.

The prior [planner validation failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43974767067/job/133675776517) reported five inherited Knip findings, [reproduced on the exact base](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200290#issuecomment-6932122120). Integrated already-landed [#200133](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200133) at `ba92f3086c3db2524a7a66a53deaf5e6611aff36` by a non-force merge. No changes to the registry optimization. The integrated Knip compiler had a consecutive-ignored-destructuring lint error; replaced it with equivalent `match[2]` access in the same touched configuration. No suppression, baseline relaxation, or findings removed by this expression change.

Integration proof:
- Actual production and full-tree unused-file scans both passed with **zero findings**.
- **34 Knip configuration/consumer tests passed**, including rerun after the lint expression repair.
- Both real registry regressions passed on the integrated tree.
- Scripts and tooling-test typechecks passed; exact CI-mode targeted lint, format, and whitespace checks passed.
- The local-independent-review waiver remains in force; hosted review and exact-head CI remain required. No merge or release is authorized by this task.

prs.title: fix(cron): refresh stale script preparation after plugin publication
prs.body:
Fixes #199478

## What Problem This Solves

A script automation created before a plugin was installed kept failing with `ReferenceError: <tool> is not defined` after the plugin was enabled online and explicitly reloaded (`plugins reload --wait`). A new automation on the same Gateway worked, and only restarting the Gateway recovered the old one.

## Why This Change Was Made

The per-job preparation cache in `src/cron/trigger-script.ts` judged freshness only by the retained registry's lifecycle: epoch unchanged, not retired, instances still admitting. Enabling or reloading a plugin publishes a new active registry without retiring the retained one, so all three signals stayed true and a stale preparation was reused. The existing `configEpoch` check only sees publications that rewrite the config object; a reload (or any publication without a config write) slips past it.

The fix captures the existing `getActivePluginRegistryVersion()` when preparation starts and adds version equality to `isCurrent()`. The hook runs after the cached promise resolves, so publications during preparation or while waiting on the cache also trigger a conservative re-preparation — never a stale reuse. This mirrors the capture-then-recheck precedent in `src/agents/openclaw-plugin-tools.ts` and adds no new API. Related to #199492, which pursued the same direction with a new accessor; this reuses the existing one.

## User Impact

After any plugin publication — enable, reload, or per-plugin replacement — the next invocation of an existing script automation sees the current enabled plugin inventory without a Gateway restart. Already-running evaluations keep their admitted generation (no abort, no replay). With no publications, cache reuse is unchanged — no extra preparations.

## Evidence

Before/after on the issue repro sequence (shipped built dist, isolated Gateway, zero credentials):

| Cell (issue repro sequence) | Before (base arm) | After (fixed arm) |
|---|---|---|
| Old job warm run (plugin absent) | ReferenceError | ReferenceError |
| Steady job ×2 (no publication) | succeeded | succeeded |
| `plugins install --link --no-enable` + `plugins enable` | ok | ok |
| Old job run ×2 after enable | succeeded (config write trips the config-epoch check) | succeeded |
| New job, same Gateway PID | succeeded | succeeded |
| `plugins reload --wait` → old job run | **failed — stale preparation reused** | **succeeded — tool resolved** |
| Restart with tool registration gated off (flag file) → old job (caches tool-less preparation) | ReferenceError | ReferenceError |
| Gate flag restored + `plugins reload` (same plugin source, no config write) → old job | succeeded (control: this path does not discriminate on this build) | succeeded |
| Second restart → old job run | succeeded | succeeded |
| Running evaluation across enable (tool effect before publication) | completed on retained generation | completed on retained generation |
| In-flight tool call across reload (observation) | instance-replacement error | same (pre-existing contract, unchanged) |

Setup: shipped built dist (`build-all.mts runtime` profile), isolated Gateway (scratch HOME/state/config, loopback token auth), a synthetic local tool plugin and script payloads, no model involved. Before arm = the same build with exactly the `isCurrent` version predicate reverted in the single cron chunk; blast-radius sweep shows 1 file differing and all 324 dist symlinks resolving identically; each arm self-attests its bundle form (predicate marker grep + full dist sha256 manifest).

Discriminating cell, verbatim `automations run … --wait --json` output after `plugins reload probe-board --wait` (same Gateway PID, no restart; loopback token is the synthetic proof credential):

```
$ node dist/index.js automations run d47c403f-b769-4be0-941c-79c26675dc66 --wait --json --url ws://127.0.0.1:33771 --token proof-token-199478  # BEFORE arm (predicate reverted)
{
  "ok": true,
  "enqueued": true,
  "runId": "cron-request.76ed6fc7-b26a-40be-81b9-0e39fe1faeaa",
  "processInstanceId": "dc53b176-64cb-418f-8389-3138e76cd36b",
  "completed": true,
  "status": "error",
  "completionStatus": "failed",
  "run": {
    "ts": 1794849512666,
    "jobId": "d47c403f-b769-4be0-941c-79c26675dc66",
    "action": "finished",
    "status": "error",
    "completionStatus": "failed",
    "error": "cron script payload failed (internal_error): Plugin probe-board was reloaded or disabled; use its current tools.",
    "runId": "cron-request.76ed6fc7-b26a-40be-81b9-0e39fe1faeaa",
    "runAtMs": 1794849512603,
    "durationMs": 63,
    "nextRunAtMs": 1794935853612,
    "deliveryStatus": "not-requested",
    "jobName": "old-probe"
  }
}
$ node dist/index.js automations run 32960e1c-7099-4a85-b73f-f272e08474fd --wait --json --url ws://127.0.0.1:41667 --token proof-token-199478  # AFTER arm (fix head)
{
  "ok": true,
  "enqueued": true,
  "runId": "cron-request.835e4130-e557-4f95-abee-9a21f88ffba3",
  "processInstanceId": "303484cb-c94a-418f-9c99-0d09dec6c8d0",
  "completed": true,
  "status": "ok",
  "completionStatus": "succeeded",
  "run": {
    "ts": 1794849250807,
    "jobId": "32960e1c-7099-4a85-b73f-f272e08474fd",
    "action": "finished",
    "status": "ok",
    "completionStatus": "succeeded",
    "runId": "cron-request.835e4130-e557-4f95-abee-9a21f88ffba3",
    "runAtMs": 1794849250390,
    "durationMs": 417,
    "nextRunAtMs": 1794935587042,

    "delivery": {
      "intended": {
        "channel": "last",
        "source": "explicit"
      }
    },
    "jobName": "old-probe"
  }
}
```

The probe script throws unless the tool actually returned published:true, so succeeded ⟺ the tool executed. On this build, two existing invalidation dimensions mask the issue's literal `ReferenceError` surface: enable's config write trips the config-epoch identity check, and the tool-less-catalog + reload path (flag-file cells, unchanged plugin source) recovers on both arms. The stale-reuse bug that remains on current main surfaces after a plain reload: the cached preparation already contains the tool, the reload replaces its instance without retiring the retained registry, and the before arm keeps dispatching to the disposed instance while the after arm re-prepares and resolves the current tool. The regression test pins the general mechanism — a publication that keeps the retained registry unretired and admitting — which is the shape the issue reports on its release version.

Local checks: `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` (259 rules) clean on both touched files; the cron vitest shard's cache-semantics tests pass. Full-graph typecheck is unavailable in this environment; the added expression reuses an accessor already exported on main and mirrors the compiled capture-then-recheck pattern in `openclaw-plugin-tools.ts`.

Regression: `src/cron/trigger-script.plugin-reload.test.ts` gains a third refresh case built on real publication primitives (no mocks). It asserts the retained registry stays unretired and admitting after the publication (so the refresh cannot be attributed to retirement/disposal), steady-state `prepares === 1` (guards against always-re-prepare), then generation 2 with the old generation disposed. RED on base, GREEN with the fix; the existing retired-registry and disposed-instance refresh cases stay green.
