prs.title: fix(worktrees): restore PostgreSQL cleanup jobs
prs.body:
Closes #200316

## What Problem This Solves

On a PostgreSQL-backed Gateway, `openclaw worktrees gc --json` queues a cleanup job whose terminal result is `failed` with `column reference "value_json" is ambiguous`. Automatic startup cleanup fails with the same error. I observed this while starting an isolated PostgreSQL Gateway; no malformed command or injected database error is needed.

## User Impact

PostgreSQL operators can complete worktree cleanup jobs. The reproduction uses an empty worktree inventory and establishes failed cleanup, not disk exhaustion or loss of user files.

## Why This Change Was Made

Qualify the existing-row column in the shared pending-sweep upsert so PostgreSQL can distinguish it from the conflict candidate. Preparation, projection changes, and maintenance keep using the same owner. The epoch/grace policy and schema are unchanged.

## Evidence

Built and ran the packaged CLI/Gateway on both base `b81742c8bfb591847601678178ff824336fc73eb` and fix `3df872256f0fbba88a84e0df680e58dcdf07ae82`. Linux x64, Node 24.22.2, PostgreSQL 16.10 with the documented extensions and a non-superuser runtime role. Synthetic state only, plugins disabled, no external network.

```sh
node openclaw.mjs gateway run --allow-unconfigured
node openclaw.mjs worktrees gc --json
node openclaw.mjs worktrees gc --job <returned-job-id> --json
```

| Observation | Base | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Startup maintenance | `managed worktree cleanup failed: column reference "value_json" is ambiguous` | No managed-cleanup failure |
| First terminal CLI result | exit 1, `state: "failed"`, ambiguous-column error | exit 0, `state: "completed"`, `error: null` |
| Repeated cleanup | — | exit 0, `state: "completed"`, `error: null` |

<details>
<summary>Actual terminal receipts (selected fields)</summary>

```json
{"jobId":"609da07b-4b0c-46e4-8542-32952af9410d","state":"failed","error":"column reference \"value_json\" is ambiguous","eligibleCount":0,"removed":[]}
{"jobId":"9698e3b8-4842-48bf-bfe3-9664600b6ef5","state":"completed","error":null,"eligibleCount":0,"removed":[]}
{"jobId":"b7c5ef71-c935-4ecc-8394-717016dbcad0","state":"completed","error":null,"eligibleCount":0,"removed":[]}
```

</details>

- Extended the existing real PostgreSQL conformance fixture: first insert, duplicate demand, preservation within the grace epoch, clearing at its boundary, and renewed demand. The production writer failed red on the base with the same SQL error; the final fixture passes on the fix. Test body: 1.50 s; wall time including isolated worker compilation: 238 s.
- Existing SQLite CAS owner suite: 13 passed; wall time including isolated worker compilation: 259 s.
- Targeted format, core type-aware lint, and typecheck passed. Both CLI startup builds passed. No full test suite was run; CI time is not available yet.
- Simplified to one changed production line and 18 added test lines in an existing fixture. Reviewed the complete committed diff locally in the author Codex session; no actionable findings. No independent autoreview or ClawSweeper result is claimed.

The CLI proof covers empty-inventory cleanup and repeat execution; it does not claim populated-worktree disk reclamation, live model execution, or a stable-release upgrade.

## What Problem This Solves

Full Release Validation's decision and diagnostic-drain watchers check out release tooling that they do not use when an admitted qualification verifier is already supplied.

## User Impact

Release operators avoid two redundant checkouts without changing release evidence, failures, platforms, coverage, or runner routing. There is no product-runtime change or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Skip the root tooling checkout only when the immutable qualification verifier is present. Preserve the fallback checkout when it is absent. Both callers advance their immutable reusable-workflow pin to the commit containing this condition; compared with the previous pinned watcher, that condition is the only workflow change. The summary job's separate tooling checkout remains necessary and unchanged.

This is deliberately a small deletion of unnecessary work, not a new cache or scheduling layer.

## Evidence

- Regression: the existing materialized-verifier test fails on the old unconditional checkout and passes with the condition; the no-verifier fallback still passes.
- The continuation, no-push, and release-state suites passed all 232 tests before updating caller pins. After pin updates, all 619 continuation, nightly, and package-workflow tests passed (108.77 seconds). These groups overlap; no aggregate count is claimed.
- A local replay executed the actual watcher evaluation Bash and production Node collector with only the qualification-verifier scripts present and no root tooling scripts. Both decision and drain modes preserved success (exit 0, passed) and child-policy failure (exit 1, blocked_complete): all four outcomes passed. GitHub responses were synthetic; this is production-path local proof, not a live GitHub end-to-end run.
- Tooling typecheck, targeted lint/format, complete workflow validation, and whitespace checks passed after the caller pin updates.
- In FRV run 43770476915, attempt 2, the unnecessary decision checkout took 4 seconds and drain checkout took 5 seconds. Removing both saves 9 runner-seconds in that trace, but at most roughly 4–5 seconds of the final tail, not 9 seconds of wall time. In a child-dominated run such as 43757970051, the expected wall-time gain is zero. No full hosted before/after FRV gain is claimed.

## Readiness audit — November 16, 2026

Exact head `a50becfbe38e85ca743bcf1757f43e8c81c93d15` is conflict-free. [Completed ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199920#issuecomment-6906522177) reports no code findings and raises a Boat-route rollout compatibility requirement. The [original extraction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193509) and `docs/ci/runners.md` require coordinated caller-pin and restricted runner-group updates. Retain the referenced definition commit while callers use it.

**Scope correction:** the watcher selects `BOAT_RELEASE_RUNNER_GROUP` only when `OPENCLAW_CI_RUNNER_BACKEND == 'boat'`. The observed active backend is hybrid, not Boat; this is not evidence that current FRV execution is denied. The repository's Boat group variable is `Boat release`. Before enabling or relying on the Boat route with these caller pins, its effective policy must permit `openclaw/openclaw/.github/workflows/full-release-state-watcher.yml@0bfca9316a086a140894c74fbf7ad26b33d9e202`.

The automation's read of `GET /orgs/openclaw/actions/runner-groups` was refused with HTTP 403. That is a visibility gap, not proof of denied admission. No runner policy was changed. Boat compatibility remains **unverified**, so the hosted review's rollout concern remains unresolved; this PR is not counted review-ready. Confirmation belongs to an operator with runner-group read access, with a policy update only if the existing policy actually requires it.

[CI 43797164058](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43797164058) failed `check-lint-core-2` on `src/agents/tool-search-prepared-catalog.ts:118` (`unicorn/prefer-structured-clone`), plus its dependent aggregate. The failing checkout was merge `cb138ceabbbcf580614a2631c276e5df92d9c963` over main `2159567b9ffc17a770579d7e6487836789c67be5`, not the standalone branch tree. [Baseline reproduction and unchanged-input evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199920#issuecomment-6931072235) attribute this outside the watcher patch. Failed CI is not represented as green.

prs.title: fix(memory-lancedb): group chats recall and forget the owner's stored memories
prs.body:
Closes #200281

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a group or channel member gets the owner's stored memories in a reply, and can have the agent delete them, when memory-lancedb owns the memory slot.

## User Impact

User impact: by default only the owner's sessions recall or forget memory-lancedb memories. In groups, channels and direct chats with anyone else, `memory_recall` and `memory_forget` return a refusal with the reason and the next step, and automatic recall skips the turn before the prompt reaches the embedding provider. `ownerOnly: false` in the plugin config brings back today's behavior. `memory_store` and auto-capture are unchanged, and `openclaw ltm` still lists and searches for operators.

Owner sessions are the ones the Gateway gives an owner-private memory audience: direct chats with anyone in `commands.ownerAllowFrom`, Gateway clients with `operator.admin` (the Control UI, WebChat and the TUI connect with it), `openclaw agent` on its default session, and sessions and linked scheduled runs that inherit one of these. Sessions without that audience lose recall they have today: `openclaw agent --session-key` on a key that names no chat, Gateway clients without `operator.admin`, `tools.invoke`, and unlinked cron and hook runs. The docs list them.

Update behavior: existing configs stay valid and nothing is migrated. After updating, those sessions stop recalling until an operator sets `ownerOnly: false`. The key is read from live config on every call, so setting it applies on hot reload with no restart. Checked on an upgrade from 2026.11.4 below. Separately, main's memory-lancedb already needs a core newer than 11.4 (it imports `openclaw/plugin-sdk/node-crypto-runtime`), so a plugin-only update fails to load before and after this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin's provider already had the rule (`provider-runtime.ts`, `resolveReadDenial`), but the tools and the prompt hook never used it. This moves it into `memory-access.ts`, which the provider, both tools and automatic recall now share, and adds `ownerOnly` (default true) as the explicit way back. Automatic recall checks that the audience is still current once, right before it embeds the prompt; a recall that has started finishes, as root `AGENTS.md` asks. The provider's own answers stay owner-private whatever `ownerOnly` says, as on main.

Root `AGENTS.md` asks before new config options. If you'd rather ship this with no key, or with the default open, either is a few lines.

Not addressed here:

- `memory_store` and auto-capture still save group turns into the owner's store, as today, and `memory_store` still answers `Already stored` when the exact text is already there. Someone who can guess a memory's full text can confirm it that way.
- A session with `exec` or file tools on the Gateway host can read the LanceDB files directly, and no plugin check stops that. One of my live runs did exactly that, with the store under the workspace. The live scenario below denies those tools so it measures the plugin. Sandboxing non-owner sessions is the control for it.
- #196265 also edits `config.ts` and `index.ts`, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

## Evidence

Head `6837762d09c` over main `aa4d490a848`, on macOS (Apple silicon); current main `48cd549b1c4` has no changes to these files. The tests, typecheck, lint, guards and mutants below ran at the head. The QA Lab runs and the upgrade cell ran at `6df03ea2817`. Since then the branch restored three docs paragraphs that `6df03ea2817` dropped by mistake, named the CLI case in the docs, dropped the audience check after the search, and made every refusal name the `ownerOnly: false` opt-out (both from review). None of those runs has an audience go stale mid-search.

- Fails on main, passes here. The new rows in `auto-recall.test.ts` run the registered `memory_recall`, `memory_forget` and `before_prompt_build` handler as the owner's direct chat, a group chat, a session with no audience, another agent's owner chat, and a group with `ownerOnly: false`. On main: `Tests 5 failed | 3 passed (8)`. The group, no-audience and other-agent rows each fail with `expected [ undefined, undefined ] to deeply equal [ …(2) ]`, because main returns results and deletes where the test expects the refusal. The `ownerOnly: false` row fails with `memory config has unknown keys: ownerOnly`, and the stale-audience row with `expected { result: undefined, embeds: 1, …(1) } to deeply equal { result: undefined, embeds: +0, …(1) }`, because main embeds the prompt anyway. Here: 8 of 8.
- Mutants: making the rule always allow fails the 3 refused-session rows; dropping the audience check before embedding fails the stale-audience row. The refusal-text assertion fails on `8f1eb66b9f4` for the no-audience and other-agent rows (`expected { …(5) } to deeply equal { …(5) }`): that head told sessions with no chat to check `commands.ownerAllowFrom`, which cannot give them one.
- Tests: 26 files (the plugin's 21, active-memory's index test, and 4 config and plugin contract tests), 319 passed, 0 failed.
- Typecheck: `tsgo`, all 7 lanes, 0 errors. A type error planted in the new module and in the test was reported by `extensions:all` and `extensions:test`.
- Lint and guards: oxlint, oxfmt, the test-lines, line-cap, max-lines and assertion-safety ratchets, both extension boundary lints, `docs:check-mdx`, `docs:check-config-examples` and `config:docs:check` all pass. `docs:check-links:anchors` fails on the same 3 anchors as main, none in files touched here.
- Config inventory: plugin count 5080 -> 5081 for `ownerOnly`, regenerated rather than hand-edited.
- Test cost: `pnpm test extensions/memory-lancedb/auto-recall.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 8 tests, 9.1 s and 8.5 s wall (vitest 6.73 s and 6.11 s). No timers, sleeps or Gateway boots. CI seconds to follow once the run exists.
- End to end, QA Lab with qa-channel and the mock provider: main fails the group step (recall, forget and the prompt block all reach the owner's fact). This head passes all 4 steps, including `ownerOnly: false` applied live through `config.patch`.
- End to end, QA Lab with qa-channel, a self-hosted 27B open-weight model and real 4096-dimension embeddings: main fails (the member gets `4412` and deletes the memory; the owner's fresh session answers `UNKNOWN`). This head passes all 4 steps.
- Upgrade from 2026.11.4 (npm core and plugin) to this change with 11.4's own updater: details below.
- Not run: a Telegram, Discord or Slack e2e. Those use maintainer-leased credentials I don't have, and no channel code changes here; qa-channel drives the same direct, group and channel audiences. `memory-lancedb.live.test.ts` fails the same way on main and here (`api.registerMemoryCapability is not a function`, because its plugin API mock predates that method), so its one-line change is covered by typecheck only. That mock is worth a follow-up.

The QA scenarios aren't in this PR. Happy to add them under `qa/scenarios/memory/` if you want to keep them.

<details>
<summary>QA Lab, mock provider: group member, before and after</summary>

```text
main aa4d490a848, rc=1 (75 s)
  [x] runs memory-lancedb as the memory slot
  [x] the owner stores and recalls in a direct chat
  [ ] a group member cannot recall or forget the owner's memory (fail)
  group prompt: <relevant-memories> ... 1. [fact] QA owner-only fact: the storage locker code is 4412. </relevant-memories>
  group memory_recall: Found 1 memories: ... QA owner-only fact: the storage locker code is 4412. (86%)
  group memory_forget: Forgotten: "QA owner-only fact: the storage locker code is 4412."
  owner recheck: No relevant memories found.

6df03ea2817, rc=0 (77 s)
  [x] runs memory-lancedb as the memory slot
  [x] the owner stores and recalls in a direct chat
  [x] a group member cannot recall or forget the owner's memory
  [x] ownerOnly off in the live config lets a group recall again
  group prompt: no memory block
  group memory_recall and memory_forget: Stored memories are not available in this session: this session has no
    owner-private memory audience. They are used only in the agent owner's direct chats. An operator can set
    ownerOnly: false in the memory-lancedb config to use them in every conversation.
  owner recheck: Found 1 memories: ...
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>QA Lab, real model and embeddings: channel member, before and after</summary>

```text
main aa4d490a848, rc=1
  [x] runs memory-lancedb on real embeddings and seeds the owner's memory
  [x] the owner's direct chat answers from memory            reply: 4412
  [ ] a channel member neither gets nor deletes the owner's memory (fail)
  member question: 4412 (no tool call)
  member delete request, memory_forget: Found 1 candidates. Specify memoryId: - [a7d32da7-...] The owner's storage locker code is 4412....
                                        Memory a7d32da7-dc6b-458d-9d6b-ec316faeba82 forgotten.
  owner, fresh session: UNKNOWN

6df03ea2817, rc=0
  [x] runs memory-lancedb on real embeddings and seeds the owner's memory
  [x] the owner's direct chat answers from memory            reply: 4412
  [x] a channel member neither gets nor deletes the owner's memory
  [x] ownerOnly off in the live config lets the channel member get the answer
  member question: UNKNOWN; memory_recall: Stored memories are not available in this session: this session has no owner-private memory audience. ...
  member delete request: NOT_DELETED; memory_forget: Stored memories are not available in this session: ...
  owner, fresh session: 4412
  Gateway log after config.patch:
    [gateway] Plugin replacement applied: memory-lancedb
    [reload] config hot reload applied (plugins.entries.memory-lancedb.config.ownerOnly)
  member, new channel, after the patch: reply contains 4412
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Upgrade from 2026.11.4</summary>

Fresh prefix and HOME. Installed `openclaw@2026.11.4` and `@openclaw/memory-lancedb@2026.11.4` from npm, configured them with the CLI (memory slot, plus `hooks.allowConversationAccess: true`, which 11.4 needs before it runs `before_prompt_build` for an npm-installed plugin), and pointed chat and embeddings at a loopback stub that records whether each turn's prompt carries the memory block. Stored one fact from `agent:main:main`. Then `openclaw update --tag <candidate core tarball>` with 11.4's own updater (version now `2026.11.4 (6df03ea)`), `openclaw plugins install <candidate plugin tgz> --force`, and `openclaw doctor` (rc 0).

| probe | 2026.11.4 | this change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `memory_recall` through `tools.invoke`, `agent:main:telegram:group:-1001234567890` | returns the fact | refused |
| `memory_recall` through `tools.invoke`, `agent:main:main` | returns the fact | refused (no chat) |
| `chat.send` from an `operator.admin` client, `agent:main:main` | block with the fact | block with the fact |
| `openclaw agent`, default session | block with the fact | block with the fact |
| `chat.send` from a client without `operator.admin`, new key | block with the fact | no block |
| `openclaw agent --session-key agent:main:upcell-cli` | block with the fact | no block |
| `openclaw ltm list` | 1 row | 1 row |

For the custom-key CLI run the candidate Gateway logs `memory audience unavailable: root session agent:main:upcell-cli has no durable chat type`. `memory_store` through `tools.invoke` from the group key still stores. `openclaw config set plugins.entries.memory-lancedb.config.ownerOnly false` logged `Plugin replacement applied: memory-lancedb` and `[reload] config hot reload applied (plugins.entries.memory-lancedb.config.ownerOnly)` with no restart, and the group key's `memory_recall` then found 2 memories. Across the update the config diff is doctor's own additions only (`agents.entries.main`, `skillLibraryToolSplit`, `skillWorkshopPlugin`, the `wizard` stamp); the plugin entry and the hook grant came through unchanged.

</details>

prs.title: fix(storage): allow first session after missing-store reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes first-session creation failing after an earlier read found no agent database.

## User Impact

A fresh agent can create its first session after an empty state read. Existing admitted databases keep their normal warm-worker behavior; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Releasing the last reader could retain a generation that had never admitted a database file. That left a pending opener which later blocked creation. Only generations with an admitted file are now eligible for idle retention; the existing close path releases empty readers.

## Evidence

- The real storage-worker regression fails before the fix with `Agent creation cannot capture another pending native opener`, then passes after the fix: read an absent store, release the reader, create the first session, and read it back.
- Exact PR head `15bb782f6ce61969f9804c7764a6c0cde4e341b3`: all 36 creation-witness and idle tests pass with Node 24.22.1 and the pinned fs-safe 0.27.1 dependency. Targeted format and type-aware lint pass for all three changed files.
- The same patch passed 134 owner/lifecycle tests on the integrated RSS candidate. That candidate completed a real model request under a 1 GiB service limit; its separate 768 MiB run still OOMs. These integrated results are not exact-PR-head runtime or RSS qualification.
- Independent source review found no correctness issues. Local ClawSweeper reviewed the complete committed range `726a8dd4985723c6b1050a65e05502dd010f2ae8..15bb782f6ce61969f9804c7764a6c0cde4e341b3`: no findings, security cleared. Broader CI runs on this PR.

prs.title: improve(ci): narrow FRV admission helper checkout
prs.body:
## Summary
- Limit the FRV admission helper checkout to its runtime imports, workflow sources, workspace manifests, and patches instead of materializing the entire repository.
- Keep the same immutable Q, target C, full frozen dependency installation, source checks, publication inventory, and validation coverage. No cache, new scheduler, relaxed admission, or changed dependency owner.

## Wall-time evidence
The helper checkout in the critical `resolve_target` prefix took **31 seconds** in both observed attempts of FRV [43770476915](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43770476915). It gates downstream dispatch; unlike work in a slack lane, any checkout saving advances the critical path. This change does not add a runner or setup phase.

At base `210e3c4282c5b3549b239f8c21a6788b08ba9a29`, an actual sparse checkout retained **35,536 / 65,473 tracked files** and **321,903,260 / 777,473,576 uncompressed blob bytes**: 45.7% fewer files and 58.6% fewer bytes materialized. All **72** publication tooling paths and **213** child workspace manifests (plus the root manifest) remain. Existing full `scripts`/`src`/`packages` trees intentionally avoid introducing a fragile import-closure owner.

**No measured hosted wall-time gain is claimed.** The local shared-object checkout took 1.40s, but it is not comparable with the hosted 31s checkout. Sparse materialization is smaller; Git object transfer, queue time, filesystem/cache behavior, and the unchanged pnpm install bound actual improvement. Expected wall benefit is within that existing checkout prefix, not proportional to removed bytes. No full FRV dispatch was needed or performed.

## Validation
- Existing trusted-checkout regression: fails on base (1 failed / 12 passed), green with the sparse checkout. It still checks immutable refs and disabled persisted credentials; no new test case/scaffold.
- **211 tests passed** on the original revision: continuation workflow, publication admission, and no-push release workflow suites.
- Isolated actual sparse checkout: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline --ignore-scripts` passed (6.4s), without reconciling the shared worktree install.
- Actual production qualification preflight passed for same-revision and frozen-C/different-Q inputs; neither selected a parser-required branch, so these alone are not parser proof.
- Actual `full-release-publication-admission.mts` in the isolated sparse Q checkout admitted frozen C `d843d6af39a42cd3c30084edbeabeece732fd93a`: **102 packages / 4 platforms**, inventory digest `185d52d411ca7fcca0d87612cde138a8adf5a5096c2c02ead7887b0ffeb3305c`. This exercised the real retained-object inventory/parser and exact tooling-byte checks, not an import-only stub. Registry observation collection is unchanged and was not rerun in this local proof.
- Tooling typecheck, touched type-aware lint, format, `git diff --check`, full pinned actionlint/zizmor and workflow guards passed. An empty-token environment initially prevented zizmor startup; removing the empty credential environment variables allowed the normal guard to pass.

## Simplification / risk
The smallest change is the checkout declaration, not a filtered installation or new dependency manifest. Production/workflow **+14/-0**; tests **+8/-1** against merge base, unchanged after upstream integration. Every retained pattern serves imports or the unchanged workspace install. No local independent review was run (explicit task waiver).

Rollback: remove the sparse-checkout declaration. Future admission imports outside these retained trees must extend the checkout and its real-workload proof.

## CI repair and current readiness

Current head **`fdc78cef9dc2e0ac8a521f8fd046340d0e800f02`** integrates the already-landed [#199944](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199944) repair through main commit `54070dcab8c21f2b24cf0bf4e9c9439ff44cb753`, without force-pushing or altering lint baselines. The PR's two-file optimization is unchanged. This bounded integration resolves the inherited `unicorn/prefer-structured-clone` error from [prior CI 43796394662](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43796394662); that old red result is not a result for the new head.

Fresh integration proof:
- **52 tests passed** across continuation workflow, frozen target contracts, and lint-suppression consumers.
- The exact CI-mode core lint command now passes for `src/agents/tool-search-prepared-catalog.ts`; tooling typecheck, touched test lint, format, whitespace, actionlint, zizmor and workflow guards pass.
- Replayed actual publication admission using the same sparse patterns at integrated tooling `54070dc...`, retaining frozen C `d843d6...`: **102 packages / 4 platforms and the identical inventory digest**. Root dependency manifests and lockfile were unchanged. The initial deliberately stale tooling declaration was rejected by byte checks; updating the request to the actual tooling SHA passed, without bypassing admission.

**Fresh exact-head CI and ClawSweeper review are pending; not yet RFR.** The [previous completed review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199913#issuecomment-6906427071) covered `ecc74be...`, not this integrated head. GitHub reported the new head mergeable after publication; no merge is authorized.

prs.title: fix(gateway): publication result retries forever after its session is deleted
prs.body:
Closes #200243

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a GitHub publication result being retried and logged ("GitHub publication result reporting deferred … transcript owner changed") on every reconcile pass, forever, when the session that published it was deleted before the publication settled (a sub-agent run that ends while its publication is in recovery).

## User Impact

The gateway stops logging the same warning for each such result (about 1,250 lines a day here for one record), and the result is marked reported once. The shared receipt stays as it is and stays readable by request id. No configuration or permission change.

## Why This Change Was Made

`reportGitHubPublicationTranscript` already retires a result when its session was reset or rotated (the entry exists with another session id or lifecycle revision). When the entry is gone under the same canonical key, `entry?.sessionId !== recipient.sessionId` threw instead, and `reportDeferred` kept the record pending. A deleted entry ends that transcript for good, like a reset, so it now takes the same retire path. A changed canonical key still throws as before.

## Evidence

One test: a real session created and deleted with `deleteSessionEntryLifecycle`, then the real reporter and store resolver; it checks one `markReportedAsync` call and no transcript write.

Before (main):

```text
× retires a report whose session was deleted before the result settled
  → GitHub publication transcript owner changed
```

After: `src/gateway/github-publication-transcript.test.ts` 27 of 27 pass (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, the new test 1.3 s). Net test lines +21. `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and `pnpm tsgo:core` pass on the touched files.

Gateway run, isolated state (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` in a temp dir, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`, `openclaw gateway run --port 19077`), same seed for both runs: a session made with `sessions.create` and removed with `sessions.delete`, then one settled `failed` shared result for it with `reported_at_ms` null and its lifecycle binding, written to the state database as the stuck record on 2026.11.4 looks. Each run started from a fresh copy of the seed and ran about 200 s.

Before, `main` at 232ba9a63de: the warning on every pass, result still unreported.

```text
17:54:07.468 [gateway] GitHub publication result reporting deferred for 2b3ec4f9-…: GitHub publication transcript owner changed
17:55:06.032 [gateway] GitHub publication result reporting deferred for 2b3ec4f9-…: GitHub publication transcript owner changed
17:56:06.096 [gateway] GitHub publication result reporting deferred for 2b3ec4f9-…: GitHub publication transcript owner changed
17:57:06.166 [gateway] GitHub publication result reporting deferred for 2b3ec4f9-…: GitHub publication transcript owner changed

request_id                            status  reported
5c0f2a9e-0000-4000-8000-000000000001  failed  0
```

After, this commit on the same `main`: no publication lines in the log. The first pass (1.3 s after listening) marked it reported, and nothing more was logged for it through 18:02:36. The receipt row is kept with its status, error and branch.

```text
request_id                            status  error_code      branch     reported_at_ms
5c0f2a9e-0000-4000-8000-000000000001  failed  session_changed  fix/proof  1794869964885
```

Seen live on 2026.11.3 and 2026.11.4: the record came from a coder sub-agent session deleted on 2026-11-07 while its publication was recovering.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): shorten guest pauses during PR base refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: sandbox sessions and commands stay paused while PR base refresh captures a host-only pre-merge workspace snapshot.

## User Impact

The guest can keep working during that snapshot. A conflicting guest write still stops application and remains intact; initial pristine-workspace admission and recovery retain their existing pause boundaries.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both workspace synchronization directions have already settled before this host-only work begins. Resume through the existing quiescence owner at that boundary; the existing apply owner pauses again and confirms the target before writing. The later resume remains necessary for continuing integrations. This adds one production line, with no new configuration, schema, cache, or validation owner.

## Evidence

The registered-action regression fails before the fix because the guest is paused at the pre-merge snapshot. With the fix, it writes concurrently in that window and verifies the conflict is reported and those exact bytes survive. The production-release control passed all 74 focused tests. On repaired main, 73 passed and the existing 50,001-file test failed in fixture `git add` on a slow external temporary filesystem; that case passed unchanged in isolation on the normal test filesystem (56 seconds including cleanup). The new regression passed on both candidate bases.

`pnpm check:changed` passed typecheck, lint, format, and structural guards. Its unused-export scan failed with exactly the same 113 findings as clean parent `2435c1faa791d`, with zero added findings. These are existing main regressions from test consolidations (#198943, #198933, #198936), compaction `472cd0a2f5425`, Talk `94e34f956969a`, release-slot work #198835, and #198133; the check is not claimed green.

Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings in the complete change. The benchmark also reports cumulative main-isolate allocation on Node 26, separately from sampled profiling and excluding workers/child processes/native buffers.

Full-scale native-container comparison is complete: two A/A controls and five counterbalanced pairs, all byte-verified. The targeted third pause fell **86% (790 → 111 ms)**, and the ~430 ms pre-merge snapshot ran unpaused in every candidate. However, total pause rose 6.9%, owner elapsed rose 24%, and process CPU rose 40%. **Performance acceptance is unresolved; this is not ready to land.** The completed diagnostic profile pair separates CPU before/after snapshot entry; results below do not clear the acceptance hold. No aggregate speedup is claimed.

| Median, five samples/arm | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Targeted third pause | 789.74 ms | 110.51 ms |
| Pre-merge snapshot held paused | 429.76 ms | 0 ms |
| Pre-merge snapshot duration | 429.76 ms | 429.12 ms |
| Total pause | 11,605.82 ms | 12,410.70 ms |
| Longest pause | 10,104.18 ms | 11,400.76 ms |
| Owner elapsed | 93,784.18 ms | 116,282.36 ms |
| Host Node process CPU | 58,853.46 ms | 82,245.29 ms |
| Main-thread CPU | 3,703.47 ms | 4,195.65 ms |
| Guest CPU | 18,275.60 ms | 22,430.69 ms |
| Main-isolate allocated bytes | 1,304,296,120 | 1,308,056,160 |

A/A total pauses were 14,754.74 / 28,840.48 ms; owner elapsed 123,098.39 / 173,480.50 ms. That variability is retained, not used to waive the aggregate regression threshold. The largest hold is the earlier pause before the changed resume; every arm has five native pauses. Host process CPU includes worker threads but excludes host Git children; allocation excludes workers and native buffers. The local filesystem is APFS, not btrfs. Final-head CI [43978876106](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43978876106) is green at `dffcd6871f3ed538727f8f40af3d350f4a0b08c4`. Final-head ClawSweeper has no code findings and one open performance-acceptance item; no merge has been requested.

The diagnostic follow-up passed a native-container smoke, typecheck, lint, format and structural checks. Its full unused-export scan again matches clean parent `2435c1faa791d` exactly (113/113). Fresh Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 finding.

Measurement protocol (declared in the task report before counted runs): serial fresh processes with warm OS caches; two baseline A/A controls, then A1 B1 B2 A2 A3 B3 B4 A4 A5 B5. Require verified bytes and concurrent-write preservation, a measurable reduction in the held pause window, and investigation of any >20% regression in another metric. Report median, nearest-rank p95, spread, CPU and allocation; exclude separate profiling passes. Both arms use release `4bce7604` with identical benchmark instrumentation; only the candidate's one-line resume differs. Native Docker runs on APFS, so this is not btrfs or live deployment timing proof. The completed database is 34.66 GiB with 10,000 synthetic sessions; no production data is used.

Separate diagnostic profile pair (not counted latency samples): owner elapsed 154,184 → 118,683 ms; process CPU 100,031 → 83,869 ms; main-isolate allocation 1,283,463,112 → 1,285,110,888 bytes. CPU before the second snapshot was 35,934 → 26,523 ms and after it 64,097 → 57,347 ms. Thus the aggregate direction reverses, with variation already present before the changed boundary. This suggests environmental variability but does not overturn the five-pair acceptance failure. Captured JS profiles show less realpath/GC/dispatch sampled time in the candidate; they do not attribute all worker/native CPU.

A supported managed Crabbox qualification attempt failed before allocation because the configured private Boat route has no organization selector; its required provider CLI is also absent. No lease was created and no alternate provider was attempted. A qualified btrfs comparison remains uncovered. Recommendation: keep the performance hold until stronger evidence resolves the aggregate result or the owner explicitly accepts the reported tradeoff.

Reproduction command per sample (use the qualified synthetic fixture and the selected baseline/candidate source capsule):

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/perf/github-publication-pause-measure.ts \
  --source-root <source-capsule> --fixture <fixture-root> --output <sample-output> \
  --native-image 3b764117159b --temporary-root <short-private-temp-root>
```

Add `--allocation` and Node `--cpu-prof` options only for the separate diagnostic pass.

prs.title: fix(codex): prevent native subagent continuation loss after sessions_yield
prs.body:
Related: #167410 (not a claim to close all reported timeouts).

## Yield finalization regression — November 16

Current head: `afb80888ee822148c6eadce1f45b1b3f0f474041`. The additional commit is test-only: a typed history-worker `byte_limit` rejection must leave a yielded parent with usable continuation custody, while revoked source authority must still reject. Main's lazy finalization callback is exercised explicitly.

- Seven focused parent-continuation cases passed; targeted test types, type-aware lint, formatting, line cap, and test-line budget passed. Fresh independent scoped review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Final formatting only wrapped the mock chain; exact inverse reproduces the tested/reviewed bytes.
- Separate stable 11.4 candidate: six cases passed. Substituting only the installed 11.3 cleanup/resources implementation made the intended unrevoked-parent assertion fail; the revoked-source control still passed. Source was restored afterward.
- This validates an existing 11.4 retention repair, not a new production workaround or proof of the historical claim holder. The context warning alone does not establish a leaked claim. Ownership guards are unchanged.
- Separate stable 11.4 revision 2 is now built and isolated-runtime-qualified; exact package evidence follows. This does not certify a package built from the upstream PR head. No installation or restart is part of this PR update.

## Separate stable 11.4 package qualification — November 16

Stable source `62188beb394a88d09e85e3b8e675d8ec772f0702`, base `d843d6af39a42cd3c30084edbeabeece732fd93a`; archive SHA-256 `4b4eb6043370d56bcd15de490dbc2c7eb1a61cbe3cc0848286d576213612a19d`.

- The first 11.4 candidate failed packaged continuation with **Plugin invocation scope is closed**. Stable lacked the existing upstream announce-dispatch readmission repair from `62e0b2b7fcf5fe3e2231f3d2418cd3e0e4d3c29d` (#184243). Revision 2 minimally backports its dispatch-scope boundary; the PR base already contains this repair, so no duplicate production change is added here. Source authority, Gateway admission and closed-callback denial remain enforced.
- Fresh stable regression: two new cases fail before the backport; 10 announcement plus 14 authority cases pass afterward. Fresh types/lint/format/line-cap gates and independent scoped review pass. Total source evidence comprises 338 distinct cases, with unchanged-source proof reused explicitly rather than presented as a complete rerun.
- Canonical archive integrity/inventory/import graph passed; installed bytes matched 9,542 core and 25 bundled Codex files, using native Codex 0.164.0.
- Two network-disabled installed-package scenarios passed with scripted local inference: **baseline** (102.54 s) and **actual current-turn byte-limit rejection** (102.57 s). Each retained one parent/original child through five completed child turns, three persisted yields and three once-only automatic result consumptions. The oversized case recorded the real `byte_limit` and `context_unavailable` diagnostics, then reached suspension readiness with zero active work/no blockers and resumed successfully.
- One earlier oversized fixture only padded prior turns, which native history trimming discarded; its missing-byte-limit assertion failed and is retained as fixture evidence, not a product failure or a passing oversized result. The corrected fixture pads successful read-only calls in the current yielding turn; it does not change the package or weaken continuation assertions.
- Actual candidate/predecessor artifact guards, 62 synthetic operator guard cases, Node/predecessor checks and the exact no-restart updater dry-run passed. Neither artifact checking nor dry-run proves live retained-state admission.

This is isolated stable-package qualification, not live OAuth/model acceptance, historical claim-holder identification, a fresh stock 11.4 comparison, or certification of an upstream-head package. Existing-conversation usability and browser/reload acceptance remain for the operator trial. No installation, service restart, reset or merge was performed.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes loss of the original native child after a parent yields for completion, and yield acknowledgements being replaced by cancellation before Codex records them.

## User Impact

Users can continue work with the original child after an automatic completion wakeup. This preserves declaration continuity without reviving old tool executors. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pending completion delivery can outlive a child's execution pin. The existing completion owner now keeps the parent's saved declarations eligible only while current delivery custody remains. Terminal interruption waits for matching native model-history output receipts, including an outer Code Mode output, rather than assuming a tool-item completion or event-loop tick committed the result.

## Prior rebase validation — November 16

Exact source: `d1cd01bfe711f561a50045e2fb86d4fece61db81`, rebased onto `bd25e9ef60cc886dc6c0512927bf1cf425e364df`. Five PR commits; only conflict was test-suite inventory adjacency. Upstream's removed test entry stays removed, and all three new suites remain registered. No continuation behavior or assertion was changed by this rebase.

- Focused validation: **147 distinct cases across 11 files passed**, 511.11s wrapper wall, first attempt. Includes real native yield-output recording, direct/nested receipt ordering, pending-delivery catalog custody, current-executor denial, Gateway final-effect authority, workspace metadata, and full-suite discovery/configuration.
- Core and plugin production types plus scoped core/plugin test types: passed.
- Targeted type-aware core/plugin lint, formatting, pinned-base line-cap and test-line allocation checks: passed. No shared baseline or assertion was weakened.
- Fresh **Codex autoreview**, full 16-file committed range plus nine complete owner-context files, P0–P2: **scoped-clean, no actionable findings**. Reviewer executed no project code; this is source review, not package/live acceptance.
- The six upstream commits inspected after the pinned base do not overlap the PR's paths; a merge-tree check against `9a1d8f7f920ee61d9c5bc342e5ccbf253518f343` was clean. The qualification remains bound to the pinned base/head above.

Hosted CI for this rewritten head is pending. Earlier exact-head CI and review claims below are **historical only**. The separate stable 2026.11.4 custom-package qualification is not evidence for a package built from this upstream head. No installation, restart, or merge was performed. Duplicate-notification and parent-claim admission failures are not claimed fixed by this PR.

<details>
<summary>Historical reproduction, review, CI, and stable-backport evidence (unchanged; not current-head certification)</summary>

Related: #167410 (not a claim to close all reported timeouts).

## Current rebase validation — 2026-11-13

Head `3c0812c5f7367c18a89d6772aedcce5b98bd10dc`, reviewed against main `90c620b8e554becc8d0da785c16fea9935bd0681`. The five-commit rebase preserves upstream verified-local-home resolution and workspace-owned session metadata; pending-completion custody is rechecked after the metadata await. Earlier reviews below are historical and do not transfer to this conflict resolution.

- Fresh focused validation: **146 distinct tests across 11 files passed** (487.99 seconds), including native continuation, Gateway final-effect authority, catalog/workspace behavior and suite ownership. Duplicate tooling summaries counted once.
- Four type lanes, core/plugin targeted lint, formatting, line-cap and test-line budget checks passed on this head. All 12 preparation/validation lanes exited zero.
- Fresh local autoreview (Codex, GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2): **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings, exact base/head above. Code review is not execution proof.
- Main advanced during validation; no changed PR file overlaps the inspected advance to `77a0a8426513a024f2220c78085ddbd5731a059c`. Evidence remains bound to the reviewed base, not an untested latest-tip rebase. Hosted CI is separate and pending after publication.

### Separate stable 2026.11.3 qualification

Stable 11.3 still lacks all four retained backport fixes. Two are already on main; this PR retains only its remaining main delta. Custom source `529bac2e3a66d91ab0bf1be4cbfac1032ae6908f`, stable base `847611dcaa3bf0e2783335f961dd1fd0580e4d9f`:

- 280 distinct tests in 16 files and source checks passed. Stable source review was reused under proven patch equivalence, not a fresh review.
- Canonical packaging passed, including archive integrity, inventory and import graph. Archive SHA-256: `4280b1a571ad9af43e4121d639d9daf178d603469420c44943411b798ceeef4b`.
- Isolated installation matched 9,522 core and 25 bundled Codex files. Native Codex 0.164.0 retained its prior digest.
- Network-disabled scripted-provider runtime: five distinct completed turns on one original child, three persisted yields, three once-only automatic consumptions; 102.59 seconds.
- Operator artifact/predecessor/Node checks and exact no-restart dry-run passed. No production installation or restart occurred. Dry-run does not prove retained-state admission.

No fresh stock 11.3 runtime comparison, real-model OAuth acceptance, live plugin-selection or browser/reload acceptance is claimed. Stable package proof is not certification of this upstream PR build. Historical false-delivery warnings and active-work blockage remain separate, unverified cases.

## What Problem This Solves

Preserve a managed native parent's saved tool declarations while its last terminal child's completion is still awaiting delivery. This fixes a distinct gap after execution protection correctly ends: rebuilding the catalog for the completion turn could rotate the parent thread and make a follow-up to its original child fail lineage validation.

The PR also retains the original delayed-completion authority regression. Current main already owns that async-lifetime behavior; no stable-only lifetime patch is added to main.

## Try it on stock 2026.11.1: native Codex continuation

**Use a fresh OpenClaw conversation backed by the native Codex plugin**, with native `spawn_agent`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, and OpenClaw `sessions_yield` available. An embedded model, Claude CLI, standalone Codex CLI, or `sessions_spawn` child does not exercise this same path. Use an isolated test installation, not an in-place downgrade of your working instance:

```sh
npm install -g openclaw@2026.11.1
openclaw plugins install @openclaw/codex@2026.11.1
openclaw plugins inspect codex --runtime --json
```

Complete normal Codex authentication/configuration and start that test Gateway. Confirm the **running** Gateway is stock 2026.11.1 and the official Codex plugin is loaded; merely installing the package does not replace an already-running Gateway. The controlled stock result below used native Codex 0.164.0. Record the actual build/plugin/native versions when reporting a result.

### Copy/paste prompt — first four turns

```text
Run a native Codex child-continuation reproduction. Use exactly ONE native
child throughout, created with native spawn_agent (not sessions_spawn).
Use native followup_task to start later turns on that SAME child. If the
required native tools or OpenClaw sessions_yield are unavailable, stop and
report that this setup cannot exercise the test; do not substitute tools.

1. Spawn a child named continuation_repro with fork_turns="none". Ask it to
   return exactly NORMAL_ONE. Wait with native wait_agent, and consume its
   actual completion once. Record the returned child identity.
2. Send that same child a followup_task asking it to return exactly
   NORMAL_TWO. Wait with native wait_agent, and consume the actual result.
3. Send the SAME child a followup_task asking it to wait 30 seconds using
   its shell or sleep tool, then return exactly AUTO_THREE. Immediately
   call OpenClaw sessions_yield to end this parent turn while awaiting that
   completion. Do not wait_agent, poll, sleep in the parent, schedule a
   reminder, or ask the user to wake you. Continue only when the child's
   completion automatically resumes you.
4. On automatic receipt of the actual AUTO_THREE completion, consume it
   once and immediately send the SAME original child a followup_task:
   wait 30 seconds, then return exactly AUTO_FOUR. Again immediately call
   sessions_yield, with no polling or manual wakeup. On its automatic
   completion, consume AUTO_FOUR once and report the results so far.

Do not create a replacement child, retry through another session, or read
transcript files to obtain a missing result. Do not treat the marker text
in this prompt as a received result. If a completion has no current child
identity/result, or followup_task rejects the original child, report the
actual error instead of repairing the test.

Report: original child identity, actual completed turns, confirmed yield
acknowledgements where observable, automatic resumptions, and consumed
results. Mark anything unobserved as unknown, not passed. Duplicate notices
must not cause duplicate followups or consumption. Stop after AUTO_FOUR;
wait for my separate fifth-turn prompt.
```

**Do not send a ping while waiting.** A delayed result must resume the parent without user input. A parent that merely says it will wait has not demonstrated a successful yield. If the child finishes before the yield and it returns `nothing_pending`, that run did not exercise the required boundary; repeat in a fresh conversation with a longer child delay. An acknowledgement replaced by `aborted by user` is not a successful native yield acknowledgement.

### Only after AUTO_FOUR arrived automatically: fresh user follow-up

```text
Continue the same reproduction with the SAME original native child. Send
it a followup_task asking it to wait 30 seconds and return exactly
AUTO_FIVE. Immediately call sessions_yield. Do not poll, wait_agent, create
a replacement child, or ask me to ping. On the automatic completion,
consume the actual AUTO_FIVE result once and report the final totals:
five completed turns on one child, three confirmed yields, three automatic
delayed-result resumptions, and each result consumed once. Report missing
or unobservable evidence honestly rather than inferring success.
```

### Expected result versus observed stock failure

Expected: one original child remains usable through all five turns; turns 3–5 each have a persisted native `yielded` output and automatic once-only consumption, with no user input between a yield and its completion. The second prompt is sent **after** turn 4 succeeds, not to rescue it.

**Observed on official stock 2026.11.1 on 2026-11-06:** the same child reached three turns, but the first native yield output became `aborted by user after 0.1s`. Automatic completion started a different native parent and omitted the current child identity/result. No delayed result was consumed; turns 4 and 5 were never reached. The failing assertion was `Current event must identify original child`. This is more specific than “the parent did not wake up”: a wakeup occurred, but continuation context/ownership was lost.

For a manual failure report, preserve the child's completed result, the yield/tool outcome, the automatic wake event (if any), and any original-child follow-up error. If nothing arrives after several minutes, preserve the trace before sending another message; a stall alone does not establish which boundary failed. Native parent-ID retention and persisted yield outputs require runtime/native-history evidence, not just the model's summary.

**Evidence boundary:** the stock result above was reproduced with installed official Gateway/plugin/native binaries and a deterministic local scripted Responses provider, not by running these exact natural-language prompts against a live model. The prompts express the same sequence, but model adherence and timing can vary; one passing manual attempt does not rule out the race. Stock archive SHA-256: `611282534d576e12f10b0ac5a1ac0d2825aac360637e92815a56eb71fb5a0301`; release commit: `4ffdd2047d192dd65554de3c8c46c0e0197c6e2a`. This demonstrates the remaining stable-release failure, not independent causality for every stable backport patch or qualification of the current upstream PR head.

## Reproduction and scope

A packaged Gateway + packaged native Codex test on the prior PR head completed two ordinary turns on one child, then genuinely yielded while the third result was pending. Automatic delivery resumed with a changed tool catalog, started a second native parent, and the original-child follow-up failed lineage checks. The provider was deterministic local scripted Responses, not a real model or OAuth acceptance test.

The new regression exercises the real harness lifecycle with a nonempty native tool catalog, holds terminal-child delivery after the execution pin releases, and admits the completion with no current executors. With only the catalog owner restored to the prior implementation, it fails with two native thread starts instead of one. With the repair, it preserves the original parent and rejects execution of the old tool.

## Follow-up: preserve terminal yield acknowledgements

A fresh live run on the separate stable candidate completed five original-child turns and automatically resumed all three delayed results, but two yield acknowledgements became `aborted by user`. It was not counted as a full acceptance pass.

The native dynamic-tool `item/completed` event precedes the handler's return. Interrupting at that point can replace the model-visible result with cancellation, even after OpenClaw has recorded terminal release. Waiting a JavaScript event-loop tick does not establish native output commitment.

The lifecycle owner now waits for matching `rawResponseItem/completed` function/custom output receipts in its existing model-response inventory. These prove recording in native model history before interruption. Nested Code Mode waits for the outer output; web/image calls are not incorrectly required to emit function outputs. No new protocol, timer, persisted state, or authority relaxation is introduced.

## Ownership and safety

- Read pending-delivery custody from the existing completion owner; no new custody registry or persistent state.
- Require the same physical native client, current assignment/history ownership, and the existing claimed delivery owner.
- Recheck catalog eligibility after reading native metadata.
- Keep execution pins released at terminal completion; never restore old executors.
- Release declaration eligibility when delivery settles, is abandoned, or loses custody.
- Share the existing child-execution predicate between its two monitor consumers; the oversized monitor file shrinks.

## Historical evidence — main refresh, 2026-11-01

Source: `9b99b76361370209209833996856e7080a5eb5c6`, rebased onto pinned main `72a691e5f732b04a53ffd9e83f96a61bc16d2016`. All four original commits remain patch-identical (`git range-diff` reports `=`); a fifth bookkeeping commit adds the exact 570-line regression allocation required by current main policy. No continuation behavior or assertion changed.

- Initial refreshed head `a5ac73f00f1c8c0769caf6e7a8f02d8faf1c98e9` on `5342923d897ad8a8021bdf586753f8cd38cd3094`: 218 successful test executions across 12 files in 437.79 seconds wrapper wall, including Gateway final-effect authority, catalog custody, original-child follow-up, lifecycle/steering, real native output-before-interrupt, and test-plan ownership. The 55 configuration cases execute on both test runtimes.
- Final head: 13 cases across four files passed in 140.65 seconds wrapper wall, covering the intervening upstream MCP data-directory change, pending-completion catalog preservation, direct/nested recorded-output ordering and real native output-before-interrupt.
- Final-head production plugin types and scoped extension test types passed (23.11 s / 13.14 s). Targeted type-aware lint with pinned runtime parity passed (74.01 s); formatting (0.43 s), pinned-base line-cap (1.10 s), and test-line allocation/budget (3.51 s) passed.
- The first lint invocation passed into the parity step but could not stage pinned Bun in the offline environment. Canonical online dependency staging resolved that prerequisite; the complete lint wrapper then passed offline. No gate, source assertion or timeout was weakened.
- Independent native source review of the full final range found no P0–P2 findings and independently verified the 570-line allocation. This is a source review, not CLI autoreview or live acceptance. The reviewed previous-series evidence remains historical; the exact final base/head are pinned above.

Hosted CI for this exact head has settled: 132 check runs (67 successful, 62 skipped, 1 neutral, 2 cancelled), with zero failed or pending checks. The aggregate CI gate and dependency/security-sensitive review statuses are successful. Earlier CI and live stable-backport evidence below belongs only to its named sources/artifacts; the separately qualified 2026.10.9 package is described next. No deployment, restart or merge was performed.

## Stable 2026.10.9 backport qualification — 2026-11-01

This is a separate release-based custom artifact, not a package of the upstream PR head or certification of stock 2026.10.9.

- Base `v2026.10.9` / `8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41`; custom source `eac766eb5d61e8a5b670d1dca9b3b2234bf11c99`. Four existing custom patches remain patch-identical; upstream filesystem-policy changes are preserved. Independent source review found no P0–P2 findings.
- Build `2026.10.9-custom-continuation-eac766eb5d6-20261101`; archive SHA-256 `ea691831432719785870299aabd3a1be7d12a9c43c5dc905123f69eb3a2f64cd`.
- 722 successful test executions across 28 distinct files (736.8 seconds wrapper wall), scoped core/plugin production and test types, separate type-aware lint, and formatting passed. Controlled removal of the native-output barrier reproduced both expected premature-interruption failures; the candidate was restored and its source is clean.
- Canonical build/inventory/tarball/import-graph checks passed (566.8 seconds). Fresh exact-archive installation passed (45.77 seconds), followed by offline Doctor and bundled Codex selection checks. Installed identity matched 8,911 core files, 22 Codex files and native Codex 0.160.0.
- Exact installed package, Docker networking disabled, synthetic state and scripted local Responses provider: five distinct completed turns on one original child, three persisted yielded acknowledgements and three automatic once-only result consumptions passed (61.98 seconds). No replacement child, manual completion wakeup or polling drove continuation.

Five stable line-cap failures remain explicitly recorded as unchanged backport exceptions: +13, +1, +45, +13 and +3 counted lines. Release-base/candidate blobs and added/removed patch lines match the prior qualified 10.8 patch. These are **not passing size-check results**; no checker or threshold was weakened. An initial main-only Bun staging attempt was inapplicable because this stable release has no such module; its actual canonical lint passed without toolchain substitution.

This is fresh-install scripted-provider qualification, **not retained-state upgrade, live-model/OAuth, service-restart/recovery or browser acceptance**. No live state was mounted and no deployment, restart or release was performed. All qualification workers finished and their task-owned containers were removed through their own automatic teardown.

## Historical evidence — CI repair rebase, 2026-10-29

Source: `22540643f20c845ff5fea04408b89549d8448bbb`, rebased onto pinned main `02e19a39282d6af1cc93e01d7045681d0124b433`. All four PR commits are patch-identical to the previous series (`git range-diff` reports `=` for each); no continuation behavior or test assertion was changed in this refresh.

The previously failing `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` job reported 14 mock-export sites in two upstream Gateway tests. This base includes [upstream repair #187120](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187120) (`e25c026eb75`): justified whole-module isolation annotations for shutdown/startup tests and corresponding stale-baseline cleanup. The two red `openclaw/ci-gate` entries reflected that same underlying failure. All three PostgreSQL jobs on the previous head ultimately passed.

Current-head local validation in secretless Docker:

- Mock-export guard against pinned base: passed, 15.92 s.
- Focused continuation, native yield-output, same-child custody, Gateway shutdown/spawn-broker, and test-plan tests: 226 successful executions across 14 files, 413.22 s wrapper wall (the 54 configuration cases execute on both test runtimes).
- Production plugin types: passed, 25.40 s; scoped test types: passed, 16.18 s.
- Targeted type-aware lint with pinned runtime parity: passed, 216.57 s; formatting: passed, 0.47 s.
- Pinned-base line-cap and test-line budget: passed, 1.43 s and 4.65 s. No check or baseline was weakened by this PR.
- Independent native GPT-6-Sol source/rebase review of the full 15-file range `02e19a3..2254064`: no actionable P0–P2 findings. This is a source review, not CLI autoreview or live acceptance. Working tree and `git diff --check` are clean.

Hosted CI for this exact head passed on 2026-10-29: 132 check runs settled (68 successful, 62 skipped, 1 neutral CodeQL result, and 1 superseded/cancelled PR-context run), with zero failed or pending checks. The previously failing [baseline ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40962090873/job/123758008168) and the [aggregate CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40965138477) both succeeded. The exact tested base is pinned above; subsequent main changes are not included in this local verdict. The live 10.7/10.8 backport acceptances and stock-versus-patched Docker comparison below remain evidence for their named artifacts, not a new package or live-model acceptance of this rebased upstream head.

## Historical source validation — 2026-10-28 upstream head

Source: `9c948da8a43477fb375ba8c7e5c08b14ef4b8ec2`, rebased onto pinned main `a919e5ecc4f6c579e16ab21499ccda3acaa1fb07` on 2026-10-28.

- At source-equivalent predecessor `d2b9766017ba75a56c419f8a316214201a145bdc`, 108 targeted cases across ten files passed in 215.03 seconds wrapper wall time, including delayed-completion authority, pending catalog custody, same-child follow-up, lifecycle/steering/output receipt tests and the real native-process yield test.
- Production plugin types, scoped extension-test types, targeted type-aware lint (including pinned Bun parity), formatting, pinned-base line-cap and test-line budget checks passed.
- Independent source review of this exact range found no actionable P0–P2. The original production/test patch is unchanged; the old test-budget-only increase was removed because upstream now owns a larger shared ceiling. Upstream shutdown, subagent cleanup, sidebar and annotated UI receipt fixes are preserved.
- The real native case uses pinned Codex 0.164.0 and synthetic inference. Historical controlled-failure evidence below still documents the patch mechanism; neither a new full packaged upstream acceptance nor hosted CI success is claimed for this rebased head.
- The initial lint attempt on the preceding base could not stage the pinned Bun parity runtime in an offline container. Canonical staging resolved the tooling prerequisite; no lint gate or parity check was bypassed.

### Full-suite registration correction and hosted CI

That pre-rebase head added only the missing `run-attempt-lifecycle-controller.output-receipt.test.ts` entry to the database-worker test plan. Hosted CI on the predecessor caught that direct test selection was insufficient to prove full-suite discovery. The exact final head passed 54 configuration cases on both test runtimes plus four receipt cases (112 executions, 215.31 seconds wrapper wall), and scoped lint/format. Production/test source is otherwise unchanged, so the preceding source checks remain applicable.

A separate hosted `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` failure lists 14 mock-export sites in `src/gateway/server-shutdown.runtime.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server.spawn-broker.test.ts`. Both files are byte-identical to pinned upstream main `a919e5e`; the same diagnostics reproduce locally. That pre-rebase check was **not green**; the later rebase described in current evidence below incorporates upstream’s repair. [Failing job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40791343185/job/123177622310). No gate or baseline was weakened.

## Historical source validation — pre-rebase head

Source: `7ac126cd15dc6f67d14944b4b4a97c1b8697313e`, based on pinned main `58bf6decb46a946365900bb6d2f93b96e9b52f69`.

- Controlled original-controller comparison: both new direct/nested receipt regressions fail on premature native interruption; candidate bytes restored afterward.
- 57 lifecycle/steering/receipt/native cases passed across four files (67.60 seconds total wrapper wall time). Existing fixtures now explicitly model recorded output; no assertions were weakened. Two native-sibling cases moved out of the oversized suite.
- 29 full-attempt dynamic-tool, parent-continuation and original-child follow-up cases passed across three files (59.52 seconds wrapper wall time).
- Real pinned native Codex process plus production run-attempt/bridge/lifecycle and a synthetic local Responses provider: recorded `yielded` output precedes `turn/interrupt`, no aborted acknowledgement, owned native process exits. The case took 6.464 seconds; it exercises an actual process/history boundary that the cheaper lifecycle tests cannot prove.
- The native test's host fixture supplies an eligible yield; it does not certify child-claim admission or automatic continuation. It uses isolated state and no operator credentials. The first setup attempts exposed test-lane/session-seeding omissions; those were corrected, not counted as product failures or successful proofs.
- Production plugin types, scoped test types, targeted lint/format, pinned-base line-cap ratchet and exact test-line budget passed. Fresh independent source review found no actionable P0–P2 findings in the production repair; native proof source was separately reviewed by the lead.
- Simplification: one receipt bit in the existing call inventory replaces the assumption that a flushed response is ready for interruption; no parallel lifecycle or registry. The production delta for this follow-up is 17 added / 3 removed lines.

## Historical packaged proof (prior head, not current-head certification)

`f8699fea349def102ef4377b5009a556819583ac` passed 52 targeted tests plus packaged continuation in a fresh isolated installation: one parent, one original child, five persisted child turns, three genuine yields and three once-only automatic consumptions (96.19 seconds). Archive SHA-256 `2bbc9dc04691464cd91545c296d64651bdced78f307751d3da1699262ad13839`; build ID `2026.10.7-pr184848-f8699fea349-20261027`; native Codex `0.164.0`.

That packaged proof used scripted local HTTPS Responses/WebSocket inference with no external network. It is historical after the acknowledgement repair, not a rebuilt-package or real-model/OAuth acceptance claim. The prior controlled catalog regression fails with two parent thread starts when only its owner repair is reverted.

## Evidence — live 2026.10.7 backport acceptance

On 2026-10-28, a fresh uninterrupted live native acceptance run passed against installed custom build `2026.10.7-custom-continuation-e7de3d6695e-20261028`, backport commit `e7de3d6695e0b4881b109291c666e60121989580`. The running Gateway reported `2026.10.7` and pointed to that installed package.

One native child completed two ordinary turns, then three delayed turns (25-second delay requested each). Each delayed completion automatically resumed the parent after an explicit `sessions_yield` acknowledgement of `status: yielded`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---:|
| Turns completed with the same native child | 5/5 |
| Confirmed yields on turns 3–5 | 3/3 |
| Automatic parent resumptions | 3/3 |
| Results consumed once | 5/5 |

No polling during delayed checks, manual wakeups, child replacements, or user interruptions. No `nothing_pending` or interrupted acknowledgements were counted. Mirrored notifications were deduplicated: this proves once-only consumption, not transport-level exactly-once delivery. An earlier interrupted run was inconclusive and is excluded from this table.

These live results apply to the **stable custom backport**, not the upstream PR head. [Live acceptance report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184848#issuecomment-6480604481).

## Evidence — live 2026.10.8 backport acceptance

On 2026-10-29, fresh live native acceptance passed on the installed custom 2026.10.8 backport. The reachable running Gateway reported `2026.10.8`; session status identified build `55e31f3`, matching the qualified custom source `55e31f3e44f82154a6ffdabe58e725bec094a09c` (`2026.10.8-custom-continuation-55e31f3e44f-20261028`). This was live model execution, not the earlier scripted-provider package proof.

One original native child completed two ordinary turns and three delayed follow-up turns (20-second delay requested per delayed turn). For each of turns 3–5, the parent called `sessions_yield`, received `status: yielded`, and was automatically resumed by that child's completion.

| Check | Result |
|---|---:|
| Turns completed with the same native child | 5/5 |
| Confirmed yields on turns 3–5 | 3/3 |
| Automatic parent resumptions | 3/3 |
| Results consumed once | 5/5 |

No polling during delayed checks, manual wakeups, replacement children, or user interruptions. No `nothing_pending` or interrupted yield acknowledgements were counted. Mirrored completion notices surfaced for turns 3–5 and were ignored after the first consumption, as in the 10.7 acceptance: once-only consumption is demonstrated, not transport-level exactly-once delivery.

This is additional **stable custom backport** evidence, not certification of the upstream PR head, unmodified 2026.10.8, or a new stock-versus-patched controlled comparison. No installation, restart, configuration change, or merge was performed for this acceptance. At that live acceptance, the upstream source head was `9c948da8a43477fb375ba8c7e5c08b14ef4b8ec2`; later rebases are separately qualified.

## Evidence — stock versus patched 2026.10.8 Docker control

On 2026-10-29, **stock failed and the custom stable backport passed the same continuation-focused probe**. These were real installed Gateway and native Codex processes with scripted local Responses inference, not live-model/OAuth acceptance or a rebuilt upstream-head test.

### Pinned inputs

- Stock: npm `openclaw@2026.10.8`, release commit `dc2523e5a5c7a309517fd7fa834add938231d526`; archive SHA-256 `7e36685a0b5fd9c8c3afcfa93ee33fad871f7c6c8b6e695cae6720d14a765f18`, also checked against registry SHA-512 integrity. Matching official `@openclaw/codex@2026.10.8` installed via the supported plugin CLI, with trusted-official registry ownership verified.
- Patched: custom stable source `55e31f3e44f82154a6ffdabe58e725bec094a09c`; archive SHA-256 `192509e3911ae9bba6437dc1f1f7dbac96525d612fc3f3ade82ceefef6b10f55`, using its bundled Codex plugin.
- Both: Node 24.22.1 and native Codex 0.160.0, identical native binary SHA-256 `12eb3e81114588aca3b7998f4f19e8997b056aca08e57a7ca7c8a3ec8c652aad`.
- Separate synthetic state; dependency staging online, execution with Docker networking disabled. No production credentials/state or Docker socket mounted. Installed packages owned Gateway/plugin execution; a read-only source client supplied only Gateway RPC transport.

| Check | Stock 2026.10.8 | Custom 2026.10.8 |
|---|---|---|
| Original-child completed turns | 3; stopped at first delayed continuation | 5/5 |
| Persisted confirmed yield outputs | 1 | 3/3 |
| Automatic completion wakeup | Observed after turn 3 | All 3 |
| Native parent identity retained | No | Yes |
| Current delayed-result payload supplied | No | Yes |
| Delayed results consumed once | 0 | 3/3 |
| Runtime phase, including setup/cleanup | 89.68 s; exit 1 | 54.31 s; exit 0 |

### Observed failure boundary

The stock child persisted three completed turns. Its original parent persisted `status: yielded` before the delayed third result was released. Automatic completion then arrived under a **different native parent ID**, carrying the inter-session wakeup placeholder without the current child-result payload. Both provider-visible instructions and input were inspected: the result marker occurred only in quoted earlier task/history text, not as the delivered completion. The current original-child event assertion failed before a fourth child turn could be requested. This was not merely failure to wake the parent or a timeout.

The patched control retained one parent and one original child, five distinct persisted completed child turns, three persisted `yielded` outputs, and three once-only delayed-result consumptions. No polling or manual wakeups drove delayed completion. A separate ordinary user turn requested the fifth child action only after the fourth result was consumed.

### Probe qualifications and limits

The old custom-package probe assumed bundled Codex; stock requires the official plugin installation above. Its first setup verification failure is excluded from behavior evidence. A separate strict assertion about inbound context residing in top-level provider instructions also failed before child execution: stock carries that context in input messages. That request-layout difference is **not counted as a continuation failure or missing-context proof**. A separately identified continuation-focused variant records the layout fact without blocking child execution; all payload, identity, yield and consumption assertions remain intact. Identical variant bytes were used for both compared packages, without modifying runtime implementations.

This comparison supports the continuing need for the **combined stable backport** in this scenario, not the independent necessity of every patch or certification of this PR's current upstream head. Registry-versus-bundled plugin packaging differs; this is not a single-change causal experiment. The narrower controlled regressions above remain the evidence for individual repair mechanisms. All eight task-created containers were removed by recorded creation IDs; production Gateway identity and availability were unchanged.

## Limits and operational impact

No live installation, restart, configuration change or merge is part of this PR-body update or the live acceptance run. The stable 2026.10.7 and 2026.10.8 backports remain separate from the upstream PR; both installed custom packages passed the respective live acceptance above. That does not certify a rebuilt package of the upstream PR head. The observed duplicate native notifications and intermediate visible-reply warnings are not claimed fixed by this acknowledgement patch. No claim of production restart recovery, provider/OAuth recovery, or all-plugin test-type coverage.

## Test-line budget

The shared scalar is unchanged. The refresh adds `config/test-lines-allocations/codex-native-continuation.txt` for exactly 570 net counted test lines, as required by current main policy. These regressions exercise pending-delivery catalog custody, final-effect authority after foreground completion, direct/nested output receipt ordering, and real native dispatch/history before interruption. The allocation is bounded to this PR's independently recounted LF growth; it does not alter test assertions or forgive inherited debt. Pinned-base test-line and line-cap checks passed.
