prs.title: feat(templates): honor optional preferred models on Add
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Template authors cannot currently suggest a model that suits their agent without making the Template host-specific.

## User Impact

Authors may optionally set `agent.model` to an exact portable `provider/model` reference. Add uses it only when the host's ordinary picker reports it available and permitted. Omitted, missing, unauthenticated, unknown-readiness, denied, or failed-catalog preferences leave the agent unpinned, inheriting the unchanged Gateway default. No provider installation or credential acquisition is added.

This is a creation-time preference, not runtime failover or ongoing Template ownership of model selection. Model stays outside Template-owned fields and ownership digests. Existing operator-model preservation was inspected in code, not demonstrated by an actual Template-update integration. No migration or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse existing prepared, auth-aware model-picker facts rather than introduce another routing/discovery system. Chat Add reads the newly admitted agent's model owner; reviewed previews use the ambient owner. CLI Add/dev use the same preference rule with the ordinary offline catalog owner.

Simplification: retain the existing config/model owners and move the planning-context type to the canonical types module rather than exceed the lifecycle module's existing cap. Necessary growth is the optional manifest field, shared preference decision, adapters and regressions.

**Dependency: matching ClawHub validator acceptance must land before this PR.** The companion remains unpublished and blocked on its required reviewer authentication; no replacement reviewer is assumed authorized.

## Evidence

Comparable baseline/current schema execution: omitted model accepted before/after; `ollama/deepseek-r1:70b` rejected before and accepted after; bare alias `sonnet` and account pin `anthropic/model@work` rejected in both.

The isolated proof used the real Template builder, archive validation/download/extraction, Gateway Chat Add, persisted config and real Ollama inference. Registry HTTP metadata/trust were synthetic fixtures; those boundaries were not live registry publication. Services were stopped afterward; the live Gateway/config were unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Actual isolated Add/config/response output</summary>

The following is terminal output extracted from retained Add/response JSON receipts and the isolated persisted config, not expected-value fixtures. Only nonempty response-text rows are shown. `inherited` is the omitted-preference case. No credentials or endpoints are included.

```json
[
  {
    "scenario": "preferred",
    "addStatus": "complete",
    "persistedModel": "ollama/deepseek-r1:70b",
    "defaultModel": "ollama/qwen3:4b-instruct",
    "response": [
      {
        "provider": "ollama",
        "model": "deepseek-r1:70b",
        "stopReason": "length",
        "text": "\n\nI'll help you set up the agent based on the provided instructions. Let's go through the process step by step.\n\n1. **Greeting**:  \n   Hello! I'm your assistant, here to help you with your tasks.\n\n2. **Automations**:  \n   After reading `CLAW.md`, I"
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    "scenario": "missing",
    "addStatus": "complete",
    "persistedModel": null,
    "defaultModel": "ollama/qwen3:4b-instruct",
    "response": [
      {
        "provider": "ollama",
        "model": "qwen3:4b-instruct",
        "stopReason": "stop",
        "text": "I'm ready to assist you. Please let me know how I can help!"
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    "scenario": "inherited",
    "addStatus": "complete",
    "persistedModel": null,
    "defaultModel": "ollama/qwen3:4b-instruct",
    "response": [
      {
        "provider": "ollama",
        "model": "qwen3:4b-instruct",
        "stopReason": "stop",
        "text": "I'm ready to assist you. Please let me know how I can help!"
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

The preferred model generated length-capped text; that is not a claim of full task completion. The missing preference was `ollama/not-installed-model-spike`. Both missing and omitted remained unpinned and used the unchanged default. No browser UI, deployment or live registry proof is claimed.

</details>

Local checks:
- 105 schema/planning/application-policy tests and all 24 public Chat Add integration tests passed, covering available, missing, missing auth, unknown readiness, policy denied, catalog failure and omitted preferences.
- Core typecheck passed; eight CLI project/Gateway Add adapter tests passed in the preceding implementation pass.
- Follow-up repair for ClawSweeper's P2: both exact Gateway adapter assertions now include the new resolver callback, preserving persisted-roster and MCP checks. Reproduction: 2 failed / 31 passed. After the two-line repair: all 33 passed. Format, gateway-methods test typecheck and one-file lint passed. This is a test-contract repair, not weakened assertions or changed production behavior.
- `pnpm check:changed` failed only on the unchanged baseline unused export `resolvePluginPrereleaseExtensionRuntimes` in `scripts/lib/plugin-prerelease-test-plan.mts`; other applicable gates passed. No check was disabled or weakened.

Test cost (`--maxWorkers=1`): public Chat Add fixture 154 seconds / combined runner 184 seconds. The adapter repair file took 17.03 seconds in Vitest / 21.76 seconds wrapper time. No extra Gateway boot was added. Full OpenClaw suite was not run locally; exact-head PR CI supplies broader proof.

## Review and CI follow-up

[Hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199988#issuecomment-6908535678) completed for repaired head `612c3287aca9eecf0f5ff7c683c0d42c1a040bad` at 2026-11-16 06:51 UTC: zero actionable findings, the earlier adapter finding fixed, and terminal behavior proof sufficient. Registry acceptance remains a blocking dependency; the review does not waive required CI.

[Current CI run 43813268985](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43813268985), attempt 2, remains **failed**, not green:
- The repaired Gateway adapter job passed. The only remaining failed test leaves are the two CLI signatures below.
- `src/cli/program/message/helpers.test.ts:360`: expected original `Error`, got `ExpectedCliError` with `humanOutputWritten=true`. Main `25c97908924aaea78adb9fb2c5292ec08cd07384` reproduced the exact signature (1 failed / 51 passed); scheduled-main job `133111404499` independently reports the same assertion. A passing PR replay was not treated as a fix.
- `src/cli/program.nodes-diagnostics-auth.e2e.test.ts:290`: JSON validation expected `invalid --environment (use sandbox|production)`, got `exit`. A valid main replay at `c3413be17dd0c7f3007c52d34d036daeb8fc6b70` now reproduces that exact assertion (1 failed / 17 passed). The PR source passes all 18. The focused CLI suite owns its mocks/fixtures and used the supported `OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1` route; this is not a full runtime-build or Gateway E2E claim. Its CLI owners are unchanged between that main revision and CI's base `b9bc0def75b3d5d44d7a9b0832ec202eb4160b9e`, and untouched by this feature. The earlier failed prerequisite build remains non-evidence. Native PR checkout was restored successfully.
- Attempt-1 baseline-ratchets ended when its hosted runner lost communication; no assertion log was available. One scoped job recovery was requested after diagnosis. Replacement job `133139656489` passed. The CLI leaf results in attempt 2 are retained copies of attempt-1 results, verified by identical runner IDs and exact execution/failed-step timestamps; no new CLI execution is claimed.

The focused nodes comparison took 43.81 seconds on PR source and 41.33 seconds on main in Vitest (48.79 / 46.23 seconds wrapper time). Both remaining CLI failures are attributed to main; that attribution is not a passing required gate or a submitted CI exception. No prepare, merge, deployment or completed companion acceptance is claimed.

prs.title: fix(state): prevent retained deleted agents from blocking Gateway startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #200271: Gateway startup can crash-loop when a completed agent deletion intentionally retained an older database.

## User Impact

Active agents can start while the deleted agent’s retained files stay byte-for-byte unchanged. Pending deletions keep their existing behavior. Active-agent and shared-state validation, refusal behavior, and permanent-purge capabilities are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The startup copy-and-swap path added by #198389 (`ef930ebbad771ae219e033f8c5b59a12b5445ffb`) inventories physical agent stores without consulting deletion completion. Startup now consumes the deletion journal owner’s existing retained-ID query and excludes completed retained agents from both upgrade selection and shadow copying. No new schema, registry, fallback, or configuration is added.

The simplification pass keeps this decision with the existing deletion owner. Necessary scope: production +22/-6 lines, tests +103 lines, documentation +3 lines. Test growth is below the 400-line allocation threshold.

## Evidence

- **Red base:** unchanged production at `48cd549b1c48653061ec312e35fef62d13df62cf` plus the regression: `timeout 120s pnpm test src/state/state-upgrade.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'startup retained deletion'` — **2 failed, 1 passed, 7 skipped**; both completed-retention cases reject with `no such module: vec0` from generic fallback. The pending-deletion control passes with today’s schema refusal/fallback failure.
- **Green fix:** `timeout 120s pnpm test src/state/state-upgrade.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **10 passed, 0 failed**; 56.95 s command wall time (54.59 s Vitest duration; 13.394 s summed test time). Covers completed retention alone, completed retention beside a shared-state upgrade, and the pending-deletion control. CI seconds are not yet available.
- Real SQLite, the existing v26 schema fixture, a retained session row, and a real `vec0` virtual table reproduce the reported fallback error. Current-schema active stores are present. Retained database bytes and directory contents remain unchanged after the fixed upgrade; the active store bytes also remain unchanged.
- Targeted lint and TypeScript compiler diagnostics: `timeout 120s pnpm exec oxlint --type-aware --type-check --threads=1 --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/state/state-upgrade.ts src/state/state-upgrade.test.ts` — exit 0, zero diagnostics. A temporary negative control reported TS2322 and was removed.
- `timeout 30s pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/state/state-upgrade.ts src/state/state-upgrade.test.ts docs/install/updating.md` and `timeout 20s git diff --check` pass. Commit hooks also pass.
- Local ClawSweeper is unavailable. Independent **autoreview**, Codex, P0–P2, reviewed the full local candidate against `48cd549b1c48653061ec312e35fef62d13df62cf`: **scoped-clean, no actionable findings**. Candidate diff SHA-256: `165afa0f222e905c275028524a56758567fd7f0b550f5723b66b0baa8103814a`; committed without further code changes as `db8faf1c6e41d7f83616ec570c4204eda24d4058`. One hosted review will be requested if none is already pending.

- **Live upgrade from latest stable (Crabbox AWS Linux, Node 24.19.0):**
  - **Setup:** npm `openclaw@2026.11.4` (`d843d6a`), isolated state. Created agents `keeper` and `retired`, started the stable Gateway, then called `agents.delete {agentId: "retired", deleteFiles: false}` and stopped it cleanly. The journal row was `cleanup_completed=1, delete_files=0, phase=retiring`; state was v22 and agents were v27. One tarball snapshot was used for both runs.
  - **Base `48cd549b` (red):** startup listed `agents/retired/.../openclaw-agent.sqlite v27` for upgrade. It logged `State upgrade chain failed at agent-schema: .../retired/... is at schema 27 after the chain, expected 42`, then fell back to the generic copy and set aside 7 rows. The retained database was rewritten (its sha256 changed) and its `.seal` was removed. The stores had no `vec0` tables, so this run finished on the degraded generic-copy path instead of the reporter's `no such module: vec0` exit. The vec0 crash is covered by the in-process regression above.
  - **PR head `db8faf1c` (green):** the upgrade inventory listed only state v22, `keeper` v27 and `main` v27. Startup reported `State upgraded ... by migration chain`: no fallback, no rows set aside. `/healthz` returned 200 `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}` and `/readyz` returned 200 `{"ready":true,"coreReady":true,"failing":[]}`. After the upgrade, state was v40 and `keeper`/`main` were v42. The retained `retired` database and seal were byte-identical (sha256 `6616c54a…` / `0a5e3ed5…` before and after), and its journal row was unchanged. `agents list` shows `main` and `keeper`, and config (`gateway.port`) was preserved.
  - Both leases were stopped. The first box lost its worker connection mid-run and was replaced; the red evidence comes from that first box and the green evidence from the replacement, both from the same stable setup steps.

Limits: no live macOS launchd reproduction. The live stable-to-head proof above used stores without `vec0` tables; the `vec0` exit path is covered by the in-process regression with a real `vec0` table. Broad checks are left to PR CI under the production-host restrictions.

Reported by @hannesrudolph

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/78580230-7d1b-4329-a7dd-72554eb66323)

prs.body:
Closes #200283
Related: #179988 (stalled draft for the same gesture; this PR is an independent implementation that also covers navigation-rail session shortcuts)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Control-clicking a sidebar session reloads the entire dashboard instead of leaving its session menu open, on macOS (app WKWebView and Safari).

## User Impact

User impact: Mac users can Control-click a sidebar session to use its menu (rename, icon, etc.) without the dashboard reloading. Plain clicks, Command-clicks, middle-clicks, Shift-click selection, and non-Mac Control-clicks keep their existing behavior. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

On macOS, Control+primary click is the secondary click. WebKit delivers `contextmenu` (the row opens its menu and cancels that event) and then a trailing `click` with `button=0 ctrlKey=true`. The session link's click handler intentionally ignores modified clicks, so that trailing click follows the `href` as a full document navigation, which also tears down the menu. Sidebar session links now treat a Mac Control+primary click as a secondary click: the click is canceled and routed to the existing session-menu owner, de-duplicated against `contextmenu` in either order (and still works if `contextmenu` is not delivered). One shared helper covers regular/adopted rows, catalog rows, and navigation-rail session shortcuts.

## Evidence

### Live native WebKit before/after (macOS 26.7.2, system WebKit 21624.5.1.11.3)

Two isolated loopback Gateways (no providers/channels/cron) each serving a Control UI built from its own checkout: **base** `f947bdc94` (merge-base) and **head** `2d9ccf1dd`. Three seeded sessions. Real Control+left-clicks driven on a Mac on three different sidebar session links, in (1) a bare AppKit `WKWebView` harness (no custom context-menu or new-window handling) and (2) Safari 27.2. A passive capture-phase logger recorded events; the page document's time origin and the Gateway WebSocket log show whether a new document loaded.

| Client | Build | New document / reload | Session menu after gesture |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| WKWebView | base | **Yes, 3/3** | No (navigation dismisses it) |
| WKWebView | head | **No, 0/3** | **Yes, 3/3** |
| Safari | base | **Yes, 3/3** | No |
| Safari | head | **No, 0/3** | **Yes, 3/3** |

Representative native sequence (both clients):
```
pointerdown/mousedown  button=0 ctrlKey=true
contextmenu            button=0 ctrlKey=true  -> defaultPrevented=true (row opens menu)
mouseup/click          button=0 ctrlKey=true
  base: click.defaultPrevented=false -> href followed -> new document, socket replaced
  head: click.defaultPrevented=true  -> menu stays open, same document, same socket
```
Gateway log, base, first WKWebView gesture: `23:39:27.161 webchat disconnected` → `23:39:27.379 client connected build=2026.11.4-f947bdc94981-…`. On head the three Control-clicks stay on one socket.

**Command-click (head):** `metaKey=true`, click not canceled, no session menu. Safari opens a background tab and the original document is unchanged; the bare harness (no new-window delegate) follows the link, as expected for a plain WKWebView.

| WKWebView base — after Control-click (reloaded, no menu) | WKWebView head — after Control-click (menu open) |
| --- | --- |
| ![base](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/e-jung/openclaw/ac5375d431edd43be72de5ead55a91b82849cdde/wk-base-after.png) | ![head](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/e-jung/openclaw/ac5375d431edd43be72de5ead55a91b82849cdde/wk-fix-after.png) |

<details>
<summary>More screenshots, raw traces, harness source, method</summary>

- Safari head, menu open: ![safari head](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/e-jung/openclaw/ac5375d431edd43be72de5ead55a91b82849cdde/safari-fix-after.png)
- Command-click on head (WKWebView): ![cmd](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/e-jung/openclaw/ac5375d431edd43be72de5ead55a91b82849cdde/wk-fix-cmd.png)
- Full report with per-gesture document time origins and method: [REPORT.md](https://github.com/e-jung/openclaw/blob/ac5375d431edd43be72de5ead55a91b82849cdde/REPORT.md)
- Raw event traces, Gateway WebSocket excerpts, and the WKWebView harness source ([Proof200283.swift](https://github.com/e-jung/openclaw/blob/ac5375d431edd43be72de5ead55a91b82849cdde/Proof200283.swift)): [proof/pr-200297 branch](https://github.com/e-jung/openclaw/tree/proof/pr-200297)

</details>

### Original report (OpenClaw.app 2026.11.4)

In the shipping macOS app, each Control-click on a session link produced a page-initiated main-frame navigation in WebKit's unified log ~5–8 ms after the press, plus a Gateway `disconnected code=1001` / reconnect pair. The `click` arrived with `button=0 ctrlKey=true` and was not prevented. Correction to the issue text: the reporter's logger was a bubble-phase `window` listener, and the row's `contextmenu` handler stops propagation, so `contextmenu` was most likely delivered there too. The native runs above confirm that sequence. Canceling that click in the app stopped the reloads.

### Tests and checks (head `2d9ccf1dd`, rebased on `f947bdc94`)

- New regression suite `app-sidebar-session-secondary-click.test.ts`: 9 Mac secondary-click cases fail on base (uncanceled navigation); 30/30 pass on head. Covers mounted regular, catalog, and rail session links; both event orders; omitted `contextmenu`; next-gesture reset; non-Mac Control-click, Command-click, middle-click, Shift-click, and plain SPA navigation.
- Existing row/rail/catalog consumer tests: 140 passed. `app-sidebar.interactions.test.ts`: 77 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `check:control-ui-controllers`, targeted oxlint and oxfmt: pass. Local `autoreview` (P0–P2): scoped-clean.

### Not covered live

- The native runs exercised regular sidebar session rows. Catalog rows and navigation-rail shortcuts use the same helper and are covered by the mounted tests, not by native runs.
- Live runs used a bare WKWebView and Safari against isolated Gateways, not OpenClaw.app itself, so as not to replace a production Gateway's Control UI.

prs.title: fix(templates): authorize new-agent rollback writes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A failed offline Template Add can save its new agent and then fail while activating the local runtime. Rollback prunes that agent, but the config writer rejects the removal because it lacks explicit deletion permission, leaving the agent and workspace behind.

## What Changed

Authorize only that newly created agent ID in the existing rollback write, after the existing unchanged-agent and workspace checks. Later failures after the agent becomes available still keep the agent and conversation.

Carries forward @anmol0b's fix from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196054 onto current main, with the regression adapted to the current runtime-activation boundary. Closes #196048.

## Evidence

| Current-base proof | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Runtime activation rejects after agent registration, through the real config writer | Roster guard rejects rollback; new agent and workspace remain | Only `main` remains; new workspace is absent; replanning selects the original agent ID |

Validation:

- New regression failed on current main with the exact roster-removal guard error, then passed with the fix.
- `pnpm test src/templates/add-stateless.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 24 passed; Vitest 26.81s, wrapper wall time 99.65s. CI seconds pending publication.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, targeted lint/format, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Production change: +8/-2 ignoring whitespace. Tests: +22 lines. No new cleanup owner, configuration option, or compatibility path.

Proof limits: the runtime-readiness outage is injected; config persistence and workspace operations are real. The public CLI uses this rollback branch when local activation rejects before availability. A current CLI model-setup attempt did not reach that branch and is excluded. The original PR's cron CLI evidence and unresolved CI timeout remain historical; they are not presented as proof that the old timeout was repaired.

prs.title: fix(memory): dreaming deep phase promotes nothing when the recall store overflows
prs.body:
<!-- Based on this PR's recorded head (9e3a45f4260) so the review thread could be reopened after an earlier force-push. `main` has moved 52 commits since the PR's base and has not touched any file this PR changes, so this merges cleanly. Keeps @mariorivas1's review thread and the #150635 link. -->

## What Problem This Solves

The short-term recall store keeps a hard cap of 512 entries. When nightly staging pushes the store past that cap, the old retention rule sorted by `lastRecalledAt` and dropped the oldest rows. The nightly ingestion stamps its staged rows with the sweep time, so the rows that had actually been *recalled* - the ones carrying query provenance - were exactly the rows that aged out first. Upstream reports 0 of 512 entries left with `recallCount > 0` after the sweep, and a promotion phase that reports `Ranked 0 candidate(s) for durable promotion` every night.

This is the recall-store overflow eviction that leaves the deep promotion phase with nothing to rank (openclaw/openclaw#150635).

## What this changes

The overflow rule now keeps rows with interactive recall evidence, with three guardrails:

1. **Evidence, not age.** A protected row must carry real interactive recall evidence: `recallCount > 0` **and** at least one provenance-qualified interactive query hash. A nightly staging row never records query provenance, so it can never take a protected slot.
2. **Bounded.** At most `MAX_PROTECTED_RECALL_ENTRIES` = 128 rows (a quarter of the 512-entry window) are protected, so fresh staging admission always has room. Before this change a full protected set would evict every staging row; now at least 384 slots always remain.
3. **Ordered by evidence strength, not recency.** Protected slots go to the rows with more recalls, then more distinct interactive queries, then higher average relevance, and only then by recency. The nightly sweep refreshes `lastRecalledAt` on rows it never searched, so recency-first ordering would hand the protected slots back to the rows the sweep just staged.

Rows the promotion path can never use are still not protected: already-promoted rows, blocked provenance origins, contaminated snippets, rows outside the short-term corpus, and rows older than the promotion age window.

## Age window shared with the ranker

The age rule was previously inert in production (`maxAgeDays: -1`) while the promotion ranker's shipped ceiling is 30 days, so retention protected rows the ranker would never promote and they could never age out. The ceiling is now a named constant, `DEFAULT_MEMORY_DEEP_DREAMING_MAX_AGE_DAYS` (30), exported from `src/memory-host-sdk/dreaming.ts` and re-exported through the plugin SDK, and the retention uses the same age helpers as the ranker (`resolveShortTermRecallAgeDays` / `isShortTermRecallWithinMaxAge`).

## What this deliberately does NOT do

- **It does not mirror the promotion ranker's count thresholds** (`minRecallCount: 3`, `minUniqueQueries: 3`) **or its score threshold** (`minScore: 0.75`). Those are promotion-time selection criteria. Applying them to retention would evict exactly the rows that have not accumulated enough evidence to be promoted yet - the decay this PR exists to stop. Upstream reports a maximum recall count of 2 per entry on openclaw/openclaw#150635, so mirroring the count thresholds would protect no row at all in the field.
- **It does not make the deep phase promote by itself.** On the measured store below, the surviving candidates score 0.55-0.64 against the shipped 0.75 threshold, so the score gate still refuses them tonight. This PR stops the evidence decay; the other zero-promotion causes (the claim-key split, the path filter, the score gate, the promotion budget clamp) are separate and stay out of scope.
- **The age window uses the shipped default.** The retention ceiling is the shared 30-day constant; an operator who changes `phases.deep.maxAgeDays` keeps the shipped 30-day retention ceiling unless a caller passes `maxAgeDays` explicitly. With the shipped configuration the two agree exactly.
- **It does not change ingestion, the ranker, or the promotion apply path.**

## Evidence

Measured on Clyde's live short-term recall store (512 entries, 28 of them carrying interactive recall evidence), replayed with 40 staged rows per night:

| Nights | current main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | 28/28 evidence rows survive | 28/28 |
| 14 | **0/28** | **7/28** |
| 21 | 0/28 | 6/28 |
| 30 | 0/28 | 1/28 |

On current main every evidence row is gone by night 14 and never comes back. With this change 7 rows survive at night 14 and 6 at night 21; the rest age past the same 30-day window the promotion ranker uses, which is the intended behaviour rather than an accident.

The other 21 evidence rows are deliberately not protected: 20 carry a blocked provenance origin (`untrusted`) and 1 is already promoted.

The test-line budget is met by a reviewed allocation record: `config/test-lines-allocations/187049-memory-recall-retention.txt` (248 lines). This change adds 648 net test lines across four files - overflow regression, promotion flow, retention policy, age window - each proving a distinct shipped behavior that fails on base, against the shipped 400-line allowance.

Gates run on this branch: cold `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` exits 0, and the four focused memory-core vitest files pass (12 tests). The full memory-core suite has five failing files, all reproduced on the merge base (embedding-provider network failures plus one pre-existing `cli.test.ts` failure), so they are not diff-caused.

## Tests

- `short-term-recall-overflow-regression.test.ts` - the shipped path: record interactive recalls, overflow the store with nightly staging, then rank and promote. Fails on base (the recalled row is evicted), passes here.
- `short-term-promotion-flow.test.ts` - the full recall -> store -> rank -> promote chain, including rows written before query provenance existed.
- `short-term-promotion-utils.test.ts` - the policy itself: a row with a single interactive recall keeps its slot, the protected set stays bounded at 128 while staging rows keep entering the window, and the bounded slots go to the strongest evidence rather than the most recently recalled.
- `short-term-recall-retention-age.test.ts` - the age window: default 30 days, an explicitly wider window, and an unlimited window.

## Reviewer note

@mariorivas1 - this keeps your review thread. Two points from it are addressed: the age ceiling now shares the ranker's constant instead of a hardcoded `-1`, and the protected set is bounded so it can no longer evict every staging row. The one place I deliberately did not follow the "mirror the ranker" direction is the count thresholds, for the reason in the scope section above - upstream's own numbers (max recall count 2) say mirroring them would protect nothing.

The claim-key split you raised is a different defect and is not in this PR. Happy to file it as a separate issue if you prefer to own it - just say the word and I will leave it alone.

prs.title: HOLD: fix(sqlite): preserve evidence before offline repair
prs.body:
## Hold — recovery UX rejected
Do not merge this guidance-only patch. Product feedback on November 16, 2026 rejected requiring ordinary users to stop the Gateway and manually preserve database sidecars. Automatic preservation and a supported recovery action must be assessed instead. This patch has not been backported. Integrity refusal remains required; no orphan deletion or invented recovery is authorized.

## Problem
Integrity refusals currently promise that Doctor can inspect and repair any database, and advise preserving the database and WAL only after repair fails. Workboard SQL orphan rows have no such supported automatic repair.

## Change
Tell operators to stop the Gateway and preserve the database plus existing WAL/SHM sidecars before attempting repairs. Limit Doctor guidance to supported cases; unresolved damage needs a verified backup or database-owner reconciliation before restart. Integrity refusal, schema, stored data and repair policy are unchanged.

## Evidence
Expanded the existing real verified-snapshot regression to cover both Workboard event and label orphans. Both fresh and retained acquisition fail on original misleading guidance, after confirming all four orphan findings, unchanged DB/WAL/SHM bytes and no target publication. With the fix: 47 tests passed across snapshot-integrity and integrity-owner suites; focused typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting and diff check passed. Cold test invocation 43.5s (snapshot cases approximately 3s); CI timing pending. Dedicated allocation covers 23 net regression lines. One production string changed; no new helpers or APIs.

Local reviewer intentionally not invoked per release-owner direction. Hosted review and required CI remain outstanding. No live damaged data was accessed or repaired.

prs.title: improve(ci): avoid empty deletion probes during source preparation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Source capsule preparation runs an empty deletion probe even when no owned source path is absent.

## User Impact

The candidate removes four Git subprocesses per no-deletion capsule. **Performance hold: not ready to merge.** Fixture wall time and CPU improve, but process peak RSS has adverse tail values that have not been accepted. These measurements do not establish a memory regression in the source owner, and they do not establish a billing or full-repository speedup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Create deletion groups only for actual absent paths, create the empty blob on first use, and run source selection once without a deletion group. Cold index initialization, real deletion cleanup, privacy selection and sealed source trees remain intact.

Production: +7/-6 lines (net +1); tests unchanged. The one-line growth expresses conditional ownership of deletion work. No cache, API, configuration or dependency added.

## Evidence

- Frozen base `232ba9a63de6912b613aa7aa00ec0e0bbf9e7f99`; candidate `eb144f881f5d6cbfb8df49be227ad2af5ffcacc5`.
- `git diff --check`, native syntax check, and normal commit-hook formatting passed.
- Full-context local autoreview through P3: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Independent source review: GO. Local ClawSweeper unavailable; hosted review is deferred until readiness.
- `test/scripts/crabbox-source-capsule.test.ts`: **29/29 passed**, default Bun path, 104.75 s suite / 106.52 s wrapper. Covers cold/warm capsules, deletion/restoration, namespace replacement, sparse entries, symlinks and mirror integrity.
- Node v26.7.0 / Git 2.56.0 / macOS arm64, 18 logical CPUs. Ten paired samples per workload: five baseline/candidate, then five candidate/baseline. All 40 focused commands exited successfully; all original samples retained. Exact baseline and candidate module bytes were selected in one isolated workspace with identical remaining source/dependency inputs; candidate bytes were restored and verified clean afterward.
- Workload: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/crabbox-source-capsule.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --testNamePattern <pattern> --reporter=verbose`, wrapped in `/usr/bin/time -l` with Git Trace2. Patterns: `observes cold source only while copying` (two cold variants) and `keeps unchanged files and a warm index` (warm lifecycle, including its cold setup and deletion checks).
- Acceptance was recorded before measurement: preserve assertions, remove four Git calls per no-deletion capsule, report all metrics, no automatic regression waiver. The fixed reverse-order follow-up investigated adverse tails; no further rerun is implied.

| Workload / metric | Baseline | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Cold Git starts | 102 | 94 | -8 every sample |
| Cold median wall | 3.942 s | 3.496 s | -11.30% |
| Cold p95 wall | 4.896 s | 4.225 s | -13.71% |
| Cold median CPU | 3.340 s | 3.140 s | -5.99% |
| Cold p95 CPU | 3.670 s | 3.400 s | -7.36% |
| Cold median peak RSS | 407.855 MB | 407.527 MB | -0.08% |
| Cold p95/max peak RSS | 409.551 MB | 414.302 MB | **+1.16%** |
| Warm-lifecycle Git starts | 183 | 175 | -8 every sample |
| Warm-lifecycle median wall | 5.062 s | 4.747 s | -6.22% |
| Warm-lifecycle p95 wall | 5.518 s | 5.513 s | -0.07% |
| Warm-lifecycle median CPU | 3.865 s | 3.715 s | -3.88% |
| Warm-lifecycle p95 CPU | 4.200 s | 4.170 s | -0.71% |
| Warm-lifecycle median peak RSS | 406.856 MB | 407.036 MB | **+0.044%** |
| Warm-lifecycle p95/max peak RSS | 408.764 MB | 410.649 MB | **+0.46%** |

MB is decimal; p95 uses nearest rank and equals the maximum with ten samples. The warm workload is a lifecycle sequence, not a pure warm-only timing. The cold maximum and warm memory differences remain unresolved under the written rule. Independent final gate review: **HOLD**.

Build and receiver integration proof remain pending. The first [manual CI dispatch](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43975487388) used an invalid `validation_tier=main` for a frozen PR target and failed manifest admission; no source defect was established. The [corrected exact-target dispatch](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43975815010) was stopped after the performance hold to avoid further spend; it is not successful build proof. The earlier [Testbox allocation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43975091000) queued before tests and was stopped and reconciled.

Detailed measurements and the wider CI cost audit remain in the private campaign gist; no private host or workspace data is included here.

prs.title: fix(codex): recover blocked follow-ups with session Stop
prs.body:
Closes #194664

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a Codex conversation remaining blocked after a finished turn leaves a native command running, while session Stop reports no active run.

## User Impact

An authorized owner's session Stop can terminate retained work without resetting the thread. Refusals and `/codex binding` identify the holders, including ordinary managed sessions without an explicit conversation binding. If native termination is unconfirmed, Stop reports incomplete cleanup rather than claiming success; custody and thread protection remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Session Stop uses the existing native process authority and request-custody selector. Other requesters' commands and run-scoped Stop remain isolated. Diagnostics expose holder identities and age, not command text/output, and inspection never starts a client.

Addressed both review findings: negative native termination acknowledgments retain custody, add descendant cleanup errors, and do not increment killed; binding inspection resolves the existing managed-session identity read-only. Checked overlapping #194294: this repair preserves uncertain-termination custody without importing its broader final-receipt settlement, inventory, retry, or lifecycle changes. Shared native-process-authority edits will need reconciliation if that PR lands first.

Command-only recovery uses existing `aborted` status with a null host run ID. Confirmed terminations count even if native completion settles their admission during the request.

## Evidence

Final local gates on the repaired tree:

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: pass.
- Oxfmt and oxlint: pass on all 8 changed files.
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet`: pass, +226 net test lines / 400 allowance.
- `git diff --check`: pass.
- Focused tests, each file separately with `--maxWorkers=1`: **205 passed across 12 files**. The initial recovery-test run caught an ASCII/fullwidth display-parenthesis expectation mismatch; corrected the assertion and reran its entire file (11/11 pass).

<details><summary>Focused test results (paths relative to extensions/codex/src)</summary>

| File | Passed |
| --- | ---: |
| `app-server/run-attempt.native-background-outcome.test.ts` | 11 |
| `app-server/session-cancellation.test.ts` | 1 |
| `app-server/run-attempt-native-process-authority.test.ts` | 13 |
| `app-server/run-attempt-continuity.test.ts` | 1 |
| `app-server/native-subagent-monitor.custody.test.ts` | 21 |
| `app-server/native-subagent-monitor.direct-authority.test.ts` | 19 |
| `app-server/native-subagent-monitor.parent-retention.test.ts` | 2 |
| `app-server/thread-lifecycle.handoff-cancellation.test.ts` | 11 |
| `app-server/session-retirement.test.ts` | 8 |
| `app-server/thread-lifecycle.assignment-rotation.test.ts` | 21 |
| `command-binding.test.ts` | 3 |
| `commands.test.ts` | 94 |

</details>

The recovery regression covers retained-work refusal, managed `/codex binding` holder visibility, another requester's no-op Stop, native `{terminated:false}` producing `killed:0` plus cleanup errors while retaining protection and refusing follow-up, then confirmed owner Stop and same-thread continuation. The separate binding regression proves managed-session inspection without starting a client. These are synthetic boundary tests, not live-process proof.

### Live behavior proof
2026-11-16, 22:47:39–22:48:14 UTC; candidate `b81fbfdade2`, bundled native Codex `0.164.0`, real provider inference (no mocks).
Private temporary source copy; the four changed runtime files match candidate SHA-256 hashes. No source changes or GitHub writes.

prs.title: feat(message): let operators confine group-turn sends to the current conversation
prs.body:
Related: #190557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a group turn's `message` send can reach the owner's DM or another chat when the operator wants group turns kept in their own conversation, because the existing `crossContext` switches confine every kind of turn or none.

## User Impact

User impact: existing configs behave exactly as on main; no default changes. An operator who sets `tools.message.crossContext.confineChatTypes: ["group", "channel"]`, globally or per agent, gets group and channel turns that can only send to their own conversation. Any other target, on the same provider or another one, fails with `message_cross_context_denied` before a transport call. DM turns keep their current permissions. Separately, under the existing `allowWithinProvider: false`, a Telegram forum-topic send or poll that names the chat id with the current topic's `threadId`, or inherits it, is no longer denied. Other actions from a topic turn, such as renaming a topic, still have to name the current topic, as on main. Two deliberate tightenings apply under `allowWithinProvider: false`, or when group turns are confined. A turn in a Telegram forum topic can no longer create a forum topic in that chat, even through its own topic target, which main allows; the new topic is a sibling conversation in the base chat, and a turn bound to the chat itself still can. Telegram topic creation and topic edits that name another chat through `chatId`, `chat_id` or `channel_id` are denied. In every mode, a target that disagrees with one of those fields is refused as conflicting input. A numeric `target`, `to` or `channelId` is now read as its string, so it follows the same rules as the string: with a target the target wins, and alone it is the destination the check judges. Before, a numeric `channelId` skipped the check and Telegram acted on it, and a numeric `to` or `target` was dropped for the current conversation. A number that is not a safe integer is refused.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision (4b90fc67b80) flipped the shipped `allowWithinProvider` default to deny. That was the wrong shape. It reversed a deliberate default (#149875, #150157), it broke the required-delivery and context-isolation fixtures, and it changed bound broadcasts. My claim in the old body that broadcasts were exempt was wrong: child sends carry `toolContext` into the same check. Review also found a real matcher bug: the same-provider check ignored `threadId`, so a same-topic Telegram send could be denied.

This revision keeps the default and adds an opt-in inside the existing owner, `enforceCrossContextPolicy`:

- `confineChatTypes` keys on the conversation kind the host reports for the turn (`toolContext.currentChatType`). A listed kind may only target its own conversation; this overrides both `allowWithinProvider` and `allowAcrossProviders`. Unlisted kinds, and turns with no reported kind, keep those flags. A `POST /tools/invoke` call bound by the conversation headers reports the bound target's kind, so it is confined like a turn from that conversation. A per-agent list replaces the global one through the existing per-agent merge; `[]` lifts it.
- Broadcast child sends already go through this check, so a confined broadcast delivers the current conversation and reports a denial for every other target. There is no runner change.
- When same-provider sends are restricted, the check resolves the thread the send will actually use, with the same `resolveAndApplyOutboundThreadId` that delivery uses (on a copy of the params), and names the destination with the channel's own `resolveCurrentChannelId`. Policy and delivery now judge the same destination. Only `send` and `poll` are judged by that thread alone, because the runner delivers them into it. Other guarded actions only hand the thread to the plugin, so they are judged on their requested target as on main, and a thread they carry can only narrow that. `topic-create` must also name the current conversation through its parent chat, resolved with the channel's own conversation grammar (core's `resolveSessionConversation`, which asks `messaging.resolveSessionConversation`), because Telegram creates the topic in the base chat whatever topic or thread the request names. Telegram declares `chatId`, `chat_id` and `channel_id` as delivery-target aliases for `topic-create` and `topic-edit`, because its handler takes the chat from them ahead of the target. Normalization therefore canonicalizes them before the check, the same way the thread spellings are folded. Normalization also stringifies exact integer values of `target`, `to` and `channelId` before folding them: Telegram's chat reader accepts numbers, while the fold and the check read only strings.
  - When a Telegram target's encoded topic and an explicit `threadId` disagree, the check follows Telegram's delivery precedence: the explicit thread wins. Telegram's `resolveCurrentChannelId` now goes through `formatTelegramDeliveryTarget`, the helper Telegram already uses to name a delivered send (moved unchanged into `targets.ts`).
  - The shared param readers accept each key's snake_case form, and Telegram's handler reads `messageThreadId` or `message_thread_id` before `threadId` or `thread_id`. Action normalization now folds every one of those four spellings into one string `threadId` before any check, including a numeric `threadId`, which core's string reader would otherwise skip. Values that disagree are refused, and so is any value alongside an explicit `threadId: null`. On any channel, an action carrying only an alias, or a numeric `threadId`, gets that value as its string `threadId`.

What changed since `1cb5e029db3` (2026-11-10): `POST /tools/invoke` now reports the kind of the conversation its headers bind it to, so `confineChatTypes` applies to header-bound direct calls as it does to a turn from that conversation (`9aadc2bbc5c`). The Bot API traces at `1cb5e029db3` showed the gap: with only `confineChatTypes: ["group"]` set and the topic-A headers, all nine direct calls were delivered, including a `sendMessage` to the owner DM and `editForumTopic` and `createForumTopic` on it. `src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts` now sets `currentChatType` on the direct-invocation surface from the bound target, with the resolver outbound target resolution already uses, `inferChatTypeFromTarget` (now exported from `src/infra/outbound/targets.ts`; for Telegram it asks the plugin's `parseTelegramTarget`). Calls without the headers, the RPC `tools.invoke` and the MCP loopback surface are unchanged. `src/gateway/tool-resolution.direct-invoke-confinement.test.ts` fails on `1cb5e029db3` (`promise resolved "{ content: [ { …(2) } ], …(1) }" instead of rejecting` for a sibling-topic send from a header-bound call) and passes on this head; `92aee940aa8` raises the test-line allocation by its 62 lines.

pr-simplify: compared with the first revision, the default flip and its three default-denial tests are gone. No new plugin API, no runner or broadcast changes. Every remaining test group fails on a named control (below). The remaining growth is one config field (4 schema paths), the denial reason text, thread-aware matching, the tests (493 net test lines, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/message-cross-context-confine-chat-types.txt`), and one qa-lab scenario. Against main `9a5df3d60f1`, which this branch is rebased on:

- production source +194 −37 (`outbound-policy.ts` +86 −11; `tool-resolution.ts` +11 −1 and `targets.ts` +2 −1 for the direct-invocation kind; Telegram `targets.ts`, `channel.ts` and `action-runtime.ts` +40 −24 for the moved delivery-target helper and `channel-actions.ts` +11 for the topic chat aliases; `message-action-normalization.ts` +33; +11 across schema, help and labels)
- tests +493 (`tool-resolution.direct-invoke-confinement.test.ts` +62)
- qa-lab scenario +172
- docs +18, plus the regenerated config baseline counts and hashes

## Evidence

Focused suite (measured at `470c81210da` against its merge base `19aff5bfd42`; the current head's checks are below): `outbound-policy.test.ts`, `message-action-routing.send-policy.test.ts`, `message-action-runner.broadcast.test.ts`, plus the existing context-isolation fixtures in `message-action-routing.context.test.ts`.

- With the change: 51 of 51 pass, and the 15 context-isolation fixtures pass.
- `outbound-policy.ts` at the merge base: 8 fail, 43 pass.
  - The confined cross-provider, confined same-provider, and confined broadcast cases fail. The broadcast case gets `expected [ 'first', 'second' ] to deeply equal [ 'first' ]`.
  - 5 of the 6 Telegram topic cases fail: the chat id with the current `threadId`, and the chat id inheriting the topic, are falsely denied (`target="telegram:-1001234567890" while bound to "telegram:-1001234567890:topic:42"`). Another `threadId`, another topic target, and `topLevel: true` are let through.
  - The in-band current-topic target passes either way.
- Default flipped to deny (the first revision's shape): 6 of the 51 fail.
  - The existing `preserves required delivery when message-tool-only sends target another conversation` gets the denial instead of `missing reconcileUnknownSend`.
  - The default-delivery cases for sends and broadcasts fail, and so do the direct, untyped and per-agent `[]` cases.
  - 3 of the 15 existing context-isolation fixtures also fail with `Cross-context messaging denied`: `allows directchat target mismatch`, `allows localchat target mismatch` and `blocks cross-context UI handoff for thread-reply to another workspace channel`.

The Telegram cases run the bundled Telegram plugin's real threading code (dry run), under both `confineChatTypes: ["group"]` and `allowWithinProvider: false`.

Conflicting thread inputs (review P1), bound to topic 42:
- `-1001234567890:topic:42` with `threadId: "99"` is denied; on `7742e779d2e` it resolved.
- `-1001234567890:topic:99` with `threadId: "42"` is allowed; on `7742e779d2e` it was denied with `target="telegram:-1001234567890:topic:99" while bound to "telegram:-1001234567890:topic:42"`.
- A topic-42 target with `messageThreadId: "99"` is denied; on `5afec105d94` it resolved.
- A topic-42 target with `message_thread_id: "99"` is denied; on `470c81210da` it resolved. A dry run of the bundled Telegram plugin against a loopback Bot API delivered that send into topic 99 (`sendMessage` with `message_thread_id` 99) in 5 of 5 runs at `470c81210da`.
- A topic-42 target with a numeric `threadId: 99` is denied; on `ee49182a9c1` it resolved (`promise resolved "{ kind: 'send', …(9) }" instead of rejecting`). Through the message tool the schema already turns that number into a string, so this covers callers that pass a number to `runMessageAction`.
- Normalization: `message_thread_id`, `thread_id` or a numeric `threadId` alone becomes a string `threadId`. `{threadId: "42", messageThreadId: "99"}`, `{threadId: "42", message_thread_id: "99"}`, `{thread_id: "42", messageThreadId: "99"}` and `{threadId: null, message_thread_id: "99"}` are refused. The spelling cases fail on `470c81210da` (7 failed, 43 passed). One of them, `threadId` with `messageThreadId`, was already refused there and fails only on the new error text. `thread_id` alone was never a bypass, because core already read it. The numeric cases fail on `ee49182a9c1` (2 failed, 50 passed), and all 52 pass here.

Effect-scoped judgement (review P1) and Telegram chat aliases, through the bundled Telegram plugin under both `confineChatTypes: ["group"]` and `allowWithinProvider: false` (the Telegram table is now 30 rows x 2 switches):
- `topic-create` to `-1001234567890` with `name` from a turn bound to topic 42 is denied; on `561a13dd1af` it was allowed (the review repro), and main denies it under `allowWithinProvider: false`.
- `topic-create` through the topic-42 target, with or without `threadId: "42"`, is denied; main and `af58c646aea` allowed it. From a turn bound to the chat itself, `topic-create` to the chat id is allowed and through a topic-99 target is denied, as on main.
- `topic-edit` naming topic 42 but `chatId` or `channel_id` of another chat is refused as conflicting input; `topic-edit` or `topic-create` with only `chatId` of another chat is denied. All four were allowed on main and on `46c40dc35e6`. A same-chat `chatId` stays allowed. That Telegram acts on the other chat comes from reading the handler; a recorded non-dry handler run shows that chat reaching it.
- Numeric target keys (review P1 at `3a79b762bb7`): from a group turn bound to `-1001234567890`, `topic-create` with target `-1001234567890` and numeric `channelId: -1009999999999` now reaches Telegram's handler with only the chat target; a recorded non-dry handler run shows `channelId` dropped (at `3a79b762bb7` and on main it carried the other chat). Numeric `channelId` of another chat alone is denied for `topic-create` and `topic-edit`; the same chat's numeric id stays allowed. Normalization turns numeric `target`, `to` and `channelId` into strings and refuses `2 ** 60` and `1.5`. Through the model's message tool the agent loop already coerces the number to a string before `execute`, and Tool Search and Code Mode reject it, so a real-Gateway dry run sent `editForumTopic` to the turn's own topic. This covers callers that hand a number to `runMessageAction` or call the tool's `execute` directly (the Gateway's tool-invoke path and in-process callers), as with the numeric `threadId` case.
- Red: 3 of 29 at `561a13dd1af`, 2 of 33 at `af58c646aea`, 4 of 39 at `46c40dc35e6`, 9 of 78 at `3a79b762bb7` (normalization and send-policy tests together); all pass now. Ten mutation controls (dropping each rule or alias, making the parent check always deny or parent-only, leaving `channelId` numeric, or stringifying inexact numbers) are each caught.
- Action by action, under a restricting switch: `send` and `poll` are judged by the resolved thread; `sticker`, `edit`, `delete`, `topic-create` and `topic-edit` by the requested target plus any thread it carries (and `topic-create` also by its parent chat); `react`, `read`, `emoji-list` and `sticker-search` are not guarded.

qa-lab, `qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario message-cross-context-confine-group` (qa-channel, real gateway child, mock-openai):

- With the change: pass, at `79dbe06abbe`, `3a79b762bb7`, `561a13dd1af` and `ee49182a9c1` (merged with main), `470c81210da` and `7742e779d2e`.
  - With no config, a group turn's send reaches the DM.
  - After `config.patch` sets `confineChatTypes: [group]`, the same send returns `Cross-context messaging denied: action=send target="dm:alice" while bound to "group:qa-confine-group" (channel=qa-channel). tools.message.crossContext.confineChatTypes keeps group turns in their current conversation.`, and 0 DM deliveries follow.
  - The group's own sends and a DM turn's send to another group still deliver.
- Policy reverted: fail at the confined step. The DM was delivered.

Checks at `92aee940aa8` (on main `9a5df3d60f1`), 2026-11-10, macOS arm64:

- Focused suites under Node 26.12.1 (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`): `message-action-normalization`, `message-action-routing.send-policy`, `message-action-runner.broadcast`, `outbound-policy`, `schema.help.quality`, Telegram `action-runtime`, `channel-actions.contract` and `targets`, and the new `tool-resolution.direct-invoke-confinement`: 9 files, 0 failures. The 21 test files that import `tool-resolution.ts` or `outbound/targets.ts`, plus the five `tools-invoke` suites and the four focused `infra/outbound` suites: 30 files, 509 tests, 0 failures.
- `tool-resolution.direct-invoke-confinement.test.ts` on `1cb5e029db3`: 1 failed, 2 passed (the sibling-topic send from a header-bound call resolves). On this head: 3 of 3.
- CI's ratchets in PR form (`check:baseline-ratchets --base 9a5df3d60f1 --no-merge-base` with `RATCHET_PR_HEAD_SHA`): 10 of 10 ok, line-cap "16 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth", `Test lines OK: 6573693; ceiling: 6573741; slack: 48.` The allocation is exact: 494 is refused (`Test line allocation credit 494 exceeds allowed ceiling growth 493.`). Merged locally with current main `401a1de38b9` (the two generated config-baseline files conflict and were regenerated with `config:docs:gen`): 10 of 10 ok, `Test lines OK: 6629169; ceiling: 6629170; slack: 1.`
- `pnpm tsgo:all` passes. oxfmt and oxlint are clean on the changed files. Import cycles: `0 runtime value cycle(s)`, madge `0 cycle(s)`. `config:docs:check`, `config:schema:check` and `plugins:inventory:check` OK.

The pushed head `5db925155c3` merges main `910f6b9427d` (2026-11-16) into `2af43e00bb6`, which had merged main `d32ac41084f` into `c4bb370f344`; `c4bb370f344` merged main `401a1de38b9` into `92aee940aa8`. The only conflict this time was the generated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`, regenerated with `config:docs:gen`. Against main, the generated files differ only by this PR's 4 core config paths (`core` 2654 -> 2658), and the merge changes the same 22 paths as the PR with identical hunks outside `docs/.generated`.

Checks on `5db925155c3` (macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1):

CI on `5db925155c3` is waiting for a maintainer to approve the workflow runs. The CI results below are from `c4bb370f344`.

Not covered: a run on real Telegram. The runs above use the real Gateway and Telegram plugin with a loopback Bot API.

Revocation (measured with a real model, loopback Bot API). Tightening the policy applies from the next turn; a turn that is already running keeps the config it started with. One topic turn sent to the DM, waited 25 s in `exec`, and sent again; I tightened the policy with `config set` while it waited.

|---|---|---|---|---|

| this branch | `confineChatTypes: ["group"]` | 07:04:25.367Z | delivered (07:04:49.8Z) | denied |

## Bot API traces (2026-11-10)

On this head `92aee940aa8`, built alone, a topic-A turn under `confineChatTypes: ["group"]` puts its same-topic poll and topic rename into topic A. The sibling-topic, other-chat, alias and topic-create calls make no Bot API request at all: after each refusal, the only request is the turn's own reply in topic A. Direct calls through the Gateway's `POST /tools/invoke` that carry the conversation headers for topic A are confined the same way: under `confineChatTypes: ["group"]` alone, and under `allowWithinProvider: false`, every call that names another topic or chat is refused with no Bot API request, where main `9a5df3d60f1` (this branch's merge base) sends the numeric ones to topic 99 or acts on another chat. I ran everything twice, and both runs made the same Bot API requests (method, chat, thread, status) with the same results in all 49 recorded turns and calls.

Setup:
- The real Gateway with the bundled Telegram plugin, built from this head alone (`pnpm build`, buildstamp head `92aee940aa8`, `inputsClean: true`), and main `9a5df3d60f1` built the same way. Every Gateway log line in both runs, 2,981 of 2,981, reports runtime `node` `26.12.1` (macOS arm64).
- The Gateway polls a loopback Bot API (Crabline 0.2.0) through a recording proxy that logs each Bot API request the Gateway sends, with all of its parameters. These are HTTP requests from the Gateway, not the plugin's dry-run mode. Crabline has no `sendPoll`, so the proxy answers that one method itself, with a poll message in the requested chat and thread.
- The model is QA Lab's mock OpenAI provider, in its own process, playing a fixed list of `message` tool calls per turn. Each turn starts from a user message in topic A (thread 42) of a forum supergroup; topic B is thread 99. Chat ids are replaced with `<group>` (the supergroup) and `<owner-dm>` (a private chat).
- Run 1 18:06:58Z to 18:12:07Z, run 2 18:12:07Z to 18:17:13Z.

The HTTP caller gets `500` with `{"type":"tool_error","message":"tool execution failed"}` for a refusal, on main as well.

What these runs also showed, and what they do not cover:
- At `1cb5e029db3` the `confineChatTypes` column was all delivered: with only `confineChatTypes: ["group"]` set and the same headers, all nine calls went out, including a `sendMessage` to `<owner-dm>` and `editForumTopic` and `createForumTopic` on `<owner-dm>`, because `/tools/invoke` reported no conversation kind. `9aadc2bbc5c` makes it report the kind of the conversation its headers bind it to, which gives the refusals above.
- Without the conversation headers, `/tools/invoke` has no current conversation on either build (`Action send requires a target. This turn has no current conversation; pass an explicit target, or reply in normal text.`), so no `crossContext` switch applies. This is unchanged by `9aadc2bbc5c`: in both runs on this head, under `confineChatTypes`, a `threadId` of 99, string or number, went to topic 99, as it does on main. `topic-edit` with `channelId` `<owner-dm>` acted on `<owner-dm>` as a string on both builds, and as a number on this head; main refused the number with that "requires a target" error.
- The Bot API is a loopback, not Telegram. The traces show what the Gateway sent, not how Telegram would answer.

prs.title: refactor(cli): retire unused configure test doubles
prs.body:
Related: #171994

## What Problem This Solves

The shared CLI test fixture still implements a configure path that its tests no longer exercise.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. All 94 exercised cases and their assertion-bearing bodies remain intact; production code, command options, defaults, and dependencies are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the obsolete configure doubles and their unused fabricated config registration together, plus exactly the associated mock-export baseline row. Real configure behavior remains covered at its registered dispatch and persistence boundaries instead of by a second fake owner.

Thanks @vincentkoc for directing this behavior-preserving cleanup campaign.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/09f057fa-3479-4e1d-b851-0cad5cf713a7)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/4479d209-8c38-4d52-adeb-63688b6f7e4d)

## Evidence

- Baseline and candidate: **94/94 passing**, with identical expanded names/order across the smoke suite, all three shared-mock node suites, real configure/config dispatch, registered config persistence, and wizard tests. No test case, assertion, table row, or lifecycle hook removed.
- Targeted CLI typecheck, lint, format, non-pruning mock-export guard, and diff checks pass. The test wrapper also prepared and checked its isolated E2E runtime; no separate full package/declaration build is claimed.
- All seven required removal-scan phases ran on clean base and candidate. Unused-file and script-export scans pass. The remaining dependency/export phases are inherited reds with **byte-identical complete outputs and exit codes**; none name the changed paths. The aggregate is not green; no unrelated fix, ignore, or exception was added.
- Independent source-preservation qualification accepted the complete owner retirement. Final local Codex autoreview: **P0–P2 scoped-clean**, complete 141,209-byte frozen input against base 232ba9a63de6912b613aa7aa00ec0e0bbf9e7f99, now committed as 9636dce1630453c37989ec03a68b5fa947829595. A first incomplete review was corrected by supplying the full changed-file context; its result was not counted as clean. The reviewer did not independently rerun tests.
- Scope: three files, +0/−37; production 0, test/support −36, obsolete baseline row −1. No performance claim.
- Exact-head [CI run 43978791826](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43978791826) succeeded on ca4f264d7f29ea60a5e058b3eb30be0e068a009a; the single rollup watcher reported GREEN. All 60 jobs were accounted for (30 succeeded, 30 skipped): 1,011 seconds reported run wall time and 5,296 summed non-skipped job seconds, not billed cost or a benchmark. Native exact-head review and preparation are complete; landing is pending.

## Worked on by

- @vincentkoc
