prs.title: feat(plugin-sdk): add repository sources with a bundled GitLab consumer
prs.body:
Related: #185864

## What Problem This Solves

Repository integrations cannot join OpenClaw's new-session picker, managed checkout and worktree preparation through a public plugin contract. Supporting a second forge such as GitLab (#185864) would therefore need changes in core.

## User Impact

- **GitLab users** can enable the new bundled `gitlab` plugin, search public GitLab projects in **New session**, and start a session on a managed checkout or a new worktree. Self-managed GitLab works through `plugins.entries.gitlab.config.baseUrl`.
- **Plugin authors** can offer repositories from any Git host with `api.registerRepositorySource` and `openclaw/plugin-sdk/repository-sources`.
- **Everyone else:** no change. Built-in GitHub, existing plugins, existing sessions and existing configuration keep working, and nothing needs migrating. The GitLab plugin is off by default.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the smaller, consumer-backed stage that the first review of this PR recommended. The earlier revision proposed four SDK families at once (repository sources, execution environments, caller-bound plugin tools, Control UI V2) with no production consumer. This revision keeps **only repository sources** and adds a real consumer, the bundled GitLab plugin. The other families come back later, each together with the feature that uses it.

Plugins supply vendor policy (URL rules, transport, search). OpenClaw keeps custody of checkout storage, leases, worktree preparation, session state and authorization.

### How this relates to #192349 and #192350

This remains an **alternative** to the SDK foundation in #192349 and the GitHub migration in #192350, not an addition to them. Those PRs add GitHub-only SDK entry points (`native-github-account-host`, `native-github-publication-host`, `native-github-session-read`). Those entry points hand a plugin core's existing GitHub account records, publication receipts and `sessions.github.*` methods, which a GitLab plugin cannot use, and which keep that GitHub code in core.

The planned order:
1. **This PR:** repository sources plus a GitLab consumer.
2. **GitLab merge requests:** general account, publishing and status contracts, with the execution-environment, plugin-tool and Control UI pieces they need, all used by GitLab. This should be coordinated with the draft GitLab work in #185928 before it starts.
3. **GitHub as a plugin:** GitHub moves onto the same general contracts, Doctor migrates its data, and its code leaves core. Cloud-worker support for plugin sources arrives here at the latest, because GitHub sessions already run on cloud workers and the plugin must keep that working. If stage 2 gives GitLab cloud support first, it arrives there instead.

### Response to the first review

| Review item | Status in this revision |
|---|---|
| Choose a consumer-backed stage | Done: repository sources only, with the bundled GitLab plugin as the consumer. |
| Inherited repository children lose the source (P2) | Superseded in the third revision: plugin sources no longer create cloud repository workspaces, so a plugin-sourced repository parent cannot exist. The propagation was removed with the worker contract. |
| Unimplemented co-author hook (P2) | Removed with execution environments; it is not in this PR. |
| `extensions/AGENTS.md` rule without an incident (P2) | Removed; this PR does not change `extensions/AGENTS.md`. |
| Merge conflict | Rebuilt on current `main`; it merges cleanly. |
| Startup bundle growth | Reduced and measured; a maintainer decision remains (see Known gaps). |
| Real behavior proof | Added below: a real Gateway and Control UI with a public GitLab project. |
| Data-model compatibility | Upgrade from the latest stable release run on a real Gateway; see Evidence. |

### Response to the second review

| Review item | Status in this revision |
|---|---|
| GitLab fetches tags and commits as branches (P2) | Fixed: `resolveBase` uses a full commit as is (hydrating it when the clone lacks it), and asks GitLab with `ls-remote` whether any other name is a branch or a tag before fetching it. A new real-Git test (`extensions/gitlab/src/transport.test.ts`) covers a tag, a commit missing from the clone, the default branch and an unknown name. It fails on the previous revision with "GitLab base fetch failed". |
| A failed plugin clone leaves an unregistered target (P2) | Fixed: the host removes the unregistered target after a failed plugin `clone`, while it still holds the clone lease, unless process cleanup is uncertain. The retry regression in `repository-sources.test.ts` fails on the previous revision. |
| Unused `createRepositorySources` facade (P2) | Removed, together with its `RepositorySources` and `ResolvedRepositorySource` types. |

### Response to the third review

| Review item | Status in this revision |
|---|---|
| Decision needed: defer unconsumed worker API commitments | Done, as recommended. The optional `worker` adapter is removed from the SDK, with its checkout transfer, `performRepositoryCheckout`, `prepareRepositoryCheckoutPack`, worker admission and Gateway materialization paths. Worker code returns to its `main` behavior. `sessions.create` now rejects `repositorySource` combined with a cloud `repository` workspace, with a message that asks for a local placement (new regression in `sessions-create-worktree-base.test.ts`). |
| Low-value `readTree` assertion | Removed with the worker test it belonged to. |
| Real behavior proof for the worker path | No longer applies: there is no worker path for plugin sources. |
| Upgrade and data-model compatibility proof | Done: a real upgrade from `openclaw@2026.11.4`; see Evidence. |
| Startup budget | Reduced again by the removal; a maintainer decision remains (see Known gaps). |
| Dependency approval | Waiting for SecOps. |

## Evidence

### End to end in a real Gateway and Control UI

- **Setup:** a Gateway built from this branch, with isolated state, token auth on loopback, and the `gitlab` plugin enabled.
- **Discovery:** `plugins.controlUi.list` returned `repositorySources: [{ id: "repositories", label: "GitLab", searchMethod: "gitlab.repositories.search", pluginId: "gitlab" }]`.
- **Search and selection:** the picker showed a **GitLab** group beside GitHub. Choosing `gitlab-org/project-templates/express` set the chip to that project.
- **Session creation:** I called `sessions.create` with the same parameters the picker sends (`projectGitUrl` and `repositorySource: "gitlab/repositories"`), once for the current checkout and once with `worktree: true`. Both returned `repositorySourceId: "gitlab/repositories"`.
- **Clone:** the managed clone has origin `https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/project-templates/express.git` at `d10a6ca`, matching `git ls-remote ... HEAD`.
- **Worktrees:** both sessions received worktrees (`openclaw/kind-crab`, `openclaw/fresh-prawn`) based on `d10a6ca`, with project `express`.
- **No model:** the test Gateway had no model credentials, so the first turn reported "OpenAI didn't accept the saved credentials". Repository preparation completes before the turn, so this does not affect the proof.

Screenshots (user and device names blacked out):

| Before: plugin disabled, GitHub results only | After: GitLab group in the picker |
|---|---|
| ![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raw-labs/openclaw/f959e0164b4c74feb7de1d316aac54daca211a71/before-picker-github-only.png) | ![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raw-labs/openclaw/f959e0164b4c74feb7de1d316aac54daca211a71/after-picker-gitlab-group.png) |

| GitLab project selected | GitLab-backed session (project `express`, branch `fresh-prawn`) |
|---|---|
| ![Selected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raw-labs/openclaw/f959e0164b4c74feb7de1d316aac54daca211a71/after-selected-gitlab-project.png) | ![Session](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raw-labs/openclaw/f959e0164b4c74feb7de1d316aac54daca211a71/after-gitlab-session.png) |

### Upgrade from the latest stable release (2026.11.4)

- **Before:** `openclaw@2026.11.4` from npm ran a Gateway on fresh isolated state (loopback, token auth). It created a plain session and a GitHub project session (`octocat/Hello-World`, project `hello-world`, worktree `openclaw/cool-lobster`).
- **Upgrade:** a Gateway built from this branch started on the same state. It ran its normal state upgrade, and `sessions.list` returned both sessions unchanged.
- **After:** with the `gitlab` plugin enabled, the upgraded Gateway created a GitLab worktree session (`express`, `openclaw/crisp-claw`) and a new GitHub session (`hello-world`, `openclaw/dawn-langoustine`). In the agent database, the GitLab row holds `repositorySourceId: "gitlab/repositories"`, the other rows have no source, and all four entries are valid.
- **Cloud placement:** `sessions.create` with `repository` and `repositorySource: "gitlab/repositories"` returned `INVALID_REQUEST`: "Plugin repository sources run sessions on this Gateway; cloud workers do not support them yet. Choose a local placement."
- **Downgrade:** 2026.11.4 refuses to start on the upgraded state because `main` already moved the state database to a newer schema (40, against 22 supported by 2026.11.4). This PR changes no schema, so a downgrade to 2026.11.4 is refused for any current `main` build, with or without it.

### Checks

- **Typecheck:** every `tsgo` lane (core, UI, extensions, extension tests, all core test lanes) reports 0 errors.
- **Lint and ratchets:** `oxlint` is clean on changed files, and the export-name-collision, assertion-safety, mock-exports, max-lines, line-cap and test-lines ratchets pass.
  - `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/plugins.ts` was already over its line cap. Its Control UI catalog schemas move to `schema/plugin-control-ui-catalog.ts` so the new field causes no growth.
  - No baseline changes.
  - `plugin-sdk:surface:check` already fails on the base commit (163 public entrypoints against a budget of 162, among others). This PR adds 1 entrypoint, 8 exports and 1 callable export to that existing overrun.
- **Third revision:** 42 affected test files pass (450 tests): session creation (all `server.sessions.create.*` suites), worktree base resolution, repository materialization, the reverted worker suites (`provider-project-retention`, `repository-workspace-startup`, `worker-turn-repository-disk`), project clone, plugin sources and manifests, the loader, Control UI plugin assets and the GitLab plugin. All `tsgo` lanes, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, `protocol:check` and the ratchets above pass.
- **Earlier revisions:** 338 affected test files passed (about 4,600 tests) across session creation, worktree base resolution, project clone, the plugin loader and registry, Control UI plugin assets, the new-session UI and plugin contracts.
- **Test lines:** net +707 test lines, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/200166-repository-sources.txt` (307 beyond the 400-line allowance). Most of it is contract tests for the new public SDK surface.
- **New test files** (`--maxWorkers=1` wall time, including about 2 s of runner startup):

| File | Tests | Wall |
|---|---|---|
| `src/plugins/repository-sources.test.ts` | 3 | 8.2 s |
| `src/plugins/manifest-repository-sources.test.ts` | 8 | 6.1 s |
| `extensions/gitlab/src/url.test.ts` | 10 | 1.6 s |
| `extensions/gitlab/src/transport.test.ts` | 1 | 8.2 s |

### Data compatibility

- **New fields are optional:** `sessions.create.repositorySource`, the session entry's `repositorySourceId`, and the manifest `repositorySources`. The worker snapshot is no longer changed.
- **Old data keeps the old path:** an existing session or saved preference without them takes the unchanged built-in path. Tests cover requests without the field, and saved repository preferences with and without a source.
- **No migrations:** nothing is migrated and no SQLite schema changes.
- **Upgrade:** a real upgrade from 2026.11.4 is above. The published-driver × candidate Docker cell was not run locally. Saved New Session preferences live in browser storage; tests cover them with and without a source, but a browser upgrade was not run.

---

## Repository sources: the SDK contract

**Purpose:** let a plugin offer repositories from any Git host (GitLab, Gitea, Bitbucket, a self-hosted forge) in the new-session picker. Sessions can then check out and work on them through the same project and worktree flow that built-in GitHub uses. Plugin sources run sessions on the Gateway; cloud workers come in a later stage.

### How a plugin wires it up

**1. Declare the source in `openclaw.plugin.json`.** The search method is a normal Gateway method the plugin registers:

```json
{
  "repositorySources": [
    { "id": "repositories", "label": "Example Forge", "searchMethod": "example.repositories.search" }
  ]
}
```

**2. Register the search method** with `api.registerGatewayMethod`. It returns the existing remote-project search shape:
- `projects`: name, clone and web URLs, visibility, and an optional description and default branch.
- `credential`: whether a credential is available. It never contains the credential itself.

Discovery is backend metadata only. It needs no browser module.

**3. Register the source** with `api.registerRepositorySource(source)`. The type is `RepositorySourceV1`:

| Member | Required | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | Matches the manifest contribution ID. The host qualifies it as `pluginId/id`. |
| `resolve(url)` | yes | Accepts and normalizes a supported URL, returning `{ url, name, display? }`, or returns `undefined` to decline. `display` is presentation only and never grants access. |
| `prepare({ url, agentId, requiredCommit?, signal, assertCurrent })` | yes | Prepares a local project. Returns `{ project, assertCurrent, resolveBase(ref?) }`. `resolveBase` returns `{ commit, ref }`. With no ref, it observes the current remote default branch (including a renamed one) and returns `origin/<branch>`. |

The bundled GitLab plugin in this PR is a complete source in about 430 lines: `extensions/gitlab/src/source.ts` (the source), `src/transport.ts` (Git transport) and `src/search.ts` (search).

### Managed checkout: `createManagedProjectCheckoutV1(transport)`

The plugin supplies the transport, a `ManagedProjectSourceV1` with `resolveUrl`, `clone`, `ensureCommit`, `resolveBase` and `refresh`. The host supplies everything else:
- **Reused from the host:** checkout leases, on-disk layout and the project registry. The plugin does not pick storage paths or keep its own registry.
- **What you get back:** `materialize`, `resolveBase` and `refresh` operations. Call them from inside the plugin's managed invocation, so the host can bind the current Gateway config and plugin authority. Called outside that context, they throw.
- **The host checks the plugin's answer:** it verifies the returned base commit locally, keeps safe fast-forward checks, and records the chosen ref and exact commit before setup. Retries reuse that pinned commit instead of fetching a new base.
- **Credentials stay with the plugin:** they live in the transport closure and never become host state.
- **Only its own clones:** `resolveBase` and `refresh` refuse a managed clone whose saved origin the source does not admit, so one source cannot run its transport on another source's checkout.
- **Lease checks per command:** each transport call receives `startRun`. Running every Git command through it re-checks the host's checkout leases right before the command starts.

`executeGitCommand`, `requireGitCommandOutput`, `runProjectGitCommand`, `projectCheckoutGitEnvironment` and `configureProjectCheckoutMaintenance` in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/process-runtime` let a transport reuse the host's bounded Git runner, cancellation and maintenance settings.

### How sessions choose a source

- `sessions.create` gains an optional `repositorySource: "<pluginId>/<id>"`, sent alongside `projectGitUrl`. Combined with a cloud `repository` workspace, it is rejected with a message that asks for a local placement.
- **Field absent:** the existing built-in path runs unchanged. It accepts GitHub URLs only, as it does today.
- **Field present:** the host resolves exactly that source. It **never falls back** to another plugin or to the built-in source. These cases fail with an actionable error:
  - the source is disabled or withdrawn;
  - the source does not accept the URL;
  - several sources accept the URL and none was selected.
- **Control UI:** the new-session picker reads plugin sources from the plugin catalog (`plugins.controlUi.list` → `repositorySources`), shows them beside the built-in search, and sends `repositorySource` for a plugin result.
- **Sticky selection:** the selected source and pinned commit stay with the session through restart.

## The bundled GitLab plugin

`extensions/gitlab` is the first consumer, and is meant as a reference implementation:

- **Manifest:** declares one repository source (`gitlab/repositories`) and the `gitlab.repositories.search` Gateway method. Config takes an optional `baseUrl` (an HTTPS origin, default `https://gitlab.com`).
- **Search:**
  - queries `/api/v4/projects` anonymously for public projects through the SDK's SSRF-guarded fetch, limited to the configured host with no redirects;
  - ranks by stars, so canonical projects come before forks;
  - maps results into the existing remote-project shape.
- **Source:** admits only HTTPS project URLs on the configured server and normalizes them to `https://host/group[/subgroup]/project.git`.
- **Transport:**
  - runs Git through the host runner (`process-runtime`) with credential helpers disabled, HTTPS only, no redirects and no prompts;
  - routes every command through the host's lease-checking `startRun`;
  - error messages name the failed step and never echo transport output.
- **Off by default.** Enable it in **Plugins** or with `plugins.entries.gitlab.enabled: true`.
- **Docs:** `docs/plugins/gitlab.md`; the plugin inventory and reference pages are regenerated.

## Size

- **Total:** 93 files, +5,533 / −2,917 against its base on `main`.
- **Generated protocol and validator files:** +2,580 / −2,462. Excluding them, the change is about +2,950 / −455.
- **Tests:** +672 / −2.
- **Docs:** +202 / −5.
- **UI:** +534 / −30.
- **GitLab plugin:** +646 lines.
- **`src/plugin-sdk`:** +114.

## Known gaps

- **Startup bundle (needs a maintainer decision):** measured against the base build of the same commit, Control UI startup grows by **+498 B** gzipped on chat boot (1,314,681 → 1,315,179 B) and **+998 B** on New Session boot (816,374 → 817,372 B). The base is already over these caps, so the check allows no growth beyond 64 B.
  - **Already moved out of startup:** the plugin search client (1.3 KiB gzipped) and its result validator now load only when the user searches with a plugin source present.
  - **What remains:** the picker logic that lists plugin source groups and their status, plus the catalog field.
  - **The choice:** accept the measured growth with a budget adjustment, or ask for a follow-up that restructures the picker.
- **Cloud workers:** plugin sources run sessions on the Gateway only, and the GitLab plugin is local only. A cloud `repository` workspace with a plugin source is rejected with a clear message. In the Control UI, the picker still offers plugin results when a cloud placement is selected; submitting shows that message.
- **Public projects only:** the plugin sends no GitLab credentials. Private repositories need the account contracts planned for the next stage.
- **Pasted URLs:** pasting a GitLab URL into the picker still selects the built-in GitHub path, which ignores non-GitHub URLs, as on `main`. Pick GitLab projects from search; the docs say so.
- **Stale selection while disabled:** if the source's plugin is disabled after a project is chosen, the saved draft keeps the chip. Submission is blocked, but the chip itself shows no warning.
- **Rollback:** sessions created with a plugin source save `repositorySourceId`. A downgrade to 2026.11.4 is refused before any session is read, because the base `main` already uses a newer state schema.
- **Not run:** the published-driver × candidate Docker cell, the full test suite, and the UI e2e suites. This PR relies on CI for those.

prs.title: feat(cron): make automation inspect links configurable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves Implements #150029 by adding the strict config option `cron.announce.inspectLinks` with values `always`, `errors`, and `never`. The default is `always`, preserving existing behavior. This supersedes #175817, which was closed unmerged. The approach is rebased onto current `main` and additionally proves that the policy applies to isolated agent-run announcements through the shared delivery append path. ## Behavior - `always`: include Control UI `Inspect` links on successful completion announcements and failure alerts (backward-compatible default). - `errors`: include links only on failure alerts. - `never`: omit links from both successful completion announcements and failure alerts. - Applies to isolated/direct cron completion delivery, successful completion announcements, failure alerts, and isolated agent-run announcements that share `sendCronAnnouncePayloadStrict`. - Webhook delivery is unchanged; the setting only governs chat announcement links. ## Changes - Add `src/cron/inspect-links.ts` with the policy resolver and `shouldIncludeCronInspectLink`. - Add the strict `cron.announce.inspectLinks` schema under `cron`. - Apply the policy at the shared delivery append path in `src/cron/delivery.ts`, with an explicit completion/error kind for failure alerts. - Gate link generation in `server-cron-completion.ts`, `server-cron-notifications.ts`, and isolated agent delivery dispatch. - Document the option in `docs/gateway/config-automation.md` and `docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md`. - Refresh generated config baseline hashes/counts. - Add `config/test-lines-allocations/194794-cron-inspect-links.txt` (126 lines, exact measured net test LF growth) for the test-lines ratchet. ## Evidence Focused tests: ```text pnpm vitest run src/config/zod-schema.core.test.ts src/cron/delivery.failure-notify.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent.delivery-awareness.test.ts src/gateway/server-cron-completion.test.ts Test Files 4 passed (4) Tests 59 passed (59) ``` Schema / generated baseline: ```text pnpm check:base-config-schema [base-config-schema] ok pnpm config:docs:check OK docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256 and docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json ``` Type checks: ```text pnpm tsgo:core # passed node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json ... node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json ... # passed ``` Formatting / whitespace: ```text oxfmt --check All matched files use the correct format. git diff --check # passed ``` ## Review notes - Branch is one commit on top of base `56eb6f3fe2e6b3056727094d22add3c02322215d`; current head `67123e2245a348373f2d3a01df041fc3e739a82c`. Only generated baseline outputs changed during this rebase. - No merge is requested here; this PR is ready for maintainer review. ## Shipped-entry-point proof: 2026-11-08 Sanitized extract. Originals remain local. Contains only synthetic fixture data and `control.example` URLs. Placeholders replace credentials, ports, identifiers and paths. ### Scope Proves on the real shipped CLI entry point (`openclaw.mjs gateway run`) that the cron scheduler appends the Control UI run-inspection link according to `cron.announce.inspectLinks` with default `always`: | Mode | Completion | Failure alert | | --- | --- | --- | | `always` (explicit) | link present | link present | | `errors` | link absent | link present | | `never` | link absent | link absent | | omitted (default) | link present | link present | Transport is a **local simulated Bot API over loopback** implemented for this proof. It is **not** real Telegram, not Telegram's network, and not a real bot account. The Gateway, cron scheduler, delivery queue and channel adapter code are the shipped production paths; only the remote Bot API endpoint is simulated. ### Observed revision and build provenance - Branch: `feat/cron-inspect-link-policy-v2` - HEAD: `a89f9f80afff1db14d8135a25f0cc11fac4228fd` - `dist/build-info.json`: `{ version: "2026.11.1", commit: "a89f9f80afff1db14d8135a25f0cc11fac4228fd" }` - `dist/entry.js` sha256 `33b9d9b167163e877b373cf38dfc514dbdda460d489238e5c10980d66ba8917d` - `dist/index.js` sha256 `159f854af966f37f377090380c3c52314a27265e1f4f4f1056edf5fdece44356` - Shipped dist rebuilt from HEAD: bundler exit 0, post-build stamps exit 0. One optional plugin-asset copy step exited 1 for an unrelated plugin whose own build output was absent; it is not used by this proof. - `git diff --check`: clean. ### Reproduction (placeholders) ```bash export REPO= export PROOF_ROOT= export OPENCLAW_HOME=$PROOF_ROOT/state/ export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$OPENCLAW_HOME export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=$PROOF_ROOT/configs/.json export NO_PROXY= # 1. Start the local simulated Bot API (writes JSONL of accepted calls) node $PROOF_ROOT/harness/fake-bot-api.mjs # honors FAKE_BOT_PORT, CAPTURE_FILE # 2. Start the real Gateway through the shipped entry point node $REPO/openclaw.mjs gateway run \ --port --bind loopback \ --token --allow-unconfigured # 3. Create scheduler-driven jobs (success and failing command payloads) node $REPO/openclaw.mjs cron add --name proof-success --every 3s \ --command "echo " \ --announce --channel telegram --to --json node $REPO/openclaw.mjs cron add --name proof-failure --every 4s \ --command "echo >&2; exit 3" --json # 4. Wait for one completion and one failure-alert send, then stop the Gateway ``` Fixture config (sanitized): ```json { "gateway": { "mode": "local", "bind": "loopback", "publicOrigin": "https://control.example" }, "channels": { "telegram": { "enabled": true, "botToken": "", "apiRoot": "http://:", "dmPolicy": "open", "allowFrom": ["*"] } }, "cron": { "failureAlert": { "enabled": true, "after": 1, "cooldownMs": 0, "channel": "telegram", "to": "" }, "announce": { "inspectLinks": "" } } } ``` For the default case, omit the entire `cron.announce` property rather than writing an `omitted` enum value. ### Observed outbound payloads (redacted) Representative completion payload under `always` (complete redacted matrix below): ``` proof-completion-payload Inspect run ``` Representative failure alert under `errors`: ``` Automation "" failed 1 times Cause: command exited with code 3 Run started: Inspect run ``` No link line appears for completion under `errors`/`never`, nor for failure under `never`. ### Commands and exits (local run) - `node harness/run-matrix.mjs matrix ` → exit 0 for `always`, `errors`, `never`, `default-omitted` - `node harness/verify-evidence.mjs` → exit 0 (re-derives all cases from raw captures) - `node openclaw.mjs config validate` → exit 0 - `node openclaw.mjs gateway run ...` → readiness HTTP 200 for every case - `pnpm check:base-config-schema` → `[base-config-schema] ok` - `pnpm vitest run src/config/zod-schema.core.test.ts src/cron/delivery.failure-notify.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent.delivery-awareness.test.ts src/gateway/server-cron-completion.test.ts` → Vitest summary: **4 test files passed, 59 tests passed** (duration 526.23s; no failed tests reported). The shell pipeline exit status was not used as evidence. ### Upgrade retry and real Telegram qualification Tested revision: `a89f9f80afff1db14d8135a25f0cc11fac4228fd`. After the environment operator corrected the shared ancestor's sticky bit, the normal branch `doctor --fix` command migrated a copy of the preserved `openclaw@2026.11.1` fixture: state schema **22 → 39**, agent schema **27 → 41**. Doctor created pre-migration backups. The original fixture remains at 22/27. This was **not a fully clean upgrade**: - Doctor exited **1**: its proposed config repair failed validation with `plugins.entries.codex: plugin codex: extension entry not found: index.js`. No config changes were written. This issue was not compared against the PR base, so its attribution is unverified. - Config bytes matched the baseline; all four job names/enabled states remained (two fixture jobs plus two built-ins). Conversation and session-node counts remained one each; full session-content preservation was not compared. - The migrated branch Gateway emitted completion and failure-alert payloads with inspect links while `cron.announce.inspectLinks` remained omitted. Transport was a **simulated Bot API**, not Telegram. The failure-alert run required a direct reset of synthetic runtime deduplication state on the clone; it does not prove untouched incident continuity across upgrade. - The retry harness called its asynchronous health check without awaiting it. Its reported HTTP-200 readiness is therefore **not valid evidence**. Captured outbound payloads and measured schema versions are separate observations. **Real Telegram attempt:** ```text node .agents/skills/telegram-e2e-userbot/scripts/telegram-test-doctor.mjs --dm exit 1; ok: false QA broker unavailable through existing Convex launchers; no authenticated launcher or privately supplied broker environment pair available. ``` No Telegram scenario ran, no test message was sent, and no live-upgrade claim is made. Next prerequisite: credential-owner-provided authenticated Convex access or the existing `OPENCLAW_QA_CONVEX_SITE_URL` / `OPENCLAW_QA_CONVEX_SECRET_CI` pair, supplied privately to the test process (never in a PR or chat). Then run a dedicated leased Telegram Test Server upgrade scenario with an independent user observing both pre-upgrade and post-upgrade messages, without direct runtime-state resets. The earlier mode matrix remains synthetic-transport evidence only. Maintainer product approval for the new setting remains separate from testing. ### Maintainer approval Missing. A product decision on adding the new `cron.announce.inspectLinks` setting is still required from a maintainer; it cannot be established by tests. ### Sanitization This extract contains no credentials (including synthetic ones), no loopback addresses, no chat/session identifiers, no email addresses or phone numbers, no personal paths, and no raw logs. All URLs use the reserved example domain `control.example`; all identifiers are placeholders. Raw captures and full logs remain local and unredacted. ### Final focused test result Command: `pnpm vitest run src/config/zod-schema.core.test.ts src/cron/delivery.failure-notify.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent.delivery-awareness.test.ts src/gateway/server-cron-completion.test.ts` Observed Vitest summary (HEAD `a89f9f8`, branch `feat/cron-inspect-link-policy-v2`): ``` Test Files 4 passed (4) Tests 59 passed (59) Duration 526.23s (tests 93%, import 3%, transform 3%, worker 1%) ``` No failed or skipped test files were reported.
Complete captured outbound payload matrix (redacted) ```text === always === completion link present: true proof-completion-payload Inspect run failure alert link present: true Automation "proof-failure-branch-a89f9f8-always" failed 1 times Cause: command exited with code 3 Run started: Inspect run === errors === completion link present: false proof-completion-payload failure alert link present: true Automation "proof-failure-branch-a89f9f8-errors" failed 1 times Cause: command exited with code 3 Run started: Inspect run === never === completion link present: false proof-completion-payload failure alert link present: false Automation "proof-failure-branch-a89f9f8-never" failed 1 times Cause: command exited with code 3 Run started: === default-omitted === completion link present: true proof-completion-payload Inspect run failure alert link present: true Automation "proof-failure-branch-a89f9f8-default-omitted" failed 1 times Cause: command exited with code 3 Run started: Inspect run ```
## Rebase status Current head: `f6b1d5b67be53526c61fa43773c62728b8d1900f`, rebased onto `main` at `7d0143248` (2026-11-12). The only conflicts were the generated config baseline files, resolved by regenerating them with `pnpm config:docs:gen` (counts: `core 2653`, `plugin 5081`); no feature code required conflict resolution. Current-head local checks: ```text pnpm config:docs:check OK docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256 and docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json pnpm vitest run src/config/zod-schema.core.test.ts src/cron/delivery.failure-notify.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent.delivery-awareness.test.ts src/gateway/server-cron-completion.test.ts Test Files 4 passed (4) Tests 59 passed (59) git diff --check # clean ``` CI for this head is running after the force-push; results from earlier heads no longer apply. The shipped-entry-point matrix and upgrade notes above were captured on `a89f9f80afff1db14d8135a25f0cc11fac4228fd`, not on this head. The earlier head `1cbe665bc6aed83a752d08e885e7d36c16f526a8` had successful Node changed-test shards, production/test types, lint, and `openclaw/ci-gate` in [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42726727910). Successful CI does not establish real-Telegram upgrade behavior. No maintainer response to the QA-access request or product decision was visible at this update.

prs.title: fix(ui): prevent Cmd+K jitter when switching Search and Compose
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Cmd+K panel snaps during rapid Search/Compose switches, then jumps down and back up while search refreshes.

## User Impact

Switching modes reverses smoothly from the panel’s visible position. Search-loading feedback no longer moves the results or footer. The draft, caret, focus, and reduced-motion behavior are preserved. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep one mode-height animation and cancel the previous effect before measuring the new target. Place pending search status beside the existing filters rather than inserting another row. Search requests and result ownership are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reproduced both defects in the actual Control UI using synthetic Gateway responses: an approximately 151 px interrupted-animation snap and a 34.6 px loading-row jump.
- The new Chromium regression fails on the original animation, then on the loading-row shift when only the animation is repaired; it passes with the complete fix.
- Six focused browser tests and 51 existing search/pending/shortcut unit tests passed. UI typecheck, targeted stylesheet lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Targeted code lint completed with one existing warning in the unchanged result-ref callback.
- Inspected desktop light (1345×800) and emulated phone-width dark (400×800) captures. Loading and settled panel heights now match. Reduced motion produces no mode animations. No physical-device or live-inference test is claimed.
- **Verification gap:** WebKit’s browser-test connection and standalone test-app startup did not complete, so WebKit behavior remains unverified.
- Independent autoreview using GPT-6.1 Sol at P0–P3 returned `scoped-clean` for the complete local candidate against `ab30c20344676d8`; commit `cb9216d3c47e26c782a24f124ddd222267f606f2` contains the same reviewed patch. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable.
- Simplification pass retained the existing animation and search owners; the only new production state is the owned animation handle. Net change: +30 production lines and an 83-line focused browser regression.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Search-loading row moves the panel and footer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/032c05f4-1639-4135-aef0-f8f5c5cab9c3) | ![Loading status shares the filters without changing panel height](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/70c44645-96a0-445f-aca5-7508ce41def9) |

These are matched captures of the actual Control UI with synthetic Gateway data; the complete frame-by-frame motion was also checked.

prs.title: chore(runtime): update pinned Bun fork to 9debcc4b9
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

CI and app-managed runtimes still select the October OpenClaw Bun build.

## User Impact

Updates the shared Bun pin to [the signed November prerelease](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/releases/tag/openclaw-v1.4.4-20261115-9debcc4b9d-webkit-3357f9d63e) across all six supported targets.

## Why This Change Was Made

Regenerates the shared pin from the published manifest, including archive and executable checksums, and updates the two current documentation references.

## Evidence

**Validation remains blocked by Doctor, invitation retention and other unresolved findings. The separate POSIX fixture repair has landed with passing projected proof and its own successful CI; this unchanged pin candidate is not ready to land.**

- Candidate: `4ea5babab09c338812ae50dbcdaed990f48cd0fc`.
- [Bun publication run](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43794773536) passed six-target build/signing/smoke and its frozen OpenClaw/Birdclaw consumer gates; published checksums and cryptographic provenance were verified. Those consumer gates tested their frozen sources, not this PR head.
- Static checks passed: canonical manifest projection, signed Windows flags, JSON parsing, exact scope, and diff hygiene. Independent source/diff review found no P0–P2 issues. Full local ClawSweeper review covered the complete three-file, one-commit range with no actionable findings. After the shared repository history repair, the retained native review-artifact validator passed with the candidate and workflow unchanged. This is structural validation only: the review remains NEEDS WORK with failing tests and behavioral gaps.
- [Exact-candidate Linux Bun-only qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43808664006) passed all ten canonical package and smoke stages.
- [Exact-candidate macOS compatibility comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43809623573) passed 30 cells and 792 test cases with no new regression reported. Old-pin execution covered Darwin ARM64; the new pin also passed the Darwin x64 Rosetta probe. Linux asset checks in that run were format/hash checks, not Linux runtime qualification.
- [Actual-head dual-runtime CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43805983669) finished with failure: all 270 jobs completed, with 218 passed, 38 failed, six cancelled, and eight skipped. The macOS test job was cancelled and skipped bundled app recovery. The dual-runtime UI2 failure still needs runtime attribution.
- Focused ARM packaged-recovery proof is now accepted from the [corrected app-host run](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43825007091): seven preparation steps and all three expected native phases passed; six ARM receipts covered both native-first settings and sharing omitted/true/false at the exact candidate, new pin and build. Cleanup exited zero and source remained clean. The outer workflow failed only after native proof, when its parser selected a different-schema fs-safe receipt and raised `KeyError: 'revision'`. This closes the focused ARM recovery gap, not full Swift, x64 or overall repin qualification. The [initial broader-build run](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43818225493) timed out before cases.
- Doctor remains a qualification blocker. The [matched Linux old/new comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43813941006) had identical 1,052 case identities and five skips: 1,047 old-pin passes versus 1,045 new-pin passes and two failures, including SQLite snapshot allocation/cleanup errors and timeout with uncertain settlement. The [two unchanged cached-writer cases in isolation](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43840085160) passed with both pins and restored cleanly; that does not explain or qualify the failing original 116-file group.
- The Doctor readonly-child observer candidate still fails in the original 116-file group. The [uninstrumented helper-only run](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43942906159) timed out cached-writer=true at 120,025 ms while false passed in 6,006 ms. The [same candidate with case/cycle phase writes](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43948269897), controller `59bc44ff`, reversed those outcomes: true passed in 5,432 ms; false failed in 300,006 ms across the 120-second test and 180-second hook budgets. Both runs recorded 114 files passed, one failed and one skipped; 1,046 tests passed, one failed and five skipped. Each completed with native exit 1, no controller failure or settlement uncertainty, five passing preparation steps, and restored source/pin with tracked source clean. Native arguments, environment, full preset, reporters and budgets stayed unchanged. The phase run recorded 62 contiguous case-attributed frames: true had no unmatched entry; false entered maintenance acquisition and finally-isolation without returned markers, with afterEach preceding the finally frames. Framing completeness means only untruncated attributed records; a missing returned marker may reflect a throw, not a stall. Marker writes can affect timing and scheduling. Neither failure is waived, and no internal cause, timeout fix or unchanged-C qualification is established. The [earlier cause diagnostic](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43869768145) remains distinct: snapshot-staging readiness-deadline and channel-closed cleanup errors, native 143, uncertain settlement and no restoration.
- The same controlled comparison found a candidate-only invitation failure in `session-mention-invitation.test.ts:285`: identical 3,308 case identities and 34 skips, with 3,274 old-pin passes versus 3,273 new-pin passes and one failure. The callback sentinel remained retained while its control collected; both runs settled and restored cleanly. See the [old evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43813941006/artifacts/14204168676) and [new evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43813941006/artifacts/14203779105). prs.body:
Related: #200177 (companion fix for duplicate streamed replies in the same plugin) ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Markdown lists and single line breaks in agent replies show in Teams as one run-on paragraph, and headings show as bold text. ## User Impact Lists (bullet, numbered, nested, task), headings, and line breaks inside a paragraph or quote display the way the agent wrote them. This applies to every outbound Teams message. Headings change from bold text to Teams headings (levels 4 to 6 become level 3). Tables and code are unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made Teams joins single newlines inside a paragraph. The formatter wrote list items as plain `• item` lines and left soft line breaks as newlines, so Teams merged them. It now writes what Teams renders: `- ` and `1. ` markers (nested under the parent marker's width; a list inside `1. ` needs three spaces), `#` to `###` headings, and two trailing spaces for line breaks in paragraphs and quotes. The message keeps the default text format; this does not opt into `extendedmarkdown` (#177295). ## Evidence One example: the same reply text formatted by `main` (top) and by this branch (bottom), each posted unchanged to a Teams personal chat. ```md ### Order SO-1041 Status: late Owner: Maria Next steps: - Call the plant - Book a carrier - Ridgeline first ``` ![main on top, this branch below](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ahamilton454/openclaw/pr-proof/formatting-before-after.png) What Teams rendered (from the page HTML): - `main`: `

Status: late Owner: Maria

` and `

• Call the plant • Book a carrier • Ridgeline first

` - this branch: `

Order SO-1041

`, `

Status: late
Owner: Maria

`, and `
  • Call the plant
  • Book a carrier
    • Ridgeline first
` Before changing anything, I posted raw Markdown samples to the same chat. Teams web rendered `-`/`*`/`1.` lists, nested lists, `#` to `###` headings, quotes, code, and hard line breaks; it joined single newlines; a bullet nested under `1. ` with two spaces fell out of the list, with three it nested. Tests, head `d56f197b0` on base `8e9839128`: - `pnpm test:extension msteams`: 1,083 of 1,083 pass. - With the base `format.ts`, 17 of 85 tests fail: 8 new cases (lists, nesting, heading levels, line breaks, a quote inside a list item) and 9 expectations updated from `•` and bold headings. - `pnpm check:changed`: format, extension typecheck, test typecheck, and lint pass. Review: an independent Claude Code review of the final diff (not the openclaw autoreview tool) found two issues, both fixed with tests: a quote right after a list marker lost its `>`, and a backslash line break could be left dangling at a message chunk boundary (now two trailing spaces, which chunking trims). Limits: checked on Teams web only, not Teams mobile. Microsoft's docs list only a few constructs for the default format, so mobile rendering of lists and headings is unverified. Not run locally: SQLite worker ratchet (needs `rg`), dead-export scan. ## Merge Danger Two-way door: reverting restores the previous text output. No config, schema, or stored state. Blast radius is Teams outbound text formatting (`formatMSTeamsMarkdown`). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: feat(i18n): prepare pinned external Control UI memory
prs.body:
Related: #165234

## What Problem This Solves

Prepares the Control UI locale refresh to retain canonical translation memory outside main while keeping source checkouts and public-session builds reproducible offline.

## User Impact

After an explicit bootstrap, UI and public-session builds use checked-in digest-pinned catalogs without fetching translation storage. Raw memory is restored only for generation and published to a separately configured, append-only canonical Git repository before the corresponding main pin.

**This PR does not activate or provision production storage.** Until an administrator configures the approved destination/App and lands the generated bootstrap change, the existing tracked-memory workflow remains active. No real destination or credentials are supplied here; no remote migration was performed. Existing reachable Git history is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The prepared path retains one lossless canonical snapshot, exact revision and SHA-256 pins, and a smaller derived build representation. The same reader serves Vite and public-session runtime/worker builds. Bootstrap validates all raw bytes before local removal; restore validates the complete snapshot before writes; failed canonical publication cannot advance the main revision pin.

This is the smallest coherent preparation stage spanning both build consumers, the existing same-run artifact flow, and the terminal generated-PR publisher. It uses existing Git/GitHub infrastructure with no new runtime dependency. Production ownership/access and the explicit bootstrap remain operator actions documented in `docs/ci/control-ui-memory.md`. No history rewrite, shared repack, translation rewrite or provider call was performed.

## Evidence

- Native local Git fixtures cover bootstrap, byte-exact restore from old/new pins, rejected-push ordering, projection corruption, no new raw-memory objects in future source commits, and unchanged catalog object IDs for metadata-only refreshes.
- Full-roster local cutover: 22 locales, 270,050 translated key/value entries; current-English materialization and public-reader dictionaries are byte-identical. Raw inputs total 114,078,356 bytes; build projections total 46,251,834 bytes. These are logical file sizes, not a clone-pack forecast.
- Both UI builds pass: 4,940 output files byte-identical; only `.build-inputs.json` changes to record the new inputs. Public-reader tsdown module bytes are identical. All original raw files were restored after the local experiment.
- The old public-reader consumer fails the activated-input regression with missing French translations; the reviewed consumer passes. 59 focused locale/tooling tests, 50 Vite build-owner tests, and 225 CI workflow guards pass. Targeted tooling/UI types, typed lint, formatting, workflow validation, docs links and production/full-tree unused-file scans pass.

prs.title: fix: saved plugin config stays deferred while a native model catalog lookup hangs
prs.body:
Closes #199521

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: saving a plugin's config (for example Anthropic's) is deferred for as long as an unrelated plugin's model catalog work is pending (a native harness `loadModelCatalog` call, a catalog auth refresh, or a native login check), even with no chat sessions running, and `plugins.inspect` reports the blocking holds with owner `unknown`.

## User Impact

User impact: a saved plugin config applies while another plugin's model catalog lookup or auth check is slow or hung, and the plugin calls that model catalog work is running are attributed to the agent and the `model-catalog-discovery` service. Discovery timeouts stay owned by each plugin's own settings.

## Why This Change Was Made

Model catalog work held work on every plugin in the prepared plugin generation, and the provider catalog wrapper kept that hold while it waited for native discovery. One pending harness call or auth hook therefore kept every plugin in the generation from being replaced.

- Native and provider catalog builds, scoped catalog auth refresh and the native login recheck keep the generation's resources through custody only and take no work holds on its plugins. A plugin stays held only while a call into it is running, so a plugin whose callback already settled, or that the build never called, can reload while a slower lookup continues.
- One custody hold spans the provider and native catalog phases, so the generation stays alive between them without holding any plugin. Both phases still run outside the requesting turn's plugin scope (#196968).

Known limits:

- A call that really hangs keeps its own plugin from reloading until the call settles, within whatever discovery timeout that plugin applies. Releasing it sooner needs cancellation support for plugin calls.
- A synthetic auth hook (`prepareSyntheticAuth`) that ignores its abort signal keeps the auth refresh or login check, and its own plugin's hold, waiting until the hook settles. Callers deliberately join a hook's settlement after abort. Other plugins are not held.
- A plugin that reloads between two calls of the same catalog pass can have the later call refused. That pass then reports the failure and the next catalog read retries it.

## Evidence

- Live red/green on isolated Gateways with no real accounts or keys: Anthropic enabled, plus an external test harness whose `loadModelCatalog` never returns. `models.list` started discovery, `sessions.list` reported 0 sessions, then `config.patch` changed `plugins.entries.anthropic.config.managedNativeTools.default`. The catalog lookup was still pending at the end of both runs.
  - `main` (7ecd67ccfd5): `config.patch` returned `UNAVAILABLE` "saved but deferred: Plugin anthropic reload is waiting for retained work, calls, or previous-generation cleanup", and 5 seconds later `configRevisionHash` still differed from `appliedConfigHash`.
  - This branch (c664a4ace95): `config.patch` succeeded, the Gateway logged "config hot reload applied (plugins.entries.anthropic.config, ...)", and `configRevisionHash` matched `appliedConfigHash`.
- New tests, with each callback wrapped by its own plugin instance in one registry. Both fail without this change and pass with it.
  - `prepared-model-runtime.native-demand.test.ts`: native discovery runs a harness that returns, one that throws, and one that stays pending. While the last one is pending, the two settled plugins and a plugin the lookup never called hold nothing and their replacements drain. The pending harness keeps only its own running call, attributed to `model-catalog-discovery`, until that call settles.
  - `prepared-model-runtime.native-login.test.ts`: a hung native login probe. The sibling plugin's replacement drains while the probe is pending, the probe's running call is attributed to catalog discovery, and the probe plugin is released when the probe settles.
- Focused tests: 22 files covering catalog access, the catalog worker's metadata and native integration paths, native discovery, catalog auth, native login, synthetic auth, plugin drain, registry borrowing, run resources, owner supersession, turn handover, and plugin reload and retention: 249 tests, all passing. Lint and the core typecheck are clean. The full suite was not run locally.

prs.title: fix(tavily): allow a baseUrl override on a private or internal host
prs.body:
Supersedes #139868 (closed by the stale bot). Same change and contract, rebased onto current `main`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators who set the Tavily plugin's `baseUrl` (`plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.baseUrl` or `TAVILY_BASE_URL`) to a Tavily-compatible endpoint on a private or internal host would find every `tavily_search` and `tavily_extract` call refused before it left the process. The documented override exists for self-hosted gateways, policy proxies and test doubles, and those endpoints are normally addressed by private names such as `*.internal`, `*.local` or an RFC 1918 address, or by a loopback address on the same machine. Routing through an env proxy does not change the outcome, and no plugin setting affects it.

## User Impact

Operators can point the Tavily plugin at a Tavily-compatible endpoint on a private, internal or loopback host and use `tavily_search` and `tavily_extract` against it, directly or through an env proxy. Users of the default endpoint see no change. Cloud-metadata destinations remain unreachable, and a configured name whose DNS answer is loopback, link-local or metadata remains refused.

## Why This Change Was Made

The client posts through the trusted-endpoint guard mode, whose policy pins the hostname but keeps the private-network checks on. This change treats `baseUrl` as operator authority and trusts the host named in it by exact name, under this contract:

- The configured host is honored as typed, including loopback and private addresses and `localhost`-style names.
- Cloud-metadata destinations are always refused: `169.254.169.254` and other link-local literals, `fd00:ec2::254`, `100.100.100.200`, their mapped and embedded encodings, and `metadata.google.internal`. A `baseUrl` naming one of these is routed to the strict guard, which refuses it before any DNS lookup or request in direct and env-proxy mode alike.
- A configured name whose DNS answer is loopback, unspecified, link-local or cloud-metadata is refused, because that answer was not the operator's choice.
- Off-host redirects are refused. A redirect that stays on the configured host is followed.
- With an env proxy, name resolution belongs to the proxy, as for all trusted calls; the exact-host rule still applies to every hop.
- The default `api.tavily.com` endpoint keeps the trusted-endpoint mode unchanged.

The guard gains an internal helper that combines the existing fake-IP hostname allowlist with the existing exact-host `allowedHostnames` policy for the request URL's host, after checking the host against a new `isCloudMetadataHostnameOrIp` classifier in `src/infra/net/ssrf.ts` that reuses the guard's metadata hostname and the `net-policy` metadata and link-local IP classifiers. `postTrustedWebToolsJson`'s request shape, error handling and response parsing move into a shared helper, and `postPinnedTrustedHostWebToolsJson` is the one new export, on the local-only `plugin-sdk/provider-web-search` subpath, used by the Tavily client when the resolved base URL's host is not `api.tavily.com`. Because the subpath is local-only, the public plugin SDK surface budgets do not change. The Tavily docs state the contract under "Custom base URL".

Alternative considered: an explicit `webSearch.selfHosted` opt-in flag. Not chosen because an operator who sets `baseUrl` has already named the host, and anyone able to write `baseUrl` can write the flag, so it adds a setting without adding a control.

Also note: an invalid custom `baseUrl` still fails before any request, as on current `main` ("reject malformed endpoints instead of switching hosts"); this change only chooses which guard mode a valid URL is posted through.

prs.title: feat: keep ask_user questions answerable after you start answering
prs.body:
Closes #199174

## What Problem This Solves

An `ask_user` question can expire while someone is reading its choices or typing, losing the opportunity to submit the answer.

## User Impact

In the Control UI, clicking or tapping a question, Tab-focusing it, choosing an option, typing or pasting keeps it answerable until submission, Skip, or cancellation/end of the requesting run. Drafts survive blur and switching questions. Untouched questions retain the existing timeout (900 seconds by default, clamped to 30–3600 seconds). Secret questions retain their timeout. Terminal questions are never revived.

**CI remains red, not ready to land.** Current-head hosted performance passed, but WebKit history, automation navigation and PR-specific whole-shard timeout contribution remain **UNKNOWN**. The bounded paired hosted-load diagnostic did not reproduce navigation failure. The subsequent workload/acceptance audit found no further small representative workload capable of resolving those attributions under the existing limits; no additional diagnostic was run. No budgets or shared secret-submission behavior changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The existing Gateway question manager remains the expiry owner. `question.engage` uses the same answer authority as `question.resolve`; it stops scheduled expiry and records `expiryStoppedAtMs` only for opted-in, non-secret questions. Engagement shares pending-question continuation admission during restart/suspension drain.
- `ask_user` opts in with `stopExpiryOnInteraction`. At its wait deadline it inspects the original question and keeps waiting only when the Gateway stopped expiry. Harness-owned and MCP-form requesters do not opt in.
- The shared question panel reports trusted human input, excluding hover, automatic/programmatic focus, modifier-only keys, Escape and shortcuts. Another Control UI view reconciles with one `question.get` at its local deadline; engagement is not rebroadcast as `question.requested`, which would repeat web push.
- Additive protocol changes, since 2026.11: `question.engage`, optional `QuestionRequestParams.stopExpiryOnInteraction`, optional `QuestionRecord.expiryStoppedAtMs`. No new settings, stores, question categories or model-facing arguments.
- Latest simplification removes a temporary expired-ID collection and second loop, dispatching the same asynchronous reconciliation after local expiry mutation and carrying engagement forward directly: 2 additions, 6 deletions. No assertions or budgets removed.

Tradeoffs and limits:

- Native apps and TUI do not report engagement and can still display the original deadline. Inspected stable v2026.11.3 (`847611dc`) paths tolerate additive fields: Swift synthesized Codable; Android `Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }`. Native runtime execution was unavailable; native engagement/presentation parity is out of scope.
- Failed engagement is reported once per prompt/client, retaining the original deadline rather than retrying on each keystroke. Separate owners/remounts can report again; this is not globally exactly-once delivery.
- Run/model-attempt timeouts still apply. Restart durability remains #167266. The model-facing timeout description is unchanged and describes untouched questions.

## Evidence

**Behavior:** isolated Gateway → Chromium → original `ask_user`, scripted local OpenAI Responses model, 30-second timeout. Base `663611cb` reproduced expiry after clicking/typing. Latest local candidate `74469d7ead45d44c00aa2184006ded0b093472dd` passed **5/5 in 268.75 seconds**, exit 0. Its tree matches published head `67ee0d65e7ef29fb17393d9b24cf5d6f2619b065` exactly. Each case crosses the original deadline and checks the Gateway record and original waiting tool outcome:

| Case | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Click, type, blur | Still pending; submitted `Teal` reaches original tool |
| Tab focus, option selection | Still pending; submitted `Green` reaches original tool |
| Programmatic focus followed by real paste | Paste engages; submitted `Teal` reaches original tool |
| Type, wait, Skip | Draft retained; cancelled; original tool receives `no_answer` |
| Untouched, hover/programmatic focus only | Expires normally; late engagement rejected |

**Focused checks and review:** prompt/shared-state/secret-store consumers **84/84**; UI types, targeted lint/format and `git diff --check` pass. Independent incremental autoreview against `dadf1777`: scoped-clean P0–P2, one pass; prior integrated whole-change review against merge-base `97dd78cc2cbd4f9dff1add734a2b316ac8d8bf31`: two P0–P2 passes. Prior unchanged-owner proof includes manager/RPC/suspension/ask-user/UI/inventory/planner tests, trusted-input Chromium 6/6, protocol registry/generated/native contracts/since guard and test-line ratchet. No production source changed during attribution follow-ups. The audit reconfirmed candidate/head tree equality and existing proof coverage; it was not a new test or review run. Local results do not make CI green.

**Review/acceptance audit:** no new human review or inline finding was present. The hosted ClawSweeper review remains stale; it is not represented as current-head approval. Its historical continuation-admission and execution-inventory findings are addressed in current source, and current-head hosted performance passed. Existing integrated/incremental independent review remains reusable. No changed path matches hard-tier CODEOWNERS; the current-head security guard explicitly requires no SecOps approval for this maintainer PR. `question.engage` retains `operator.questions`, session-write classification and selected-question mutation authorization, including guest participation checks. The change adds input handlers, not visible content/styles/layout, so no appearance-change screenshot gate is claimed. Qualified local real-Gateway proof is valid; the hosted skip below is not a reason to repeat the same acceptance solely for green.

<details>
<summary>Current-head CI failure attribution and completed diagnostics</summary>

### Current-head hosted CI

[Run 43748783425](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43748783425) finished **failure: 71 passed, 22 skipped, 9 failed including aggregate gate**. It tested head `67ee0d65…` as synthetic merge `829e73a462b7e06edffdee4c2175d33aa6504193` against base `cec47fd13f23df46069da1beb65ceaec6e66d04f`.

**[Performance passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43748783425/job/132918429807)** with unchanged budgets, Node 24.22.1/Vite 8.3.5:

| JS gzip | Current | Versus paired base |

| New-session boot | 815,531 B | −330 B |

All three `checks-ui` shards passed. CSS warnings remain; this is not blanket absolute-budget clearance. An independently frozen parent-checkout comparison still failed (+262/+171 chat/new boot bytes; largest JS 557.9 KiB).

**Concrete bundle-context mismatch identified without rebuilding:** retained input manifests show nine packaged plugin distributions in the parent candidate (clawrouter, deep-research, knowledge, mcp-relay, memory-core, nostr, whatsapp, workboard, x), versus three in the exact-merge build (memory-core, nostr, whatsapp). `ui/config/control-ui-plugin-distributions.ts` generates the inventory from `dist/extensions`; frozen dependencies do not equalize those generated runtime inputs. The parent comparison's candidate/archived-base attribution records `ui/src/plugins/control-ui-distribution.ts` at **4,162/1,432 raw bytes**, **877/465 standalone gzip bytes**. Retained sourcemaps expose the same 4,675 source entries; shared chunk original sources/content are identical, while its additional **2,730 mapped raw bytes** belong to that generated inventory. The comparison does not recreate the candidate's nine-plugin runtime distribution in its archived baseline. This materially confounds the failed comparison; it does **not** prove the inventory explains every gzip byte or universal budget clearance. Original failed result and hosted pass are both preserved; no comparator/product change or new build was warranted.

| Failed lane | Evidence and disposition |
| --- | --- |
| [E2E 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43748783425/job/132918430154) | WebKit history loaded 30 versus expected 190 messages, line 106. Exact current base and merge focused cases passed (6.69s/6.65s); subsequent instrumented CI=true pair also passed. **UNKNOWN**, not inherited or repaired. Distinct from previous cached-transcript-fidelity failure. |
| [E2E 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43748783425/job/132918430204) | Cumulative 20-minute action timeout; `gateway-fresh-visit.http` queued with no cases. **PR-specific whole-shard contribution unknown.** No broad replay or timeout relaxation. |
| [E2E 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43748783425/job/132918430189) | Rail 18px versus ≤1: matches established inherited signature. |
| [E2E 5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43748783425/job/132918430195) | Lightbox 57 versus 0 matches established inherited signature. Native-plugin Transcript combobox failed at the same locator/callsite on exact current base and merge. **Deadline caveat:** local default 10s versus hosted 30s; not an exact 30-second reproduction or repair. Missing-control cause unlocalized. |
| [E2E 6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43748783425/job/132918430221) | Automation inspector times out awaiting `/automations`, line 97. Focused base/merge and bounded paired hosted-load cases passed. **UNKNOWN**, not inherited or repaired. |
| [Node changed 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43748783425/job/132918431097) | Same case-18 Closing-proof notice mismatch: input remains Owned notice plus removed-job not-found output. Consistent with previously boundary-observed inherited source migration (`3bbf6750`): capture omits transcript sessionId while `cron-job-turn-target.ts:87` requires equality and releases restored authority. Capture, codec, notice-target and fixture unchanged from prior exact base to current base and current base to merge. Prior diagnostics reached 19 provider calls then stalled in cleanup; **no terminal local current-base Vitest reproduction claimed**. Separate owner-migration/fixture-cleanup follow-up, not repaired here. |
| [Node large 13](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43748783425/job/132918431025) | Archived-session rejection's extra `retryable: false`: matches established inherited signature, reproduced on previous exact base/merge; base includes `6f8b9fa0` (#199575). |
| [Baseline ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43748783425/job/132918430152) | Hosted runner lost communication. Log blob unavailable; **no ratchet assertion established**. |

Initial current UI attribution used fresh production bundles, actual root CI wrapper, `ui-e2e-bundled`, maxWorkers=4, one focused group per revision: each 6 passed, 1 native-plugin failure, 5 skipped. No full hosted dispatch-order/load replay. Question handling is gated behind actual questions, including the lazy-loaded panel's import-time keydown listener; source-path disjointness alone is **not inheritance proof**.

### Bounded input and timeout diagnostics

- **History:** one instrumented exact-base/merge CI=true pair passed **6.810s/6.942s**. Both captured trusted wheel → one older-history request → **30→190 messages**, with no question panel or engagement RPC. Original hosted artifact has only invocation progress, no target DOM/input/RPC trace or screenshot. It cannot distinguish a missing request from response/application failure; no 190→30 transition is established.
- **Shard selection:** actual owner selects the same ordered **159 specifications** on exact base and merge; **155 completed**, four lack completion. New real-Gateway acceptance is excluded from ordinary discovery. Last bundled module completed immediately before `gateway-fresh-visit.http` was recorded queued with no cases: cumulative cap exhaustion, not proof its body hung. Exact-base push [43748563424](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43748563424) skipped UI and is **not** a timing baseline.
- **Question-flow cost:** separately instrumented sequential pair, actual bundled wrapper, CI=true, four-worker ceiling, original assertions: **16/16 both**, module **30.675s/30.618s**, versus hosted **131.1s**. Question list/get/resolve counts unchanged (**18/5/12**); merge adds **15** engage reports. Fourteen captured mock replies: maximum receipt-to-delivery **35.4ms**, sum **216.7ms**; one response event not captured at teardown. Mock default successful `{}` fails record parsing inside the catch—not a 30-second RPC timeout. Mock timings are not Gateway latency/INP. One selected file does not rule out whole-shard contention/cross-file effects.
- **Original navigation boundary:** artifact shows settled original chat, Details open, automation rows and tooltip, no router settlement error and **no `cron.get`**. The failure precedes selected-job loading; absent click/admission trace prevents distinguishing retargeted input, interrupted delivery or failed admission. An initial diagnostic lifecycle-hook wrapper recursed and halted rendering before the click on both revisions: **invalid instrumentation, not product/inheritance evidence**. Corrected passive navigation-only pair passed **1.258s/1.216s**, observing intended click → expected SPA prevention → correct URL → job read/title. No lifecycle-hook access in corrected probes.

### Paired hosted-load diagnostic — November 15

A supported Blacksmith Testbox route was available and used for one diagnostic pair: [run 43756717611](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43756717611), workflow `ci-check-testbox.yml` from `main`, sole lease `tbx_01m7gddd0ec12rc8fjjptc0k8g`. Qualified **four usable AMD EPYC CPUs, 16,556,183,552 bytes RAM, Node 24.22.1**. Independent frozen installs/caches and fresh production bundles on the exact base/merge above. No PR CI rerun or full-suite dispatch.

**Named unknown:** can the desktop input/navigation loss be captured with the three actual contemporaneous peers from the original failed shard? Cohort: automation inspection, fork command, tool-output fidelity, link-reader refresh; all **10 original cases**, actual bundled wrapper, maxWorkers=4, original CI deadlines. Passive input/DOM/request observation only; no forced click, delays, lifecycle hooks or product changes.

| Result | Base | Merge |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Cases / exit | 10 passed / 0 | 10 passed / 0 |
| Four-file invocation | 28.760s | 29.351s |
| Desktop navigation | 2,584ms | 2,387ms |

Both captured intended trusted click → expected SPA prevention → `/automations?job=release+%2B+review` → one matching `cron.get` → selected title. No question panel or question action RPCs observed; ordinary `question.list` only. This does not eliminate import-time effects or isolate question-path causation.

**Concurrency limits:** native case/module lifetimes and progress samples show four occupied workers during desktop navigation, with peers not finished. Tool-output was transitioning through setup; identical peer test-phase alignment at the exact gesture is unproven. Fixture-fixed browser clock prevents precise browser/host time joining. CPU activity reached approximately 98% in a sampled aggregate interval, but PSI was unavailable; hardware, pressure and cumulative shard history were not identical. These are single-sample behavior observations, not a stable speed benchmark. **Navigation, history and whole-shard timeout attribution remain UNKNOWN.** No failed input/admission boundary reproduced and no source repair justified.

Payload 76 seconds; wrapper settled exit 0. **44 remote-generated file hashes verified** before blocking stop exited 0; independent exact-ID status confirmed **completed**. Post-command portal synchronization reported a deadline warning; artifact retrieval and cleanup were independently verified. An unsupported warmup flag failed before allocation; only one lease and one experiment pair ran. Original budgets, 30-second CI navigation deadline, native 60-minute total-job and 15-minute idle limits unchanged. Detailed report and private raw evidence retained in the linked UI work session; private screenshots/state not republished.

### Route availability and remaining evidence gap

- Normal `ci.yml` manual dispatch supports an exact target but no shard/job/test filter, so it was not used as a bounded diagnostic. Default Boat readiness requires an unavailable `ASCII_BOX_API_KEY`; no credential/configuration change or provider-fallback chain. Matched-profile Testbox was supported and completed, so **no repository dispatch-access blocker is claimed**.
- Existing scheduled main [43752350730](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43752350730), head `257759ae…`, independently supplied loaded observations without requesting another run: history WebKit **19.372s**, automation three cases **12.981s**, question-flow **106.097s**, all passing; another shard hit the 20-minute cap. Different source, 956 versus 959 discovered specs, reshuffled shard membership and hardware mean this is **not** a paired baseline or inheritance proof.
- Original missing input/request/application bytes cannot be recovered from existing artifacts. Further route assessment is below; no claim that all investigation routes are technically unavailable.

</details>

### Representative workload and failure-capture assessment — November 15 follow-up

**Unknowns defined before any further execution:** history wheel delivery → older request → response → 160-message prefix application; navigation intended click → handler → observable route → `cron.get`; cumulative shard admission/import/setup/body/cleanup cost and any PR-specific increment. The assessment was read-only: no additional allocation, test, source edit or CI dispatch.

**Why no further subset was run:** original history admission envelope spans **410.109–451.808s**, with three ongoing peers and three replacement admissions during it. The actual WebKit wheel timestamp is missing, so selecting its gesture-time peers/phases would be guesswork. Navigation's actual contemporaneous four-file cohort was already tested; adding replacements from its later failed wait would not recover the missing click. Question-flow's initial cohort was board-fixture, markdown-table interactions and sidebar-panel contract from approximately **29.9s**, followed by replacement admissions through the **1200.263s** cap. Replaying selected files together changes their admission and predecessor history. Preserving the original cumulative conditions requires broader scheduling-history replay, excluded by the existing scope; arbitrary pressure/delays introduce a different workload. Admission envelopes are not case-execution intervals or CPU-saturation proof. No additional small selection was identified that can resolve all three causal attributions.

**Concrete capture gap and viable future design, not enabled proof:** WebKit history creates a raw `webkitBrowser.newContext()` and closes it directly in `finally`, outside the suite-owned context failure-capture path. This explains absent capture, not the history failure. There is no existing flag to enable the missing passive wheel/request/application or click/admission trace. A test/harness diagnostics change could retain bounded events before context closure and native reporter phase/resource observations, without intercepting lifecycle methods, adding gestures/waits/retries, weakening assertions or changing production behavior. A future trace could localize that future failure; it would not by itself establish original-run causation or replace a matched base timing baseline.

A proportionate future capture design would use existing artifact owners, at most **256 events per target case**, **2 MiB per shard**, resource sampling every **5s**, existing **7-day retention**, four workers and the original **20-minute cap**. These are proposed diagnostic output ceilings only, **not applied changes** to any current budget or retention contract. One natural invocation then stop whether it passes or fails; observer overhead remains a limitation. Scheduled `main` cannot consume diagnostics that exist only in this deliberately unmerged PR, while a new PR push/manual workflow would initiate CI rather than passively instrument an already-running failure. No separate main/harness change or broad replay was made. Thus unchanged future CI alone is not a completion/watch path for this missing capture.

**Current conclusion:** there is no evidence-supported production repair and no presently executable additional representative comparison under the retained scope that resolves the missing attribution. The technical constraint is missing original boundary telemetry and unmatched cumulative scheduling history—not lack of repository access. History, navigation and whole-shard contribution remain **UNKNOWN**. The **Native local 10s/hosted 30s** and **parent frozen-bundle comparison failure** caveats are retained; the latter now has a concrete generated-input confound, not a claim of universal budget clearance.

<details>
<summary>Previous-head investigation and bundle regression proof</summary>

[Run 43742956198](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43742956198), predecessor `dadf1777`, used merge `047a7feeee7c406f53958b4d1be3ec32a802cf2c` and base `8b94cfb556c3ffa2d52eb9678b51828a31bb2966`. Independent frozen installs: Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, Vite 8.3.5, Pako 3.0.3. Unmodified predecessor failed twice identically (+140/+49 chat/new boot gzip bytes; largest chunk about +90 versus unchanged 64-byte growth allowance). Latest simplification passed twice identically (−394/−485; startup +8; request counts unchanged). Earlier requested-event-reuse/hydration-helper experiments reverted. No shared secret-submission lazy loading.

Previous WebKit null-focus reproduced on exact base using UI-package entrypoint and initial tooltip/model-picker/geometry group; merge passed, underlying timing cause unlocalized. Cached transcript fidelity reproduced both (reader y −2259→−2236.609375; scrollTop 6075→6031; text/height unchanged). Previous lane labeled 5/7 was actually shard5/6: identical 159 selected,157 completed; footer newly active before cumulative exhaustion, not a proven hang. Focused footer/composer-draft passed both; hidden lightbox reproduced both. Whole-shard contribution unknown. `pnpm test:ci-failed 199205` ran for previous head, not current certification.

</details>

**Real-Gateway CI selection:** hosted real-Gateway lane was skipped. Ordinary PR CI requires `ci:full`, which the managed publisher cannot add; serial/private inventory registration alone does not select it. Automatic main selection remains release-only. Five-case acceptance above was local, not hosted.

All deadlines, assertions, budgets and secret-question behavior remain unchanged. No green-seeking reruns, full-shard replay, merge, auto-merge, deployment, release, appearance changes or live Gateway changes. Issue ownership remains @hannesrudolph.
