prs.title: fix: keep cold model catalog reads off the Gateway event loop
prs.body:
Related: #200136

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: cold model-catalog loading and refresh can stall the Gateway event loop on writable filesystem reads even when callers use the asynchronous registry APIs.

## User Impact

Async catalog create, refresh, and provider unregister remain responsive while filesystem work waits, while retaining selected-file results, refresh freshness, warnings, immediate-close behavior, and alias replacement checks. Explicit deprecated synchronous APIs and Doctor migration behavior remain supported; no configuration or schema change is required.

The measured normal owner costs increase by **0.303 ms for registry refresh** and **0.124 ms for cold admission** in separate experiments. These are accepted responsiveness tradeoffs, not a general speedup or a combined-request timing claim.

## Why This Change Was Made

Async registry methods previously prepared SQLite catalogs, then synchronously opened the selected root file and inspected legacy directories. Their cold catalog reader also synchronously resolved agent ownership and shared-state identity. The new preparation consumes the existing canonical file queue, asynchronous filesystem owner, and catalog-read worker. Cold identity preparation retains the existing state and agent resource lifetimes before yielding; it does not add another authority owner or cache.

Production grows **262 lines across 16 modules** to preserve these real close and alias contracts across the async boundary. Two substantial portions of the diff relocate existing code: the read/close lifecycle factory and the legacy inspector. All internal factory consumers migrate, and Doctor imports the inspector directly instead of retaining the obsolete re-export. The assertion allowance for the original catalog module shrinks from **3 to 1**; no allowance is added.

## Evidence

The initiating reliability evidence was Team 25c97908, 2026-11-16 05:02 PST: MAIN spent 1.97 s in D-state in `openat2(O_CREAT)` on the plugin-model-catalog lock, with `btrfs_create → start_transaction → wait_current_trans`, producing a 2,002 ms scheduler stall during `update.remote-model-catalog`. #200136 addressed that lock; this follow-up closes additional cold-read paths exposed by the broader guard. No Team data was copied or changed.

- Real public API guards fail on the original registry base; real catalog and hardlink-replacement guards fail on exact parent `775be7a709fafd9dd8e596cbdf2a1e7e89d5428b`. Correct behavior is asserted before the filesystem guard, so setup errors do not count as regressions.
- **8/8 combined broadened API/metadata guards pass**, including create/refresh/unregister, async legacy inspection, catalog replacement, alias retirement, and immediate root/agent close. Sources match the combined proof; the final import-only Doctor cleanup additionally passes **26/26** existing consumer tests.
- Reused valid owner proof includes **48/48** admission tests, **75/75** registry/discovery/catalog tests, the real session reload consumer, and **14/14** prompt-prefix tests. Final combined types, applicable guards, formatting, and lint pass. Whole-union and final delta-focused isolated Codex reviews are clean through P2.
- `pnpm check:changed` completed with only the dead-export scan failing: **116/116 findings reproduce exactly on the clean pinned parent**, with no candidate-only entries or changed finding-owner module. Four newer package-release entries are attributed to `b868ed4c21ba046aae5d41bcd9c6c61e530c0a3f` / #198835. Introducing-commit attribution for the older 112 entries remains partial; this is recorded as a main regression, not a blanket inherited/noise classification. The first exact-head CI exposed a missing native-wrapper inventory entry, now repaired; fresh exact-head CI and final-head ClawSweeper review are required before landing.

The first CI run (`43951433775`) failed native wrapper closure and provisioning because the moved state lifecycle module was omitted from `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt`. The repair adds that existing module to the inventory without changing production or test behavior. The existing closure regression fails on `751938673e55ba674cddd252bf051f5c47269f99` and passes with the inventory correction. All four closure checks and all 16 Linux-applicable provisioning cases pass; a macOS recovery case also passes. The additionally selected macOS-only full cold/warm sibling case exceeds its existing 120-second deadline (266.742 seconds observed). The outer invocation fails and source-generation verification completes. This local timeout remains unresolved, not classified as inherited; no timeout or assertion changed.

That run also hit a 15-second real Doctor child timeout in the legacy resume fixture. Bounded Bun replays passed on exact CI parent `2435c1faa791de766688ba27ca7a14a92e30b7e4` and the candidate with the original timeout (13.028 s and 10.967 s for the case). The Linux CI failure remains unexplained: these macOS replays establish neither a fix nor inherited status. No timeout or assertion was relaxed, and no CI rerun was requested.

Current head `af7e30a6be072a7583060915a9355ff17c718a54` has a separate unresolved CI failure in run `43958708556`: the runtime source-closure guard exceeds its unchanged 120-second deadline (128.029 seconds observed). Phase diagnostics identify graph construction as the dominant work; required worker roots and assertions remain intact. A single Linux comparison under a shared two-CPU budget, with the canonical cold worker compiler running concurrently, passes on exact main parent `344cc75d086dc1b1ab7e50feffeef55c63fc816f` (107.289 seconds) and exact CI merge `ff1d5d28dc1865c5b522b8582998d4379ac2ffe1` (86.750 seconds). Compiler artifact counts differ from the original CI run. These passing replays establish neither a fix nor inherited failure; no CI rerun or admin exception is selected. The temporary remote lease was released. Final-head ClawSweeper review has zero open items; landing remains blocked on the unexplained CI failure.

Two separate 30-process experiments used five A/A pairs and five interleaved A/B pairs at each of 0 ms and 2,000 ms delay. Each used synthetic agent storage of approximately 35 GiB with 5,000 sessions, a 1,000-model catalog, and a retained 62,000-file/1.1 GB workspace. The indexed owner does not scan that workspace. All children joined, assertions passed, and source hashes were checked.

| Separate owner envelope, normal medians | Owner latency ms | Main CPU ms | Process CPU ms | Main allocated bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Warm registry refresh | 10.265 → 10.568 | 6.772 → 6.920 | 24.854 → 24.551 | 7,570,480 → 7,329,504 |
| Cold catalog admission | 5.900 → 6.024 | 2.641 → 2.724 | 13.705 → 14.036 | 1,155,208 → 1,037,112 |

With a two-second selected-file fault, the registry heartbeat gap falls **2015.267 → 5.283 ms**; the cold-admission gap falls **2012.101 → 1.916 ms** (candidate maxima 5.469 and 2.027 ms). The respective owner waits remain approximately two seconds. Allocation ranges overlap; **no allocation improvement is claimed**. Responsive heartbeat work raises delayed CPU/allocation: registry main CPU 7.300 → 36.213 ms and allocation 7,763,160 → 15,239,632 bytes; cold admission 5.432 → 36.361 ms and 1,668,800 → 5,016,464 bytes. These are not normal owner overhead measurements.

Both experiments used Node 26.12.1 on macOS/APFS with fault injection, not real btrfs transaction measurements. Main-isolate allocation excludes worker/native allocation. **The final composition was functionally qualified, not benchmarked as one combined request.** The normal medians above must not be added together.

<details>
<summary>Converted call sites and preserved boundaries</summary>

| Call site | Async serving-path change |
| --- | --- |
| `ModelRegistry.createAsync` → `loadCustomModels` | Prepares selected root contents before construction, avoiding its `existsSync` and `readFileSync`. |
| `ModelRegistry.refreshAsync` → `reload` | Captures fresh root contents and errors on each call; no persistent captured-bytes cache. |
| `ModelRegistry.unregisterProviderAsync` | Its existing refresh delegation inherits the same repair. |
| `readModelRegistrySources` | Canonical `models.json` uses the existing queued source owner; arbitrary supplied filenames use async `readFile`. |
| `ModelRegistry.loadModels` | Consumes prepared legacy warning facts for async calls. |
| `inspectLegacyPluginModelCatalogs` | Both root and per-plugin `readdirSync` calls, plus each guarded `readLegacyPluginModelCatalog` read/identity chain, execute inside the existing catalog worker for async callers. |
| `loadPersistedPluginModelCatalogs` | Uses the existing async agent-ID owner and asynchronous state context, retaining unresolved agent custody before the first await. |
| State lifecycle `captureAsync` / `resolve` | Initial stat/realpath and first-creation candidate inspection use async identity facts; the existing resolver owns admission. |
| State lifecycle `findPhysicalRecord` | Retained alias probes use prepared async observations while preserving replacement retirement. |
| `captureOpenClawStateReadContextWithAdmission` → schema admission | Reuses the prepared canonical identity instead of repeating synchronous realpath. |

Private catalog task/result transport, the cache facade, and type imports carry these owner operations. The complete state lifecycle factory moves with all six consumers; maintenance scope creation remains byte-identical. Doctor retains the same synchronous inspector through a direct owner import. Explicit deprecated synchronous ModelRegistry methods remain supported through their existing documented deadline.

This PR does not claim that every remaining Gateway filesystem path is repaired. Other cold auth/execution callers and previously reported upstream filesystem-owner boundaries remain separate work.

</details>

prs.title: feat(ui): show backups in Settings instead of Systems
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Backup health lives on the Systems page, mixed in with machine telemetry and remote desktops, even though backups describe the Gateway's data rather than any machine.

## User Impact

User impact: the Backups section (each target's latest outcome, size, destination, namespace and next run, unrecorded schedules, and a **Check** action per storage location) is now under **Settings → Agent defaults → Session**, right below Session storage and its backup hint. Systems shows only devices, desktops and measurements.

There is no config, protocol or data change. Behavior differences:

- Systems polled `backup.status` every 15 seconds while its Gateway view was open. Settings reads it on open, on config change, on reconnect and on **Refresh backups**, like the Session storage block next to it.
- While the Gateway is disconnected, the last accepted status and storage locations stay visible (as in Session storage), with **Check** disabled until the connection returns.
- Settings search finds the section by "backup" and related terms.

## Why This Change Was Made

Backup state had its own request, storage-probe cache and cancellation paths inside the Systems controller. This PR removes them and gives the Settings section one owner: it reuses the existing Settings status reader (`createSettingsStatus`), which already retires reads on connection and access changes. Storage checks are local to the section. They are aborted on any connection change, cleared when re-run, and shown only for the config they ran under. Without `operator.read`, the section says read access is required, as Systems did.

Systems loses its backup render, state, i18n keys, CSS and tests. The overview now reserves only the telemetry area, and with statistics off it hides unless a notice is showing. Docs that pointed to backups in Systems now point to Settings.

## Evidence

Before/after captures use the mock Gateway with synthetic backup and session-storage data (1440 px, dark).

**Systems, before:** Backups summary under the telemetry
![Systems before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d37625e4-b3e4-4e56-9261-d5764969cae0)

**Systems, after:** telemetry only
![Systems after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7719f68f-2d49-4e6b-ada4-e86cd4c6d027)

**Agent defaults › Session, before**
![Session before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd3aeac5-ce4c-45af-87b3-b6ba03f82c03)

**Agent defaults › Session, after:** Backups and Storage locations below Session storage
![Session after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6536e7f9-7ed8-4240-940d-5d4d5c94f1ca)

Checks run locally:

- `pnpm -s tsgo:ui`: clean.
- Unit tests, `backups-settings`, `session-storage`, `session-storage-route`, `settings-search`, `settings-targets` and all `pages/systems` tests: passed. New Settings tests cover rendered outcomes and schedules with on-request storage checks, failed read → refresh → read-access-required, and dropping a status read and a storage check that started on the previous connection.
- Affected UI e2e files only (`systems-workspace`, `systems-inventory-readiness`, `session-storage-settings`): all passed. The full e2e suite was not run.
- `pnpm -s ui:i18n:verify`, `ui:i18n:baseline` (raw-copy baseline updated), oxfmt check, oxlint on the touched files, stylelint on `systems.css`, `format:docs:check`, `check:control-ui-controllers` and `git diff --check`: clean.

prs.title: fix(qa): live runs fail with configured SecretRefs
prs.body:
Related: #200202

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: live QA fails to start when a selected model provider uses a configured SecretRef.

## User Impact

User impact: live QA can reuse an existing portable resolver binding without a fixture-specific configuration hook. Host secret-store contents, installed secret integrations, and opaque exec dependencies are not cloned; those dependencies must already work in the QA environment. No new settings or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep selected provider declarations and their referenced resolver policy together. Reuse the canonical schema and credential-target registry through the existing private QA interface, anchor file paths before home isolation, and leave value resolution and deny policy with their existing owner.

## Evidence

- Four regression cases fail on the qualified baseline and pass with the repair: configured env/file refs, an implicit env default alias, dependency/path scope, and request-header deny policy.
- Focused coverage: **34 distinct cases** — 13 auth-profile/resolver cases through the default database-worker runner, 6 staging cases, and 15 prefix-stability cases. The CI repair's 13 cases passed without pool/isolation overrides; unchanged proof was reused. Targeted strict types, lint, format, whitespace, and the canonical plugin-import boundary check pass.
- Full private-QA build passed. Normal live-frontier QA passed **1 scenario / 1 cell, 0 failures, 0 skips**, with **no mutation hook or credential/model/endpoint override**. The served QA agent and canonical OpenAI primary were checked; `QA-SECRETREF-OK` was both persisted and delivered.
- Complete original staged-source autoreview and the separate CI-repair delta review were scoped-clean through P2. Full build/live proof ran on `4065e89a4c7370af5621f46265de93166be6fbb3` (tree `72d003b84f4907a5ae57568a3a720d68146b9716`). The subsequent repair changes only test ownership; production files are unchanged, so build/model execution was not repeated.

**CI correction:** [run 43955208229](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43955208229) on the original `8a269c5e` head failed two env cases before their resolver assertions because the standalone suite used ordinary QA rather than the database-worker lane. The default local replay reproduced 2 failures / 2 passes. All four unchanged regressions now live in the existing database-worker auth-profile suite; the standalone fixture is deleted, with no new routing exception, retries, timeout changes, ignores, or weaker assertions. The original CI failure is retained; the repaired head requires its own CI.

<details>
<summary>Sanitized retained real-agent runtime evidence</summary>

These are exact allowlisted fields from the retained normal-run receipt and canonical report, not a new inference. The configured credential surface was `models.providers.openai.apiKey`, already backed by a file SecretRef. Alias/ref ID, secret-file path, endpoints, model IDs, and credential values are omitted.

```json
{
  "status": "passed",
  "sourceHead": "4065e89a4c7370af5621f46265de93166be6fbb3",
  "sourceTree": "72d003b84f4907a5ae57568a3a720d68146b9716",
  "scenarios": 1,
  "passed": 1,
  "failed": 0,
  "skipped": 0,
  "expectedCells": 1,
  "observedCells": 1,
  "primaryProvider": "openai",
  "sourceUsesFileSecretRef": true,
  "mutationHookSupplied": false,
  "fixtureAddsCredentialValues": false,
  "fixtureOverridesModelsEndpointsOrRefs": false
}
```

Canonical scenario details:

```json
{
  "qaAgentListed": true,
  "canonicalServedModel": true,
  "persistedFinal": "QA-SECRETREF-OK",
  "delivered": "QA-SECRETREF-OK"
}
```

</details>

**Proof limits:** PR CI is the broad gate. The full-tree unused-file scan remains red for five unchanged, non-owned paths; the production scan reports zero. The private build also reports four nonfatal existing UI-budget advisories, not a strict UI-budget pass. The independent reviewer did not inspect unchanged resolver implementations excluded by its input policy; it reviewed the complete QA change and permitted canonical contracts.

<details>
<summary>Baseline qualification and retained local findings</summary>

The original current-main attempt ran zero QA cases because of the moved OAuth path-helper import. A separately recorded, local-only import correction first qualified the actual regression. The existing repair then landed as `0879f3e98833e64ec4f3d09df032e9f70ebfed2c` (#200242); it is not part of this PR. The four regressions were red for the intended resolver-policy failure, not compiler setup. The initial focused checks used fork/isolation overrides, which did not establish default CI routing; the later CI failure and default-run repair are recorded above. An initial review omitted the untracked regression and remained incomplete; the complete staged capture and later two-file CI-repair review passed.

The five full-tree unused-file findings are:
- `scripts/lib/stable-publish-recovery.mjs`
- `src/gateway/tools-invoke.policy.test-support.ts`
- `src/plugins/test-helpers/install-account-policy.test-support.ts`
- `test/scripts/fixtures/vitest-worker-scheduling.cjs`
- `test/scripts/vitest-worker-cache-retention.test-support.ts`

The nonfatal private-build advisories are CSS gzip 57.8 > 56.9 KiB, chat boot requests 21 > 20, chat boot gzip 1294.1 > 1293.6 KiB, and new boot gzip 797.5 > 797.0 KiB. This PR changes no UI code.

</details>

prs.title: fix(update): openclaw cannot start when the first release-layout update is killed mid-conversion
prs.body:
Related: #198835

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw` cannot start when the updater dies (SIGKILL, power loss) partway through the first update that converts an OpenClaw-owned npm prefix to release directories.

That conversion renamed the package directory `lib/node_modules/openclaw` into `releases/` and then renamed a link onto the package path. Between the two renames the package path did not exist. Recovery was a manual rename of a leftover `lib/node_modules/.openclaw.release-link-*`.

## User Impact

User impact: on macOS, and on Linux with a system perl (x64, arm64) or Node 26, the package path names a complete package at every instant of that conversion, also when the updater is killed. Nothing needs manual recovery.

Where no atomic exchange is available (Alpine without perl on Node 24, other architectures without Node FFI, a filesystem that refuses the call) the update still converts the directory with the previous two renames. The brief missing-path instant and its documented recovery remain there. An update never fails because the exchange is unavailable. The `package-swap` step text says which method ran, for example `...; the package directory became that release by an atomic exchange (perl)`.

No config, schema, protocol or dependency changes.

**Update behavior.** The installed version's updater performs the conversion, not the candidate's. Published updaters do not know release directories, so an installation that updates from a published version to a build with this change gets a plain package swap, as before, and its package path stays a plain directory. The first update that such a build runs itself converts the directory with the exchange. A build between #198835 and this change converts with the two renames, and nothing in a later candidate can change that. The exchange adds no marker and no state. If the updater is killed before the exchange, an unused directory in `releases/` holding one link that names nothing is left behind. Existing code already skips it in `openclaw update status` and removes it once it is a day old, so an older build that later reads the prefix handles it too.

## Why This Change Was Made

POSIX `rename` cannot replace a non-empty directory with a link, so two renames always leave that window. One atomic exchange of two paths closes it: `renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE)` on Linux, `renamex_np(RENAME_SWAP)` on macOS. Adoption now creates the link inside the release, where the directory will live, and exchanges the two paths in one step.

Node has no API for either call, so `src/infra/path-exchange.ts` runs one short-lived tool with absolute paths, no shell, an empty environment and a 30 second limit:

- Node's built-in `node:ffi` when the running Node accepts `--experimental-ffi` (26.8.1 and 26.12.1 here, 26.13.1 in Docker; not 24.x). Detection reads `process.allowedNodeEnvironmentFlags`, so the parent never loads the module and its experimental warning reaches no output.
- `/usr/bin/osascript` (JavaScript for Automation) on macOS.
- `/usr/bin/perl` with `syscall` on Linux, where perl's own build picks the number (316 on x86_64, 276 on aarch64) and any other architecture is refused.

The exchange never trusts an exit code. It records `dev:ino` of both paths first and decides from `lstat` afterwards: exchanged, unchanged (try the next route, then report unavailable), or anything else (throw, another writer). Cleanup after a failed adoption is no longer recursive. It removes the waiting link and the empty directories, so it cannot delete a package that already moved.

Production growth is the new 136-line module (three embedded tool scripts and the identity check) and 43 net lines in `adoptPackageReleaseSlot` and its caller. The plain directory swap and Windows are untouched.

Design notes for review:

- The waiting link is dangling until the exchange, not self-referential. Its text is relative to the package path's directory, so from inside the release it resolves to a path that does not exist.
- Node FFI goes first where it exists. Each route is then the first choice in some mainstream environment (FFI on Node 26, osascript on macOS Node 24, perl on Linux Node 24), so the tests pin each one by name there. An API change in the experimental module fails safe to the system tool.
- `mv --exchange` (coreutils 9.5+) would be another Linux route, and `src/commands/doctor-sqlite-nocow.ts` already probes with it. I left it out to keep this change small. It is a reasonable follow-up, together with the same window in the plain directory swap.

## Evidence

Head `9ae24fde38f` on base `48cd549b1c4`. The red and green runs and the Docker run were made on `eb0f76cc24f` (base `bd25e9ef60c`), the same change before a rebase. The ten commits in between touch none of the changed files, the release slot, its callers or its fixtures, so only the focused tests and the changed-scope checks were rerun on the rebased head.

**Regression, red then green.** `src/infra/package-update-release-switch.process.test.ts` runs the real release switch (`swapStagedPackageInstall` on a plain package directory) in a child process once to the end, then once per boundary with the child SIGKILLed right after that boundary. A boundary is one completed `fs/promises` mutation or the start or end of one exchange tool process, counted by interposing at the Node API in the child. After each kill the package path must serve a complete package.

Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/package-update-release-switch.process.test.ts src/infra/package-release-slot.test.ts src/infra/path-exchange.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`

- Base production code (`package-release-slot.ts` and `package-update-release-switch.ts` from `bd25e9ef60c`) with these tests: 3 failed, 15 passed. The sweep fails with exactly one boundary that leaves no package, `rename lib/node_modules/openclaw -> releases/2026.11.3/lib/node_modules/openclaw`. The other two failures are tests of behavior that exists only on head (the reported method and the waiting link).
- Head: 18 passed on Node 26.12.1 (route `node:ffi`, 10 boundaries) and 18 passed on Node 24.22.1 (route `osascript`), macOS 27.2 arm64.
- Negative control, in the same file: with every exchange tool failing to start, adoption takes the two renames (14 boundaries) and the same sweep finds exactly that one boundary again, then proves the documented recovery from the leftover link.

**Other tests.**

- `path-exchange.test.ts`: a directory and a link in different directories, under a path with spaces and non-ASCII names, exchange with both inodes preserved and the route named. A kernel refusal (a directory with its own descendant) and a missing path report unavailable with nothing changed. A path replaced while the tool ran throws.
- `package-release-slot.test.ts`: adoption refused before the exchange removes the waiting link and its release directory and leaves the package directory untouched.
- Leftover: a switch killed with the link waiting is followed by a real next update, which adopts again. `listPackageReleases` (what `openclaw update status` reads) does not list the leftover and `collectPackageReleases` removes it after a day.
- With `package-update-release-switch.test.ts`, `package-release-retention.test.ts` and `update-managed-service-handoff-interrupted-release.test.ts`: 6 files, 40 tests passed on the rebased head. The two `src/cli/update-cli/*release-link.test.ts` files: 4 passed (before the rebase).

**Routes run by hand** with one probe that exchanges a directory and a link under a non-ASCII path: macOS arm64 Node 26.12.1 and 26.8.1 (`node:ffi`), Node 24.22.1 (`osascript`); Docker `node:24.22.1-trixie-slim` arm64 and amd64 (`perl`), `node:26-trixie-slim` and `node:26-alpine` arm64 (`node:ffi`, glibc and musl). `node:24.22.1-alpine` reports `perl: ENOENT` and stays unavailable.

**Docker, Linux.** `pnpm test:docker:published-driver-release-adoption` with the candidate packed from `eb0f76cc24f` (image `node:24.22.1-trixie-slim`, aarch64, perl 5.40.1 present).

- As committed, the cell stops before the follow-up update at an unrelated assertion: `Installed candidate tree exceeds the release budget (52228 entries, 613092717 bytes)`. The budget is 47,500 entries. A package built the same way from base `bd25e9ef60c` has the same 27,102 tarball entries as this head, so this change did not cause it. Published 2026.11.4 has 15,230 files.
- With only that one assertion bypassed in a local, uncommitted edit of the driver, the cell passed: `PASS published 2026.11.4 → candidate 2026.11.4 (eb0f76cc24ff...)`. The candidate's own follow-up update adopted the published updater's plain directory, and its `package-swap` step reads `...; the package directory became that release by an atomic exchange (perl)`. This PR adds an assertion on that text to the cell, and it passed.

**Checks.** `git diff --check`, `oxfmt --check` on the changed files, `pnpm tsgo:all`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <changed files>`, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` (+336 net test lines, allowance 400), `pnpm check:test-mock-exports`, and `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs` all pass. The dead-export scan (`scripts/check-deadcode-exports.mts`) exits 1 with 122 entries. None is an export this PR adds. Three are in a touched file but predate it (`isOpenClawOwnedPackagePrefix`, `resolvePackageReleaseTarget`, `sweepPackageReleaseTemporaryLinks` in `package-release-slot.ts`, from #198835).

**Test audit.** Files audited in full: `package-update-release-switch.process.test.ts`, its child fixture `package-update-release-switch.process.test-support.ts`, `package-release-slot.test.ts`, `package-update-release-switch.test-support.ts`. Removed: the named cut `adoption-window` and its test "between the adoption renames". The fallback sweep covers the same boundary more strictly (it also proves no other boundary is broken) and keeps the same recovery assertions. No other case was pruned. The three link-switch cuts and the seven older slot cases still prove distinct behavior. The compensation case in `package-release-slot.test.ts` now mocks `process.platform` as `freebsd` to reach the two-rename path through the real "no route on this platform" branch. Test time for the process file rose from about 1.5 s to about 5.3 s (26 more child processes, run in parallel).

**Review.** The autoreview helper cannot run on this machine. A fresh read-only agent reviewed the diff instead. Resolved from its findings: the sweep is gated on the environment and can no longer skip on a regression; route names are asserted; cleanup is non-recursive; tools get an empty environment (no `NODE_OPTIONS` or `PERL5OPT`); Bun is excluded from the FFI route; killed runs are matched to boundary labels; the refused-adoption and other-writer cases have tests; the method is a typed result that the caller formats. Not changed: route order (see above) and errno detail in the FFI and osascript failure text.

**Not proven.**

- The Docker cell did not pass as committed, for the unrelated tree budget above. The exchange proof there depends on the local bypass.
- No run on a native x86_64 host (amd64 ran under emulation), on a real `install-cli.sh` installation, or on filesystems other than APFS and the Docker volume and overlay filesystems.
- An updater killed while the exchange tool is still running: the tool can finish the one system call afterwards, which leaves either valid state. Reasoned, not tested.
- The fixture makes tools "missing" by failing `execFile` with `ENOENT`. A really missing tool was observed only in the Alpine probe.
- Bun as the running runtime, and Node 26.1 to 26.7.
- CI has not run yet.

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): members with an admin role are administrators
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An owner can define an OpenClaw ID member role that includes `operator.admin`, and its members receive that scope. Several administrator actions still refuse such a member, because they check the kind of connection and not the scope. Gateway-managed GitHub publication also rechecks the requester's profile before each write, which does not see a member's role, so removing a member does not stop a publication they queued.

## User Impact

User impact: a member whose role includes `operator.admin` is treated as an administrator by the Gateway's administrator actions. Members without that scope gain nothing. No preset role includes it. OpenClaw ID is a Labs feature and is off by default.

Risk an owner should know: an administrator member can edit Gateway config, including role definitions and the OpenClaw ID switch.

What stays with owner devices: inviting, approving, removing, changing roles and admitting nodes all need an owner device signature. Linking, unlinking and recovery-kit steps stay owner-only. An administrator member keeps their own profile and is never treated as the shared owner profile.

Required action: a GitHub publication queued before upgrading to this change, from a profile linked to OpenClaw ID, that records neither how it was authenticated nor a member identity is refused after the upgrade and must be requested again. This covers owner requests and member requests from builds older than #197739. Without that record, current membership cannot safely tell a removed member's request from anyone else's. Member requests queued by builds that include #197739 carry the member identity and are rechecked against current membership instead. Requests queued after the upgrade record their source and are unaffected.

Turning on remote access is not changed by this PR. Since #198349 it is available to an admin signed in through a verified personal sign-in.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Profile administration, model-account administration, personal files, mentions and the personal-profile scope check use the member's current role definition when the connection is a member with `operator.admin`. Before, they used the member profile's named role, which on a team Gateway is usually the restrictive default.
- A publication request records whether it came from a member connection. Before each GitHub write the Gateway rechecks current membership and the current role definition. A removed member, a downgraded role, a deleted definition or OpenClaw ID being turned off stops the write. If membership cannot be read, the request waits; it is never treated as authorized.
- A stored request from before this change has no recorded source. If it also has no member identity and its profile is linked to OpenClaw ID (member or owner), it is refused. A stored member request with a member identity is rechecked against current membership. Requests from profiles with no OpenClaw ID identity behave as before.

## Evidence

- An audit of 169 administrator method descriptors plus HTTP surfaces found the connection-kind refusals fixed here. A reviewer spot-checked more than 15 actions across config, users, pairing, plugins, secrets, terminal, update and restart, cron, cloud dispatch and HTTP, and found no further exclusion and no path wrongly opened.
- Tests: an administrator member performs each fixed action and was refused before; operator and viewer members, nodes and a Tailscale user under a denying default are still refused; an administrator member cannot submit a membership change and is not the owner profile; publication stops after removal and downgrade; a pre-change stored request is refused for a member profile and still works for others.
- Final focused run: 12 files, 204 tests pass. Five typecheck lanes, lint, format, docs checks, import cycles and ratchets pass.
- Independent review of the first two commits found no P0 or P1 and one P2, the pre-change stored requests. The third commit fixes it. A second review of that commit found nothing.

Test lines: 596 added, 196 over the 400-line allowance, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/member-administrator-authority.txt`.

Not run: the full repository suite, real GitHub writes, browser tests, and an upgrade with a real queued publication.

Rebased onto main after #197770 merged. One new test-only commit adapts to main; one conflict in mention policy kept both main's connection authority and this PR's administrator-member behavior. After the rebase: 533 focused tests and the publication suites pass (one host-only failure: a CRLF snapshot test that cannot run on the development host), with typechecks, static checks and ratchets.

Later commit: test-only CI fixes after the rebase (an expected publication snapshot gains the new `authenticationSource` field, a test registry entry is reordered, a policy mock gains the new export, and the test-line allocation is updated). No production change.

Live proof on head `a953b4f20220` (isolated Gateway on a second machine, real staging services): upgrading an installed 2026.11.4 to this build kept configured values, profiles and a stored session; upgrading this PR's base with OpenClaw ID live kept config, members, roles, profiles and pairings, and the claw stayed published. An administrator member's profile-administration action was refused on the base build and allowed on this PR; owner-only operations stayed refused. Removing or downgrading the member removed admin access. See the proof comment.

Queued publication, proven live on head `279fb0dc3880` against a throwaway private repository (see the proof comment): an administrator member's queued request was refused before any write after the member was removed, and after a downgrade; a control request from a still-authorized requester published its branch and PR. Across the upgrade from this PR's base, the linked owner's old request was refused with a request-again outcome and the non-linked request published as before; a member request from the base carries the member identity and published while the member was still authorized. Not shown live: an old member request without a member identity (from a build older than #197739); that case is covered by unit tests.

prs.title: fix(msteams): replies with lists, headings, or tables post twice in personal chats
prs.body:
Related: #158103

## What Problem This Solves

In a Teams 1:1 chat, when the agent's answer has a list, a heading, or a table, the user gets the answer twice. The second copy has its bullet points squashed onto one line.

## User Impact

Users get the answer once, and it still streams in as it is written. List items and line breaks each show on their own line, in normal Teams messages too.

## Why This Change Was Made

Teams only accepts a streaming update that adds to the text already shown. Today the plugin streams the raw text, then at the end swaps in a formatted version. Teams rejects the swap, so the plugin sends the whole answer again as a new message.

The fix has two parts:

1. **Stream the formatted text from the start.** The end of the stream then only adds text, so Teams accepts it.
2. **Keep line breaks.** The formatter writes list items as plain `• item` lines (its mobile-safe style, unchanged), but Teams joins single line breaks, so the items ran together on one line. It now adds a Markdown line break at the end of those lines, and of the author's own line breaks.

The two parts belong together: without part 2, the single streamed answer would show the run-together list.

## Evidence

The same question to the same bot, before and after:

| Before: the answer arrives twice | After: once |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ahamilton454/openclaw/pr-proof/double-reply-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ahamilton454/openclaw/pr-proof/after.png) |

What Teams answered to each streaming update (from our network log):

```text
before  202 202 201 202 403 403 201   <- two updates rejected, then the answer is sent again
after   202 202 201 202 202 202       <- every update accepted
```

- **Tests:** all 1,088 Teams plugin tests pass. With the old code, 15 of the 58 tests touched here fail, including one whose fake Teams server rejects updates exactly like real Teams does.
- **Checks:** format, typecheck, lint, and the SQLite check pass. The dead-code scan lists 103 old entries in other files; this PR adds no exports.
- **Code review:** OpenClaw's autoreview tool (Claude engine on Opus, since Codex isn't installed here and the default Claude model was over its limit) rated it correct. Its one finding, a half-written line that later becomes a table header, is fixed. An earlier independent review found eight issues, all fixed with tests.
- **How often it happens:** across our bots, Teams rejected 47 streaming updates in 14 days, in 4 customer workspaces.
- **Not checked:** the Teams mobile apps (tested on Teams web, including at phone size), and the `progress` streaming mode, which this PR does not change.

## Merge Danger

Easy to revert. No settings or stored data change. It affects how the Teams plugin formats and streams messages.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: feat(voice-call): add LiveKit SIP and native RTC provider
prs.body:
Related: #169991

## What Problem This Solves

Operators who run telephony on LiveKit SIP cannot use Voice Call: it only accepts Twilio, Telnyx, Plivo, and mock carriers.

## User Impact

Operators can select `provider: "livekit"` to place and receive phone calls over a LiveKit SIP trunk. Native RTC audio feeds the existing Voice Call realtime bridge, so model, voice, agent consultation, tools, call history, and playback stay with their current owners. Existing carriers are unchanged.

Supported:
- Outbound calls on a selected outbound trunk. Each call gets a unique room, and the plugin correlates the exact SIP participant identity and SID before it publishes audio.
- Signed inbound LiveKit webhooks for the selected inbound trunks. These use the existing inbound policy and caller allowlist.
- Outbound-only operation (`inboundPolicy: "disabled"`) with no public webhook or media WebSocket.
- `fromNumber` as an E.164 number or, for LiveKit only, a 1–15 digit PBX extension. Targets and allowlists still require E.164, and other carriers still require an E.164 `fromNumber`.
- `wss://` by default. `allowInsecureWs` allows `ws://` only to loopback or private literal IPs.

Not supported: classic STT/TTS mode, carrier XML notify playback, pre-connect DTMF and `send_dtmf`, and Twilio answering-machine detection. Restored calls are retired after a restart, not resumed. The Linux musl native binding is not supported.

New runtime dependencies: `@livekit/rtc-node` 1.1.0 (native) and `livekit-server-sdk` 2.19.1. These need maintainer dependency review.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider reuses the existing manager, realtime handler, and transcript owners instead of adding a separate LiveKit agent worker. Admission is rechecked immediately before the token-bearing RTC connect. Joined disposal persists final transcripts before the call terminates. Shutdown keeps manager finalization failures visible instead of reporting success after carrier cleanup.

<details>
<summary>Changes since the previously published head (42099fa)</summary>

- Merged current `main` (`6a6007663b3`) to clear the new GitHub merge conflict. The new head is `1634010b66c`, a normal merge commit on top of `42099fa` with no rebase or history rewrite. All three conflicts were metadata only:
  - `extensions/voice-call/package.json`: took main's `2026.11.4` version and kept the two LiveKit dependencies and the description that names LiveKit.
  - Config baseline (`counts.json`, `sha256`): took main's files and regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`; the plugin count is again +9 (5080 → 5089).
- `pnpm-lock.yaml` merged without conflict. `pnpm install --lockfile-only` (pnpm 12.15.0) leaves the merged file byte-identical and the supply-chain policy check passes. Its delta against `main` is +206/−0 and is line-for-line the delta already published on `42099fa`; no dependency version changed in this refresh.
- The feature-code patch is unchanged from `42099fa`. Comparing `git diff da3cea2 42099fa` with `git diff 6a60076 1634010` (lockfile excluded) shows only the regenerated baseline hashes and counts. Feature code, tests, docs, `tsdown.config.ts` and the test-line allocation are unchanged.
- Between the two bases, `main` changed two files this PR also touches, and both merged cleanly as main wrote them: the `isProviderConfigured` context pass-through in `webhook.ts` (#199858) and the `tsdown.config.ts` build restructuring (#198664, #196386), where the single `@livekit/rtc-node` external entry keeps its place. No plugin SDK subpath imported by the LiveKit files changed except `provider-selection-runtime`, whose only Voice Call caller is that `webhook.ts` line.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Earlier refresh (ae5340a → 42099fa)</summary>

- Merged current `main` (`da3cea2ce4a`) to clear the new GitHub merge conflict. The new head is `42099fa42e8`, a normal merge commit on top of `ae5340a` with no rebase or history rewrite. All four conflicts were metadata only:
  - `extensions/voice-call/package.json`: took main's `2026.11.1` version and kept the two LiveKit dependencies and the description that names LiveKit.
  - `pnpm-lock.yaml`: took main's lockfile and re-resolved it with pnpm 12.15.0 `--lockfile-only`. The supply-chain policy check passed. Compared with `main` it is still +206/−0 (LiveKit entries only). The one change from the earlier LiveKit delta is the transitive `fast-copy` 4.3.1 (was 4.2.0), pulled in through `livekit-server-sdk` → `pino-pretty`.
  - Config baseline: regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`; the plugin count is again +9.
- The feature-code patch is unchanged from `ae5340a`; metadata and lockfile resolutions are described above. Comparing `git diff aeeff2c ae5340a` with `git diff da3cea2 42099fa` (lockfile excluded) shows only the regenerated baseline hashes and counts and the `version` context line. Feature code, tests, docs, `tsdown.config.ts` and the test-line allocation are unchanged. Main's auto-merged Voice Call changes are kept as written: timer-probe cleanup (#193309), Twilio `listenAfterPlayback`/`turnToken` (#193137), manifest starter prompts (#193694), and the harness service `apiVersion` check (#176886).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Earlier refresh (8278146 → 59eeeba → ae5340a)</summary>

- Merged `main` (`aeeff2c6340`) to clear the GitHub merge conflict. This is a normal merge commit on top of `8278146`, with no rebase or history rewrite. Conflicts:
  - `extensions/voice-call/package.json`: took main's `2026.10.10` version and kept the two LiveKit dependencies and the description that names LiveKit.
  - `realtime-handler.ts`: kept the extracted `createRealtimeTelephonyBinding`. Main's removal of the "idle monitor armed" log (#191794) is ported into `realtime-call-binding.ts`, and that file's now-unused `idleHangupMs` parameter is dropped. Main's other realtime-handler changes auto-merged and are present: transcription language, transcript start timestamps, playback echo filtering, and greeting protection.
  - Config baseline: regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`.
- Compared with `main`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` is +206/−0 (LiveKit entries only). `extensions/openai` is unchanged, and #189358 (`181342878c0`) is still an ancestor.
- No feature code changed.
- Hosted CI then exposed the new test-line budget gate: this PR adds exactly 2,529 test LF bytes against the captured base. Follow-up `ae5340a` adds only `config/test-lines-allocations/livekit-voice-call-provider-170000.txt`, using the documented per-change allocation mechanism. The record explains the SIP/RTC admission, native audio, joined cleanup and compiled-package regression coverage. The shared baseline scalar, assertions, timeouts and production/build/dependency bytes are unchanged. The staged ratchet passes with 25 lines of headroom; this is not a blanket exception or a claim that the earlier failed hosted run passed.

</details>

## Evidence

Focused source checks used local offline fixtures. No phone calls, inference sessions or production credentials were involved.

Source head: `1634010b66c058159a86512d1db4cc8a90570c0d`, which merges main `6a6007663b36db8badd6967e7f2bed5c6b3a724e` into the previously published `42099fa42e8fb11b963a845848b4542bd2e0a92c`. Pinned pnpm 12.15.0 frozen install. prs.title: fix(process): Gateway shutdown fails when broker groups retain zombies
prs.body:
Related: #170000

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes joined Gateway shutdown failing when a spawn broker's private process group contains only dead processes awaiting reaping by another supervisor.

## User Impact

Gateways launched under a child subreaper that does not reap adopted children can stop cleanly instead of reporting retained broker resources. Live descendants still receive TERM/KILL cleanup and must be joined. Timeouts, shutdown budgets, permissions, and non-Linux behavior do not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Node's process-group existence probe still succeeds for unreaped zombies. The host previously treated that as proof that broker work remained alive, waited through the TERM and confirmation windows, and reported `Spawn broker group cleanup could not be confirmed`.

After the existing group probe, Linux confirmation now uses the existing asynchronous process census, own-procfs guard and zombie/definite-death predicate to distinguish live members from zombies. This matches the broker-side drain policy without changing invocation or child custody. An empty or unavailable census does not prove death: while the kernel still reports that group, cleanup remains pending and preserves the existing TERM/KILL escalation and deadline error. Zombies pin the group identifier while they await their reaper; retiring their group observation does not authorize signaling a reused identifier.

A short-lived fork during a census remains an accepted edge of the existing census-based policy. This patch does not alter detached command-group cleanup or the global-singleton grace budget.

**Refresh onto current main.** Head `9ef4c65c411` merges main `6a6007663b3` into the previously published `49b93b101d0` (normal merge commit, no rebase). Since the old base, main rewrote `terminateBrokerProcessGroup` around asynchronous kernel and census probes and added a census fallback that applies only when the host denies the group probe (#197510, #198132). It did not fix this case: with a working probe, a zombie-only group still reads as alive. The one conflict was resolved by keeping main's structure and porting the check onto it as `isBrokerProcessGroupExtinct`. The synchronous process-exit `force` path and the SIGKILL escalation are main's, unchanged. Against main the diff is still three files (+165/−2); the two test files carry the same added tests as before. On a host that denies group signals and still has live members, each 50 ms confirmation tick now reads the census twice; that is accepted for this rare path rather than widening the shared probe API.

## Evidence

- **Current-base regression, exact main `6a6007663b3`:** the real-process fixture from the new test launches a Node subreaper, a private group leader and a delayed-TERM child, with no mocked census or signals. With main's exact `cleanup.ts` it ends in `Spawn broker group cleanup could not be confirmed` after 7,031 ms. With this head it settles in 462 ms while the adopted child is an unreaped zombie, which is after the child's 300 ms exit delay and before the 5,000 ms TERM grace.
- **How that was run, and what is not yet proven:** on the 9.9 GiB development host every check ran inside a cgroup capped at 3 GiB RAM. The repository test runner's compiled-worker build exceeds that cap, so `cleanup.test.ts` and the other real-broker spawn-broker test files **did not run under Vitest on this head**. The red/green above executed the test's own driver script, extracted byte-for-byte from `cleanup.test.ts`, directly under Node. Exact-head hosted CI must run the spawn-broker suite itself.
- **Mocked contract tests on head `9ef4c65c411`:** `cleanup-group.test.ts` passes 18 of 18 in 1 file. With the empty-census and unreadable-census guards removed from the fix, exactly the two "retains and escalates a kernel-visible broker group" cases fail, so those cases do protect TERM/KILL escalation.
- **Exact-head static checks:** core production typecheck (`tsgo:core`), the `src` test typecheck (22 shards), core-scoped type-aware lint and format on the three changed files, and `git diff --check` pass. Ratchets against `6a60076` pass for max-lines, line-cap, assertion-safety, session-identity, timeout-race, mock-exports and test lines (net +132, within the 400-line allowance). The `database-dialect` ratchet exceeded the memory cap and the `database-worker` ratchet was not attempted; this change touches no database code, and hosted CI runs both. Frozen dependency installation passed without manifest or lockfile changes.
- **Earlier published head `49b93b101d0` (historical):** 45 tests passed across 6 spawn-broker files with 1 Node-only case skipped, on base `af300f44712`. Those results are not claimed for the current head.
- **Earlier isolated-runtime red/green:** with the same cleanup fix in an integration candidate, a real loopback Gateway launched under a synthetic non-reaping subreaper reproduced the failure before the fix: native-resource cleanup took about 7.2 seconds, exceeded the singleton grace, and ended in `stop_close_failed`. With the fix it logged clean shutdown in **445 ms** and exited 0. Four normal-shell control runs were already clean. Temporary processes, zombies, state and ports were removed.

The original operator run's ancestor reaper state was not captured. The matching error and timings support this diagnosis, but the exact live ancestry and post-failure linger are not independently proven. No new call, model connection, production deployment, or live-service change was performed. The full build, the Vitest spawn-broker suite and the two database ratchets were not run on the current head; PR CI remains required. No canonical autoreview has run on this head.

<!-- runtime-proof-20261031 -->
### Inspectable isolated-Gateway red/green proof

Baseline integration source: `3488f3f09731c1e1c0f83e9ce7ab7f080b0f70be`. Fixed integration source: the same base with the `cleanup.ts` production change subsequently committed as `18e0aa7b5f051d7115ae09f76d67b88f4a15141b`. This earlier runtime experiment predates both the previously published head `49b93b101d062edff8e1acb436140e80c1594433` (with its additional conservative empty/unavailable-census guards) and the current head `9ef4c65c41184f9991efc271ad6457eda5811209` (ported onto main's asynchronous cleanup); it is not relabeled as a runtime run on either head. No isolated-Gateway run exists for the current head.

Both runs launched the real source Gateway with isolated synthetic state, loopback listeners and a synthetic non-reaping child subreaper. No model, SIP or phone session was used. Here is selected original process-watch output for the baseline; numeric PIDs/PGIDs are consistently aliased. Columns within each entry are PID, PPID, process state and command. `Z` entries remain adopted by the synthetic supervisor while their broker groups await confirmation.

```text
t=1 BROKER_A GATEWAY_A Ssl  MainThread;HELPER_A BROKER_A Sl   esbuild;NATIVE_BROKER_A GATEWAY_A Ssl  MainThread;HELPER_B NATIVE_BROKER_A Sl   esbuild;ZOMBIE_A SUPERVISOR_A Z    esbuild;ZOMBIE_B SUPERVISOR_A Z    esbuild;ZOMBIE_C SUPERVISOR_A Z    esbuild;
t=5 ZOMBIE_A SUPERVISOR_A Z    esbuild;ZOMBIE_B SUPERVISOR_A Z    esbuild;ZOMBIE_C SUPERVISOR_A Z    esbuild;
t=11 ZOMBIE_A SUPERVISOR_A Z    esbuild;ZOMBIE_B SUPERVISOR_A Z    esbuild;ZOMBIE_C SUPERVISOR_A Z    esbuild;
t=12 
```

The same run's recorded zombie census associates `ZOMBIE_C` with `BROKER_A`'s PGID, and `ZOMBIE_A`/`ZOMBIE_B` with `NATIVE_BROKER_A`'s PGID (all three commands were `esbuild`). This is a projection of recorded process identities, not an inferred relationship from the PPID column above.

Baseline Gateway log excerpt (timestamps/messages preserved; PGID aliased):

```text
2026-10-31T12:37:50.590+00:00 [gateway] received SIGTERM; shutting down
2026-10-31T12:37:53.992+00:00 [shutdown] failed in 3315ms
2026-10-31T12:37:58.171+00:00 [gateway] shutdown step restart.close.global-singleton.openclaw.nativeWorkerLifetimes settled after 7183ms
2026-10-31T12:38:01.182+00:00 [gateway] shutdown step shutdown.spawn-broker settled after 7147ms
2026-10-31T12:38:01.184+00:00 [gateway] gateway-server-close: Plugin runtime still owns resources; inspect cleanup failures before retrying Gateway close. | global-singletons resources remain after grace; Spawn broker cleanup did not complete | Spawn broker group cleanup could not be confirmed for pgid=BROKER_A | ERR_SPAWN_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE | ERR_SPAWN_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE; resources remain
```

Fixed Gateway log excerpt:

```text
2026-10-31T12:45:55.103+00:00 [gateway] received SIGTERM; shutting down
2026-10-31T12:45:55.631+00:00 [shutdown] completed cleanly in 445ms
```

Recorded launcher wait status for the fixed process:

```json
{
  "status": 0,
  "elapsedS": 120.823
}
```

`status: 0` is the recorded OS wait status; `elapsedS` is total launched-process lifetime including cold startup, **not** shutdown duration. The Gateway log reports its measured 445 ms shutdown. Temporary processes, zombies and listeners were checked absent afterward. The original operator run's supervisor ancestry was not captured; this proof establishes the controlled topology, not that unseen ancestry.


### Refresh review

An independent parent review checked this exact committed range against main `6a6007663b3`, the merge resolutions, preserved upstream owners and terminal verification logs. The carrier feature and dependency patch was independently compared with the previous published range and remains unchanged. For the shutdown repair, the parent also reran the real-process fixture on `9ef4c65` under a task-owned memory cgroup: it settled in 460 ms while the adopted child was a zombie, with all four fixture checks passing. This is a focused refresh review, not a canonical autoreview, not full original-feature re-review, and not a current installed Gateway or conversation proof. The disclosed missing Vitest / resource-limited checks still require exact-head hosted CI.

prs.title: fix: complete replay-safe turns after deferred item conflict recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a turn failing with saved conversation `item_conflict` after partial model output even though no tool effects have occurred. A one-shot cron job can otherwise disable itself on that avoidable terminal error.

Related: #200020, #200165, #200190.

## User Impact

Replay-safe turns apply the saved repair and retry once inside the same active run. Turns with potential tool effects, delivery, interruption, or unproven replay safety still stop visibly. A second deferred conflict exhausts the one-retry budget. No configuration or SQLite schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transport intentionally defers after emitting output because it cannot establish execution safety. It already saves the repair used by the next request, but the runner previously received only a terminal error. The same recovery owner now publishes its typed outcome, and the existing attempt-recovery owner consumes whole-run execution safety plus the host delivery observer before using its existing retry path. Pending or committed host block delivery, and observation failure, prevent replay. Cron therefore receives the completed turn without adding a scheduler classifier or risking tool replay.

Production growth is 23 lines: a typed outcome, one run-scoped retry latch, and the guarded branch using the existing execution safety and host-delivery observers. No new cache, scheduler, timer, or recovery implementation.

## Evidence

The runner-boundary regression fails on main parent `2435c1faa791de766688ba27ca7a14a92e30b7e4`: safe deferred turns return `incomplete_turn`, and the exhaustion case never makes the expected second request. The negative control passes on the parent: an actual synthetic file-writing tool executes once before the conflict and is never retried.

Candidate proof passes 296 focused backend cases: ten cold-reopen/runner scenarios with real SQLite and plugin tool execution, 151 recovery siblings, 35 transport integrations, 83 terminal-resolution cases, 15 prefix-stability cases, and two whole-run safety cases. The ten-scenario runner file took 112.42 seconds on the final revision, after compilation; the actual host-block regression is red on the first PR head and green with the delivery observer gate. One Chromium transcript-extraction case and ten messaging E2E cases also pass. Provider events are synthetic; this is not an external live-provider latency claim.

`pnpm build` passes, including declarations, bundled plugins, and Control UI (2m 53s on the final revision). Codex autoreview is clean through P2. `pnpm check:changed` completed its formatting, lint, core and 29 test-graph typechecks, and remaining static guards. The retry lives in the existing attempt-recovery owner and the final line-cap check passes. The remaining dead-export gate reports exactly the same 108 findings on the candidate and exact parent `2435c1faa791de766688ba27ca7a14a92e30b7e4` (zero added/removed findings).

These are inherited main regressions, not waived new failures. Introduction attribution: 43 findings from `b90c5739fa5c` (#198943), 17 from `9bfad2b180b4` (#198933), 34 from `a0423637196f` (#198936), eight from `472cd0a2f542`, one from `18136c960eaf` (#198133), four from `b868ed4c21ba` (#198835), and one from `94e34f956969` (Talk thinking normalization). The exact-parent scan and per-symbol history are retained in the task proof.

The measured owner consumes retained execution facts without database or workspace I/O. Five interleaved A1/A2/B rounds used 5,000 synthetic sessions with 40-message histories and 8 KiB content, plus separate inspector allocation sampling. Existing synthetic storage-shape evidence from #200020 is reused; no production data was copied.

Related: #174805

## What Problem This Solves

Visual PR evidence is scattered across several guides, and small technical annotation labels make it harder to see what changed and why it matters.

## User Impact

Reviewers get visible clean and annotated before/after comparisons for affected web, macOS, iOS, and Android UI. Agents choose the targets, plain-language labels, and colors appropriate to each screenshot; users do not need to mark screenshots.

The existing annotation tool now renders rounded, filled cards with optional supporting detail and a delta pill. App Store, Google Play, release assets, and their screenshot pipelines remain unchanged. No application UI or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Make the existing PR media guide the shared workflow and link the platform guides, contributing guide, and PR template to it. Reuse the current capture and annotation tools rather than add another framework.

Show clean comparisons first and annotated copies second, without collapsing either. Stack wide images when side-by-side would be unreadable. The shared renderer handles the selected card shape and derives coordinated colors from an agent-chosen accent; it does not guess the screenshot theme. Measurements remain optional supporting information, not the whole explanation.

prs.title: fix(process): avoid blocking procfs census while waiting for exit
prs.body:
Related: #197510

## What Problem This Solves

Waiting for a command process group to exit can synchronously scan Linux procfs after a denied kernel probe, blocking the Gateway event loop.

## User Impact

That exit-waiting path now performs the bulk procfs reads asynchronously. Existing synchronous signal and identity checks, conservative permission handling, and process reaping remain unchanged. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the asynchronous census only for Linux exit observation. Keep existing effect-boundary checks and non-Linux behavior, and preserve terminal-leader/live-sibling handling through the shared status parser. This does not move all process discovery off-thread or claim that the complete filesystem-isolation project has landed.

Independent extraction from draft reference #197510, based on e741fd0d21ff7f9857a9c49f91d95166beaae83f. Original process work: Peter Steinberger, c37b0d7df5c59e6bd303e286112dadedcc7f5e37. Broader spawn, PTY, Codex, identity/admission and cleanup conversions remain separate slices. No dependency on the worker-lifecycle PR.

## Evidence

- New exit-waiting owner regression failed on unchanged base, then passed with the patch.
- 146 tests passed across nine files, including real command-scope cleanup, termination, custody, broker-group, reaping and liveness cases.
- Targeted typecheck, changed-file lint/format, git diff --check, and generated runtime-assets check passed. No generated manifest update was needed.
- Canonical autoreview (OpenClaw engine) reviewed the final local patch against e741fd0d21ff7f9857a9c49f91d95166beaae83f; that patch is unchanged in published 0bc4853763e02d22d9b5a193b2b6242fbd415353. Coverage: changed production and tests plus supplied owner context; reviewer did not independently execute tests. Outcome: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings; no production changes after review.
- Follow-up `a28577308f188c3a05788bf7d4bc1c082a3ca0e9` prunes exactly one obsolete mock-export baseline allowance. The owner ratchet passes against the pinned base (6,322 grandfathered factories); production and regression source remain unchanged.
- Broad PR CI is rerunning on that follow-up head. No live Gateway/model end-to-end or latency benchmark was run for this narrow slice.

prs.title: fix: prevent worker writes to trusted runtime storage
prs.body:
Stacked on #193823, targeting `codex/node-trusted-writable-ancestors`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes filesystem-isolated workers being able to overwrite trusted runtime files or replace peer scratch storage when writable paths overlap protected storage.

## User Impact

Unsafe workspace, model HOME, and scratch layouts are rejected before worker execution. Valid projects beneath broad read grants, including `/usr/src`, continue to run with confined workspace writes and existing descendant cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Landlock grants within one ruleset are additive: a read-only runtime grant cannot cancel an overlapping writable grant. The existing filesystem-launch owner now checks all writable roots against protected runtime paths and captured trust files, and prevents them from encompassing captured execution HOME or the shared temporary root.

The checks protect canonical targets and replaceable pathname entries along the resolution chain. This includes original bundle, HOME, and shared-temporary-root paths, relative targets, intermediate aliases, repeated/trailing separators, and ordinary directories before `..`. Precise executable/library roots and the selected native helper storage remain protected without treating the entire broad `/usr` or `/proc` read grant as private storage. Scratch rejection retains the existing cleanup owner. The fix stays in the existing filesystem-launch owner, with no new public API or test-only production hooks; the added traversal is needed because canonical-target checks alone miss proven pathname redirection. Relative to the parent, production code grows by 77 lines and tests by 267 lines.

## Evidence

- Secretless task-owned UTM guest: Ubuntu 24.04 arm64, Linux 6.8.0-147, Landlock ABI 4, non-root UID 1001.
- Native before/after proof: the original implementation allowed a confined worker to replace a disposable Node executable, followed by unconfined host re-execution. The candidate rejects that layout before execution. The original also allowed peer-scratch replacement through a `/tmp` workspace; the candidate rejects it while preserving the peer.
- Native controls demonstrated replacement of captured CA pathnames through aliases and ordinary directories before `..`, while their canonical targets remained intact. Separate bundle/HOME/temp alias proofs demonstrated later trusted resolution changing while canonical storage stayed intact; the temp case used the real selector. The candidate rejects these layouts. A valid `/usr/src` project still runs, writes inside its workspace, and receives `EACCES` outside it.
- All 81 relevant tests passed: 31 grant regressions, 3 real filesystem-owner cases, and retained proof for 18 startup and 29 idle cases. The new regression file ran through `pnpm test ... --maxWorkers=1` in 2.25 seconds wall time. Negative cases were demonstrated red on the applicable unfixed implementation, including native helper storage, system executable directories, and original-root aliases.
- Production and node-host test type graphs, focused repository oxlint (zero warnings/errors), focused oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed. Pinned-Bun lint parity was unavailable because the guest could not stage that artifact; the documented focused oxlint route passed.
- Fresh local autoreview covered the complete four-file snapshot against `1632274c7895819d4054fa2364bbb0ff0666defb`, including unchanged owner context, at P0–P3. Outcome: `scoped-clean`, complete, no remaining actionable findings. The reviewed tree was committed unchanged as `412ae587c5f4c9236c05e6339398c54fb1ef4714`. Earlier findings were reproduced and repaired before this final review. This is source review, not independent deployment certification.
- At `f9123897`, the [hosted architecture check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43499789637/job/132143303982) passed. The [production typecheck](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43499789637/job/132144681498) still fails on the parent’s two dependency pins. On Linux, 41 focused tests passed with a locally packed proc-safe launcher and fs-safe 0.28.0.

The 267-line allocation covers this change's focused security regressions and valid-layout controls. The test-line ratchet remains 259 lines over its ceiling, exactly matching inherited parent debt: the parent has 6,635,609 lines against a 6,635,350 ceiling; this candidate adds 267 lines and 267 allocation credit. This PR does not request additional credit for that existing debt.

[proc-safe #39](https://github.com/openclaw/proc-safe/pull/39) has merged. The original Linux proof used guest-only overrides for fs-safe 0.28.0 and openclaw/proc-safe#39 at `8c9a12144f1923059b90349172c35466394dfb66`, with its matching native helper. The parent still needs released dependency pins/lockfile updates and final installed-package/hosted validation. Those overrides and generated artifacts are excluded from this PR. The parent's deployment and crash-recovery qualification gates remain outstanding.

## What Problem This Solves

Large images in the chat workspace Files panel showed "This file not previewable inline" even though they are perfectly viewable in a browser. The previous 256 KiB cap was too restrictive for common screenshot and photo sizes.

## Changes

- `src/gateway/workspace-file-limits.ts`: add `WORKSPACE_IMAGE_PREVIEW_MAX_BYTES` (5 MiB)
- `src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-files.ts`: use the image cap for image files whose content has been verified locally as a browser-supported image
- `src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-files.preview-cap.test.ts`: new test file (8 tests, incl. 3 remote-parity tests)

## P2 content-verification (review remediation)

The 5 MiB cap previously trusted the file extension alone. `toSessionFileEntry` now sniffs the first 4100 bytes of image-extension files and applies the image cap only when the sniffed MIME type is a browser-supported image (avif/gif/jpeg/png/webp); anything else falls back to the 256 KiB text-preview path.

Follow-up commit (P2 remote-bypass fix): remote-bridge roots report prefix sniffing as `unsupported`. Extension alone is never trusted there: when content verification is unavailable, the generic 256 KiB cap is kept for all files, and the 5 MiB image cap applies only after local content has been verified as a browser-supported image. This matches main's behavior for remote workspaces and the remote-preview contract of #159895.

## Evidence

- `workspace-files.preview-cap.test.ts`: 8/8 tests pass, including 3 remote-parity tests asserting that `unsupported` prefix reads keep the 256 KiB cap for image- and non-image-extension files alike

prs.title: test(research): expect lifecycle-only changes to keep transcript jobs
prs.body:
Related: #200099

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `test/plugins/deep-research-routing.gateway.test.ts` fails on `main` ("expected true to be false" at the lifecycle-only read) because it still expects an edit or rewind to hide a conversation's research jobs.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. This is test-only. It aligns the Gateway routing test with #200099 and stops this failure from showing up on unrelated PRs.

## Why This Change Was Made

#200099 (edbc5bcea9b6) made deep-research job views follow the transcript instead of the lifecycle revision. It lists "Deep-research jobs disappear from the chat after an edit" among the bugs it fixes, and its commit says "Deep-research job views drop the revision compare; the job store stays per transcript". `view-state.ts` no longer compares `lifecycleRevision`, and `view-api.ts` hashes the view token from the session id alone. The test still asserted the old lifecycle fencing.

For a lifecycle-only change that keeps the same session id, the test now asserts that the transcript's jobs stay visible:

- The completed job's read, the job list and the view token are unchanged.
- The idempotent start replays the original job.
- Model-tool `result`/`status` still work, and a repeated model start returns its existing job.
- No extra provider dispatch happens.

The retired-job denial checks (empty list, stale-token start rejected, model-tool `result`/`status`/`resume`/`cancel` and view `resume`/`cancel` denied) now run after the reset that **changes** the session id, for every earlier job. Foreign-user, role-revocation and cross-session denials are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Red before the change: the file under CI's pinned Bun (`1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`) fails 1 / 3 passed at the line-839 assertion. Earlier triage reproduced this 3 of 3 on main `a0423637196f` and `964ab5223098`.
- Green after the change: 3 of 3 runs with the CI command below (4/4 tests each, 78–83 s), plus `pnpm test test/plugins/deep-research-routing.gateway.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (4/4).

  ```sh
  OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH=<ci bun> OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=3 CI=true \
    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-database-workers.config.ts \
    test/plugins/deep-research-routing.gateway.test.ts
  ```
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, `pnpm check:test-types`, `check:test-lines-ratchet` (net +22), `check:line-cap-ratchet` and `check:max-lines-ratchet` pass.
- Independent review: no P0–P2 findings.
- Note: current `main` (`9e66164c0ce4` and later) does not compile under the test runner. `src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-refresh-peers.ts` imports `resolveIdentityPathViaExistingAncestor` from `infra/boundary-path.js`, but #200203 moved it to `infra/path-existence.js`. The local runs above used a one-line uncommitted import shim for that. This PR does not change that file, so any CI failures from that break are inherited.
