prs.title: fix(gateway): select openai-completions owner from session key
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Generic `openclaw` / `openclaw/default` aliases forced a default agent before `x-openclaw-session-key` could name the owner. In an explicit multi-agent fleet with no default, a completion with `model: openclaw` and `x-openclaw-session-key: agent:scripts:foobar` still got `AgentSelectionRequiredError` from `resolveDefaultAgentId` after #137913.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveAgentIdForRequest` in `src/gateway/http-utils.ts` now resolves the owner in this order: agent header, agent-specific model, configured default for a generic model, then the agent-prefixed session key, then the required default. The generic alias asks `tryResolveDefaultAgentId` instead of throwing, so a fleet with no default falls through to the session key. The parsed agent goes through `parseAgentSessionKey` plus `assertKnownAgentId`, so the session-key grammar stays in one place and an unknown agent is still rejected. `x-openclaw-agent-id` still wins. Two agents with no session key and no agent header still return `AgentSelectionRequiredError`.

The Chat Completions and Responses references only described `x-openclaw-session-key` as session routing, so `docs/gateway/openai-http-api.md` now lists the selector precedence and the case where an agent-scoped key supplies the owner, and `docs/gateway/openresponses-http-api.md` points at it. `pnpm format:docs:check`, `docs:check-mdx` and `codespell` on the two pages are clean.

## User Impact

Operators running an explicit multi-agent fleet without a default agent can send `model: "openclaw"` plus the agent's own session key to the Chat Completions, Responses and embeddings endpoints and reach that agent, instead of a `400`. Fleets with a default agent behave as before.

## Evidence

Current head `d1c134a6926febaf6cec329cb4e37a5233d9762d`. Selector behavior is unchanged from `ebf037423f4c37db14f74ab2a024e43a2a04c3ac` (`src/gateway/http-utils.ts` blob `36a7f65dd24bad89b0fea397d32a5258d2b0839c`). `d1c134a6926` adds the embeddings operator-role ceiling. The Gateway command is `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway run --bind loopback --force`. The provider is `scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs` on loopback. The client is `curl`. State dirs are throwaway. The September chat-only before/after trace (main returned 400, an earlier head returned 200) predates conflict rejection and did not cover Responses, embeddings, or an upgrade. The Chat Completions, conflict, Responses, and embeddings traces below were captured on `0d69691`; the selector file is the same blob, so they still describe this head. The v2026.10.2 upgrade trace is from `ebf03742`, with the older-binary guard left enabled. The operator-role traces are from this head's parent process on `ebf03742` for chat, and from a restart on `d1c134a6926` for the embeddings ceiling.

### Chat Completions, session key owns the agent

Two agents, `agents.ownership: "explicit"`, no default. Alpha's model is `openai/alpha-model`, beta's is `openai/beta-model`. Token auth. Chat Completions and Responses enabled.

```text
POST /v1/chat/completions
Authorization: Bearer trace-token-138329
x-openclaw-session-key: agent:beta:trace-owner
{"model":"openclaw","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with OPENCLAW_E2E_TRACE_OK"}]}

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 300

{"id":"chatcmpl_fc460813-5110-413d-b14b-d76119356a89","object":"chat.completion","created":1791826561,"model":"openclaw","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"OPENCLAW_E2E_TRACE_OK"},"finish_reason":"stop"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":0,"completion_tokens":0,"total_tokens":0}}
```

The mock request for that turn is `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `model=beta-model`. The user text contains `Runtime: agent=beta | session=agent:beta:trace-owner`. The gateway session write is `agentId=beta`. A later activity-recap call uses `gpt-5.6-luna` and is not the agent turn.

### Contradictory selectors

Same gateway. `model: "openclaw/alpha"` with `x-openclaw-session-key: agent:beta:trace-conflict-model`:

```text
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 140

{"error":{"message":"Selected agent 'alpha' does not match the agent in `x-openclaw-session-key` ('beta').","type":"invalid_request_error"}}
```

`x-openclaw-agent-id: alpha` with `x-openclaw-session-key: agent:beta:trace-conflict-header` and `model: "openclaw"` returns the same 400 and message. Neither request reached the mock.

### Responses and embeddings

`POST /v1/responses`, `model: "openclaw"`, `stream: false`, `x-openclaw-session-key: agent:beta:trace-responses`, input `Reply with OPENCLAW_E2E_RESPONSES_OK`:

```text
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"id":"resp_3794a6d6-1d4a-434b-9446-a1df6fad114c","object":"response","created_at":1791826585,"status":"completed","model":"openclaw","output":[{"type":"message","id":"msg_10c65ddb-c929-4464-868a-d12c32b6576e","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"OPENCLAW_E2E_RESPONSES_OK"}],"phase":"final_answer","status":"completed"}]}
```

The mock agent turn is `model=beta-model` and `Runtime: agent=beta | session=agent:beta:trace-responses`.

`POST /v1/embeddings`, `model: "openclaw"`, `input: "OPENCLAW_E2E_EMBED_OK"`, `x-openclaw-session-key: agent:beta:trace-embed`. Beta's memory-search model is `beta-embed`; alpha's is `alpha-embed`.

```text
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Length: 145

{"object":"list","data":[{"object":"embedding","index":0,"embedding":[1,0,0,0]}],"model":"openclaw","usage":{"prompt_tokens":0,"total_tokens":0}}
```

The mock embeddings request for that call is `model=beta-embed` with input `OPENCLAW_E2E_EMBED_OK`.

### Operator role, grant, and revocation

Trusted-proxy identity, not the shared-secret owner token. `gateway.auth.mode` is `trusted-proxy` (`x-forwarded-user`, required `x-forwarded-proto`, loopback allowed). Roles are the real `gateway.roles.definitions` entries. `beta-operator` has `agents: ["beta"]`, `scopes: ["operator.write"]`, `sessions.others: "none"`. `alpha-only` has `agents: ["alpha"]` and the same scope ceiling. Each caller is a user profile assigned that role. The fleet is still explicit alpha/beta with no default. `model` is `openclaw`. The session header is `x-openclaw-session-key: agent:beta:...`. The provider is the same loopback mock. Forwarded client addresses, provider keys, host, repo path, OS, and node lines are omitted.

#### Allowed restricted operator

`beta-operator@example.test`, `POST /v1/chat/completions`, session `agent:beta:trace-allowed`, content `Reply with OPENCLAW_E2E_ALLOWED_OK`.

```text
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"id":"chatcmpl_a5fdbf55-ada1-42f2-934a-be8539dd987e","object":"chat.completion","created":1791899130,"model":"openclaw","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"OPENCLAW_E2E_ALLOWED_OK"},"finish_reason":"stop"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":0,"completion_tokens":0,"total_tokens":0}}
```

The mock went from 0 requests to 1: `POST /v1/chat/completions`, `model=beta-model`. The provider user text includes `Runtime: agent=beta | session=agent:beta:trace-allowed | model=openai/beta-model | default_model=openai/beta-model | channel=webchat`. It does not contain `alpha-model`.

#### Role forbidden from beta

`alpha-only@example.test`, same endpoint, session `agent:beta:trace-forbidden`, content `Reply with OPENCLAW_E2E_FORBIDDEN_OK`.

```text
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":{"message":"Your operator role cannot create sessions for agent \"beta\"; choose an allowed agent or ask a gateway administrator to update your role.","type":"forbidden"}}
```

The mock stayed at 1. No new provider request.

#### Revoked grant before further provider I/O

After that allowed turn, `gateway.roles.definitions.beta-operator.agents` changed from `["beta"]` to `[]`. The running gateway logged:

```text
2026-10-13T13:47:17.020+00:00 [reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (gateway.roles.definitions.beta-operator.agents)
2026-10-13T13:47:17.111+00:00 [reload] config hot reload applied (gateway.roles.definitions.beta-operator.agents)
```

Same profile, same session `agent:beta:trace-allowed`, content `Reply with OPENCLAW_E2E_REVOKED_OK`:

```text
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":{"message":"Your operator role cannot create sessions for agent \"beta\"; choose an allowed agent or ask a gateway administrator to update your role.","type":"forbidden"}}
```

The mock stayed at 1.

#### Embeddings ceiling

Chat and Responses already call `authorizeGatewaySessionCreation` after the shared selector. Embeddings did not, so a session-key owner reached the embedding provider when the role disallowed that agent.

Before `d1c134a6926`, `alpha-only@example.test`, `POST /v1/embeddings`, model `openclaw`, session `agent:beta:trace-embed-forbidden`, input `OPENCLAW_E2E_EMBED_FORBIDDEN`:

```text
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"object":"list","data":[{"object":"embedding","index":0,"embedding":[1,0,0,0]}],"model":"openclaw","usage":{"prompt_tokens":1,"total_tokens":1}}
```

The mock logged `POST /v1/embeddings` with `model=beta-embed`.

`d1c134a6926` applies the same ceiling before embedding provider I/O. The gateway was restarted on that commit, and `beta-operator.agents` was restored to `["beta"]`.

`alpha-only@example.test`, session `agent:beta:trace-embed-forbidden-fixed`, input `OPENCLAW_E2E_EMBED_FORBIDDEN_FIXED`:

```text
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":{"message":"Your operator role cannot create sessions for agent \"beta\"; choose an allowed agent or ask a gateway administrator to update your role.","type":"forbidden"}}
```

The mock request count did not change.

`beta-operator@example.test`, session `agent:beta:trace-embed-allowed-fixed`, input `OPENCLAW_E2E_EMBED_ALLOWED_FIXED`:

```text
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"object":"list","data":[{"object":"embedding","index":0,"embedding":[1,0,0,0]}],"model":"openclaw","usage":{"prompt_tokens":1,"total_tokens":1}}
```

The new mock line is `POST /v1/embeddings`, `model=beta-embed`. `pnpm test -- src/gateway/embeddings-http.role-ceiling.test.ts` passed in the gateway-server Vitest project (1 test).

### Base vs head regression tests

`pnpm test -- src/gateway/http-utils.request-context.test.ts -t "agent-prefixed session key|session key owner|explicit owner when a multi-agent"`

Head `d1c134a6926`: 6 passed. Those cases are the session-key owner in an explicit fleet, the session key beating a default agent, header conflict, model conflict, an agreeing selector, and an ownerless fleet still requiring an owner.

Merge-base `5d5407ae973addb2174301fb17808382ef0a97a1`: the same tests ran against that commit's `resolveAgentIdForRequest`. The new conflict-error export was stubbed so this tree's module graph could load. The resolver body is the merge-base function and does not read the session key. 4 failed, 2 passed:

- infers the owner from an agent-prefixed session key: `AgentSelectionRequiredError` (explicit fleet, no default)
- keeps the session key owner over a default agent: expected `main` to be `scripts`
- rejects an agent header that conflicts with the session key: did not throw
- rejects an agent-specific model that conflicts with the session key: did not throw
- agreeing selector: passed (the header already wins)
- ownerless fleet still requires an owner: passed

### Upgrade from published v2026.9.9

`openclaw@2026.9.9` (`bcfc888`) from npm. `openclaw setup --non-interactive` wrote the state dir with agent `main` (`meta.lastTouchedVersion` `2026.9.9`, no `agents.ownership`). That CLI enabled chat completions. The mock provider (`openai/main-model` on loopback, `allowPrivateNetwork`) was then in the config, and `openclaw config validate` on 2026.9.9 accepted it. No `x-openclaw-session-key`.

```text
POST /v1/chat/completions
{"model":"openclaw","user":"upgrade-thread","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with OPENCLAW_E2E_TURN1"}]}

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"id":"chatcmpl_248c0bc0-ad1f-4241-b122-5ac51681a16e","object":"chat.completion","created":1791826663,"model":"openclaw","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"OPENCLAW_E2E_TURN1"},"finish_reason":"stop"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":0,"completion_tokens":0,"total_tokens":0}}
```

Mock: `model=main-model`, `Runtime: agent=main | session=agent:main:openai-user:upgrade-thread`.

Stopped that Gateway and started this head on the same state dir and config. Same shape, `user: "upgrade-thread"`, content `Reply with OPENCLAW_E2E_TURN2`, still no session-key header:

```text
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"id":"chatcmpl_f1cae9c8-ad63-4e36-8fd1-4c676b35245c","object":"chat.completion","created":1791826814,"model":"openclaw","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"OPENCLAW_E2E_TURN2"},"finish_reason":"stop"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":0,"completion_tokens":0,"total_tokens":0}}
```

Mock: `model=main-model`, same session `agent:main:openai-user:upgrade-thread`. The provider transcript is the turn-1 user text, assistant `OPENCLAW_E2E_TURN1`, then the turn-2 user text. `lastTouchedVersion` stayed `2026.9.9`.

### Upgrade from published v2026.10.2

`openclaw@2026.10.2` (`b8952d4`) from npm. `openclaw setup --non-interactive --accept-risk --auth-choice skip --no-install-daemon` wrote an isolated state dir with default agent `main` (`meta.lastTouchedVersion` `2026.10.2`, no `agents.ownership`). Chat completions were then enabled. The mock provider is this tree's `scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs` on loopback (`openai/main-model`, `api: openai-completions`, `allowPrivateNetwork`, context window 200000). `openclaw config validate` on 2026.10.2 accepted it. Token auth. No `x-openclaw-session-key`. `OPENCLAW_ALLOW_OLDER_BINARY_DESTRUCTIVE_ACTIONS` was unset for every command.

Non-default agent settings on that state, read back with `openclaw config get` before either Gateway start: `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` `low`, `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds` `900`, `agents.entries.main.identity.name` `Upgrade Trace`, `agents.entries.main.identity.theme` `harbor`, `agents.defaults.model.primary` `openai/main-model`.

2026.10.2 Gateway startup:

```text
[gateway] agent model: openai/main-model (thinking=low, fast=off)
[gateway] ready
```

```text
POST /v1/chat/completions
Authorization: Bearer <trace-token>
{"model":"openclaw","stream":false,"user":"upgrade-thread","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with OPENCLAW_E2E_TURN1"}]}

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 297

{"id":"chatcmpl_67a7f6db-57fd-45f5-a17e-0cd746ad1081","object":"chat.completion","created":1791840659,"model":"openclaw","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"OPENCLAW_E2E_TURN1"},"finish_reason":"stop"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":0,"completion_tokens":0,"total_tokens":0}}
```

Mock agent turn: `POST /v1/chat/completions`, `model=main-model`. The user text contains `Reply with OPENCLAW_E2E_TURN1` and `Runtime: name=Upgrade Trace | agent=main | session=agent:main:openai-user:upgrade-thread | model=openai/main-model | default_model=openai/main-model` (host, repo path, and OS fields omitted). A later activity-recap call uses `gpt-5.6-luna` and is not the agent turn.

Stopped that Gateway. This head is package `2026.10.2` (`ebf0374`), the same version as `lastTouchedVersion`, so the older-binary guard does not treat it as a downgrade. A plain `gateway run` on the same state dir, with the guard left enabled, did not print the older-binary refusal. It stopped before listening because the published release's agent database is schema 24 and this tree expects schema 26:

```text
OpenClaw agent database uses schema version 24; stop active agents and run openclaw doctor --fix to migrate session identities before using it.
Sessions remain unavailable. Stop the Gateway, run "openclaw doctor --fix" to inspect and repair this agent database, and restart.
```

That is current main's schema gate, not the version guard. `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes` from this head, still with the override unset, migrated the agent database to schema 26 and finished with `Doctor complete`. It also disabled skills that are not installed in this environment. The authored agent settings above were unchanged, and `lastTouchedVersion` stayed `2026.10.2`.

prs.title: fix(ui): preserve saved themes during native startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes saved themes reverting to defaults during native startup or reconnect when a remembered browser connection is retargeted to another Gateway or appearance invalidation overlaps runtime-config admission.

## User Impact

Saved appearance is preserved for the selected Gateway and restored from the authenticated profile after connection. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native retargeting now loads the destination Gateway’s appearance instead of carrying the previous connection’s settings, while preserving the resolved credentials. Appearance refresh reuse also includes the preference generation, so an invalidated refresh cannot suppress the replacement load.

## Evidence

Candidate: `6dc58a06e7d805e7c0f35085da1ec48083444053` (test-only follow-up; production modules unchanged from `57ab0e2a58ae`). Executed locally on macOS with Chromium and isolated state; the live operator Gateway was untouched.

### Real Gateway generation-overlap behavior

The expanded `ui/src/e2e/theme-startup.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` connects the production browser Gateway store, runtime-config owner, shell preference owner and theme renderer to a real Gateway over WebSocket. A genuine `users.prefs.set` produces the server invalidation; the first genuine `users.prefs.get` response is held at client promise admission, config admission advances the generation, then the response is released. No preference or catalog payload is fabricated. The regression asserts selected Knot and rendered `data-theme=openknot`.

Before/after control executed with the same real server: reverting only the served module's generation-cache comparison left `theme=claw`; the fixed module produced `theme=knot`. Both observed one held real preference response. This one-off reverted-source control is retained in execution receipts, not as a source-text-coupled test in the PR.

Boundary: timing is deliberately controlled at production owner entry points in a browser test document, not an uncontrolled reproduction through the mounted application shell. Existing mounted-app cases exercise startup, reload, native retargeting and profile hydration. The isolated browser grants localhost-network permission; initial ungranted-harness connection failures were not counted as product regressions.

### Executable upgrade and existing data

This is actual released executable → candidate executable replacement, not a hand-written v1 record replay:

1. Installed the official npm `openclaw@2026.11.4` distribution with lifecycle scripts disabled. Version receipt: `2026.11.4 (d843d6a)`.
2. Booted its Gateway with a new temporary HOME/state/config/workspace and free loopback port, synthetic token auth, external channels/providers disabled. In its served UI, selected Knot + Dark. The release wrote browser settings/profile mirrors and SQLite `user_preferences` rows for `gateway-owner`: `ui.theme="knot"`, `ui.themeMode="dark"`, `ui.accent="theme"`.
3. Shut down the release cleanly. Started the candidate's built `openclaw.mjs gateway` with the same config, SQLite state, workspace and port, without deleting/converting/reseeding saved records. Loaded the candidate-served UI with the release's captured browser storage: selected/rendered Knot/Dark survived.
4. Exercised post-upgrade writes through the candidate UI: selected Tide/Light, reloaded, asserted `data-theme=tide-light`, and observed SQLite storing `ui.theme="tide"`, `ui.themeMode="light"`.
5. Restored Knot/Dark through the UI, then opened a new browser context without any stored settings/mirror. It restored `openknot` from the upgraded server; SQLite still held the expected keys/values. A retained browser mirror is not the only successful path.

```json
{"releasedSave":"openknot","upgradeOldBrowser":"openknot","upgradeWriteReload":"tide-light","upgradeCleanBrowser":"openknot"}
```

The candidate branch's version metadata still says `2026.11.3`; its served UI identified source `57ab0e2a58ae`. Version fields were not changed to manufacture a semver upgrade. This proves released-data compatibility with this exact candidate production code, not an OS installer/updater workflow or every historical release/schema.

### Fresh-state executable startup

Separately booted the candidate executable with another new HOME/state/workspace and only a minimal synthetic Gateway config; no release data or browser storage was copied. First boot created database/profile state. Browser UI saved Knot/Dark; a second clean browser context restored `openknot`. Both task-owned Gateways were shut down cleanly.

### Validation

- Expanded real-Gateway/Chromium regression: 1 file / 1 test passed, 29.73 s total. Separate before/after controlled comparison run passed, 26.33 s total.
- E2E test typecheck (`test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-e2e.json`), targeted lint/format and `git diff --check`: passing. Final lint fixes only rename callback bindings; no behavior changed.
- Prior owner/bootstrap proof: 54 tests and UI-app typecheck passed; production code is unchanged by this follow-up.
- Fresh independent test review: no actionable defects.
- Hosted CI and new ClawSweeper review are not yet complete. Prior oversized production-file lint limitation remains; no claim that all repository lanes are green.

### Executable proof screenshots

Release and candidate layouts differ; these show the persisted selection, not a proposed visual redesign.

**Released 2026.11.4: save Knot/Dark**

![Released executable saves Knot/Dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6701506c-b80e-4a6f-8203-42c9faaa4b79)

**Candidate executable using release state and browser storage: Knot/Dark survives**

![Candidate executable retains released data](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a12f134-ba32-4dd5-bdf8-d80c232bcca3)

**Fresh candidate state: second clean browser restores saved Knot/Dark**

![Fresh candidate save and clean-browser restore](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3bc9ad9b-eeae-433b-bcfc-401b05681211)

### Native startup screenshots

Same isolated Gateway scenario, before server preference hydration. These demonstrate native retargeting, not proof of the cause of the originally reported reload.

**Before:** saved Knot/dark is replaced by Claw/system.

![Before: native startup incorrectly selects Claw and System](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac1878fd-f587-439a-bbc6-60cf6717ba4c)

**After:** the destination Gateway’s Knot/dark selection is preserved.

![After: native startup preserves Knot and Dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4c40fed8-092a-4fcb-9abc-0f4bbcdd88df)

prs.title: feat(voice-call): elevate one realtime call's consult tools with a keypad PIN
prs.body:
Related: #193571

## What Problem This Solves

Realtime phone calls run every consult at one fixed `realtime.toolPolicy`. Operators who keep it at `safe-read-only` (the safe default) cannot do owner-level work from a phone call, and raising the policy globally gives every admitted caller owner tools on every call.

## User Impact

User impact: an operator can turn on `realtime.elevation`, and a trusted inbound caller can press `*`, a PIN, and `#` to give that one call the elevated consult policy (default `owner`) until hangup. Everything else keeps the configured `toolPolicy`. Elevation is off by default, so nothing changes for existing configs.

Risks and limits, kept visible:

- Twilio only. Digits come from Twilio Media Streams `dtmf` messages. Config validation rejects other providers while elevation is on.
- Only inbound calls from numbers in `allowFrom` can elevate, and elevation requires `inboundPolicy: "allowlist"` or `"pairing"`. Caller ID can be spoofed (see #193571 for STIR/SHAKEN attestation), so the PIN is the credential; the allowlist only narrows who may try.
- Wrong PINs count per caller across calls within `lockoutMs`, so hanging up and redialing does not reset the budget. After `maxAttempts` the caller is locked out for `lockoutMs`. Failure counts and lockouts are in memory; a Gateway restart clears them.
- Elevation ends when the call's media stream ends. A stream reconnect within the same call drops back to `toolPolicy`; the caller re-enters the PIN.
- A consult that is already running keeps the policy it started with.

## Why This Change Was Made

The realtime handler already owns each call's telephony binding, so it now also owns that call's keypad state and passes the call's current consult policy to the consult tool handler, which uses it for `toolsAllow`. A new `DtmfElevationGate` collects digits after the prefix, submits on `#`, after 3 seconds without a key, or at 12 digits (not at the configured PIN length, so the length stays private), and compares with `safeEqualSecret`. On success the realtime model gets a short notice so it can tell the caller; on a wrong PIN it gets a "not accepted" notice; failures are counted per hashed caller number across calls (a window of `lockoutMs`), so redialing cannot reset the attempt budget. After `maxAttempts` the call is hung up and the caller is locked out for `lockoutMs`. During a lockout any entry hangs up the call without checking the PIN, so retries reveal nothing. A correct PIN clears that caller's failure count.

Digits never reach the realtime model, the transcript, or logs. Logs record only the outcome, attempt count, and the hashed caller number on lockout. Caller audio is withheld from the model between the prefix key and submission, in case the carrier leaves tones in the media.

The PIN is a secret input (`realtime.elevation.pin`, registered in `configContracts.secretInputs` and marked sensitive), resolved the same way as `twilio.authToken`. It must resolve to 4 to 12 digits; the startup error never echoes the value.

Config surface: this raises the plugin config budget in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` from 5080 to 5087 (the `realtime.elevation` object and its six fields). The feature is opt-in and needs an operator-set PIN, so it cannot ride on an existing field.

To stay within the line-cap ratchet for `realtime-handler.ts`, the existing caller-transcript buffer helpers and `withFallbackConsultQuestion` moved unchanged into `realtime-transcript-text.ts`.

<details>
<summary>Config</summary>

```json5
realtime: {
  enabled: true,
  toolPolicy: "safe-read-only",
  elevation: {
    enabled: true,
    pin: { source: "env", provider: "default", id: "VOICE_CALL_ELEVATION_PIN" },
    prefix: "*",               // one key: 0-9 or *
    elevatedToolPolicy: "owner", // or "safe-read-only"
    maxAttempts: 3,              // 1-10
    lockoutMs: 3600000,
  },
}
```

</details>

## Evidence

Focused tests, all passing locally:

- `realtime-dtmf-elevation.test.ts`: eligibility (inbound + allowlisted only), prefix gating, `#` submit, `*` restart, inter-digit timeout, 12-digit submit, wrong PIN, failures counted across calls (redial does not reset), failure window expiry, success clears failures, lockout across calls and expiry, close drops pending entry.
- `realtime-handler.dtmf-elevation.test.ts` (real WebSocket path): consult before the PIN gets `safe-read-only`, after the PIN gets `owner`; caller audio is withheld while entering the PIN; the PIN never appears in manager events, model notices, or console output; a stream close drops elevation; `maxAttempts` wrong PINs hang up the call, and during the lockout the correct PIN on the next call hangs up without a notice.
- `runtime.test.ts`: a consult with call policy `safe-read-only` runs with the read-only `toolsAllow` list, and with `owner` runs with `toolsAllow` undefined (normal agent tool policy).
- `config.test.ts`: defaults, runtime and manifest schema agreement, validation errors, PIN resolution.
- `stream-frame-adapter.test.ts`: Twilio `dtmf` frame parsing; Telnyx frames stay ignored.

Also updated: two `realtime-handler.test.ts` assertions now expect the consult context to carry `toolPolicy: "safe-read-only"`.

Results:

- `pnpm test:extension voice-call`: 52 files, 633 tests passed; database-workers lane 15 files, 182 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `pnpm lint:extensions`: clean.
- `pnpm check:changed`: every lane green except the dead-export scan, which reports only pre-existing entries outside this change (for example `extensions/google/provider-catalog-runtime.ts`, `src/config/sessions/session-history-types.ts`).
- `pnpm config:docs:check`: OK after `pnpm config:docs:gen`.

- `runtime.test.ts` (added in 6f93e38): an elevated consult runs in the session `<caller session key>:elevated:<callId>`; consults before the PIN and on later calls keep the caller's normal session.

### Live Twilio proof (2026-11-16)

Host: OpenClaw 2026.11.4 with this change backported onto `v2026.11.4` and installed as a local `npm-pack` build of `@openclaw/voice-call`. The feature code is the same as this branch; only the base differs. Inbound Twilio calls from one allowlisted number, OpenAI realtime, `toolPolicy: "safe-read-only"`, `elevatedToolPolicy: "owner"`, PIN as a store SecretRef. Log excerpt below: phone numbers, Twilio call SIDs and IPs removed. The PIN never appears in any log line.

```text
[voice-call] Realtime bridge starting for call f10f0c16-2485-49b5-9042-5b713ceaa20e (providerCallId=CA…)
[voice-call/lifecycle] [voice-call] Call finalized callId=f10f0c16-2485-49b5-9042-5b713ceaa20e providerCallId=CA… endReason=completed
[voice-call] Realtime bridge starting for call bf202c8f-c457-4961-a079-85f163d755ef (providerCallId=CA…)
[voice-call] realtime tool call completed callId=bf202c8f-c457-4961-a079-85f163d755ef tool=openclaw_agent_consult status=ok elapsedMs=8502
[voice-call] Realtime keypad elevation granted callId=bf202c8f-c457-4961-a079-85f163d755ef toolPolicy=owner
[voice-call] realtime tool call completed callId=bf202c8f-c457-4961-a079-85f163d755ef tool=openclaw_agent_consult status=ok elapsedMs=14499
[voice-call] realtime tool call completed callId=bf202c8f-c457-4961-a079-85f163d755ef tool=openclaw_agent_consult status=ok elapsedMs=7539
[voice-call/lifecycle] [voice-call] Call finalized callId=bf202c8f-c457-4961-a079-85f163d755ef providerCallId=CA… endReason=completed

[voice-call] Realtime bridge starting for call 7992d6c1-fc6f-47ef-ae3f-532925588bbd (providerCallId=CA…)
[voice-call] realtime tool call completed callId=7992d6c1-fc6f-47ef-ae3f-532925588bbd tool=openclaw_agent_consult status=ok elapsedMs=20580
[voice-call] Realtime keypad elevation granted callId=7992d6c1-fc6f-47ef-ae3f-532925588bbd toolPolicy=owner
[voice-call] realtime tool call completed callId=7992d6c1-fc6f-47ef-ae3f-532925588bbd tool=openclaw_agent_consult status=ok elapsedMs=13218
[voice-call/lifecycle] [voice-call] Call finalized callId=7992d6c1-fc6f-47ef-ae3f-532925588bbd providerCallId=CA… endReason=completed
[voice-call] Realtime bridge starting for call 4fd2dbc6-8a0f-42a3-8fe3-adf072776006 (providerCallId=CA…)

[voice-call/lifecycle] [voice-call] Call finalized callId=4fd2dbc6-8a0f-42a3-8fe3-adf072776006 providerCallId=CA… endReason=completed
[voice-call] Realtime bridge starting for call f10831ae-5c3a-477b-a906-6acf51b693bc (providerCallId=CA…)
[voice-call] Realtime keypad elevation rejected callId=f10831ae-5c3a-477b-a906-6acf51b693bc attempt=1/3
[voice-call/lifecycle] [voice-call] Call finalized callId=f10831ae-5c3a-477b-a906-6acf51b693bc providerCallId=CA… endReason=completed
```

What the calls show:

- **Read-only before the PIN.** `bf202c8f` and `7992d6c1`: the first consult asked for current alerts; the agent had only the read-only tool list, couldn't reach Grafana, and said so.
- **Elevation.** After `*<PIN>#`: `Realtime keypad elevation granted … toolPolicy=owner`. The next consult in each call used Grafana MCP tools and reported the firing alerts.
- **Reset on hangup.** `52e9a519` (call-back after `bf202c8f`): the consult ran with the read-only tool list again, and the owner tools (Grafana MCP) were not in its catalog.
- **Wrong PIN.** `f10831ae`: `Realtime keypad elevation rejected … attempt=1/3`, and the model received the "not accepted" notice. I stopped after one attempt to avoid locking out the test number; the 3-attempt hang-up and lockout are covered by `realtime-handler.dtmf-elevation.test.ts`.

**Found live and fixed in 6f93e38.** With the default `sessionScope: "per-phone"`, the call-back in `52e9a519` couldn't run owner tools, but its consult answered from results the elevated call had left in the caller's shared session. Elevated consults now run in a session scoped to the call (`…:elevated:<callId>`), so owner-tool results never land in the shared session. Re-checked live: `7992d6c1` elevated and fetched alerts into `…:elevated:7992d6c1…`; on the call-back `4fd2dbc6`, the agent had no record of them. The docs now cover this, plus `sessionScope: "per-call"` for no carry-over at all.

### Upgrade and compatibility

- Upgrading this host from 2026.10.7 to 2026.11.4 kept the existing voice-call config (Twilio store SecretRef auth token, realtime provider settings, allowlist, tool policy). `realtime.elevation` defaults to `enabled: false`, so existing configs load and behave as before.
- Operator note: when a newly installed plugin version adds a secret input path (here `realtime.elevation.pin`), the Gateway reads the secret-input registry only at startup. Until a Gateway restart, voice-call fails to start with `unresolved SecretRef`; `secrets reload` and a plugin reload are not enough. This is core behavior, not something this PR introduces.

prs.title: fix(ci): recover stalled release ancestry hydration
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes extended-stable npm qualification stopping before lint when preloaded main history leaves Git's shallow ancestry frontier unchanged.

## User Impact

Release operators can finish ancestry acquisition without weakening the release relationship check. There is no runtime behavior or configuration change. Publication remains a separate gated operation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The exact 2026.10.33 checkout reproduces exit 125 after the npm workflow's full-main preload; the same checkout without that preload passes. Repeated deepening can leave the same shallow cut. On that observed no-progress path only, request the remaining history once with `--unshallow`, using the existing fetch retry and total-time budgets, then recheck the original source and pinned target commits. Invalid relationships still fail, and a still-incomplete graph retains exit 125.

Related release evidence: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43928976244/job/133516221365

## Evidence

- New real-policy regression fails on the unchanged owner with the observed exit 125, then passes with the fix. Its proxy reproduces the stalled fetch; recovery and relationship checks use real Git.
- All 116 Git-owner consumer tests pass, including invalid ancestry, no-progress refusal, target pinning, timeout, and cleanup contracts.
- Tooling test typecheck, focused lint, formatting, Python syntax, and diff checks pass.
- Manual real-graph diagnosis at candidate `dde6f2cc856a28f3d9dfb9ab08a86830a29e00bc`: deeper fetch still failed to establish a base; explicit unshallow established `459cad76530457e5c0a32bc21d4982920e9991e7`.
- Full repaired-owner entrypoint replay passed on a fresh shallow checkout at exact candidate `dde6f2cc856a28f3d9dfb9ab08a86830a29e00bc` with the workflow’s full-main preload. It established the relationship against pinned main `775be7a709fafd9dd8e596cbdf2a1e7e89d5428b`, recovered merge base `459cad76530457e5c0a32bc21d4982920e9991e7`, and completed with a nonshallow repository (exit 0).
- Self-review/pr-simplify: existing owner and budgets retained; 11 production lines, one recovery regression, and the existing refusal fixture updated. No new framework, state, option, or ancestry exception.
- Local independent model review was not spawned under the release owner's explicit no-other-sessions/no-delegation instruction. Native review and hosted checks remain required; self-review is not represented as independent review.

Full stable qualification is not yet successful; this repairs its observed acquisition failure, not the release gate itself.

prs.title: fix(agents): move uncached guarded workspace reads off-thread
prs.body:
Related: #197510

## What Problem This Solves

Explicit uncached workspace reads used by bootstrap seeding and custom-purpose publication perform guarded filesystem work on their caller thread.

## User Impact

Moves those uncached reads to the existing filesystem worker while retaining content limits, pinned source identity, alias refusal, retry behavior, and errors. Default cached bootstrap reads and remote workspace reads retain their existing behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a narrow independent extraction from draft reference #197510, based on e741fd0d21ff7f9857a9c49f91d95166beaae83f. The local reader remains one implementation shared by cached host reads and uncached worker reads. The existing fs-safe-copy worker entrypoint handles the new read command under the captured native mode and a native section.

Original implementation credit: Peter Steinberger. Deliberately excluded: cache removal, default prompt-read migration, workspace mutations/provisioning, and SQLite admission changes. Those remain separately tracked in the reference split.

## Evidence

- Same public-owner regression is red on unchanged base: both native-mode cases call openRootFile twice on the caller thread instead of zero. Restored candidate byte comparison confirmed after the negative control.
- 18 tests pass: six real-worker guarded-read cases, five existing cache/identity/retirement cases, and seven bootstrap publication cases. Covers native auto and fallback off, content freshness, exact file identity, missing/oversized errors and alias refusal.
- Core production types and all core test type shards pass; targeted typed lint, formatting, and git diff --check pass.
- Canonical runtime build via tsdown-build.mts --filter openclaw-unified --no-dts passes. Declaration coverage comes from typechecks, not this runtime-only build.

prs.title: fix(installer): macOS onboarding cannot install plugins after the shell installer
prs.body:
Closes #200244
Supersedes #200247

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: first-run macOS onboarding fails with `Install failed: Codex` (`npm view failed … Assertion failed: (err) == (0)`) when OpenClaw is installed with `curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash`.

## User Impact

macOS users who install with the shell installer can finish onboarding, including plugin installs, without leaving the wizard. Upgrades that run `openclaw doctor --fix` and `openclaw plugins update --all` from the installer get the same fix. Linux and Windows behavior is unchanged. No settings or migration are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`curl | bash` gives the installer a pipe for stdin, so before onboarding it reattached stdin with `exec </dev/tty`. OpenClaw starts npm and other helpers detached, in a new session, so it can clean up their process trees. On macOS, `/dev/tty` refers to "the calling process's terminal" every time it is used. A detached Node child has no terminal, so its startup terminal check fails and Node aborts. On Linux, opening `/dev/tty` binds to the real device, so the same path works.

The installer now hands OpenClaw the terminal's own device, such as `/dev/ttys003`, resolved with `ps -o tty=`. It falls back to `/dev/tty` when that is unavailable. This fixes every detached child at the one place the `/dev/tty` alias was created, so the roughly 80 `killProcessTree` call sites do not need individual stdin workarounds. That is why this replaces #200247, which patched six npm call sites.

## Evidence

- **Real product path on macOS 26.6.2 arm64, Node 24.22.1, installed OpenClaw 2026.11.4.** I piped a script into `/bin/bash`, like `curl | bash`. It sources this branch's `install.sh`, runs the handoff, then `openclaw plugins install npm:@openclaw/codex@2026.11.4` with throwaway state:
  - Old handoff (`exec </dev/tty`): `npm view failed: # node[…]: void node::PlatformInit(…) at ../src/node.cc:613 # Assertion failed: (err) == (0)`, which is the error in #200244.
  - New handoff (stdin `/dev/ttys007`): `Installed plugin: codex`.
- **Minimal probe** (a detached Node child with inherited stdin): `/dev/tty` exits with SIGABRT. The real `/dev/ttysNNN` device, normal terminal stdin, and `/dev/tty` without detaching all exit 0.
- **Tests:** `test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts` passes 233 of 233. That includes a new test for the device lookup: the reported device when `ps` gives one, and `/dev/tty` when `ps` prints `??` or fails. The handoff and stdin-routing tests are updated. Format and lint are clean, and `bash -n` passes under macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2.
- **Review:** local autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode, P0–P2, with `src/process/exec-runner.ts` as source context) on head `6161543` against base `2435c1f` was `scoped-clean`, with no findings. The branch was then rebased onto `bd25e9e`, which does not touch installer files, so the patch is unchanged.
- **Gap:** I did not click through the interactive wizard end to end, and shellcheck was not run locally; CI runs it.

prs.title: fix(exec): keep gateway exec open for legacy GitHub profile ids
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A leftover PAT-shaped `tools.github.profileId` after the 2026.9.1 upgrade fail-closed every gateway exec, including `echo`, with "GitHub Identity credential is unavailable or insecure". Managed identity is only the opaque `ghp_[a-f0-9]{32}` profile id, so a PAT-shaped id left behind in the config is not a managed identity and should never have bound a profile.

Closes #137836

## Why This Change Was Made

An invalid explicit `profileId` stays selected. Gateway exec does not throw, and it does not fall through to a shared managed profile or to native authentication. Opaque managed profiles that are missing or insecure still fail closed before launch. Direct `gh` uses the refusing launcher. Indirect `gh` (`sh -c`, scripts) and native local harness shells receive a config directory that is never created, plus a non-credential token, so GitHub CLI cannot read another shared profile or the runtime user's stored account. Ordinary commands such as `echo` still run.

Doctor-led recovery versus this runtime exception is unchanged.

## Evidence

Current head `08685cbebb9d1087fd512430cb45f83c16766b22`. Gateway `createExecTool` with a legacy agent override (`ghp_` + 36 `A`), a valid shared profile that has a fixture account on disk, and that same fixture account planted in `GH_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` / enterprise token env, `GH_CONFIG_DIR`, and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. The `gh` on `PATH` is a local stub that prefers a non-empty token env and otherwise reads `hosts.yml` from `GH_CONFIG_DIR` or the default config dir. Paths and the fixture token are redacted.

```text
prepare legacy {
  managed: true,
  invalid: true,
  ghConfigDir: '<missing-dir>',
  ghConfigDirIsOther: false,
  ghConfigDirIsShared: false
}
echo hello-legacy { status: 'completed', exitCode: 0, aggregated: 'hello-legacy' }
direct gh {
  status: 'completed',
  exitCode: 1,
  aggregated: 'GitHub Identity credential is unavailable or insecure. Reconnect or change GitHub Identity, then retry.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '(Command exited with code 1)'
}
indirect sh -c {
  status: 'completed',
  exitCode: 1,
  aggregated: 'AUTH=sentinel\nFALLTHROUGH=none\n\n(Command exited with code 1)'
}
script {
  status: 'completed',
  exitCode: 1,
  aggregated: 'AUTH=sentinel\nFALLTHROUGH=none\n\n(Command exited with code 1)'
}
```

Native Codex start and resume use the admitted host environment for the same legacy id. `prepareCodexAttemptConnection` sets `disableLoginShell`, the sentinel `GH_TOKEN`, and the missing `GH_CONFIG_DIR`. The app-server start env and both `thread/start` and `thread/resume` `shell_environment_policy.set` maps, laid over a hostile other-account env, produce `AUTH=sentinel` and `FALLTHROUGH=none` from that same client stub.

```text
OPENCLAW_TEST_PROFILE=low pnpm test -- \
  src/agents/bash-tools.github-identity.test.ts \
  src/agents/github-tool-identity.invalid-selection.test.ts \
  src/agents/github-invalid-selection.test.ts \
  src/agents/harness/host-capability.environment.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-connection.environment.test.ts

github-invalid-selection.test.ts          3 passed
bash-tools.github-identity.test.ts       10 passed
github-tool-identity.invalid-selection   2 passed
host-capability.environment.test.ts      3 passed
run-attempt-connection.environment.test.ts  native case passed
pnpm tsgo:core                           passed
pnpm tsgo:extensions:test                passed
```

prs.title: fix(infra): decode OEM console code pages in Windows subprocess output
prs.body:
Related: #135856, #136203

Not a fix for #135856. That report is `doctor --fix` refusing maintenance, and this pull request no longer changes Doctor or Scheduled Task inventory.

The Spanish and German `schtasks /FO LIST` parser was dropped. Current main reads task inventory from typed COM (`Schedule.Service`) through `listScheduledTasks`, and #151608 superseded the localized LIST-parser part of this pull request.

## What Problem This Solves

Windows subprocess output on a Spanish or German console comes back with U+FFFD in place of accented characters. Those consoles default to OEM code page 850. `chcp` reports 850, the console encoding probe only consulted the ANSI code-page map, and Node's `TextDecoder` has no label for the OEM `cp###` pages, so the bytes were decoded as UTF-8.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `chcp` probe now falls back to the existing OEM code-page map that the `.cmd` launcher already uses. Legacy decoding goes through iconv-lite for the `cp###` labels ICU lacks. `decodeWindowsOutputBuffer` and `createWindowsOutputDecoder` share that decoder. Valid UTF-8 is still tried first, and UTF-16 BOM handling is unchanged. The system ANSI probe is unchanged. Main's locale-independent task inventory is left as it is.

`src/infra/windows-encoding.ts` is on the PR wrapper inventory, so iconv-lite is pinned in that extracted dependency context. Without the pin, wrapper boot could not load the module.

## User Impact

Windows command output on the OEM console pages in that map, including 850, decodes accented text instead of replacement characters. English and UTF-8 consoles are unchanged. Deep Scheduled Task scanning stays on main's COM inventory.

## Evidence

No native localized Windows run was done. The previous Linux stand-in exercised the `schtasks /FO LIST` parser, and that path has been removed, so it is not proof for this scope.

Focused tests on the decoder head (Node 24.21.0):

prs.title: fix(exec): count only real services against the exec service cap
prs.body:
## Problem

#199079 adopts every process a completed host `exec` command leaves running as a service, up to 16 per session and 64 per Gateway. Over that limit it stops the new survivors.

The census runs at the instant the root command exits. Helpers that are still exiting at that instant (`git`, `cp`, `tee`, `tail`, a short `sleep`) are counted as services. Two bad results follow:

- Helpers fill the 16 slots and push out real work. In one evening of a production Gateway, 5 sessions hit "16 of 16 allowed services" while the Gateway held only 18 to 36 of 64. OpenClaw stopped 2 to 14 processes in each: test-harness `nohup` loops, a test `gateway run`, the `git` processes of a worktree switch.
- Each helper is reported to the model as a background session that "keeps running", although it exits a moment later.

Agents then spent calls killing leftovers or restarting stopped work.

## Fix

Two changes to the existing owners. No new state.

1. **Adopt after a settle window** (`service-child-group-ownership.ts`). After the root exits, the process owner repeats its survivor census every 100 ms until nothing is left or 2 s pass. Only what still runs at the end is reported and adopted. Each census keeps the earlier survivors that still run the same command, so a process cannot escape custody by outliving the parent that tied it to the command. A root that still runs (a one-shot hand-off of a `background: true` service) is handed off at once. A cancellation during the window owns the tree, as before. No command names are special-cased.
2. **Never stop a survivor for capacity** (`bash-process-adopted.ts`). The cap is checked only where a service is declared (`reserveServiceSlot`, `background: true`). Adoption now tracks every survivor and never stops one as over the limit. The overflow kill and `killReleasedProcess` are deleted. Survivors still count, so a `background: true` start is still refused at the limit.

Production code: +67 / −71 lines.

## User impact

- Short-lived helpers no longer take service slots, are not reported as services, and are never stopped.
- A real service a command leaves running (`nohup server &`, a fork loop) is still tracked, listed by `process list`, stopped by `process kill`, session reset and Gateway stop.
- Commands that leave a real process running now return up to 2 s later. Commands that leave nothing running are not delayed.
- At the limit, a declared `background: true` service is refused. A survivor over the limit is tracked instead of stopped.

## Proof

**Real Gateway E2E** (dist build, macOS, scratch state, service-managed exec path, real model `claude-opus-5-5`). Base is the merge base `aa4d490a`. Each arm is one Gateway with three sessions driven through `chat.send`.

| Journey | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| 20 calls of `for i in $(seq 18); do (git status --short; sleep 0.5) & done; git status --short; cp a.txt b.txt` | every call at "16 of 16": 288 helpers adopted as services, 431 stopped as over the limit | 0 adopted, 0 stopped, 20 of 20 clean results |
| `nohup python3 -m http.server &`, then 16 × `nohup sleep &` | 16 adopted, the 17th stopped | 17 adopted and listed; no process stopped |
| then a 17th declared service (`background: true`) | (not run on base) | refused: "This session runs 17 of 16 allowed services" |
| busy fork loop `while :; do sleep 0.05; done &` | adopted, listed | adopted, listed |
| Gateway stop | all tagged processes gone | all tagged processes gone (17 → 0) |

**Regression test** (`bash-tools.exec-group-cleanup.real.test.ts`, vitest-source, real processes, macOS): one call leaves 17 helpers of `sleep 0.5`, 20 times, then a fork loop.
- Base: fails, "Stopped 1 process the command left running, over the service limit … 16 of 16 allowed services".
- Head: passes; no helper is adopted or stopped, and the loop is adopted.

The cap tests now assert that every survivor stays tracked past the limit and that `background: true` is still refused. Whole file on head: 10 passed, 3 skipped (Linux only).

prs.title: fix: keep credential diagnostics responsive on slow filesystems
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: cold credential reads, updates, and migration diagnostics can freeze the Gateway while the filesystem is busy.

Related: #197510, #200136, #200192.

## User Impact

Credential operations continue waiting for their required files without blocking other Gateway work. Existing migration refusals, provider scope, credential authority, FIFO admission, and reader retirement remain intact. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The async row reader still reached synchronous legacy-file presence checks and diagnostic reads. Prepare those facts asynchronously through the existing file-observation and diagnostic owners; live readers subscribe to their own candidate paths and release subscriptions when disposed. Credential effects consume the prepared refusal and retain their final authority checks without an intervening await. Shared-store bootstrap prepares physical identity and source facts through the existing asynchronous admission hook.

Production grows by 291 lines across 20 modules (tests/support: +210 lines) to preserve live-reader observation and the named synchronous SDK/maintenance contract. This adds no cache, worker, schema, configuration, or protocol. The normal measured path costs about 0.64 ms more; this change targets responsiveness rather than a general throughput gain. Remaining generic writer reverse lookup, source-cohort comparison, credential-boundary canonicalization, explicit secrets rebuilds, and deprecated synchronous SDK paths are outside this stage.

## Evidence

The motivating read-only Team observation was 25c97908, 2026-11-16 05:02 PST: MAIN spent 1.97 s in `openat2(O_CREAT)` on `~/agents/roboclaw-x/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite.plugin-model-catalog.lock`, with `btrfs_create → start_transaction → wait_current_trans`; `scheduler:update.remote-model-catalog` stalled the loop for 2,002 ms during a btrfs commit triggered by managed worktree removal. That specific lock was removed in #200136; this PR closes additional auth paths found by the same audit. No Team data was copied or changed.

- Four guard regressions fail on exact stage-1 production, then pass with this change. Candidate consumer proof: 177/177 across 10 files; final integration replay: 63/63 across five files, with wrapper source verification. Required stable-prefix guard passes 15/15 on the final publication source. Coverage includes late legacy restoration, provider scope changes, disposal, source retirement, shared bootstrap settlement, updates, FIFO admission, and credential/config consumers.
- Twenty serialized processes include A/A controls and interleaved no-delay/two-second-delay arms. Each uses an actual synthetic 35 GiB queried database with 5,000 sessions and an empty canonical auth row, and asserts the exact fixture-provider migration refusal. Scoped main-thread synchronous calls fall from three to zero. The two-second legacy-file read delay changes median maximum heartbeat gap from 2,013.721 to 16.980 ms (candidate worst 32.374 ms), while the operation still waits roughly two seconds.
- Without injected delay: median owner time 5.518 → 6.156 ms; main CPU 2.768 → 3.110 ms; parent CPU 14.980 → 15.646 ms; main-V8 allocated bytes 1,333,936 → 1,336,292. A/A owner range is 5.297–7.621 ms and allocation 941,520–2,110,968 bytes. These observed costs are retained; no speed or allocation improvement is claimed. Delayed candidate CPU/allocation includes the 1 ms heartbeat continuing during the async wait. APFS plus injection is not direct btrfs proof; OS cache is uncontrolled and child/native allocation is excluded.
- Final-base `pnpm check:changed` completed: production types, all 29 test type graphs, lint, format, and structural/security/worker/schema/import guards passed. The command exits 1 on unused exports: 116 entries, including 112 matched to a clean earlier baseline and four package-release exports added by #198835 / `b868ed4c21ba0`. A clean exact parent `9323fb9d` reproduces all 116 entries with zero candidate-only findings. Parent-relative history proves the four new declarations and their absence of external production callers in #198835; the older 112 remain baseline matches, with individual causal attribution incomplete. This is not a blanket inherited-CI waiver. The earlier exact-667 failures (`ProjectedContinuationSource`, `partContinuation`) were introduced by #200056 / `24385a20428a`. Fresh isolated Codex review completed three clean passes through P2. No changed module is runtime-imported by the Control UI.

Earlier stage-1 native-staging runs had two unexplained 10 s timeouts; passing replays do not establish a fix or inherited cause. The separately attributed main watch-benchmark regression (#197445 / `36afa92b2370`, exact parent `4a74c61ae7c438587bc272840d180d16f7c5a283`) also remains a follow-up. This PR does not change those tests or claim a global zero-sync result. Exact-head CI and final-head ClawSweeper review will gate landing.

Consumer repair: CI run 43935316801 at `a59eac28` exposed four failures in three fixtures. The admission interceptor now forwards the existing async preparation callback; the pure diagnostic fixture supplies its affected provider; and the permission-error fixture intercepts the asynchronous identity inspector. Existing rollback, provider-isolation, and legacy-ownership assertions are unchanged. Exact-head local reproduction was four failures and one passing control; the same five cases pass after the repair. Both affected test type graphs, scoped lint/format, and a fresh isolated Codex delta review pass. Production is unchanged.

Real isolated built-Gateway proof also passed (1/1, generation verified) on `a59eac28`, whose 20 changed production modules are byte-identical to final `fc5bf62e`. Two concurrent MAIN-initiated legacy diagnostic reads were held for 2,183.079 ms. During that hold, three health RPCs returned in 32.183/25.475/25.542 ms and an unrelated real-model turn completed in 2,099.627 ms with the expected terminal reply. The affected session retained its provider-specific migration refusal and Doctor instruction. Its total 65,923.944 ms includes failed loopback-only synthetic provider retries; this proves eventual refusal, not immediate pre-network refusal. Health payloads were cached and retained a startup CPU-degraded flag, so RPC timings and the completed real-model turn establish responsiveness, not a newly sampled healthy event-loop state. APFS plus targeted async read injection; all owned processes/state were cleaned up. Full sanitized receipts are in the accompanying PR comment.

A subsequent CI failure in run 43941147230 was confined to an obsolete screenshot-positioning scroll in the UI ACK ownership test. Commit `21febc760a6f5` deletes only that action; all draft, tool visibility/content, ACK/history ordering, continuation, and Stop-target assertions remain. The scroll was introduced for screenshots in #155746; #178793 removed the screenshots but left this action. That is provenance, not an established introducer of the timing failure. The unchanged exact main-parent case passed locally, so no inherited-failure exception is claimed. All four cases pass both on that parent with the fix and on the exact PR source with the same one-line fix; formatter and isolated Codex review are clean. Production is unchanged. New exact-head CI and zero-open final-head Claw review gate landing.

While final CI was running, main also received the same UI scroll deletion in #200183 and a resolved-command-row locator in #200202. The merge retains both compatible fixes; no auth production file changed on main. This PR does not claim either peer change as newly introduced auth behavior.

CI run 43946411593 tested `21febc76` against main `800bd59c` and exposed a main integration regression: #200203 moved the identity helper but missed an OAuth caller introduced by #200192. The exact main parent reproduces `TS2724`; the build and affected UI collection logs report that same missing export. Main already repairs the import in #200242 / `0879f3e9`. Final head `fc5bf62e55c79c64d43e77848a2bd71e6cc79311` integrates that material dependency without conflicts. All 20 authored production modules remain byte-identical; the peer UI fixes are retained and no longer part of this PR's diff. Core types pass; the two affected browser fixtures pass **8/8**, compiled generation verified, and fresh isolated Codex P0–P2 review is clean. The failed run remains failed; fresh exact-head CI and zero-open Claw review are required.

prs.title: fix(storage): use async auto-enable to avoid cold setup failures during update doctor
prs.body:
Refs #194528

## What Problem This Solves

During `openclaw update` finalization on Windows (2026.11.1, win32/x64), the pre-plugin Doctor failed with `step-refused` and 4 redacted failing checks.

When a plugin's setup module is cold, the synchronous auto-enable path can run before the setup probes have been loaded, so the auto-enable step refuses. `acquireStorageProvider` is already async, but it called the sync `applyPluginAutoEnable`, so it could hit the same cold-setup failure during Doctor/update — even though the async owner (`applyPluginAutoEnableAsync`) prepares setup first.

## What Changed

- `src/storage/provider.ts`: use `applyPluginAutoEnableAsync` in `acquireStorageProvider` (async context) instead of sync `applyPluginAutoEnable`, so plugin setup probes are prepared before auto-enable.

This matches the cold setup module fix already landed in `repair-sequencing.ts` (#194674), so both cold-setup paths now prepare setup through the same async owner.

No behavior change when setup is warm; the change only ensures setup preparation happens in async context.

## Evidence

- `bunx vitest run src/storage` — targeted storage tests pass.
- Project typecheck passes for the changed file.
- Manual: `openclaw update` on Windows no longer fails at `finalize-doctor` with a storage-related `step-refused`.
- Diff is minimal (1 file, async API swap) and follows the existing pattern from #194674.

Behavior addressed: storage provider acquisition no longer uses the synchronous plugin auto-enable path.
Real environment tested: Windows 11, win32/x64, openclaw 2026.11.1 update finalization.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: bunx vitest run src/storage
Evidence after fix: storage suite green; no step-refused at finalize-doctor.
Observed result after fix: Doctor completes and update proceeds to the plugin stage.
What was not tested: macOS and Linux update flows were not exercised locally.

prs.title: feat(memory): grant spawned sessions the verified human sender's memory audience
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an owner who types into a spawned session (for example, a subagent session in the Control UI) loses all memory access when any ancestor session was reset, because the child's memory audience comes only from its spawn lineage and is permanently denied as `stale-lineage`.

## User Impact

An authenticated owner typing directly into a spawned session now gets their own owner-private memory for that turn, as in their own direct chat. Parent resets, stale lineage and sidebar-root promotion no longer matter for that turn, and nothing is inherited from the parent. A non-owner operator typing into a spawned session now gets **no** memory audience, even when an owner spawned it (previously such a turn borrowed the spawn receipt's owner bit). Turns with no human sender keep today's lineage rules exactly.

## Why This Change Was Made

Maintainer direction: a spawned session should not inherit the parent conversation's authority, but a human typing into it should get the authority of that human. The Gateway already knows who typed a `chat.send` turn on an authenticated transport. This PR carries that fact to memory audience resolution as a host-issued capability, so the resolver can use the current sender instead of the spawn receipt.

## Security model

- **Issuer.** Only the external `chat.send` entry issues a `HumanSenderTurn` (`src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-external-entry.ts`). It requires all of the following:
  - the request frame arrived on the operator's WebSocket transport (`markExternalGatewayRequestFrame` in `authenticated-request-dispatch.ts`, checked in `chat-send-input-dispatch.ts`);
  - `client.internal.authenticatedOperator` (set at handshake, never from wire params);
  - `isDirectGatewayUserClient` (no synthetic, agent-runtime, plugin, approval, cron-continuation or delegated markers);
  - no input provenance, explicit origin, restored cron continuation, reconnect resume, or system-generated receipt, and `turnKind: "main"`.

  The owner bit is the connection's `operator.admin` scope. That is the same standard `chat.send` uses for `senderIsOwner` on top-level direct sessions.
- **Not forgeable.** The turn is an opaque frozen object registered in a module `WeakMap`. It is never serialized into transcripts, chat metadata or launch text. A copied or model-authored lookalike reads as nothing.
- **Bound to one run.** The turn binds to the `operationalRunInstance` of the first run that admits it (`agent-runner-admission.ts`). Followups, stranded or transcript retries, maintenance copies, and any other run that carries a copy read nothing. Collected queue batches are forced to drain individually (`queue/envelope.ts`), so one sender's turn never binds to a batch with other inputs.
- **Forwarded and delegated turns can't take the path.** In-process dispatch (plugin RPC re-entry through `dispatchGatewayMethod`, agent tools, internal facades, in-process `sessions.send`) builds its own frame, so it is never marked, even when it keeps the operator client. Subagent runs, cron and scheduled runs, `sessions_send`, announcements, heartbeats, restart sentinels, event triggers, and steer and followup injections never reach the external entry, or they carry provenance that the issuer rejects. Internal re-entry via `handleChatSend` passes no external admission.
- **Resolver** (`src/plugins/memory-audience.ts`). The path applies only when the admitted row has `spawnedBy` and the run has no `scheduledParent`:
  - An owner (both the attested bit and `run.senderIsOwner`) gets `owner-private`. Only this session's admitted incarnation is leased; ancestors are never read.
  - A non-owner is denied (`ineligible`).
  - A spawned group or channel session keeps its lineage rules, so owner-private memory never enters a shared room.
  - Top-level sessions are unchanged.
- **Unchanged.** The ancestor `sessionId` and lifecycle-revision comparison, `stale-lineage`, and the scheduled owner cap.

<details><summary>Trust path (file:line at head)</summary>

1. `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/authenticated-request-dispatch.ts:545`: marks the transport frame.
2. `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-input-dispatch.ts:169-174`: checks the frame and issues the turn via the external admission.
3. `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-external-entry.ts:49-63`: issuance predicate and owner bit.
4. `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-agent-dispatch.ts:387` → `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run-execute.ts:651`: `replyOptions` → `FollowupRun.run`.
5. `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-admission.ts:54`: binds to the admitted run.
6. `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.ts:508` (embedded) and `agent-runner-cli-candidate.ts:522` (CLI): run params.
7. `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-memory-audience.ts:67`; CLI via `src/agents/cli-runner/mcp-memory-audience.ts`.
8. `src/plugins/memory-audience.ts:267-285`: reads the turn for this run and session, then decides.

</details>

## Evidence

- `src/plugins/memory-audience.human-sender.test.ts`: covers a spawned child with a stale ancestor.
  - Granted for an owner typing in, including after sidebar-root promotion and with a legacy receipt; only one lease, and no ancestor is read.
  - Denied for a non-owner operator, and for an owner-attested turn whose run sender is not the owner.
  - Still `stale-lineage` for turns without a human sender, a forged object, an unbound turn, a turn copied to another run, and a turn issued for another session.
  - The scheduled owner cap is kept.
  - A spawned group session keeps its lineage rules.
- `attempt-memory-audience.test.ts`: the attempt resolver reads the turn only from its own admitted run.
- `chat-send-human-sender.test.ts` (real SQLite, real `chat.send` admission): issued for an authenticated transport frame, with the owner bit following admin scope. Not issued for an unauthenticated connection, in-process re-entry of the external entry, or internal `handleChatSend` re-entry.
- Existing suites pass unchanged: `memory-audience.test.ts`, `cron/execution-context-memory-audience.test.ts`, `cli-runner/prepare.test.ts`, `stranded-reply-recovery.test.ts`, `chat-send-session-binding.test.ts`, and `authenticated-request-dispatch.policy-close.test.ts`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass; oxlint is clean on the changed files.
- Fresh independent security review. Its one verified P1 is fixed in the second commit: plugin RPC re-entry kept the authenticated client and could mint the turn.
- Gap: no live Gateway or Control UI end-to-end run yet.

prs.title: improve(ui): show the voice level as a timeline across the composer
prs.body:
Closes #200233

## What Problem This Solves

While you dictate or use Talk in the Control UI, the voice level shows as seven bars that pulse together in a small fixed spot, so it reads as one block going up and down rather than as your voice.

## User Impact

User impact: while you dictate or talk, a strip of fine bars shows your recent speech sliding in from the right across the free width of the composer. Pauses show as gaps, and silence settles into a row of dots.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Dictation and Talk share one level meter. It draws a timeline: each new level enters on the right and slides left, and both ends fade out. Bars are 2px wide on a 4px pitch, and their number follows the width the meter gets.
- Dictation: "Listening…" comes first and the timeline fills the rest of the status row. This applies in the chat composer, the new-session page and side chat.
- Talk: the timeline grows with the composer's width up to 160px, and phone-width composers keep it at 56px. While Talk runs, the model and speed pickers sit further left to make room.
- Connecting sweeps a highlight across the dots, thinking drifts two slow waves across the bars, and with reduced motion each state keeps its own still shape: an even row of short bars while listening, taller bars in the middle while thinking, and dim dots while connecting.
- Audio capture, levels and settings are unchanged.

## Evidence

The Control UI ran with a mocked Gateway and a fake microphone. Main and this branch got the same made-up speech levels.

Light, 1000px:
![Before and after, light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/32622310b6426310735ef029731f26f21a7012f7/images/2026/11/b7fd9673-c5d7-4594-bff7-5dffdb4d6c20.png)

prs.title: fix(onboard): import memories through the running Gateway
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Custom setup onboarding exits with code 1 right after "Set up memory embeddings?". By that point setup has started the Gateway service, and the memory import step refuses to run while a Gateway owns the state ("This operation requires exclusive offline state ownership"). `openclaw onboard --classic` with a running Gateway service exits 1 with the same error right after "OpenClaw setup". Fixes #199895.

## Solution

When a Gateway owns the state, the onboarding memory import plans and applies through that Gateway's existing `migrations.memory.plan` and `migrations.memory.apply` methods. The terminal prompts stay the same: offer, confirm, pick sources, summary.

- `withPluginMigrationProviders` accepts an optional `onForeignOwner` handler and passes it to `runWithLocalStateOwner`. Callers that leave it out refuse.
- `withMemoryMigrationOffers` in `src/commands/migrate/memory-import.ts` is the one place that turns plans into offers. With no Gateway it plans and applies locally. With a Gateway it asks the Gateway for plans and applies by plan fingerprint and idempotency key.
- If the Gateway cannot answer the plan request, onboarding shows a "Memory import failed" note that points to the dashboard's Memory import page, then continues with nothing to import.
- `runSetupMemoryImportStep` only renders offers and calls `offer.apply()`.
- `detectSetupMigrationSources`, which the classic wizard calls first, returns no detected sources when a Gateway owns the state, without loading migration providers locally.

## Impact

Onboarding continues past the memory step while the Gateway runs, and detected Claude Code memories are offered and imported into the agent workspace. A Gateway that cannot answer the plan request does not end onboarding. `openclaw onboard --classic` with a running Gateway completes, and its memory step imports through the Gateway. Offline runs keep the local apply.

## Evidence

Real `openclaw onboard` runs in a clean macOS 26.6 VM, each with a stand-in Claude Code CLI for the AI check and one made-up Claude Code memory file. The guided runs use Custom setup, and every run that reached the embeddings question declined it.

- `main`: exits 1 with "Cannot admit migrate for migration providers ... requires exclusive offline state ownership" right after "Set up memory embeddings? No".
- This branch: shows "Memories found: Claude (1 memories)", the import is accepted and reports "Claude: 1 migrated, 0 skipped". The Gateway log has `res ✓ migrations.memory.apply`, the file lands in `workspace/memory/imports/claude-code/`, and onboarding goes on to app recommendations and the browser handoff.

  ![Memory import summary on this branch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/0f15d09e7bf991e886213e5bcbc7de3744739340/images/2026/11/bb4fe238-563a-4a2f-9c55-d4791e0fb0fe.png)

- This branch, with the Gateway frozen (`kill -STOP`) just before the plan request: a "Memory import failed" note that points to the Memory import page. After the Gateway resumes, onboarding goes on to the browser handoff.

  ![Memory import failed note on this branch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/0f15d09e7bf991e886213e5bcbc7de3744739340/images/2026/11/90eae6e1-c101-483f-871c-eabfecab096b.png)

- `main`, `openclaw onboard --classic` after a guided run left the Gateway service running: exits 1 with the same ownership error right after "OpenClaw setup".
- This branch, `openclaw onboard --classic` after a guided run that left the Gateway service running and declined the memory import: the setup mode prompt appears, the memory step shows "Memories found: Claude (1 memories)" and reports "Claude: 1 migrated, 0 skipped", the Gateway log has `res ✓ migrations.memory.apply`, and the wizard ends with "Onboarding complete" and exit code 0.

  ![Classic setup memory import on this branch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/0f15d09e7bf991e886213e5bcbc7de3744739340/images/2026/11/e2c9d6d4-f642-4237-89fd-fb58732d2f8c.png)

- Upgrade from 2026.11.4, in a fresh VM: on 2026.11.4, Custom setup exits 1 with the same ownership error right after "Set up memory embeddings? No". On that install, `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds` was set to 900 and a memory note was added. After upgrading to this branch, restarting the Gateway and rerunning `openclaw onboard` (embeddings declined again), onboarding exits 0. The Claude memory is imported through the Gateway ("Claude: 1 migrated, 0 skipped", `res ✓ migrations.memory.apply` in the Gateway log), and the hatch TUI connects to the running Gateway (`openclaw tui - ws://127.0.0.1:18789`, "gateway connected"). `timeoutSeconds` is still 900. Of the 29 config keys set on 2026.11.4, 25 are unchanged and none were removed; the 4 that changed are `meta.lastTouchedVersion` and the `wizard.lastRun*` fields. The memory note, AGENTS.md, IDENTITY.md, SOUL.md and USER.md match their 2026.11.4 hashes; BOOTSTRAP.md, the first-run file, is gone after onboarding.

  Limits of this run: the package was built from 74887de, and the later commits change only tests. No agent reply is shown in the TUI, because the stand-in CLI is not on the Gateway service's PATH, so the turn reports "CLI backend executable could not be resolved: claude".

  ![2026.11.4: onboarding exits after the embeddings question](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/5686066e9829d98ac1cf6e3da602465fab37ad2b/images/2026/11/cb3801b2-301d-41e8-9775-7612133c2d70.png)

  ![After the upgrade: hatch TUI connected to the running Gateway](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/5686066e9829d98ac1cf6e3da602465fab37ad2b/images/2026/11/6cba854f-c471-42de-a52c-75ab20b4611d.png)

Tests:

- `src/wizard/setup.memory-import.owner.test.ts` (new) uses the real Gateway lock, owner selection and `migrations.memory.*` handlers, for accept, decline, nothing to import, lost apply response, Gateway without the plan method, and offline, plus classic migration detection while a Gateway holds the state lock. On `main` 6 of 7 fail with the ownership error (offline passes); on this branch 7 of 7 pass.
- `src/commands/migrate/memory-import.test.ts`: offers carry only planned item ids, a source with only already-imported items gets no offer, and apply receives exactly the planned ids with the reviewed plan. 3 of 3 pass.
- `src/wizard/setup.memory-import.test.ts`: decline, selection with the multi-select defaults, outcome recording, and continuing after a failed apply. 5 of 5 pass.
- Consumer tests pass: wizard i18n locale parity, `gateway/server-methods/migrations`, `plugins/migration-provider-runtime`, `system-agent/hosted-setup.memory`, `commands/onboard-guided-memory-import`, `wizard/setup`, `commands/migrate`, `commands/migrate.resources`, `wizard/setup.migration-resources`, `wizard/setup.post-install-migration`, `wizard/setup.migration-transaction`, `wizard/setup.default-agent`, `commands/onboard-non-interactive.migration`.
- `tsgo` for core and core tests, plus oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files: clean.
- Not run: the full suite.
