prs.title: fix(exec): autoAllowSkills ignored for gateway-host exec
prs.body:
Closes #158165

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with exec approvals in `allowlist` mode and `autoAllowSkills: true`, an agent whose commands run on the Gateway host is still denied (`exec denied: allowlist miss`) the binaries its own workspace skills declare in `requires.bins`. `autoAllowSkills` only took effect on node hosts.

## User Impact

User impact: Gateway-hosted agents (containers, servers, most self-hosted setups) can use `allowlist` mode with `autoAllowSkills` and have the binaries of their eligible skills allowed, without a hand-kept allowlist that duplicates skill metadata. Binaries of disabled or otherwise ineligible skills, and binaries no skill declares, stay denied. With `autoAllowSkills` off (the default), nothing changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway exec host evaluated the allowlist without skill bins, while the node host passes them (`skills.bins`). When the agent's effective approvals enable `autoAllowSkills`, the gateway host now trusts only the bins declared by **the executing agent's eligible skills**: the set its prompt sees (`resolveWorkspaceSkillPromptEntries`: enabled, allowed by the bundled-skills allowlist and the agent's skill filter, requirements met). It never trusts every installed skill, so a disabled bundled skill cannot grant execution trust. Those bins go to the same allowlist evaluation the node host uses. This is the agent-scoped option recommended in the issue review. Bins are resolved on the same `PATH` the command resolves on: the Gateway's `PATH` plus operator `tools.exec.pathPrepend`. Host exec already rejects a requested `PATH` (`Custom 'PATH' variable is forbidden during host execution`), so a tool call cannot point a skill bin name at another binary; a test pins that invariant. The evaluation moves into a sibling module, so the already-over-cap gateway host file shrinks.

## Evidence

**Real Gateway, allowlist mode, before and after.** Same script for both: a fresh state dir; approvals `agents.main = { autoAllowSkills: true, allowlist: [] }`; two workspace skills, `skill-tool` (requires `skill-tool`) and `disabled-skill` (requires `disabled-tool`, with `skills.entries.disabled-skill.enabled: false`); the three executables on the Gateway's `PATH`; `openclaw gateway run`; then one `openclaw agent` turn per command. The model is a scripted local OpenAI-compatible stub (deterministic, no keys) that asks the `exec` tool to run one command and replies with the result.

```
===== BEFORE (published 2026.9.5 image)
[before] OpenClaw 2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1)
[before] approvals main: {"autoAllowSkills":true,"allowlist":[]}
[before] agent turn: the model asks exec to run: skill-tool
[before]   reply:   "error": "exec denied: allowlist miss"
[before] agent turn: the model asks exec to run: disabled-tool
[before]   reply:   "error": "exec denied: allowlist miss"
[before] agent turn: the model asks exec to run: other-tool
[before]   reply:   "error": "exec denied: allowlist miss"

===== AFTER (this PR, built from 659b5e30dc)
[after] OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (659b5e3)
[after] approvals main: {"autoAllowSkills":true,"allowlist":[]}
[after] agent turn: the model asks exec to run: skill-tool
[after]   reply: exec returned: skill-tool ran
[after] agent turn: the model asks exec to run: disabled-tool
[after]   reply:   "error": "exec denied: allowlist miss"
[after] agent turn: the model asks exec to run: other-tool
[after]   reply:   "error": "exec denied: allowlist miss"
```

Eligibility is OpenClaw's own: when the executables sit only in a `tools.exec.pathPrepend` directory, `openclaw skills check` lists `skill-tool (bins: skill-tool)` under missing requirements, so the skill is not in the agent's prompt and its bin is not trusted either. The trusted set always matches what the model is shown.

**Tests and checks**

- New `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.auto-allow-skills.test.ts` (real exec tool, gateway host, allowlist mode): an eligible skill's bin runs with `autoAllowSkills` on; denied with it off; **a bin only a disabled skill declares stays denied**; a bin no skill declares stays denied; a requested `PATH` reaching a planted skill-named binary is refused. The eligible-skill test fails with the source change removed (1 failed / 4 passed). The disabled-skill test fails against an earlier revision of this PR that collected bins from every installed skill, and passes now.
- `pnpm vitest run` over the gateway exec host, exec run, and exec allowlist test files: 7 files, 218 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test`: clean.
- `pnpm check:changed`: all steps pass (including the line-cap ratchet) except `core tsgo graph boundary` ("agents-root: 721 test roots exceeds the advisory 720 limit"), which reports the same 721 on a clean checkout of main and is unrelated to this change.


---

## Authority-chain proof (revision 3)

Addresses the P1 finding: the resolver reloaded eligible skills from agent config
alone, ignoring the admitted session's narrowing.

Driven through the real gateway exec path — real skill loader, real PATH
resolution, real process supervisor, nothing mocked. The skill's declared bin
appends to a marker file, so a denial is observable as the absence of any I/O
rather than only as a returned error.

**Before (`659b5e30dc3`, the previously reviewed head)**

```
[1] baseline: skill eligible for the run
    outcome: status=completed exitCode=0        marker: I/O HAPPENED (1 run)
[2] session filter excludes the declaring skill
    outcome: status=completed exitCode=0        marker: I/O HAPPENED (1 run)
[3] session override turns the declaring skill off
    outcome: status=completed exitCode=0        marker: I/O HAPPENED (1 run)
[4] bin repointed after authorization, before launch
    outcome: allowed                            marker: no I/O
```

A session-excluded skill's binary reached process launch and executed.

**After (this revision)**

```
[1] baseline: skill eligible for the run
    outcome: status=completed exitCode=0        marker: I/O HAPPENED (1 run)
[2] session filter excludes the declaring skill
    outcome: DENIED: exec denied: allowlist miss        marker: no I/O
[3] session override turns the declaring skill off
    outcome: DENIED: exec denied: allowlist miss        marker: no I/O
[4] bin repointed after authorization, before launch
    authorized: deniedResult=no, revalidateBeforeExecution=function
    outcome: DENIED at spawn boundary:
      Exec denied (SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED: skill bin authorization changed
      before execution): probe-tool                    marker: no I/O
```

Case [4] covers the revocation-before-launch request. The approvals file records
the `autoAllowSkills` flag but never the executable a skill authorized, so the
committed-policy recheck cannot see that binary change while approval settles;
the bins are re-resolved at the spawn boundary instead. The trust comparison is
now shared with the allowlist evaluator (`isSegmentAuthorizedBySkillBins`) so the
granting and revalidating checks cannot drift.

Scope note: the recheck observes executable identity and the admitted scope. A
skill's on-disk source changing mid-run is picked up by the skills watcher's
version bump, not by this path.

Regression coverage added in
`src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.auto-allow-skills.test.ts`: session
filter exclusion, session override exclusion, the allowed case under an
including filter, and spawn-boundary denial on a swapped bin.


### Detached approval launch (revision 5)

Addresses the follow-on P1: the detached launch kept its own spawn gate that
rechecked only cwd and mutable-operand drift, so `revalidateBeforeExecution` —
which carries the skill check — was never consulted on that path.

All five gateway launch paths now recheck skill authority at their spawn
boundary: inline ask, ask-fallback, auto-review allow-once, detached approval,
and the direct allowlist path. The check is split into a reason-returning
resolver and the result-returning wrapper the inline paths use, so both call
shapes share one implementation.

Regression test `revalidates skill authority in the detached approval launch`
drives `ask: "always"` with a backgrounded approval, has the launch adapter
invoke `beforeSpawn` as the real runtime does, and asserts the follow-up reports
the denial and that spawn is never reached. Reverting only the `beforeSpawn`
change flips it to the bypass, which is the reported defect:

```
with the fix:      DENIED ... skill bin authorization changed before execution
without the fix:   Exec finished (gateway id=req-1, sess...)   <- launched and ran
```

`pnpm tsgo:core` clean; 137 passed across the two gateway exec test files, 907
across the exec-approvals and bash-tools exec suites.



### Rebased onto main (revision 6)

Rebased onto current main. Two things on main changed what this PR has to cover.

**A sixth launch path.** Main added a gateway launch path: a cron occurrence that consumes a standing grant. It rechecked only the grant, so a segment admitted on skill-bin trust could launch after that trust was withdrawn. It now rechecks skill authority **before the grant is consumed**, so a withdrawn skill denies the launch without spending the grant. All six launch paths now recheck at their spawn boundary: inline ask, ask-fallback, auto-review allow-once, detached approval, the direct allowlist path, and cron standing grants. New regression test: `rechecks skill authority before spending a standing grant` in `bash-tools.exec-cron-grant.test.ts`. It fails without the recheck.

**The line-cap ratchet now runs on pull requests.** The gateway host, its unit test and the infra allowlist evaluator stay at or below their size on main:

- The spawn-boundary rechecks (approval-binding drift, the denial result, chaining, the skill-authority recheck) moved to `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway-revalidation.ts`.
- Skill-bin trust matching moved to `infra/exec-approvals-skill-bins.ts`, re-exported through `exec-approvals`.

**Detached approval proof, without mocks.** The revision-5 test `revalidates skill authority in the detached approval launch` mocked the launch adapter. It is replaced by `detached approval launch …` in `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.auto-allow-skills.test.ts`, which runs the real approval, launch adapter and spawn boundary. The command launches while skill trust holds, and is denied before spawn once the authorizing skill is uninstalled while approval is pending. The denial case fails without the detached-launch fix.

`docs/tools/exec-approvals.md` now says the recheck covers every gateway launch path.

Checks: `pnpm tsgo:core` and the changed test files typecheck clean. The autoAllowSkills suite, the gateway exec host tests, the cron-grant tests, `exec-approvals` and the node-host allowlist tests pass. The line-cap, mock-exports and import-cycle checks pass. The one red CI job on this head, `checks-node-changed`, fails only in `src/gateway/x-publication-owner-composition.e2e.test.ts` (404 vs 200), an X-publication route this PR doesn't touch. The exec e2e tests in the same job pass.


### Final-initiation recheck (revision 7)

**What was wrong.** The skill-authority recheck ran once, before launch preparation. The launch could then still await four things before the native spawn: standing-grant consumption (cron), secret-egress registration, the supervisor scope fence, and adapter preparation. The synchronous guards at the end of `runExecProcess` checked only source, operator and committed-policy/grant authority. So a skill uninstalled, or a bin repointed, during one of those waits still let the pinned command launch.

**What changed.**

- Each async re-resolution (`verifyGatewaySkillBinAuthority` in `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway-allowlist.ts`) now returns the authority it verified, and the recheck holds it. That held authority is the skill source revision (`getSkillsSourceVersion`, read before discovery), the bins that authorized the command, and the PATH they resolve on.
- A new synchronous check, `findStaleHeldGatewaySkillBinSegment`, rechecks that held authority. It denies in three cases: nothing was verified, the skill source revision moved (a skill was installed, removed or reconfigured), or an authorizing bin now resolves to a different executable. It uses the same `isSegmentAuthorizedBySkillBins` comparison as allowlist evaluation, so the single shared implementation is kept.
- `createGatewaySkillBinAuthorityRecheck` (in `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway-revalidation.ts`) exposes that check as `assertSkillBinAuthorityCurrent`. The gateway composes it into the `assertCurrent` it hands to the runtime: the committed-authorization assertion for the inline paths and detached approval, and the grant's assertion for cron standing grants.

**Where it runs.** `runExecProcess` passes that `assertCurrent` to the supervisor as `beforeSpawn`. It also wraps it into `initiateSpawn` (`createExecLaunchLifecycle().wrap`), which calls it synchronously right before `launch()`. No await sits between the check and the native spawn. All six launch paths go through it: inline ask, ask-fallback, auto-review allow-once, detached approval, direct allowlist, and cron standing grant. A refusal at initiation throws `GatewaySkillBinAuthorityWithdrawnError`, an `ExecProcessPreflightError`. The exec tool unwraps it into the usual denial result, and a detached launch reports it in its follow-up. On the cron path the grant has already been consumed when this final check refuses. That matches how the other final-initiation refusals already behave there.

**Regression tests.**

- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.skill-initiation.test.ts`, new. It runs the real gateway authorization, `runExecProcess`, supervisor, child adapter and native launch. The skill bin is a copy of `touch` that writes a marker file. Trust is withdrawn inside the secret-egress registration await, after the spawn preflight has passed. That is the only seam: the registry is wrapped through `importOriginal`.
  - `launches the skill bin while skill trust holds through initiation` is the allowed control. The marker is written.
  - `denies at native initiation when the authorizing skill is uninstalled after preflight`
  - `denies at native initiation when the trusted bin name is repointed after preflight`
- `detached approval launch denies at native initiation when trust is withdrawn after preflight`, in `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.auto-allow-skills.test.ts`. The supervisor stand-in uninstalls the skill and then calls the real `initiateSpawn` hook. The launch callback is never invoked, and the follow-up carries the skill denial.

With the fix (3 + 12 tests across the two files, all pass):

```
✓ launches the skill bin while skill trust holds through initiation
✓ denies at native initiation when the authorizing skill is uninstalled after preflight
✓ denies at native initiation when the trusted bin name is repointed after preflight
✓ detached approval launch denies at native initiation when trust is withdrawn after preflight
```

Without the fix (the three source files reverted, tests kept), the withdrawn command launches and runs:

```
× denies at native initiation when the authorizing skill is uninstalled after preflight
  → expected { status: 'completed', …(7) } to be undefined   (exitCode 0, exitReason "exit")
× denies at native initiation when the trusted bin name is repointed after preflight
  → expected { status: 'completed', …(7) } to be undefined   (exitCode 0, exitReason "exit")
× detached approval launch denies at native initiation when trust is withdrawn after preflight
  → Received: "Exec denied (gateway id=…, spawn-failed): skill-tool"   (initiation was not refused)
```

Checks: `pnpm tsgo:core` and the core test typecheck are clean. oxfmt and scoped core oxlint pass on the changed files. `check:changed` passes the line-cap growth ratchet, the max-lines suppression ratchet, the first-party mock export ratchet, the SQLite worker ratchet and format; the import-cycle check (0 cycles) and the remaining lint guards were run separately and pass. Its one failure is the dead-export scan, on `extensions/voice-call/src/types.ts: CallBrief`, which this PR doesn't touch. The gateway exec host tests and the cron-grant suite pass, with one exception. Locally, `executes a cron occurrence via a standing grant without prompting` fails with `service child cleanup identity lost`, and it fails the same way on the unmodified revision-6 head. It passed in CI on that head, so it is a local process-tree environment issue.

Not included yet: real-Gateway traces of delayed detached and standing-grant launches, with an allowed and a withdrawn-trust case. They are pending maintainer acceptance of the Gateway `autoAllowSkills` scope.



### Executing-agent skill ownership and real Gateway traces (revision 8)

Head: `0a4297accba` (one commit on top of `e0e151ea91b`; no rebase, the branch merges cleanly with main).

**What was wrong.** Tool assembly can borrow another agent's tool policy. `agent-tools.ts` then has two ids: `agentId`, the policy owner from the capability profile (`options.policyAgentId`, or the profile a caller passes in), and `executionAgentId`, the agent that actually runs (`options.agentId`, or the agent of `runSessionKey`). Exec defaults received only `agentId`, and `resolveGatewaySkillBins` used it. So under a borrowed policy, `autoAllowSkills` loaded the **policy** agent's workspace, while the run's skill snapshot (`skillScope`) came from the executing agent. A bin declared only by the policy agent's skill was trusted, and a bin declared by the executing agent's own skill was not.

**What changed.**

- `ExecSkillScope` gains `ownerAgentId`. `agent-tools.ts` now always sets `skillScope.ownerAgentId = executionAgentId`, next to the session filter and overrides from the same run's snapshot. Before, the scope was only set when a snapshot existed.
- `resolveGatewaySkillBins` (`bash-tools.exec-host-gateway-allowlist.ts`) resolves the workspace and the eligible skills from `skillScope.ownerAgentId`. It falls back to `agentId` only for callers that don't separate the two. That one resolver feeds all three skill checks: allowlist evaluation, the async re-resolution in `verifyGatewaySkillBinAuthority`, and the authority it holds. **Correction to the cron standing-grant wording (revision 6).** Revision 6 said the cron recheck means "a withdrawn skill denies the launch without spending the grant". That is too broad. The skill recheck applies only to segments the occurrence's own preflight admitted on **skill trust**. A command the operator explicitly allow-always granted runs on that grant, whether or not a skill still declares its bins. The grant was minted for the exact operation (command, cwd, env), so it authorizes the command independently of skill trust. Grant consumption in detail:

- **Not consumed:** the occurrence's preflight admitted a segment on skill trust, and the async recheck before consumption finds that trust withdrawn. The launch is denied and `useCount` is unchanged.
- **Consumed, then denied:** trust is withdrawn after consumption but before native initiation. The synchronous initiation check refuses the launch, and the use is already spent (as revision 7 noted).
- **Consumed, launched:** the skill is withdrawn before the occurrence starts. Its preflight then admits nothing on skill trust, the grant covers the whole command, and the occurrence runs on the grant. This is `occ3` below.
- **Grant not used at all:** every segment is admitted on skill or allowlist trust, so nothing asks. The command runs directly and the grant is neither checked nor consumed.

### Merged with main after the async exec-resolution cutover (revision 12)

Main's #197634 moved command and executable path resolution off the Gateway's synchronous path. `resolveExecutionTargetTrustPath` and the skill-bin PATH lookup are now async, and `safeRealpathSync` is gone from exec resolution. That conflicted with this PR in `src/infra/exec-approvals-allowlist.ts` and `src/node-host/runtime-skill-bins.ts`. The port:

- **One behavior change to the native-initiation recheck.** It still runs synchronously with no await before spawn, but now reads only in-memory authority: it denies when no skill authority was verified, or when the skill source revision moved since verification (a skill installed, removed or reconfigured). - This follows main's own split. prs.title: fix(plugins): reuse captured package metadata during reconstruction
prs.body:
Related: #197510, #200136, #200193.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: preparing a plugin can freeze other Gateway work while the main thread reopens package metadata already inspected by its preparation worker.

## User Impact

Plugin reconstruction reuses the metadata its existing owner already inspected. Optional malformed package bytes remain available for Node to reject with `ERR_INVALID_PACKAGE_CONFIG` when selected; unselected malformed metadata does not cause an earlier failure. No configuration or migration is needed.

This is a metadata-reader repair, not a claim that all plugin preparation or execution is nonblocking. Physical capture/retirement, native validation and module resolution remain separate boundaries. The candidate still showed a 276.5 ms whole-operation heartbeat gap and one unexplained 539.1 ms retirement observation in the measurements below.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker's existing metadata owner already holds parsed manifest facts, but runtime source custody omitted them, causing the host to reopen each private package.json. Carry those facts through existing custody, including the distinction between uninspected and inspected-invalid metadata. Consolidate optional parsing beside its state owner, delete the separate exported capture helper/setter handoff, and let frozen custody delegate to its artifact owner.

Production decreases by two lines across four existing modules; tests grow by 65 lines in two existing files. No new files, cache, worker, schema, configuration, physical-capture policy, native-integrity policy, or public protocol.

The wider audit follows read-only Team evidence 25c97908, 2026-11-16 05:02 PST: MAIN spent 1.97 s in `openat2(O_CREAT)` on `~/agents/roboclaw-x/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite.plugin-model-catalog.lock`, with `btrfs_create → start_transaction → wait_current_trans`; `scheduler:update.remote-model-catalog` stalled for 2,002 ms during a btrfs commit triggered by managed worktree removal. #200136 removed that lock. This PR removes a separate synchronous metadata reader; no Team data was copied or changed.

## Evidence

The real async preparation regressions fail on exact parent `9323fb9d`: two main-thread manifest reads for ordinary dependency preparation and three for malformed optional metadata, after correct scalar/native-error assertions. The fix passes 144 tests across five files, including generation worker/preparation, native conditions, frozen snapshots and recovery. Compiler-generation verification passes. Isolated Codex review is scoped-clean through P2; production remained frozen afterward. Control UI runtime import traversal reaches none of the four changed modules.

A serialized campaign contains five A/A pairs, five alternating A/B pairs, and two separate fault children; every process and wrapper exited successfully with exact source/workload hashes. Each timing process runs real cold and warm preparation, compiles/executes 20 typed modules, and retires the artifact. The deterministic metadata-stress fixture has 201 manifests / 843,446 JSON bytes and 200 typed sources / 13,107,200 bytes. It does not claim Team plugin size; the surrounding synthetic 35 GiB database and 62,000-file workspace are not scanned by this owner. Main-thread manifest reads fall from 201 to zero in both cold and warm preparation.

| Warm median | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Complete owner | 1,792.396 ms | 1,806.913 ms |
| Main CPU | 179.118 ms | 171.068 ms |
| Node process CPU | 1,957.852 ms | 1,969.699 ms |
| Main-V8 allocation | 122,229,552 bytes | 122,737,000 bytes |
| Prepared used-heap delta | 28,094,296 bytes | 28,100,936 bytes |

Warm owner time rose 0.81% (A/A 0.79%); cold owner time rose 1.32% (A/A 12.43%). Whole process-tree CPU rose 5.74% (A/A 3.39%). These are retained observed costs, not a general speedup or noise claim. Candidate warm retirement p95/max is **539.062 ms**, compared with baseline **55.790 ms**; with five samples, nearest-rank p95 is the maximum. That row has elevated non-main/system CPU but normal main CPU and nearly unchanged prepared heap. Physical retirement code/workload is unchanged, but the new metadata transfer can affect memory/scheduling. Phase CPU and GC were not sampled, so the cause is unknown; the observation was neither discarded nor rerun.

A separate two-second wait targets the actual captured root-manifest read. Baseline has one worker read and one MAIN replay; candidate has only the worker read. The baseline MAIN fault interval produces a **2,060.493 ms** heartbeat gap; during the candidate worker wait, the gap is **6.380 ms**. Whole-owner maximum gap is **2,060.493 → 276.501 ms**, and elapsed time is **6,137.637 → 4,020.821 ms**. The remaining whole-flow gap is explicit. This is Node 26.12.1 on APFS with fault injection, not direct btrfs latency; V8 allocation excludes other isolates/native allocation, and used-heap delta is not post-GC retained size.

`pnpm check:changed` completed with all format, lint, production types, 29 test type graphs and other applicable guards passing. It exits 1 only for 116 unused-export entries exactly matching the clean parent census, with no candidate-only entries. Four newer package-release exports are causally attributed to #198835 / `b868ed4c21ba0`; earlier named attributions are retained, but many test-support entries still lack an introducing commit. No blanket inherited-CI waiver, new allowance or threshold change is claimed. Exact-head CI and zero open final-head ClawSweeper items will gate landing.

Owner decision: accept the measured costs for this bounded responsiveness repair. That explicitly includes the unexplained candidate retirement p95/max of 539.062 ms versus 55.790 ms, warm owner +0.81%, process-tree CPU +5.74%, and the reported allocation/heap changes. Eliminating 201 duplicate MAIN reads and the demonstrated 2,060.493 ms main-thread fault stall is the intended gain. I accept the possible roughly half-second retirement delay in this workload; I am not labeling it noise, claiming an overall speedup, or asserting its cause is understood. Physical retirement is a separate owner boundary and remains in the wider audit. No sample is discarded and no passing replay is presented as a fix.

- #200073 (`30e9d3ee295e9`) moved Google registration to `loadGoogleLiveCatalog`. Remove the provider-only wrapper now used solely by tests and migrate its callers to the unchanged loader's provider result.
- #200056 (`24385a20428a3`) left a module-only session-history type and a test-only grouping export public. Keep those declarations private; tests inspect emitted groups through the existing continuation metadata reader.
- #200063 (`225d22fc5020`) deliberately removed the credential lookup path from replay identity. Remove the superseded profile-isolation test option/arm while retaining same-session replay, rejection across sessions, request authentication, usage, and transcript immutability assertions.
- #198133 (`18136c960eaf7`) added another continuation caller and intentionally limited the transcript wait to the current handoff. Migrate that new caller without changing its assertions. Update the real-Gateway test to require the initial generic handoff wait without an elapsed clock, then require its absence after a settled parent update and reload while the same child continues. Child activity, persisted parent lifecycle, completion, and exactly one parent resume remain checked.

Production code shrinks by six lines and test code by thirty-one lines. The obsolete elapsed-clock parser and polling helper disappear. No schema, configuration, production wait/replay boundary, timeout, or dependency-audit exemption changes.

The shared overflow fixture from the original PR revision is already identical on main through `472cd0a2f5425`; it is no longer part of this PR's diff.

A subsequent PR run exposed an obsolete screenshot-only scroll in the ACK ownership fixture. #155746 added it for captures; #178793 removed those captures but left the scroll. #181052 later introduced a legitimate lazy placeholder that can be replaced while Playwright waits for scroll stability. Remove only the unused scroll operation; all four receipt/ownership cases, draft/visibility/command assertions, send counts, and abort identity checks remain intact. The hosted log does not identify the detached node, so this does not claim a renderer defect or an inherited failure.

## Evidence

Scheduled run [43878996712](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43878996712) reported the three dead exports. The original repair's required changed-file check covered all 43 obligations: 36 passed in the original 537.99-second aggregate, and seven initially failed because compiler/declaration dependencies resolved outside the task checkout. After exact-version private dependency materialization, only the failed gates were replayed and passed. A candidate fixture type error was corrected with the real production snapshot type; that fixture has since landed independently. The original aggregate failure remains recorded, and successful gates were reused.

The first exact-head PR run [43917418516](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43917418516) failed. Its merge tree added #198133's third continuation caller after the original two-caller migration, causing TS2304 and a Bun ReferenceError. The correction integrates that exact main parent, `4a0e45492b898`, and migrates the third caller. The integrated pre-fix tree is identical to the actual failed CI merge `2746e91ef32c8`; this is a corrected PR/main interaction, not an inherited-failure waiver.

| Focused proof | Result |
|---|---|
| Google catalog and registration | 45/45 on Node and 45/45 on Bun |
| ClawRouter replay, exact qualified parent | Original two cases failed on Node and Bun; both pass after migration, one unrelated case unselected |
| Continuation UI owner, corrected exact CI tree | 44/44 on Node 24.22.1 and 44/44 on Bun 1.4.4 |
| Failed UI-chat type leaf and touched caller lint | Both pass |
| Chromium continuation E2E with production UI assets | Passes with both assistant groups and all four exact Resumed labels |
| Real-Gateway child handoff/update/reload | Original exact-main case fails at the stale wait assertion; migrated case passes with native child activity, persisted lifecycle, final completion, five parent requests, and complete Gateway/provider cleanup |

The corrected continuation proof took 4.63 seconds for the type leaf, 7.82/5.67 seconds for Node/Bun owner tests, 5.37 seconds for lint, and 31.88 seconds for Chromium including its production UI build. The real-Gateway case changed from an original failure at 19.900 seconds to a passing case in 16.572 seconds. These are validation costs, not production performance or allocation claims.

No new authenticated Google calls were made: the mechanical live-test migration receives the same provider value from the unchanged loader, with deterministic catalog and extension-test type proof. No live-provider behavior change is claimed.

Fresh complete eight-file Codex review and the subsequent full-fixture one-line ACK delta review are scoped-clean through P2. The newly affected UI E2E chat type leaf passed in 4.11 seconds and the changed wait-clock test lint passed in 4.56 seconds under Node 24.22.1; canonical formatting and diff checks also passed. Prior seven-file proof and independent wait-clock red/green proof remain bound to their exact source inputs.

Run [43928243586](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43928243586) at `5db76fd51b9d` again failed the ACK fixture before resolving the deferred receipt, at the obsolete scroll. After the one-line removal on that exact published head, all four original Chromium cases passed once (35.61 seconds wall; browser exited cleanly). All assertions and deadlines remain. The same run also failed `model-key-save-check.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts:155`: the first rejected-key Save took 2,520 ms against the unchanged 2,000 ms requirement. This key-save latency family is unresolved and also blocks #200133; this ACK-only correction does not fix it or establish that it is flaky or inherited. The original run's mobile sharing-access and Slack inline-identity failures remain separately investigated; their passing appearances in this run do not establish fixes. The run is terminal with 47 successful jobs, the two substantive failures above, the failed aggregate gate, and 25 skipped jobs. The final correction at `1e7bdc2b9040469af8beabbe669287e20a941bee` passed exact-head CI [43939175453](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43939175453): 49 successful jobs, 26 skipped, zero failures, including both real-Gateway shards and the combined CI gate. The prior key-save latency failure did not recur in this run; it remains unresolved, and this PR does not claim to fix it. ClawSweeper reviewed that exact final head with zero findings and zero open items. The unused worker fixtures remain owned by #200133. Later consolidation-related dead-export findings are reported separately, and a green changed-file export check does not imply the hourly unused-files gate is green.

prs.title: fix(claude-cli): completion turns lose child results above 10,000 characters
prs.body:
Closes #199633

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on the Claude CLI backend, a subagent completion delivered to a direct chat loses everything after the first 2,000 characters of the private context when the child result is longer than about 7,000 characters.

## User Impact

User impact: the requester agent receives the complete child result in completion turns, up to the documented 160,000-character findings cap, so long subagent reports reach the user intact instead of as a summary of their beginning. The same applies to any other private turn context above 10,000 characters on Claude CLI turns.

## Why This Change Was Made

Claude Code caps each hook `additionalContext` string at 10,000 characters. A longer string is saved to a file and the model gets only the path and a 2,000-character preview. Message-only completion turns have no tool that can open that file. The Claude Code hooks reference also says each hook's string is measured on its own and that Claude receives every value when several hooks return context for the same event.

OpenClaw now registers 20 `UserPromptSubmit` hook callbacks and returns one slice of the private context, at most 10,000 characters, from each. Context up to 10,000 characters still travels in the first callback exactly as before. Slices never split a surrogate pair. The privacy check that withholds turn context applies to every slice. Tool grants and the message-only policy are unchanged.

Accepted edge case: private context above 200,000 characters still spills its tail to the saved file, as all context above 10,000 characters does today.

## Evidence

- Live run through an isolated Gateway and real Claude CLI (see Runtime output). Base loses the tail of a long private context; head delivers it complete and in order.
- Regression test `extensions/anthropic/cli-runtime.test.ts` "keeps private context above Claude Code's hook limit readable". The fixture calls every registered prompt hook and applies Claude Code's per-string spill rule.
  - Base `4a0e45492b8`: fails, the model context is the spill notice plus the preview, without the tail marker.
  - Head `0cb5bc02717`: passes. With the runtime change reverted (`git apply -R`), it fails again the same way.
- `cli-runtime.test.ts` 71/71. With `cli-runtime.task-ownership`, `cli-runtime.yield`, `cli-runtime.nested-tasks`, `cli-process`, `execute-plugin.steering`, `prompt-context`, `prepare.durable-context` and `agent-tools.prefix-stability`: 155 passed, 1 skipped.
- `pnpm check:changed` against `163519e26c9`: 34 of 35 lanes pass, including typecheck, lint, format and the line-cap ratchet. The dead export scan fails on existing exports in files this PR does not touch. `git diff --check`: clean.
- Local ClawSweeper review (Claude runner, `--local-range`, base `origin/main`, head `0cb5bc02717`): complete, checkout verified, no findings, patch correct, security cleared. Ratings: overall C, proof D, patch B. The proof rating predates the live run below.

### What the live run covers

- Covered: an isolated QA Gateway with the `qa-channel` direct chat, the `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-5-5` model on a Claude subscription login, Claude Code 2.1.296, and a real inbound DM turn. A temporary local `before_prompt_build` plugin (not part of this PR) adds an 11,669-character report as `appendContext`, so the turn's private context, including OpenClaw's own runtime facts, is above 10,000 characters. That context reaches Claude through the changed `UserPromptSubmit` hook path. The first and last report lines carry markers that appear nowhere in the prompt. The same build ran twice, once with the two runtime files at base and once at head.
- Not covered live: the subagent completion trigger itself. On the proof host, `sessions_spawn` in the QA Gateway refused the child with "sessions_spawn model "claude-cli/claude-sonnet-5-5" is not usable: The selected account or native runtime is unavailable for claude-cli/claude-sonnet-5-5", although the parent turn ran on the same login. No child started, on base or head, so no completion turn ran live. A completion turn's child result reaches Claude through the same private context and hook path that the live run exercises.

### Runtime output

DM prompt: "Private context probe. This turn carries a private report in your context. Reply with exactly two lines and nothing else: the first line of that report, then the last line of that report, both copied exactly. Do not use any tools."

Command, run once per runtime: `pnpm openclaw qa suite --provider-mode live-frontier --cli-auth-mode subscription --model claude-cli/claude-sonnet-5-5 --alt-model claude-cli/claude-sonnet-5-5 --scenario <local context-proof scenario>`

Base runtime (`cli.runtime.ts` from `4a0e45492b8`, sha256 `e34c8bb8...0d17f`, one hook callback), final assistant text and the delivered DM:

```text
Report start CTX-HEAD-7Q2
I can't give the last line. The report was truncated in my context after Line 012, and I was told not to use tools to read the rest.
```

Head runtime (`0cb5bc02717`, sha256 `30626686...a9394`, 20 hook callbacks), final assistant text and the delivered DM:

```text
Report start CTX-HEAD-7Q2
Report end CTX-TAIL-Z3P
```

<details>
<summary>Claude Code protocol probe outside OpenClaw (Claude Code 2.1.325, tool-free turn)</summary>

Real Claude Code on the stream-json control protocol, one tool-free turn (`--tools ""`, like a message-only completion), with `UserPromptSubmit` hook callbacks returning a 12,088-character context that holds three markers. Machine-specific paths and IDs are redacted.

One callback with the whole string (what main sends today):

```text
mode=single context_chars=12088 chunks=12088
callback_order=UPS0
result:

<invoke:Read
<parameter name="file_path"><claude-projects>/<session>/tool-results/hook-<id>-UserPromptSubmit-<id>-1-additionalContext.txt</parameter>
</invoke>
error: File does not exist. Current working directory: <tmp>

<invoke:Bash
<parameter name="command">ls -la <claude-projects>/<session>/tool-results/ 2>&1; grep -o 'MARKER-[A-Za-z0-9_-]*' <claude-projects>/<session>/tool-results/hook-<id>-additionalContext.txt 2>&1</parameter>
</invoke>
error: Permission to use Bash has been denied.
exit=0
```

The same text split across callbacks of at most 10,000 characters (what this change sends):

```text
mode=split context_chars=12088 chunks=9000,3088
callback_order=UPS0,UPS1,UPS2,UPS3
result:
MARKER-HEAD-7Q2
MARKER-MID-K8V
MARKER-TAIL-Z3P
3
exit=0
```

</details>

prs.title: fix(sessions): stop self-only recall from scanning unrelated sessions
prs.body:
Related: #198855

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes slow or failed history recall under self-only visibility when unrelated session inventory is large or unavailable.

## User Impact

Self-only recall searches the current conversation directly, without waiting for an unrelated roster scan. Explicit targets, host-bound read scopes, sandbox clamps, incognito restrictions and broader visibility modes retain their existing authorization paths. This does **not** fix the separate broad-search fanout investigation.

prs.title: feat(ui): show prompt cache hit rate in the context popover
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The composer's prompt budget popover shows token counts and cost, but not how much of the prompt the provider served from its prompt cache. On long cached sessions the "In" count looks tiny (for example `In 6`) and gives no sense of whether caching is working.

## User Impact

The popover's two usage rows now show the prompt cache hit rate, to two decimals:

- **Latest run:** `Cache 99.34% · Cost $0.0024`. The run's In/Out token counts move to the row tooltip when the run is priced. Plan-billed runs (no cost) keep In/Out on the row.
- **Session total:** `Cache 49.79% · Cost $0.048`. Plan-billed sessions now also see this row with the cache rate only; the dollar figure stays hidden for them.

No new rows; no Gateway, protocol or storage change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Hit rate = cache reads ÷ (uncached input + cache reads + cache writes), the same formula the usage dashboard already uses.

- The run rate sums every model call since the latest user message from the transcript's per-message usage, so multi-call tool runs count fully.
- The session rate comes from the `sessions.usage` read the popover already makes for the session cost: no extra request.
- The value rounds down, so `100.00%` only appears when every prompt token was a cache read.

## Evidence

Real Gateway, real model (`openai/gpt-5.4-mini`), isolated state, same four-turn chat on the merge base and on this branch:

| Before (merge base) | After (this branch) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Popover before: Latest run In 29.2k · Out 51 · Cost; Session total Cost](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ecd545e-63f4-4724-901a-f3bd451c5050) | ![Popover after: Latest run Cache 99.34% · Cost; Session total Cache 49.79% · Cost](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3745b598-6493-425c-8d86-a9aff93fd3d9) |

The values shown match the Gateway: the last assistant message reported `input 192 / cacheRead 28928 / cacheWrite 0` (99.34%), and `sessions.usage` reported `58195 / 57728 / 0` for the session (49.79%).

- `ui/src/e2e/session-context-breakdown.e2e.test.ts` now covers a two-call cached run and the session total: red on the merge base, green here.
- Affected popover suites pass (`session-context-breakdown`, `chat-quota-pill-93041`, `chat-flow.navigation-presentation`: 19/19). `tsgo:ui`, `check:test-types`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean; full `ocx build --dts` build passes.
- New English strings only; other locales are filled by the locale refresh workflow after merge.

Merge danger: two-way door. UI-only rendering change; a revert fully undoes it. Blast radius: the Control UI composer context popover.

prs.title: fix(update): --no-restart update fails when the Gateway restarts itself during Doctor's stop
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update --no-restart` fails with `doctor-failed` and rolls the package back when the running Gateway restarts itself for the replaced installation while update Doctor is stopping it.

`--no-restart` leaves the managed Gateway running while the package is replaced. The Gateway's 30-second installation check sees the new `dist/build-info.json` and restarts the process. On a Linux systemd service, if that restart lands while the stop is in flight, the stop refuses with `Gateway process changed during maintenance drain`. Doctor fails, the update rolls back, and recovery verification then finds the restarted Gateway running the new version from the restored files.

Measured on plain `main` (b58c23cac0f, Docker cell): the exposed window is about 1.8 s per update, so roughly 5-6% of `--no-restart` updates with a running managed Gateway. One measured run missed the failure by 0.24 s.

## User Impact

User impact: a `--no-restart` update no longer fails or rolls back because the Gateway restarted itself for the new installation. The update stops the restarted process, records a warning in update history, and continues. As before, the Gateway that Doctor had to stop is started again on the updated installation.

A Gateway process that changes for any other reason during the stop is still refused, with the same message.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stop bound its authority to the PID it first inspected and treated every later PID as a foreign process. The Gateway's own restart for the replaced installation is the one change that is expected under `--no-restart`, and the exiting Gateway already records it in its boot lifecycle (reason `gateway.installation_replaced: ...`, with its PID).

The managed-service stop owns service inspection, so the fix is there. When the drain, or the Linux PID check just before the native stop, reports a changed process, the stop asks whether the latest recorded shutdown belongs to the PID it inspected and names the replaced installation. If so it inspects the service once more with the existing ownership, definition and ancestry checks, warns, and drains and stops the current process inside the same time budget. There is one re-inspection, and a second change fails as before. Matching on the PID needs no clock comparison.

Alternatives I rejected:

- Making the Gateway's installation check stand down during an update. The running Gateway is the installed version, so that fix would miss the first update onto a release that contains it, and it needs a new cross-process signal.
- Accepting any PID change of the same verified service. Simpler, but it also accepts an operator restart or a crash loop in the middle of the stop.

Two moves in this diff are mechanical. The maintenance module was already over the 700-line lint cap, which is an error for any touched file, so its update-history recording (`warn` and the stop record) and the pre-stop PID check moved to sibling modules unchanged. The shared shutdown-record read now also selects `pid`. `gateway status --json` and `update status --json` output is unchanged.

`withGatewayMaintenanceDrain` itself only gained a typed error. Its other caller, immutable activation, binds an explicit lease to one exact process and is unchanged. launchd and Windows have no PID check on this path.

### Still refused, on purpose or by scope

- A change the Gateway did not record. If the exiting Gateway could not persist its record, or the record cannot be read, the stop refuses as it does today. An unreadable record adds a warning that says so.
- systemd's restart delay. The managed unit has `RestartSec=5`. A stop that inspects the service in those seconds, when neither process is running, still fails, with a service ownership check that reports the service as unavailable. This is the same race at a different check. Handling it means letting ownership be verified for a unit in `activating`, which is a larger change than this one. I left it out.

### Release directories (#198835)

#198835 landed while this PR was open, and `main` is merged into this branch. It changes how the package path is replaced, not the maintenance stop, so the two do not overlap in code: no `update-command-service-*.ts` file changed on `main`, and the merge had no conflicts.

I read the paths that meet this fix. None changes what the stop assumes:

- The self-restart still happens on that layout. The Gateway's installation check reads `dist/build-info.json` through the package path (`resolveOpenClawInstallationRootSync` maps a release's real path back to its link). A release replaced in place, or a link moved to another release, both show the running Gateway a new build, and it restarts and records the same reason.
- The re-inspection runs the same ownership check with the same root as the first inspection in that stop. That check compares real paths, so a service that starts a release's real path and one that starts the package path are judged the same way both times.
- Nothing rewrites the service definition between the two inspections. Under `--no-restart` the service is not rebound at all.

This is from reading the code. I did not run the release cells with the Gateway up.

### Rollback side

After a failed `--no-restart` update, a Gateway can be running the new version from rolled-back files. This fix removes the trigger measured here. It also means a Doctor failure after the stop leaves a stopped Gateway, which recovery starts from the restored files. The state stays reachable when the update fails after the Gateway restarted itself and before the stop succeeds, for example in the restart-delay case above. That Gateway corrects itself on its next installation check, but recovery verification can report a version mismatch first. That needs its own handling in recovery verification and is not in this PR.

## Update behaviour

All of the fix runs in the new version's maintenance stop, which the installed updater starts from the replaced package through update Doctor. Nothing has to run in the installed updater or in the Gateway that is already running. It applies to the first update onto a release that contains it.

It depends on the running Gateway recording `gateway.installation_replaced:` as its shutdown reason. The 2026.11.4 source does. The installation check itself shipped in 2026.9.6.

A published driver x candidate run takes the new path only when the race occurs, which needs `--no-restart` and a Gateway restart during the stop. The default cell uses a managed restart and does not reach it.

No config, schema or protocol changes. No added waits.

## Evidence

The reproduction is deterministic and sits at the owner. The new test runs update Doctor's real predecessor stop (`stopSupervisedPredecessorGateway`), the real maintenance stop and drain, and the Gateway's real boot-lifecycle write operations and reader on a private state database. The service manager, its systemd policy helpers and the Gateway connection are simulated. The Gateway is replaced once, either before it answers the drain or after it answers and before the native stop.

`pnpm test src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-resident-restart.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`

- Red, production sources at 4e9812cdef8 (those files are identical on `main` at aa4d490a848, the commit merged into this branch): 4 failed, 4 passed. The two restart cases fail with the production errors, `Error: Gateway process changed during maintenance drain` and `GatewayServiceUpdateOwnershipError` with code `service-process-changed`.
- Green, head 4c63b23b15b (821f76db06e with `main` at aa4d490a848 merged in): 8 passed. Both restart cases stop the service once, write the stop receipt with the restarted process's PID, and record the warning in update history.
- Controls that pass on base and head: the same process change with an operator stop on record, and with an installation replacement recorded by an earlier process, is refused. The service is not stopped and no receipt or warning is written.
- Controls for the new path, red on base: a restarted Gateway whose service definition changed is refused at re-inspection, and a second process change after the accepted restart is refused.

The test passes Doctor no database write capture, and that matches the real update on this path. The updater hands Doctor its database generations only when it captured them with exclusive state ownership (`captureUpdateDatabases`, the same rule in 2026.11.4). A Gateway that is running at capture time holds that ownership, so the stop's receipt is the plain ledger write the test runs. If the Gateway is already between processes at capture time, the updater can capture, and the restarted Gateway's writes then meet Doctor's capture. That is the restart-delay family named above and is not covered here.

Other checks. All of these except the Docker run were rerun on the merged head 4c63b23b15b. `main` moved to 7cb238ad89a before the push (#200172, #200208). Neither touches these files, their callers or the tests below, so it is not merged here. #200172 changes Doctor's first admission of a database capture, which this path does not have.

- 16 related and consumer test files (drain, maintenance, immutable activation, Doctor maintenance, boot lifecycle, both status readers): 440 passed, 51 skipped, exit 0. The 51 skips are Linux-only tests on macOS, in `update-immutable-activation.test.ts`, `update-command-service-drain.native.test.ts` and `update-command-service.integration.test.ts`. CI has to cover them.
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: exit 0. The dead-export scan is skipped because it fails on `main` for three untouched files (`extensions/google/provider-catalog-runtime.ts`, `src/config/sessions/session-history-types.ts`, `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-agent-run-grouping.ts`). Run alone with this patch applied it lists only those three.
- `oxfmt --check` on the changed files and `git diff --check`: clean.
- `bash scripts/e2e/published-driver-update-docker.sh` (published 2026.11.4 updater, candidate built from this patch at cef2bbad990): PASS, update finished, `readyz` 200, running version verified. This ran before #198835 landed and was not rerun on the merged head, so it is evidence for the earlier head only. It is a regression check of the normal update path through the changed stop. It does not exercise the race: this cell updates with a managed restart, not `--no-restart`.

Test cost: one new file, about 260 lines, 13 s wall locally with about 5 s of test time. The first case pays the cold module load. No CI timing yet. It is registered with the database-worker (forks) test list because it needs the host SQLite broker. No existing test file changed and nothing was pruned.

Not proven:

- The live race was not reproduced end to end. The Docker update cell cannot force the window: the Gateway's check interval is a fixed 30 s with no test override, the cell drives a `systemctl` shim, and the tick phase depends on when the Gateway started relative to a 26-30 s package swap. I did not loop a timing-dependent run as proof.
- Real systemd behaviour, including the restart-delay case above.
- The shutdown-record read from inside the real update Doctor process, against a predecessor database that has not been migrated yet. By reading the code, state reads refuse newer schemas and not older ones, and a failed read keeps the old refusal.
- The unreadable-record warning branch has no test. Doctor's own maintenance stop shares the fixed owner but has no dedicated case for this race.

Review: the repository's autoreview helper cannot run on this machine, so an independent read-only reviewer agent reviewed the diff twice. The first pass led to PID attribution in place of a timestamp comparison, the definition-changed control, and naming the restart-delay case. The second pass found no blocking defect. Its points on the stop receipt PID, the shared drain budget, the non-snapshot read and the second-change test are applied.

## Follow-ups

- Once this is on `main`, the `in-place` Docker cell from #198835 (`test:docker:published-driver-release-in-place`, in `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/published-driver.mjs`) can run with the Gateway up again. It stops the Gateway before the `--no-restart` update to avoid this race. This PR leaves the cell unchanged.
- The systemd restart-delay case.
- Recovery verification after a rolled-back `--no-restart` update, as described under "Rollback side".

prs.title: improve: avoid repeated history scans before replies in long chats
prs.body:
Related: #185111

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: repeated history scans before replies in long SQLite chats. Demonstrated with Codex: recording the accepted prompt invalidates the history index, forcing another full scan before the next reply even though the conversation's structure has not changed.

## User Impact

User impact: later replies can reuse the history index instead of scanning the entire saved conversation again. In the 200,003-event Gateway proof, the second and third reads examined 325 and 327 navigation rows instead of about 200,000.

**The first uncached read is still slow.** Restarting the Gateway or genuinely changing the history can require another full scan. This addresses repeated scans between replies, not all of #185111. No settings, database format, or upgrade action changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing navigation index when a canonical user-message rewrite changes only private `__openclaw` metadata. Continue rotating the normal transcript generation, refreshing changed page sizes, and reading selected message payloads afresh. Real edits, replacements and copied histories still invalidate navigation; a read from an older SQLite snapshot cannot certify the next read's index. PostgreSQL retains its existing generation-based reuse.

When account usage and chat history share the agent database, updating usage also invalidates the history index. This PR prevents that unrelated invalidation while the existing auth receipt still refreshes account usage/health. Credential and shared-state writes retain their existing behavior.

Most of the diff in `session-accessor.sqlite-model-context.ts` is re-indentation; view it with whitespace hidden.

This complements #190615, which removes unnecessary additional history reads within a reply. It neither includes nor depends on that PR.

## Evidence

### Full-product repro on main

A built Gateway, native Codex app-server and QA channel processed three incoming messages against a seeded 200,003-event conversation. On main `b03fd2fed06`, the Gateway returned all three expected answers but scanned the entire archive before every turn:

```text
navigation rows: 200003 / 200005 / 200007
history read ms: 8452 / 7791 / 7694
```

### Live Gateway run: isolating the two causes

The same workload on `059db8a7c5a` shows why both corrections belong together:

| Change applied | First navigation read | Second | Third |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| History correction alone | 200,003 | 200,005 | 200,007 |
| Auth correction alone | 200,003 | 200,005 | 200,007 |
| Both corrections | 200,003 | 325 | 327 |

Captured combined-candidate summary:

```json
{
  "scannedRows": [200003, 325, 327],
  "historyMs": [5226, 528, 421],
  "messages": [3208, 3214, 3216]
}
```

With both, whole-history reads took 5,226 / 528 / 421 ms. All three answers were correct; selected message counts remained 3,208 / 3,214 / 3,216. Actual auth usage writes ran on every turn without clearing the history index. These are single-run timing observations, not a statistical speedup claim; work counts are the acceptance measure.

Proof artifice: synthetic saved history, temporary count/timing instrumentation, and a local scripted model with a declared 1,048,576-token capacity to avoid fixture-induced fallback. Built-in context handling was used; this is not a real-provider or Lossless Claw qualification.

### Regression and compatibility checks

The permanent tests cover bounded navigation work after prompt recording, fresh content after edits/replacement, an older read snapshot followed by a committed write, and auth-state freshness without unrelated history invalidation. Test lines are net +204 against `main`: reuses the existing model-context fixture and agent/shared-state table to protect distinct navigation-work, read-snapshot and auth-publication contracts; no permanent Gateway harness is added. The navigation-work and auth-scope assertions fail on unpatched code; the snapshot test also rejects the unsafe candidate that omitted the read-lifetime guard.

Earlier validation on `059db8a7c5a` passed 8 real PostgreSQL tests and exact returned-history/error comparisons across byte/event limits. The existing PostgreSQL inline-auth startup probe also fails on main with a missing `openclaw_engine_anchor`; the separate admitted-owner PostgreSQL tests passed. No schema or stored transcript bytes are changed by this optimization.

Current branch base: `1fa849cee30`. The candidate passed 113 targeted tests. The test-line check passed at +204/400; production and test type checks, changed-file lint and formatting passed. The broader check's unused-export failure also reproduces on unmodified main. Hosted CI has not run. Earlier runtime results above retain their original source versions.

prs.title: fix(ui): listed ACP sessions of agents outside agents.entries cannot be opened or deleted
prs.body:
<!-- template: .github/pull_request_template.md at upstream main 65cf8cdc378 -->

Related: #199373

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI sidebar lists ACP sessions (`agent:<harness>:acp:<uuid>`) of ACP agents that are not in `agents.entries`, but opening or deleting one fails with `Unknown agent id "<harness>"`, so the row cannot be removed.

## User Impact

User impact: describe and delete requests for these ACP sessions no longer fail with `Unknown agent id` when the UI path sends the harness id, so the rows can be deleted again, single or batch, without adding the harness to `agents.entries`.

Not fixed here: opening such a session still shows "Couldn't load this conversation: Unknown agent id". The chat page also calls agent-scoped methods (`chat.metadata`, `models.list`, `board.get`, `talk.catalog` and others) that reject an agent outside `agents.entries`. That needs its own change.

## Why This Change Was Made

`sessions.list` keeps these rows on purpose since #83397. The UI then sent the harness id as an explicit `agentId` next to the session key. The Gateway rejects an explicit id outside the agent roster, and #164993 pins that rejection as intended, while the same request without the id is admitted through the key.

The shared session request builder and the describe owner now drop `agentId` when it only repeats the agent of a free ACP key. This follows the #164993 fix for `sessions_history`. A different `agentId` and every non-ACP key still send it, so roster, global alias and ownership checks are unchanged. The Gateway is not changed.

Alternative: #199398 fixes the same issue on the Gateway side, by accepting an explicit `agentId` that matches the key's agent.

## Evidence

Base 65cf8cdc378, head df871cfecc2.

- Real Gateway: isolated Gateway on a pinned port with temp state, `agents.entries: { main }`, `acp.allowedAgents: ["claude"]`, and one ACP session seeded the way an ACP spawn persists it (session row plus canonical ACP metadata). Requests use the params the Control UI's own request builders produce at each commit.
  - Base: `sessions.list` returns the row, short URL resolve works, and `sessions.describe` and `sessions.delete` fail with `Unknown agent id "claude"`. The row stays.
  - Head: describe and delete succeed and the row is gone from `sessions.list`. An explicit harness `agentId` is still rejected by the Gateway.
  - Browser run (Playwright, same kind of isolated Gateway, Control UI from source): the Sessions page lists the ACP rows, and single and batch delete there work on both base and head, because that page already sends no `agentId`. Opening a row fails on both base and head, as noted above. prs.title: fix(chat-ui): keep a budget-rejected voice note recoverable
prs.body:
Closes #193813

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: finishing a voice note in a nearly full attachment draft destroys the recording. `addVoiceNoteAttachment` deleted the capture file in an unconditional `defer`, the aggregate-budget rejection from `stageAttachment` was ignored, and the recorder returned to idle — so removing another attachment could not recover the note, and the only copy of the recording was gone.

## User Impact

User impact: a capture the aggregate budget rejects is now retained with its file and surfaced in the composer as a retry/discard row. Removing an attachment retries it automatically (the issue's recovery case), the Retry button re-stages against the current budget, and Discard deletes the file explicitly. Successful staging still removes the temporary file, and the upload limit itself is unchanged. Recordings over the per-note 5 MB limit or unreadable files are still discarded, since no amount of freed budget can admit them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recorder handoff now retains a capture the draft cannot admit instead of destroying it. The retained note (`OpenClawRetainedVoiceNote`, module-internal: recording URL, duration, and the exact localized rejection message captured at retention time) belongs to the draft that recorded it:

- The draft pins its owner (`isAttachmentOwnerPinned`, send paths, and programmatic `send()`) until the note is staged or discarded, so a pending session switch cannot strand it; `syncSession` completes after the note resolves.
- Removing an attachment retries staging synchronously through the MainActor retry guard; the voice-note button is disabled while a note is retained, so there is never more than one retained capture and no supersession races.
- Retry validity is identity-based (`retainedVoiceNote?.recording == recording` re-checked after every await), so a discarded note's bytes cannot reappear; the rejection banner is cleared by exact message match, which is locale-safe.
- Discard deletes the file explicitly; staged transfers delete it; a fresh `readAndStageVoiceNote` failure with a superseded or cleared retention leaves the draft untouched.

## Evidence

- Regression tests in `ChatFileAdmissionTests.swift`: the retained note keeps the draft pinned ("Keep this recording with the draft" scenario — pending session switch waits, auto-retry after removal admits the note into the original draft, then the switch completes) and a short-budget retry keeps the note until discard. The parametrized `all staging paths count existing attachment bytes` voice branch pins retention plus explicit-discard deletion; aggregate enforcement stays pinned; the success/oversize/malformed-duration tests pass against the retained signature.
- Two independent review rounds drove the implementation (a compile-level setter visibility defect, a locale-dependent error-prefix match, and lifecycle/concurrency gaps including discard-retry resurrection and duplicate staging); the final design replaces the generation counter with draft ownership plus identity re-validation, reviewed to confirmation.
- Local gates on this commit: `swiftc -parse` clean on all nine touched Swift files, `scripts/format-swift.sh ios` reports 0/514 files needing formatting, `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passes (inventory carries the new apple-surface strings). This host has Command Line Tools only — no full Xcode — so the SwiftUI SDK macro plugins cannot load and the native build/test gate is the iOS/macOS CI on this PR, consistent with `docs/platforms/mac/dev-setup.md`.

## Current review status

Draft: the repair for the published revision's build failure is pushed as the current head. Remaining before ready, per the review plan: hosted iOS/macOS build lanes on this head, the focused regression suites in CI, and isolated iOS simulator evidence covering recording, rejection, retry, and discard.

prs.title: fix(goals): require a note to resume a blocked goal
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resuming a blocked goal with an empty note made it active again and queued another pursuit turn. The operator had not said what changed, so the same blocker came back. A blocked goal now stays blocked until the resume includes a note. Paused, limited, and completed goals can still resume without one.

The command table and the blocked-status paragraph still told people that a bare `/goal resume` makes a blocked goal active. Those two lines now say the note is required, and that an empty resume leaves the goal blocked.

## Evidence

Head `834bd8c1ed7` on macOS. An isolated loopback Gateway served the Control UI. Session `agent:main:main` held a blocked goal whose objective was `Read the operator inbox.`

In the browser, Resume with an empty note showed `Enter what changed before resuming.` The Gateway did not receive `sessions.goal.update`.

Typing `The mail grant is still missing, so stop this goal.` and choosing Resume called the Gateway. The card changed from `Goal blocked` to `Pursuing goal`, and the same run started a model turn.

```console
[ws] res ok sessions.goal.update 65ms runId=aa506ced-2261-46a0-b6a5-c3948291ae49
[ws] event agent run=aa506ced-2261-46a0-b6a5-c3948291ae49 agent=main session=main stream=lifecycle phase=start
[openai-transport] responses start provider=xai model=grok-4.7 sessionKey=agent:main:main runId=aa506ced-2261-46a0-b6a5-c3948291ae49
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A blocked goal cannot resume from the Control UI until the operator enters what changed. That noted Resume is admitted by `sessions.goal.update` and starts the model continuation. An empty note stays on the card and does not call the Gateway.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node v26.12.1, worktree `/tmp/oc-192883`, head `834bd8c1ed7`. Loopback Gateway and its Control UI in Chromium. Model `xai/grok-4.7`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Open the chat for `agent:main:main` with a blocked goal. Choose Resume with an empty note. Enter a note and choose Resume again. Read the Gateway log for `sessions.goal.update` and the following model turn.
- **Evidence after fix:** Control UI text and Gateway log:

  ```console
  empty note: Enter what changed before resuming.
  after note: Pursuing goal
  [ws] res ok sessions.goal.update 65ms runId=aa506ced-2261-46a0-b6a5-c3948291ae49
  [ws] event agent run=aa506ced-2261-46a0-b6a5-c3948291ae49 stream=lifecycle phase=start
  [openai-transport] responses start provider=xai model=grok-4.7 sessionKey=agent:main:main
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The empty Resume stays on `Goal blocked` and does not call the Gateway. The noted Resume returns `sessions.goal.update`, switches the card to `Pursuing goal`, and starts the `grok-4.7` turn.
- **What was not tested:** A goal database written by the latest stable package, then opened by this build. The blocked goal in this run was created on this head.

## Summary

A blocked goal stays blocked until `/goal resume` or the Control UI Resume includes a note. The command table and the blocked-status paragraph say that. Paused, limited, and completed goals can still resume without a note.

prs.title: feat(templates): install local projects through live Gateway
prs.body:
Closes #196193

## What Problem This Solves

Template authors cannot install unpublished local projects while their Gateway is running without downtime or premature ClawHub publication.

## User Impact

Install with `openclaw templates add ./my-template`, or click **+ Import** in the Templates page header to choose a `.tgz` from your computer. Selection opens a review modal with the filename, disclosures, and a **Choose another file** action; installation still requires explicit confirmation. No Gateway restart is needed.

Templates remain Labs-gated. Local paths refer to the **Gateway host**; browser uploads transfer the selected archive. Neither source is published to or scanned by ClawHub. Online `--workspace` overrides are rejected; offline behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both entry points reuse the existing Gateway Add owner, consent, integrity checks, leases, rollback, and runtime activation—rather than bypassing its state lock. Preview/apply are bound to canonical artifact integrity; local/upload sources require current operator-admin authority. No new state store or configuration option.

- Upload limits: **1 MiB compressed / 8 MiB extracted / 4,096 entries**, with unsafe-path/link rejection and temporary cleanup.
- Diagnostics contain correlation ID, source kind, stage, outcome, and duration—not archive bytes, template contents, request data, or caught errors.
- Invalid-project responses include corrective validation guidance.
- Latest repair preserves explicitly empty `--agent-id ""` for validator rejection, uses the canonical source type in handler tests, and fixes real-Gateway CI routing and inventory ordering.

## Evidence

### Main-conflict resolution — `f8842fe40b3c32205fec8cc7945d41be3f5c170e`

Integrated main through `b21829a4c85f` without rewriting the existing PR commits. Three content conflicts were resolved:

- `test/vitest-ui-e2e-config.test.ts`: retain both browser-pair-code and Template upload in serial-Gateway expectations.
- `test/vitest/vitest.ui-paths.mjs`: retain both real-Gateway test registrations.

Main's auto-merged catalog detail, automations naming, and config-activation changes were also checked. Fresh independent review of the conflict resolution and those integration contracts found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

**Post-integration proof:** all **54 affected tests passed** (15 UI E2E inventory/ownership, 30 Gateway Add handlers, 6 Template schema validators, 3 CLI ownership), core typecheck, focused lint/format, and staged diff checks passed. The Chromium real-built-Gateway upload scenario also passed (**1 test**, test body **12.73s**), exercising header picker → modal review → explicit Add → persisted agent config/workspace. Production Gateway/configuration untouched.

The WebKit and upgrade evidence below remains **prior-head evidence**; it was not rerun after this main integration. New-head broad CI remains separate. The existing hosted ClawSweeper review is in progress against `dfcd6f485d74`, not this integration head; no duplicate active request was posted. No PR merge is authorized/requested.

### Header Import UX — `dfcd6f485d748e7b396826e4cfb47be1674198ed`

**WebKit verification passed on 2026-11-10.** Playwright WebKit **27.2** ran the existing `ui/src/e2e/template-upload.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` scenario against an isolated built Gateway and production Control UI assets: **1 test passed**, test body **16.52s**, Vitest duration **42.12s** (excludes build/setup). Runtime logging confirmed `engine=webkit version=27.2`.

The test clicks the header Import button, receives a native filechooser event, selects a real `.tgz`, checks the review dialog and selected filename, explicitly confirms Add, checks the installed-agent message, and verifies persisted agent config/workspace. It also compares the served entry asset hash with the built asset. Screenshots of the header, review controls, and installed state were retained locally and inspected. The review screenshot is scrolled to the manifest/footer, not the full disclosure panel.

**Harness scope:** the shared E2E launcher currently hardcodes Chromium. For this run only, its browser factory was temporarily replaced with `webkit.launch({ headless: true })`, omitting Chromium-only connection/executable/arguments; assertions, fixtures, application code, and Gateway behavior were unchanged. The launcher was restored after the run and the checkout is clean. The wrapper still initializes/logs its unused Chromium pool; the actual scenario browser was independently identified as WebKit above. This is Playwright WebKit proof, not a manual Safari/native-macOS file-dialog test or a permanently added WebKit CI lane.

Focused invocation (with that temporary launcher adaptation):

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/template-upload.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
```

Earlier verification of this same header-import change passed the Chromium real-Gateway scenario (1 test), Template review tests (2 tests), UI typecheck, scoped lint/format, and i18n baseline.
