prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/188252

## What Problem This Solves

Same-version V1 decision delegation snapshots the full admitted state even though result validation needs only its original questions.

## User Impact

No intended behavior or public contract change. Caller and question mutation protection, live authority, admission, deadlines, physical settlement, cross-version conversion and final result cloning remain required.

## Why This Change Was Made

For a V1 caller delegated to a V1 provider, keep the offered batch object and every field while cloning its questions. A V2 caller delegated to V1 retains the complete batch clone. Provider-V2 paths are unchanged.

The production change is confined to provider-host.ts. The proof amendment extends the existing committed decision transport driver/worker, with only necessary build provenance changes. It reuses the unchanged shared harness and keeps HTTP as the default, with case-specific imports and results. No product instrumentation, compatibility bypass, cast or runtime option is added.

## Declared protocol (recorded before the first workload)

- Exact baseline: 0eb84f967507089583117c874983c8358e991fcf. Local signed candidate and shared benchmark revision: afa38a32c75b2f58c10dffc18c2c131ac2bdb6b7. Hosted source is still 377cfd1e3d984ff7e63e31253fd896523eb29107; the local correction is unpublished until normal exact-candidate READY.
- Actual flow: production registry and plugin registration, host-issued operator authority, evaluateDecisionInRegistry, normal V1 host and owned-instance disposal. The provider deliberately mutates its admitted state/questions; independent expected answers, caller preservation and returned-result cloning are checked. No direct host/helper evaluation or fake admission replaces this path.
- Fixed small JSON fixture: 32-byte evidence string and one boolean question. Near-limit fixture: 1,046,528-byte evidence string in the same shape, below the existing 1,048,576-byte JSON admission limit with framing headroom. Both use the identical registered production route.
- Work-only runs temporarily wrap the original native structuredClone, forwarding all arguments/options/results unchanged. The known caller fixture and its admitted native clone are identified by reference; unrelated input is not traversed or read. The binding is restored in finally before disposal. State-bearing arguments are counted separately from question/result clones. Prediction only: state-bearing work 2 to 1 per evaluation; total calls unchanged.
- Cost runs keep the original unwrapped native function throughout. For EACH small/near-limit cell and each work/cost mode: 20 serial interleaved ABAB pairs, 50 evaluations per fresh worker, same committed worker/harness and matched frozen manifest/lock/workspace/runtime/platform. First measured entry after registration/setup is cold; no checksum/warmup consumes it. The other 49 entries supply warm median/p95.
- Report raw work counts, median/p95/min/max spread, complete command/worker wall/CPU/RSS, host load and separate ordinary Node CPU profiles on the real hot path. Work-mode timing is not cost evidence. Source/input/output hashes bind both exact builds; an eligible physical native graph may serve them only exclusively and serially after full input qualification.
- Acceptance: all existing behavioral/authority/mutation/lifetime oracles remain green, predicted work must be measured, every remaining performance gate applies, and a 20% adverse cell is STOP. A worse metric needs explicit owner acceptance under normal policy; no noise waiver or failed-cell retry.


## Measured results — landing held

Both exact revisions passed all96 tests in the five unchanged owning suites: runtime, runtime-V2, compatibility, runtime admission and runtime preparation. This includes mutation, cross-version, live authority, deadline and physical-settlement contracts. Script types, targeted type-aware lint, formatting and line-cap checks pass; the shared harness remains unchanged. Fresh full-range local ClawSweeper review from the baseline through the local candidate found no actionable correctness/security findings (confidence0.88).

Each fixture's work-only run completed20 ABAB pairs, 50 evaluations per worker:1,000 successful registered evaluations per revision, with owned-instance teardown and native-binding restoration. All20 workers per revision had the following exact cohort counters:

| Native arguments per50 evaluations | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| All structuredClone calls | 150 | 150 |
| Known state-bearing batch arguments | 100 | 50 |
| Known admitted questions | 0 | 50 |
| Provider results | 50 | 50 |

These are measured argument counts, not allocation bytes or deleted calls. Actual encoded input sizes were98 bytes and1,046,594 bytes (state evidence32 and1,046,528 bytes; one question). The counters are whole-worker cohort totals: they do not separately emit a first-entry/warm argument-count partition. Timing separates those phases, and that count-reporting detail remains a proof gap.

Ordinary unwrapped cost also completed20 ABAB pairs per fixture, with the same committed worker/harness on both exact revisions. Values below are median / p95 [min,max]; time and CPU are milliseconds, RSS is bytes.

prs.title: fix(macos): retain Peekaboo generation across refreshes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Routine macOS capability refreshes rebuild the Peekaboo computer-use descriptor. A new generation on every read makes the unchanged provider look like a replacement and causes unnecessary node reconnects.

## User Impact

An unchanged Peekaboo provider keeps its node connection identity across routine refreshes. Changing providers still rotates the generation and invalidates the old route.

## Why This Change Was Made

The macOS node coordinator owns the Peekaboo generation for its provider lifecycle and changes it only when the selected provider changes. Existing connect-option equality and route invalidation remain in place.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto `openclaw/openclaw:main` at `ec46689460eca425f101ef9366b6f28f881bcd54`; resolved the two conflicts while preserving the upstream bounded-native-bridge test.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`: passed.
- Current-head checks for `110847813b25b57dc47f722d63c3ddec5b5523d6` are running: [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43507960134). This repair session did not run the native tests locally.
- Historical hosted macOS proof for the prior head `1df0eda5b877f3032b803974e9105e011b311d74` against base `ce7788f5a24e5e2d0ef146a5dcea3ef4d0bb0983` passed 82 tests across 4 suites: [previous run](https://github.com/aashish254/openclaw/actions/runs/42691454605). That result predates this rebase and is not current-head proof.
- The native tests use an in-process `GatewayTestWebSocketSession`; they do not launch an interactive OpenClaw.app or connect to a separate live Gateway process.

## What Problem This Solves

The source-scan test fixture forgets temporary directories when removal fails, preventing a later cleanup attempt.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Failed fixture removals stay tracked for retry, while healthy roots are removed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing async hook now uses the shared cleanup owner after settling and resetting its pending scan. All five declarations / eight cases remain, including concurrency, ordering, byte limits, decoding, error propagation, and file mutations through both collect and map. The `rm` import remains for the deletion case.

## Evidence

- Actual Vitest-hook fault injection on baseline and candidate: the original removal error propagates, every root remains intact while a real scan is held, and the pending scan is reset before removal. Baseline loses the failed root and never retries it; candidate retains it, removes the healthy sibling, and succeeds on retry.
- Each fault run has one intentional hook failure and seven passing cases. Temporary instrumentation was removed and exact candidate bytes restored.
- All eight clean cases pass on baseline and candidate (1.71 s / 1.88 s command time). These establish correctness, not a performance comparison.
- Scoped scripts-test typecheck, targeted lint and formatting, both line-cap ratchets, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent classification, repair planning and preservation review found no blockers. Local ClawSweeper reviewed `10f6b53ce51827256689604e821c34a7f5e84323..404e9f680d4aee8891611cd828df95a26a8b32aa` at high reasoning: no actionable findings. The subsequent commit records proof only.
- Test code is +2/-1 lines; production and shared helpers are unchanged.

- CI run [43869870450](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43869870450) completed with 17 runner-setup failures caused by Boat's exhausted daily sandbox-start allowance. Each stopped before checkout; no candidate code executed in those jobs. All 61 jobs are terminal, no jobs were cancelled, and security-fast passed. prs.title: fix(cli): request scopes a session-only device grant covers
prs.body:
Related: #199692

Depends on #199693. This branch is stacked on it, so until #199693 merges the diff also shows its commits.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a device paired with only `operator.sessions.write`, as the multiplayer guide recommends for guests, can't use `openclaw gateway call` or `openclaw tui`. The CLI asks for `operator.read` and the TUI for admin, read, write and approvals, so every connect becomes a scope-upgrade request for the admin.

## User Impact

User impact: a session-only guest can list, read and create its sessions from the CLI and use the TUI within its grant. Once the TUI has stored the grant with a device token, its connections and `gateway call` file no upgrade request. Behind trusted-proxy auth the Gateway issues the TUI no device token and `gateway call` stores none, so there each connection is refused once with a scope-upgrade request and then works within the grant. #199699 removes that refusal as a Gateway opt-in.

Devices whose grant holds the general scope are unchanged, and a device that needs a real upgrade (for example `operator.read` to `operator.admin`) still files one.

In the TUI, a session-only device gets no command list or pending approvals, because those need `operator.read` and `operator.approvals`.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Where the client learns its grant:**
- `gateway call` projects its least-privilege scopes through the stored device grant with the existing `projectOperatorScopesForMethod`. It narrows only when the method's session-scoped alternative still authorizes the call.
- The TUI connects within a stored grant that holds `operator.sessions.*` and none of its default scopes, unless `--token` or `--password` is given.

**A device approved before it ever connected:** it has no stored grant, so its first request can exceed it. The Gateway's scope-upgrade refusal already reports `approvedScopes`, and the client uses that:
- The gateway client gains an opt-in `fitScopesToApprovedGrant` hook that reconnects once within the reported grant, which the TUI uses.
- `gateway call` retries once with the session grant.
- The TUI stores the device token it receives with the grant, so its later connections, and `gateway call` reading that stored grant, fit it. `gateway call` keeps its read-only storage mode on the retry and stores nothing.

Until a grant is stored, each connection still files that request first, because nothing tells the client its grant before it asks. Behind trusted-proxy auth nothing is stored, so that holds for every connection. The opt-in Gateway change in #199699 removes it.

**Moves:** two moves keep the touched files within the line-cap ratchet without changing behaviour:
- CLI scope selection, including the existing `sessions.create` cwd escalation retry, moves to `src/gateway/call-scopes.ts`.
- The gateway client's host-dependency defaults move to `packages/gateway-client/src/client-host-deps.ts`. `client.ts` re-exports their types, so the package API is unchanged.

**Docs:** `docs/start/multiplayer.md` and `docs/cli/tui.md` describe the guest behaviour and when the first-connect request remains.

## Evidence

- **New tests:**
  - `src/gateway/call.stored-grant-scopes.test.ts` 5/5. A session-only grant reads with `operator.sessions.read`; a read grant and a method without a session scope keep their request; a refused request retries with the reported grant and keeps read-only storage on both attempts (this case fails without the read-only fix); a grant that can't serve the method does not retry.
  - `packages/gateway-client/src/client.approved-grant.test.ts` 3/3, against a real WebSocket server that refuses with a scope upgrade: reconnects once within the reported grant; pauses without the hook, or when the hook keeps the request.
  - `src/tui/gateway-chat.connection.test.ts` 16/16, adding session-only, read, `operator.pairing` and `--token` grants.
  - Without this change, the session-only, retry, `operator.pairing` and `--token` cases fail; the keep-behaviour cases pass on both.
- **Existing tests:** `call.test.ts` 91/91, `client.test.ts` 95/95, `client.handshake.test.ts` 22/22, `client.device-auth.test.ts` 25/25, `reconnect-policy.test.ts` 19/19, `tui.test.ts` 51/51.
- **Static checks:** typecheck, lint and format are clean.
- **Restack onto #199693's pairing hint:** this branch now sits on `a675d1b23b7`, which adds the `openclaw gateway call` hint for an unpaired edgeAuth device and keeps an explicit `--url` in it. `git range-diff 3411a94ae50..48d8e528f08 a675d1b23b7..74994fa1a99` shows this branch's two commits unchanged, and the runs below were made at `48d8e528f08`, before the restack. prs.title: fix(auto-reply): show revoked queued input as a withheld failure instead of a silent cancel
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A queued follow-up whose operator authority was revoked (token rotated, device or role revoked) was consumed as an abort. Only a log line recorded it ("canceled input after loss of operator authority"). The chat showed nothing, and the source of the input got an abort instead of a failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

- A revoked queued input now settles like the other terminal follow-up failures. The reply operation fails with the refusal reason (`run_failed`). The source gets a failed completion with the notice `withheld: <reason>`, which the chat send path already shows to the user.
- This also applies when the refusal happens before turn admission. In that case no turn exists, so the source is settled directly from the queued input.
- The authority probe has one owner, `isFollowupOperatorAuthorityCurrent` in `queue/types.ts`. The drain, the stalled-turn handoff and goal continuation use it instead of their own `try { assertCurrent() }` copies.

Out of scope: subagent completion delivery after a `session.store` switch is unchanged. The store-switch boundary stays: a child result from the old store must not reach a same-key chat in the new store (#152288).

## Security model

- No authority is widened. Revoked input is still refused and is never replayed.
- The only change is that the refusal is visible and reported as a failure.

## User Impact

- A queued message that is refused after access is revoked shows a `withheld: <reason>` failure instead of disappearing.

## Evidence

- `followup-runner.test.ts`: two tests (revoked input refused before admission, and refused during execution). Both fail on the merge base f4fa17a7 and pass on the head.
- `subagent-registry.store-replaced.test.ts` passes on the head. The PR has no diff in `src/agents` or `src/gateway`.
- Real Gateway check of a config commit that touches `env.*` while a child runs (base and head): on both, the Gateway defers the restart, delivers the child result to the parent (requester-settle run ends with `stopReason=stop`) and then restarts. This is why the store-switch boundary is kept.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm check:test-types` pass.

prs.title: feat(gateway): connect approved trusted-proxy CLI and TUI devices within their grant
prs.body:
Related: #199692

Depends on #199698. This branch is stacked on it, so until #199698 merges the diff also shows its commits.

## What Problem This Solves

A device approved for fewer scopes than its client requests, such as a team guest approved for only `operator.sessions.write`, can't know its grant before it connects. Its first connection after approval therefore always files a scope-upgrade request, for scopes the admin already decided not to give.

## User Impact

User impact: with the new opt-in `gateway.auth.trustedProxy.narrowToDeviceGrant`, an approved CLI or TUI device behind the trusted proxy connects within its grant from the first connection. No upgrade request is filed and no audit entry is written. The TUI also keeps a device token, as the CLI already does. When named operator roles are enforced, a human operator identified by the proxy still receives no device token, as before; their CLI and TUI connect within the grant on every connection without storing it.

The option defaults to `false`, so existing Gateways behave exactly as before.

With the option on, `openclaw security audit` reports a new warn-level finding, because the TUI's token, like the CLI's, authenticates a direct Gateway connection without the proxy identity until the device is revoked.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Existing mechanism:** the Gateway already narrows a same-key scope upgrade to the paired grant, with no pairing request or audit entry, for browser and native UI clients when `trustedProxy.deviceAutoApprove` is enabled. This change gives that lane to CLI and TUI devices under its own option.

**Which connections it applies to:** same-key operator devices that authenticate through the trusted proxy and send no browser `Origin`. For those:
- A request that exceeds the grant connects with the intersection, and the hello reply reports the resulting scopes. That is how a newly approved device learns its grant.
- A connection never receives more than the grant. A request that includes `operator.admin` overlaps every grant, because admin implies every operator scope, so it connects within the grant.
- Only a request that shares no scope with the grant, such as `operator.pairing` alone against a session-only grant, still files the upgrade.
- Browser clients and new device enrollment are unchanged.

**TUI device token:** trusted-proxy auth treats the TUI like the Control UI and issued it no device token. Under the option it gets one, so it keeps the grant between runs. With the option off, its default, nothing changes. Named-role human operators stay tokenless either way.

**New audit finding:** `gateway.trusted_proxy_narrow_to_device_grant` (warn). `deviceAutoApprove` already reports a warn finding; this option reported nothing. The finding and `docs/gateway/trusted-proxy-auth.md` tell the admin to keep the proxy as the only Gateway ingress, and to remove a device with `openclaw devices remove <deviceId>` when its user's access ends.

**Config-surface budget, 2654 to 2655:** the option adds one boolean key, so the core count in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` grows by exactly one. It has to be an option rather than a default because it changes which connections file upgrade requests and which clients hold device tokens; existing admins rely on both. No existing key fits: `deviceAutoApprove` also auto-approves new device enrollment, which an admin who only wants guests to stay within their grant should not have to accept. No other config is added.

**Docs:** `docs/gateway/trusted-proxy-auth.md` gains a section for the option, its config reference entry and the audit checklist line. The section says that the option is off by default and that named-role human operators get no device token. `docs/start/multiplayer.md` points guests' admins to it. `docs/cli/tui.md` marks the TUI's trusted-proxy behavior without a device token as the default and links the option.

## Evidence

- **Server tests:** in `src/gateway/server.auth.trusted-proxy-device-autoapprove.test.ts` 20/20:
  - An approved session-only TUI connects within its grant and receives a device token, with no pending request and no upgrade audit line.
  - The same holds for a CLI requesting `operator.read`, which connects with `operator.sessions.read`.
  - With the option off, the TUI still files the upgrade.
  - Without the Gateway change, the TUI and CLI cases fail; the option-off case passes on both.
- **Audit test:** `src/security/audit-gateway-exposure.test.ts` 27/27, with the finding present only when the option is on. Without the finding, the new case fails. `audit-gateway.test.ts` 8/8.
- **Config tests:** `zod-schema.gateway-auth.test.ts` 57/57, `doc-baseline.integration.test.ts` 10/10, `configure.gateway.test.ts` 16/16. Typecheck, lint and format are clean.
- **Rebased on current `main` with #199693's pairing hint:** this branch is now on `main` at `3a3eed8695e` and includes `5ce6d65f695` and `49d8da05cf6`, #199693's `openclaw gateway call` hint for an unpaired edgeAuth device, which keeps an explicit `--url`. `git range-diff 987c04a0086..465d5ab0c3c origin/main..1c9cb58e474` shows all ten commits unchanged except the regenerated config baseline hashes in the gateway commit (the core count is still 2654 to 2655). The live run below was made at `4cce58081cc`, before the restacks. prs.body:
## Current repair and validation status

Published head `1be335c060b0815f9d5bce4a3dc8c216830aa300` on repaired prerequisite `8c67ab5e26fc741768e84a1dfcaea0f94053d8d1`. **Selected-check CI completed at the root-reported 19:25:07Z snapshot: 30 successful checks, zero failures, 55 skipped, one cancelled, and no active checks; the aggregate CI gate succeeded.** This records the selected checks, not execution of every lane. Independent source and mapping review approved publication. This is fix-only work; no merge is authorized.

This PR remains stacked on [PR #198739](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198739), whose repaired head is not merged. Its GitHub base remains `test/reduce-million-lines-20261114`. This packet's own delta from old shared ancestor `10e4db504e396a36e1d61a4a0152a55e0eb159c0` is reapplied onto that repaired prerequisite. Its CLI and Workshop suites, catalog fixture, retired post-compaction owner and current-main changes remain intact.

## What Problem This Solves

Script tests repeat setup, equivalent input permutations and assertions covered by retained suites. This packet consolidates them while preserving explicit failure contracts and removing unused committed review metadata.

## User Impact

No production change. Relative to the repaired prerequisite: **32 test paths, +1,382/-2,268: 886 net lines removed**. Relative to the prerequisite's frozen main `aa4d490a848b4d96801fd7afcdea6cc01cc80d6e`, the cumulative stack is **74 paths, +4,137/-6,362: 2,225 net removed**. The stack count includes PR #198739, not an independent saving for this packet.

The README and twelve JSON manifests are no longer committed: **734 review-only lines removed from the old published packet**. Useful mappings appear below instead of in a new repository artifact. Restoring the direct parser cases costs 27 net test lines against the old packet without those manifests.

## Repairs and keepers

- `test/scripts/check-no-random-messaging-tmp.test.ts`: the selected-main `finds tmpdir named import calls from node:os` and `finds tmpdir calls imported from os` cases are restored, each checking actual parser output `[3]`, with the original parser creation and `afterAll` closure. Source: native main `869734209368313e7bcbc325ee72752fd2b57a71`; both complete case blocks match it exactly. The retained integration still checks all selected runtime roots, local functions, allowed plugin support, exact `:2` diagnostics and nonzero exit.
- `test/scripts/check-deadcode-exports.test.ts`: the only content conflict retains main's `models the workflow planner without retaining removed consumers` case, current async runtime-process export assertions and the neighboring consolidated Solid/Vite table. No new main assertion is discarded.
- `test/scripts/ios-release-prepare.test.ts` and `test/scripts/ios-release-signing.test.ts`: kept retired into `test/scripts/ios-release-wrapper-args.test.ts`, which retains preparation metadata, signing-team rejection and wrapper argument coverage.
- Both prerequisite CLI suites remain exact-main; its retired post-compaction suite stays absent with its removed owner.

## Evidence

Signed head `1be335c060b0815f9d5bce4a3dc8c216830aa300` has sole parent `8c67ab5e26fc741768e84a1dfcaea0f94053d8d1`. Normal hooks, targeted formatting, all 30 changed-file TypeScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed. Main-added nonblank lines in every overlap are retained. Removed manifest files have no executable consumers in the selected prerequisite; named keeper files survive. The only absent source references in those mappings are the two explicitly retired iOS suites and synthetic tmpdir fixture paths.

No dependency install, runtime test or typecheck ran locally; the native checkout has no dependency install. Root observed exact-head selected-check CI completion at 19:25:07Z: 30 successful checks, zero failures, 55 skipped, one cancelled and no active checks. The [aggregate CI gate succeeded](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43935503352/job/133549105636). Skipped and cancelled checks are not passing executions; this is not an all-lanes proof. This update uses the root-reported snapshot and performs no new CI poll. The unmerged PR #198739 prerequisite remains a separate gate; this PR remains open, ready and fix-only, with no merge authorized.

## Preserved coverage mappings

The following data moved from the twelve unused JSON files. Historical schema/validation/baseline fields are omitted. The two restored tmpdir cases are removed from retired-case records: each now keeps itself. Remaining mappings describe retained contracts, not fresh runtime proof.

prs.body:
## Current repair and validation status

Published head `8c67ab5e26fc741768e84a1dfcaea0f94053d8d1` on frozen main `aa4d490a848b4d96801fd7afcdea6cc01cc80d6e`. **CI snapshot at 19:18:30Z: 66 successful checks, 68 skipped, one neutral and three failures; no active checks. CI is not green.** Independent source review approved this repair for publication. This remains fix-only and open for Vincent's review; it is not a merge request or a claim of green CI.

The actual failing test is `ui/src/e2e/chat-send-ack-ownership.e2e.test.ts:77`: `locator.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded` encountered `Element is not attached to the DOM` in [UI E2E 1/2 job 133536194940](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43934378634/job/133536194940). The other two failures are aggregate CI gates: [job 133543839762](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43934378634/job/133543839762) and [run 43936950902](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43936950902). The retained test's static source/config/helper closure is unchanged against `aa4d490a848b4d96801fd7afcdea6cc01cc80d6e`; no deletion-caused dependency or justified restoration was identified. Runtime causality remains **UNKNOWN**: no matching main execution proves inheritance. The requested fixes are published, but the failure is unresolved. This records the root-reported scheduled snapshot, not a new CI poll.

This refresh preserves main's automatic overlap changes and restores both CLI suites exactly from that main revision:

- `src/cli/program/command-registry.test.ts`: grouped lazy registration is exercised through real `parseAsync`, including no duplicate commands and secondary command-name loading.
- `src/cli/program/command-tree.test.ts`: missing names return `false` without removing an existing sibling, alongside name and alias removal.

Main retired `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/post-compaction-loop-guard.test.ts` and its production owner in `3a3eed8695e68e182c4851285a3de90ca2cba0ff`, replacing result-sensitive loop detection with the arguments-only repeat guard. The refresh preserves that deletion; it does not restore the obsolete owner or claim its five-line historical consolidation as a current saving.

The stale WebKit selector for the deleted legacy ModelPicker suite is removed. The retained Solid ModelPicker suite remains selected by the existing `src/components/solid/*.browser.test.tsx` pattern.

## What Problem This Solves

Repeated test setup and overlapping assertions add maintenance cost across CI tooling, agents, gateway, plugins and UI. This preliminary packet consolidates those fixtures while retaining distinct CLI registration and missing-command contracts.

## User Impact

Internal test/support cleanup only. Against frozen main `aa4d490a848b4d96801fd7afcdea6cc01cc80d6e`, the published head adds **2,752** and removes **4,091** lines across **44 paths**: **1,339 net lines removed** (**6,843 gross changed lines**). Production delta is **0**. Four whole-file retirements remove 912 lines; the two CLI suites are retained, not counted as retirements. The original published `5c489a3f` count was 1,470 net lines against its historical `fa40e292` baseline and is not the current diff.

## Why This Change Was Made

Repeated fixtures and equivalent cases share helpers or table rows, with covering suites retained. This preliminary packet has no separate deletion manifest: its actual diff and the four-file coverage map below define its retirement scope. Later campaign manifests do not apply retroactively. Four stale entries in `config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt` are removed because their mock factories moved from `index.test.ts` into the annotated catalog fixture. No production algorithm or runtime configuration changes are included.

## Evidence

- Signed published head: `8c67ab5e26fc741768e84a1dfcaea0f94053d8d1`; sole parent `aa4d490a848b4d96801fd7afcdea6cc01cc80d6e`.
- Normal repository commit hooks completed successfully, including formatting of 39 source/config files. The targeted pre-commit format check and 36 TypeScript syntax checks passed; the additional UI config syntax/format check and `git diff --check` passed.
- Both CLI files are byte-identical to frozen main. All newly added nonblank main lines in overlapping test files are preserved. The four remaining deleted paths have no surviving exact executable import or selector reference; their named keepers exist.
- No dependency installation, runtime test, typecheck, fresh CI or new main replay ran during this local preparation. The native checkout has no dependency installation; runtime validation remains pending.
- The catalog synthesis mock remains intentionally retained to preserve the existing cold-owner TTS fixture. Prior native cancellation and catalog experiment results below are historical evidence on their recorded source revisions, not validation of this new head.

## Current Coverage Map

| Retired file | Retained owner coverage |
| --- | --- |
| `src/commands/agents.list.dep-warning.test.ts` | `src/commands/channels.list.dep-warning.test.ts`: real agents-list row, asynchronous authentication marker and absence of `DEP_PLUGIN_SDK` warning. |
| `ui/src/components/model-picker.browser.test.tsx` | `ui/src/components/solid/model-picker.browser.test.tsx`: the same ModelPicker/select-picker owner, disabled groups, catalog, unknown model, tooltip and custom-model rows. |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-composer-height.browser.test.tsx` | `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-composer-layout.browser.test.tsx`: content-sized height through the same rendering and overflow owner. |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-composer-width.browser.test.tsx` | `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-composer-layout.browser.test.tsx`: border-width controls through the same width-edge owner. |

| Retained file | Preservation reason |
| --- | --- |
| `src/cli/program/command-registry.test.ts` | Exact-main self-keeper for real grouped `parseAsync` and secondary-name lazy registration. |
| `src/cli/program/command-tree.test.ts` | Exact-main self-keeper for the missing-name `false` result and unchanged sibling. |

The composer layout keeper was created by this packet (659 lines); it is not described as a pre-existing keeper. The Workshop suite remains present; its previous retirement/transfer claim is withdrawn. Other changes consolidate partial test files and fixture setup, not additional whole-file retirements.

## Historical native cancellation and catalog evidence

The following records belong to the original published head and its explicitly recorded bases. References to an actual or then-current main identify those historical SHAs; they do not classify a future CI failure on the published head.

**Validated against the then-current-main baseline for the sole executed failure; raw CI and the required gate remain RED.** [Run 43610042885, attempt 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/attempts/3) reran only the failed large-16 job. [Job 132513350800](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/job/132513350800) again executed the 14-case native-control file: **10 passed and the same four cancellation rows failed**; [aggregate gate 132515407749](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/job/132515407749) failed. The checkout was again `c410968c` (base `20cb257f` plus this head), with the same failure payload, stack and runtime.

The three observed PR-native failures are [the original 299b36e7 run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43582240086/job/132409626919), [this head's attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/job/132507684218), and [the targeted attempt 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/job/132513350800). A separately executed, independently reviewed then-current-main proof now confirms the same failure on [main `d867f1791447e20904bfc2d39c43b1616311035b`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d867f1791447e20904bfc2d39c43b1616311035b). Native RUN 13687 ran only `src/gateway/talk/handlers/client-native-control.test.ts`, using the original `gateway-database-workers` isolated group, inner parallelism 1 and no case filter: **14 tests, 10 passed, the same four cancellation rows failed, exit 1** (68.62s test duration). The exact source HEAD and lock hash matched before and after execution; Node `24.22.1` and Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1` matched the PR run. Independent review read the native command, metadata, timing and automatic stdout; stdout SHA256: `89830d6fde9f8044fcc2149bb2f544d5e267dfc44d63e1f01b11639856caf4e8`.

The matching cancellation suffixes are `transcript-first, rejection`, `delegation-first, rejection`, `transcript-first, empty` and `delegation-first, partial`. Each again expected `Real runner consultation completed.` and received `I need a moment to verify that before answering.`, at test `474:78` / support `316:9`. This is **executed then-current-main failure proof**, alongside the [existing actual-base CI proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610133604/job/132493534359) below. The [native provisioning workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43617502605) is a launcher only, not the test result.

The sole executed PR failure is therefore **pre-existing on both its actual CI base and the freshly resolved then-current main**. This establishes baseline equivalence for that failure, not a green required gate, full-suite main success or a flaky passing result. No deletion-caused failure was identified; no restoration or further PR retry is justified by this evidence.

**Catalog mock retention.** The three lines at `src/gateway/talk/handlers/catalog.test-support.ts:76–78` intentionally restore the direct `tts-synthesis` mock, its isolation comment and spacing. The retained cold-owner TTS case in `index.test.ts:327` sets `providerMocks.synthesizeSpeech` at line 388 and checks its call at line 415. Removing that mock in `cb1f` caused an observed zero-call failure in [job 132457376704](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43598130392/job/132457376704); `794fa6` restored it. The native-control file has no import path to this helper. This is intentional fixture wiring, not a claim of a literal byte-for-byte main revert.

**Earlier attempt-2 result: FAILURE.** [Run 43610042885, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/attempts/2) completed with **45 successful jobs, two failed jobs, 27 skipped jobs and zero active jobs**. The failed jobs are [changed-compact-large-16](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/job/132507684218) and its [aggregate CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/job/132510898410). The sole executed test failure is the four native cancellation rows described below. All UI shards and changed-compact-large-3 passed.

**Raw CI remains RED; the sole executed failure is baseline-equivalent** at historical head `5c489a3fa321a4269ccd94c24e3a75e8ddd74bf4`. On [CI attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/attempts/2), [changed-compact-large-16, job 132507684218](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/job/132507684218) actually executed `src/gateway/talk/handlers/client-native-control.test.ts`: **14 tests, 10 passed and four native cancellation rows failed**. The tested checkout was merge `c410968c` into base `20cb257f`; this is an executed test failure, not a runner-admission failure.

Historical source-boundary review of the 46 changed paths from base `20cb257f` to tested merge `c410968c` found no changes to the failing process's runner, config, setup, test or native fixtures. The group runs `client-native-control.test.ts` alone in a fresh Bun child. The changed Talk support, `catalog.test-support.ts`, is imported only by the catalog/index tests; neither is selected in that child. This source comparison is complemented by the executed same-base result below.

Existing CI on the actual base `20cb257f` also executed the target file: [main job 132493534359 in run 43610133604](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610133604/job/132493534359) recorded **14 tests, 10 passed and the same four cancellation rows failed**. Independent review matched the four case suffixes, expected/actual speakable fallback payload, assertion locations `474:78` and support `316:9`, Node `24.22.1`, and Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`. Main checked out `20cb257f` directly; the PR tested merge `c410968c`, whose parents are that base and this PR head.

The main assertions failed **before that job was later cancelled**. This is executed same-base failure evidence, not a successful main job or full-main validation claim. The PR's sole executed test failure is therefore **confirmed pre-existing on its actual CI base**. The PR and required CI gate remain **RED**. No deletion-caused failure was identified, and no restoration or additional CI action is warranted by this result.

Earlier attempt 1 quota failures in [large-3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/job/132493405528) and [large-16](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/job/132493405391) occurred before checkout/tests at the 10,080-start limit. Those are historical admission failures. The earlier job-specific retry request was rejected while the workflow was active; it admitted no new attempt. The user subsequently started attempt 2. Skipped jobs remain outside execution proof; this attempt has no active jobs.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/198737

## Other historical validation evidence

Catalog-only CI experiment and repair: `cb1f1508758b30c1c3d0a4f3a5c4859458781a26` restored only the exact frozen `06bfea7` catalog preimage. Its [node-large-15 job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43598130392/job/132457376704) failed on `src/gateway/talk/handlers/index.test.ts` → `talk.speak handler` → `uses the runtime snapshot with cold owner tts`: **84 passed, 1 failed**, `Expected mock call 0` at `index.test.ts:415:26`. The matching blob IDs are benchmark `5442f57315c67a03aa38e41891086da19a495836`, diagnostic type `5c0685a58618377f416e1bce98eb57bf354b261c`, and worker owner `be0892deee832cc769176ba9d1fcd435a461b2ef`. This is a deterministic inherited-main type-contract failure supported by exact source and ancestry, **not a separately executed main typecheck**. Follow-up outside this test-only campaign: the benchmark consumer must narrow pool-only numeric task metrics before summing them; broker metrics deliberately omit this field. No source fix or green result is claimed.

Additional failures on earlier head `794fa6b` observed in run `43600220141`: the [baseline-ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43600220141/job/132463634589) reports a closed `../logging/subsystem.js` mock at `src/infra/worker-idle-gc.test.ts:13`; the [changed-Node job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43600220141/job/132463635025) fails the worker import budget with `agents/identity-file.worker.js: 240 evaluated modules exceeds budget 220`, at `scripts/check-worker-module-budget.mjs:57:9` via `scripts/check-cli-bootstrap-imports.mts:595:5`. The experiment run also has an inherited-main [baseline-ratchet failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43598130392/job/132457376515): `src/infra/worker-idle-gc.test.ts:13` closes the `../logging/subsystem.js` mock without export preservation or an isolation annotation. The guard scans all tracked factories; `--base` does not limit it to changed files. Independent source review establishes a pre-existing main guard violation, **not a separately executed main CI reproduction**. No branch repair is applied for that main-only mock. Raw historical failures remain recorded; queued/skipped work is not a pass.

Prior catalog-only counterfactual: diagnostic `2632be5e62480d7e3424873f5a1c9918d54b9c47` replaced only `src/gateway/talk/handlers/catalog.test-support.ts` with its exact frozen `06bfea7` bytes. Line 474 again expected `Real runner consultation completed.` and received `I need a moment to verify that before answering.` Comparison to the earlier PR/main results uses their previously independently verified records; the old main capture had already been disposed after review.

The earlier diagnostic rollback did not improve the failure and was not pushed; that diagnostic checkout was restored byte-for-byte to `10e4db5`. The separate signed `cb1f150` commit now publishes the same catalog-only preimage for the explicitly requested CI experiment. [Workflow 43596561909](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43596561909) provisioned the diagnostic runner only and is **not a CI test result**. Actual test evidence is the independently reviewed native execution receipt. Prior exact-head CI remains **RED**; the new push-triggered run is pending. No manual full-workflow dispatch, old-head rerun, or successful validation is claimed.


**Historical CI status (head `794fa6b`): RED: source-proven inherited-main script-types and closed-logging-mock failures, plus the observed 240/220 worker import-budget failure with main-side source growth identified but no executed-main census. The catalog-only experiment failed an index case before the native group. The four earlier native cancellation failures were independently reproduced on pinned main.** Attempt 1 of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43591273159 failed [changed-compact-large-15](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43591273159/job/132436744396) and [the aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43591273159/job/132440021093). prs.title: fix: older conversation drops out of the model view when screenshots fill the history byte cap
prs.body:
Related: #159799

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: older conversation silently drops out of the model's view, without any summary, when screenshot or other large tool results fill the history byte cap of an embedded session.

## User Impact

In image-heavy sessions such as computer use, an agent keeps its earlier requests, decisions and replies in context. Old screenshot bodies are replaced with omission notices instead, so token-based compaction can summarize the conversation once the context actually fills. Below the byte cap nothing changes. The stored transcript is never modified.

## Why This Change Was Made

The embedded runtime bounds replayed history at eight bytes per context token. A stored screenshot result costs 0.25–2.5 MB of that bound but only around 1.5k model tokens, so the bound fills long before the token threshold, and older rows fall off the front of the window unsummarized. #177410 and the comments on #159799 show the same thing on several providers.

The selector already has a policy for this: `toolResultOverflow: "omit"` (#171239) replaces tool-result bodies with notices, largest first, before it drops older messages, and restores the newest bodies that fit once a prefix is dropped. Until now only settled-tool finalization used it (#184704). This change applies the policy to every caller of `resolveEmbeddedSessionContextLimits`, so ordinary attempts, recovery, and the preflight estimate all read the same model view, as the resolver's contract requires.

Accepted cost, documented in the code and in `docs/concepts/compaction.md`: above the byte cap, each newly omitted body changes the prompt prefix from that message on. Today the prefix already changes there whenever the window steps, and the dropped history is lost for good.

<details>
<summary>Scope notes</summary>

- The ordinary path already passes the limits object through: `[sessionManagerReadInitialContext]` rereads through `readSessionManagerModelContextAsync` with the manager's full `boundedContextLimits`. The session manager's own writer branch keeps its strict row read, so the truncation and rewrite paths still see real bodies.
- The `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` guard still charges raw transcript bytes. The bounded read in `compaction-transcript-bytes.ts` only locates expired runtime-context bodies to subtract, and omitted tool bodies are never in that set.
- Compaction input is unaffected; it already reads its complete window independently of the hydration cap.
- Not addressed: byte pressure that doesn't come from tool results (for example encrypted reasoning, see the no-image data point on #159799).

</details>

## Evidence

**Regression test through the ordinary entry point** (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/session-context-limits.test.ts`). A user goal, four `computer` screenshot results, a reply and a new prompt are opened with `SessionManager.openBoundedAsync(scope, resolveEmbeddedSessionContextLimits({ contextTokenBudget: 1_024 }))`, and then `[sessionManagerReadInitialContext]()` reads the history:

- `main` (`913e6ea2944`): fails. The history starts at the toolCall before the last screenshot, mid-turn, and the user goal is gone.
- This branch: passes. The goal, the reply, the prompt and all four tool results are present, the older bodies are notices, and the view stays within `maxBytes`.

**Focused suites, all passing** (113 tests in 11 files): `session-manager-model-context-limits`, `session-manager-bounded`, `attempt-history-prepare`, `run-embedded-agent.finalization-scope`, `settled-turn-finalization.silence`, `attempt-session-boundary`, `agent-runner-memory-transcript-context`, `agent-runner-memory.byte-preflight`, `agent-runner-memory.byte-pressure`, `harness/builtin-openclaw`, plus the new test. `pnpm check:changed` on this head: format, lint, core and core-test typecheck (all 29 graphs), and the guards pass. The only failure is the dead-export scan, which flags inherited exports in files this change doesn't touch (`src/state/*-swap.ts`, `src/state/state-upgrade*.ts`, `ui/src/lib/openclaw-id/member-welcome.ts`); the base commit already has them.

**Measured on a real session** (read-only copy of a 2026.11.3 agent database, Anthropic route, 500k-token budget, 4,000,000-byte cap). One afternoon of computer use stored 189 screenshot images (about 84 MB of active branch) after a compaction. Replaying the selector newest-first:

| Run | Stored bytes (today) | Screenshot results charged as notices |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | window starts mid-turn, 47 of 743 rows | all 743 rows since the compaction, about 2.3 MB |
| 2 | 61 of 760 rows, the model got only the summary | all 760 rows |
| 3 | 88 of 787 rows | all 787 rows |

With notices the estimated prompt is about 245–260k tokens, below the session's 375k compaction threshold, so nothing would have been lost. Charging images at `IMAGE_BLOCK_TOKENS × 8` instead would only have reached back about 100 minutes and was estimated over the threshold. Details are in the comments on #159799.

prs.title: fix: isolate transport policy between shared-worker test files
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes order-dependent CI failures when transport policy from a completed test file remains active in the next file.

## User Impact

Tests get their intended provider policy. Retained native SDK calls reinstall guarded transport and configured request preparation after test-file retirement. No configuration, schema, or public SDK changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

#199956 correctly shared transport state across native and transformed modules, but the shared runner did not retire file-owned callbacks. This change retires policy in place after cleanup while preserving shared identity, asynchronous scope, and accepted-work custody. Base and runtime installation share the existing installation record; actual core-owned selection, preparation, and invocation boundaries call that installer after retirement. Explicit active overrides survive, and package-only consumers retain inert defaults until a real installer runs.

Captured current main `4a0e45492` moved session streaming into `sessions/session-stream.ts`. The integration preserves that extraction and its admitted-caller assertions, and relocates the already reviewed installer invocation into the new owner. Peer diagnostics isolation and mock-baseline pruning are preserved.

Production grows by 15 lines: nine for shared installation lifecycle and six for the actual consumer boundaries that prepare or invoke requests. The probe test now preserves the real AI namespace while overriding only its runtime factory. Three unit fixtures explicitly retain their existing provider-bootstrap isolation, and canonical pruning removes obsolete mock-baseline entries.

## Evidence

- Original ordered producer/consumer sequences reproduce Anthropic policy, completion diagnostics, transport logging, OpenAI image-carrier, and compaction eligibility failures under Node and pinned Bun, then pass with the correction. Local worker/order evidence does not assert the historical hosted predecessor.
- The three-file native regression preserves egress guards, sentinel decoding, package-only defaults, and source/native sharing. Its configured prepared request fails on published `92316c744` because the real wire payload omits chat_template_kwargs; all three cases pass with the correction under Node and pinned Bun.
- Named affected owner contracts pass 101 cases under Node, including all 14 prompt-prefix cases, and 87 under pinned Bun. The historical functional Node version was not captured. Existing runner, native-override, deferred-import, and probe red/green evidence remains valid for unchanged inputs.
- The pre-integration cumulative 17-file Codex review and canonical baseline-shrink review are clean through P2; that exact source passed all 38 changed gates in 739 seconds. A fresh isolated review of the current-main resolution is also clean through P2. Integrated affected-owner proof passes 54 cases under Node 24.22.1 and 40 under pinned Bun 1.4.4, including the new session-stream owner, SDK, no-auth, stream ownership and diagnostics contracts, plus 14 Node prefix cases. The current-base changed check completed in 803 seconds: 37 of 38 gates passed, with only the dead-export scan failing. Three production findings belong to #200183; eight additional production findings trace to main’s compaction extraction `472cd0a2`, and one to #198133. The exact main parent `4a0e45492` reproduces the identical 12 production and 107 full-tree diagnostics in hourly CI 43918534788 and a separate canonical parent scan, with zero set differences. The failed local invocation remains recorded as exit 1; these real main regressions are separately owned, and a later CI parent requires its own qualification.
- Previous exact-head CI 43896141364 exposed separate real main regressions: retired inventory references introduced by #200097 (peer #198936 merged its repair), and the ClawRouter auth-profile replay fixture missed by #200063 (separately owned correction). Neither is treated as noise or evidence of this correction passing CI.
- TTS and package failure-metadata cases remain outside the qualified fix claim. This is a correctness repair; no performance improvement is claimed.

The unchanged warm prepared-completion driver compared published `92316c744` with the pre-integration correction `6f4e8546` under pinned Node 24.22.1: three A1/B/A2 rounds each for timing and sampled allocation, 200 measured calls per process after 100 warmups. All request counts and 380,706-byte payloads matched. Baseline/candidate medians were 3.488/3.288 ms thread CPU and 2,191,258/2,189,050 sampled bytes per call. CPU paired changes were −15.8%, +36.4%, and −5.2%, with A/A variation of −14.7% to +16.5%; high observed host load and the outlier prevent a speedup or confident no-regression claim. Allocation differences were within A/A variation. This measures the prepared-completion owner, not DB/workspace scale or all six consumers.

Final-head CI 43931486839 on `101d7ce315` completed with 42 successful jobs, 28 skipped, and two failed jobs: the ClawRouter shard and its aggregate gate. Both original ClawRouter cases reproduce on the actual tested main parent `ec025eba2` under Node 24.22.1 and pinned Bun 1.4.4. #200063 introduced the missed auth-profile fixture migration; #200183 owns its qualified repair. This is an attributed inherited-failure landing, not a green CI result. ClawSweeper reviewed the exact final head with zero findings and zero unchecked items.

prs.title: fix(update): retain leased interrupted releases
prs.body:
Source bug: Release retention deleted interrupted collecting directories without checking live release leases.

## What Problem This Solves

If release cleanup is interrupted after moving a deselected release into a temporary collecting directory, the next cleanup run could delete that directory even while a process still held a live lease on the release.

## User Impact

An interrupted update cleanup preserves a release that is still in use, preventing a running Gateway or updater from losing files during recovery. Unleased collecting remnants remain eligible for cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

The collecting-remnant cleanup ran before the normal lease checks and treated every `.collecting-*` directory as disposable. It now extracts the release id from the temporary name and retains the remnant while the corresponding lease is live. The normal age, open-run, selected-release, and lease rules remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before: a deterministic release-retention fixture with a live lease and an interrupted `.collecting-*` rename deleted the collecting directory.
- After: the same fixture keeps the collecting directory and reports no removal; the regression test covers the recovery case on POSIX.
- Supporting checks: focused oxlint, focused format check, `git diff --check`, and the repository retention test command passed. Windows skips the POSIX release-link tests; the deterministic fixture was replayed separately on this host.
- Scope: changed `src/infra/package-release-retention.ts` and its focused regression test only.
- This proves leased interrupted release directories are retained during cleanup; it does not claim live update delivery or cross-platform release-link behavior on Windows.

prs.title: fix: reduce Gateway stalls during session GitHub actions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session GitHub actions repeatedly scan the complete GitHub-login role-assignment map while revalidating delegated authority, adding synchronous Gateway CPU and allocation.

## User Impact

Exact normalized login assignments resolve directly from the current map. Explicit profile roles, mixed-case/padded configured logins, default roles, and live authority revalidation keep their existing behavior. No configuration, schema, cache, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The role-selection owner enumerated every assignment even when the requested login was already an exact key. Config validation guarantees unique normalized logins, so an own-key lookup can serve that case directly. The existing normalized search remains for other key spellings. Production code shrinks by one line; all authority checks remain in place.

## Evidence

Five warm A/A control pairs and five interleaved A/B pairs completed at depths 1 and 16. Timing and sampled allocation used separate runs. Per-edit medians:


| Delegation depth | Main-thread CPU, ms | Maximum segment, ms | Wall time, ms | Sampled allocation, MiB |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 95.525 → 12.204 | 61.427 → 5.232 | 226.425 → 16.228 | 80.017 → 6.399 |
| 16 | 576.378 → 45.166 | 468.255 → 32.081 | 584.514 → 50.556 | 827.797 → 36.828 |

Depth-16 CPU improves 92.2%; sampled allocation improves 95.6%. CPU p95 is 579.358 → 46.996 ms (ranges 573.527–579.358 → 44.566–46.996). Allocation p95 is 923.763 → 38.223 MiB (ranges 819.042–923.763 → 34.195–38.223). A/A baseline edit CPU spans 590.696–680.861 ms; allocation spans 814.693–862.880 MiB. Shared-host load varied 23.8–38.8 during timing, so absolute wall/segment tails include scheduling noise. The effect is much larger than the A/A CPU/allocation spread. These are synthetic measurements, not a claimed production deployment.

- The extended owner regression fails on baseline `091a90e567c19d1dd2e3bcd8f5a35d479fd9d3e9` with two full enumerations; the candidate avoids both and reads an assignment update immediately.
- 69 focused tests passed, including registered GitHub actions and post-await revocation, policy changes, and lifecycle rotation. Three-file run: 139.99 s including compilation, 145.03 s wrapper duration.
- `pnpm check:changed` completed: affected typecheck, format and other structural checks passed; a test-only shadowed callback was fixed and its lint rerun passed. The whole-repository unused-export scan fails identically on exact main parent `091a90e567c19d1dd2e3bcd8f5a35d479fd9d3e9` (13 production and 108 full-tree diagnostics). All 40 reported owner files are unchanged. Source attribution: test-support consumers removed by #198933 (`9bfad2b180b4d`), #198936 (`a0423637196f`), and #198943 (`b90c5739fa5c`); production exports left unused by compaction extraction `472cd0a2f542`, #198133 (`18136c960eaf`), #200073 (`30e9d3ee295e9`), #200056 (`24385a20428a`), and the Talk fix `94e34f956969`. These are main regressions, retained for the lead; no unrelated exports or test contracts were changed here.
- Codex autoreview of the complete local change against that baseline: scoped-clean at P0–P2, no findings. No Control UI imports of the changed production module.
- Initial synthetic depth-16 CPU profile: role selection is 59.6% of sampled self time; edit calls use 574–591 ms main-thread CPU with 466–468 ms maximum segments. This profile includes standalone assertion/model probes and registered actions; it is not a production attribution or live-network measurement.
- Separate census with 32 configured agents: depth-16 edit assignment enumerations fall 8,570 → 0; role selections, source assertions, sharing checks, plugin entries, and Gateway scope entries are identical.

Acceptance recorded before final timing: reuse the committed registered-action benchmark with a generated 35.13-GiB database (10,000 sessions, 1,000,000 events), 62,000 workspace files/1.116 GB, 10,000 active run records, 2,000 neighboring role assignments, and a 32-agent roster generated by `scripts/perf/team-shape-fixture.ts`. Run warm A/A controls and five interleaved A/B pairs at depths 1 and 16. Keep work counts, timing, and sampled allocation in separate runs; report CPU, wall, maximum synchronous segment, and allocation median/p95/spread. Require at least 20% CPU/allocation improvement and no 20% latency/segment regression. External GitHub I/O is synthetic; local filesystem is APFS, not btrfs. No production data is used.

Rerun with `scripts/perf/github-action-scope-measure.ts --capsule <frozen-baseline> --output <new-output> --lineage --compare-role-selection --depths 1,16 --pairs 5 --sessions 10000 --runs 10000 --roles 2000 --active-runs --large-fixture <synthetic-large-fixture> --team-fixture <team-shape-output>`. Add `--allocation` or `--counts` in separate runs. Use a short temporary directory on the fixture volume for clone copies.


Hosted CI [43932789376](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43932789376), attempt 1, completed with one failing nonaggregate job: `checks-node-changed-compact-small-17`. The assertion at `test/plugins/deep-research-routing.gateway.test.ts:839` reproduces identically on the actual tested main parent `aa4d490a848b4d96801fd7afcdea6cc01cc80d6e` (1 failed / 3 passed). #200099 (`edbc5bcea9b605a826cc722d298c784c6a8fef78`) intentionally removed lifecycle-only comparison from research view ownership but left the old integration expectation. The test and its research owners are byte-identical in tested merge `4ff09d9d665bef1e1ca805ed02838703f2a0c149`; the failing fixture has no GitHub-login assignment map. The automatic table says unknown because no matching scheduled-main job exists; this exact-parent reproduction and source history establish the independent attribution. This is a main regression, reported for its owner, not ignored noise. All other jobs in this CI run, including security-fast and UI end-to-end checks, passed.

[ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200211#issuecomment-6926029531) covers final head `fd9b8620f4cb953b8086ffc1dbf36d56651f8cea`: zero findings and zero open checklist items. It notes the already-disclosed synthetic boundary instead of running-Gateway proof. The performance change preserves behavior and is measured through the real registered handler and authority owners.

Remote Gateways now use the existing `tts.speak` inline-audio RPC, decode the returned base64 payload, and pass it through `writeOutputAsset`. Remote Gateway TTS can now save audio with `--output`; calls without an explicit output path also produce a locally accessible media artifact. Explicit model and voice overrides continue to reach the Gateway.

prs.title: fix(ci): accept intentional activated Gateway startup skips
prs.body:
## Problem
Full release validation 43898101600 rejects successful package updates in the update/restart-auth lane (job 133429743809): the update owner intentionally records an activated-gateway-startup skip with exitCode=null and a recoverable-maintenance advisory for profiles without a local Gateway. The success assertion treats it as a failed core step.

## Fix
Recognize only that named, advisory-marked skip, with no termination, signal, killed process, output truncation, or failure facts. Real failed startup steps still fail. No update behavior, restart/survivor assertions, integrity checks, or release thresholds change.

Inspected the candidate producer at src/infra/update-activated-gateway-check.ts: the same skip contract covers remote/TLS profiles and an existing Gateway owner. The real restart proof remains separate and required.

## Evidence
- Real assertion CLI on the exact synthetic step shape: base fails with 'successful update contained a failed core step'; fixed passes.
- Nine real CLI cases pass in 1s: intentional skip accepted; nonzero exit, unclassified skip, another step, timeout, signal, killed process, truncation and failure facts rejected.
- Added equivalent regression cases to the existing assertion suite.
- oxfmt, Node syntax and git diff --check pass.
- Full touched Vitest file attempted: blocked before tests by unavailable quickjs-wasi in the local shared dependency tree (15.43s, zero tests). Initial setup also lacked the UI dependency link; fixed only the owned worktree link. No shared installs changed.
- Local lint blocked loading eslint-plugin-solid. Hosted lint/types/full touched tests remain required; Docker update/restart proof is not claimed green.

## Review and scope
Self-reviewed and simplified: one existing assertion branch, no new owner/helper, 10 harness lines plus 42 regression lines. Independent review explicitly waived by Dallin for this release; no independent verdict claimed. CI/security gates are not waived.

prs.title: fix: keep native resource startup responsive on slow filesystems
prs.body:
Related: #200136, #200193

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: starting a Gateway operation that needs a native resource worker can pause other requests while its private socket directory is created synchronously.

## User Impact

The Gateway stays responsive while broker directory creation or cleanup waits on the filesystem. Existing resource admission, private directory permissions, readiness errors, and joined cleanup remain enforced. Windows continues using its named pipe and avoids allocating an unused directory.

A SIGKILL between child directory creation and readiness can leave a private temporary directory: the parent has not yet observed ownership and must not remove an unrelated existing path. This recoverable edge is accepted instead of adding another handshake.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Team 25c97908 incident on 2026-11-16 at 05:02 PST showed a 1.97 s main-thread btrfs transaction wait during catalog lock creation, producing a 2,002 ms event-loop stall. #200136 removed that lock. This audit found synchronous directory creation and cleanup at the existing native resource broker boundary.

The parent now allocates only the random path and secret. The existing broker process owns exclusive directory creation, chmod, socket startup, and normal cleanup. The parent retains async crash cleanup after readiness has established ownership. Existing error settlement preserves startup failures and independent cleanup failures. No new service, worker, protocol, cache, schema, or configuration.

Production grows by 13 lines across three existing modules. The growth moves physical startup and cleanup to their process owner while preserving exclusive directory ownership and error reporting.

## Evidence

The original real cold create/attach/close guard fails on one mkdtempSync, chmodSync, and rmSync each. Earlier affected startup/retirement/stderr proof passes 32 cases; the final lifecycle and permission replay passes eight cases, including actual resource attachment, completed removal, private mode under an inherited umask, and refusal to delete an existing unrelated directory. The shared filesystem guard also covers direct writable opens and synchronous metadata mutation APIs after #200193.

Canonical check:changed completed: structural gates, core types, and all 29 test type graphs passed. A task-owned cleanup lint finding was repaired; final scoped lint/type/format/diff checks pass. The known dead exports reproduce on exact base 6670297776a00 and originate in #200056 / 24385a20428a; no full-command success or baseline waiver is claimed. Final isolated Codex review has no actionable P0–P2 findings. The final widened cold guard passes (one selected case), and affected test types, lint, format, and fresh final-source Codex review are clean. Production is byte-identical to the measured candidate; no timing rerun was needed.

Twenty serialized fresh Node 26.12.1 processes provide five interleaved A/A controls and five A/B pairs through the real broker readiness, native resource attachment, and joined retirement flow. Exact source hashes and the creation API/PID are checked. The synthetic fixture includes a 35 GiB database, 5,000 sessions, and 62,000 workspace files; this owner does not scan that unrelated data. No Team data was used. This is source-checkout startup on APFS, not bundled-runtime or btrfs timing.

| Median | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Constructor return | 2.712 ms | 2.465 ms |
| Broker ready | 292.052 ms | 291.072 ms |
| Complete owner operation | 366.219 ms | 362.789 ms |
| Main-thread CPU | 9.899 ms | 9.778 ms |
| Parent-process CPU | 11.289 ms | 14.340 ms |
| Main-isolate allocation | 3.176 MB | 3.079 MB |
| Whole process-tree CPU | 1.49 s | 1.51 s |

A/A owner medians were 365.614 / 366.654 ms. Parent-process CPU rose 27%, or 3.051 ms, in A/B; its A/A medians varied by 19.5%. This bounded observed cost is accepted for moving the wait off main; it is not called noise. Allocation controls varied by 34.5%, so no allocation improvement or general speedup is claimed. Owner p95 was 369.342 → 379.789 ms.

Two separate qualified fault runs delay the actual directory create by 2,000 ms. Maximum heartbeat gap falls from 2,013.902 ms to 6.571 ms, while total operation time stays about 2.39 s in both arms. Each run asserts exactly one create in the expected process: baseline main, candidate child. The first histogram detector missed the initial blocked interval; its assertion failed and that attempt is retained. Only the two fault arms were rerun with a heartbeat armed before invocation; the 20 timing samples were preserved.

No changed module is imported by the Control UI. Local Windows proof is not claimed. Exact-head [CI43932457792](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43932457792) succeeded on `eb65d27c33870e6e2a331beeb320acdc3e745bb3`. Final-head ClawSweeper [review6926208501](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200216#issuecomment-6926208501) has zero open items and no actionable findings. Native preparation is complete.
