prs.title: fix: native Codex MCP config keeps plugin OAuth credentials
prs.body:
Closes #197763

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: plugin-provided MCP servers that use OpenClaw-managed OAuth (for example `@openclaw/atlassian`) are projected into the native Codex thread config with the URL but no credential, so Codex fails to initialize them with `invalid_token` and no tools appear, even though Settings reports the connection as authorized.

## User Impact

Authorized plugin MCP connections now reach native Codex with a usable bearer, so Jira-style remote MCP tools become discoverable and callable right after the plugin is authorized. No configuration change or re-authorization is required, and servers without a saved credential are still omitted rather than sent unauthenticated.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bundle projection path built Codex `mcp_servers` straight from the prepared bundle config, while only the owner-configured path ran `resolveMcpBearerBundleConfig` first. The plugin server therefore kept `auth: "oauth"` into normalization, which has no credential to emit, leaving `http_headers` and `bearer_token_env_var` empty. The bundle path now resolves the same way the owner path does — literal token projection, `omitUnavailableOAuthServers` so a missing credential drops that one server instead of failing the thread, and a diagnostic naming the plugin whose credential could not be resolved. Unauthenticated and non-OAuth servers are projected exactly as before.

## Evidence

- [x] Regression test red→green: `projects the resolved OAuth bearer for a plugin-only server` in `src/agents/codex-mcp-config.test.ts`. With the previous projection line restored, the test fails because `http_headers` is absent (`1 failed | 7 skipped`); with this change it passes (`8 passed`, file-level run). Command: `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts src/agents/codex-mcp-config.test.ts --reporter=verbose`.
- [x] Targeted suite: `src/agents/codex-mcp-config.test.ts` → `8 passed (8)`, including the pre-existing projection, grant, and requester-scope cases, so the added resolution step changes nothing for servers that carry no OAuth credential.
- [x] Lint/format on the touched files: `oxlint` reports `0 warnings and 0 errors`; `oxfmt` reports the files formatted.
- [x] Scope: `src/agents/codex-mcp-config.ts` only gains the bearer-resolution step plus its diagnostic; the owner-config projection path, `resolveMcpBearerBundleConfig`, and the Codex TOML/args paths are untouched.
- [x] Honest boundary: this proves the bundle projection now emits the Authorization header produced by the existing resolver, using a stubbed credential store. It does not perform a live OAuth refresh or a real Jira tool call against Atlassian; token acquisition itself is covered by the existing resolver path, which this change now reuses rather than reimplements.

prs.title: fix(update): honor server recovery captures in supervised migrations
prs.body:
Closes #198334

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: during a supervised migration (`oc update` migrate path), the database backup is created without the `postgresSchemaCaptures` setting, so a configuration with `database.postgres.recoveryCaptures: "server"` produces local exports for non-state PostgreSQL stores and leaves behind an ambiguous recovery set instead of the server captures the recovery inventory expects.

## User Impact

When recovery captures are configured as `server`, a supervised migration now backs up non-state PostgreSQL stores on the database (server captures), matching what the native update path already does and what the recovery inventory expects to find. No configuration change, migration, or user action is required; behavior is unchanged for every other `recoveryCaptures` setting.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native update path passes `postgresSchemaCaptures: source.config.database?.postgres?.recoveryCaptures === "server"` to `createUpdateDatabaseBackup`, but the supervised migration path (`updateMigrateCommand`) omitted the flag entirely. The two paths therefore disagreed about where non-state PostgreSQL stores live after a backup: the migration wrote local exports while recovery tooling expected server captures, which surfaces as ambiguous recovery sets and failed Doctor finalization during update repair. The fix forwards the same flag from the same config source, restoring parity between the two update paths; no other backup options or migration steps are touched.

## Evidence

- [x] Regression tests red→green: "honors the configured recovery captures in the migration database backup (server)" and "(portable)" in `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-migrate.test.ts` fail on main (expected `postgresSchemaCaptures === true`, received `undefined`) and pass with the fix. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cli/update-cli/update-command-migrate.test.ts` — before: 2 passed / 16 failed; after: 4 passed / 16 failed (the same 16 failures, unchanged).
- [x] Related targeted suites: the other 16 failures in that file are pre-existing and unrelated to this change — they fail identically before and after the fix with local-filesystem environment errors (`FsSafeError` `path-mismatch`, a `linkedom` `entities/decode` export resolution error) on this Windows contributor machine; the failing set is byte-identical across the red and green runs, which is the relevant comparison.
- [x] Behavior verification: the new tests assert `createUpdateDatabaseBackup` receives `postgresSchemaCaptures: true` when `recoveryCaptures: "server"` in both server and portable configurations; on main the option arrives as `undefined`, with the fix it arrives as `true`.
- [x] Scope: one production file (`update-command-migrate.ts`, 4 added lines forwarding the existing config flag) plus two regression test cases (31 added test lines). The native update path, backup implementation, and all other migration steps are untouched.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): preserve failing cause when operator authority is lost mid-run
prs.body:
Closes #198360

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a scheduled same-session continuation whose operator authority is revoked mid-run ends with the generic persisted error `Session event was abandoned before execution`, and the Gateway log only says `followup queue: canceled input after loss of operator authority`. Neither the original failure nor the failing authority condition is preserved, so the cron receipt gives no actionable reason and diagnosis requires source inspection.

## User Impact

When authority is legitimately revoked, the continuation stays denied exactly as before, but the session-event failure and the Gateway log now carry the real cause (the original failure and the failing authority check), so the cron receipt names what happened instead of a generic abandonment line. Queue semantics are unchanged: the input is still consumed terminally and never replayed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The authority-loss branch in the followup runner swallowed both errors: it re-checked `operatorAuthority.assertCurrent()` in a bare catch, discarded the caught exception, and — unlike the adjacent internal-event failure branch — never called `internalEventExecution.onFailed(error)`, so the session-event lifecycle filled its unset failure with the constant "abandoned before execution" text. The fix reports the original error through the same `onFailed` callback the sibling branch uses and logs both causes. Disposition stays `consumed` and completion stays `aborted`, preserving the documented no-retry behavior for revoked input.

## Evidence

- [x] Regression tests red→green: "preserves the failing cause when operator authority is lost mid-execution" (both `original cause` and `authority check cause` scenarios) in `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.authority-loss.test.ts`. With the fix reverted to the committed version both cases fail (`internalEventExecution.onFailed` never called — "Number of calls: 0", log line lacks either cause); with the fix both pass. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.authority-loss.test.ts` — green: 2 passed (2) in 57.33s.
- [x] Related targeted suites: `followup-runner.*.test.ts` sibling suites run with the fix applied; numbers below. Pre-existing unrelated failures are called out explicitly.
- [x] Behavior verification: before — the authority-loss catch branch re-checks `assertCurrent()` in a bare catch, discards the caught condition, never calls `internalEventExecution.onFailed`, and logs one constant line; the session-event lifecycle settles with the generic "Session event was abandoned before execution" text. After — `onFailed(original error)` runs before lifecycle settlement, so the persisted receipt names the real cause, and the log line names both the original failure and the failing authority condition. Queue disposition stays `consumed`, completion stays `aborted`.
- [x] Scope: one production file (`followup-runner.ts`, authority-loss catch branch only) plus a new regression test file. Queue disposition, retry policy, and all other branches are untouched.

This proves the diagnostic path preserves the cause at the followup-runner boundary when authority is revoked mid-run; it does not identify which upstream authority condition fires in a given production incident (the report itself marks that NOT_ENOUGH_INFO). The fix makes whichever condition fires visible in the receipt and logs.

The requested fix must make replies visible and persistent in WebChat AND deliver them to the original Telegram chat/topic with its exact transport thread preserved. The current draft repairs local WebChat routing only and does not yet implement that complete outcome.

## User Impact

Required outcome: a Telegram-origin conversation opened in WebChat delivers progress/final tool replies to both the WebChat transcript and its authorized original Telegram chat/topic, without changing the topic, account, or recipient and without duplicate messages. **This dual-surface behavior is NOT IMPLEMENTED by the current draft.** Pure WebChat, native Telegram, explicit destinations, opt-outs, and unrelated conversation boundaries must remain intact.

**Draft:** dual-surface implementation and its owning-entry/channel proof are pending, along with current-head required CI and completed ClawSweeper review. This PR is not ready to merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

The admitted turn now owns message-tool execution routing, while session-derived routing remains an ambient fallback. WebChat source admission selects the existing internal reply sink. Dashboard-authorized external reads retain their existing grant despite the new local source marker. Source completion and group-thread attribution use the same admitted account and thread.

## Evidence

The checks below cover the previous local-only candidate at `5ec70fe2283926ab6335f9d43bc10301c689b9a6`. They are retained evidence, **not acceptance proof for the corrected dual-surface requirement**.

- 450 focused tests passed across 17 suites: the requested eight message-tool/reply suites (279), outbound contracts/execution/mirroring/routing (115), and dashboard-read/hosted-transport/current-prompt consumers (56).
- The source-routing regression fails against base production for Telegram- and Discord-shaped WebChat sessions, then passes with the repair. This proves incorrect external route selection, not a live Telegram API failure. A separately discovered dashboard-read regression also has red/green proof.
- Core and affected test typechecks, type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed.
- Full `pnpm build` passed, including declarations and the Control UI. Its UI budget report emitted advisory size/request-count warnings; those warnings are not claimed resolved by this routing change.
- Auto Review of the complete candidate against `45b3fb10691ef02911a0ebb9e59060b239d09812`, with full routing/authorization, source-mirror, and group-thread context: P0–P2 `scoped-clean`, exit 0, no remaining findings. The earlier dashboard-read finding was repaired and rechecked.
- Added a real-Gateway Control UI regression for WebChat prompt → host admission → message tool → local progress → reload persistence. Only inference is synthetic. It typechecked, linted, and formatted; the initial browser attempt stopped before its test body because Chromium lacked native libraries. A subsequent, explicitly unpublished-candidate browser proof is recorded below. No real-model inference or live Telegram-service delivery is claimed.
- Measured focused test wall times: requested eight suites 53.48s; outbound siblings 59.20s; dashboard/transport/reaction suites 52.02s. Hosted CI seconds are not yet available.

### Unpublished dual-surface candidate: browser and loopback proof

This evidence covers the retained, **unpublished** candidate patch SHA-256 `2ba01337a61031f7a818153704ba3eaa150ac4b649b36e10259b1a145aec4786`, not this PR’s current code head. Product source was unchanged during this proof. Independent review admission remains blocked; no unreviewed product code was pushed.

- A real isolated Gateway and Chromium exercised a Telegram-origin private topic created through the real Telegram ingress path, then opened that same conversation in Control UI. The browser submitted an ordinary prompt; targetless progress and final message-tool replies each appeared once and survived reload.
- The actual Telegram plugin sent each reply exactly once to a task-local Bot-API-shaped HTTP peer: `chat_id: "123"`, `message_thread_id: 456`, account `default`. The persisted session discriminator contained `123:456`; the original transport topic remained the structured numeric `456`. The source record was produced by ingress, not seeded as an expected result.
- The loopback scenario passed (one test, 10.00s test time, 31.44s invocation). The separate unbound-WebChat browser scenario also passed. No external Telegram service or real inference provider was used; these remain separate acceptance gaps.
- Chromium native libraries came from signed configured Debian repositories, downloaded and extracted into task-private storage without root or system installation. The browser-dependency blocker is resolved for this sandbox.

These are **scenario-state before/after images of the unpublished candidate**, not a pre-fix/post-fix code comparison.

Before sending from WebChat — the conversation was established through native Telegram topic 456.

![Before the WebChat prompt in the original Telegram topic conversation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8824e8f2-1803-457f-ad5f-15d95c73f6ac)

After both message-tool replies and a browser reload — one ordinary progress message and one final result remain visible.

![After progress and final replies persist through reload](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cd12c3a1-196d-4803-b82c-d91bef4814dc)

### Unpublished candidate: local failure-independence repair

The November 16 owning-entry check reproduced a remaining defect in the prior retained candidate: a Telegram adapter exception left zero local assistant messages where one was required. That defect is now repaired **locally, not in this PR’s published code**. The new 27-file candidate patch SHA-256 is `28a8b012d48761b2bb184b345c47247b92c680891242b7de13b1d5ab1b112de5`.

- The existing internal sink persists the admitted WebChat reply before the normal original-destination send. Local persistence and the successful transport mirror use the same logical transcript receipt, so settlement/replay cannot add a second bubble. There is still only one external platform-send path, not a broadcast or second sender.
- The current user-turn identity is carried through the existing source admission/mirror context. A local final mirror is not a Telegram receipt: external errors remain errors, typed retry/queue custody is preserved, and the source-completion owner is not marked delivered on an external failure.
- The exact red assertion now passes. The final owning-entry suite passed **17 cases** (58.68s invocation), covering progress/final, cached failure replay, a new eligible attempt after retiring its cached failure, retry success versus repeated failure, one local row, exact account/chat/topic, explicit local opt-out, different-route isolation, and dry-run/no-side-effects. Adapter I/O is synthetic; these are not live Telegram-service tests.
- Additional owner checks passed **71 tests across five suites**, and the affected consumer graph passed **364 tests across 12 suites**; the owning regression overlaps those receipts and is not counted as extra unique coverage. Core plus messaging/agent-tools/Gateway test types, eight-file type-aware lint, targeted formatting, staged whitespace and test-budget checks passed.
- A fresh full build passed on the repaired source (2m 35.9s). Existing advisory UI-size/request-count warnings remain; they were not changed by this repair.

The prior browser screenshots below/above remain evidence for the older retained candidate, not a fresh browser qualification of this repair. Full independent review admission is still blocked. Parent-owned isolated QA is queued; frozen source-packet qualification is pending. No real external-service binding or live Telegram/provider proof is claimed. No unreviewed product code was committed or pushed, and the PR remains draft pending review, applicable real proof, current corrected-head CI and satisfactory completed ClawSweeper review.

### Unpublished candidate: explicit terminal source-reply visibility

A separate real-Gateway/Chromium scenario exercised native Telegram ingress followed by an explicit `message.send` with `final:true`, account `default`, chat `123` and structured transport topic `456`. Inference and the Telegram HTTP peer were synthetic; this is not live Telegram-service proof.

- The successful tool result reported `sourceReplyRoute: current-source`. The normal producer persisted exactly one terminal assistant mirror, and its `sourceTurnId` matched the naturally persisted inbound user message's idempotency key.
- The real stored row had `navigation_type=message`, `navigation_display=0` and `navigation_valid=1`. That row appeared once in the same authorized browser's `chat.history` and live transcript, including while the run still displayed Stop, then once after reload. The unrelated sibling conversation's DOM/history did not contain it. This covers same-user session isolation, not a new cross-user ACL test.
- The Telegram plugin made exactly one final HTTP send with `message_thread_id: 456`. The focused scenario passed (9.59s test time, 53.78s invocation); UI types, type-aware fixture lint and formatting passed.
- No additional product change was justified by this reproduction. In this source, `navigation_display=0` alone does not hide normal message events. The unpublished candidate, publication/review gaps and current PR head remain unchanged.

After reload — the explicit terminal reply remains an ordinary assistant message. This is scenario evidence, not a code-fix before/after comparison.

![Explicit final Telegram source reply remains visible after reload](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f366f597-1ac4-41b4-bf96-cde831362e4d)

Before ready: complete independent review and publish the corrected original-Telegram-topic implementation; prove exact chat/account/thread, progress/final, deduplication, retry/failure and opt-out behavior through the owning entry and applicable real UI/channel path; then verify current-head required CI and completed satisfactory ClawSweeper review. Missing implementation and proof are not waived by this draft.

prs.body:
Closes #189041

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes speech integrations losing structured provider failure details when TTS returns a failed synthesis attempt.

## User Impact

Callers can inspect optional HTTP status, provider/transport error code, WebSocket close code and retry delay without parsing human-readable messages. Existing messages, provider selection, fallback and retry policies are unchanged. No configuration migration or new dependency.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider HTTP owner already creates structured errors, but the shared TTS attempt projection drops those fields. Preserve a bounded subset on the existing result contract and document it. Numeric fields are range-checked; codes must be bounded machine tokens. No response bodies/headers are copied, no message parsing or nested-cause flattening is added, and ordinary logging is unchanged. Metadata is not a guarantee that retry is safe.

## Evidence

### Branch refresh — 2026-11-16

Current head: `25aee5199a37a3d0f0cd0e845fc0936be61a7374`, incorporating upstream main `ec025eba2df15ab949239fa17dfd99ac4286b50c` to resolve a real modify/delete conflict.

Upstream intentionally retired the old fallback test suite. This refresh keeps it deleted and relocates only this PR's metadata regressions into the existing `tts-runtime-routing.test.ts` fixtures. The production change remains the same 42-line additive projection; no retry/fallback policy or public-contract expansion beyond the original proposal. The obsolete allocation record is removed: the current test-line check passes with +89 lines within its 400-line allowance. The full diff is four files, +136 lines.

Source review found no actionable defect; exact-file formatting and diff whitespace checks passed. New executable tests and typechecks are **not yet verified**. prs.title: feat: let plugins finalize streamed speech without provider-specific code
prs.body:
Closes #187368

## What Problem This Solves

Voice-integration plugins need to upload audio during capture, then end input and obtain a complete transcript without implementing each speech provider's WebSocket protocol.

## User Impact

Plugins can use optional `api.runtime.mediaUnderstanding.transcribeAudioStream` through the existing typed plugin runtime, with ElevenLabs Scribe v2 Realtime as the first adapter. Existing continuous sessions keep synchronous `sendAudio` and their close/VAD behavior. Older hosts without the optional runtime method retain batch behavior.

Streaming requires an explicitly selected supported model and format. Omitted models, CLI selections, and unsupported batch-only profile/request/header/prompt/provider options return unsupported **before input is consumed**. Once admitted, failure throws instead of automatically replaying audio or changing provider. This does not make every existing batch provider realtime-capable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing session exposes callbacks and close, but no end-of-input acknowledgment covering every accepted sample. Add awaited finite writes/finalization, and let the runtime reuse media selection, policy, credentials, secret admission, and configured limits. The finite helper owns bounded completion/cancellation; ElevenLabs owns framing and acknowledged manual commits.

The consumer no longer imports a private-local SDK facade: the new operation is declared on the already-published `OpenClawPluginApi.runtime.mediaUnderstanding` type and lazily bound by the host. The private-local transcription/provider helpers remain private and official-provider-only. No new public subpath, package export, or blanket promotion of private SDK internals is introduced. Registered-plugin projection preserves optional absence and applies the existing selected plugin scope/revocation guard.

**SDK-owner decision requested before merge:** accept this optional extension of the existing typed runtime capability. This PR proposes that direction; neither the linked issue nor source review is represented as upstream owner approval.

## Evidence

### Branch refresh — 2026-11-16

Current head: `e1f81d130eaa93d960a237ffc0d1d1a4dbeb0f6f`, incorporating upstream main `ec025eba2df15ab949239fa17dfd99ac4286b50c` to resolve merge conflicts. The finite-input contract and no-replay-after-admission behavior remain unchanged.

The refresh follows upstream's split provider-context types and `PluginCapabilityCatalogHostContext`, preserves lazy saved-key lookup on both continuous and finite connections, and carries the upstream caller-authority callback through finite completion. Existing tests now cover direct/saved credentials and revoked caller authority before final commit. Upstream proxy, reconnect, backpressure and continuous-session behavior remain intact. No new retry loop, dependency or public SDK subpath was added.

Source review found no actionable defect; exact-file formatting and diff whitespace checks passed. The current test-line budget passed: +1468 test LF, 400-line allowance, 1068 allocation credit (reduced from the old record). The added growth protects progressive input, acknowledged completion, cancellation and live ownership at separate boundaries; no unrelated test allowance changed.

Fresh executable validation is **pending**, not passing. The local lint attempt could not initialize because this checkout lacks `eslint-plugin-solid`; this is an incomplete-tooling result, not a code verdict. No local full dependency installation, test/typecheck run, paid provider call, deployment or restart occurred. [Current-head GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43930692011) is `action_required`, waiting for upstream approval to run. Please approve the run; no test pass is claimed. Current test wall time and CI seconds are not yet available.

SDK-owner acceptance of the optional runtime contract remains required before merge. All proof below belongs to the explicitly named earlier revisions; it does not establish a pass for this refreshed head.

<details>
<summary>Historical evidence and review context — prior heads only</summary>

### Branch refresh — 2026-11-03

Refreshed PR head: `9cb1098365adeeff8f21e97bbc75d73f9e77430c`, integrating upstream main `a4727b5506f371ae656fbee82fa93a3f29d91157`.

The only textual conflict was adjacent import additions in `src/realtime-transcription/websocket-session.ts`. The resolution retains both `createNodeProxyAgent` from merged proxy fix #187369 and the finite-runtime `getPluginRuntimeGatewayRequestScope` import. Main's environment-proxy routing and provider-shutdown queued-audio cleanup (#191761), and this PR's finite lifecycle and final-effect ownership checks, are preserved. The feature diff remains 28 files, +2347/-38 against the incorporated main.

Executable validation for this refreshed head is owned by [GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41663533787). The run completed **failure**: all 108 scheduled jobs finished, with **76 passed, 28 skipped and 4 failed**. The failures are the three component jobs described below plus their dependent aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`; there were no additional component failures. Production and test types, architecture/source contracts and documentation checks have passed. No local dependency installation, build or test execution was used for this refresh. SDK-owner acceptance of the optional runtime contract remains requested before merge. Nothing has been merged upstream, installed or restarted.

### Current-head built-Gateway proof — passed on GitHub

[Job 126014134718](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41663533787/job/126014134718) passed the existing `finite-transcription.e2e.test.ts` through a built Gateway process, loaded consumer plugin, injected typed runtime, bundled ElevenLabs adapter and synthetic WebSocket origin. The emitted `FINITE_STT_GATEWAY_PROOF` records complete input of 288000 bytes, acknowledged commits at 256000/288000, the complete combined transcript, and cancellation after 32000 bytes with zero commits. There were two connections and zero unexpected HTTP requests. This is current-head process-boundary evidence, not a live ElevenLabs account, published-package or microphone claim.

### Current-head CI outcome and remaining blockers

- [Control UI E2E](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41663533787/job/126014131210): the Brave/Firecrawl settings-edit mock-request timeouts match [scheduled-main job 125978618719](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41653621604/job/125978618719), including the same test/stack locations and empty request log. The affected UI test, controls, suite support and mock Gateway helper are byte-identical across that baseline, incorporated main and this PR.
- [Core lint stripe 4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41663533787/job/126015859338): `ui/src/pages/about/view.test.tsx:143:32`, `typescript(no-misused-spread)` on the navigator spread. This file is byte-identical to incorporated main (blob `affa75cf344c6dc3989243a7934fb6411fbc68f4`); the older scheduled baseline has a different lint failure, so a matching baseline execution is **not** claimed.
- [Test-line ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41663533787/job/126014132071): global total 6437667 exceeds effective ceiling 6437534 by 133. The exact CI merge/base comparison adds this PR's 1442 test lines and exactly 1442 allocation credit, leaving the same 133-line base-tree deficit. No baseline/credit increase or check waiver was applied.

The [aggregate CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41663533787/job/126026091513) failed because those three dependency groups failed. These findings do not represent passing CI or permission to waive its gate. No unrelated UI repair or CI rerun was performed. The older proof below remains explicitly prior-head evidence.

### Prior-head process and lifecycle evidence

The proof sections below were executed on `79b395a14b0a03bf31c66a88e950a7c13af83232` or the explicitly named earlier heads.

### Stronger process-boundary proof — executed on this head

The new `test/e2e/qa-lab/media/finite-transcription.e2e.test.ts` replaces the duplicate mocked happy-path test with a real Gateway process. [Exact-head build and execution job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40886048121/job/123490837973) **passed**:

1. Existing CI built `qaRuntime` with private-QA support for this directly selected E2E. The existing media-Gateway owner starts the prepared CLI with packaged plugins and isolated configuration/state; no live installation is involved.
2. The Gateway loads a temporary consumer plugin and the bundled ElevenLabs adapter. An authenticated Gateway RPC invokes the consumer's injected `api.runtime.mediaUnderstanding.transcribeAudioStream`; the test does not call that implementation directly. The returned Gateway PID must differ from the test PID.
3. Producer gates hold source input after the first 32000-byte upload reaches the actual WebSocket origin. The test then releases the remaining input and requires 288000 bytes, commits at 256000/288000 bytes and the complete combined transcript.
4. A second RPC request is canceled through the loaded plugin while input is stalled. It must close the actual socket with only 32000 bytes, zero commits and no batch replay.

This extends executed proof beyond in-process registration/provider composition to CLI bootstrap, plugin discovery/loading, authenticated Gateway RPC and the built runtime. The job ran `pnpm build qaRuntime` with `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1` successfully (13:56:06–13:59:03 UTC), then executed the E2E with `OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1`. The test passed in 48.581 seconds (85.06 seconds for the file), with shard exit 0. Those durations include test/Gateway work and are **not transcription-latency benchmarks**.

Actual `FINITE_STT_GATEWAY_PROOF` emitted by that execution:

```json
{"entry":"Gateway RPC -> loaded consumer -> typed host runtime -> bundled ElevenLabs -> WebSocket","complete":{"bytes":288000,"commits":[256000,288000],"result":{"result":{"supported":true,"text":"First segment. Final starlight.","no_speech":false,"mode":"realtime","provider":"elevenlabs","model":"scribe_v2_realtime"},"inputEnded":true,"gatewayPid":5508}},"cancellation":{"bytes":32000,"commits":[]},"connections":2,"unexpectedHttp":0}
```

The Gateway PID in the result was asserted different from the test process. This still uses a **synthetic protocol origin**, not live ElevenLabs recognition, a published npm artifact or physical satellite. No such broader claim is made.

Fresh independent source review of the proof found no actionable P0/P1/P2 after fixing the shared audio-selection config and using the existing prepared media-Gateway owner, claimed listener and joined cleanup. Formatting, commit hooks, line caps, strict extension import boundaries and whitespace checks passed locally. No new workflow, QA-lab source changes, public SDK exports, dependency installation or full local build/test rerun were added.

### Executed lifecycle and transport proof on `351cad743` (unchanged production code)

- The existing private request scope binds the real registered consumer's authority assertion and instance disposal signal before awaits. Final socket construction/send, finite frame/commit, resumed acknowledgment and completion recheck that owner. No new public authority parameter, lifecycle manager or polling loop. Bare record revocation fences the next continuation/effect; actual disposal also cancels stalled runtime waits.
- **Red baseline:** tests/helper-only `9da755ec7b9c64d7edcb38b61b3fa389082d034b`, unchanged production `60b79011`, failed all six real-owner revocation cases with "promise resolved instead of rejecting"—not setup failures. [Core final connect/send](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40869483776/job/123433196562), [registered consumer/runtime/ElevenLabs/socket](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40869483776/job/123433196535).
- **Green after repair:** [final WebSocket connect/send](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40872410391/job/123443230837) passed; [actual registered-consumer/runtime/provider composition](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40872410391/job/123443230833) passed all seven finite-runtime tests, including all four revocation cases.
- Observed `FINITE_STT_BOUNDARY_TRACE` records in the latter job:

```json
[
```

prs.title: fix(stt): retain realtime provider and connection failure codes
prs.body:
Closes #189042

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes realtime speech consumers losing provider error codes and pre-readiness WebSocket close codes from transcription failures.

## User Impact

Callers receive `errorCode` on ElevenLabs protocol Errors and `closeCode` on pre-readiness socket Errors. Error messages, callback delivery, connection lifecycle and provider-owned reconnection are unchanged. No configuration migration, new dependency or retry policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve classification at the existing error producers: the ElevenLabs helper retains the explicit code, falling back to the event type; the shared transport retains the numeric close code. No raw payload or close-reason metadata is copied. This is independent of finite-utterance STT work and the separate TTS metadata PR.

## Evidence

### Maintenance check — 2026-11-16

This fix remains needed on upstream main `ec025eba2df15ab949239fa17dfd99ac4286b50c`: the ElevenLabs error producer still omits `errorCode`, and the shared transport still omits the pre-readiness `closeCode`. GitHub reports this PR mergeable without conflicts. The patch remains unchanged at `666c2a5e07828b84ecb39740a2b6d2d7d9a80f53`; no unnecessary base merge or empty commit was added.

The existing exact-head CI and before/after transport proof below are historical evidence, not a new current-base test run. The latest review found no actionable defects and marked this ready for maintainer review. No new runtime validation or deployment is claimed.

**Reviewed head:** `666c2a5e07828b84ecb39740a2b6d2d7d9a80f53`. **Pre-fix production base:** `3f2791e7b620d5023877090e56e265df3f3cfa47`.

- [Exact-head upstream CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41170379928), including selected tests, production/test types, lint and guards.
- [GitHub-hosted standalone runtime proof: PASS](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/41175867415/job/124463178906). A plain Node process calls public `getRealtimeTranscriptionProvider("elevenlabs", cfg)` to cold-load the shipped provider through native discovery/registration, then connects its actual WebSocket transport to a controlled loopback endpoint. No provider factory, registry, parser or transport is mocked or manually seeded.
- Three real transport cases pass before and after: explicit protocol code before readiness, event-type fallback after readiness, and pre-ready close 1011. The base omits the fields; the candidate delivers `rate_limited`, `input_error`, and 1011 respectively. Each case makes exactly one connection and one error callback. Rejected connections expose the identical Error to the callback and `connect()` rejection; no raw close reason is retained.
- The existing selected regressions fail on pre-fix production files at the intended metadata assertions (2 provider cases + 1 close case), then all 3 pass after restoring exact candidate files. No fixture/setup failure is counted as an expected regression.
- Regression command wall time, including compiler preparation: 171.585s before / 160.992s after, entirely on GitHub.
- [Download SHA-verified receipts, JSON test results and terminal traces](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/41175867415/artifacts/13033411725). [Immutable harness](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/tree/03ab7fba323c7ad2584b9c52bdba1738bfafbeaf/proof/speech-errors). Earlier harness attempts stopped while interpreting abbreviated/redacted Vitest assertion output; the corrected reader verifies the selected metadata assertion and failure count. No product changes or passing-head substitutions were made to resolve those harness failures.

<details>
<summary>Redacted runtime trace excerpt</summary>

```json
{"proof":"stt","expected":"base","scenario":"explicit-code-before-ready","provider":"elevenlabs","requests":1,"callbacks":1,"connectRejected":true,"callbackMatchesRejection":true,"errorCode":null,"closeCode":null,"rawCloseReasonRetained":null,"ok":true}
{"proof":"stt","expected":"base","scenario":"message-type-after-ready","provider":"elevenlabs","requests":1,"callbacks":1,"connectRejected":false,"callbackMatchesRejection":null,"errorCode":null,"closeCode":null,"rawCloseReasonRetained":null,"ok":true}
{"proof":"stt","expected":"base","scenario":"close-before-ready","provider":"elevenlabs","requests":1,"callbacks":1,"connectRejected":true,"callbackMatchesRejection":true,"errorCode":null,"closeCode":null,"rawCloseReasonRetained":false,"ok":true}
{"proof":"stt","expected":"head","scenario":"explicit-code-before-ready","provider":"elevenlabs","requests":1,"callbacks":1,"connectRejected":true,"callbackMatchesRejection":true,"errorCode":"rate_limited","closeCode":null,"rawCloseReasonRetained":null,"ok":true}
{"proof":"stt","expected":"head","scenario":"message-type-after-ready","provider":"elevenlabs","requests":1,"callbacks":1,"connectRejected":false,"callbackMatchesRejection":null,"errorCode":"input_error","closeCode":null,"rawCloseReasonRetained":null,"ok":true}
{"proof":"stt","expected":"head","scenario":"close-before-ready","provider":"elevenlabs","requests":1,"callbacks":1,"connectRejected":true,"callbackMatchesRejection":true,"errorCode":null,"closeCode":1011,"rawCloseReasonRetained":false,"ok":true}
```

The harness verifies exact production-file hashes against the two revisions and executes the same current regression tests against both production states.

```sh
SPEECH_PROOF_EXPECT=base node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .speech-proof-stt.mts
# Restore candidate production files, then:
SPEECH_PROOF_EXPECT=head node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .speech-proof-stt.mts
pnpm test extensions/elevenlabs/realtime-transcription-provider.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'reports provider errors exactly once'
pnpm test src/realtime-transcription/websocket-session.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'reports pre-ready close failures'
```

</details>

Proof scope: registered source-SDK provider and real WebSocket transport, using synthetic credentials/events. Not a paid ElevenLabs cloud call, installed-package canary, Gateway conversation or microphone test. All dependency preparation and executable proof ran on GitHub. No production installation or auto-merge.

Production delta remains +14/-9; regression delta +19/-5 with allocation of 14 lines. No new upstream harness, finite-STT dependency, lifecycle or retry policy.

prs.title: feat(memory): let workspaces exclude generated files from search
prs.body:
Related: #101422 Supersedes #177868 by @CheekyHobson: their reviewed head `a2008ab09`, ported onto current main with co-author credit on the commit, plus the proof ClawSweeper asked for. ## What Problem This Solves Generated dreaming reports under `memory/dreaming/` are indexed like curated notes and crowd them out of memory search, and there is no setting to exclude paths inside the default memory folders. ## User Impact User impact: operators can set `memory.search.excludePaths` (globally or per agent), for example `["memory/dreaming/**", "memory/.dreams/**"]`, to keep matching workspace files out of memory search and file watching. - Unset or empty changes nothing. The index scope hash is identical to the one 2026.11.3 writes, so this setting adds no rebuild on upgrade. - Setting or changing the list is a scope change, like changing `extraPaths`: `openclaw memory status` reports it, vector search pauses, and `openclaw memory index` rebuilds and drops the excluded rows. - Search only: excluded files are not deleted, `memory_get` can still read them, `memory forget` still scrubs them, and short-term recall/promotion eligibility is unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made One workspace-relative glob check, using the same minimatch options as the `extraPaths` matcher beside it in the memory host SDK (so patterns behave the same on Node and Bun), is applied where search scope is decided: file discovery (local and remote workspace providers), watcher eligibility, and the index scope hash. Shared watchers include the exclusions in their selection keys, so agents with different exclusions on one workspace rebaseline when one joins or leaves (the P2 ClawSweeper found on #177868). **Portable glob matching (ClawSweeper's 2026-11-09 review on `05585b7`):** the exclusion matcher called `path.posix.matchesGlob`, which Bun implements with `Bun.Glob`: extglobs never match and wildcards match dotfiles, so `["memory/dreaming/**/!(*.keep).md"]` excluded a report on Node but not on Bun. Main's #194912 had just moved the `extraPaths` matcher to minimatch for the same reason. `1463f6e` moves those minimatch options into one shared constant and uses it for `excludePaths` too, with compiled matchers cached per configured list. Results on Node are unchanged; on Bun they now match Node. Changes compared with #177868 at `a2008ab09`: - Rebased onto main: the scope hash goes through the single `resolveConfiguredMemoryScopeHash()` owner, and the matcher is exported from `plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-engine-fs`, the subpath #181891 narrowed the file worker to, instead of `engine-storage`. Both are private local-only subpaths, so this adds no third-party SDK contract. - The matcher lives in `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts` beside `matchesExtraMemoryPathEntry` instead of core `src/memory/root-memory-files.ts`. - Added the config field label, corrected the docs about the rebuild step, and linked the setting from the dreaming docs. - Tests: replaced the 13 s CLI e2e case with a manager test of about 4 s that mirrors two unforced `openclaw memory index` runs (the real CLI run is below). Dropped a test that indexed an excluded file through a private method, a `selectionKeys` shape test covered by the join/leave behavior test, a worker integration test that still passed with the P2 fix reverted, and (after ClawSweeper's review) a test that only checked the worker request shape. Size against main `11a13b6`: production +89/-21 in 15 files (including moving main's glob options into the shared constant); tests +159/-3; docs +16/-4; generated baselines +3/-3. (#177868 was +439/-18 in 33 files.) ### Maintainer decision needed #101422 asks for both search exclusion and recall/promotion eligibility control. This PR is the narrow first stage: search discovery, watching, and index scope only, with defaults and promotion safeguards unchanged. ClawSweeper's review of #177868 recommended approving that narrow search stage and leaving recall inclusion and diagnostics to follow-up work; the alternative is one combined search+recall include/exclude design. An operator on #101422 said the search-only step covers their need. Config surface: `pnpm config:docs:gen` raises the core count by 4 (2654 -> 2658 on main `b03fd2f`) for `memory.search.excludePaths` and `agents.entries.*.memory.search.excludePaths`, each with its `.*` item path. That is the new setting itself. ## Evidence Real runs on head `c210875` (on main `c7152f3`), starting from the latest stable release, `openclaw@2026.11.3` from npm (installed with `--ignore-scripts`; the CLI runs without the package's install scripts). The branch CLI on `c210875` reports `2026.11.2` because main's version string trails the release. Earlier runs from 2026.11.2 on `1463f6e` and on `05585b7` (before the portable-matcher change), from 2026.11.1 on `6d9ace7` and from 2026.10.10 on `b607675` showed the same behavior. Synthetic workspace: 3 curated files (`MEMORY.md`, `memory/backups.md`, `memory/garden.md`) and 7 generated reports (5 light, 2 REM, one REM report containing only "No strong patterns surfaced."). Isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` under `env -i`, Node 26.12.1, and a local OpenAI-compatible embeddings stub on 127.0.0.1 (deterministic vectors, no provider calls). **Upgrade from 2026.11.3 and existing data:** 2026.11.3 builds the index (10 files, 10 chunks). After this branch's `doctor --fix` (main's agent-database migrations since 2026.11.3, v27 -> v41), the existing index loads clean (`Dirty: no`) and returns the same results and scores as 2026.11.3, before any re-index. With `excludePaths` unset, `memory index` keeps the stored scope hash, the chunking version and every stored chunk row (same count and same fingerprint over `id`, `path`, `hash`). This PR adds no database schema or stored fields; the scope hash changes only when `excludePaths` is set. **Opting in:** setting `excludePaths` marks the index dirty with a scope change and pauses vector search until a rebuild, both shown in `memory status`. `memory index` then drops the 7 reports and keeps the 3 curated files; the curated note ranks first, and an edit refreshes it.
Terminal output (paths redacted to $OPENCLAW_HOME) ```text $ openclaw --version # npm openclaw@2026.11.3 OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d) $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.449 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.279 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.272 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.266 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.260 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.254 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 # stored index identity (2026.11.3): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":6} # stored rows (2026.11.3): {"chunks":10,"chunkIdsSha256":"e538aca49c37a70e"} $ openclaw --version # this branch OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (c210875) $ openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive # main's state migrations since 2026.11.3 Upgraded agent database schema in $OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: v27 -> v41 $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/10 files · 10 chunks Dirty: no $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main # existing 2026.11.3 index, before any re-index 0.449 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.279 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.272 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.266 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.260 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.254 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. # stored index identity (this branch, no excludePaths): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":6} # stored rows (this branch, no excludePaths): {"chunks":10,"chunkIdsSha256":"e538aca49c37a70e"} $ openclaw config set memory.search.excludePaths '["memory/dreaming/**","memory/.dreams/**"]' --strict-json Updated memory.search.excludePaths. Restart the gateway to apply. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/3 files · 10 chunks Dirty: yes Index identity: index scope changed (owner: configuration, code: scope) Vector search: paused until memory is rebuilt $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 3/3 files · 3 chunks Dirty: no # indexed rows by path: {"path":"MEMORY.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/backups.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/garden.md","chunks":1} $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. # edit memory/backups.md: 02:30 -> 03:15 $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 03:15 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. ```
**Gateway watcher:** a throwaway loopback Gateway with `excludePaths` set. One agent turn opens the Gateway's default memory manager and its watcher: a local chat-completions stub calls `memory_search` once, through `dispatch_action`, because current main keeps `memory_search` behind Tool Search for this model. Then, with no further CLI calls, a new dreaming report is written and the curated note edited: the watcher refreshes the note within about 2 s and never indexes the report.
Terminal output ```text $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw gateway run --bind loopback ... # throwaway Gateway [gateway] ready $ openclaw agent --agent main --message "When does the nightly backup run?" # stub model calls memory_search once via dispatch_action Done. tool call: dispatch_action {"id":"memory_search","args":{"query":"nightly backup"}} # memory_search result paths (from the stub log): memory/backups.md # indexed memory/ rows before edits: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # wrote memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-29.md and edited memory/backups.md (02:30 -> 04:45); no CLI calls from here # after the Gateway watcher sync (~1s), plus 5s more: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 04:45 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # dreaming rows: {"dreamingRows":0} ```
**Regressions fail without the fix:** - `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts` "rebaselines shared exclusions when a differently scoped agent joins and leaves" fails with `excludePaths` removed from `selectionKeys` ("expected setScopes to be called once, but got 0 times"). - `manager-workspace-files.test.ts` "drops generated Dream reports once excluded and keeps curated edits fresh" fails when the config resolver drops `excludePaths` (the report is still found). - `internal.test.ts` "keeps generated dreaming reports out of default and overlapping extra paths" also lists files with `memory/dreaming/**/!(*.keep).md`. With the old `path.posix.matchesGlob` matcher, `listMemoryFiles` under Bun still returns the report: on stock Bun 1.3.14 it lists `memory/current.md, memory/dreaming/light/pinned.keep.md, memory/dreaming/light/report.md`, and with `1463f6e` only `memory/current.md, memory/dreaming/light/pinned.keep.md`. On Node both matchers agree, so the Node run passes either way; the CI shard that runs this test (`checks-node-changed-compact-large-6`) sets up the pinned Bun 1.4.4 test runtime. **Changed test files** (`pnpm test --maxWorkers=1` on `685db0c`, same test code as `8eb4b7b`, where they pass again; CI seconds to follow): | File | Result | Wall | Vitest duration | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts` | 29 passed | 48s | 41.65s | | `manager-reindex-state.test.ts` | 49 passed | 40s | 36.19s | | `manager-workspace-files.test.ts` | 11 passed | 71s | 64.91s | | `watch-policy.test.ts` | 6 passed | 47s | 41.51s | | `internal.test.ts` | 43 passed | 4s | 749ms | | `memory-search.test.ts` | 39 passed | 46s | 42.06s | Vitest time is mostly cold transform; the new manager case takes about 4 s and the other new cases take 1-24 ms. **Checks:** `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` on `83eb31b` (main `200afde`, same code) passes typecheck (core, core tests, extensions, extension tests), lint, format, config docs baseline, Plugin SDK package exports, plugin boundaries and the other changed-file guards. Three lanes fail outside this PR: wrapper shadowing (`buildSkillWorkshopPromptSection`) and the public Plugin SDK surface budget (`agent-harness-runtime`) fail identically on clean main `200afde`, and the dead-export scan lists only auto-reply, gateway and UI exports this PR does not touch. The `pnpm check:docs` content checks pass. Test lines grow by a net +154, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/memory-search-exclude-paths-188294.txt`: default scope-hash compatibility, the shared-watcher rebaseline, discovery and portable (Node/Bun) glob matching, and the exclusion rebuild. **PR CI:** earlier runs had failures inherited from main: `read-file.test.ts` after the fs-safe 0.26.14 bump (#188352) and `archive-restore.postgres.test.ts` from #155538, both fixed on main (#188531, `34a4e118dc1`), then `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` while main was over its test-line ceiling (main's own scheduled job logged the same overage with net delta 0). #188780 restored the headroom. The branch merged main `11a13b6` at `2401ff9`, `1463f6e` adds the portable-matcher fix (its CI passed), `c210875` merged main `c7152f3`, `edb9fd1` merged main `aab88e3`, `fc2ef72` merged main `ba6147a`, `5985aa9` merged main `81ca4f4`, and `e768746` now merges main `b03fd2f`; earlier merges conflicted only on the generated config baseline, which was regenerated each time, and the PR diff is unchanged. The v2026.11.3 proof above ran on `c210875`. `edb9fd1`, `fc2ef72`, `5985aa9` and `e768746` add only main's changes. In `5985aa9` and `e768746`, main's #195369 adds an embedding-cache hook to `manager-sync-base.ts` and #197128, #198348, #199226 and #199694 edit other entries in `schema.help.models.ts`; both files merge cleanly next to this PR's lines. In `edb9fd1`, main's #196480 changed session-export paging in neighboring memory-core sync files, which do not call the file listing, the exclusion matcher or the scope hash. Main's #194912 replaced `path.posix.matchesGlob` in the `extraPaths` matcher in `internal.ts`, which this PR also edits; the merge kept both, and `1463f6e` then shares main's options with the exclusion matcher. Main's #139230 reworked dirty-index maintenance and the watcher's background sync in `manager-watch-ops.ts`, which this PR also edits; the merge keeps this PR's one `excludePaths` line there, and `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts`, `watch-policy.test.ts` and `manager.watcher-config.test.ts` pass on `e768746`. Main's #191749 bounded the realpath deduplication at the end of `listMemoryFiles`; it merges cleanly because `excludePaths` filters files as they are collected, before that step. Main's #192488 moved the search manager types into `search-manager.types.ts`; this PR does not import them. Main's #193952 added provider name and icon help to `schema.help.models.ts`, which this PR also edits; both sets of entries merge cleanly. On `1cc43f3`, `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (and so `ci-gate`) failed because main `bf10667` was over its own test-line ceiling by 137 lines; main's own scheduled job logged the same overage and passed only because that run added no test lines. Main `d1ffc39` got back under the ceiling, and the ratchet passes locally on `e768746` (net +154 test lines, covered by this PR's 154-line allocation). On `df4f9e6`, `check-prompt-snapshots` failed on three JSON prompt snapshots this PR does not touch: main's #192596 stopped formatting JSON snapshots without regenerating the committed ones (the content was identical, only the layout differed). Main fixed it in #192628, `5d93337` merged that fix, and `prompt:snapshots:check` passes locally on `e768746`. prs.title: fix(config): prevent PostgreSQL startup failure during backup recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a PostgreSQL-backed Gateway can fail to start when recovering a valid backup after its active configuration unexpectedly shrinks.

## User Impact

Users can restart the Gateway and recover the retained settings without the “PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker” failure. Recovery retains its source, backup-selection and lease-ownership checks. No schema or storage-format change is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepared recovery now uses the existing asynchronous backup validator. The final durable lease-ownership read uses existing engine-store admission while remaining synchronous immediately before filesystem effects. Expired or revoked ownership still refuses recovery.

## Evidence

Exact PR head: `f4f3b0cf1fcfbba16b8d19038300844f8b3cee05`.

- [Independent disposable Gateway proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193596#issuecomment-6664220296): clean exact-head worktree, Node 24.22.2, pnpm 12.15.0 frozen install and runtime build, PostgreSQL 16.15 / pgvector 0.8.7. A real Gateway accepted 13,269 bytes, then cold-recovered from an 873-byte active config with the retained backup. Ready in 7.37 seconds; clean shutdown; restored coach/bootstrap roster and preserved clobbered snapshot. Subsequent real local tool requests returned 401 without authentication, 200 for authenticated session_status and 404 for policy-disallowed read.
- [Official stable upgrade and retained-data proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193596#issuecomment-6665250290): stable 2026.11.1 → exact-head SQLite upgrade and explicit native Doctor migration → supported PostgreSQL state-family port → actual cold backup recovery → another restart. Public RPCs preserved the same session ID, message ID, history, label and thinking preference. Recovery logged `size-drop-vs-last-good:13915->1179`; the state anchor matched the port manifest and PostgreSQL schema.
- 23 async-recovery tests and 34 PostgreSQL recovery/lease/SQLite tests pass. Regressions cover the failing cold metadata path, expired/revoked leases refusing filesystem changes, and ordinary main-thread PostgreSQL reads remaining forbidden. Production types, scoped typed lint and the worker-boundary ratchet pass.
- [Latest exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193596#issuecomment-6663467986): sufficient real proof, no actionable findings, ready for maintainer review.

Stable used SQLite for shared state and agents; the proof does **not** claim a stable PostgreSQL-state upgrade. Only shared state was ported; agent/session storage remained SQLite. Doctor completed with two Skill Workshop policy-inspection findings, disclosed in the evidence. Live inference/channel behavior and broad exact-head hosted CI remain unqualified.

Downstream source `149ae747c2dc53310ee7c71ba89f2864a7f5a8b8` has byte-identical production fixes and passed the full package build, matching build-info, sequential root/Mattermost packs, archive checks, installed pair and actual Linux full-plugin-installer. Separate prelaunch authoring work is tracked in #193636; normal recovery restoring its accepted backup roster remains intentional.

This recovery fix can land independently of #193636. I checked OpenClaw main at `8ae6b3852f97`: both recovery gaps are still present, and none of the files in this PR have changed on main since its base.

[Hosted CI after marking ready](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43044906589) failed its bundled UI shard. The real-Gateway home-read-only test received `UNAVAILABLE` from `chat.metadata` while preparing metadata for the main agent. Attribution to this PR is unverified. The focused cold recovery and upgrade results above still apply to their recorded scenarios.

prs.title: fix: avoid synchronous compiler files during plugin loading
prs.body:
Related: #200136, #200162

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: loading captured TypeScript and JSX plugins can stall Gateway requests while synchronous compiler output writes wait for a filesystem transaction.

## User Impact

Compilation consumes verified captured text and delivers generated modules through load hooks, eliminating the compiler's synchronous source opens, output writes, temporary directory creation, and cleanup. This trades memory for event-loop safety: the measured 13.1 MB source fixture retains about 13.2 MB more heap. Preparation still has separate synchronous metadata paths being repaired in follow-up work; this PR does not claim a globally filesystem-free loader.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Team 25c97908 incident on 2026-11-16 at 05:02 PST showed a Gateway main-thread lock create blocked for 1.97 s in btrfs_create → start_transaction → wait_current_trans, producing a 2,002 ms event-loop stall during scheduler:update.remote-model-catalog. Back-to-back managed worktree removals triggered the filesystem commit. #200136 deleted that redundant catalog lock; this PR repairs the compiler boundary found by the same audit.

The existing capture traversal publishes stable typed-module execution paths and retains source text only after its existing hash/size verification. The compiler consumes those facts and supplies generated code through its existing hooks. Instance admission continues to own source resolution; only private generated helpers are resolved directly by the compiler. The temporary compiler tree and its lifetime are deleted. No new cache, configuration, schema, dependency, or protocol is added.

Production grows by 76 lines across nine existing modules. The growth carries verified text and execution paths through the existing capture projection and serves output/helper text in memory. It is a bounded representation change, separated from the larger capture-custody repair.

## Evidence

The real compiler mutation guard fails before the change. The final regression prepares the artifact through its actual worker, removes its captured typed source, and still executes the expected result from verified retained text with zero compiler mutations. The source-reopen regression also fails before the change. The shared observer also distinguishes read-only opens from writable string/numeric flags, including O_RDONLY | O_CREAT. Its new actual-open regression is red on the previous observer; that regression and the final compiler process guard pass together. Existing mutation guard coverage now includes this flow.

Initial focused runs passed 50 cases in five files and 192 cases with one existing skip in four interop/snapshot files. An attempted source-resolution shortcut caused eight startup-condition failures; it was removed because it bypassed instance admission. Final focused proof passes all twelve selected cases covering those eight failures, three existing resolve/compile cases, and the actual process guard. Core types, touched type-aware lint, script lint, format, and diff checks pass. Isolated Codex autoreview is clean P0–P2.

Two full `pnpm check:changed --base HEAD` runs completed. Task-owned findings were repaired and their final focused gates rerun. The unchanged dead exports reproduce on exact parent 6670297776a00 and were introduced by 24385a20428a / #200056; they are a main regression, not a waived baseline. The complete command is not claimed green on final source. Exact-head PR CI remains the broad gate.

Twenty serialized fresh Node 26.12.1 processes provide five A/A controls and five A/B pairs, with separate first-use and warm operations. The fixture contains 200 typed files totaling 13,107,200 UTF-8 bytes; each operation executes twenty modules and checks their results. The surrounding synthetic 35 GiB database, 5,000 sessions, and 62,000 workspace files are not queried by this compiler owner. No Team data was used. Measurements are on APFS, not btrfs; filesystem audit instrumentation was excluded from timings.

| Warm median | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Preparation | 953.86 ms | 1,010.38 ms |
| Compile | 247.36 ms | 240.02 ms |
| Retirement | 10.95 ms | 14.63 ms |
| Total owner time | 1,214.18 ms | 1,255.91 ms |
| Main-thread CPU | 83.80 ms | 82.12 ms |
| Node process CPU | 1,061.33 ms | 1,153.37 ms |
| Main-isolate allocation | 48.41 MB | 62.17 MB |
| Prepared heap growth | 6.10 MB | 19.33 MB |
| Compiler mutation API calls | 42 | 0 |
| Compiler readFileSync / openSync calls | 40 / 40 | 0 / 0 |

A/A owner medians were 1,219.16 / 1,228.81 ms; allocation 46.30 / 48.95 MB; heap growth 6.084 / 6.088 MB. Owner p95 was 1,331.97 → 1,474.92 ms. The 28.4% allocation increase and 33.6% retirement increase are accepted, measured costs: retained text accounts for about 13.23 MB and preparing all 200 aliases adds cleanup compared with twenty demand-created compiler files. No speedup or noise claim is made. Separate profiles show existing compiler child execution remains the dominant cost. The reproducible workload is included in this PR.

Twenty native alias canonicalization calls remain, as does a host-module Jiti lstat. Cold dependency loading, known plain JS/CommonJS native loading, legacy synchronous capture, and unknown runtime-selected imports remain explicit follow-up boundaries. Removing alias canonicalization by bypassing admission was demonstrated incorrect and is not part of this fix. Runtime UI import tracing found no changed module in the production or browser-test closures; no browser-facing Node import was introduced.

Initial CI 43921438718 failed only the HTTP runtime-readiness fixture. The identical case fails on exact CI main parent 410c0dda40702e25263b49b8b7d0786a5e49e366: #200038 / 5bd858c0094a5b16dd3eb0864050502f3960e89a changed readiness from access to a probe plus stat without migrating this fixture. The included one-line-net test repair holds stat, returns its real identity, and preserves all liveness/draining assertions. The targeted case, affected types/lint, and fresh Codex review pass. This is a confirmed main regression repaired here, not ignored CI noise; production and measured compiler behavior are unchanged.

Final-head CI [43924328562](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43924328562) succeeded on94e6bd66b684c262b9c87e584aade952fd027880. Final ClawSweeper review6924654208 has zero open items; native review and preparation are complete. Landing is pending.
