prs.title: feat(update): keep each release in its own directory on OpenClaw-owned installs
prs.body:
Related: #197949 (design, slice 4). Builds on #198489 (linked-root Docker mode, now on `main`); this PR adds only the owned-prefix and follow-up modes to those harness files.

## What Problem This Solves

A package update on an OpenClaw-owned install displaces the old release from its path: two directory renames, whole-tree fingerprints, a launcher backup, deletion of the old tree inside the activation window, and a journal to survive a crash in between.

## User Impact

On macOS and Linux, installs made by `install-cli.sh` and the durable service copy at `<state dir>/npm` now keep each release in `<prefix>/releases/<id>/`, and `lib/node_modules/openclaw` becomes a link to the selected one. An update installs the new release beside the old one and switches the link with one rename; rollback renames a link to the previous release back. The previous release is never written and is kept for at least a day. `openclaw update status` lists the active and retained releases.

**This changes what existing installations do.** The first update by an updater with this change converts a plain package directory on those prefixes. npm prefixes you manage, `npm link` checkouts, pnpm, Bun, Git checkouts and Windows keep today's swap. A manual `npm install -g` into an owned prefix turns the link back into a directory; the next update converts it again.

## Why This Change Was Made

It implements route 3 of the [update generations design](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197949) as one cutover, because the parts only work together:

- **Install identity is the link.** `resolveUpdateInstallRoot` returns the link's own path for a release link, and maps a path inside the release the link currently selects to the link (a process finds its own root by real path). The executor key, child admission, the restart sentinel, post-core and native-receiver root checks, and the managed handoff lease key stay the same across a switch. A published updater on a linked root keys its leases by the release path, so a candidate child checking its executor grant takes the parent's spelling when `updateInstallRootsMatch` says both name one installation. Root discovery (`resolveOpenClawInstallationRootSync`, used by `resolveUpdateRoot` and Gateway update admission) maps the selected release to the link, which covers a start through the `bin` launcher. Only a link into `<prefix>/releases/<id>/lib/node_modules/openclaw` of the same prefix and owner counts.
- **Releases are installed where they stay.** `runGlobalPackageUpdateSteps` (flag set only by `openclaw update`) stages into `releases/<label>` and hands the stage to the switch instead of the swap.
- **The switch:** capture the link; stop the service; record `origin.packageRelease` (validated before the stop); create a temporary link, sync, recheck the lease and the captured link, rename, confirm, sync. Rollback decides from the link on disk (it handles a failure after the rename), and refuses a previous release whose content changed since it was recorded.
- **The layout never fails an update.** Everything that rules it out for this run is found before the Gateway stops, and the existing swap installs the same stage instead, with a warning on the `package-swap` step that names the reason; the next update tries the layout again. `installStagedPackage` in `package-update-release-switch.ts` is the one owner of that decision. The conditions: the candidate's `bin` links differ from the prefix's; `releases/` cannot be created or is on another filesystem than the package path (checked when the stage is allocated, so the candidate is staged beside the package path); the package path cannot be captured, the candidate cannot be read, the adoption prefix cannot be allocated, or the record fails its schema. A fallback over a release link turns the link back into a directory (the documented result of a manual `npm install -g`), and the next update adopts it again.
- **Adoption** (plain directory): the directory moves into `releases/` and a prepared link naming it takes its place, then the normal switch. Between those two renames the package path is missing. That moment is not journaled: the journal's candidate is a sealed tree, and nothing can run `openclaw` while the package path is missing anyway. A process killed there leaves `lib/node_modules/.openclaw.release-link-*` naming the unchanged old tree; renaming it onto `lib/node_modules/openclaw` restores the install. The docs say so. A failed second rename moves the directory back and keeps the leftover link if that fails too.
- **Run record:** optional `origin.packageRelease` (slot, from and to: path, `dev:ino`, version, build), kept exact by the codec beside `origin.packageStage` and removed from the public projection. Interrupted managed handoff reads the install identity through the link and takes the candidate from this record. `assertManagedServiceUpdateHandoffRoot` is unchanged.
- **Service bound to a release path:** a published updater run through the link writes the release's real path into the service definition (2026.10.9 and 2026.11.3 both do), which would keep the service on the old release after a switch. The npm destination gate retargets the update at that release, so the swap replaces it in place, as published updaters do, and the Gateway starts the new version. The update reports the package path as its root (`resolvePackageReleaseSlotForRootSync`), so the restart's service refresh reinstalls the service from the package path, and the next update switches releases. The warning names `openclaw gateway install --force` for the case where the restart cannot rewrite the definition or does not run (`--no-restart`). For the in-place swap, executor slot reservation accepts the release the link selects (`updateInstallRootsMatch`), and the publication journal is skipped because it publishes at the installation key, which is the link.
- **Retention:** after a verified update, a release is removed only when the link does not name it, no Gateway lease (`releases/.leases/`) holds it, no open update run names it, and it was not selected or changed for 24 hours. A switch stamps the release it deselects.

Not done here, by decision or for follow-up: Windows, npm-owned prefixes, the macOS app; the node host is not made a caller (it would move its activation without removing code), and its collection and `activation.lock` rule from slice 4 are left for a follow-up. A future release that adds or renames a `bin` command takes the swap for that update; the next update adopts the layout again. Only Gateways take leases; other processes rely on the 24-hour age. A plain CLI update killed between the switch and its post-switch Doctor is left to `openclaw update repair` (not exercised). `package-update-steps.ts` was already over the 700-line lint limit on `main`; the pnpm environment binding moved, unchanged, into `package-update-manager-preflight.ts`.

The design doc in #197949 is updated with an "as built" section for these changes.

## Evidence

Branched from `origin/main` a9a3d628b34ae; rebased onto 09d322ab2 before opening (the 45 commits between touch no update, package, root-discovery or Docker-cell path; typecheck and the release tests were rerun on the rebased head). Local runs on macOS (Node 26.12.1); Docker cells on linux/arm64.

**Red on base, green with the change** (each run with the production file reverted to `origin/main`, then restored):

| Test | Fails on base because |
| --- | --- |
| `package-release-slot.test.ts` › link path stays the installation identity across a switch | base keys the install by the release's real path |
| `package-update-release-switch.test.ts` (8 cases: record before change and before the database capture, previous release bytes unchanged, rollback, rollback after a post-rename failure, refused rollback of a rewritten release, adoption, launcher refusal, automatic rollback) | base swaps a directory over the link |
| `package-update-release-switch.process.test.ts` (real child, SIGKILL before the temporary link, after it and before the rename, after the rename and before confirmation, and between the adoption renames) | base never reaches those cuts and leaves no release layout |
| `update-command-executor-release-link.test.ts` › post-switch child runs under the installation's lease | base acquires a second lease for the new release path |
| `update-managed-service-handoff-interrupted-release.test.ts` (continue, not activated, neither) | base refuses the link as an unsafe publication object |
| `update-command-package-destination.release-link.test.ts` › service bound to a release path | base switches it (superseded: it is now updated in place, see below) |

Regression guards for defects found in review and Docker (red against the earlier version of this branch): collection age stamped at deselection, rollback reading the link after a failed `fsync`, adoption keeping its leftover link when both renames fail, restart sentinel accepting the selected release, record written before the database capture. Negative controls that pass on base too: `npm link` checkout, plain directory, another prefix's release, unselected release takes no lease, non-owned prefixes keep the swap.

**Docker published-driver cells** (`scripts/e2e/published-driver-update-docker.sh`, with #198489's linked-root mode; run before #198489 landed, with its commit cherry-picked):

| Cell | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Published 2026.11.3 → candidate on an `install-cli.sh`-shaped prefix, then candidate → second candidate (`OWNED_PREFIX=1 FOLLOW_UP=switch`) | Pass. The published updater's swap left a plain directory; the candidate's update adopted it, switched the link, kept the previous release byte for byte, restarted the Gateway on the new release (readyz 200, version checked, durable session kept), the service unit still names the package path, and `update status` listed both releases with the new one leased. |
| Same, second candidate's post-activation Doctor fails (`FOLLOW_UP=rollback`) | Pass. Switch, Doctor failure, database rollback, link pointed back, previous Gateway verified. A first run that wrote `origin.packageRelease` after the database capture failed here (database rollback refused, link left on the candidate); fixed. A control on a plain npm prefix (today's swap) rolled back. |
| Published 2026.11.3 on a linked root → candidate (`LINKED_ROOT=1`) | Pass, on earlier packages of this branch (first hop of superseded rollback runs). Those runs also found the post-core, native-receiver and executor-grant root checks fixed here. |

Update behavior per hop: published drivers on a plain prefix keep today's swap (plain directory stays); this candidate adopts on its first update of an owned prefix; published drivers on a linked root swap inside the release behind the link and keep it; this candidate refuses to switch a service a published driver bound to a release path.

**Suites** (`pnpm test` on all `package-update-*`, `package-release*`, `update-run-*`, `update-managed-service-handoff*`, `restart-sentinel*`, `update-plugin-cohort*`, `update-migrated*`, gateway update methods, `stale-install`, `openclaw-root`, `src/cli/update-cli/*` and `update-executor*`): 2,927 of 2,929 pass. Two `update-command-database-rollback.test.ts` variants hit the 120 s test timeout while the whole set ran in parallel; that file alone passes 16/16 on this branch (those variants 22–38 s) and on base (28–41 s). `pnpm tsgo:all` passes; oxlint and formatting clean on changed files; `pnpm lint:docker-e2e` passes; docs format and markdownlint clean.

**CI on 0225b110212, fixed in 7180dfe7401.** The local suites above covered `src/cli/update-cli/*` but not the `src/cli/update-cli.*.test.ts` files next to it, which is where most of the failures were:

| Failure | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 18 `update-cli.*.test.ts` files (compact shards) | `resolveUpdateRoot` called `resolveOpenClawInstallationRootSync`, which the shared update-cli mock of `openclaw-root.js` does not export. The destination gate also read the service layout before returning an owned destination, so tests whose layout read throws now reported `unreadable-layout`. | `resolveUpdateRoot` applies the reverse rule (`resolvePackageReleaseSlotForRootSync`) directly; the answer is the same because only a release slot was ever kept. The service layout is read early only when the package path is a release link. |
| `eager-import-closure`, `pr-wrapper-source-closure`, `pr-worktree-provision` | The PR wrapper imports `openclaw-root.ts`, which now imports `package-release-slot-path.ts`; the file was missing from `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt`, so extracted provisioners failed before receiving their private store. | Added it to the inventory. |
| `madge-import-cycles` | Type-only cycle between `package-release-slot.ts` and `package-update-swap-contract.ts`. | `PackageReleaseTarget` now lives in `package-release-slot.ts`. |
| `check-lint-core-3` | `prefer-array-find` in `package-release-slot.test.ts` (plain `oxlint` missed it; `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` reports it). | Fixed. |
| test-lines budget (+1,280 vs 400) | New subsystem tests. | Audited the touched files: three slot-level cases (adoption contents, launcher refusal, rewritten-release refusal) duplicated switch-level cases that also check that nothing stopped and that the inode is unchanged; removed them (-60 lines). The remaining +820 is recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/update-linked-package-root.txt`. |

Existing failures, the same on base 09d322ab2 with this branch's sources swapped out: `check-extension-package-tsc-boundary.test.ts` (the canary copy lacks `src/infra/directory-walk.ts`, imported by `native-declaration-emitter.mts` since #198661), `extensions/telegram/src/send.history.test.ts` › edited captions, `update-cli.fresh-doctor.test.ts` › Git version before a dry-run downgrade, and `update-cli.target-schema.test.ts` › previews explicit artifacts. On this Mac, `pr-worktree-provision.test.ts` › cold/warm PR siblings takes 184 s against its 120 s timeout when run alone; its other 17 cases pass. Rerun on 7180dfe7401: the failing files above pass apart from those cases, the release tests pass, and `pnpm tsgo:all`, madge, the test-lines ratchet, oxfmt and `run-oxlint` on changed files all pass.

**Merged `origin/main` (99157f8f8c4), CI on 7180dfe7401 fixed in af223b77056.** #198489 landed as eb1a21dad24; the merge takes `main`'s version of its five harness files and keeps only this PR's additions (owned-prefix and follow-up modes, two `package.json` scripts, the follow-up budget and env passthrough, docs). No history was rewritten. Remaining diff-caused failure on 7180dfe7401: `checks-node-changed-compact-small-11` › `update-command-executor-settlement.test.ts` (7 cases), whose hand-written mock of `update-install-root.js` lacked `updateInstallRootsMatch`, now used by the executor grant. The mock now spreads the real module and overrides only `resolveUpdateInstallRoot`; red 7 failed, green 22/22. That retires one `config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt` entry (pruned) and costs one test line (allocation 820 → 821). `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` failed in `mock-exports` on `src/infra/worker-request-diagnostics.test.ts`, a `main` file this PR does not touch, because the old ratchet base predated it; against current `main` the ratchet passes. The OpenClawKit, Telegram `send.history` and package-acceptance failures were fixed on `main`. On the merged head: `pnpm tsgo:all`, madge (0 cycles), test-lines and mock-exports ratchets, `lint:docker-e2e`, oxfmt and `run-oxlint` on changed files pass; 321 affected test files (`src/cli/update-cli*`, package release/update, managed handoff, restart sentinel, root discovery, PR wrapper closure, tsc boundary) pass apart from 9 cases that timed out or lost their temp state database under that parallel load; those three files pass 47/47 run alone.

**Fallback instead of refusal (head f094976013d).** The release layout no longer fails an update. Red runs used the production files of 30e5edc75b8 (e69fb641248 merged with `main`; of the changed production files only `update-command-target.ts` differs from e69fb641248, from `main`, and no case below exercises it); green runs are on the head.

| Removed refusal | Test | Red (refusal or failed update) | Green |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Candidate launcher differs | `package-update-release-switch.test.ts` › takes the package swap when the candidate's launchers differ, and the next update adopts again | failed `package-swap` step | committed through the swap with the warning, launcher replaced, previous release untouched; the next update adopts and switches |
| Package directory cannot be adopted (adoption prefix) | › takes the package swap when the previous directory cannot be adopted | failed step | committed, warning, no record written, the allocated adoption prefix removed |
| `releases/` cannot be created | › stages beside the package path when releases/ cannot be created, then swaps | failed `package-stage` | stage beside the package path, swap committed with the warning |
| `releases/` on another filesystem | › stages beside the package path when releases/ is on another filesystem | release stage on the other filesystem (adoption then refused after the Gateway stop) | plain stage, `releaseUnavailable` recorded, empty release prefix removed |
| Service bound to a release path | `update-command-package-destination.release-link.test.ts` › replaces the release in place when the service starts it by its real path | `foreign` refusal | `owned`, install target at the selected release, warning names `gateway install --force` |
| (in-place support) | `update-command-executor-release-link.test.ts` › reserves the selected release by its real path as the installation, and refuses a deselected one | reservation throws | selected release accepted, deselected refused |

Negative controls on the head: a candidate that adds a command the update does not manage still switches (red on 3813375e22f, which fell back on every such update); a plain package reached through a symlinked prefix keeps its journaled activation (`package-update-publication-durability.test.ts`, red on 1a25681257a, see review below); in-place composition (`resolvePackageReleaseStage` picks no release for a release root, the swap replaces it behind the unchanged link). Commands: `pnpm test` on each file above (red with the production files of 30e5edc75b8 checked out, then restored: switch 4 failed / 12, destination 1 / 2, executor 1 / 2; green on the head: switch 13 / 13, slot, retention, process, destination, interrupted-link, executor, settlement and interrupted-release files all pass, publication durability 19 / 19, reclamation 11 / 11, `test/scripts/update-restart-module-outcome.test.ts` passes).

Docker cells on this branch (`scripts/e2e/published-driver-update-docker.sh`):

| Cell | Package | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Published 2026.10.9 on a linked root, its service bound to `releases/2026.10.9` (asserted), candidate update, then a second candidate update (`LINKED_ROOT=1 FOLLOW_UP=rebind`) | 56bb795b3ef; 115668d2baa | Pass on both. Release replaced in place, link unchanged; the restart reinstalled the service from the package path (unit names no release path); Gateway on the new version; the second update switched to a new release with the service still on the package path. |
| Same start, Gateway stopped, update with `--no-restart` (`FOLLOW_UP=in-place`) | 56bb795b3ef (cell from f2ebcb5bb2c); 115668d2baa | Pass, 3 of 3 on 56bb795b3ef and 1 of 1 on 115668d2baa. Release replaced in place, link unchanged, warning with `gateway install --force`; after a service restart the Gateway runs the new version. |
| Published 2026.11.3 on an `install-cli.sh` prefix, prefix `bin/openclaw` replaced by an absolute link, candidate update, then a second candidate update (`OWNED_PREFIX=1 FOLLOW_UP=launcher`) | 56bb795b3ef; 115668d2baa | Pass on both. On 115668d2baa the cell starts from published 2026.11.4, the latest release, instead of 2026.11.3. The first update took the swap and recorded the launcher reason, `bin/openclaw` replaced, no empty release directory left; the second update adopted the directory and switched, service on the package path. |

All three cells were rerun on 56bb795b3ef (this branch merged with `main` at 3900bb2366e, which includes #198268). #198268 replaced the candidate canary with a runtime contract check: the release stage, the fallback swap and the in-place path still call the candidate check on the staged root before the swap, through the same `validateCandidate` callback (none of `package-update-*` or `package-release-*` changed). It also removed `updateRehearsalProtocol` from `package.json`, which the published drivers read on the first hop, so every cell's path changed. The later merges touch no file of this change and no harness file these cells load: bc8ef0c3b6d (10 commits), and 823fa6d2b07 (51 commits, through adf70ab2ecf, including #199882). Of the latter, only `package.json` scripts overlap; its `src/state` upgrade changes (#199847) are not imported from `src/infra`, `src/cli/update-cli` or `src/daemon`.

**Merged `origin/main` again (115668d2baa, then f094976013d).** 115668d2baa merges 171 commits through 99eb4aa8ce7. The update commits among them, read against this change:
- #199918 (ae678bf4c6b) refuses Gateway-started updates under a Windows Scheduled Task, in `update-managed-service-handoff.ts`, which this change also edits. The merge is textually clean. The new check runs at handoff admission, before any mutation, and the release switch, fallback swap, in-place path and executor reservation never reach it. The systemd admission it wraps is unchanged.
- #200004 (41b339be059) adds a config projection that only the team-server deploy controller uses, and passes semantic validation through Doctor's legacy-config repair. None of the paths above call it.
- #199943 (a238f1c6367) moves the Doctor migration context into its own module with no change in behavior.
- #200153 (181a0edf80e) touches the git update path and one error message.
- #200044 (82974f3026e) and #200171 (89d07fe54e1) change the upgrade-survivor assertions and frozen-target scripts. The published-driver cells do not load those files.
- #199897 (ef8d709a05a) makes one test-support function private.
- The coverage consolidations #198943 (b90c5739fa5) and #198936 (a0423637196) delete no file and no baseline entry this change adds or edits. Their two deleted update tests, `update-command-failure-recovery.test.ts` and `connect-hello.update-scope.test.ts`, were never changed on this branch.

The 2026.11.4 close-out (#199956, ea69fcbb62f) bumps the candidate to 2026.11.4 and records 2026.11.4 in `update-compat-inventory.json`, which the first-hop fixture reads. All three cells were rerun on the 115668d2baa tarball for that reason, and all pass. The follow-up fixture is now 2026.11.5-first-hop.1. f094976013d then merges 6 more commits through 4a74c61ae7c (Control UI, subagents, compaction, plugin tests, local path commands). They touch no update, package, daemon, Docker-harness, `package.json` or lockfile path, so no cell or unit file was rerun for them.

Checks:
- On 115668d2baa: `pnpm tsgo:all` exit 0. The 15 update test files pass (212 tests), and `main`'s handoff lifecycle and command tests pass (2 files, 94 tests).
- On the 99eb4aa8ce7 diff: `run-oxlint` on 50 changed code files, oxfmt on 59 changed files, `git diff --check` and `lint:docker-e2e` all pass.
- On f094976013d against 4a74c61ae7c: the mock-export ratchet, the test-lines ratchet (+1476 net, within 400 + 1076 allocation), madge (0 cycles), the PR wrapper closure test and `git diff --check` all pass.

**Known `main` defect: `--no-restart` while the Gateway runs.** The first in-place run on 56bb795b3ef, with the Gateway running, failed. The update exited 1: `openclaw doctor` failed with `Gateway process changed during maintenance drain`. The package was rolled back, the link was unchanged, and the Gateway was left running the new version from the rolled-back files (`Expected Gateway version 2026.11.3; observed 2026.11.4-first-hop.1`). Cause: under `--no-restart` the updater leaves the Gateway running. Every 30 seconds the Gateway checks `build-info.json` at its installation (`src/gateway/stale-install.ts`) and restarts itself when the package changed. If that check lands between the swap and update Doctor's stop of the old Gateway (`src/infra/update-candidate-predecessor-stop.ts`), Doctor reaches the restarting process and fails. A probe watcher polling `build-info.json` every 100 ms measured that window: 1.80–1.88 s for the in-place path, and 1.75–1.83 s for a plain install with a candidate from `main` b58c23cac0f. In one `main` run the self-restart fired 0.24 s before Doctor's stop. Runs: in-place 1 failure in 13; plain `main` 0 failures in 11, with that one near miss; 567a560ad1f (before #198268) 3 of 3 passed. The window is the same on both paths and runs after the swap, so this change does not cause or widen it, and #198268 (which removed a step before the swap) does not move it. The in-place cell now stops the Gateway before its `--no-restart` update, with every assertion unchanged, so it checks the in-place replacement without that race. The race is left for a separate fix at the drain or installation-check owner; its evidence is with the fix owner.

A first `rebind` cell on 038d6fb8080, which switched the link and left the rebind to the restart, failed: post-update revalidation re-inspects the service against the recorded root, which now resolved to the new release, and stopped with `service-revalidation-failed`. Published 2026.11.3 on a linked root binds its service to the release as well, so the in-place update is the only path for that state.

Refusals kept, because they protect an installation another writer is changing, not a layout precondition: the link and candidate rechecks immediately before the rename (`switchPackageReleaseLink`), the rollback guard when another writer changed the link, refusing a rewritten release as a rollback target, and a failed write of the run record (`onPackageRelease`, after the Gateway stop): that is the run ledger, which the swap's own transaction writes use too, and interrupted-handoff recovery reads the record. A link changed between capture and the first rename is not captured again: the record and the database capture already name the previous release.

Cleanup after a fallback: the stage under `releases/<label>` loses its release marker and is removed by the steps' stage cleanup (the Docker launcher cell asserts no empty release directory); its packages were moved out by the swap. Old releases stay while the package path is a plain directory, because collection runs only behind a link; the next update adopts and its collection removes unselected releases older than 24 hours that no lease or open run names.

Review: the repository autoreview helper cannot run on this machine; an independent reviewer agent reviewed 038d6fb8080. High: the in-place swap would be refused by executor slot reservation and would publish over the link through the activation journal; fixed (selected-release reservation, journal skipped for a release behind its link), with the reservation test and the in-place Docker cell. Low: the gate's restart condition differed from the restart decision; superseded by always updating in place. Low: adoption-prefix cleanup untested; the adoption test now fails after the prefix exists and asserts its removal. A later review of 1a25681257a found the journal skip matched any non-canonical spelling; confirmed with the symlinked-prefix test and fixed, the skip now reported through `onUnavailable`. CI on b3f067fb361 then found two regressions from this work, fixed in 567a560ad1f: the broad reservation check let an occupied symlink slot skip its own lease (`update-managed-service-handoff-reclamation.test.ts`), and plain swaps called the release owner, which the swap fixture stubs (`update-restart-module-outcome.test.ts`).

The `update-cli.candidate-admission.test.ts` failure noted for 567a560ad1f was `main`'s stale test, which #198268 fixed. It passes on 56bb795b3ef, along with the other update files this change touches (15 files, 212 tests), and again on 115668d2baa (15 files, 212 tests; with `main`'s handoff lifecycle and command files, 2 files, 94 tests).

**Not proven:** a published reader of `origin.packageRelease` (published 2026.11.3 cannot open state this candidate migrates, schema 40 vs 22; by source, its `origin` schema is a plain `z.object`, which drops unknown keys); the durable service copy prefix; launchd/macOS; a Gateway-initiated update on a linked root; an unmanaged CLI crash after the switch (left to `openclaw update repair`). Earlier review: an independent reviewer agent reviewed the first version; both high findings and the low ones were fixed. Also not proven: a release-bound service whose definition the update cannot rewrite (in place by the same path as `--no-restart`, not run in Docker); the local suite sweep on the final head (CI is the broad proof). The in-place cell no longer runs with the Gateway up: `--no-restart` with a running Gateway is covered by no cell until the separate fix for the race above.

prs.title: refactor(auth): keep published store lookup passive
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reading already-published shared auth ownership currently imports database preparation and inspection code, even when the caller only needs the existing in-memory fact.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible behavior change. Auth selection, storage, schema, configuration and permissions stay the same. This change establishes a passive auth lookup boundary; it does not claim an RSS reduction or complete the wider passive catalog-read refactor.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing global ownership map and synchronous readers in their current owner. Move asynchronous preparation/reload into a small active module, and native inspection into the existing native module. Internal callers import the owner they actually use; retired internal exports are removed.

The same map, exact database-path keys, published object identity, and cold-publication limit remain. Admission capture still occurs before the first await; pending reads retain the existing currentness check and committed-owner recheck. Explicit commits and reloads are not newly capped. Filesystem fixtures move unchanged into their existing test-support module to satisfy the test-file line cap.

Production: +3 net lines. Tests/support: +79. Benchmark code: net zero.

## Evidence

- Frozen source: base `6f5d3b399b31855501cc3f38f1221f7165554c59`, initial head `3fdbed9e9ef746fc004f95be1cd7f544809bb799`; current head `1086709b6faceb428a1870d2807c174151998fda`. Signed commit; formatting, commit-hook ratchets and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent complete-source owner/caller review found no blocker. Native autoreview completed five semantic assignments at P0–P3 with no findings and a final scoped-clean result. All 66 changed patches are included. Two import-only files under `src/secrets/` use diff context because the native extra-source policy refuses that directory; their full bodies were reviewed independently and are unchanged.
- The initial-head Node CI selected exact `3fdbed9` on Node 24.22.1. Verified passes include both new auth boundary tests (within 34 boundary cases), 11 direct ownership cases, asynchronous bootstrap, real model-auth publication, 29 agent-creation cases, 92 agent-mutation cases, and 110 reload cases. Production and build inputs are unchanged in `1086709`; its test-only correction still requires ordinary PR CI.
- Required focused coverage: passive import boundary, direct ownership identity, asynchronous bootstrap, model-auth refresh, real model-auth concurrency/rotation, agent creation/mutation, and shared non-isolated runner fixtures, plus affected caller tests selected by CI. Required gates include relevant type graphs, mock-export/format/lint checks and build.
- CI artifact build, generated validators, launcher/native-host and built-artifact checks passed on `3fdbed9`. The resulting runtime artifact (SHA-256 `264a2c4eb9e39c569f675ff4b6d6c4bfa1dbbf72524f8826c3b88b7948a32fec`) binds that exact source. The passive owner's complete emitted relative static closure contains 39 chunks and excludes active auth/database loaders; its external fs-safe paths were checked at pinned 0.27.1. This is static compiled-boundary evidence, not an executed compiled-lifetime or RSS claim. The separate [Docker seed job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43917795521/job/133477910662) ran `scripts/build-all.mts` on `3fdbed9`, including cache-miss unified declaration emission and the complete build. Its later `npm pack --ignore-scripts` step timed out after 900 seconds, so the packaging/Docker job failed; the timeout cause remains unknown. Declaration proof carries to `1086709` because production and build inputs are unchanged. There is no new dedicated commit-during-read or pre-await-capture race witness.

Node CI on the initial head: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43917795521. Its preflight confirms the exact `3fdbed9` checkout and Node 24.22.1. It found a stale namespace in the real model-auth concurrency test: the captured function and spy still referenced the passive module after the function moved. Commit `1086709` retargets only those test references and keeps the passive path lookup, barrier, rotation assertions and cleanup unchanged. A separate source review of that correction is scoped-clean with no findings.

Current [ordinary PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43922644435) selected merge `9f97cab1923938a22473e456dab9a0c924010baa`, with ordered parents `4a74c61ae7c438587bc272840d180d16f7c5a283` and `1086709b6faceb428a1870d2807c174151998fda`. The state-logging type graph passed. Execution proof for the corrected real model-auth concurrency/rotation test remains pending. [Exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200185#issuecomment-6924786434) reports no findings or before-merge items.

Three current CI failures remain unresolved:

- [UI E2E](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43922644435/job/133494908591): two chat-send acknowledgement cases encountered a detached DOM element before releasing the deferred send. Failure artifacts still show the expected tool card, completed message and preserved draft. The wider job includes real state setup, so the mock Gateway alone does not establish isolation from this change. Cause and attribution remain UNKNOWN.
- [Real runtime proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43922644435/job/133494910596): the admitted-facts refresh/replacement case received `SessionMutationAuthorizationChangedError`. The log does not identify the originating RPC or failed authority fact. No qualifying same-signature baseline is available; attribution remains UNKNOWN.
- [Config RPC](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43922644435/job/133494910805): the fresh-revision create/update/delete case hit the existing 10-second `agents.delete` request timeout. The other 66 cases passed. Setup and teardown completed, but the log does not identify the stalled deletion/reload phase. Attribution remains UNKNOWN.

These failures are not classified as pre-existing and do not qualify an inherited-CI landing exception. No retry, timeout increase or assertion weakening was applied. Initial-head supporting behavior/build results remain distinct from current-head validation; neither full CI run is claimed green. The failed native backend executed no producer, its allocation custody remains UNKNOWN, and local dependencies remain unqualified.

The log-follow overflow regression maintains a separate mocked command harness even though the existing shutdown suite can protect the same polling contract.

prs.title: fix(runtime): defer optional work on low-memory Linux hosts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Optional background work can continue consuming memory on Linux hosts that are low on available physical memory but have no finite process memory limit.

## User Impact

On Node/Linux, the existing five background-work callers also defer when available host memory is at or below 20% of total memory, and resume through their existing checks after pressure clears. No configuration or migration is needed. This does not change the separate startup-prewarm or diagnostic-retirement policies.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared memory-pressure predicate previously considered only finite, safe process limits. It now independently checks physical host headroom, while preserving process-limit handling, including zero available process memory. An unknown or zero host reading does not manufacture pressure. Bun and non-Linux behavior remain unchanged.

The five existing consumers share this owner; no new cache, timer, poller, or fallback is added. Production changes add 8 net lines; tests and shared test setup add 120.

## Evidence

Baseline: `b90c5739fa5cbff09f35de8985e1579b4442d5cd`. Candidate: `3abd7087d6999fa735efad34d8ce28a8930874a9`.

A bounded Node 26.7 source-mode predicate check with controlled platform and memory readings changed the no-limit and unsafe-sentinel low-host-memory cases from false to true. Existing finite-limit pressure, zero available process memory, healthy host, and unknown physical-memory cases retained their results. This is a behavior check, not an RSS measurement.

The native Node/Linux proof attempt timed out while waiting for Testbox readiness, before any producer command or test ran. No build or type-check result is claimed from that attempt. Native cleanup has no GitHub run association, so the retained allocation claim remains unresolved.

[The exact-head Node CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43914849970) selected the full candidate SHA on Node 24.22.1. All 17 targeted test files are covered: 245 passed cases and 24 declared PostgreSQL-only skips, including host-pressure recovery and the unchanged prewarm sibling. All six requested type graphs passed. The CI artifact build, generated-output checks, launcher/native-host checks, and built-artifact checks passed. prs.title: improve(ios): catch blank chat transcripts in the simulator behavior harness
prs.body:
Related: #191478

## What Problem This Solves

`pnpm ios:behavior` did not catch the iOS blank-transcript bug (#191478): send with the keyboard up in a long agent chat, and the messages disappear until the keyboard drops. The harness had no case for that, and its checks read app state, which kept listing content while the screen was blank. Since the transcript became a `List` (#192232), the harness was also broken on `main`.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Developers get a harness that catches a blank transcript and runs again on `main`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Screen check:** blank-transcript gates now read pixels. `scripts/ios-screen-text.swift` uses Apple Vision text recognition on each screenshot. A sample is blank when no text lies inside the transcript area. The progress card and run footer stay drawn while the messages are gone, so they are excluded.
- **Realistic turns:** the QA mock gets `UXAGENT`, an agent turn: commentary plus a tool call for each step (progress card updates alternating with `exec`), then a long reply. Before this, every case used a plain markdown reply.
- **New cases:** 8 `blank-*` cases, keyboard up or down × new or long chat × plain or agent reply. Every case is now recorded to video and ends with a screen check.
- **`List` transcript fixes:**
  - `scrolled-up` swipes by coordinates, because the UI driver does not offer a `List` as a scroll container.
  - `stream-turn` judges motion from the recording. On the `List` transcript the probe reports cell layouts of 5–79 pt that never reach the screen; each one I checked showed a still reply on the native video frames. `scripts/ios-screen-motion.swift` reads every frame of the case's video and measures how far the transcript content shifts; the gate allows 1 pt. It reads two windows. The early one starts just after the first second and covers the area above the growing reply's footer row. The late one starts when the reply fills the screen and covers the whole transcript. Probe drift is still reported, and the probe still gates teleports and remounts. `motion()` is back to its `main` form.
- **Sampling rate:** screenshots run back to back (about 0.4 s apart). The slow accessibility read (about 1.9 s), which finds the transcript area, runs in a parallel loop, and each screenshot uses the read closest in time. Running them one after the other left 2.5–6 s between samples.
- `--sessions <key>[,<key>…]` runs the history cases on existing chats. To judge real conversations, copy a profile to a scratch profile and keep those copies out of git.

Not included, because neither case failed on the build that has the bug:
- A reply that another client starts while the chat is open: 0 blank samples out of 63.
- Switching chats from the sidebar (`switch-session`): it went blank there (16 of 48 samples) only while the fixture's progress card calls were failing. With working calls it showed no blank sample on either build.

## Evidence

The same simulator, same session setup and same mock ran 3 samples per case on two builds: a Debug build of `81ca4f4d712` (the parent of #192232) and current `main` (`33d26e441f9`).

| Case | Before #192232 | `main` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `blank-up-long-agent` (the #191478 bug) | **0/3**: 135 of 143 samples blank (median), blank at the end in all 3 | 3/3: 0 of 111 blank |
| other 7 `blank-*` cases | not run | 3/3 each, 0 blank of 100–121 samples |
| `scrolled-up` | — | 3/3 (was broken on `main`) |
| `stream-turn` | — | 3/3: drawn motion 0 pt; the probe reported 58–79 pt on the same runs |

Same case, keyboard up, after the reply finished. Left: before #192232 (blank). Right: `main`.

- `ocx test test/scripts/ios-behavior-grade.test.ts`: 10 passed, including `transcriptText` on recognized lines from blank and filled screenshots.
- Motion tool controls, built from clips of a real recording: a 200 pt jump reads 200 pt, a 350 pt jump reads 188 pt (still fails the 1 pt gate), a 30 pt bounce of 100 ms reads 30, three 1 pt steps read 3, a single 1 pt blip of 50 ms reads 1, a still clip reads 0. Twelve earlier `stream-turn` recordings read 0 pt (their probe drift was 10–79 pt).
- Found while checking the tool: at the live bubble → final row handoff, `main` redraws the reply about 2 pt right and 1 pt down for a few frames. The harness reports these frames as `drawnUnexplainedFrames` and does not gate on them.
- Tests under `extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai`: 200 passed.
- `oxlint --type-aware`, `tsgo:scripts` and format checks pass on the changed files.

Gaps:

- Simulator only. The original report came from a device, and these runs reproduced it on the simulator with the pre-fix build.
- Times are simulator wall-clock and were not compared.

Review:

- Local ClawSweeper review of `79c7df5b276` (the merged head): complete, patch correct, no findings. The one change after the clean review of `841b131227d` is a `// SAFETY:` note on the mock's tool item assertion, which CI's assertion ratchet required. Earlier rounds and their fixes follow.
- Hosted ClawSweeper review of `c682d1b6e84` found 2 P2 problems. Both are fixed:
  - The end-of-case screen check now carries its setup gate. Before, a missing transcript passed on zero samples.
  - A `blank-*` case whose reply never shows "Done in" within 90 s is now a setup failure. Before, it still recorded the post-reply window.
  - After these fixes, `main` passed `blank-up-long-agent` 3/3 with "reply finished" detected. The pre-fix build failed it with 20 of 28 samples blank, and its setup gates passed.
- Local ClawSweeper review of `8d56b7543a2` found 2 P2 problems in the motion tool. Both are fixed:
  - The content check read one row past the area when its height was a multiple of 40 pt.
  - A jump of more than 150 pt matched no shift and could read as still. The search now covers 400 pt, the probe's teleport threshold.
- Local ClawSweeper review of `f74f9df48fe` found 1 P2: no motion was measured between 1 s after the send and the moment the reply fills the screen. Fixed with the early window.
- Local ClawSweeper review of `bfe7405371b` found 1 P2: in a 104 pt early area, strips shifted by a jump left the area and could not match. The tool now searches shifted strips in the screen around the area. A 30 pt jump in 104–167 pt areas now reads 27–29 pt up and 23 pt down. All 15 real recordings still read 0 in both windows.
- Local ClawSweeper review of `3aabd830416` found 2 P2 problems. Both are fixed:
  - Samples with no transcript on screen were skipped, so one chat switch that never showed a transcript could pass. Each sampling window now needs at least one judged sample, or setup fails.
  - A failing case left the screen recording running. `fail()` now stops it.
- Local ClawSweeper review of `dfa3e3dd462` found 1 P2: the two windows met exactly, so a jump at the boundary became the late window's starting position. The early window now runs 500 ms past it. A 30 pt step inserted at the boundary read 0 pt before this change and 29 pt after. All 15 real recordings still read 0.
- Local ClawSweeper review of `01757831777` found 2 problems. Both are fixed:
  - P2: a sample with no transcript on screen inside an otherwise judged window still passed. Now every sample must show a transcript, or setup fails; the count is reported as `unjudgedSamples`. It was 0 in every window of a run of `switch-session`, `blank-up-long-agent`, `blank-down-short-plain` and `stream-turn` (2 samples each, all passed).
  - P3: a frame where every strip changed but no shift matched two of them was not counted as unexplained. Fixed; the motion controls read the same.
- Local ClawSweeper review of `112518fa491` found 1 P2 in the `UXAGENT` fixture: tool calls bypassed the request's tool surface, and a tool error still advanced the turn. The `ios-ux` transcripts confirmed it: every `progress_card` call had failed with "Tool progress_card not found", so no progress card was ever drawn in the earlier runs. Fixed:
  - Tool steps go through the existing `buildScenarioToolCallEvents` routing (here `dispatch_action`), and `exec` gets script input under code mode.
  - A failed step ends the turn with `UX-AGENT-TOOL-FAILED`.
  - The last step closes the card, so the runtime's plan-completion check adds no extra turn.
  - Agent cases now require a progress card on screen, as a setup gate.
  - A CLI `UXAGENT` turn on the `ios-ux` profile: all 4 tool results succeed, and the turn ends on the long reply.
  - Rerun with the working fixture and a real progress card: the pre-#192232 build still fails `blank-up-long-agent` 0/3 (8–19 blank samples per run), with every setup gate passing, the progress card included. `main` passes `blank-up-long-agent`, `blank-down-long-agent` and `blank-up-short-agent` 2/2 each, with 0 blank samples. The evidence table above predates this fixture fix; these runs replace its `blank-up-long-agent` row.
  - `switch-session` was removed (see "Not included").
- Local ClawSweeper review of `0ca6b2555e4` found 1 P2: the card check passed if the first card drew and a later step failed. Agent cases now require the card to read "Plan, N of N steps done". The mock sends that closing update only after every earlier step succeeds, and the long reply always follows it. Two mock tests cover the fixture: routing through `dispatch_action` (with the card closed before the reply), and the `UX-AGENT-TOOL-FAILED` reply when a step fails. Both would fail on the old fixture.
- Local ClawSweeper review of `38ea21293ad` (rebased onto `main`; `server.tool-routing.test.ts` had been deleted there, so the two fixture tests moved to `server.ux-agent.test.ts`) found 1 P2: the seed turn of a long chat also leaves a completed card, which could satisfy the check if the new turn failed early. The mock now names plan steps after the prompt's `label=` (`SEED` for the seed, `REPLY` for the reply), and the check requires the reply's label.
  - Negative control: the reply prompt swapped for a plain stream with no tool steps, after a seed that leaves a completed `SEED` card. Setup failed ("every agent tool step succeeded" 0/1).
  - `main` passes `blank-up-long-agent` and `blank-down-long-agent` 2/2 each. The build from before #192232 still fails `blank-up-long-agent` 0/2 (8–17 blank samples), with setup passing.

![Keyboard up after a reply: blank before #192232 (left), text on main (right)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2de513dd-aa50-4455-bfd5-059f9e7b8717)

prs.title: fix: retain channel requester when child completion resumes parent
prs.body:
Related: #182043, #168823. Adjacent cohort work: #164366 (completion-wave selection is unchanged).

## What Problem This Solves

A parent resumed by child completion loses the original channel requester's identity and can reject already-authorized owner tools.

## User Impact

In-process child completion resumes as its original requester, subject to current owner checks and the existing completion tool-policy ceiling. Guests are not promoted to owners. No configuration or state migration is required.

Successful-child live proof is now established. Human security/domain review and current-head CI/review remain outstanding; this authorization-boundary change stays draft pending those gates. Crash recovery and automation-management grants are outside this fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

Registration and refreshed followup custody already retain the operator source, but did not opt into the existing retained-requester capability. Single-child and batch delivery now re-enter that capability only for dispatch, passing its selected origin and matching live assertion into normal agent admission. Synchronous cleanup checks do not reacquire requester identity.

Operator source/scopes govern batch delivery independently of requester identity. Homogeneous batches retain the canonical requester principal, ignoring display-name changes. Mixed-human batches retain existing operator-owned delivery without selecting a member's personal identity. Cancellation-only fallback is unchanged. No owner bit is directly set or denylist relaxed. One shared source-comparison owner serves both consumers; no new schema or persisted authority manager.

## Evidence

### Successful-child live proof — November 15

Published head: `72e1afde461c17d25eea1c55efd7e6428eff7ed5`; tree: `c8b1bd8c868d1465f281d54ae08a90148d2cc351`. The published tree is identical to successful-child live-tested source `95d3c159e330ec66c204f82b8dbf36166a0c3408`. Managed publication and Git tree equality were read back; publication is complete. This does not establish exact-head hosted CI or review approval.

The observed harness failure was diagnosed, not waived: completion execution retained a released plugin invocation scope and failed with `agent harness host capability is no longer active` / `Plugin invocation scope is closed`. The maintained upstream repair [#199618](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199618), merged commit `7789e95139dc42390c506d8bc835816dc5e3ec43`, was integrated for this evidenced base risk. Four requester-retention patches remained range-diff equivalent. No authority guard was disabled; diagnostic instrumentation was removed before the final build.

Isolated Hetzner cx33, managed Crabbox 0.83.0, actual Discord dedicated canary and OAuth-backed Codex. Runtime build run `run_ef7f98426c65a22759ed382c265373e8` passed. Live run `run_6cbacb2b5d039ae9bc64d29924127505` exited 0. Direct provider has no hosted run URL.

Acceptance was verified from stored parent/child histories, actual tool results, terminal RPC observations and runtime logs—not merely a success marker:

1. One real bot-authored owner stimulus reached Discord; parent `config.get gateway.mode` returned `ok/local`.
2. Exactly one isolated child produced its requested final; exact child run `a1e93a32-609e-435a-a051-488aa7a00ff9` settled with `agent.wait status=ok`.
3. Actual `announce:v1` completion resumed the waiting parent.
4. Resumed parent's second owner-only `config.get gateway.mode` returned `ok/local`; its exact completion run also settled `status=ok`.
5. Runtime logs contained zero prior host-capability, closed-plugin-scope, lane-error or cleanup-failure signatures.

The harness now rejects absent/failed child finals, checks both terminal statuses and both actual owner reads, and captures diagnostics on failure. Guest retention uses `--stop-after never` independently of runner success; TTL/safety limits remain active. Failed V5/V6 captures were preserved. V7's 13 evidence files were downloaded, read back, hashed and checked against both injected credential values (zero matches) BEFORE provider deletion. Exact lease absence and Gateway shutdown were verified. Raw captures remain private. Existing dedicated bot secret and a static OAuth access token were used only in isolated state; no refresh-token transfer, production-state copy, API-key fallback or production deployment.

### Deterministic checks and review

- Rebased-source focused suites: 29 requester-policy + 69 registry + 24 direct-delivery tests = **122 passed**, wrapper 89.41s.
- Targeted TypeScript, oxlint and `git diff --check` passed; publication reconciliation has an empty source diff against the validated source/tree.
- Original regression failed on base `c99807a541c86cc49ffcc4d9dbabd1219f65bc53`.
- P1 mixed-human rejection and P2 display-name-sensitive comparison were repaired and independently reviewed before the base integration. That review is prior-head evidence, not current-head approval.
- Guest denial, source revocation, mixed-human cohorts and cancellation non-borrowing remain deterministic proof, not live Discord claims. No crash/restart, upgrade or full-package-build proof is claimed.
- Earlier error-completion run `run_864c67a5c1af1389d068c700b2b46fea` remains valid only for child-error recovery; it has been superseded for successful-child acceptance by V7 above.
- Exact-head broad CI/hosted review and human security/domain approval remain unverified. No merge or production deployment is claimed.

Rollback is a revert of the requester-retention change. Earlier setup failures and the failed required scenarios were retained, not relabeled as success. Driver-authored test prompts remain where cross-conversation cleanup was denied; no permission bypass was attempted.

prs.title: improve(compaction): prepare large histories outside the Gateway thread
prs.body:
Related: #185111 (large-history preparation context; not a claim to resolve its Codex pre-turn workload).

## What Problem This Solves

Preparing a large retained history for default safeguard compaction can block the Gateway thread and delay unrelated sessions.

## User Impact

Eligible default compaction prepares and rerenders history in the existing transcript reader. Provider requests, authentication, hooks, custom providers, mutable SDK behavior and guarded writes remain host-owned. Oversized or unsupported windows retain complete acknowledged host hydration, not truncated context.

**Paired performance acceptance remains pending.** This is not a proven CPU/memory improvement or global no-blocking guarantee. No configuration, public SDK signature, schema or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

One internal preparation algorithm preserves row provenance and the public four-argument API. Canonical tool, replay, hydration and summary-budget owners serve worker and host consumers. No worker is held across inference, new cache, whole-history graph-transfer protocol or public read-only extension API.

The #194536 worker-memory fix is preserved: private plan/render cohorts are admitted **before payload decoding**, with a 16 MiB serialized-input ceiling and the unchanged 512 MiB worker heap. Larger windows retain complete streamed host hydration. This input ceiling is not a universal decoded-heap guarantee. Renders use the maintained filtered JSONL budget check in the same snapshot.

Current-main integration preserves repeat-guard metadata, announced compaction IDs and #200063's session/model-only checkpoint replay identity. Transport authentication is unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Scope, simplification and test cost</summary>

The signed series contains five coherent owner prerequisites and private producer/consumer adoption. Yield-only, exclusive-handoff and held-worker alternatives were rejected; duplicate materialization and eager replay work were deleted. Existing SQL position/retention bodies have one context-navigation owner, unchanged except exported-signature formatting, without a line-cap suppression.

The CI repair moves canonical worker data types out of host implementation modules and migrates every internal type caller. Sixteen moved casts are removed through real type narrowing; sparse legacy billing does not acquire fabricated zero-cost data. The wrapper inventory now includes its hydration decoder. Shared prepared-runtime fixtures supply their required catalog. Existing Gateway tests still make 40 real reads and assert over 64 transcript events, using distinct valid read limits rather than weakening the repeat guard. Diagnostic tests own a scoped transport host rather than inheriting another test's mocked provider callbacks.

Against main fcf29c460d159337ee2ea69c5e359f28aedfa88e: **107 paths, +6,882/−2,665 lines**, including mechanical moves. The runtime CI repair is 43 paths, +232/−206; its subsequent fixture-only follow-up changes two existing tests and their allocation. Test growth passes at **2,101 net lines = 400 allowance + 1,701 reviewed allocation**: the earlier 93-line real-worker admission case plus 17 further net lines in existing CI fixtures. There is no new test case/file/cold shard, timeout change or raised shared threshold. Obsolete assertion and mock debt only shrinks; no unrelated UI allowance is added.

The changed 13-case hydration file costs **101.528 s cold wall / 174.598 local child CPU-seconds**, including bootstrap; the new case takes **2.599 s** in the affected batch. PostgreSQL conformance costs **79.568 s wall / 135.495 local child CPU-seconds**. The diagnostic red reproduction costs **68.920 s wall**, mostly transformation; its original lifecycle cases remain present. CI seconds are unobserved, and these different workloads are not speed comparisons.

</details>

## Evidence

The runtime implementation is normal-hook signed **2557ac2dc5b90671157772adf9292bf92d87d11a**, tree **68e73028926dae2bebb772f62519c683bd753963**. Its exact **sourcePerformance** build passes with unchanged tracked source. The preceding whole-feature review retains its original scope; fresh P0–P2 review of the complete 43-path runtime CI repair is scoped-clean with **412,619 bytes of intact input**.

The latest fixture-only follow-up is normal-hook signed **a05d6ff7b2dfa2b3655991adebbf7686e82f021c**, published tree **57ab8bd72361aba17d7eb8f90c22803d6b4fa71d**. Production inputs are byte-unchanged from 2557, so its build, Gateway and native proofs are reused, not relabeled as new-source captures. A fresh three-file P0–P2 review is scoped-clean with **31,559 bytes of intact input**.

- **331 distinct focused cases across 14 files pass** through current or unchanged-input-reused proof: the earlier 169-case batch, a further 154-case batch with four overlapping diagnostic cases, seven isolated Gateway E2E cases, and the latest nine-case fixture run with four diagnostic repeats.
- The diagnostic isolation reproduction fails at the unrelated throwing provider host before the fixture fix, with the other three lifecycle cases passing; all four pass after the fix. Model-call lifecycle and no-prompt-serialization assertions remain intact.
- Hosted CI exposed two additional fixture type errors. The explicit inert plugin host now supplies its complete existing port contract. The prepared-session test consumes `SettingsManager.inMemory` directly with the former fixture's exact settings after main retired an unused private helper export; no compatibility export is restored. Both failing owning graphs, **agents-root and agents-sessions**, now pass locally, as do matching strict type-aware lint, format and all nine fixture cases. Remote CI must still finish.
- Earlier targeted type graphs pass; the combined import graph has **zero cycles**. Assertion, mock, max-lines and test-growth ratchets pass without weakening their limits.
- The earlier replay migration passed **127 cases**. The unchanged memory/SDK/hydration repair passed **121 focused cases** and **two PostgreSQL cases with zero skips**, including catalog/migration/trigger checks and disposable cleanup. These overlapping runs are not added to the distinct count above.
- The real 18 MiB admission fixture preserves byte/navigation facts while corrupting a payload: pre-fix decoding wins over rejection, while fixed plan and render reject before decoding. Restoring it verifies complete streamed hydration. The initial 33,000-row attempt failed at projection rebuilding and remains invalid setup evidence, not a product reproduction.
- An initial offline E2E build preparation failed before any tests at an unavailable registry fetch. The documented same-source prebuilt route then passed all seven real Gateway cases after the exact build succeeded. An interrupted diagnostic attempt remains interrupted; completed static phases are not relabeled as a completed test run.

### Runtime Gateway qualification — source 2557, reused unchanged

`defaultauto-landing3-warm-q1` binds signed **2557ac2d**, its exact build and common workload **178e6b14eb40c725396b838c8114dd85ced6dcce**. **300/300 probes are valid**; warmup and measured phases share PID **1035**. Each verifies **one actual prepared plan, four rendered results, four HTTP 200 maintenance requests and durable boundaries 18 → 19**. The outcome is degraded-quality fallback, not normal-quality summary success. Both original 47,184-row prefixes match their recorded bytes/SHA-256. All **71 raw files and two links** are unchanged, inspection copies removed and cleanup valid.

This is one source-bound qualification, **not matched performance acceptance**. All measured costs remain visible:

| Metric | Source-2557 qualifier |
| --- | ---: |
| Stream RPC median / p95 / p99 / max | 3.478 / 6.385 / 42.212 / **279.563 ms** |
| Maintenance-window RPC median / p95 / p99 / max | 3.500 / 14.560 / 180.152 / **279.563 ms** |
| Stream / full maximum sampler gap | 120 / **374 ms** |
| Stream / full Gateway process CPU | 23,176.989 / **99,603.749 ms** |
| Stream / full main-isolate CPU | 1,831.857 / 14,109.509 ms |
| Stream / full sampled maximum RSS | 2,631,634,944 / 2,631,634,944 bytes |
| Stream / full main heap | 510,138,232 / 545,380,976 bytes |
| Stream / full observed worker heap | 127,378,848 / 158,638,504 bytes |
| Stream / full worker large-JSON parse count | 81,882 / 194,371 |
| Stream / full worker large-JSON parsed bytes | 559,635,186 / **1,274,631,589** |
| Stream / full distinct observed worker IDs | 5 / 13 |
| Stream / full retained transport chunks / frames | 1 / 8; 2 / 16 |
| Stream / full retained transport bytes / events | 333,107 / 4; 666,244 / 8 |
| Whole-rig child CPU | 188,673.716 ms |

The stream brackets are immediate samples, 0 ms before and 60 ms after, without prorating. Full CPU includes startup/warmup and is last observed cumulative CPU per Gateway PID; unsampled shutdown tails remain unobserved. Process CPU already includes workers. Worker counters cover successful userland JSON strings of at least 1,024 UTF-16 units, not host parsing; overlapping tasks include overhang. Worker IDs are distinct observations, not simultaneous peaks. Full capture has two plans/eight renders including warmup; measured request count five includes its pressure request, not five maintenance requests.

<details>
<summary>Prior-source qualifications — retained separately, never pooled</summary>

`defaultauto-landing2-warm-q1` qualified signed 3ff / published 3f with 300 valid probes, same PID 1047, one plan/four renders/four maintenance requests and 18 → 19 degraded boundaries per phase. Both original prefixes matched; 69 raw files/two links were unchanged.

| Metric | Prior 3ff qualifier |
| --- | ---: |
| Stream RPC median / p95 / p99 / max | 5.485 / 8.092 / 56.596 / **314.547 ms** |
| Stream / full maximum sampler gap | 107 / **768 ms** |
| Stream / full Gateway process CPU | 23,569.405 / **106,636.022 ms** |
| Full sampled maximum RSS | 2,713,694,208 bytes |
| Full observed worker heap | 153,459,776 bytes |
| Full worker large-JSON parse count / bytes | 228,660 / **1,527,489,040** |
| Whole-rig child CPU | 201,379.135 ms |

Earlier exact-623 stream max 13.764 ms/full gap 407 ms and c58/77 max 71.683 ms/full gap 1,388 ms remain separate, each with 300 valid probes and the same degraded class/four maintenance requests. Every earlier CPU/RSS/parsing/failure cell, the 267/162 overlapping checks and all-19-file cost proof retain their original source scope. None is relabeled as current-source regression acceptance.

</details>

**Open:** exact-head CI/landing gates, formal paired cold/warm acceptance, live-provider follow-up, effective SDK window and per-worker/JIT warmth. No performance-win or no-regression conclusion is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Prospective acceptance protocol — draft, not an admitted cohort</summary>

Before acceptance, pin both production commits/build receipts, the signed controller, fixture, image and sampling manifests; freeze and read back the published rule. Previous diagnostics and qualifiers are ineligible.

Run five serial baseline/candidate cold pairs, then five separate process-warm pairs. Warm requires a distinct physical session to durably complete default maintenance in the same Gateway PID first; it does not establish per-worker/JIT warmth or global idle. Use unique immutable tags and stopped imports, auditing unchanged original prefixes, durable outcome class and maintenance request counts.

Keep all 300 scheduled slots and every error, timeout, suppression and cancellation. Retain full-stream and declared broad-window latency, sampler gaps, process/main CPU, RSS/heaps, parsing/transport and full-capture startup/warmup costs. No post-result window selection, outlier removal, replacement tags or diagnostic pooling.

Report n=5 per arm/population, median, nearest-rank p95, spread and paired rows. Incomplete capture or source/outcome mismatch stops the cohort with its prefix retained. A median/p95 metric worsening at least 20% stops before the next population. Every adverse cell remains visible; a worse user-facing metric needs explicit owner acceptance. Lower worst latency does not excuse higher CPU or memory.

No acceptance cohort has started under this draft. Qualification does not grant acceptance.

</details>

## Contributor credit

Requested by @RomneyDa; publication authorized by @vincentkoc. Human contributor credit retained in the signed series: @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc and @jalehman.

prs.title: fix(gateway): detached work keeps its origin's authority when the parent chat is edited
prs.body:
## Scope

This is the first slice of "authority from saved facts". It moves accepted work onto the saved-facts path and fixes the user-visible bug. The next slice deletes the machinery this makes redundant: the subagent completion custody map, the store-replaced suspend path, the remaining parent-authority reads for detached children, the follow-up queue's silent cancel, the cron occurrence authority and the duplicated restore glue.

## What Problem This Solves

Editing a message in a chat stopped every subagent that chat had started, and dropped their results. The people involved still had access; nothing had revoked it.

How it happened: accepted work that outlives its request (a child run, a subagent completion, a node event) reused the live authority object of the request that accepted it. For a child, that object also checked the parent `chat.send`'s admitted input, which asserts that the parent chat's transcript revision has not changed. An edit (`sessions.rewind` plus a new send) changes that revision. So at its next boundary the child failed with `source_authority_refused` / "admitted run authority is no longer active | session changed before chat.send", its exec calls failed with "tool invocation authority is no longer active", and its completion failed with "requester settle wake failed: session changed before chat.send".

The bug class: detached work held a closure over a live owner (request, turn or run) as its authority. When that owner ended or its target changed, the work lost authority although nothing revoked it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Accepted work now carries values, not the accepting closure. `captureGatewayOperatorContinuation` restores the work's authority from the origin's saved facts (the operator recovery snapshot that restart recovery already uses) and checks it against current policy. The accepting request, turn or run is no longer part of the chain.

- One path: `captureGatewayOperatorContinuation` (in `operator-run-recovery.ts`) replaces the `independentContinuation` flag. It is used for accepted agent turns (`retainGatewayOperatorRun`: child launches, sent turns), subagent completion custody (`captureOperatorToolGatewayContinuationContext`) and node event sources.
- Deleted: the `continuationAuthorities` map, `bindGatewayOperatorContinuationAuthority` and the `independentContinuation` parameter. The restored authority in restart recovery is now one object instead of a policy object plus a claim wrapper.
- A source without saved facts (`unavailable` in the recovery codec) keeps its live authority, as before.
- Continuations of one origin keep its opaque `source` identity, so sibling children still settle as one completion batch. The accepted work still retains the inherited object for its lifetime, because other holders of that object (for example the queued input's transcript write) keep using it; its checks no longer gate the work.
- No schema, stored-row or protocol change. Production delta: −3 lines (+60 / −63).

## Security model

- **Revokes authority now:** a change of the origin's policy: paired device revoked, shared Gateway token or password rotated (shared-secret generation), profile identity or email binding changed, role assignment or role policy changed, access grant ended, OpenClaw ID membership changed. These are the checks restart recovery already runs, with the same revocation subscriptions, so a refusal arrives at the same boundaries as before (each authority check: admission, model request, tool call).
- **No longer revokes:** the accepting request ending, the parent turn ending or being replaced, and an edit or new message in the parent chat.
- **Explicit stops are unchanged:** Stop / `chat.abort` cancels descendants; reset (`/new`, `/reset`) stops controlled subagents, as `docs/concepts/session-controller.md` documents; delete stops them during lifecycle cleanup.
- **Ceiling:** the restored authority is the saved snapshot's scopes intersected with the caller's scopes (the same narrowing as before) and the current role; the model policy is the intersection of the saved and the current policy. Saved facts are captured only from a live host-issued authority (`captureQueuedOperatorRecoverySource` asserts it current first) and decoded by the strict codec. Work can never hold more than its origin had when it was accepted, and less if policy tightened since.

## User Impact

- A subagent keeps running and its result reaches the parent chat when the person edits or resends a message in that chat.
- Revoking access still stops the work: rotating the Gateway token cancels a running child at once.

## Evidence

Real agent on an isolated source Gateway (`ocx src`, scratch state, port and HOME, scrubbed env), Claude Opus through the shared Claude proxy. base = merge base `edbc5bce`, head = this PR.

| Journey | base | head |
|---|---|---|
| J1: parent spawns a child and yields; the person sends a second message, then edits it (`sessions.rewind` + resend) while the child runs | child refused (`source_authority_refused`, "session changed before chat.send"); completion dropped (`delivery=not_required`); parent never gets the result | child finishes; parent replies `parent-got child-final`; registry `delivery=delivered` |
| J2: child running; the operator rotates `gateway.auth.token` | child cancelled ("operator source authority is no longer active") | child cancelled within a second of the reload ("Restart recovery operator authority changed; start a new user turn."; the restored authority reuses the restart-recovery messages); no further tool call ran |
| J3: input A queued behind a busy turn, then human message B | A and B both run (`busy-done a-ack b-ack`) | A and B both run (`busy-done a-ack b-ack`) |
| J1b: parent spawns two children and yields; the person edits a later message; both children settle as one batch | both children refused (`source_authority_refused`); no result | both finish; parent replies `parent-got one-final two-final` |
| J4: cron occurrence; job edited mid-run | occurrence finishes (`cron-done`) | occurrence finishes (`cron-done`) |
| Parent gets a new message / `chat.abort` + new message while a child runs (yielded and busy shapes) | child survives, completion delivered | child survives, completion delivered |

The first journey matches the production incident: the transcript there shows a user message, a `leaf` (branch) event and the resent message, and every running child of that chat failed in the same second.

`/new` while the parent is yielded on a running child stops the child on both arms. That is the documented reset behavior (reset stops controlled subagents), so this PR keeps it.

Not covered by E2E: role downgrade and device revocation for a running child (the scratch Gateway uses shared-token owner auth). Unit tests cover device revocation and email reassignment of retained child authority (`operator-run-recovery.test.ts`, `operator-run-cancellation.test.ts`).

Gates: oxfmt, oxlint on changed files, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm check:test-types`, import-cycle and madge checks, `ocx test` on the operator-run authority, cancellation and recovery suites, in-process dispatch suites, requester pause authority, session restart resume and `src/agents/subagents/`.
