prs.title: fix(codex): stop background exec completions from replaying full history into a fresh thread
prs.body:
Related: #183286, #179363, #172026, #178982

## What Problem This Solves

When a background `exec` finishes in a Codex-backed WebChat session, the completion wake does not continue the session's bound native thread. It starts a fresh transient thread, replays the full session history into it uncached, and does it again for the follow-up turn. On a long session every completion wake costs a full uncached history read. In one observed session, four completion wakes each sent about 190k uncached input tokens.

This finishes, for event wakes, what #183286 started: tool declarations belong to the session, not to the turn. #183286 kept seven native Codex thread, plugin, and supervision declarations stable across owner and completion turns. A completion wake still differed from the user turn in three other ways, and each one alone forces a new thread:

1. **Tool-policy scope.** The default session-event source policy caps every follow-up at the producer's tool list. A wake with a cap runs as a turn-scoped restricted turn, which the Codex harness serves on a transient thread with native code mode off (48 eager dynamic tools instead of 10).
2. **`skill_workshop` schema.** The personal-library schema is published only on human turns that carry an authoring grant. A wake publishes a narrower schema, the dynamic tool catalog fingerprint changes, and the bound thread rotates. The Claude CLI runner already fixed this in #172026 (`resolveStableCliSkillAuthoring`); the embedded/harness path never used it.
3. **Conversation context.** An internal (WebChat) session stores no delivery route, so `buildSessionEventContext` never matched the wake's own WebChat route and dropped the session chat type. The wake's developer instructions then lacked the "You are in a WebChat direct conversation" line, the live thread config fingerprint changed, and Codex had to cold-resume the thread.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each layer is fixed where the difference starts, without widening authority:

- **Scope (A).** A cap from a conversation-scoped producer turn is the session's own policy, and the follow-up re-derives that policy itself. `createCodingToolsGatewayCaller` marks the caller identity session-scoped when the policy scope is `conversation` and no caller-supplied source policy exists, and `session-event-target` skips it only when the follow-up's destination is the same session. The mark is not set when group, per-DM, or sender policy narrowed the producer (`groupPolicy`/`senderPolicy`). Those come from the inbound request, the wake cannot rebuild them, and the cap keeps carrying them. The caller-inheritance merge keeps the mark only for an inherited owner of the same agent and session that has no narrower cap of its own. Cross-session follow-ups, sender-narrowed producers, and turn-scoped producers keep the cap exactly as before.
- **Policy lifetime stays host-owned.** No public SDK option is added. The host already computes the attempt's policy lifetime for Codex (`pluginHarnessToolPolicyScope`, `resolvePluginHarnessToolPolicies`). Host policy preparation now records that value in the attempt's host capability, and the host's tool construction (`createToolSurfaceAsync`, which is how Codex builds every dynamic tool) passes it to the internal tool options. A plugin cannot set it through tool options: a plugin-supplied `toolPolicyScope` is overwritten by the host value, and when the host has none the cap stays in place (fail-closed).
- **`skill_workshop` (B).** The #172026 helper moves from `cli-runner/` to `src/agents/stable-skill-authoring.ts` as a per-runtime factory and is also applied at the embedded attempt dispatch. Internal turns publish the session's last human shape with an expired grant: the declaration matches, personal-library calls fail with `AUTHORITY_EXPIRED`, and workspace calls keep the ordinary no-grant rule (unsandboxed runs only). Grants that are already expired (transcript follow-ups, stranded-reply recovery) carry `expired: true`, publish the remembered human shape without replacing it, and continue refusing personal and workspace authoring.
- **Context (C).** For a session that stores no delivery route, an event on that session's own WebChat route (`channel: "webchat"`, `to: <sessionKey>`, the shape `chat.send` and subagent announce already use) keeps the session chat type. Events routed to any other session still get none.

Out of scope, noted for follow-up: when a thread's config does change (for example a model switch), Codex can take longer than OpenClaw's 2-second unload budget to close a code-mode thread after `thread/unsubscribe` (measured 0.7 s, 2.9 s, and 10.6 s in this harness). The cold resume then fails with "Codex did not confirm unloading its previous configuration". With this change, completion wakes no longer take that path.

AI-assisted: written with Claude Code. Every claim below was checked by running it.

## User Impact

- Background `exec` completion wakes in Codex-backed sessions continue the bound thread with native code mode on. The wake reads the session prefix from cache instead of replaying the full history uncached, and the next user turn stays on the same thread.
- No tool, personal-library, or workspace access is widened. Sessions narrowed by group, per-DM, or sender policy keep today's behavior, including the fresh-thread wake.

prs.title: fix(subagents): retry completion delivery after requester interruption
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: completed subagent results can be dropped permanently when a newer foreground turn interrupts the requester’s completion turn.

## User Impact

An interrupted completion retries through the existing bounded schedule when the execution owner positively proves the whole run was replay-safe. Unknown or committed effects remain failed for explicit recovery with the existing blocked-delivery notice. Successful `NO_REPLY` or empty parent reviews still settle quietly. Explicit Stop, retired work, confirmed delivery, uncertain sends, and intentional suppression retain their existing behavior. No config or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The response owner classified cancellation as `visible_reply_missing`; registry settlement defaulted it to `permanent_failure`. The runner now preserves its existing whole-run replay-safety evidence in a typed abort, and the Gateway carries that fact while preserving the original abort reason. The response owner distinguishes `requester_aborted`; only positive safety evidence permits the existing three-attempt schedule (30-second and two-minute delays).

Related: #200020, #200005. This preserves the committed-effect protection in #155357 and the documented quiet-completion contract. Production delta: +53 lines; tests +118; docs +8. The necessary growth carries execution-owned evidence across cancellation instead of inferring safety from missing outbound metadata. No additional scheduler, cache, or state owner.

## Evidence

The caller-signal cancellation regressions fail on parent `4e9812cdef8992e63622e6d621d8e5d36f564539` with `visible_reply_missing` and no retryable disposition. Separate regressions failed on the first candidate for opaque cancellation and cancellation after an effectful tool; the final predicate refuses those retries. All 274 focused tests pass, including bounded retry/exhaustion, prior effects, opaque metadata, runtime refresh, Gateway propagation, committed progress, quiet settlement, Stop, and wake ownership.

A built isolated Gateway with a synthetic Responses SSE model passed on the final production code: one foreground turn interrupted the first settle, and the scheduler delivered `SETTLE_RECOVERED_PROOF` on the second settle without another user message. The fixture asserted exactly two settle attempts and one foreground turn, and verified the result through public `chat.history`. Sanitized synthetic trace:

```text
2026-11-16T08:36:39.240-08:00 lane task error: lane=main durationMs=190 errorName=AbortError
2026-11-16T08:36:39.241-08:00 model fallback chain stopped: reason=caller_signal_aborted
2026-11-16T08:36:39.278-08:00 completion agent was aborted before delivering a reply
Gateway fixture: 1 passed; announceAttempts=2; foregroundTurns=1; recovery visible in chat.history
```

An earlier live attempt hit a missing build chunk because validation rebuilt `dist` beneath that Gateway. The successful rerun used a settled build and serialized runtime execution. No external provider or production state was used.

`pnpm check:changed` on exact head `91657aa2677c9` passes every gate except the three inherited dead exports. A fixture literal-type error was corrected before this final run. The remaining dead exports reproduce on the exact parent: `ProjectedContinuationSource` and `partContinuation` introduced by #200056 (`24385a20428a`), and `buildGoogleLiveCatalogProvider` introduced by #200073 (`30e9d3ee295e9`). These are outstanding main regressions. No UI imports of changed modules.

The 5,000-context synthetic classifier measurement used interleaved A/A/B controls, CPU time, and sampled allocations. Healthy and quiet paths remain within A/A spread; cancellation adds about 0.06 μs and 312 sampled bytes per call. This is an in-memory owner measurement, not storage or end-to-end latency.

Codex autoreview of the complete final staged candidate, P0–P2: scoped-clean. All core test typecheck shards pass after the fixture correction. The three attributed baseline dead exports remain outside this repair.

CI run [43910107119](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43910107119), attempt 1, found a separate inherited main regression in `checks-node-changed-1`: `run.shared-integration.test.ts` crashes at `run-loop.ts:501` because the shared prepared-runtime fixture lacks `modelCatalog.providerOutcomes`. The selected completion/abort cases reproduce the identical TypeError on exact original main parent `4e9812cdef8992e63622e6d621d8e5d36f564539` and this head. The introducing patch is #200073 (`30e9d3ee295e9`). All six failure-owner/fixture sources are blob-identical across that original parent, CI main parent `b90c5739fa5c`, and tested merge `2fe6e5452e79`. This is an outstanding main test regression for its owner, not a passing result or a waived PR defect. ClawSweeper's final-head rereview has zero open items and no actionable findings.

prs.title: feat(channels): notify on terminal disconnect via --fail-on-unhealthy exit code
prs.body:
Add an opt-in `--fail-on-unhealthy` alias `--exit-code` to `openclaw channels status` so a cron or monitoring job can detect a channel account that is stuck in a terminal disconnect instead of parsing JSON.

## What Problem This Solves

A channel can sit in a terminal disconnect (revoked session, `terminalDisconnect: true`) for weeks while the gateway stays up, and `channels status` still exits 0. Operators are left to poll and parse JSON themselves. `--fail-on-unhealthy` makes a one-line cron job sufficient, and distinguishes transient reconnects from terminal states through the existing shared `evaluateChannelHealth` policy.

## What changed

- `openclaw channels status --fail-on-unhealthy` (alias `--exit-code`): after printing status, exits `1` when any selected channel account is unhealthy. Health uses the shared `evaluateChannelHealth` policy on the Gateway's recorded snapshots, read-only — no credential probes are run by the flag itself.
- Terminal disconnects (`terminal-disconnect`), `blocked`, `not-running`, `disconnected`, and other unhealthy reasons fail; transient states the policy treats as healthy (reconnect grace, startup grace, busy) do not. Unmanaged/disabled/unconfigured accounts are ignored, and an unlinked account with a terminal disconnect still alerts (policy checks terminal before the unlinked exemption, matching the revoked-session case).
- User-visible notification: each unhealthy account is reported on stderr (`terminally disconnected` wording for terminal states). With `--json`, output gains `unhealthyAccounts: [{channel, accountId, reason, terminalDisconnect}]`.
- CLI wiring: `src/cli/channels-cli.ts` registers both flags, `src/cli/route.ts` fast-path forwards them, health evaluation is dynamically imported only when the flag is set (plain status path stays cold), and `ExitError` from `runtime.exit(1)` is correctly rethrown past the fallback catch.
- Docs: `docs/cli/channels.md` documents monitoring/cron usage and the read-only semantics.

## Evidence

- New: `src/commands/channels.status-unhealthy.test.ts` (13 tests) —
  `bun .\node_modules\vitest\vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts src/commands/channels.status-unhealthy.test.ts` — 13/13 pass.
- Cold-path guard: `src/commands/status.cold-imports.test.ts` — 2/2 pass, so the plain status path still does not load the health evaluator.
- Typecheck: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` — passes.
- Format: `run-format --check` on the touched files — clean; `oxlint` — clean.
- Baseline ratchets: `check-assertion-safety-ratchet` and `check-test-mock-exports` now pass (the two remaining payload casts carry `// SAFETY:` invariants, and each test mock states its isolation reason).
- Existing `channels.status.command-flow` / `channels-status-cold-imports` show pre-existing Windows/Bun `getSystemErrorMap` failures identical on clean `upstream/main` (verified via stash), unrelated to this change.

Closes #194433

prs.title: fix(gateway): move managed update lease operations off the main thread
prs.body:
Related: #200136

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: preparing a managed Gateway update can block the event loop on lease-database and helper-file metadata operations before the helper starts.

## User Impact

Gateway requests remain responsive during handoff preparation and lease operations. Process identity, cross-process single flight, Stop settlement, and legacy handoff validation stay enforced. Cold preparation now starts a worker and costs more CPU and elapsed time; the measurements below make that tradeoff explicit. No configuration, schema, dependency, or external protocol changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Team 25c97908 incident on 2026-11-16 at 05:02 PST exposed a 1.97 s btrfs transaction wait in a main-thread catalog lock create, causing a 2,002 ms event-loop stall. #200136 removed that redundant catalog lock. This audit found another synchronous boundary inside managed update preparation.

The existing handoff-engine worker now owns coordinator admission, lease operations, process identity checks, and runtime staging. The serving parent keeps lifecycle decisions and awaits the worker's authoritative results. Captured Stop work retains that worker until cancellation and settlement finish. The lease remains necessary across the helper/executor boundary; synchronous helper and CLI contracts remain available off the serving path.

Runtime production delta is +312 lines: a typed async facade and worker commands replace main-thread lease operations, with settlement logic moved into the existing current-owner module. No new lease authority or cache is added. A separate ancestry-module extraction could reduce the worker's eager dependency graph; it is deferred to preserve the existing validation contract in this focused fix.

## Evidence

The real pre-spawn guard fails on the exact parent 6670297776a00 and passes after moving both lease admission and helper staging. Focused final proof includes the actual-entry guard, 26 Gateway refusal/diagnostic cases, and 23 single-flight cases; prior full affected lifecycle suites cover real parent/helper subprocesses, cancellation, and Stop. Codex autoreview is scoped-clean P0–P2. `pnpm check:changed` completed; its one task-owned fixture lint error was repaired and targeted lint passed. The two unchanged dead exports reproduce on the exact parent and originate in 24385a20428a / #200056.

Five A/A controls and five A/B pairs used fresh Node 26.12.1 processes, a real compiled worker, a private 12 KiB coordinator, and a deliberately refused helper-spawn boundary. The surrounding synthetic fixture has a 35 GiB agent DB, 5,000 sessions, and 62,000 workspace files; this owner does not scan that unrelated content. No Team data or live service was used. Filesystem: APFS, not btrfs.

| Median | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Preparation and cleanup | 53.93 ms | 599.29 ms |
| Maximum heartbeat gap | 42.93 ms | 3.38 ms |
| Main-thread CPU | 28.58 ms | 28.47 ms |
| Process CPU, including worker | 43.49 ms | 821.00 ms |
| Main-isolate V8 allocation | 6.94 MB | 12.01 MB |
| Observed main-thread writable-path metadata calls | 17 | 0 |

A/A owner medians were 54.58 / 53.79 ms; allocation controls varied 5.88–8.35 MB. All 20 processes completed and reached exactly one refused spawn. The serving path starts one lease worker; offline callers without an admitted database engine may also use the existing engine-inspection worker. These are byte-verified compiled Vitest-artifact measurements, not production-package startup measurements; package chunking/minification may change the cold cost. No warmup or cache hides it.

One earlier local lifecycle run failed because its helper outcome file was absent; its original helper log was removed by fixture cleanup. Focused, full affected, and exact-parent replays passed, which does not prove a fix or establish an inherited failure. The assertion now preserves the helper log on recurrence. This uncertainty remains explicit for exact-head CI. The first CI run 43907208459 exposed two stale startup-readiness fixture cases. Both fail on exact CI main parent 2516bca9fdb8544c7289fa6a451fbbe1c6cf0876; #200038 / 5bd858c0094a5b16dd3eb0864050502f3960e89a switched runtime viability from fs.access to a child probe and fs.stat without updating the fixture gate. The fixture now waits on fs.stat with the same assertions, and both cases pass. PostgreSQL conformance 3/3 was cancelled in that run; no inherited classification is claimed for that cancellation.

ClawSweeper also identified a task-caused observer-ordering race: helper stdout was already flowing while identity validation awaited the worker, so early readiness or exit could be missed. The parent now installs both observers before yielding and retains their results through identity validation. Two real-process regressions fail before the repair and pass afterward, covering actual staged-helper readiness and an early child exit during a held identity reply. Launcher validation lives beside the existing child-process controls; it preserves failed-spawn and kill behavior. The timing table covers the unchanged pre-spawn lease/staging region; this subsequent observer-ordering repair is proved separately.

Repair head `9514a09e8963bcf2067b3c18e9666a39a8c65695` passed 26 final focused cases, affected type/lint/format and line-cap checks, with fresh Codex review clean P0–P2. Exact-head CI [43916191379](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43916191379) succeeded. The final-head ClawSweeper re-review has zero open items after the numbered response covering its original finding. Native preparation is complete; landing is pending.

prs.title: fix: Talk falls back to a supported thinking level instead of failing
prs.body:
Closes #194183

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: chat-backed Talk consultations fail before agent execution when the configured thinking preference is unsupported by the consult target model.

## User Impact

Talk can consult the selected agent without requiring one global thinking setting to fit every model. Supported choices and ordinary explicit user-command validation remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The internal Talk setting is a machine-selected preference, not a user command targeting a particular model. Keep the normalization switch internal, outside the public plugin options. Mark only trusted internal Talk requests with an explicit preference for normalization, then use the existing thinking policy after the actual execution model and runtime are resolved.

Keep the original preference for per-candidate fallback normalization; do not persist the normalized value or clamp inherited session preferences.

## Evidence

- Stock admission source: **1 failed, 5 passed**. The new unsupported-`off` case returns before the agent executes.
- Patched admission: **6 passed**. Covers unsupported `off` → `low`, supported `low`/`high`, retained original preference, inherited preferences, and ordinary explicit rejection. Command: `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts --maxWorkers=2 -t 'resolves Talk preference|validates .* thinking|does not clamp inherited thinking'`.
- Trusted request policy: **4 passed**, covering explicit Talk, absent preference, unrelated internal tool, and ordinary input.
- Chat dispatch integration: **1 passed**, verifying ordinary thinking metadata stays out of command text and does not opt into normalization.
- Scoped lint and `git diff --check` pass.
AI-assisted implementation.


The 72-line allocation matches the added regression coverage. Merged current main without rewriting branch history (head `69543ab3ced6`). Full Git-index test-line check passes: **6,556,085 lines / 6,556,093 ceiling** (8 spare). Admission regressions rerun on this head: **6 passed**. Exact-head CI is running.

**Real shipped Talk consultation: stock rejects, patched returns the agent result.** Both isolated Gateways used `consultThinkingLevel: off`, the same authorized `opencode-go/grok-4.7` target and the same question. Its current live-advertised ladder excludes `off`; both overlays pin that same ladder to align provider metadata across builds.

- **Stock:** final rejection `Thinking level "off" is not supported for opencode-go/grok-4.7`, zero model tokens.
- **Patched:** real Grok agent lifecycle, streamed output, and final reply **`TALK_CONSULT_OK_194184`**.
- [Live proof, exact builds, requests, and redacted event excerpts](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/pr-evidence-talk-thinking-194184/LIVE-PROOF.md). This uses the shipped legacy Talk tool-call ingress without an audio session; it proves consultation dispatch and returned result, not audio playback. The four changed production files in the tested candidate are byte-identical to this PR head.
- The normalization switch is now in `InternalReplySessionOptions`, not the public plugin contract. The low-value manual fallback-helper test was removed.

Report provenance: the original report was the November 6 task brief recording three rejections of `off` for `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`. No production log excerpt was captured. The stock-versus-patched admission results above independently reproduce the rejection.

prs.title: refactor(infra): keep SQLite signal reads out of worker runtime
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Callers that only read the current SQLite inspection cancellation signal import the worker facade and its pool machinery. The signal's existing scope owner can answer that query directly.

## User Impact

Cancellation keeps the same scope, caller-first abort reason, and retired-scope behavior. Internal consumers avoid the unnecessary worker import path. No configuration, schema, or public API changes are required; no measured RSS saving is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The unchanged getter moves to the existing SQLite read-only worker context module. All 48 internal consumers use that owner, with mixed consumers retaining their worker imports for actual worker operations. The old facade export is removed. Production changes are net -5 lines; tests add 55 lines.

## Evidence

Baseline: `4bce7604f0a5e6a706d06cf4243708379a79f0e6`. Candidate: `76bb70dae25c1b391873be34bde7eb5f5ab123b2`.

Three fresh source-mode processes on Node 24.22.1 established the original boundary: the context control loads 7 module URLs, the doctor migration context 536, and the client credential store 953. The latter two load the read-only worker and pool modules. These are loaded file URLs including dependencies, not compiled-module or memory measurements.

On the same runtime, the candidate keeps the context control at 7 URLs and reduces the migration context from 536 to 210 and the credential store from 953 to 870. All three preserve isolated configuration. Neither consumer loads the read-only worker facade or pool through the signal query.

Seven focused suites produced 95 passing cases and six named macOS-only skips on Linux. Coverage includes scope cancellation and caller-first abort reasons, real credential-worker retirement/recreation, shared-client custody, real inspection cancellation, facade IPC/disposal, and four static import boundaries. The first proof process exited 1 because its collector expected 20 facade cases instead of the actual 22; all test commands exited 0. The saved JSON/JUnit reports were independently checked, with rejection checks for missing, duplicate, pending, failed, and unexpected skipped cases. That run has no final source seal.

The separately closed remaining-gates run passed targeted formatting, lint, four type graphs, and a full build with declarations enabled. Its before/after/build/completion seals match all 63 source files and 232 dependency inputs from the focused run. It reran no tests and preserves the first collector failure explicitly. The build completed with six soft Control UI budget warnings; these are recorded warnings, not a claim that those budgets passed.

Native proof runs: [focused cases and source witnesses](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43908907646) and [remaining gates and full build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43911423656). Their delegated Actions sessions ended cancelled during native cleanup; the scoped results above come from the retained command/report receipts, not that Actions conclusion.

Independent source review completed all three declared ownership groups with no actionable findings. Runtime and build evidence are tracked separately from that review.

The completed [PR CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43914021933) tested merge `c29b9162ec0f3df9d6270e8caf6af4a3aa55b4e3` (base `472cd0a2f542599eea763f013eba2d34033ca25f`, candidate above). Its 115 jobs ended with 88 successes, 25 skips, one underlying failure and the failed aggregate gate. Security and the PostgreSQL jobs passed. The two failing readiness cases wait on `fs.access`, while the existing executable-viability owner uses its executable probe followed by `fs.stat`. Those test/support/owner files are byte-identical at the base, candidate and tested merge; the viability change predates both parents. This is source/history-attributed inherited failure, not a passing baseline rerun. Existing [PR #200133](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200133) owns the readiness-test repair, so it is not duplicated here. The native inherited-CI landing evidence preserves the failed run and exact tested merge.

[Exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200179#issuecomment-6923703838) reports no findings or remaining moves. The source head remains unchanged.

prs.title: fix(knowledge): keep historical claims distinct and reject changed retries
prs.body:
Related: #193959

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Knowledge can discard a distinct historical claim as a duplicate, or accept changed input when a caller retries a completed save.

## User Impact

User impact: Claims with different dates, precision or origins remain distinct, and retrying a save with changed input is rejected instead of returning a misleading old receipt. Distinct same-title claims can be saved together. No migration is required; existing records are not rewritten or recovered automatically.

## Why This Change Was Made

Validate the existing retained input digest before reconstructing any remember retry. Use the same assertion metadata comparison for saved and within-call duplicates, preserving source date representations and ownership/validity bounds. Reserve filenames already selected within the current batch so the newly distinct claims can publish atomically without weakening filesystem collision checks.

The repair stays in the existing Knowledge planning/publication owners: no new recovery manager, journal, schema, permissions or background job.

## Evidence

- Two service-boundary regressions failed on base 90814f56c00611df01b44ba9eeb7916a10f53d33 for the expected reasons: a changed retry resolved, and a distinct dated claim was reported as duplicate.
- Final focused Node tests: 22 passed across remember, ingestion and page-budget/extraction suites. Covers accepted/published retries, changed input, date/origin distinctions, unchanged duplicate behavior, batch interruption recovery and snapshot-only preparation callers.
- Extension production and test typechecks passed. Changed-file lint, formatting, line-cap/max-lines ratchets, assertion-safety and git diff whitespace checks passed.
- Local autoreview of the complete final candidate against the base above: P0–P2, no actionable findings. The reviewed local source was committed as d593a62e2c0a15cdc8a5e6c863f81d43672cdfd8. Hosted ClawSweeper remains advisory under the repository workflow.
- Scope/gap: synthetic isolated service/storage fixtures; no production-vault recovery, update/deploy, or live-model end-to-end claim.

Fixes requested by @vincentkoc.

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: feat(gateway): notify session-message subscribers of resets and deletion
prs.body:
Replaces https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/69822 with a maintainer-owned branch. Original feature by @gdibble (Gabriel Dibble), credited as co-author.

Related: #63374

## What Problem This Solves

Session-message subscribers can retain stale session state when a session is reset, replaced with a new session, or deleted while their WebSocket stays connected.

## User Impact

Subscribers can consume `socket.drain` notices for `reset`, `new`, and `delete`, including the session key, reason, timestamp, and resolved agent scope. Delivery remains best effort and subject to current subscription and access checks; existing sharing rules still fail closed when a deleted row no longer establishes access. Clients must reconcile state after reconnects.

No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing ordered session-change publisher sends the notice to the union of session-list and matching message subscribers, once per connection, before `sessions.changed`. The broadcaster retains its scope, subscription, and sharing checks, including per-agent global-session routing. The protocol catalog, mobile non-consumption allowlist, and event documentation describe the new event.

This replacement carries only the session lifecycle feature and its review repairs. It excludes 21 database/deployment paths whose changes are already represented on main. It also excludes the later OpenAI-compatible HTTP 503 mapping and admission tests: those were added after the original May feature commit and are a separate concern. No unrelated ancestry is carried forward.

## Evidence

- Real WebSocket coverage exercises reset/new/delete with message-only, list-only, and overlapping subscriptions. Publisher tests cover ordering, union/deduplication, and selected-global routing; transport tests cover wrong-session, revoked-access, and node exclusion.
- The focused four-file run passed 47/49 tests. The existing recovery-state reset test hit its 120-second limit, and the delete socket case hit its event waiter. Exact replays of both passed with unchanged assertions and timeouts: recovery-state reset in 53.4 seconds; delete in 7.6 seconds, with all three notices and a successful RPC around 2.8 seconds after the request. The initial timeouts remain unexplained; the passing replay is not claimed as a fix. Temporary timing diagnostics were removed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, all 11 selected changed-test type graphs, targeted Oxlint, changed-file formatting, `git diff --check`, and `pnpm check:protocol-coverage` passed. Protocol coverage accounts for all 67 events.
- Codex branch autoreview: scoped-clean through P2, with no actionable findings.

prs.title: feat(ui): redesign tool-call rendering, grouping, and lifecycle narration
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Tool-call history was noisy and hard to follow: routine wrappers competed with useful work, launches could be confused with later outcomes, and expanded details could shift or disappear as history refreshed.

## User Impact

Chat now shows compact, chronological tool activity with independent disclosures and distinct subagent launch, stop, success, failure, and timeout facts. Commands use one muted, truncated line while expanded details retain their content. Image inspection previews remain separate from attachments in the final answer.

Questions stay in the composer, and inline command output keeps its existing opt-in preference. These narration changes are for the Control UI, including the macOS dashboard; they do not introduce extra messages to Discord, Telegram, or other channels. No schema migration or new user configuration is required. Existing bundle budget adjustments approved during the cleanup remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recorded execution identities and result-time placement keep lifecycle rows stable across streaming, output caps, history refreshes, and reloads. Nested tool-search calls share the same presentation as direct calls. Mixed collections retain their error details while completed workers get their own factual outcome rows. Explicit disclosure choices stay shared between panes; automatic expansion for reading stays local to its pane.

Original design and implementation: @vyctorbrzezowski. Simplification and follow-up fixes: @obviyus (Ayaan Zaidi). Both contributions are retained.

## Evidence

Maintainer review of `c4ae85d1`, test-only correction `21286219`, and integration `e4cd6537` on `main` at `9bfad2b`:

- Inspected the linked real-Gateway verification history and the published screenshots, including the later direct/tool-search completion proofs. The extensive live campaign is reused at the maintainer's request; historical captures below retain their actual execution/render heads.
- Corrected stale continuation and missing-tool-result expectations, removed the obsolete empty-Stop test after confirming Stop still requires captured nonblank text, and replaced the lint-invalid fixture spread. Production code and the approved design were not changed.
- Strengthened the existing mixed-success/error collection case: its wait details remain accessible alongside the worker completion, both live and after output truncation.
- Backend owner suites: **144 passed across 5 files**. Reported runner stages: 0.26 s, 32.62 s, and 39.04 s.
- UI lifecycle, disclosure, ordering, and rendering suites passed after the fixture corrections. The final renderer rerun passed **565 cases including 535 required canaries**, in 33.09 s; these overlap earlier runs and are not an additional unique-test total.
- Browser checks: **4 passed across 2 files**, covering swarm lifecycle and nested tool presentation/reload, in 21.48 s.
- Type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. The verified test-line allocation is **1,425 net lines = 400 standard + 1,025 allocated**, recalculated after main's test consolidation.
- Fresh independent review covered the complete candidate in two passes and reported no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Integrated `main` at `9bfad2b`, preserving its removal of two test suites. Independent integration review confirmed that the overlapping delivery code keeps main's current-chat ownership; the PR adds only display metadata there.
- Integration validation passed: **542 UI cases** (73.35 s), **1 continuation browser case** (18.83 s), **1 Gateway delivery owner case** (118.46 s including the cold build), and **33 requester-settle ownership/dispatch cases** (34.78 s). Type-aware lint on the five overlapping delivery files also passed.

**Known inherited CI failure:** `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.context-engine.test.ts:631` expects no `markSentToProvider` call but receives one. It reproduced on both the reviewed PR (18 passed / 1 failed) and an isolated `fcf29c4` baseline (same assertion, 58.13 s). The test and its notifier/active-turn sources are byte-identical between them: the notifier calls `markRuntimePersisted` and then `markSentToProvider` synchronously. Those inputs remain unchanged after integrating `9bfad2b`. This failure remains disclosed; it was not hidden or repaired by changing this PR's behavior. Current-head integration checks are pending.

The earlier live verification used UI/runtime `726c42e` for the image/disclosure refinements, `e4e46df` for six refreshed compositions, and `0f5247c` for typography. Other images retain their stated earlier provenance. The source-card absence after reload and visible output truncation are disclosed below, not claimed as fixes here.

prs.title: fix: local path commands pick a neighboring file when a symlinked folder is followed by `..`
prs.body:
Closes #199950

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `plugins install`, `gateway diagnostics export --output`, `backup create --output`, `backup restore --target`, `agents set-identity`, the `infer` file inputs and outputs, and `templates` commands read or write a different, valid file than the one the path names, and report success, when the path goes through a symlinked folder followed by `..` (for example `./selected/../plugin-b` with `selected -> ../physical/nested`).

## User Impact

User impact: on macOS and Linux, these commands open the same file that `ls` or `cat` shows for the same path. Paths without a `..` segment, and every path on Windows, resolve exactly as before. A symlink at the end of the path keeps its spelling, so `plugins install --link ./link-to-plugin` still records the link and follows it when its target changes.

Visible differences:

- When the folder before a `..` does not exist or is a file (`missing/../x`, `notes.txt/../x`), the command fails with the operating system's error instead of quietly using `./x`. `plugins install` reports it as `Plugin path not found: <typed path> (<OS error>)`.
- `backup verify` and `backup restore` report the archive path the filesystem opened (`physical/backup.tar.gz`) rather than the typed `link/../backup.tar.gz` spelling.

## Why This Change Was Made

The paths were folded with `path.resolve`, which removes `folder/..` as text before the filesystem is consulted. The OS applies `..` to the folder's real location, so the two answers differ when `folder` is a symlink.

One shared resolver in `src/infra/home-dir.ts`, next to `resolveUserPath`, serves the affected commands:

- `resolveFilesystemPath` replaces `path.resolve` for a path that is about to be opened or written.
- `resolveUserFilesystemPath` replaces `resolveUserPath` (trimming and `~` expansion stay the same).

Only when a `..` segment is present does the resolver check the segment before it: a symlink is replaced by its target, then `..` applies. Other segments stay as typed. If that segment is missing, unreadable or not a folder, the resolver throws the operating system's error (`ENOENT`, `ENOTDIR`, `EACCES`), so no later step can fold the path back to `./x`. A trailing `/` or `/.` on such a path must name a folder, as the OS requires. `plugins install` and `--marketplace` treat a spec the filesystem cannot traverse as not a local path and keep classifying it as before (npm, git, URL). The backup commands report it as `Could not resolve --output`, `--target` or `<archive>`, with the OS error.

`resolvePathPrefixSync` from `@openclaw/fs-safe` was not used: it follows every symlink, including the last one, which would change the paths `--link` installs record.

Two commands already had their own fix of this kind: the `infer audio`/`infer video` `--file` path (#192718) and the `backup verify`/`backup restore` archive path (#197688). This PR moves both to the shared resolver. It keeps #192718's rejection of a missing folder before `..` and of a trailing `/` or `/.`. All three backup paths (`--output`, `--target`, `<archive>`) go through `resolveBackupArchivePath`, so they resolve the same way.

Accepted edge cases, not handled:

- Paths stored in config (`plugins.load.paths`, workspace dirs and so on) keep `resolveUserPath`. Changing them would change how existing configs load after an update, so this PR covers only paths typed for a command.
- A folder without search permission before `..` (`locked/..`) still folds as text, as before. The OS would refuse it.

## Evidence

Live CLI runs with made-up plugins and an empty config in a temp folder, isolated HOME and state dir, on macOS, built from this branch and from `main` (`02dc1855e2d1` for the plugin and diagnostics rows, `b58996d69286` for the backup rows). Setup: `selected -> ../physical/nested`, with `physical/plugin-b` (id `plugin-real`) and a lexical neighbor `./plugin-b` (id `plugin-decoy`).

| Command | `main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| `plugins install ./selected/../plugin-b` | `Installed plugin: plugin-decoy` | `Installed plugin: plugin-real` |
| `plugins install --link ./selected/../plugin-link` (`physical/plugin-link -> plugin-b`) | records `<root>/cwd/plugin-link` (the neighbor link) | records `<root>/physical/plugin-link` (the link kept as typed) |
| `gateway diagnostics export --output selected/../bundle.zip` | writes `<root>/cwd/bundle.zip` | writes `<root>/physical/bundle.zip` |
| `backup create --output selected/../backup.tar.gz` | `Created <root>/cwd/backup.tar.gz` | `Created <root>/physical/backup.tar.gz` |
| `backup restore <archive> --target selected/../restored` | `"targetPath": "<root>/cwd/restored"` | `"targetPath": "<root>/physical/restored"` |

Tests:

- New regressions fail on `main` and pass here: diagnostics export (1), plugin install with and without `--link` (2, the `--link` row through the linked validate-in-place install), local `git:` install source (1), `backup create --output` (1), `backup restore --target` (1), and the `Plugin path not found` message for a missing folder before `..` (1). The resolver contract in `home-dir.test.ts` (symlink before `..`, final link kept, no `..` unchanged, missing or file segment before `..` throws) runs only with the resolver.
- `infer audio transcribe --file` refuses `missing/../memo.wav`, `link/../memo.wav/` and `link/../memo.wav/.` before any transcription while a decoy `memo.wav` sits at the lexical spot (3, as on `main`).
- Existing tests of every changed caller pass: `capability-cli` (121, including the #192718 audio/video symlink case), `agents.identity`, `templates` project/reader/build/CLI, `plugin-install-plan`, `dev-source-root`, `git-install`, `plugins-install-preflight`, `diagnostic-support-export`, `home-dir`, and the 31 `backup` command and `backup-create` test files (including #197688's case, which expects the archive path the filesystem opened).
- `tsgo` (core and the touched test configs), `oxlint` and `oxfmt` are clean on the changed files.
- Not run: Windows (the change is skipped there by design), and the full suite (left to CI).

prs.title: fix(android): page archived threads beyond the first 200-row window
prs.body:
Closes #193828

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android Threads → Archived loads only the first 200 archived conversations with no way to browse further pages. The controller parsed the response's pagination metadata and then cleared it for archived results, `loadMoreSessions` refused the archived scope outright, and the archive screen offered no Load More affordance — so the loaded window was silently incomplete and sorting only reordered it.

## User Impact

User impact: with more than 200 archived conversations, the archive screen shows a Load More action with the same loading and failure states the sidebar already uses; continuing loads subsequent archived pages in scope, a failed continuation keeps the loaded rows and offers a retry, and a same-scope refresh preserves rows already loaded beyond the first window instead of pulling the view back to page one. Searching still finds conversations outside the loaded window. The Recent filter in the same screen gains the same Load More affordance when its roster reports more pages, so both scopes behave consistently.

## Why This Change Was Made

`applySessions` kept continuation state only for non-archived results (`if (archived) clearSessionRosterPaging()`), so archived responses discarded `nextOffset`/`hasMore` even though the Gateway already reports them. `loadMoreSessions` also hard-refused when `sessionsListArchived` was set, and its continuation request hardcoded the non-archived scope. Archived pages now keep the same continuation state as the recent roster, the continuation passes `archived = sessionsListArchived`, and the window-refresh path no longer exempts the archive from preserving already-loaded members (`fetchSessionsForCurrentWindow`'s `preserveWindow` guard). The Sessions screen collects the existing roster paging flows and renders the sidebar's Load More row, loading state, and failure caption when the current roster reports more pages.

## Evidence

- New regression `archivedRosterPagesKeepTheirScopeAndRetainLoadedRows` in `ChatControllerCatalogTest.kt`: a 200-row archived refresh reports no more pages; the same request with 201 rows keeps `sessionRosterHasMore` set; a failing continuation returns false, keeps the 200 loaded rows and surfaces `sessionRosterLoadFailed`; a retry loads offset 200, keeps every row `archived == true`, and exhausts paging; a same-scope refresh preserves all 201 loaded rows.
- Red/green: with the production change stashed on this exact commit's base, the new test fails on unmodified `main` (`sessionRosterHasMore` stays false after the 201-row archived refresh — the cleared paging state this PR restores); with the change applied the whole file passes 11/11 (`:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest`, Gradle 9.7.1, Java 21).
- `:app:ktlintCheck` passes. `apps/.i18n/native-source.json` gained the three usage records for the strings this screen reuses from the sidebar ("Load more sessions", "Loading", "Could not load more sessions. Try again."); no new translatable sources are introduced.
- Independent review of the branch found one P1 and four P2s in the first revision; all are fixed in the second commit. The paging slot now belongs to the listed scope: `loadMoreSessions` takes the caller's scope and refuses a stale listing, so an archive left listed cannot page hidden archived rows into the recent sidebar (the sidebar also hides its Load More row while the archive is listed, and the Threads screen shows the row only on the Recent and Archived tabs of the listed scope). A fresh roster page supersedes a stale continuation failure, and a scope switch no longer reuses the other scope's loaded window. The regression test pins the recent-scope refusal (no request issued) and the failure-flag clear on a fresh page.
- Full `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest` suite on the updated head: 3651 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors (Gradle 9.7.1, Java 21, local).
- The Android Play Debug APK builds passed locally on the PR base and the current revision. The official Android 31 ARM64 image installed, but the emulator cannot initialize its data partition with the available disk space. The live Threads and Gateway screenshot and retry scenario remain unverified.
- Follow-up for the search review: roster pagination and its error caption are now shown only when the normalized search query is empty. Search has its own results and does not issue unfiltered roster continuation. On the follow-up, the search and catalog suites passed 13 tests, Android ktlint passed, and the P0–P2 independent review found no actionable issue.
- Follow-up Android CI passed, including Play, third-party and Wear tests, ktlint, and the [aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42265368116/job/128061978484).

prs.title: fix(ui): keep loaded history visible during compaction
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an already-loaded conversation disappears into a short tool-only tail when compaction refreshes history during an active goal with a queued follow-up.

## User Impact

The loaded discussion stays visible while the goal and queued input remain intact. Real branch switches, resets, and transcript rewrites still replace incompatible history. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reconcile refreshed history using native physical positions and rewrite generation, rather than display order or an advancing transcript tip alone. The existing lazy recovery owner does the work after live-state prerequisites and rechecks request ownership before using held state. The bounded older-page read, 1,000-row limit and lazy fallback are unchanged.

CI investigation also exposed two input-lifecycle holes: a first upward jump could compare against a stale native offset, and completed paste recovery could resurrect text cleared by a later edit. Refreshing the actual pre-input origin and canceling recovery on the first input repair those owners without relaxing request or paste guards. Main’s explicit skills-used performance retirement is preserved.

## Evidence

- Compaction overlap, unheld-result, relocated-activity and rewrite-generation regressions failed before their fixes. The original candidate passed 114 focused tests and seven shipped-bundle Chromium cases. After integrating main’s retirement, 76 focused history/cursor/identity cases passed; the three recovery owners are byte-identical to the previously reviewed core.
- The stale-offset request regression fails with the previous owner and passes with the fix: Home from a real 5,500px origin loads older rows with null or stale-zero tracking, while both no-input controls stay inert. The affected history owner, maintenance and autofill suites passed. The paste inserted-then-cleared regression also fails before repair and passes afterward; 12 paste cases and 84 New Session/command-palette consumer cases passed.
- Final tree `cd766ef83678b4a681a1b8d4d51cae6177e87aaf`, based on main `a0423637196f7d999b91240f5d0938ef680b694f`, passed all 16 browser cases across the reading, compaction and native-paste files on isolated AWS (Node 24.22.1, 8 vCPU/16 GB; 87.31 seconds). WebKit phone and Chromium phone/desktop each completed 240 reading samples at 190 messages; maximum residuals were 0.765625px, 0.5px and 0.46875px respectively. Initial viewport, committed-prefix and runway readiness are observed explicitly; the >200-sample and 2px gates are unchanged. Ordinary and Shift-paste coverage remains intact.
- UI production, Chat-test and E2E-Chat typechecks, targeted lint/format, controller guards and diff checks passed. Net test growth is 551 lines; exactly 151 justified allocation lines cover the excess over the unchanged 400-line allowance. No timeout, shard-selection, asset-cap, compressor or baseline changes.
- Fresh independent full-patch review and Codex autoreview against pinned main `a0423637196f7d999b91240f5d0938ef680b694f` found no P0–P2 findings in the final 11-file candidate. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable on the selected route; hosted review previously acknowledged the PR.
- Published head is `2cb2d36bc21a7e629aa5d56470e82220ed403953`, with the tested tree above. Required exact-head CI remains pending; this PR is not merged. [Previous-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43899929112) failed WebKit setup at 30 messages and native paste with duplicated text. The repaired defects have independent red/green proof, but those CI logs do not establish their exact event/timer ordering. A focused passing replay is not claimed as causal attribution or an inherited-failure waiver.
- Browser evidence uses synthetic Gateway responses, not live model-triggered compaction. It exercises real browser input and the shipped UI bundle, but does not replace exact-head CI.

<details>
<summary>Earlier asset and deadline investigation</summary>

Earlier asset gates exposed shared/New boot growth and then Chat growth. Moving reconciliation into the existing lazy recovery owner removed that growth without increasing a cap. Canonical boot generation was unchanged; paired original-base proof measured Chat −216 B gzip and New +1 B, with request counts unchanged. Earlier hosted performance gates subsequently passed.

An older CI attempt hit browser deadlines. Shard 4 completed 161 files without an assertion failure, including both compaction cases, but its timeout causality remains unresolved: main and PR discovery flags produced different coverage. No deadline increase, blind CI rerun or inherited-failure waiver was used. That old run is not current-head evidence.

</details>

prs.title: fix(package): stop shipping private CI/QA docs and Chrome extension test helpers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the npm package ships maintainer-only CI docs, the private QA stack docs, and a Chrome extension test helper, which spends installed-tree entries that the update budget needs (shipped updaters refuse trees over 50,000 entries; the release budget is 47,500).

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Installs and updates carry fewer files, which keeps headroom under the installed-tree budget that every published updater enforces.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `!docs/ci.md` stopped excluding anything useful when the CI page split into `docs/ci/` (#140501); the split pages still shipped. Exclude `docs/ci/**` too, matching the original maintainer-only intent from #126448.
- `docs/concepts/qa-e2e-automation*` is the index of the private QA stack (qa-lab, qa-channel), whose plugins and channel page are already excluded from the package.
- The Chrome extension copy filter listed test suffixes one by one and missed `background.lifecycle-test-helpers.ts`. Chrome loads only JavaScript, so the filter now drops every colocated `.ts` file (tests, helpers, declarations).

Not done here (needs a maintainer decision): dropping precompressed `.gz` Control UI sidecars, plugin-contract declarations that no package export reaches, or tiny shared chunks.

Related: #200136

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: starting a terminal under Bun can stall the Gateway event loop while cold Node discovery creates a probe file, waits for Node, and removes the file.

## User Impact

Terminal startup and QA subprocess discovery leave the Gateway event loop responsive while the filesystem or Node probe is slow. Supported-version selection, missing-runtime errors, and synchronous CLI/previously shipped callers keep their contracts. Cold asynchronous discovery adds modest CPU/allocation overhead; no new configuration, schema, dependency, or cache is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

This follows the Team 25c97908 incident (2026-11-16 05:02 PST): a native catalog lock create spent 1.97 s in btrfs transaction wait and stalled the event loop 2,002 ms. #200136 removed that redundant lock. The continuing audit found the same main-thread metadata dependency in Node executable discovery.

The existing probe owner now offers awaited creation, child execution, and joined cleanup. Terminal and QA callers use it; synchronous bootstrap/CLI callers remain supported. Both forms share the same selection policy and existing 16-entry cache. Production growth is 97 handwritten runtime lines plus 29 generated lines and 7 generator lines, needed to preserve synchronous callers while moving serving callers to the async contract. The old probe policy is not duplicated.

The existing main-thread filesystem guard fails on the exact parent 6670297776a00 with mkdtempSync/writeFileSync/rmSync and passes through real cold discovery after the fix. Actual terminal helper cancellation/spawn-failure tests and affected QA/materializer consumers pass; all core, UI, extension, script, and test type graphs pass. prs.title: fix(openai): replay encrypted reasoning without unverifiable item ids
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long OpenAI Responses chats fail with "The AI service could not recover saved conversation state (item_conflict)". Subagent completions sent to those chats fail with the same error.

On the shared team Gateway, 4 to 15 real conflicts happened each day. Every conflict on November 16 had the outcome `deferred`, so each one failed a visible turn or a completion delivery. The reported rate jump on November 16 (28, then 82 per hour) was not new conflicts. After a deferred repair, `outcome=recovered` is logged on every later request in that chat: one run logged it 26 times. That day there were 4 real conflicts.

## Root cause

OpenAI item IDs show if their response was stored. When a turn is sent with `store:false`, its reasoning item IDs name no stored record. For example, every turn that carries a compaction checkpoint is sent with `store:false` (#198357).

The replay converter sent those reasoning items again with both `id` and `encrypted_content` whenever the current request had `store:true` (`openai-responses-replay-messages-internal.ts`, reasoning branch of `convertMessage`). The first stored request records that ciphertext under its ID. The next stored request that sends it again fails with `item_conflict` ("An input item conflicts with an existing record."). The server returns this error only after the whole output has streamed. In-turn recovery then defers the repair to the next request, so the current turn fails.

Session history from the affected team chats agrees (only structural fields were read, no message content). Each chat that failed had reasoning from unstored responses, followed by stored full-history requests:
- One chat had 45 unstored reasoning items after a compact-endpoint checkpoint. Its next stored turn failed after 100 seconds of output.
- In two other chats, stored and unstored responses alternate.

The fix for function-call argument bytes (#200020) does not cover this. The real API accepts a changed `function_call` under the same ID.

## Fix

On the native OpenAI Responses endpoint, reasoning that has encrypted content is replayed without its ID. Ciphertext is self-contained. Message and function-call IDs need their reasoning ID, so they are omitted with it. This is the shape that stateless replay already used. Reasoning without ciphertext keeps its ID, as before. Microsoft Foundry and other routes that opt in to item IDs are unchanged: Foundry checks ciphertext against its original ID (#91033).

Production code: net -1 line. No config, schema or stored-data change. Existing transcripts are fixed when the next request is built.

## Evidence

Real OpenAI API probes (`gpt-6.1-sol`):

| Replayed input | Stored replay 1 | Stored replay 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| reasoning from a `store:true` response, with ID | ok | ok |
| reasoning from a `store:false` response, with ID | ok | `item_conflict` after output |
| same reasoning, ciphertext only (no ID) | ok | ok (also a third time) |
| message or function call from an unstored response, with ID | ok | ok |

`cached_tokens` is the same with and without the reasoning ID: 5327 of 5362 tokens in both cases.

Real OpenAI route through OpenClaw's Responses transport. One `store:false` turn is followed by two stored turns, cold replay each time, 3 trials per arm:
- base `fcf29c4`: the third turn fails 3 out of 3 times with `item_conflict` "An input item conflicts with an existing record.", and the log shows `item_conflict_recovery outcome=deferred`. This is the production failure.
- this PR: 3 out of 3 trials pass, with no conflict.

Real scratch Gateway with `gpt-6.1-sol` and `gpt-6-astra`. The journey: a turn, a compact-endpoint checkpoint, a `store:false` turn, a model switch with server compaction, then three stored turns. Both arms finish every turn. `cacheRead` for the last three turns is 22614/23293/23516 on base and 22620/23299/23522 on this PR. I did not find a Gateway-only path on current `main` that drops a checkpoint and also keeps the reasoning ciphertext. The transport run above is the reproduction of the failure.

Regression test: `replays reasoning from an unstored response without a conflicting ID`, over SSE and WebSocket. The loopback server follows the real store rule: it records ciphertext under its ID, and it requires a stored message ID to come with its reasoning ID. The test fails on base with `item_conflict` and passes here. It also fails if message IDs are kept without their reasoning ID. The conflict triggers of the existing item-conflict and cold-reopen recovery tests used function-call IDs, which are no longer sent. They now use the identity that their repair removes, so recovery stays covered. Focused transport, provider and agent replay suites pass, and so do `tsgo:core` and `check:test-types`.

Merge danger: two-way door. It only changes the request projection; no stored state is written, and a revert restores the old wire shape. Blast radius: native OpenAI Responses requests only. They no longer send reasoning, message or call IDs next to encrypted reasoning. Azure, Copilot, Foundry and custom routes keep their current wire shape.

## What Problem This Solves

An initial `sessions_send` retained-followup policy denial can be misreported as revoked access, without identifying the failing endpoint or preserving its safe error category.

## User Impact

Callers can distinguish initial admission rejection from later revocation and identify whether the parent or child endpoint failed, without changing permissions or exposing hidden-session details.

This diagnostic change does not fix early session-resolution failures, explicit message source-admission failures, or automation management scope reported in the issue's later evidence. It does not grant additional continuation authority.

Preserve a bounded `followupAccess` diagnostic containing phase, endpoint, and policy code through the followup tool and completion paths. Do not include session keys, identities, policy messages, or policy details.

prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

Closes #200142

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where operators running `openclaw models auth login --device-code --method <other>` or `openclaw attach <session-url> --url <other-url>` would see only `[openclaw] The CLI command failed.` plus a `openclaw doctor` hint, even though the CLI had already composed the exact remedy at the point of failure. The doctor hint sends them to the wrong next step for two routine argument mistakes.
- Both guards raise plain `Error`s outside `runCommandWithRuntime` (the login guard fires in the Commander action before the wrapper; `attach` uses `defaultRuntime` directly), so the shared JSON-mode diagnostics fix did not cover them.
- **Related:** #200142 (this issue, filed per the closing note on #198333/#198345: "if you find a case the shared fix doesn't cover, open an issue with a reproduction"); #199970 (merged shared-wrapper fix whose body explicitly excludes these two paths); #192127 (same producer-side shape, merged).

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** The four remedy producers classify their already-composed messages with the canonical `throwExpectedCliError` from `src/cli/expected-cli-error.ts` (message text verbatim), so the root renderer's expected-error path prints them in human mode and `formatCliJsonFailure` keeps the identical message in the JSON envelope. `attach` already used `throwExpectedCliError` for its own positional/`--session` conflict; this brings `resolveSessionTarget` and the models login guard onto the same established path.
- **Out of scope:** Per the ClawSweeper review guidance on the issue, the `Gateway returned a session without a consistent agent identity.` invariant is deliberately **not** converted (a regression test pins it as a generic failure), and `shapeTargetError`'s caught-failure reshaping is untouched. No message text changes, no renderer changes.
- **Highest-risk area:** Other consumers of `resolveSessionTarget` — the TUI action catches and prints `formatErrorMessage(err)`, which renders `Error: <message>` exactly as before (`ExpectedCliError extends Error`, message unchanged).

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** With isolated `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `models auth login --provider openai --device-code --method password` exits 1 and prints `--device-code cannot be combined with --method unless method is device-code.`; `attach "https://gw.example/dashboard/main/abc123" --url wss://other.example` exits 1 and prints `pass one target: use either the session URL or --url, not both` — instead of the generic failure + doctor hint.
- **What should reviewers focus on:** `src/cli/models-cli.ts` (login guard), `src/cli/session-target.ts` (three remedy sites, invariant left generic); regression tests: `models cli > surfaces the --device-code/--method conflict remedy through the terminal renderer`, `session target operator remedies reach the terminal renderer` (asserts through the real `formatCliFailureLines` renderer path), and `openclaw attach (action) > surfaces the session URL/--url conflict remedy through the terminal renderer`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** worktree at `origin/main` @ `59d9759d025` (Linux, Node v26.12.1), CLI run from source via `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts` (same entry as `dist/entry.js`; full tsdown build refused on this host by its memory admission gate), isolated `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. Before state produced by targeted file revert (`git checkout origin/main -- <files>`), after state with the patch applied.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # 1) terminal proof (after patch)
  HOME=/tmp/oc-home OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/oc-home/openclaw.json \
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-home/state \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts \
    models auth login --provider openai --device-code --method password
  HOME=/tmp/oc-home OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/oc-home/openclaw.json \
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-home/state \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts \
    attach "https://gw.example/dashboard/main/abc123" --url wss://other.example
  # 2) regression tests (RED on origin/main, GREEN with patch)
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cli/session-target.test.ts src/cli/models-cli.test.ts \
    src/cli/attach-cli.action.test.ts src/cli/session-ref.test.ts \
    src/cli/program.smoke.test.ts src/cli/failure-output.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  $ … src/entry.ts models auth login --provider openai --device-code --method password   # exit 1
  --device-code cannot be combined with --method unless method is device-code.

  $ … src/entry.ts attach "https://gw.example/dashboard/main/abc123" --url wss://other.example   # exit 1
  pass one target: use either the session URL or --url, not both
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** Both commands exit 1 and print the composed remedy on stderr; the generic `[openclaw] The CLI command failed.` / doctor hint no longer replaces it. Test suites: 6 files / 114 tests passed; `tsgo` config-cli core-test shard exit 0.
- **Before evidence (optional, visual changes encouraged):** Same commands on reverted files (`origin/main` @ `59d9759d025`), both exit 1 with only:
  ```text
  [openclaw] The CLI command failed.
  [openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
  ```
  Regression tests on `origin/main`: 5 new assertions failed (RED) — `5 failed | 40 passed (45)` across the three touched suites.
- **What was not tested:** The ambiguous-reference and no-session-found remedies were not reproduced against a live Gateway (requires a running gateway with colliding sessions); their terminal presentation is covered by regression tests asserting through the real `formatCliFailureLines` path, and they share the exact classification path verified live via the pass-one-target site. Local `oxlint` could not run on this host (oxc arena allocation fails under the machine's commit accounting — same signature as oxc-project/oxc#20331, reproducible on unmodified `origin/main`); lint is deferred to CI `check-lint`. `oxfmt --check` passed locally. Remaining CI lanes pending at creation time.
- **Proof tier:** L2
- **Proof limitations:** none beyond the disclosed live-gateway and local-lint gaps above.
- **Review state:** Awaiting CI + maintainer review.

prs.body:
feat(tencent): add Hy4 Flash model to TokenHub and TokenPlan

## What Problem This Solves

Tencent users can't pick Hunyuan's faster, cheaper Hy4 tier (`hy4-flash`) in OpenClaw on either the TokenHub or the TokenPlan endpoint.

## User Impact

User impact: users can now pick `tencent-tokenhub/hy4-flash` or `tencent-tokenplan/hy4-flash` (or the "Hy4 flash" aliases). The model accepts text and image input, has a 1,048,576-token window, and supports `none`/`high` reasoning effort, so it works well for high-throughput agent and tool-use loops at a much lower cost than `hy4`.

The default model doesn't change: fresh onboarding still selects `hy4-preview`. Existing configs aren't migrated, and Doctor doesn't move anyone onto `hy4-flash`. If an API key uses a limited access scope, the user has to add **hy4 flash** to its allowed models.

## Why This Change Was Made

`hy4-flash` is added to the catalogs and model aliases of both Tencent endpoints:

- It accepts the same image formats as `hy4` and uses the same `none`/`high` effort ladder (default `high`).
- Its context window is 1,048,576 tokens, with a 983,040-token input limit and 65,536 max output tokens.
- Pricing comes from Tencent's published Flash rates: input 0.07, output 0.281, cache read 0.003.

Reasoning-effort handling needs no new code. The existing logic already reads each model's supported effort levels from the catalog. The hy3-specific effort map stays scoped to hy3.

The Doctor allowlist (hy3, hy3-preview, hy4-preview) is left as is on purpose. Doctor shouldn't silently move users onto a model with different pricing and key scope.

The Tencent provider docs now include `hy4-flash` in the model table, the key-scope note and a short description of the tier.

## Evidence

Unit tests updated in `extensions/tencent/index.test.ts`:

- Both endpoints' auth/catalog tests now expect `hy4-flash` in the configured model list.
- The reasoning-effort tests check that `hy4-flash` maps OpenClaw thinking levels to Tencent's effort values like `hy4-preview` does: `off`/`none` → `none`, and `minimal`/`medium`/`xhigh` → `high`.

prs.title: fix(update): refuse Gateway-started updates on Windows Scheduled Task installs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Updates started from the Gateway (Control UI, chat, automatic updates) on a Windows Scheduled Task install never finish. The task ends up disabled, the Gateway stays stopped, and the package is unchanged. This PR refuses those handoffs before any mutation, with a message that points to a terminal update. Terminal `openclaw update` keeps working.

This is a mitigation, not the full fix. Gateway-started Windows updates are refused rather than repaired. See "Full fix needs a decision" below.

Refs #169844
Refs #199617
Refs #164639

## Root cause

The Gateway spawns the managed update helper `detached`, and the helper spawns the updater. On Windows, libuv's detached spawn does not set `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB`. Both processes therefore stay in the Scheduled Task's kill-on-close Job: the launcher Job from `bindWindowsTaskLauncher` / proc-safe `bindCurrentProcessLifetimeTo`, plus Task Scheduler's own Job.

During activation the updater disables the task and stops it (`schtasks /Change /DISABLE`, then `/End`). Ending the task ends the Job, and that kills the helper and the updater. Nothing is left to swap the package or re-enable and restart the task.

## Evidence

Native lanes ran on Crabbox AWS (Windows Server 2025, Node 24.22.1, Scheduled Task Gateway).

| Installed (updater) | Lane | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 2026.11.5-beta.2 | `update.run` → npm beta (beta.3) | Validation passed, then stuck at `activating`. Task Disabled, 0 node processes, readyz down, CLI still beta.2. |
| 2026.11.5-beta.2 | Same, with a watcher outside the Job (`IsProcessInJob`) | Helper (parent = Gateway) and updater both show `job`. Within 1.5 s of the task becoming Disabled, every task descendant, helper and updater included, is gone. |
| 2026.11.3 (stable) | `update.run` → npm beta (beta.3) | Same stranding: task Disabled, 0 node processes, run stuck `activating`. |
| this branch | `update.run` | See "Proof on this head" |

Terminal `openclaw update` runs outside the task's Job and passes. It is covered daily by the update matrix's Windows lanes.

## What changed

`admitManagedHandoffSupervisor` (in `update-managed-service-handoff-service.ts`) now owns the admission of Gateway-started handoffs. It throws `UpdatePreMutationError("managed-service-handoff-failed")` for the `schtasks` supervisor, and keeps the existing systemd admission unchanged. `startManagedServiceUpdateHandoff` calls it before any spawn, lease, or service mutation. Foreground (terminal-origin) handoffs skip it, as before.

All three callers surface the refusal without stopping anything:
- `update.run` records `managed-service-handoff-failed`;
- the in-Gateway `openclaw update` handoff reports it;
- the startup auto-update reports it.

## Full fix needs a decision

Gateway-started updates can only work on Windows if the helper and updater run outside the task's Job. The options are:

1. A proc-safe spawn with `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB`. This also needs `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_BREAKAWAY_OK` on the launcher Job, and Task Scheduler's Job must allow breakaway.
2. A one-shot Scheduled Task that launches the helper.
3. A WMI `Win32_Process.Create` launch.

Options 2 and 3 replace the helper's stdio control pipes, so the park handshake protocol has to change. Any of them touches the lifecycle authority boundary. Until one is chosen, the refusal turns a guaranteed outage into a visible, actionable message.

## Tests

- `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-lifecycle.test.ts`: the new test "refuses a Windows Scheduled Task handoff before spawning the updater" fails on base (the promise resolved with a started handoff) and passes with the fix. The launch-metadata case no longer covers `schtasks`. The full file passes 71/71.
- `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-settlement-control.test.ts` passes.
- `tsgo:core`, oxfmt and oxlint pass.

## Reviews

- autoreview: scoped-clean at P2.
- Independent `codex exec` read-only review: NO FINDINGS. It covered the gate placement, all three callers, foreground reachability and the message.

## Proof on this head

Native, on the exact head `ad95856ffb6`. Crabbox AWS `cbx_e08fe5efd047`, Windows Server 2025, Node 24.22.1, Scheduled Task Gateway, package sha256 `93de4bd8…`, built on Linux from this branch.

| Lane | Result |
|---|---|
| Terminal `openclaw update --tag <this package>` from published 2026.11.3 | rc=0 in 893 s. Task Running, readyz 200, version 2026.11.30 (ad95856). |
| Gateway `update.run` on the updated Scheduled Task Gateway | Refused before any mutation: `status: error`, `reason: managed-service-handoff-failed`, with the Scheduled Task message. No handoff was spawned. 45 s later the task is still Running, readyz 200, and the version is unchanged. |

The stable 11.3 result is the third row of the Evidence table: a published 11.3 Gateway-started update strands the Gateway.

prs.title: fix(plugin-sdk): export deriveSessionChatTypeFromKey from routing subpath
prs.body:
Re-export the host's session chat-type classifier from the `openclaw/plugin-sdk/routing` subpath so plugin tool factories can gate on `ctx.sessionKey` without re-implementing the session-key rule by hand.

## What Problem This Solves

A plugin tool factory receives `ctx.sessionKey` but no chat type. A tool that should only be offered in a direct chat (for example, one that shows the owner something a group or channel should not see, since group and channel replies are read by everyone) currently has to copy the host's canonical parsing: strip the `agent:<id>:` prefix, then read the `direct`/`dm` vs `group`/`channel` token. That copy drifts from the host's peer-shape parsing, including the legacy `group:`/`channel:`/`@g.us` shapes and the plugin-supplied legacy fallback. A plugin cannot import the host classifier today because `openclaw/plugin-sdk/routing` exports only `parseAgentSessionKey`.

With this change, plugins import `deriveSessionChatTypeFromKey` from the routing subpath and drop their copy.

## What changed

- `src/plugin-sdk/routing.ts`: add `deriveSessionChatTypeFromKey` (value) and `type SessionKeyChatType` re-exports from `../sessions/session-chat-type-shared.js`, alongside the existing `parseAgentSessionKey` export from the same subpath.
- `src/plugin-sdk/routing.test.ts`: new unit-fast test locking the host classification through the SDK subpath (direct/dm/group/channel, legacy `group:`/`channel:`/`@g.us` shapes, unknown, and plugin-supplied legacy fallback).

## Evidence

- `src/plugin-sdk/routing.test.ts` via the vitest unit-fast config — 14/14 pass.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` — passes.
- `run-oxlint` on the two changed files — clean.
