prs.title: fix(agents): long conversations get stuck when the primary model's explicit auth order has no usable profile
prs.body:
Related #194689

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a long conversation gets stuck with "This conversation is too long, and OpenClaw couldn't shorten it" on every message when the session model's explicit `auth.order` has no usable profile, even though ordinary turns already answer from the configured fallback model.

## User Impact

User impact: when the primary model's ordered credentials are all unusable, compaction now summarizes with the next model in `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks`, the same chain ordinary turns already use, so long sessions keep working until the operator signs in again. Ordinary turns behave as before (the primary is tried, fails, and the "Model switched from … to …" notice is posted, now with `(auth)` instead of `(unknown)`). With no fallback configured, the reply names the cause, "This saved login isn't available. Choose another login…", instead of "Your request couldn't be completed." A user-pinned login with no stored credential, which the rate-limit pre-check used to move behind the fallbacks silently, is now tried first, then the turn switches with the notice.

Accepted edge case: the message is the same whatever made every ordered login unusable (missing, expired, permanently disabled); it names the login rather than the underlying reason, which the operator's auth status already shows.

Not changed, on purpose: the reporter's second case, an explicit `agents.defaults.compaction.model` that cannot authenticate on the embedded path. That override stays exact and has no fallback chain, as `docs/concepts/compaction.md` documents; checking at config time whether a compaction model can work is not part of this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Auth preparation refused the explicit-order case with a plain `Error`. Turns fall back on any candidate error, but compaction moves to the next model only for a classified failover error, so it stopped after one attempt (`attempt=1 maxAttempts=1 outcome=failed reason=unknown`). The refusal is now a `FailoverError` with the existing `selected_auth_profile_unavailable` code (reason `auth`, no HTTP status): it is a local refusal, not a provider response, so it gets that code's "saved login isn't available" copy and no re-authenticate hint. Compaction already forwards the failure code to its fallback classification, which maps this code to `auth`.

The rate-limit pre-check that reorders fallback models before each turn treats an auth-preparation `FailoverError` as "skip this candidate" and records nothing for it. It now leaves `selected_auth_profile_unavailable` to the fallback runner, which attempts the primary, logs `candidate_failed`, and posts the notice, as on `main`.

Docs: `docs/concepts/compaction.md` lists this case beside the cooldown case, and `docs/auth-credential-semantics.md` (Explicit auth order filtering) says what happens when no ordered profile is usable.

Not changed: the turn fallback order and policy, compaction's failover classification, `compaction.model` exactness, the other route refusals (`configured-auth`, `required-profile`).

## Evidence

### Live run: full-product repro on `main` and the same runs on this change

Built Gateway (`openclaw.mjs gateway run`, bench tree at `main` `3d172a63470`; this change = `89d82d887f1`, whose later amendments added only doc lines) in a no-network container. Config: `primary/main-model` with `auth.order.primary: ["primary:revoked"]` (declared, no stored credential), fallback `backup/backup-model`, both 16k-token windows, served by a local Responses model that reports request size as usage. The shipped CLI sends long messages with `gateway call chat.send` and reads `gateway call chat.history`.

With the fallback configured, `main`:

```
turn 1-3: Model switched from primary/main-model to backup/backup-model (unknown).
          log: lane task error "Explicit auth order for primary has no usable profiles." / candidate_failed primary / candidate_succeeded backup
turn 4:   [compaction-diag] end ... trigger=budget provider=primary/main-model attempt=1 maxAttempts=1 outcome=failed reason=unknown
          preflight compaction failed: Explicit auth order for primary has no usable profiles.
          ⚠️ This conversation is too long, and OpenClaw couldn't shorten it. ...
summary requests to backup-model: 0
```

This change:

```
turn 1-4: Model switched from primary/main-model to backup/backup-model (auth).
          log: candidate_failed primary / candidate_succeeded backup
          compaction summary requests to backup-model: 4; history ends with a Compaction entry; every turn answered
```

(Repeated `candidate_failed` lines for the same auth refusal are coalesced by the existing decision-log rule, so fewer lines appear than on `main`.)

With no fallback configured, one message: `main` replies "Your request couldn't be completed."; this change replies "This saved login isn't available. Choose another login under Models in the OpenClaw app or run `openclaw configure`."

Proof artifice: both models are one scripted local Responses server, and the dead login is a profile declared in config with no stored credential.

What the substitute proves and what it does not: the reporter ran `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` with a Codex OAuth profile; this run uses a local provider on the OpenClaw runtime. Compaction hits the same refusal through the same `rejectionError` (the reporter's `[compaction-diag] end … attempt=1 maxAttempts=1` line comes only from the embedded compaction path this change covers), so the compaction fix applies to their route; the OpenAI/Codex route itself was not run. prs.title: fix(ui): dashboard reports are cut off and catch swipes on phones
prs.body:
Part of #199401 (proposal 1).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on a phone, dashboard reports are cut off and scroll inside small boxes, so swipes over them get stuck instead of scrolling the dashboard.

## User Impact

User impact: on a phone, native reports and session progress cards show all their content, and swiping anywhere on the dashboard scrolls the dashboard. A card's saved size is still the smallest it gets, so making a card bigger with the resize corner or a size preset works as before. Website, Browser, custom HTML and other plugin widgets keep their saved height.

Desktop does not change, including the dashboard panel docked beside chat (448 px wide): every card keeps the size the user gave it, and content that does not fit scrolls inside the card, as on `main`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Without this, stacked cards keep the row height they have on the 12-column desktop grid: a report pinned at the default size (6 × 4) gets a 220 px window for content that stacks to over 1,000 px at phone width, so it becomes an inner scroller. In the phone layout (the app's shared `PHONE_LAYOUT_QUERY` breakpoint), when the board stacks its cards, the grid rows are at least 56 px and grow with content-fitting cards: reports and session progress grow to their content but never below their saved size, and every other card keeps its saved height because its body is size-contained. The core widget registry marks which kinds fit their content. The rules are limited to the phone layout because on desktop users size cards to compose their dashboard, and scrolling inside a card is intended there.

Total Control UI CSS on `main` is over its cap, so a change may add at most 64 B. The phone layout rules add more than that, so this also removes two new-session styles that no page has rendered since #197820 (the project search status line and the browser list loading line).

## Evidence

Desktop, before (`main`) and after (this PR), 1440 × 900, same report (an 8-row table at the default 6 × 4 size). The dashboard area is pixel-identical in both: the card stays 260 px tall and its table scrolls inside it.

Expanded dashboard panel (1098 px):

Phone, before (`main`) and after (this PR), 390 × 844, same report, panel expanded so the whole card is in view. Before: the table stops at Issue 5 and the rest scrolls inside the card. After: all 8 rows show.

![Phone, before and after: on main the report is cut off at Issue 5; with this PR all eight rows are visible](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/34e8e85da59be03c998cd6a6c474bebe6ce5d219/images/2026/11/aec84921-9824-486b-ae17-ed82f04cf98f.png)

Before and after at iPhone width, mocked Control UI with synthetic data, same scroll positions. Before: the Release status metrics are cut off and the Blockers table shows one row in a box. After: both show in full.

Before:

![Before: on a phone, the Release status report is cut off and the Blockers table shows one row inside a small scrolling box](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/1447105c8f2657beaaecd8997c9b9d09d10f8110/images/2026/11/5915ddef-58be-4e15-bcc7-e4c15ccfe9d7.png)

After:

![After: the Release status report and the whole Blockers table are visible, and the dashboard scrolls as one page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/1447105c8f2657beaaecd8997c9b9d09d10f8110/images/2026/11/5e968069-9468-4528-858f-f66e5722eeef.png)

Swipe over a long report at phone width (393 × 852, Chromium with touch emulation, mocked Control UI with synthetic data). Left is `main`, right is this PR. Each side gets the same three upward touch swipes, each starting on the Blockers report (checked with `elementFromPoint` before every swipe). The yellow dot is the finger. The yellow bar is a test overlay that reads the dashboard's and the report's scroll offsets live.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/41535a8f-f975-4ab0-8f81-456e6f1e8e51

![Mid-swipe at phone width. Left, main: the dashboard stays at 330 px while the Blockers report scrolls 498 px inside its card. Right, this PR: the dashboard has scrolled to 828 px and the report has no inner scroll](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/2d4340bac75584185ca0f64ee5e289bd5c74edbb/images/2026/11/4031ee28-9c2d-426e-aa82-833368dd122f.png)

| | `main`: dashboard | `main`: report inside its card | This PR: dashboard | This PR: report inside its card |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Start | 330 px | 0 px | 330 px | 0 px |
| Swipe 1 | 330 px | 249 px | 579 px | 0 px |
| Swipe 2 | 330 px | 498 px | 828 px | 0 px |

Resizing on a phone (390 px), checked in the same mocked Control UI with a report saved at the default size (6 × 4): Resize > XL grows the card from 262 to 532 px, and dragging the resize corner down grows it to 532 px and saves 6 × 8.

Tests:
- New end-to-end test in `ui/src/e2e/native-report-widget.e2e.test.ts` (390 × 844 touch viewport, default-size report with an 8-row table, real touch swipe): fails on `main` with 145 px of the report hidden, passes with this change. About 2–5 s.
- New end-to-end test in the same file (1440 × 900 desktop, the same report in the 448 px docked panel): checks the report keeps its saved size and scrolls inside. Fails on the previous head of this PR, which fitted reports in the desktop panel too; passes now.
- Board browser tests 25/25.
- UI end-to-end typecheck, oxlint, stylelint and formatting clean.
- `pnpm ui:check-performance:base` against `main` (ade4216): total CSS +46 B gzip, +55 B raw, within the 64 B allowance.
- The two existing tests in the same end-to-end file can time out opening the report's link in a new tab on a heavily loaded machine; the same happens on `main`.

Not run: a physical iPhone or iOS Safari, and a live Gateway with a real agent (the mocked Control UI and the end-to-end suite's mock Gateway were used).

prs.title: fix(update): stop reporting unset git config keys as failing checks
prs.body:
Refs #199582

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Git-checkout update failure reports name `git-config-update-upstream (command-failed)` as a failing check when a tracking key such as `branch.main.remote` is simply unset, and the runtime-publication refusal claims "Runtime artifacts changed" even when the checkout did not change and the artifacts were already stale before the update.

## User Impact

User impact: A Git-checkout update report now points at the step that actually failed instead of a harmless unset-key read, and the Gateway-running refusal says the artifacts must be republished (changed by this update or already stale), which matches same-SHA updates like #199582.

## Why This Change Was Made

`git config --get`, `--get-all`, and `--get-regexp` exit 1 with no output when the key is unset. Target discovery already treated that as absence, but the step runner recorded it as a failed step with `command-failed` facts, and the failure report always surfaces the first fact-bearing step. The Git owner now classifies that exact outcome (exit 1, normal termination, no stdout or stderr) as a completed read in one place, `runGitConfigReadStep`, and every config read in update target discovery goes through it. Other exit-1 cases that do print something, such as an invalid key, along with timeouts, kills and output-limit stops, still fail.

The publication refusal is shared by every runtime-artifact republish. That includes the case in #199582, where the pre-update source admission had already found `dist-runtime` stale on an unchanged checkout. The wording now covers both causes, and the operator steps are unchanged.

The primary #199582 action (republishing stale artifacts while the Gateway runs) is still correctly refused. That is why this PR only references the issue. The recovery is `openclaw gateway stop`, `pnpm build`, `openclaw gateway start`, as noted on the issue.

Production delta: +21/-7 across 3 files. Tests: one new real-git regression test, plus one tightened wording assertion.

## Evidence

- Regression tests are red on base f6d0c3ea69a, with the fix temporarily reverted:
  - `update-runner-git-config-read.test.ts`: two failed `git-config-update-upstream` reads were recorded.
  - Eight wording cases in `update-command-service-publication.test.ts` failed.
- The same tests are green on the fix.
- The sibling real-git runner suites pass with the fix: `update-runner-git`, `-replay`, `-candidate` and `service-publication`, 178/178 tests across 5 files.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` are green.
- An independent read-only Codex review found nothing (NO FINDINGS).
- Live CLI before/after on Crabbox AWS Linux (fresh clones built at each commit, isolated HOME, local `main` without upstream keys, on a feature branch). Each run used `node openclaw.mjs update --channel dev --json --yes --no-restart`, and both runs finish `skipped / no-upstream` as before:

  ```text
  base f6d0c3ea69a  git config --get branch.main.remote       exit 1  facts git-config-update-upstream(command-failed)
  base f6d0c3ea69a  git config --get branch.main.remote       exit 1  facts git-config-update-upstream(command-failed)
  base f6d0c3ea69a  git config --get-all branch.main.merge    exit 1  facts git-config-update-upstream(command-failed)
  fix  348dd1a53dd  git config --get branch.main.remote       exit 0  facts none
  fix  348dd1a53dd  git config --get branch.main.remote       exit 0  facts none
  fix  348dd1a53dd  git config --get-all branch.main.merge    exit 0  facts none
  ```

- Gap: the reworded publication refusal is proven only by the service-publication suite. A live repro needs a running Gateway plus stale `dist-runtime`, and the message text is the only change on that path.

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins cannot react to definitively failed runs or replace the fixed issue-report action with their own reporting result.

## User Impact

Plugins can observe committed terminal failures and show a named, linked reporting receipt beside the failure notice without creating another agent turn. Without a plugin, the existing report link remains unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses the accepted lifecycle, existing failure receipt, plugin hook runner, and Control UI action registry. `run_failed` fires only for a newly committed terminal failure receipt; retries, Stop, yield, admission rejection, and incognito do not leak into reporting callbacks. External plugins require conversation-access permission.

prs.title: revert: skills-used full-transcript scan on every chat history page (#196065)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Production regression on the Team Gateway right after deploying `ade42165` (2026-11-16 07:36 PST). #196065 made `readChatHistoryPage` (`src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-pages.ts:177`) call `readChatHistorySkillLoads` on every first history page (offset 0, no messageId). That runs `readSessionTranscriptSummaryAsync(scope, { kind: "skills-used" })`, a single deferred read that visits and prepares visibility for every message in the session's transcript.

On Team, a session with 36,428 transcript events took 55.2 s (07:38:38) and 58.9 s (07:39:46) of SQL per scan. Clients re-request first pages after a restart and on every chat open, so the scan repeated about once a minute. Each time, the session actor was held and its live transcript appends queued 48–59 s. Restart-resume for `agent:roboclaw:main` timed out (140 s) during this window.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is containment: a clean `git revert` of #196065 (no later commits touch its files). It restores the previous history-page cost on the default chat-open path. A bounded re-land is being worked on separately: an incremental skills-used inventory recorded at append time or as a session fact, or a bounded read only when the details pane opens. Reverting first keeps the large-session write freeze off production meanwhile.

## User Impact

Opening chat history no longer triggers a full-transcript scan, and large sessions' writes stop freezing. The "skills used" section in conversation details goes away until the bounded version lands.

## Evidence

- Team Gateway journal on `ade42165`: `sessions.history.read` readerOperation `sessions.history.skills-used`, sqlMs 55,224 (07:38:38 PST) and 58,930 (07:39:46 PST); reservation queue waits up to 59,131 ms on `session.actor.appendTranscriptEvent`.
- `git revert 3038e2d37d79c` applies cleanly on `origin/main`.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` on the revert: see the PR checks; local run below.

Original feature credit: @jacobtomlinson (#196065). The revert is not a judgment on the feature, only on the unbounded read it added to the default chat-open path.

prs.title: fix(gateway): avoid filesystem stalls during catalog refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway event-loop stalls when a filesystem transaction delays the catalog refresh sidecar lock or audited runtime metadata operations.

Production evidence: Team `25c97908`, 2026-11-16 05:02 PST, showed the Gateway main thread in D-state for 1.97 seconds inside `openat2(O_CREAT)` for `openclaw-agent.sqlite.plugin-model-catalog.lock`. The kernel stack was `btrfs_create → start_transaction → wait_current_trans`; `scheduler:update.remote-model-catalog` recorded a 2,002 ms event-loop stall while worktree removals drove a btrfs commit.

## User Impact

Catalog publication no longer creates that sidecar lock on the Gateway thread. Audited config, OpenClaw ID, installer, skill, cron and session-artifact paths use async filesystem operations or consume existing owner facts. Prompt reduction preserves disclosed output paths without probing temporary files; a later read reports an expired artifact.

This is a bounded repair stage, not a claim that every Gateway path is sync-free. General fs-safe locks, source-capture custody, timeline durability and managed update handoff require separate owner work. No schema, configuration or dependency change is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

The catalog's async file-lock wrapper reached synchronous native filesystem operations. Its sidecar duplicated canonical database writer custody. Publications now use that existing writer; credential cleanup queues its candidate read behind earlier publications, then releases the read barrier before entering individual writers. Later publications retain transactional auth revalidation. Outside writers require exclusive offline custody.

The accompanying audit converts direct runtime metadata calls, preserves async key creation and launch/stop ordering, deletes redundant existence probes, and reuses async catalog identity and inspection-budget readers. Config startup also reuses its existing fingerprint instead of computing it again. Production delta: **−9 lines**; guards and reproducible proof tooling are separate.

## Evidence

The synthetic fixture contains a 35.06 GiB agent database, 5,000 sessions and 62,000 workspace files totaling 1.10 GB. No production data was copied. Five interleaved baseline/candidate pairs and A/A controls used Node 26.12.1 on APFS. The fault targets the actual native catalog `openBeneath(O_CREAT)` call; this is fault-injection evidence, not a btrfs kernel reproduction.

| Median measurement | Parent | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Publication, 2,000 ms create fault | 2,016.48 ms | 4.83 ms |
| Maximum heartbeat gap, fault armed | 2,012.03 ms | 1.82 ms |
| Publication, no fault | 4.963 ms | 4.219 ms |
| Main-thread CPU, no fault | 2.986 ms | 2.307 ms |
| Sync Node FS calls / native catalog creates | 20 / 1 | 0 / 0 |

Every process verified committed catalogs through a fresh reader. Allocation medians were 4.31 MB → 3.44 MB, but A/A variation was too large to claim a precise gain. An initial +0.37 ms undelayed heartbeat difference did not reproduce in a bounded 20-sample-per-arm followup; both series and CPU profiles are retained. Reproducer: `scripts/perf/catalog-publication-measure.mjs`.

Focused proof passed: 39 catalog tests, 47 model/prompt-prefix tests, 84 session/spill tests, 32 skill-install tests, 62 OpenClaw ID tests, and the audit batches of 58, 96 and 349 tests. The final reloader simplification passed all 146 reloader tests. Twenty existing native-iroh tests were skipped because that addon is unavailable locally. Regression guards fail on the exact parent for catalog publication, spill probes and the other reproduced mutation paths.

Codex local autoreview is **scoped-clean through P2** for the main change against parent `6670297776a00` and the subsequent four-file CI repair at `225aaebe7329c`. `pnpm check:changed` and the scoped repair rerun pass the applicable type, lint, format and boundary checks except two proven parent dead-export failures: `ProjectedContinuationSource` and `partContinuation`. A clean exact-parent run reproduces both; their exports were introduced by `24385a20428a3` / #200056. These are recorded main regressions, not ignored noise. No guard baseline was changed.

Initial CI at `dc75193ca69fd` found stale synchronous fault hooks in three peer-link consumer suites and unregistered benchmark lint suppressions. The repair preserves all authority assertions, passes all seven affected cases under pinned Bun and all 14 suppression-guard tests, and replaces global module-loader interception with the native addon selected by fs-safe. A repeated native smoke still observes one delayed baseline create versus zero candidate creates. `pnpm check:changed --base dc75193ca69fd` passes its applicable gates except the same two attributed parent dead exports.

Exact-head CI and hosted ClawSweeper review are required before landing. No open ClawSweeper checklist item will be bypassed.

prs.title: feat(agents): keep absolute workspace paths out of cached system-prompt prefix (#191485)
prs.body:
Closes #191485

## What Problem This Solves

When multiple agents configured with identical instructions (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, IDENTITY.md) run in separate isolated workspaces, their system prompts diverge before character 2,200 due to absolute workspace paths in injected file headings and the `## Workspace` section, preventing prefix prompt cache sharing at the provider.

## User Impact

User impact: Multi-agent setups using shared template instructions across separate workspaces can now benefit from prompt-prefix cache reuse at providers supporting prompt caching (e.g. Anthropic prompt caching, OpenAI prefix caching), reducing input token latency and inference overhead for templated multi-agent deployments.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. **Workspace-relative headings**: Files located inside the agent workspace now render their prompt headings as workspace-relative paths (`## AGENTS.md` instead of `## /abs/path/AGENTS.md`), while files outside the workspace retain their original paths.
2. **Symlink and canonical alias support**: Recognizes canonical workspace identity when workspaceDir is supplied as a symlink or alias (e.g. `/tmp/alias` -> `/tmp/real`), ensuring context files reporting resolved paths render relative headings while genuinely external files stay absolute.
3. **Missing-file marker normalization confined to prompt preparation**: The exported harness SDK loader (`buildBootstrapContextFiles` / `buildBootstrapContextForFiles`) and its `EmbeddedContextFile` type are completely unchanged, preserving the exact public SDK surface and contract without adding metadata fields. The loader carries missing-file facts privately into prompt preparation (`prepareContextFilesForPrompt`), which renders workspace-relative markers (`[MISSING] Expected at: BOOTSTRAP.md`) for cache parity, including budget-clamped spellings, without inferring provenance from content spelling and leaving genuine loaded file content completely untouched.
4. **Directory section placement**: The `## Workspace` and `## Directory Roles` sections containing absolute workspace paths were moved below `SYSTEM_PROMPT_CACHE_BOUNDARY` adjacent to `## Runtime`.
5. **Cache key identity**: The stable prefix cache key now tracks `headingPath` and file `contentHash` via `projectStableContextFiles` rather than raw file objects with absolute paths, enabling cross-workspace cache hit evaluation while preserving invalidation upon content changes and keeping `system-prompt.ts` within its line cap.

## Evidence

### 1. Shipped Workspace Loader & Native Runtime Provider Request Trace

Executed end-to-end through OpenClaw's shipped workspace loader (`resolveBootstrapContextForRun`) reading real files from isolated temporary directories on disk, followed by the native runtime turn executor (`createNativeRuntime` + `rt.withTurn`) capturing actual serialized HTTP request payloads sent to the provider model endpoint:

```

      * Absent BOOTSTRAP.md: left unwritten on disk
  - Agent B: /tmp/ws-b-4mN8vX/

      * Absent BOOTSTRAP.md: left unwritten on disk

Step 2: Shipped Workspace Loading (resolveBootstrapContextForRun)
  - Loader A reads files from /tmp/ws-a-9F2kL1 on disk
      * Preserves genuine SOUL.md content starting with missing-file text
      * Detects absent BOOTSTRAP.md -> generates missing marker
  - Loader B reads files from /tmp/ws-b-4mN8vX on disk
      * Preserves genuine SOUL.md content starting with missing-file text
      * Detects absent BOOTSTRAP.md -> generates missing marker

Step 3: Native Runtime Turn Execution (createNativeRuntime -> rt.withTurn)
  - Runtime A bound to workspace /tmp/ws-a-9F2kL1
  - Runtime B bound to workspace /tmp/ws-b-4mN8vX
  - Model requests captured at mock provider endpoint (POST /v1/chat/completions)

================================================================================

```

- The first **32,134 bytes** of both outgoing provider requests are **byte-identical** despite completely distinct workspace paths — exactly the property providers need for prefix-cache reuse.

## What Problem This Solves

Native iOS Talk leaves completed public progress messages silent while waiting for the final answer.

## User Impact

Talk queues completed progress before the final reply. Each message keeps its own voice directive. Growing previews, reasoning, tool output and foreign runs remain silent. Stop, disconnect and speech interruption discard queued playback.

Automatic progress narration still needs the iOS owner's decision.

## Why This Change Was Made

One subscription created before `chat.send` consumes the owned run's canonical chat and completed public preamble events. The existing speech queue carries each message's directive and applies persistent voice/model changes in playback order. Progress stays out of the cumulative final-answer buffer. Interrupted speech cannot regain ownership when a late final reply arrives.

Depends on #173035. The original lifecycle prerequisite remains in this branch; review and merge it first.

## Evidence

Current head: `9d9a323038a177ceaf32492c65caf7867261c8c2`.

- Reconciled the observed merge conflict with upstream `b367b1fd64d8daa5f91aa7a8a78b9a90f92d0df6`. The send path preserves upstream startup-admission retries and transcript cancellation while inheriting the Gateway execution budget. Upstream routine-trace removal and current realtime recovery are retained.
- Added regressions for one-shot and persistent local ElevenLabs directives at the HTTP boundary, ordered progress/final playback, and interruption without resumed history readback. They use synthetic requests and audio; no provider call is needed. The iOS voice CI lane now selects `TalkTranscriptCompletionTests`.
- All 1,037 current workflow/native-policy guard tests passed across 10 files (774.91 seconds for both shards). Pinned workflow lint, generated Git-owner checks, composite-input checks and the candidate diff check passed. These validate CI wiring, not native speech playback.

This PR stays draft until #173035 lands, the iOS owner decides whether completed public preambles should be spoken automatically, and current-head native behavior proof is available for Gateway and local ElevenLabs playback, including Stop/disconnect suppression.

prs.title: refactor(sessions): follow the chat by key for stored delivery references
prs.body:
## Problem

A message edit, rewind or `/new` mints a new lifecycle revision. References that were stored before the change still compared that revision, so the result was dropped:

- A background exec that exits after a rewind or edit is withheld. The chat gets the note "Background command result withheld … reset, rewound or moved".
- A background result (cron or subagent) commit fails with `session rebound`.
- An automatic goal continuation stops after an edit.
- Deep-research jobs disappear from the chat after an edit ("not found in this conversation generation").
- A queued outbound send and a memory audience lease are revoked after an edit.

Only the session key stays the same across edit, switch, reset and compaction.

## Fix

- Stored references match the chat by key alone (`matchesSessionGeneration`). Live transcript writers keep their exact transcript pin. A scheduled cron occurrence keeps its exact lifecycle (`exactLifecycle`).
- Queued outbound sends follow the key across a reset.
- A session event follows the key to the chat's current transcript before reply admission, so a compaction successor still gets the wake.
- Deleted: `followSessionEventTargetForHost`, the exec withhold note, and the `expectedLifecycleRevision` thread through background results, cron conversation results, confirmed visible messages and outbound transcript pins.
- Goal continuation matches by key and goal. Deep-research job views drop the revision compare; the job store stays per transcript.
- New CI ratchet `check:session-identity-ratchet`: production `src` counts of `expectedSessionId`, `expectedLifecycleRevision` and `.lifecycleRevision` must not grow.

Not changed here:
- Reactions still read by transcript id. Message ids are 8 hex characters and unique only within one transcript, so a key-wide read is not safe yet.
- GitHub publication keeps its incarnation pin. Its transition worker stores the revision in publication rows, so following the key needs a stored-row change.
- Subagent requester ids and process ownership belong to a separate change.

Production code: +48 / −208.

## User impact

- Results that finish after an edit, rewind or `/new` arrive in the chat as it is now.
- A deleted chat still drops the result. Delete already stops the key's processes, subagents and queued inputs, so a recreated key gets nothing.
- An archived chat gets no wake (same as before).

## Proof

Source-tier scratch Gateway (`ocx src`), base = merge base, scripted model with a real background `exec` (exit after 60–75 s):

| Journey | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| Rewind while exec runs | withheld (note in chat) | wake delivered |
| Edit (rewind + new message) while exec runs | withheld | wake delivered |
| Queued input across a rewind during an active turn | input runs | input runs |
| Archive while exec runs | no wake | no wake |
| Delete, then recreate the key | no wake, process stopped | no wake, process stopped |
| Compaction successor (new transcript id) | wake delivered | wake delivered |

Focused tests: lease, session events, exec notify, goal continuation, deep research, background results, cron delivery, outbound transcript. `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm check:test-types` pass.

prs.title: fix(update): bridge 2026.11.5-beta.4 updaters
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: updates driven by a 2026.11.5-beta.4 updater can fail with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` on their recovery path when the target is a build from main.

## User Impact

User impact: beta.4 users updating to the next release keep a working failure and recovery path. Their old updater finds the chunks it lazily imports after the package swap, and a failed update stays recoverable instead of crashing mid-recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

2026.11.5-beta.4 was published to npm (beta tag) on 2026-11-16 02:41Z, but main's update compatibility inventory stops at 2026.11.5-beta.3. Without an inventory entry, builds from main ship no post-swap bridges for beta.4 updaters. This is the same gap fixed for 11.2/beta.1 (#195249), 11.3/beta.2 (#197844) and beta.3 (#199653).

The inventory was regenerated with `pnpm update:compat:gen` over the full published window, from integrity-verified npm tarballs. Every existing entry is byte-identical, including 2026.11.4, which already matches its npm integrity. The only addition is `2026.11.5-beta.4` (77 chunks, commit `2c173a37a48`, the `v2026.11.5-beta.4` tag).

## Evidence

- **Registry match:** `npm view openclaw@2026.11.5-beta.4` has the same `dist.integrity` and `openclaw.schemaVersions` (state 36, agent 38) as the new entry. npm records no `gitHead`; the commit matches the release tag.
- **Bridge requirements:** beta.4 requires exactly the same (origin module, symbol) exports and importer owners as beta.3 (184 requirements, none added or removed). Main already serves beta.3's set. `scripts/runtime-postbuild.mts` writes these bridges on every build, so the PR CI build exercises the new entry natively.
- **Reviews:** autoreview was scoped-clean at P2. An independent read-only Codex review ran the inventory parser, checked ordering and beta.3 consistency, and found no defects.

<details>
<summary>Notes</summary>

This is the fifth time the inventory has lagged an npm publish (#195249, #196855, #197844, #199653, and now beta.4). Regenerating it at release cut or publish would close this gap; that remains a maintainer decision.

Separately, the inventory inside the published 2026.11.4 package ends at 2026.10.7, so 10.8 through 11.3 updaters targeting 11.4 have no post-swap bridges on their failure path. That needs a release-branch regeneration, which this main PR does not change.

</details>

prs.title: fix: keep ordinary tests from reaching GitHub
prs.body:
Thanks for maintaining OpenClaw. I found this while running ordinary development tests in my fork.

## What Problem This Solves

**Ordinary tests should not contact real GitHub services or borrow the developer’s GitHub credentials.** Some fixtures did reach for real release downloads and Git remotes. This PR fixes those destinations and adds a guard against future accidental access.

## User Impact

Ordinary test runs block supported GitHub requests **before dispatch**, remove ambient GitHub credentials from test children, and report unexpected attempts even when a test catches the rejection. Intentional live tests retain a separate, explicit entry point; a flag inherited from the developer’s shell cannot silently enable access.

## Why This Change Was Made

The audit caught **four GitHub-bound attempts**: two release-asset downloads, a worker Git fetch, and a fork-publication Git fetch. Their fixtures now use local substitutes. The guard covers fetch/HTTP, sockets, Chromium, and child `gh`, `git`, and shell commands.

It also repairs release fixtures whose fake `gh` executable was rejected by the guard, triggering repeated polling. Moving the fake into the admitted temporary location eliminated that fixture conflict; all 44 affected release tests subsequently passed.

**The 17,331 repeated refusals were local fixture commands—not 17,331 GitHub API calls.** All four confirmed GitHub-bound attempts were blocked during the audit. We did not measure quota consumption or demonstrate a rate-limit lockout.

## Evidence

Rebased onto `8937cb4fa8c` on October 25, preserving main’s updated cursor assertions and guarded browser navigation. On Node 24.22.1, the focused browser/guard/configuration run passed 112 tests (four platform skips, 61.21 s); nine selected Git lifecycle, worker identity, and merge-workflow cases passed (168.55 s). Both runs used the OS network fence: zero unexpected attempts, 102 intentional blocking controls, and zero omitted attributions. Targeted formatting, lint, and four type-check graphs pass. The mechanical integration reuses the prior review; the original commit sequence and historical audit gaps remain unchanged.

The commits preserve the requested order: first the blocking guard and audit evidence, then fixture repairs with the guard retained.

ClawSweeper’s four fixture conflicts are now repaired: Git cancellation uses a held local transport; worker identity admits only its declared synthetic profile; shell inspection distinguishes literal arrays and lowercase `path` from commands and `PATH`; Chromium starts with an empty standalone page before guarded navigation. The original behavior assertions remain intact.

Affected fixture scenarios and 115 guard regression tests pass behind the OS network fence, with zero unexpected attempts. Formatting, affected lint, and five relevant test type graphs pass.

**The full ordinary-suite audit remains incomplete.** The JavaScript guard cannot fully police opaque native executables. Tests also ran behind an OS network fence. The earlier broad check recorded two inherited failures; it was not rerun for this scoped rebase.

prs.title: fix: gateway pending-install reload test flakes when post-ready maintenance holds the plugin lease
prs.body:
Closes #199854

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the gateway plugin-lifecycle test "hot-applies pending installs without restarting a sibling whose package metadata keys were reordered" fails intermittently (original CI: echoed=false, 1 failed / 530 passed on the frozen release candidate) when post-ready startup maintenance still holds the plugin/config lifecycle lease at the moment the test issues its explicit `plugins.reload`.

## User Impact

User impact: no end-user-visible change; restores reliability of the gateway plugin-lifecycle suite whose unwaived CI failure blocks publication of the frozen release candidate (#199854 is the fix-in-parallel tracking item).

## Why This Change Was Made

The pending-install case awaited startup readiness but not post-ready maintenance, which the runtime schedules as an independent idle task outside `startupSettled`. When the derived plugin-registry refresh still owns the lifecycle lease, the explicit `plugins.reload` fails fast (`waitMs: 0` → retryable `UNAVAILABLE`, `mutationAccepted=false`) and never reaches metadata resolution, so the config-watcher echo spy never fires and the case fails opaquely on `echoed=false`. The webhook cases in the same file already observe and await the real maintenance via `observePostReadyStartupMaintenance`; this change gives the pending-install case the same barrier and asserts the RPC receipt (with its refusal message) before the downstream metadata assertions, so any future refusal names its cause. No production code, lease-policy, retry, or sleep changes; all sibling ownership/channel assertions retained.

## Evidence

Controlled real-owner reproduction: the real idle scheduler fired the real `runGatewayPostReadyStartupMaintenance`, which held the real lifecycle lease while the real registry refresh was bounded-held for 45s; the real `plugins.reload` RPC was then issued. No synthetic RPC/lease responses; probe code was removed after the runs.

### Before fix (barrier absent)

```
[probe] maintenance entered 19.9s
[probe] refresh entered (holding 45s) 20.0s
[probe] lease call waitMs=0 24.5s
[probe] reload done ok=false err={"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"Another plugin or config operation is already running; retry when it completes.","retryable":true,"retryAfterMs":1000,"details":{"mutationAccepted":false}} 24.5s
 × hot-applies pending installs without restarting a sibling whose package metadata keys were reordered 66231ms
AssertionError: expected false to be true // echoed
```

Matches the original CI failure (run 43770968712: echoed false) and the issue's controlled diagnostic.

### After fix (barrier present)

Same 45s real lease hold: the case joins real maintenance, then the unchanged assertions pass.

```
✓ hot-applies pending installs without restarting a sibling whose package metadata keys were reordered 69409ms
 Tests  1 passed | 2 skipped (3)
```

### Suites

- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-plugins.lifecycle.channels.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 3 passed (3), 242s
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/gateway/server-plugins.lifecycle.channels.test.ts` → no problems
- `oxfmt --check` → clean; `git diff --check` → clean

Gaps: tsgo lanes cannot run on this host (glibc 2.28 < 2.32 requirement); CI covers them. Whole-file replay also passed locally on the same base before this branch (all 3 cases).

prs.title: fix(agents): keep read-only steering carriers when publishing suppressed user envelopes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Team Gateway crashed on 2026-11-16 at 07:04:29 PST (release 25c97908) with an unhandled promise rejection:

```
TypeError: Cannot assign to read only property 'Symbol(openclaw.steeringRuntimeContext)' of object '#<Object>'
    at Object.assign (<anonymous>)
    at publishPersistedUserEnvelope (session-tool-result-guard-wrapper)
    at Object.onUserMessagePersistenceSuppressed
    at guardedAppend … drainStoreWriterQueue
```

The throw happened inside the store writer queue, so the process exited and systemd restarted it. The restart interrupted 13 sessions (restart-resume), 6 subagent waits, 3 cron jobs and two long runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

`attachSteeringRuntimeContext` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/runtime-context-prompt.ts`) defines the steering carrier with `Object.defineProperty`, enumerable but non-writable. Spread copies of the runtime user message carry that enumerable symbol into the prepared/persisted envelope. `publishPersistedUserEnvelope` deletes the runtime message's string keys and then ran `Object.assign(runtime, persisted, { content })`. `Object.assign` also copies enumerable own symbols, so it tried to overwrite the read-only carrier and threw.

The function's own comment says symbol-carried media and steering facts stay on the runtime message. The fix publishes only string-keyed envelope fields (`Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(persisted))`), which matches that contract. Production LOC: +2 (one changed line plus a two-line comment explaining the read-only carrier hazard).

## User Impact

Steered user turns whose persistence is suppressed no longer crash the Gateway, and the steering carrier on the runtime message is preserved.

## Evidence

- New regression test `publishes a suppressed user envelope without rewriting the steering carrier` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.guard.test.ts`. On unfixed `main` it fails with `TypeError: Attempted to assign to readonly property`; with the fix it passes.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.guard.test.ts src/agents/session-tool-result-guard.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/runtime-context-prompt.test.ts`: 18 + 37 passed.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: all lanes pass except the dead-export scan, which flags `ProjectedContinuationSource` in `src/config/sessions/session-history-types.ts`. That file is untouched here; it's an inherited `main` regression.
- Codex autoreview: scoped-clean, no actionable findings.
- Production evidence: Team Gateway journal, 2026-11-16T15:04:29Z; first occurrence in 7 days of logs.

issues.title: `gpt-image-1`, `dall-e-3` and `dall-e-2` are retired but still offered in the OpenAI image model list
issues.body:
### Bug Description

OpenAI retired `gpt-image-1` on October 23, 2026, and `dall-e-3` and `dall-e-2` on May 12, 2026 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations). Requests that name them now fail, but nanobot still offers all three in the OpenAI image model list:

- https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/ce3f36983d6bee40d1f4cee58f71f3a1888ea648/nanobot/providers/image_generation.py#L1096 (`OpenAIImageGenerationClient.model_options`, which the WebUI settings show as the OpenAI image models)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. In the WebUI settings, pick OpenAI for image generation.
2. Choose `gpt-image-1`, `dall-e-3` or `dall-e-2` from the model list.
3. Generate an image. The request fails because OpenAI no longer serves that model.

### Expected Behavior

The list offers only models OpenAI still serves. The default, `gpt-image-2`, still works, so dropping the three retired ids fixes it. OpenAI's replacement for `gpt-image-1` is `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` or `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, if you want to offer one of those instead.

### Environment

Not environment-specific: found by reading the code at commit ce3f369. Provider: OpenAI. Models: `gpt-image-1`, `dall-e-3`, `dall-e-2`.

---
Found by [Since](https://since.dev), which watches code for model and API retirements and opens the fix before the date. It's free for open source, and I work on it. Full scan of this repo: https://since.dev/scan/HKUDS/nanobot

Happy to open a PR if that helps.

prs.title: fix(webui): settle completed turns across reconnect paths
prs.body:
## Summary

Fix a WebUI lifecycle-accounting bug that can leave a conversation showing an active response after its turns have completed. When canonical history explicitly confirms an older turn's completion but a newer turn is still running, completion fencing must also settle the older turn's existing ownership record. Otherwise the fence discards the very terminal events that could release that record.

The fix is limited to frontend lifecycle accounting and its history/reconnect callers. In addition to the original mounted completion-fence repair, unmounted reconnect now settles explicit per-turn completion even when a newer active turn prevents adopting the whole page. Lifecycle-only settlement retains buffered/late content and independent anonymous recovery. No gateway execution, cancellation, database, wire API/protocol, dependencies or configuration changes.

## User-visible problem

The reported symptom was a conversation continuing to show the running/Stop-response UI after the backend had finished. Clicking Stop returned `No active task to stop.`. Read-only investigation of that session found persisted turn completions and no corresponding active checkpoint or pending input. The Stop response is consistent with an already-idle backend; this change does not alter that response or force gateway cancellation.

The original browser's WebSocket/HTTP event trace was not recorded, so this PR does **not** claim to establish the unique cause of that historical incident. The ledger defect described below was independently reproduced with the current source, the mounted history hook and a real `ThreadShell` in controlled browser tests. It is a conditional lifecycle race, not a claim that every completed conversation remains active.

## Original revision environment

The following versions describe the author's original revision `21ab11c16`, not the Windows follow-up verification below. The original incident's precise browser cache/bundle state is unknown.

| Component | Local environment |
| --- | --- |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (Noble Numbat), x86_64 |
| Kernel | Linux 7.0.0-31-generic |
| Desktop | GNOME Shell 46.0 |
| Browser used for controlled browser verification | Google Chrome 153.0.8010.52 |
| nanobot source | Declared package version 0.4.1; unpatched base `e91906bc3a83c8a3f37ed94ef6c44f750b92b4c1` |
| Installation context | Local source/editable installation; implementation and review performed in isolated source copies, without modifying the running gateway |
| Gateway installation's Python | 3.12.14; the defect reproduction does not require a model call or Python gateway execution |
| Node used for the final revised implementation and independent review | 22.17.1 |
| System-default Node / npm | 18.19.1 / 9.2.0; **not** the runtime used for the final revised verification reported below |
| Git | 2.43.0 |
| React / React DOM | 18.3.1 / 18.3.1 |
| TypeScript | 5.9.3 |
| Vite | 5.4.21 |
| Vitest | 2.1.9 |
| ESLint | 10.4.0 |
| Playwright test runner | 1.64.1 |
| Bun | Unavailable locally; Bun-only checks were not executed |

These are local verification versions, not new dependency requirements or a claim of a fresh lockfile installation. The browser runs used the official Playwright runner with local Google Chrome, not CI's downloaded Chromium. Controlled HTTP/WS fixtures were used, rather than a real gateway/model recovery session.

## Reproduction

### Required event ordering

A deterministic reproduction needs to control the history response and lifecycle events; simply disconnecting and reconnecting does not guarantee this ordering. Use the same client/gateway contract and a mounted conversation with a nonfragment latest-history response.

1. Let the client observe turn `A` running.
2. Complete `A` on the server, but prevent its terminal WebSocket events from reaching this client, for example during a transport gap.
3. Let the client observe a newer turn `B` running, as can happen through reconnect hydration. The client still retains `A`'s unresolved ownership record.
4. Resolve the mounted conversation's latest-history request with `A` explicitly completed and `B` still active. The response includes:

   ```json
   {
     "schemaVersion": 3,
     "projection": "events",
     "completed_turn_ids": ["A"],
     "has_pending_tool_calls": true,
     "active_turn_id": "B",
     "events": [
       {"event": "user_message", "chat_id": "repro", "turn_id": "A", "text": "First task", "starts_turn": true},
       {"event": "message", "chat_id": "repro", "turn_id": "A", "text": "Completed first answer"},
       {"event": "turn_end", "chat_id": "repro", "turn_id": "A"},
       {"event": "user_message", "chat_id": "repro", "turn_id": "B", "text": "Next task", "starts_turn": true}
     ],
     "page": {"before_cursor": null, "has_more_before": false, "user_message_offset": 0}
   }
   ```

5. Because `B` is still active, the mounted history owner cannot settle the entire run from this page. It records a completion fence for `A` instead. Confirm that `B` remains active and can display new output.
6. Deliver `B`'s normal terminal events:

   ```json
   [
     {"event": "turn_end", "chat_id": "repro", "turn_id": "B"},
     {"event": "goal_status", "chat_id": "repro", "turn_id": "B", "status": "idle"}
   ]
   ```

7. Observe the run state and the Stop-response control. Optionally deliver a delayed `turn_end` for `A`; on the unpatched code that event is discarded by the fence and does not clear the stale state.

**Actual result before the fix:** both turns can be recorded as completed while the run remains `active=true`, `unsettled=true`, `startedAt=null`; the UI can continue showing `Stop response`. A new applicable canonical read or local reset can clear it, but the delivered terminal events alone do not repair the residual ownership record.

**Expected result:** settling `A` must preserve active `B` and its output/clock; once `B` ends, the client must become idle (`active=false`, `unsettled=false`, `startedAt=null`). Delayed events for `A` must not stop or reopen `B`.

### Deterministic automated reproduction included in this PR

With the repository's WebUI dependencies installed, run the maintained regressions in an isolated checkout of the current PR:

```bash
cd webui
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run \
  src/tests/nanobot-client.test.ts \
  src/tests/useReconnectRuns.test.tsx \
  -t 'settles an older completed turn|notifies subscribers when a completion fence|settles a missed old completion|unmounted old completion|independent anonymous recovery' \
  --maxWorkers=1 --minWorkers=1
```

The original four mounted/ledger regressions failed against the original production base. The follow-up first added four regressions against `21ab11c16`: both timings of a newer turn relative to an unmounted full-page read, and independent anonymous recovery with full/fragment responses. All four failed before the follow-up production changes and pass after them. The bounded model retains the legacy failures separately as negative controls; the default current-implementation checks must have no counterexamples. Do not replace source files in a live installation to reproduce these comparisons.

The hook regression `settles a missed old completion from mounted history while a newer turn remains active` exercises the actual mounted `useNanobotStream` history/reconnect path. The client regressions cover both direct canonical adoption rejected by a newer owner and the fence-only path, plus subscriber updates when the latest completed turn has no terminal WS frame.

## Root cause

`ClientRunLedger.view()` considers a run active while any turn retains an `openOrder`. Previously `fence()` recorded completed IDs and pruned buffered frames, but did not settle their existing turn records. `applyObservation()` then dropped subsequent top-level frames for every fenced ID, including terminal events. This allowed the state to say a turn was completed while retaining its open lifecycle ownership.

Three paths expose that inconsistency:

- `useNanobotStream` uses fence-only reconciliation when a mounted full history page cannot safely settle the entire current run.
- Canonical adoption records explicit completion fences even if a newer owner prevents accepting the whole snapshot.
- Unmounted full-page reconnect previously returned on active metadata or failed preflight before applying an older turn's explicit completion. This was traced to the reconnect path introduced by #6211; the later fragment path already separated lifecycle settlement from content coverage.

Explicit completion of `A` is authoritative independently of whether the page can settle `B`. The ledger must release only the named completed turn, rather than requiring acceptance of the whole page or waiting for a terminal frame it will subsequently discard.

## Fix and regression protection

- Record lifecycle closure and use the existing settlement primitive for each explicitly completed fenced turn. This removes its ownership record and discards pending sends for that exact chat/turn identity.
- Clear the effective start timestamp only when the completed ID matches the latest named owner. Do not change the newer owner's identity, generation or clock.
- Preserve independent anonymous recovery activity. An unscoped `attached`/`recovery_state` can start a new recovery before its canonical turn ID arrives, while the old `latestTurnId` is still retained. Completing that old named turn must not stop the new anonymous recovery. The existing parameterized tests now cover both event variants with this fence boundary.
- Generalize the existing fragment lifecycle-only operation as `settleCompletedRunLifecycle`. Unmounted full pages use it even when the whole-page preflight rejects adoption, without fully fencing or discarding live content. Mounted fragments retain their transcript-owner handoff.
- Cache adoptable history before notifying completion subscribers. Only an idle snapshot can clear activity without a named identity; a partial named completion preserves independent anonymous recovery.
- Retain late-frame fencing and read-only canonical preflight. No polling, timeout reset or artificial successful Stop response is added.

Production changes remain in `client-run-ledger.ts`, `nanobot-client.ts`, `useReconnectRuns.ts` and the renamed lifecycle call in `useNanobotStream.ts`; tests and the bounded verification model accompany them.

## Original revision verification (`21ab11c16`)

The final revised patch was verified in separate implementation and independent-review copies. Both matched the reviewed source snapshot before and after verification. All final runs below used Node 22.17.1; no shared development-tree tests or production deployment were performed.

| Check | Implementation-side result | Independent-review result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Four original bug regressions on the unpatched production base | 4 expected failures at the final-idle/subscriber assertions | Same 4 expected failures |
| Focused client, reconnect, stream, turn-completion and thread-shell tests | 409 passed | 409 product tests + 7 private behavioral probes passed (416 total) |
| Exact final-patch full WebUI suite with V8 coverage | 3878 passed, 1 skipped; two workers | 3878 passed, 1 skipped; one worker |
| Coverage | Statements/lines 94.31%, branches 89.52%, functions 91.88% | Same percentages; repository thresholds met |
| Application/unit-test, browser and production TypeScript checks | All passed | All passed |
| Full WebUI/channel ESLint with `--max-warnings 0` | Passed | Passed |
| Real Vite production build | Passed | Passed |
| Existing browser selection: history-hydration, session-transition, queued-guidance, sidebar-activity and session-messages | 49 passed | The same 49 cases + 1 private real-`ThreadShell` reproduction passed (50 total) |
| `git diff --check` and final source integrity | Passed | Passed |

Both final-patch full-suite runs were their respective first completed runs, not passing retries after full-suite failures. Existing React/KaTeX/DOM-test-environment warnings and Vite's chunk-size warning were retained in the logs. The private reviewer probes/browser test are additional local evidence, not files added to this PR or promised CI coverage. The maintained regression tests are the two changed test files above.

Independent review also checked newer queued/running owners, per-chat/per-turn send cleanup, anonymous recovery, pure preflight, bounded terminal bookkeeping and fragment content retention. An initial local revision incorrectly cleared anonymous recovery activity; it was blocked, fixed and covered by the existing recovery tests before the final revision was freshly approved. Its other passing checks were not treated as approval of that rejected revision.

## Follow-up verification

The follow-up `6af86525c` was verified on Windows in an isolated worktree with a clean dependency installation. Production behavior is covered by maintained regressions; the TLA+ artifact is in [`webui/verification/turn-sync`](https://github.com/IndigoC/nanobot/blob/6af86525c60d3852d029ea83c168d0e1e6a5f69f/webui/verification/turn-sync/README.md).

| Check | Follow-up result |
| --- | --- |
| New unmounted/anonymous regressions on original PR head | 4 expected failures before the production changes |
| Focused reconnect, client, stream and thread-shell tests | 402 passed |
| Full WebUI suite with V8 coverage | 212 files, 3883 tests passed; statements/lines 94.3%, branches 89.52%, functions 91.88% |
| TypeScript, ESLint, import-boundary check, production build | Passed; build chunk-size warning retained |
| Browser TypeScript and headless `browser/answer-order.spec.ts` | Passed; 12 browser cases |
| Isolated real-client mounted/unmounted PoC replay | 5 passed |
| Implementation-aligned TLC | All 6 configurations exhausted with exit 0 and zero counterexamples; full-page safety/conditional liveness and fragment safety |
| Separate historical TLC controls | 2 invariant and 2 temporal counterexamples retained with the expected exits; not positive implementation passes |

One local `bun run test:imports` invocation had 41 passes and a 5000ms timeout in the CLI-acceptance case while other checks ran concurrently. That failed result is retained; no timeout increase, assertion change or passing retry was used. Final-head CI is reported separately rather than treating this local command as a pass.

[Final-head CI run 44034227906](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/44034227906) **passed**. Checkout logs confirm synthetic merge `2d5f5c710` (main `e76717445` plus follow-up `6af86525c`); the model-mapped production sources and model files are identical to the verified PR head. WebUI static checks and production build passed, all **3886 unit tests across 213 files** passed with coverage thresholds intact, all **590 browser tests** passed across four full-suite shards with exact-once execution verified, and Docker acceptance passed. The remote import-checker suite passed with 41 passes and one Windows-only platform skip; this does not erase the separate local timeout recorded above. Python/native/TUI lanes were outside the selected change scope. TLC was run locally from the committed artifact, not by a CI job.

TLC reproduction (Python, Java and an external official TLA+ v1.7.4 jar required):

```powershell
cd webui/verification/turn-sync
python -B run_tlc.py --jar 'C:\path\to\tla2tools.jar'
# Optional, separate historical comparisons including the four expected failures:
python -B run_tlc.py --compare --jar 'C:\path\to\tla2tools.jar'
```

The six implementation graphs have 10,299 / 16,844 / 79,117 / 105,114 / 10,299 / 16,844 distinct states. No state constraint or depth cutoff is used. The README maps each abstraction to its code owner and states the fixed mounted-state, content-token, complete-page and fairness limits. In particular, liveness does not cover missing completion IDs or unbridgeable fragments.

## Scope and remaining verification

- This change covers the reproduced completed-turn fence defect and the unmounted full-page completion/adoption separation. It does not implement a complete reconnect synchronization protocol or claim to fix every stuck-running symptom.
- The formal result is bounded: one chat, two sequential turns, one reconnect and declared history/fairness assumptions. The model is manually mapped to selected code, not a refinement proof of the complete implementation.
- Separate synthetic-provider probes exercised the real Gateway transport and durable history, including missed A terminal, reconnect while B is active, and an actual latest page completing A. Those probes used raw protocol clients, not a browser connected to the live Gateway; deployed-asset acceptance and the original incident's missing trace remain unverified.
- The running installation was not modified or restarted. Applying the frontend fix requires rebuilding the WebUI assets through the normal deployment process.

prs.title: fix(goal): block goals after terminal execution failures
prs.body:
## Why

A sustained goal could remain active after output-limit recovery, repeated empty responses, or another terminal execution failure had already stopped its run. Some refusal and truncated responses were also reported as successful turns.

## What changed

- Settle terminal failures in the gateway's goal execution policy: atomically block only the current active goal, preserve its objective, and record a safe reason and timestamp before notifying clients.
- Preserve terminal runner reasons and report failed model turns, including refusals, content filtering, and exhausted output/empty-response recovery.
- Add `update_goal(action='resume')` for an explicit user request to continue the same blocked goal, retaining its objective, start time, and progress. Expose the blocked recap in runtime guidance.

## Scope

No changes to token settings, retry budgets, client protocols, `/stop`, or `/cancel_goal`. Retries and recoverable tool errors keep working; ordinary conversation does not automatically resume blocked goals.

## Tradeoffs

Terminal failures block rather than retry indefinitely. Resume intent is interpreted by the model, but the tool requires freshly consumed user input; automation and subagent inputs cannot grant that permission. Resuming grants no permission to create or replace a goal.

## Blast Radius

Durable goal execution and model-failure reporting use the existing blocked-state projection. Generation checks and compare-and-set writes prevent stale runs or concurrent cancellation from being overwritten. Hard process crashes and unavailable storage cannot guarantee a persisted transition.

## Verification

- Runner/loop, goal tools, cancellation, sessions, commands, and SDK regression checks: **1142 passed, 3 skipped** on Windows/Python 3.14.
- WebUI goal/wire/background, runtime-context/model-event checks and gateway smoke suite: **59 passed, 1 skipped**.
- Real isolated gateway + local synthetic SSE model: normal completion, `/stop`, exhausted length recovery, reconnect, status inquiry, and resume-to-completion passed through the public WebSocket interface.
- Full CI lint command, strict BasedPyright, Python import boundaries, and `git diff --check` passed. Full-project/cross-platform CI is pending; the running user instance and its configuration were not changed.

Resolves [NAN-455](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-455/执行终止性失败时自动阻塞-goal并支持显式恢复原目标)

prs.title: perf(ci): speed up full WebUI regression gates
prs.body:
## Why

Frontend changes currently wait roughly 14 minutes for the browser lane. Across 150 recent CI runs (117 PR runs, November 12–16), successful PR browser jobs had a 13m54s median and 17m21s p95; the combined static/unit/build lane had a 4m42s median. This PR shortens the full-suite critical path rather than selecting fewer tests.

## What changed

- Run static checks, production build, full unit coverage, and four browser shards independently. Balance every natively discovered browser file using recorded timings; new tests are included without timing entries. Check executed case identities against full discovery and require every lane to pass.
- Load only the selected browser fixture and its existing mocks/provider. Preserve all 40 scene URLs, moved component bodies, real components/styles/motion, and ordinary local commands. Retain JSON results, coverage summaries, and browser failure traces.
- Preserve every existing assertion. Add a responsive-toolbar readiness assertion before comparing activity-label positions across toggles. Fix attachment details' redundant delayed focus restoration, which otherwise steals focus from the next keyboard Tab; the existing keyboard/download regression remains unchanged.

## Scope

One integrated frontend CI improvement. The only production behavior change is the two-line attachment focus fix exposed by verification. No dependency upgrade, affected-only selection, merge-queue/protection change, automatic retry, increased timeout, disabled isolation, or reduced-motion shortcut. SHA-based workflow concurrency and per-file browser scheduling remain unchanged. Uses standard free-tier `ubuntu-latest` runners with seven-day artifact retention.

Resolves [NAN-452](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-452/在保留全量回归保障的前提下加速-webui-ci)

## Tradeoffs

Parallel browser runners repeat setup, so lower wall time is not a claim of lower total runner minutes. Timing weights are scheduling hints, not a test inventory.

Unit coverage deliberately remains one full native Vitest run with the original 85/80/80/85 thresholds. We tested native blob sharding and rejected it: Vitest 2.1.9 merges already-converted Istanbul maps, and an unhit inner branch can inherit hits from another shard's outer range (a real 0-hit branch became 949 hits). Merely retaining numeric thresholds would therefore weaken the gate. This PR does not introduce a custom coverage merger or upgrade the toolchain to work around it.

## Blast Radius

Browser-fixture initialization, CI job/failure aggregation, and the attachment detail focus handoff. Artifact/discovery checks prevent an empty or incomplete browser shard from turning green. The new resize precondition waits for the real responsive action row, not a fixed delay; all position tolerances and keyboard assertions remain intact.

## Verification

Baseline: [`e91906bc3` CI run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/43882721408), 212 unit files / 3,875 unit tests and 64 browser files / 590 browser cases. Local runs used Node 22.18, Bun 1.3.13, Chromium 156, and an eight-logical-CPU Linux host.

- Full baseline: 3,875 unit tests and 590 browser cases passed. Coverage: statements/lines 94.31%, branches 89.51%, functions 91.88%.
- Browser discovery assigns all 64 files exactly once. Initial four-shard execution ran all 590 cases; three shards passed, and one exposed the responsive-toolbar measurement race. The unchanged attachment keyboard test also reproduced a focus race on the baseline (1/5 paired trials), not just the candidate. After the two narrow fixes, both existing cases passed five fresh repetitions each (10/10), with no retries or relaxed assertions.
- Final local full suite: all 212 unit files / 3,875 tests and 64 browser files / 590 cases pass. Original native coverage: statements/lines 94.31%, branches 89.51%, functions 91.88%, matching local baseline percentages. Seven CI helper tests and 97 Python scope/workflow/failure-gate tests pass. Import boundary checks/checker tests, ESLint, application/browser/production TypeScript, production build, frozen Bun install, npm lock verification, and whitespace checks pass.
- Both hosted frontend runs passed every lane. Independently compared all four native browser artifacts with the baseline: the same 590 case identities, all 64 files exactly once, no skipped/flaky/failed cases and zero retries. Full native unit artifacts contain all 212 files / 3,875 passing tests. Hosted coverage is statements/lines 94.31%, branches 89.52%, functions 91.88%; original thresholds remain enforced.

### Actual hosted critical path

| Run | Longest browser job, including setup | Change selection finished → WebUI gate finished |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| [Baseline `e91906bc3`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/43882721408) | 17m35s | 17m44s |
| [Initial PR code `691108c90`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/43913643900) | 4m00s | 4m09s |
| [Final timing weights `e55eccdfe`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/43915386888) | 4m34s | 7m45s |

The final observation reduces the longest browser job by 74% and frontend gate latency by 56% versus the baseline run. One final browser runner started 3m06s after change selection, explaining much of the wider gate latency; the initial observation was faster. These are two candidate observations with the same full workload, not a newly established median or p95. Timing-weight balance is predictive, not a guarantee of equal runtime across hosted runners. The table measures the frontend gate, not whole-workflow completion: unchanged Python/native-package checks can still dominate the complete CI.

The initial PR's entire workflow passed. The final timing-only commit's first attempt passed all frontend checks but hit a 30-second Python gateway process-exit timeout in `test_real_gateway_goal_single_run_and_stop[True]`. That check passed in the initial full workflow. A single manual rerun of failed jobs passed unchanged, and the final workflow is green on `e55eccdfec5b1c950bc6c03afe4c93ccf0dbf749` (attempt 2). The timeout's root cause is unconfirmed; its initial failure is retained rather than hidden. No backend code, timeout or automatic retry policy was changed.

### Fixture measurement

Five alternating paired trials per scene, fresh isolated browser contexts with HTTP caching disabled, warm Vite/OS caches, identical semantic readiness checks, and real motion. All 70 measured and 14 warmup navigations passed without page/console/request/HTTP errors. Measurements were serialized with the other heavy runs. This measures local scene readiness, not hosted CI p95.

| Scene | Baseline → candidate median readiness | Script requests at readiness |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Default dialog | 420.5 → 239.8ms | 498 → 61 |
| Reopened history | 475.7 → 329.9ms | 536 → 200 |
| Heavy Markdown | 668.9 → 497.2ms | 564 → 252 |
| Settings/API preview | 500.1 → 417.0ms | 498 → 317 |
| Skeleton | 394.7 → 253.3ms | 498 → 273 |
| Initial history loading | 505.3 → 440.1ms | 498 → 393 |
| Chinese history paging | 440.8 → 293.4ms | 556 → 267 |

Retained readiness improvements are 12.9%–43.0%; selected fixture-source script requests fall from 37 to 2–3. Existing targeted layout, highlighting, settings, skeleton, history-loading and anchor cases also passed (25/25). The hosted comparison above uses actual CI job boundaries rather than extrapolating from these samples.
