prs.title: fix(mcp): isolate server startup and retries from chat
prs.body:
## Summary

A slow or unresponsive MCP server no longer blocks ordinary chat or delays tools from healthy servers. The gateway reports slow startup after 10 seconds and cancels an unfinished startup attempt after 60 seconds. Tools that become ready during a turn are available on the next model request. Users do not need to send another message to use them.

This is a draft for design review. The change is not ready to merge.

## Benchmarks

### Latest change: use a tool that becomes ready mid-turn

A real gateway and stdio MCP server processed one user message against a local test model endpoint. The first request arrived before the MCP server was ready. The server finished discovery during that request, and the model made a built-in tool call to continue the same turn. We did not send a follow-up message.

| What we measured | Better result | Previous draft `2065ef90f1` | Current draft `bc62a8a82` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First chat request reaches the model endpoint | Lower; one paired run, not a latency comparison at scale | 1.22 s | 1.25 s |
| Model can call the newly ready MCP tool | Earlier, with a successful tool result | Not available during the current turn | Available on request 2; request 3 received `pong` |
| Ordered definitions on consecutive requests with no further tool change | Identical | Identical where the list was unchanged | Identical on requests 2 and 3; existing definitions stayed in their original order |

The tool list can change when a tool becomes ready. A model provider may reuse less of the previous prompt on that request. The earlier equal-prefix result does not apply to this transition. No provider cache hit rate was measured.

### Previous change: slow startup, timeout, and chat

**Compare:** draft `47edc783fa` vs. draft `2065ef90f1`. Both ran the same gateway workload on macOS arm64 with Python 3.11, real stdio MCP child processes, and a local model endpoint. The endpoint captures model requests and returns test responses. No external model was called.

**Result:** Chat latency was similar in these runs, and the reusable prompt prefix did not change. The slow server still worked. The unresponsive child exited, and the next attempts started after the expected delays.

| What we measured | Better result | `47edc783fa` | `2065ef90f1` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **First chat request reaches the model endpoint** with a 12-second MCP startup in the background. Time starts when the client sends the chat message. | **Lower** | 1.14–1.17 s | 1.06–1.21 s |
| **Slow MCP tool becomes available** with the same 12-second startup. Time starts when the gateway process launches. The tool must return `pong`. | **Lower**, with a successful tool call | 13.41–13.75 s; `pong` | 13.33–13.40 s; `pong` |
| **A child that never answers the handshake exits** while the gateway stays running. Time starts when the gateway process launches. | **Lower**; no child left running after cleanup | Still alive after 63 s; no startup deadline | Exited and reported a timeout at 62.86–63.12 s |
| **Wait before restarting an unresponsive child**, measured from timeout cleanup to the next child launch. | **Match the target**, not faster: 15 s, then 30 s | No retry; the original attempt was still running | 15.12 s, then 30.16 s; no overlapping child processes |
| **Reusable prompt prefix** across two model requests for one user input. The MCP tool becomes ready between the requests. | **Higher** for the same workload; **unchanged** is the goal for this timeout change | 5,259 identical tokens | 5,259 identical tokens; same prefix content |

The first two rows show the range of two paired runs. The chat measurement includes gateway and network overhead; the **1-second** limit applies only to how long the gateway waits for initial MCP discovery. The **10-second** slow notice does not cancel the process. The **60-second** deadline starts cancellation; the timeout is visible after transport cleanup. A healthy sibling tool returned `pong` before and after that timeout.

The cache row counts tokens in the **matching start of two requests**, not extra tokens sent or billed. We normalized temporary checkout and workspace paths and used the same tokenizer on both sides. Ordered tool definitions matched byte for byte across all four compared requests. The next user input called the recovered tool. These measurements do **not** show a live provider's cache hit rate.

<details>
<summary>Earlier benchmarks: discovery, reconnect, and the tool list</summary>

These measurements use different earlier versions or prototypes. Each row identifies its comparison; they are not all comparisons with `main` or new runs on the latest commit. The original PR base was `d3bb330f57`.

| What we measured | Better result | Reference | Earlier PR result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First chat request reaches the model endpoint while a 12-second MCP server starts | **Lower** | Original `main`: 12.64 s | 1.11–1.13 s |
| Healthy MCP tool becomes available next to an unresponsive peer, using the slower configuration order in two runs | **Lower** | Serial background prototype: 2.91–3.17 s | Per-server discovery: 0.43–0.52 s |
| A 12-second stdio MCP tool becomes available after the gateway launches | **Lower**, with a successful tool call | Draft `f02258e39e`: no tool within 16 s | 13.2–13.7 s; returned `pong` |
| Healthy MCP tool becomes available when four unresponsive servers are configured ahead of it | **Lower** | Draft `f02258e39e`: 11.6–11.7 s | 2.45–2.58 s |
| Hot reload replaces a stalled server: time to a successful tool call | **Lower** | Draft `f02258e39e`: 10.05 s | 0.23 s |
| A healthy server reconnects while another server stalls: time to a successful tool call | **Lower** | Draft `f02258e39e`: 10.01 s | 0.22 s |
| Status requests in 60 seconds while Apps is open and a server is still connecting | **Lower** if Apps still shows the result | Old polling schedule: 61 | 21; same schedule for the first 10 s |
| Reusable prefix with a tool added between two requests in the same turn | **Higher** for the same workload | Live tool list: 4,360 matching tokens | Tool list held for the turn: 5,305 matching tokens |
| Total input tokens in request 1 / request 2 in that same cache test | **Lower** if the requests still support the same task | Live tool list: 5,306 / 5,462 | Tool list held for the turn: 5,305 / 5,423 |
| Discovery time for 4,000 synthetic tool definitions through the connector, with no network | **Lower** | Draft `0c367b5a2d`: 36.48 ms | 28.87 ms; same ordered tool definitions |
| Discovery time with an allowlist that selects 40 of the 4,000 definitions | **Lower** | Draft `0c367b5a2d`: 12.85 ms | 6.72 ms; same result |

The healthy-peer test used the same 2.5-second test timeout on both sides. It measures when a tool becomes available, not when a model answers. The reload and reconnect rows are single paired observations. The Apps row uses a virtual clock. The synthetic discovery values are medians of three interleaved batches, not end-to-end latency. The token rows are local estimates, not provider usage or cache hit rate.

</details>

### Verification

- Recovery follow-up (`3022ed495`): cancelling a tool call while its old connection closes no longer stops background recovery. Reload and shutdown drain that cleanup before proceeding. Apps continues polling after ordinary connection failures and reflects recovery without a page refresh.
- This follow-up passed 392 focused Python tests (one Windows-only case skipped on Linux), 20 WebUI component tests, WebUI type checking/build, focused lint, and the Python import-boundary check. A real HTTP MCP fixture verified cancellation, recovery, reload, and shutdown. A real Chromium browser against the built WebUI and an isolated gateway showed a failed stdio MCP recover without refreshing the page. All test MCP children exited. The full CI and native upgrade matrices were not rerun locally.
- The `bc62a8a82` draft passed 266 focused Python tests, the import-boundary check, and Ruff. In a separate real gateway run, a healthy MCP tool returned `pong` while its peer was stalled. A peer configured to delay startup by 12 seconds later connected and returned `pong`. No test MCP child remained after shutdown.

- A real Chromium browser used the authenticated Gateway and the built Apps page. It showed slow startup, recovery, and timeout, and exposed **Reconnect** for the timed-out server.
- The preceding draft passed **403 Python tests**, **347 Python tests with minimum dependencies**, and **19 WebUI tests**. The Python checks cover transport cleanup, hot reload, request formatting, proxy and redirect safeguards, and protected gateway activation. WebUI type checking and build, import boundary checks, and Ruff also passed.
- Earlier real stdio checks verified that a name conflict could not send a tool call to the wrong server. Renaming and reloading restored the tool under the new name. The timeout follow-up did not re-run the full native packaged-upgrade matrix.

## Before this PR

The gateway waits for MCP connection attempts before it starts the agent. Its readiness hook also waits for another attempt before each turn. A configured MCP process that starts but never replies can delay ordinary chat, even when the user does not need an MCP tool. If a process fails quickly, the next message can start it again. Serial discovery also delays other MCP servers.

Keeping chat off the connection path also lets a server finish discovery during a turn. The next model request uses the live tool list. An earlier draft held additions until the next user input to preserve a longer prompt prefix, but that could hide a useful tool for the rest of a long turn.

## How the draft works

1. **Gateway and MCP lifecycle.** The gateway starts one MCP maintenance task after normal startup admission. It gives initial discovery one shared window of up to one second. It does not wait for MCP in each chat, Dream, or heartbeat run. The provider cancels an unfinished startup attempt after 60 seconds and closes its transport before retrying. Failed attempts retry independently of chat after 15, 30, 60, then at most 120 seconds. The delay resets after a successful connection or a configuration change.
2. **Separate discovery from publication.** The connector opens one server and returns one handle for its capabilities and cleanup. It does not write to a tool registry. The provider permits up to four concurrent stdio process launches. The handshake and discovery do not hold a launch slot or the configuration lock. Each configured server has at most one connection attempt, so stalled servers do not delay healthy ones. A failed server does not publish partial tools. OAuth and the WebUI connection test consume the discovery result directly and keep their own deadlines. Each SDK transport still opens and closes in its owning task.
3. **Use live tool definitions during a turn.** Discovery publishes ready tools immediately. The next model request can use them, even for the same user input. Removed tools stop appearing in the next request, and execution still checks the live registry. Built-in tools stay first, and the order stays deterministic when the registry is unchanged. This change does not alter an in-flight model request or trigger an extra one.
4. **Do not redirect a conflicting tool name.** Two server names can generate the same wrapped tool name. The provider removes the ambiguous name rather than replacing its target. It unregisters each tool by object ownership, not a name prefix. An ambiguous name cannot be reassigned during the gateway's lifetime. Non-conflicting names stay unchanged. Rename one server or tool and reload to use its new name.
5. **Report the active connection.** The provider uses the active connection and attempt tables for status. Reload revokes removed or changed connections and cancels obsolete attempts. It can return a pending result while discovery continues, instead of canceling a healthy slow connection. The gateway reports a slow connection after ten seconds without canceling it. The Apps page checks every second during the first ten polls, then every five seconds while open and visible. It continues to check after startup times out or a connection fails so it can show the next attempt.

The gateway owns startup and shutdown. The connector owns the SDK connection and discovery. `MCPProvider` owns routing, publication, and retries. The existing runner reads the live tool list for each request. `AgentLoop`, `AgentRunner`, provider payload formats, OAuth consent, network policy, and rules for replaying tool operations do not change. No new installed dependency, setting, or on-disk cache is added. At `bc62a8a82`, the production diff was **+516 / −641** Python lines and **+61 / −17** WebUI lines against the draft base; test and documentation changes are separate.

### Reuse existing libraries

- The existing `referencing` library resolves JSON Pointers inside the document. nanobot still moves local targets under `$defs` for model compatibility. Resolution does not retrieve files or URLs.
- AnyIO provides stream iteration and context-manager cleanup. A small receive adapter keeps malformed progress notifications out of SDK logs, which can otherwise include the raw payload.
- Tools, resources, and prompts use one loop over the MCP SDK's page requests. The loop checks repeated cursors and completes a list before publishing it. The SDK's session group does not fetch subsequent pages, so this change does not use it for discovery.
- SSE and Streamable HTTP use the same preflight and HTTPX client setup for URL validation, proxy routing and redirects. Each transport keeps its own request headers, timeout settings, and SDK lifecycle.
- Tool results use SDK content types directly. Images and embedded image blobs still become local artifacts. Python's stable list sort preserves the exact built-ins-first tool order without maintaining two intermediate lists.
- Discovery reuses each wrapped tool name for the allowlist, diagnostics, and registration. The allowlist still runs before tool schemas are normalized. The turn-history owner preserves MCP mention metadata directly; its unused WebUI import shim is removed.

## Compatibility and open decisions

- **Background discovery:** The ten-second reload wait limits the response, not the lifetime of discovery. A slow stdio handshake can finish after the reload returns, without changing `toolTimeout`. A startup attempt still running at 60 seconds is canceled. The gateway waits for the connection owner to close its transport, even if shutdown overlaps the timeout. A server that really needs more than 60 seconds to start now times out. Interactive OAuth and explicit connection tests retain their own deadlines.
- **Intentional change for conflicting names:** Older versions could silently replace a tool with another tool under the same name. The draft disables that name instead. The configuration guide explains how to rename and reload. Restart the gateway after removing a conflict if you need to restore the original name. This does not change stored configuration or existing non-conflicting names.
- **Update continuity:** An earlier macOS arm64 run used the published 0.4.1 native wheel and the actual 0.4.1 updater code with an isolated local feed. It completed both jumps to private `0.4.2.dev0` and `0.4.2.dev1` fixtures from this source. In a separate run, an injected restart failure restored 0.4.1, and the restored installation then updated successfully to `0.4.2.dev1`. An MCP process started but never replied on the candidate gateways. Existing chat history, later writes, restart, the next update, and the shutdown of all fixture MCP children passed. This is not public-feed, signature, or all-platform upgrade evidence. No settings schema, stored chat data, install layout, or update protocol changes.

## Related work

This builds on the existing MCP lifecycle owner and readiness recovery from #5343 and #5535. It preserves the transport cleanup ownership addressed by #3640 and the tool replay safeguards from #6537.

Resolves [NAN-450](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-450/mcp-后台连接不阻塞聊天工具就绪后可在当前轮使用).

## Why

The WebUI has a fixed background. This lets people personalize their workbench with an image while keeping the interface readable across their devices.

## What changed

- Add an image picker with preview, removal, blur and background fade controls.
- Store the image and appearance on the gateway, so they persist across restarts and are available to devices using the instance.
- Preserve photo orientation and PNG transparency; support PNG, JPEG and WebP images up to 6 MiB and 32 megapixels.
- Report partial save failures and allow retrying the remaining changes.
- Keep the previously approved appearance and add coverage for storage, settings and affected rendering surfaces.

## Scope and tradeoffs

Images are centered and cropped to cover the window. A theme-colored overlay and adjustable blur help keep text legible. Stylized filters and plugins are out of scope. Settings are designed for normal single-user use; simultaneous edits on separate devices are not conflict-resolved.

Other devices load the latest image and settings after a refresh; no active background notifications are sent. JPEG and WebP uploads are currently normalized to PNG, which can produce substantially larger files.

prs.title: fix(session): replay passive history in native continuations
prs.body:
## Why

Fixes #6678. After an SDK import, the updated supplier quote was present in session history but missing from the next Responses request because native continuation replayed only its saved items and pending turn input. Recorded channel notifications, including Heartbeat deliveries, had the same gap.

## What changed

- Add a session-owned passive-history outbox in the existing private SQLite `pending_inputs` table. Imports and recorded deliveries append canonical history and an independently identified replay batch in one transaction, even before the first native continuation exists.
- Stage a finite snapshot of those batches before the next user input when resuming compatible provider state. Without compatible state, use the normal full-history path. Share the existing canonical message projection for sanitization, tools, and media breadcrumbs.
- Acknowledge captured batch IDs atomically with prepared input and continuation state. Checkpoints and turn completion preserve later arrivals; failed writes retain the outbox. Restart preserves pending batches, reset removes them, and forks/SDK exports do not copy their private bookkeeping.

## Scope

Covers SDK `ingest()`/`restore()` and gateway-recorded passive deliveries. Public APIs and provider wire formats are unchanged; Responses reasoning/compaction payloads remain opaque. Passive deliveries do not start a model run or wait on the active run's lock.

## Tradeoffs

The outbox temporarily stores the appended canonical records, rather than introducing message IDs into public history or depending on mutable history positions. Entries are removed when their replay obligation transfers to prepared input. This avoids a schema migration and keeps the journal independent of runner-owned provider state; clearing native state on every append would discard retained reasoning and compaction.

## Verification

- SDK runs against a purpose-built local HTTP/SSE peer verify actual Responses and Chat Completions request bodies: imports before/after an initial run, identical messages in separate batches, restart, ordering, subsequent turns without duplicate replay, retained native reasoning, and canonical tool/media projection.
- The real gateway delivery path is exercised while the first or a later model request is blocked; its notification survives checkpoints and appears once on the next turn. Interrupted prepared requests and failed-write rollback are covered, along with newer arrivals, fork/reset isolation, and private export boundaries.
- Focused SDK/session/provider/delivery suites: **350 passed, 3 skipped** on Windows.
- Additional agent save/recovery/policy/concurrency/governance/subagent suites: **216 passed**.
- Full-repository Ruff, import-boundary checks, strict BasedPyright on changed production sources, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Full-project CI remains pending. These checks use synthetic responses, not a live provider or external messaging delivery.

Reported by @UnZHGPPT; credited as a co-author.

prs.title: fix: 使用本地时区规则计算 cron 下次运行时间
prs.body:
## Problem

When `CronSchedule.tz` is not set, cron uses the current local UTC offset. This offset does not include daylight-saving rules. A task set for 09:00 can run one hour early or late after a seasonal clock change.

## Change

Use `tzlocal.get_localzone()` to get the local timezone and its rules. This also works when the system has timezone data but no known IANA timezone name.

An explicit `CronSchedule.tz` still has priority. If the system cannot read local timezone rules, keep the previous local-offset behavior. Do not change the schedule to UTC. No new dependency or configuration option is required.

## Validation

- Regression tests cover both directions across a daylight-saving change, an explicit timezone, local rules without an IANA name, and a failure to read local rules.
- The missing-name test reproduced an eight-hour error in the earlier patch. It passes with this change.
- On head `2dade4474f2c8c7dc7c4094591a8959ca40f02f0`, the cron suite and config timezone tests passed: 167 tests on macOS / Python 3.11.
- Ruff, BasedPyright for the changed runtime module, and diff checks passed.
- [CI for this head](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/37132446486) passed on Linux Python 3.11 and 3.14, Windows Python 3.14, Windows process compatibility, and Docker.

Tests use real timezone rules and croniter with an isolated clock. They do not change the host timezone.

prs.title: fix: 禁止关闭的后台日志流重新打开文件
prs.body:
## 问题与修复

`RotatingTextOutput` 继承 `io.TextIOBase`，但 `close()` 或退出上下文管理器后，`write()` 和 `fileno()` 仍会通过 `_ensure_open()` 重新打开日志文件。此时 `closed` 依旧为 `True`，文件却可被创建、追加或轮转，与已关闭文件流的行为不符。

本修改在写入锁内检查关闭状态，并在打开文件前再次检查，阻止关闭后的写入和文件描述符访问；空字符串写入也会正确抛出 `ValueError`。未关闭流的延迟打开和日志轮转逻辑保持不变。

## 复现

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from nanobot.utils.rotating_output import RotatingTextOutput

with TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
    path = Path(folder) / "gateway.log"
    output = RotatingTextOutput(path, max_bytes=8, backup_count=1)
    output.close()
    output.write("after")  # 修复前创建日志并返回 5；修复后抛出 ValueError
```

## 验证

- 新增 6 个用例，覆盖空日志和已有日志，以及关闭后的普通写入、空写入、`fileno()`；检查没有创建、修改或轮转文件，并可再次关闭。
- 旧实现：6 failed、6 passed；修复后：12 passed，包括原有子进程 stdout/stderr 重定向测试。
- 修改文件的 Ruff 检查通过；修改的运行时代码 BasedPyright 检查通过（0 errors、0 warnings）；`git diff --check` 通过。

```text
python -m pytest tests/utils/test_rotating_output.py -q
ruff check nanobot/utils/rotating_output.py tests/utils/test_rotating_output.py
basedpyright nanobot/utils/rotating_output.py
git diff --check
```

验证环境：Windows、Python 3.12.13。未执行包含全部可选渠道依赖的全库检查。

本修复由 Codex 在账号持有者授权下生成，差异检查、复现和测试均由 Codex 执行。

prs.title: fix: 按 token 截断时保留完整 Unicode 字符
prs.body:
## 问题与修复

tokenizer 就绪后，`truncate_text_to_tokens()` 直接解码被截断的 token 序列。汉字或 Emoji 可能跨越多个 token；截断点落在字符内部时，默认解码会生成原文中不存在的替换字符 `�`。

三个 token 前缀解码路径改为忽略末尾不完整的 UTF-8 字节，保留完整字符、截断提示和 token 预算检查。

已合入上游 `main` 的 `5294dc2`，解决与 tokenizer 后台初始化改动的冲突。保留上游的非阻塞加载、`encode_ordinary()` 和 tokenizer 尚未就绪时的 UTF-8 字节预算回退。相对该上游版本仅修改 `nanobot/utils/helpers.py` 和 `tests/utils/test_helpers.py`。

## 验证

- 8 个参数化回归用例覆盖中文、Emoji、混合文本，以及有无截断提示、完整和不完整字符边界。
- 复用上游 `byte_encoding` 夹具，使用真实 `tiktoken.Encoding` 和内存词表，不下载词表，也不依赖后台初始化时序。
- 在最新上游实现上运行上述用例：**5 failed、3 passed**，复现替换字符问题。
- 应用修复后，以下 5 个测试文件合计 **146 passed**，包含 tokenizer 后台加载、离线回退、token 估算、自动压缩和记忆存储测试。
- `ruff check nanobot/` 和修改测试文件的 Ruff 检查通过；`basedpyright nanobot/utils/helpers.py` 为 **0 errors、0 warnings**；`git diff --check` 通过。

```text
python -m pytest tests/utils/test_helpers.py tests/utils/test_token_estimation.py tests/utils/test_token_encoding.py tests/agent/test_autocompact_unit.py tests/agent/test_memory_store.py -q
python -m ruff check nanobot/
python -m ruff check tests/utils/test_helpers.py
python -m basedpyright nanobot/utils/helpers.py
git diff --check
```

prs.title: feat(webui): anchor prompts while replies stream
prs.body:
## Why

Streaming responses currently keep the latest text at the bottom of the viewport, forcing readers to scroll back to find their place. A submitted prompt now starts at the top of the reading area while the answer grows below it.

## What changed

- Animate each newly submitted prompt into place, using the available gap so the preceding reply moves fully out of the scrollport. Respect reduced-motion settings and allow user input to take control.
- Reserve enough scrollable space for short responses without following streamed output or completion to the bottom.
- Retain the prompt's reading position through viewport reflow and canonical message replacement. Observe the natural message list as well as its minimum-height wrapper so lazy Markdown layout cannot silently displace the prompt.
- Preserve explicit navigation, history loading, and session handoff, including settling a reopened transcript if its initial grid layout temporarily exceeds the viewport.
- Consolidate duplicate motion/viewport test setup, exact animation timing and internal-call assertions. Relative to the preceding PR revision, the two unit-test files shrink by 799 lines and their cases go from 114 to 109; canonical handoff, first-send ownership, manual takeover and session-layout branches remain covered. The eight browser cases are retained, with resize and deferred-render regressions folded into existing cases.

## Scope and blast radius

WebUI chat motion only; no gateway protocol or other client changes. The shared thread viewport and history navigation are affected. A temporary minimum content height provides room for short answers and is cleared on conversation handoff.

## Verification

- `bun run test:coverage --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=2`: 210 files and 3,862 tests passed.
- `bun run test src/tests/thread-motion.test.ts src/tests/thread-viewport.test.tsx`: 109 tests passed.
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run check:imports`, and `bun run test:imports`: passed; the import-check tests include 42 cases.
- Production build passed with `bun x tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` and `bun x vite build --outDir <isolated-directory>`, without replacing the retained preview's assets. Vite reported chunk-size warnings.
- `bun run test:browser browser/thread-prompt-anchor.spec.ts --workers=1`: eight Chromium scenarios passed against the real chat components and a synthetic WebSocket. Coverage includes rendered movement, reduced motion, desktop/mobile widths, short/long replies, manual scrolling, bottom navigation, immediate completion, session switching, responsive reflow, and deferred Markdown rendering inside reserved space. The reflow failure was reproduced before the fix; the deferred-render regression also failed before observing the inner message list.
- `bun run test:browser browser/history-hydration.spec.ts --workers=1`: 15 passed, one failed. The Windows touch hydration case still stops at a 109px offset; the same case and offset were previously reproduced on the untouched `d3bb330f57cc297c2a41043be78f3b366965d73b` baseline. This suite is not fully passing.
- Earlier end-to-end verification on the preceding PR revision used an isolated local gateway with Luna and two purpose-generated prompts. That smoke check was not rerun for this geometry/test-only follow-up; the current regressions use the synthetic transport described above.

## CI follow-up

- The animation browser check now advances Playwright's controlled clock instead of requiring a minimum number of native frames within a wall-clock window. Its existing intermediate-position and final-geometry assertions are retained. A 4x CPU-slowdown probe passed, while an instantaneous-jump negative control failed the retained assertion.
- The context-graph 150ms long-task budget is unchanged. The original 183ms CI spike was not reproduced in local baseline/candidate runs or the final CI run; its specific cause remains undetermined.
- [Final-head CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/43841928678) passed: all 587 browser cases, 3,862 unit tests across 210 files, WebUI lint/type/import checks and production build, Docker acceptance, and the required gate. Both previously failing browser cases passed. The checkout logs confirm the current PR head merged with the audited target.

Resolves [NAN-449](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-449/webui发送消息后锚定用户消息流式回复不再自动滚动)

Inspired by https://x.com/MananTank_/status/2122007666835009733

issues.title: ACP session/new / session/load hangs forever on Windows: git version check inherits the ACP stdin pipe

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: area/sessions
labels.description: Session lifecycle, resume, persistence, history

labels.name: os/windows
labels.description: Native Windows behaviour or breakage: PowerShell install, Windows paths, cmd.exe, WSL-vs-native diff

issues.body:
**Summary**
On Windows, when Hermes runs as an ACP agent (`hermes acp`, spawned by a client over stdio), `session/new` and `session/load` never return. `initialize` answers normally in about 1 s. The hang is in the git version lookup that builds the request header while the model catalog is being built.

**Environment**
- Windows 11, Git for Windows
- hermes-agent at commit `081e8d9b75` (Nov 16, 2026), run from a git checkout
- ACP client: OpenMausBot (any stdio ACP client should reproduce it)

**What happens**
1. The client sends `initialize`, and Hermes replies in about 1 s.
2. The client sends `session/new`, and there's no reply, ever.
3. A thread dump shows the worker stuck in `hermes_cli/version_info._run_git`, called from `acp_adapter/model_catalog.build_model_state`.
4. Orphaned `git.exe rev-parse HEAD` processes are left running. The same command finishes in about 0.04 s from a normal shell.

**Cause**
The `subprocess.run(["git", ...])` calls in `_run_git` and in the `git status` check in `_git_version_info` don't set `stdin`, so git inherits the ACP stdio pipe. Hermes always has a read pending on that pipe, which blocks Git for Windows at startup. The `timeout=3` kills only the outer `Git\cmd\git.exe` wrapper. The inner `mingw64\bin\git.exe` stays alive and keeps the stdout and stderr pipes open, so `subprocess.run` never returns.

**Fix**
Give both git calls their own empty stdin:

```diff
--- a/hermes_cli/version_info.py
+++ b/hermes_cli/version_info.py
@@ def _run_git(repo_dir: Path, *args: str) -> str | None:
-            ["git", *args], capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", timeout=3, cwd=str(repo_dir),
+            ["git", *args], capture_output=True, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", timeout=3, cwd=str(repo_dir),
@@ def _git_version_info(repo_dir: Path, *, include_untracked: bool = False) -> VersionInfo:
             capture_output=True,
+            stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
             text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace",
```

After this change, `session/new` returns in about 1 s, and `session/prompt` works with both a local llama.cpp provider and a custom OpenAI-compatible provider.

**Suggestion**
Other helper subprocesses that run while ACP is serving over stdio could hang the same way on Windows. Setting `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` on them by default would prevent it.

issues.body:
## Summary

The `active_pr` respawn guard (`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py::check_respawn_guard`) blocks a **review task** from being re-spawned for up to 24 hours after it is unblocked, because the reviewer's own prior verdict comment references the PR under review — the guard mistakes it for an implementer who "already opened a PR."

Result: a card sits `ready` with no worker (surfaced as a `stranded_in_ready` diagnostic) while the dispatcher logs `respawn_guarded {'reason': 'active_pr'}` on every tick.

## Repro / observed behavior

1. An `aptive-review` task is dispatched from the `ready` lane (status `ready`).
2. Reviewer runs, finds issues, and **blocks** the card, posting a verdict comment that contains a full GitHub PR URL (both the PR link and the posted-review URL, e.g. `https://github.com/org/repo/pull/1234#issuecomment-...`).
3. A human/operator resolves the blockers and **unblocks** the card back to `ready` (status change `unblocked`).
4. Every dispatcher tick from here on: `check_respawn_guard(conn, task_id)` runs with the default `lane="ready"` and hits the `active_pr` rule (line 9309) — a comment within `_RESPAWN_GUARD_PR_WINDOW` (86400s / 24h, line 7886) matches `_RESPAWN_GUARD_PR_URL_RE` (line 7889). The spawn is deferred; the card stays `ready` for up to 24h with no worker.

## Root cause

The `active_pr` rule is meant to prevent a worker from opening a **duplicate PR** on an implement task. It is deliberately skipped in the `review` lane (`if lane == "review": return None`, line 9372) because a PR URL in a comment is the *precondition* of the canonical review handoff — not a duplicate-work signal.

But when review tasks are dispatched from the **`ready` lane** (status `ready`) rather than the `review` lane — which is a common board convention — the guard cannot distinguish:

- "I (implementer) **opened** PR X" (the duplicate-PR signal it should block), from
- "I (reviewer) **reviewed/referenced** PR X" (normal review output).

So any review card that is unblocked within 24h of its reviewer's PR-referencing comment strands in `ready`.

## Suggested fix

The `recent_success` rule already handles the same "explicit re-queue after the signal" case: it is bypassed when an explicit re-queue event (`status`, `promoted`, `unblocked`, `reclaimed`) arrives *after* the completion (lines 9389–9398). Mirror that bypass onto `active_pr`: if an explicit re-queue event occurs after the PR-referencing comment, treat it as a deliberate "run it again" and don't defer. A human dragging a card back to `ready` is an explicit intent signal that the guard should honor.

Alternative/complementary options:
- Skip `active_pr` for tasks whose assignee is a review profile, or when the matching comment was authored by the reviewer profile.
- Distinguish "opened" from "referenced" by checking whether the task actually owns/created the PR (e.g. compare against a stored PR URL on the task) rather than scanning any comment.

## Environment

- hermes-agent `0.20.1` (commit `f80f453ae`)
- Review cards assigned to `aptive-review`, dispatched from `ready` status (not the `review` lane)

issues.body:
## Summary

Add Google **Antigravity** (formerly Project Genie) as a first-class OAuth provider, alongside the existing `openai-codex` and `nous` OAuth plugins. Antigravity currently exposes Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Opus 4.6, and Gemini 3.x/3.6 family models through a Google OAuth flow, and Hermes users are forced to wire it in via an `OpenAI-compatible` bridge script (`agy -p` wrapped in a local HTTP server) which is fragile, loses thinking content, and breaks on long prompts (kernel `ARG_MAX`).

## Why

Antigravity is the most direct way to use the Claude 4.6 + Gemini 3.x line **without burning paid API quota** for free-tier users. The official `agy` CLI (v1.1.11, https://github.com/google/antigravity) handles the OAuth refresh, quota buckets, and a full agent toolset (terminal/web/browser/files) on top of these models. For a Hermes user it's a one-line benefit: free Claude + Gemini 3 models behind a Google login, instead of paying OpenRouter per token.

## Current state of the art (workaround)

Users currently:

1. Install `agy` CLI via `~/.local/bin/agy`
2. Run a personal wrapper script (`~/.hermes/scripts/agy_bridge.py`) that exposes `agy -p` as an OpenAI-compatible HTTP server on `127.0.0.1:8765`
3. Register it in `config.yaml` as a `custom:<name>` provider with `base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8765/v1` and a dummy key

Problems with this pattern:

- **Prompt length limit (~131KB–2MB)**: `agy -p` takes the prompt as a single argv entry. Long contexts hit kernel `ARG_MAX` (`Errno 7 Argument list too long`) and the bridge returns HTTP 500. Even with stdin, `agy` triggers its model picker — the CLI doesn't expose a documented `--prompt-stdin` flag.
- **No thinking-content streaming**: `agy -p` only emits `thinking_tokens` count, not the actual reasoning text. Hermes's `reasoning_content` adapter path is unused.
- **No multi-turn tool-calling**: `agy -p` is single-turn; users who want Hermes's own tool loop have to disable `agy`'s built-in toolset.
- **Hidden OS-level integration**: `agy` runs skills with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`-style semantics by default; without the bridge requiring explicit per-model opt-in (e.g. `:agent` suffix), users may not realize `agy` is executing terminal commands on their machine.

## Proposed implementation

Add a new plugin at `plugins/model-providers/antigravity/` following the `openai-codex` + `qwen-oauth` pattern. Suggested skeleton:

- `plugin.yaml` — declares `auth_methods: [oauth]`, `oauth_flow: device_code` (or browser PKCE if Antigravity supports it), `models: ["Claude Sonnet 4.6", "Claude Opus 4.6", "Gemini 3.6 Flash (High|Medium|Low)", "Gemini 3.5 Flash (High|Medium|Low)", "Gemini 3.1 Pro (High|Low)", "GPT-OSS 120B"]`
- `__init__.py` — model registry + adapter that translates `chat.completions` requests into `agy -p` invocation (or, if upstream exposes a true HTTP endpoint, direct REST). Should emit `reasoning_content` where the CLI exposes it.
- `auth.py` — handles the `agy auth login` → token-pickle capture → refresh path. Token storage should reuse the existing `credential_pool` infrastructure (`hermes auth add` / `hermes auth list` already shows provider prefixes).
- `README.md` — `hermes auth add antigravity` → device-code flow → ready.

Implementation note: since `agy` is the official entry point and ships its own OAuth/cache, the cleanest first cut is to **reuse the existing CLI as a subprocess** rather than reimplementing the OAuth + quota dance. The plugin's `auth` step would just shell out to `agy auth login` and reuse `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/antigravity-oauth-token` (already auto-refreshed by `agy`). Long prompts should be passed via stdin (or a `--file` flag if upstream adds one); today `agy` does not accept stdin when `-p` is empty, so an upstream issue/PR may be needed too.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `hermes auth add antigravity` launches a browser/PKCE flow and stores a refreshable token in the credential pool
- [ ] `hermes auth list` shows `antigravity (1 credential)` alongside `anthropic` / `gemini` / `openai-codex`
- [ ] `/model --provider antigravity claude-sonnet-4-6` switches seamlessly; `/model` autocomplete shows the Antigravity model list
- [ ] Long prompts (>200KB) succeed without `ARG_MAX` errors
- [ ] Per-model opt-in for agentic tool execution (since `agy` runs terminal/web/browser by default)

## Willing to help

Happy to open a PR with the plugin skeleton + a parallel `agy-bridge` reference plugin (the existing wrapper pattern), and to maintain the long-prompt stdin workaround if upstream accepts an upstream PR. Looking for maintainer guidance on:

1. **Approach**: subprocess to `agy` (faster, defers to upstream) vs. **direct OAuth** (more work, no subprocess dependency)
2. **Provider name**: `antigravity` vs `google-antigravity` vs `agy` — what's the user-facing convention
3. **Tool permissions**: how to surface the `:agent` / `:plain` model-suffix pattern (or equivalent) so the agent-mode opt-in is explicit, not default

Refs: Antigravity CLI v1.1.11 (current at `~/.local/bin/agy`); current unofficial bridge at `~/.hermes/scripts/agy_bridge.py` on user systems.

issues.body:
## Feature Description
Add a user-facing option to hide the persistent “Use of Hermes Agent is subject to our Terms of Service and Privacy Policy” footer in Hermes Desktop.

## Motivation
The footer sits below the chat composer and permanently consumes vertical space. It is distracting and wastes room, especially in a compact window. Users should be able to dismiss it or disable it in settings.

## Proposed Solution
Provide a setting to hide the notice, ideally persisted across restarts. Keep links to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy accessible elsewhere (for example, About or Settings).

## Context
The current desktop implementation registers this as a persistent, non-closeable butterbar for free-tier users (`apps/desktop/src/app/shell/terms-butterbar.tsx`). There does not appear to be a config setting to turn it off.

`plugin-catalog/web-oxylabs.yaml` (added in 5d59366, "feat(plugin-catalog): add
66 community plugins from the Discord #plugins-skills-and-skins sweep"):

    name: web-oxylabs
    repo: https://github.com/oxylabs/hermes-web-oxylabs
    sha: e6a5ee8fbabae43a7cd7f77610f187dbc890e76a
    tier: community

Both the repository and the commit return 404, so the entry cannot be installed.

Checked 2026-10-25:

    GET /repos/oxylabs/hermes-web-oxylabs                                              -> 404
    GET /repos/oxylabs/hermes-web-oxylabs/commits/e6a5ee8fbabae43a7cd7f77610f187dbc890e76a -> 404

    $ git ls-remote https://github.com/oxylabs/hermes-web-oxylabs
    remote: Repository not found.
    fatal: repository 'https://github.com/oxylabs/hermes-web-oxylabs/' not found

A search for repositories owned by `oxylabs` with "hermes" in the name returns
zero results. The organisation does have public repositories (for example
`oxylabs-mcp`, `oxylabs-agent-browser-mcp`), so this looks like the plugin was
renamed, never published, or created privately, and the catalog kept a pin that
no longer resolves.

The listing itself is otherwise complete and well-formed: `entry_from_mapping`
accepts it, it survives `load_catalog()`, and every other field is filled in.
Only the source is unreachable.

Suggested change, either one is fine:

* point `repo` and `sha` at the public source of the plugin, if it exists under
  a different name;
* or drop the entry until it does, so `hermes plugins install web-oxylabs` fails
  with "not in the catalog" instead of a clone error.

I have not opened a pull request for this. Say which way you prefer and I will
send it.

Simin Yuan

issues.body:
### What happens
A gateway turn can settle as `completed` while leaving **no trace in the session store**: no `sessions` row for its session id and no `messages` rows, so the turn is invisible in every list, cannot be resumed, and its reply exists only in the delivery that was sent.

The turn's durable admission result is present and claims the agent wrote the transcript itself:

```sql
select value from state_meta where key = 'gateway.admission.result.v1.<admission_id>';
-- {"result": {"agent_persisted": true, "messages": [], "api_calls": 40, "completed": true,
--             "final_response": "<2407 chars>", ...}}
```

and `gateway.terminal_admission.v1.<admission_id>` holds `outcome: completed`. Yet:

```sql
select count(*) from sessions where id = '<session_id>';   -- 0
select count(*) from messages where session_id = '<session_id>';  -- 0
```

### What the turn was
A webhook-triggered agent run (a route in `~/.hermes/webhook_subscriptions.json`, `chat_type: webhook`, delivering the reply to a chat platform) that ran ~8 minutes and 40 API calls and produced a 2407-character reply. The delivery obligation row for the reply exists (`delivery_obligations`, `state: delivered`), and the legacy routing mirror (`~/.hermes/sessions/sessions.json`, written from `gateway_routing`) still has the session key with `session_id`, `display_name: webhook/<route>`, `platform: webhook`, `chat_type: webhook`. The session itself is gone from `state.db`.

Two things were logged for the same settlement, seconds apart:

```
ERROR gateway.session_settlement_recovery: Settlement or publication of admission <id> failed: TypeError: FooteredReply.__new__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'footer'
INFO  gateway.platforms.base: [Webhook] Sending response (2445 chars) to webhook:v2:...
```

(The `FooteredReply` deepcopy failure is reported separately — see the issue “Runtime footer: FooteredReply cannot be deep-copied”.)

### Hypothesis (not yet isolated)
`gateway/run_turn_persistence.py` skips the gateway's own transcript write when the turn result says the agent already persisted its rows:

```python
agent_persisted = agent_result.get("agent_persisted", self._session_db is not None)
...
# "The agent already persisted these messages to SQLite via _flush_messages_to_session_db(), so skip
#  the DB write here to prevent the duplicate-write bug (#860 / #42039)."
```

When the agent reports `agent_persisted: true` but its own flush wrote nothing for that session (the comment at the same site mentions exactly this failure mode: a no-handle turn whose flush silently no-ops, “dropping the turn from state.db entirely”, #140823), the gateway trusts the flag, writes nothing, and the turn disappears. The empty `messages: []` in the result is consistent with “the turn suffix was intentionally not captured because the agent claimed to have persisted it”.

### Requested
1. A guard that makes the trust explicit and checkable: after a turn reports `agent_persisted: true`, verify the session has at least one row for this turn (or persist anyway when the session row is missing), so a no-op flush cannot silently drop the turn.
2. If the settlement error above can also abort the transcript write in some orderings, that ordering is worth a test.

### Minimal repro to try
On a gateway with `display.runtime_footer.enabled: true`, POST a signed event to a webhook route that delivers to a chat platform, wait for the delivery, then compare `state_meta` (`agent_persisted: true`, non-empty `final_response`) with `select count(*) from messages where session_id = '<the session id from sessions.json>'`. Expected 0 (bug), expected > 0 (fixed).

### Environment
- hermes-agent HEAD of 2026-11-16, Python 3.14, Linux.
- SQLite state at `~/.hermes/state.db` (WAL), gateway serving several profiles.

issues.body:
### What happens
With `display.runtime_footer.enabled: true`, a settled turn's completion frame cannot be published. `SessionEventStream.publish` deep-copies its payload while holding the stream lock (`gateway/session_events.py`, the `'payload': deepcopy(payload)` line), and the reply it carries is a `FooteredReply` — a `str` subclass whose `__new__` takes a second argument (`gateway/runtime_footer.py`):

```python
class FooteredReply(str):
    runtime_footer: str
    def __new__(cls, text: str, footer: str):
        instance = super().__new__(cls, f"{text}\n\n{footer}")
        instance.runtime_footer = footer
        return instance
```

`copy.deepcopy` on an instance of a `str` subclass goes through `copyreg.__newobj__` → `cls.__new__(cls)`, which is missing the required `footer` positional argument.

### Minimal repro (no gateway, no network)
```python
import copy
from gateway.runtime_footer import FooteredReply

reply = FooteredReply("hello", "model · 1% · ~/project")
copy.deepcopy({"payload": {"response": reply}})
```
```
TypeError: FooteredReply.__new__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'footer'
```

### Observed behaviour
`gateway/session_settlement_recovery.commit_and_publish()` calls `_publish_completion()` after `finish_result()` has committed the turn, so the commit lands but the live completion frame for that session never reaches any viewer (TUI, desktop, mobile), and the settlement is logged as a failure:

```
ERROR gateway.session_settlement_recovery: Settlement or publication of admission <id> failed: TypeError: FooteredReply.__new__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'footer'
```

Seen twice in a row on webhook-triggered turns whose reply carried the runtime footer (route delivering to a chat platform). Other turns on the same gateway did not log it.

### Expected
Publishing a settled turn must not depend on the payload being copyable; a reply that happens to be a `str` subclass should publish like any other reply.

### Suggested fix (one of)
- Give `FooteredReply` a reduction, e.g.
  ```python
  def __reduce__(self):
      text = str(self)[: -len(self.runtime_footer) - 2]
      return (FooteredReply, (text, self.runtime_footer))
  ```
  (`__getnewargs__` alone is not enough — `str` subclass state also needs the attribute restored.)
- Or stop deep-copying the payload in `session_events.publish` for values that are already immutable strings, or copy the response to a plain `str` in `completion_payload()`.

### Environment
- hermes-agent HEAD of 2026-11-16 (installed via `hermes update`), Python 3.14.
- `display.runtime_footer.enabled: true` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`.
- Local mitigation available to operators: `display.platforms.<platform>.runtime_footer.enabled: false`.

issues.title: Feature: /microcompact — Instant, LLM-Free Surgical Context Stripping (inspired by vicnaum's Claude Code RE)

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: comp/cli

labels.name: P3

labels.name: area/compression
labels.description: Context compression and continuation sessions

issues.body:
## Overview

Inspired by [@vicnaum's reverse-engineering of Claude Code](https://x.com/vicnaum/status/2029579972688379928) to add surgical context management, this proposes a new `/microcompact` command for Hermes Agent. It surgically removes heavy context artifacts — tool call/result pairs AND reasoning/thinking blocks — from conversation history **without LLM summarization**. Instant, free, and lossless for actual conversational content.

The core insight from vicnaum's work: when context fills up, the current options (`/compress` for LLM summarization, `/clear` for nuclear reset) are too coarse. Context is often 70-90% tool call/result pairs and thinking blocks — stripping these selectively can recover enormous context space while preserving every actual user/assistant message exchange intact. As one commenter put it: "/compact is a grenade. This is a scalpel."

This complements the existing automatic compression system (#513, #499, #415) by giving users a **manual, surgical** option when they want precise control.

---

## Research Findings

### How Claude Code's Context Management Works

Claude Code uses a three-layer system, revealed through vicnaum's reverse engineering:

**Layer 1 — microcompact (silent, every turn):** Runs silently before each API call. Replaces OLD tool_result content with placeholder text like `[Previous: used {tool_name}]`. Only targets results > 100 chars. Keeps a "hot tail" of the N most recent tool results intact. Never removes `tool_use` blocks themselves.

**Layer 2 — auto-compact (threshold triggered):** At ~75-95% context capacity, runs full LLM summarization. Saves full transcript to `.transcripts/` before replacing. Structured summary replaces entire history.

**Layer 3 — /compact (user triggered):** Manual LLM summarization with optional focus hints.

Vicnaum identified the gap: even after Layer 1 runs, tons of tool artifacts remain. Thinking blocks inside messages with tool_use survive all cleanup. So he built `/microcompact` and `/clear-thinking` — instant commands with no LLM calls that surgically strip these artifacts.

### Key Design Decisions

1. **Surgical over summarization** — Stripping artifacts is lossless for conversational content. LLM summarization always loses detail and costs an API call.

2. **User-controlled scope** — A picker UI lets users choose how far back to strip, rather than all-or-nothing. This preserves recent tool results that may still be relevant.

3. **Prompt caching consideration** — Stripping elements from the message array destroys prompt cache prefixes. This is a real tradeoff: you save context space but may increase costs on the next API call due to cache miss. However, when you're at 90%+ context, the alternative (full compaction) destroys the cache anyway.

### Anthropic's Server-Side Context Editing API

Anthropic has released a server-side [Context Editing API](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/context-management) (beta) that handles this at the API level. See #526 for integration details. The server-side approach preserves prompt cache (edits applied after cache lookup). Anthropic reports 29-39% performance improvement. That issue covers the Anthropic-specific server-side approach; this issue covers the universal client-side approach that works with ALL models.

---

## Current State in Hermes Agent

### What We Have

1. **`/compress` command** (cli.py, gateway/run.py) — LLM-based summarization. Protects first 3 + last 4 messages, summarizes middle turns using auxiliary model (Gemini Flash). Costs an API call, loses detail.

2. **Automatic compression** (run_agent.py) — Triggers at 85% context capacity. Same LLM summarization as `/compress`. Also triggers on 413 context-length errors.

3. **100K char hard cap** on tool results (run_agent.py L2606) — Only caps individual results at insertion time.

4. **Reasoning storage** — Reasoning/thinking text stored in `msg["reasoning"]` field. `reasoning_details` preserved for multi-turn continuity. When building API messages, `reasoning` is converted to `reasoning_content` for API compatibility.

### What's Missing (the Gap)

- **No selective stripping** — Can't remove specific message types (tool artifacts, thinking) without full summarization
- **No instant cleanup option** — Every cleanup path requires an LLM call or nuclear reset
- **No thinking block management** — Thinking blocks accumulate across turns with no cleanup mechanism

### Related Open Issues

- **#513** — Two-Phase Context Management (automatic tool output pruning before compaction). Complementary: #513 is automatic, this is user-initiated.
- **#499** — Context Compaction Quality Overhaul (better summarization prompts). Complementary: improves the LLM path, this adds a non-LLM path.
- **#415** — Insertion-Time Tool Result Trimming (head+tail trimming at insertion). Complementary: trims at insertion, this removes retroactively.
- **#526** — Anthropic Context Editing API (server-side, Claude-only). Complementary: server-side automatic approach vs this client-side manual approach.

---

## Implementation Plan

### Skill vs. Tool Classification

This should be a **core codebase change**, not a skill or tool. Reasons:
- It modifies the conversation message array directly, requiring access to internal state (`conversation_history`, session transcripts)
- It needs integration with the CLI command system and gateway command dispatch
- It must coordinate with the existing compression system
- It's a fundamental context management capability, same layer as `/compress`

### The Command: `/microcompact`

A single command that strips BOTH tool artifacts AND thinking/reasoning blocks. One command, one action — no unnecessary complexity.

**Usage:**
```
/microcompact        # Strip all tool artifacts + thinking, keep last 3 turns intact
/microcompact 5      # Keep last 5 turns intact
/microcompact 0      # Strip everything (aggressive)
```

### What We'd Need

1. **`microcompact()` function** in `run_agent.py` or a new `context_stripper.py`:

```python
def microcompact(messages: list[dict], keep_last_n: int = 3) -> list[dict]:
    """Surgically strip tool call/result pairs and thinking blocks
    from all but the last N assistant turns. Preserves all actual
    user/assistant text content."""
    
    # Find assistant messages with tool_calls (these are the "turns" to count)
    tool_turns = [(i, m) for i, m in enumerate(messages)
                  if m.get("role") == "assistant" and m.get("tool_calls")]
    
    # Determine which turns to strip (all except last N)
    turns_to_strip = tool_turns[:-keep_last_n] if keep_last_n else tool_turns
    
    # Collect tool_call_ids to remove
    strip_call_ids = set()
    for idx, msg in turns_to_strip:
        for tc in msg.get("tool_calls", []):
            strip_call_ids.add(tc["id"])
        # Remove tool_calls from the assistant message
        del msg["tool_calls"]
        # If the message has no content left, mark for removal
    
    # Remove corresponding tool result messages
    messages = [m for m in messages
                if not (m.get("role") == "tool" and 
                        m.get("tool_call_id") in strip_call_ids)]
    
    # Remove empty assistant messages (had only tool_calls, no text content)
    messages = [m for m in messages
                if not (m.get("role") == "assistant" and 
                        not m.get("content", "").strip() and
                        not m.get("tool_calls"))]
    
    # Strip thinking/reasoning from all but last N assistant messages
    assistant_msgs = [m for m in messages if m.get("role") == "assistant"]
    for msg in assistant_msgs[:-keep_last_n] if keep_last_n else assistant_msgs:
        msg.pop("reasoning", None)
        msg.pop("reasoning_content", None)
        msg.pop("reasoning_details", None)
        msg.pop("codex_reasoning_items", None)
    
    return messages
```

2. **CLI command** in `cli.py`:
   - Register `/microcompact` in the COMMANDS dict
   - Handler: parse optional N argument, call `microcompact()`, report savings

3. **Gateway command** in `gateway/run.py`:
   - Add `microcompact` to known commands
   - Handler mirrors `/compress` pattern: load transcript, strip, rewrite

4. **Session transcript rewrite** — After stripping, rewrite using `rewrite_transcript()` (same as `/compress` uses)

### Phased Rollout

**Phase 1: The Command**
- Implement `microcompact()` stripping function
- Add `/microcompact [N]` to CLI and gateway
- Report before/after token estimates and message counts
- Default: keep last 3 turns intact

**Phase 2: Automatic Integration**
- Integrate with #513's two-phase approach — use `microcompact()` as Phase 1 pruner before LLM compaction
- Add config option for automatic microcompact (e.g., run before every `/compress`)
- Config: `microcompact.keep_last_n: 3` default

**Phase 3: Smart Defaults**
- Auto-run microcompact before LLM compaction kicks in (saves the LLM call when stripping alone frees enough space)
- Per-provider optimization: use Anthropic's server-side Context Editing API when available (#526)
- Token savings telemetry

---

## Technical Details

### Message Structure Reference

```python
# Assistant message with tool call + thinking
{"role": "assistant", "content": "", "reasoning": "...(thinking)...",
 "reasoning_details": [...],
 "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_abc", "function": {"name": "terminal", "arguments": "{...}"}}],
 "finish_reason": "tool_calls"}

# Tool result message  
{"role": "tool", "content": "...(potentially huge output)...", "tool_call_id": "call_abc"}

# Assistant message with actual text content
{"role": "assistant", "content": "Here's what I found...", "reasoning": "...",
 "finish_reason": "stop"}
```

### Orphan Prevention

When stripping tool_calls from an assistant message:
- If the message also has `content` text → keep the message, only remove `tool_calls`
- If the message has NO content (purely a tool-calling turn) → remove the entire message
- Always remove the corresponding `role: "tool"` result messages
- This prevents orphaned tool_call_id references

### What Gets Stripped vs Preserved

| Component | Stripped? | Notes |
|-----------|----------|-------|
| `tool_calls` on assistant msgs | ✅ Yes (except last N turns) | The tool invocation metadata |
| `role: "tool"` result msgs | ✅ Yes (matching stripped calls) | The heavy tool output content |
| `reasoning` field | ✅ Yes (except last N turns) | Thinking/reasoning text |
| `reasoning_details` | ✅ Yes (except last N turns) | Opaque provider reasoning state |
| `reasoning_content` | ✅ Yes (except last N turns) | API-format reasoning |
| User messages | ❌ Never | All user text preserved |
| Assistant `content` text | ❌ Never | All assistant text preserved |
| System messages | ❌ Never | System prompt untouched |

---

## Pros & Cons

### Pros
- **Instant and free** — No LLM call, no API cost, sub-second execution
- **Lossless for conversation** — Every actual user/assistant text message preserved
- **Massive space recovery** — Tool results are typically 60-80% of context. Thinking blocks 10-20%. Combined: 70-90% recovery.
- **Dead simple** — One command, one function, ~50 lines of core logic
- **Universal** — Works with any model/provider
- **Interpretable** — Single command name, obvious behavior, clear output

### Cons / Risks
- **Prompt cache invalidation** — Modifying the message array destroys cached prefixes. Same tradeoff as `/compress`.
- **Loss of tool context** — Model loses knowledge of old tool results. May re-run tools. Mitigated by keeping last N turns.
- **Reasoning continuity** — Stripping `reasoning_details` may break multi-turn reasoning chains on providers using opaque reasoning state. Mitigated by keeping last N turns' reasoning.

---

## Open Questions

1. **Default keep count** — Keep last 3 turns? 5? Claude Code defaults to 3.
2. **Should `/compress` auto-microcompact first?** — Before LLM summarization, strip artifacts for free. Relates to #513.
3. **Token counting** — Show exact counts or rough estimates (4 chars/token)?

---

## References

- [@vicnaum's Twitter thread](https://x.com/vicnaum/status/2029579972688379928) — Reverse-engineering Claude Code to add surgical context management
- [bun-demincer](https://github.com/vicnaum/bun-demincer) — Toolkit for reverse-engineering Bun-compiled binaries
- [Anthropic Context Editing API](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/context-management) — Server-side approach (see #526)
- Related issues: #513, #499, #415, #526

labels.name: area/billing

issues.body:
The voice route itself makes sense (faster replies to voice notes). This is about a cost side effect on
native Anthropic that is easy to miss.

**Version:** v0.22.2 (Docker). Same code on `main` today (`agent/voice_turn_route.py`, `auxiliary.voice_chat` default).
**Provider:** native Anthropic (`provider: anthropic`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`), `prompt_caching.cache_ttl: "1h"`, messaging gateway (WhatsApp).

#### What happens

With the default `auxiliary.voice_chat.reasoning_effort: "none"`, a voice-note turn is sent with
`thinking: {"type": "between_tools"}` and no `output_config`, while text turns send
`thinking: {"type": "adaptive", ...}` + `output_config.effort`. Anthropic namespaces the prompt cache by
the thinking configuration, so the two kinds of turn never share cache entries.

`voice_turn_route.py` undoes the route "before post-turn work (memory sync, background review)". So the
background-review fork that runs right after a voice turn is built with the session's normal
`reasoning_config` (adaptive). If the recent turns were voice notes, nothing exists in the adaptive
namespace and the fork rewrites the full prefix:

```
00:24:12 API call #1 (voice turn)  in=56786 cache=55861 write=921
00:24:16 API call #1 (bg-review)   in=57661 cache=0     write=57657   <- full miss (~0.23 USD on Sonnet, 1h TTL)
00:24:18 API call #2 (bg-review)   in=58307 cache=57657 write=648
```

Second, smaller effect: every switch between voice and text turns in the same chat rewrites everything after
the last cache entry of the other namespace, because the main turn itself changes namespace:

```
01:15:17 text turn   cache=69125/69348
01:18:27 voice turn  cache=56782/70021 write=13235   <- read the voice-namespace entry from 00:24, not the text one
```

#### How we confirmed it

`HERMES_DUMP_REQUESTS=1` on the gateway: system blocks, `tools[]`, messages and `cache_control` (all
`ttl: 1h`) were byte-identical between the main request and the fork; the only difference was
`thinking` / `output_config` on voice turns. After text turns, `/refine` and the automatic nudge both read
the cache correctly (98–99 %). Outside the gateway (direct `AIAgent` + fork, text turns only) the fork
also reads the cache correctly; the miss only appears when the parent's last turn ran on the voice route.

#### Workaround

```yaml
auxiliary:
  voice_chat:
    reasoning_effort: ""   # no voice route: voice turns keep the session's thinking
```

**Suggested fix:** like #30531, build the review fork with the `thinking`/`reasoning_config` the parent's
last outbound request actually used, not the session default.

Related, fixed: #30531 (fork `thinking` mismatch), #103579 (fork tools[] parity).

issues.body:
## Bug Description

Bot Mode group chat rooms disappear from the Bots roster after a gateway restart and do not come back on desktop relaunch. Observed on two rooms across two incidents. Transcripts and per-member room sessions remain intact in the session store — only the room record/mirror is lost, so the rooms become unreachable from the UI.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a Bot Mode group chat (3 local bots), exchange several rounds.
2. Restart the gateway (`hermes gateway restart`, or let an update/reboot restart it).
3. Reopen the desktop (or keep it open and reconnect).
4. Observe: the group row is gone from the Bots roster.

## Expected Behavior

Per the Bot Mode docs ("Rooms follow your gateways, not one Desktop" — every connected Desktop keeps the full room locally and re-seeds any gateway it reconnects to), the room should reappear with its history after a gateway restart.

## Actual Behavior

- Room rows vanish from the roster (two rooms, two restarts: machine reboot via Windows Update on 11-13; gateway restart on 11-17).
- `hosted_rooms` and `hosted_room_events` in shared-state.db / state.db are EMPTY (0 rows) after the restart — the shared mirror is gone.
- The desktop's Local Storage also loses the room records entirely: room UUIDs no longer appear anywhere under `%APPDATA%\Hermes` (on the first incident the UUID was still present in leveldb workspace-layout data; after the second it is absent everywhere).
- One room once spontaneously reappeared after a later desktop relaunch (re-seed works sometimes), then vanished again after the next gateway restart.
- Per-member room sessions in each profile's state.db keep full transcripts (e.g. 51/22/24 messages across three members; sessions un-archived, hidden=1). **No message data is lost — only visibility.**
- Related symptom: in-flight turns are dropped when the client restarts (room sessions picked up `end_reason=startup_orphan_reap` in one incident); running task conversations survive in the store but their active turn is lost.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 (native install)
- Hermes Desktop + gateway, code_version 0.23.1 (code_sha b7db40d82568ea68ce321ac1ead3bfea354c7f56)
- Multiple profiles (default + several named), Bot Mode group with 2–6 local bot members

## Error Output

No crash or error logged at disappearance time; gateway_state.json shows `gateway_state: running` and the gateway continues serving other sessions normally.

## Additional Context

- Possible related state: a profile carrying leftover platform env vars created a persistent `"<profile>:weixin": "fatal"` platform entry in gateway_state.json which survived until the env vars were removed and the gateway restarted. One room loss happened while this fatal entry was present (may be coincidental).
- Workarounds in use: persist room conclusions to files immediately; recreate rooms when lost (fresh room; old history remains in the session stores and is exportable).
- Happy to provide DB snapshots, leveldb dumps, or further logs on request.

issues.body:
### Summary
When the first keyless vendor is unreachable at the network level, `web_search` returns the error instead of trying the next vendor in the ring. Failover only happens for rate limits and HTTP 401/402/403/5xx. A vendor that cannot be reached at all is the clearest case where another vendor may still serve the request.

### Where
`plugins/web/keyless_mcp.py` (v0.23.1, commit 3b42157858; same code on `main`):
- `mcp_call` turns `requests.RequestException` into `KeylessMCPError("request failed: ...")`.
- `_is_search_failover_eligible` only accepts rate-limit markers or `_VENDOR_REFUSAL_RE` (`40[123]|5\d\d`), so `request failed: HTTPSConnectionPool ... Failed to resolve ...` is terminal.
- `_walk_ring` therefore stops at the first vendor.
- `extract_with_failover` has the same gap (`_throttled` only checks `_is_rate_limitish`).

### Repro (no network needed)
Patch `requests.post` to raise `requests.ConnectionError`, force the ring order to `["exa", "parallel"]`, stub the parallel searcher to succeed, then call `search_with_failover("exa", "q", 1)`.

- Expected: success with `data.served_by == "parallel"`.
- Actual: `success: false`, `Keyless Exa search failed: request failed: ...`.

Found by reading the code and reproduced with the in-process simulation above on Windows 11; not reproduced with a real outage.

### Suggested fix
Classify by exception type, not by message text: if the exception or its `__cause__` chain is `requests.ConnectionError` / `requests.Timeout` / `httpx.TransportError` / builtin `ConnectionError` / `TimeoutError`, tag the error with a prefix produced by Hermes itself and accept that prefix (anchored at the start) in `_is_search_failover_eligible` and in the extract `_throttled`. A malformed query (HTTP 400) must keep stopping the walk.

A local patch along these lines keeps the existing tests in `tests/tools/test_web_keyless_fallback.py`, `test_web_keyless_rescue.py` and `tests/plugins/web` green.

Related but different causes: #91609 / #113893 (403), #146853 and #99500 (throttle not shaped as an error).

issues.title: [Mobile] Markdown images and MEDIA attachments render at the end of the message instead of in place

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
## Summary

In the Hermes mobile app, images referenced in a reply are always rendered **after all the text**, regardless of where they appear in the message. This applies to both `MEDIA:` local attachments and standard markdown block images. Author order is lost, so an image that is meant to explain the paragraph above it ends up at the bottom of the bubble.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have the gateway send a reply whose body contains an image between two paragraphs, e.g.:

   ```
   Paragraph A — points at the diagram below.

   ![topology](https://example.com/topology.png)

   Paragraph B — continues the explanation.
   ```

2. The image URL is publicly reachable: verified `HTTP 200`, `Content-Type: image/png`, ~298 KB.
3. Open the chat in the Hermes mobile app (TestFlight beta build) on iOS.
4. Also reproducible with a local attachment: put `MEDIA:/path/to/image.png` inside the text instead of the markdown tag.

## Expected

The image renders between paragraph A and paragraph B, preserving the author's ordering.

## Actual

The image is extracted from the body and rendered at the end of the message bubble. Two different mechanisms produce the same result:

- `MEDIA:<path>` → stripped from text, delivered as an attachment after the text.
- `![alt](https://…)` → rendered, but hoisted below all paragraphs.

Screenshot: text shows "Paragraph A" → "Paragraph B" → image at the bottom.

## Why this matters

Architecture diagrams, screenshots and charts are usually referenced mid-explanation. With the image pinned to the end, the reader has to scroll down and back up to map the image to the sentence describing it. Splitting the reply into several messages is not a workaround: `hermes send` has no target for the mobile session, so it can only post to platform channels (Feishu/Telegram/etc.), not into the app conversation.

## Environment

- Client: Hermes Agent mobile app, TestFlight beta build, iOS.
- Gateway: hermes-agent v0.23.0, macOS host.
- Image serving: static file over HTTPS via a Cloudflare tunnel (correct MIME type confirmed).
- The same markdown renders correctly in other clients, so this looks specific to the mobile renderer's block ordering rather than to the gateway's message payload.

## Suggested direction

Keep image blocks in the parsed markdown/AST position when composing the rendered message instead of collecting them into a trailing attachment list. If `MEDIA:` must stay a trailing attachment (platform constraint), at least let markdown images preserve inline position.

prs.title: fix(computer_use): close a session's cua-driver after the Bot Desktop idle window
prs.body:
## What this fixes

`computer_use` keeps one cua-driver per Hermes session (`tools/computer_use/tool.py`, `_backends`), and closes it only when the session ends: `release_computer_use_session`, reached from session reset, `/new` or process exit. Agent-cache eviction keeps it on purpose so a resumed session finds its driver (`run_agent.py`, `release_clients` with `close_computer_use=False`).

On the gateway host that costs one idle process. When the Bot Desktop runs **inside the terminal backend** (placement `terminal`: a Docker, SSH or plugin sandbox with `supports_streams`), the driver is a remote exec stream (`sandbox_host.cua_mcp_invocation` → the backend's `exec_prefix`). Sandboxes that pause when nothing is connected treat an open exec stream as activity. On Sprites this is measured: a Sprite with one open exec stream stayed `running` for the whole 90 s sample, while the same Sprite with nothing open paused after its idle timeout. So after a single `computer_use` call the sandbox stays awake and billed for as long as the session lives, which on a messaging gateway can be days. Sprites now supports this placement through [hermes-plugin-sprites#15](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-plugin-sprites/pull/15), which is what turned this up.

## The change

A backend unused for its profile's `bot_desktop.idle_stop_minutes` (default 30, `0` = never) is released by a process-wide sweep every 60 s, and the next call starts a fresh one. This is the same window, and the same "comes back on next use" contract, as the Bot Screen itself. No new setting.

- **Profile scope:** the window is read when the backend is installed, inside the calling profile's scope, and stored with it. The sweep runs outside any profile and applies each backend's own window, so a gateway serving several profiles applies each profile's setting rather than the launch profile's.
- **Races:** a backend whose call lock is held is in use, however long that call has run, and is skipped. Otherwise the next call could start a second driver for the same session while the first action still runs. Once the sweep holds the lock it checks again that the backend is still cached and still idle before detaching it. A call queued behind it re-admits onto a new backend (`_backend_for_call` already rechecks after taking the lock).
- **Teardown scope:** the driver's `stop()` rebuilds its child environment from profile state, and the sweep runs outside any profile. So each backend's stop runs in the context its install ran in.
- **Activity:** each admission and each finished call restart the window.
- **What is lost on release:** the driver's per-session state (element indexes, last focused app). After 30 idle minutes the screen has to be captured again anyway.

Docs: `bot-screen.md` (idle paragraph and the config example) and the `idle_stop_minutes` comment in `config_defaults.py`.

## Tests

`tests/tools/test_computer_use_idle_release.py` drives real dispatch through `registry.dispatch` with only the device boundary faked:
- an unused backend is released after the window, and the next call gets a new one
- each call restarts the window
- two profiles with different windows (0 and 1 minute) are each judged by their own
- a call running past the window keeps its backend
- teardown sees the owning profile

I checked that the tests can fail. Each of these mutants fails its own test: no refresh on use; the sweep reading the launch profile's window; a blocking lock acquire; teardown outside the owning context.

`scripts/check`: 21 checks pass. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/ -k 'computer_use or bot_desktop or cua'` gives the same 33 failures and errors with and without this change. They are environmental on my host and happen on unmodified `main` too.

## Infographic

![idle-driver-release](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab2cbb5/yVfq1bXkoE1Nu_SDJhBXt_sEq1XiDe.png)

prs.title: fix(agent): preserve OpenRouter reasoning through proxy URLs
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Keeps the configured reasoning effort when the built-in `openrouter` provider uses a proxy URL. `_supports_reasoning_extra_body()` currently returns `False` for an unclaimed non-OpenRouter host before reaching the existing model capability check, even though the selected provider profile builds OpenRouter requests.

Let an explicitly selected `openrouter` provider reach that same capability check. A definitive negative catalog result still omits the reasoning field; an unknown model still uses the existing static fallback. Unknown custom endpoints, endpoint-profile precedence and the Mistral-host exclusion are unchanged. This does not change credential selection or send keys to a different endpoint.

## Related Issue

Fixes #156806

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/reasoning_params.py`: recognize the named OpenRouter provider as well as its standard host at the existing gate.
- `tests/agent/test_openrouter_proxy_reasoning.py`: check the ordinary request builder and iteration-summary send path with catalog-positive, catalog-negative, static-fallback, unknown-model, custom-provider and Mistral-host cases.

## How to Test

Using a PM-built Python 3.14.9 test environment:

```bash
HERMES_PYTHON=/path/to/test-env/bin/python HERMES_TEST_FILE_RETRIES=0 scripts/run_tests.sh \
  tests/agent/test_openrouter_proxy_reasoning.py \
  tests/agent/test_reasoning_gate_claimed_hosts.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_openrouter_reasoning_metadata.py \
  tests/agent/test_iteration_summary_reasoning_details.py \
  tests/agent/test_provider_hook_policy.py \
  tests/agent/test_provider_parity.py \
  tests/agent/test_unset_reasoning_effort_default.py \
  tests/agent/transports/test_chat_completions.py \
  tests/providers/test_provider_profiles.py -j 4 -q
/path/to/test-env/bin/python scripts/check --base origin/main
```

- New regression on pristine `40d1e95f`: 2 failed, 4 passed. The proxy drops reasoning for a catalog-supported model and for the existing known-model fallback.
- Candidate: 9 files, 161 passed, 0 failed, retries disabled.
- Full `scripts/check`: 21 checks passed; code-health 0 blocking, 0 advisory.

Manual check used the actual CLI (`python -m hermes_cli.main chat --cli --oneshot`) with a disposable home, `--provider openrouter`, a loopback OpenAI-compatible HTTP peer, `--reasoning high` and a seeded reasoning-capability catalog. Both base and candidate returned the local peer's reply and exited 0. The captured base request omitted `reasoning`; the patched request included `reasoning: {enabled: true, effort: "high"}`. No live model service or real credential was used. This checks local request construction, not live provider acceptance. No full repository test run is claimed.
