prs.title: catalog: add omp (oh-my-pi terminal backend)
prs.body:
# Catalog entry: omp — oh-my-pi terminal backend

Adds `plugin-catalog/omp.yaml` for a community terminal-backend plugin that
runs Hermes's terminal/file/code tools through a long-lived
`omp --mode rpc` (oh-my-pi) session shell on the host.

## What it does

Registers a `TerminalEnvironmentProvider` via
`ctx.register_terminal_environment_provider()` — the same public seam the
official `singularity` backend uses. Selected with
`terminal.backend: omp`. Each Hermes task gets one `omp --mode rpc --no-ui
--no-session` process; commands dispatch over the JSONL RPC `bash` surface,
serialized per env (omp's `abort_bash` is session-global). cwd is restored
per command and reported through the `cwd_observed` contract; output is
spooled to temp files and transferred as base64 chunks to stay lossless past
omp's 50 KB inline cap.

## Surfaces used

Terminal environment provider registry only. No tools, hooks, middleware,
Desktop surface, or credential access.

## Rule 13 disclosure

- No Python dependencies; no network calls of its own.
- Drives the user-installed `omp` CLI (`@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent` from npm,
  requires `bun`) — one long-lived child process per Hermes task.
- Writes temp spool files under the scratch dir and a live-observation log
  at `~/.hermes/omp-live/` (symlink to the running command's output +
  `last.json` metadata).
- Same-host backend (`is_remote=False`, `is_container=False`): Hermes
  approval guards stay active.

## Validation

`hermes plugins validate <tree> --install-deps` passes clean (manifest,
loadable, capability probe, security scan, no-core-override). Regression
tests (14) run without an omp binary present. Two rounds of independent
fresh-context review (round 1: split core vs manifest reviewers; round 2:
adversarial fix-verification with live probes) — all findings fixed and
mutation-checked; two accepted low-probability edges are documented in code
comments (base64 volume-vs-integrity on corrupt chunks; chunk eviction
under >64 concurrent large streams).

## Notes

This backend has been the author's daily-driver terminal backend for months;
the bugs fixed before submission (cwd quoting injection, cwd-marker
poisoning, missing-binary blinding, stderr pipe deadlock, cleanup respawn
race, silent output truncation) came from that production use and from the
review rounds, each pinned by a regression test.

prs.title: fix(agent): the empty-response ladder sees every reasoning shape
prs.body:
## Summary

Two gaps in the empty-response ladder let a model that **had reasoned** be treated as silent, so the ladder spent a round-trip on a response that never needed one.

1. **The inline detector matched opening tags only.** MiniMax M2 is an interleaved-thinking model whose chat template *prefills* the opening `<think>`, so the completion arrives as `…reasoning…</think>` — a bare **closing** tag with no opener. The regex (`<think>|<thinking>|<reasoning>`) missed it, the content stripped to empty, and the post-tool nudge fired on a model that had reasoned in full. This is the residual reported on #21847.

2. **The thinking-only reminder read fewer channels than the helper.** `thinking` (Ollama's native `/api/chat` field) and the OpenAI SDK's `model_extra` fall-through were invisible to the branch that routes a reasoning-only reply to the completion reminder, so such a reply fell through the empty-response retry as if the model had said nothing. This is the control-flow gap teknium1 raised on #21847: *"share this predicate with the prefill branch … so the control flow matches the helper's contract."*

The detection now lives in `agent/reasoning_channels`, so every caller agrees on the channel set and the tag names.

## What this does NOT change

A separate-channel response **after a tool call still takes the nudge**. The model still owes an answer, and suppressing the nudge there would let a reasoning model end its turn with empty output and call it done — upstream's decision on #21811 / #22799 (`#22799` was closed without merge; `main` pins this routing in `tests/agent/test_request_only_empty_recovery.py`). Only the two gaps above change.

## Tests

`tests/agent/test_empty_nudge_reasoning_channels.py` — 31 cases.

Both fixes are **planted-checked**:
- reverting the inline detector → the orphan-closing-tag test fails;
- reverting the prefill predicate → the `thinking` and `model_extra` tests fail.

The surrounding empty-response suites (132 tests across 8 files) pass unchanged.

## Notes for review

- The tag names come from `agent.think_scrubber.THINK_TAG_NAMES` — the one list every reasoning-hiding surface binds to — so a name added there is covered here, and the opening/closing forms are both matched.
- The channel list mirrors `agent.agent_runtime_helpers.extract_reasoning`, plus `thinking`.

## Relationship to the adjacent open issues

- **#153104** (think-tag stripping deletes legitimate answer text) is the same tag family but a different layer: that one is about `strip_think_blocks` removing an answer that *is* a tag on a route whose reasoning arrives out of band. This PR does not touch the stripper. The one behaviour it does shift is the branch selection for that shape — a content that is a bare closing tag now routes to the thinking-only reminder instead of the post-tool nudge, because the tag is no longer invisible to the detector.
- **#64732** (prefill cascade on reasoning responses that also have visible content) is unreachable in current `main`: the ladder is only entered when `agent._has_content_after_think_block(final_response)` is false (`agent/turn_final_response.py:180`), so a reply carrying visible text never reaches the prefill branch. This PR does not change that gate.
- **#73336** (thinking-budget exhaustion detector misses `reasoning_content`-only models) is a different detector (truncation handling, not the empty-response ladder). The channel list here matches `extract_reasoning` plus `thinking`; the two surfaces are separate.

Related: #21811, #21847, #22799, #34655, #153104, #64732, #73336.

prs.title: Prompt cache stays warm for every model, compacts once then waits for you, and never loses tool output
prs.body:
A chat's cached prompt gets more expensive to re-send the longer it sits, so Hermes now keeps that cache warm for one controller per chat and, when that stops paying, shrinks the chat instead of re-sending it at full price. Old tool output is never thrown away: it is saved byte-for-byte to disk with a pointer the agent can read back.

## What it does

1. **Cache rules follow the API spec.** A request with cache markers is Anthropic spec on any wire or gateway: the 5m or 1h it asks for is trusted, capped by the route ceiling. A request without markers is OpenAI spec: assumed 30 minutes, renewed by each cache hit. On Nous Portal the model catalog decides: a model priced with `input_cache_write` gets markers (Claude, Qwen 3.7/4, Gemini, GPT-6, ...), and one without is OpenAI spec. A 1h write is billed at the catalog's own rate (Claude 2x input, Qwen 1.25x).
2. **Warm at 5/6 of the TTL** (5m → 4m10s, 30m → 25m, 1h → 50m), re-sending the last request with a 1-token cap (16 for GPT-5/o-series).
3. **Idle: 3 keep-alives per user message** (only in chats a person types into).
4. **While a tool runs: keep warming until it returns**, with no count limit. The keep-alives of one tool wait together never cost more than the single rewrite they prevent (~12 on a 5m cache, ~20 on 1h, ~10 on 30m), and they do not use the idle 3.
5. **The first miss ends warming for the session.** New messages and compactions do not restart it. A model or provider switch, or `/new`, does. `/context` shows `Keep-alives: off (one missed).`
6. **Then compact, if it qualifies.** The conditions: a window of 30 minutes or more, context at least 50% of the compaction threshold, and the chat grew since the last compaction. The summary reads the ORIGINAL tool output and archives only after it exists.
7. **Otherwise offload at expiry.** Old tool output goes to disk once the window passes.
8. **Nothing is sent after a compaction** until the next user message.
9. **Offload also on cold return, release and route switch** (`/model`, fallback).
10. **Every pruned result is saved byte-exact** to `cache/pruned/…` with a one-line pointer in the chat, and listed in the summary.

A keep-alive sent while a tool call is pending is a side request with the same prompt. Nothing is appended to the conversation, the model never sees it, and the tool result lands normally.

## Live (real `hermes chat --cli` on Nous Portal, `cache_ttl: auto`, harness clock shift: keep-alive due 5-12 s after send; total ≈ $0.52)

| Run | What | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A: DeepSeek V4 Flash, forced miss on keep-alive #1 | first miss → session blacklisted; another user message; idle 45 s | `warming disabled for session: keep-alive missed`; **0** keep-alives after the new message; `/context`: `… (30m, declared). Keep-alives: off (one missed).` ($0.002) |
| B: Claude Sonnet 4.6, `sleep 80` tool | keep-alives during the pending tool | **10** keep-alives mid-tool, every one `cache_read=8808 write=0` ($0.0027 each); tool result `slept-ok` landed; rows `user, assistant, tool, tool, assistant` (nothing added); next request read 8,808 cached, the rest was the new tool output ($0.26) |
| B': Haiku 4.5, real miss mid-tool | first keep-alive wrote more than it read | warming disabled at once; no more sends during the 100 s tool; next request 100% cache hit; rows unchanged ($0.12) |

Qwen 3.7 Max on Nous (raw probe, ~31k-token prompt):

| Request | Write billed | 2 s | 4 min | 13 min idle |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| no markers (automatic) | — | hit | **miss** | — |
| `cache_control` 5m | 1.25x ($0.0565) | hit | hit | miss (9 min after the 4-min hit) |
| `cache_control` 1h | 1.25x ($0.0578) | hit | — | **hit** |

Tests changed by these rulings: `test_warming_follows_the_shared_clock_and_never_warms_without_a_guarantee` (gateway 1h is trusted now), `test_tool_rounds_inside_one_user_turn_share_one_budget` and `test_a_tool_run_that_spent_its_keep_alives_still_compacts_at_the_end_of_the_turn` (the 3-cap is the idle budget), `test_moa_records_the_resolved_aggregator_route_and_payload` (`anthropic_spec`). New invariants are in `tests/agent/test_prompt_cache_rulings.py` (7 tests, all red on 7fff25a7).

## Credits

- @kshitijk4poor: the proactive tool-result prune and archive (#136488) and prepared compaction (#144684).
- @100yenadmin: `cache_ttl: auto` (#145432) and the review of #156081.
- @kvnloo: JSON-array archive paging and preserving unflushed originals before the prune.
- @mitsuhiko: the original prompt-cache warming design in earendil-works/pi#9668, ported in #122094.
- @npetroff24: the idle-compact idea (#151785).

Supersedes #122094, #156081, #156253.

## NOT_COVERED

- No real 25/50-minute Hermes wait: the live rows shift the keep-alive clock. Real retention comes from raw probes (Claude 1h at 25 min, Qwen above).
- Qwen 3.7 Max through Hermes was not run live (raw probe only). The catalog rule is unit-tested.
- Messaging platforms, native Anthropic, OpenRouter, TUI/Desktop on Nous and sandboxed-backend offload were not run live. The gateway housekeeping tick is 300 s, so a gateway compaction or offload can land up to ~5 min after the budget ends.
- When the Nous catalog is unreachable, the built-in marker policy applies (Claude and Qwen by name).

## Infographic

![Prompt cache lifecycle](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab2cbb3/fyfww4JFQiwdISYHIk_dm_nhTLZKYV.png)

prs.title: fix(prompt): name the remote session's workspace and load its project context
prs.body:
## Problem

With a remote terminal backend (`ssh` / `docker` / `modal` …) a Desktop session is **blind about its own project**, in two ways:

**1. No workspace anchor.** The environment block suppresses every cwd signal:

> `The sandbox's current user, $HOME, and working directory are not listed here; if you need them, probe directly with a terminal call like whoami && pwd.`

But the runtime *does* know the session's workspace: the gateway freezes it into the session policy at session open (`gateway/session_policy.py` → `terminal['TERMINAL_CWD'] = cwd`), and the backend executes commands there (`tools/environments/base.py` per-session cd state). The model is the only party kept ignorant — so it reconstructs "which project am I in" from prompt text and memory/skill priors. When the first message is project-agnostic ("commit the current stage"), the guess lands on whatever repo dominates recent context, and file/shell work silently routes into the wrong repository.

Local backends never hit this — `_local_host_hints()` prints `Current working directory:` unconditionally. The gap is remote-backend-only.

**2. Project instructions never load.** `build_context_files_prompt` discovers `AGENTS.md` / `.hermes.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `.cursorrules` on the **Hermes host** only. A backend-side workspace (`/Users/…`, `/srv/…`) never exists host-side, `resolve_context_cwd()` drops it at the `Path.is_dir()` check, and remote sessions run their repo with **zero project instructions** — no conventions, no build commands, no warnings. Same root cause, worse consequence.

## Fix (two commits)

**Commit 1 — anchor.** `_remote_backend_hint()` renders the session's runtime-declared workspace (via `scoped_session_cwd()`, which deliberately skips host-side path validation):

```
  Session workspace: /Users/dev/ABR/direct/MOBILE-3634 — the directory this session was opened in on the backend. Treat it as the project root: start file and shell work there unless the request names another path.
```

When no workspace is declared (CLI turns, multiplexed turns, placeholder cwds like `.`/`~`/`auto`) the block is **byte-identical to before**, pwd-probe instruction included.

**Commit 2 — context loading.** `build_context_files_prompt` gains a remote branch: discovery runs as **one throwaway bash script on the backend** (same build path as the existing probe — isolated ssh ControlMaster, `probe_only=True` so no `~/.hermes` sync, single exec, 8 s timeout), mirroring the local one-type-wins priority exactly: `.hermes.md` walk nearest-first → `AGENTS.md` chain root→cwd (per-directory first name wins, identical copies dedup) → `CLAUDE.md` → `.cursorrules`. Payload frames are nonce-tagged (hostile file content cannot forge markers; a forged `END` can only clip its own file); the cwd reaches the shell only through `shlex.quote`; every file passes the same `_scan_context_content` threat scan, which stays the hard gate (the containment policy is intentionally not mirrored shell-side — the scan blocks, not merely warns). Failure ships **no** project context rather than falling back to this host's launch dir, which names nothing in the session.

## Privacy contract (#117262)

That ban is on probe-**observed** sandbox identity (user/$HOME/cwd fetched out of the box by `_BACKEND_PROBE_CMD`). This PR names a runtime-**declared** value: a backend-side path the user picked when opening the session. It is not probed (probe command untouched), never the Hermes host's cwd, and is precisely the datum the "nothing consumes it" rationale excluded by accident. The privacy regression test is untouched and still passes.

## Tests

11 new tests next to the existing privacy/probe tests: workspace rendering + byte-parity when unset + probe-fallback block + placeholder cwds; agents chain ordering/dedup, `.hermes.md` shadowing + frontmatter strip, injection blocked from a backend file, **no host launch-dir fallback**, local path untouched without a declared cwd, script quoting, forged-marker parsing. The discovery script was additionally exercised against real bash 3.2 (macOS) on live git fixtures: override-wins, root→cwd ordering, symlinked-cwd label normalization (`cd -P`).

```
tests/agent/test_prompt_builder.py + test_system_prompt.py + test_runtime_cwd.py
+ test_relay_cwd.py + test_platform_hint_desktop.py   167 passed, 1 skipped
```

(3 pre-existing failures in `test_compaction_prompt_rebuild.py` reproduce identically on unmodified HEAD — unrelated.)

## Related

Addresses the context-anchor half of #45893 — this PR names the session's execution anchor **and** loads its project files; #45909 covers host-local-path warnings (complementary, not duplicate). Related: #38369 (make execution target explicit), #19214 (terminal.cwd foot-gun).

Known scope note: `agent/context_file_sources.py` (the `/context` manifest) still enumerates host-side only and will show nothing for remote sessions — a natural follow-up on top of this plumbing.

prs.body:
## Summary

Adds three community plugins for the **Hermes Agent Plugin Hackathon** from [`misakamikotoghr-5205/hermes-hackathon-plugins`](https://github.com/misakamikotoghr-5205/hermes-hackathon-plugins) pinned at commit `d4a7f0938b975c36c0d7fc65c8d32313a52d6f1b`:

1. **`claim-market-router`** (`category: models`, `subdir: claim-market-router`)
   - **Extension Surfaces:** Pluggable `DelegationProvider` (`delegation.backend: claim_market`, returning `model`, `provider`, `reasoning_effort`, `service_tier`, `fallback_providers`, `request_overrides`, and `label`), `llm_request` middleware, `post_llm_call` & `post_api_request` hooks, `claim_market_auction` & `claim_market_ledger` tools, `/claim-market` slash command, and `hermes claim-market` CLI command.
   - **What it does:** Adapted from [`Cost-aware-claim-based-multi-model-AI-orchestrator`](https://github.com/misakamikotoghr-5205/Cost-aware-claim-based-multi-model-AI-orchestrator) (*MISAKA AGENT*) and [`watt-window`](https://github.com/misakamikotoghr-5205/watt-window). Publishes task cards (`role_needed`, `complexity`, `max_cost_units`), synthesizes capability-fit and quota-health claims with convex shadow pricing across current models (`google/gemini-3.8-flash`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`, `openai/gpt-6-astra-pro`, with `fallback_providers` chains to `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5`, and `google/gemini-4-argon`), resolves disagreements via weighted voting, nominates an independent verifier route, and returns explainable sensitivity reports when budget constraints are infeasible.

2. **`hunk-consent-guard`** (`category: tools`, `subdir: hunk-consent-guard`)
   - **Extension Surfaces:** `tool_execution` middleware, `pre_tool_call` & `post_tool_call` hooks, 4 tools (`hunk_propose`, `hunk_review_status`, `hunk_apply_approved`, `hunk_rollback_receipt`), `/hunk-desk` slash command, and `hermes hunk-desk` CLI command.
   - **What it does:** Adapted from [`patch-review-desk`](https://github.com/misakamikotoghr-5205/patch-review-desk) and [`cart-consent-paypal`](https://github.com/misakamikotoghr-5205/cart-consent-paypal). Stages multi-hunk file proposals (checking `agent.file_safety.get_read_block_error` / `get_write_denied_error` and resolving relative paths against terminal cwd), requires user-only hunk consent (`/hunk-desk approve`, `hermes hunk-desk approve`, plus `pre_tool_call` approval gate on `hunk_apply_approved`), dispatches all file writes through `ctx.dispatch_tool("write_file", ...)`, automatically revokes approvals if the target file's SHA-256 baseline drifts on disk before application, and records drift-checked rollback receipts in SQLite.

3. **`source-trail-supervisor`** (`category: general`, `subdir: source-trail-supervisor`)
   - **Extension Surfaces:** 3 tools (`source_trail_ingest`, `source_trail_verify`, `session_supervisor_node`), 3 hooks (`on_session_start`, `post_tool_call`, `post_llm_call`), bundled `epistemic-supervision` skill (`ctx.register_skill`), `/trail-supervise` slash command, and `hermes trail-supervise` CLI command.
   - **What it does:** Adapted from [`source-trail-otari`](https://github.com/misakamikotoghr-5205/source-trail-otari), [`volc-casedesk`](https://github.com/misakamikotoghr-5205/volc-casedesk), and [`codex-session-supervisor`](https://github.com/misakamikotoghr-5205/codex-session-supervisor). Enforces exact zero-based Unicode code-point span citations (`source[start:end] == quote`), withholds unilateral claims when valid sources carry conflicting position labels on the same topic (`withheld_contradiction`), and fingerprints tool/turn progress to detect stuck loops and log recoverable causal decision nodes.

---

## Disclosure (Catalog Rule 13)

- **Network & Subprocesses:** None across all three plugins. Pure Python 3.11+ standard library (`sqlite3`, `difflib`, `hashlib`, `json`, `argparse`).
- **Credentials & Core Safety:** None of the plugins read `.env`, `auth.json`, or provider secrets, nor do they override core tools or weaken built-in approval prompts.
- **Profile-Scoped Storage:** Each plugin writes only to `<HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/<plugin-name>/data.db` via `plugins.plugin_storage.plugin_db`.
- **Middleware Behavior:**
  - `claim-market-router`'s `llm_request` middleware is a no-op by default (`auto_effort_shaping: false`); when enabled, it modifies only `reasoning_effort` on exploratory turns when rolling-window shadow price $\ge 0.20$.
  - `hunk-consent-guard`'s `tool_execution` middleware wraps file-writing tool calls solely to capture before/after SHA-256 rollback receipts (up to `max_snapshot_kb`, default 256 KB) without altering tool arguments or bypassing Hermes approvals.

## Verification

- `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` passes cleanly.
- `hermes plugins validate` capability probe (`provides_tools`, `provides_hooks`, `provides_middleware`), `tools/plugin_guard.py`, `check_private_imports`, and `scripts/scan_plugin_payloads.py` pass with zero errors or warnings.

prs.title: fix(plugins): mark detached-fork tool hooks with detached=True
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A detached fork (background review, `/btw`, plugin session fork) shares its parent's `session_id` and deliberately skips `post_llm_call`, but still fires `pre_tool_call` / `post_tool_call`. Status plugins see work start after the turn ended and never see it end, so the session stays "working" (#133603).

This is option B from #133603, the alternative to #133669 discussed in [this comment](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/133669#issuecomment-6706357347): the fork's tool hooks keep firing and carry `detached=True`.

Why B rather than silencing: `pre_tool_call` is a policy hook. If a fork's calls skip it, guard and audit plugins stop seeing (and can no longer block) the tools the fork runs. With a flag, status/observer plugins can skip `detached=True` events, and policy plugins keep working unchanged.

- The flag comes from the agent object (`_persist_disabled`), not thread state, so it also reaches concurrent tool batches on pool workers (`propagate_context_to_thread`). A test checks that.
- Live turns are unchanged: no `detached` key at all (not `False`), so their payloads are byte-identical to before. Plugins read it with `kwargs.get("detached", False)`.
- `transform_tool_result` carries `detached=True` too. It receives the same tool-hook id kwargs as pre/post_tool_call (one helper builds them), so a plugin sees the same marker on every tool hook.
- No `parent_session_id` added: a detached fork already reports its parent's `session_id` (same value), so the field would repeat information the hook already has.

## Related Issue

Refs #133603 (alternative to #133669)

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/inline_tool_executors.py`: `detached_hook_kwargs(agent)` helper; `tool_hook_ids()` includes it.
- `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`, `agent/tool_executor.py`: pass it at the inline pre-hook site and both `handle_function_call` dispatches (sequential and concurrent).
- `model_tools.py`: `_CallIds.detached`, emitted only when true; threaded to pre/post/transform hooks.
- `hermes_cli/plugins.py`: `pre_tool_call` dispatch forwards it.
- `website/docs/user-guide/features/hooks.md`: `detached` in the three tool-hook rows, plus a short note.
- `tests/agent/test_detached_fork_tool_hooks.py`: 11 tests (new).

Not covered: the agent-less path (`execute_code` RPC → `handle_function_call`) has no agent, so it carries no flag, the same as its `session_id`/`conversation_id` gap today. Tool middleware context on a fork also sees `detached=True`, since it shares the id helper.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_detached_fork_tool_hooks.py` → 11 passed. The tests use a real plugin through discovery and a real `build_cache_parity_fork` fork, and they cover: sequential and concurrent paths, ok/error/blocked/cancelled outcomes, a plugin `block` still blocking a fork call, a 3-call concurrent batch held at a barrier on pool workers, and live-agent hooks with no `detached` key.
2. Mutation check: make `detached_hook_kwargs` return `{}` → 11/11 red.
3. All 60 test files that reference `pre_tool_call`/`post_tool_call`: the set of failing test IDs is identical before and after the change (0 new, 0 fixed). The pre-existing failures are local-environment ones (Python 3.14 venv, macOS).

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs (#133669 is the variant-A fix for the same issue; this is the variant-B alternative discussed there)
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix
- [x] I've run the tests for the code I changed, and they pass
- [x] `scripts/check --base <merge-base>` passes (19 checks, code health 0 blocking)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26, Python 3.14

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (`hooks.md`)

prs.title: fix(codex): send plain JSON to the official Codex backend by default (salvage #149579)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Since #136916 (teknium1, aefffa077f, merged 2026-10-12), Hermes zstd-compresses every request body sent to the official ChatGPT Codex `/responses` endpoint. That endpoint rejects some valid zstd frames with a bare `HTTP 400 {"detail":"Bad Request"}`. Hermes classes that as non-retryable, so the turn ends and fallback providers never run. One user report shows it at call 137 of a 52-minute turn, on v0.23.1 with `gpt-6-luna`. Fixes #148898.

This salvages #149579 (by @TheMethodicalJosh, building on @kvnloo's opt-out commit). Request bodies now go out as plain JSON by default. zstd stays available as an explicit opt-in, `agent.codex_request_compression: true`. Both contributor commits keep their authorship.

## What changes

```diff
  official Codex /responses request
- always zstd (Python 3.14+)          -> some frames: bare 400, turn ends
+ plain JSON unless agent.codex_request_compression: true
+ opt-in read raises / backend refuses / --ignore-user-config -> plain JSON, HTTP client kept
```

Commits:
1. `chore(contributors)`: maps TheMethodicalJosh's email for the attribution check.
2. @kvnloo: adds the `agent.codex_request_compression` profile key (opt-out at that point).
3. @TheMethodicalJosh: flips the default to plain JSON and adds docs, the example config and sync/async default tests.
4. Ours, on top (two commits: the first fix, then the review-wave fold):
   - The opt-in read moves into `_codex_compression_opted_in()`. Before, a failing read raised out of `build_keepalive_http_client`, whose blanket `except` returned `None`. The agent then fell back to the SDK default client and lost Hermes' proxy and keepalive policy. Now it logs and sends plain JSON. That includes `ConfigBackendUnavailable`, a `SystemExit` that would otherwise escape the builder's `except Exception` and could end a gateway turn worker during a client rebuild. Main never read config here. It is caught the same way `agent/redact_phone_policy.py` catches it.
   - `HERMES_IGNORE_USER_CONFIG=1` now ignores a stored opt-in.
   - Restores the meaning of the `api_max_retries` comment that commit 3 reworded. It is two lines now, so `config_defaults.py` stays at its line cap.
   - Docs say custom endpoint URLs always get plain JSON, replacing "proxies": an official URL behind an HTTP proxy is still official. They also say a running gateway must restart after a change, because cached clients keep the encoding they were built with.
   - Adds an async opt-in lossless test, plus tests for the ignore-config and failed-read cases and the backend-unavailable case.

## Evidence

Live, against the official endpoint with real ChatGPT OAuth and `gpt-6-luna`. The same JSON bytes went through each tree's real `build_keepalive_http_client`:

| raw body bytes | main | this PR | this PR + opt-in |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 131072 | zstd 200 | plain 200 | zstd 200 |
| 131073 | zstd **400** | plain 200 | zstd **400** |
| 131243 | zstd **400** | plain 200 | |
| 200000 | zstd **400** | plain 200 | |

Real `AIAgent` turn (`run_conversation`, gpt-6-luna) with a ~131 KB user message:
- main: 1 of 23 runs ended `failed=True`, with `API call failed (attempt 1/3, not retryable) ... HTTP 400: {"detail":"Bad Request"}`. The failure depends on the exact bytes, and the bytes vary per session.
- this PR: plain JSON on the wire in 15 of 15 runs, all completed.

Tests: the new default-plain-JSON tests fail on main. The ignore-config and failed-read tests fail on the #149579 head. All 18 tests in `test_codex_request_compression.py` and `test_codex_cloudflare_headers.py` pass locally. `scripts/check` is ok.

Not changed: a client built for a gateway session with a frozen config reads the live profile's `agent.codex_request_compression`. Route resolution reads the frozen config; client construction reads the live one, like the other build-time settings such as TLS verify. Only the opt-in is affected, and the default stays plain JSON. In the same way, an unparseable `config.yaml` keeps serving the last-known-good config (#31188), so a previous `true` survives it.

## Why this PR and not #155201

#155201 (@jean-de-bot) keeps zstd for bodies of 128 KiB or less and sends larger ones raw. It fixes the cases measured so far. But it keeps a known-failing encoding as the default, behind an empirical size premise. Compression only stays on for bodies small enough that it saves little. If the backend's failure band moves, users have no switch. Its 128 KiB block-boundary analysis is what pinned down this bug, and it is credited here.

## Credit

- @TheMethodicalJosh: #149579, the default flip.
- @kvnloo: the config key.
- @enckequity: the original report and 36/36 A/B.
- @jacko2bot, @harrisrobin, @100yenadmin, @jngonzales, @vince-winkintel, @viktorrosenkilde-blip: boundary measurements and reproductions.
- @jean-de-bot: #155201.

Supersedes #149579 and #155201 (both stay open until this merges).

prs.title: Fix Implicit "open" Policy Default in Feishu Group Rules
prs.body:
## Description
This pull request fixes an issue where configuring an allowlist or blacklist for a Feishu group without explicitly specifying the `policy` key caused the adapter to default the policy to `"open"`[cite: 4]. Consequently, explicitly defined allowlists and blacklists were silently ignored during group authorization checks[cite: 4].

## Changes
- Updated `FeishuAdapter._load_settings` in `plugins/platforms/feishu/adapter.py`[cite: 4].
- If the `policy` key is omitted in a `group_rules` entry, the policy is now automatically derived from the configuration keys:
  - Defaults to `"allowlist"` if an `allowlist` is provided[cite: 4].
  - Defaults to `"blacklist"` if a `blacklist` is provided[cite: 4].
  - Falls back to `"open"` only if neither list is present[cite: 4].

## Testing
- Tested locally using proof-of-concept scripts to ensure that unlisted senders are properly restricted when allowlists/blacklists are specified without an explicit policy key[cite: 4].

prs.title: Reopened chats keep the picked model after a fallback answered (Desktop, TUI, CLI --resume) (salvage #121629)
prs.body:
Pick a model in a Desktop chat, have it fail once so a backup model answers, then restart the app (or let it update): the reopened chat used to come back on the backup model, sent to the provider you picked, which is a pair that can't work. Now a reopened chat goes back to the model you picked, and the backup only covers the turn where it was needed, the same as a chat that stayed open.

Resuming a fallback-served chat (Desktop, TUI and `hermes --resume`) restores the user's picked model and provider instead of mixing the fallback model with the picked provider.

Salvages #121629 by @calvinnwq (commit kept as authored) and extends it to the CLI reader the PR listed as out of scope. Fixes the resume half of #118969 (the non-chat-model picker half stays open). Supersedes #118982, which took the opposite design (resume on the fallback); Teknium ruled for this one.

## Changes

- `tui_gateway/agent_factory.py::_stored_session_runtime_overrides` (Calvin): the model comes from the same record as the route. The pick in `model_config` wins, unless the column was written with its route (`gateway_runtime` with a provider, or a confirmed Browser/API lock naming the column). `billing_provider` never fills the provider for a different pick.
- `hermes_state_gateway.py::SessionDB.session_resume_model` (new, beside `session_gateway_runtime`): that rule as one shared seam.
- `hermes_cli/cli_model_switch_mixin.py::stored_session_route`: `hermes --resume` reads the same seam, so a Desktop row resumed from the CLI no longer gets the mixed pair.
- `sessions.model` / `billing_*` stay the billing record of what actually served the call (unchanged, `first_accounted_route`).

## Live A/B

A real `hermes serve` in a scratch home, two loopback providers (`pickprov`/`pick-qwen` picked, `mainprov`/`main-grok` default + `fallback_providers`), driven over the Desktop WS calls: `session.create` with the pick → turn 1 while the pick 404s → stop serve → start serve → `session.resume` → turn 2 with the pick healthy. Requests are read from the stubs' own logs.

| | main `40d1e95f` | head |
|---|---|---|
| turn 1 requests | pick-qwen@pickprov 404 → main-grok@mainprov ok | same |
| stored row | model=main-grok, billing=mainprov, model_config={pick-qwen, pickprov} | same (billing record unchanged) |
| `session.resume` info | **main-grok / pickprov** | pick-qwen / pickprov |
| turn 2 request | **main-grok sent to pickprov** | pick-qwen sent to pickprov |
| CLI `stored_session_route` on that row | **('main-grok', 'pickprov')** | ('pick-qwen', 'pickprov') |

Control legs on main, all already correct and unchanged: create-with-pick, mid-chat switch, mid-turn switch (deferred to next turn), gateway restart with a healthy pick, pick failing with no fallback configured (turn errors visibly, no silent switch).

## Tests

- `tests/tui_gateway/test_resume_switched_provider_endpoint.py`: Calvin's tests plus a CLI assertion on the real-SessionDB fallback test. That test is red on main for both readers and green on head.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_resume_switched_provider_endpoint.py tests/hermes_cli/test_resume_model_restore.py tests/hermes_state/`: 2025 passed, 0 failed, 16 skipped.

## Known limits (unchanged from main, from #121629)

- A chat with no stored provider whose fallback used the same model id still resumes on the fallback's provider (indistinguishable from the stale-provider heal row).
- A confirmed Browser/API lock that changed provider resumes on the locked model with the pick's provider.
- Desktop still shows the picked model in the pill while a fallback is serving a live turn; that display gap is a separate follow-up.

## Infographic

![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab2cbb9/3rczRDIwWzm7-Nn6sdKUS_L5M8vgVD.png)

prs.title: fix(api-server): a trailing empty assistant turn is not the user's message
prs.body:
Fixes #154758

## What was wrong

Open WebUI ends a `/v1/chat/completions` request with an empty assistant turn, the slot the reply will fill. `_handle_chat_completions` takes `conversation_messages[-1]` as the user's turn, finds no text in it, and answers:

```
HTTP 400 (invalid_request_error)
No user message found in messages
```

so every Open WebUI chat failed. Repro on `main`:

```json
{"model": "hermes-agent", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": ""}]}
```

## The fix

`_parse_chat_messages` drops trailing assistant turns that have no visible content before the user turn is picked. "No visible content" uses the same `_content_has_visible_payload` check that rejects empty user turns: empty, whitespace-only, an empty parts list, or no `content` key. This is the workaround the reporter tested. A request whose last real turn has no user text is still refused with the same 400.

`_parse_chat_messages` has one caller, the chat-completions handler. `/v1/responses` and `/v1/runs` parse their input separately and aren't touched.

## Tests

New `tests/gateway/test_api_server_trailing_empty_assistant.py`, end to end through the aiohttp handler with `_run_agent` stubbed:
- one or two empty, whitespace-only, empty-list or content-less assistant placeholders → 200; the user turn is `"Hello"` and the earlier turns stay as history (5 cases, all fail on `main` with the 400);
- a whitespace user turn followed by an empty placeholder is still refused with 400.

Run on Windows 11 with the repo's PM test environment's `python -m pytest` (`HERMES_HOME` set to a temp dir, `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`), not `scripts/run_tests.sh`. Across the 22 gateway test files that hit `/v1/chat/completions`: 287 passed and 2 failed. Neither failure is from this change:
- `test_api_authority_daemon.py::test_ordinary_daemon_api_ws_fifo_retry` fails identically on `main` here (`WinError 10106` from the Windows socket provider);
- `test_api_server.py::TestAdapterInit::test_create_agent_forwards_runtime_config` passes alone and with its whole file (114 passed). It only failed inside the combined run, so it depends on test order.

`python scripts/check` passes, and the lefthook pre-commit ran clean.

prs.title: fix(models): list MiniMax-M3.1-Flash in the MiniMax catalog
prs.body:
Fixes #154585 (the MiniMax part; see "Not in this PR")

## What was wrong

MiniMax has no `/models` endpoint, so `hermes_cli/models_catalog_static.py` is the whole list Hermes has for it. The desktop picker shows that list (`explicit_only=True`) and `/model` validates against it. `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` (released 2026-10-19) wasn't in it, so:
- it showed in the picker only on a profile whose current pick already was that model (current-pick injection), and nowhere else;
- `/model MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` was accepted but warned that it was not found in the MiniMax catalog.

## The fix

Add `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` to:
- `_MINIMAX_MODELS`, which feeds `minimax` (Global) and `minimax-cn` (China);
- `minimax-oauth` (OAuth Coding Plan).

Source: [models.dev](https://models.dev/api.json) lists the id under `minimax`, `minimax-cn`, `minimax-coding-plan` and `minimax-cn-coding-plan`, with a 1M context. Hermes already resolves that 1M window through the existing `minimax-m3` prefix entry in `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_LENGTHS` (`get_model_context_length("MiniMax-M3.1-Flash", provider="minimax")` → `1000000`), so `model_metadata.py` doesn't change.

## Not in this PR

- **`MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview`** is listed only for the coding-plan slugs and is a dated preview, so I left it out.
- **The `*-highspeed` variants** that models.dev carries for the direct API are a separate catalog decision. `test_minimax_model_validation.py` also uses `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` on purpose as its "not in the catalog" case.
- **The `alibaba-token-plan` comment on the issue** is a different mechanism: that endpoint does expose `/models`. It deserves its own PR.

## Tests

New `tests/hermes_cli/test_minimax_m3_1_flash_catalog.py` (5 cases, all fail on `main`):
- `validate_requested_model("MiniMax-M3.1-Flash", …)` is recognised with no warning on `minimax` and `minimax-cn`;
- the id is offered by `curated_models_for_provider` for `minimax`, `minimax-cn` and `minimax-oauth`.

Run on Windows 11 with the repo's PM test environment's `python -m pytest` (`HERMES_HOME` set to a temp dir, `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`), not `scripts/run_tests.sh`. I ran the 85 test files that read the model catalog (`curated_models_for_provider`, `provider_model_ids`, `validate_requested_model`, `build_model_options_payload` and the static catalog) on this branch and on unmodified `main`. The results were 1943 passed vs 1938, with exactly the same 28 failures and 1 collection error on both. The 5 extra passes are the new tests. Those failures are Windows environment problems on this machine, for example `WinError 10106` when the e2e catalog helper starts a subprocess.

`python scripts/check` passes.

prs.title: fix(gateway-client): don't keepalive-ping a loopback gateway
prs.body:
Fixes #154910

## What was wrong

`connect_gateway()` (`hermes_cli/gateway_client.py`) dials the owner's WebSocket with the `websockets` default keepalive: a ping every 20 s, with 20 s to answer. The owner answers pings on the same event loop that runs the turn. When a long, tool-heavy turn keeps that loop busy past the timeout, the pong never comes back, and the **client** closes every socket it holds with `1011 keepalive ping timeout`. The user then sees `Gateway disconnected; turn outcome is unknown…` even though the turn finishes on the gateway.

The dashboard server already avoids this on its side. `hermes_cli/web_server.py` turns the ping off for loopback binds (#53773 / #48445 / #50005), because on loopback a dead peer sends a real FIN/RST and the ping only ever catches half-open tunnels.

## The fix

`_keepalive_options(url)` passes `ping_interval=None, ping_timeout=None` when the owner's host is loopback: any loopback IP (`127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`) or `localhost`, case-insensitive, trailing dot ignored. Any other host gets no extra arguments, so a remote owner reached through `HERMES_TUI_GATEWAY_URL` keeps the default ping, where a half-open tunnel really does look like a stall.

This is the two-argument change the reporter tested, limited to loopback as the issue suggests. The issue's second idea, multiplexing command sockets over the event socket, is not in this PR.

## Repro (real sockets, no mocks)

`repro.py` starts a loopback `websockets` server per client. Each server sends `hello` and then blocks its own event loop for 45 s with `time.sleep`, which stands in for a GIL-holding call during a turn. One client dials with `main`'s options and one with `_keepalive_options(url)`:

```
[main (websockets default ping)] hello
[fix  (_keepalive_options)     ] hello
[fix  (_keepalive_options)     ] 'turn finished' after 46s: socket kept
[main (websockets default ping)] lost after 46s: ConnectionClosedError: sent 1011 (internal error) keepalive ping timeout; no close frame received
```

## Tests

New `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_client_loopback_keepalive.py` checks the arguments `connect_gateway()` passes to `websockets.asyncio.client.connect`, without dialing anything:
- `127.0.0.1`, `127.8.0.1`, `localhost`, `LOCALHOST.` and `[::1]` → no ping (5 cases, all fail on `main`);
- `wss://gateway.example.com` and a LAN IP → the default keepalive is untouched.

Run on Windows 11 with the repo's PM test environment's `python -m pytest` (`HERMES_HOME` set to a temp dir, `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`), not `scripts/run_tests.sh`. I ran the 96 test files that use the gateway client (`connect_gateway`, `gateway_ws_target`, `hermes_cli.gateway_client`) on this branch and on unmodified `main` side by side: 769 vs 762 passed, with exactly the same 39 failures and 13 errors on both. The extra passes are the 7 new tests. Those failures come from this Windows machine's environment and fail on `main` too.

`python scripts/check` passes, and the lefthook pre-commit ran clean.

prs.title: fix(cron): keep a monitor change pending when the script gate skips the agent
prs.body:
Fixes #154959

## What was wrong

A cron job can have both a monitor source (`monitor_script` / `monitor_url`) and a pre-run `script` that acts as a wake gate. On each tick, `check_monitor()` (`cron/monitor.py`) detected a change and immediately saved the new hash and snapshot as seen. Only after that did `_prepare_job_prompt()` (`cron/scheduler.py`) run the gate script. If the gate said `{"wakeAgent": false}`, or printed nothing, the tick ended as a silent skip with no agent run.

The change had already been saved, though. On the next tick the monitor output matched the stored hash, so it was reported as "no change" and the agent was suppressed again. The change was lost until the source changed once more, and the job status showed only successful silent runs.

## The fix

- `check_monitor()` no longer saves anything. On a change it returns the new hash and output as `MonitorOutcome.pending`, and `MonitorOutcome.commit(job_id)` saves them.
- `_apply_monitor_gate()` returns the outcome instead of only its `context_block`.
- `_prepare_job_prompt()` calls `commit()` after both script-gate skips (`wakeAgent: false` and empty output), just before it hands the prompt to the agent.

The existing rule still holds: the change is saved before the agent runs, so a failed agent run doesn't re-alert on the same content forever.

One side effect to flag: a tick refused by the prompt-injection scanner also no longer saves the change, because no agent ran on it. That tick is still reported as a blocked error, as before. The next tick will report the same change again, so it reaches the agent once the blocked content is fixed.

## Tests

New `test_change_skipped_by_the_script_gate_stays_pending` in `tests/cron/test_monitor_kind.py`, run once for `wakeAgent: false` and once for empty gate output, with real scripts and `run_job()`:
1. The first tick runs the agent and records the baseline.
2. The monitor output changes and the gate closes: a silent skip with no agent run.
3. The gate opens again: the agent runs, and its prompt contains the `+state B` diff.
4. One more tick: no agent run, so the change is delivered once.

Both cases fail on `main` at step 3 (`assert 1 == 2`, no agent run).

`tests/agent/test_redact_telegram_boundary.py` called `check_monitor()` and read the saved snapshot, so it now calls `outcome.commit()` first. It still checks that the saved snapshot is redacted.

Run on Windows 11 with the repo's PM test environment's `python -m pytest` (`HERMES_HOME` set to a temp dir, `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`), not `scripts/run_tests.sh`. I ran all of `tests/cron/` plus the other test files that use the monitor or the wake gate (188 files) on this branch and on unmodified `main` side by side: 1822 vs 1820 passed, with exactly the same 35 failures on both. The extra passes are the 2 new test cases. Those failures come from this Windows machine's environment (for example `WinError 193` when a test runs a `#!` script directly) and fail on `main` too.

`python scripts/check` passes, and the lefthook pre-commit ran clean.

prs.title: fix(gateway): mark one-time tips seen in the served profile's config
prs.body:
Fixes #154977
Fixes #156007

## What was wrong

The gateway shows two one-time tips: the busy-input tip (`gateway/run_busy.py`, "I queued your message instead of interrupting…") and the `/verbose` tool-progress tip (`gateway/run_turn_progress.py`). Each checks `onboarding.seen.<flag>` in the config from `_load_gateway_config()`, which reads `_gateway_config_home()`, the profile this turn serves. Each then recorded the flag with `mark_seen(_hermes_home / "config.yaml", …)`. `_hermes_home` is the gateway process's own home.

With one profile those are the same file. Under a multiplexing gateway, a served profile's turn reads its own config but writes the flag to the host profile's config. So:
- the served profile gets the busy tip on every busy message, because its own flag is never set;
- the host profile's `config.yaml` gets marked seen for a tip it was never shown.

## The fix

Both calls now write to `_gateway_config_home() / "config.yaml"`, the same home they just read. The issue names the busy tip; the tool-progress tip has the same read/write split, so it is fixed too.

## Tests

New `tests/gateway/test_onboarding_tips_served_profile.py`. A host home is patched in as `gateway.run._hermes_home`, and a served profile is bound with `set_hermes_home_override`:
- busy tip: the first busy ack includes it and the second doesn't; the flag is in the served profile's config and not in the host's;
- tool-progress tip: queued once across two long tool calls; the flag is in the served profile's config and not in the host's.

Both fail on `main`: the busy tip shows again on the second ack, and the tool-progress tip is queued twice.

Run on Windows 11 with the repo's PM test environment's `python -m pytest` (`HERMES_HOME` set to a temp dir, `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`), not `scripts/run_tests.sh`.

I ran the 136 test files that touch the busy path, turn progress or onboarding on this branch. I then reran the 34 files with failures on unmodified `main`. Every failure in those files also fails on `main`, except 25 in 6 files (setup, daybreak, welcome trial, inventory pricing), which only failed in the larger run. Run on their own, those 6 files give the same result on `main` and on this branch (1 failed, 85 passed), and running the new test file first changes nothing. So those 25 depend on test order in the larger run, not on this change. The failures that remain come from this Windows machine's environment and fail on `main` too.

One more note: on both trees, one test in this set sometimes hangs while waiting on a `tui_gateway.compute_host` child process. It hung on `main` in one run and on this branch in another, so it is unrelated to this change.

`python scripts/check` passes, and the lefthook pre-commit ran clean.

prs.title: feat(delegation): opt-in read-only memory lookups for subagents (delegation.memory_read)
prs.body:
## What

Opt-in, read-only long-term memory lookups for delegated subagents: `delegation.memory_read` (default **false**).

Today every subagent runs with `skip_memory=True`, so a child can't look up anything the parent's memory provider knows (past decisions, project facts, preferences), and the parent has to paste that context into the task by hand. Turning memory fully on for children would let them write, which is why it's off. This adds a narrow middle ground: a child may call the provider's **lookup** tools and nothing else.

Related: #68903, #30269.

## Design

- **The provider declares what is read-only.** New `MemoryProvider.read_only_tool_names()` (default `[]`). If a provider declares nothing, or the call raises, the child gets **no** memory (fails closed). Stock in-tree providers declare nothing yet, so with them the feature grants nothing until a provider opts in.
- **Config can only narrow.** `delegation.memory_read_tools` picks a subset of the declared set; it can never add a name. Malformed values (`0`, `{}`, `None`, `""`, `[" "]`) → no memory. Missing key or `[]` → the provider's declared set.
- **A child never gets a tool its parent lacks.** The grant is intersected with the parent's live tool surface; grandchildren get at most their parent's grant.
- **The parent's config decides**, resolved before entering a delegated profile scope, so a child profile can't switch it on.
- **Read-only from the start.** The manager is restricted *before* `provider.initialize()`, and `initialize()` receives `read_only=True` so providers can skip startup writes (RetainDB skips its write-queue replay and SOUL seed). Every automatic hook is off for a read-only manager: turn sync, prefetch/queue_prefetch, session end, session switch (incl. compression), delegation note, memory-write mirror, best-effort pre_compress. Dispatch refuses any tool outside the allowlist before it reaches the provider.
- **Identity:** the child gets the parent's memory-scoping identity (`user_id`) only, not gateway routing (session key, chat/thread IDs).
- **Toolset rules still apply.** Only delegation's own built-in `memory` denial is bypassed (via an explicit spawn-time grant, not a list marker). `enabled_toolsets` narrowing, disabled `all`/`*`, and a caller's explicit `memory` denial (incl. a later refresh with `disabled_override=['memory']`) still withhold the tools. The built-in `memory` tool (MEMORY.md/USER.md) stays blocked; those files aren't loaded.
- **Shared instances are refused.** A child never reuses, re-initializes or shuts down a provider instance owned by another manager (e.g. a singleton entry point): it gets no memory instead. A handed-in shared manager is detached, not restricted.

Docs: delegation guide (new "Read-only memory lookups" section), configuration reference, memory-provider plugin guide (`read_only_tool_names()`, the `read_only=True` init kwarg).

## Known limits (all fail closed: no access, never extra access)

- With `plugins.isolation: host`, read-only children get no memory: proxied instances can't be reliably checked for sharing.
- A provider that only exposes tool schemas after `initialize()` grants nothing (the allowlist is fixed before init).
- A tool refresh that changes the child's disabled set drops the grant for the rest of that child's run.
- Out of scope: a plugin that registers write tools through `ctx.register_tool` in a *regular* toolset reaches children that inherit that toolset today, with or without this setting. This PR doesn't change that path.

## Evidence

- **Tests:** 4 files (unit, spawn-policy, RetainDB, real-import E2E with an isolated `HERMES_HOME` + stub provider plugin: config.yaml → `delegate_task` spawn → child offers only the declared lookup → a write call is refused; default-off unchanged). On this branch: **99 passed**. Same 99 tests with the code reverted to `main`: 75 fail (the 24 that pass cover behaviour that must stay unchanged). Memory + delegation suites run serially on both: identical failure set (2 pre-existing stall-stop tests fail on `main` too). `ruff` clean.
- **Live check (final design)** on a real gateway install, back-ported to the current release, with an external plugin-catalog memory provider that was given a one-method `read_only_tool_names()` returning its recall tool: a delegated child was offered only that recall tool and answered a recall query about a past project date correctly. The save, reflect and built-in `memory` tools were absent from its surface; `tool_search` for them returned no matches; `tool_call` by both prefixed and bare names returned "not a known tool name". Nothing was written to the provider. The same provider without the method gives children no memory, as designed, so **external providers need the one-method opt-in** (documented in the plugin guide).
- **Small A/B** (5 delegated tasks, with vs. without read-only lookups): the lookup arm won 2, tied 2, was faster on 1; 21 lookups, 0 write attempts. Small and single-run, so take it as a signal, not a benchmark.

## Notes for reviewers

- `agent/agent_init.py` is not grown (new logic lives in `agent/memory_read_policy.py`).
- Locally (macOS) a few pre-existing failures are unrelated and identical on `main`: a heartbeat timing test, a `/var` vs `/private/var` path comparison, and three async tests that need `pytest-asyncio` in the venv.

prs.title: Seedance 2.5 Flash is now a video generation option (FAL)
prs.body:
fal released the fast tier of ByteDance's Seedance 2.5 on Nov 15, but Hermes offered only the slower flagship. Now "Seedance 2.5 Flash" is an option in `hermes tools` → Video Generation and as `model="seedance-2.5-flash"`, for text-to-video and image-to-video.

**Outcome:** one new FAL video family, `seedance-2.5-flash`, routed to `bytedance/seedance-2.5/flash/{text-to-video,image-to-video}`.

## Changes
- `plugins/video_gen/fal/__init__.py::FAL_FAMILIES`: new `seedance-2.5-flash` entry. Its capability flags match the existing `seedance-2.5` entry because fal's OpenAPI schemas for the two are the same: string duration enum `"4".."30"`, `480p`/`720p` (base also offers 1080p/4k), `generate_audio` toggle, no `seed`, image-to-video `aspect_ratio` is `auto` only (dropped on i2v).
- Test: `bytedance/seedance-2.5/flash` (a config stem without the modality leaf) resolves to Flash, not to the base family. Red on `origin/main`, where it resolves to nothing.

| `video_gen.model` / tool `model=` | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `seedance-2.5-flash` | unknown family → falls back to the default | Flash endpoints |
| `bytedance/seedance-2.5/flash` | unresolved | `seedance-2.5-flash` |
| `bytedance/seedance-2.5` | `seedance-2.5` | `seedance-2.5` (unchanged) |

Default family stays `pixverse-v6`.

## Validation
- Schemas: `fal.ai/api/openapi/queue/openapi.json?endpoint_id=bytedance/seedance-2.5/flash/{text,image}-to-video`, compared field by field against `bytedance/seedance-2.5/text-to-video`.
- Live, real `FALVideoGenProvider.generate()` on this branch, direct `FAL_KEY` route:
  - t2v `model="seedance-2.5-flash", duration=4, resolution="480p", aspect_ratio="16:9"` → `success: true`, endpoint `bytedance/seedance-2.5/flash/text-to-video`, 1.49 MB mp4. `ffprobe`: video 854x480 4.04 s + audio stream 4.09 s
  - i2v with an image URL → `success: true`, endpoint `bytedance/seedance-2.5/flash/image-to-video`, `modality: image`, 0.91 MB mp4
  - control: `seedance-2.0-mini`, same prompt → `success: true`
- Tests: `tests/plugins/video_gen/` + `tests/tools/test_video_generation*.py`: 117 passed. `scripts/check --only health`: ok.

## Cost / trust
- fal list price: about $0.144/s at 480p and $0.309/s at 720p (token-billed, $0.014 per 1K tokens). A 4 s 480p clip is about $0.58. Same vendor, key and data flow as the existing Seedance families. No new dependency.

**Not covered:** the Nous-managed FAL gateway leg. This host's managed route needs the real Nous OAuth, which is not copied into scratch homes, and recent token-billed fal slugs (GPT Image 2.6, MiniMax H3 Image, Seedream 5.5) have all returned `unsupported_pricing_meter` on managed until the Portal meters them. Expect the same here until then. The managed error path already tells the user to set `FAL_KEY` or pick another model.

prs.title: fix(tui): resume a fallback-served chat on its picked model and provider
prs.body: ## What does this PR do? > **Design choice to settle first: this PR and #118982 can't both merge.** Both stop a resumed chat from getting a mismatched model and provider. This PR resumes on the user's pick (reader side). #118982 resumes on the fallback by copying the serving route into `model_config` (write side), which would also defeat this reader. If you prefer resume-on-fallback, #118982 is the way to go and this PR can be closed. The reasoning is under Reviewers. A chat whose **first** successful call was served by a configured fallback provider is rebuilt from `state.db` with the wrong pair: the fallback's **model** on the primary's **provider**. A rebuild happens after an app restart, a Desktop auto-update, an idle reap, an LRU eviction or a backend crash. Reattaching to a chat that is still live is not affected. This isn't only a display problem: - The Desktop model picker shows the fallback model checked under the primary provider's group, a pairing nobody configured. - The next turn really sends the fallback model to the primary provider. That call fails, and the fallback chain then "falls back" from model X to the same model X. **Root cause.** Two writes are each correct on their own, but together they produce a bad read: 1. `hermes_state_usage.py::update_token_counts` (`first_accounted_route`, from `d14006ead2`) rewrites `sessions.model` / `billing_provider` to the route that served the first accounted call. That's right for billing and telemetry, and it leaves `model_config` alone. 2. `tui_gateway/agent_factory.py::_stored_session_runtime_overrides` (in `tui_gateway/server.py` before `main` moved it) takes the model from the column (`row.model or model_config.model`) and, since #126159, the provider from `SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime` (nested `gateway_runtime`, then the top-level pick, then `billing_provider` to fill a missing provider). So it combines the fallback model with the picked provider, and a pick saved without a provider gets the fallback's provider. **Fix.** Read the model from the same record the route comes from: - Rows whose `gateway_runtime` carries a provider keep the column model. The gateway's route sync writes both together, so that pair is unchanged from `main`. - Rows with a confirmed Browser/API `browser_model_lock` whose model equals the column also keep the column model. The lock writes the column but not the pick, so these resume exactly as on `main`. A fallback rewrite makes the column differ from the lock, so the fix still applies to those rows. - Otherwise the model comes from `model_config`'s pick, and the column is used only for older rows without one. - `billing_provider` is passed to the shared reader only when the resolved model is the column's model, because it is the provider that served that model. `sessions.model` and `billing_*` stay the billing record, and `d14006ead2`'s behaviour is unchanged. `SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime` and the CLI reader are unchanged. Mid-chat switches still resume correctly, because every writer that saves one updates `model_config.model` together with the column, or writes `gateway_runtime` with it: - TUI/Desktop `model.switch`: `_persist_live_session_runtime` → `_runtime_model_config`. - CLI and gateway `/model`: `update_session_model(provider=…)`, which writes the top-level pick and `gateway_runtime`. - Gateway turns: `_sync_session_model_from_agent`, which writes the column with `gateway_runtime`. ## Related Issue Fixes the resume half of #118969. That issue also asks the chat picker to hide non-chat models (for example image models); this PR doesn't do that, so it shouldn't close the issue. - **#118982 (open): the alternative design for the same bug.** It syncs `model_config` to the fallback when the first accounted route rewrites the column, so resume lands on the fallback. This PR resumes on the pick. See the note at the top and Reviewers. - #110282 (closed) took the same resume-on-fallback approach in this function. - #126159 (merged) moved the route read into `SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime`, which addressed #125942. It did not change where the model comes from, which is the half this PR fixes. - #110279: same symptom from a gateway-written row. Rows that carry `gateway_runtime` keep the gateway's own pair here, as on `main`. - #121506: argues a resumed chat should go back to the primary instead of staying on the fallback. This PR agrees for the TUI/Desktop reader but does not close it: the CLI `--resume` reader is unchanged. - Complementary: #121533 (saves the requested route across fallback turns, on the write side). It prevents new bad rows; this PR repairs rows that are already mixed when they are read. #121533 edits `tui_gateway/server.py` on an older base, where this function lived before `main` moved it to `tui_gateway/agent_factory.py`, so whichever lands second rebases and keeps both invariants. Also seen in a real Desktop session: the primary failed on the first turn, the fallback answered, Desktop auto-updated, and the next turn logged `model= provider=`. ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) ## Changes Made - `tui_gateway/agent_factory.py`: `_stored_session_runtime_overrides` takes the model from the record the route comes from, and keeps `billing_provider` out of the route when the model is not the column's. - `tests/tui_gateway/test_resume_switched_provider_endpoint.py` (all new tests live here; `test_tui_gateway_server.py` is over its code-health line cap): - Seam test, parametrized over a picked pair and over a picked model with no provider. The fallback route in the row must never be mixed with the pick. - Runs through a real `SessionDB`. It creates the row with the pick, runs `update_token_counts` with the fallback route, and checks two things: the billing columns hold the fallback, and resume restores the picked pair. - Two contract tests that pass on `main` and guard against a simpler "pick first" change, which fails both: - a gateway turn after a Desktop pick resumes on the gateway's pair, never the older Desktop pick on the gateway's provider; - a confirmed Browser/API lock (through the real `update_session_runtime_lock`) resumes on the locked model, not the Desktop pick it replaced. **Not modified:** `hermes_state_usage.py` (`first_accounted_route` keeps writing the serving route to the billing columns), `SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime`, the session writers, and every existing exemption in `_stored_session_runtime_overrides` (room plumbing, Bot Chat / `composer_override_profile`, foreign-endpoint drop, stale-provider healing, `_BARE_BILLING_PROVIDERS`). **Does not fix:** the CLI `hermes --resume` reader (`stored_session_route`), which still takes the model from the column. See Reviewers. **Known limitations** (each behaves exactly as on `main`): - A chat with no stored provider (`model_config = {model: M}`) whose first call a fallback served under the same model id `M` still resumes on the fallback's provider. That row is identical to the stale-provider-healing row pinned by `test_resume_overrides_get_no_stale_provider` (`9ddc6fb23a`), where `billing_provider` stands in for the profile default, so the reader cannot tell them apart. The write side (#121533, recording the requested route) is where this becomes distinguishable. - A confirmed Browser/API lock that changed provider as well as model resumes on the locked model with the Desktop pick's provider. The reader takes the route from `session_gateway_runtime`, which doesn't read the lock. - A `/model` switch made before the first accounted call writes `gateway_runtime`; if a fallback then serves that first call, the chat resumes on the fallback model with the `/model` provider. ## Reproduction **Before the fix, in the Desktop app.** Setup: Provider A is the primary and always returns 503, Provider B is the fallback, and a Desktop chat is picked on Provider A. Send one message, which Provider B answers. Quit and relaunch the app, then reopen the chat. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d602cd81-170f-42bc-823f-b6204b6514be The picker shows the fallback **Model B** checked under **Provider A (primary)**, and the Provider B group is gone: **Before and after, end to end without the UI.** This uses the real `_make_agent`, `AIAgent.run_conversation`, `SessionDB`, `_persist_live_session_runtime` and resume, against two local OpenAI-compatible mocks: prov-a always returns 503, prov-b answers. It ran in a throwaway `HERMES_HOME` with the provider credential env vars unset. (Recorded on the original branch, before the rebase onto #126159.) | | Resumed model + provider | Turn 2 requests | |---|---|---| | Before | `model-b` + `custom:prov-a` | prov-a/**model-b** ×2, then prov-b | | After | `model-a` + `custom:prov-a` | prov-a/model-a (retried), then prov-b/model-b (normal fallback) | In both runs the stored row keeps `model=model-b`, `billing_provider=prov-b`, so the billing record is unchanged. ## How to Test 1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_resume_switched_provider_endpoint.py`: 9 passed. With `main`'s `tui_gateway/agent_factory.py`, the 3 fix cases fail and the 2 contract cases still pass. 2. Every test file that calls `_stored_session_runtime_overrides`, `session_gateway_runtime`, `stored_session_route`, the resume entry points, `update_session_runtime_lock` or `browser_model_lock` (252 files after the rebase onto current `main`, including `tests/tui_gateway/test_resume_*.py`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_resume_model_restore.py` and `tests/gateway/test_session_api.py`): 2972 passed, 9 failed, 92 skipped. The same 9 fail on `main` without this change (macOS environment tests: 8 state DB auto-vacuum and connection-lifecycle tests in `tests/hermes_state/test_hermes_state.py`, and `tests/tui_gateway/test_profiles_list_canonical_session.py::test_canonical_session_scoped_per_profile_db`). 3. `tests/hermes_state/` (recorded before the rebase): 1470 passed, 63 failed, 50 skipped. 62 of them also fail on `main` without this change (macOS environment tests: auto-vacuum holder gates, cross-VM filesystem detection, FTS admission). The other, `test_concurrent_quarantine_no_clobber`, failed once under the parallel run and passes 3/3 in isolation on both `main` and this branch; it doesn't touch the resume path. 4. Manual: configure a primary that fails plus a fallback, pick the primary in a Desktop chat, send one message, restart the app and reopen the chat. The picker shows the primary pair, and the next turn tries the primary model on the primary provider before falling back. ## Reviewers - **Which consistent pair should a resumed chat get: the pick or the fallback?** This PR and #118982 both stop the mismatched pair; they differ on this, and they conflict if both merge. This PR resumes on the user's pick, because: - fallback is turn-scoped by design: `restore_primary_runtime` (`agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`) runs at the start of every turn so a live chat retries the primary. Resuming on the pick gives a rebuilt chat the same behaviour; - resuming on the fallback makes it the rebuilt agent's primary, so the chat never returns to the primary even after it recovers (#121506); - `sessions.model` / `billing_*` stay the record of what served the call, and `model_config` stays the record of the pick. The cost: if the primary is still broken, the first turn after each resume fails once before falling back. For a pick that can never work (the image model in #118969), that happens on every resume until the user re-picks. #118982 avoids it. If you prefer the resume-on-fallback design, #118982 is the way to go and this PR can be closed. - **Rows that carry `gateway_runtime`.** These keep the column model, because the gateway's route sync writes it together with `gateway_runtime`. A Desktop pick made after a gateway turn updates the column but leaves `gateway_runtime`, so it resumes exactly as on `main`: the picked model with the gateway's provider. That precedence comes from #126159, and this PR doesn't change it. - **Rows written before `56a41715dc` (2026-08-14).** On those builds, a CLI or gateway `/model` switch updated the model column but not `model_config.model`. If such a switch happened on a Desktop or TUI row, the chat now resumes on the model that was picked before the switch, with its matching provider. Before, it resumed on a mismatched pair. Is that acceptable for those old rows? - **Picked model with no stored provider.** If the model column holds a different model, the chat now resumes on the picked model with the configured default provider, instead of the fallback route. - **api_server browser lock.** `update_session_runtime_lock` writes the model column but not `model_config.model`. A confirmed lock whose model still equals the column is treated like `gateway_runtime`: Desktop resume keeps the locked model, as on `main`, so Desktop and the API don't disagree about the chat's model. Unconfirmed locks don't get this exception; api_server only persists them when it creates a new session, which has no Desktop pick. - **Out of scope: the CLI `hermes --resume` path.** `stored_session_route` in `hermes_cli/cli_model_switch_mixin.py` has a related version of this bug. It takes the model from the column and the provider from `session_gateway_runtime`, so a Desktop row resumed from the CLI would still get the mismatched pair. I plan to fix it in a separate PR unless you'd rather it land here. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the Contributing Guide - [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits - [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix - [x] Tests run with `scripts/run_tests.sh` (see How to Test; the failures listed there also fail on `main`) - [x] I've added tests for my changes - [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26.6 ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] Documentation: N/A - [x] `cli-config.yaml.example`: N/A - [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md`: N/A - [x] Cross-platform impact: N/A --- Model and harness: Claude Opus 5.5 via Hermes Agent.

prs.title: feat(catalog): update hermes-borealis to 0.3.0
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Updates hermes-borealis from 0.2.0 to 0.3.0. I own and maintain the plugin repository.

This replaces #156010 (0.2.2), which was still open when 0.3.0 was released. I'm closing that one so there is a single pin to review; this PR includes everything it did.

Changes since the current pin:
- **The moon shows tonight's real phase (0.3.0).** The night scene's fixed crescent is replaced by the moon in its current phase. The phase is computed in the plugin from the system clock (mean lunar motion plus six periodic terms); nothing is fetched. Contributed by ShawnCRMer in [Adolanium/hermes-borealis#3](https://github.com/Adolanium/hermes-borealis/pull/3).
- **The scene sits further back in conversations (0.2.1, 0.2.2).** Once a chat has text, the scene canvas fades to 15% opacity in dark mode (it was 26%) and to 9% in light mode, so the app's grey tool-call lines stay above 4.5:1 contrast over the scene. The empty chat still shows the scene at full strength.
- **The sessions sidebar has a veil (0.2.1).** It now has a translucent fill in the theme's background colour: 55% in conversations and 82% on the empty chat.
- **New screenshots (0.2.1).** The night and day shots and the banner were retaken at 0.2.1. They predate 0.3.0, so the night shot still shows the old crescent.

No SDK, scanner, permission or Hermes core change is required.

## Disclosure changes for review

Two wording changes in the entry's description:
- "sidebar edge" becomes "sidebar edge and background", because the theme's stylesheet now sets a background colour on the sessions sidebar while the theme is active.
- The list of what the plugin does while active gains "reads the system clock to draw the moon in its current phase". The plugin calls `new Date()` once per frame and passes one number to its shader.

Everything else in the disclosure is unchanged. These releases add no network requests, file access, agent tools or hooks.

`hermes plugins validate` reports the same two warnings as at the current pin: no `__init__.py` (manifest-only plugin) and catalog rule 8. Rule 8 lists 24 app markup selectors in `desktop/plugin.js`, up from 22: the two new ones are the sidebar veil on the empty chat and the light-mode scene opacity. 0.3.0 adds none.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- Change only `plugin-catalog/hermes-borealis.yaml`: the full commit pin, the quoted version label, the `image:` URL, the two `screenshots:` URLs, and the two description changes noted above.
- Pin [catalog-v0.3.0](https://github.com/Adolanium/hermes-borealis/releases/tag/catalog-v0.3.0) at `c514f28a8e58f179e6bae9e834d59598f102522f`. [Review the source diff](https://github.com/Adolanium/hermes-borealis/compare/c1ab3313172631808373a018d24ff69b7fbc0bfb...c514f28a8e58f179e6bae9e834d59598f102522f).
- Point `image:` and `screenshots:` at the same commit. `assets/catalog-banner.png` is there (200, `image/png`).

## How to Test

- `python scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` passes (2382 files).
- `hermes plugins validate` passes on the repository at the pinned commit (security scan `safe`, no core override, desktop surface inside the plugin SDK surface).
- The 0.2.x changes were exercised live in Hermes Desktop on macOS from a local checkout, in light and dark mode.
- The 0.3.0 moon was rendered from the plugin's shader in headless Chrome at 11 phases, and its phase function was checked against six known new and full moons between 2000 and 2026 (within 0.4 hours). It has not been exercised inside Hermes Desktop.

## Checklist

- [x] Checked existing catalog pins, release tags, and open catalog PRs.
- [x] Owner submission with a public immutable tag and a full 40-character SHA.
- [x] Conventional Commit; this PR changes one catalog entry only.
- [x] Relevant local plugin, scanner, and catalog checks passed.
- [x] No Hermes core code or dependency changes.
- [ ] Upstream admission CI passes at this PR's current head.
