prs.title: fix(gateway): keep admitted API inputs out of notification presentation
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Keeps an API caller's input from being recorded as a gateway notification. API admission sets `internal=True` for its existing trust handling, but `display_kind_for_event()` also uses that flag to classify the persisted user row as `internal_notification`.

The executor now marks an input restored from a committed `api_turn_v1` descriptor separately. That input gets the ordinary user-row presentation (`display_kind=None`), while `internal=True` and `allow_gateway_control=False` stay unchanged. A new internal follow-up on the same API source remains a notification. Client metadata does not select the new marker.

This changes new turns only; it does not rewrite existing transcript rows.

## Related Issue

Fixes #156802

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/session_ingress.py`: identify the admitted API input without changing its trust flags.
- `gateway/response_filters.py`: keep that input out of the machinery presentation kinds.
- `tests/gateway/test_api_input_presentation.py`: exercise real API admission through execution and check ordinary input, internal follow-ups, unchanged trust flags, submission identity and untrusted metadata.

## How to Test

Using a fresh PM-built Python 3.14.9 environment with the `dev`, `test` and `messaging` selections:

```bash
HERMES_PYTHON=/path/to/test-env/bin/python HERMES_TEST_FILE_RETRIES=0 scripts/run_tests.sh \
  tests/gateway/test_api_input_presentation.py \
  tests/gateway/test_display_admission.py \
  tests/gateway/test_api_cutover_contract.py \
  tests/gateway/test_api_canonical_projection.py \
  tests/gateway/test_automation_notification_category.py \
  tests/gateway/test_heartbeat_poller.py \
  tests/gateway/test_silence_after_reply_line.py -j 4 -q
/path/to/test-env/bin/python scripts/check --base origin/main
```

- Regression file on unmodified `40d1e95f`: 1 failed, 1 passed. The admitted input is classified as machinery, allowing a silence marker even with `reply_expected=True`.
- Candidate: 7 files, 46 passed, 0 failed.
- Full `scripts/check`: 21 checks passed; code-health 0 blocking, 0 advisory.

Manual reproduction used the actual CLI gateway (`python -m hermes_cli.main gateway run`), a disposable home, an authenticated `POST /v1/runs`, and a model peer listening only on loopback. The run returned 202 and reached terminal state with a stored assistant reply. On pristine base the stored user row had `display_kind='internal_notification'`; with this patch it had `display_kind=NULL`. No live model service or real credentials were used.

### Wider-run limitation

A separate 24-file API batch reported 63 passed and 1 failed on both pristine base and candidate in the same environment, with four workers and retries disabled. Both failures were `tests/gateway/test_api_admission_off_loop.py::test_admission_waits_for_the_writer_off_the_owner_loop[chat]`: its event-loop gap exceeded the 0.5-second assertion (base 0.537s, candidate 0.603s). That test passed when run alone on base. The underlying timing cause is not established; this PR does not change the assertion or claim the wider API suite is green. No full repository test run is claimed.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide.
- [x] The proposed commit follows Conventional Commits.
- [x] I searched open and closed PRs and the source for duplicate work.
- [x] This PR contains only changes for this defect.
- [x] Relevant tests pass through `scripts/run_tests.sh`, the implementation of `just test`, as listed above.
- [x] `just check` passes through its `python scripts/check` implementation.
- [x] Regression tests fail on the unfixed base for the intended reason.
- [x] Tested on Linux with Python 3.14.9, including the actual CLI/HTTP/persistence path.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Documentation: the admission comment explains why trust and presentation differ; no user-facing configuration changed.
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example`: N/A.
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md`: N/A; no workflow change.
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered: no OS-specific operations added; only Linux was tested.
- [x] Tool descriptions/schemas: N/A.

prs.title: fix(tools): tell the model to close the tab it opened in the browser_exec helpers digest
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The `browser_exec` description tells the model to open a tab with `new_tab(url)` but never says it can close it, so each run leaves a page tab behind on a shared browser. This adds one sentence to `_HELPERS_DIGEST`:

```diff
-new_tab(url) opens/navigates (use for the FIRST navigation), goto_url(url) navigates the current tab, ...
+new_tab(url) opens/navigates (use for the FIRST navigation) and returns the tab's targetId; when done, close it with close_tab(tid) in a finally block, and never close tabs you did not open. goto_url(url) navigates the current tab, ...
```

Text-only change to the schema description. `new_tab`, `close_tab` and the Lightpanda header (one page per session) are untouched.

## Related Issue

Refs #145386 (same gap; the earlier attempt #145812 was closed by its author without merging). Tracked in #127647.

## Type of Change

- [x] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Changes Made

- `tools/browser_use_cli.py`: one sentence in `_HELPERS_DIGEST`; rewrapped the neighbouring string literals only.
- `tests/fixtures/prompt_surface/`: regenerated with `scripts/ci/prompt_surface.py render` (`tools/browser_exec.json` carries the new sentence; `surfaces.json` `tool_tokens` +32 on each of the 9 surfaces).
- `tests/tools/test_browser_use_cli.py`: `TestSkillTextDescription.test_description_tells_model_to_close_its_own_tab` asserts the generated `browser_exec` description names `close_tab(`, the returned target id, the `finally` block, and never closing tabs it did not open.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_browser_use_cli.py tests/ci/test_prompt_surface.py -q` gives 88 passed, 0 failed.
2. Remove the new sentence from `_HELPERS_DIGEST`: the new test fails (`assert 'close_tab(' in 'Drive a real browser…'`); restore it and it passes.
3. `python scripts/check` passes (14 checks, ruff 0.15.22).

`close_tab(target=None)` and `new_tab(url)` returning the target id were checked in `browser_harness` 0.1.13 `helpers.py`. When the attached tab is blank, `new_tab` reuses it and returns its id, so `close_tab(tid)` closes that tab, the session's own blank tab.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. **Blast Radius:** prompt text only, one sentence added to every `browser_exec` description (a few tokens per request; the description changes once, so cached prefixes rebuild on the next session).

prs.title: fix(kanban): wake text reports the batch's current state, not its joined history
prs.body:
## What's wrong

A batched kanban wake can describe a card's superseded states as if they were current, and can pair a stale review verdict with a newer result.

Observed live: a card that was **reviewed and APPROVED** was delivered to the operator as:

```
Task t_896b2efb completed, handed off for review; the implementation is done,
review requested changes (BLOCK); implementation is not approved.
...
Result: Reviewed and APPROVED (round 3)
```

So the notification simultaneously says the work was approved and that it was blocked and not approved. The operator cannot tell which is true, and the only safe response is to go re-check the board by hand — which defeats the purpose of the wake.

## Why

In `gateway/kanban_watchers_notifier.py`:

- **:577** — `self.wake_kinds = {ev.kind for ev in self.d["events"] if ev.kind in _WAKE_KINDS}` collects *every* wake kind present in the batch.
- **:589** — `_parts = [t(f"gateway.kanban.wake.{k}") for k in _WAKE_KINDS if k in self.wake_kinds]` joins all of them in tuple order, regardless of which event is current.
- **:563-572** — `format_event` accumulates `wake_handoff` / `wake_review_detail` last-writer-wins across the batch, so the detail slots can come from a different event than the headline.

Each event is individually correct; the composition is not. A card that moved `review -> changes_requested -> review -> approved` within one batch renders all of those states at once.

## Fix

`build_wake_text` now:

1. selects only the newest wake event by `(created_at, id)`;
2. derives both detail slots from that same event, so headline and detail cannot disagree;
3. never emits a queued verdict for a card that is already `done` or `archived`.

Behaviour is unchanged for single-event batches — the common case is byte-identical.

## Tests

`tests/gateway/test_kanban_changes_requested_notifier.py` — 7 tests, **7 passed** on this head:

```
.......  [100%]
7 passed in 54.05s
```

Two of them fail on the base commit with the exact wrong message (verified by applying only the test file to an unmodified tree):

```
FAILED ...::test_batched_review_cycle_wake_names_only_the_current_state
FAILED ...::test_closed_card_never_wakes_with_a_superseded_block
```

2 files changed, +185/-18. `python -m py_compile` exits 0.

prs.title: fix(kanban): a per-profile cap hold is correctly idle, not "dispatcher stuck"
prs.body:
## What

The `dispatcher stuck` health warning is a false RED whenever ready work is held back only by `kanban.max_in_progress_per_profile`. The bad-tick counter treats "ready queue non-empty, 0 spawned" as a broken-profile signal, but the readiness probe (`has_spawnable_ready`) answers without honouring the per-profile cap — so a saturated cap, which is the dispatcher behaving *exactly as configured*, climbs `bad_ticks` forever and pages the operator at `venv, PATH, credentials`.

Measured on a production fleet: 812 `kanban dispatcher stuck` warnings in one gateway log, including one continuous 80-tick (~81 min) streak that reset only when the two capped workers were reclaimed and a third could finally spawn.

## The fix

Work the tick itself held back joins the existing "correctly idle" category — the same one the readiness probe already forms for control-plane `claim_task` lanes — instead of counting as stuck:

- **`held_ready_task_ids(result)`** — enumerates the per-task deliberate holds the tick recorded: `skipped_per_profile_capped`, `respawn_guarded`, `rate_limited`. Both health paths subtract these ids from the ready-queue probe via the new `exclude_task_ids` parameter on `has_spawnable_ready` / `has_spawnable_review`.
- **`whole_tick_hold(result)`** — `skipped_locked` (another dispatcher owns the board lock) and `memory_pressure` (the guard restricted new workers) hold the whole board for the tick; the probe skips that board entirely.
- **`describe_suppression()` now counts `per_profile_capped=N`** — so where the counter legitimately stays positive (the cap held some work back *while another profile is genuinely stuck*), the warning names the actual held-back reason instead of only pointing at profile health.

The cap policy itself is untouched — this fixes the telemetry, not the policy.

## Tests

`tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_dispatcher_stuck_telemetry.py` + `tests/gateway/test_kanban_dispatcher_stuck_hold.py`:

- **regression (red on pre-fix, green here):** a queue held only by the per-profile cap must not raise `dispatcher stuck` — driven through the real `_cmd_daemon` health callback with two real `dispatch_once` ticks saturating `max_in_progress_per_profile=1`.
- whole-tick holds (memory-pressure shape) are correctly idle too (red on pre-fix).
- mixed case: cap held two tasks while a second profile's spawn keeps failing → the warning still fires **and** names `per_profile_capped=2` (red on pre-fix: it fired without naming the cap).
- positive control: an unexplained zero-spawn tick with no holds still warns — the real signal is preserved.
- gateway probe: `ready_nonempty(results)` subtracts per-board held ids and skips whole-tick holds.
- unit pins for `held_ready_task_ids` / `whole_tick_hold` / `describe_suppression`.

Verified locally: the 7 new tests fail 6/7 on the pre-fix base (the positive control passes on both, by design) and pass 7/7 post-fix; the surrounding family (per-profile cap, host cap, memory guard, dispatch lock, CLI passthrough, review lifecycle, core functionality, claim allowlist, gateway dispatcher harness — 133 tests) shows zero new failures vs the base (2 pre-existing worktree-environment failures, identical on pristine `main`). `ruff` clean on all touched files; `ty` diagnostics byte-identical to base.

## Disclosures

- CI ran locally (macOS, Python 3.14); no fork-receipt CI lane was collected for this PR — happy to run one if the full-suite receipt is wanted.
- `contributors/emails/bunnyfu@gmail.com` is re-added here because the attribution check needs the mapping in this PR's tree; note it duplicates the same file added in #149023 — whichever lands first wins, the other needs a trivial rebase.
- The standalone `hermes kanban daemon --force` path never enforces the per-profile cap today (`run_daemon` doesn't pass it), so the cap half of the fix is future-proofing there; the guard / rate-limit / board-lock / memory-pressure holds it shares with the gateway path are live on both.

prs.title: fix(state): retry transient persist receipt timeouts before latching worker failure
prs.body:
## Problem

Managed workers (kanban, delegation, cron) intermittently died with exit code 1 and `WorkerPersistenceError: worker_receipt_timeout` at close-time flush, killing otherwise-finished runs. Observed repeatedly on this host's kanban coder workers (runs crashed mid-task and after completion; the dispatcher's retries re-hit the same failure).

The worker persists every write as an RPC to the owner gateway (`worker.persist`) with a 20-second reply budget (`_OwnerLink.receive(20)`). When the owner is slow to reply — a loaded host, memory pressure — `TimeoutError('worker_receipt_timeout')` is raised. `retry_pending()` latches ANY exception as `self.failure`, which is sticky for the rest of the process. Every later store operation then raises, including `flush_token_counts()` during teardown, so the managed worker exits 1 even though its work succeeded.

## Fix

In `agent/runtime_session_store.py::retry_pending`, treat `TimeoutError` as transient: re-attempt the same pending journal entry up to 3 times (0.5s pause between attempts) before latching. This is safe by the journal's existing design — a failed write stays pending, replays are idempotent, and the owner resolves the original receipt on an exact retry (`_connection()` redials on any exception, so each attempt rides a fresh owner connection). All other failure classes (filesystem, capacity, owner_unavailable) remain sticky exactly as before.

## Tests

- `test_receipt_timeout_is_transient_and_replays`: two missed receipts then success → write lands, `failure` stays None, journal empties, `close()` does not raise.
- `test_receipt_timeout_exhaustion_still_latches`: persistent timeouts → exactly 3 re-attempts, sticky failure latched, later writes refused, `close()` raises the latched error.

Both files green: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_runtime_session_store.py` (9/9), plus `ruff check` clean on the changed files.

prs.title: fix(cli): bare `hermes secrets <provider>` recurses instead of printing help
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`hermes secrets bitwarden` (or `onepassword`) with no leaf action crashes with `RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded` (~1000 frames of `_dispatch_secrets` calling itself).

`register_subcommands()` installs `func` defaults on the leaf handlers (`setup`/`status`/...) but leaves the intermediate group parser (`bitwarden`, `onepassword`) without one. argparse propagates the parent parser's `set_defaults` into child parsers, so the group parser silently inherits the `secrets` parser's `_dispatch_secrets` as its `func`. Dispatch then sees `secrets_command` set and redispatches through `args.func`, which is itself, forever.

The fix installs a help-printing default on the group parser at registration time, inside `register_subcommands()` itself, so every current and future provider group exits 0 with its own usage text instead of inheriting the parent dispatcher. This addresses the mechanism-level concern raised in review on the earlier attempt (#93655): patching only the two current children reintroduces the bug with the next provider.

## Related Issue

Fixes #92799

Supersedes the stalled #92800 and the withdrawn #93655 (both patched the dispatch site in `main.py` rather than the registration helper; #92800's review explicitly asked for child-parser help output, which this approach produces naturally).

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/_secrets_common.py`: `register_subcommands()` now sets a default `func` on the parent (group) parser that prints the group's own help and returns 0.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_lazy_secrets_dispatch.py`: three subprocess regression tests covering bare `secrets`, `secrets bitwarden`, and `secrets onepassword`. Each exits 0, prints the right usage line, and never emits `RecursionError`.

## How to Test

1. `python -m hermes_cli.main secrets bitwarden`. Before: RecursionError. After: prints the bitwarden group help, exit 0.
2. `python -m hermes_cli.main secrets onepassword`. Prints onepassword group help (including `sync`), exit 0.
3. `python -m hermes_cli.main secrets`. Still prints parent help, exit 0.
4. `scripts/run_tests.sh --require-paths tests/hermes_cli/test_lazy_secrets_dispatch.py`. 9 passed.

## Checklist

### Code
- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate (closest: #92800, #93655, both stale/withdrawn with a different approach; see above)

prs.title: ElevenLabs speech-to-text now uses Scribe v3 and Scribe v3 Live by default
prs.body:
If you use ElevenLabs for speech-to-text, Hermes still sent your voice notes and live dictation to last year's Scribe v2 models. ElevenLabs shipped Scribe v3 on Nov 10; Hermes now uses it by default, at the same price, and you can still pin the old model in config.

**Outcome:** ElevenLabs STT defaults to `scribe_v3` (files) and `scribe_v3_live` (`stt.streaming`), and the live model can now be changed in config.

## Changes
- `tools/transcription_common.py`: `STT_MODEL_CATALOG["elevenlabs"]` = `scribe_v3, scribe_v2, scribe_v1` (default first). The `hermes tools` picker, dashboard select and auto-correction read this table.
- `tools/transcription_streaming.py`: live default `scribe_v2_realtime` → `scribe_v3_live`. It was a hard-coded constant; `stt.elevenlabs.streaming_model` now picks the model, the same way `stt.openai.streaming_model` already does.
- `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py`, `hermes_cli/web_server_config.py`, `hermes_cli/tools_config.py`, Desktop `settings/constants.ts`: new defaults and a `stt.elevenlabs.streaming_model` select.
- **Bug fix found on the way:** `tools/voice_client_config.py` (Desktop provider-direct dictation) read `stt.elevenlabs.model`, a key nothing writes (the config key is `model_id`). A user's pinned model was ignored on the Desktop direct route and the default was always used. It now reads `model_id`, the same key the relay path reads.
- Docs: `voice-mode.md` live-provider table + an ElevenLabs row in the STT comparison table.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| voice note / file STT, no pin | `scribe_v2` | `scribe_v3` |
| live dictation (`stt.streaming: true`) | `scribe_v2_realtime` (fixed) | `scribe_v3_live`; `stt.elevenlabs.streaming_model: scribe_v2_realtime` pins the old one |
| Desktop direct STT with `model_id: scribe_v2` | sent the default (pin ignored) | sends `scribe_v2` |

Existing configs that name `model_id: scribe_v2` keep it. Only unpinned installs (and fresh ones) move.

## Validation (live, real ElevenLabs API, ELEVENLABS_API_KEY)
- `POST /v1/speech-to-text` with a bogus id lists the valid ids: `scribe_v1, scribe_v1_experimental, scribe_v2, scribe_v2_medical, scribe_v3`. `scribe_v3` with `tag_audio_events`/`diarize`/`language_code` returns 200 with words and `speaker_id`, the fields Hermes already sends.
- Realtime WebSocket `wss://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/speech-to-text/realtime?model_id=scribe_v3_live&audio_format=pcm_16000&commit_strategy=vad` (the URL Hermes builds): `session_started`, then 11 partials and a `committed_transcript`. The live model also adds `turn_probability` to partials, which the existing handler ignores.
- Through Hermes on this branch, in a scratch `HERMES_HOME` (`stt.provider: elevenlabs`, `stt.streaming: true`), on an ElevenLabs-TTS clip "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog near the riverbank.":
  - `transcribe_audio()` → `{"success": true, "transcript": "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog near the riverbank.", "provider": "elevenlabs"}` (resolved model `scribe_v3`)
  - `open_streaming_session()` → URL `model_id=scribe_v3_live…`, 12 partials, final `The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog near the riverbank`
  - with `streaming_model: scribe_v2_realtime` → URL `model_id=scribe_v2_realtime`, 4 partials, same transcript (rollback path works)
- Response headers: `fiat-cost-before-overages: 0.000165` for the ~3.6 s clip on both v2 and v3, so v3 costs the same as v2.
- Tests: 2 invariant tests, both red on `origin/main` (files swapped to base) and green here: `test_elevenlabs_live_model_defaults_to_scribe_v3_live_and_follows_config`, `test_elevenlabs_stt_direct_uses_the_configured_model_id`. `tests/tools/test_transcription_{streaming,tools}.py` + `test_voice_client_config.py`: 101 passed. `scripts/check --only health`: ok.

## Cost / trust
- Price (elevenlabs.io/pricing/api): Scribe v3 $0.20/h, Scribe v3 Live $0.22/h, the same as v2 / v2 Realtime. No new dependency, credential, endpoint or data flow: same host, same key, same request shape.
- Vendor claims (elevenlabs.io/blog/scribe-v3): 27% fewer word errors than Scribe v2 across 102 languages (internal FLEURS), 17% fewer diarization errors with 3+ speakers; v3 Live is 43% lower semantic WER than v2 Realtime and adds realtime diarization.

**Not covered:** no Desktop UI screenshot of the new `stt.elevenlabs.streaming_model` select (it is one more entry in an existing config-field list, rendered by the generic field component); the CLI/TUI voice-mode recorder was not driven by microphone. The streaming session it opens was exercised directly above.

prs.title: fix(desktop): show new empty Bot roster sections with several gateways
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

With more than one gateway connection, **Bots › + › New section** saved the section but drew it nowhere. The section reached `$botSections` and plugin storage, but in multi-gateway mode the roster only draws user sections inside each gateway bucket (`renderUserSections(rows, '<gateway>:')`). Inside a bucket, an empty named section was drawn only while a drag was in flight:

```ts
.filter(block => block.rows.length || (block.id && (!nested || dragging)))
```

A section you have just created is always empty, so it stayed invisible until you happened to start dragging a Bot. Single-gateway rosters were not affected. The behaviour came in with e9dd0bf5d5, which nested user sections under gateway buckets.

This PR keeps the gateway-first layout and:

1. **Draws every named section that has no row in any bucket once, at the top level, below the gateway buckets.** It uses the same block as a nested section: drop zone, heading with the rename / move / delete menu, and the dashed "Drag bots here" slot. Filing a Bot into it moves the section into that Bot's gateway bucket, as before.
2. **Keeps cross-gateway filing by drag.** While a drag is under way, each bucket also offers, empty, the named sections that already have a row in another bucket. A Bot of gateway B can then be dropped into a section that so far only holds Bots of gateway A, even when A's bucket is folded. A section with no row anywhere is not repeated per bucket: it keeps its single top-level block. Nothing changes at rest. prs.title: fix(agent): keep a key_cmd token provider when rebuilding a routed client
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

An `AIAgent` built without an explicit `api_key`/`base_url` gets its client from the provider router: `_routed_client_kwargs` calls `resolve_provider_client`, then rebuilds an OpenAI client from `_client_kwargs_from_routed` (`agent/agent_init.py`). That function copied only `client.api_key`.

A `key_cmd` provider (and an Entra ID one) hands the SDK a per-request token provider. The OpenAI SDK stores it in `_api_key_provider` and sets `.api_key` to `""`. The rebuilt client therefore had no credential, and with the current SDK agent init fails:

```
RuntimeError: Failed to initialize OpenAI client: Missing credentials. Please pass an `api_key`, ...
```

The fix passes the token provider through uncalled when the routed client has one, the same way `_swap_fallback_clients` in `agent/client_lifecycle.py` already does for the fallback client. The token is still minted per request, so short-lived tokens keep working. A static-key client is unchanged.

The file is above the 2,000-line cap, so the change is line-neutral (the docstring now names the credential it mirrors).

## Related Issue

No dedicated issue. Same credential class as #109837, and the closed consolidation PR #109851 (not merged) also touched this function. Nothing open covers this call site.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `agent/agent_init.py`: `_client_kwargs_from_routed` uses the client's `_api_key_provider` when it is callable, else `client.api_key`.
- `tests/agent/test_agent_init_routed_key_cmd.py` (new):
  - the routed kwargs carry the provider itself, uncalled;
  - end to end: a temp `HERMES_HOME` whose `config.yaml` names a `key_cmd` provider pointing at a local HTTP server, an `AIAgent` built with no explicit key, and one chat completion. The server must receive `Authorization: Bearer <minted token>`.

## How to Test

1. In a fresh `HERMES_HOME`, configure a provider with `key_cmd` and no static key:
   ```yaml
   model:
     provider: dbx
     default: m1
   providers:
     dbx:
       base_url: http://127.0.0.1:9/v1
       api_mode: chat_completions
       key_cmd: printf minted-token
   ```
2. Build an agent without an explicit key: `AIAgent(model="m1", provider="dbx", quiet_mode=True)`. On `main` this raises `Failed to initialize OpenAI client: Missing credentials`. With this PR the agent starts and its client carries the token provider.
3. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_agent_init_routed_key_cmd.py`: both tests fail on `main` (the first with `'' is <function ...>`, the second with the "Missing credentials" error) and pass here.

Also run with `scripts/run_tests.sh`:

- the init and credential tests: `tests/agent/test_command_token_source.py`, `test_init_fallback_refusal_warning.py`, `test_init_fallback_on_exhausted_pool.py`, `test_init_exhausted_pool_billing_error.py`, `test_openai_client_lifecycle.py`, `test_meta_agent_init.py`, `test_per_model_threshold_init_ordering.py`, `test_serves_routed_profile_pin.py`: 84 passed.
- the whole `tests/agent/` directory: 13,129 passed. The files that did not pass on this Mac:
  - `test_compaction_prompt_rebuild.py` (3 tests): fails the same way on unmodified `main` (`/var` vs `/private/var` in the workspace root).
  - `test_inline_edit_persistence.py`: hits the runner's 300 s file timeout on unmodified `main` too.
  - `test_compression_rotation_state.py`: hits the 300 s cap here; on `main` it passes in 290.7 s. It builds every agent with an explicit `api_key`/`base_url`, so it never reaches `_client_kwargs_from_routed`.

Those tests, helper sources, dependency locks and desktop test-runner inputs are unchanged by the 99-commit base update; the tests were not rerun for this rebase. The final earlier rerun used an explicit existing Python interpreter and did not invoke setup or launch Electron. An earlier run omitted that interpreter and triggered native setup against the shared tool store. Its temporary test outputs are cleaned up. The old launcher and shared environments remain with the live installation owner and are excluded from future development calls. Future PM commands use a checkout-local data home and tool store; independent provisioning remains unverified. This rebase invoked neither activation nor PM.

Both helper builders previously passed with `SDKROOT=/nonexistent/hermes-sdk-probe`, producing arm64/x86_64 bundles. Neither helper was executed. prs.title: fix(doctor): do not live-probe MCP servers disabled in config
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`hermes doctor --live` probes every server under `mcp_servers`, including servers set to `enabled: false`. A switched-off server is never loaded, so the probe can only invent a failure for something the user turned off on purpose — and it lands in the final **"Found N issue(s) to address"** list.

On a config with three deliberately disabled servers, that produced this:

```
Found 3 issue(s) to address:
  1. Live probe failed: MCP: attio (MCP OAuth for 'attio': non-interactive environment and no cached tokens found…)
  2. Live probe failed: MCP: grafana (… no cached tokens found …)
  3. Live probe failed: MCP: mixpanel (… no cached tokens found …)
```

All three are `enabled: false` in `config.yaml` and are listed as `✗ disabled` by `hermes mcp list`.

With this change:

```
→ MCP: attio (disabled in config) — skipped
→ MCP: grafana (disabled in config) — skipped
→ MCP: mixpanel (disabled in config) — skipped
```

They stay in the report — the row still says what was left out and why — but as a `skip`, using the same result shape the other not-applicable rows already use (`(malformed config entry)`, `(no servers configured)`).

## Related Issue

No issue; found while running `hermes doctor --live`.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/doctor_live.py` — in the per-server probe, return a `skip` result for `enabled is False` before probing. Servers that omit `enabled` are unchanged (still probed), matching the gateway, which only refuses to load an explicit `false`.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_doctor_live.py` — new `test_disabled_mcp_server_is_not_probed` in `TestConfiguredOnlySelection`: one enabled + one disabled server, asserts only the enabled one reaches `_probe_mcp_server`, that the disabled one reports `status == "skip"`, and that no issue is appended.

## How to Test

1. `just test tests/hermes_cli/test_doctor_live.py` — the new test plus the existing MCP probe tests (`test_mcp_servers_probed_per_configured_server` still passes: servers without `enabled` are still probed).
2. Manually: set a server to `enabled: false` in `config.yaml`, run `hermes doctor --live`, and confirm it reports `(disabled in config) — skipped` and no longer appears in the issue list.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(doctor): …`)

- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix (two files, +20/−0)
- [ ] I've run `just test` on the tests for the code I changed, and they pass — **not run locally**: this machine is a `hermes update`-managed install with no separate test environment (`pytest` is absent from its runtime env). CI covers it. The behaviour itself **was** verified end-to-end with `hermes doctor --live` on this machine, before and after (output above).
- [ ] `just check` passes — **not run** for the same reason (no repo test env / ruff 0.15.10 locally). The change is one branch inside an existing loop; `python -m py_compile` is clean.

The row's wording is a judgement call: I kept the server visible (`MCP: <name> (disabled in config) — skipped`) rather than dropping it silently, so the probe list still accounts for every entry under `mcp_servers` and the user can see their own off-switch was honoured. prs.title: fix(display): hide the compaction in-flight restatement from transcripts
prs.body:
## Problem

After a mid-turn compaction, `agent/context_compressor.py` re-appends the still-running request as a
`role=user` row: the content leads with `[STILL IN PROGRESS — this is the active request, restated after
the compaction boundary …]` and `display_metadata` carries
`compaction_inflight_task_restatement: True` (`agent.message_metadata.mark_inflight_restatement`). That row
is what keeps the model's active task across the handoff boundary — the person at the keyboard never typed
it.

Neither display projection reads the flag:

- `tui_gateway/session_history.py::_history_to_messages` (which also backs `session.resume`'s
  `display_projection`) filters only `display_kind == "hidden"` and the `[System:` sniff.
- `hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py::_project_for_display` types only untyped `[System: …]` rows hidden.

So Desktop and the Web UI paint the scaffold prompt as a normal prompt bubble (#155495).

## Change

- `agent/message_metadata.py`: `is_inflight_restatement(msg)` reads the flag, so a human pasting the same
  header text (which carries no `display_metadata`) is unaffected.
- `tui_gateway/session_history.py`: drop the stamped row beside the existing `display_kind == "hidden"`
  filter.
- `hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py`: type it `hidden`, the way this projection already types other
  display-only rows, so pagination offsets and "Show earlier" stay stable.

The row is deliberately left untyped at the producer: `display_kind` is also read by agent-side code
(`ContextCompressor._is_actionable_user_turn`, turn receipts), so stamping `hidden` there would change
compaction behaviour rather than display.

## Tests

`tests/hermes_cli/test_inflight_restatement_display.py` (new, 3 tests, drives both projections over the
stored row shape):

- the gateway projection drops the stamped restatement and keeps the real opener and the reply;
- the REST projection keeps the row count and types the row `hidden`, without mutating the input rows;
- an unstamped row with the same header still renders as a user turn in both — the flag, not the header
  text, is the signal.

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_inflight_restatement_display.py
→ 1 files, 3 tests passed, 0 failed

related suites (test_sessions_rest_scaffold_notices, test_history_commentary_display,
test_canonical_resume_display_projection, test_message_metadata, test_history_identity,
test_history_inline_images, test_notification_persistence, test_inline_edit_persistence)
→ 9 files, 67 tests passed, 0 failed

tests/tui_gateway (whole directory) → 409 files, 3272 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed
  the failure is test_generated.py::test_generated_files_are_current (stale
  apps/shared/src/gateway-contract.openrpc.json); reproduced on a clean worktree of
  upstream/main c9c87fc12b, unrelated to this change

.venv/bin/python scripts/check --base upstream/main → 19 checks, ok
```

Sabotage evidence — the same test file with the three source files reverted to `upstream/main`:

```
2 failed, 1 passed
  test_gateway_projection_drops_the_stamped_restatement
    AssertionError: assert ['please rename the widget', 'done']
                 == ['please rename the widget', '[STILL IN PROGRESS — …', 'done']
  test_rest_projection_hides_the_stamped_restatement
    KeyError: 'display_kind'
```

## Not in this change

- Search hits (`hermes_state_search`) and the session-list preview still see the row; the report is about
  the transcripts, and widening those SQL filters is a separate decision.
- Nothing changes in what the model is sent: the restatement row keeps reaching the model exactly as
  before.

No competing PR: `gh search prs` for `compaction_inflight_task_restatement`, `is_compaction_scaffolding`
and the header text returned no hits, and the issue timeline had no cross-reference before this branch.

Closes #155495

Adds **Bitquery** to the community plugin catalog. This PR adds one file, `plugin-catalog/bitquery.yaml`.

prs.title: fix(desktop): drop a deep link with a malformed percent escape instead of throwing
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`handleDeepLink` (`apps/desktop/electron/main.ts`) decodes the link's path with a bare `decodeURIComponent`. A `hermes://` link with a stray or truncated percent escape, such as `hermes://open/%E0%A4%A` or `hermes://blueprint/%`, therefore throws `URIError` out of the `open-url`, `second-instance` and cold-start handlers.

On Windows and Linux the `second-instance` handler throws before `ensureMainWindow`. A second launch carrying such a link then never brings the running app forward, which breaks the contract from #130810 that a relaunch must restore the primary window. On a cold start, the throw ends the rest of the `whenReady` callback.

This PR moves the link parsing into a small module, `electron/deep-link-url.ts`. It refuses such a link with a logged reason instead of throwing. The parsing rules are otherwise unchanged: the same schemes, the same `{ kind, name, params }` payload, and the renderer routes it as before. While moving the code, the "malformed url" log line stops quoting the raw link, since a link's path and query can carry tokens. This follows the rule `window-open-policy.ts` already applies to denied URLs.

## Related Issue

No existing issue found (searched issues and PRs for malformed / URIError / decodeURIComponent deep links).

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/electron/deep-link-url.ts` (new): `parseDeepLink(url, schemes, reject)` returns the payload, or `null` after calling `reject` with a reason; a malformed escape no longer throws.
- `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts`: `handleDeepLink` uses it (21 lines removed, 6 added).
- `apps/desktop/electron/deep-link-url.test.ts` (new): a malformed escape is refused, never thrown, and the reason does not quote the link. A payload re-encoded the way `hermes:deep-link-ready` re-dispatches a queued link parses back to itself. Only the accepted schemes parse.

## How to Test

1. The base expression throws: `node -e "decodeURIComponent('%E0%A4%A')"` gives `URIError: URI malformed`. On Windows/Linux, start Desktop, then launch it again with `hermes://open/%E0%A4%A` as its argument. `desktop.log` records the uncaught `URIError`, and the running window is not restored.
2. `cd apps/desktop && pnpm exec vitest run --project electron electron/deep-link-url.test.ts electron/deep-link-protocol.test.ts`: 4 passed.

prs.title: fix(gateway): FooteredReply survives deepcopy of the completion payload
prs.body:
Fixes #156709

## Problem

With `display.runtime_footer.enabled: true`, the final reply is wrapped in `gateway.runtime_footer.FooteredReply(text, footer)` — a `str` subclass whose `__new__` takes two required arguments. `gateway/session_events.py:publish()` deep-copies the completion payload, and `copy.deepcopy` reconstructs str subclasses via `cls.__new__(cls, <the str value>)` (`copyreg.__newobj__`) — a single-argument call. Every footer-bearing turn crashed publication with:

```
TypeError: FooteredReply.__new__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'footer'
```

so `gateway.session_settlement_recovery` logged `Settlement or publication of admission ... failed` and CLI/API clients never received the completion event.

## What changed

`FooteredReply` gains copy support:

- `__getnewargs__` returns the original `(text, footer)` pair (the stored value minus the constructor's unconditional `\n\n` separator and the footer) — this fixes `copy.deepcopy`, `copy.copy`, and `pickle` round-trips alike.
- `__deepcopy__` writes the memo entry before returning so shared references inside one payload stay shared after the copy.

Any rewrite still yields a plain `str` (the documented contract), so behavior is unchanged everywhere else.

## Verification

New `TestFooteredReplyCopy` in `tests/gateway/test_runtime_footer.py` (7 tests): deepcopy preserves type/text/footer; the nested-payload shape of the reported crash (`deepcopy({'payload': <FooteredReply>})`) fails on main and passes here; shared references stay shared; empty-footer degenerate round-trip; `__getnewargs__` reconstruction; pickle round-trip; and the rewrite-drops-the-subclass contract.

The suite's pre-existing Windows-environment failures (`HOME`-expansion tests) reproduce on clean main and are unrelated. `ruff check` clean.

prs.title: fix(state): bound state.db growth from settled-turn retry caches, and reclaim space while serving
prs.body:
On a busy gateway `state.db` kept growing even though sessions were pruned. Three causes:

- **Retry caches were never reclaimed.** Settled-turn retry caches (`worker_receipts`, `gateway.admission.result.v1.*`) had no age bound.
- **Stored results were heavy.** Each stored result held a second full copy of the turn's tool output and reasoning.
- **No way to shrink a live store.** The only reclaim path was a full `VACUUM` at gateway boot. That blocks startup on large stores, so deployments turned it off.

This PR bounds the caches, stores results by reference to their transcript rows, ties the result horizon to `sessions.retention_days`, and moves space reclaim off the boot path into short incremental batches.

### 1. Reclaim the retry caches a settled turn leaves behind (#149591, by @troyml42)

Cherry-picked unchanged from #149591. Authorship is preserved, and `contributors/emails/coder@localhost` maps the commit email to troyml42.

- **Worker receipts.** A terminal worker execution keeps its newest 32 receipts, and none once its session is past the retention window. A registered, running or unknown execution is never touched.
- **Settled results.** A settled turn's stored result keeps the newest 16 per session, and none for a session quiet past the retry horizon. A result with no admission and no live tombstone is dropped.
- **Orphaned policy receipts.** A `gateway.local_policy.v1` receipt whose session and target are both gone is dropped.
- **Past the bound, a retry is refused, never re-executed.** Worker publications get `stale_generation`. API and bot reads get a definitive miss. Cron falls back to the stored outcome.

Tests: `tests/hermes_state/test_dead_cache_reclaim.py`.

### 2. Result size: store a settled turn's heavy output by reference

The agent flushes every message of a turn to `messages` before settlement, so the stored result duplicated tool output, reasoning blobs, the Bedrock reasoning sidecar and inline images.

- **What is stored.** The row now keeps the reply, flags, usage and cost by value. Heavy message fields are kept as row ids (`row_refs` in the `_stored` envelope) and only when the row's stored value equals the dict's value.
- **Readers are unchanged.** `admission_result` reloads and redacts referenced fields, so exact retry, Responses `previous_response_id` chaining and receipts get the same dict as before.
- **Dropped or replaced fields.** The live-only `bedrock_content_blocks` sidecar is dropped, since a reloaded turn replays `reasoning_details`, which carries the same data. Inline images become the transcript's `[screenshot]` marker.
- **Compatibility.** Rows written before this change decode as they did. A turn whose rows were never flushed is stored by value.

**Documented degradation:** if a referenced `messages` row is deleted out of band (not through session delete or prune), that field reloads as `None`, and a row rewritten in place reloads as the transcript now holds it. Session delete and prune compact the result to its reply before they delete the transcript, so the normal paths never hit this. Nothing raises.

Tests: `tests/gateway/test_admission_result_by_reference.py`. A turn with about 400 KB of tool output, signed and redacted reasoning, a Bedrock sidecar and a screenshot stores in under 4 KB. Exact retry, usage, the bot outcome, the API settled result, reload redaction, delete retirement and Responses chaining (json and sse) all read back.

### 3. Retention: a stored result never outlives its session's retention

Before this change a stored result's only age bound was the fixed 7-day exact-retry horizon, so with `retention_days: 3` results lived twice as long as their sessions.

- **Horizon.** `result_horizon_s(retention_days)` caps the horizon at the retention window. The floor is one day and the ceiling is the 7-day `RETRY_HORIZON_S`.
- **Which prunes use it.** Retention prunes (auto-maintenance and a bare `hermes sessions prune --older-than N`) pass it. Filtered prunes keep the 7-day default.
- **Compressed conversations.** Activity counts the conversation's tip as well as its root, so a compressed conversation still in use keeps its results.
- **Deletion tombstones keep their own clock.** A deleted session's compacted result follows its tombstone on `RETRY_HORIZON_S`, so an exact retry after a delete still replays the reply for the full horizon, whatever the retention.

Tests: `tests/hermes_state/test_admission_result_retention.py`, including `test_a_deleted_session_keeps_its_retry_result_as_long_as_its_tombstone`. That test uses `retention_days=3`: at day 4 the tombstone and result both remain and the exact retry replays the reply. At day 8 both are gone.

### 4. Vacuum off boot: a gateway never runs a full VACUUM at startup

With `vacuum_after_prune` on, a gateway's first start of the day ran a full `VACUUM` before it served. On a 3.6 GB store over NFS that held the boot for 22 minutes.

- **No full VACUUM in the gateway.** The gateway passes `full_vacuum=False`, and its startup pass only archives and prunes.
- **Reclaim while serving.** `vacuum_after_prune` now runs `reclaim_free_pages_incrementally()` on the housekeeping thread once the gateway is serving. Each `PRAGMA incremental_vacuum(256)` batch is its own short write transaction, so other writers get the lock between batches. A pass is capped at 20 s. No checkpoint reset is issued.
- **New stores start incremental.** New stores are created with `auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL`, set before WAL and before the first table. The writer open reads the file's freshness before that pragma, so a new store stays silent about the WAL switch and does not log the #89293 journal-mode warning.
- **CLI unchanged.** The CLI's full `VACUUM` path, its throttles and its gates are unchanged.

**One-time step for existing stores:** SQLite only changes `auto_vacuum` on a full rewrite, so a store created before this change keeps `auto_vacuum=NONE`. Incremental reclaim does nothing on it until `hermes sessions optimize` runs once, with Hermes stopped. Until then the gateway logs one INFO line per process naming that command.

Tests: `tests/gateway/test_state_db_vacuum_off_startup.py` (the boot pass returns at once while a stand-in VACUUM blocks, and a housekeeping tick shrinks a pruned incremental store). `tests/hermes_state/test_incremental_vacuum_reclaim.py` covers:

- bounded batches
- a foreign writer landing between batches
- a legacy store left alone with one hint
- `optimize` converting a legacy store
- the gateway flag
- a fresh store opening with no journal-mode warning and `auto_vacuum == 2`

### Already on main, no change here

- **Repeat `skill_view` calls are deduplicated.** Repeat calls in one session return an unchanged-content stub (2a3a7e6f53b, eedf3944e9e, b002dfc04d3).
- **FTS already limits tool rows.** The trigram index skips tool rows, and the base index keeps only an 8 KB prefix (9acc4b47f5b, 57162d0cc18, 42e97f38083). A store on the legacy inline FTS layout keeps both indexes until `hermes sessions optimize-storage` runs.

### Tests run

- **Focused files.** The five new test files plus `test_watch_notification_reset_pin.py`, `test_journal_mode_upgrade_warning.py`, `test_api_idempotency_after_delete.py` and `test_retained_response_chain_after_delete.py`: 9 files, 52 passed, 0 failed.
- **Area gate.** The state, admission, gateway housekeeping and CLI session test area: 368 files, 3178 passed, 0 failed, 16 skipped.
- **Checks.** `scripts/check`: 18 checks ok, code health 0 blocking, 0 advisory.

prs.title: fix(agent): compaction stores the same text projection as the per-tool flush
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The per-tool flush stores a multimodal message as its text projection (`agent/session_persistence.py::_durable_content`: text parts kept, each image part becomes a `[screenshot]` line at its position). The writers that store a new generation of rows hand `SessionDB` the live message dicts instead, and `SessionDB` stores a part list verbatim as `\x00json:` JSON (`hermes_state_messages.py::_encode_content`). So every compaction stores each carried vision result again, base64 image included, and the copies pile up with each compaction.

bb87e6abce kept this difference on purpose ("keeping the writer's shape (compaction: raw parts; flush: text projection)"). This PR proposes the other choice: compaction, and the other writers that turn message dicts into rows, follow the flush's text-only contract. The vision guide, `agent/image_replay.py` and #152946 already describe stored rows that way.

**Measured on a 1.2M-message store** (read-only scan of a copy, aggregates only; the rows were written by released builds):
- Rows holding base64 image data total 907.8 MB.
  - 890.7 MB of that is in 823 part-list (`\x00json:`) rows: 824.0 MB in rows archived by compaction, 66.7 MB in active rows.
  - The other 17.1 MB is in text rows, mostly tool output (`read_file`, `terminal`, ...) that happens to contain a `data:` URL. This PR does not touch it.
- The part-list rows come from 446 tool calls. For every one of them, the first stored row is the flush's `[screenshot]` text, and every later copy (2 to 9+ per call) carries the image.
- `vision_analyze` has 626.3 MB of exact-duplicate bodies, and 99.3% of that is copies within the same session.
- Active rows are what a turn rebuilt from the store resends (gateway, API server, resume). #148146 reports 51 MB of `vision_analyze` base64 in one session's active rows.

**The change.**
- New helpers in `agent/session_persistence.py`:
  - `durable_row(msg)` returns a copy holding the flush's projection when the content has parts. Otherwise it returns the same dict, so text-only sessions write exactly what they write today.
  - `durable_rows(messages)` is a context manager used by the generation writers. After a successful write, each live dict adopts the row state `SessionDB` stamped on its copy: row id, digest, timestamp and durable ids. It does this through the worker path's existing `row_annotations` / `apply_row_annotations`. A failed write leaves the live dicts untouched.
  - `durable_copy(...)` builds the row for branch and seed copies.
- The live dicts keep their parts, so the model still sees the image for the rest of the process. The next flush or compaction then names the row that was actually written.
- **Writers routed through the projection:**
  - in-place compaction (`archive_and_compact`), rotation (`publish_compression_child`) and their carried messages;
  - micro-compaction;
  - the proactive prune and its full-rewrite fallback. The in-place prune projects only the replacement; the original stays as held, so it still names its row;
  - the TUI edit/resend truncation, and the ACP save of an agent that does not persist itself;
  - the gateway's `rewrite_transcript` (`/retry` without a session authority, and a rotated child that was not published);
  - two writers that read the transcript back from the store and write it again, so they meet part lists only in rows an older build's compaction wrote. They take `durable_row` copies:
    - the gateway `/retry` under a session authority, the normal running-gateway path (`replace_messages_in_transaction` inside the admission);
    - the canonical `session.mutate` compress commit (`hermes_state_mutation_compress.compress_in_transaction`, in place or rotated), which `/compress` from Desktop, the TUI and the gateway chat uses;
  - the CLI, TUI and gateway `/branch` copies, and the TUI seed;
  - the gateway's transcript appends: a runtime that does not persist itself, the user row kept for a failed turn, and the spool replay. Plain text skips the import there, so spool recovery at startup stays within its memory bound;
  - the turn prologue's multimodal context backfill (`agent/turn_context.py`). It rewrites a user row that in-place preflight compaction or a raced flush stored first.
- **The backfill hands the new row digest back.** `SessionDB.set_user_message_content` and its worker op share one UPDATE (`hermes_state_common.rewrite_user_row`), which also returns the rewritten row's digest. The backfill passes `live=`, so the live dict takes that digest.
  - Without it, the dict kept the digest of the row the backfill replaced. Its next re-flush then read the backfill as another writer's write. For example, the surrogate repair after a `UnicodeEncodeError` pops the persist marker and forces that re-flush. The flush then adopted the stored text, `[screenshot]` included, over the live image parts.
  - On main the same stale digest exists, but the row there holds the parts, so adopting it keeps the image; it reverts the surrogate repair instead.
- **Recognition of carried rows** now compares the projected copy with the stored row, so an image row is matched instead of being read as edited:
  - a restored copy is not inserted again (`_same_as_stored`);
  - a carried row above the watermark is claimed instead of cloned (`_replays_as`);
  - micro-compaction supersedes the original instead of keeping it as summarized history beside its copy;
  - `_images_replaced` also recognises, in text rows, a `[screenshot]` line swapped for a placeholder line. Before, it did this only in part lists.
- **Why at the callers and not in `_encode_content`:** the `SessionDB` API is meant to round-trip structured content. `tests/hermes_state/test_compression_watermark_commit.py` passes a multimodal tail through rotation and expects it back.

**Effect.** New writes only.
- No migration touches existing rows.
- A later compaction, prune, rewrite or copy of a row an older build stored with parts, by one of the writers above, writes it as text.
- Session import, the API server's session fork (`POST /api/sessions/{id}/fork`, which copies `get_messages` output with `replace_messages`) and `SessionDB`'s own SQL copies (clones, archived twins) keep the stored bytes.
- On the measured store, the compaction-written copies that hold the 890.7 MB would have been written as text.
- **Subagents have no separate writer.** Each child `AIAgent` gets its own `SessionDB` and persists through the same flush and compaction writers. Of the active subagent tool rows on that store that contain base64:
  - 72 rows (12.6 MB) are compaction part lists, which this PR covers;
  - 332 rows (7.8 MB) are plain-text output that contains `data:` URLs, which it does not.

**Behaviour changes that need a maintainer decision:**
1. **One prompt-cache miss per compaction that carries a live image, on surfaces that rebuild a turn from the store** (gateway, API server, resume; #142288).
   - Today a compacted vision result replays its image by accident, from the raw copy. After this PR the first rebuilt request has `[screenshot]` where the compaction's request sent the image, so the cached prefix diverges from that row on.
   - #152946 reports that a signed-thinking route then refuses the request ("The block is bound to a different conversation"), and Hermes strips the thinking and re-caches the chat.
   - A flushed image result already causes this divergence today. This PR adds one more per compaction that carries an image, in exchange for #148146's 413 loops and the base64 resent on every rebuilt turn.
   - #152946 replays retained tool images from native-inputs inside `vision.replay_recent_images`, which removes the miss for those images. Older carried images keep `[screenshot]`, as user images outside that window already do.
   - **Land this with or after #152946.**
2. Compaction rows drop audio and file parts, as the flush already does.
3. The user row the gateway keeps for a failed turn is now stored as text. This also stops base64 from being stored when an image turn fails.

## Related Issue

No `Fixes`: this PR does not close any open issue by itself.

- **Refs #148146.** This PR covers the stored half: rebuilt turns reloading images from compaction-written rows. The byte-blind token estimator, the in-process image-strip recovery and rows already stored are unchanged, so the issue stays open.
- **Refs #137540 (part 2).** New compaction generations no longer carry base64 image copies. Other duplicated tool bodies are unchanged, and this PR does not choose among options 1–4 for archive rows. A separate RFC comment there proposes content-addressed storage for long tool outputs.
- **Depends on / coordinates with #152946** (tool-image replay from native-inputs). I've left a coordination note there.
- **Related:** #142288 (gateway drops native vision images after one turn).
- **Credit:** no code is salvaged from another PR.
  - sjay2055's measurements on #148146 and djagya's part-2 analysis on #137540 pointed at this path.
  - youssofal's #152946 is the replay half that makes the change cheap.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

There are two commits, rebased onto main at 1408145c11. The first adds the tests, which fail on main. The second is the fix. Together they change 30 files, +727/−123.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `agent/session_persistence.py` (+33/−3) | `durable_row`, `durable_rows`, `durable_copy` |
| `agent/conversation_compression.py` (+22/−22) | in-place and rotation writers and carried messages use `durable_rows` (file size unchanged) |
| `agent/micro_compaction.py` (+8/−4) | writer and carried list |
| `agent/context_compressor_prune.py` (+14/−7) | full-rewrite fallback; in-place rewrite projects only the replacement |
| `agent/turn_context.py` (+8/−9) | the backfill always writes `_durable_content` and passes `live=` so the live dict takes the new row digest; the unused `preflight_compressed` parameter is removed |
| `hermes_state_common.py` (+17), `hermes_state_messages.py` (+9/−11), `hermes_state_worker_lifecycle.py` (+4/−10), `agent/runtime_session_lifecycle.py` (+6/−2) | `rewrite_user_row`: the one UPDATE `set_user_message_content` and its worker op run, returning the rewritten row's digest; `live=` on `SessionDB` and on the worker facade (`hermes_state_messages.py` shrinks by 2 lines; it is near the 2,000-line cap) |
| `hermes_state_mutation_compress.py` (+5/−2) | the `session.mutate` compress commit writes `durable_row` copies, in place and rotated |
| `hermes_state_coverage.py` (+9/−1) | `_images_replaced` text-row rule |
| `gateway/session_transcript.py` (+14/−6) | `transcript_append_kwargs` projects list/dict content; `rewrite_transcript` uses `durable_rows` |
| `gateway/slash_commands_session.py` (+12/−5) | gateway `/branch` row; the `/retry` rewrite inside the admission writes `durable_row` copies |
| `hermes_cli/cli_commands_mixin.py` (+7/−8) | CLI `/branch` uses `durable_copy` (net −1 line in a file over the cap) |
| `tui_gateway/methods_prompt.py` (+7/−3), `tui_gateway/methods_session.py` (+4/−4), `tui_gateway/session_workdir.py` (+7/−7) | edit/resend truncation, `/branch`, seed |
| `acp_adapter/session.py` (+4/−1) | `replace_messages` caller |
| `website/docs/developer-guide/session-storage.md` (+1) | the text-only `content` contract and which writers apply it |
| `tests/agent/test_compaction_text_projection.py` (new, 303 lines) | one test parametrized over eight writers (in-place, rotation, micro-compaction, prune, prune full-rewrite, ACP save, TUI `/branch`, TUI seed); micro-compaction supersedes; a restored copy is not re-inserted; prune of a row an older build stored with parts; the prologue's backfill after in-place preflight compaction leaves the live turn its image across a re-flush |
| `tests/gateway/test_gateway_writers_store_image_rows_as_text.py` (new, 126 lines) | one test parametrized over the gateway writers that reload the transcript: `/retry` under a session authority and through `rewrite_transcript`, `/branch`, and the `session.mutate` compress commit in place and rotated each write an older build's part-list row back as text |
| `tests/hermes_state/test_compaction_carried_tail_not_cloned.py`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_branch_command.py`, `tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server_deep_truncate.py` | stripped carry claims its text row; `/branch` copies text; edit/resend cut keeps earlier rows in place |
| `tests/agent/test_api_content_sidecar.py`, `tests/agent/test_compression_rotation_state.py`, `tests/gateway/test_failure_writer_ownership.py` | four assertions that pinned raw parts on stored rows now expect the projection |
| `tests/hermes_state/test_runtime_worker_metadata.py` | the backfill's live dict holds the rewritten row's digest on the direct and the worker store; signature update |
| `tests/agent/test_image_replay.py`, `tests/agent/test_turn_context.py` | signature update only |

## How to Test

All runs use the hermetic environment of `scripts/run_tests.sh`, invoked directly so that no file from the real Hermes home is added to `PYTHONPATH`.

1. **Targeted tests:**
   ```
   env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$HOME" TZ=UTC LANG=C.UTF-8 LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 PYTHONHASHSEED=0 PYTHONUTF8=1 \
     .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider \
       tests/agent/test_compaction_text_projection.py \
       tests/gateway/test_gateway_writers_store_image_rows_as_text.py \
       tests/hermes_state/test_runtime_worker_metadata.py \
       tests/hermes_state/test_compaction_carried_tail_not_cloned.py \
       tests/hermes_cli/test_branch_command.py \
       tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server_deep_truncate.py \
       tests/agent/test_api_content_sidecar.py \
       tests/agent/test_compression_rotation_state.py \
       tests/gateway/test_failure_writer_ownership.py
   ```
   | Tree | Result |
   |---|---|
   | first commit only (main + tests) | 25 failed, 110 passed: the 20 new cases, the extended worker parity test and the 4 updated assertions |
   | this PR | 135 passed |

   Each routed writer has its own parametrized case. Reverting one writer's routing alone fails exactly that case. I checked this for the ACP save, the TUI `/branch` and seed, the gateway `/retry` (both paths), the gateway `/branch`, the compress commit and the backfill's digest handback (on the direct and the worker store). One exception: the in-place compaction's `carried_messages` projection. In the reinserted-reply case I built, reverting it changed nothing, because the positional tail rewind supersedes the same original. It is kept so it matches micro-compaction, where the carried projection is load-bearing and pinned.

2. **Regression runs.**
   - For this revision, after the rebase, I ran 33 files with `scripts/run_tests_parallel.py`: the PR's tests plus the suites around every touched writer (`set_user_message_content` callers, the worker lifecycle and compaction ops, `session.mutate` compress, including managed, plugin-engine and preview, `/retry`, in-place and micro-compaction, `/compress`, the watermark commit). Result: 477 passed, 0 failed.
   - The broad run below was made on the previous revision, on 67664e236d. I have not re-run it after the rebase and these fixes:
   ```
   env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$HOME" TZ=UTC LANG=C.UTF-8 LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 PYTHONHASHSEED=0 PYTHONUTF8=1 \
     .venv/bin/python scripts/run_tests_parallel.py -j 16 \
       tests/agent tests/hermes_state tests/acp_adapter tests/tui_gateway tests/gateway tests/hermes_cli
   ```
   - The run covered 5,777 files. At that revision: 51,558 passed, 459 failed, 188 errors, 1,342 skipped.
   - The 647 failing or erroring test IDs were identical on main, so that revision added no regressions.
   - The failures come from the macOS environment, and main has the same ones:
     - the `aiohttp`, `acp` and `keyring` extras are not installed;
     - the conftest guard against the real home directory trips;
     - some tests assume Linux or depend on timing.
   - Two first-attempt flakes passed on the runner's retry: `test_compression_failure_session_sync` and `test_zeroed_state_db::test_concurrent_quarantine_no_clobber`. Run alone, they passed at that revision and on main.
   - An earlier revision regressed `tests/gateway/test_shutdown_spool_limits.py`: spool recovery went over its memory bound because the projection was imported for every row. The import is now skipped for plain text, and the test passes.
3. **Checks:** `scripts/check` reports "19 checks, ok" on the working tree, on `--commit HEAD~1` and on `--commit HEAD`.
   - Code health: 0 blocking, 0 advisory.
   - ruff: clean.
   - `tests/ci/test_docs_drift.py` passes.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate (#152946 is complementary; #133281 took a different, closed approach)
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `just test` on the tests for the code I changed, and they pass (I ran pytest and `scripts/run_tests_parallel.py` directly in the same hermetic environment; commands above)
- [x] `just check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26.6, Python 3.14.7 (Linux CI not yet run)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

## Risks and open points

- **Prompt cache:** see behaviour change 1. This should land with or after #152946.
- **Mixed-version profiles.** An older build's compaction still writes part lists, and this build reads both forms. With rows an older build stored with parts:
  - micro-compaction can show such a row twice in display and search. This is cosmetic; the model context is unaffected;
  - a TUI edit/resend cut re-inserts from that row onward once, as text;
  - a wire-stripped re-hand of such a row still inserts a text twin, as it already does on main.
- **API server session fork.** `POST /api/sessions/{id}/fork` copies `get_messages` output with `replace_messages`, so it still copies an older build's part-list row with its base64. Routing it is one `durable_row` call. I left it out because the `aiohttp` extra is not installed here, so I could not run a test for it.
- **Storage refactor (#149558 / #151855).** `git merge-tree` against #151855 at 714b7bcfb9 shows 17 conflicted files beyond those main (1408145c11) already has. They include modify/delete conflicts on `hermes_state_coverage.py`, `hermes_state_messages.py` and `hermes_state_mutation_compress.py`. #151855 may have moved since. The port map:
  - the `_images_replaced` text-row rule moves to `persistence/sqlite/conversation/_store/coverage.py`, plus `tests/contracts/_reference/conversation/messages_compact.py`;
  - `row_annotations` moves to `persistence/workers/vocabulary.py`;
  - `_durable_content` moves to `session_rules/turns.py`;
  - the compress commit's `durable_row` call moves to `compress_in_transaction` in `persistence/sqlite/authority/_mutation_publish.py`;
  - `rewrite_user_row` and the `live=` digest handback go to `set_user_message_content` in `persistence/sqlite/conversation/_store/messages.py` and to `worker_user_content` in `persistence/sqlite/workers/_lifecycle.py`. #151855's interface returns a `bool` there, so the digest needs a way back through `persistence/conversation/messages.py`;
  - the moved tests go to `tests/persistence_sqlite/conversation_store/` and `tests/persistence_sqlite/workers/`, and the new tests' `SessionDB(db_path=…)` calls move to the store interface.

  I'm happy to rebase if #151855 lands first.
- **Not verified:**
  - Linux CI;
  - running the patched build against a real store. The size figures above come from a read-only scan, not from this branch.

prs.title: fix(cron): migrate the executions ledger once per file, not per connection
prs.body:
Fixes #155907.

**The three multipliers in the issue are all real, and two of them are in one function.** The ledger opened with nine schema-lock acquisitions per execution, on every execution:

```
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS executions           1
_widen_status_check()                           1
add_column_if_missing × 5 (ALTER each time)     5   ← every one a lock, guaranteed to fail
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS × 3                  3
```

**What this changes.**

| file | change |
| --- | --- |
| `hermes_cli/sqlite_util.py` | `initialize_if_outdated(conn, version=…, migrate=…)` — run the DDL only when `PRAGMA user_version` is behind; `add_column_if_missing` now asks `PRAGMA table_info` before it issues an `ALTER` |
| `cron/executions.py` | `SCHEMA_VERSION`; the file is migrated once, then stamped |
| `cron/incidents.py` | uses the same gate: the incidents table lives in this database, so a second per-module stamp would have starved whichever module migrated second |

`user_version` rather than a "first connection in this process" flag, for the reason the issue gives: a database restored from an older backup carries `user_version = 0` and gets migrated again, which an in-process flag would silently skip.

**Measured, same machine, a copy of the ledger** (statement counts from a `set_trace_callback` trace, not wall-clock claims):

| connection | statements | DDL |
| --- | --- | --- |
| one-time migration (fresh or restored backup) | 17 | 10 |
| every connection after that | 3 (the ledger write + its PRAGMAs) | **0** |

So the per-execution 9-lock burst is gone; it happens once per file instead.

**On `busy_timeout`.** Not raised. The issue offers it as optional, and the measurement in the issue shows the write contention itself is not the problem — 15 concurrent `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` + `UPDATE` finish in 2.66 s — so raising the timeout would hide contention rather than remove it. If a deployment still needs headroom after this, the knob is a one-line change and worth a separate issue with a measurement attached.

**Tests.** `tests/cron/test_executions_schema_gate.py`, five cases:

- `add_column_if_missing` issues no `ALTER` when the column exists (traced);
- the first connection stamps `SCHEMA_VERSION` and creates both tables;
- a later connection runs **zero** DDL statements (traced) while doing real ledger work;
- a database restored from an older backup (no `user_version`, no `delivery_outcome`/`scheduled_instant`/`progress_at`, old `CHECK`) is migrated, and `missed` becomes an accepted status;
- `cron.incidents`' connection uses the same gate and runs no DDL.

RED with the three source changes reverted and the tests kept: 5 failed. GREEN: 5 passed.

**Regression check, with the delta stated.** `tests/cron/test_claim_job_for_fire.py`, `test_missed_window_catchup.py` and `test_scheduled_occurrence.py`: 22 passed, 6 failed — and the same six fail identically on the unmodified base on this host (`test_claim_seconds_before_the_slot_owns_it_once`, the two `MissedWindowCatchUp` restart cases, and the three `prestamp_rollback` variants), so the delta from this change is zero. They look environment-bound rather than ledger-bound; I did not chase them inside this PR.

All 21 native `scripts/check` checks pass on this head. The released-source contract was checked offline; no paid generation or document upload was run. prs.title: /restart from a source checkout comes back up, and a broken profile lookup stops instead of running the default profile (#152714, #152716, salvage #152941)
prs.body:
If a gateway runs from a source checkout and you send `/restart`, the gateway now actually comes back; before, it stopped and never restarted, and nothing said why. Separately, if `hermes` cannot load the profile you asked for (`-p work` or `hermes profile use work`), it now stops with an error instead of quietly running in the default profile.

Fixes #152714
Fixes #152716

Salvaged from @phon-t's #152941 (their two commits, authorship kept). That PR's Telegram log-level part already landed as #153448; its scrapling docs part (#152702) is not in this PR.

## What changes for the user

| Scenario (real processes, scratch `HOME`/`HERMES_HOME`) | main (`951ec092848c`) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Gateway found Hermes only through `PYTHONPATH`; detached `/restart` helper runs | watcher `PYTHONPATH: None`, helper exits 1 with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hermes_cli'`, no log anywhere | watcher `PYTHONPATH` = the running checkout, helper imports `hermes_cli.main`; output and `detached restart exited with status N` land in `<HERMES_HOME>/logs/detached-restart.log` |
| Sticky `active_profile=work`, profile lookup raises (`hermes config path`) | `Warning: profile override failed (...), using default`, prints the **default** profile's config path, exit 0 | `Error: profile override failed (...)`, exit 1 |
| `hermes -p work config path`, profile lookup raises | `-p` stays in argv: `Did you mean: worktree?`, exit 2 | `Error: profile override failed (...)`, exit 1 |
| No profile requested, lookup broken | starts normally | unchanged |

**Live repro:** both rows were run on main and on this head. Restart: I ran the real `_restart_watcher_env()` plus the real detached shell line with `PYTHONPATH=<checkout>` and the bare venv interpreter, with `gateway restart` swapped for an import check so no gateway is touched. Profile: I ran the real `python -m hermes_cli.main` with a `sitecustomize` that breaks `resolve_profile_env`, under `env -i`. Inheriting `HERMES_SUPERVISED_CHILD` would skip the sticky read.

## Changes

- `gateway/restart_watcher_env.py` (new sibling): `keep_running_checkout_importable()` puts the running checkout back on the watcher's `PYTHONPATH` (site-packages installs are skipped). The root comes from `hermes_cli._startup_fast.project_root_str`, the same resolver the Windows watcher already uses. `detached_restart_shell()` sends the helper's output and exit status to `logs/detached-restart.log`.
- `gateway/run_shutdown.py`: `_restart_watcher_env` and `_launch_detached_restart_command` call those helpers. The Windows watcher picks up the `PYTHONPATH` fix through the shared env builder.
- `hermes_cli/main.py::_apply_profile_override`: an unexpected lookup failure exits 1. This handler is only reached when a profile was requested, so the silent fallback remains only for the no-profile case.

**Root cause:** the child-env builders strip Hermes-owned `PYTHONPATH` entries by design, and the restart helper is the one child that has to re-run this same install. The profile handler treated every unexpected error as "use default".

## Tests

Red on main, green here (`scripts/run_tests.sh` over the 3 touched test files: main 4 failed; head 71 passed, 2 skipped):
- `test_restart_watcher_restores_checkout_pythonpath`, `test_posix_detached_restart_logs_helper_output_and_exit_status`
- `test_unexpected_profile_lookup_failure_exits_nonzero[flag|sticky]`, plus the no-profile control

`python scripts/check`: 19 checks ok.

## Infographic

![restart and profile guard](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab275dc/MHWV0pqQ_EereUqGLsBPx_bkaUb9sh.png)
