issues.title: [Bug]: Provider integration test sends GET to a PUT-only route
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

Upstream main at `f47dd19bd1442b989eeb8df8d146cbbab572d0b1`.

## Description

The integration test `test_providers_get_nonexistent` sends `GET` to `/api/models/{provider_id}/config`, which only registers `PUT`. The request fails at HTTP method dispatch and never checks whether the provider exists.

**Related PR(s):** None at the time of filing.

**Security considerations:** None. This concerns an integration test using a synthetic provider ID.

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** `f47dd19bd1442b989eeb8df8d146cbbab572d0b1`
- **OS:** Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS on WSL2 (x86_64)
- **Install method:** Editable install from source with test dependencies
- **Python version:** 3.12.13

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Check out `f47dd19bd1442b989eeb8df8d146cbbab572d0b1`.
2. Install the development, test, and full extras with `python -m pip install -e ".[dev,test,full]"`.
3. Run `python -m pytest -q tests/integration/test_providers_router.py::test_providers_get_nonexistent`.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** `GET /api/models/nonexistent-provider-12345/config` returns HTTP 405 (`Method Not Allowed`). The assertion expects 400 or 404.
- **Expected:** The integration test exercises the Console's model-pool lookup and asserts HTTP 404 with `{"detail":"Provider not found"}` for the unknown provider.

## Logs / Screenshots

```text
E   assert 405 in [404, 400]
E    +  where 405 = <Response [405 Method Not Allowed]>.status_code
FAILED tests/integration/test_providers_router.py::test_providers_get_nonexistent
```

## Additional Notes

Proposed fix: use `GET /api/models/{provider_id}/pool` in this one test and assert the exact response.

AI disclosure: Codex drafted this report and reproduced the failure in the contributor's local environment. The contributor confirmed the reproduction and review before submission.

issues.title: [Feature]: Plugin-facing theme extension point (semantic token override layer)
issues.body:
## Summary

The Console theme system added in #7741 lets **users** pick a palette (6 built-ins) and customize accent / hover / background / surface / radius. But **plugins** still have exactly one theme knob: `window.QwenPaw.chat.theme.set(pluginId, { colorPrimary })`. Plugin authors who want deeper theming (backgrounds, glass / `backdrop-filter`, full palettes) have no official hook, so they end up injecting CSS.

Proposal (for discussion): add a **plugin-facing semantic token override layer**, built on QwenPaw's *own* semantic tokens rather than the upstream UI library's raw tokens — so plugins can theme deeply **without coupling to upstream upgrades**.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Console (frontend web UI)

## Problem / Motivation

1. **Plugin theming is one-dimensional today.** The plugin theme API only accepts `colorPrimary` (see `plugins/types/qwenpaw.d.ts` and `plugins/hostSdk/install.ts` → `themeFieldMap`). Everything else is unreachable from a plugin.
2. **The marketplace already proves both the demand and the fragility of the workaround.** Appearance plugins such as *QwenPaw Skin Studio*, *background-wallpaper*, and *No Glass (Flat UI)* all describe themselves as "pure frontend, zero-dependency" — i.e. they inject CSS and poke the DOM directly. That breaks whenever the Console's markup or styles change.
3. **Why not simply expose the upstream tokens?** Because `plugins/types/qwenpaw.d.ts` deliberately keeps the public surface stable *"across vendor upgrades"* — exposing the upstream UI library's raw tokens would couple every plugin theme to that library's token names. The layer worth opening is **QwenPaw's own semantic layer**, part of which already exists (see #7682).

## Proposed Solution

Two steps, in order:

1. **Own the layer.** Make the Console's theming go through **QwenPaw-owned semantic tokens** (semantic role names → mapped internally to whatever the underlying UI library expects). #7682 ("use semantic tokens in SettingsCenter") is already a step in this direction.
2. **Open the layer to plugins.** Add a plugin API to override those semantic tokens, with the same disposable / registration semantics as the rest of the plugin SDK, e.g.:

```js
const dispose = window.QwenPaw.chat.theme.overrideTokens("my-plugin", {
  "surface":         { light: "#ffffff", dark: "#1f1f1f" },
  "chat.background": { light: "#fafafa", dark: "#111111" },
  // ...any semantic token; both light & dark required, so an override
  // never goes illegible when the user flips the color scheme.
});
```

Because plugins override **QwenPaw's semantic names**, an upstream library upgrade only changes QwenPaw's internal mapping — plugin themes keep working. That removes the exact risk that motivates keeping the surface closed today.

Happy to start with a **minimal first cut** (e.g. the handful of tokens the Console already uses for surface / background / border / text) and grow from there, rather than a big-bang "full skin system".

## Alternatives Considered

- **Status quo — each plugin injects CSS.** Works, but fragile and duplicated; breaks on Console changes; no clean restore. (This is what marketplace appearance plugins do today.)
- **Expose the upstream UI library's raw tokens directly.** Rejected — couples plugins to upstream token names and contradicts the existing "do not expose vendor config" design intent.
- **Only widen the current scalar list** (accent / surface / radius / …). Helps a little, but still cannot reach backgrounds / glass / full palettes.

## Additional Context

- Related: #7741 (merged — 6 palettes + accent/hover/background/surface/radius), #7406, #5909, #6312 (superseded by #7741), #7287 (external frontend gateway — `not_planned`).
- **Reference design**: DeepSeek Harness ships exactly this — `ctx.theme.overrideTokens(source, tokens)` plus a `ThemeDefinition` type (alias-token overrides, light + dark required), documented as *"Third-party themes can register alias-token overrides through `ctx.theme`."*
- Marketplace plugins currently working around this: `@osier-yi/qwenpaw-dream-skin`, `@levodoubt/background-wallpaper`, `@erickcharles/qwenpaw-no-glass`.

## Willing to Contribute

- [x] I am willing to open a PR for this feature (after discussion).

---

### 中文摘要

Console 的主题系统（#7741）让**用户**能换 6 套预设、自定义 accent / 背景 / 表面 / 圆角；但**插件**目前只有一个主题接口 `chat.theme.set(id, { colorPrimary })`。插件想深度定制（背景、毛玻璃、整套配色）没有官方入口，只能注入 CSS —— 市场里的外观类插件（Skin Studio、背景壁纸、去玻璃化）都是这么干的，Console 一改版就失效。

建议：**在 QwenPaw 自己的语义 token 层上加一个面向插件的覆盖接口**（而不是暴露上游 `AgentScope Runtime WebUI` 的原始 token）—— 这样上游升级时插件主题不受影响（只需 QwenPaw 内部重新映射）。愿意在讨论通过后提 PR，可先做最小版本。

issues.title: Creator: the only bundled inspiration example (cat-perspective-0803) still cannot be opened on Windows in 2.0.4 — regression of #7291, which was closed as fixed in 1.1.2
issues.body:
## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| QwenPaw core | **2.2.2.post1** (latest stable, published 2026-10-22) |
| qwenpaw-creator | **2.0.4** |
| Python | 3.12.13 |
| OS | Windows Server 2022 (10.0.20348), x86_64 |
| Locale / TZ | zh-CN / Asia/Shanghai |

## Summary

`POST /api/qwenpaw-creator/examples/cat-perspective-0803/open` fails with
`503 STORAGE_INTEGRITY_ERROR`. The archive downloads fine and its checksum
verifies; the failure is in extraction, because one directory inside the
archive contains a `:` and Windows cannot represent it.

`backend/examples/manifest.json` ships **exactly one** example, so on Windows
the entire "inspiration examples" feature is dead — there is no example a
Windows user can open.

This is the same failure reported in #7291, which was closed as `completed`
on 2026-08-31 with the note:

> Both issues (the `os.fsync` failure during archive download and the
> extraction failure caused by Windows-illegal characters like `:` in archive
> paths) are **fixed in qwenpaw-creator 1.1.2**. Please upgrade the plugin and
> try again — feel free to reopen if anything still fails.

2.0.4 is much later than 1.1.2, and it still fails. So this looks like a
regression, or the fix never landed in the released line.

## Reproduction

1. Install QwenPaw 2.2.2.post1 + qwenpaw-creator 2.0.4 on Windows.
2. Open Creator → home → inspiration examples → click "小猫视角"
   (`cat-perspective-0803`).
3. The download succeeds, then the request fails with 503.

Reproduced twice in a row (17:13 and 17:14 local), identical failure.

## Observed

Surfaced to the UI:

```
status=503 code=STORAGE_INTEGRITY_ERROR
method=POST path=/api/qwenpaw-creator/examples/cat-perspective-0803/open
error_id=error-999601b341b9492e925238c0ff9c2483
StorageIntegrityError: 灵感示例归档无法解包: cat-perspective-0803
```

The underlying exception, which is only visible in `creator.log`:

```
File ".../backend/api/example_routes.py", line 322, in _materialize_example
    _extract_example_archive(archive_path, extract_dir)
File ".../backend/services/project_files/archive.py", line 133, in extract_archive
    raise BadRequestError(
BadRequestError: archive path is not supported on Windows:
  'project-10ee251e37e45f64aaf560b1f5b5b09f/assets/source-intelligence/source:cat_cam_1/';
  import on Linux or macOS to preserve its media references
```

Download and integrity are **not** the problem:

```
17:13:32  Downloading remote file | url=https://creator-store.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com/example/cat-perspective-0803.zip max_bytes=2147483648 timeout=300s
17:13:49  Downloaded remote file | path=<data_root>/.example-staging/<uuid>/archive.zip, size_mib=106.2
17:13:50  Creator request failed ... status=503 code=STORAGE_INTEGRITY_ERROR
```

106.2 MiB in 17 s, and the sha256 check passed (a checksum mismatch would have
raised "校验失败" instead).

## Root cause, verified against the actual archive

I downloaded the archive independently and inspected it without extracting:

- `https://creator-store.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com/example/cat-perspective-0803.zip`
- compressed `111,352,101` B, sha256 `e91955b3b44ae4e78c117519e8e83887f7e6fab41df00976a786ed17b1f64c7b`
  — **matches** the manifest
- 465 members, 122.6 MiB uncompressed, 83 directories
- members with Windows-illegal characters: **2**
- members hitting reserved names (`CON`/`NUL`/`COM1`…): **0**
- members with trailing space/dot: **0**
- members with a path longer than 240 chars: **0**
- the only illegal character present: **`:`**

The two offending members:

```
DIR   project-10ee251e37e45f64aaf560b1f5b5b09f/assets/source-intelligence/source:cat_cam_1/
FILE  project-10ee251e37e45f64aaf560b1f5b5b09f/assets/source-intelligence/source:cat_cam_1/source-intelligence-5ee4da7fd8e35741bd8fc87189e3b170.json
```

That file is 32,817 B. So a 122.6 MiB / 465-member project is rejected in its
entirety because of one 32 KB sidecar.

`extract_archive` raises on the **first** unrepresentable member and aborts the
whole extraction, discarding everything already unpacked (`.example-staging` is
left empty).

### What the sidecar is

It is a source-intelligence index for a 21 m 48 s cat-POV clip: `8` shots,
`15` semanticEntries, `8` entities, a summary, `2` modelRuns,
`id = source-intelligence-5ee4da7fd8e35741bd8fc87189e3b170`.

Per the docstring on `SourceMemoryRef` in `schemas/assets.py`, this class of
artifact is *"Hydrated at read time from `runtime/source-intelligence/<index-id>/memory`;
never persisted inside the immutable index JSON"* — i.e. a derived cache, not
authoritative project data.

### How `project.json` references it

`source:cat_cam_1` occurs 4 times in `project.json` (86,832 B):

1. as a **dict key** under `sources.sources.items`
2. as the value of `"source_id"`
3. inside `"order": ["source:cat_cam_1"]`
4. as a **path**: `"relative_uri": "assets/source-intelligence/source:cat_cam_1/source-intelligence-5ee4da7fd8e35741bd8fc87189e3b170.json"` (with its own `sha256` and `file_id`)

Only **#4 is a filesystem path.** #1–#3 are logical identifiers that live
inside JSON and are legal on every platform.

Two facts that make a rename-based fix straightforward:

- The on-disk path is resolved **from the registry**, not derived from
  `source_id`:
  - `services/media/source_observation.py:401` → `Path(project_root, indexed.relative_uri)`
  - `services/file_agent_runtime/driver.py:9384` → `(project_root / indexed.relative_uri).read_text(...)`
  - `services/project_files/assets.py:412` → `project_root / PurePosixPath(indexed.relative_uri)`
- `_validate_relative_uri` (`services/project_files/models.py:170`) rejects only
  empty/untrimmed values, `\`, NUL, absolute paths, `<2` parts, a first part
  other than `assets`, and traversal segments. It accepts a sanitized name
  just as readily as the colon form — which is also why `project.json` itself
  loads fine on Windows and only *extraction* fails.

The registry `sha256` covers file **content**, so renaming the containing
directory does not invalidate it.

## The promised sanitizing logic is absent from 2.0.4

`services/project_files/archive.py` has exactly two `sys.platform == "win32"`
branches:

- line 127 — the hard `raise BadRequestError(...)` shown above
- line 149 — the `\\?\` long-path prefix

Grepping the whole backend for `sanitize`, `sanitize_windows`, `windows_safe`,
`def _sanitize`, `rewrite` returns **no hits**. There is no code path that
maps an unrepresentable member name to a legal one, and nothing that rewrites
`relative_uri` to match.

## Suggested fix

Essentially what #7291 said would ship:

1. When materializing an archive on Windows, map illegal characters in member
   names to legal ones (`:` is the one that actually occurs here) instead of
   aborting.
2. Rewrite the affected `relative_uri` entries in `project.json` so the
   registry keeps pointing at the real on-disk path.
3. Leave logical identifiers alone — `source_id`, the `sources.items` dict key
   and the `order` array are JSON-internal and need no change.
4. Apply the same handling to **user-imported** archives, not just bundled
   examples.

Two additional points worth considering:

- **Don't fail the whole import over one unrepresentable member.** Here the
  member is a 32 KB derived cache that is documented as hydrated-at-read-time.
  Skipping it with a warning would yield a fully usable project; aborting
  throws away 122.6 MiB of good data. A per-member skip-with-warning (or at
  least an explicit "N members could not be represented on Windows" summary)
  would degrade far more gracefully than a 503.
- **The error message loses the only actionable hint.** `example_routes.py:324`
  re-raises the `BadRequestError` as
  `StorageIntegrityError("灵感示例归档无法解包: cat-perspective-0803")`, so the
  user sees a bare 503 while the useful text ("archive path is not supported
  on Windows … import on Linux or macOS") stays in the log. Chaining the
  original reason into the user-facing message would make this self-diagnosing.

## Possibly wider impact (inference — not yet verified)

`source_id` values are generated by the app with a literal colon prefix
(`services/file_agent_runtime/driver.py:3197`:
`source_id = f"source:{uuid4().hex}"`, and the query expression
`("source:" + $logicalId) as $sourceKey` at `driver.py:10053` /
`services/project_files/agent_tools.py:562`).

If a project created on macOS/Linux materializes a source-intelligence
directory named after that id, then **any** such archive exported there and
imported on Windows would hit the same wall — not just the bundled example.
I have not verified this path end to end; flagging it because it would make
the fix worth prioritizing beyond the demo project.

## Minor: the #7184 cross-reference in #7291 does not resolve

The comment on #7291 says *"This is the same approach described in #7184 for
import archives"*, but #7184 is
"[Feature]: Add an Agent-level cross-session recall toggle for Scroll", which
is unrelated. Possibly a wrong issue number; mentioning it so the intended
prior art can be found.

## Workaround used while waiting

None needed for me — I do not require this example. Documenting the manual
route for anyone who does: fetch the archive, verify its sha256, extract the
463 representable members, rename `source:cat_cam_1` to a legal name, and
update the single `relative_uri` occurrence in `project.json` accordingly.
`source_id`, the dict key and `order` stay untouched.

issues.title: DoomLoopGate never triggers when agentscope accumulates a reply into one assistant message
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0 (Docker image `agentscope/qwenpaw:v2.3.0`). Also reproducible on `main` at `fc1db1a`.

## Description

With the default loop configuration (`window_size=3`, `similarity_threshold=1.0`, stages `after=3 / modify_prompt` and `after=4 / stop`), a turn that repeatedly calls the same tool with identical arguments never triggers either stage.

In a real 9-iteration console session on the default mode (the same failing SQL through `execute_readonly_sql` every round), `--log-level debug` showed `DefaultMode configured 2 gate(s)` and `LoopGate 'doom-loop' activated` on every iteration, but never `Doom loop: sim=`; the turn only ended via `IterationGate`. The persisted `agent.state.context` contained just two messages: the user message and one assistant message with 8 accumulated `tool_call`/`tool_result` block pairs.

**Root cause**

- agentscope 2.0.10 keeps **one assistant message per reply**. `Agent._save_to_context` uses `state.reply_id` as the message id and appends every iteration's blocks (reasoning, tool calls, tool results) to that same message.
- `DoomLoopGate._auto_record_from_ctx` (`src/qwenpaw/loop/gates/doom_loop.py`, around L205) returns as soon as the latest message id matches the last recorded one:

  ```python
  last_msg = context[-1]
  if last_msg.id == state.last_recorded_msg_id:
      return
  ```

  Within a reply the id never changes, so after the first check no further tool calls are recorded, `history_dirty` stays `False`, and `check()` returns `BYPASS` for the rest of the turn.
- Consequence: only a model response whose **first** snapshot already contains at least `window_size` identical tool calls (parallel calls in one response) can trip the window. Even then `consecutive_hits` is seeded to `window_size` and only increments on a later dirty check, so the `after=4 / stop` stage is unreachable in the default mode.

**Related PR(s):** coming in a follow-up PR.

**Security considerations:** none.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0 (`main` at `fc1db1a` also affected)
- **OS:** Debian 12, aarch64
- **Install method:** Docker
- **Python version:** 3.12 (agentscope 2.0.10)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use the default mode (console chat) with the default `agents.running.loop.doom_loop` stages.
2. Ask something that makes the agent call the same tool with exactly the same arguments at least 4 times (for example, the same failing SQL).
3. Observe that no doom-loop warning is injected and the loop is never stopped by the doom gate.

Minimal reproduction without an LLM:

```python
import asyncio
from types import SimpleNamespace

from qwenpaw.config.config import DoomLoopStageConfig
from qwenpaw.loop.gates.doom_loop import DoomLoopGate


async def main():
    msg = SimpleNamespace(id="reply-1", role="assistant", content=[])
    agent = SimpleNamespace(state=SimpleNamespace(context=[msg]))
    ctx = {
        "agent": agent,
        "final_msg": None,
        "iteration": 0,
        "has_tool_calls": True,
    }
    gate = DoomLoopGate(
        window_size=3,
        similarity_threshold=1.0,
        stages=[
            DoomLoopStageConfig(after=3, action="modify_prompt", prompt="warn"),
            DoomLoopStageConfig(after=4, action="stop", prompt="stop"),
        ],
    )
    for i in range(1, 7):
        # Same message id, one more identical tool call per formatting round,
        # exactly like agentscope accumulates blocks into one reply.
        msg.content.append(
            {
                "type": "tool_call",
                "name": "execute_readonly_sql",
                "input": {"sql": "SELECT 1"},
            },
        )
        result = await gate.check(ctx)
        state = gate._ensure_state()
        print(i, len(state.history), state.consecutive_hits, result.action.value)


asyncio.run(main())
```

Actual output on 2.3.0 / `main`:

```
1 1 0 bypass
2 1 0 bypass
3 1 0 bypass
4 1 0 bypass
5 1 0 bypass
6 1 0 bypass
```

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** `history` stays at 1 for the whole reply; both the warning and the stop stage never fire. The `after=4 / stop` stage is unreachable.
- **Expected:** the third identical call produces `INTERRUPT_AND_CONTINUE` with the configured warning prompt, the fourth produces `TERMINATE` with the stop prompt.

## Logs / Screenshots

```
[DEBUG] DefaultMode configured 2 gate(s)
[DEBUG] IterationGate: 1/100
[DEBUG] IterationGate: 2/100
...
[DEBUG] IterationGate: 9/100
(no "Doom loop: sim=" line anywhere)
```

## Additional Notes

The current unit tests only call `gate.record()` directly (`tests/unit/loop/test_doom_loop_gate.py`), so the `_auto_record_from_ctx` path has no coverage and this regression shipped unnoticed. A fix that consumes the tail of the accumulated message (count of already-recorded `tool_call` blocks) restores the intended 3-warning / 4-stop behaviour and keeps the 2.3.0 improvements (recording every tool call in the message, the `has_tool_calls` guard, and warning injection).

issues.title: 微信渠道报错
issues.body:
[Bug]: Official WeChat channel plugin fails to activate on startup with ACCOUNT_IN_USE — channel startup path and workspace projection both reserve the same runtime key
Summary
After upgrading to QwenPaw 2.3.0, the official WeChat channel plugin fails to activate on every startup with:

ProjectionError: channel 'wechat' failed: default@<id>:Projection channel failed: ACCOUNT_IN_USE
The channel never connects. This happens with a single QwenPaw instance, a single enabled agent, and no other process holding the WeChat account — so it is not the "account logged in elsewhere" case, and it is not the same bug as #8682 (that one crashes the worker at import with Could not determine home directory; here the worker starts fine and the failure is on the host side during projection).

The failure is deterministic and reproduces on every restart.

Environment
QwenPaw 2.3.0 (fnOS NAS app-center deployment, com.dustinky.qwenpaw, port 19091)
Linux x86_64, kernel 6.18.18.c1126-trim
Official WeChat channel plugin wechat 0.1.0.dev0 (qwenpaw_channel_wechat.driver.WeChatDriver)
Agents configured: 4 (default, QwenPaw_QA_Agent_0.2, Mikasa, Eren1) — only default has channels.wechat.enabled = true
Symptom (host log, every startup)
Plugin 'wechat' registered startup hook 'channel_wechat_wechat' (priority=80) Plugin 'wechat' registered workspace_created hook 'channel_ws_wechat_wechat' (priority=80) ... ERROR Plugin 'wechat' Projection channel failed: ACCOUNT_IN_USE ERROR Plugin 'wechat' marked FAILED after startup: channel 'wechat' failed: default@<id>:Projection channel failed: ACCOUNT_IN_USE ERROR Failed to activate plugin 'wechat': channel 'wechat' failed: ... ACCOUNT_IN_USE qwenpaw.plugins.workspace_projector.ProjectionError: channel 'wechat' failed: ... ACCOUNT_IN_USE
The worker's startup_diagnostic trace shows it reaches control / process_ready normally with platform_state: "disconnected" — i.e. the worker process itself does not crash. The failure is raised by the host while projecting the channel into the workspace.

What I ruled out
Not a second QwenPaw instance / not "logged in elsewhere". Confirmed only one qwenpaw process running and no other listener on the WeChat token. The worker never reaches the WeChat server (platform_state stays disconnected), so the account is not being contested remotely.
Not a cross-agent token conflict. Only default has wechat enabled. I computed wechat_auth_scopes for default vs every other agent — the scope intersection is empty, so the "cross-agent credential intersection" branch of _reserve_wechat_auth_evidence is not what fires.
Not stale custody / leftover worker. No leftover worker.py / channel_wechat process after a clean stop; no lease/lock files on disk (plugin_provisions/wechat.json is empty, no persistent owner rows).
Suspected root cause
In 2.3.0 the WeChat channel moved from the built-in in-process implementation to the plugin + workspace-projection architecture. During startup two code paths both try to reserve the same channel/wechat runtime key for the default workspace:

the channel startup hook (channel_wechat_wechat) → start_channel → manager._reserve_channel_auth → reserve_wechat_auth_async, which reserves RuntimeKey("channel", "wechat", workspace_dir) plus the wechat_auth claims; and
the workspace projection path (workspace_projector._apply / channel_ws_wechat_wechat), which reserves the same key again.
Whichever path runs second finds the key already owned by a different owner and raises ACCOUNT_IN_USE (via _reserve_wechat_auth_evidence, the resource.owner != owner branch). With the old built-in implementation there was only one path, so this never collided.

The plugin is then torn down and marked FAILED, so the channel never recovers without a restart (and a restart hits the same race).

Suggested direction (for maintainers to confirm)
Make the two paths idempotent for the same workspace — e.g. have the projection path reuse an existing channel/wechat lease owned by the same plugin/instance instead of treating it as ACCOUNT_IN_USE, or ensure only one of the two startup paths performs the reservation. (I'll leave the exact fix to you — happy to test a candidate build.)

Reproduction
QwenPaw 2.3.0 on Linux, official WeChat plugin installed and enabled for a single agent.
Start / restart the app.
Observe Plugin 'wechat' ... ACCOUNT_IN_USE and the channel stuck failed.
Deterministic — reproduces on every restart.

Notes
Separately, #8682 / PR #8692 address a different failure mode (worker crashes for lack of HOME / QWENPAW_WORKING_DIR). Applying #8692 does not fix this ACCOUNT_IN_USE issue — the worker here starts fine; the failure is in the host projection/lease path.
Happy to provide more logs or test a fix.

issues.title: [Bug] Agent switch deletes the agent's last session (lastChatIdByAgent) and makes historical sessions unclickable - 2.2.1-beta.2
issues.body:
## Summary

Two concrete defects in the console's session bookkeeping that fire on **every agent switch**. They are independent of the "always start on a blank conversation" behaviour discussed in #7687 — I understand from the reply there that landing on a blank chat is intentional, so the sections below are about **state loss** and a **dead interaction**, not about that design choice. (Design feedback of my own is at the bottom, clearly separated.)

**Environment:** QwenPaw Desktop **2.2.1-beta.2**, Windows 10 (AMD64). Console bundle built **2026-09-10 17:48:28**: `index-8OrhnpZF.js` + chat chunk `index-BAFRWhpS.js` (71,879 B). I also compared tags `v2.2.1-beta.2...v2.2.1` on GitHub: it contains **0 `console/` file changes** (the only diff is README/version/release-notes), so this applies to **2.2.1** as well. Line numbers below are from tag `v2.2.1`'s `console/src/pages/Chat/index.tsx` (byte-identical to `v2.2.1-beta.2`).

## 1. The agent's "last session" record is **deleted**, not skipped

The switch effect (L2719-2723) creates a draft-shaped local id on every switch:

```ts
sessionApi.preferredChatId = null;
sessionApi.lastActiveChatId = null;
navigate(CHAT_BASE_PATH, { replace: true });
sessionApi.userInitiatedCreate = true;
void sessionApi.createSession({});   // id like 1789094161754-iyotsc2
```

and `onSessionCreated` (L2667-2673) then persists it. But the store treats draft-shaped ids as **delete** signals:

```ts
setLastChatId(agent, id) {
  if (/^\d+-[a-z0-9]+$/.test(id)) { delete lastChatIdByAgent[agent]; return; }
  /* else: record */
}
```

⇒ Every agent switch **erases `lastChatIdByAgent[agent]`**. That forms a self-reinforcing loop — *no memory → draft id created → memory deleted* — so an agent that is switched to but not messaged in can never regain its last session. Verified in `localStorage["qwenpaw-agent-storage"].state.lastChatIdByAgent` (read out of the WebView2 leveldb): the entries are either real UUIDs or missing entirely; the agents missing there are exactly the ones that were never messaged while sitting on the blank chat.

Suggested fix: on a draft-shaped id, **skip** the write (`if (isDraftId(id)) return;`) instead of deleting the existing record.

## 2. Historical sessions become unclickable while a draft is active

`onSessionSelected` (L2588-2594) returns early as soon as the active chat is an unresolved local draft:

```ts
if (sessionApi.lastActiveChatId && sessionApi.isUnresolvedLocalSession(sessionApi.lastActiveChatId)) return;
```

After a switch, clicking a conversation in the sidebar does nothing — there is **no manual way back** to the previous session, which is what makes defect 1 so visible in practice.

## 3. A message sent right after a switch is silently registered as a new chat, and the backend then rejects tool calls

`%USERPROFILE%\.qwenpaw\qwenpaw.log`:

```
Auto-registered new chat: c463285d-… -> 1789094161754-iyotsc2
tool_calls.py:91 session_id mismatch: url=1789094161754-iyotsc2 backend=<real session uuid>   # 10+ occurrences within one minute
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open agent A and go into one of its existing conversations.
2. Switch to another agent (B).
3. Switch back to A and **send a message immediately**.
4. The message appears in a **new conversation** (title auto-generated from the first line); the original conversation shows no trace of it, and per defect 1 the agent's last-session record has been erased.

## Minimal fixes I would suggest

1. In the switch branch, restore `getLastChatId(selectedAgent)` when it is a real backend id — this is what the 2026-08-31 build (`index-DeBQK-i1.js`) did — and fall back to a blank chat only when there is none.
2. `setLastChatId`: never `delete` for a draft-shaped id; skip the write.
3. Don't return early from `onSessionSelected` for draft ids (or give the user an explicit way out of the blank chat).
4. Never send with a draft id as the session target: resolve/register first, so the `session_id mismatch` rejections stop.

*(No upstream change was made here; to validate 1–3 I string-patched my own installed console chunk off-line. Happy to share the diff if useful.)*

## Design feedback (separate from the bug report)

Even granting "always start the newly selected agent on a blank conversation", the practical effect is a loss of continuity: after switching agent — or simply reopening the app the next day — you cannot continue where you left off, and per defect 2 you cannot even click your way back. The 2026-08-31 build restored the agent's last session instead. If the blank start is deliberate, a per-agent "remember the last conversation" option (default on) would solve this without changing your intended first-run behaviour.

## 中文小结

切智能体时会**删掉该 agent 的"上次会话"记录**（草稿形 id 在 store 里是 `delete` 而不是跳过），同时"草稿态守卫"会让侧栏的历史会话**点不动**，所以切回来直接发消息就会被静默 `Auto-registered` 成一条新对话、原对话被一分为二，后端还会成片 `session_id mismatch` 拒绝工具调用。这三条与 #7687 里"切过去落在空白对话"的设计无关（那部分我接受），建议按上文 4 条最小改动修一下；另外希望能把"记住上次会话"作为可选项。谢谢！

issues.title: Bug reports from a guardrail-plugin build: console attachment stale blob, one-shot cron misfire drop, console tail-drop, on_acting never fires
issues.body:
### Environment
QwenPaw 2.2.0 (pip, macOS 25.6.0 arm64, Python 3.12.14), single daemon on 127.0.0.1, WeChat + console channels, custom gate plugins registered via `register_middleware`.

**1 — Console channel: 2nd+ image attachment in a session re-sends the first attachment's bytes (stale blob).**
Repro (~2 min): open a fresh console page → attach image A, send → agent reports A correctly → attach image B, send → the image block delivered to the agent is still A (bytes/filename of the first upload). Only the first attachment per session survives. WeChat and on-disk paths are unaffected.

**2 — One-shot cron jobs whose fire time passes while the daemon is down are dropped, not served after restart.**
Observed 2026-09-11: a one-shot `scheduled` job (14:46:31, `misfire_grace_seconds: 600` in its own spec) expired while the daemon was offline; after restart it was never executed and left no failure record. Impact: notification/watchdog jobs silently vanish exactly when they are most needed (i.e. after a crash or reboot). Expected: serve late within the grace window, or mark the job failed with a visible reason.

**3 — Console UI drops the tail of a completed assistant message (persistence intact, render truncated).**
Observed 2026-09-11 19:1x: the persisted message in history.db / session store holds the full text; the browser showed everything except the last two blocks (a closing paragraph and a final standalone sentence). The following message rendered fully, so it is not a global rendering failure. This makes delivery completeness unverifiable from the receiving side, which matters for agents that assert "I sent X".

**4 — Agent middleware `on_acting` is not invoked on the shell/tool path; `on_model_call` and `ToolMiddlewareBase` are.**
A middleware registered normally (priority-checked, loaded, no errors) never fired a single event across hours of real tool calls, while the same turn's `on_model_call` fired reliably. Post-restart live probe confirmed zero invocations. This makes tool-call interception impossible via agent middleware and pushes gate authors into in-tool guards or `ToolMiddlewareBase`. Expected: documented (or fixed) — the plugin docs advertise `on_acting` wrapping as a supported extension point.

**5 — Docs gap: per-tool / per-turn call budgets.** `loop-engineering` covers iteration, doom-loop and rubric; per-tool caps exist in config but are undocumented, so plugin authors reimplement them via wrapper indirection.

Found while building a guardrail layer over the agent loop (deterministic pre/post checks + telemetry); happy to test patches on the above.

issues.title: [Bug] Plugin install fails with 'No package metadata was found' for qwenpaw-creator
issues.body: ## Description  When attempting to install the official `qwenpaw-creator` plugin (v2.0.4) via both the extension UI and the CLI, the installation fails with the error:  ``` QwenPaw is running — using hot-install via API... ❌ API install failed: No package metadata was found. ```  ## Environment  - QwenPaw version: 2.3.0b2 - OS: Windows 10 (AMD64) - Plugin: qwenpaw-creator 2.0.4 - Plugin URL: https://agentscope-platform-sg-bucket.oss-accelerate.aliyuncs.com/plugin-platform/qwenpaw-creator/2.0.4/qwenpaw-creator-2.0.4.zip  ## Steps to Reproduce  1. Open QwenPaw Desktop 2. Try to install qwenpaw-creator plugin from the extensions panel 3. OR run via CLI:    ```    qwenpaw plugin install https://agentscope-platform-sg-bucket.oss-accelerate.aliyuncs.com/plugin-platform/qwenpaw-creator/2.0.4/qwenpaw-creator-2.0.4.zip    ``` 4. Observe error: `API install failed: No package metadata was found.`  ## Investigation  - The plugin zip URL is accessible and downloads successfully (5MB, 392 entries) - The zip contains a valid `plugin.json` at `qwenpaw-creator/plugin.json` with proper metadata:   - id: qwenpaw-creator   - name: QwenPaw Creator   - version: 2.0.4   - type: app   - entry: backend/main.py, ui/dist/index.js   - qwenpaw_version: min 2.1.0 - The error occurs during the 'hot-install via API' step, suggesting the backend API cannot find/parse the package metadata  ## Expected Behavior  The plugin should install successfully since the package metadata is present in the zip.  ## Additional Context  - This affects both the extension UI install and CLI install paths - The same error appears in both cases - QwenPaw version 2.3.0b2 should satisfy the plugin's minimum version requirement of 2.1.0

issues.title: Creator: a FAILED remote asset_ingest is terminal — no retry path exists, so the asset preview 404s forever even after the transient cause is gone (the store already sanctions FAILED -> QUEUED)
issues.body:
## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| QwenPaw core | 2.3.0 |
| qwenpaw-creator | **2.0.6** |
| Python | 3.12.13 |
| OS | Windows Server 2022 (10.0.20348), x86_64 |
| Image model | `wan2.7-image-pro` via an **Aliyun Token Plan** endpoint (`https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/api/v1`) |

## Summary

A remote-URL asset whose `asset_ingest` task fails once is **bricked forever**.
The asset preview returns `404` for the rest of the project's life, even after
the transient cause of the failure is gone and the URL is demonstrably alive
again. There is no retry path — not in the UI, not in the API.

## Observed

```
GET /api/qwenpaw-creator/media/assets/<asset-version-id>
-> 404 {"code":"NOT_FOUND","message":"远程 Asset 本地缓存尚未完成"}
```

The version record is intact and registered:

```json
{
  "version_id": "asset-version-...",
  "file_id": null,
  "media_type": "image/png",
  "metadata": {
    "sourceKind": "remote_url",
    "publicSourceUrl": "https://<user-host>/temp/<name>.png",
    "checksumKind": "source_url_sha256",
    "cacheTaskId": "task-..."
  }
}
```

Its ingest task:

```json
{
  "kind": "asset_ingest",
  "status": "FAILED",
  "error": {
    "code": "ASSET_INGEST_FAILED",
    "message": "无法读取远程 Asset: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: certificate has expired (_ssl.c:1010)",
    "type": "ValidationError"
  }
}
```

The failure was **transient**: the source host's certificate has since been
renewed. A direct `HEAD` on the same URL now returns `200`,
`content-type: image/png`, `content-length: 2400646`. The bytes are available;
Creator just never asks again.

(Another instance of the same shape failed with
`ConnectError: [WinError 10055]` — WSAENOBUFS — which is equally transient.)

## Why it cannot recover

`api/file_media_routes.py::_indexed_response` allows `indexed is None` for a
source version, then calls `resolve_remote_cache(...)`, and raises
`NotFoundError("远程 Asset 本地缓存尚未完成")` when it returns `None`.

`services/project_files/remote_cache.py::resolve_remote_cache` only considers
tasks where:

```python
task.kind is TaskKind.ASSET_INGEST
and task.status is TaskStatus.SUCCEEDED
and task.metadata.get("assetVersionId") == version.version_id
```

and then requires `result.items[]` to carry `cacheRelativeUri`,
`cacheSizeBytes`, `cacheChecksum`. A FAILED task has no result, so the cache can
never resolve — **even if the file were placed at the expected path by hand**.

The one endpoint that looks like a retry,
`POST /projects/{pid}/source-cache/{vid}/download`, cannot help either: it calls
`_source_cache_task_item`, whose docstring is *"Locate the bundled SUCCEEDED
asset_ingest result for one version"* and which filters on
`task.status is TaskStatus.SUCCEEDED`. With a FAILED task it returns `None` and
the route answers:

```
404 {"code":"NOT_FOUND","message":"缺少远程素材入库任务记录，无法下载原片"}
```

That endpoint is for re-fetching footage whose ingest *succeeded* but whose
cache was evicted — not for retrying a failed ingest.

Re-POSTing `/projects/{pid}/assets` with the same URL and `clientRequestId`
does not retry either, because `_run_remote_task_sync` returns early:

```python
if task.status in {TaskStatus.SUCCEEDED, TaskStatus.FAILED, TaskStatus.CANCELLED}:
    return
```

## The store already sanctions a retry

`services/runtime_files/execution_store.py`:

```python
# The durable Task identity and request fingerprint stay fixed across an
# explicitly authorized retry; only a FAILED Task may reopen as QUEUED.
TaskStatus.FAILED: frozenset({TaskStatus.QUEUED}),
```

So the state machine explicitly anticipates an authorized retry, but **no
caller exposes it for `asset_ingest`**.

## Verified workaround (what I did)

1. Reopen the task through the official store API (checksum CAS, not raw JSON):

```python
store.transition_task(pid, tid,
    expected_status={TaskStatus.FAILED},
    status=TaskStatus.QUEUED,
    updates={"error": None, "progress": 0.0})
```

2. Re-POST `/projects/{pid}/assets` with the **original** identity, taken from
   the task's own metadata so the stable ids and request fingerprint match:

```json
{"kind":"url","value":"<original sourceUrl>","name":"<original requestedName>",
 "clientRequestId":"<original key>","postIngestAction":"ATTACH_SOURCE"}
```

Because remote ingest derives deterministic ids
(`_stable_id("asset-version", project_id, key, "0")`), this returns the **same**
`assetVersionId` and the **same** `taskId` — no duplicate asset, and every
existing reference (`sources…selected_asset_version_id`,
`visual…reference_asset_version_ids`) stays valid.

Result: `202` -> task **SUCCEEDED within 3 seconds**, cache materialized at
`runtime/asset-cache/<version-id>.png` (2,400,646 B), and the preview route
returns **200** with `content-type: image/png` and a matching sha256 ETag.

## Suggested fix

Expose the already-sanctioned `FAILED -> QUEUED` transition for `asset_ingest`
as a first-class retry — e.g. let
`POST /projects/{pid}/source-cache/{vid}/download` accept a FAILED task and
re-run the ingest, or add an explicit retry route. A transient network or TLS
failure on a user-supplied URL should not permanently destroy an asset that the
project still references.

Secondarily: `_version_in_project` converts a `ProjectIntegrityError` into
"no match" (and logs a warning), which makes an unloadable project
indistinguishable from a missing asset in the 404 response. That is deliberate
and documented, but it makes this class of problem harder to diagnose from the
client side.

prs.title: feat(sdk): expand plugin SDK 1.1 APIs, lifecycle management, and developer tooling
prs.body:
## Description

Expand the public plugin SDK to version 1.1 so plugins can implement common features through supported APIs, with identity, permissions, coordination, and resource lifecycle managed by the host.

This PR adds or extends:

- Request identity, model selection, scoped conversation history, and run queries.
- Dynamic prompts, stop conditions, scheduled workflows, and pluggable shell execution backends.
- Skill market language/category filters and cancellation during installation.
- Managed threads and interactive processes, file uploads/downloads, workspace paths, and legacy storage import.
- Draft reading and safe replacement, frontend registration, and checkpoint save/preview/restore APIs.
- Process-based channel drivers, structured messages, approvals, delivery tracking, management operations, and HTTP/WebSocket ingress.
- Public types, SDK version checks, channel templates, and plugin testing tools.

Representative plugins were used for local validation. Their implementations and dedicated acceptance tests are excluded from this PR. Shared SDK regression tests remain self-contained.

**Related Issue:** None linked.

**Security Considerations:** Resource access remains scoped to the applicable plugin, user, workspace, and session. Checkpoint restoration uses host coordination and approval. Stale results cannot overwrite a changed draft. Remote execution failures do not automatically fall back to local execution. Cleanup must not report completion while owned threads or processes remain active.

prs.title: fix(scroll): recognize url-referenced media in tool-result folding
prs.body:
## Description

When a chat session accumulates enough turns to trigger context compression, historical completed tool results are inspected by `ScrollContextManager._tool_result_fold_candidates()` to collapse long or media-carrying results into compact pointer stubs (`[scroll folded] ...`).

Previously, `_tool_result_has_inline_media()` only checked for `source.get("type") == "base64"` or `source.type == "base64"`. URL-referenced media blocks (`source.type == "url"`), such as video, audio, or image outputs generated by `send_file_to_user` and similar tools, were not recognized as inline media. Consequently, these media tool results failed the `has_media` check and, having short text captions (<= 200 chars), were skipped by `_tool_result_fold_candidates()`.

As a result, uncollapsed media blocks were carried over across turns and re-spliced verbatim into rebuilt request payloads after compression. Subsequent model API requests failed repeatedly with errors such as `400: Video count 2 exceeds limit 1 per request`, permanently hanging the session for that channel.

This change extends `_tool_result_has_inline_media()` to recognize `source.type == "url"` with non-empty URL values for both dictionary-based and object-based sources.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8474

**Security Considerations:** None.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Why the issue happens

In `src/qwenpaw/agents/context/scroll/manager.py`:

```python
    @staticmethod
    def _tool_result_has_inline_media(block: Any) -> bool:
        ...
        for item in output:
            if ScrollContextManager._block_type(item) != "data":
                continue
            source = (
                item.get("source")
                if isinstance(item, dict)
                else getattr(item, "source", None)
            )
            if isinstance(source, dict):
                if source.get("type") == "base64" and source.get("data"):
                    return True
            elif getattr(source, "type", None) == "base64" and getattr(
                source,
                "data",
                None,
            ):
                return True
        return False
```

When a tool output provides a data block with a URL source (`source={"type": "url", "url": "https://..."}`), `_tool_result_has_inline_media` returned `False`.

In `_tool_result_fold_candidates`:

```python
    has_media = self._tool_result_has_inline_media(block)
    if (
        not has_media
        and self._tool_result_text_chars(block) <= _PRE_TRIM_MIN_CHARS
    ):
        continue
```

Because `has_media` was `False` and media tool results generally have little or no text characters (`<= 200`), the block was skipped and never folded. During context compression and payload rebuild, the raw media block remained in the active payload.

## The change

1. In `src/qwenpaw/agents/context/scroll/manager.py`, `_tool_result_has_inline_media` now also checks:
   - For dict sources: `source.get("type") == "url" and source.get("url")`
   - For object sources: `getattr(source, "type", None) == "url" and getattr(source, "url", None)`
2. In `tests/unit/agents/context/test_scroll_manager.py`:
   - Added `test_tool_result_has_inline_media_recognizes_url_sources` to test both base64 and URL sources across dict and object representations as well as negative cases.
   - Added `test_pressure_fold_recognizes_url_media_independently_of_text_length` to verify that tool results carrying URL media bypass the text length restriction and fold into pointer stubs under context pressure.

## Checklist

- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [x] Ready for review

## Testing

Verified with pytest on the scroll context manager suite:

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/agents/context/test_scroll_manager.py -k 'test_tool_result_has_inline_media_recognizes_url_sources or test_pressure_fold_recognizes_url_media_independently_of_text_length' -v

======================= 2 passed, 83 deselected in 1.26s =======================
```


prs.title: fix(providers): read a gateway-reported status from the error text
prs.body:
## Description

`extract_status_code()` reads a status from the exception's `status_code`, `code`, `response`, and `body`/`details` fields, and falls back to the message text for one narrow gateway format — `Streaming response failed: [503] ...`.

An OpenAI-compatible gateway that fails mid-stream can instead report the status only inside the message text, for example `status_code=502, 请联系管理员处理！ (request id: ...)`. The OpenAI SDK raises a base `APIError` for such a response: no `status_code`, no `response`. The real status is present in the text, but the fallback does not recognise that shape, so `classify_model_error()` returns `unknown` — no same-model retry, no cross-model fallback, and the turn or scheduled job dies. The same upstream failure wrapped as a real HTTP 502 is `transient` and does fall back, so identical failures behave differently only because of how the gateway phrased them.

This adds one more narrow pattern for gateway error text, keeping the same deliberate narrowness the existing fallback documents: only `4xx`/`5xx` are read, so a success code quoted in a message (`expected status_code=200`) is never mistaken for a failure, and unrelated three-digit numbers in provider messages are still ignored.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8505

**Security Considerations:** None — this only affects how a provider error is classified, never what is sent to a provider.

## Type of Change

Running the same full check with the base `c26d31c06` `error_utils.py` in place exits 1 with the identical findings, so this change neither adds to nor removes any of them. The issue also raises form A — a gateway that reports `type=upstream_error` / `bad_response_status_code` and wraps the upstream 5xx in HTTP 400, which is classified as `bad_request` and so is not fallback-eligible. That one is a policy question about what counts as transient, so this PR leaves it alone.

prs.title: fix(task_tracker): bound the run completion callback and always clean up
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes the **run-cleanup half** of #8173: a chat run whose completion callback hangs or is cancelled never releases its entry in `TaskTracker._runs`, so the run stays `running` forever.

### Root cause

`TaskTracker._producer` clears its `_runs` entry and pushes the end-of-stream sentinel at the end of a `finally` block, *after* awaiting the `on_finished` completion callback. Two paths meant that cleanup never completed:

1. **The callback hangs.** `on_finished` is `ChatManager.mark_chat_finished`, which persists a completion marker under a lock shared with ~24 other manager methods. Lock contention or a stalled repo suspends the producer task *inside its own `finally`*. The task is then not done **and** the entry is still registered, so every status reader reports `running` — workspace reload is blocked and inbound messages are dropped with HTTP 409.
2. **The producer is cancelled mid-callback.** `CancelledError` is a `BaseException`, so it escapes the `except Exception` guard and skips cleanup entirely, leaving subscriber streams without their sentinel.

### The fix

- Run the callback through `asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(...))` bounded by `ON_FINISHED_TIMEOUT`, so a hung callback is logged and given up on rather than holding the run open.
- Move the cleanup into a nested `finally` so it always runs.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8173

Deliberately *not* `Fixes` — see the scope note below.

### Scope — what this does **not** fix

This addresses the cleanup leak only. The other items from #8173 are **not** implemented here: the post-spawn connection health probe, the idle watchdog, `force` semantics on the reload/disable-enable paths, and in-channel hints for `/new` and `/stop` on backends that do not support them. Those are larger design questions and I would rather land the narrow fix first.

Note that the wedge is now **bounded** by `ON_FINISHED_TIMEOUT` rather than eliminated: the run stays `running` while the callback runs, because `test_attach_or_start_reports_completion_before_becoming_idle` pins that ordering deliberately (it asserts `get_status == "running"` from inside the callback). Reordering the pop ahead of the callback would break that contract.

### What the new tests cover

New `tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py` (6 tests) covers a hung callback, a callback that raises, a callback that raises `TimeoutError`, a producer cancelled mid-callback, and `request_stop` against a slow callback. Waits are event-based rather than fixed sleeps.

Against unmodified source these fail on behavioural assertions (`run entry survived a hung completion callback`, etc.), not on import or attribute errors.

### Security Considerations

Not applicable — no change to channel auth, credentials, or config handling.

## Evidence

Verification is a real failure on unmodified source followed by the **same command** against the patched tree. Base is `5c56644a` (`main`), patch is `e2b7b8be`.

**1. Unmodified baseline — the new tests genuinely fail.**

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py
=========================== short test summary info ============================
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_hung_completion_callback_does_not_block_new_messages
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_completion_callback_timeout_is_logged_not_raised
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_cancellation_during_callback_still_clears_the_run
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_request_stop_with_a_slow_callback_does_not_wedge_the_run
4 failed, 1 passed in 8.32s
```

**2. Same command with the patch — all green.**

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py
.......................                                                  [100%]
23 passed in 0.49s
```

**3. Full `tests/unit/app` with the patch — no regression.**


prs.title: fix(providers): allow fallback for 4xx quota errors
prs.body:
## Summary

Some providers return HTTP 400 with a quota or rate-limit message instead of
HTTP 429 when the primary model's quota is exhausted. The shared error policy
classified these responses as `bad_request`, which made them ineligible for
cross-model fallback.

This change recognizes structured provider error codes and narrowly scoped
quota and rate-limit messages on 4xx responses before the generic
`bad_request` fallback, allowing `FallbackChatModel` to try the next
configured model without retrying an exhausted quota.

## Changes

- Read normalized provider `code` and `type` values from structured error
  payloads, with complete semantic phrases as the message fallback.
- Classify non-429 quota exhaustion as `quota_exceeded`, allowing fallback
  without retrying the same model.
- Preserve retry behavior for standard HTTP 429 and explicit rate-limit
  errors, along with the existing priority of authentication,
  model-not-found, request-size, context-overflow, and content-safety
  classification.
- Add negative tests proving that unrelated quota and rate-limit parameter
  errors remain `bad_request`.
- Add a production-style `FallbackChatModel` to `RetryChatModel` regression
  test proving that the primary and fallback models are each called once.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest tests/unit/providers/test_model_error_policy.py tests/unit/providers/test_fallback_chat_model.py -q`
  - 73 passed.
- `python -m pytest tests/unit/providers -q`
  - 1170 passed, 1 skipped, 2 failed.
  - Both failures are unrelated to this change and occur while importing the
    unavailable `reme.components.as_decision_model` module.
- All pre-commit hooks applicable to the changed Python files passed.

Fixes #8776

prs.title: fix(desktop): safely replace bundled Windows runtimes during upgrades
prs.body:
## Description

Windows upgrades can fail when an external process restarts `qwenpaw --version` after the installer stops processes, locking bundled Python extensions again. File-by-file replacement also leaves obsolete or unknown files in the bundled runtime directories.

Keep the CLI unavailable throughout replacement, including the "uninstall before installing" path. Immediately before copying the new payload, remove only the four bundled directories under `binaries`: `qwenpaw-backend`, `python-runtime`, `channel-runtime`, and `node-runtime`.

- Gate the old CLI and Native Messaging launcher during installation; publish the staged CLI only after all resources have been copied.
- Keep the installation marker outside the directories being replaced, recognize interrupted installations even when their binaries are gone, and retain compatibility with the previous marker location.
- Validate installation ancestors and runtime trees before deletion, rejecting directory links and other reparse points. Cleanup failure prevents copying the new payload.
- Guard the registered previous installation before invoking its uninstaller, preserving the selected destination when upgrading to another directory. Runtime cleanup runs only in the new installation section.
- Prevent skipping failed writes. Cancellation before replacement restores the old entry; after destructive work begins, rerunning the installer repairs the installation. No runtime rollback is added.

**Related Issue:** No linked issue; reproduced on Windows during a desktop upgrade.

**Security Considerations:** Cleanup is restricted to the four bundled runtime directories. User history, configuration, plugin dependencies and unrelated installation directories remain outside this cleanup. Files manually added inside the four bundled directories are removed.

prs.title: fix(loop): record tool calls appended to one reply message
prs.body:
## Description

`DoomLoopGate` never fired on 2.3.0. agentscope 2.0.10 appends every iteration's blocks to the same assistant message and uses `state.reply_id` as its id, so `_auto_record_from_ctx` — which treated the message id as a per-iteration cursor — recorded only the first snapshot of a reply. With the default `window_size=3`, the warning could fire only when that first snapshot already held 3 identical calls, and the `after=4 / stop` stage was unreachable.

A reply is not always a single message either: when a warning is injected, `check_pending_gates()` appends a user continuation message and the next reasoning step opens a new assistant message that reuses the same `reply_id`. Neither the message id nor a per-message block count can tell which calls were already recorded, so this revision tracks the `id` of every recorded tool-call block for the turn and records only ids it has not seen yet. Every iteration contributes its own calls, and re-checking an unchanged snapshot stays a no-op. (Thanks to @lalaliat for pointing out the message-count gap in review.)

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8700

**Security Considerations:** none.

```bash
# warning is skipped, so the stop stage never fires
pytest tests/unit/loop/test_doom_loop_gate.py -q
# 1 failed, 11 passed
# FAILED test_auto_record_survives_injected_continuation_message
#   assert <StopAction.BYPASS: 'bypass'> == <StopAction.TERMINATE: 'terminate'>

# current revision (tool-call id dedupe)
```

```bash
Lint GitHub Actions workflow files......................................Skipped
```

```bash

# reuses reply_id; the block count still says 3, so the call is never recorded
FAILED tests/unit/loop/test_doom_loop_gate.py::test_auto_record_survives_injected_continuation_message
E   AssertionError: assert <StopAction.BYPASS: 'bypass'> == <StopAction.TERMINATE: 'terminate'>
1 failed, 11 passed in 0.83s
```

prs.title: feat(plugins): expose the semantic colour roles to plugin themes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#8071 asks for a plugin theme extension point. #8422 landed the first slice:
six roles (`bg`, `surface`, `surface-raised`, `border`, `text`,
`text-secondary`). Those cover the page frame, but not the semantic colour
surface a theme actually has to touch — a plugin that wants its own accent,
status colours, or the lower-contrast text and border tiers still has to reach
into raw `--app-*` names, which this closed API deliberately rejects.

This PR widens the closed set to the 31 semantic colour roles that
`console/src/styles/tokens.css` already defines and the console already
consumes, and keeps the compatibility story honest:

- the original six roles keep their current minimum SDK version, so plugins
  that already call `overrideTokens` are unaffected;
- the new roles sit behind `sdk.version >= 1.2.0` plus a `themeTokens`
  capability, so a plugin cannot silently depend on a role that an older host
  does not know.

Group 2 from #8071 (fifteen shape and layer roles: radius, shadow,
focus-ring, scrollbar, fill) stays out of this PR and is left for a separate
discussion, as requested.

## Evidence

Every role below is already read by the console. No component was changed and
no new colour was invented — this only opens roles that exist.

| family | role | representative consumer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| surface | `surface-subtle` | `layouts/index.module.less:324` |
| surface | `surface-sunken` | `components/RenderableCodeBlock/index.module.less:122` |
| surface | `shell-bg` | `layouts/dockableSidebar.module.less:13` |
| text | `text-tertiary` | `layouts/dockableSidebar.module.less:36` |
| text | `text-quaternary` | `layouts/index.module.less:254` |
| border | `border-subtle` | `layouts/index.module.less:53` |
| border | `border-strong` | `layouts/sidebarA.module.less:99` |
| accent | `accent` | `App.tsx:421` |
| accent | `accent-hover` | `App.tsx:422` |
| accent | `accent-soft` | `App.tsx:423` |
| status | `success-bg` | `components/LoopInput/index.module.less:57` |
| status | `warning-border` | `components/Chat/ToolCards/shared/offloadBanner.module.less:11` |
| status | `error-text` | `tauri/BackendLoadingPage.module.less:52` |

Both schemes are exercised rather than assumed: `themeTokens.test.ts` asserts
each role lands in the `:root` block with its light value and in the
`html.dark-mode` block with its dark value.

## Self-review

1. Overlapping registrations — `install.test.ts` keeps the existing
   "stacks per token and falls back on dispose" case, and the new semantic
   roles go through the same stacking path.
2. Switching scheme or preset while an override is active —
   `themeTokens.integration.test.ts` keeps "wins over the preset's inline
   `--app-surface` in both schemes" and "restores the preset when the plugin is
   unloaded".
3. Cleanup — "removes the element once every override is gone" and
   `disposeAll(pluginId)` both still clear the new roles.
4. Invalid input — a role missing one scheme and a genuinely unknown name both
   still throw; the unknown-name case now uses `not-a-role` so it does not
   accidentally test a role that became valid in this PR.
5. Backward compatibility — `sdk.version: 1.0.0` stays valid for the original
   six roles; `1.1.0` with `themeTokens` is rejected with a clear message;
   `1.2.0` with `themeTokens` is accepted.

## Test scope

- Console: `src/plugins/hostSdk/install.test.ts`,
  `src/plugins/themeTokens.test.ts`,
  `src/plugins/themeTokens.integration.test.ts` — 41 passed.
- Python: `tests/unit/plugins` — full directory passed, including the new
  `test_theme_tokens_capability_gates_on_sdk_version`.
- `tsc -b --noEmit`, eslint and prettier on the touched files.

## Coordination with #8764

#8764 also moves `SDK_VERSION` to `1.2.0` and touches
`src/qwenpaw/plugins/frontend/index.d.ts`. This PR needs the same version slot.
Whichever lands first, the other rebases onto it — the two changes are additive

prs.title: fix(crons): drop invalid jobs.json entries on startup (migration)
prs.body:
Fixes #4835

The migration approach discussed in #5040 (root-cause cleanup rather than runtime tolerance).

## What

`migrate_invalid_jobs()` runs on workspace start — right after the existing weixin→wechat jobs migration, **before `cron_manager` loads**. It validates each job in `jobs.json`, keeps the valid ones **verbatim**, drops invalid ones, and **backs up the original** before rewriting.

## Why

A single invalid job (e.g. one missing `dispatch.target.session_id`) makes `JobsFile.model_validate` fail for the whole file, so `cron_manager` can't start and the workspace hangs.

As traced in #5040, such entries don't arise from normal operation — writes always serialize a validated `JobsFile`. They come from a **schema change across upgrades**, or a manual edit / interrupted write, and `migration.py` had no content migration for them. This adds it.

Relative to #5040 (which tolerates invalid jobs at *load* time), this **cleans the file once on upgrade** — the root-cause fix you preferred — backing up the original so nothing is lost. The two are complementary; happy to keep either or both.

## Behaviour

- All jobs valid → no-op (no rewrite, no backup).
- Some invalid → drop them, back up original to `jobs.json.<hex>.invalid-jobs.bak`, atomically rewrite the cleaned file. Idempotent.

prs.title: fix(cron): display schedule time and timezone in user's local timezone
prs.body:
## Description

The Cron Jobs list page displayed schedule times in the task's stored timezone
(defaulting to UTC) rather than the user's configured timezone, which was
confusing. This PR makes the schedule display consistent with the user's timezone.

**Changes:**
- **Execution time column (recurring tasks)**: For daily/weekly tasks, the
  cron hour/minute is converted from the task's stored timezone to the user's
  timezone before display. e.g. a task stored as `0 22 * * *` (UTC) now shows
  as `每天 06:00` for UTC+8 users.
- **Execution time column (once-type tasks)**: `run_at` is converted to the
  user's timezone for display (previously shown in UTC with no conversion).
  When the task timezone differs from the user's, hovering the cell shows the
  original task-timezone time (e.g. `2026-05-29 06:00 (UTC)`) for reference,
  instead of the raw ISO string shown before.
- **Timezone column**: Instead of showing the task's stored timezone string,
  the column now displays the user's timezone as a UTC offset (e.g. `UTC+8`).
- **New task default timezone**: Changed from hardcoded `UTC` to the browser's
  local timezone (`Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`), so new
  tasks default to the user's timezone.
- **i18n** (en/zh): Updated `timezoneTooltip` wording to reflect the new default.

**Related Issue:** N/A

**Security Considerations:** None

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Console (frontend web UI)

- [ ] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [ ] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [ ] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [ ] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [x] Ready for review

## Testing

1. Open the Cron Jobs page
2. Verify recurring tasks show times in your local timezone
   (e.g. `0 22 * * *` UTC → `每天 06:00` for UTC+8 users)
3. Verify the timezone column shows `UTC+8` instead of `UTC`
4. Create a new task — verify the timezone field defaults to your local timezone
5. For once-type tasks: verify the execution time is shown in your local
   timezone, and hovering shows the original UTC time for reference

## Additional Notes

`userTimezone` is sourced from the existing `/config/user-timezone` API.
If the user has not configured a timezone, it falls back to UTC — that is a
separate concern and not addressed here.

prs.title: fix(qwenpaw-data): restore datasource connection feedback on React 19
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Data-source connection tests complete with HTTP 200 but the Context console showed no toast on either success or timeout. The response contract is intentional: HTTP 200 means the test operation completed, while `success: false` and the message carry the connection result. The missing feedback was a frontend rendering bug.

QwenPaw-Data fixed the underlying React 19 / antd v5 static-renderer issue in agentscope-ai/QwenPaw-Data#82 and shipped it in `v0.3.4`. QwenPaw's release workflow still vendored `v0.3.3`, and the Data app version had not changed since the fix, so that flow could not publish a refreshed snapshot.

## Changes

- Bump the QwenPaw-Data app to `1.0.5` and declare runtime minimum `0.3.4`.
- Derive the Context console checkout ref from the manifest runtime version instead of a stale hard-coded `v0.3.3`.
- Configure the 0.3.4 console's `QWENPAW_DATA_CONSOLE.databridge` gateway object before its module bundle loads, while retaining the pre-0.3.4 compatibility variable.
- Align runtime installers, optional dependencies, error guidance, and release docs with 0.3.4.
- Add release-contract tests that reject a return to the pre-fix Context console version and verify gateway wiring.

## Evidence

- `pytest tests/unit/pawapp/test_qwenpaw_data_release.py -q` — 3 passed.
- `npm run typecheck` — passed.
- `npm test` — 3 passed.
- `npm run build` — passed.
- Release workflow YAML parses successfully.
- End-to-end against the live Data service:
  - success toast: `connected to 127.0.0.1:5432/qwenpaw_data_demo（46ms）`
  - failure toast: `connection timeout expired`

The API intentionally continues to return HTTP 200 for a completed test whose result is `success: false`; changing that would be a separate public-contract change.
