prs.title: feat(creator): release 2.0.5-2.0.6 with safe assets, audio, and skill market updates
prs.body:
## Description

Release QwenPaw Creator **2.0.4 → 2.0.6**. The 2.0.5 release PR was never merged upstream, so this single PR now carries **both version increments**: everything completed after the previous upstream release at `d09c34f6c` (merged 2026-11-02 from fork head `df983dd5d`), through the 2.0.6 bump. The 2.0.5 notes below are retained in full because none of that work has reached upstream yet; the 2.0.6 section covers what merged into the release branch afterwards. The previous release's non-DashScope transport, probe-origin hardening, and medium-neutral visual guidance are already upstream and are not repeated here.

**Branch state.** This PR comes directly from **`xuanrui-L:dev/creator`**, now at `e269cdd6cdddebc335e37583dc2692c81638f105`. At opening, the head was `b5b555c272ff1aa14796d521148e06f1d171fab5` (2.0.5), synchronized with upstream `main` at `14b02c597aee1b314f9bd12f8813e01543c3c328` through https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/251 using a merge commit; eight squash-history conflicts were resolved against the exact prior fork release head, and the integrated tree equalled the clean reference merge `012c71c1440c7d660f4c4c2d418343a41d2971c9`. Since opening, six more fork PRs merged into this head (subtitle policy, media-context compression, skill market, list performance, the Windows archive fix, and the 2.0.6 bump), plus https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/262 which commits the pre-commit auto-fixes that had turned the upstream Pre-commit check red. Upstream `main` has meanwhile advanced to `747e91778`, but **no upstream commit since the merge base touches the plugin directory** (verified: zero files), and the PR remains `MERGEABLE`.

**Scope: 146 Creator plugin files, +29,727 / −1,006** relative to merge base `14b02c597`. Every changed file is under `plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/`; the PR contributes no host application, Console, other-plugin, dependency-declaration, or CI/release-workflow changes.

### What's new in 2.0.5 (never published upstream; included here in full)

- **Source asset deletion and content reuse.** The asset library now offers confirmed deletion and removes unreferenced source, thumbnail, native-media, and intelligence files along with their metadata. Shared files remain protected. References from both active timelines and snapshots block ordinary deletion, with structured `ASSET_IN_USE` details. A separately confirmed force-delete can detach references that an element can survive without and mark affected element/final outputs stale; required audio/edit or sole-content references remain blocking. Force deletion also changes affected snapshots, so it does not promise that deleted inputs can later be restored from history. Duplicate local content reuses an existing compatible, healthy source version instead of creating another file/identity, and the UI reports reuse. Post-delete refresh failures no longer masquerade as deletion failures, while late responses cannot rebind a different project or clear a newly selected asset.
- **Cancellation and conversation recovery stay consistent.** Deleting a source cancels its in-process specialist and standalone observation, source-memory, and video-reader workers as well as settling persisted task state. Admission, initialization, repeated cancellation, and shutdown paths share protected terminal cleanup so work is not left falsely running or allowed to publish a result for a deleted source. Agent Dock avoids cascading scroll during event replay while honoring manual scroll-up; project changes replay full event history rather than truncating terminal-state evidence, and manual older-history loading remains usable when SSE is unhealthy.
- **Qwen-Audio 3.1 TTS and voice-correct narration reuse.** Register the 3.1 Flash/Plus models with model-specific voice lists, correct the 3.0 voices and Plus entry, and expose provider availability to the model picker. The unsupported non-realtime instruct model is no longer advertised. Explicit invalid voice requests still fail before synthesis; a stale deployment default resolves to a valid voice for the selected model. Synthesis and narration reuse use the same resolved model/voice identity, avoiding another paid generation when a retry can reuse existing audio. Agent-facing voice lists are bounded rather than dumping the entire table. Connection probes distinguish read-only voice listings from actual audio evidence.
- **Aliyun Token Plan follows its actual media channels.** Image/video reference inputs use shared, bounded inline-image downscaling instead of an unavailable temporary-upload route; image edit/translation remains explicitly unsupported on this path. ASR production and probing share one route selector, including the Qwen-Audio family. Because Creator's normal source transcription consumes local audio and Token Plan requires public audio URLs, Token Plan is removed from the ASR picker and local-audio configurations get actionable refusals. TTS uses the plan's WebSocket synthesis endpoint and its supported model; the endpoint is bound per synthesis instance rather than mutating the SDK's process-global URL. The plan's TTS connection test synthesizes a short sample rather than calling unsupported voice-management routes. Grounding no longer rejects the plan's Responses search channel at save time, and a fallback LLM roster remains available when the host registry has no configured plan models.

### What's new in 2.0.6

- **Caption roles and an opt-in subtitle policy.** `OverlayCreation` gains `caption_role` (dialogue, narration, title, credits, epilogue, location, chapter, interview summary) with schema v10 and a migration that stamps existing dialogue cards; decorative overlays without copy are untouched. Role presets follow film-typography conventions and are edge-anchored so growth stays inside the canvas safe area, enforced as a hard composition gate with per-role × per-aspect guard tests; the model now fills only the role and the system places the box. Project settings gain `subtitle_policy` (auto/on/off, **default off** — subtitles become an explicit user choice at creation), and `toggle_subtitles` batch-switches caption overlays through the frontend-edit impact pipeline so the final cut is marked stale and must be recomposed. The workbench shows role labels on timeline tracks, a one-click subtitles toggle with a count badge, per-card switches, and a plain-caption live preview that mirrors backend placement; both toggle paths send direct single-field patches instead of reusing element drafts.
- **Media joins context compression, with overflow recovery and recall.** Inline media is now priced by the host vision token estimate instead of a private byte heuristic; the token window resolves from the host model catalog (operator override `CREATOR_MODEL_CONTEXT_TOKENS`), with the platform scroll's reply reserve, and the 384 KB byte gate remains a transport floor. Overflow runs a measured demotion ladder: derived observation media first, human uploads only when the refusal's own accounting shows media can bridge the gap, each step all-or-nothing into the project's content-addressed vault with a recall pointer left in place; `recall_media` (main agent and specialists) brings originals back as native user-role media. Model calls wrap the platform `call_with_overflow_recovery`; a request proven unable to shrink terminates as non-retryable `MODEL_CONTEXT_UNFIT` with dedicated zh/en UI copy instead of promising a retry that can never succeed. Text history compaction archives elided turns into a recallable seq/headline map (reusing the platform `EvictionIndex`, with a standalone flat-map fallback), adds a bounded `recall_history` tool (expand/search), and an optional fail-closed LLM continuation summary (`CREATOR_CONTINUATION_SUMMARY_ENABLED`). A resuming run carries exactly one, newest project view. The overflow classifier lives entirely in the plugin — no host file is modified. Both READMEs document the budget knobs and the known boundary that URL-carried media is neither charged nor demotable.
- **Skill Market browser and stronger URL import.** New `market/search` and `market/providers` endpoints reuse the host QwenPaw market service (provider discovery off the event loop, no hard registry dependency, graceful degradation when the runtime has no market service). The browser paginates the committed search term (not the input draft), retries the failed page without skipping it, and drops stale pages on a new search. One-click install reports the name the backend actually installed (slug folding included), keeps that row→name identity across pane remounts in origin-scoped browser storage with defensive reads, and frees the row automatically once the skill leaves the library. Unavailable markets are listed with the host's own reason, and backend search guidance/failure detail passes through instead of a generic string. The URL import modal gains real-time source detection and clickable market examples (QwenPaw, Skills.sh, GitHub, ClawHub, LobeHub, ModelScope, SkillsMP), with zh/en strings.
- **Project-list and polling load reduction.** The project list reads one summary record per project, invalidated by `project.json` `(mtime_ns, size)`; the stamp is captured before the read and re-verified before publish, so a concurrent commit can never pin a stale card as latest. Corrupt, wrong-project, wrong-typed, or timezone-naive summaries degrade to a cache miss (full read), never a 500. A live 34 MB deployment measured 0.87 s → 0.001 s on a warm hit; `CREATOR_LIST_SUMMARY_CACHE=0` disables it. Identical overlapping read-only GETs coalesce into one shared request (requests carrying an abort signal opt out), and polling intervals back off with page activity (250 ms floor, instant recovery on activity). The entrypoint caps glibc malloc arenas (`MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=4`) to stop per-thread 64 MB arenas from pinning gigabytes of freed-but-unreturned memory.
- **Windows archive imports sanitize instead of aborting** (fixes https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8547). Archives produced on Linux/macOS embed `source:<uuid>` sidecar paths that are illegal on Windows; the shared extractor previously rejected the whole bundle over one 32 KB sidecar, which is why the bundled cat-perspective example failed with 503 on Windows in 2.0.4. Illegal path components are now mapped deterministically and idempotently (`:` etc. → `_`, reserved device names prefixed, trailing dots/spaces stripped); only `IndexedFile.relative_uri` is rewritten while logical identifiers (`source_id`, dict keys, order arrays) stay as authored. Post-sanitization collisions are still refused as real corruption. The `project.json` registry rewrite is published atomically in canonical form, unreadable registries warn instead of silently skipping reconciliation, archive-provided names are CR/LF-neutralized before logging, and the 503 message chains the underlying extraction reason. SKILL.md bundles get the same rename without a registry pass.

**Version and dependencies.** `plugin.json`, `ui/package.json`, and both package-lock root-version fields all read **2.0.6** (the intermediate 2.0.5 bump is included in history but was never published). The host minimum remains **2.1.0**. No Python or npm dependency changes are introduced relative to current upstream. Publication remains governed by the unchanged version-driven main-branch workflow; no immutable artifact is being overwritten.

**Related Issue:** Release follow-up to https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8529. Included 2.0.5 source changes: https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/240, https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/242, https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/249, and the 2.0.5 bump https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/246. Included 2.0.6 source changes: https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/253 (caption roles/subtitle policy), https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/245 (media context compression/overflow recovery), https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/257 (skill market/URL import), https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/255 (list performance), https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/254 (Windows archive sanitize), and the 2.0.6 bump https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/258. Pre-commit auto-fixes: https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/262.

**Security Considerations:** No credentials, user projects, generated media, or runtime directories are committed. Deletion checks actual references, protects shared files, and uses existing project/path validation; force-delete is explicit and does not bypass indispensable references. Provider endpoint changes remain local to the configured request rather than leaking across later synthesis calls. Archive sanitization rewrites only on-disk relative URIs, keeps logical identifiers intact, refuses collisions, publishes the registry atomically, and neutralizes CR/LF in archive-provided names before they reach logs. Demoted media is archived inside the project's own content-addressed store; human uploads move only under measured pressure and only when the durable write succeeds. Skill-market installs go through the host market service with the host's own provider availability and failure reasons surfaced; no new credential surface is added. Real provider connection tests, including Token Plan TTS, may consume provider quota; this release validation made **no paid-provider calls**. Browser testing used only a synthetic project in a temporary data root. Existing host authentication and secure download boundaries are unchanged.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [x] Scripts / Deploy — plugin version metadata and entrypoint arena cap only
- [x] Creator app plugin (`plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/`)

## Checklist

- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes — ran over the **complete 146-file release delta** (not the whole repository) at a verified fixed point: a repeat pass modifies nothing. The prettier hook environment cannot be installed on this machine (npm `EALLOWGIT`), so prettier ran as the pinned `npx prettier@3.0.0 --check` over all 56 changed ts/tsx files — all pass. CI's `--all-files` run remains authoritative.
- [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks — the four failing auto-fix hooks (fix-encoding-pragma, add-trailing-comma, black, prettier) were committed via https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/262 and every hook reruns clean.
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass — 2,648 backend tests and 542 UI tests on the current head's tree.
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed) — both plugin READMEs document the context-budget knobs and boundaries; model/prompt guidance and bilingual UI descriptions are updated; no website documentation change is required.
- [x] Ready for review

Channel-specific checklist: not applicable; this upstream diff contains no host channel changes.

## Testing

Tested the current head's tree in a **Python 3.11.12** environment with upstream host test extras (`agentscope==2.0.10`, matching the branch lock) and Creator requirements. UI used the committed lockfile (`npm ci`). UI tests ran under **Node 22.23.4** (upstream `.nvmrc`, via `npx node@22.23.4`) for CI parity; this machine's default Node 25.9.0 produces 17 environment-only failures in the SkillMarketBrowser/SkillsConfigPane suites because Node 25's native webstorage shadows jsdom's `localStorage` — the identical tree is fully green under Node 22, matching upstream CI. No source change was made to suppress those failures.

```bash
# From Creator backend on this macOS machine:
NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1,::1 no_proxy=localhost,127.0.0.1,::1 \
QWENPAW_CREATOR_MOTION_BROWSER="/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" \
  PYTHONPATH=. <repo>/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests -q --timeout=120

# From Creator UI:
npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
npm run typecheck
npx --yes node@22.23.4 node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run
npm run build

# From repository root (release delta = merge-base 14b02c597 .. HEAD):
git diff --name-only -z 14b02c597 HEAD | SKIP=prettier xargs -0 uvx --python 3.11 pre-commit run --files
# prettier separately, pinned to the hook's version:
npx --yes prettier@3.0.0 --check <all 56 changed ui ts/tsx files>
python scripts/pack/generate_plugin_metadata.py \
  --plugins-root plugins --dist dist/plugins \
  --metadata-out dist/plugins/index.json \
  --cdn-prefix /files/plugins --only qwenpaw-creator
```

The `NO_PROXY` normalization is test-process-only: this machine's inherited `NO_PROXY` includes the bracketed IPv6 entry `[::1]`, which HTTPX parses as an invalid port. No source, assertion, system proxy setting, or provider security check was changed. The supported system-Chrome override covered caption rendering; the bundled-Chromium motion-clip test also ran and passed in this round.

**Browser behavior proof (recorded at the 2.0.5-era head `b5b555c27`, retained as evidence for the 2.0.5 features):** a live Vite UI used real asset API routes against an isolated temporary project. Uploading identical synthetic text under two request IDs returned `reused=false` then `reused=true` with the same asset version and one source. Cancelling deletion kept the card; confirming deletion removed the card/selection, source/file index entries, and the actual file on disk. The TTS model dropdown rendered Qwen-Audio 3.1 Flash and Plus from the backend capability API without uncaught JavaScript errors. The harness bypassed model-config binding and disabled Agent upload notifications, so no model was invoked. This focused asset/settings smoke is **not** a claim of full production-runtime or paid-provider E2E coverage. The 2.0.6 increment is verified in this update by the full backend/UI suites, typecheck, build, and packaging checks below; no new browser or paid-provider E2E was performed for it, and none is claimed. Temporary servers and the browser were stopped afterwards.

prs.title: feat(chat): add append-only session storage, paginated history and native Turn forks
prs.body:
## Description

Long conversations previously depended on mutable session snapshots and loading large history windows. That made historical Turn forks, runtime recovery, and reconnect behavior difficult to keep consistent. This branch introduces durable per-session SQLite history with append-only facts and rebuildable projections, and bounds the Console's history and replay work.

This draft covers the complete branch, including:

- Store message/content facts and immutable context revisions separately from current message/runtime projections. Rebuild projections without rewriting historical facts; reuse state component references for usage-only revisions and avoid redundant block events.
- Migrate legacy JSON sessions and history databases, preserve available historical messages, reconstruct legacy runtime where possible, and retain provider session/Turn mappings.
- Fork completed Turns with their historical runtime boundary. Codex/Qoder branches use native provider interfaces and stored Turn mappings rather than rebuilding third-party context. Failed native restoration/reset must not silently create a fresh context.
- Add stable history pagination, bounded rendering, message-directory navigation, streaming/reconnect replay, and safe session switching/deletion.
- Integrate storage with clear/new, compact, dump/load, Scroll/Recall, cloning, backup, checkpoints, statistics, and PawApp/SDK session access. Preserve reset and checkpoint restoration semantics; roll back failed/cancelled compaction.

## Issues addressed

- Fixes https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/3915 — measured virtual rendering, incremental history loading, scroll anchoring, and bottom-follow behavior.
- Fixes https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/3923 — bounded Console history reads and windowed rendering address the full-history/full-DOM paths. This does not claim a measured memory result for the reporter's exact dataset or include all optional bundle-size suggestions.
- Fixes https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8134 — durable display history is independent of the model's compacted context.
- Fixes https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/6542 — completed turns persist their final messages and session state. This covers the real-time archival proposal, not zero loss of uncommitted output after a forced process termination or external notebook synchronization.
- Fixes https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8744 — durable display history is independent of the model's compacted context.


## PRs superseded after merge

The following PRs can be closed manually as superseded after this PR merges. This is a functional replacement assessment, not a claim that every change from those PRs was incorporated:

- https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7361 — history pagination and virtual rendering.
- https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7542 — access to pre-compaction history through paginated durable transcripts. Retention changes are outside this PR's scope and are not a prerequisite for replacing the pagination implementation.
- https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/6704 — use the completed-Turn Fork implementation, including the latest completed turn, rather than adding a second whole-session fork path.
- https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8091 — route-driven active-chat tracking also covers sidebar navigation and cached sessions.
- https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/1481 — metadata updates exclude messages without mutating the caller's session.
- https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/803 — per-agent last-chat persistence and route restoration replace the older global storage-key approach.
- https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/1489 — backend cancellation, cancellation-state persistence, and history/reconnect handling replace the older cancel-endpoint approach.

Some of these behaviors are inherited from main and retained by this branch; they are not all new contributions of this PR. PR #7413 / issue #7410 are already addressed by main's #8212, and the workspace-owned HistoryStore work in #8471 is superseded by #8482 and subsequent maintenance. Those are independent cleanup items, not closure claims of #8532.

**Security Considerations:** Session ownership and active-session deletion checks remain part of history access. This PR does not include local databases, conversation exports, screenshots, profiling dumps, or environment credentials. Provider contexts remain provider-owned.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Refactoring
- [x] Breaking change (session storage representation changes; legacy data is imported)
- [ ] Documentation

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend
- [x] Console
- [x] Channels (Console streaming/reconnect)
- [x] Tests
- [x] Scripts / Deploy (replay verification tooling)

## Checklist

- [ ] `pre-commit run --all-files` passes (changed-file checks passed; no all-files claim)
- [ ] Full default test configuration is green (see known failures below)
- [ ] Documentation published in this repository
- [ ] Ready for review / merge

## Testing

Focused implementation-audit validation on **2026-11-06**, against HEAD **95bc9c73e8108a7645332087149c209d56a2a14c**:

- Frontend: **111 passed** across 10 files covering measured/history windows, route gates, bottom follow, large-session handling, ownership, transitions, initialization, and replay parsing.
- Backend: **207 passed** across the selected persistence, migration, projection-rebuild, Fork/catalog, replay, task, and lifecycle tests. This includes the regression test from #7413 run from a temporary file, without adding it to this PR.
- These are focused regressions, not a new full-suite run or browser E2E run. No fresh Edge performance measurement, OS-level SIGTERM test, Windows extended-path test, or browser network-disconnect injection is claimed.

Earlier branch validation retained for context (not rerun as a full suite at the HEAD above; groups overlap and should not be summed as unique coverage):

- Chat storage suite: **478 passed** after each of the three storage optimizations.
- Backend combined regression: **2337 passed, 1 platform skip**.
- HTTP integration retry (backup, checkpoints, conversation commands, PawApp context): **54 passed**, using the existing `QWENPAW_INTEGRATION_HTTP_TIMEOUT=180` setting after initial fixture startup timeouts.
- SDK lifecycle: **2 passed** with a 180-second test timeout after a 45-second dependency metadata scan timeout. Other plugin/SDK contracts: **147 passed**.
- TypeScript noEmit, changed-file pre-commit checks, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Frontend full single-worker run: **657 files passed / 2 failed**; **8475 tests passed / 1 failed / 2 expected failures / 9 skipped**. This was not a green default full run.
  - JobDrawer JSON validation did not display its error within `waitFor`; the unchanged complete file passed on isolated retry (**29 passed**).
  - PawApp SDK session routing exceeded the default 10-second initialization hook timeout, also on isolated retry (**45 passed / 9 skipped**). With command-line `--hookTimeout=30000`, all **54 passed**. No source or test configuration was changed to hide this limitation.

## Evidence

Historical terminal results retained from the earlier branch validation:

```text
pytest tests/unit/app/chats/ -q
478 passed

Backend combined regression
2337 passed, 1 skipped

HTTP integration retry
54 passed

SDK lifecycle / other contracts
2 passed / 147 passed

vitest run --maxWorkers=1
Test Files  2 failed | 657 passed (659)
Tests       1 failed | 8475 passed | 2 expected fail | 9 skipped (8487)

Isolated JobDrawer retry: 29 passed
Isolated sessionRouting --hookTimeout=30000: 54 passed
```

Earlier behavior checks (not repeated in the 2026-11-06 focused audit):

- A database generated by the previous implementation containing four `block.committed` events was rebuilt twice: messages, runtime, and original events remained unchanged.
- Eight database command scenarios and sixteen Fork boundaries verified state preservation, with Codex/Qoder native reset failure protection probes.
- Console browser flow: create two Turns, fork the first, continue with the remembered first-Turn marker, fork again, and reload. Both forks closed the dialog, navigated automatically, and incremented the name. Long-history scrolling and the message directory also loaded.
- Synthetic SQLite usage-write benchmark (1000 context entries, about 1 KiB each): median **34.174 ms → 4.975 ms**, SQL statements **2013 → 10**. JSON state reading/parsing remains; this is not a production latency guarantee.

## Additional Notes

This is a large draft covering the whole storage/pagination branch, not just its final optimization commit. Historical legacy runtime reconstruction can be approximate where exact snapshots were never stored. The previously recorded browser smoke used the built-in agent; native-provider behavior was covered by automated adapters/probes, not a fresh five-Turn provider UI run in this validation. Reconnect checks do not claim a new browser network-disconnect injection run.

Local verification artifacts are retained outside the Git diff. The known default frontend timing failures and upstream CI results need review before promoting this PR out of draft.

prs.title: chore(deps): bump reme-ai to 0.4.2.3
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QwenPaw pins `reme-ai==0.4.2.0`. On Windows the memory tag index never rebuilds, so `/memory/tags` and `/memory/tag-files` answer 503 (#8580). The root cause was fixed in ReMe by canonicalizing legacy Windows paths instead of failing the rebuild — ReMe #717.

**That fix first ships in 0.4.2.3, not in 0.4.2.2.**

```
v0.4.2.1  has #717 = False
v0.4.2.2  has #717 = False
v0.4.2.3  has #717 = True
          "* fix(tag-index): canonicalize legacy Windows paths instead of failing rebuild
             by @BeiMu-new in https://github.com/agentscope-ai/ReMe/pull/717"
```

So bumping to 0.4.2.2 would install cleanly and still leave #8580 broken. This PR goes to 0.4.2.3, the first release that actually carries the fix.

0.4.2.3 requires `mcp<3,>=1.28.1`. QwenPaw pins `mcp 1.28.1`, which sits inside that range, so the new build resolves without touching any other constraint.

## Scope

Type: A (single-point fix)

Four places spell the version out and they move together:

- `pyproject.toml` — `reme-ai==0.4.2.0` → `reme-ai==0.4.2.3`
- `src/qwenpaw/agents/memory/reme_light_memory_manager.py` — `_REQUIRED_REME_VERSION = "0.4.2.3"`
- `tests/unit/agents/memory/test_reme_start.py` — the monkeypatched `reme.__version__` must equal the constant, otherwise the version check fires before the assertion under test
- `tests/integration/test_reme_watch_contract.py` — the install line in the module docstring

## Self-review

1. **Only the target semantics move** — `git diff --stat` is 4 files, `+4 −4`. Every changed line is a version literal.
2. **Callers of `_REQUIRED_REME_VERSION`** — three uses, all inside `reme_light_memory_manager.py`: the startup comparison, the mismatch message and the reinstall hint. None of them branch on a specific version, so the value change is safe.
3. **`0.4.2.0` left in place where it is a historical statement** — the comment in `reme_tags.py:59` describes what 0.4.2.0 did (why the long-tag fallback exists) and `website/public/release-notes/v2.3.0.*` records what that release shipped. Rewriting either would make the record wrong; neither is the current pin.
4. **Local environment untouched** — the regression run below used a separate venv with 0.4.2.3 installed, so the running instance keeps 0.4.2.0 until this lands.

## Test scope

Run with `PYTHONPATH=src` against a venv where `reme-ai==0.4.2.3` is installed:

- `tests/integration/test_reme_consistency_contract.py` + `test_reme_embedding_contract.py` + `test_reme_tags_contract.py` — **6 passed**
- `tests/integration/test_reme_watch_contract.py` — **1 passed**
- `tests/unit/agents/memory` — **303 passed** (1 pre-existing asyncio warning)
- `pre-commit run --files <the four files>` — all hooks passed

The tag-index contract above is the one that exercises the #717 path on a real ReMe application; it passes on 0.4.2.3.

## Evidence

```
$ python -c "import reme; print(reme.__version__)"
0.4.2.3                      # venv used for the regression run

$ PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/integration/test_reme_*_contract.py -q
6 passed                     # consistency + embedding + tags
1 passed                     # watch

$ PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/unit/agents/memory -q
303 passed
```

Refs #8580, ReMe #717

prs.title: fix(media): enforce the inline byte budget and gate media by capability
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The downscale pass added in #8632 judged an image by its longest side alone. Three gaps followed from that, and they are fixed together because they meet on the same path.

**1. The byte budget and the side limit are two independent limits.**
A 2000x2000 PNG is well inside the 8192 px side limit and can still weigh 11.46 MiB, so the pass returned it untouched and the formatter rejected the request on bytes right afterwards. Both limits are now checked, and a formatter that provisions its own limits passes them down, so this pass and the cap cannot disagree about what fits.

**2. PNG has no quality knob.**
Every quality step emitted the same bytes and paid for another full deflate. The quality loop is skipped for PNG; only reducing the side makes it smaller.

**3. A rejection could not name the image it rejected.**
The retry log said "some media" while every image in the request was dropped, which left no way to tell which one the provider objected to. Each wire media block now gets a label (position, media type, decoded size) across the Anthropic `source`, OpenAI `image_url` and Gemini `inline_data`/`file_data` spellings, and the log names them.

## Scope

Type: D (cross-layer)

- `src/qwenpaw/providers/capping_formatter.py` — `MAX_IMAGE_SIDE` moves here, beside the byte cap, so both media limits have one home; new `max_image_side` field (`ge=0`, default 8192).
- `src/qwenpaw/agents/utils/image_resize.py` — two limits decided independently, `max_side` threaded through, quality loop skipped for PNG.
- `src/qwenpaw/agents/model_factory.py` — reads the formatter's limits and passes them down; new `_describe_wire_media_blocks` / `_wire_media_label`.
- `src/qwenpaw/agents/utils/message_request_normalizer.py` — threads `max_bytes` / `max_side` to the resize pass.
- `src/qwenpaw/agents/react_agent.py` — the retry log names the labelled blocks.

## Self-review

1. **Callers of `downscale_image_bytes`** — `_rescale_source` is the only intermediate, `normalize_messages_for_model_request_async` the only entry point; both are updated, and both keep the old behaviour when the new keyword arguments are omitted (`max_side=MAX_IMAGE_SIDE`, `max_bytes=MAX_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES`).
2. **`MAX_IMAGE_SIDE` relocation** — `grep -rn MAX_IMAGE_SIDE src/` returns only `capping_formatter.py` (definition) and `image_resize.py` (import + defaults); no stale constant remains in `image_resize`.
3. **`max_image_side` as a new field** — declared with `ge=0` and the same default as before (8192), so every existing formatter subclass inherits it; `_normalize_messages_for_formatter` reads it with `getattr(..., MAX_IMAGE_SIDE)` so a custom formatter without the field still works.
4. **`_describe_wire_media_blocks`** — used only by `QwenPawAgent._last_wire_media_summary`, which returns `[]` when no formatter is active.
5. **Reversal** — `max_bytes <= 0` keeps its old meaning of "no byte limit" rather than shrinking forever; verified with the probe below (`unchanged=True`).
6. **Both limits agree** — the resize pass receives `formatter.max_bytes` / `formatter.max_image_side` instead of the module constants, so a provider override cannot make the pass shrink to a different budget than the one enforced a moment later.

## Test scope

- Targeted: `test_wire_media_labels.py` + `test_image_resize.py` + `test_cross_provider_normalization.py` + `test_model_factory_message_normalization.py` — **101 passed**
- Adjacent: `tests/unit/agents/utils` + `tests/unit/providers` — **1448 passed, 1 skipped**
- `pre-commit run --files <the eight files>` — all hooks passed

## Evidence

A 2000x2000 high-entropy PNG, well inside the side limit and far over the byte cap:

```
INPUT   side=2000x2000  bytes=12,015,257  (11.46 MiB)
        longest side 2000 <= 8192 -> the old side-only check returned this unchanged
OUTPUT  bytes=596,065  (0.57 MiB)  media_type=image/png  changed=True
        under 2 MiB cap: True

max_bytes=0 -> unchanged=True  (11.46 MiB)
```

The media labels, one per wire spelling:

```
#1 image/png 1.0 MiB      (Anthropic source)
#1 image/jpeg 1.0 MiB     (OpenAI image_url data URL)
#1 image/webp 1.0 MiB     (Gemini inline_data)
```

Refs #8632

prs.title: fix(skills): keep rollback backups until every workspace is restored
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Rolling back a multi-workspace skill install had five separate weak points. Each one can lose a skill or keep a user waiting, and they sit on the same code path, so they are fixed together.

**1. A restore failure abandons the remaining workspaces.**
`_restore_workspace_skills` used to run every target inside one `try`, so the first failure skipped the targets that had not been undone yet, and the `finally` cleanup then removed their backups as well. A target whose restore failed now keeps its backup, and every target is attempted before the first error is re-raised.

**2. The restore marker is written after the backup has been consumed.**
`_restore_workspace_skill` renames the backup back into place and only then sets `files_restored`. A process killed inside that window leaves a target that looks un-restored while its files are already back, and the next pass would delete the skill as "nothing to put back". A target with no backup but a present skill directory is now counted as restored.

**3. Overwriting an installed skill waits for the old tree.**
`install_staged_skill_dir` deleted the previous tree inline before installing. `rmtree` cannot be interrupted, so cancelling an overwrite had to wait for every file of the old tree. The old tree is now renamed aside first and reclaimed on a daemon thread; cancellation is honoured before anything is replaced.

**4. Pre-existing defect, not introduced by #8477: deleting a skill can lose all three copies.**
`garbage_collection` of the rollback `finally` removed every backup root unconditionally, including the root of a target whose restore had just failed. After a failed restore that backup is the only copy of the previous version on disk, so the cleanup turned a recoverable failure into permanent loss. It is now kept and marked, so a later sweep does not reclaim it either.

**5. New cleanup logic (not a defect fix): reclaim stale rollback roots.**
Backups now live under `skills/` instead of the workspace root, so a restore is a sibling rename rather than a second copy. That move leaves a root in place when a process is killed mid-install, so the next install sweeps the roots that are neither in use nor marked as retained.

## Scope

Type: B (state machine / cancellation / rollback)

Touches `src/qwenpaw/agents/skill_system/store.py`, `src/qwenpaw/app/routers/skills.py` and three test files.

## Self-review

1. **Failure** — `test_restore_continues_after_one_target_raises` (a restore that raises no longer strands the later targets) and `test_failed_restore_keeps_its_backup` (the kept root survives the cleanup and carries the marker).
2. **Cancellation** — `test_cancelled_overwrite_does_not_wait_for_the_old_tree` (measured 6.4s → 0.013s over 12k files) and `test_install_failure_moves_the_old_tree_back`.
3. **Skip / no-op paths** — `test_missing_backup_with_present_skill_counts_as_restored` (the killed-between-rename-and-marker case) and `test_restore_without_a_backup_removes_the_new_copy`.
4. **Concurrency** — the reclaim runs on a named daemon thread and `test_stale_rollback_roots_are_reclaimed_once` covers two installs in one skills directory; the retained marker is what keeps a failed restore's root out of a later sweep.

## Test scope

- Targeted: `test_staged_install.py` + `test_skills_router_pool_ops.py` + `test_skills_router_helpers.py` — **191 passed**
- Adjacent: `tests/unit/agents/skill_system` — **811 passed**; `tests/unit/app/routers -k skill` — **270 passed**
- `pre-commit run --files <the five files>` — all hooks passed

## Evidence

Before this change, injecting one restore failure across three targets left the later targets on the new content with their backups already deleted. After it, the failing target keeps its backup (marked) and the remaining targets are restored.

Overwriting a 12k-file skill took **6.4s** to cancel (the inline `rmtree`) and **0.013s** after the tree is renamed aside.

```
# cancellation timing, 12k files
before: 6.4s   (rmtree of the old tree inside the request)
after : 0.013s (rename aside + daemon reclaim)
```

Refs #8013

prs.body:
## Description

WeChat could return `ACCOUNT_IN_USE` during startup or Console QR login because the host treated saved credentials and shared file paths as evidence of a running Bot. This could happen with a disabled channel or with a single agent whose workspace ID differed in case from its profile key.

- Check for duplicate Bot credentials against active runtime leases. Disabled channels and shared token file paths no longer trigger a conflict on their own.
- Check the new credential when Console QR authorization is confirmed. If it is in use, stop polling and show the conflict. On successful save, release the QR session lease before scheduling the agent reload.
- Default the Bot Token file and reply context cache to `<workspace>/wechat/`. Explicit `bot_token_file` paths remain supported. Users who relied on the old root-level token file can point `bot_token_file` to it or scan again. Incoming messages rebuild the reply context cache.

Fixes #8693. Addresses the WeChat startup failure reported as Bug 1 in #8709.

## Testing

- Python regression suite covering WeChat, the channel host, configuration, and CLI.
- Console tests covering the channel drawer and QR authorization.
- Isolated QwenPaw instance with a simulated iLink service.

## Evidence

```text
./scripts/check-channels.sh wechat
14 passed
All channel checks passed.

Python regression suite
282 passed, 17 skipped

Console tests
3 test files passed, 93 tests passed
```

With a duplicate token in a disabled agent's config, the Console QR endpoint returned HTTP 200. Confirming and saving the QR authorization wrote the new token to `agent.json`, and the reloaded worker used it to poll iLink. A separate worker-initiated login wrote its token to the workspace's `wechat/` directory.

prs.title: fix(media): downscale oversized images and mark stripped media as omitted
prs.body:
## Scope

Type: A (single-point fix) — media handling on the freezing, request-normalization
and agent-recovery paths. No public API or configuration changes.

## What Problem This Solves

An oversized image is sent verbatim and rejected by the provider; the recovery
then strips every image from the request while the tool text still says
`Image loaded: x.png`, so the model answers as if it had seen an image it
never received.

## Description

Two defects on the media path share one real-world trigger: an agent loaded a
9000px-wide PNG through `view_image`, the provider rejected the payload
("You have uploaded an unsupported image"), and QwenPaw's recovery stripped
**every** image from the request. The model then answered from a tool result
that still read `Image loaded: timeline_states_48h.png` — it was told it had
seen an image it never received.

**1. Oversized images are downscaled on the request copy only**

`freeze_image_bytes` enforced the byte cap but never checked dimensions, so a
wide-but-lightweight PNG (line art, timeline charts) passed straight through
and was rejected downstream. Freezing now keeps the original bytes, and
`downscale_oversized_images` (`agents/utils/image_resize.py`) shrinks the
cloned request inside `normalize_messages_for_model_request`. History, memory
and any later explicit request for the same media keep full resolution.

The helper:

- keeps the source format when it can carry alpha, so a transparent WebP no
  longer becomes a multi-megabyte PNG;
- if the re-encoded payload still exceeds the byte limit, steps quality down
  and then halves the dimensions; if every attempt fails it returns the
  original bytes, never a larger payload;
- detects animation with `n_frames > 1` **before** resampling and passes it
  through untouched (GIF, animated WebP, APNG) instead of keeping only the
  first frame;
- applies `ImageOps.exif_transpose()` before `thumbnail()`, so a rotated JPEG
  is scaled along its displayed axes.

**2. Stripping media now leaves an explicit marker**

When only some blocks of a `tool_result` were stripped, the surviving text was
kept as-is — that is how the model ended up holding an "Image loaded" claim
with no image behind it. The blanket "this model supports no media" strip now
appends `MEDIA_UNSUPPORTED_PLACEHOLDER` to the surviving output, in the same
shape as its siblings (dict for 1.x blocks, block object for 2.0).

Targeted strips (audio / video / document / empty) are deliberate per-modality
decisions, so they keep their current output shape. This is a deliberate
behaviour change and is covered by an updated assertion in
`test_react_agent_media_strip.py::test_nested_media_in_tool_result_stripped`.

## Evidence

Before / after, same input (9000x60 PNG):

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| stored message | 9000x60 | 9000x60 (unchanged) |
| request copy | 9000x60, sent verbatim | 8192x55 |
| provider payload | rejected as unsupported | accepted |
| tool result text after strip | `Image loaded: x.png` | `Image loaded: x.png` + `[Media content removed - model does not support this media type]` |

Regression tests, grouped by the module they cover:

- `tests/unit/agents/utils/test_image_freezing.py` — an oversized image stays
  byte-identical after freezing; an in-limit image is not re-encoded.
- `tests/unit/agents/utils/test_image_resize.py` — oversized side is
  downscaled with the aspect ratio preserved; transparent WebP stays WebP with
  alpha; animated WebP and APNG keep every frame; EXIF orientation is applied
  before resizing; the normalizer shrinks the request copy while the stored
  message keeps its bytes.
- `tests/unit/agents/test_message_request_normalizer.py` — a partial strip
  yields the full output list `["Image loaded: a.png", placeholder]`; an
  all-media strip collapses to the placeholder string.

Checked the tests are not vacuous: with the `src/` changes stashed the same
files report 2 failed (freezing still downscales, normalizer does not
rescale), and pass again once restored.

## Follow-up direction

The other two halves of the same bug. They are deliberately left out because
both need an interface decision first, and neither is required for this fix:

- **Per-provider media capability table** (max side / max bytes / accepted
  formats). Today the limit is inferred from a 400 response; with a declared
  table the request could be shaped correctly instead of being repaired after
  a rejection. It touches provider registration and the formatters.
- **Rejection-site attribution.** If each image carried an id, a rejection
  could name the offending one, and the recovery could transcode and retry
  *that* image instead of stripping every image in the request.

Happy to open an issue with the exact failure shapes and take either item once
the owning layer is agreed.

## Test scope

- Target: `test_image_freezing.py`, `test_image_resize.py`,
  `test_message_request_normalizer.py` — 81 passed.
- Adjacent: `tests/unit/agents -k "image or media or normalizer"` — 488
  passed, 3 skipped.
- Lint: `pre-commit run --files <changed>` — all hooks passed (black 23.3.0,
  mypy, pylint, flake8, add-trailing-comma, docstring-first, AST,
  private-key, encoding-pragma, trailing-whitespace).

prs.title: perf(skills): install a staged pool skill by renaming it in place (#8013)
prs.body:
## Description

Item 4 of #8013: a pool download copies a skill twice — pool → staging directory, then staging → workspace. The second hop should be a rename, not another full tree copy.

### Where the two copies come from

```text
pool/<skill>                 one shared tree, read by every workspace
   ↓ copy #1                 cancellable, into a private stage
<system temp>/qwenpaw_skill_stage_<name>_xxxx
   ↓ copy #2                 ← this PR replaces this hop with a rename
<workspace>/skills/<skill>
```

Copy #1 has to stay. The pool tree is shared, so a skill must not be visible
there half-written or half-scanned; `staged_skill_dir()` gives the scan a private
tree, and gives the request something it can throw away when cancelled.

Copy #2 has no such job. It exists only because a workspace needs a real
directory, and it walks and rewrites every file the skill ships a second time.
That is the cost this change removes: on one volume the second hop becomes a
directory rename, and on two volumes nothing changes.

The stage lands wherever `tempfile.mkdtemp()` puts it, which is usually the
workspace's own volume (both under the user's home on Windows and on most Linux
installs) but not always: a tmpfs `/tmp`, or a workspace on another mount, makes
`os.rename` raise `EXDEV` and the copy fallback runs exactly as before. That is
also why nothing inspects the volumes first — equal `st_dev` does not guarantee
that the rename is accepted.


- `rename_or_copy_directory(source, target, *, copy_directory)` lives in `utils/io_utils.py`. It tries `os.rename` and hands a refusal to the copy function the caller passes in. The attempt itself is the probe: equal `st_dev` does not guarantee that a rename succeeds, so nothing inspects the volume beforehand.
- `install_staged_skill_dir(staged_dir, target_dir)` keeps the install policy in `store.py`: cancellation is checked before anything is replaced, the previous target is cleared, and `copy_skill_dir` is the fallback so cancellation is still honoured per file during the copy.
- The rollback snapshot keeps its policy in the router and calls the same helper. The backup is created **inside the workspace** when that directory accepts a temporary directory, so restoring it renames it back instead of copying every file again. When it does not, the backup goes to system temp and the restore copies. The rollback passes `shutil.copytree`, because it has to finish even after the request was cancelled.

Removing the previous target and renaming the stage are two separate steps, so this is **not** an atomic replacement: an interrupted install can leave the target absent, the surrounding context manager discards the stage, and the caller's rollback restores the previous contents.

Staging itself is untouched: it still carries scan isolation and cancellation, and cross-volume installs still go through both copies.

Two things worth calling out for review:

1. `install_staged_skill_dir` installs the staged tree **as it stands**, so it is only equivalent to `copy_skill_dir` when the stage was produced by it — that copy filters OS artifacts and dereferences symlinks, which a rename cannot do. The pool download builds its stage that way, and the docstring states the prerequisite.
2. The backup lives inside the workspace directory while a download runs, so it is visible to anything that lists the workspace root. It is removed by `_restore_workspace_skill` and by the download route's `finally` in both the success and the failure path.

### Updates since first review

- Dropped `same_volume()`: a device-id match does not guarantee that `rename` succeeds, so the rename attempt is the probe and the copy is the fallback. The volume-probe tests went with it.
- Installation and rollback share the helper while keeping their own copy function — cancellable copy for the install, plain `copytree` for the rollback.
- Backups still live inside the workspace, falling back to system temp only when the workspace refuses the temporary directory. `_rollback_backup_parent()` and `_install_rollback_copy()` are gone.
- The claim of atomic replacement is removed from the code, the commit and this description.

### Updates since second review

- **Fallback bug fixed.** `mkdtemp()` is now inside the `try`, so a workspace that exists but refuses new entries falls back to system temp instead of raising. The fallback test now fails the workspace-local `mkdtemp()` call rather than `Path.mkdir()`.
- `rename_or_copy_directory()` moved to `utils/io_utils.py` (exported in `__all__`); install policy stays in `store.py`, recovery policy stays in the router.
- Contracts and comments corrected: the stage is not retained for a retry; backups are inside the workspace; the helper states it requires an absent target and an existing parent; `copy_directory` is typed `Callable[[Path, Path], object]`; the cancellation test uses the real `SkillImportCancelled`.

### Updates since third review

Comment and docstring cleanup only, no code changes: `+29 −56` over five files.

- `install_staged_skill_dir` — 19-line docstring down to 10. Keeps the staged-tree
  prerequisite and why a rename is only equivalent to `copy_skill_dir` when that
  function produced the stage.
- `_build_download_plan` — 7-line docstring down to 5. Keeps why the `ExitStack`
  owns the backups until the plan is complete.
- Backup and replay comments in the router — trimmed to the constraint each one
  states. The "rollback must ignore cancellation" comment is unchanged, as asked.
- `rename_or_copy_directory` — 11-line docstring down to 8. Keeps the absent-target
  contract and why the rename attempt is the probe.
- Test docstrings — each reduced to the behaviour it pins.

The background that used to sit in those comments is now in *Where the two copies
come from* above.

## Evidence

Targeted tests — `tests/unit/agents/skill_system/test_staged_install.py`, `tests/unit/app/routers/test_skills_router_helpers.py`, `tests/unit/app/routers/test_skills_router_pool_ops.py`:

```
182 passed in 9.57s
```

Neighbouring packages (`tests/unit/agents/skill_system`, `tests/unit/app/routers`,
`tests/unit/utils`):

```
2191 passed, 7 skipped, 11 warnings in 94.16s
```

The warnings are pre-existing and unrelated: one is the `hub.py` "coroutine was
never awaited" runtime warning in
`test_aclose_hub_client_drain_timeout_warns`; the rest are `ORJSONResponse`
deprecation notices emitted by `app/routers`.

Pre-commit on every touched file — `check-ast`, `docstring-first`, `fix-encoding-pragma`, `detect-private-key`, `trailing-whitespace`, `add-trailing-comma`, `mypy`, `black`, `flake8`, `pylint`: all Passed.

Covered by the tests: the rename path installing without calling `copy_skill_dir`; replacement of a pre-existing target that still holds stale files; the fallback when `os.rename` raises (the copy runs with `(stage, target)` and the stage survives); cancellation touching nothing; the download installing the stage instead of copying it a second time; the rollback renaming a local backup back; and the backup falling back to system temp when the workspace refuses a temporary directory.

Not measured: no wall-clock benchmark is included. The change removes a full tree copy, but this PR does not claim a number.

Environment note: this worktree is Windows, so the rename path is exercised on NTFS; the copy fallback is covered by forcing `os.rename` to raise rather than by mounting a second volume.

## Related follow-ups

This PR changes only how an installation is moved into place: rename on the same
volume, copy across volumes. The rollback backup it creates sits next to the
workspace on that same volume, precisely so that restoring can also be a rename.
The consequence is that a hard kill between creating the backup and finishing the
restore leaves a `.qwenpaw_skill_rollback_*` directory behind until something
removes it.

Reclaiming those directories needs its own pass that holds the per-workspace lock,
at which point nothing else can be using them. That is out of scope here and will
be handled separately.

prs.body:
Fixes #8521

Addressed an issue where models returning empty responses were incorrectly treated as successful completions, and ensured that a notification appears when an output limit is reached—allowing users to identify whether a response is incomplete.

Changes:
- If the final response is empty or contains only whitespace, the system now triggers an existing error flow, prompting the user to retry or switch to a different model.
- Implemented pass-through for original "finish reasons" from OpenAI and DashScope, covering streaming and non-streaming responses, events, message persistence, and SSE (Server-Sent Events).
- When an output limit is reached, the system retains the content generated so far and displays a notification indicating that the response is incomplete; also supports message collapsing and history restoration.
- Added truncation notifications in seven languages: Chinese, English, Japanese, Russian, Brazilian Portuguese, Indonesian, and Vietnamese.
- Maintained existing functionality for "thought" continuation, tool calls, multimodal output, and cancellation behavior.

prs.title: feat(qwenpawmail-mcp): add save_draft tool
prs.body:
### Summary

Adds a `save_draft` MCP tool to qwenpawmail-mcp that writes a message into the mailbox **Drafts** folder via IMAP APPEND with the `\Draft` flag — **without sending over SMTP**.

Closes #8780.

### Changes

- `packages/qwenpawmail-mcp/src/qwenpawmail_mcp/mail_client.py`
  - `MailClient.save_draft(to, subject, body, cc, folder)` — builds the message with the existing `_build_message` helper, appends it to the Drafts folder, and returns the parsed `APPENDUID`.
  - `MailClient._drafts_folder()` — auto-detects the folder flagged `\Drafts`, falls back to `Drafts` / `草稿箱`.
  - `_extract_appenduid()` helper to parse the APPEND response.
- `packages/qwenpawmail-mcp/src/qwenpawmail_mcp/server.py`
  - New `save_draft` MCP tool (thin async wrapper, consistent with existing tools).
- `packages/qwenpawmail-mcp/tests/test_save_draft.py`
  - Unit tests: tool registration + argument coercion, cc/explicit folder handling, drafts-folder auto-detection and fallback.

### Why

For agent workflows where the user wants the agent to *draft* an email for later human review, there was no way to write into the mailbox Drafts folder without immediately sending. `send_message` / `reply_message` / `forward_message` all transmit via SMTP as soon as they are called.

### Verification

- End-to-end verified against a NetEase enterprise mailbox (`imap.qiye.163.com`): APPEND → Drafts folder, fetch-by-UID round-trip, and cleanup all work.
- `pytest tests/` → 7 passed (4 existing + 3 new).
- black / flake8 / pylint / mypy clean for the touched files.

### Notes

- On some providers, IMAP SEARCH does not index freshly APPENDed messages, so the tool returns the `APPENDUID`; callers fetch the draft by UID via the existing `get_message(folder, uid)`.

prs.title: fix(runtime): reject chats until background startup completes (#8746)
prs.body:
## Description

During background startup, a chat submitted before the runtime is fully initialized was accepted (HTTP 200), but the agent was built against a half-projected workspace (`tools=1` in the logs) and the run hung before its first LLM call — no error, no timeout, no log. The stall was process-wide: every subsequent chat (new sessions, different models, Console and Feishu) was swallowed the same way until the process restarted. Fixes #8746.

This PR fixes the issue in four layers, so the user-visible failure mode is gone regardless of which internal wait was poisoned:

1. **Runtime readiness gate** — new `qwenpaw.utils.runtime_readiness`, a lifespan-bound, process-wide gate. The existing `startup_ready` only covers core agents; this gate is published only after the *entire* background startup (plugins, workspace projection, provider sync, skill pool) completes. Failures wake all waiters with a concrete reason. CLI/embedded callers that never run the lifespan are unaffected (inert gate).
2. **HTTP admission** — `POST /console/chat` (new sends, not reconnects) and `POST /console/chat/task` wait up to 5s for readiness (`QWENPAW_RUNTIME_READY_HTTP_TIMEOUT`) and then return **503 + `Retry-After: 5`** instead of admitting into a half-initialized runtime. Reconnects still attach to an existing stream as before.
3. **Single entry-point gate** — `AgentBuilder.build()` awaits runtime readiness (`QWENPAW_RUNTIME_READY_TIMEOUT`, default 180s), covering Console, all channels, cron and sub-agents in one shared point.
4. **No more silent stalls**:
   - `MultiAgentManager.get_agent()` no longer returns a workspace in the window between publication and the plugin `workspace_created` hooks (the half-projected toolkit behind the `tools=1` build).
   - Pre-model watchdog (`QWENPAW_AGENT_PRE_MODEL_TIMEOUT`, default 180s): if a built agent produces no non-heartbeat event before its first model call, the run ends with a visible `AGENT_PRE_MODEL_STALL` error and a task-stack dump. Heartbeats deliberately do **not** disarm it (they prove the transport is alive, not that the model call started).
   - Rate-limiter registry hardening: the module-level `asyncio.Lock` (which could become a no-wait process-wide wait if its lazily-created loop went stale) is replaced by a thread lock, and each limiter is bound to its event loop — cross-loop reuse now raises an immediate `RuntimeError` instead of deadlocking, and closed-loop limiters are replaced.

`/healthz` now additionally reports `runtime_ready` and `runtime_startup_error`, so monitoring can distinguish "core agents loaded" from "background startup finished".

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8746

**Security Considerations:** The task-stack dump logs only `file:line` and coroutine names — no prompt content, message bodies or credentials. The readiness gate does not touch authentication/channel-trust logic. New environment-variable reads reject non-numeric and negative values and fall back to defaults.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)

prs.title: fix(channels): scope WeChat credentials per agent workspace
prs.body:
## Description

Two agents could not hold separate WeChat accounts in one installation.

The custody check hashed every *other* agent's credential scope against the
process-wide `WORKING_DIR`, so an agent without an explicit `bot_token_file`
fell back to that same path. Both agents then produced the same "token file"
and "context tokens" hashes, the second one failed with `ACCOUNT_IN_USE`, and
its channel page could not even fetch a QR code (`409 ACCOUNT_IN_USE`).

`wechat_auth_scopes()` already resolves a missing `bot_token_file` against the
`working_dir` it is given, so the fix is to pass each agent's own workspace:

```python
other_dir = Path(profile.workspace_dir).expanduser()
wechat_auth_scopes(other, working_dir=other_dir)
```

Agents that deliberately share a credential directory still collide, which is
the intended guard: the context-token file lives beside the token, and one
directory means one account.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #____ (replace with the issue number; the linked issue
also covers the upgrade migration that duplicates an inline `bot_token`, and the
single-execution-source limit, which this PR deliberately does not change)

**Security Considerations:** Only the *scope hashing* of other agents' configs
changes; credential storage, custody leases, approval authorization and the
plugin execution source are untouched. Agents with identical credentials still
collide by design.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature

> Note: this machine has no network access to the pre-commit hook
> repositories, so `pre-commit run --all-files` cannot bootstrap here. The
> hooks were run directly with the same arguments as `.pre-commit-config.yaml`
> (`black --line-length=79`, `flake8`, `mypy`, `pylint`, `add-trailing-comma`,


Reproduce the original failure (QwenPaw 2.3.0, two agents, each with its own
`bot_token_file` under its workspace):

```bash

curl -s -H "X-Agent-Id: <agent-b>" \
  http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/config/channels/wechat/qrcode
# before: {"detail":"ACCOUNT_IN_USE"}   after: 200 with qrcode_img
```

```
......                                                                   [100%]
6 passed in 0.26s
```

```
channel 'wechat' failed: default@…:Projection channel failed: ACCOUNT_IN_USE;
                        VRPUDS@…:  Projection channel failed: ACCOUNT_IN_USE
```

and `GET /api/config/channels/wechat/qrcode` returned `409 ACCOUNT_IN_USE` for
both agent ids.

The two adjacent problems are tracked in the issue rather than this PR:
the upgrade migration copying an inline `bot_token` into every agent profile,
and the channel plugin's single execution source (a second agent's channel
cannot run, and its QR fetch returns `500 RUNTIME_SOURCE_MUTATING`, while the

Dragging upward near the bottom edge of a chat shrinks the conversation and composer, leaving a blank area underneath even though the terminal is closed. `TerminalDock` hides the terminal content and removes its `Separator`, but keeps two enabled panels. `react-resizable-panels` also creates implicit resize targets between adjacent panels without a separator.

prs.title: fix(console): keep conversation groups stable while dragging
prs.body:
## Description

Long-pressing a conversation currently collapses every source/date section and scrolls the history to the top. This changes the drop target under a stationary pointer, so releasing immediately can move the conversation into a different group. Expanded lists and the customized clients that reuse this component are affected.

Preserve the user's expanded/collapsed sections and scroll offset during dragging. Keep the original row in place, with only `DragOverlay` following the pointer. Select drop targets by pointer position within their visible scroll viewports rather than the overlapping drag rectangle; virtualized rows mounted outside the viewport cannot receive a drop.

Keep the official theme colors and fine border, but highlight only the drop zone actually under the pointer. Do not highlight the source group, which cannot be a move destination. This avoids tinting every conversation in an expanded group during dragging. The drop-zone highlight now uses the same exact DnD target as the drop handler instead of a separate group-wide hover state. Attach group-header highlighting to the actual 32px title surface instead of the 36/42px virtual row. This keeps ordinary/system group labels centered and prevents the title background from covering the left border. Include a component-scoped border fallback for Chromium 108, where color-mix theme tokens cannot resolve. Restrict the shared virtual list to vertical scrolling and reserve its scrollbar gutter to avoid the redundant horizontal scrollbar. Mouse/touch long-press sensors, edge autoscrolling, and the group-update API remain in use. Dropping onto an expanded, empty, or collapsed group still works; releasing in the source group, outside the list, or cancelling does not update the group.

prs.title: fix(console): align sidebar drag and dock hit targets
prs.body:
## Description

On touch-capable desktops (`any-pointer: coarse`), the sidebar drag handle grows from 32px to 44px inside a transport row that remains 32px high. Its hover background and grip shift downward relative to the account card. When the sidebar floats, the return-to-edge button still uses a 32px offset, so the two 44px hit targets overlap. The collapsed rail also uses fixed offsets that overlap and miscenter these controls.

Center the controls in the transport row, align the row with the account card center, and use the shared `--app-hit-target` token for their size and horizontal separation. In the rail, place the docking button below the transport row and center it using its actual hit-target width. The account card has 8px bottom spacing and a 52px height, so the 32px transport row needs an 18px bottom offset: `8 + (52 - 32) / 2`. This preserves the 32px desktop and 44px touch targets, existing drag handlers, and keyboard docking behavior.

The change is limited to `console/src/layouts/dockableSidebar.module.less`.

prs.title: fix(auth): don't skip auth for loopback peers forwarding proxy headers
prs.body:
Fixes #8695

## Description

`AuthMiddleware._should_skip_auth()` skips token validation when the resolved client IP is in `security.allow_no_auth_hosts` (default `127.0.0.1`, `::1`). `_resolve_client_ip()` only honours `X-Forwarded-For` / `X-Real-IP` when the TCP peer is in `security.trusted_proxies`, which is empty by default. Behind a same-host reverse proxy (nginx, Caddy, 1Panel) the resolved IP is therefore the proxy's own `127.0.0.1`, and the loopback defense-in-depth check passes too because the peer really is loopback. Every proxied request was treated as a local CLI request and skipped auth.

In the loopback branch of `_should_skip_auth()`, the skip is now refused when the peer is not a configured trusted proxy and the request carries `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Real-IP` or `Forwarded`. This is the first fix suggested in the issue. Direct loopback requests without proxy headers (the CLI path) still skip auth, and a deployment that lists its proxy in `trusted_proxies` resolves the real client IP as before.

This is a narrower change than #2840, which removes the localhost bypass altogether; it does not conflict with it.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8695

**Security Considerations:** Closes an auth bypass in the default config behind a same-host reverse proxy. A local client that sends one of those headers itself now has to authenticate; no other request path changes.

prs.title: feat(console): preview docx, xlsx and pptx files in the file drawer
prs.body:
## Description

The Console file drawer only previews images, PDF, Markdown, HTML and CSV, so `.docx` / `.xlsx` / `.pptx` files that agents produce show "Preview is unavailable" and have to be downloaded to be read.

This adds a read-only, client-side preview for those three formats:

- **docx** – converted to HTML with [mammoth](https://github.com/mwilliamson/mammoth.js) (new dependency, BSD-2), sanitised with DOMPurify (scripts, event handlers, inline styles and live links removed) and shown with the existing Markdown typography.
- **xlsx** – read directly from the zip container with the already-bundled `jszip` (no spreadsheet engine added). Shared/inline strings, numbers, booleans and date-formatted cells are resolved; each sheet gets a tab; rows/columns are capped at 500 × 50 (same limits as CSV) with a note showing the real size.
- **pptx** – slide text in presentation order (resolved through `presentation.xml`, not file names), with a note that layout/images/charts need the download.

The parsing code is in `officeDocument.ts` and is imported lazily, so mammoth/jszip land in their own chunk (confirmed in a production `vite build`) and only load when an Office file is opened. Files over 25 MB, corrupt archives and failed downloads fall back to the existing "preview unavailable" message. Legacy `.doc` / `.xls` / `.ppt` are unchanged.

New UI strings are added to all seven locale files. `vitest` is aliased to mammoth's browser build so tests run the same entry point Vite bundles.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8404

**Security Considerations:** Document HTML is untrusted, so it goes through DOMPurify with `href`, `target`, `style` and `<style>` removed before `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; xlsx/pptx content is rendered as plain text nodes only. Files are fetched with the existing authenticated blob loader.

prs.title: fix(crons): persist cron and heartbeat token usage to turn records
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cron and heartbeat runs drive `workspace.stream_query` directly instead of going through `Channel.consume_one`, so their token usage was never committed to the session's turn records. The console usage panel undercounts all scheduled task consumption: cron jobs (daily digests, reminders) and heartbeat runs make model calls whose usage never lands in the persisted turn records, even though the session data model already distinguishes cron sessions from chat turns.

Failed runs had a second, subtler problem: staged usage was never dropped, so a failed run's tokens could leak into the next run on the same reused session.

Fixes #8705

## Description

- Extract `commit_turn_usage` / `discard_turn_usage` into `qwenpaw.token_usage.turn_usage`:
  - `commit_turn_usage` resolves and persists one finished turn's usage, never raises
  - `discard_turn_usage` drops staged usage when a run does not finish normally
- `Channel._commit_turn_usage` and `_clear_session_turn_usage` now reuse the shared helpers (no behavior change)
- Cron executor: commit usage after a successful run; discard on timeout / cancel / error
- Heartbeat: same treatment for all three `stream_query` sites
- New e2e regression: `e2e/tests/test_cron_usage.py` (auto-skips without a model API key via `requires_llm`)
