- [X] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

issues.title: [Bug]: Tool-context collapse (`keep_tool_context_turns`) breaks Claude Opus 5.5 chats with a thinking-signature 400 after a few tool-using turns

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: release:v0.9.1
labels.description: Required for the v0.9.1 release: must land or be explicitly deferred before the tag

issues.body:
### Affected component

runtime/daemon

### Severity

S1 - workflow blocked

### Current behavior

Since v0.9.0, a chat on the native `anthropic` provider with `claude-opus-5-5` fails for good once an older tool-using turn leaves the `keep_tool_context_turns` window. Every request from then on is rejected:

```text
400 invalid_request_error
messages.13.content.0: Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block. The block is bound to a different conversation. Remove the block, or set `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior` to "drop_block". That setting requires the `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` value in the `anthropic-beta` header. Content that preceded this block when it was created is missing from this request, starting at `messages.4.content.0`.
```

The dashboard shows only "The selected model provider rejected the request". Reopening the chat recovers it, because the reopened socket reseeds from the stored transcript, which has no tool rows or thinking blocks.

Cause, from the code at v0.9.0:

- #11297 made the tool loop build each provider request from a collapsed copy of the history (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/turn/mod.rs` L2180–2189, `collapse_tool_context_older_than` in `history_trim.rs` L518). Turns older than the newest `keep_tool_context_turns + 1` are sent as their prompt and closing reply only; their tool-call and tool-result rows are left out. The default is 2 (`schema.rs` L6845).
- The Anthropic adapter replays the signed thinking blocks of the turns that are still sent whole, unchanged.
- Opus 5.5 binds each thinking block to the conversation that preceded it. A block from a retained turn was created while the older turn's tool rows were still in the request. Once those rows are collapsed away, the block no longer verifies, and the API rejects the request. Anthropic enforces this check by default for accounts created on or after 2026-08-31.
- Nothing strips or adjusts thinking blocks when the collapse changes the history, the adapter doesn't send `thinking.block_binding`, and the error is classed as non-retryable.

This is separate from #11696 / #11698 (the system prompt changing mid-session). It happens with #11698 applied and with no file edits; the API's diagnosis names missing message content, not the system prompt.

### Expected behavior

Collapsing older tool context should not end the session. The request should stay valid for models that bind thinking to the conversation.

### Steps to reproduce

```text
1. Native `anthropic` provider, `claude-opus-5-5`, on an account where Anthropic enforces the
   thinking-block conversation check. Set `keep_tool_context_turns = 1` in the agent's runtime
   profile (the default of 2 needs one more turn) and reload.
2. Open a new dashboard chat.
3. Send three messages that each make the agent use a tool, for example
   "search the web for <topic> and tell me the 3rd result".
4. The third message fails with the 400 above, and so does every later message in that chat.
   (It needs the previous turn's tool call to carry a thinking block, which Opus usually but
   not always produces; if it doesn't fail, the next tool-using message usually does.)
```

With `keep_tool_context_turns = 0` it does not fail: only the running turn is sent whole, so no retained block predates a collapse. With a large value (1000) it does not fail either, because nothing is collapsed.

### Impact

Any long enough tool-using chat on Opus 5.5 breaks on an affected account, with default settings from about the fourth tool-using turn. Anthropic's documentation says the same check applies to Claude Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.1, which I have not tested. The collapse also rewrites the middle of the cached prefix each time the window moves.

Workaround: set `keep_tool_context_turns` high enough that nothing is collapsed (I use 1000), at the cost of sending all older tool output.

Possible fixes:
- When a collapse removes rows, also leave out the thinking blocks that were created before it (text and tool calls can stay).
- Skip the collapse for models that bind thinking to the conversation, or use Anthropic's server-side context editing to clear old tool results there, which does not count as a history edit.
- As a stopgap, catch this 400 and retry with the `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` beta and `prefix_mismatch_behavior: "drop_block"`, keeping that for the rest of the session.

### Logs / stack traces

```text
One occurrence with a profile that keeps 8 prior turns (times UTC):
16:07:47.732  Tool context collapsed for this request: 1 older turn(s) sent without 6 tool row(s); the newest 9 turn(s) sent whole
16:07:48.042  HTTP 400 invalid_request_error: messages.13.content.0: Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block. […] Content that preceded this block when it was created is missing from this request, starting at `messages.4.content.0`.
16:07:48.219  Non-retryable error, moving on (error_kind=client_error)

Two earlier occurrences the same day had the same diagnosis (`messages.3` / missing from `messages.0`, and `messages.31` / missing from `messages.24`); I did not capture the collapse line for those.

With keep_tool_context_turns = 0 (no failure), every request logs e.g.:
16:59:14.860  Tool context collapsed for this request: 11 older turn(s) sent without 30 tool row(s); the newest 1 turn(s) sent whole
```

### ZeroClaw version

v0.9.0 (with open PRs #11698, #11660, #11875, #11918, #12250, #12374 and #12375 merged locally; none changes the collapse or the Anthropic adapter). #11297 is in v0.9.0 and not in v0.8.7. Before it, per its description, `keep_tool_context_turns` only acted as a boolean and no request-time collapse existed, so v0.8.7 could not fail this way; I did not test that on v0.8.7 itself.

### Rust version

_No response_

### Operating system

Linux server (amd64)

### Regression?

Yes, it worked before

### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I reproduced this on the latest master branch or latest release.
- [x] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

issues.body:
### Task

Make `dashboard_core::tests::a_chat_whose_reply_end_cannot_be_written_ends` (crates/zeroclaw-gateway) pass on Windows, or limit it to the platforms where its premise holds.

### Context

The test was added in #12244. It shrinks the socket buffers at both ends so that a reply's final frame can't be written, then expects the chat to close its conversation at the write deadline. PR CI runs no Windows tests. The scheduled Platform Tests on master fail on Windows every run, starting with the first run after #12244 merged. That includes run 42952365996 on 1a79f89d1e and the run on the v0.9.0 release commit 6c78ba59bc:

```
FAIL [  32.623s] zeroclaw-gateway dashboard_core::tests::a_chat_whose_reply_end_cannot_be_written_ends
thread 'dashboard_core::tests::a_chat_whose_reply_end_cannot_be_written_ends' panicked at crates\zeroclaw-gateway\src\dashboard_core.rs:2417:13:
a chat that could not write its reply's end closes its conversation: still live: ["647b7f83-20bc-4c75-8c33-e74d7387a76b"]
```

Likely cause, not yet reproduced: Windows sockets accept writes beyond a small `SO_SNDBUF`/`SO_RCVBUF`. If so, the final write completes, and the conversation stays live because the client socket is still open, which is correct. If that's right, product behavior is unchanged and only the test's premise fails on Windows.

### Acceptance criteria

- On Windows, either the stuck write is forced another way, or the test is gated to non-Windows targets with the reason in a comment.
- The scheduled Windows Platform Tests job no longer reports this test.
- If a reproduction shows the write deadline is not enforced on Windows, file that as a separate bug.

### Likely files or areas

`crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/dashboard_core.rs` (the test near line 5973 and its `serve_with_small_send_buffers` / `open_chat_with_small_receive_buffer` helpers)

### Contributor fit

maintainer-scoped task, not yet ready for pickup labels

### Mentor, reviewer, or contact

Reviewers of #12244

### Risk notes

Test-only. It doesn't affect released binaries.

issues.title: [Feature]: Honor runtime-profile thinking levels for OpenAI
issues.body:
### Summary

Honor each runtime profile's existing thinking level when building native OpenAI reasoning requests.

### Problem statement

Two agents sharing an OpenAI provider cannot select different native reasoning efforts through their runtime profiles. The selected profile's thinking configuration reaches the turn layer, but OpenAI request construction reads the provider-wide effort resolved from `runtime.reasoning_effort`. Profile prompting and temperature adjustments can still apply; the missing behavior is native OpenAI effort.

Source inspection against master `5d4b18d335780af8bf15979b2f45e541f91c5eb9` identifies these boundaries:

- [Runtime profile resolution](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/5d4b18d335780af8bf15979b2f45e541f91c5eb9/crates/zeroclaw-config/src/schema.rs).
- [Turn thinking resolution](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/5d4b18d335780af8bf15979b2f45e541f91c5eb9/crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/thinking.rs) and [provider request contract](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/5d4b18d335780af8bf15979b2f45e541f91c5eb9/crates/zeroclaw-api/src/model_provider.rs).
- [Global provider options](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/5d4b18d335780af8bf15979b2f45e541f91c5eb9/crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/lib.rs) and [OpenAI Responses requests](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/5d4b18d335780af8bf15979b2f45e541f91c5eb9/crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/openai.rs).

Reproduction to cover in regression tests: configure two runtime profiles with `native_thinking = true`, select `low` and `high` respectively, bind two agents to those profiles and the same reasoning-capable OpenAI model, and set a conflicting global effort. Capture the outgoing requests: each should use its profile's effort. This report is based on source inspection; no live-provider reproduction has been run.

### Proposed solution

Keep `native_thinking = true` as the opt-in. Resolve the existing inline override, then session override, then runtime-profile default. Carry that neutral ZeroClaw level with the request independently of token-budget parameters, and map it at the selected OpenAI model/endpoint boundary. The opted-in request setting overrides global effort; otherwise existing global/default behavior applies.

Map `off` to `none` where supported, otherwise the lowest supported effort. Map `minimal`, `low`, `medium` and `high` to the matching effort, or the next supported higher effort capped at the model maximum. Map `max` to the highest supported effort. Use verified capabilities, with separate treatment of subscription endpoints. Unknown/non-reasoning models retain existing gating and global/default behavior, with diagnostics explaining an unmapped request.

Apply this consistently to Responses, Chat Completions, streaming, tools, fallbacks and existing OpenAI Codex subscription requests. Preserve explicit raw-body override precedence and current bounded compatibility retries. Record requested/effective effort and the selected provider/model in diagnostics.

### Non-goals / out of scope

New native thinking support for other providers, new configuration keys, changing global accepted effort values, authentication changes, broad runtime extraction, or deployment.

This differs from #10705, which requests accepting literal `max` in global `runtime.reasoning_effort`. That issue is related, not resolved by this proposal.
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10705

### Alternatives considered

- A global effort cannot express two profiles sharing one provider.
- Fixing provider construction alone misses per-turn overrides and model fallbacks.
- Provider-specific profile strings would bind runtime policy to one backend instead of mapping the existing ZeroClaw levels.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two profiles sharing an OpenAI endpoint produce their own requested efforts despite a conflicting global effort.
- [ ] All six ZeroClaw levels work independently of a native token budget; native opt-out preserves global/default behavior.
- [ ] Model-specific mappings, unsupported/unknown cases and subscription distinctions are tested.
- [ ] Streaming, tools, request reconstruction and fallback attempts preserve and correctly map the selected level.
- [ ] CLI, channels, Agent/RPC and delegates use the appropriate profile/session policy; concurrent turns remain isolated.
- [ ] Cache reuse cannot hide a changed explicit effort.
- [ ] Existing other-provider budgets, fallback accounting, attribution and replay guarantees remain compatible.
- [ ] Configuration survives save/reload without a new key or migration; behavior and Rust API compatibility changes are documented.

### Architecture impact

Canonical level and request data belong in `zeroclaw-api`, configuration re-exports preserve the existing schema, and model/wire mapping belongs in `zeroclaw-providers`. Runtime/channel changes are limited to propagating existing selected thinking policy and request-cache behavior.

Any new functionality in the transitional runtime crate requires the bounded Core Team-approved exception prescribed by its AGENTS.md, recorded with scope, destination and review condition. This request does not grant that exception. The intended destination of turn plumbing is the planned agent-loop owner in `zeroclaw-kernel`.

#### Bounded runtime exception requested

Core Team review is requested for the following proposed scope; no exception has been granted by this issue.

Paths are relative to `crates/zeroclaw-runtime`:

- `src/agent/thinking.rs`: carry the selected level independently of native token budgets.
- `src/agent/{agent,loop_}.rs` and `src/agent/turn/{mod,provider_call,stream_consume,max_iter}.rs`: propagate that request-bound level through existing turn/recovery/stream paths and bypass cached responses for explicit native-thinking overrides.
- `src/tools/delegate.rs`: use the target profile for independent delegates and preserve bounded-delegate inheritance.
- Focused regression tests in those existing owners.

**Destination:** agent-loop/request-context owner in the planned `zeroclaw-kernel` extraction. Level/request types, configuration policy and OpenAI wire mapping retain their API/config/provider owners.

**Review condition requested:** reconsider at agent-loop extraction, or before widening provider families, retained state or native-thinking policy.

After implementation validation and review, publish the exception-only PR first so the implementation PR can name it with `Depends on #...`. Both PRs target `master` from separate task branches. The implementation PR links this feature request with closing semantics; the exception PR links it as related work.

Publishing either PR does not grant the exception. The implementation PR remains blocked from merging until the Core Team approves and records the exception through the separate PR.

issues.body:
## Summary

Complete ZeroClaw's emergency-stop contract by interrupting cancellable in-flight tool work and enforcing `network-kill` and `domain-block` at the shared network-egress boundary.

## Problem statement

PR #9440 adds the first honest runtime enforcement slice for #9390: `kill-all` and `tool-freeze` are checked before supported tool dispatch, while `network-kill` and `domain-block` are rejected instead of reporting a stop that is not enforced.

That intentionally leaves two operator-safety gaps:

1. A tool already executing when `kill-all` is engaged continues until it finishes. Long-running shell processes and network requests can therefore keep producing side effects after the operator reaches for the stop.
2. ZeroClaw has no shared enforcement point that can revoke all outbound network access or block selected domains across browser, HTTP, provider, plugin, and delegated execution paths.

The original emergency-stop proposal in #1134 included both behaviors. Earlier Phase issues and PRs were built against an older stacked architecture and do not establish that the current runtime enforces them.

## Proposed solution

Define one runtime-owned emergency-stop control contract and integrate it with the current cancellation and network-egress boundaries.

### In-flight cancellation

- Propagate an emergency-stop cancellation signal to every cancellable concrete tool execution.
- For child processes, terminate the owned process tree and await cleanup rather than only dropping the Rust future.
- For async network work, cancel the request and release owned connections, tasks, and response streams.
- Classify tools that cannot be safely interrupted, and do not claim immediate cancellation for those paths until they have an enforceable contract.

### Network and domain enforcement

- Put `network-kill` and `domain-block` checks at the shared outbound network authority rather than duplicating checks in individual tools.
- Cover direct tools, pipeline children, skill aliases, plugins, provider calls, redirects, and other runtime-owned egress paths that use that authority.
- Re-check redirect destinations and normalize hostnames before domain matching so an allowed initial URL cannot redirect around an active block.
- Keep either CLI mode rejected until every path represented by its user-facing claim is actually enforced.

### Operator-visible state

- Make engage, status, and OTP-authorized resume reflect the state enforced by running processes.
- Emit correlated observer and streaming lifecycle events for cancellation, refusal, and resume outcomes without exposing credentials or sensitive request data.

## Non-goals / out of scope

- Reworking the pre-dispatch state authority, pipeline-child gating, or direct/skill-alias enforcement owned by #9440.
- Restoring channel or gateway estop commands from the earlier stack.
- Auto-trigger policy, anomaly detection, or hardware emergency-stop inputs.
- Claiming hard interruption for third-party operations that ZeroClaw cannot cancel or contain.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep pre-dispatch checks only:** honest for the next call, but insufficient when the dangerous operation is already running.
- **Add checks inside each network-capable tool:** easy to bypass as new tools, plugins, providers, or redirect paths are added.
- **Kill the entire daemon:** stronger containment, but loses scoped tool/network/domain behavior and controlled OTP-authorized recovery.

## Acceptance criteria

- Engaging `kill-all` while a cancellable shell tool is running terminates the owned process tree, waits for cleanup, and reports a cancelled result.
- Engaging `kill-all` while a cancellable HTTP operation is running aborts the request and closes its owned resources.
- `network-kill` blocks every runtime-owned outbound path covered by the mode while local-only tools remain usable.
- `domain-block` enforces exact and wildcard host rules across initial requests and redirects without affecting unrelated domains.
- Direct, delegated, sequential-pipeline, and parallel-pipeline paths cannot bypass the applicable cancellation or network gate.
- OTP-authorized resume changes the state actually enforced by running agents, and `status` reports that same state.
- Deterministic integration or system tests drive the real CLI/control boundary against an isolated runtime, an owned child process, and a local HTTP server.
- Documentation names any operation that remains non-cancellable and does not describe rejected or partial modes as enforced.

## Architecture impact

This spans the runtime cancellation owner, concrete tool-execution boundary, shared network-egress policy, security state/control plane, CLI status/resume surface, and observer/streaming events. The implementation needs a design checkpoint before coding so it does not recreate per-tool enforcement or revive the obsolete stacked architecture from #1159, #1160, and #1162.

## Risk and rollback

Risk is high because incorrect cancellation can leak child processes or corrupt tool cleanup, while incomplete egress coverage would create a false security guarantee.

Mitigations:

- default closed for modes whose full enforcement is not available;
- one shared cancellation and egress authority;
- deterministic failure-path tests at the real process and network boundaries;
- explicit ownership and cleanup for every interrupted resource.

Rollback is to disable the newly exposed modes and revert to the honest pre-dispatch behavior from #9440. No persisted-state migration should be required.

## Expected routing

Needs design or RFC discussion first.

## Next decision surface

Use this issue to agree on the runtime cancellation owner, shared egress boundary, interruptibility contract, and phased implementation after #9440 establishes the prerequisite pre-dispatch authority.

## Breaking change?

No. The modes remain rejected until their enforcement contract is complete; enabling them afterward is additive.

## Data hygiene checks

- [x] I removed personal or sensitive data from examples, payloads, and logs.
- [x] I used neutral, project-focused wording and placeholders.

issues.body:
### Affected component

runtime/daemon

### Severity

S1 - workflow blocked

### Current behavior

Agent cron jobs (`run_agent_job` in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/cron/scheduler.rs`) await `agent::run` with no outer `timeout` / cancel budget (shell jobs have a 120s cap). `release_job` comments that failed releases are recovered by `clear_stale_locks` **at next startup**. A hung agent job therefore occupies a `max_concurrent` slot until daemon restart. Sync SQLite open/claim on the async scheduler tick worsens stalls under load.

### Expected behavior

1. Enforce a configurable wall-clock timeout + cancellation around agent cron runs.
2. Reclaim stale `locked_at` locks on a TTL during the poll loop (not boot-only).
3. Prefer pooled/`spawn_blocking` SQLite access on the scheduler path.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Schedule an agent cron job whose prompt hangs the model/tool loop.
2. Observe the job remains claimed (`locked_at` set) with no timeout.
3. Further due jobs block once `max_concurrent` slots are exhausted until process restart clears stale locks.

### Impact

Affected users: cron agent jobs.
Frequency: any hung LLM/tool path.
Consequence: scheduler slot leak until restart; overdue jobs pile up.

### Logs / stack traces

_No response_

### ZeroClaw version

v0.8.1 / commit 74a806943

### Rust version

rustc 1.83.0 (90b35a623 2024-11-26)

Linux 6.12.94+ x86_64

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`; merge only after the dependencies below.
- **What changed and why:** Use the canonical registry RPC editor and exact model references in Zerocode configuration, Quickstart and chat selection; retain masked edit baselines, add text navigation and update independent Fluent catalogs.
- **Scope boundary:** Backend and protocol contracts are provided by the parent. Web dashboard changes are a separate child.
- **Blast radius:** TUI onboarding, configuration save/reload, model selection and validation feedback.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related to #9809. Stack part 10; reference implementation `921b8ee993a0b2439a0c2c41cb84337270942a06`. Depends on #12450.

### What this does, simply

The terminal setup and configuration screens need to edit the same connections and models that the backend resolves. This change switches Zerocode to exact registry keys and adds connection/model editing, replacing the old provider-profile workflow. The exact-head ZeroCode edit/save/reopen workflow has been verified with the matching daemon and synthetic data; the reopened registry shows the persisted model and masked credential.

## Testing (required)


### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes` — the interactive workflow below supplements the passing required CI gate.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Requested surface: `tui`, exercised interactively at `904b56d40d7849f69ee6aff31952fd141949723c` with the matching daemon; English locale, xterm 160 columns × 50 rows.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Check out this head with its parent commits. Use an isolated V5 configuration with a synthetic `openai.demo.gateway` connection, a `chat.demo.gateway` model and an enabled agent referencing that model and a supervised risk profile. Build ZeroCode and its matching daemon together.
- **Steps to run:** Run `cargo build --offline --locked -p zeroclaw -p zerocode --bins`; launch `target/debug/zerocode --config-dir <isolated-config-dir>`. Open Config → Provider registry → providers.registry. Change `models["chat.demo.gateway"].model` from `gpt-synthetic-before` to `gpt-synthetic-after`, press Ctrl+S, then press Enter to reopen the registry.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The TUI reads and writes V5 registry documents, preserves complete model names and reports edit failures without discarding the draft.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The TUI edits provider-family tables and derives selections by splitting profile references.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** At `904b56d40d7849f69ee6aff31952fd141949723c`, CI Required Gate, Test, Lint and Zerocode RPC Boundary pass. These cover compilation, automated tests and RPC boundary checks. The actual terminal interaction is covered separately by the exact-head evidence below. The report-only risk workflow fails on file-evidence/head binding.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** This manual run covers registry editing, Ctrl+S persistence, reopening, dotted keys and credential masking. Quickstart and chat model selection were not manually exercised in this run; no old #9809 screenshot is substituted for the ZeroCode result.
- **Commands run and tail output:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0, no formatting diff. `git diff --check`: exit 0, no whitespace errors. `cargo build --offline --locked -p zeroclaw -p zerocode --bins`: exit 0, both binaries built in this worktree’s `target` directory.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Ran the actual ZeroCode registry edit/save/reopen sequence against the matching local daemon. Parsed the persisted TOML independently and confirmed the literal dotted model key holds the updated value; the credential was not replaced by the mask, and the terminal capture does not contain the stored credential. No provider inference request was made.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Direct screenshot of the reopened actual xterm/ZeroCode interface, using synthetic data. Captured with ImageMagick `import` on an isolated Xvfb display; the UI was not reconstructed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `904b56d40d7849f69ee6aff31952fd141949723c`; `tui`, 160×50 terminal, November 16, 2026. [Evidence and reproduction record](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/8ceccb989b7eff9bac4090242db52288568293aa/README.md). Evidence files are on a standalone fork branch and do not change this implementation PR’s diff.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [Direct reopened-editor screenshot](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/8ceccb989b7eff9bac4090242db52288568293aa/zerocode-registry-reopened.png), [save-result capture](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/8ceccb989b7eff9bac4090242db52288568293aa/saved-terminal.txt), [reopened-editor capture](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/8ceccb989b7eff9bac4090242db52288568293aa/reopened-terminal.txt).

  ![Actual ZeroCode registry after Ctrl+S and reopening: updated dotted-key model and masked credential](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/8ceccb989b7eff9bac4090242db52288568293aa/zerocode-registry-reopened.png)

- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Ctrl+S returned `Saved "providers"`. Reopening displayed `"model": "gpt-synthetic-after"` under the intact `chat.demo.gateway` key, `"api_key": "***MASKED***"` and `No pending edits`. The saved TOML independently contains the updated model value. Result: PASS.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No duplicate local full test/clippy matrix was run; the existing required CI covers it. A local build and focused real TUI interaction were performed to fill the reviewer-identified evidence gap.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No additional permissions.
- New external network calls? No additional provider endpoints; existing backend RPC remains the transport.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes; editors preserve masked connection fields through the backend registry-edit contract.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No additional model-visible input path.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: A masked value must never overwrite a real credential. The editor carries the backend edit baseline and uses the same validated persistence path; the real edit/save/reopen check confirmed the stored credential is preserved and the reopened editor remains masked.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Requires the parent V5 backend and its registry-edit RPC contract.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes; terminal onboarding and editors use connections and exact model keys.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: Merge dependencies first, migrate existing configuration to V5, and rebuild Zerocode against the matching backend. Old profile editing is not retained in the new UI.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this client layer together with dependent UI layers; retain the matching server and V5 config or restore the V4 backup for a full downgrade.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None added for staging the stack.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** CI compile errors, configuration load failures, or changed provider behavior in the layer-specific regression tests.

Stack integration: this repository grants this author read-only access. These fork PRs therefore target `master` and have cumulative diffs. Review the incremental layer against its declared parent; merge parents first and refresh each child before merging. Original #9809 remains the reference PR and is not superseded or closed.

Incremental review: [declared parent to this layer](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/compare/b46ac874c036def0c6da63856eb0200492c8ec5f...904b56d40d7849f69ee6aff31952fd141949723c).

prs.title: feat(web): manage scoped HTTP credentials
prs.body:
Merge order: merge this PR (#12408) before its dependent PR #12490 (Authorization: Token). Both can be reviewed in parallel.

## Summary

- Base branch `master`. Depends on #12402.
- Related #12373. Adds separate Secrets tabs for HTTP Basic credentials and API tokens alongside plugin TLS.
- Authenticated operators can create, replace, and delete encrypted credentials. The catalog returns alias, type, and origin.
- The HTTP request tool accepts an alias for Bearer, X-API-Key, or HTTP Basic authentication. The alias is scoped to one HTTPS origin and the existing HTTP policy still applies. Browser form sign-in is outside this change. The catalog also stores TOTP, SSH-key and service-password records; those require compatible consumers. SSH transport integration is tracked separately in #12418.

### What this does, simply

An operator can register an API token as INVENTORY_API and ask the agent to use that alias with the inventory endpoint. The HTTP tool adds the token during the request.

## Testing

### How you can test

- Reviewer testing requested. Surface is web.
- With secret encryption initialized, open Settings → Secrets and register a disposable credential against an allowed HTTPS test endpoint. Use its alias in an HTTP request. Try another origin and then delete the credential and retry.
- This branch should show metadata in the editor, authenticate only at the configured origin, and refuse use after deletion. The corresponding tabs and scoped argument are absent on master.

### How I tested

- `cargo check --locked --release -p zeroclaw-gateway -j2` completed successfully.
- `npm ci` and `npm run build` completed successfully.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Added targeted tests for refusing HTTP, another host, and another port. Authenticated live observations, the tested integration revision, and the redacted Secrets editor capture are linked below.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes. The HTTP tool can use an operator-created reference within the existing tool and network policies.
- New external network calls? Yes. Opt-in external secret providers are resolved through their installed CLIs and service identities before the existing HTTP tool sends the origin-scoped request. Other providers use simulated CLI-output tests; OpenBao live observations are recorded below.
- Secrets handling changed? Yes. Values are encrypted at rest, omitted from the catalog, and sent only to the registered HTTPS origin. Redirects remain disabled.
- PII in fixtures or documentation? No.
- New untrusted model-visible content? No. HTTP responses continue to be untrusted. Common reflected credential strings are redacted.

## Compatibility

- Backward compatible with existing config and requests. The optional credential map defaults to empty.
- Config surface changed. Existing installations require no migration. The editor requires an initialized encryption key.
- Toolchain floor unchanged.

## Rollback

Delete the new aliases to disable their use. Before reverting to a binary without the new config field, remove its entries and retain an encrypted backup as needed. Existing HTTP auth references continue to use their established config.


### Live integration evidence

An authenticated operator registered disposable Basic, X-API-Key, and Bearer credentials through the WebUI. The protected HTTPS fixture returned 200 for each applicable credential. The X-API-Key continued working after replacement, and a deleted alias was refused before dispatch. OpenBao certificate authentication was limited to the scoped KV paths. The agent authenticated to a protected endpoint using an OpenBao alias, with the endpoint confirming HTTP 200. The SSH keys tab was opened in an authenticated browser and a scoped OpenBao SSH reference was registered. The broker integration and live transport validation are tracked in #12418. External providers other than OpenBao use simulated CLI output tests.


## Operator authorization and exact live evidence

Enabling HTTP use for an alias authorizes any caller already permitted to use http_request at the configured HTTPS origin. This implementation has no per-agent or per-principal credential grants. The broader cross-consumer authorization contract is under discussion in #12422. The mutually exclusive HTTP credential arguments now return a Fluent-localized error. The [follow-up integration evidence](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12408#issuecomment-6880721152) records protected HTTPS and SSH endpoint observations before and after grant changes.

The authenticated Jarvis WebUI at integrated revision 77c0b647d was used to provision disposable HTTP and SSH credentials, revoke both grants, rotate their values while revoked, and grant access again. The live catalog returned the expected permission metadata at each step and both records were deleted afterward. This run verified the editor and persistence. It did not re-run protected service requests at each step.

Authenticated editor capture on integrated revision 77c0b647d, cropped to the form with synthetic input and the secret field redacted: [view capture](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/183107bbb34fd9f94144c600d73b28c7b1eb4880/.pr-evidence/pr-12408-authenticated-secrets-editor.png).


## Live WebUI evidence for explicit grants and mutation audit

Tested in an authenticated, headed Chrome session against the Jarvis integration build `7fb70389a`, which includes the changes at PR head `98712cc2e`. The integration build also contains the local external-vault writer. The steps below exercised the local encrypted credential path with a disposable API-token alias and a synthetic value.

| WebUI action | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Create an API token alias for https://example.com | HTTP 204. The HTTP Request grant was unchecked in Permissions. |
| Grant HTTP Request access | HTTP 204. The checkbox remained checked after a full reload. |
| Revoke HTTP Request access | HTTP 204. The checkbox remained unchecked after a full reload. |
| Delete the test alias | HTTP 204. The alias was absent after a full reload. |

The persisted runtime audit trace contained four successful events for the fixture: create, grant enabled, grant disabled, and delete. Every event recorded an authenticated actor and credential kind. The synthetic secret value was absent from all four events. The served OpenAPI document also exposed GET 200 and POST 204 and marked token values, passwords, TOTP seeds, and SSH private keys as write-only.

The test verified permission persistence and the audit trail. It made no outbound authenticated request.


## Retained audit follow-up and live verification

The persisted outcome is now recorded in the task that owns the config write, so a dropped HTTP request cannot discard the audit emitter after the write was admitted. The existing `cancelled_prop_saves_block_generation_handoff_until_publication` regression passed, along with the 10 targeted gateway credential and OpenAPI tests.

On the running Jarvis integration build `9f0509ef7`, repeated the authenticated Chrome Token fixture. Create, grant, revoke and delete all returned HTTP 204. Token selection and grant changes persisted across reloads, and the test alias was absent after cleanup. The runtime trace contained the four expected events with authenticated actors and without the synthetic value. This live test exercised normal completion. The cancellation test ran locally at the shared config-write boundary.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`; merge only after the dependencies below.
- **What changed and why:** Activate canonical registry admission and backend consumers, promote V4 configuration to V5, materialize complete models for routing/fallback/switching, and wire secret-safe registry editing. Registry types, native protocols, chat transport and reflection are prepared in #12454, #12455, #12456 and #12457.
- **Scope boundary:** V5 admission, persistence/editor wiring, canonical model construction and backend consumer/lifecycle cutover. Activation and affected consumers remain together so no intermediate revision clears profiles that active consumers still read. Zerocode and Web follow separately.
- **Blast radius:** Config persistence and secret handling; provider construction; agent/session lifecycle; memory, speech and decision consumers; channel/gateway/RPC dispatch.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related to #9809. Stack part 9; reference implementation `921b8ee993a0b2439a0c2c41cb84337270942a06`. Depends on #12457.

### What this does, simply

The preceding layers prepare independent registry types, native capability protocols, chat transport and generic reflection. This layer activates those components: V4 input is promoted at the V5 admission boundary, backend consumers resolve exact model references, and routing, fallback and switching build complete target bindings. Configuration activation and dependent consumers stay together to avoid a partially switched runtime. This remaining cutover is still large; the preparatory layers make their own architectural boundaries independently reviewable.

## Testing (required)


### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes` — the migration or interactive workflow below supplements passing current-head CI.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Requested surface: `cli`. Not exercised interactively at this revision.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Check out this head with its parent commits; use the repository toolchain and existing test fixtures.
- **Steps to run:** Run workspace Quality Gate, migration and registry edit tests, provider protocol tests, runtime route/switch/fallback/refresh tests and feature-matrix checks; exercise `zeroclaw config migrate` with a V4 backup.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** V4 configuration becomes V5 connections/models; internal consumers resolve exact model keys; switching/fallback materializes all target configuration and a failed update preserves the previous binding.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Master stores provider-owned profiles and consumer-specific capability settings, and has no canonical decoupled registry.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Current-head CI](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/43691399717) passes `CI Required Gate`, workspace tests, opt-in tool tests, lint, security, and the applicable feature/platform build checks at `b46ac874c036def0c6da63856eb0200492c8ec5f`.

Live CLI/migration verification remains pending; passing CI does not establish the two old-configuration migration restrictions identified in review. Original #9809 CI does not validate intermediate stack revisions.
- **Commands run and tail output:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0, no formatting diff. `git diff --check`: exit 0, no whitespace errors.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Addressed previous-head split dependency errors (retained embedding factory, complete timeout helpers, deferred dispatch-dependent sampling, and secret-test trait import). New-head execution remains pending. Compared the integrated provider and UI trees byte-for-byte with the saved pre-split snapshot. Preserved the frozen V4 fixture. Corrected previous-head CI failures caused by unnecessary TOML rewriting; the existing comment-preservation and atomic-save assertions remain intact. New-head execution is pending. - **Visual interface evidence:** Pending: CLI Quickstart and configuration command output require exact-head verification before interface sign-off.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `b46ac874c036def0c6da63856eb0200492c8ec5f`; source formatting only.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** No interactive action performed; current-head CI passed, while manual runtime checks remain pending.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local Cargo build/test/clippy were intentionally skipped at the author’s request to use GitHub CI instead of repeated heavy local compilation.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes; existing capability selection is represented in the new registry. Existing admission boundaries remain in force.
- New external network calls? Yes; native capability adapters use the selected connection and protocol. No additional allowlist bypass is introduced.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes; connection credentials and sensitive headers use the existing encrypted persistence and masked edit contracts.

Preserve ciphertext, use masked compare-and-swap edits, validate references before installation, and keep the previous binding when construction fails. Provider output remains subject to runtime tool admission.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Older files are converted at the migration boundary; the new internal API and persisted V5 shape replace profile-owned construction.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes; connections, models, presets, fallback references and configuration editing use the V5 shape.

Inspect the resulting connections/models and exact model references. V1-V3 first migrate through the frozen V4 step, then V4-to-V5. prs.title: feat(web): manage write-only plugin TLS credentials
prs.body:
## Summary

- Base branch is `master`.
- Add a write-only operator panel under Config → Storage → Secrets for credentials already referenced by a plugin TLS profile.
- Reuse the canonical encrypted plugin configuration and existing host-mediated TLS authorization. The catalog returns instance, property, destinations and configured state.
- This is the first implementation slice of Related #12373. The broader catalog, reversible disable, and references usable by other consumers are open design work. This PR leaves the issue open.

### What this does, simply

An authenticated operator can provision a PEM value for a configured plugin TLS profile without putting the value in a chat. Rotation and deletion use the existing configuration commit path. New connections continue to use the existing instance and destination checks.

## Testing

### How you can test

- Reviewer testing requested. Surface is web.
- Pair the dashboard, enable encryption with an initialized key, and configure a plugin TLS profile referencing a schema-declared secret.
- Open Storage → Secrets → Plugin TLS credentials. Set, replace, refresh and delete a synthetic PEM value. Inspect the responses and verify they contain only metadata or configured state.
- On master, the dedicated panel is absent.

### How I tested

- `cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --tests -j2` completed successfully.
- Web TypeScript type checking passed. The four existing read-only configuration UI regression tests passed.
- Rust formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Added a real config-router test for scoped-principal rejection, missing key, encrypted persistence, duplicate creation, replacement and deletion. The gateway test exposed a deletion failure. The follow-up persists only the selected credential and tests that neighboring ciphertext and the TLS profile survive. The current-head gateway test is pending CI. A Chrome walkthrough of the real WebUI with a synthetic API passed create, replace, refresh, delete, and draft clearing on cancel. This browser test did not use a live gateway.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. The new route requires a current authenticated administrator. It accepts only existing TLS binding slots.
- New external network calls? No.
- Credential handling changed? Yes. Bounded request bodies carry write-only values. The route requires encryption and an existing key, returns metadata with no-store, and emits mutation metadata without the submitted value.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in the diff or fixtures? No.
- Model-visible inputs or prompt injection surface changed? No.

## Compatibility

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config, env or CLI surface changed? No. The API and dashboard gain a panel for existing bindings.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.

## Rollback

Revert this change to remove the panel and route. Values already saved remain standard plugin configuration. Restore a known-good encrypted configuration backup to undo a credential rotation or deletion, and retain the corresponding encryption key. Watch for unexpected 403, 409 or 412 responses on the new route and for connection failures after credential edits.

prs.title: fix(channels): hand replied-to documents to the agent as files
prs.body:
## Summary

Quoting (replying to) a Telegram message that contains a document previously produced only a bare `[Document]` marker in the reply context. The agent could not read the referenced file - e.g. a user replies "summarize this" to a posted PDF and the model has nothing to summarize.

This change pre-downloads the replied-to document into the agent workspace before parsing and quotes it as `[Document: name] path` followed by the media caption:

- New `reply_file_paths` cache keyed by `{chat_id}:{message_id}`. The pre-download runs before the mention-only gate can drop the original message, so quoting works even for messages the bot never acknowledged.
- `extract_reply_context` resolves the cache for the document branch; with no cached path it keeps the previous `[Document]` marker, so nothing regresses when downloads are unavailable.
- Media `caption` on the replied-to message is now included after the file reference.

Scope is documents only; voice/audio reply context is covered separately.

## Test evidence

- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib repl` - 112 passed, 0 failed (includes a new wiremock end-to-end test: getFile + download + cache + quoted path with caption, and a no-cache marker regression test).
- Battle-tested in production on our fork (Windows service, live group): quoting a document hands the agent a readable path.

## Risk

Medium - `crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/telegram.rs` behavior change, no boundary/security impact. Rollback: revert; cached files are best-effort workspace artifacts.

## Side effects

Replied-to documents are downloaded once per `{chat_id}:{message_id}` into `{workspace}/telegram_files/` (same directory the existing attachment pipeline uses).

prs.title: fix(runtime): honor cost.enforcement.mode when a budget limit is exceeded
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The budget gate (`enforce_tool_loop_budget`) never read `[cost.enforcement] mode`. Every exceeded daily or monthly limit ended the turn, so the documented default, `warn`, behaved like `block`, and `route_down` never substituted a model.
  - The gate now reads the mode from the scoped tracker's live cost config, the same place the limits come from. `warn` records a warn-level event and lets the call through. `block` stops the turn, as before.
  - `route_down` has no model substitution in the turn loop yet. It now stops the turn as `block` does (unchanged for anyone using it) and logs that it fell back to `block`. Unrecognized values do the same, so a typo can never loosen the control.
  - The mode covers the shared `daily_limit_usd` and `monthly_limit_usd` limits only. A delegated agent's per-hop ceiling (`max_cost_per_day_cents`) still stops it in every mode. `check_budget` returns at the first limit it finds exceeded, before it reads those ceilings, so the tracker gains `check_ceilings()`. The gate asks it before `warn` lets an exceeded shared limit through.
  - Tests that relied on the old stop under the default config now set `mode = "block"` explicitly.
- **Scope boundary:** No model substitution for `route_down`. No change to `allow_override`, to config-reload plumbing, to `warn_at_percent` notices, or to how spend is priced and recorded. No new config keys. `check_budget` keeps its signature and results; its per-agent loop moves into a helper that `check_ceilings` shares.
- **Blast radius:** Every turn that runs in a cost-tracking scope: CLI `agent`, gateway chat and webhook turns, channel turns, cron, delegated sub-loops, and the one-shot `run_model_query` seam (skill reflection, graceful summary). With the default mode, those turns no longer stop at the shared daily or monthly limit.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12477. Related #11585 and #11589. #11589 adds an approval-based override of an exceeded limit. It shares no lines with this change, and `git merge-tree` combines the two without conflicts. If both land, its override prompt should be offered only in `block` mode, because `warn` already lets the call through.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw can stop spending when a daily or monthly cost limit is reached, and `[cost.enforcement] mode` is meant to choose what happens then: `warn` logs it and carries on, `block` refuses further calls, and `route_down` switches to a cheaper model. The setting was parsed but never used, so every limit acted like `block`. With the defaults (`mode = "warn"`, $10 a day), pricing your models was enough for an agent to stop answering mid-task for the rest of the day.

With this change, `warn` and `block` do what the docs say. `route_down` still refuses, as it always has, because the model swap it describes isn't built yet, and it now says so in the log. Per-agent spending ceilings on delegated agents keep stopping those agents whatever the mode is.

This changes behavior for anyone on the default mode who relied on the stop: they now keep spending past the limit, with a warning in the log. One line keeps the old behavior:

```toml
[cost.enforcement]
mode = "block"
```

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. This is a user-visible behavior change on the default config, and an A/B run against a loopback mock shows it in a minute.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` = `cli` (`zeroclaw agent`). The `web` surface (gateway webhook SSE) is covered by a test, not by a manual step.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A loopback OpenAI-compatible mock that answers every chat request with `usage.prompt_tokens = 10000`, a throwaway config dir, and this config:

  ```toml
  schema_version = 4
  [providers.models.openai.mock]
  model = "mock-model"
  uri = "http://127.0.0.1:18765/v1"
  api_key = "dummy"
  [agents.repro]
  enabled = true
  model_provider = "openai.mock"
  risk_profile = "default"
  runtime_profile = "default"
  [risk_profiles.default]
  [runtime_profiles.default]
  [cost]
  daily_limit_usd = 0.01
  [cost.enforcement]
  mode = "warn"        # then "block", then "route_down"
  [cost.rates.providers.models.openai."mock-model"]
  input_per_mtok = 100.0
  output_per_mtok = 100.0
  cached_input_per_mtok = 100.0
  ```

- **Steps to run:** Run `zeroclaw --verbose --log-level warn --config-dir ./cfg agent -a repro -m "hi"` twice for each mode, starting from a fresh config dir each time.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** `warn`: turn 2 prints `ok` and exits 0, the mock sees 2 POSTs, and stderr shows a WARN `note` record with `{"current_usd":1.0005,"enforcement_mode":"warn","limit_usd":0.01,"period":"Day"}` and `cost limit exceeded; the call proceeds because cost.enforcement.mode is warn`. `block`: turn 2 exits 1 with the same `Budget exceeded` error as before, 1 POST, and the `reject` record now carries `"enforcement_mode":"block"`. `route_down`: same refusal and 1 POST, plus a WARN `note` with `"enforced_as":"block","enforcement_mode":"route_down"`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** In all three modes, turn 1 prints `ok` and records $1.0005. Turn 2 exits 1 with `Error: Budget exceeded: $1.0005 of $0.01 Day limit. Cannot make further API calls until the budget resets.` and the mock sees one POST in total. Same on the v0.9.0 release binary.

### How I tested

Ran on Linux x86_64 with rustc 1.98.0, on base `69ea0ae1ae` plus this change. The tested tree is `5997d68d64`, the tree of commit `757621a413`.

New tests at the behavior boundary:

- `agent::turn::provider_call::tests`: the budget gate in a cost scope. Default (`warn`) lets an exceeded shared limit through and records it. `block` stops it. `route_down` and an unrecognized value (`"Warn"`) stop it and record the fallback. The mode is read live (warn → block → warn on one tracker). Under `warn`, a delegated agent is still stopped by its own ceiling and by the shared-capped ceiling, and goes ahead when those ceilings hold. Under `block`, the shared limit stops it whatever its ceiling.
- `agent::loop_::tests::warn_mode_turn_past_the_daily_limit_still_reaches_the_provider`: a full `run_tool_call_loop` turn past the limit returns the provider's answer. `budget_rejection_emits_no_waiting_on_model_lifecycle` now runs the same turn under `block`.
- `tests::webhook_sse_production_warn_mode_past_the_budget_reaches_provider` (gateway): a webhook SSE turn past the limit reaches the provider and ends with `done`. The existing budget-exhaustion test now sets `block`.
- `cost::tracker::tests::check_ceilings_reads_only_the_ceilings_behind_an_exceeded_shared_limit`: the new tracker method across shared, per-agent, ancestor-chain, shared-capped and disabled scopes.

Red first, with the new tests applied to the untouched base:

```text
test agent::turn::provider_call::tests::the_default_warn_mode_lets_an_exceeded_shared_limit_through_and_records_it ... FAILED
  warn must not stop the turn: Err(Budget exceeded: $10.2500 of $10.00 Day limit. ...)
test agent::turn::provider_call::tests::warn_mode_still_stops_a_delegated_agent_at_its_own_ceiling ... FAILED
  unexpected stop: Budget exceeded: $16.5000 of $10.00 Day limit. ...
test agent::loop_::tests::warn_mode_turn_past_the_daily_limit_still_reaches_the_provider ... FAILED
test result: FAILED. 6 passed; 7 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 6202 filtered out
test tests::webhook_sse_production_warn_mode_past_the_budget_reaches_provider ... FAILED
  left: 0  right: 1   (event: error ... Budget exceeded: $2.0000 of $0.01 Day limit)
```

The `block` tests' stop assertions pass on base. The block gate test fails there only on the new `enforcement_mode` record attribute.

Green, with the change:

```text
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- agent::turn::provider_call::tests:: agent::loop_::tests::budget_rejection_emits_no_waiting_on_model_lifecycle agent::loop_::tests::warn_mode_turn_past_the_daily_limit_still_reaches_the_provider
test result: ok. 13 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 6202 filtered out
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib -- webhook_sse_production_budget_exhaustion_skips_provider_request webhook_sse_production_warn_mode_past_the_budget_reaches_provider
test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 915 filtered out
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check                                  # exit 0
$ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 50s
$ RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway --no-deps
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 24s
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config
test result: ok. 1987 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out   (lib; integration targets all ok)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway
test result: ok. 916 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out    (lib; integration targets all ok)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --no-fail-fast
test result: ok. 6205 passed; 0 failed; 10 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out   (lib; all 16 integration targets ok; doc-tests 0)
$ cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2m 02s
$ scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh   # Summary: 0 error(s)
$ scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh     # Checked 1 local docs link target(s). No added HTTP(S) links detected
$ scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh <changed files>   # Comment hygiene gate passed.
```

An earlier full `zeroclaw-runtime` run on the same tree, under heavy load, failed one test: `rpc::dispatch::tests::rtg_10197_reaped_prompt_publishes_before_close_kill_or_delete_can_remove_it` (`prompt must publish the rehydrated incarnation: Elapsed(())`, a 1-second timeout in RPC session rehydration, which does not reach the exceeded-budget path). It then passed 3/3 alone on this branch, 3/3 alone on the untouched base, and in the full rerun above.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** CI Required Gate (Lint, fmt, tests) once it runs on this head; it covers the same three crates. Everything above is from local runs made before CI.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None known. The changed code is on every platform's common path. The binary A/B run under "How you can test" adds what unit tests can't show: CLI exit codes and the log records an operator sees.
- **Commands run and tail output:** above.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The A/B binary run under "How you can test", on the v0.9.0 release binary (before) and a debug build of this branch (after). It ran in an isolated network namespace with a loopback mock, a throwaway HOME and a throwaway config dir. Not verified: real paid providers; channels other than CLI and the gateway webhook (Telegram, Discord, cron and ACP run the same gate); Windows and macOS; the dashboard UI. Past the limit in `warn` mode the dashboard shows no banner, which is unchanged and not added here.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `Exact plain-text output` (stderr records and stdout of `zeroclaw agent`, quoted above).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** tree `5997d68d64`, `cli` surface, `zeroclaw --verbose --log-level warn --config-dir <dir> agent -a repro -m hi`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** the turn-2 lines quoted under "Expected on this branch".
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** the second turn past a $0.01 daily limit. `warn` answers; `block` and `route_down` refuse.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No `--all-features` clippy run; clippy ran with default features on the three touched crates. `zeroclaw-desktop` was excluded from the workspace check (it needs desktop toolchains).

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: None are `Yes`. One cost-control note: on the default mode this lets spend continue past the shared limits, which is the documented behavior of `warn`. Per-agent ceilings still stop delegated agents, and `route_down` and unrecognized values fail closed to `block`.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No. On the default `mode = "warn"`, an exceeded shared daily or monthly limit no longer stops the turn. It logs a warn-level `cost limit exceeded` event and the call goes ahead. `block` and `route_down` installs behave as before.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new keys. The existing `[cost.enforcement] mode` now takes effect.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: to keep stopping at the limit, add this to `config.toml` before upgrading:

  ```toml
  [cost.enforcement]
  mode = "block"
  ```

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`. An operator who needs the old behavior without a new build can set `[cost.enforcement] mode = "block"`, which applies at the next check, with the same reload rules as the limits.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `[cost.enforcement] mode` (`warn` / `block`).
- **Observable failure symptoms:** In `warn` mode, WARN records `cost limit exceeded; the call proceeds because cost.enforcement.mode is warn` with `current_usd`, `limit_usd`, `period`. A refusal is still the WARN `tool-call loop budget exceeded` record, which now carries `enforcement_mode`. A `route_down` or unrecognized mode adds the WARN `... so the exceeded limit is enforced as block`. A failed ceiling check logs `cost ceiling check failed; ...` and refuses.

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep per-connection task records out of the INFO trace
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Since #11901, the gateway runs every connection it accepts, every relay-forwarded dashboard connection, and every task hyper hands to its executor (HTTP/2 streams) through `ServeTasks::spawn`. That function spawned with `spawn!`, which records `task spawned` and `task complete` at INFO. The daemon records INFO by default, so each connection wrote two records to the runtime trace. A client that opens a connection per request fills the trace with them.
  - `spawn!` now takes an optional level: `spawn!(level = DEBUG, future)`. Without one, it records at INFO as before.
  - `ServeTasks::spawn` uses `level = DEBUG`. That one call covers all three kinds of connection task, so their lifecycle records drop below the default recording level.
- **Scope boundary:** `spawn!` still defaults to INFO, and no other call site changes. The gateway's other records stay as they are: connection errors and TLS handshake failures (already DEBUG), the drain and retirement records, and the 503 a stopped gateway answers with. Trace persistence, rotation and retention are not touched. The separate loss of trace history across a restart (#12391) is not addressed here.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-spawn` is used across the workspace. The new macro arm is additive, and a call without `level` expands to the same two INFO records as before. `cargo check --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets` passes. In the gateway, anyone who counted connections from the per-connection INFO records now needs `--log-level debug` (or `RUST_LOG=debug`) to see them.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12476. Related #11901, Related #12391.

### What this does, simply

The runtime trace is the daemon's own record of what it did, kept on disk so you can look back after something goes wrong. Since v0.8.7, the gateway has written two trace entries for every HTTP connection it accepts: one when the connection's task starts and one when it ends. A dashboard polling through a proxy, or a health check, opens connections all day. Those entries then crowd out everything else. With the default trace settings (keep the newest 200 entries), 100 requests replace the whole trace.

This PR records those two per-connection entries at DEBUG instead of INFO. The daemon stores INFO and above by default, so they are no longer stored unless someone asks for debug logs. Tasks that run for a long time, such as the daemon's components, still record their start and end at INFO, and connection errors are still recorded as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. An A/B with a throwaway config dir takes a few minutes.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** the gateway's HTTP listener (`web`), driven with `curl` against `/health`. No `channel` is involved.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A throwaway config dir, so your own config and trace are not touched. Widening the trace window makes the counts exact (by default the trace keeps only the newest 200 entries):

  ```sh
  export ZC=$(mktemp -d)
  zeroclaw --config-dir "$ZC" config set observability.log_persistence_max_entries 5000 --no-interactive
  ```

- **Steps to run:**

  ```sh
  zeroclaw --config-dir "$ZC" daemon & pid=$!   # gateway on 127.0.0.1:42617
  sleep 5                                        # let the gateway start listening
  for i in $(seq 1 200); do curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:42617/health; done
  kill -INT "$pid"; wait "$pid"
  python3 - "$ZC/data/state/runtime-trace.jsonl" <<'EOF'
  import collections, json, sys
  c = collections.Counter()
  for line in open(sys.argv[1]):
      e = json.loads(line)
      a = e.get("attributes") or {}
      if a.get("task_site", "").startswith("crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/lib.rs"):
          c[(e["severity_text"], e["message"], a["task_site"])] += 1
  print(c.most_common())
  EOF
  ```

- **Expected on this branch (after):** `[]`: no lifecycle records from `ServeTasks::spawn`. Start the daemon with `zeroclaw --config-dir "$ZC" --log-level debug daemon` and they come back at DEBUG, one `task spawned` and one `task complete` per request, from `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/lib.rs:1082`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** 200 INFO `task spawned` and 200 INFO `task complete` from `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/lib.rs:1079`.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Required Gate (fmt, Clippy, workspace tests) on this PR's head. The local runs below cover the same commands for the two touched crates, plus a workspace check of every target, because `spawn!` expands in 11 crates.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none for the changed code. CI does not run a daemon and count trace records; the manual run below does.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Linux x86_64, rustc 1.98.0, at this branch's head, except where noted.

  The new test fails on `master` with the fix left out:

  ```text
  $ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib serve_tasks_record_their_lifecycle_below_info
  assertion `left == right` failed: a connection's or stream's task lifecycle must stay out of the INFO trace
    left: ["INFO task complete", "INFO task complete", "INFO task spawned", "INFO task spawned"]
   right: ["DEBUG task complete", "DEBUG task complete", "DEBUG task spawned", "DEBUG task spawned"]
  test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 916 filtered out
  ```

  With the fix:

  ```text
  $ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib serve_tasks_record_their_lifecycle_below_info
  test tests::serve_tasks_record_their_lifecycle_below_info ... ok
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 916 filtered out

  $ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-spawn
  test tests::spawn_records_its_lifecycle_at_info_unless_given_a_level ... ok
  test result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

  $ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway
  unittests src/lib.rs:        test result: ok. 916 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored
  tests/golden_frames.rs:      test result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed; 7 ignored
  tests/nodes_mdns.rs:         test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
  tests/relay_dashboard_ingress.rs: test result: ok. 8 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored

  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check
  (no output, exit 0)

  $ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-spawn -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings
  Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)   (0 warnings)

  $ RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --locked -p zeroclaw-spawn -p zeroclaw-gateway --no-deps
  Generated .../target/doc/zeroclaw_gateway/index.html and 1 other file

  $ cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets
  Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)   (0 warnings)
  ```

  rustfmt asked for one line break in the new `zeroclaw-spawn` test to be joined after the first run. The gateway tests, rustdoc and the workspace check ran on the head before that one-line test-only change. fmt, the `zeroclaw-spawn` tests and Clippy were run again after it.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** A daemon built from `master` and from this branch, each run in a fresh network namespace (loopback only) with a throwaway `HOME` and config dir, followed by the steps above:

  ```text
  master, default trace window, 100 requests:
    trace lines: 200 (the window is full)
       91 INFO task complete  crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/lib.rs:1079
       90 INFO task spawned   crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/lib.rs:1079
  master, window 5000, 200 requests:
    trace lines: 447
      200 INFO task spawned   crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/lib.rs:1079
      200 INFO task complete  crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/lib.rs:1079
  this branch, window 5000, 200 requests:
    trace lines: 47
    no records from crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/lib.rs; the daemon's other tasks still record at INFO
  this branch, default trace window, 100 requests:
    trace lines: 47, the same counts per site as above
  this branch, --log-level debug, 20 requests plus one malformed request:
       21 DEBUG task spawned   crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/lib.rs:1082
       21 DEBUG task complete  crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/lib.rs:1082
        1 DEBUG 'connection error from' (the malformed request, answered 400)
  ```

  Not verified: a TLS listener and a live HTTP/2 client in the daemon run. Both go through the same `ServeTasks::spawn` call, and the new gateway test drives the executor path that HTTP/2 streams use. Windows and macOS were not run; the change is a log level and has no platform-specific code.

- **Visual interface evidence:** `Exact plain-text output` (runtime-trace record counts above).

prs.title: fix(tools): bound agent-browser subprocess waits with a deadline and kill_on_drop
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Both `agent-browser` subprocess waits in `crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/browser.rs` were unbounded — the `--version` availability probe and the `run_command` executor awaited the CLI with no wall-clock deadline and no `kill_on_drop`. A wedged CLI (e.g. a page paused on a JavaScript `confirm`, see #9945) hung the agent turn indefinitely. Same defect class as #8560, whose fix covered only `browser_open`.
  - The availability probe now runs under a short fixed 5s deadline (it is a liveness check, deliberately not configurable) and reads as unavailable on timeout.
  - `run_command` is bounded by a new `browser.timeout_secs` config key (default 60), following the `timeout_secs` naming already used by `text_browser`, `http_request`, and `web_fetch`. The timeout error names the action and the config key, so a hung action is distinguishable from a hung probe. Both children are killed when the deadline passes or the awaiting future is dropped, mirroring the `browser_delegate` pattern the issue cites.
  - A zero value is rejected at use with the same style of error as the existing `browser.computer_use.timeout_ms` validation.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to the computer_use, rust_native, or browser_open paths; no change to which actions exist (the missing `dialog` action stays tracked in #9945); the CLI's own `--idle-timeout` flag (mentioned as a consideration in the issue) is not passed — that belongs with #9945's dialog work if wanted.
- **Blast radius:** `browser` tool on the `agent_browser` and `auto` backends; every action now has a 60s default ceiling where it previously could wait forever. Operators with legitimately slower actions can raise `browser.timeout_secs`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #9946. Related #8560, #9945.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `config`, `distinguished contributor`, `risk:high`, `runtime`, `size:M`, `tool`, `tool:browser`

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes — the issue's stub reproduction shows the delta directly.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (agent turn using the `browser` tool).
- **Setup / preconditions:** shadow the CLI with a stub that never returns:
  ```sh
  mkdir -p /tmp/ab-stub
  printf '#!/bin/sh\nsleep infinity\n' > /tmp/ab-stub/agent-browser
  chmod +x /tmp/ab-stub/agent-browser
  ```
  and configure `browser.backend = "agent_browser"`.
- **Steps to run:** with `PATH=/tmp/ab-stub:$PATH`, drive any agent turn that invokes the `browser` tool (e.g. an `open` action).
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the availability probe gives up after ~5s (backend reads unavailable / falls through per `auto` resolution); if the probe is satisfied and an action runs, it fails within `browser.timeout_secs` with `agent-browser 'open' timed out after 60s (browser.timeout_secs); the subprocess was killed`, and the stub process is gone afterwards.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the turn hangs indefinitely with the stub process still running.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** standard Rust fmt/clippy/test CI covers all three touched crates on the default feature set (none of the changed code is feature-gated).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the new subprocess tests are `#[cfg(unix)]` (mirroring the existing `browser_open` timeout tests); Windows only compiles them out. The Windows code path differs only in the binary name.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` — finished with no warnings.
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib browser` —
    ```
    test result: ok. 161 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1482 filtered out; finished in 0.74s
    ```
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib` —
    ```
    test result: ok. 1383 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 7.94s
    ```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** New unit tests cover: stalled probe times out (<2s wall clock) and reads unavailable; successful probe still reads available; missing binary reads unavailable; a stalled command errors naming both the action and `browser.timeout_secs` while killing the child; a completing command passes its output through; `timeout_secs = 0` is rejected. Config tests assert the serde default (60) and a round-trip of an explicit value. Not verified: a live `agent-browser` install (not present on this machine); the bounded wrapper is exercised by the tests above and the wrapped call sites are unchanged otherwise.
- **Visual interface changed?** `N/A`
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** none skipped.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`
- New external network calls? `No`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes` — with one behavioral bound: actions that previously ran longer than 60s (while the wait was unbounded) now need `browser.timeout_secs` raised.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `Yes` — new optional `browser.timeout_secs` key, default 60; existing configs need no action.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- Upgrade steps: none required; raise `browser.timeout_secs` only if agent-browser actions legitimately exceed 60s.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` of this PR's squash commit restores the unbounded waits.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `browser.timeout_secs` can be raised to effectively restore long waits without a revert.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** tool results containing `timed out after Ns (browser.timeout_secs); the subprocess was killed`, or the availability-probe debug log `agent-browser availability probe timed out`.
