prs.title: fix(mcp): evict poisoned connections instead of reusing them
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - One failed recovery attempt used to poison an MCP connection permanently. `RecoveryBarrier::poison()` sets a flag nothing clears, and `McpServer::health_check()` only asked the transport, which still answered `true`. Every later tool call on that server failed closed against a connection the rest of the system believed was healthy. `health_check()` now also reports poisoned recovery as unhealthy.
  - Region: the daemon's registry reconciliation (`health_check_all` → keep healthy, drop dead, reconnect) now sees the poisoned server as dead, drops it, and establishes a fresh connection instead of reusing a permanently failed one.
  - Remote MCP POSTs no longer follow redirects automatically. A 307/308 can arrive after the first server already received and executed the request; following it replays the JSON-RPC body against a second endpoint, so a `tools/call` with side effects could run twice. The original response is surfaced as an HTTP status instead.
  - A connect-stage failure restores the `REQUEST_PRE_WRITE` classification. A connect error proves nothing reached the server, so the request may be retried, instead of staying at "outcome unknown" and being blocked from ever retrying.
- **Scope boundary:** The poison flag itself is still never cleared — a poisoned server is evicted and re-established, not repaired in place. No change to retry/backoff policy, no second recovery attempt, no change to the stdio transport, no change to the TLS-CA loading path other than the redirect policy it shared.
- **Blast radius:** Remote HTTP/SSE MCP transports and MCP registry health reporting. The redirect policy is strictly narrower, so an MCP endpoint configured to rely on an https→https redirect now receives the redirect status instead of being followed.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #10807

### What this does, simply

When a remote MCP server blips — container restart, proxy reload, laptop sleep — ZeroClaw makes one reset-and-handshake attempt. If that attempt fails, the connection was marked unrecoverable forever, but nothing outside the connection knew: health checks still passed, so it stayed in rotation and every tool call on it failed from then on. This PR makes that state visible to the health check, so the dead connection is dropped and replaced by a fresh one.

Two related hazards came out of the same code path. A redirected POST could be re-sent to the new location after the original server had already acted on it, so a side-effecting tool could run twice — redirects are no longer followed. And a connection error that happened before any bytes were sent was being classified as "outcome unknown", which blocked safe retries; it is now classified as pre-write.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — the behavior is covered by unit tests in `zeroclaw-tools` plus required CI; no manual setup is needed.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `None`

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate` runs the workspace `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test`, which is exactly the surface this touches; `MSRV (declared floor)` confirms no toolchain-floor drift, and the platform build checks (incl. `Check x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) confirm the transport change compiles where `reqwest` picks a different TLS backend. All green on this head.
- **Commands run:** the workspace-wide fmt / clippy / test commands above, executed by the required CI gate on this head — I did not run additional commands beyond that.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Nothing beyond the tests below; the failures are exercised with in-process fake transports and `wiremock`, not against a live MCP server.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — no user-visible interface changed.

The tests added on this branch, by claim:

- `poisoned_recovery_is_reported_as_unhealthy_to_registry` — a server whose transport answers healthy but whose recovery is poisoned now reports unhealthy.
- `poisoned_http_recovery_is_evicted_without_replaying_unknown_tool` — after a failed background re-handshake, the registry reports the server unhealthy, `kill_dead_connections` evicts it, the registry empties, and the tool body was written exactly once (no replay).
- `http_post_redirect_is_not_followed_or_replayed` — a 307 pointing at a dead port is surfaced as `HTTP 307`, the mock received exactly one request, and the lifecycle is left neither `outcome_unknown` nor `pre_write`.
- `pre_write` classification on connect errors, and the existing HTTPS→HTTP redirect rejection updated to assert the original `HTTP 302` is reported rather than a post-follow failure.
- `cargo fmt` applied to the redirect regression test (`style(mcp)` commit) after a reviewer run flagged formatting.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`
- New external network calls? `No` — the opposite: automatic redirect following is removed, so an MCP POST can no longer reach a location the operator did not configure.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No` — session headers are applied exactly as before; they are not attached to a redirected request any more, because there is no redirected request.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No` — tool results are unchanged; what changed is whether a failed call can be retried and whether it can be replayed.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: —

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `No` — narrowly: an MCP server URL that relied on the client following an https→https redirect now returns that status to the caller.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: point the MCP server entry at the final endpoint URL instead of a redirecting one. Nothing else changes — the request that used to be replayed to the redirect target is now a normal non-2xx response the caller can inspect.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk PRs: `git revert <sha>` is the plan unless otherwise noted.

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the branch as a whole (the commits are independent and revert cleanly in reverse order).
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `None`
- **Observable failure symptoms:** after a revert, `MCP server <name> is unavailable: a prior request's outcome became unknown and recovery failed` reappears in logs after a single failed recovery and never goes away for that server; registry reconciliation keeps listing the server as healthy.

prs.title: fix(tools): enforce Act policy on send_message_to_peer
prs.body:
## Summary
`send_message_to_peer` could start another agent's turn (or post to an external peer) without consulting the sender's autonomy level or action budget. Sibling Act tools (`a2a_send`, `spawn_subagent`, `delegate`) already call `enforce_tool_operation(ToolOperation::Act, …)` at the start of `execute`.

This PR threads a `SecurityPolicy` into `SendMessageToPeerTool` (registration passes the turn's policy; convenience constructors derive via `SecurityPolicy::for_agent`) and refuses Act before any delivery path runs.

Fixes #12167

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib send_message_to_peer_denied_in_readonly_autonomy`
- [x] `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib send_message_to_peer_readonly_for_agent_creates_no_peer_inbox`
- [x] `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib send_message_to_peer_consumes_action_budget`


## Security & Privacy
No new permission, network call, secret handling, or personal data. The change closes an Act bypass: the tool now refuses to run when the sender's policy does not allow Act, before either the in-process inbox or the external announcement path.

## Compatibility
No config key, environment variable, or CLI flag changes. The tool refuses more calls than before, by design; callers that pass a policy keep the same behaviour for allowed Act.

## Rollback
Reverting this branch restores `SendMessageToPeerTool::new(config, alias)` without a policy and removes the Act check, which re-opens #12167. No data or config migration is involved, so the revert is a plain code revert.

## Fixture isolation
The three `tests/system/multi_agent_e2e.rs` fixtures now point `config_path` and `data_dir` at a `TempDir`, so `SecurityPolicy::for_agent` no longer creates `~/.zeroclaw/agents/<alias>/workspace` on the machine running `cargo test`. Verified by running `cargo test --test system multi_agent_e2e` with `HOME` pointed at an empty directory: on the previous head it creates `.zeroclaw/agents/alpha/workspace`, with the fix it creates nothing. Local runs: 5/5 in that file, 19/19 `send_message_to_peer` unit tests, `cargo fmt --check` clean.

prs.title: fix(cli): honour [gateway.tls] for local admin HTTP commands
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #12091

When `[gateway.tls] enabled = true`, CLI admin commands (`gateway get-paircode`, `sop pending|logs|approve|deny`, and `gateway restart`'s graceful `/admin/shutdown`) still built `http://…` URLs with `reqwest::Client::new()`, so they failed against a TLS-only listener and restart treated the gateway as absent.

### Changes

- `gateway_admin_url` takes `use_tls` and emits `https://` / `http://` accordingly; wildcard binds `0.0.0.0` / `::` rewrite to `127.0.0.1` / `::1` respectively for the outbound host.
- `gateway_admin_http_client` trusts only the PEM chain at `[gateway.tls].cert_path`: the webpki roots and the OS trust store are turned off for this client, so nothing the machine already trusts can stand in for the configured gateway (no silent plaintext fallback).
- Required `[gateway.tls.client_auth]` fails with an explicit error (CLI does not present a client certificate yet).
- Documented in `docs/book/src/gateway/api.md`.

## Tests

```sh
cargo test --locked --bin zeroclaw --features agent-runtime gateway_admin_
```

The original local run passed 6 tests, including `gateway_admin_shutdown_reaches_tls_listener`. On head `dd5ae50abc45bd306b77e108a4ddb89564d6fa01`, the [Linux Test job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41310037900/job/124858289004) passes all 12 gateway-admin helper tests and 3 CLI component tests, including real TLS listeners and refusal paths.


## Security & Privacy

Secrets handling: yes. `gateway get-paircode` sends the gateway admin token, so the peer identity matters more than for a normal outbound call.

Before this change the admin client was an ordinary `reqwest` client: `rustls-tls` plus the OS store from feature unification, and the configured PEM added as one more anchor. Any certificate those stores accepted for the host satisfied the connection, and a fullchain file installed its intermediates as anchors as well.

After this change the configured chain is the only source of trust for these three commands: `tls_built_in_webpki_certs(false)` and `tls_built_in_native_certs(false)` are set on this client only, so a public CA, the OS trust store, or a proxy cannot vouch for the gateway. Redirects stay refused and proxies stay cleared, so the token is not forwarded.

Residual, called out in review: the file is read as a chain, so a gateway certificate issued by a private CA trusts that CA for this host. See the reply on the review thread for why pinning only the first certificate breaks CA-issued gateway certificates in rustls.

## Compatibility

No config key, environment variable, or CLI flag changes. TLS-enabled gateways whose certificate chains to a CA in `cert_path` keep working; so do self-signed gateways. Setups that relied on the admin client accepting a certificate the machine trusts but `cert_path` does not contain now fail to verify, which is the intent.

## Rollback

Revert the branch: the admin commands fall back to `reqwest::Client::new()` over `http://`, which is the pre-#12091 behaviour against a TLS-only listener. No data, config, or credential migration is involved.

prs.title: fix(sop): use the fail-closed mode when the decision answers are unusable
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `resolve` in `sop/decision.rs` now treats the whole answer set as untrusted when the gate answer is missing or invalid, or when `modes` is non-empty and the mode answer is missing, rejected, or below `min_confidence`. In that case the run uses the fail-closed mode and every step runs; the per-step `decide` answers are discarded. Before, a valid-looking set of step answers was still applied next to an unusable gate or mode answer (#11124).
  - `fail_closed_mode` is now one `match` on the authored mode with explicit arms. `priority_based` is no longer reduced below its own gating; it goes to `step_by_step` only when `step_by_step` is listed in `modes`.
  - The rationale note "step answers ignored; every step runs" is written only when the run actually starts.
  - Docs (`decision-models.md`, `syntax.md`, and the `decide` description in `sop/mod.rs`) describe the fail-closed behavior.
- **Scope boundary:** no change to the engine (`engine.rs`), to routing, or to approval handling (see "Related, not fixed here"). No new config keys.
- **Blast radius:** SOPs with a `[decision]` table and `decide` steps, through `resolve` and `apply_decisions` (`dispatch.rs`). SOPs without `[decision]` are not touched.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11124

### What this does, simply

A decision model can answer a gate ("should this SOP start?"), a mode ("how much supervision?") and one yes/no question per step. If the gate or mode answer cannot be trusted, the SOP falls back to a strict mode. The reported bug: the step answers were still used in that case, so steps could be skipped while the run was already in the strict fallback. Now, when the gate or mode answer is unusable, none of the step answers is used and every step runs.

Behavior changes beyond the reported case, declared on purpose:

1. **Mode answer unusable, gate valid.** With `modes` set and the mode answer missing, rejected, or below `min_confidence`, step answers are now ignored too. Before, they were kept (checked in `resolve` at the base commit). This follows the same rule as the gate: one answer set, trusted as a whole or not at all.
2. **`priority_based` with `step_by_step` listed.** An invalid gate answer and the "model unavailable" path now give `step_by_step` instead of leaving the authored mode. It is stricter; the Safety section says so.
3. **Routing guards.** A `switch` whose ports all read `$.decisions` matches no port when the answers are ignored (an absent answer reads as false) and completes the run without its remaining steps. This already happened when the model was down; the fix adds the cases above. Routing is not changed. The docs now say it. No test exercises this consequence.

### Related, not fixed here

A different mechanism, found while reviewing this change and read in the code but not run: for a `supervised` SOP the only approval is tied to step 1 (`execution_mode_needs_approval`, `sop/engine.rs:7116-7118`), and a step skipped by a valid "no" answer is skipped before its approval gate (`skip_for_decision` at `sop/engine.rs:3145`, approval at `:3193`). So a valid "no" on a `decide` question in step 1 appears to leave the run with no approval. `decision-models.md` already says a skipped step never asks for approval. Here `resolve` works as intended and the gap is in the engine, so it is outside this PR's invariant (unusable answers never reduce supervision). I did not reproduce it, did not check whether a third party can influence the answer, and did not search for existing issues. Per-step `requires_confirmation` and checkpoints still gate.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — the behavior is covered by unit tests on `resolve` and by dispatch tests with a scripted decision model; no interface is involved.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust test and lint jobs cover `zeroclaw-runtime`; `Docs Style` and the link gate cover the changed Markdown.

prs.title: fix(security): refuse `zeroclaw estop` while no runtime path enforces it
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `zeroclaw estop` loaded `estop-state.json`, mutated it, and printed "Estop engaged." although nothing that runs the agent reads that file. Every form of the command now returns a not-enforced error and exits non-zero, so it no longer reports a stop that did not happen.
  - The `--help` text, the `zeroclaw status` line, the `EstopConfig` field docs, the security model, the YOLO comparison, the philosophy page, and the repo's agent skill no longer describe `estop` as halting anything.
  - The new error text is the Fluent key `cli-estop-not-enforced` in the five catalogs.
- **Scope boundary:** This does not implement emergency-stop enforcement: no daemon authority, no RPC, no dispatch gate, no in-flight cancellation, no network or domain enforcement. Those are the follow-up work tracked in the linked issues.
- **Blast radius:** The `zeroclaw estop` command, the `[security.estop]` config docs, the `cli-estop-*` and `cli-status-estop` catalog strings, and the docs and agent-skill pages that mention `estop`. Scripts that call `zeroclaw estop` now fail (see Compatibility).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9390, Related #9802. #9390 stays open: the enforcement it asks for is not implemented here.

### What this does, simply

`zeroclaw estop` is documented as the operator's emergency stop. In practice it only wrote a JSON state file and printed that the stop was engaged; no runtime path reads that file, so a running agent kept working and the operator had been told otherwise. Until enforcement exists, this PR makes the command refuse to run, with a message that says nothing was stopped and that stopping the ZeroClaw process is the way to halt the agent. The state file is no longer read or written by the command.

Unchanged: `[security.estop]` still parses and validates (an empty `state_file` is still rejected, `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/schema.rs:25327-25330`), and `EstopManager` stays in the runtime crate. It now has no caller and is marked `TODO(debt)` (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/security/estop.rs:64`), to be connected to the daemon authority when enforcement lands or removed.

Known leftovers, declared rather than hidden: nine Fluent keys in each catalog are now unused (`cli-estop-engaged`, `cli-estop-resume-done`, `cli-estop-status`, `cli-estop-domains`, `cli-estop-domains-none`, `cli-estop-tools`, `cli-estop-tools-none`, `cli-estop-updated-at`, `cli-otp-received`; see `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/locales/en/cli.ftl:934,1213-1256`). I left them so the enforcement work can reuse them; no CI gate flags unused keys.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, short.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli`
- **Setup / preconditions:** A config directory with `[security.estop]` set to `enabled = true`.
- **Steps to run:** `zeroclaw --config-dir <dir> estop`, then `estop status`, then `estop resume --network`; check each exit status and `<dir>/estop-state.json`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Each command prints "`zeroclaw estop` is not enforced: ..." on stderr, exits non-zero, and does not create or modify the state file.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** From reading `src/main.rs` at the base commit (not re-run on a `master` build): `estop` writes the state file and prints "Estop engaged.", and `estop status` prints the state and exits 0.

### How I tested

CI-equivalent checks run in WSL, tested on `55c80be5bacc80cb31fc88c4dedafd30016f9a91`, same tree as the head `bda01ac3c2405d3824d734b9481983b8222cc287` (only the commit message differs):

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check                      # rc=0
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh <changed .rs files>   # "Comment hygiene gate passed."
cargo test --bin zeroclaw estop                 # test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --test component estop               # test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --test architecture cli_fluent       # test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib i18n       # test result: ok. 49 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --test component config_schema       # test result: ok. 41 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib estop       # test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the required Rust test, lint, and docs jobs, for the workspace-wide and docs coverage I did not run locally.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None known for the changed surface. Not run locally: the full workspace tests, `scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh`, `scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh`, and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`. The last fails in `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/lib.rs:1121,1125`, files this PR does not touch; I did not compare against `master`.
- **Commands run and tail output:** see the block above; each line shows the `test result` tail.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - `tests/component/estop_cli.rs` runs the real `zeroclaw` binary on 13 argument forms, with `enabled = true` and `enabled = false`. It asserts a non-zero exit, the not-enforced message on stderr, no "Estop engaged" on stdout, an unchanged state file when one exists, and no state file created when none exists.
  - The unit tests in `src/main.rs` parse 15 argument forms through `Cli::try_parse_from` and check that `handle_estop_command` returns the catalog string.
  - `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/i18n.rs` checks the five new or rewritten keys in every catalog: present, translated, and saying the command is not enforced.
  - The claim "no running agent, daemon, or tool reads the estop state file" rests on a search of the workspace with a pattern calibrated against the removed call site in `src/main.rs`. Outside `estop.rs`, only the re-export in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/security/mod.rs:49` and the write-protection by file name in `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/policy.rs:5416` match. I did not search third-party plugins or dependencies.
  - Not verified: how the translations read to native speakers, the on-screen layout of `zeroclaw status` and `zeroclaw --help`, and the behavior on Windows or macOS.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `Exact plain-text output`: a deterministic, unstyled stderr message. No presentation-sensitive claim.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `55c80be5bacc80cb31fc88c4dedafd30016f9a91` (same tree as the head `bda01ac3c2405d3824d734b9481983b8222cc287`; only the commit message differs), `cli`, `tests/component/estop_cli.rs`; locale `en`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** the message text is the `en` value of `cli-estop-not-enforced` in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/locales/en/cli.ftl`.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** `zeroclaw estop <any form>` -> non-zero exit, not-enforced message, state file untouched.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The full workspace test and `-D warnings` clippy were skipped because they exceed this machine's memory budget and clippy already fails outside the touched files.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No` (the command stops reading and writing a file).
- New external network calls? `No`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No` (the OTP prompt on `estop resume` is no longer reached; `--otp` is accepted and ignored)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No` (the only model-visible text changed is the in-repo agent skill, which is trusted repository content; it now tells the agent not to offer `estop` as a way to halt it)
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The security effect is the removal of a false assurance: operators can no longer be told a stop was engaged when nothing stopped.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `No`
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `Yes` (CLI behavior only: no command or flag is removed or renamed; config keys still parse)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- Upgrade steps for existing users:
  - Scripts or runbooks that call `zeroclaw estop`, `estop status`, or `estop resume` will now get a non-zero exit and the not-enforced message. With `enabled = true`, `estop status` previously exited 0; with `enabled = false` every form already failed, with a different message.
  - To halt the agent, stop the ZeroClaw process (service manager, `SIGTERM`, or the process itself). That is the only halt that works today.
  - An existing `estop-state.json` is ignored by the runtime. It can be left in place or deleted.
  - `[security.estop]` keys (`enabled`, `state_file`, `require_otp_to_resume`) remain accepted but are documented as not enforced.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk surface; `git revert <sha>` restores the previous behavior.

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <merge or commit sha>`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Operators or scripts report "`zeroclaw estop` is not enforced" on stderr with a non-zero exit.

prs.title: fix(plugins): enforce aggregate store allocation budgets
prs.body:
## Summary

- Bound the sum of linear memory bytes and table elements across each plugin store. The previous Wasmtime limits applied the configured amount separately to every memory and table.
- Keep multiple memories and tables supported, preserve the configured instance limit, and retain allocation accounting across warm-store calls.
- Cover initial allocations, guest growth, multiple instances, independent stores, and failed-growth accounting; the existing refueling tests cover execution fuel.

**Base branch:** `master`

**Scope boundary:** Guest linear memory and table-element allocations. Host allocations, Wasmtime bookkeeping, virtual address reservations, fuel, deadlines, and resource-count defaults retain their existing behavior.

**Blast radius:** Tool, channel, and memory plugins share this store constructor.

Closes #12145.

### What this does, simply

A component can contain several memories and tables. Previously, each could grow to the operator's entire store budget. This change makes them share that budget, including their initial allocations. Running another export restores execution fuel but does not restore allocation quota. Reservations remain charged if the underlying allocator subsequently fails, because Wasmtime's failure callbacks cannot reliably identify a reservation to refund.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The automated component regressions exercise actual store construction, instantiation, and exported growth with tiny budgets.

### How I tested

The reproduction used a component containing two one-page memories and two two-element tables. Before the repair, the second memory and table could grow past their store-wide budgets, and over-budget initial allocations succeeded. The same regression checks now reject those allocations while allowing growth within the budget.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Current-head required CI passes. The local checks below cover the owning crate and its component adapters.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None identified for the repaired shared limiter. Local execution used Linux and Cranelift.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```text
  cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib
  test component::tests::store_resource_budget_includes_initial_allocations ... ok
  test component::tests::store_resource_budget_spans_tables ... ok
  test component::tests::store_resource_budget_spans_memories ... ok
  test component::tests::store_resource_budget_spans_instances_but_not_stores ... ok

  cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --tests --examples
  test tests::sign_payload_records_digest_and_verifies_with_strict_host_policy ... ok
  test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.00s

  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --all-targets -- -D warnings
  Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 28.85s

  cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --features plugins-wasmtime
  Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 13.45s

  cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --features plugins-wasm-pulley
  Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 10.88s
  ```

  Workspace formatting passed with `cargo fmt --all -- --check`. Full-file documentation lint for the changed protocol page reported `Summary: 0 error(s)`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** No manual or live-service test was needed. Automated fixtures exercise supported tool, channel, and memory components.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A, no visual interface changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Patch based on `683d10139bc2`, plugin component execution through `new_store` and the component linker. Regression tests are in `crates/zeroclaw-plugins/src/component.rs` and `component_limits.rs`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Instantiation rejects aggregate initial allocations above the cap. Exported growth returns failure above the aggregate cap. Allowed growth still succeeds.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace tests are outside the affected crate. No external service is required for the selected fixtures.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.

The existing plugin resource boundary now enforces aggregate allocation budgets. This reduces the availability risk from a component multiplying its allowed allocation across many memories or tables.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Plugins within the documented store-wide limits remain compatible. Components that previously exceeded those totals can now fail instantiation or growth.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: No migration. Operators who intentionally need larger aggregate guest allocations can increase the existing `plugins.limits.max_memory_mb` or `max_table_elements` settings. Underlying allocator failures conservatively consume reserved quota until the store is replaced.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the merge commit.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** No new toggle. Existing plugin limits remain configurable.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Components exceeding aggregate limits fail instantiation with Wasmtime memory/table limit errors, or receive failed growth results during exports.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A.

prs.title: fix(install): verify Windows prebuilt release checksums
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`, at `b28d1c3de99099fd565cdedd4d80d8cff7f6a855`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Resolve one release tag, then download the Windows archive and `SHA256SUMS` from that tag. Require one exact asset entry and a matching SHA256 before extraction.
  - Use one PowerShell helper for `setup.bat --prebuilt` and the generated Windows guide. Missing, malformed, duplicate or mismatched checksums stop installation. A failed download also stops this mode.
  - Add offline tests under PowerShell 5.1 and 7 to the existing required Windows job. Helper-only changes now select that job.
  - Set the bundled helper process execution policy explicitly so the batch entrypoint works when the inherited policy is Restricted. User/machine policy settings are unchanged; organizational Group Policy still takes precedence.
- **Scope boundary:** Windows x86_64 prebuilt installation only. No change to Unix installers, release publishing, signing, PATH policy or the existing Rust prerequisite check in `setup.bat`.
- **Blast radius:** The Windows batch entrypoint, its shared helper, the generated PowerShell guide and Windows CI selection.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12122.

### What this does, simply

The Windows installers currently extract a downloaded archive without checking its release checksum. This checks the checksum first. If it fails, the archive is not extracted and the existing install is left alone. Both files come from the same resolved release, so a change to `latest` between requests cannot mix releases.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A for additional manual checksum testing: the checked-in offline fixtures exercise the hash and extraction path, the complete documented failure path and the real batch entrypoint. A live release installation and binary startup are not claimed.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Current-head [run 41359345404](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41359345404) passes [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41359345404/job/125008855004), [Security](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41359345404/job/125006156219), [Installer Drift](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41359345404/job/125006156522) and the [required Windows job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41359345404/job/125006301814). Both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and 7 checksum steps pass in that job. Test, Lint, targeted Windows Clippy and Docs Style pass. The Windows log confirms the real batch fixture passes under inherited Restricted policy in both steps. This covers the original true-rebased repair and the two-file launch correction.

- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The full generator and required Windows checks pass on this corrected head. The checksum suites use synthetic archives and mocked downloads, including the Restricted-policy launch case. They do not run an installed ZeroClaw binary, persist a user PATH change, or reproduce organization-enforced Group Policy/App Control.

- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
powershell.exe -NoProfile -File scripts/ci/windows_prebuilt.test.ps1
pwsh.exe -NoProfile -File scripts/ci/windows_prebuilt.test.ps1
# Each shell:
PASS setup.bat --prebuilt under Restricted policy: checksum mismatch, exit 1, no extraction, source fallback or PATH write
PASS 22 checksum cases, explicit tag and 3 invalid tags; all network calls mocked

bash scripts/ci/windows_test_scope.test.sh
Required Windows package ownership: pass
Required Windows gate consistency: pass
windows test scope contract tests: pass

rustfmt --edition 2024 --check xtask/src/generate/docs.rs
git diff --check
bash -n install.sh
# exit 0

bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
Summary: 0 error(s)
```

  The link gate's six unit tests and changed-link collector passed under Linux. No invalid local targets were found. Optional `lychee` validation was unavailable. The repository comment-hygiene filter passed on the changed supported source files.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Two adversarial passes checked same-tag URLs, exact and duplicate manifest entries, fail-before-extraction behavior, temporary-file cleanup, batch error propagation, generator/helper parity and CI selection. Two disposable mutation controls failed as intended: removing the hash comparison and changing the archive URL back to `latest`. The October 31 release inventory listed both the Windows archive and `SHA256SUMS`; neither asset was executed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text output. No layout or rendering change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 8c7dd665ca80f1c7eddd6e549381bf113bba7278; Windows, PowerShell 5.1 and 7, scripts/ci/windows_prebuilt.test.ps1. Both complete checksum suites and the revised actual-batch case pass. The test failed before the launch correction with running scripts disabled; it now reaches checksum refusal and returns 1 without installation side effects. Other selector/generator/source controls above ran at the preceding rebased commit, whose helper, generator and CI-selection code are unchanged.

- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** The output above includes the observed batch failure and fixture results. The helper prints `SHA256 verified: zeroclaw-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip (v1.2.3)` for a valid synthetic archive.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** A valid archive replaces the fixture payload. Corrupt or unverifiable input leaves the existing fixture unchanged, removes temporary downloads and stops before PATH or Quickstart. The batch process returns 1.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The full workspace generator, Cargo tests and Clippy were not duplicated locally in the sparse source checkout; the current-head hosted Installer Drift, Test, Lint and required Windows checks supply that evidence. Earlier Linux link tests and changed-link collection remain historical evidence for unchanged links; optional `lychee` validation was unavailable. No live installation or new private CI job was run.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No new file-system scope.** The helper uses process-only `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass`; it does not modify user/machine execution-policy settings or override organizational Group Policy. Downloads use a unique temporary directory; the install destination is unchanged. [Execution-policy scopes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_execution_policies?view=powershell-5.1).
- New external network calls? **Yes.** Both routes fetch the manifest. The batch route resolves the release through the public GitHub API instead of the previous `gh`/mutable-URL fallback. Asset URLs use one validated version tag.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.** No credentials are required or added.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No.**
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Downloads stay on the existing GitHub release boundary. Missing or invalid verification data fails closed. A checksum is not a signature: this does not protect against an attacker who can replace both the archive and its manifest.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No for the former automatic fallback and standalone copies of `setup.bat`.** Valid prebuilt archives install as before.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No new installer flags or application configuration.**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- Exact upgrade steps: Keep `setup.bat` with `scripts/install_windows_prebuilt.ps1` from the same checkout or unpacked source archive, or use the self-contained PowerShell guide. If a prebuilt download or checksum fails, select `--dist` explicitly to build from source. The existing `setup.bat` Rust prerequisite is unchanged.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the landed commit through a reviewed PR. This restores the unverified Windows extraction paths; use a source build while a replacement fix is reviewed.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `SHA256 mismatch`, a missing/invalid `SHA256SUMS` entry, a download error or a missing helper causes an error before installation. `setup.bat` prints `Setup failed` and returns 1.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A. This does not supersede another PR.

prs.title: fix(tools): inherit headless SOP step scope on peer-send turns
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `send_message_to_peer`'s in-process delivery path starts the recipient turn in a detached `zeroclaw_spawn::spawn!` task.
  - Task-locals (including the active headless SOP step scope) do not cross that spawn, so the recipient rebuilt its full tool surface and escaped the step's capability boundary.
  - Capture `active_headless_step_scope()` before spawn and restore it with `with_inherited_headless_step_scope`, matching `delegate` and `spawn_subagent`.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change Act/autonomy checks on the sender, external-peer delivery, or live (non-headless) SOP step scope publishing.
- **Blast radius:** Recipient turns started from a scoped headless step now see the step's tool exclusions; unscoped / non-headless peer sends are unchanged (`None` inherits as a no-op).
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12169

### What this does, simply

When a headless SOP step is only allowed to message a peer, calling `send_message_to_peer` must not give the peer agent the whole tool list. The step's limit was kept in a task-local; the peer turn runs in a new task that never saw that limit. This PR copies the limit into the peer turn the same way `delegate` and `spawn_subagent` already do for the work they start.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — lib regression covers the tool/provider boundary offline.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** N/A
- **Setup / preconditions:** N/A
- **Steps to run:** N/A
- **Expected on this branch (after):** N/A
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** N/A

### How I tested

Focused lib test drives `execute()` inside an enforced headless step scope (`allow = [send_message_to_peer]`), with a local OpenAI-compatible mock that records the recipient's first request body. Asserts the offered tools are only `send_message_to_peer`.

```sh
CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --locked -j 2 \
  peer_turn_started_inside_headless_step_keeps_step_tool_scope -- --test-threads=1
# test tools::send_message_to_peer::tests::peer_turn_started_inside_headless_step_keeps_step_tool_scope ... ok
# test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; ... 5902 filtered out
```

Comment hygiene: `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/send_message_to_peer.rs` passed.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Lint / Format / unit tests for `zeroclaw-runtime`
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No full headless SOP cron run was performed; the focused test covers the tool-to-recipient provider boundary
- **Commands run and tail output:** see above
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Did not run a full headless SOP cron end-to-end; tool-level path matches the issue repro
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** local lib test on this branch
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** full workspace `cargo test` / clippy not re-run locally (focused lib test + CI)

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)
- New external network calls? (`No`)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`No`)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (`No`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation:

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (`Yes` — restores the documented step-boundary promise for peer turns)

prs.title: fix(tools): require read access before uploads and edits
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`, at `b28d1c3de99099fd565cdedd4d80d8cff7f6a855`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Require the existing read-policy check before `file_upload` or `file_upload_bundle` reads a file for its configured HTTP endpoint. A write-only sibling grant no longer permits uploads; a read grant now suffices.
  - Require read access before `file_edit` opens the existing target. Its existing write check remains. Denied edits cannot reveal match counts or indentation diagnostics.
  - Add permission-matrix and loopback HTTP regressions. Confirm that `file_write` still permits a write-only deposit. Document the contract.
- **Scope boundary:** Five files; no policy state, dependencies, schema, tool registration or transport changes. This does not add descriptor-based race hardening or change hard-link handling.
- **Blast radius:** Uploads and edits under per-agent file grants. The existing `SecurityPolicy` remains the source of truth.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12144. Related #11997; this does not replace its separate `send_via` work. Includes the merged #12129 Security-gate dependency repair through the true rebase.

### What this does, simply

A write-only grant lets one agent leave files for another without reading that agent's existing files. These three tools used the write permission to authorize operations that read content. This repair checks read permission before that content is opened. Uploads require read access; edits require both read and write access. A plain file deposit still needs only write access.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. Independent Core Team/CODEOWNER security review remains required before merge. Current-head native Linux CI executes all four access-tier regressions, including the Unix symlink case.

- **Interface(s) exercised:** The production tool API (`Tool::execute`) and a loopback HTTP upload endpoint. No `web`, `tui`, `cli` or messaging `channel` attribution is claimed by this test harness.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A supported Rust toolchain and the normal test dependencies. Fixtures create isolated workspaces, synthetic content and loopback servers; no provider credentials or external destination are needed.
- **Steps to run:** Run the two commands below. For A/B verification, copy only `crates/zeroclaw-tools/tests/file_access_tiers.rs` into a clean checkout of the base revision and run the first command there with production files unchanged.

  ```sh
  cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --test file_access_tiers -- --nocapture
  cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib file_ -- --nocapture
  ```

- **Expected on this branch (after):** Three tests pass on Windows; Unix also runs the symlink case. Write-only uploads make no HTTP request. Edit attempts return the same policy denial for exact, absent, repeated and indentation-only matches. The file stays unchanged. Read-capable uploads and read/write edits succeed; write-only deposits still succeed.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Historical Windows execution against base 1c1cd118ac536a1dd1bc79b9cce69cbdc04e4f29 gave one pass and two failures: a write-only upload sent the file, and a write-only edit changed it. The separate bundle-only negative control also detected the missing read guard. Those controls were not rerun on the current base.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Current-head [run 41358936353](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41358936353) passes [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41358936353/job/125007642064), [Security](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41358936353/job/125004913334), [Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41358936353/job/125004913544) and [Lint](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41358936353/job/125004913539). I checked the Test log: all four file_access_tiers regressions pass, including the native Unix symlink case, as do 122 existing file-tool tests. The checkout merges this head into b28d1c3de99099fd565cdedd4d80d8cff7f6a855; merge snapshot 49c0aa0396269f1b83f248706bd98da58196578b. The one-commit range-diff is unchanged. Two independent Core security approvals remain required.

- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Current-head Linux Test covers the access-tier matrix and Unix symlink regression. Windows Application Control blocked the local test executable after compilation; zero local tests ran on this head. The earlier Windows execution and mutation controls below remain historical evidence for the unchanged patch. No live-agent, external upload or full OIDC acceptance run is claimed.

- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```text
  cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-tools --test file_access_tiers -- --nocapture
      Finished test profile
      Running tests/file_access_tiers.rs
  could not execute process ... (never executed)
  An Application Control policy has blocked this file. (os error 4551)

  cargo clippy --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
  # package scope; exit 0
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
  git diff --check
  # exit 0
  npx --offline markdownlint-cli2@0.20.0 docs/book/src/agents/internals.md
  Summary: 0 error(s)
  ```

  Two warnings come from unchanged Windows-gated config fields, `DockerRuntime.resolved_launcher` and `NativeRuntime.resolved_shell`. Their definitions and platform gates match the base; no suppression is added.

  Historical execution on 28ab00fb521abe14719bb82e978c4adde9b0f05b: the Windows access-tier suite passed three tests; the existing file suite passed 125 tests. The unpatched baseline failed two of the three regressions. Restoring only the bundle's old write guard made the upload regression fail; source was restored afterward. That unchanged-patch control was not rerun after the current Windows execution block.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Two adversarial source passes traced canonical policy, registry wrappers, grant unions, reads and final network/file effects. A denied later bundle item must produce zero requests; write-only edit refusal precedes content diagnostics; read-only uploads and write-only file deposits remain valid controls. No new policy state is added. No live agent, provider or external upload was run, and no full OIDC acceptance is claimed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A: file authorization at the tool API; no renderer, layout or focus behavior changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 5c82d3d2e3aef1a0deeb9f3c6086f72008d2ecbd; production tools and `crates/zeroclaw-tools/tests/file_access_tiers.rs`. Current local evidence is compilation and static checks; execution is blocked as recorded above. Historical executed controls are identified separately.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Relevant current command output and historical execution counts are above. The checked-in regressions record loopback requests and verify returned denials and unchanged file content.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Current-head hosted fixtures verify that write-only grants produce zero upload requests and no content-derived edit diagnostic. Read grants allow uploads, combined read/write grants allow edits, and write-only file deposits remain supported. A denied later bundle item sends no partial upload; a workspace symlink does not grant read access to its write-only target.

- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** After Windows Application Control refused the test executable, I did not run the broader local suite or a fresh mutation control. Current-head upstream Linux Test supplies the executed regression and workspace evidence. No policy bypass, extra private CI job, live-agent test or external upload was run. macOS runtime execution and independent security review remain outside the completed validation. No new documentation links were added.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes, a correction to access scope:** read-only grants now allow these read-side uploads, while write-only grants no longer allow uploads or edits. The configured endpoint and network policy remain unchanged. Tests assert both allowed and denied effects.
- New external network calls? **No.** The existing upload calls are gated before reading; regressions use loopback only.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.** No new credential path. The repair prevents these tools from reading content under a write-only grant.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** Fixtures are synthetic.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No.** The new refusal reuses the existing policy diagnostic and exposes no file contents.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: The access-scope change is explicit above. Existing deployments that relied on the incorrect write-only behavior must grant read access deliberately; the repair does not infer it.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No** for callers that used write-only grants to upload or edit; that behavior is the defect being removed. Read-only uploads now work.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No.** Existing grant values are reused.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- Exact upgrade steps: Keep `Write` for deposit-only workflows and use `file_write`. If an agent must inspect and edit a sibling's files, change that sibling grant to `ReadWrite` after reviewing the trust boundary. Use `Read` when only reading/uploading is intended. Do not broaden unrelated grants.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this change's landed commit through a reviewed PR. This restores the reported read leak, so prefer a targeted correction if a regression appears.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None added. Existing per-agent `Read`, `Write` and `ReadWrite` grants control intended access.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Upload/edit tools return `Resolved path escapes workspace allowlist` for a write-only sibling. That is expected after this repair; failures with a correct read/read-write grant would be a regression. The tool result must contain no content-derived edit diagnostic on denial.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A. No PR is superseded and no contributor branch is modified.

prs.title: fix(mcp): confine SSE endpoints and redirects to the server origin
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Validate each resolved SSE message endpoint before a write starts. A server can no longer send configured headers or JSON-RPC content to another origin through an endpoint event.
- Bind SSE GET and POST redirects to the same origin. Reject URL credentials and report sanitized origins without query strings or userinfo.
- **Scope boundary:** SSE transport destination validation and its documentation. HTTP transport, stdio, CA trust, tool authorization, DNS pinning and gateway admin authorization retain their existing behavior.
- **Blast radius:** Remote MCP servers configured with `transport = "sse"`. Same-origin relative/absolute endpoints and redirects remain supported.
- Fixes #12146. #12129 merged as f87368a6aa53d16b0bd7411b002331a22622c2a7. This branch now contains that dependency repair through a single true rebase onto master 4c9edcf33716381b2c3455649cbd0f3e6b3a38b1; its two-file patch is unchanged.

### What this does, simply

An MCP server can tell the client where to send its next message. The client now checks that address against the server URL the operator configured. A different scheme, host or effective port is refused. HTTP redirects cannot bypass this check. The refusal happens before credentials or content reach the other destination.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Local HTTP fixtures exercise the production transport and record requests at the destination; no real server or credential is needed. The commands below run these checks.

### How I tested

Rebased revision: d8199da11070690344d3ca3e0e0d02ec638d979a. Fresh local validation on Windows x86-64, Rust 1.97.1, 2026-11-01. Exactly one own commit, with parent 4c9edcf33716381b2c3455649cbd0f3e6b3a38b1. `git range-diff` reports the original repair and this rebased commit as equivalent. No source edits followed validation.

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib mcp_transport::tests::
87 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored

cargo fmt --all -- --check
exit 0

cargo clippy --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
exit 0 (no tools-crate warnings)

npx --yes markdownlint-cli2@0.20.0 docs/book/src/tools/mcp.md
Summary: 0 error(s)
```

The changed-link collector also passed: zero added links in the edited document. Test/dev debug info and incremental compilation were disabled; builds used two jobs.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** On d8199da11070690344d3ca3e0e0d02ec638d979a, [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41262135860/job/124719523203) and [Security](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41262135860/job/124717381898) pass. [Run 41262135860](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41262135860) also passes Test, Lint, MSRV, Linux build, Windows compilation and targeted Clippy, macOS compilation, Docs Style and Installer Drift. Path-gated skips are not runtime execution evidence. The old b09f760f72 run is historical evidence only. Independent Core Team/CODEOWNER security review remains required; reviewers have been requested.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The hosted required gate is complete and passes; independent security review remains pending. The local tests use loopback HTTP fixtures; no live external MCP service or native macOS execution was performed. A macOS compile job does not establish runtime execution.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Two adversarial self-review passes and a final reread covered endpoint-to-write ordering, redirects, URL normalization, error privacy, the constructor policy and non-SSE compatibility. The checks happen before headers, pending-sender registration and the write outcome marker. These passes are not independent approval. Historical negative control on b09f760f72: removing the two new guards made both capture tests fail because a foreign server received a request; restoring them passed all 87 tests. That mutation control was not repeated on the unchanged rebased patch; the 87-test result above is fresh on this head.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No CLI, TUI or web rendering or interaction code changed; the network boundary is exercised directly.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** The revision above; `SharedMcpTransportConn::send_and_recv` through real loopback HTTP servers, with synthetic `Authorization` and `X-Api-Key` headers. Tests are in `mcp_transport.rs`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Test summaries above. Five new tests cover origin rules, refused endpoint/redirect destinations, and accepted same-origin endpoint/redirect controls.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Foreign destinations received zero requests with the fix. Accepted destinations received the configured headers and returned the JSON-RPC result. Refused endpoints left no pending sender or post-write outcome marker.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No full workspace or live-service run; the focused transport module includes existing TLS, cancellation, fallback and response-limit controls. The locked test run fetched missing cached dependencies; Clippy then used offline resolution.

Two existing Windows warnings remain in unchanged `zeroclaw-config` files: `resolved_launcher` in `platform/docker.rs` and `resolved_shell` in `platform/native.rs`. Their reads are Unix-only. No warning suppression was added.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No.**
- New external network calls? **No.**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** SSE credentials and payloads stay on the configured origin. Redirects receive the same check; URLs with credentials are refused. Errors name only sanitized origins.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No.** This validates server-controlled transport metadata.

This changes a network credential boundary. Independent Core Team/CODEOWNER security review is required; this submission is not self-approval.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No** for servers that advertise another origin or use URL credentials. Same-origin endpoints and redirects remain supported.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No.**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- **Upgrade steps:** Serve the message endpoint through the configured origin. Put authentication in `headers` instead of URL userinfo. An origin check does not restrict the initial configured destination or pin its DNS addresses.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert d8199da11070690344d3ca3e0e0d02ec638d979a`. This restores the unsafe cross-origin behavior; prefer correcting the server endpoint.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A server with an incompatible endpoint or redirect has an error chain containing `MCP SSE endpoint must use the configured server origin ...`. The error identifies both origins and omits URL credentials and query strings.

prs.title: fix(gateway): treat forwarded loopback as non-local for SOP cancel
prs.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #12114 for #12280: `authorize_sop_cancel` used `forwarded_client_ip` and treated a loopback result as local, so a trusted forwarded `127.0.0.1` (loopback peer or remote peer) could cancel without pairing. The rate-limit path already refused that case.

- Add `request_is_local`, defined as the rate-limit key being a loopback address (`client_key_from_request` + `is_loopback_key`), so the two locality decisions cannot drift.
- Use it in `authorize_sop_cancel` when pairing is off.
- Direct loopback with no forwarded header still cancels without pairing.

Fixes #12280

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib request_is_local_matches_rate_limit_loopback_exemption`
- [x] `authoring_cancel_rejects_forwarded_loopback_with_loopback_peer`

- CSP still admits `cdn.jsdelivr.net` and `'unsafe-inline'` for the Scalar explorer; dropping `'unsafe-inline'` / vendoring the bundle is left for a follow-up if maintainers want a stricter policy.

prs.title: docs(adr): propose daemon-held OIDC refresh and Okta/Entra ID support in ADR-017
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Amends proposed ADR-017 with a decision for **device-session continuity**: the daemon holds the IdP refresh token as a sealed *refresh grant* keyed by provider alias + ledger `device_id`; a pre-auth RPC authorized by the device's mTLS certificate (admitted like `cert/renew`) refreshes it, verifies the new access token through the same `oidc.<alias>` provider and same `sub`, and returns only the access token for an ordinary `initialize`. Today a Zerocode session cannot outlive one access token: the gateway discards the refresh token and Zerocode replays the login-time token on every reconnect, so sleep/resume past `exp` ends in `-32010`.
  - Adds a decision for **Okta and Entra ID** (required for v1.0). Neither issues RFC 9068 tokens: Okta access tokens have no `typ` and use `cid`; Entra uses `typ: JWT`, `uti` instead of `jti`, and has no introspection endpoint. The amendment keeps token-purpose separation by requiring audience ≠ every configured client_id when `typ: at+jwt` is absent (an ID token's `aud` is always its client), and admits vendor claim spellings only as named, tested compatibility rules (precedent: the Keycloak `azp` rule). Device-grant scopes become per-provider so Entra can request the API scope that sets the audience.
  - Adds matching acceptance gates (sleep/wake + rotation/revocation tests; real-tenant Okta and Entra verification), consequences (daemon now holds long-lived IdP secrets; partially deployment-side audience invariant; Entra revocation bounded by token lifetime + refresh interval), and standards/vendor references. Updates the ADR index gate summary.
- **Scope boundary:** Docs only. No code, config schema, or behavior changes. Browser dashboard stays refresh-free. Existing docs describing current behavior (`zerocode/remote.md` "no refresh-token cache") are left alone until the implementation lands.
- **Blast radius:** None at runtime. Constrains future work in `auth_provider/oidc.rs`, `auth_provider/enrollment.rs`, `cert_ledger.rs`, RPC dispatch pre-auth methods, and Zerocode's connection/auth path.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8289

### What this does, simply

Signing in to ZeroClaw from Zerocode through an identity provider currently lasts only as long as one access token, often minutes to an hour. If your laptop sleeps longer than that, the session can't resume and you have to restart and sign in again, even though your identity provider would happily keep you signed in. This records the plan to fix that: the daemon keeps the provider's refresh token (never your laptop), and your device certificate lets Zerocode quietly ask the daemon for a fresh token.

It also records how ZeroClaw will accept Okta and Entra ID tokens. Their access tokens are shaped differently from what the verifier accepts today, so Entra cannot sign in at all and Okta only works through introspection. The plan accepts their formats without weakening the check that stops an ID token being used as an access token.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Docs-only ADR amendment with no behavior change.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Docs style and link checks cover the two changed Markdown files.

Token formats were checked against the Microsoft Entra access-token claims reference and Okta's OIDC overview. Not verified: behavior against real Okta or Entra tenants (now an acceptance gate).

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Carry the existing opted-in runtime-profile thinking level with each request, independently of native token budgets, so two profiles sharing an OpenAI alias can select different reasoning efforts.
  - Resolve the neutral level against the actual selected OpenAI model, API, tool mode and public/subscription capability set, including fallback attempts and lazy streams.
  - Preserve the selected level across existing runtime adapters and disable response-cache reuse for explicit native-thinking overrides; document precedence, capability fallbacks and Rust source migration.
- **Scope boundary:** OpenAI Responses, native Chat Completions and the existing Codex subscription path. No new configuration key, global `runtime.reasoning_effort` values, authentication path, compatibility retry, provider family or runtime subsystem. Other providers keep their existing native budgets and wire behavior. Approval and dispatch authority, receipt/observer-event formats, history handling and cancellation semantics are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** Public Rust request construction, runtime CLI/channel/Agent/RPC/delegate request propagation, routing and recovery, streaming/tool rounds, and response-cache eligibility. This requires cross-owner review and the separate runtime exception before merge.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12054. Depends on #12057. Related #10705 concerns accepting literal global `max`, which this PR does not implement.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12054
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12057
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10705

### What this does, simply

A profile could change thinking prompts or temperature while OpenAI's native reasoning effort still came from global provider options. The native Chat Completions path also lacked profile-derived effort. With `native_thinking = true`, a turn now carries the selected level to the actual OpenAI model making that request. Inline override takes precedence over session override, then the profile default; direct Agent/RPC sessions use their profile default.

`off` becomes `none` when supported, otherwise the lowest supported effort. `minimal`, `low`, `medium` and `high` use the matching effort, or the next higher supported effort capped at the maximum. `max` selects the model's highest supported effort. Public API and subscription capabilities stay separate. Unknown models and API/tool combinations absent from the capability table retain existing global/default behavior and emit an explanatory diagnostic. The GPT-5.x Chat Completions-with-tools entries are inferred from separately documented capabilities rather than verified by a live request; the remaining rejection risk is described under Testing.

The level survives tool rounds, max-iteration summaries, request rebuilding, recovery, fallback model changes and deferred streams. Independent delegates use their own profiles; bounded delegates inherit their caller's level. Legacy auxiliary one-shot requests keep their existing behavior. Existing raw-body overrides in Azure, custom and other compatible adapters retain their precedence.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: automated mock HTTP regressions exercise the real CLI/channel/Agent/delegate paths and assert outgoing efforts; judging model answers manually would not verify the wire setting. The real CLI regression is reproducible with `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib agent::loop_::tests::native_thinking_cli_profiles_override_global_effort_on_the_shared_endpoint -- --exact`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? Yes: bypassing response-cache reuse for an explicit native-thinking override can issue an existing model request where a cached result was previously returned. Requests use the same configured endpoints and authentication; tests use local mock servers.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No: existing thinking-prompt selection is preserved.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Explicit overrides can increase model calls, latency and token cost regardless of provider. The existing `native_thinking` opt-in and rollback path control this behavior. Diagnostics include requested/effective effort, provider alias, model and mapping outcome; they exclude credentials, prompts, endpoint URLs and response bodies.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for downstream Rust source constructing or exhaustively destructuring affected public structs. Existing TOML values, schema enum values, provider defaults and serialized configuration remain compatible.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new key, environment variable or CLI option. Existing opted-in profile levels now affect supported OpenAI native requests.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Exact upgrade steps for existing users: No configuration migration. Downstream `ChatRequest` literals must initialize `thinking_level` (`None` for unrelated requests); rebuilders copy the original level, and exhaustive patterns add the field or `..`. `ThinkingLevel` remains available from its old configuration paths through a re-export. Callers of `default_budget_tokens()` through that path must import `zeroclaw_config::scattered_types::ThinkingLevelBudget`. Public runtime `ThinkingParams` literals need `native_level`; use the existing resolution helper where applicable. Recreate/reconnect Agent/RPC sessions after changing their profile defaults.

A successfully mapped non-`none` public OpenAI reasoning request omits optional `temperature`, as the verified models require. Existing runtime prompt/temperature policy, unmapped/global requests and other providers retain their behavior. Effort changes may affect latency and token usage; subscription model access still depends on the account's existing entitlements. Public API capabilities were checked against [official OpenAI model pages](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models) on 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-27; subscription sets come from list-visible entries in the [Codex catalog at commit `126a0ee92ed2c5e73cd8a8f7e37563e8527552d7`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/126a0ee92ed2c5e73cd8a8f7e37563e8527552d7/codex-rs/models-manager/models.json). Client delegation modes such as `ultra` are excluded and never sent as wire efforts.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Set `native_thinking = false` on affected runtime profiles and apply it through the existing runtime reload or restart lifecycle, including recreating/reconnecting Agent/RPC sessions, to return OpenAI requests to the existing global/default effort path. For a full rollback, revert this PR's merge/squash commit; if merged as separate commits, revert the complete feature commit range, including its API, config, provider and runtime changes together.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Existing `native_thinking` only. Disabling it on a mixed-provider profile also disables its existing native token budgets; revert the complete feature when those budgets must stay enabled.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Upstream request rejection, unexpected latency/token use, an unmapped-level diagnostic, or an effort substitution inconsistent with the serving model. Inspect `requested_level`, `effective_effort`, provider/model and mapping outcome diagnostics without logging request bodies or credentials. Exact and substituted mappings log at DEBUG; unmapped requests log at INFO.
