prs.title: feat(zerocode): effort and display session controls
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `claude/zeroclaw-model-selection-53f2db` (stacked on #10611; retarget to `master` once that lands). Head `2a6d281b350c3e2a65205c2d6a00efda9616da1b`, which merges #10611's refreshed head `d74778eb1396736869780c431995c56de43a2ac3`, so the branch carries that PR's merge of `master` at `46479bdca7` too.
- **What changed and why:**
  - zerocode sessions could not reach the reasoning controls the adaptive-thinking work added: daemon sessions resolved no thinking level at all, `/think:<level>` typed into zerocode reached the model as plain text, and the display was a config-only knob. This adds an **effort** picker and a **display** picker next to the model picker, reachable from the chat title and from `/effort` and `/display`, plus a one-message `/effort:<level>` prefix that daemon turns now honor (`/think:` still works).
  - The options are **model-adaptive** and data-driven: a capability matrix in the provider crate, keyed on the provider slot and the model generation, says which depths and displays a model takes. Opus 4.6 offers no `xhigh` and no display, Haiku 4.5 offers nothing unless the profile opts into budgets, Bedrock offers depths but no display, other providers offer nothing. Both adapters use the same matrix to fit a depth the model lacks and fit a display it does not take, which also covers channels, delegate and config-driven refreshes. The daemon now reports the fitted values too, so the title, the picker's current marker and the request agree even when the standing default is a value the picker does not offer.
  - Choices live on the daemon session (`session/configure` gains `thinking_level`, `thinking_display` and a `reset` list; a model or provider switch clears both), the new `session/thinking-options` method reports what a session may pick and what it currently has, and zerocode remembers the last choice per agent in `zerocode-config.toml` and re-applies it only where the new session's model offers it.
  - The shared channel command is renamed `/effort` (`/thinking` and `/think` stay as aliases) and is advertised on the TUI surface; a new `xhigh` level lands everywhere levels are listed.
  - RPC turns apply native parameters only (no prompt prefixes, no temperature nudge): rewriting the system prompt per level would restart the prompt cache and break signed-thinking replay within a tool round. That is also why `off` and `minimal` are not offered on daemon sessions.
  - **Transport:** an Anthropic request that names a depth and no display used to take the non-streaming fallback, and now streams. That is load-bearing rather than incidental: this PR makes daemon sessions resolve the runtime profile's `default_level` where they previously sent no level at all, so under the old condition every zerocode turn would have left the streaming path and the TUI would have stopped streaming output. The non-streaming path is now taken by fixed-budget requests only, whose budget cannot ride on the streaming API. Signed-thinking replay is preserved on the streaming route because a signature-only block is flushed even with empty thinking text.
  - **`updates` (progress notes)** is gated by generation, not withheld everywhere: generations 4.7 through 5.0 take it, and generation 5.1 narrowed the field to `summarized` and `omitted`, so from there on a configured `updates` is sent as `summarized` with a warning naming the substitution (the maintainer probe on #10611 shows `claude-fable-5-1` answering 400). The beta header follows the value actually sent. `ThinkingDisplay::Updates` and `THINKING_DISPLAY_UPDATES_BETA` are therefore unreachable for the current generation, kept alive by the data table; re-enabling them is a one-line edit to `DISPLAYS_CURRENT` in `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/claude_models.rs` (Refs #10617).
  - **Display precedence, settled:** session, then the Anthropic entry's `thinking_display`, then the runtime profile's `agent.thinking.display`, then the API default. Both resolvers say the same thing: `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/thinking_options.rs` for what the session reports, and `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/anthropic.rs` for what the request carries. To make one order expressible in both, `NativeThinkingParams` now carries the two ends of the chain in separate fields, `display` (chosen for this request) and `profile_display` (the standing default the alias outranks).
- **Scope boundary:** no change to how the CLI loop, channels or the delegate tool apply levels beyond the new `xhigh` value and the `/effort` spelling; no Bedrock display support; no config-pane exposure of the per-agent memory; no live Anthropic call was made (no key was used). The reconciliation with #10542 is confined to the base merge commit and is described there.
- **Blast radius:** Anthropic and Bedrock request shaping (effort fitting, display fitting with progress notes sent as summaries from generation 5.1, the beta header following the display actually sent, adaptive requests streaming again); the RPC session store and the `session/configure` contract, including which patches take the Agent mutex; zerocode chat title, pickers, slash commands and its own config file; docs for zerocode, provider configuration, the RPC socket and provider routing.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #10611. Related #10542 (the display beta this reconciles with). Refs #10617 (`updates` rejected on Fable 5.1).
- **Labels:** `agent`, `channel`, `channel:core`, `cli`, `config`, `distinguished contributor`, `docs`, `enhancement`, `needs-author-action`, `provider`, `provider:anthropic`, `provider:bedrock`, `risk:medium`, `runtime`, `size:XL`, `tool:delegate`, `topic:provider-transport`, `zerocode`

Explainer with diagrams (private until shared): https://claude.ai/code/artifact/09d7d7eb-d382-4df4-8f3e-6ca9f7e8017c

## Since the last review (`f4cd05ae7a` to `2a6d281b35`)

Addressing @Audacity88's `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review and @JordanTheJet's review, then @Audacity88's approval suggestion, plus two base merges.

| Commit | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `4a1338f004` | **Blocker.** `session/configure` no longer waits for the running turn on a thinking-only patch. `SessionStore::set_overrides_gated` decides from the incoming patch whether the Agent has to be touched (`rpc/session.rs:431`, `:444`), so `/effort`, `/display` and their resets commit and return while a turn holds the Agent mutex, instead of storing the value and then reporting the five-second RPC timeout as a failure. Model and temperature changes keep the lock. Regression: `thinking_only_configure_completes_while_a_turn_holds_the_agent` (`rpc/dispatch.rs:12620`). |
| `221cb1f977` | Display precedence settled as session, alias, profile, API default, in both the RPC resolver and the adapter; `NativeThinkingParams.profile_display` added so the two ends of the chain travel apart. |
| `dde4483166` | `thinking_options` reports the effort and display the turn will actually send: `off` and `minimal` report as `low`, a budget-less level on a budget model reports as the default level, and alias and profile displays go through `fit_display` rather than a plain support check. |
| `6a710db0ff` | `ThinkingEffort` serializes as `xhigh`, not `x_high`, matching `as_str`, `ThinkingLevel` and `ThinkingDisplay`. |
| `8e94db62b7` | `ClaudeFamily` and `claude_family` removed: no production caller, and the matrix keys on slot and generation. |
| `e4a8be848d` | The `/effort` rename finished in `channel-runtime-thinking-set` and `channel-runtime-thinking-default` across all five catalogues, with the committed-catalogue assertions moved with them. |
| `a7084dcece` | A production-path regression for the newly common streaming route (adaptive depth, no display), and the redundant `!display_sent` half of the non-streaming guard removed. |
| `00f74fe0c2` | Provider docs corrected: the non-streaming fallback applies to fixed-budget requests only; `updates` is described by the generation that gates it; `native_thinking` gates the token budget, not the adaptive depth. |
| `1fc18e0516`, `91841a8bf8` | Base reconciliation. #10611 added `claude_accepts_display_updates`; this branch already expresses that rule in the capability matrix, so the gate exists once, in the matrix, with the base's cases ported onto it. |
| `6cb2b91f13` | Base refresh onto #10611's new head `d74778eb13` (which carries `master` at `46479bdca7`). Two conflicts needed judgement: `apps/zerocode/src/client.rs`, where the base added `session_state` next to the `session_configure` doc comment this PR rewrote (both kept), and `apps/zerocode/src/chat.rs`, where the base replaced `switch_to_session_entry` with a multi-session `attach_session` path, so this PR's session-boundary options refresh and remembered-choice re-apply moved onto that shared path (`chat.rs:1849`) and ten of the base's tests gained the matching `session/thinking-options` exchange. The PR was reported `CONFLICTING` against its base before this merge; the base head is now an ancestor of this head. |
| `96c225746d` | Compile fix the merge required. The base widened `emit_turn_complete` with the client turn generation and the message count, while the `thinking_level_unsupported` rejection this PR added still called the three-argument form. It now passes the request's generation and no message count (`rpc/dispatch.rs:2309`), matching the `session_not_found` rejection beside it. |
| `2a6d281b35` | @Audacity88's approval suggestion. The provider display section (`docs/book/src/providers/configuration.md:114`) and the `ThinkingConfig.display` doc comment (`crates/zeroclaw-config/src/scattered_types.rs:131`) no longer say the display needs `native_thinking = true`; both now say that flag gates only the fixed token budget, which is what `apply_thinking_level_with_config` does (`agent/thinking.rs:120` gates `budget_tokens`, `:148` fills `profile_display` unconditionally). Regression: `display_mode_propagates_without_native_thinking` (`agent/thinking.rs:670`). |

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui` (zerocode over the daemon socket), `rpc` turns; channels only for the `/effort` spelling.
- **Setup / preconditions:** `cargo build --release -p zeroclaw -p zerocode`; a scratch config dir with a short path (Unix socket paths are capped at 104 bytes on macOS), `schema_version = 3`, an explicit `[gateway] port`, one agent on an Anthropic alias with `model = "claude-fable-5-1"` and a second alias on `claude-haiku-4-5` (a placeholder key is enough for everything but sending a prompt), and `[runtime_profiles.default.thinking] default_level = "high"`. Start `zeroclaw daemon --config-dir <dir>` with `ZEROCLAW_SOCKET=<dir>/data/daemon.sock`, then `zerocode --config-dir <dir>`.
- **Steps to run:** Alt+Right to the Chat pane, pick the agent. Then `/effort`, Esc, `/display`, Down, Enter, `/effort xhigh`, `/effort` again, Esc, `/effort reset`, `/effort bogus`, `/model claude-opus-4-6`, `/effort`, Esc, `/model-provider <haiku alias>`, `/effort`, Ctrl+N. With a real key: `/effort:max explain the classifier` and watch the daemon log.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the title reads `... claude-fable-5-1  effort:high  display:omitted`; the effort picker lists low, medium, high (marked current), xhigh, max; the display picker lists omitted (current) and summarized; choosing summarized updates the title; `/effort xhigh` reports "Effort set to xhigh." and the reopened picker shows a `reset` row; `/effort reset` reports the profile default; `/effort bogus` shows the daemon's rejection text; on Opus 4.6 `xhigh` and the display segment disappear; on Haiku both segments disappear and `/effort` says the model offers no effort levels; Ctrl+N re-applies the remembered `xhigh` and `summarized` where offered; the daemon logs "thinking request resolved for the turn" with `effort: max` and `inline: true` for the prefixed message only.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** no `effort:` or `display:` segment; `/effort` and `/display` are not commands (`/thinking` exists on channels only); `/think:high hello` reaches the model as the literal text; daemon sessions send no thinking level at all, so the runtime profile's `default_level` never reaches the request.

### How I tested

- Hosted CI on this head (`2a6d281b350c3e2a65205c2d6a00efda9616da1b`): `CI Required Gate` SUCCESS, run 34566062312.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The hosted evidence in this bullet is from the previous head; this head adds the base merge, the compile fix it required and one documentation change on top of it. At `91841a8bf8a0`, the [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34187113894/job/101942982244) and required checks pass, including Lint, Test, cross-platform checks, and the Zerocode RPC Boundary check. The [advisory Windows nextest run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34187113894/job/101940103350) passed the new dispatcher, option-reporting, precedence, and production-streaming regressions; its sole failure was the gateway packaging assertion about `../../web/dist`. That test and the gateway files are unchanged from the current stack base. That advisory job is not a required check, and its failure is inherited from the CI script rather than attributed to this PR; it did not pass. The commands and results below are the author's local macOS runs, separate from hosted CI.
- **Known coverage gap, if any:** no live Anthropic or Bedrock request was made and no key was used; the wire shape is pinned at the serialization boundary and through a local SSE server on the production streaming path. The `/effort:<level>` message prefix is exercised with a recording provider rather than a real key. The zerocode session-attach path this merge reworked is covered by unit tests only; it was not re-driven against a live daemon at this head. The pty capture below is historical evidence from `f4cd05ae7a` and was not repeated at this head. The workspace run at this head has one macOS-local failure, in a subprocess-spawning suite this branch does not touch, and it is green when rerun serially; it is listed below with its rerun.
- **Commands run and tail output** (all at `2a6d281b35`, macOS, local toolchain):

```sh
cargo fmt --all --check
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
BASE_SHA="$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD)" bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh

bash scripts/ci/zerocode_no_zeroclaw_dep_gate.sh

cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --test-threads=1
cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-config

cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-run
cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-fail-fast
```

The single workspace failure is `zeroclaw-providers grok_cli::tests::unix_fake_child::timeout_kills_leader_and_descendant`, the known macOS-local timing flake in a crate this branch does not touch. It is green when rerun serially:

The tests this PR adds all pass in the workspace run: `thinking_only_configure_completes_while_a_turn_holds_the_agent`, `options_report_the_level_and_display_the_turn_will_send`, `options_report_the_alias_display_between_session_and_profile`, `adaptive_thinking_without_a_display_uses_the_streaming_production_path`, `the_display_chain_runs_request_then_alias_then_profile`, `effort_serializes_as_the_token_the_adapters_send`, `display_updates_is_refused_from_generation_5_1`, `non_claude_ids_take_no_display_at_all` and the new `display_mode_propagates_without_native_thinking`.

The new regression was proven to fail before the behavior it pins. With `profile_display` temporarily gated on `config.native_thinking`, `cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -E 'test(display_mode_propagates_without_native_thinking)'` fails with `left: None, right: Some(Summarized)`; with the source restored it passes.

`chat::tests::todo_ctrl_p_reopens_latest_plan_after_hidden_update`, which failed on macOS at the head before the first base merge, passes here too.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The release binaries against a scratch daemon, driven through a pty at 120x40 and captured with a terminal emulator: title segments on the Fable agent, both pickers with the current marker, the reset row, `/effort xhigh` and `/effort reset` copy, the model switch to Opus 4.6 dropping `xhigh` and the display segment, the provider switch to Haiku 4.5 and to OpenAI hiding both segments with the "no effort levels" note, Ctrl+N re-applying the remembered per-agent choice (and the `[thinking.agent_override.<alias>]` section written to `zerocode-config.toml`), and the Japanese locale with no unresolved keys. Not verified: a live Anthropic or Bedrock request, and the `/effort:` prefix on a real turn (unit-tested with a recording provider instead).
- **Visual interface changed?** Yes
- **Tested revision, interface, and terminal or viewport dimensions:** the gates and test runs above at `2a6d281b35`; the live pty pass below is historical evidence from `f4cd05ae7a` and was not repeated at this head. The commits since then touch the daemon resolvers, the provider adapters, the runtime channel strings and, through the base merge, zerocode's session-attach path; no zerocode rendering path changed, and the scenario in the frames (profile `default_level = "high"`, no alias display) resolves to the same reported values under the new fitting rules. `tui` (zerocode) over a local daemon socket, 120x40.
- **Terminal transcript evidence (historical, from `f4cd05ae7a`):** terminal frames captured from the pty run (exact cell contents, attributes dropped): These text frames are not screenshots.

`C02` Fable session, `/effort` opened (current row marked):

- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** none. `scripts/ci/zerocode_no_zeroclaw_dep_gate.sh` was skipped at the previous head for want of `tomllib`; it now runs and passes ("no zeroclaw-* dependencies").

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No` (zerocode writes its own existing config file)
- New external network calls? `No`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No` (daemon turns apply native request fields only; no prompt text is added)
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Partially`. Older ZeroCode clients ignore the new fields. With an older daemon, the new client hides effort/display title segments and an explicit picker read reports method-not-found. An unadvertised `/effort high` is submitted as prompt text. An explicit `/display summarized` can currently report and remember success even though the old daemon ignores the new field; that compatibility defect remains to be repaired. Existing channel users keep `/thinking` and `/think` as aliases.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `Yes`: new `xhigh` thinking level; the channel command is `/effort` (aliases kept), and the `channel-runtime-thinking-set` / `channel-runtime-thinking-default` strings name it in all five catalogues; `session/configure` gains `thinking_level`, `thinking_display` and `reset`, and a thinking-only patch no longer waits on the running turn; new `session/thinking-options`, which reports the fitted values a turn will send; zerocode writes `[thinking.agent_override.<alias>]` into `zerocode-config.toml`; daemon sessions now apply the runtime profile's `default_level` natively (they sent no level before); `agent.thinking.display = "omitted"` sends nothing, the API's own default, instead of an explicit `omitted`; a display the model generation does not take is fitted or dropped with a log line instead of being sent; an Anthropic request that names a depth and no display now streams instead of taking the non-streaming fallback; `ThinkingEffort` serializes as `xhigh` rather than `x_high` (the variant is new in this PR, so nothing persisted the old token).
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: none required. Operators who relied on `thinking_display = "updates"` on a non-Fable alias will see it dropped (it was rejected by the API before).

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <squash-merge-sha>`; no data migration is involved. A single session can drop its choices with `/effort reset` and `/display reset`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `session/configure` answering invalid params for a choice the model should take; a missing `effort:` segment on a current Claude model; provider 400s mentioning `effort` or `display` (the matrix would be wrong for that model); the daemon log line "thinking request resolved for the turn" showing an unexpected depth.

prs.title: feat(providers): adapt Anthropic and Bedrock to adaptive-thinking Claude models
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Anthropic's current Claude generations (Fable 5.1, Fable 5, Opus 4.7, 4.8, Opus 5, Sonnet 5) think adaptively: they reject the fixed thinking budget, and they reject a temperature other than 1 while thinking is active, which on these generations is the normal state. The Anthropic and Bedrock adapters now read the model generation from the alias `model` and pick the request shape from it, so a new release needs no code change. Earlier models keep the fixed budget and their temperature.
  - The thinking level maps to `output_config.effort` on those generations, sent together with `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`. A configured temperature is dropped with a warning naming the value, and a warning fires when the output cap is still at the 4096 baseline, because reasoning now counts against it.
  - The streaming parser never read thinking blocks (a long-standing TODO), so streamed tool loops dropped the reasoning the model had signed. They are now captured as one record per block and replayed only within the tool round that produced them, which keeps every existing history-trim path valid under the preserved-thinking rule.
  - New optional `thinking_display` field on the `anthropic` slot (`omitted`, `summarized` or `updates`) so an operator can read the reasoning per provider entry; the runtime shows only the readable text, never the signed record. The generation matrix also carries a display axis: generation 5.1 and later accept only `summarized` and `omitted`, so a configured `updates` is sent to them as `summarized` with a warning naming the substitution (option (b) of #10617), whichever knob it came from.
- **Scope boundary:** No typed provider-refusal handling: that work is consolidated in #9272 and was removed from this branch (see "Relationship to #9272"). No global default changes for output caps or timeouts. No reasoning display on Bedrock. No doctor checks for these aliases. No quickstart auto-fill of `context_window`. No capture of `redacted_thinking` blocks. RPC sessions (zerocode) still send no thinking level, so they run at the model's default depth. No behavior change for temperature on the adaptive generations beyond the existing drop-with-warning; only the wording was narrowed.
- **Blast radius:** Every Anthropic and Bedrock alias (request shape changes only on adaptive-generation models), the config schema (one additive optional field), the runtime's reasoning display forwarding, and the display value sent for `agent.thinking.display = "updates"` on generation 5.1 and later (now `summarized`).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10617 (this PR implements its option (b) for both display knobs; closing it is the maintainer's call). Related #9272 (owns typed provider-refusal handling; see below).
- **Labels:** live snapshot: `enhancement`, `docs`, `core`, `agent`, `channel`, `config`, `gateway`, `provider`, `runtime`, `distinguished contributor`, `provider:reliable`, `provider:anthropic`, `channel:core`, `provider:bedrock`, `tool:delegate`, `needs-maintainer-review`, `risk:medium`, `size:XL`, `channel:acp`, `cli`.

## Relationship to #9272

This PR carries no refusal code. Commit `4dfc2b985e` removed everything this branch had added for declined requests, so there is one implementation of typed provider refusals to review and carry forward, and it lives in #9272. What went: `RefusalCategory`, `ProviderRefusal`, `is_provider_refusal` and `StreamError::Refusal` in `zeroclaw-api`; the refusal stop-reason parsing, the stop-details struct, the category classifier and the fallible `parse_native_response` shape in the Anthropic adapter; the whole refusal layer in `ReliableModelProvider`; the typed cause on `StreamErrorWithUsage`, the category message keys and the `Refused` render arm in the runtime; the seven refusal keys in all five `cli.ftl` catalogues; and the one docs sentence about classifier declines. `grep -ri refusal` over this PR's diff against `origin/master` returns nothing.

Until #9272 lands, a `stop_reason: "refusal"` is not special-cased: the response has no text and no tool calls, so it takes master's existing semantic-empty terminal path, which retries twice and then delivers the invalid-semantic-completion message. That is the behavior on `master` today, unchanged by this PR.

This PR keeps what it is for: adaptive request shaping, effort and display compatibility, and signed-thinking replay.

## Reconciliation with #10542

#10542 (merged, shipped in v0.8.5) landed the shared `ThinkingDisplay` wire enum, the optional `display` field on `NativeThinkingParams`, the beta header plumbing, and streamed thinking capture on the display path. This branch merges master and keeps all of it: the two adapters resolve one `display` value per request, the beta header `thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18` goes out whenever the request carries a display field (master's rule since #10542), and this PR's broader generation matrix and Bedrock work sit on top. The one behavior this PR adds on the shared path is the generation gate on `updates` described above.

## Precedence decision

Both display knobs stay. The order, highest first:

1. An explicit session-level display (the RPC `session/configure` control added by the stacked PR #10636).
2. `providers.models.anthropic.<alias>.thinking_display`, whenever it is set. `omitted` on the entry means the API default: no display field is sent, whatever the profile says.
3. `agent.thinking.display`, applied only when the entry leaves its knob unset.
4. The API default (no display field).

This is the same entry-overrides-profile pattern that `temperature` and `max_tokens` already follow. Before this revision an entry set to `omitted` mapped to no value and fell through to the profile's setting; an explicit entry value now always wins. #10636, which stacks on this branch, implements the session-level step at the top of that order and so reflects the same decision; it is refreshed on this head.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` and `tui` (zerocode)
- **Setup / preconditions:** An `[providers.models.anthropic.<alias>]` entry with `model = "claude-fable-5-1"`, `max_tokens = 32000`, `timeout_secs = 900`, `context_window = 1000000`, `thinking_display = "summarized"`, `fallback_models = ["claude-opus-5"]`; a second alias with `temperature = 0.2` and `max_tokens = 2048` as a negative control; a third on `claude-sonnet-4-5` with `native_thinking = true` in its runtime profile as a regression control; a fourth on `claude-fable-5-1` with `thinking_display = "updates"` as the display-fit control; a runtime profile with `[runtime_profiles.<alias>.thinking] default_level = "high"`.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. `zeroclaw --verbose --log-level debug agent -a <agent> -m "Use the shell tool to run ls, then summarize what you found."`
  2. Send the same with a `/think:max` prefix, then `/think:low`, then `/think:medium`.
  3. Run one turn on the negative-control alias with `-p anthropic.<bad-alias>`.
  4. Run one tool turn on the regression-control alias.
  5. Run one turn on the display-fit alias.
  6. In zerocode from this branch (`./target/release/zerocode`, so it spawns the sibling `zeroclaw`): pick the Fable alias from the title bar, run a tool task with the thought panel open, then switch to `claude-opus-5` from the title bar and send another message.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The `anthropic streaming provider request prepared` debug event reports `"thinking": "adaptive"`, `"effort": "high"`, `"stream": true`, no `budget_tokens` and no temperature; the second tool round succeeds. Step 2 changes the logged effort to `max`, `low`, then none. Step 3 logs `temperature dropped: this model generation only accepts temperature 1 while thinking is active` and `max_tokens is at the baseline; reasoning counts toward it on this model generation, so raise it on the provider entry`. Step 4 still sends `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: 10000}` with `temperature: 1.0`. Step 5 logs `thinking display fitted: this model generation accepts only summarized or omitted, so updates was sent as summarized` and the request succeeds with `display: "summarized"` on the wire. Step 6 shows prose in the thought panel, and the request after the model switch succeeds.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** With `native_thinking = true`, master (since #10542) sends `claude-fable-5-1` the adaptive shape with the temperature pinned to 1 and no `output_config.effort`, so `/think:` levels change only the prompt prefix and never the request depth; with it off, a configured temperature goes out unchanged and is rejected while thinking is active, and no thinking object is sent at all. Streamed tool loops replay no thinking blocks unless a display value is set. `agent.thinking.display = "updates"` on `claude-fable-5-1` returns 400 (`thinking.adaptive.display: Input should be 'summarized', 'omitted'`), and an entry-level `thinking_display` does not exist. The thought panel shows nothing or raw JSON records.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The required `cargo nextest` workspace job covers the provider, api, config and runtime crates changed here; `Docs Style` (docs quality and links gates) covers the two changed Markdown files; the comment hygiene gate covers the Rust comments this branch adds.
- Hosted CI on this head (`d74778eb1396736869780c431995c56de43a2ac3`): `CI Required Gate` SUCCESS, run 34560876208. `Advisory Windows nextest (scoped, plugin-host=true)` failed (non-required; maintainers attribute it to an inherited CI-script problem, not this PR).
- **Historical hosted CI:** the previous exact-head run for `22d912be378a10b30b5d998e1da7d989e2d83a60` ([run 34164949852](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34164949852)) reported `CI Required Gate` SUCCESS, along with `Test`, `Lint`, `Format`, `Security`, `Docs Style`, `MSRV (declared floor)` and the per-target `Check` jobs.
- **Advisory Windows nextest:** that run's non-required `Advisory Windows nextest (full, plugin-host=true)` job failed. Maintainers attribute this to an inherited CI-script failure (blank `--package` arguments and the `../../web/dist` packaging assertion) rather than to this PR; it is not claimed as passing here.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No CI job calls the live Anthropic API, so the adaptive request shape, the streamed thinking capture, and the fitted `summarized` request on generation 5.1 are verified by unit tests and SSE fixtures rather than a real response. The 5.1 display boundary rests on one live probe of `claude-fable-5-1` (by the reviewer, 2026-09-04); `updates` was not probed on Opus 4.7, 4.8, Opus 5 or Sonnet 5. Whether Bedrock forwards `output_config` through `additionalModelRequestFields` is likewise unverified. The removal in `4dfc2b985e` carries no regression test of its own: a test for the post-removal `stop_reason: "refusal"` path would reintroduce the vocabulary the removal is meant to clear from this branch, and that path is master's existing semantic-empty terminal behavior, already covered by master's tests.

prs.title: fix(cron): bound agent job runs with a wall-clock timeout that releases the lock
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Cron agent jobs now use the owning agent's existing `runtime_profiles.*.agentic_timeout_secs`, with the scheduler's 1,800-second default when the value is unset or zero.
  - Agent runs and scheduled delivery execute on independently driven runtimes. A deadline requests cancellation, but the durable claim remains owned until the private runtime has dropped the user-visible work, preventing a replacement run from overlapping a non-yielding provider or tool operation.
  - `supervise_owned` records a monotonic `completed_at` timestamp on private worker completion and teardown, checking it against the deadline instant so that a worker completing past the deadline while the caller runtime is stalled is authoritatively treated as `DeadlineExceeded` rather than ordinary failure or late success.
  - The supervised run token is the canonical cancellation source for direct and SOP-reassembled delegate registries. Supervised cron runs explicitly reject background delegation (`background=true`) before spawn with localized error `delegate-background-cron-owned-rejected` because background tasks would outlive the scheduler's private runtime and escape the durable claim boundary. `DelegateTool` description, schema, and book documentation (`docs/book/src/agents/delegation.md`, `docs/book/src/architecture/background-work-lifecycle.md`) are aligned with this contract; cron jobs must use synchronous or parallel delegation instead.
  - Run ownership is opt-in per registry, not a property of any cancellation token. `DelegateTool::with_cancellation_token` keeps its pre-existing ordinary cascade semantics, and the new `DelegateTool::with_run_owned_cancellation_token` is what the tool factory uses when a supervised cron run supplies its token. An external caller that passes its own token therefore keeps `background=true`.
  - In-process peer delivery is the second detached route out of a run. `SendMessageToPeerTool` accepts the supervised run's token and, when it is set, waits for the recipient's turn to finish rather than reporting acceptance and walking away, so an accepted send cannot be aborted when the run's private runtime is dropped and the reported outcome is the delivery that actually happened. Cancellation aborts the recipient and reports that the message was not delivered. Callers with no supervised run keep the detached behavior.
  - Ownership now reaches the peer recipient's own registry, not just the send. `process_message` reads the same `AGENT_RUN_CANCELLATION` task-local that `agent::run` reads and passes it into `all_tools_with_runtime` and the SOP step reassembly, and the peer tool re-scopes that owner on the delivery task (a spawned task does not inherit task-locals). Under an owning run the recipient's rebuilt `delegate` and `send_message_to_peer` are therefore fenced the same way the direct path already was, so a recipient cannot detach a child that outlives the claim.
  - Cron claims carry an opaque token that fences persistence and release. Claims do not expire by elapsed wall-clock time. A full process restart clears claims left by dead workers; on in-process daemon reload, dropping the old supervisor requests cancellation and the replacement scheduler waits for cron-owned workers keyed by the canonical jobs database path before stale-lock recovery.
  - Scheduled delivery, synchronous persistence, and isolated-session cleanup each have an explicit boundary. Persistence that misses its await deadline reports `persistence-pending` instead of false success and retains the claim. Persistence worker admission is bounded by a process-wide semaphore (`MAX_PERSISTENCE_WORKERS = 16`), and a completed result waits for admission under the same deadline that bounds the write rather than being discarded while the pool is busy, so a concurrency burst above the pool size only delays persistence. Best-effort cleanup admits at most one detached worker process-wide so a permanently blocked backend cannot leak threads.
  - A completed result is never dropped when admission stays full through the whole deadline. The result is packaged as `PendingPersist` and handed to its own bounded owner task, which waits for capacity without a deadline and then performs the same durable write, releasing the claim under the same token fence with no scheduler restart. `MAX_RETAINED_RESULT_OWNERS = 16` bounds how many retained owners contend for a permit at once, and the queueing happens on the owner's task so the scheduler loop is never blocked. The blocking write is extracted as `write_pending_persist` so the inline path and the retained owner share one implementation.
- **Scope boundary:** This does not add process owner IDs, heartbeats, polling-time claim reclamation, or a cross-process lease protocol from Related #9191. Shell-job timeout behavior and the delegate tool's existing zero-timeout interpretation are unchanged. Persistence capacity is not pre-reserved before a run starts; the retained owner covers the completed-result case instead.
- **Blast radius:** Cron agent execution, delegate children owned by cron, in-process peer delivery under cron (including the recipient's own rebuilt registry), scheduled announcement delivery, isolated-session cleanup, and cron result persistence/broadcasting. The `tight` and `local_small` runtime presets now apply their existing 120-second agentic deadline to cron jobs.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9191
- **Labels:** `bug`, `docs`, `agent`, `channel`, `config`, `cron`, `daemon`, `gateway`, `runtime`, `distinguished contributor`, `channel:core`, `tool:delegate`, `needs-author-action`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes; a daemon-level A/B run adds signal beyond deterministic scheduler and provider-boundary regressions.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` = `cli`; cron scheduler runtime behavior.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Configure a cron agent job with a custom provider endpoint that accepts a connection without replying. Set a short nonzero `agentic_timeout_secs` on the owning agent's runtime profile.
- **Steps to run:** Schedule the job, observe its run history and claim state through the timeout, then let the next scheduled tick arrive.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The deadline remains observable, yielding work is cancelled, non-yielding work retains the claim until it stops, the terminal timeout is not retried for that tick, and the next run starts only after ownership is released.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** A hung agent run had no wall-clock bound and could retain its in-flight lock until daemon restart.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Validation below was run locally at the exact current head `b37fa87a0b047add9309764b06bfb6be303e75aa`, which merges `origin/master` at `46479bdca74bedb5c71e30afab657ccaac77dab4` and adds the two review fixes plus their docs alignment.
- Hosted CI on this head (`b37fa87a0b047add9309764b06bfb6be303e75aa`): `CI Required Gate` SUCCESS, run 34555807598.
- **Historical hosted evidence:** The previous head `654fb2b1fe81912af6121241dfcb60d4fea8c941` was green on its required checks: run [34199824963](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34199824963) passed `CI Required Gate`, `Test`, `Lint`, `Format`, `Parallel Runtime Test`, `Test (Landlock)`, `Security`, `MSRV (declared floor)`, `Semgrep`, `Docs Style`, and the platform `Check` matrix, with the Nix, Windows-clippy and relay-smoke jobs skipped. The `8e71093ec6c7860c7185571d71fe1ef908b57f86` and `f943f78b28f5d4e0e569326c5a1fb3a8d139cead` evidence quoted in earlier revisions of this body is superseded and historical.
- **Advisory Windows:** On current head `b37fa87a0b047add9309764b06bfb6be303e75aa`, the non-required [Windows nextest job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34555807598/job/103130303805) failed `published_crates_never_include_files_outside_their_own_directory` and `run_tool_call_loop_reuses_fallback_image_cache_across_iterations`, and aborted `process_line_session_new_creates_session_on_two_megabyte_stack` with a stack overflow. These are the current hosted failures; their root causes have not been reproduced locally. `CI Required Gate` passed.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No deliberately killed production database, live 30-minute daemon hang, real stalled PostgreSQL backend, or daemon-level A/B smoke was used. No live multi-daemon peer topology was exercised; the nested peer regression drives the real tool boundary against an HTTP-level provider mock rather than a real model. Deterministic regressions cover non-yielding pre-await work, persistence stalls, bounded persistence admission, recovery of a completed result once capacity returns, recovery of a result retained past its own admission deadline, claim fencing, delayed delivery, cleanup admission, late caller resume deadline enforcement, generic-versus-run-owned delegate cancellation, run-owned peer delivery surviving the private runtime's teardown, and ownership propagation into the peer recipient's rebuilt registry. The peer-delivery regression drives a private current-thread runtime dropped at parent return, which is the shape `supervise_owned` uses, not the scheduler's supervisor end to end. The Linux `voice-wake` feature smoke was not run locally because this host does not provide the ALSA development package; there are no voice-wake code changes in this PR.

Confirmed both new regressions fail with only their production change reverted and pass with it applied. `run_owned_peer_send_fences_background_delegation_inside_the_recipient` fails with the `process_message` token read reverted (the recipient's advertised `delegate` contract is the ordinary background one) and passes with it applied; `persist_claimed_job_result_persists_a_result_retained_past_its_deadline` fails with the retention handoff replaced by a drop (the second job's run row never commits inside the 15-second poll budget) and passes with it applied. Also verified that `supervise_owned` carries monotonic completion timestamps and treats completions after deadline expiry as non-retryable `DeadlineExceeded`, and that `DelegateTool` description and parameter schema truthfully reject `background=true` only under run-owned cancellation.
- **Visual interface changed?** N/A; no rendered text, layout, or visual interaction changed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The external daemon, PostgreSQL, and Linux ALSA gaps are described above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? Yes
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Timeout/error cleanup can construct the already-configured memory backend and purge the run-unique isolated session, which may reuse existing Qdrant or PostgreSQL network access. Memory-free and main-session jobs skip cleanup, the call is best-effort with a short deadline, and detached cleanup admission is capped at one process-wide worker.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes; the existing `runtime_profiles.*.agentic_timeout_secs` setting now bounds cron agent jobs, and cron-owned agent jobs now reject background delegation (`background=true`) before spawn.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`:
  - **Operators:** Existing cron configurations or agent prompts requesting `background=true` via the `delegate` tool will receive the localized error `delegate-background-cron-owned-rejected`. That now also applies to an agent reached through in-process peer delivery from a cron run, because the recipient's turn runs under the same owner. Cron jobs requiring concurrent sub-agents must migrate to synchronous delegation (`background=false`) or parallel delegation (`parallel=[...]`). A cron agent that sends to an in-process peer agent waits for that recipient's turn instead of getting an immediate acceptance, so the recipient's own duration counts against the cron run's `agentic_timeout_secs`. Operators of long cron agent jobs should set an appropriate nonzero `agentic_timeout_secs`; zero uses the scheduler default. The cron database adds an internal claim-token column automatically.
  - **Downstream Rust callers of the published `zeroclaw-runtime` crate:** `cron::claim_job` and `cron::release_job` are no longer unconditional public exports; they are `#[cfg(test)]`-only, and their token-qualified replacements (`claim_job_with_token`, `release_claim`) are crate-private because a claim can only be released by the token that took it. `all_tools_with_runtime` takes a new required `run_cancellation: Option<CancellationToken>` argument; pass `None` for the previous behavior. `DelegateTool::with_cancellation_token` keeps its existing meaning, and run ownership is requested explicitly through the new `DelegateTool::with_run_owned_cancellation_token` and `SendMessageToPeerTool::with_run_owned_cancellation_token`. `process_message` keeps its signature: it resolves run ownership from the ambient run scope rather than from a new parameter. These are deliberate pre-1.0 API changes rather than accidental removals: an unfenced public release helper cannot be kept without reopening the claim-ownership hole this PR closes.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's eventual squash commit. The internal database migration is additive and can remain present after rollback.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** No dedicated feature flag. Raising the existing per-agent `agentic_timeout_secs` increases the run deadline; disabling the cron job stops future attempts.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Legitimate jobs ending with `agent job timed out after Ns`; `Cron persistence exceeded its deadline` or `Cron persistence pool stayed at capacity; retaining the completed result for a later write` followed by `Cron retained result persisted once capacity returned`; `Cron retained result failed to persist`; `best-effort cleanup worker capacity is exhausted`; a cron run whose duration now includes an in-process peer recipient's turn; or scheduled delivery timeout/failure logs.

prs.title: feat(oidc): accept untyped access tokens and declared claim names for JWKS
prs.body:
> **Stacked:** Depends on #12497. Until that merges this PR also shows its commit (`140e9e594f`); review only `fd2bb3da4c`.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Okta and Entra ID are required for v1.0 (#12496), and the JWKS verifier refused both. Okta access tokens have no header `typ` and name the client in `cid`. Entra ID tokens have `typ: JWT`, use `uti` instead of `jti`, and name the client only in `azp`, including for service principals. Entra has no introspection endpoint to fall back to.
  - **Untyped tokens, without weakening token purpose.** `require_at_jwt = false` (previously rejected for `jwks`) now admits a header with no `typ` or `typ: JWT` only when `audience` is an API identifier that no client signs in as: not `client_id`, not in `interactive_clients`/`service_clients`/`allowed_authorized_parties`/`service_profile_map`, and not a client of another `[oidc.*]` entry for the same issuer. Every ID token's `aud` is the client it was issued to (OIDC Core), so an ID token cannot carry that audience. Config validation enforces this; the verifier re-checks the entry's own clients through the same `OidcConfig::audience_shared_with_a_client` so a provider built from unvalidated config is still safe. Other header types (`logout+jwt`, `dpop+jwt`, ...), `nonce`, and non-access purpose markers are still refused.
  - **Declared claim names instead of vendor detection.** `client_id_claim` (default `client_id`) and `token_id_claim` (default `jti`). Chosen over built-in fallbacks (`cid`/`uti`) because `azp` means different things on Keycloak (stamped on user tokens of service clients) and Entra (the client of every token): only an operator declaration can safely let `azp` prove a *service* client, and fallbacks would grow into a per-IdP mapping table. A declared client claim has no `azp` fallback and must agree with any present `client_id` or `azp`. Both are JWKS-only and refused for introspection (RFC 7662 answers use `client_id`).
  - Removes the now-unread `Claims.jti` field; the token id is read from the declared claim.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to introspection, typed (`at+jwt`) tokens with default claim names, the resolver, or refresh. Okta and Entra are NOT added to "Tested providers": they still need real-tenant verification (an acceptance gate in #12496).
- **Blast radius:** JWKS bearer verification for every surface (RPC/WSS, gateway, dashboard). With defaults the accepted set is unchanged; the new behavior is reachable only by setting `require_at_jwt = false` or the new claim keys.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #12497. Related #8289, Related #12496

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw checks that a sign-in token is really an *access* token meant for it, and not an *ID token* (which only proves someone logged in to some app). It did this by requiring a "this is an access token" label that Okta and Microsoft Entra ID don't put on their tokens, so neither could sign in. This adds a second, equally strict way to tell them apart, based on who the token is addressed to: ZeroClaw's own API identifier, which no app ever logs in as, so an ID token can never be addressed to it. It also lets the operator say which field a provider uses for the app's name and the token's ID, rather than ZeroClaw guessing per vendor. Existing setups behave exactly as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Verification is covered with signed tokens against a mock JWKS issuer; real Okta/Entra tenants are a tracked gate in #12496.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Rust lint/test jobs cover `zeroclaw-config` and `zeroclaw-runtime` (verifier) and `zeroclaw-gateway` (consumer). Docs style covers `identity-providers.md`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No real Okta or Entra tenant in CI.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (CI-pinned toolchain `1.98.0`, on `fd2bb3da4c`)

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(no output, exit 0)

$ cargo +1.98.0 clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 19s

$ cargo +1.98.0 check --workspace --all-targets
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 17s

$ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-config
test result: ok. 1999 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
(integration targets: 106, 9, 8, 5, 1, 1 passed)

$ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib security::auth_provider
test result: ok. 139 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 6083 filtered out

$ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib oidc
test result: ok. 49 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 867 filtered out

$ DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/security/identity-providers.md scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
Summary: 0 error(s)
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Tests were written first. Config tests failed to compile (missing fields); of the 9 new verifier tests, the 4 asserting newly accepted shapes failed on behavior before the implementation, while the 5 refusal tests already passed, confirming nothing previously refused was relied on. New verifier coverage: untyped refused while typing is required; `typ: JWT` and no-`typ` accepted once waived with a separate audience; other header types, an untyped ID token (`aud` = client), and `nonce` still refused when waived; the verifier refuses untyped tokens without separation even if config validation was skipped; Okta `cid` names the client and is refused when undeclared; declared claim contradicted by `client_id` refused; declared claim has no `azp` fallback; Entra service token (`typ: JWT`, `azp`, `uti`) resolves to a service principal only when `azp` is declared, and is refused with defaults; token id read from the declared claim only. New config coverage: defaults, separation against `client_id` (empty and equal), each client list, a same-issuer sibling entry (and not a different-issuer one), TOML round-trip with an Okta shape, claim-name format, JWKS-only. Not verified: real Okta/Entra tokens.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `fd2bb3da4c`
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full `cargo test --workspace` skipped: changes are confined to `OidcConfig` and the OIDC provider; affected crates were tested and the workspace type-checked.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No (synthetic ids, `example.com`/`example.okta.com`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: This changes which bearer tokens authenticate. Risk: an ID token accepted as an access token. Mitigation: opt-in only (`require_at_jwt = false`); accepted only when the audience is provably not any configured client of that issuer, enforced at config load and re-checked in the verifier from one shared definition; non-access header types, `nonce`, and payload purpose markers remain refused; tests mint an untyped ID token and assert refusal. Residual (documented, and recorded in #12496): the IdP must never sign anyone in *as* the API registration itself, which ZeroClaw cannot observe. `azp` proves a service client only when the operator declares it as the client claim; the Keycloak default (azp never proves a service) is unchanged.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes (defaults unchanged; `require_at_jwt = false` was previously a validation error for `jwks`)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: `[oidc.<alias>] client_id_claim`, `token_id_claim`; `require_at_jwt = false` newly permitted for `jwks` under the audience-separation rule.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: None required. Okta: `require_at_jwt = false`, `client_id_claim = "cid"`, `audience` = the authorization server's audience. Entra ID: v2.0 tokens (`accessTokenAcceptedVersion = 2`), `require_at_jwt = false`, `client_id_claim = "azp"`, `token_id_claim = "uti"`, `audience` = the API app's client ID (a separate registration from the signing-in client), plus scopes from #12497.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert fd2bb3da4c`. Per-deployment, set `require_at_jwt = true` and remove `client_id_claim`/`token_id_claim` to return to exact prior verification without a code change.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `[oidc.<alias>] require_at_jwt` (opt-in), `client_id_claim`, `token_id_claim`.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** After a revert, entries with `require_at_jwt = false` fail config validation ("require_at_jwt must be true"), so affected deployments surface the problem at load rather than silently. Mis-configuration shows as `-32010` / "OIDC authentication refused" for Okta/Entra users.

prs.title: feat(tools): scaffold async sessions_message (#11119)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** Scaffold for durable async `sessions_message` per RFC #11027 / tracker #11119: delivery ID, same-alias auth, 32 KiB body limit, `SessionBackend` trait hooks (store/load/admit) with default no-ops, tool that creates message events (not direct history appends).
- **Scope boundary:** Does **not** include sync `sessions_prompt` (see #12258), cross-alias messaging, receiver admission/processing, Zerocode UI, concrete durable storage, ACP/RPC wiring, or active-turn delivery.
- **Blast radius:** New tool + trait methods with default no-ops; callers unchanged until a backend implements storage.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11119, Related #11027. Sibling sync extract: #12258.

### What this does, simply

Starts the async “leave a message for another session” path from the accepted RFC: same-alias only, with a delivery id, without forcing the receiver to reply.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A for this scaffold slice — unit tests cover auth/size/target validation.

prs.title: feat(oidc): make requested OAuth scopes configurable per provider
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds `[oidc.<alias>] scopes` (device grant + browser Authorization Code, including dashboard sign-in) and `service_scopes` (`client_credentials`). Every flow previously hard-coded `scope=openid`.
  - Entra ID derives the access token's audience from the requested scope, and its `client_credentials` grant accepts only `api://<app>/.default` (no `openid`). With a fixed `openid`, Entra cannot issue a token for ZeroClaw's audience at all, which blocks the v1.0 Okta + Entra ID requirement recorded in #12496. Two lists are needed because the interactive and service flows want incompatible scope sets on Entra.
  - Validation fails closed: each entry must be an RFC 6749 §3.3 scope-token (rejects blank, whitespace that would split one entry into two scopes, `"`, `\`, control, and non-ASCII), no duplicates, and interactive `scopes` must include `openid` because browser sign-in validates an ID token. No scope, including `offline_access`, is ever added implicitly (its meaning differs by issuer; on Keycloak it yields an offline token that outlives the SSO session).
  - Removes the "No configurable scopes" limitation from `identity-providers.md` and updates the two lines that depended on it.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change token verification (Okta/Entra token-format compatibility is a separate PR), does not add RFC 8707 `resource`, and does not touch refresh tokens. Defaults are unchanged: an entry without the new keys sends exactly `scope=openid` as before.
- **Blast radius:** `Enrollment` request building, used by gateway device/browser enrollment, dashboard sign-in, and `zeroclaw oidc login|token`. `OidcConfig` gains two `#[serde(default)]` fields; the field reference in `authentication.md` is rendered from their doc comments via `{{#config-fields oidc}}`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8289, Related #12496

### What this does, simply

When ZeroClaw asks an identity provider to sign someone in, it says what it wants access to through "scopes". Until now it always asked for just `openid`. That's enough for Keycloak, but Microsoft Entra ID decides who a token is *for* from the scopes requested, so with only `openid` Entra hands back a token for Microsoft's own APIs that ZeroClaw rightly refuses. This lets an operator list the scopes per provider, separately for people signing in and for headless service accounts. Nothing changes for existing setups.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Request building is covered end-to-end against a mock IdP that matches the decoded form field exactly. Manual testing needs an Entra tenant, which is a tracked acceptance gate in #12496.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Rust lint/test jobs cover `zeroclaw-config`, `zeroclaw-runtime`, and `zeroclaw-gateway`. Docs style covers `identity-providers.md`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None for request building. Real-IdP behavior (Entra/Okta) is not exercised by CI.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (CI-pinned toolchain `1.98.0`)

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(no output, exit 0)

$ cargo +1.98.0 clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2m 00s

$ cargo +1.98.0 check --workspace --all-targets
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2m 10s

$ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-config
test result: ok. 1992 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
(plus integration targets: 106, 9, 8, 5, 1, 1, 1 passed)

$ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib security::auth_provider
test result: ok. 130 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 6083 filtered out

$ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib oidc
test result: ok. 49 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 867 filtered out

$ DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/security/identity-providers.md scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
Summary: 0 error(s)
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Tests were written first and failed to compile against `master` (missing fields/methods) before the implementation. New tests: default `openid` for device, PKCE, and `client_credentials`; configured scopes sent space-joined in order for the device grant (S256 variant the gateway relays) and the PKCE authorize URL; `client_credentials` sends `service_scopes`, not the interactive list; TOML round-trip with an Entra-shaped entry; validation of scope-token charset, duplicates, and the `openid` requirement. The mock matcher decodes the form body and compares the `scope` field exactly, so order and encoding are both checked. Not verified: a real Entra or Okta tenant.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `140e9e594f`
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full `cargo test --workspace` skipped: the change is confined to `OidcConfig` and `Enrollment`; affected crates were tested and the workspace was type-checked. Locally, `clippy` on the newer rustc 1.99 reports `needless_borrows_for_generic_args` in `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/lib.rs:1121,1125`. That is pre-existing, untouched by this PR, and does not fire on CI's pinned 1.98.0.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No (same endpoints; only the `scope` value is configurable)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No (all-zero/all-one GUIDs and `example.com` only)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. Note: scopes widen what the IdP *issues*, never what ZeroClaw *accepts*; verification rules are unchanged, and `offline_access` is never added implicitly.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes (both fields default to empty, which sends `openid` as before)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: two optional keys, `[oidc.<alias>] scopes` and `service_scopes`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: None required. To use: `scopes = ["openid", "offline_access", "api://<app>/<scope>"]` and/or `service_scopes = ["api://<app>/.default"]`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: `git revert 140e9e594f`. `OidcConfig` does not deny unknown fields, so entries that set `scopes`/`service_scopes` still deserialize after a revert; the keys are ignored and every flow goes back to `scope=openid` (for Entra ID that means sign-in fails as it does on `master` today).

prs.title: feat(tools): add opt-in task-owned SSH transport reuse
prs.body:
## Summary





Base branch: `master`.





Add opt-in task-owned SSH transport reuse. Related #11867.





### What this does, simply





One logical task owns its transport pool. Healthy idle connections can be recreated; failed or unexpectedly dead transports remain unavailable until the task ends.





## Testing (required)





### How you can test (when useful)





Run `python3 scripts/ssh/test_ssh_task.py -v` and `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib task_ssh::tests`. Native Linux/OpenSSH lifecycle checks should cover process death, expiry and task cleanup.





### How I tested





Current-head CI Required Gate and all executed checks pass at 1add22e4e970f98fb1e018e0c07d9e56b4876515, including CLI-only artifact ratchet, parallel Runtime Test and Windows coverage. All 14 helper regressions and 20 native Linux/OpenSSH candidate checks passed. The integrated composition c67330cc221ffdee48494424071833f8b2165230 passed 13 follow-up validation groups: the actual opt-in helper steering test observed one task ID across both tool rounds; five streamed lifecycle tests, two task-scope tests, strict Clippy and release passed. Alias/effective-configuration isolation, per-key network setup, 8 KiB in-memory stderr and idle retirement/generation leases are covered. Earlier recommended maintainer commits retain their authorship. The Core ownership decision remains pending.





Visual interface evidence: this follow-up changes integration, lifecycle or tests; prior feature UI evidence remains linked in the review discussion. No new presentation claim is made from source inspection. Remaining platform/integration gaps are those not covered by current-head hosted CI and the named local checks.





## Security & Privacy Impact (required)





The feature reuses existing SSH authentication and host-trust settings. No credential export or trust override is added. The failure-cache repair reclaims process/log/socket resources while retaining the task failure record. New transport access remains opt-in and task-scoped.





- New permissions/capabilities/filesystem scope: No — existing configured SSH authority only.


- New external network calls: Yes — configured SSH destinations through the opt-in helper; no new trust source.


- Secrets/credentials handling changed: No — existing SSH agent and host-trust policy remain authoritative.


- PII, real identities or private messages in the diff/tests/docs: No.


- Untrusted model-visible content changed: No





## Compatibility (required)





Backward compatible when disabled. The documented opt-in uses the ZEROCLAW_SSH_TASK_HELPER environment variable and helper/PATH contract; no new stored configuration field is added. No toolchain-floor change.





## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)





Disable the opt-in transport reuse or revert the feature. End the owning logical task before starting a new one after diagnosing a cached failure; task close reclaims remaining transports. Observe explicit transport-unavailable errors and leftover task processes.





## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)





None. Incorporated maintainer commits retain their original authorship.





## Pending Core Team decision





Pending the Core Team task-owner/configuration/runtime-entrypoint decision and any recorded bounded exception. Transport ownership remains in zeroclaw-tools. The proposed runtime wrapper destination is the planned kernel agent-loop owner, reviewed at extraction design review or before expanding transport, configuration or cleanup authority. The lifecycle repair does not grant that exception.



## Review follow-up - 2026-11-09



The sandbox finding is addressed in the current head. A shell command is refused before spawn when its turn owns a host SSH broker and an OS sandbox is active; stripping the environment alone would not prevent socket discovery through shared directories. The final safe/TUI environment overlay also removes all host-broker variables and injects the current task identity only for the native unsandboxed path. Two real child-process regressions cover environment stripping and stale-identity replacement. The exact shared shell source passed all 68 shell tests in the recovery integration worktree; task-helper lifecycle tests passed. Fresh exact-head CI is requested. The unrelated Telegram test delta was removed. The approved exception record #12266 still must land before this feature; approval is not being treated as a merged record.




SQLite follow-up: the workspace-only bridge from #12322 was removed from this independent PR after review identified the crates.io consumer limitation. Registry dependency compatibility is preserved. The shared security advisory remains tracked in #12320; #12322 is not a merge prerequisite for this PR.

## Foreground transport and runtime placement

The [isolated Linux/OpenSSH check](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11869#issuecomment-6880479690) exercised an alias with `ForkAfterAuthentication=yes`, waited for the remote command, and checked cleanup after both normal shutdown and forced helper termination. The required CI gate passes on the current head. Depends on #12266 for the recorded runtime placement.


## Managed SSH argument boundary

Commit `f317b4ca2` rejects option-looking destination aliases and places the argument terminator before the destination in both effective-config lookup and master creation. The command client already placed the terminator there. The README now specifies OpenSSH 8.7 or later for ForkAfterAuthentication.

```text
python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/ssh -p 'test_ssh_task.py'
Ran 16 tests
OK
```

The focused test verifies rejection before launch and the expected boundary in both argv lists. The companion #12418 suite with the updated base passed all 18 tests. These tests use no network or real keys. The production Rust helper already implements the destination boundary.


## Proxy subprocess shutdown

At `f702e8290`, the managed OpenSSH master starts in a dedicated process group. Task shutdown signals the whole group and escalates to SIGKILL for survivors, including a proxy that outlives the master. A Linux test uses real OpenSSH and a local ProxyCommand that ignores SIGTERM. Before the change the proxy was still running after closing the pool. After the change the proxy stopped and the control-socket path was absent. The fixture opens no external connections and uses no keys. ProxyJump was not exercised separately.

```text
python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/ssh -p 'test_ssh_task.py'
Ran 17 tests
OK
```

The dependent #12418 suite passed 19 tests. The Rust broker source is unchanged by this Python helper patch.
